entry: POKENAME are constantly seen closed and at rest, their tough shell and sharp spikes deterring most predators. Those who attempt to forcefully pry open the shell will see it open suddenly to launch a devastating punch from within.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its powerful grip, POKENAME feels like it would be cheating to use it. Anyway, because of how weak their arms are, they end up using that strength to power up its punches.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME creates deafening shockwaves by snapping its powerful claws. By doing this they usually make their opponents faint without landing a single punch.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME release a sticky saliva from their tongue that is difficult to remove. One lick from a POKENAME can prevent gills from functioning properly, which makes them great aquatic hunters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its tongue is over twice its body length, so it mainly uses it to determine its surroundings. If any bird Pokémon tries to eat it, it will coat their wings in its sticky saliva, making it difficult for them to fly.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's awkward body forces it to hop on its tongue, causing pain that keeps it stationary. It sustains itself by licking Electric-Type Pokémon for energy.
author: matpal6

entry: Thanks to a hive mind, any flavor one egg's tongue comes across, the others will taste as well. Should one of the clutch find something particularly delicious, the entire group will swarm and lick it intensely from all sides.
author: sk372

entry: Between the stone whip it carries and its thick tongue, POKENAME is never lacking a tool to bludgeon opponents. It's quite protective of smaller, younger Pokémon it resides near.
author: sk372

entry: If something piques its interest, it will charge towards it, intent on licking it thoroughly. It will bowl over anything unfortunate enough to get between it and its target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slams its tongue against cave walls to dislodge gravel. It consumes the stones to harden and reinforce its tough body.
author: .izik

entry: Before offering any of its nutritious eggs to others, POKENAME will thoroughly lick them to ensure they are clean. While meant as a gesture of goodwill, this often makes the exchange feel awkward for the other party.
author: sk372

entry: Like its vines, POKENAME's tongue will be replaced by a new one within 24 hours if severed. A severed tongue flops and wriggles for several seconds afterward, a sight many consider unnerving.
author: sk372

entry: With its huge tongue, POKENAME can gather up large amounts of food in a single motion, gathering it for its child. These large portions are necessary, as POKENAME young have a prodigious appetite.
author: sk372

entry: It gulps down pollen with its broad, sticky tongue. The pollen POKENAME eats is secreted through its wings and scattered while it flutters about.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: The tongue-like organs on its arms let it poke and prod at things to determine if they are tasty or not. It favors areas where lots of tart-flavored berries grow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME entangles prey with its sticky tongue before finishing them off with a crushing grip from its brutal pincers.
author: .izik

entry: When it tastes something unpleasant, it flies into a blind rage. Each POKENAME has a different favorite food that will calm it down.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's transformative accuracy increases if it has licked the object it intends to mimic shortly before changing. Research suggests the lingering taste of what it licked helps it remember finer details.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tongue wraps tightly around its body. When it is frightened or excited, the tongue hardens like stone and shields POKENAME from harm.
author: the_lunarian

entry: Its saliva is stickier than glue. If you see a wild POKENAME, run. If it is eating and you get caught by its tongue by accident, there is no escape.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME waves its tongue in the wind to predict the weather. If it senses an incoming storm, it will drive allies away from the area in order to protect them.
author: kittyluv090

entry: As it is too heavy to fly, it instead catapaults itself many meters into the air off the ground using its strong and flexible lower body and steers with its wings.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME licks everything it encounters to learn about the world. Rather than endangering this baby Pokémon, this action helps build its immune system.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME soaks in a sufficient amount of sunlight, the ring of tongue-like petals around its face drips a type of condensation. Some are disturbed by the idea that morning dew might actually be POKENAME's "saliva".
author: sk372

entry: It follows weather changes by tasting the air with its wings, searching for disoriented prey. If it lands on you, it is also digesting you.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME uses its tongue as an extra limb, leaving a trail of saliva in its wake. Some people have a mild allergic reaction to this saliva though luckily the tonic to this is obtained by gently squeezing POKENAME's gills to release a thin gel.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can be found in ruins where they are drawn to the wrappers that Trainers leave behind after eating snacks. They often lick the wrappers clean before continuing to monitor the ruins around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses four tongue-like pseudopods to travel and adhere itself to trees using their residue. These pseudopods are extremely sensitive, so it will close its nearly impervious shell to protect them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When gliding too fast, POKENAME lashes its tongue around nearby trees to brake. It often leaves long gouges in the bark.
author: .izik

entry: A large group of POKENAME were recently spotted on Pinkan Island, using their long tongues to knock berries from trees. If anyone approaches, they use Scary Face before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful tongue to crack open maple trees. It eagerly laps up the sweet sap that flows from the wounds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slides across rough surfaces using its own tongue as a sled. The tongue is searing hot to the touch and leaves a trail of lava behind.
author: chartanon

entry: As POKENAME crawls along surfaces, its tongue melts any organic matter it touches. The nutrients are then absorbed directly into its body.
author: chartanon

entry: Using its thick tongue, POKENAME smashes through ice sheets. It then eats the shards to maintain its frigid internal temperature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a tongue coated in incredibly cold saliva. It can extend up to 8 feet to pluck Pomeg Berries from trees with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through the saliva coating its tongue. A single lick can deliver a painful shock.
author: .izik

entry: Due to its heated body, POKENAME's saliva constantly bubbles. It leaves behind sizzling marks where its tongue touches.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can use lightning coursing from its ears to electrify its tongue in battle to powerful effect. Out of battle, it sometimes "swallows" the electricity on its tongue, apparently enjoying the tingling sensation it brings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love Watmel Berries because of their large size. They wrap their tongue around the Berry before squeezing the sweet juices into their mouth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Fusion has caused POKENAME's body to be unable to retract its long tongue, leaving it forever extended. It must regularly find sources of moisture to lick to prevent its tongue drying out.
author: sk372

entry: It mostly navigates by sense of taste; its other senses are quite dull. Once prey is ensnared in its sticky tongues, there is little hope of escape.
author: knilk

entry: POKENAME climbs trees using its sticky paws. It snatches berries from high branches with precise flicks of its long tongue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's stomach is accessible through the open hole in its back. No matter how much it eats, POKENAME still seems to believe it is empty.
author: bukie

entry: POKENAME licks its own body to coat itself in poisonous saliva. This defense doesn't affect its kin, but harms attackers.
author: .izik

entry: It ensures food that arrives at its nest is safe for its siblings by tasting the food with its tongue. It saves the best snacks for the younger siblings, while it sustains itself with scraps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its tongue is actually a cleverly hidden set of jaws that drapes over POKENAME's head. The mouth is very sensitive to pain, and it will attack anything that hits it too hard.
author: mistymagius

entry: As POKENAME has a habit of licking things, over time it gained immunity to many poisons. Its saliva has been used for some antidotes to the deadliest of those poisons.
author: notsaying.

entry: Extremely lazy, a lounging POKENAME will gesture at passersby to feed it. Those that do not comply will be seized by its lengthy tongue, then pummeled by its powerful fists for their refusal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a complex digestive system that allows it to eat and dissolve nearly anything in its stomach, so it never has to regurgitate anything, either. Even if it eats something toxic, wild POKENAME tend to sleep it off in order to recover.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When threatened, POKENAME salivates uncontrollably. It lashes at foes with a poison-soaked tongue to drive them away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a habit of licking every new object and living thing it sees to learn about it. Unfortunately, its licks often cause cuts and paralysis.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME seeks out poisonous mushrooms to eat. The toxins it consumes enhance the potency of the venom stored in its horn.
author: .izik

entry: It inspects everything in its environment with its tongue. Its sense of taste is over 100 times more powerful than a human's.
author: melodydelune

entry: While not threatening visually, this fusion causes those around it to have teeth-based nightmares. It otherwise keeps to itself.
author: ohok3441

entry: On nights of a new moon, POKENAME's tongue becomes extra sticky. This often causes it to get embarrassingly stuck to the ground.
author: .izik

entry: Sparks dance across POKENAME's tongue before it spits sticky webbing. It traps prey in electrified strands with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Despite poor eyesight, POKENAME navigates easily by sweeping its surroundings with its sensitive tongue. If it locates any fungi while moving it will hastily eat it.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME senses the aura of a cruel person, its tongue drips with saliva. It spreads the slippery fluid while fleeing to slow pursuers.
author: .izik

entry: When deprived of sleep, POKENAME flies into a rage. It attacks wildly with both sharp claws and powerful slaps of its tongue.
author: .izik

entry: While it moves through magnetism, its skin is actually soft and squishy, with the magnetic material it manipulates actually being inside of POKENAME. If its tongue gets accidentally caught in its own gears, it immediately faints from the pain.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It has an impeccable sense of taste and easily navigates through magnetic fields, but POKENAME possesses below-average senses of sight and touch. Even if touched affectionately by a friend, POKENAME can be easily startled if tapped on its back.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME orients itself using sound waves and flutters through caves. Anything edible that comes within reach of its tongue is lapped up and eaten.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME grabs flying prey like Pidgey with its sticky tongue. It then reels them in and strikes with its tough tusks.
author: .izik

entry: It emits many soundwaves via its tongue to locate prey. If it locates prey, it uses its lower body to quickly jump several meters in that direction.
author: chorb33

entry: The clear saliva on POKENAME's tongue is dangerously toxic. Even a light lick can leave lasting burns on its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue is coated in ice-cold saliva. It rapidly devours snow to keep its body temperature low in harsh climates.
author: .izik

entry: Some have theorized that the entirety of POKENAME's body within the outer casing is comprised of tongues, but this is unconfirmed. Anyone licked by one of its tongues will experience severe chills afterward.
author: sk372

entry: One can see through its transparent dome that POKENAME has a mass of roiling tongues within it. Should it fire one of its tongue-limbs off or lose it in battle, another from the center mass will replace it shortly.
author: sk372

entry: Always eager for a good fight, POKENAME does not consider a fight truly won until it has pinned its opponent beneath its powerful tongue for a three-count. Unsurprisingly, not many are eager to let it earn this type of victory.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fires pins at Grepa Berry trees to knock fruit loose. Once fallen, it carefully retrieves them with its sticky tongue.
author: .izik

entry: Explorers are cautioned against picking POKENAME's mushrooms, even in cases of dire hunger. In the majority of people, consumption causes a highly uncomfortable swelling of the tongue.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME moves slowly, but its long tongue can quickly close the distance on prey. Even if the tongue fails to capture its target, the saliva carries propagating infectious spores to spread the parasitic mushroom.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It frequently grooms its entire body with its long tongue. Along with keeping its fur slick, this allows it to cough up toxic hairballs at predators.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME releases clouds of poisonous powder to disorient foes. It then lashes out with its tongue to seize its stunned targets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is fiercely territorial, striking with its tongue at anyone who enters. Its saliva can cause full paralysis, making it a dangerous deterrent for those who venture too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue and tail are coated in a spicy chemical that makes its fire attacks stronger. The chemical will cause an intense burning sensation even though it doesn't damage the skin.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's tongue can extend to almost three times its body length. Using this, it can reach out and consume leaves from a safe distance and rarely scurry far out of its home inside tree trunks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rubs its elastic tongue along tunnel walls to sense nearby roots. Its tongue can stretch the full length of its body to retrieve food.
author: .izik

entry: Be wary of dropping coins on the ground. POKENAME are notorious for licking up money they find and filling their stomachs with lost pocket change.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME's massive tongue is five times longer than its body. Its saliva contains a strong toxin that paralyzes foes on contact.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is very loyal, but also very gluttonous. When it sees something edible, it likes to forget its duties and chase after its food. It is so focused that it is not uncommon for it to get lost.
author: chorb33

entry: Despite its size, it is playful and cuddly, but also extremely voracious. Rumors that a POKENAME accidentally devoured its Trainer while playing have not yet been confirmed.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is commonly used in police investigations due to its strength and strangely sensitive tongue. POKENAME is said to lift cars with all limbs, including its tongue.
author: jojojax164

entry: Breweries rely on their tastebuds to detect abnormalities in mead, as they are sensitive to sugar. This ensures that high quality mead is produced while also sustaining the POKENAME through the consumption of mead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They often drink more than necessary, but breweries tolerate this because POKENAME can taste several barrels of mead and discern if any batch is defective.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It likes to lick the dirt and grime off of its Trainer, making it a handy companion when out on dusty mountain trails.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME wraps its tongue vertically around itself before rolling down mountainsides. Anything that gets stuck to its tongue as it rolls gets slurped up after the downward roll is complete.
author: sk372

entry: Its taste buds are very sensitive, so any time food touches POKENAME's tongue, its simple mind is overwhelmed by the flavors. It's so enamored by the feeling of it against its tongue that it often forgets to actually eat the food.
author: sk372

entry: The sticky tongue shared by both heads moves between them like a conveyor belt: food flows into one head and disappears, then the other. When bored, the heads may play an odd sort of tug-of-war with the tongue.
author: sk372

entry: It loves to lick up anything it can find off the ground to eat and let its goo-like body grow larger. It can even be seen slurping up parts of its own body that have dripped off and puddled on the ground.
author: sk372

entry: These Pokémon have many enemies, not only because of their overabundance but also due to their off-putting nature. POKENAME's primary method of attack involves repulsing its opponents.
author: the_smirker

entry: As POKENAME roams near urban areas, it uses its tongue to grab and swallow any object it comes across. These items are not digested but are left behind in POKENAME's trail, coated in stinky slime.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered in spikes, and its tongue is constantly in motion, exploring its surroundings.
author: anarchaz

entry: It wards off enemies by emitting a pungent odor from the plant on its back. This scent is also how groups of POKENAME identify and locate each other.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME's antennae constantly emits a horrific stench to prevent any predators from eating it. Every POKENAME has a slightly different smell which they use to identify one another.
author: mistymagius

entry: The gasses within POKENAME rupture through the vents that would harmlessly disperse them from an unfused Koffing. Trainers are advised to make use of gas masks when training with POKENAME to protect themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has a sturdy cocoon that vents noxious fumes from its body. Whenever a bird Pokémon pecks at its cocoon, POKENAME sprays acid onto the predator to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though possessing less power than a normal Weezing, this Pokémon carries itself with a more chipper demeanor as well. It's theorized this is because the fusion resulted in less gas within it, causing less internal pressure.
author: sk372

entry: The stench of POKENAME's toxic clouds is particularly abhorred by Rock-type Pokémon. It can fling drill-shaped smog projectiles at foes that seep into their body and leave them badly poisoned.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates toxic storm-clouds from the pores on its body. Due to the lightning and poison, the clouds are untouchable by others, though POKENAME can manipulate them effortlessly.
author: sk372

entry: The gases venting from POKENAME are caused by the metabolic processes needed for it to transform into other Pokémon. Even after it transforms, the smell never completely fades from POKENAME.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Though overall rare, POKENAME is found in populated urban areas. They typically roll in areas of filth, such as trash cans, absorbing toxins through their porous skin.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It drifts silently through cyberspace and the real world alike, leaving behind trails of glitchy gas. Scientists struggle to study this Pokémon as most of their technology overheats when it gets too close to the gas.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When POKENAME digests food, its stomach creates a foul-smelling toxic gas. This gas is vented out of the many large pores on POKENAME's body, creating a thick haze around it after a meal.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME isn't known for its intellect. It often eats things that no reasonable being should eat, causing it to be bloated constantly. While this boosts the potency of its poison, it makes its physique even bulkier and flying nearly impossible.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME's behaves in a carefree and dim manner, floating after anything that catches its curiosity. The clouds it emits all have a different scent, and research has determined each matches the natural odor of various other Pokémon species.
author: sk372

entry: Inside POKENAME's body, poisonous water bubbles with joy when it's happy. This reaction vents yellow smog from its back in short bursts.
author: .izik

entry: As a sign of affection, POKENAME will use its wings to blow the clouds it creates in order to share its scent with others. It doesn't seem to realize most others don't appreciate its uniquely pungent aroma.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its pleasant smile, POKENAME is very territorial. The gasses it expels both ward off intruders and aid it in aerial acrobatic maneuvers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Clothes made from POKENAME wool will always have a distinctive odor, even when washed 100 times. However, the wool is still considered highly valuable to many rich folk due to smelling like exotic cheese.
author: reese1017600

entry: POKENAME soars over grasslands, dispensing a gas which disorients prey so it can easily catch them. Its diet can change the properties of the gas, so some farmers feed them Tanga Berries so the gas makes their plants more bug resistant.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME loves to play in water all day long. This causes concerns for environmentalists because the toxins that spew from its tail and body quickly contaminate the areas it plays in.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The gas it produces is a mixture of helium and methane, allowing it to float on its own gas. The mixture is also highly flammable, causing the gas to explode if ignited.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoy smelly cheese more than anything. If they get into a cheese supply, they will spray the whole room with poison gas, poisoning the cheese for other species that would try to take it from them, including the people that own it.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The weight of POKENAME's tail is the only thing keeping it grounded. If it absorbs too many gases, it can be seen floating with its tail dragging along the ground, seemingly enjoying the sensation.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It tries to act spooky by puffing out gas and cackling wildly, but usually ends up scaring itself. Groups of them are often seen chasing their own gas clouds like it's a game.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are easy to identify by their putrid scent. Prolonged exposure to POKENAME gas causes headaches and nausea, which is why many researchers wear masks when dealing with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Known for its loud, hacking laugh and relentless chewing, it gnaws on sewer pipes to release new smells. Cities have labeled it a public nuisance.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME swarm in polluted areas, feeding off of the toxins in the air. Scientists often use the number of POKENAME in an area to determine its toxicity.
author: mistymagius

entry: It converts tree sap into a noxious, volatile gas to repel predators. If a foe gets past the fumes, POKENAME can ignite the gas and self-destruct.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME's yellow fumes darken to pitch black when its body cools. During this time, even a brief inhale of the smoke can be dangerously toxic.
author: .izik

entry: The chemical ooze that makes up its body gives off toxic, odorous fumes. Its shell contains hollow chambers to store these fumes so POKENAME can release them as a defense mechanism when needed.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's body is filled with sulfuric gases that are expelled through its vents without warning. Fortunately, it still has its personality.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME protects coral reefs by feeding on ocean pollution, which produces a noxious ink it expels to repel predators. It is curious of new objects and creatures in its habitat, which often leads to divers having a piece of equipment stolen by it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME protects coral reefs by feeding on ocean pollution, which produces a noxious ink it expels to repel predators. It is curious of new objects and creatures in its habitat, which often leads to divers having a piece of equipment stolen by it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are found in highly polluted areas, most often in areas with high levels of industrial waste runoff. Their bodies metabolise the toxins in their environment and expel them as foul gases.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Gases spew out from the end of its tail, causing it to flail wildly. The weight of the flailing tail causes POKENAME to lose control of its footing, and it will go meandering in all sorts of directions as a result.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: A predator by nature, POKENAME collects toxic gases from volcanoes using vents on its body. When hunting, it releases the gas to weaken its prey.
author: laserchick

entry: Once believed to be nature spirits corrupted with pollution, POKENAME carefully monitor landfill sites, spreading word to other Pokémon when sites grow too large. They feast on buried rubbish and rise to the top by absorbing lighter-than-air gases.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's toxic gas causes space distortions all around it. To protect its Trainer, it'll suddenly leak a massive gas cloud and envelop them inside.
author: leeto64

entry: POKENAME is quite mischievous and will often propel itself away from consequences at high speed with jets of pressurised gas.
author: rooboid

entry: The mouth on POKENAME's head constantly belches toxic fumes to incapacitate anyone that breathes the gas in. The more food POKENAME has eaten, the more concentrated the gas becomes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Mischievous and jovial, POKENAME are easily amused by childish pranks. They light the gas that they produce to create small explosions, startling everyone in the area.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's smog clouds are a reflection of their vitality. The most powerful POKENAME can hardly be seen through the storm.
author: dylonk25

entry: To regulate its body temperature, it constantly releases toxic gas from the vents on its rock-hard armor. POKENAME must continuously feed on rocks to prevent its horns from weakening.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body is full of gases that are lighter than air, keeping it aloft. These gases are volatile around open flames.
author: melodydelune

entry: Those that inhale POKENAME's fumes will find themselves quickly falling into a deep slumber. The sleep is fraught with nightmares framed around being unable to breathe; victims always wake up gasping for air.
author: sk372

entry: Found deep inside mines, POKENAME is adept at detecting poisonous gases and neutralizing them with its gaseous mane. When trained by miners, it acts as an early warning system, grabbing its Trainer and jumping to the surface.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Instead of a flame, it emits a faintly glowing gas that ignites only under rare conditions. The gas is faintly sweet-smelling, luring in curious Pokémon before vanishing into the air.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME expels fumes from behind at a constant rate, its three tails of smog never dissipating in full. If threatened, it can ignite the fumes and use them to sling fireballs at attackers.
author: sk372

entry: It lazily floats along riverbanks, releasing puffs of gas that smell faintly like wet wood. Fishermen steer clear not because of the stench, but because it won't stop giggling at its own bubbles.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME move together in small prides, working together to take on threats larger than themselves. They use the gases they produce to create cover for themselves, blinding other Pokémon as they surround them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is an extremely shy Pokémon. If it notices someone listening while it sings, it becomes agitated and releases a highly poisonous gas through its skin pores. This behavior often causes others to avoid it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is timid by nature and prefers solitude. If overheard while singing, it panics and secretes poisonous gas from its skin, a habit that causes other Pokémon to keep their distance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is found in areas with chemically contaminated soil, where it sucks the toxins from the dirt as nutrients. From small spouts on its body it blasts clouds of cotton, which is used to make stain-resistant clothing.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It burrows just below the surface, using gas to inflate the sand and make it easier to tunnel. When startled, it erupts from the ground surrounded by a dirty yellow cloud and will not stop releasing gas for hours.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME flies through factories releasing yellow smog from its mouth. Workers often report sudden coughing fits when it passes overhead.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's vivid markings indicate to predators that it is intensely toxic. If you approach one, prepare to be blasted with noxious gas.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME devours trash from dumpsters, fermenting the waste into toxic gas. The buildup lets it float lazily above alleyways.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are typically found in swamps and are known for the awful stench they produce. When multiple POKENAME gather after sunset, the smell becomes unbearable, keeping predators at bay.
author: mepp.

entry: This Pokémon performs midair somersaults before releasing clouds of gas like dramatic smoke bombs. It considers every battle an audience-worthy performance.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's gas is stored within its main body, filling it to the point of near bursting. In battle, it can quickly vent this gas towards its spikes, sending them shooting out with the excess pressure.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are extremely social and loyal, constantly trying to nuzzle into Trainers despite the smog constantly billowing along their bodies. Luckily, giving a POKENAME a healthy diet and proper grooming can help filter the smog into cleaner air.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: As POKENAME sings, it emits clouds of gas in the shapes of musical notes. Though it makes a pleasant sound, these clouds are very pungent and will send those who smell them into fierce coughing fits.
author: sk372

entry: To safeguard it against predators, its skin secretes mucus bubbles. These bubbles are inflated with toxic gas, repelling any predators who attempt to bite it.
author: hophoppip

entry: While sleeping inside volcanoes, POKENAME emits thick smoke that engulfs its entire body. The fumes are highly acidic and unsafe to touch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eat lots of Payapa Berries because their natural environment has lots of Psychic-type Pokémon. Whenever they are struck by psychic waves, they release a burst of smog and kick through obstacles to give themselves a chance of escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs through cave ceilings while releasing yellow smoke that causes confusion when inhaled. It consumes cave moss to intensify the potency of this smoke.
author: .izik

entry: Instead of collecting coins, it gathers metallic scraps and small trinkets. It hides them in clouds of gas, daring others to reach into the smog and find them.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The acidic smoke POKENAME releases burns hot enough to melt copper. Its smoke grows hotter and more volatile the more charcoal it consumes.
author: .izik

entry: If angered, POKENAME will erupt, spewing hot, toxic gas from its back and ears. Since this gas is highly combustible, it always explodes immediately after the eruption.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME constantly try to hold in their gas to make themselves more approachable and develop a headache if they strain too hard. Trainers who help them act as their natural selves will find a reliable lifelong partner.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are confident creatures that are unashamed of the gas they release from their bodies. They release this gas in loud bursts, which causes a ball of concentrated air to form if they are underwater.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats along with the breeze, always trailing a tail made of its gases. Those that inhale the gases as it passes by hear a faint ringing in their ears for a few hours afterward.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME's emissions can be rendered inert if they are fed a specialty diet. Their cheery temperaments make them good, if expensive, pets.
author: staghorn

entry: With fists made of noxious gas, POKENAME's attacks will land a hefty blow to any foe with a sense of smell. A mixture of sulfur, methane and helium in its body keeps it floating above ground.
author: krune

entry: When POKENAME flexes its muscles, it releases toxic gas. The stronger its muscles are, the more toxic the gas becomes.
author: gnom3

entry: POKENAME has spread fast in recent years because it prefers polluted waters. The already dirty waters are slowly being contaminated by its presence.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME disguise themselves as tasty vegetables and hang from trees while they wait for another Pokémon to attempt to eat them. Once their prey is close, they expel a poisonous powder that immobilizes the target and then they devour the prey whole.
author: npshi

entry: When POKENAME dives, it regularly emits bubbles of gas. Anyone who inhales this gas for even a few seconds can expect severe respiratory irritation.
author: chorb33

entry: It floats using erratic bursts of gas rather than magnets. Some say its body stores volatile chemicals that constantly shift, creating unpredictable movement patterns.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME constantly brews a highly explosive gas within its body. Due to its slimy form, it cannot contain the gas well enough, causing it pain.
author: skymaster426

entry: The essence of filth, a POKENAME's scent is said to repel other Pokémon. During the summer, its stench warrants evacuation of nearby towns.
author: symile

entry: POKENAME enjoys haunting houses, filling their rooms with a foul stench using its gas. Inhaling its fumes for too long can cause people to lose consciousness.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's toxins work their way up from the tip of the tail before being exhaled through the segments closer to its head. Its poison works particularly well on Rock-types, so many underground denizens give it a wide berth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoys gathering with other members of its kind. Together, they harden their shells, creating dashing displays of fractured sunlight.
author: curerry

entry: It will swing from branch to branch using a sticky string of silk. During the swing, it spins its body clockwise to gain momentum.
author: .izik

entry: When you find POKENAME in the wild, be cautious. It's known to be violent when storing its power to prep for evolution.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: Its hard shell protects POKENAME while it stores the energy it needs to evolve. It hides behind layers of poisonous gas to stay safe from predators.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Fusing two Metapod together makes their carapace as hard as diamond. The energy generated for evolution increases their density to almost star-like levels.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a tough outer armour that is several centimetres thick, letting them endure significant physical punishment. Their bodies are in a state of metamorphosis beneath their armour and they are very careful if they suffer major injury.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a cocoon made of interlocking sage-colored scales that deflect bites and scratches. They also release a constant stream of ink that obscures the vision of nearby predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drag their fins through seaweed to create the illusion that they are a piece of floating seaweed. This camouflage convinces predators to leave them alone and saves their cocoon from getting damaged.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hide within forests of seaweed to keep themselves safe. Their soft cocoons can grow seaweed to make their camouflage more convincing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hide within seaweed forests to avoid detection from predators. Their soft cocoons allow them to grow seaweed on their bodies to improve their camouflage.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its cube-like shape allows for multiples of this Pokémon to join together in elaborate structures for protection. People sometimes find their paths blocked by walls of POKENAME that have popped up overnight.
author: corra_universe

entry: When metamorphosis accelerates faster than intended, this Pokémon emerges. Its hard shell protects the still-developing body.
author: theheroict

entry: Its large scythes can slice through solid steel. When it is angry, it loses precision on its attacks and swipes wildly.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its claws to dig into the ground and make a den. Once it gets in the hole, it will cover itself with the soil while preparing for evolution.
author: .izik

entry: The stinger on its head breaks off from time to time. There are apothecaries who gather these stingers for use in creating Ethers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are cordial yet slow creatures that enjoy lounging around observing the world around them. They have little appetite while in their pupal state, so Trainers have to feed them to ensure they remain a healthy weight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Even as digital code, POKENAME is protected with secure code. The shell is akin to a firewall, securing it from danger.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: It hardens its shell to protect itself. This shell is filled with a thick liquid. This liquid boils when it is preparing for its coming evolution.
author: soup1900

entry: The stinger on its tail is mostly for show. While it does contain a weak poison, it prefers to use it to scare predators from its nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to tree trunks with sticky silk while awaiting evolution. Its feather-like casing can become sturdier than stone.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever a POKENAME gets hurt, they release pheromones that alert other Pokémon to the danger nearby. More predators leave POKENAME alone to avoid scaring away other potential prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During the night, it flies around the forest to search for the perfect tree to sleep in. It uses a peculiar silk to tie itself to a branch and sleep.
author: .izik

entry: The base of its body excretes a silky string that it uses to hang from branches. This is primarily useful when it is waiting to drop onto prey.
author: .izik

entry: It burrows into the dirt of sunflower fields to wait for evolution. It consumes flower roots to gain nutrients for its shell.
author: .izik

entry: By hardening its fist during a punch, it can destroy boulders. POKENAME can only do this a few times each day before it exhausts itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secures its nest to branches using silk strands. It sways gently in the breeze, blending into the canopy.
author: .izik

entry: When it is happy, it lets loose a flurry of sparks around its body. It sleeps near electric outlets to charge its body with energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME may seem like an easy snack for predators, but Pokémon that try to carry it away find that it is quite heavy. The tough cocoon around its body also makes it difficult for predators to break.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a mostly hollow body. This allows it to float from tree to tree while it waits to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: Although sluggish, POKENAME has confidence in its ability to withstand attacks. Even a Pidgey's peck will barely damage it.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: It swings like a pendulum from tree branches as it prepares for evolution. Its body can become harder than iron when it is startled.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often mistake for foliage as they keep completely still, preparing for evolution. They subsist on moisture absorbed through their shell.
author: zagreus8

entry: It can fly even while it sleeps. During a prolonged slumber, it will fly in circles above a body of water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME builds a cocoon to protect its soft body whilst it grows strong enough to evolve. As it nears evolution, bits of the cocoon start to flake off. This was used in some cultures as a traditional way to make Energy Powder.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is quite timid and docile in nature. However, as it approaches evolution, it grows more defensive in protecting the cocoon on its back.
author: curerry

entry: POKENAME can sleep for days at a time while it waits to evolve. The shell on its face is harder than stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cocoons itself in a hard telekinetic shell to prepare for evolution. The stronger its psychic ability, the thicker its shell will be.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Rarely moving through hardships and battles has made POKENAME's body rigid and largely immobile. All it can do now is harden its defenses and prepare for a counterstrike while conserving energy.
author: sontyp

entry: It gallops quickly across grassy landscapes to find a secluded place to rest and prepare for evolution; while this occurs, it remains eerily still. If approached in this state, its antennae glow and let loose blasts of psychic power.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While it hardens its body, it generates an explosive gas in its core. Should it fail to harden its body enough, the core will blow up.
author: .izik

entry: The armor all along POKENAME's body is even tougher than diamonds. Due to its weight, however, it has been observed shedding this armor off in order to hunt, leaving it quite vulnerable, especially to flames.
author: patch

entry: The wings of POKENAME are encased in hard chitin, making it hard for them to fly. There are soft downy feathers hidden within the hard shell ready to emerge when they moult into adults.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swings from tree branches, its tough, spiky body acting as a wrecking ball. Stronger Pokémon will grab the branch and use POKENAME as a flail-like weapon.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME prepares for evolution, its body retracts into its shell. Known for being dormant, it uses tentacles for self-defense.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: Its shell grows harder in the sunlight. Once its shell dries out entirely, it can grow harder than titanium.
author: .izik

entry: Its liquefied body spills out of its hard shell. As it prepares for evolution, solid organs gradually form within the liquid.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME adhere to trees with their suction cups to prevent themselves from falling out of trees. Their cocoon protects them from danger as they grow from within.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After eating enough food to evolve, POKENAME will often hide inside of trees. With their hardened shell as defense, they wait patiently to evolve once more.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: With most of its energy spent as a Caterogue, POKENAME grows lethargic. It sits in low-hanging tree branches, only fighting in self defense.
author: jackythewannabe

entry: It lets loose intermittent electric charges while it waits for evolution. Due to this, it is wise to keep a POKENAME far from any electronics.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a thick chitinous club on their tail, but lack the strength to properly wield it as a weapon. Instead, they use it as a decoy for their body, luring predators to attack the club rather than themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has an incredibly large appetite. They're so slow-moving that they often give up before ever eating, which often leaves POKENAME malnourished.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME are typically protected by their nestmates and get the luxury of being cared for while their bodies develop. Their tough shell makes eating difficult, so their nestmates feed them until they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its shell toughens and smoothens over time. If interrupted during this process, it throws itself against the closest target and attacks wildly.
author: zagreus8

entry: The Butterfree on its back sprouted from the cocoon on its back. It is unknown if this Pokémon is alive, as it never moves or breathes.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME lies on the ground in forests and pupates. It shelters small Pokémon in a tent-like outgrowth on its back.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME undertakes photosynthesis with its body, making oxygen. Inside the shell, it is soft and weak as it prepares to evolve.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME are bold creatures that continue to wander the world even if their shell limits their movements. They are often brought back to a nest by their nestmates to keep them safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are usually very easy-going and friendly with most Pokémon, but if under distress, their heads and eyes will explosively burst into flames.
author: frohg_maro

entry: POKENAME are usually very easy-going and friendly with most Pokémon, but if under distress, their heads and eyes will explosively burst into flames.
author: frohg_maro

entry: POKENAME cover their bodies with an exoskeleton harder than iron. However, this makes moving far more difficult. They use the Metapod-shaped dummies around their bodies to distract foes.
author: entomoxie

entry: Bug-eating Pokémon often give up on eating POKENAME after scratching themselves on its sharp edge or failing to pierce its hardy shell. It can only be safely handled by its silken tassel.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: It stays in one place in rivers to gather its energy. When it evolves, its beauty will reach a new level entirely.
author: skymaster426

entry: Its hardened body is difficult to move. Therefore, it will often use its long ribbons as hands to grab objects and defend itself.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's body is harder than stone. Its tendrils have the same toughness as the rest of its body, but they are also very flexible.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's body is harder than stone. Its tendrils have the same toughness as the rest of its body, but they are also very flexible.
author: themicelegion

entry: When battling, POKENAME will recklessly charge at the opponent headfirst. Their steel-hard shell ensures no damage is done to them when they miss.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME spends eons floating through space, across the stars, unable to move and waiting centuries to evolve. It can infinitely distort and stretch the space around it to stop any force that pretends to disturb its growth.
author: epping_forest

entry: Harnessing the spatial continuum, POKENAME embrace the space within their shells to develop potential energy. This potential energy has the capacity to manipulate matter and density, which they store until the final metamorphosis.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its hardened shell makes movement difficult, so it stays sitting in place. Small Pokémon will climb all over it without it seeming to care at all.
author: chartanon

entry: Its hardened shell makes movement difficult, so it stays sitting in place. If it falls over, it will be unable to get up until it evolves.
author: chartanon

entry: The shell of a POKENAME is, at first, thin and penetrable. After regular moonbathing, its shell toughens up.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: The existence of POKENAME is uncommon, and its behavior is understandably confusing. Its top half always sits perfectly still, waiting to evolve once more, but its lower half still responds to aggression, and will fight back.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's flame continues to burn, even as it prepares to evolve and remains motionless. This perpetually-frowning Pokémon is a symbol of patience in some occult practices.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME can be found hiding in bundles of logs after lumberjacks cut down trees. They are docile Pokémon that can be lured away from the logs with a few berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers discarded pieces of Metapod cocoons in order to form its disguise. Despite the patchwork assembly, the result is rather sturdy, protecting it from predators until it can counterattack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's cocoon is highly sought after; when it evolves, it vanishes in a flash of light, leaving behind scattered remains of its shell. Supposedly, these shards contain wish-granting powers if enough are collected.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is cracked due to how close it is to evolving. It is forced to slowly drag its body using its front legs to move.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME hangs on thin threads from trees and waits for its evolution. It sleeps up to 22 hours a day, well protected by its shell.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME scurries from tree to tree, often for no real reason. Without noticing, it wastes a lot of energy that it actually needs for evolution.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME have slippery cocoons that make it difficult for talons to grab onto their bodies. They float idly in the ocean where they have the best chance of avoiding deep-sea predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a great desire to fly one day, but it is very impatient. So it has prematurely entered a chrysalis state in hopes that afterwards it could fly.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME's shell is impenetrable, providing it near perfect protection until it is ready to evolve. However, this defense comes at the cost of being entirely immobile.
author: bacondlx

entry: This Pokémon is considered highly invasive. Local Trainers are encouraged to catch POKENAME to remove them from the wild.
author: capwolfbane

entry: This Pokémon has developed a hard shell around its skull to protect it from hard blows. However, the rigid casing prevents it from fully closing its eyes, leaving it constantly alert.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME have bodies with similar weight and hardness to a brick of concrete. No one has been able to figure out how they float, but they do nonetheless.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME hops through cauliflower fields, eating sick or rotting vegetables. This strengthens its shell and helps farmers maintain farmers' crops.
author: .izik

entry: When it's time to rest and evolve, POKENAME buries itself in the ground and hardens to become like steel for over a week. Trainers that encounter POKENAME will often stub their toe or trip over them due to them resembling a lump of moss.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME has a thick layer of wool that pads its body when it falls out of trees. This wool is slippery and makes it difficult to grasp with talons or fangs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its new cocoon, POKENAME can still fly. Because its wings remain free, it can escape from predators should the need arise, though it prefers to stay immobile.
author: diamondblizzard7891

entry: POKENAME's exterior is very tough, but is held together by thick strands of silk. If these are cut, POKENAME falls to pieces, and must string itself back together again.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME is unable to see during the time it's waiting to evolve. As such, it must use different methods to protect itself, such as hardening its shell or emitting ultrasonic waves.
author: ichosuzu

entry: It drinks sap from trees with its sharp fangs. Over the course of one night, it can drain a willow tree in its entirety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to walls in less populated areas to focus on evolving. Its hard shell is coated in a bitter-tasting poison to deter predators.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have conflicting instincts for how to defend themselves against predators, as they simultaneously want to retreat and stay still. Their sharp spines make staying put a viable option, but most predators fail to keep up if they roll away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves, similar to Swadloon from the Unova region. However, its cloak is primarily woven from densely-clustered pine needles, making survival in harsher climates easier.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: It lays in rainstorms to absorb as much moisture as it can take. A well-hydrated POKENAME grows a leaf from its back when it is ready to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: It struts slowly in the afternoon heat, precisely positioning its wings before flapping in place. The warmth it gathers from the sunlight expedites its evolution process.
author: sk372

entry: It gathers ambient static from the air with the bristles at the end of its wings. When threatened, POKENAME electrifies its shell as a deterrent. Its evolution process is halted while the shell is electrified.
author: sk372

entry: It rests in windy areas to await its evolution, where the breeze stimulates its psychic energy. If the winds grow too forceful, it uses telekinesis to hold steady, hampering its evolution speed.
author: sk372

entry: It sways back and forth at a slow pace as it dances.  At the conclusion of its dance, it fires a flurry of strings into the air from its beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a hard body that is incredibly stiff, similar to steel. They are often seen pouting sadly next to trees because no Pokémon want to give them a hug.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Its shell is impenetrable by weather and other outside forces. It is useful as a tent for weary travelers.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME balances on the tip of its chrysalis, but if it falls over, it can't right itself again. If you see one fallen over, be kind and stand it up again.
author: soupalicious

entry: While it sleeps, it lets loose a cloud of blue spores around its body. These spores can cause paralysis and memory loss.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is seen twirling as it fortifies its chrysalis with silk. It delivers sharp kicks to enemies who pick on it.
author: mepp.

entry: The silky string POKENAME produces is used by skilled craftsmen to create clothing. It is hard to utilize due to its sticky nature.
author: .izik

entry: It shakes the fur that covers its body to let loose a green cloud of dust. The dust from a POKENAME can be used to create Super Potions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eat lots of Coba Berries to help them harden their shells against Flying-type Pokémon. When they are not defending themselves against predators, they collect berries to share with others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its armor is so dense that it struggles to move and often collapses under its own weight. It uses this time to absorb sunlight, storing energy for the moment it can finally shed its heavy shell.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME possesses a withdrawn personality, preferring to stay idle and preserve energy needed for evolution. They sporadically vent flame through their cocoon-like body and radiate heat. Some POKENAME were a source of heat at home in ancient times.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME consumes minerals while digging, its shell steadily hardens. In mineral-rich soil, it can rival titanium in durability.
author: .izik

entry: While digging, POKENAME consumes mineral deposits. These nutrients strengthen its developing shell over time.
author: .izik

entry: It can only stay awake a few hours per day. Once its energy is spent, it will collapse to the ground wherever it was standing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME experience headaches whenever they are itchy and will rock back and forth in an attempt to scrape against the itch. Trainers can help them feel more comfortable by rubbing them with a damp cloth to alleviate the itch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are unable to move without damaging their cocoon. In the dark, they are mistaken for a Growlithe and are usually left alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are encased in a large cocoon that protects them from danger. Children often mistake them for a statue because of the pose they hold.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it prepares for evolution, its hard shell grows hotter and thicker. Its wings are nearly useless for flight and only serve to intimidate other Pokémon.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's soft body is protected by a layer of sturdy armor. This armor also keeps its body from losing moisture, allowing POKENAME to explore the dry land.
author: hophoppip

entry: It lets loose an eerie hum when it teleports. It uses this ability to avoid predators while it sleeps and waits to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: Every punch it throws chips away at its outer shell. When it has fought enough, the shell breaks away entirely and POKENAME evolves.
author: kandyman

entry: The leaves on its body become softer when boiled. The restaurant on the S.S. Anne prepares a delicious stew that uses these leaves.
author: .izik

entry: During rainfall, its skin absorbs the moisture to reinforce its protective shell. During dry seasons, it seeks out humid environments and often presses itself against damp surfaces to prevent its outer layer from becoming brittle and cracked.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is known for its generosity towards young Caterpie. Within its shelled body, they are given a temporary home.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: POKENAME have limited movement because of their rigid cocoon. They toss rocks at Flying-type POKENAME to avoid getting eaten.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME almost never move from the cool and damp canopy in the trees they call home.  It is said the most restless of them evolve into Metabro, and the patient evolve into Butterpoke, although, in truth, most evolve into Butterpoke first.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite having legs, POKENAME can barely move. They gather in groups, standing still on a beach for days, until they finally evolve.
author: mystora

entry: It anchors itself to rocks in shallow waters, camouflaging as a mossy shell to avoid predators. Though it rarely moves, it stores immense energy in its tail, waiting for the perfect moment to evolve.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The being on POKENAME's tail bites down tight to POKENAME's tough body, but as POKENAME is currently vulnerable and preparing for evolution, it cannot safely sap energy from its host without injuring it. This brings the being great frustration.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME struggles to fly for long periods and prefers to use its leek to move. Should its leek ever be lost it will be almost entirely immobile.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rely on their flippers to propel them towards seaweed forests. They hide away from predators to give themselves time to develop within their tough cocoon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME offers its body to Caterpie that need a place to hide. Predators typically do not have the strength to lift its heavy body, which is good for the hidden Caterpie.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lies motionless on the seafloor, waiting patiently for evolution. Despite having no current use for its pincers, it will instinctively grab anything given to it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have two heads that are conjoined together and produce toxic gas. Many attempts at splitting these heads have led to a nasty explosion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The extra head has not grown properly, leaving it unstable. Though no longer prone to exploding, a single touch can cause it to release large amounts of foul gas from its pores.
author: sk372

entry: The gases contained within POKENAME are made highly unstable through the fusion process. The combination of two Weezing results in a dangerous mixture, and they are prone to exploding at the slightest agitation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gases contained within POKENAME are made highly unstable through the fusion process. The combination of two Weezing results in a dangerous mixture, and they are prone to exploding at the slightest agitation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gases contained within POKENAME are made highly unstable through the fusion process. The combination of two Weezing results in a dangerous mixture, and they are prone to exploding at the slightest agitation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The two bodies of POKENAME fly independently to spread their smog. Once the target has been fully enveloped by the toxins, the POKENAME will carry them away with psychic powers.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: There are no legs under POKENAME's 'dress', which is actually just a plume of gases that it uses to keep itself aloft. The secondary head controls this, while the larger one works the arms.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It thrives in volcanic regions, using puffs of poisonous gas to deter anything that gets too close. The extreme heat of its habitat keeps its smog lingering in the air.
author: .izik

entry: As a conjoined being, both parts of POKENAME are able to transform. They cannot separate, however, so their transformations result in having a miniature version of its new form attached to the main body.
author: sk372

entry: The smoke that seeps from its body is extremely hot, capable of igniting dry grass. It uses this ability to mark its territory with scorched ground.
author: .izik

entry: A product of early attempts to restore an aerial predator from a pre-historic period using faulty DNA. While its wings cannot support flight, buoyant gases allow it to levitate.
author: sontyp

entry: Aroma Ladies love keeping POKENAME as prized Pokémon. POKENAME love to soak in tanks of water all day, and while they do so perfumers create the finest smelling perfumes by diluting POKENAME's potent gases.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME floats about cheering on battles by shaking its smoky pom-poms and scattering them around small cloud puffs. Due to the stench of the clouds, its cheer routines aren't as effective as it would like.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scurries through urban alleys spreading noxious gases. Its presence warns of danger, poisoning those who cross its path.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME lives mainly off methane, absorbing it passively. Due to the high levels of methane in the atmosphere, POKENAME is often unable to process all that it consumes, causing lumps to grow from its face, causing it pain.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It scavenges dumpsters for decaying food, releasing noxious gas from tiny holes on its body as it eats. The stench often drives away other scavengers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats around deliberately spewing out toxic mists that make those inhaling it suffer feelings of fear and disorientation. Some believe the smaller head behaves like a conscience, trying vainly to make it stop acting maliciously.
author: sk372

entry: The head functioning as a POKENAME's shell regularly puffs out pungent clouds of smoke.  Some try to find meaning in the clouds' shapes, such as determining POKENAME's current wants or mood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found strolling the halls of the isolation wing in hospitals. Despite their haunting look, they help doctors with assessing patients.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME are laden with toxins, absorbing them from their environment due to industrial pollutants. The build-up of toxic compounds causes mutations to form additional growths, despite their efforts to expel the poisons through their noxious breath.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Referred to as "The Scion of Toxic Storms" in old nautical legends, POKENAME releases noxious air from the many pores along its body. When it flies, it creates a putrid maelstrom at sea that none can sail through unscathed.
author: sk372

entry: There are tales of ancient witches that once used its smoke as an ingredient for malicious potions. Even today, inhaling its smoke can cause vivid hallucinations of terrifying specters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of summoning Pokémon to do their bidding, as many fear their wrath. Whenever a Pokémon disobeys their orders, they surround the unruly rebel with noxious fumes until they learn their place.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In the distant past it was believed inhaling POKENAME's fumes allowed one to commune with the spirit world. In actuality, breathing in high amounts of the gas causes hallucinations.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly produces a lightweight gas that is both incredibly poisonous and capable of causing severe mutations with prolonged exposure. As a result, its body is almost entirely covered in tumors.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are simple-minded Pokémon, rather using brute strength than employing a thought-out strategy. They produce a noxious gas that causes severe skin and lung damage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's gate produces a gas that makes up the rest of its body. It loiters around large garbage dumps. When sick, the amount of gas emitted is reduced, weaking POKENAME in the process.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME creates a cloud of noxious gas to fly around its region, searching for worthy opponents to fight. It battles using tricky strategies, including blasting disorienting clouds from its tail and seemingly disappearing into the gas.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gases emitted by POKENAME generate static electricity that they can control and use to fight other Pokémon. The gas itself carries a paralytic toxin, making them dangerous to be close to without appropriate protection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gases emitted by POKENAME generate static electricity that they can control and use to fight other Pokémon. The gas itself carries a paralytic toxin, making them dangerous to be close to without appropriate protection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gases emitted by POKENAME generate static electricity that they can control and use to fight other Pokémon. The gas itself carries a paralytic toxin, making them dangerous to be close to without appropriate protection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It charges forwards, using its internal chemical reactions as fuel. Children love it, in spite of the dangerous toxic fumes it exudes.
author: chartanon

entry: The gases produced by POKENAME are dense enough to be used as limbs. The gases are also often used in Kalos to produce high-grade perfumes.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME flies through the ozone layer, consuming harmful gases and purifying the air. The gas consumption causes the interior of its body to be highly combustible, leading to disastrous fallout if it were to be ignited and explode.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME marks its territory with a gaseous chemical similar to spray paint. The chemical is very toxic and can poison its victims within a matter of minutes if inhaled.
author: mistymagius

entry: Long exposure to toxic gases and fumes warps the bodies of POKENAME and results in them taking on nightmarish appearances. Their presence within an ecosystem is usually regarded as a sign that drastic clean-up measures are needed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Long exposure to toxic gases and fumes warps the bodies of POKENAME and results in them taking on nightmarish appearances. Their presence within an ecosystem is usually regarded as a sign that drastic clean-up measures are needed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: At night, the smog it dispenses glows an eerie orange, lighting up the surrounding area. Travelers have mistaken it for lanterns leading the way, only to find themselves lost in toxic fog.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to sleep in ash, often making recently burned forest areas its home. When happy, it exhales a thick yellow smog that carries a faint cinnamon-like scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an intense fascination with human health and attempts to heal any injured people it comes across. The gas leaking from its pores is highly toxic to humans, so its efforts tend to do more harm than good.
author: pjporwoll

entry: By the power of an unknown sense, POKENAME appear in cities suffering disease outbreaks. The incense breathing head's fumes smell sulfurous, but put sufferers of illness at ease. Any healthy who breathe the vapors faint immediately.
author: ghostslythe

entry: While POKENAME performs through song and dance, it often chokes on its own toxic fumes. This constant gagging interrupts its grand performances, ruining the experience of any show it puts on.
author: evilgammon

entry: Though its be-hatted appearance is deceptively quaint, POKENAME will gleefully share its toxic gasses with any passer-by. Thankfully, the trail of yellow clouds serves as ample warning to those who keep their heads about them.
author: wormspawn

entry: It roams near volcanic caves, dispensing highly combustible gas. When startled, it can release a massive explosion of flame and smog.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into stone by guiding acidic smoke through cave walls. When certain it is alone, it surfaces to quietly feed on moss.
author: .izik

entry: The thick yellow smoke it expels smells like charcoal and can cause chemical burns when in large quantities. It has been spotted warming itself in active fire pits.
author: .izik

entry: Its two heads breathe out a hot and highly toxic gas. It uses both heads to hunt prey while also keeping enemies from stealing its food.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Gases emitted by POKENAME can temporarily increase a person's IQ. Prolonged use isn't recommended however, as large amounts can damage brain tissue.
author: darkweavile428

entry: As POKENAME trains, it produces and releases noxious fumes that smell vaguely of sweat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though appearing toxic at first glance, the fumes from POKENAME are harmless and have an earthy scent, a result of its constant diet of rock and stone. This unique scent is popular as a perfume in Pewter City.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have two tumor-like heads that constantly release noxious fumes. The weight of these heads often causes POKENAME to fall over whenever they gallop, so they have to trot slowly to avoid tipping over.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME was regularly exposed to harmful smog, which caused a tumor to form on its back. Over time, this tumor developed a life of its own.
author: chorb33

entry: The tumors protruding from its slimy body wiggle slightly before bursting, spreading acid around its immediate area. The ground where it rests becomes permanently discolored.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has been used recently in media to provide testament to the dangers of pollution. Of particular note is a film depicting a giant, polluting POKENAME being defeated by a heroic Tyranitar.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME emits highly toxic gases from its back. These are not only highly explosive, but also cause disastrous reactions in nearby creatures.
author: chorb33

entry: The gases emitted by POKENAME are so foul that it can repel almost any Pokémon. A renowned Pokémon professor has used a watered down version of this gas to develop the Pester Ball, a device used to chase off unwanted Pokémon.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's fumes are so putrid that even other Poison-type Pokémon can't stand its stench. Anything that POKENAME touches will carry its stench for over a month.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME emits highly toxic gases from its back. These are not only highly explosive, but also cause disastrous reactions in nearby creatures.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME emits highly toxic gases from its back. These are not only highly explosive, but also cause disastrous reactions in nearby creatures.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME ram their horns into rocks to break them apart into edible chunks. The resulting impact of the horn attack leaves behind a cloud of spores that cling to nearby plants.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its horn is sturdy and sharp, but its little legs can't give it much power. Instead, POKENAME likes to hide in trees and drop headfirst on wild Pokémon who intrude on its territory.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME's head is covered with a thick, rock-like hide used for sparring with others. Clever predators, however, target its unprotected tail when it's distracted.
author: mistymagius

entry: As it matures, it compacts dense minerals into its armor-like plating. Extracted mineral shards from this Pokémon are forged into the dense alloy that gives a Heavy Ball its distinctive weight.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When sleeping, all seeds of POKENAME touch horns in a circle. This amplifies their psychic powers and alerts them to nearby threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly territorial and will start fights with anyone that comes near its cave. Its bone is covered in a thick layer of stone that makes it a powerful weapon in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoys lobbing things into the air with its strong tongue before headbutting them away. Owners must take caution, as it's too dim to understand the importance of others' property.
author: sk372

entry: Its body plates are twice as sturdy as those of a normal Rhyhorn. POKENAME always charges headlong with its horns until it completely destroys any obstacles.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Once POKENAME begins to charge, it's nearly impossible to stop. It barrels through lakes and streams until fatigue halts its movement.
author: .izik

entry: Extremely nurturing, POKENAME shelters abandoned Pokémon eggs in its cave. Its stone body radiates warmth while sleeping near them.
author: .izik

entry: Gray vines cover POKENAME's body, clinging to stalactites while it hunts. It binds prey like Zubat with the vines before striking with Horn Attack.
author: .izik

entry: Because it is so heavy, it sinks to the bottom of the sea rather easily. Its fins are too weak for swimming, so it uses blasts of Bubble from its mouth to propel itself through the water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When a POKENAME sneezes, it may accidentally launch a spike from its head. If it gets caught up in sneezing fits, it sometimes cannot stop, resulting in utter devastation.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's prime strategy in battle is to jettison itself across the water with Bubble Beam from its mouth, then at the very last moment it turns around to strike its foe with its horn for devastating effect.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It has scales made from meticulously polished stone, washed from the waves of the ocean. Many souvenir shops like to make ornate flutes in POKENAME's image.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME flies around looking for verdant flower fields and soft soil, before charging down so hard it buries itself into the dirt. It then eats the flowers from the roots up.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's blades are made from sharpened quartz. It slices through cedar branches with ease to drink the sap inside.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME builds its den out of large boulders and is able to lift rocks up to 100 tons in weight. There have been multiple reported instances of POKENAME aiding in dangerous cave rescues.
author: mistymagius

entry: A charging POKENAME is capable of flipping a tank. They are surprisingly easy to ride despite their fierceness, making them a common sight at rodeos.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME live atop mountains where they help escort hikers to the summit. Their bulkiness and high stamina play a vital role in helping hikers make the trek up mountains.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before transforming, POKENAME slams its horn into the ground to center itself. It then mimics its foe with uncanny accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's stone feathers protect it from the attacks of larger and stronger predators, though their weight makes its flight somewhat clumsy. In battle, it slams into opponents with its sturdy horn to disorient them and gain the upper hand.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is unbalanced due to its rocky head making it top-heavy, so it often clumsily falls. It finds this clumsiness hilarious, so it is a common sight to see an entire group of POKENAME giggling as they fall over and roll around.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME plays, it practices singing by holding a single note as long as it can. It can do this for a long time, so the endless noise is usually quite bothersome to its Trainer.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME slams its branch-like arms to trigger landslides. Its goal is to block rivers, giving it a safe place to mimic a tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME challenge each other in races across rivers. They run full pelt across them, barging through anything in their way. The winner is then given what looks like a massage by the losers, using a goo that builds up in their horn while underwater.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME produce a thick sap from their horn that is said to make a great exfoliant. Harvesting this sap can be difficult because they love to poke at the harvesters they work with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Mysterious symbols scattered among ruin walls confounded researchers for years, until it was discovered they were simply the results of POKENAME charging around, hitting the walls and leaving impact silhouettes of its shape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME briefly closes its shell, hardening its exterior further. Once reinforced, it charges at anything nearby with brutal force.
author: .izik

entry: Miners often find POKENAME in between rocks near cave entrances. They create large nests with oddly shaped stones deep within their caves.
author: schwaus

entry: While burrowing through canyons, POKENAME breaks volcanic rocks with its horn. Eating them strengthens its body to handle the above soil's immense pressure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores Cheri Berries in its skull-like shell. When it charges at trees, the berries inside shake into a semi-spicy juice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's horn is made out of particularly sturdy stone, able to withstand the force of their savage attacks without issue. When it puts its head down and starts charging, that is the signal to get out of the way fast.
author: evilgammon

entry: Its body is harder than granite, but is highly susceptible to the cold. During the winter months it covers its body in mud to stay warm.
author: .izik

entry: The shells on the back of POKENAME are made of lava that has cooled to a safe temperature. They remain close to volcanoes where they can take a dip in the lava to mend their shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rams trees with its rock-hard beak to knock loose prey like Caterpie. It follows up with a Horn Attack to finish the job.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blend into rocky pathways with their greige scales. They ram their horn to stun prey before sinking their venomous fangs into their meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roam savannas in large herds. If any predators approach, the largest POKENAME run at the threats to deliver a stinging tackle, no matter how much larger the attacking Pokémon are.
author: .realthree
