entry: Often seen carrying its young safely through the sky, POKENAME became a popular mascot for transportation companies. Many children point excitedly when they see one passing overhead, believing it brings safe journeys.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Storing their young in the fluff of their ears, POKENAME cover large stretches of savannah, keeping them safe from predators. If a kit falls out, they immediately stop, scooping it into a tight hug before continuing their run.
author: ghostslythe

entry: It has spent much of its time honing the strength of its fists and legs in order to fight or leap away to protect its young from harm. It can leap into the air and send even the heaviest flying Pokémon crashing to the ground with a single punch.
author: sk372

entry: Its young cannot fly, so it remains perched on the parent's head while it hunts. Due to its speed and maneuverability, POKENAME is always able to catch its child should it lose its grip and fall during flight.
author: sk372

entry: During a full moon, POKENAME lifts its child toward the sky. If others do the same, it hurls its young higher to compete in height.
author: .izik

entry: Not much is known about the creature that pilots the mechanical body of POKENAME, as any attempts to investigate will be met with force by the mech. However, the cries coming from the pilot lead people to believe this is an automated response.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: This Pokémon is constantly wary for any potential danger and will quietly usher its young into the thick fur on its tails to hide them when it senses a threat. It will protect its young to the end, no matter the cost.
author: chibitales

entry: Boundless energy mixed with parental instinct means POKENAME is always running from one domain to another to keep its child safe. The youngster is often a bit dizzy and disoriented from all the constant running around.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an extremely overprotective parent, using its tails and brute strength to both protect its children and crush trespassers. It marks its den with burnt foliage, so stay away if you spot it.
author: cpnquacken

entry: POKENAME's child is filled with helium and struggles to land. Oddly, when the parent sings, the baby gently floats back down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hops from tree to tree with its joey clinging tightly to its spiked back. The baby squeals with joy as they bounce through the canopy.
author: .izik

entry: It has recently been discovered that the mechanical exterior of a POKENAME is designed to provide heat and light, leading scientists to believe that the armor was designed as a sort of incubator for the creature within.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hides behind a Poké Doll that resembles a Kangaskhan. Whenever it gets caught during one of its pranks, it cowers behind the doll to appear remorseful.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whether POKENAME can be considered a good parent is hotly debated in some circles. While there's no doubt it is caring and protective, it also raises its child to be domineering and bully other child Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was created when a mother and child succumbed to the cold on a snowy mountain. It captures souls from travelers to feed to its child.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME has grown its body into a bassinet to protect its young. Some report to have seen its treelike body move quietly across fields at night.
author: gasmaskblacky

entry: In far-away regions, wild Drampa and POKENAME will often raise families together and live on snowy mountaintops. This is for the best, as their combined parental rage could level a perceived bully's entire neighborhood.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: Its young develop from the mushrooms that grow on POKENAME's back. When the young reach maturity, they will fall off their mother.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME, its child, and the mushroom that grows on its back all live together in harmony. POKENAME and its child are sheltered from harsh weather and can defend themselves from foes using the mushroom's spores.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hides its offspring within its thick fur. If startled, it emits a sudden Psybeam from its twitching antennae.
author: .izik

entry: Fiercely protective, POKENAME releases paralyzing powder clouds against those who threaten young Pokémon. Few dare approach its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's two heads share a pumpkin-like body. It uses its long limbs to tear up entire crop fields, devouring unattended plants in large quantities.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's child struggles with long swims, so it carries it safely on its lily pad. POKENAME has also been seen rescuing other small Pokémon from drowning.
author: .izik

entry: The larger entity of a POKENAME always descends to the ground first, so as to help cushion the smaller entity's landing. Seeing the pair shooting across the night sky is believed to be a good sign for an expecting parent.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME floats near mountain peaks with its young orbiting around it. The faster they spin, the more agitated they have become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically come in pairs of meteorites, one parent and one child. Whenever they are excited, they dance around each other and glitter with stardust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME displays strong paternal instincts toward abandoned eggs it encounters. It digs concealed pitfalls nearby to trap approaching predators.
author: .izik

entry: It carries around its young in its mouth, as it prevents its young from getting dirty. It would behoove itself to let go on occasion to allow the child to explore on its own, yet this seldom occurs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fiercely territorial, and spend their entire lives training to defend their children. Many threats entering its territory would see the POKENAME's powerful form rapidly approaching, and then eternal nothingness, in the blink of an eye.
author: jemeremmazza

entry: The child is immune to POKENAME's digestive fluids, so the inside of the parent's body is the safest place for it to be. POKENAME protects its young with a flurry of whipping vines and poisonous powders.
author: sk372

entry: The creature nestled between POKENAME's two heads is its child, which burrows comfortably in POKENAME's feathers as it stomps around at high speeds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The child it carries has fused into POKENAME's body; scientists have been unable to properly study how this affects POKENAME due to it being ornery with strangers. It has a powerful jump and a distinctive laugh-like cry.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME protects its child in its mouth until they're grown enough to survive alone, and they share meals. Overprotective mothers are often jokingly referred to as POKENAME.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME are caring parents, teaching their young how to avoid dangers by outrunning or intimidating aggressors. If they have to resort to fighting, POKENAME try to end fights as quickly as possible, using dirty tricks and brutal attacks.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME uses Hypnosis to help its babies sleep. Motivated by motherly love, it stays up every night to protect them from predators or nightmares.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME uses the feelers on its head to detect vibrations in the water. This allows it to retreat from predators before it is caught.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME utilizes deep-sea currents to travel at surprising speeds. When in danger, it shoots powerful electric blasts from its trunk.
author: akujules

entry: POKENAME can emit both water and smoke from the many orifices covering its body. They are able to live in both water and air. Groups of many POKENAME are thought to be a sign of a nearby factory causing too much pollution.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses the feelers on its head to detect vibrations in the water. This allows it to retreat from predators before it is caught.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is fairly weak, but it can move quickly in water by shooting a jet of liquid from its mouth.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME fusions sometimes produce oddities such as duplicated heads and tails. Their twin tails give them greater grip strength on the kelp they make their home in, but their decision making suffers from having two distinct minds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fusions develop wing-like fins that help them move more swiftly through the water. Their unusual appearance is theorised to be a result of their latent Dragon-Type potential being expressed early in their evolution line.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have long tails used to cling onto seaweed to avoid being swept away by ocean currents. POKENAME has a tail that can stretch five times the length of its body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are extremely friendly Pokémon and will try to follow people they like home from their natural habitat. As a result, POKENAME are a part of many home aquariums.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are needy and demanding Pokémon, poking the glass of their home aquariums to get the attention of their owners. When upset, POKENAME will play dead, floating upside down until their owner notices.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flutters over the surface of ponds and rivers, often in small groups. If it senses danger, it dives, using its wings as flippers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has five arms and five fins that circle around the center spout. When agitated, POKENAME releases a cloud of ink before skittering away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has five arms that latch onto the sea floor, spewing ink from its center spout to catch prey. When prey is caught in its ink, POKENAME uses its psychic power to put its prey to sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME sleeps, bubbles release from its snout with each breath. This may attract the attention of some predators, but those who bump into a bubble will be scorched with heat and blinded by smog.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are popular with fishermen, as they are considered lucky when caught early in the day. As a result, many fishermen consider it taboo to bring POKENAME into home aquariums.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are agile swimmers, using their long tail to ride along oceanic currents. POKENAME use their snout to siphon food into their mouths.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It ferries humans across the waters happily, defending them with ink shots from its mouth. POKENAME Trainers sometimes play games of tag this way, seeing which POKENAME can hit the other with ink first.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a heavy shell that can resist being swept away by underwater currents. They remain close to seaweed forests to hide from aquatic predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shuffles around the ocean floor before dispersing a thick smokescreen of ink. The blinding ink cloud stirs up small organisms that POKENAME sucks up while they flail about in blind confusion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly social creatures that have a higher population living in aquariums than in the wild. They love to eat Wepear Berries that are difficult to find in the wild.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are curious and friendly Pokémon that enjoy following divers as they make their way down to the ocean depths. POKENAME have two antennae that emit a soft glow, helping the diver see.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live deep underwater, spending most of their lives in darkness. POKENAME dislike light and will either shoot ink at or quickly flee from the source.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Easily startled, POKENAME unwittingly releases ink from its snout at the slightest provocation. It is recommended Trainers pack extra sets of clothes.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME are playful and energetic Pokémon. They enjoy climbing atop cliffs by the ocean, only to jump into the water. When they are done playing, they form clusters on the beach to nap.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swoops over water and sprays ink across the surface to make it murky. As the ink obscures vision and causes chaos beneath, it makes it easier for POKENAME to swoop once more and snatch up the confused prey.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME float around fields and meadows to play with different Pokémon in the area. When threatened, they spew out a blinding ink before scattering.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When threatened, POKENAME squirts a mucousy ink, allowing it to escape and slowing down its predators. The ink is slightly toxic but has been found to be a good antidote to other more severe poisons.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When threatened, POKENAME squirts a mucousy ink, allowing it to escape and disorientating its predators. The ink is mildly toxic but has been found to be a good antidote to other more severe poisons.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are laid-back creatures that are never in a hurry. Their heavy bodies prevent them from getting swept up by ocean currents, but they still remain near kelp forests out of habit.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At first, POKENAME was thought to be poisonous due to the liquid dripping from its spines. It's actually more ink so that POKENAME can deploy vast amounts around it to make underwater smokescreens.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live on the rocky shores close to coral reefs, causing the coral reef to appear to extend onto land. POKENAME use their snouts to spit out ink when anyone gets too close.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pick at the seafloor looking for scraps to eat. They are skittish, running away and hiding at the first sight of danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME blend into their surroundings to hide from predators. They use their ink to further help them blend in, as their horny spines glisten in the light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wander throughout the oceans protecting coral reefs from danger. Their long flippers help shield such coral reefs from oil and other toxic chemicals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gather baby aquatic Pokémon around them to form a nursery. POKENAME travel in schools and shoot out ink to ward off predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time near the shoreline, as it is a clumsy swimmer. When it wants to rest for a longer period of time, it finds cooler water to rest in before becoming inactive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its body can absorb and hold ocean water for weeks without leaking. When in a pinch POKENAME can shoot muddy bubbles at sonic speeds to deter predators.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME are capable of great bursts of speed through the ocean, but have very poor manoeuvrability. They typically move together in large schools for protection, jetting quickly away if they're threatened.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are common companions for divers, able to move underwater whilst pulling a large amount of weight. They are often vital for search and rescue missions around capsized ships.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wraps its head fin around sea grass to prevent being swept away by strong currents. Seeing two POKENAME with their fins intertwined is said to bring eternal happiness.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are often kept as pets, as they are fiercely loyal and great with children. When POKENAME evolve, these traits only grow more prevalent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its saliva naturally mimics bubble solution, making it tempting to play with. Be careful, this Pokémon feeds by catching others in its bubbles.
author: .fedoraman

entry: It uses its ribbons to help it aim where it fires its ink. They often challenge Pokémon twice their own size.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME can launch sticky internal organs from their mouths to grab nearby food. While they prefer to stay stationary, they can use their tail fins to move around when needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME floats through the shallows, keeping its true body hidden beneath a soggy, doll-like cloth. Despite its appearance, the fabric is fully waterproof, shielding it from both rain and prying eyes.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME rolls backward slowly while sleeping in deep waters. If it has a bad dream, it unintentionally expels a massive burst of bubbles, propelling itself at high speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats through the ocean eating plankton and other microscopic critters. When threatened, it releases a Smokescreen full of spores that irritate the mouths and gills of predators.
author: chibitales

entry: It is thought to form when ocean ecosystems are damaged by large amounts of trash pollution. The recent increase in their numbers is considered to be a dangerous sign.
author: linhasxoc

entry: POKENAME live in damp caves, flying around in search of food. POKENAME dive into cavern lakes, using their large mouth to bite onto their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME frequently practices a cheer routine using pom-poms made of seafoam. It squirts pitch-black ink from its mouth for more dramatic entrances and exits.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: Combining the natural behaviors of both of its components, POKENAME loves to snack on ocean trash. Ecologists are considering using this fusion to clean up the seas.
author: hophoppip

entry: Due to the appearance of their fins, POKENAME are often bought for casino aquariums. When food sinks to the bottom of the tank, POKENAME turn to use their snouts to eat, showing the coin-like fins to guests.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though it appears decorative, the seaweed POKENAME holds acts in accordance with its will, usually to grab and hinder other creatures so that POKENAME can blind them with an inky smokescreen.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lure prey towards themselves by using their small heads as a lure. POKENAME then use their long, poisonous tentacles to attack their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rest in shallow waters near beaches and eat food dropped by tourists. Children like to pick up POKENAME and use them to float on the water, as they are friendly and comfortable to hold.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spars deep underwater, constantly seeking challengers. If outmatched, it escapes by releasing thick ink clouds and vanishing.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME fires powerful bursts of bubbles to disable foes. It immediately retreats underground once the enemy is subdued.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's heart-shaped body bobs gently on the water's surface as it sleeps. If disturbed, it releases a burst of pink ink before darting away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float all over the oceans of the world, traveling in migratory groups. POKENAME migrate to warmer waters during cold seasons and return home when the weather warms up again.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of swimming quite quickly through the water but have a difficult time maintaining proper nutrition because of their small mouths. Many are malnourished because there are not enough predators to cull their numbers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have two giant eyes that bulge from their head. POKENAME prefer to live in darkness and will release clouds of ink to hide from the light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME spreads its tentacles wide to sense any movement nearby. Soft bubbles escape from its mouth as it snores, creating a gentle ripple effect in the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME laze around the beach and sleep for 18 hours a day. When disturbed from their sleep, POKENAME sneeze out ink from their snouts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are popular at aquariums and resorts, as their cautious but playful temperament gives tourists excitement without causing too much mischief. POKENAME enjoy playing with Berries, balancing them on their snouts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have adapted to the icy tundra of the world. POKENAME uses its snout to spit out black ink, marking its hunting grounds and territory to other POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a strong shell that resists the ocean's currents. When threatened, POKENAME spit out a cloud of ink before hiding in its tough shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has adapted to live in the most frigid of oceanic environments. POKENAME is able to spit out a chilling ink, allowing it to freeze its predators and give it the chance to escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They can spray inky-black bubbles from their snout that explode and smokescreen the general vicinity. Wild POKENAME only use their pincers in emergencies, and prefer an idyllic life of eating underwater plant life.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME scuttles across sandy beaches, using its ink to mark its territory. If one POKENAME crosses into the territory of another POKENAME, they will fight using their large claw.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have an elongated snout and long back fins. Their tails remain undeveloped, so POKENAME rely on their fins for movement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A fusion of two Seadra produces POKENAME, a Pokémon that swims at over 40 knots. They can shoot out a jet of water from their mouths that has enough force to cut through steel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are friendly but needy Pokémon that demand lots of attention from their owners. If left alone for too long, POKENAME will tap on the glass of their enclosure incessantly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME, despite their appearance, are loyal and caring Pokémon. POKENAME frequently outgrow their enclosures and are often released into a pond or lake to give them more room.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live on the seafloor, the center spout releasing built-up ink when necessary. It is said that the ink from POKENAME helps coral reefs grow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live on the ocean floor, where many barb-like arms surround the center spout, which occasionally shoots out built-up ink. The nutrient-rich ink is eaten by many other aquatic Pokémon in the region.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their long noses to pick at the ocean floor to find food. POKENAME use their fins to stir up the sand, finding bits of plant matter to consume.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fly through the ocean skies, their scales providing aerodynamic flow. POKENAME shed scales often, which fall onto beaches or the ocean floor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their long noses to pick up scents in the air, as POKENAME never forget an island's smell. POKENAME then use their large shells atop their backs to ferry people between islands.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have rugged scales on their bellies, which they use to protect themselves from attacks. When a scale is damaged, POKENAME shed and regrow that scale.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies alongside large ships as they travel across the ocean, dutifully guarding them. If it spots aggressive Pokémon breaching the waters in preparation to attack, it stuns them with precision shots of ink from its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fight by firing compressed fireballs with extreme precision via their barrel-like mouths or by unleashing jets of steaming hot water. They are quite agile in water and can easily outmaneuver many underwater opponents.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have two long antennae that help them remain balanced when swimming. POKENAME will shoot electrified ink in small gooey blobs to stun opponents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dive deep below the surface where the light is weaker, as bright lights cause POKENAME irritation. POKENAME will shoot blobs of ink at bright lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME releases a burst of ink from their barbs whenever they are threatened. They were once hunted by poachers for their ink, but poachers lost interest when cheap ink became widely available.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It shoots water with enough force to fracture bones. It can accurately hit a target from over 45 meters away.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME have large fins and tentacles that they use to fight. The tentacles are sticky, able to latch onto the ocean floor to remain stationary in ocean currents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME travel from coral reef to coral reef, ensuring the natural wildlife is protected from danger. POKENAME travel in schools with other Pokémon to fulfill their natural calling.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shoots pressurized ink from its two cannon-like mouths with enough force to pierce steel. They often compete in standoffs to determine the quicker shot.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its coiled tail acts as a rudder in water. They use their ribbons and legs to paddle at speeds that allow them to swim against strong currents.
author: melodydelune

entry: The spikes all over POKENAME's body are poisonous to the touch. They live in underwater caves, draining minerals from rocks around them.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME have many rough, sharp scales they use as a natural defense mechanism. POKENAME will rub against rocks to keep those scales sharp.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generates powerful Gusts to create its own underwater current, which it uses to increase its speed. When POKENAME needs to surface quickly, its wings expand and effectively become flotation devices.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME fires jets of vibrant blue ink from its mouth to ward off attackers. While the ink is sought after for its unique pigment, it is also highly corrosive and will slowly melt its way through any hard material.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME fires water at high pressure to hit foes from a distance. If a foe manages to get close, it instead swings the anchor it covers at them. Touching a POKENAME can result in infection due to the poisonous film that covers its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME use their head to lure prey towards themselves. POKENAME will then use their snouts to shoot ink before closing in with their barbed tentacles to secure a meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hide their head inside their tentacles, drawing in unsuspecting prey. POKENAME then use their barbed tentacles to wrap around their meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rest on the ocean floor, eating food swept there by the ocean currents. First-time divers often look out for POKENAME, as POKENAME release psychic energy that discourages predators from approaching.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME engages in duels by firing high-powered jets of water at its rivals. The first to flinch or move from the stream is declared the loser.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is allergic to the various powders its own body produces. Its sneezes launch high-power water jets that can pierce steel.
author: chartanon

entry: If disturbed while digging, POKENAME spits dark ink into its foe's eyes. It remains equally capable of fighting in soil or water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires pressurized jets of ink from its mouth, powerful enough to break through coral. If two schools end up running into each other, a massive fight will break out, staining the water black with ink.
author: mistymagius

entry: Internal water storage allows POKENAME to survive in arid environments. If angered, it will defend itself with an eruption of sticky black ink.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME migrate alongside other Pokémon during the cold seasons and return home during hot seasons. They are known to attack sailors who they cross paths with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have sharp fins that cover tentacle fists. When fighting, POKENAME are known to spit ink into the eyes of their opponents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have two large unblinking eyes that stare at the world. When in danger, POKENAME will release inky waves of sludge to slow down predators as they make their escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have two eyes that hide behind a giant mask. POKENAME avoid conflict by hiding deep below the surface of the sea, using clouds of ink to obscure their presence.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their fins to emit psychic energy and defend themselves. POKENAME cannot remove the shell on its tail, despite their best efforts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are great for aquariums, as their mild and easily amused temperament give tourists joy. POKENAME love hugging people and are slow enough that photographers take adorable photos.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a strong shell with large fins that allows them to glide through the ocean's currents. POKENAME fins are razor thin, and very sharp.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can fire dangerous, high velocity jets of water from over a mile away both above and below water, but in close combat POKENAME is forced to retreat into its shell.
author: alumed

entry: POKENAME are territorial, spewing ink to mark their territory. This is because POKENAME need plenty of room to wander and are solitary by nature.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Once evolved into POKENAME, it will shed its more peaceful lifestyle and act as a guard for nearby marine Pokémon. Its pincers are laced with a mind-numbing poison. Very few POKENAME evolve further than this state.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are very weak and are a common food source for many aquatic Pokémon. POKENAME swim in schools with numbers in the thousands trying to defend themselves but it's not very effective.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are priceless, sought after by chefs all over the region. Contrary to their revered status in the culinary field, they are pathetic fighters.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME are carried by others so that they can remain part of the school of aquatic Pokémon. Without the support of others, they quickly succumb to predators who break into their cocoons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spits ink that changes color based on its mood. This ink was once prized by cartographers for its vivid and varied hues.
author: .izik

entry: The venom from POKENAME's spike is boiled down to create high-quality wood tarnishes. These tarnishes enhance the durability and shine of wooden furniture.
author: .izik

entry: Despite a somewhat distorted appearance, POKENAME functions normally and seems perfectly peaceable in behavior. It's even become something of a mascot of a power plant located in a remote part of Unova.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries enormous potential for growth. This helps its long fins quickly heal from the tears it accumulates while fighting.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME's horn glows blue, it summons powerful whirlpools. These spinning waters are said to disorient even the most experienced swimmers.
author: .izik

entry: Its beautiful, colorful fins allow it to hover slightly above the water's surface to catch small insects. POKENAME is a very delicate creature, in fact if the lake or river it lives in becomes polluted, it must be moved immediately to clean waters.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME watch over schools of Goldeen to ensure they stay organized and safe. If a predator approaches, POKENAME will rapidly sway its fins and shine a light from its eye to scare them off.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME protect schools of Goldeen by ramming into predators with their jeweled horn. One precise stab is enough for most predators to get the message, especially when POKENAME give chase if they don't escape far enough.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME reaches speeds of over 40 mph when swimming with its body shifted horizontally. It leaps out of the water to nip at tree leaves.
author: .izik

entry: Many sea-based merchants train POKENAME to guard their vessels during voyages. Its keen senses help it detect threats from afar.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hums loudly in foggy conditions. Some believe it is searching for others of its kind, while others fear it lures fishermen to their doom.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in its glossy and pristine coat. It refuses to swim in an waters that aren't clean enough, and will show no mercy to those that dirty its fur.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its extended mouth to fight for dominance. The winner of the fight gets to claim the highest nesting spot.
author: .realthree

entry: As POKENAME grow and shed their skin, their scales become more beautiful. Their fins dance dreamily as they swim the rivers and lakes they live in.
author: gloomymort

entry: POKENAME spend a lot of time polishing their orbs and scales in an effort to make themselves more enchanting. They will only be satisfied when they glitter in the sunlight.
author: gloomymort

entry: POKENAME glide through the night sky like shooting stars, guiding lost ships to shore by reflecting the moonlight in their shimmering scales.
author: rooboid

entry: This petite Pokémon snacks on autumn leaves and acorns to gain weight and stay warm during winter. Those who ruffle its hair will suffer a nasty fate.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME are known for their persistent vanity, and create walls of water to admire their gorgeous reflection. They are protective of their hair.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME who are well-cared for boast a gorgeously patterned collar. Those who are not will see their petals wilted. They need lots of beauty sleep.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME are often gifted as a starter Pokémon to young children, as the bubbles from its back are much safer than the fiery embers of Cyndaquil.
author: rooboid

entry: The bubble formation on POKENAME's back allows it to breathe for a limited time while out of water. However, it is rarely seen above the surface.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME can now let off flames from its crown when enraged. Its gorgeous tail twists in the breeze as it dashes towards unsuspecting foes.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME makes light work of foes by sweeping them off their feet and barraging them with a hail of bubbles. Flames burst from its mane when enraged.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME makes its nests in the center of lakes where it is safe from land predators. It stays away from lakeshores where predators like Ursaring are known to gather.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A popular nursery rhyme claims POKENAME is an omen of good weather. Children often make dolls in its image when they wish for sunny days. However, these dolls often get lost and swept away in rivers, polluting POKENAME's home and driving it away.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME's horns glow yellow when a thunderstorm approaches. It raises its antennae to absorb lightning, protecting others nearby from shocks.
author: .izik

entry: A famous Trainer in the Alola region showcased this petite Pokémon on TV. Now, many Trainers dress their POKENAME to also look like that Trainer's.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME splashes its tail playfully when near allies. When happy, it can create splashes reaching up to 30 feet in height.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to chip away at submerged parts of icebergs. It creates intricate carvings to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: Before thunderstorms, its tail-like whiskers quiver intensely. It dashes to open fields, hoping a lightning strike hits its horn to invigorate it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very proud of their beauty, gathering clay to build urns depicting the colors and patterns of their scales. Washed-up fragments of these urns make for popular jewelry, leading people to paint seaglass to sell as counterfeit imitations.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME take the form of a glyph that has fins and communicates with other aquatic Pokémon by swirling and flapping their fins. Whenever they encounter a Trainer, they release bubbles from their body in an effort to communicate.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Water from rivers containing POKENAME is sent through specialized treatment plants to clear the poison. Unfortunately, POKENAME enjoy using the vents to polish their horns, blocking the flow and releasing excess toxins, delaying the whole process.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Many POKENAME are found fidgeting with their tails in small ponds. POKENAME drink through their skin, but it's agonizingly slow, so they need to find a way to fill the time.
author: jojojax164

entry: Fire and magma burns from its body despite its underwater habitat. Its frills are packed with minerals absorbed through a diet of small pebbles.
author: seaslux

entry: Water boils inside its hardened shell. As an elegant, somewhat hard-to-obtain Pokémon that also functions as an airstone, it is prized by aquarists.
author: seaslux

entry: POKENAME searches the seafloor for the most beautiful shells, discarding any once it finds a better one. It values beauty above all else.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims quickly upstream during thunderstorms, using its horn to divert lightning from its allies.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME will make its home within a shipwreck, using lost treasure to disguise its shiny horns and colorful frills. If it's spotted by a diver, it will offer them treasure in exchange for being left alone.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's metallic talons can tear through even the toughest shells. A single swipe is said to be strong enough to pierce a Squirtle's defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be observed raising young Golcute in its pouch. While they aren't particularly strong, they are excellent and speedy swimmers.
author: rooboid

entry: Newly created POKENAME start off clumsy and struggle to swim or walk, but they soon develop powerful muscles that allow them to outpace athletes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although their exaggerated movements and billowing fins make them a joy to behold, POKENAME refuse to stay confined to one spot, and therefore will not tolerate being in an aquarium. They rapidly kick both to swim and to fight.
author: bobosmith01

entry: In the spring, schools of POKENAME can be seen swimming up falls and rivers. Every several years it sheds its scales, and new, supple ones grow back.
author: fuzzythelion

entry: POKENAME are often seen with a school of male Goldeen. They are able control the flow of the water to guide their school.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME who lose a limb are able to reconstruct the body part with a prosthetic of bubbles. This is a testament to their incredible will and resolve.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME who lose a limb are able to reconstruct the body part with a prosthetic of bubbles. This is a testament to their incredible will and resolve.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME lure sailors with their gorgeous, flowing scales and enchanting singing voice. However, the hair-like jaws on their head bite anyone foolish enough to approach.
author: mistymagius

entry: In Kanto, fishing contests are often held to catch POKENAME, and whoever catches the largest one is declared the winner. It does not hesitate to impale enemies with the poisonous horn on its forehead to protect itself or its family.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's shimmering scales are often sewn into wedding gowns. If it rains during the ceremony, the dress sparkles like stars as water strikes the scales.
author: .izik

entry: Known as "The Sea Princess," they swim by swishing their dress-like fins and legs. They are high-value pets for the rich because of their beauty.
author: melodydelune

entry: Trainers who seek power evolve their POKENAME into Seaxorus, but Trainers who seek beauty are more than happy with this gorgeous, shimmering Pokémon.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME is rumored to have been created by Lugia to serve as a protector of the seas. It is very rarely seen by people.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are able to become completely invisible underwater thanks to its psychic powers. The patterns on its body ripple across its body like waves.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body seems to be an extension controlled by the orb of its chest. When it loses limbs, they quickly decompose and disintegrate, so it uses the biomass of plankton to grow them back.
author: epping_forest

entry: With its round body, POKENAME can roll across land for short distances. If it encounters an obstacle, it shatters it effortlessly with its powerful horn.
author: .izik

entry: Schools of POKENAME emerge from ocean caves as soon as the sun sets. They remain hidden during the day to avoid predators.
author: .izik

entry: Known for its bulbous eyes and cowardly nature, POKENAME are often won as carnival prizes, making it a common and rather odd-looking starter Pokémon.
author: rooboid

entry: The density of POKENAME's body differs from water, allowing it to navigate riverbanks with ease. On particularly hot days, groups of POKENAME can be found compacted together in the shade of stones and water lilies.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME walks along the ocean floor, sucking up small bits of food. It doesn't do very much other than that.
author: themicelegion

entry: Large groups of POKENAME rest upside-down under bridges that extend above water during summer days. When the sun sets, they fly off into the sky. This event is a popular tourist attraction for Cerulean City.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Each POKENAME was once a Goldeen held in cramped living conditions. When it died, it took this form. It holds a fishbowl as a reminder of its past.
author: .realthree

entry: While it is indeed delicious and fatty, POKENAME is a surprisingly good swimmer, and many activists ensure the protection of this unique Pokémon.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME lives in underwater caves. It decorates its home with rusted shipwreck parts and drowned sailors.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME resembles a Goldeen trapped inside an animate plastic bag. The Goldeen looks just as it did before fusing, but it seems to have inherited some of Trubbish's poison tolerance, as it has no trouble surviving in dirty, unbreathable water.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME struggles to turn after it jets forward at high speeds. Losing track of its surroundings, it often becomes disoriented or lost.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swings its anchor-like tail to stun enemies before attacking with a Peck. The blow can send opponents flying over 100 feet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's toxin smells strongly of vinegar. If boiled, it can be repurposed as an effective nail polish remover.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bite off bait from fishing lines, stealing it to use for themselves. They return to the ocean floor decorated in trinkets and lures to entice their prey.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lies in wait for other fish. Once a suitable target is within range, it shows its "unique" beauty by winking to stun them. While they are dazzled, it sabotages their scales so that they look just as "pretty" as POKENAME does.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME fights with an elegant, ballroom dance-style of combat. It will distract opponents with its flowing tail before landing a spinning strike from its large claws.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sway in place within coral reefs, waving their patterned arms and fins to mimic the movements of small Water-type Pokémon. These movements lure would-be predators into striking range, providing POKENAME with plenty of food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be seen floating calmly along rivers with its shell visible on the surface. The geyser that comes from its back is said to shimmer beautifully in the sun.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Despite being amphibious, POKENAME must return to the waters periodically or their body starts not being able to function. As a result, they usually do not stray far from the water-filled mountain valleys where they live.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Some regions attempted to use POKENAME as a more glamorous gift counterpart to Luvdisc, but the Pokémon's aggressive temperament made it ill-suited to be a loved one's present.
author: sk372

entry: When in an aquarium, POKENAME routinely cleans the substrate. This makes it popular among aquarists for its utility, as well as its looks.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME skims across lake surfaces at remarkable speed when threatened. It dashes forward to strike with its horn, which is sharp enough to pierce solid stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are well known to hang out at the bottom of wishing wells. By doing so, it allows them to steal any coins that people throw in.
author: kitarchen

entry: Despite POKENAME's large fins, it is quick and precise while hunting. The many patterns and colors POKENAME's scales can take on have inspired luxury gowns all over the world.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME attempt to communicate swimming patterns telepathically, but it almost always results in them getting intense headaches. As a result, their swimming tends to be a lot less coordinated than their appearance would suggest.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: In spring, groups of POKENAME can be seen migrating to the streams and rivers of their birth. The water they spout leaves intense burns on their prey.
author: melodydelune

entry: They swim together in large groups. POKENAME do not get along with Poliwag or Goldeen, and battles between them are not unheard of.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon raises Goldeen in its glassy pouch. The overall health of a POKENAME can be determined by the condition and size of its Goldeen.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME hosts a small ecosystem within its body. Its love of hand-to-hand combat often results in this ecosystem being smashed open.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME is a common choice for household aquariums and gets along well with other small, aquatic Pokémon. It is voracious and often gobbles up more food than it can handle, so owners need to carefully spread out small feedings.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME paralyzes foes with its tentacles before drilling into them with its horn. This swift combination leaves its enemies incapacitated in moments.
author: .izik

entry: Acid seeps from its tendrils to dissolve driftwood for nourishment. For larger pieces, it uses its sharp horn to break them apart before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: In the springtime, schools of POKENAME swim up falls and rivers, causing the waters to foam and bubble with heat.
author: togetik

entry: POKENAME scatter scales as they swim, creating a shimmering trail behind them. Their scales collect seawater as they drift, causing them to be popular material for scented candles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME never parts with the reed it carries like a weapon; if it loses it, it cries for weeks. Thanks to its vibrant colors and elegant swimming, it is highly appreciated in beauty competitions.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's scales can endure freezing temperatures. During the summer, they shed into the sea, creating reflective trails on the water's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME closely monitors underwater oil pumps, quickly alerting humans to any leaks. It is fiercely protective of its clean territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats near passenger ships, waiting for trash to be discarded. It uses its horn to drag waste beneath the waves and consume it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell patterns become more vibrant and intricate when it has a good diet, so in the wild a beautiful shell will attract mates. Its large ears are sensitive to underwater noises, allowing it to detect predators with plenty of time to hide.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME makes its nest in large freshwater ponds where it can burrow into the mud at night, only the cannons visible. Despite its bulk, it swims gracefully thanks to its powerful tail.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When happy, POKENAME spits out tiny pink pearls as gifts to its friends. These pearls are highly valued by collectors for their unique hue.
author: .izik

entry: Operated by a school of Goldeen, the ghastly remains of an Onix live again in the form of POKENAME. This Pokémon acts and thinks as a combined entity.
author: rooboid

entry: The strongest POKENAME lead their school with high prestige, but they are not much stronger and are often picked off first. As they age, more black spots appear on their fins.
author: mistymagius

entry: Kept aboard ship medical bays, POKENAME's eggs have been known to heal everything from seasickness to scurvy. If a Sailor falls overboard, it is the first in the water, able to swim against even the strongest of undertows.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME releases Smokescreen to obscure predators before climbing waterfalls. The first to reach the top becomes the school's leader.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its small stature, POKENAME is aggressive and territorial, blinding intruders with shots of ink to the eyes before swiftly closing in to gore them with its sharp horn.
author: sk372

entry: In the wild, POKENAME are rejected and attacked by both Goldeen and Seaking, so they are forced to live a solitary life and compete with other Pokémon for food and territory. As a result, they are unusually aggressive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are protective of aquatic Pokémon and attack fishermen who fish in their waters. They snap fishing lines by curling them around their horn before pulling as hard as they can.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wrap their limbs around fishing lines to protect their aquatic brethren. Once fished up by bewildered fishermen, POKENAME wreak havoc by frantically stabbing anything they can with their horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's rather unique swimming style makes it look like it's climbing an imaginary ladder. It can also create invisible barriers, and has fun using them to imprison big predators as if they're in a fish tank.
author: epping_forest

entry: A common fusion that breeds in nearly any kind of water. Scientists have noted that they appear more intelligent compared to Magikarp: many avoid common fishing hooks, even ones with quality bait.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are well known for their beautiful patterns and horns, and the ones with the longest horns and most intricate patterns are sought out by collectors.
author: astral1447

entry: POKENAME are a common fusion that breeds in nearly any kind of water. Scientists have noted that they appear more intelligent compared to Magikarp: many avoid common fishing hooks, even ones with quality bait.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are highly opportunistic feeders that frequently attack humans in search of food. Despite their aggression, POKENAME meat is considered a delicacy, marked by a tough, buttery texture and its distinctive striped scales.
author: turron_turron

entry: It has no bones to speak of, so its body jiggles about like a water balloon. It thrives in neglected ponds, where it feasts on algae.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: The sight of a POKENAME swooping over the water evokes a primal fear in Water-type Pokémon. Its massive fins capture swirling updrafts effortlessly.
author: .realthree

entry: Upon evolving, POKENAME gains the ability to leap from the water at great speeds and fly for short periods of time. Whether above or beneath the waves, its entire body leaves boiling water and steam in its path.
author: alestrius

entry: POKENAME make their home in rocky riverbeds where sentries can easily poke their heads out of the water. At the first sign of danger, the sentries will cry loudly, causing the entire colony to hide away until the danger passes.
author: chibitales

entry: Its lures resemble a pair of Goldeen. When predators approach in hopes of easy prey, POKENAME delivers an electric shock that knocks them unconscious.
author: cartoonhostage

entry: Antennae on POKENAME leak Kelpsy Berry-flavored fluid loved by Goldeen. It guards Goldeen schools with swift horn strikes.
author: .izik

entry: Sought after for its delectable, melt-in-the-mouth texture, chefs the world over will pay handsomely for a POKENAME. It hides in its egg when scared.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME's once-delicious skin becomes sour as it evolves; this is a defense mechanism to ward off poachers and anglers alike. It is a weak swimmer.
author: rooboid

entry: This Pokémon tends to sleep in freshwater and rises into the skies at the break of dawn. Though many say this is a beautiful sight, it will attack anyone who strays too close to its nest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lies at the bottom of the ocean, swimming around looking for sea grass. When the water current gets too strong, it will anchor itself to a nearby rock with its long tail.
author: mistymagius

entry: Great shoals of POKENAME gather every 3 years, to swim upstream to mate and lay their eggs. They have great strength, but little coordination, so are constantly bumping into each other and getting pushed out of the water, making rivers look alive.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite its heavy, durable body, POKENAME is an adept swimmer. If an obstacle gets in its way, regardless if it's a human, boulder, or Pokémon, this species' titanium-tough horns break right through.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Even during storms, POKENAME swims with unmatched power. Waterspouts and violent waves never slow its pace.
author: .izik

entry: Warmth emanates from the soft internal shell on its back. When threatened, it releases this heat from its body, boiling the surrounding water.
author: seaslux

entry: It has an obsidian shell, and a silvery film has hardened over its underside. It looks intimidating, but it's surprisingly weak with delicate frills.
author: seaslux

entry: POKENAME clings to docked ships with its tentacles. It carefully scrapes and eats barnacles using its sharp horn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dive deep into the depths of the ocean to break apart sunken ships with their hefty horn. If they encounter any people trying to retrieve lost treasure, they respond with hostile aggression.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Ancient civilizations judged the shift from summer to autumn by the color of POKENAME's scales, its colorless body glowing into a vibrant red before making way for other colors. When water catches the light, it looks like a fallen piece of a rainbow.
author: backgroundnoisegalore

entry: On the rare occasion that two POKENAME meet, their courtship dance is a sight to behold. No firsthand depictions of the event exist, for all who witness it claim they could not do the spectacle justice.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME treads along the seafloor in search of food. Their sharp horns and rubbery skin protect them from predators above. If food is scarce, POKENAME can enter a hibernation state by completely ceasing any movement.
author: roniodove

entry: POKENAME swim in large schools, leaping out of the water in a gorgeous spectacle. Male POKENAME are incredibly competitive and will attempt to pierce each other's wings with their horns.
author: mistymagius

entry: It punches holes in boulders on streambeds. Every several years, POKENAME sheds their scales and new, supple ones grow back in their place.
author: fuzzythelion

entry: Although POKENAME mainly lives in river waters, it can survive for quite some time on land when searching for berries to feed on. It keeps its sharp horn polished by rubbing it against the rocks found in the stream.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Although POKENAME mainly lives in river waters, it can survive for quite some time on land when searching for berries to feed on. It keeps its sharp horn polished by rubbing it against the rocks found in the stream.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In the water, POKENAME are powerful and swift, capable of making sharp turns to pursue darting prey. The bright colors and beautiful patterns on their bodies help in attracting potential mates.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's luxurious scales have been the inspiration for many high-end fashion designers. They float alone in the open ocean waiting for the mouth on its head to gobble up passing fish Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep ocean, using its large horn to fight off other large Pokémon. However, its numbers have severely declined, as its horn has become a desired collector's item.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME defend themselves with a horn that is as long as a cue stick. Their auxiliary shield on their side also protects them from harm but is less intimidating than their horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to its veil-like tail, it is considered good luck for a wild POKENAME to be caught by someone awaiting a proposal.
author: dicedragon20

entry: Once a year, groups of POKENAME gather by the shore to perform courtship rituals. Males will attract females with vibrant patterns and dances.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME has grown to the point that it can no longer leave its tank. However, the force of its love for its Trainer has allowed it to manifest arms.
author: .realthree

entry: This Pokémon is said to have inspired the creation of dragon rolls. Its torso moves independently from its lower body, though it cannot stray too far.
author: rooboid

entry: Its special technique consists of turning the sea into the void of space for a couple of seconds, causing severe damage to any living creature nearby. Its sole presence seems to awaken the adrenaline of Kyogre, the Lord of the Ocean.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is a territorial bully that inhabits large lakes. It uses its bulk and solid horn to attack and steal food from other Pokémon, as well as taking gnawing on any boats that happen to float through its territory.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME that are treated with care exhibit the most strikingly golden masks. Despite what rumors claim, its memory is excellent.
author: .realthree

entry: Though POKENAME isn't well-suited for battle, it boasts a dexterity that far surpasses the average human's. POKENAME are seldom seen in the wild.
author: rooboid

entry: For many generations, POKENAME was cast aside in Pokémon contests due to its ugly appearance. However, in recent years others have started to find POKENAME charming and built clubs around raising them.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME use their delicate, silky fins to mimic dancing as they swim, distracting any threats and attracting prey. They adorn themselves with pearls, Heart Scales, and various other items to add to their dazzling performance.
author: ohok3441

entry: It swims at high speeds, attempting to ram targets with its large horn that is as hard as rock.
author: pokopish

entry: Coordinators love extremely smelly POKENAME for one specific reason: the stronger their stench, the brighter and healthier their scales are. Using perfumes to douse the scent is frowned upon in several circles.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's legs retain water easily. It stands in deep puddles to soak water up into its limbs so it can use the extra weight to increase the power of its blows.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its long, powerful limbs to swim up waterfalls. If threatened, it punches with enough force to shatter stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the large hooks in its arms to cling to rocks to avoid being swept away. The mushrooms on its back move to propel it through the water.
author: .realthree

entry: The extravagant fins that POKENAME have are a symbol of beauty. Enthusiasts often compete to see whose POKENAME has the most magnificent fins.
author: .realthree

entry: Its chant is heard underwater as a perfectly tuned caress to the soul that a whole ocean can feel. However, on the surface, it sounds like a wet balloon being deflated.
author: epping_forest

entry: Its pirouettes, jumps and acrobatics look gorgeous to see underwater. However, it tends to look dumb when trying that on the surface, due to the gravity and how heavy its fins become.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is very proud of its scales and will flaunt them to any passing Pokémon. However, it is incredibly temperamental and will viciously attack those who don't appreciate its appearance.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are prized for their luxurious, patterned fins. Their popularity makes them a common sight at exotic aquariums as they preen along the floor of the tanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are prized for their luxurious, patterned fins. Their popularity makes them a common sight at exotic aquariums as they preen along the floor of the tanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are prized for their luxurious, patterned fins. Their popularity makes them a common sight at exotic aquariums as they preen along the floor of the tanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wings are sturdy enough to be used underwater, but it spends more time fluttering from one riverside flower to another.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME tunnels across ocean floors in search of coral to consume. When exhausted between reefs, it feeds on seaweed to recover.
author: .izik

entry: Red scales from POKENAME were once used in ancient love potions. In liquid, they shimmer and glow faintly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME communicates telepathically, which is effective for coordinated small groups. Once they reach a sizable group of POKENAME, their telepathic communication breaks down, leading to headaches and disorganized swimming.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME zip past other Pokémon while swimming as they gracefully dodge obstacles in their path. During the mating season, they search for mates who exhibit great agility, as being able to perform complex maneuvers is seen as attractive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have special webbing on their flippers that allows them to swim up waterfalls. This is particularly helpful during their mating season, as being able to swiftly climb waterfalls is seen as a desirable trait.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It considers itself a fierce and just king of underwater Pokémon, defending its kingdom from usurpers and aggressors. It will grapple and stab even Gyarados into submission for the sake of its subjects.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is aggressive, chasing other Pokémon to bash them with its horn. It will even swim up a waterfall to launch itself at flying Pokémon that have gained its ire. If kept in a tank, it will most likely smash its way out.
author: pjporwoll

entry: At night, dozens of POKENAME drift across the sea with glowing horns. They're seen as beautiful despite their aggressive swarms.
author: .izik

entry: The bell of POKENAME resembles an injured Seaking, which it mimics to lure in predators of Seaking. When they get close, POKENAME wraps them in its tentacles and jabs them with its venomous beak so it can feed leisurely.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME often forgets what it's doing mid-swim. It sometimes even loses focus while climbing waterfalls and drifts back down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is much more docile than other members of its evolution line, preferring to bask just below the surface of the water. It can be safely kept in decorative ponds where Everstones have been carefully scattered around.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME developed the ability to catch fish, using its leek as a rod. If a Pokémon bites, it is sure to be pulled out of the water and battled immediately.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME smashes icebergs with its horn as a show of strength. It prefers testing itself this way over real combat.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being friendly towards humans, POKENAME is a vicious arctic predator and will prey on anything smaller than it. It uses its sharp horn to break through thick ice.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a highly invasive species after owners released it once previous forms grew too large to care for. It outcompetes other freshwater predators, fighting viciously and only firing its spikes as a last resort, as they take weeks to regrow.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Before it sleeps, POKENAME places a grain of sand in its lips. By morning, it forms a beautiful orange pearl prized by jewelers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is baked to bring out the juicy oils that are stored in its body. It is usually served with a side of rice and a few slices of citrus to balance the natural salt content of the dish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their claws can come in a variety of colors and patterns. Fishermen love collecting POKENAME solely to see what new patterns they will see with each catch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After gathering enough sunlight, POKENAME finally grew out of its shell. They shoot sticky webs from the seed on their back.
author: imagine1.

entry: If it senses danger, it will flutter its wings and spread a purple powder. This powder can paralyze a full-grown man if ingested.
author: .izik

entry: The orb at the end of its bone-staff spreads a pollen similar to that of its wings, but much more potent. Non-violent by nature, it puts aggressors to sleep with a wave of its wand before running away.
author: sk372

entry: It regularly becomes exhausted during flight, plummeting to the forest floor. Some travelers have been knocked unconscious by a falling POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides gracefully along cliffs, skillfully riding air currents. It nests in rocky outcroppings, safe from most predators due to the perilous terrain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often seen taking care of lost Metapod and Caterpie. It keeps them until they are fully rehabilitated.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It glides over the ocean surface in search of tiny insects to suck up with its mouth. Each graceful movement of its beautiful wings releases colored dust into the water, enriching nearby algae and coral.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its paralyzing powders to weaken prey, which it then catches while flying above the ocean waves. It can shoot jets of extremely salty water from its mouth to put its opponents at a disadvantage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its paralyzing powders to weaken prey, which it then catches while flying above the ocean waves. It can shoot jets of extremely salty water from its mouth to put its opponents at a disadvantage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its paralyzing powders to weaken prey, which it then catches while flying above the ocean waves. It can shoot jets of extremely salty water from its mouth to put its opponents at a disadvantage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME produce many eggs throughout their lifetime, but they are unable to defend the eggs with their small horn. This leads to an unfortunate situation where many eggs are eaten by predators before they hatch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are unable to defend their eggs effectively without horns or other defense mechanisms, so they focus on producing as many eggs as possible. This has led to many POKENAME abandoning nests if they have a chance at making more eggs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though beautiful, it requires lots of space to keep due to its massive size. Rich landowners often breed POKENAME for their iridescent colors.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: It is unaffected by most plant-based toxins, allowing it to eat as many flowers as it likes. By using its sharp limbs, it is able to cut down entire fields of flowers in minutes.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME flutters through the air, it leaves behind a glimmering dust that can temporarily boost a Pokémon's vitality. This dust is a rare ingredient in crafting PP Max.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It prefers the sap of Shuca Berry trees above all others due to its spicy taste. It is very careful not to drain too much of the liquid so that it does not permanently damage the tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rides on the winds created by a stampede, matching the energy of charging Pokémon. It often joins herds, using their momentum to travel great distances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flops around helplessly. Scientists believe POKENAME is attempting to fly with its inherited instincts from Butterfree, but sadly lacks wings. Instead, clouds of dizzying spores spurt out from its scales every time it lands or takes off.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's scales are highly toxic; touching them could be fatal. It uses its wings to create massive bursts of wind that can trap its opponents.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's scales are highly toxic; touching them could be fatal. It uses its wings to create massive bursts of wind that can trap its opponents.
author: soup1900

entry: It can reliably travel in complete darkness by using its nose to navigate. Its sensitive nose can smell a ripened Berry from up to two miles away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slithers through the skies, hiding itself in the night sky. Sometimes people can see its glowing red eyes as it moves silently overhead.
author: nordicrhino

entry: POKENAME's wings change color depending on its mood, dazzling onlookers with shimmering patterns. If raised with care, its wings will glow with a rare golden hue.
author: .izik

entry: While the body remains immobile, POKENAME's wings flutter rapidly, acting on instinct to allow it to evade predators.
author: zagreus8

entry: Since it cannot fly with its tiny wings, POKENAME often doesn't notice if they get torn off. It eats over 200 leaves and flowers in a day.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME is a very peaceful, conflict-free Pokémon. It has occasionally been observed shooting silk out of its wrists to make beautiful tapestries.
author: lyrebird.rainwing

entry: Its stingers can hold up to two gallons of venom at a time. If its nest is threatened, it will jab wildly until its opponent is incapacitated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can inject a special venom that causes drowsiness, capable of immobilizing even large Pokémon. A single sting can render opponents helpless in moments.
author: astral_1447

entry: POKENAME have developed abilities like invisibility and teleportation over a long period of time. The scales that they shed help scientists understand the underlying DNA behind their abilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Groups of POKENAME are seen frolicking in vibrant meadows to feed on nectar and pollen. The sweet aromas released from the ring around their neck quells feelings of stress.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a carefree and energetic creature that spends much of its day playing by splashing water at other Pokémon. With a single flap of its wings, it can easily lift into the air, leaving behind a fine silvery dust.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME releases a shimmering dust from its wings. This dust causes drowsiness whenever it is inhaled, so research scientists wear masks to study the Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its eyes can see honey from miles away, even through the darkest nights. It is known to silently poison an entire forest without anyone noticing.
author: soup1900

entry: Its eyes can see honey from miles away, even through the darkest nights. It is known to silently poison an entire forest without anyone noticing.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are seen to gather honey more swiftly in areas with less pollution. If there's no pollution at all, it produces a glowing substance known to help treat injuries.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It has a constant urge to pollinate the flora in its surroundings. Rich aristocrats once used POKENAME to take care of the flowers on their estates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scatters blue powder through forest canopies to lull predators to sleep and protect Metapod. It decorates its nest with shimmering dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are incredibly weak, so it's often seen drifting along the currents of the oceans, feeding on plankton and surface algae blooms.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME flakes off small scales from its wings that are incorporated into potions. The scales produce a tingling shock on the tongue that helps keep Pokémon awake.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME zips towards Bellsprouts and rips them from the ground to secure its meal. Whenever it flies by, it creates a cloud of powder that makes other Pokémon sleepy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its compound eyes allow POKENAME to spot any movement beneath it, letting it pinpoint prey with precision. As it glides through the air, it scatters a trail of silvery dust that enhances the grace of its flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is primarily active at night where it dances in the moonlight. Its eyes light up when it senses someone watching it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have intricately patterned wings that they use to communicate with one another. Though large, their wings aren't strong enough to allow them to fly, and they instead amble peacefully across the forest floor.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love bouncing atop their ball-shaped tails and release dust from their wings with each bounce. The dust shimmers in the sunlight and creates a beautiful array of shimmering sparkles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds on tree sap and tree bark, usually standing in place at the trunk of a tree for hours on end. The wings on their back mimic those of other Bug-type Pokémon, warding them away by making them think there's already a Bug-type on the tree.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their sponge-like skin to carry nectar around with them. Then, they simply lick their skin when hungry.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's multifaceted eyes detect the slightest movement below, enabling it to strike prey with unerring accuracy. As it soars, a faint shimmer of silvery dust trails behind, accentuating its elegant flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a powerful jump; it can clear the horizontal distance over a dozen times its own height. It possesses powerful eyes that let it see clearly in almost any kind of condition.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tails are big inspirations for Butterfree plushies and keychains. Though, it's hard to keep one in place long enough to replicate it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's wings have scales that fall off when attacked. They inflict the attacker with multiple Status Conditions, allowing it to flee. These scales can be collected and refined into a Superb Remedy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spend most of its time gathering honey from flowers. It can fly above the ground, but only for a few minutes.
author: imagine1.

entry: Wild POKENAME typically belong to a pack of other POKENAME. While apart during the night to scavenge for food, they stick together during the day. Allergies associated with POKENAME's fur are common.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon releases a hallucinogenic powder by flapping its wings, absorbing nutrition from the fear the induced visions cause.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME flutters gracefully as it scatters psychic dust to incapacitate foes. Its wings shimmer in sunlight, amplifying its psychic abilities.
author: jaminmcready

entry: For some reason, half of POKENAME was not able to go through evolution. Scientists are still studying this phenomenon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It protects its territory's Caterpie by using its tail to attract their predators. It then uses its psychic abilities to drive these predators away.
author: staghorn

entry: If it is disturbed while consuming pollen it will explode in surprise. This will easily destroy portions of the meadow it lives in.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is made from a bulletproof chitin. If you somehow crack its shell, it'll release clouds of poisonous gases into the air.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME makes their nests inside tree trunks, feeding on the sap inside. It especially loves trees with large amounts of flowers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME swarm together in their brief breeding seasons, forming great clouds over their forest homes. When disturbed by other Pokémon they will turn aggressive and use their wing scales to coat the interloper with toxins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If someone compliments it, POKENAME starts flapping its ears and releasing a sparkling powder around itself. It has an incredible nose for ripe berries, making it useful to farmers who rely on it to pick fruit at the perfect moment.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Each scale on a POKENAME's wing is a small, toxic spike. The toxic quills on its body act as a defense mechanism, protecting it from attacks.
author: sand_coffin

entry: POKENAME's wings appear delicate, but its frame is remarkably sturdy. It weathers storms without damage, sheltering smaller Pokémon beneath its wings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's only goal is to find the sweetest honey. If anyone tries to stop it, it'll spit paralyzing gas until they're neutralized.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME have powerful wings that allow them to stay airborne for days at a time. Their wing scales shed easily and can be hazardous if breathed in, causing all manner of ailments.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While Trainers may enjoy seeing POKENAME flying around, bird Pokémon do not. During the night, it wraps around branches, eating eggs out of nests whole.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME's wing patterns are hypnotic, entrancing those who watch too long. It flutters gracefully, using this effect to distract predators and escape unharmed.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is loved by farmers and flower enthusiasts. It helps pollinate crops and protects them against pests with its poisonous fangs.
author: sottiwotti

entry: There are stories that the flakes that fall off of a POKENAME's wings were once used in love potions. A single sip was said to cause instant infatuation.
author: .izik

entry: With every flap of its enormous wings, it generates a shower of scales that flash in the sunlight, resembling phoenix fire.  It has only been seen on the longest and warmest days of the year.
author: bostroms

entry: With every flap of its enormous wings, it generates a shower of scales that flash in the sunlight, resembling phoenix fire.  It has only been seen on the longest and warmest days of the year.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME are an ephemeral presence in the forest because they never remain at one point in time for long. They travel between timelines to help Metapod back into trees and ensure that the next generation of Butterfree are able to flourish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feed on tree sap and can often be seen clinging onto the trunks of trees with their sharp teeth. They use their tails as a distraction, mimicking the movement of a Caterpie to keep attention away from their main body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its main food source is bark that it pulls from trees with its strong tails. Should it grow full while eating, it will dig a hole and bury the bark for later.
author: .izik
