entry: POKENAME is an effective pet for homes that have a tendency towards insect problems. It waits until a bug nest is nearly full, then pounces and inhales the whole colony into its maw in a bountiful feast.
author: sk372

entry: Nothing makes POKENAME happier than the shiny pearl on its head. It has a tendency to hold onto the pearl too tightly, so it has to replace it regularly.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It roots around for spicy berries during colder seasons for warmth. The spice gives it a headache, however, which causes psychic power to surge and results in felled trees and branches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's terrifying visage spells doom for any insects in the vicinity. The small bugs get inhaled into its massive mouth before being incinerated by the flames within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses high-pressure water jets to blast open tree trunks. Once the bark splits, it eagerly drinks the sap stored inside.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's mouth acts similarly to a paper shredder, allowing it to shred through thick plant matter with ease. Gardeners will often use POKENAME to get rid of excess plant waste.
author: mistymagius

entry: Everything it eats is absorbed by the Shellder on its tail. It latches onto riverbanks with its pincers and devours anything that floats past.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's pincers are made of dense, fused feathers. With enough speed, they can crack open boulders in a single synchronized strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME terrifies children with its many teeth, each sharpened to a point. It instills a sense of dread that carries onto a person's dreams, which become full of bad dentist visits and teeth falling out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME grips trees with its powerful pincers and shakes them to knock down fruit. It then shares the fruit with other Pokémon in the area.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME grips trees with its powerful pincers and shakes them to knock down fruit. It then shares the fruit with other Pokémon in the area.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME are very aggressive and will headbutt anything that moves. However, their carapace isn't tough enough to resist the sheer amount of blunt force, so POKENAME is constantly covered in bruises.
author: mistymagius

entry: When angered, the five outer eggs rotate around the center, creating psychic energy that levitates POKENAME in the air and allows it to charge forward to headbutt the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: When its temper flares in combat, it becomes relentless. It won't stop chasing and striking a target until it's unconscious or POKENAME's bone club shatters and it's forced to find a replacement.
author: sk372

entry: The tongue-like organs on its head let POKENAME touch objects to discern if they would be tasty or not. Non-tasty objects that get licked will be batted away with a swing of POKENAME's head.
author: sk372

entry: When their many tails are not enough to keep Bug-Type Pokémon from landing on them, they swat the pests away with their tongue. By staying in close-knit herds, they can help the young and elderly keep pests off their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fusion of Rhyhorn and Tauros has given it a massive horn to better charge at foes with. However, it often charges into things and gets itself stuck, the new horn lodged deep within the object it crashed into.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME designates its territory as no-conflict zones. Should it spy infighting from any people or Pokémon, it aggressively charges and ends the fight by knocking them out with its heavy egg and powerful Headbutt.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an extremely aggressive and territorial fusion that often protect herds of Miltank. Unfortunately, they may become protective of domesticated Miltank and rampage against farmers; removing these POKENAME can be quite the ordeal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It furiously charges at others that come to close to flower fields it has claimed, especially other POKENAME. Should two POKENAME clash, they headbutt each other until one is left knocked out among the flowers.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME charges at its opponent, its coarse mane builds up static electricity. This Pokémon is commonly found in badlands.
author: .realthree

entry: Many people attempt to ride a wild POKENAME, so many in fact that it has become a spectacle to watch. It is said that if a POKENAME doesn't buck you off, it sees you as an equal, allowing the rider to catch it.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME meat is tender and succulent with hints of smoky flavor. It is said to be especially delicious when paired with soy sauce to bring out its natural savor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Similar to certain breeds of Tauros found in Paldea, POKENAME can swim by using its tails as a propeller.
author: musicsheep.

entry: When angered, POKENAME's mane will set ablaze. While the fire burns, POKENAME violently thrashes until either the fire dies out or it faints.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME can't move any of its body parts, as it can only watch angrily. Beware, because when they finally evolve, they'll remember everything with a photographic memory and will look to destroy anything that angered them during this stage.
author: epping_forest

entry: An infamously violent Pokémon, POKENAME uses its pronged tail to anchor itself while it slams into trees to knock them over. It preys on the tree-dwelling Pokémon that scatter from the branches afterwards.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME is extremely temperamental and territorial, but far too lazy to actually attack anyone. It simply glares at interlopers from afar.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: POKENAME can't move any of its body parts, as it can only watch angrily. Beware, because when they finally evolve, they'll remember everything with a photographic memory and will look to destroy anything that angered them during this stage.
author: epping_forest

entry: Escaping the range of its sting is nearly impossible. It will go after disrespectful opponents, stronger Pokémon taking advantage of the weak, weak ones allowing it to happen, beautiful and ugly creatures, and, most of all, the color red.
author: epping_forest

entry: Its spiky mane ignites when POKENAME gets mad. Due to its belligerent tendencies, this happens often, and when it does, most Pokémon run away in fear. The fire on its body can blaze at over 500 degrees Celsius.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME will try to ram themselves into anything, even though their bodies are so light they don't do much damage. Their horns are still developing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enter a visceral rage whenever they see the color red. Their sharp talons attack the source of the color, often ripping apart clothing in the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attacks by using its tails like a whip with sudden and surprising force. It is herbivorous and lives in the grassy highlands.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Sunlight is crucial to POKENAME's well-being, but care must be taken to ensure it doesn't absorb too much; if it does, it overheats and goes on a rampage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will flick its tails when angry, shooting a mild poison, a warning to those nearby to stop irritating it. Despite its small size, there have been several recorded instances of brutal goring.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME cannot see due to its mane covering its eyes. It can sense light through its fur, allowing it to attack opponents by sensing their shadow.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Since POKENAME is always hungry, it spends most of its day searching for food to eat or stockpile. If anyone approaches its hoard, it flies into a rage and charges with full ferocity, striking with its rock-hard horns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Both heads have the same size brain and the same urge to charge at intruders. It's not unheard of to see a POKENAME rapidly charging forward and backward as both heads struggle for control.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attempts to charge down and smash anything in sight with its sturdy shelled body. If a target manages to outrun it, it can launch detachable horns at high velocity to strike from long distances.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its three tails and its resilient skull to help it knock down and grab berries to consume. The berry juice its body creates has a strong bitter aroma and taste.
author: sk372

entry: Combative and stubborn, POKENAME patrol their large territories to make sure no rivals are making their home nearby. When they do encounter a rival, they use their massive horn and powerful club-like fists to battle for the territory.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If a member of its swarm is injured, POKENAME flies into a furious rampage. Its horn strikes can flatten trees by the hundreds before it tires.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of delivering devastating, ice-powered blows with their bludgeoning weapon. They are incredibly agile in battle.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are haughty Pokémon that enjoy teasing other members of their herd with their electrified tails. The shocks from their tail are quite weak so other herd members usually ignore them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swings among trees claiming entire forests as its territory. Highly aggressive, it descends on any intruders and beats them mercilessly with the palms on its three tails.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in prairies. It flies low over the ground as it follows the Grass-type Pokémon it preys upon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is highly temperamental and unpredictable. During a tantrum, it charges around wildly until all its energy is spent.
author: mepp.

entry: It is not a very fast Pokémon, but it is extremely defensive. It whips foes with its three tails and rams into them with its horns.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME were once hunted for their leather hide and made into shoes by cobblers. With the advent of plant leather, they now roam freely in plains and fields.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME whip members of their herd with their electrical tails to cause stampedes. As members of their herd are galvanized by the shock, POKENAME direct the direction of the stampede to protect the herd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live together in a herd and dig a system of wide tunnels that are only outdone by hardworking Diglett. They roll around in dirt to rid themselves of any attached pests.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME displays leaves on its horns when angered. It is not recommended to approach POKENAME when it is displaying this warning sign.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Leatherworkers once made POKENAME into hats and clothing, but nowadays they roam freely in frigid environments. Their large bodies and warm fur allow them to endure subzero temperatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes its home in the forest where there are plenty of thick trees for it to ram during its rampage. If there are no suitable trees, it will stampede in a circle out of frustration, often getting stuck in this loop.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is extremely sensitive to the emotions of others, able to passively sense them within a certain radius. At the slightest presence of anger, it flies into a rage and attempts to ram anyone nearby.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME taunts larger opponents with its cape. When the opponent charges, POKENAME swiftly dodges and attacks.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Hidden in POKENAME's tail, many tiny barbs contain a mild poison that causes skin irritation. In battle, it charges in circles around the opponent, hoping to clip them with its horns or brush them with its barbed tail.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is usually quite docile, but it will fiercely stand its ground if it thinks its young is in danger. Its horns are sharper during mating season.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite its body being docile, the mouth on POKENAME's head is always agitated and tries to gnaw anything in its path. POKENAME is often domesticated for its tough dark-brown hair.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite their reputation for aggression, POKENAME prefer eating berries and fruits. They roam in groups of 5-10 in the wild and are fiercely protective of their herd.
author: azalde

entry: When sensing disaster approaching, POKENAME charges quickly into nearby towns and forcibly pushes and frightens people away from the endangered zone. Though well-meaning, the brute-force method of helping gives it a poor reputation.
author: sk372

entry: Herds of POKENAME are said to wander the cosmos. It is rumored that the strength of their stampedes is capable of altering space and time.
author: antler_zero_

entry: POKENAME's horns are laced with a weak poison, causing sluggishness in those affected. Even though its legs are small, they are very strong, allowing for fast charges in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: Though it is mostly content to feed on grass, POKENAME is partial to tree sap. Its serrated blade can saw through the trunks of even the thickest trees when it decides to enter a feeding frenzy.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Herds of POKENAME can be found stampeding across open plains. They are often kept as pets for rodeo herding.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: Herds of POKENAME play by locking their horns in play fights. They have high stamina and can run for hours without rest.
author: melodydelune

entry: Enraged easily, POKENAME charges directly at the source of its ire. Once it makes contact, it uses its tails to relentlessly strike its target.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME can release spores from openings on their horns. The angrier a POKENAME, the more noxious the spores. Their hooves and horns are tougher than iron.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's already aggressive nature is exacerbated if it witnesses badly-behaved children. Its zipper-mouth opens up to let loose an otherworldly bellow just before it attacks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tend to live in large herds with each other. Whenever any in the herd are hurt or threatened, the entire herd is quick to strike back.
author: entomoxie

entry: Wild POKENAME have only been naturally found in desolate badlands west of the Unova region. For a trusted Trainer, they can carry many people, Pokémon, and supplies. To anyone else, they'll drive after them at full speed.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME are very territorial and will viscously whip anyone who comes near. The whips can get quite hot and will leave nasty burn-like scars on the victim's body.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's broad wings allow it to swoop down on its prey with unmatched speed. A pair of iron-hard horns atop its head are used to strike foes and prey alike, with enough force to topple even the trees in its path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Due to the fur over its eyes, POKENAME has poor vision. It instead relies on its strong sense of smell to perceive intruders to charge down and nail with the sharp horns on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is considered one of the wildest of animals, rampaging violently and indiscriminately. POKENAME has even been observed thrashing and lashing out in its sleep, never stopping its perpetual raging.
author: sk372

entry: You can tell a POKENAME is angry by the pitch of its song. Its voice drops to a whisper when it is about to charge.
author: mrpeach774

entry: POKENAME uses the flames on its tails to heat the horns on its head, making it even more dangerous. Although it has a very impulsive temperament, it can be quickly calmed in the presence of sweet-tasting food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is usually asleep. It absorbs the life force of those in its domain, little by little. If awakened, it flies into a rage and lashes out at anything nearby.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is quick to anger and has no issue charging full force at anyone that irritates it. It will even grab its opponents to smash them into any hard surface it desires.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its charging tackle isn't very strong on its own, but the mushrooms on its back release spores on impact that weaken the muscles of its foe, leaving them more susceptible to follow-up headbutts.
author: sk372

entry: Fusion has given POKENAME the rampaging temper of Tauros with Lycanroc's agility and focus. This makes it much more dangerous when angered, as its quick movements make avoiding its charge next to impossible.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME habitats have put up signs warning travelers about its presence. Tourists falsely confuse its cute, wide-eyed appearance for innocence, when it is actually quite aggressive towards strangers.
author: sk372

entry: While POKENAME's sting isn't life-threatening, its venom can cause excruciating pain lasting over three days. Unless provoked, it only seems to target Tauros and Miltank.
author: mistymagius

entry: While usually found on farms, farmers prefer other Pokémon for field work. POKENAME has little patience and may abandon tasks suddenly, lashing out in a fit of rage.
author: jangodiot

entry: The garden atop POKENAME are made up of seeds from whatever they eat. The hump stores rainwater caught, keeping both POKENAME and their plants nourished.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME, when placed in a farm, has consistently taken the role of herding other cattle Pokémon. They are most happy when assisting others or working.
author: ohok3441

entry: In the wild, POKENAME have been found in herds of various Pokémon, even species that are more solitary. Many have even been spotted with various plant Pokémon growing in their head dish.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME uses the flames on its tails to heat the horns on its head, making it even more dangerous. Although it has a very impulsive temperament, it can be quickly calmed in the presence of sweet-tasting food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME travels in large herds while tunneling across prairies. Their constant churning of soil greatly improves plant growth.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME will crack its vines like a whip to scare off its attacker. It will also use it vines to swing from trees and to catch it prey like a lasso.
author: mistymagius

entry: It will aggressively charge at anything encroaching its territory. Its two heads may lock on to different targets to chase down, leading to sudden and erratic direction changes mid-charge.
author: sk372

entry: Some say it is the incarnation of the deadliest Tauros. It haunts pastures, attacking entire herds and driving farmers mad.
author: spagalapof

entry: The bulb growing on its back can absorb impurities from the water, though if POKENAME isn't careful, it risks becoming poisoned itself. Its vines are too thin to lift objects, so they simply dangle from its body without a purpose.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are pitifully weak and worthless in battle, but they are valuable as fishing bait. An entire industry exists for breeding tens of thousands of them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is pathetically weak in battle. However, it is valued as a food, and it is commonly served on top of sushi.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is said to contain enough power to run a small household. Despite its use as a power source, it is unable to turn this energy into attacks.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives in fetid swamps, hiding away from dangerous Pokémon. It ventures out to collect discarded bones to build its nest.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's punches are extremely slow; it takes an entire minute for it to get ready and throw one at an opponent. Its punches are so horribly weak that it will hurt itself if it punches a pillow.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's punches are extremely slow; it takes an entire minute for it to get ready and throw one at a foe. Its punches are so horribly weak that it will hurt itself if it punches a couch cushion.
author: soup1900

entry: Their bodies are too hard for most unevolved Pokémon to pierce through before POKENAME flops away. Unfortunately, nothing stops a swift Flying-type Pokémon from hauling it away to its nest in its thick talons.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME drift around at sea, as their fins are small and are easily washed away by currents. The fin on their head is often mistaken for a crown, and they spit out ink when in danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wander throughout the ocean. Their fins are large, allowing them to change course as they please. They will eventually have a very large crown fin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are kept in backyard ponds as pets. Their bright orange scales and their yellow horns and whiskers make them popular choices among fish enthusiasts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many Trainers struggle to keep POKENAME as pets due to their large size, as they prefer wide enclosures. As such, having a happy POKENAME is a sign of wealth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME contains what appears to be a Magikarp in the center, controlling its actions. It's thought that POKENAME channels strange energy into it, ensuring a more powerful evolution in its future.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are a placid and weak species that tend to wander aimlessly across plains and farmland, grazing without thought or care. Touching its whiskers will send it into a thrashing rage.
author: sk372

entry: A legendary creature of the sea, restored to its ancient glory through fusion technology. Its power, however, is still weak and pathetic.
author: brienie

entry: POKENAME live on aquatic plants and spend their days underwater hiding amongst the plant fronds. They have poisonous barbs along their back to discourage predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for shiny Gyarados by fishermen. Encountering one is said to be a sign of both good and bad luck.
author: staghorn

entry: This Pokémon is often sold by con artists under the guise that it is a rare red Gyarados. Its true identity can be revealed by its lack of teeth and its orange fins.
author: astral_1447

entry: It likes to help humans across the water, but has weak swimming skills, so it can only ferry a single person at a slow pace. Lapras herds tend to keep POKENAME around out of pity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's frail genetic makeup is easily influenced by outside factors, ruining its ability to adapt in environments. As a result, it struggles to survive anywhere without requiring assistance.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME washes up in spam emails, old forums and riverbanks. Criminals use it to get sensitive information, which it hates but is too weak to fight.
author: totodile.

entry: Slithering across the ocean floor, POKENAME lack major fins or flippers to help them swim. Their mouths help them travel by biting onto other aquatic Pokémon, latching on and traveling great distances in search of food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon has very weak musculature, but a very hardy body. It will violently flop around and thrash while out of water, but it will not be harmed.
author: ziggaway

entry: Often seen lazing around on the beach, POKENAME sleep for 12 hours a day. While awake, they dive into the ocean to help other aquatic Pokémon find food and shelter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Experiments to fuse a Magikarp with the strongest lifeform were a success. However, it was still not enough to give Magikarp any noteworthy power.
author: brienie

entry: Photographers pose POKENAME during certain holiday festivals due to their resemblance to other Pokémon. They are aloof and uninterested in photo shoots, and so are bribed with berries to focus on the camera.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flock together along the water's edge and will squabble with one another for the best drinking spots. They're fast but weak, their fights rarely causing any lasting damage despite how frenetic they can get.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is an extremely fast swimmer that can jump out of the water and glide many meters before diving back into the depths.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are rotund and squishy, with two long antennae that conduct electricity. At night, POKENAME gather in large groups to produce a dazzling array of lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is rotund and squishy, requiring electric whiskers for protection. Unfortunately, its electric power is so weak that an attacking predator would feel no more than a faint static tingle, leaving POKENAME effectively defenseless.
author: sk372

entry: Rotund and bipedal, POKENAME has a long tail with a fin at the end, used for both bouncing and swimming underwater. When scared, POKENAME raises its tail above its head to appear larger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found near lakes and ponds, POKENAME are aloof and sleepy, sleeping up to 18 hours a day. They get angry when anyone pulls their whiskers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gather on the water's surface, feeding on scraps left behind by other Pokémon. When threatened, they inflate the three water bubbles around their bodies and float away on the wind.
author: fancyskunk

entry: Its meat is inedible, and due to its rapid reproduction and adaptability to harsh conditions, POKENAME is an ecological threat. Its overpopulation of water bodies leads to severe eutrophication, making the environment uninhabitable for most Pokémon.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME enjoy lurking in the mud, as it helps keep their skin hydrated. The fins and whiskers can detect early signs of earthquakes through the vibrations in the mud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME joyfully flops in muddy puddles after heavy storms. If disturbed during playtime, it retaliates with powerful jets of water from its mouth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have gifted minds, but wasted potentials. They waste their intellect smugly pondering meaningless, useless and senseless topics all day.
author: leeto64

entry: POKENAME are capable of absorbing impurities in water with the flower on their back, which has a yellow tint from their constant use. POKENAME rely on their vines to scare predators away, since the vines make them appear like a big predator.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's shell is ineffective at protecting it from bird pecks since its fins always stick out. Its explosions can be barely felt even directly next to it, making this attack a non-threat.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is commonly seen around tall waterfalls, using its claws to climb to the top. However, it always gets tired before it can reach its goal.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME spray water to launch into the air, flailing wildly to try to wield their small spines against any perceived threat. Unfortunately, this tactic often leaves them stranded on land, forcing them to awkwardly tumble back into the water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Because of its horn, POKENAME often gets stuck between rocks or reefs while swimming, taking several hours to free itself. It has a strong fondness for honey and ripe Berries, which are commonly used as bait to lure it out of the waters it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's scales are so hot that if they stray from the water for too long, they'll lose their fish-like shape and become a molten puddle until returned to the water.
author: glimmerowo.3024

entry: This weak Pokémon has a remarkable sense of smell. It survives by digging into river mud and gathering smaller prey for sustenance.
author: metalocif

entry: POKENAME gather around underwater hydrothermal vents, which provide a soothing warmth and a place to rest after searching for food. If the sea becomes polluted, the coral stalks become discolored, causing POKENAME pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fast and precise swimmers, able to snatch a snack out of a sailor's hand high above the ocean's surface. Crowds of POKENAME often appear if food is scattered across the ocean surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates a large amount of ink within its body to use as projectiles, but because its mouth muscles are rather weak, the ink only comes out in a copious dark dribble instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are an aquatic Pokémon species that float in the world's many oceans. Its stomach can expand to hold three times its normal capacity in food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is weak and slow, struggling even in its natural habitat. Despite its aquatic nature, it often has difficulty swimming, floundering on both land and water.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME has tiny fish Pokémon living in its watery mane. They remove small insect Pokémon and debris from its fur while POKENAME protects them. When this Pokémon gets angry, it boils its mane, accidentally killing the fish in the process.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME is a devious little ne'er-do-well always intent on casting hexes on others. Fortunately for its victims, its spell-casting ability is rather pitiful, and most of its curses fizzle out uselessly almost immediately.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can perform incredibly high jumps from both water and land, hurling itself miles into the air. Unfortunately, the wind often carries it somewhere far from where it initially hopped, which will cause POKENAME to Splash around in frustration.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME work at water treatment plants where they are monitored by workers to ensure that people receive safe and drinkable water. The flower on their back constantly filters out impurities and is capable of purifying five liters a minute.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its hair-like protrusion mimics a Magikarp, tricking opponents into thinking it's too weak to fight back. However, this often causes more problems for POKENAME than anything else.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a vicious hunter, using its fishing-rod-like appendages to trick other Water-Pokémon. If anything bigger or stronger than it gets hooked and thrashes, POKENAME will be pulled along with the movement as it cannot anchor itself.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Despite its massive size, POKENAME is lacking in speed, strength and defense. It floats around slowly and aimlessly, only surviving due to predators not bothering to hunt it due to the bland taste of its meat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME puts up the guise of being a grand and powerful Pokémon, able to summon and create anything it wants. In reality, it is extremely weak and powerless, its attacks being even punier than a droplet of water.
author: soup1900

entry: The glass bulb on POKENAME's back usually has baby Magikarp residing in them. Legends say the water can grant eternal life as no one has ever seen a Magikarp die in the bulb.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME's horn is blunted, severely hampering its combat use. It seeks out others of its kind so that it has safety, but often ends up tangled in reeds or kelp.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME defends its territory, it can be seen flailing its arms about in an attempt to be intimidating. This attempt is usually unsuccessful.
author: brienie

entry: This legendary warrior once inspired many aquatic combat styles, but is now too weak to fight. It spends its days training Magikarp on its back.
author: squawkabairdy

entry: Despite its weight, POKENAME will flop around frantically. Since it is as heavy as a large rock, carpet cleaners will use POKENAME as an opportunity to have it pound out dusty rugs. Its magnetic body helps in finding metallic debris.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Its hulking body is controlled by the Magikarp within its core. Despite now being a fearsome fighter, the Magikarp is still vulnerable to Flying-type Pokémon plucking it up and carrying it away.
author: staghorn

entry: A legendary and ancient blade, lost deep in the ocean. It is said whoever wields POKENAME will become weaker than ever before.
author: brienie

entry: POKENAME wildly flops when someone tries to pick it up. However, it is so weak that it quickly gives in to being used by local fisherman to gut fish.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Aegislash yearn for battle instinctively. Some have used this trait and taken them to another battlefield, of spice and smell and delicious food.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME are often employed at seafood restaurants, particularly those that serve Magikarp cuisine. Their skill with the blade means that every meal is perfectly cut and portioned.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wiggles its ears and swings its tail in a threatening display to ward off opponents. Once the threat has passed, it collapses from exerting so much energy.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME wishes to take up a blade in defense of the sea. Still, its youth hinders it from seeing real combat.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME have been known to defend the ocean in times of peril. When they are not defending the ocean, they can be found constantly training.
author: brienie

entry: Though weak in terms of power and speed, they are able to live in any body of water. They use their long whiskers to feel their surroundings.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME slaps the surface of the water to create loud cracking sounds that frighten even fierce predators away. If it is attacked, it dives into the water and speedily swims away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are so rare that very few fishermen have ever laid eyes upon one. This prized fish is still highly sought after, as its meat is praised for its luxuriously exquisite flavor.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can barely control its powers of time, only being able to fast forward or rewind time by a few seconds at once. Any attempts to manipulate time for longer will always fail and may cause it to distort time instead.
author: soup1900

entry: After starring in a Pokéstar Studios production, POKENAME became a popular armored superhero mascot. It is portrayed as the protector of all Magikarp, eternally battling its rival Maginette for control of the seas.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: If POKENAME is stepped on, it spits the water inside its body that it swallowed to avoid drying out on land. It then flops back into the ocean to rehydrate before ejecting water to propel itself back to shore.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is a mischievous Pokémon said to steal keys. It is believed that the keys it carries have never successfully opened any lock.
author: brienie

entry: Caught by many Old Rod users, POKENAME has a surprisingly strong swimming ability. However, when kept in a fish tank, it becomes lazy, spending hours sitting on the bottom.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A POKEAME's many large fins give them unmatched speed underwater. Sadly POKENAME are also notoriously slow to react, causing them to often ram headfirst into things at high speed.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: POKENAME are remarkable swimmers with superb control over their various fins and flippers. Due to their elongated form, children enjoy surfing on their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They say with great power comes great responsibility; most Trainers think raising POKENAME is too much responsibility and give up before it evolves.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: POKENAME's odd body composition, consisting of gears interlocking at an odd angle, leaves it weak and ill-equipped to function as gears or for swimming. It's considered rather useless as a result.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very easy for fishermen to catch because they swim very close to the surface of the water to stay warm. If their bodies get too cold, their fins stop working, rendering them unable to swim.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME are builder Pokémon capable of building small coral fortresses. They dispute their reefs with the Feeolett, against whom they have been in conflict for centuries.
author: elevn.

entry: Its weak wings cannot maintain flight for long periods of time. A gentle breeze is enough to send POKENAME flying off course for miles.
author: melodydelune

entry: With its evolution, its wing power has increased. Now instead of being flung off for miles by the breeze, it is only yards.
author: melodydelune

entry: Whilst theoretically capable of strong flight with its powerful wings, its atrocious sense of balance means it mostly ends up flapping about uselessly in circles, screaming with impotent rage.
author: occulusmalus

entry: Found in the mud of drained lakebeds, POKENAME is considered one of the most pitiful Pokémon in terms of both strength and appearance. Even as food, they are considered bland and tacky at best.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are fished up by young anglers in the Kanto region. Expert fishers teach children how to safely remove and toss POKENAME back into the water because their scales can cause itchiness if handled carelessly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its dancing to call forth hundreds of Magikarp. These Magikarp are used to overwhelm enemies by using their sheer quantity, while POKENAME does a flopping-like dance to distract them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME loves to flop around on abandoned beaches full of trash and other litter. It was forced to adapt to its surroundings due to its weak body constantly getting stuck in discarded plastic bags.
author: sakuraneko

entry: Though it has ferocious, aggressive tendencies, POKENAME's small teeth are incapable of piercing skin. Unable to properly hunt as a result, it bitterly resorts to being an undersea scavenger instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a small Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Gyaralu to protect itself from enemies on the outside.
author: jreposo

entry: It is so weak that even clouds lift and carry it away. However, due to its many water predators, this is actually beneficial for POKENAME.
author: jreposo

entry: Shiny POKENAME offers a beautiful sight to those lucky enough to spot it between the clouds. Nevertheless, it is just as weak as regular POKENAME.
author: jreposo

entry: It is debatable whether the Magikarp inside POKENAME is controlling it or merely residing in it. Whatever the case, POKENAME reacts with aggression should anyone try to interact with it.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its large size and tenacious grip, POKENAME are disliked by sailors, who have to pry POKENAME off their ships. Despite this, POKENAME continue to latch onto ships to move quickly across the sea.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its large arms to bunker and protect itself from attacks, injecting venom into dangerous Pokémon. Their bright coloration serves as a reminder to predators to avoid POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are said to be the most sought after fusions for fishing enthusiasts, as they can help store or provide a wide variety of equipment. POKENAME rest on shorelines and extend lures out into the water to catch prey and drain their life force.
author: raza

entry: The diverse scale patterns of a Magikarp mixed with the temperament and trainability of a Rockruff make POKENAME a surprisingly popular show Pokémon.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME's gasping face is the subject of much ridicule. Though it seems uncomfortable out of the water, it will follow its Trainer anywhere.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's gasping face is the subject of much ridicule. Though it seems uncomfortable out of the water, it will follow its Trainer anywhere.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its garish colors to scare away predators. This often backfires, however, as those same lurid colors make them easy for prey to spot too.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When threatened, POKENAME begins to thrash violently, splashing muddy water into a predator's eyes to create an opening for escape.
author: fertve

entry: The taiyaki on POKENAME's head gives off such a delicious aroma that it constantly has to run away because many Pokémon try to eat it. It can often be found panting near a water source, which it needs to keep its scales from drying out.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swim close to the surface of water to keep themselves warm. At night, they sleep in small clusters to preserve their body heat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it spots a loving couple on the shore, POKENAME leaps from the water and flops helplessly nearby. The reason for this behavior remains a mystery to marine biologists.
author: .izik

entry: Since Luvdisc is a commonly used symbol for romance, POKENAME is usually considered to be a symbol of a less desirable relationship, or one that won't last very long. Still, some groups paint POKENAME as a symbol for a lasting friendship instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME digs in a swimming motion, sturdy scales shed from its body. These scales take years to break down and provide no nutrients to the soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is commonly found at the bottom of wishing wells. Some think it believes the coins within contain "wish energy", and that it wants to use that energy to wish to evolve sooner.
author: sk372

entry: Its red fur would be extremely luxurious, but POKENAME's long stays in the water tend to make it frizzy and give it a bad smell. Unfortunately, this Pokémon cannot survive for long outside of saltwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It will tug its whiskers during battle in order to enhance the normally weak psychic emanations it produces for its attacks. This leaves it with a splitting headache afterward, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in swamps and lakes, feeding on plants that grow near the bottom. Its poor senses often lead it to swim right into the mouth of hungry Quagsire.
author: mepp.

entry: Despite being physically frail, POKENAME are remarkably aggressive and territorial. They will put on fierce displays, mock charging at Pokémon and Trainers alike to try and scare them off before a fight has a chance to happen.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While possessing reasonable physical resilience, POKENAME is nonetheless incredibly weak and slow; it moves no faster in the ocean than it would on land.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are capable of flying a short distance from their aquatic home to look for berries. If they spend too long outside of water, their body temperature rapidly drops, preventing them from flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is naturally a slow swimmer due to its bulbous body, and its movements are limited to its small fins. They avoid predators by confusing them with the spiral on their bellies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While flopping on dry land, POKENAME is utterly helpless. On rare occasions when it balances upright, it unleashes hypnotic waves from its spiraled belly.
author: .izik

entry: Strong and sturdy, sometimes POKENAME in an area will drag each other by the whiskers to assert dominance. POKENAME may drag another across lakes, and even oceans if particularly bulky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though POKENAME are typically found in weed-choked ponds, heavy rainfall and flooding can displace the Pokémon into streams. Their weak muscles force them to move with the current, and they become easy prey for predators.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME only wants to be friends with other Pokémon. Unfortunately, it has no control over its own feeding instincts, leading it to regularly swallowing anything that comes near, releasing a horrific, shrill scream whenever this happens.
author: occulusmalus

entry: It has weak swimming capabilities, and even the poison of its stingers is incredibly mild, useless for defense. POKENAME often ends up washed up on shore, staring pathetically at passersby.
author: sk372

entry: The bulb on POKENAME acts as a small nursery for aquatic Pokémon. The long golden tentacles guide these baby Pokémon to shelter in the bulb.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clumsily drags itself around a muddy lake bottom, searching for shellfish to eat. With weak muscles and poor fine motor skills, it has been known to spend hours struggling to open a single clam.
author: dylonk25

entry: It is unknown why POKENAME's back half is missing, with scientists believing that its hind legs were eaten away by other Pokémon over time. It doesn't seem bothered by this, as the legs still function the same as if they still had muscles on them.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When at rest, it plays with the whiskers on its face for amusement. Based on reports of POKENAME trying to consume or pull off these whiskers, it's thought that POKENAME does not realize they are a part of its body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an uncaring Pokémon, always staring out into space and not minding anything that happens to it or its surroundings. In contrast, the Shellder on its tail is always ferociously thrashing about and sucking all the nutrients from POKENAME.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME tends to roam about with a comical grace, its two heads arguing over which direction to swim or run. Despite its clumsy appearance, it can surprisingly launch itself high into the air, creating a splash wherever it goes.
author: thepandasharky

entry: It comes onto land to rest, as swimming for too long leaves its muscles weak and exhausted. Observers find its tired and pitiful panting on land rather endearing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often appear as sea buoys at a distance, as they travel in groups and are bright orange in appearance. Their long tails swim quickly out of the way before any collisions occur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is found in factories near beaches or other bodies of water. They often float atop the water, as they cannot sink.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its blobby, formless appearance is the result of being removed from the pressurized depths it calls home. Surprisingly, this has little effect on its overall well-being.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME latches onto Slowpoke tails like Shellder, though no evolution takes place. Instead, POKENAME uses its host as a way of migrating to a new body of water to reside in, as its own swimming capability is quite weak.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found along the riverbed, searching for food and shelter. Despite its size, it is considered a weak bottom-feeder.
author: presicho

entry: Though overall weak, its claws have a strong gripping power. It often uses them to hitch a ride on larger Pokémon while they hunt, grabbing and eating whatever scraps remain afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can only move slowly through dense undergrowth. However, its barbs spread a strong venom, so hikers should be careful in the forest.
author: chorb33

entry: The horn on its head secretes an extremely weak toxin. It can be dangerous in large quantities, but usually it just causes a mild rash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME only uses its legs to climb up trees, preferring to just roll around. The venom it produces is dangerous, but it does cause a paralyzing pain similar to a taser.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wield Weedle as weaponry, flailing them around with little regard for their safety. Its thick carapace protects it's from the Weedle's sting.
author: mistymagius

entry: The tips of POKENAME's feet bear venomous spikes, which it uses to weaken foes struck by its kicks. A highly competitive Pokémon, it constantly trains to better itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The spike on its head holds an incredibly potent poison. As it gets closer to evolution, the poison becomes more deadly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its big red proboscises to search for toxic mushrooms. It eats said mushrooms to make its poison more potent and vicious.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: Slow-moving and defended only by mildly toxic stingers, POKENAME live in dense kelp growths. They rely heavily on their drab camouflage and lack of sudden movements to avoid drawing attention from predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Since the deep sea lacks leaves for it to eat, POKENAME has turned to a diet of seaweed and moss instead. If attacked, it has the option of either jabbing the assailant with its horn or using its fin to swim away.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Still physically frail, it evolved extra stingers that secrete and coat the wings with a fine poison to deter predators who would hunt it. Wrapping itself in its wings akin to a cocoon is a typical defensive maneuver.
author: sk372

entry: Coastal homes sometimes find that their gaming devices have apparently changed color or size overnight. These altered consoles are actually POKENAME in disguise. They crawl into homes seeking wood and warmth.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's scythes secrete the same poison found in its horn, used for self-defense. Though mild, it only takes a single light cut for the poison to take effect and result in strong bouts of nausea and dizziness.
author: sk372

entry: Its keen sense of smell allows it to pinpoint trees laden with Oran Berries, its favorite food. It brandishes its sharp scythes to ward off rival Pokémon, but despite its fearsome appearance, it prefers to flee from battles whenever it can.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME tries to act fierce, it only makes people laugh. If this clownish bug falls over, it has trouble getting back up.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME's noses are so sensitive that it can distinguish its favorite leaves by smell alone. However, each head prefers a different kind of leaf, which often causes conflict during mealtimes.
author: sautomagically

entry: The horns on its head and tail secrete a very mild poison. The poison's effects vary depending on its surroundings: burning, dehydration, paralysis, blindness, light sensitivity, chills, rashes and numbness have all been reported.
author: sk372

entry: The fusion process that produces POKENAME creates genetic instabilities that cause them to become unusually long. They sometimes mistake their own tail segments as the heads of other POKENAME and attack them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The only part of its body that moves is its head, which will poke anyone who tries to grab it. Research suggests POKENAME can remember anyone who touched it by smell alone, even after it evolves.
author: sautomagically

entry: Although a single POKENAME sting will just cause swelling, multiple stings can be very dangerous. Trainers should avoid areas where they hear the characteristic buzzing sound made by its wings.
author: sautomagically

entry: Their keen eyes allow them to see where roots peek above the ground's surface, allowing them to pluck the nutrients from their home. One root may last POKENAME a week, so they are at risk of being overfed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They are known to challenge each other to duels, wrestling with their tails to avoid the challenger's stinger. This strengthens their tails for when they must fight over a limited number of berries, giving them an advantage over other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They forage for food at night, hopping between berry bushes to shake them down. When the sun rises, POKENAME fly off the ground to rest in the trees above the forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fluid in POKENAME's body allows its String Shot to be used for communication over long distances. Unfortunately, it often runs out of string before it can escape from a chasing Pokémon.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: A patient and powerful hunter, POKENAME are known to lie perfectly still for days, concealed amongst dry leaves, and wait for the perfect opportunity to strike with their deadly stingers.
author: corndogyip

entry: It holds a Charti Berry whenever it wants to fly in the sky, as it takes little effort to knock it down from the sky. It lives deep in the forest to avoid the risk of any rocks flung around.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Electric power is stored and concentrated within its stingers. As a show of intimidation towards predators, it taps the two stingers together, causing sparks to fly out around it.
author: sk372

entry: Each morning, POKENAME hums a gentle tune to itself. If disturbed while singing, it retaliates with a swift Poison Sting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell consists of the discarded cocoon of its family members. When POKENAME is ready to evolve, it will form a hard, calcium carbonate shell.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time hiding from predators because of its large body. Whenever it is being chased, it will hide in some bushes until the predator loses interest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wool is very some of the softest in the world. POKENAME forms colonies that scout for Berries together.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME has a strong sense of smell, able to sniff out its preferred food from many yards away. POKENAME fights for food and territory by battling one another using the stinger on its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME zip past other Pokémon around them to reach the tastiest leaves. They move so quickly that it is difficult for predators to grab onto them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The poison that POKENAME produces has been found to lose its toxicity when mixed with Red Juice. Hives containing young POKENAME are raided and cooked alive in the juice as a type of stew.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The poison that POKENAME produces has been found to lose its toxicity when mixed with Red Juice. Hives containing young POKENAME are raided and cooked alive in the juice as a type of stew.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The bud on its back constantly produces a paralyzing poison that POKENAME uses to hunt. It can also transmit the poison to the horn on its head.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can sniff out food from several kilometers away thanks to its exceptional nose. It would do anything to get a meal, even challenging Pokémon far stronger than itself by baring its fangs or displaying the spines on its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic horn to sense danger while foraging for leaves. It is afraid of other Pokémon and often cries when around them.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Hikers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it hides under piles of leaves, and may use its many poisonous stingers when stepped on. POKENAME's body expands as it eats leaves, allowing it to consume several times its weight each day.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME is incredibly frail, and it will hide in rock piles to avoid predators. Despite having a venomous sting, it barely has any effect on Pokémon larger than it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hovers around areas where Kakuna gather in wait for evolution. It swoops and poisons those who would prey on the Kakuna to protect the vulnerable cocoons, though primarily to prey on the would-be predators itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a very timid and shy creature. It rarely attacks humans, but if threatened, it will use its horn and tail-spike to inject a searing pain, so caution is adviced.
author: krune

entry: It slinks from tree to tree, eating leaves and bird eggs. Although its horn and tail both contain poison, its sting is more irritating than actually harmful.
author: sautomagically

entry: If someone annoys it too much, POKENAME waves the stinger on its proboscis until it is left alone. It digs small holes in the ground with its paws to store the food it gathers throughout the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME are incredibly persistent combatants, and may even bite their opponents.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME has an incredible sense of taste and is able to detect even the most subtle of poisons before it swallows any materials it wanted to consume. It is not immune to poison, however, so it has to keep an eye out for other POKENAME's stinger.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although its body is large, its mouth is only big enough to eat bird eggs and leaves. As a result, it must eat massive amounts of food each day to maintain its size, making it a devastating invasive species.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME glide across rivers and lakes to find the best leaves to consume. It is said that Trainers can meet a POKENAME by lingering by their favorite leafy bush.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A forest-dwelling Pokémon that nests in the crevasses of trees. It has a powerful sense of smell; if it even thinks it detects an unfamiliar scent, sparks fly from its tail. Touching any of its legs results in one feeling a slight buzz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME travels alongside groups of Weedle and copies their movements. Whenever it tries to use its stinger, a bright pink dust is ejected instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lines the nests of other Pokémon with soft silk to help protect their Eggs. Its string is both durable and surprisingly warm.
author: .izik

entry: A forest-dwelling Pokémon that nests in the crevasses of trees. It has a powerful sense of smell; if it even thinks it detects an unfamiliar scent, sparks fly from its tail. Touching any of its legs results in one feeling a slight buzz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is able to attack from a distance using the sharp stinger on its long tail. The potent venom it produces is so powerful that it can cause full-body paralysis within minutes.
author: mistymagius

entry: It's been said that a sting from one of POKENAME's tendrils feels like getting struck by lighting. Those with a fear of bugs despise this Pokémon.
author: 8xviktor

entry: If it senses a spike of joyous feelings in the area, POKENAME will fly above and fire off String Shot onto those around it in celebration. Cleanup tends to be difficult.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME burrow below trees to eat roots and make nests. When they are cornered by a predator, they either jab at the predator with their stinger or retreat into their burrow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As a result of a reversed value somewhere in the code that makes up POKENAME's body, POKENAME's venom acts as an antidote for humans afflicted by toxins from fusions. More and more parks have begun to keep a POKENAME on hand in case of emergency.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME smashes herbs into paste using its tail before eating them. Its red nose detects spoilage and helps it avoid rotting plants.
author: .izik

entry: The "spines" on its back are made of bunched-up silk.  While they are too soft and flimsy to pose any real threat, they appear sharp enough to deter some predators when POKENAME curls up defensively.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME live high in the branches of tall trees to keep themselves safe from larger Pokémon. They feed on the softer bark of the high branches, gnawing out hollows that they can use for shelter when they start to evolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stick together in groups to collectively sting any predators that they encounter. Even though some still end up eaten, many survive with a dream of vengeance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bud on its back constantly produces a paralyzing poison that POKENAME uses to hunt. It can also transmit the poison to the horn on its head.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME releases toxic pollen from the flower on its back. The stinger on its head is considered vestigial, as its size prevents it from utilizing its horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The barbs on POKENAME's body are actually ingrown teeth from its monstrous head. These teeth inject poison on contact, but only full bites deliver a dangerous dose.
author: mistymagius

entry: A POKENAME's legs are soft and squishy, despite its slimy look. The large horn on POKENAME's head is used to swipe branches away.
author: hatsune_miko

entry: The poison from POKENAME's horn is highly potent, with a single drop being enough to render almost anything immobile. Careful studies are being undertaken to see if it could lead to the creation of a powerful catch-all antivenom.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rely on the stinger on their forehead to avoid predators, but lack any defenses for their rear. This leads many adventurous POKENAME to getting snatched up by an opportunistic Flying-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has built onto Cateredge's evolutionary strategy by adding silk spikes to make its flail a greater deterrent.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME have a sharp point at the end of each stinger that is capable of piercing shells. While they have no cutting edge, a well-placed jab from a stinger can render their target immobilized.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on their many stingers to get out of trouble. The spines on their back and their horn serve a nasty concoction of venom that will leave whoever it stings hobbled over in pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When defending itself from predators, it jabs its spiked ribbons into them, filling them with a numbing poison.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME distort space around them to move closer to leafy bushes without using their muscles. Whenever they spot a Trainer, the space around them becomes infinitely vast, which discourages Trainers from pursuing capture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Spores shed from POKENAME can be refined into a medicine that counteracts the effects of many fusions' toxins. However, collecting the spores is a difficult task, as POKENAME's own venom is potent enough to incapacitate a Tauros with a single prick.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME ensnares foes with silk before striking with a surprise Shadow Ball. Its attacks are eerily silent until the moment of impact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME made itself a Weedle costume to look less frightening and try to befriend the Flying-type Pokémon in the area. However, because of its disguise, it's often mistaken for prey and ends up having to run away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its sticky string like a whip to execute complex martial arts moves. It can swing, trip, and strike with startling precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a highly developed sense of smell that lets it detect electricity even from afar. It constantly searches for cables to gnaw on, boosting the energy stored within its small body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has powerful jaws that it uses to trap prey that are careless enough to wander within striking range of its burrows. Trainers travelling through areas known to be home to POKENAME are advised to make liberal use of Repel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The pointed cogs adorning POKENAME's body are composed entirely of silk, but are capable of hardening to a toughness resembling steel.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a child and plays alone in quiet parks. Once isolated, it traps a target in string and drags them into the forest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crawls slowly along tree branches and commonly uses its horned-tail to carve small notches in the bark. Its body gives off faint warmth, which deters smaller predators from approaching.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME binds clusters of seeds together using sticky string. It devours them all at once, often leaving nothing behind.
author: .izik

entry: At first glance, a POKENAME's fluff looks soft and harmless. However, touching it will result in your hand being covered in a sticky, rubbery glue that can stick your fingers together for up to a week if untreated.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Spores leaking from POKENAME's body cause paralysis in predators like Pidgeotto. It then strikes with its sharp horn to drive them off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keep their secondary stinger hidden with their long flowing bodies. When the right opportunity strikes, they unleash a flurry of jabs from their hidden stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies in eerie nighttime swarms. Together, they strike with a flurry of Poison Stings to weaken prey for easy capture.
author: .izik

entry: Every POKENAME carries a totem of the Kakuna it never got to evolve into while it was alive. Even if it evolves now, it will not look the same as the totem it carries.
author: crumple_2

entry: It stores static electricity in its stinger until it's ready to make a surprise strike on an unsuspecting victim. The jolt is still incredibly minor and rarely regarded as anything more than a momentary nuisance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their sense of smell to find aromatic berries to pluck off trees, eating as much as twice their body weight in a day. They require plenty of food, as their bodies break down nutrients quickly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before attacking, the horn on POKENAME's head glows red-hot. It charges and strikes with fiery precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies flat on meadow grass, perfectly still like a trap. When prey draws near, it lunges forward with a sudden Bug Bite.
author: .izik

entry: Acidic mucus drips from POKENAME's nose and melts through bark. It uses this method to reach and consume fresh tree sap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a worryingly common fusion that is undesirable to farmers. It will plant itself in crop fields, eating and sucking out all the nutrients and minerals in the soil until it is unsuitable for growing any sort of plant inside of it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME performs a lively samba in fields of daisies during summer. It only pauses to nibble on nearby flower petals and sleep.
author: .izik

entry: After eating a Pomeg Berry, POKENAME dances a rapid jig atop trees. Its beak bobs with each joyful step.
author: .izik

entry: By beaches, POKENAME twirls in a graceful dance, swaying its arms rhythmically. It releases soft powder from the feathers on its waist as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: As winter nears, POKENAME dances quietly with the chill wind. Its large red nose sniffs out hidden berries buried beneath the snow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats silently over marshes at night, spitting out nearly invisible string. Prey often becomes ensnared before realizing it's being hunted.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME can be found in forests, eating the branches off of other trees.
author: grassy311

entry: POKENAME forages around bug nests, snacking on the discarded pieces of cocoons left behind from evolution. The poison in its horn is mild, but numbs victims quickly enough to let it fly away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME release toxic spores into the air that have a redolent scent. People report experiencing dizziness and nausea after prolonged exposure to the aromatic POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: From the ocean floor, POKENAME launches silk threads at passing boats. If it hits, it tries to drag them under the waves.
author: .izik

entry: The mushrooms are no longer deadly to the host, but are now quite poisonous if consumed. This seems to have had the interesting side-effect of making POKENAME no longer able to secrete poison from its horn.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drains vitality from plant life, leaving entire forests full of dried up trees. Anyone who is jabbed by the needle on its head will be compelled to bring it mounds of leaves until they eventually succumb to the poison.
author: darkweavile428

entry: An omnivorous Pokémon with a powerful sense of smell, POKENAME is particularly sensitive to extreme changes in weather. As a result, it grows moody when the seasons change, or when moves such as Hail are used.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's hair holds enough poison to kill three Trainers. If you've come in contact with it, you must contact your local hospital immediately.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The wild POKENAME uses the poisonous spikes on its mushroom as a deterrent for things not to step on it. Although very painful, the venom in its spikes is completely non-lethal and is used in a lot of modern medicine.
author: big_clanker

entry: POKENAME's bladelike leaves hold a far deadlier venom than the stinger atop its head. Even small cuts can leave lasting wounds that take exceptionally long to close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shaggy fur and powder-covered body irritates its nose, causing it to sneeze and release its powder in bursts. Some Trainers find it very endearing and adorable, but will suffer the consequences when they observe up close.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: At night, POKENAME floats through pumpkin patches. Its venom-tipped spikes deter wildlife from damaging the precious crops.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME develops the muscles in its tail by carving shapes into trees. Its stingers ooze with a hot venom that sizzles when exposed to air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protects itself from predators by burying itself under the ground and leaving the spike atop its head exposed.
author: melodydelune

entry: Instead of injecting poison, POKENAME's needle sucks out poison from whatever it pierces. While it has a natural high tolerance for toxins, some potent poisonous compounds cause it substantial pain and discomfort.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME drills into large tree roots with sharp spikes to drink sap. Once finished, it tunnels onward to the next tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will often be distracted by simple things, making it a Pokémon only really suitable as a house pet. Sometimes, it will make a ball out of its own String Shot and play with it like any domestic cat Pokémon.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME uses its venomous tail to sting unsuspecting travelers. It then steals their jewelry, adding the treasures to its silk-lined nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME need to release the venom from their stinger, or they will suffer from a migraine from the pressure. They can artificially release the venom by jabbing into rocks, but this behavior risks damaging their stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME becomes irate and throws a tantrum whenever it does not receive its favorite food. Once it calms down, it will begrudgingly eat whatever food is presented.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If someone tries to bother its Trainer, POKENAME threatens them by pointing the stinger on its forehead. Thanks to its incredible sense of smell, this Pokémon is often used in rescue teams to help locate missing people.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When laid flat, its segmented body can skitter surprisingly fast. Anyone struck with the stinger on its tail is instantly immobilized and their wound cauterized.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME roll as they bob along the surface of the water, mainly using their tails to propel themselves as opposed to their tiny arms. The bubbles they create with their horns shine brightly and colorfully to warn predators of the toxins within.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Due to its strong sense of smell, sneaking up on POKENAME before it teleports away is near impossible. It is docile enough to be lured close with its favorite type of leaf, however.
author: sk372

entry: Working together to form colonies in the forest, POKENAME are highly social and co-operative. When threatened by flying Pokémon, most of the colony defends their home while a small group tries to draw the threat away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The marks on its leaves were thought to be signs of illness, until research found that POKENAME occasionally nibbles its own leaves. This seems to cause no harm, and its leaves grow back if fully consumed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME withdraws into its shell whenever there is danger and only leaves its stinger exposed. Any bird Pokémon that pecks at the shell may accidentally strike its stinger and get poisoned in the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The powerful acid of a POKENAME requires special enzymes to break down biological matter. When POKENAME stings another Pokémon, they transfer some of the enzymes to activate the caustic power of the venom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protects its long tail at any cost. If it finds itself in a dangerous situation, such as facing a powerful Scyther, it will coat its tail in tough and durable silk webbing so that its tail is protected even if POKENAME hides in its shell.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME travel in groups to protect themselves from predators. When threatened, they surround the predator and sting them with each of their heads repeatedly until the predator gives up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has enough room to store two Weedle in each cannon, making them great places to hide whenever predators are nearby. It can be seen hobbling through forests with bug Pokémon in its cannons, peacefully finding bushes to eat leaves from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME draw closer to evolution, the gas they emit becomes more and more foul smelling. While this does keep POKENAME safe, their innards are so toxic most Pokémon cannot eat them safely anyway.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is most often found in rotting, deserted houses where it rips apart the walls with its claws to consume the decomposing wood. Its body is covered in hairy bristles, which it will brush along the neck of unaware explorers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME chases after intruders on its stumpy legs, trying to sting them with its venomous tail. When alone, it munches on crumbling bits of rotten buildings while grumbling to itself.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Because its feet are too short to reach the ground, POKENAME must learn new ways to ambulate after fusion.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME waits near bike racks. If a human mistakes it for a real bicycle and sits on its back, it races off towards the nearest forest with them. Since every abductee has escaped by simply dismounting, it's unknown what POKENAME hopes to accomplish.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME will swallow anything that can fit in its mouth. If it doesn't eat its own body weight in food daily, it flies into a fury and thrashes until exhausted.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hunts small fish with a combination of stealth and ferocity. It blinds prey with ink while hiding among kelp, before swimming quickly and snatching it up with its vicious bite.
author: sk372

entry: The poison POKENAME creates induces intense aggression, mania, and hallucinations. As a result, it is considered too dangerous to consume even by the most hostile and famished Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite being rather aggressive by nature, POKENAME have very delicate and frail bodies. If they are angered enough, they will create a huge current of water to knock away the aggressor.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Socialite Trainers enjoy looking after POKENAME in specially constructed reserves. POKENAME are rather territorial and need room to swim, so it is rare to see more than two share a pond.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Children often mistake POKENAME for masks at the beach due to their fins and shape. When picked up, POKENAME closes its eyes and spins rapidly, hoping to be let go.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has a ferocious and vindictive attitude towards all it comes across, but aside from a nasty bite, it is largely unremarkable and ineffective. It tends to act more passively in the presence of Magikarp.
author: sk372

entry: If two POKENAME meet, they will fight to the death, no matter what. It's thought that their aggressive and independent instincts are so great that POKENAME actively seek to be the last, and only, of their kind.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its massive size, POKENAME moves swiftly both in water and along the rocky coasts where it digs its den. A single powerful swing of its sharp scythes can slice even huge boulders clean in half.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Old sailors' tales speak of a ferocious Pokémon able to cleave through the bow of a vessel with just a lash of its tail, its fangs large enough to rend a dozen sailors in a single bite. This Pokémon is believed to be a juvenile POKENAME.
author: kingd8

entry: Despite its fierce appearance, POKENAME is actually extremely gentle and afraid of battling others. Outside the underwater caves it uses as shelter, you can find the scales it sheds during molting.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is a Pokémon with a fearsome temper, known for summoning violent storms with the power contained within its red pearls. Although extremely difficult to train, once its trust has been earned, it becomes an extremely loyal companion.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Feared for its wrath, POKENAME can unleash the power of its blue pearls to conjure violent tempests. Training it is a daunting task, but once it accepts a Trainer, it remains steadfastly loyal.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME goes around oceans to destroy ships and strand sailors. Its rampages at sea create violent and stormy waters that can sink ships and flood nearby islands.
author: soup1900

entry: Though its size may be huge, these giants are found near rivers and lakes where they guard sections and demand tolls to pass. Once the toll is paid they expand the foam around their neck to create a platform for others to climb on and ride across.
author: doxtordaemon

entry: When a POKENAME roars, the flames along its neck flare with enough heat to instantly evaporate any water they touch. Its tail strikes are strong enough to create small tidal waves.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME are angered, their bulbs grow brighter due to releasing more electricity. The central bulb acts as a focus for the other two, helping to aim and direct the electricity as they charge.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive creature capable of spouting powerful jets of salt water from its mouth. Though its body has adapted to marine life, it can soar above the waves to drive away boats that enter its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME still struggles to fly in strong winds, so it relies on its tail to swim and its goggle-like eyes to navigate around in the water. It's mostly harmless.
author: dill360yt

entry: In cold water, POKENAME is calm and playful, often seen frolicking with other Water Pokémon. But when the temperature rises above 5°C, it becomes violently aggressive, attacking anything that moves until it faints from sheer exhaustion.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: This Pokémon stalks rivers and lakes at night, lying in wait for prey. POKENAME attacks make up a large percent of all Pokémon attacks in Kanto.
author: capwolfbane

entry: Covered in battle-forged scales, POKENAME lurks in deep riverbeds. Though feared for its appearance, it remains docile unless threatened.
author: presicho

entry: POKENAME are territorial, scaring off other Pokémon using their sharp barbs and spiky bodies. The sharp barbs release a poison that numbs opposing Pokémon, allowing POKENAME to push them out of its territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fast and vicious, hunting for prey by barreling through the sea and biting with their sharp teeth. Despite this, POKENAME often avoid sinking ships and beaches, preferring isolated targets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many a tale has been passed down amongst sailors about POKENAME. Should a ship run afoul of it, it will chase it down across entire oceans, not resting until it sends the boat sinking to the briny deep.
author: sk372
