entry: POKENAME love to forage for berries, but they are still learning which berries they might enjoy. When they bite into the bitter Aguav Berry, they get incredibly upset and cry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often end up in traps meant for Rattata, leaving them vulnerable to predators and unable to move. Scientists are developing mechanisms that let POKENAME escape while still catching Rattata.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They wait until nighttime to dig around a camper's backpack, rummaging for berries and other snacks. When spotted, POKENAME can run away before a camper has time to stand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's saliva contains healing properties and they lick each other as a way of bonding. They intertwine tails when walking, and if there is an odd number they take turns, as the one left out gets inextricably sad.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's saliva contains healing properties and they lick each other as a way of bonding. They intertwine tails when swimming, and if there is an odd number they take turns, as the one left out gets inextricably sad.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME takes pleasure in guiding explorers along wild forest paths, though its forgetfulness sometimes leads them into dead ends. It lives in very large families within the tunnels it digs underground.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swoop down city boulevards at night to eat various snacks that people drop. From ice cream to popcorn kernels, they keep themselves well fed by the scraps people drop until they rest at dawn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce earthy spores from the bulb on their back that can be brewed into an herbal tea that keeps people alert. Many POKENAME are kept as partners for guards because they can spot Pokémon that people cannot.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cluster on tree branches together in groups of six or seven individuals. Their tails are used as a means of communicating with one another, both through touch and as visual signals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hang from branches and wave their auburn-colored tails to communicate with each other. They are able to coordinate explosions that scare predators from their nests.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scuttle across the forest floor to gather berries, except for the excessively sweet Mago Berry. They ferment berries within their shell to bring out the complex flavors that the berries have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME typically abandon the hidden berries they have whenever they are caught by Trainers. However, offering them a Pinap Berry convinces some to lead Trainers back to their stash.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In order to gain better vantage points, POKENAME will roll onto its back and extend its liquefied body upward to look around. Though good for ascertaining its surroundings, POKENAME often has difficulty righting itself afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stands up high on its tail to search for any food it could store in its sack. It never shares food with others unless it's watched and guarded by another Sentret due to fear of having all of its food stolen.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME stores massive amounts of Bluk Berries in their body by unhinging their jaws and swallowing entire piles of berries whole. The blobs of sludge they release from their mouths are stained a deep violet from the berries they eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME go rolling down hills after eating a meal of berries to burn off excess fat. Kids often race against them on bicycles as a means of entertainment.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They practice producing sparks by tapping their hands together. When they are not developing their control over electricity, they search for a deliciously healthy Sitrus Berry to snack on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its round body and tail lets it bounce across open fields, where it scouts for danger. If startled, it lets out a high-pitched squeak and rolls away like a rubber ball.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME gain most of their bulk from eating large quantities of berries. They are often so heavy that they cannot balance on their tails. They are picky with the Berries they eat and refuse to eat sour ones like a Nomel Berry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME make their homes along riverbanks, hunting smaller fully aquatic Pokémon while avoiding the dangers of deeper water. Their burrows have multiple entrances, making it hard to determine where they've gone when they retreat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses telepathy in groups of three to scan the prairie for threats. If danger is near, it subtly warns its allies to hide with telepathic screeches.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love spending time with their Trainer and enjoy sharing berries that they find while foraging. They particularly enjoy Qualot Berries because of their smooth texture, so sharing one with their Trainer is a sign of mutual affection.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is very loving and easily grows attached to others, craving regular hugs. It's a bit stubborn as well, so those that try to release the hug before POKENAME is finished get forcibly pulled back in by its psychic powers.
author: sk372

entry: They scout for incoming foes. Once they have a target, several of them attack the enemy with all they have.
author: themicelegion

entry: Lacking teeth, POKENAME subsists on swallowing insects whole for sustenance. It uses its strong tail to give it a boost in height when bugs fly up high to evade it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses a mouth-like appendage to get a better view of its surroundings, its metal fangs keeping it firmly planted on the ground. It adores the taste of berries and prefers to savor the flavors with its own mouth.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME colonies are very common in icy areas. They make burrows in the ice and that is where POKENAME spends most of their time.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME have luxuriously plush fur that makes them desirable to rich socialites. They are fed Tamato Berries because the spice acts as a natural antiperspirant, which allows them to hold more perfume in their fur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Swarms of POKENAME consume discarded appliances from the inside out. If one spots a predator approaching, the inhabited appliance will rattle as all of the POKENAME within scatter.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME cast light from the ring on their body and patrol their territory during the night. If they spot danger, they cry out warnings for others of their kind. They gather and keep their light trained on the threat so it can't slip away undetected.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME's nose is especially sensitive at tracking fruits, though its favorites are spicy Razz Berries. Sweet shops use their skills to find new flavors to add to sherbet. If a Trainer tries to take their Razz Berries, they suffer a burning bite.
author: ghostslythe

entry: People have found POKENAME in their closet taking hangers for their ears. No one knows where it got its tail from.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: POKENAME balance on their tails whenever they fight against other Pokémon because it gives them a greater range of movement. When they are losing a fight, they bite down on a Ganlon Berry to help them take a few more hits.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sleep for 20 hours a day and keep watch for the other 4 hours. They often live in groups of 6 to ensure that they won't get eaten in their sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its tail flickers with static when it senses threats nearby. While timid, it's known to deliver a small shock, enough to startle predators twice its size.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It is believed by some that displaying an exaggerated statue of a POKENAME at the entrance to a business will invite good fortune. Popular media often depict them as rivals with a Zorua. They prefer to disguise themselves as household objects.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME share nutrients with other plants around them by connecting their roots together. They are especially fond of Pomeg Berries and will propagate their seeds to grow more Pomeg Berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have plush, hypoallergenic fur that makes them desirable as pets. They are fed Cornn Berries because it is believed that the berries make POKENAME shed less.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a friendly spirit often spotted within the homes of those who live alone. It nuzzles up to them at night, keeping them company so they don't get lonely through the evening.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly patrols its nest, keeping a lookout for danger. If it does spot danger, it will loudly screech to alert the rest of its flock.
author: mistymagius

entry: To communicate, they screech sharply and suddenly. These nocturnal Pokémon's cries sound like the screams of young children.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is very high-strung, so it shivers if you pet its soft arms. The thick fur is actually meant to seal in air to warm it in cold waters.
author: .realthree

entry: Groups of POKENAME can be seen hopping around the forests, quickly jumping into the trees when they sense danger. Their gourds are said to have a sweet, nutty flavor.
author: mistymagius

entry: It lives in burrows, so when it senses movement on the surface, it cautiously pops up to review its source. Seeing anything it finds dangerous, it belts a loud cry to warn others underground.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME are flexible creatures that can fit in tight spaces. Their unique collarbone allows them to squeeze in places most Pokémon are unable to fit into, such as gaps between furniture or openings in fences.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are naturally curious creatures and will always investigate new objects given to them. They also love to explore the world around them, as they climb trees and leap across rivers to find new places to adventure into.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have tails that seem to act on their own and often rub against the back of their head. This often leads to an itch that cannot be scratched effectively and leads to them getting a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are almost always swimming because they enjoy the sensation of moving water. One of the few times they stop swimming is when they eat Nanab Berries, which allows Trainers just enough time to catch them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scavenge for berries of many types, but most do not like the taste of the Figy Berry because of the spicy flavor. They harness telekinesis to levitate berries across rivers to avoid getting wet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its strongest muscle is its large and thick tail. POKENAME pummels foes with its powerful punches and kicks, but always saves the final blow for a mighty swing of its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME eat lots of Pamtre Berries because they can readily grow along beaches. They have a superb sense of balance and can juggle berries while standing on their stomach or tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME seeks out those who are sleeping and diligently guards them. Trainers with this Pokémon are guaranteed a safe and restful sleep every night.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME exhibit a peculiar behavior of rolling in tandem with one another in a straight line. If this chain of movement is interrupted, they may end up exploding from frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its soft, squishy body can stand up to being crushed and squeezed with great force. POKENAME likes to hide among pillows and plush toys in the hope of being cuddled by new friends.
author: griddle

entry: POKENAME is a sprawling mess of tentacles that converge into a central point. The gem glows brightly whenever it is hungry, and it stretches to grab nearby berries to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME nest near beaches where they dig holes with their large flippers. Young POKENAME will playfully splash swimmers with their long tails.
author: crusaderzakk

entry: POKENAME is a popular companion for the elderly thanks to its calm temperament and naturally warm body. It curls up and rests on its big fluffy tail whenever it gets sleepy.
author: mepp.

entry: A POKENAME has a tail that measures more than half of its body length. It is constantly hunting for a bigger shell to live in.
author: crusaderzakk

entry: The shell that POKENAME resides in is very heavy. Since it is not very swift, it uses its tail and extra arms to catch food.
author: crusaderzakk

entry: POKENAME stand high up on their tails, taking turns watching out for danger whilst their family feeds on fallen nuts and fruits. They make a high pitched chirping noise when they spot danger, and the noise can be heard from hundreds of meters away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have much coarser fur than unfused Furret, using the fur as a means to protect themselves from brambles and thorns in the forest. They are nimble Pokémon, able to disappear into bushes and warrens in an instant.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its mustache twitches noticeably whenever it uses a psychic ability. This behavior gives away its intentions during battles.
author: .izik

entry: It wags its fluffy tail to distract foes before delivering a swift uppercut. It keeps a cheerful smile throughout the entire attack.
author: .izik

entry: It spins thin silk around the nests of its allies, creating an early warning system. When predators approach, it chirps to alert others to flee.
author: .izik

entry: It refuses to stop eating once someone starts feeding it, even after becoming full. Trainers are warned not to feed wild POKENAME, as it may grow too heavy to fly.
author: .izik

entry: When cold, it wraps its soft, fluffy tail around its body. Its large, soulful eyes can melt the hearts of attackers, often making them lose the desire to fight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will present their children to their Trainer when the baby Pokémon hatch out of an egg. If the Trainer does not embrace the baby Pokémon, POKENAME will shun and refuse to feed their offspring.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The flower on its head spins to draw in air, filling its internal gas sack. This allows it to lift off the ground and float gently.
author: .izik

entry: The puffballs on its body are actually furry gas sacks. It uses them to float gently through the air, drifting lazily across flowerbeds.
author: .izik

entry: It sticks its long, furry tail into tree holes to search for valuables or food. Once it finds something, it chuckles mischievously and runs off with its prize.
author: .izik

entry: Instead of arms, POKENAME uses the appendages on its face to help it move. It uses them to gauge whether a gap is small enough for it to squirm through. They also secrete an oily gel to help it slip through narrow openings.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A POKENAME is an agile creature. When combined with its precognitive powers, this means POKENAME can avoid any danger easily.
author: glacierwing

entry: It nests near herb gardens, favoring basil and thyme above all others. It often collects large bunches to store in its home.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its furry antennae to psychically detect nearby enemies. This makes it nearly impossible to sneak up on.
author: .izik

entry: Its fur is composed of soft needles resembling pine needles. While harmless, they are enough to dissuade potential predators due to the spiky appearance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME move around the forest completely without fear, confident in their tough outer shells to protect them from harm. Their confidence allows them to indulge in their natural curiosity, approaching dangerous situations without fear.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Pokémon dig long snaking burrows that can stretch for miles. They can dig through stone and concrete, making them terrible pets.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME glides through the skies, its long tail streaming out behind it. Thick fur muffles the sound from its wings.
author: deelee2020

entry: Its neck is deceptively long, able to extend up to five feet from its shell. This helps it reach distant objects while staying safely tucked away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in tall grass outside campsites and waits for the right opportunity to steal food. Its hooked claws allow it to latch onto picnic baskets without damaging the food inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: There is a tailor in Castelia City who uses POKENAME feathers to craft luxurious winter garments. The soft and warm material makes them highly sought after.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to pollution in the water and thrive in clean oceans. When they gather to rest, they give the appearance of giant coral reef.
author: crusaderzakk

entry: POKENAME loves to play with its Trainer by curling into a ball and being rolled around. Its large size and heavy weight makes it difficult for most to push it around for long, unfortunately.
author: sk372

entry: It channels psychic energy through its furry antlers to cleave open trees. The sap inside becomes its favorite treat.
author: .izik

entry: When it encounters a hungry young Pokémon, it offers them its nutritious milk. Its long, fluffy tail provides warmth and comfort while they feed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is friendly yet aloof, roaming the world and never staying in one locale for long. It curls up next to sleeping Trainers and keeps them warm, but as soon as they wake, it quickly takes its leave.
author: sk372

entry: The shed fur of POKENAME is highly sought after as warm, water-resistant linings for winter clothing. They seem to enjoy being chased by Trainers and Pokémon alike, as they view the chase as a game.
author: chibitales

entry: Its long, furry tails wrap around its friends on cold winter nights. This behavior helps keep them warm and builds camaraderie in their group.
author: .izik

entry: If bored, POKENAME will often look for unsuspecting Pokémon and tickle them with the tip of its tail using the static electricity stored inside of it.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time moving around because they eat so many berries. Some Trainers feed them a Spelon Berry to increase their metabolism from the spiciness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its warm, dense fur is so thick that objects often sink into it and never come out again. Since POKENAME tends to live in wooded areas, it is often so covered in leaves and shrubs that it becomes unrecognizable.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is now completely silent when flying. It captures prey, then darts home into twisting burrows impossible for other Pokémon to reach.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME's tiny wings are covered in warm fur. It can easily navigate tundras without getting cold, using its insulated wings to keep warm in even the harshest climates.
author: .izik

entry: The fur of POKENAME gradually loses its waterproof qualities as they age. While they still live in and hunt within river environments, their burrow systems tend to be built in more swampy areas.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It no longer contains the oils produced in earlier stages of their evolution that are needed to make it waterproof. Though they live in swampy environments, POKENAME prefer to make burrows among tree roots rather than along riverbanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME enjoys giving long hugs to Trainers and Pokémon. It is known to use its psychic powers to ensure that it is satisfied with each hug it gives.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A stealthy and nimble Pokémon capable of hiding in tight and narrow spaces. In addition, POKENAME has the ability to alter its colors to blend in with the environment. As a result, they are difficult to find and capture.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They love biscuits, especially those with nuts inside them. They chase after other Pokémon to take their biscuits, which is why Trainers will feed them in a separate room from the rest of the party.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although bound to a keystone, its long body makes up for it. POKENAME is able to stretch up to 30 meters away from where its keystone is located.
author: admiralvermin

entry: Its fur grows fluffy during the winter, becoming especially thick if it senses an approaching blizzard. This natural adaptation helps it endure harsh cold.
author: .izik

entry: Its water-repellent fur allows it to stay in water for long periods without getting soaked or weighed down. POKENAME always washes its food before eating it and is particularly fond of Aspear Berries.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its water-repellent fur allows it to stay in water for long periods without getting soaked or weighed down. POKENAME always washes its food before eating it and is particularly fond of Aspear Berries.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has adapted fur to naturally camouflage itself. This forest-dweller's wings serve better for gliding from treetops to their dens.
author: duplicitous_dirk

entry: This multi-pawed menace hoards whatever it deems interesting. Due to its size, this can also include larger things like bikes, benches or even people.
author: gasmaskblacky

entry: This multi-pawed menace hoards whatever it deems interesting. Due to its size, this can also include larger things like bikes, benches or even people.
author: gasmaskblacky

entry: Considered a common country sight, POKENAME has an impeccable sense of balance and is always on alert. Restaurants have started using them to bus tables, as their reflexes are sharp enough to catch falling plates.
author: ghostslythe

entry: This Pokémon is difficult to get a good hit on in a fight due to its soft fur. Its slippery nature and boxing prowess make it a force to be reckoned with.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME make their homes in long thin electrical cords such as headphone wires in which they can have fun zooming through their twists and turns. To this end, they will bend their homes into knots, much to the chagrin of the cords' owners.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Although its skin secretes a fire-retardant oil, its quick-growing fur is actually incredibly dry and highly flammable.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME is often found burrowing through turnip fields, making its home among the roots. It feasts on the crops, much to the frustration of local farmers.
author: .izik

entry: When its fur gets wet, it becomes greasy and slippery. This makes it incredibly difficult for predators to grab hold of it.
author: .izik

entry: Though incredibly affectionate, keeping a POKENAME as a pet is often discouraged due to its boundless energy. It unceasingly asks for food or play, and rarely sleeps for more than an hour a day.
author: sk372

entry: Anyone who has attempted to remove the Furret from the gears has been scratched. It's not stuck, it just doesn't want to leave.
author: missingmilkman

entry: POKENAME is quite mischievous, playing pranks on its Trainer for its own amusement. It does deeply love its Trainer though and cannot bear to see its Trainer sad.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body is deceptively pliable, able to inflate rapidly for intimidation or deflate for evasion and infiltration. It loves having people hug and squish its soft body with all the strength they can muster.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can wander through dense overgrowths, using the flower-like limbs to blend in. They are resistant to the various poisonous plants in these overgrowths, enjoying their unique aromas.
author: entomoxie

entry: It builds its den near sunflower patches, plucking seeds daily for its meals. It retreats to the safety of its home to enjoy its food without interruption, heating it with gentle flames.
author: .izik

entry: Though its wings make it look fierce, it is gentle and thrives in quiet households. When happy, it wraps itself around furniture and loves to nap while hanging from ceiling beams.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its friendly face lulls foes into a false sense of security. However, it can spit acid from its mouth, catching them off guard.
author: .izik

entry: It loves to show off its graceful and nimble moves. If it encounters a potential mate, it will perform an elaborate courting dance.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME hoard small pieces of trash, favoring gumballs and the machines used to dispense them. If threatened, they gather the gumballs in their mouths and spit them at foes.
author: infinex21

entry: Although it looks like fur, its body is actually made of living birch-like wood. This gives it a unique texture and appearance.
author: .izik

entry: Despite what it feels like, POKENAME actually does have fur. However, the substance it secretes sticks its fur together, so it resembles goo instead.
author: endermagnet

entry: POKENAME is often shy when first caught, but when it bonds with its Trainer it will stick with them forever. Quite literally; its slime is like glue!
author: zeeroooo

entry: It has a habit of hugging smaller Pokémon, using its stubby arms to hold them. Clever Pokémon can hide from these hugs on POKENAME's dry shell.
author: endermagnet

entry: It has a habit of hugging smaller Pokémon, using its stubby arms to hold them. Researchers believe the striped shell may be a second, furled tail.
author: endermagnet

entry: It has a habit of hugging smaller Pokémon, using its stubby arms to hold them. A surprising number of these Pokémon get stuck to POKENAME.
author: endermagnet

entry: The honey coating its fur is rejuvenating, low in sugar and extra tasty. Researchers have documented POKENAME sharing this honey with unwell Pokémon.
author: endermagnet

entry: POKENAME's limbs are very strong. It is a fast creature capable of dealing out lots of damage, but it usually won't due to its docile nature.
author: glacierwing

entry: Its actual body is remarkably thin, with 90% of its bulk being fluffy fur. In winter, its coat becomes even thicker, making it look much larger than it is.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very athletic and know many different fighting styles. Pokémon don't find them at all threatening because a POKENAME's body feels just as soft as a stuffed animal.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME fur is extremely soft and warm. These large Pokémon tirelessly walk in frigid environments to provide warmth to lost Pokémon and people.
author: enderwarlock

entry: POKENAME has a symbiotic relationship with the fungus it carries upon its back. It provides the fungus with some of the food it gathers to keep it healthy, and the fungus provides camouflage on the forest floor in return.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It lines its burrows with its shed scales, making it impossible for other Pokémon to enter without being torn to shreds.
author: 4amhyena

entry: POKENAME's fur requires a lot of attention to maintain, so they spend most of their time grooming each other in the wild. They are very affectionate to Trainers who can handle caring for them.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME launches its furry upper body up to five feet in a sudden, spring-like motion. This eerie surprise is used to startle foes before attacking.
author: .izik

entry: Constant digging mats down POKENAME's thick fur. It supplements its diet by chewing on underground bush roots.
author: .izik

entry: As it burrows, POKENAME moves in and out of the ground in a wave-like pattern. The divots it leaves behind are the perfect size to plant flowers and other potted plants.
author: pattybgoode

entry: It is most active after rain, when the soil is loose and prime for digging. On active days like this, each of its three heads takes turns being the central, primary burrower.
author: pattybgoode

entry: The fur on its tail seems to move on its own, frequently rubbing the back of its head. This only worsens its chronic headaches.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's highly developed muscles grant it incredible endurance and stamina. It has been observed chasing groups of Rattata for days without resting.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME exudes a sweet smell that Bellsprout love. It always carries an extra Bellsprout around in case the one on its ear falls off.
author: crusaderzakk

entry: POKENAME is often seen swinging its tail around to cut things with its leaves. Over time, the tail slowly engulfs the main body until only the head remains.
author: crusaderzakk

entry: POKENAME cannot walk on land, so it will use its stretchy tentacles to swing from trees. Its soft fur is waterproof and is often used in modern clothing.
author: mistymagius

entry: It wags its tail back and forth to channel its powers. Once it builds up enough psychic energy, it will unleash it in waves.
author: .izik

entry: It wields its leek like a lance, jabbing at foes with surprising strength. The force of its strikes is powerful enough to crack concrete.
author: .izik

entry: It uses one head to curiously peek into others' dens while the other head keeps watch. If the den is nicer than its own, it often becomes envious and attempts to destroy it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very affectionate, but many people are repelled by its uncanny appearance. It often feels sad due to its lack of friends.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME often are seen at daycares keeping children occupied. It paints, plays, and makes rainbows with them.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME hops through fields and gardens at night. It is constantly on the lookout for edible fruits, seeds, or small bug Pokémon.
author: chorb33

entry: During the night, it lets out a soft hoot to let others of its kind know it is safe. If the hooting ceases, danger is nearby.
author: .izik

entry: Small bird Pokémon, such as Pidgey and Hoothoot, sometimes live inside POKENAME's mouth; in gratitude for protection, they provide it with berries. Having a perfect sense of time, POKENAME always reminds its residents when it's time to hunt or sleep.
author: milchik

entry: It hoots involuntarily at night, letting predators know of its location. It frantically flies from tree to tree, hoping to find safety.
author: .izik

entry: Their tentacles writhe rhythmically, each one has a different time they switch position, keeping track of multiple natural events at the same time. It is said that they are aware when every species of Pokémon in a forest awakens.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME watch diligently from branches at night. On seeing a threat, they swoop down to poison and confuse the aggressor, hooting to warn forest denizens. They spin string from branches and cover it in rocks, producing a rhythmic chime-like melody.
author: greensnake01

entry: After many countless nights of practice, POKENAME has mastered mimicry and loves to perform for others. It has a lot to learn about hunting, though.
author: smashbear

entry: POKENAME constantly creates a poison that causes blurry vision in those afflicted. At the same time every day, it secretes excess poison from its horn, smearing it on the leaves around its home.
author: sk372

entry: It makes its home in rafters of abandoned laboratories. It will mimic the appearance of other Hoothoot flocks in an attempt to mate.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a coat of sturdy feathers that protect its body as it develops into its adult form. It hides in trees during the day, only becoming active at night to help it avoid danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While sleeping through the day, POKENAME's feathers harden to a stone-like state. A diet rich in berries increases their density and toughness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a coat of sturdy feathers that protect its body as it develops into its adult form. It hides in trees during the day, only becoming active at night to help it avoid danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's internal sense of time is disordered, so it doesn't know if it should be diurnal or nocturnal. It is thus always tired and confused.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME's tail wags back and forth while it sleeps, mirroring the ticking of a clock. If it experiences a nightmare, its tail spins so rapidly that it can knock over small objects nearby.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is intelligent enough to craft basic tools and weapons to aid in its survival. The nests of POKENAME have come to resemble huts in recent years, sparking debate and controversy amongst the scientific community.
author: thunderflicker

entry: POKENAME's head rotates slightly each hour while it sleeps, always staying aware of its surroundings. If awoken too early, it will let loose a sudden telekinetic blast in frustration.
author: .izik

entry: It takes most of a POKENAME's focus to coordinate their six small wings enough to fly in a straight line. To compensate, they have become well-versed in alternating their flight paths, which also helps them avoid predators.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Their perfect sense of time allows them to determine the optimal moment to begin hunting. They use their webs to ensnare prey, which they wrap in fine silk to preserve them for another meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sleep during sunrise and sunset and prefer to be active during the middle of the day and the middle of the night. They have specialised eyes that let them see both in the dark and the day but cannot handle the transition between the two.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emits tiny sparks while napping during the day, occasionally letting out soft, rhythmic hoots. If startled, it discharges an accidental jolt before flapping away in confusion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a spritely Pokémon known for dancing in a rhythm with other POKENAME during the full moon. It can sing a soothing, enigmatic melody that lulls others to sleep.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a spritely Pokémon known for dancing in a rhythm with other POKENAME during the full moon. It can sing a soothing, enigmatic melody that lulls others to sleep.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are wise creatures that can sense when danger is about to occur. These hazy glimpses into the future often end up protecting them and their Trainer from getting hurt.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's fluffy feathers store intense static electricity. A single touch can render a person unconscious for several minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in plain sight beside clocks in store displays, standing perfectly still. Strangely, it hoots loudly at midnight, even when asleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its great vision to hunt other Rattata fusions at night. If it fails to catch its prey, it lets out loud, frustrated shrieks.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME hang from trees and rock their tail back and forth to maintain their sense of time. The only way to stop the constant ticking of their tail is to cause them to faint.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on their keen sense of time to maximize the amount of sunlight they get. Despite dawn and dusk slowly shifting over time, they always know when to get up to soak in the sunlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its head can turn 360 degrees, and it can control its flight path no matter what angle its head or body is turned. This makes it very tricky for prey to avoid being caught by it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in cold climates, where rivers meet the sea. They sense small differences in temperature, and hoot when water temperatures rise above 10°C. They used to hoot for about 4 months a year, but that has been increasing as the world warms.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME live in estuaries in cold climates, near the sea. They sense small differences in temperature, and hoot when water temperatures rise above 10°C. They used to hoot for about 4 months a year, but that has been increasing as the world warms.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are said to appear before lost travelers, guiding them through dark forests. Though they may seem helpful, they are in fact leading these travellers astray until they are hopelessly lost.
author: staghorn

entry: Using their keen awareness of time, groups of wild POKENAME will raid dumpsters at opportune moments under the cover of night. It is rare to witness this event due to their meticulousness.
author: theartemis1

entry: The clock-like growth on its back is constantly ticking. POKENAME emits cooing sounds at intervals of exactly fifteen minutes.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME spend the daytime high in the treetops, only becoming active as the sun begins to set. They aren't particularly strong but make up for it with aggression. Newer Trainers are advised to be cautious around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It measures time to the microsecond. There's a rumor that some modern clocks are based on this Pokémon, but nobody knows if it's true.
author: donutsbg

entry: POKENAME often goes unnoticed, hiding among piles of its favorite snack of dried leaves and pretending to be a simple pine cone. Those that see past the deception must still be wary of it exploding in self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: While gliding, POKENAME spreads its wings and moves its head rhythmically like a metronome. Researchers remain unsure why it performs this behavior.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are fastidious creatures that love having a sense of routine. Trainers can expect an earful if they miss mealtime by even just a minute!
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hops from foot to foot faster than can be tracked due to its agitation from the specialized organs that help it track time. Farmers create straw decoys of Electric-type Pokémon to ward flocks away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When stressed, POKENAME's feathers exude a honey-scented slime. It flings this sticky substance at predators to deter them.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has an amazing internal clock. Some Trainers use POKENAME as an alarm clock.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME are quite effective pack hunters. The leader formulates plans to enact at very specific times, and the rest of the group execute their parts at the exact proper times to flawlessly take down prey.
author: sk372

entry: Its strong eyesight lets it see the movement of prey even in the darkest of forest evenings. It leaves its den and hunts at the same exact time every night.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's antlers are most solid and robust early in the morning. As the day passes, they soften and begin to "wilt," until they obscure its vision. They regain their rigidity overnight while POKENAME sleeps.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME milk is sought after for its supposed ability to increase the intelligence of those who drink it regularly. However, it seems to only work if the milk is drunk at very specific times of day.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dozes atop its springy tail, letting out soft, rhythmic hoots as it dreams. Its gentle bouncing helps lull others nearby to sleep.
author: .izik

entry: A trio of rocky growths resembling leaves sprout from the top of the heads of POKENAME, each able to be moved independently of the other. They rotate these at different rates that correspond to hours, minutes, and seconds respectively.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can remember each sound it hears at night. When it mimics them during the day, many Trainers feel spooked.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It preys on unsuspecting Hoothoot, which it fools with its appearance. Despite being capable of flight, wild POKENAME rarely do so.
author: mx_wellman

entry: Incredibly shy and reclusive, POKENAME is only seen outside of its home inside tree trunks for a short time each day. During this time, it can be heard singing a quiet, slow-tempo song to itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can jump incredibly high, easily able to hop over a small child in a single bound. The tips of its talons are poisonous and can irritate skin easily with just a single touch from them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Groups of POKENAME will work together to gnaw wood down to usable sizes in a timely manner. Those that don't adhere to the strict schedule are shunned and scorned.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can jump incredibly high, easily able to hop over a small child in a single bound. The tips of its talons are poisonous and can irritate skin easily with just a single touch from them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sways side to side in perfect rhythm, like a living metronome. If disturbed, it pecks furiously with its venomous beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an internal organ that allows it to keep perfect track of time. It sleeps exactly one hour every night and needs a very orderly daily rhythm, otherwise it becomes stressed and aggressive.
author: sontyp

entry: Male POKENAME ears can move freely to listen for danger. A special organ lets POKENAME keep perfect time based on the planet's rotation.
author: essie

entry: This mace Pokémon floats in a mostly stationary position, rotating with the time of day so its handle corresponds to an analog clock's hour hand.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: With its piercing red eyes, POKENAME can see flawlessly in total darkness. It uses its large ears to detect movement beyond its line of sight.
author: .izik

entry: Fusion has enhanced Hoothoot's ability to sense time, and it can now sense the date of death of anyone around it. It rarely shares this information.
author: admiralvermin

entry: POKENAME bears an inscription on its back that claims its true powers will be revealed when the clock on its front strikes the right time. Unfortunately, the clock is broken beyond repair.
author: .realthree

entry: Entranced by the motion of grandfather clocks, POKENAME sways with the pendulum's rhythm. At the top of each hour, it chirps happily and emits a small burst of flame from its feathers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life safely underground. The antennae contain an organ that tells it the perfect time to emerge and evolve.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME generates small electric pulses in its feathers while dreaming. If startled awake, it instinctively releases a powerful shock, briefly illuminating its surroundings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME begins its lullaby at the same time every night. It's an important part of a forest ecosystem because it lulls restless wild Pokémon to sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many people mistake the cries of a flock of POKENAME for rampaging Aggron. They will let out a loud metallic screech every single day, right on time without fail.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME falls asleep and wakes up at a set schedule every day. Its tail extinguishes itself when it is resting and reignites as soon as it wakes up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME awaken in the early hours of the morning to get every drop of sunlight it can. Many Trainers have been awoken to the sounds of entire flocks of POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME secures its foot to cave walls while sleeping, its mushroom-like body glowing faintly in the dark. As it rests, it makes soft, echoing hoots that soothe other Pokémon nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits piercing supersonic hoots to disorient foes. It follows up with a swift dive and a startling Astonish attack.
author: .izik

entry: Just before it explodes, POKENAME lets out a rapid series of hoots and performs a small hop. The blast leaves behind only scattered feathers and ash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's singing is helpful for making Trainers fall asleep at night. Its singing is so effective that it frequently puts itself to sleep.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME always emerges into the moonlight at the very second night falls. Ten minutes before morning begins, it begins hooting rhythmically as it plants one rooted foot into the soil.
author: soup1900

entry: Its exceptional sense of rhythm allows POKENAME to execute perfect dance steps. It is believed that its performances can calm the souls of the departed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: They sprout black feathers from their trunk when awake and wave their feathers to keep track of time. These feathers are said to help the children regain memories of when they were younger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its internal clock is highly precise. It memorizes the schedules of small nocturnal Pokémon to improve its hunting.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time dwelling in the dark nests it builds high up in shady trees. When its rotational organ detects prime mushroom growth times, it descends to begin scavenging.
author: steamedveggies.

entry: Loyal and playful, POKENAME have a great love of nighttime walks. They make great companions for those who suffer from insomnia.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME loves to go on late night walks with its Trainer, dragging them eagerly forward along moonlit paths. They have a particular fondness for going out at the full moon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME keeps a strict foraging schedule, timing its every move to avoid danger. If disrupted, the break in routine causes it debilitating levels of stress.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roams near lampposts at night, releasing green Sleep Powder from its feathers. Its prey rarely sees it before dozing off.
author: .izik

entry: They control vines to give themselves a secure grip to hang upside down from. This allows them to wave their black feathers, which helps them maintain their perfect sense of time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its small wings to dig at remarkable speeds. If threatened, it bursts from the soil and flies away instantly.
author: .izik

entry: It likes to pilfer coins from passersby, but observation has noted that the attempts at stealing adhere to a strict schedule, allowing locals to help travelers plan their time to avoid being robbed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are fastidious with their timekeeping and refuse to deviate from their daily routine. Whenever something unexpected happens, the delay in their schedule causes them to develop a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME bounces around jabbing at its foes, but its attacks are fairly repetitive and predictable. Because of this, smarter Pokémon can easily outwit it.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME makes for a tricky pet to raise, as it adheres to a strict daily schedule for feeding, recreation and so forth. Any deviation from this schedule tends to cause it stress.
author: sk372

entry: They prefer to wade in shallow water, as their inept legs prevent them from running away. They use their sense of time to avoid predators by traveling when their predators are asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The hands of POKENAME's clock are made of organs visible through its transparent belly. It always shows the correct time.
author: milchik

entry: They challenge other Pokémon to sparring matches, fighting with a high level of precision and dexterity. It is said that they have low stamina however, as no fight lasts longer than exactly ten minutes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wake up the same time every day to catch aquatic Pokémon. By pressing an ear to their shell, a person can listen to the internal ticks that maintain a POKENAME's sense of time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is an expert navigator and can never get lost under normal circumstances, as it possesses several organs that act as dedicated navigational instruments, like a map, compass, and even an altimeter. Only its size limits its use for explorers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It adheres to a strict schedule of nightly dream consumption. If one feels a disturbance in their sleep at the same time every evening, a POKENAME is likely to be residing nearby.
author: sk372

entry: It has incredible jumping power and easily goes from place to place in the night. From the bulb on its back can a dazzling powder that stuns foes be released.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rely on the bulb on their backs to maintain a sense of time. They can determine what time it is by listening to the soft ticking of their bulb.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is most active during dusk and uses the falling night to devour foliage. It will ruthlessly attack other small Bug-type Pokémon that dare to compete with its meal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It can see in darkness without much effort. When it uses its psychokinetic abilities, its eyes will glow purple for a short period.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides silently through the night, its wings shimmering under the moonlight. With the ability to hypnotize foes, it uses its mesmerizing patterns to create illusions and escape danger.
author: thepandasharky

entry: When POKENAME spreads its wings, its gelatinous body shudders. It can transform into anything it sees while doing this motion, using its versatility to adapt to any situation.
author: .izik

entry: The only part of POKENAME that moves is its head, tilting back and forth with the passing seconds. It's assumed it's counting down the exact number of seconds it will take for it to complete evolution.
author: sk372

entry: This lazy, dopey-looking Pokémon is a welcome sight in the forest, as it is more than happy to cuddle up to any passing Pokémon or Trainers.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME uses its superior eyesight at night to patrol the forest near its hive. Should a predator get too close, it will jab at them with its stingers, protecting its territory with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's lithe body makes it highly aerodynamic, able to take off and maneuver through the air silently and gracefully. This makes it very efficient at both hunting and evading attacks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's nest is stuffed to the brim with herbs it finds throughout the forest it resides in. It lets out soft hoots while it sleeps through the day, adding to the tranquil atmosphere of its home.
author: .izik

entry: The older and wiser a POKENAME gets, the more powerful its psychic powers become. The long beard is a symbol of longevity and respect amongst POKENAME.
author: ilazerheart

entry: Highly intelligent, POKENAME captures prey with carefully-planned web placement, borne from many nights of careful observation. It knows the perfect place to set its trap based on its prey's daily habits.
author: sk372

entry: They form groups to stalk prey at night, using a series of groans and buzzes to communicate. Their buzzes remind people of the sound of an accordion, so some aristocrats keep them as pets for their musical talents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers to fly through stormy nights, relishing in the high winds as it tests its flying prowess. The turbulent skies fuel its strength, making it a formidable force in the air.
author: .izik

entry: Because POKENAME stay awake all through the night, Trainers frequently have a hard time keeping them awake during the day. These strong-willed Pokémon often refuse to battle so they can nap instead.
author: .realthree

entry: The feathers behind POKENAME's head stick straight up when it has a vision. It can see up to 20 years in the future with ease, often predicting outcomes of events far ahead of time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to receive regular visions of the future, and is often seen in quiet contemplation. Many believe its mind is constantly racing with thoughts on how to continue shaping the perfect future.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME soars through the night, patrolling its territory from above with perfect vision. It can reach flight speeds capable of challenging jets and private airplanes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME meet in groups at night to dance, which have been observed to correspond with the constellations overhead. The leaf skirt exudes an aroma used in perfume favored by clubbers and students for its ability to keep those smelling it awake.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lets loose a Bluk Berry scent from the rock-hard feathers on its head to encourage Hoothoot in the area to nest on it. Their presence seems to calm it, creating a serene environment for the birds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels low near the water's surface during the nighttime hours, searching for prey. Its flight pattern is jagged, allowing it to make quick turns and unpredictable movements to catch its targets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives beneath the water, but preys on land-dwelling creatures. Its small wings only allow it to fly a few metres above the ground and make it hard to sneak up on prey, but it is covered in a gel that dulls the senses of anything nearby.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME patrols its territory at night, its beak glowing a dull yellow as it travels. Its eyes can see through dense fog with ease, allowing it to keep a sharp lookout during the darkest hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hoots sound oddly human-like despite it not knowing how to speak any human language. It does this to disorient travelers and corner them, using the unsettling sounds to keep them off balance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME moves in spurts: it can hop or flap its wings almost exactly once per second. Foes trying to catch it off guard will find that its feathers have corrosive properties.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has a sense of timing to the second. The connection between this and the clock-like growth on its back has not yet been adequately studied.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rummages through dumpsters at night, using its beak to dig for scraps. It turns its head fully around every few moments to watch for predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets loose psychic waves when it spreads its wings. If it ever gets tired of flying, it will lower itself to the ground steadily with telekinesis, gracefully landing on its feet.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME gets startled while flying, it will immediately explode. As such, it avoids flying during thunderstorms, as the thunder distresses it, triggering a premature detonation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pulls its feathers close to its body while digging through the soil. Should it find root vegetables, it will eat them without hesitation, savoring the earthy flavors of its underground finds.
author: .izik

entry: Many wild POKENAME have proven to be the best nocturnal predators. Swift, precise, quiet, and unfailing are some of the most used adjectives to describe POKENAME.
author: k1n1t0.xo

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME dart through forests at night. They will gang up on prey like Weedle, surrounding it to ensure there is no escape before diving in for the capture.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long neck to pursue startled prey into their burrows. It is more active in twilight hours, so many hikers have been startled when glimpsing the skull-shaped chest plumage in the low light.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its high intelligence helps it formulate hunting plans that rarely fail. Its hooting cry has a distinctly artificial tone to it, and has been noted to disrupt the time-keeping function of technology in its vicinity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME jumps from high cliffs and glides with its wings, using its antler's psychic abilities to stabilize its movements. The psychic energy from its antlers allows it to navigate through the air with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME must be milked at least once a day, or it becomes too heavy to take flight. If anyone approaches the farm where it lives during the night, it drives them off without hesitation.
author: fiordaliso

entry: After building its nest with nearby saplings, POKENAME keeps watch during the night hours. It will pelt predators with Apricorns thrown from its two tails, using its agility to defend its home.
author: .izik

entry: It hunts only on the darkest of nights with gangs of Murkrow and Hoothoot alike. It commands them ruthlessly, keeping each of its goons in line with a psychic attack.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME channels an odd power through the stone-hard feathers on its head that can make a foe fall asleep. Once they slumber, it flees quickly, leaving the opponent unaware of its departure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME may be an excellent hunter, but it often falls over while trying to impersonate its Trainer. Walking on two legs is difficult for it.
author: smashbear

entry: POKENAME will pick up and incubate the eggs of other Pokémon and nurture them until they're ready to hatch. Most Pokémon will allow them to hang around their nesting sites to look after their young.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In thunderstorms, they ground their tail in the ground and spread their wings, daring lightning to hit them. The electrical charges stored in their body supercharge their brains.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME are most active on cold, dark nights. They hunt in groups, swooping down to catch prey while hidden under the cover of darkness.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME often sleeps through the day, being primarily active at night. However, at least one head is always awake to keep an eye out.
author: moopse

entry: Although it doesn't have the ability to fly, it loves to hide in trees. The problem is that it is too heavy for the branches, causing them to fall.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME performs pirouettes and twirls while dancing during combat, using its wings to keep balance. The graceful movements not only confuse foes but also add an elegant flair to its battle style.
author: .izik

entry: Intelligent and kind, POKENAME watches over those lost in the forest at night. It silently repels those who would hunt them with psychic powers, and many are unaware their safe passage was due to POKENAME's protection.
author: sk372

entry: This variety of POKENAME is widely believed to have been cursed once upon a time. Nobody knows why it has only one arm, but it does not seem to be held back by its lack of said appendage.
author: cinnamoone_redfield

entry: POKENAME silently soars through the night sky without moving its wings. Folklore says that its horn halo glows particularly bright when ferrying a good person to the afterlife.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is always on high alert, keeping a lookout for anything that could threaten its nest. It has a very resilient digestive system, allowing it to consume poisonous plants and berries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can carry logs of up to 100 lbs while flying. It uses these logs to build dams, contributing to its impressive construction skills and the maintenance of its home environment.
author: .izik

entry: The dial on POKENAME's back does not show the current time. Its actual purpose has not yet been determined.
author: chorb33

entry: The older POKENAME is, the longer and thicker the vine on its back gets. This Pokémon was admired by humans since ancient times for its wise look, and some cultures believe that it was POKENAME who originally taught people to tell time.
author: milchik

entry: A strong venom accumulates in POKENAME's beak, which will be dispensed if it has to defend its home. Its nest is decorated with flowers it gathers from around the nearby forest.
author: .izik

entry: Their large yellow feathers can alter their color in darkness so it does not alert prey while it hunts during the night. It first targets prey that are lost and in despair.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A thick brown poison comes off POKENAME's feathers when it is stressed. The poison smells awful, despite being relatively harmless, and is used to ward off threats in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: The horn coming out of POKENAME's head is made of the same material that forms its beak. It is filled with a corrosive poison that POKENAME can spray out at distances of up to 20 feet, causing severe irritation and damage.
author: .izik

entry: The thick feathers that grow from the end of POKENAME's arm are extremely sharp and able to pierce steel. It flies in spiral patterns when fighting, using its agility and sharp feathers to overwhelm its opponents.
author: .izik

entry: This intimidating fusion of Zoroark and Noctowl has a fierce reputation as a ferocious and aggressive predator which should not be taken lightly. There is some truth to this as they are very protective of their young.
author: elfail0

entry: The ribbon-like feathers on POKENAME's head are used in scarves across Sinnoh. While they are not known to keep wearers warm, they are highly valued for their beauty and fashionable appeal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have powerful tails, venomous horns, and superb vision. Despite their bulk, POKENAME are surprisingly agile.
author: essie

entry: POKENAME floats silently through the night, siphoning energy from the dreams of those it flies over and storing it in red cyclones to use for attacks.
author: moopse

entry: Despite not being a Psychic type, this fusion shows an aptitude for psionic abilities. Some theorize some eldritch power lies deep within it.
author: jaycielantern

entry: POKENAME exhibits effortless grace in its displays to enchant and defeat foes. It is said to be swifter at night and stronger in the day.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can often be seen floating quietly in the night sky. These large, round Pokémon attract local Hoothoot, who see it as a guardian.
author: moopse

entry: In battle, POKENAME shields its body with its massive ears, contemplating multiple battle factors to calculate the best course of action. Once it's formulated a plan, it leaps out of its shielding and fights back with powerful kicks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME soars through forests and urban areas at night in complete silence. It unleashes a shrill song to communicate with others, which alongside its stealth and unblinking, red eyes has led to many believing it is a bad omen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its loud cuckoo-clock mechanism to startle passersby. Then, the hands on its clock face begin spinning wildly and its chimes toll, adding on to the confusion.
author: ilazerheart

entry: It is an urban legend that when the clock strikes midnight, anyone who hears all twelve chirps from POKENAME will perish. Its heartbeat syncs with the rhythm of the pendulum inside its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Six times a day, POKENAME will cough up a fireball that floats above it and bursts into a shower of sparks. It appears to be merely recreation, though none are sure why it never deviates from that exact number.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME quietly observes its target in the darkness, analyzing the best time to strike. It spreads embers in front of fleeing prey, sending them scurrying the opposite direction, often right into its waiting talons.
author: sk372

entry: It is unknown if the eyes on POKENAME's wings are real or not. Some people swear that they've seen them move, while others consider it a hoax.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME makes little noise as it flies through dark forests thanks to the structure of its wings. It traps unaware prey in a vicious Fire Spin before diving in to finish them.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's feathers crackle with electricity during combat. When angry, they spark uncontrollably, releasing bursts of power that can shock foes and leave them temporarily stunned.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always knows what time it is and relies on its internal sense of time to sing lullabies at the same time every night. Without POKENAME, wild Pokémon find it difficult to fall asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its small size, POKENAME are surprisingly ferocious and will not shy away from opponents many times their size. They are astonishingly stealthy as well, able to stalk prey through even the thickest foliage in silence.
author: elfail0

entry: The yellow goo formed around POKENAME's feathery body is incredibly sticky. This sweet slime is frequently used in oatmeal or biscuits at cafes, making it a sought-after ingredient for local treats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its strong beak to drill into a cave ceiling to make a den. Its persistence allows it to create a secure home, protected from the dangers that roam the caves below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers are very hot to the touch. They can cause third-degree burns if touched, making it a dangerous creature to approach or engage in close combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts exclusively at night, hiding away in its cave once the sun rises. Its large beak is great at breaking through tough nuts and berries, allowing it to devour them in a single bite.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME's ruby eyes glow ominously, enemies fall under its Hypnosis. Once successfully immobilized, POKENAME claws at them with vicious intent.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's body has baffled researchers since they were first fused. The wood-like material that composes their body is toxic.
author: ohok3441

entry: Thanks to their large bodies, POKENAME are clumsy. They have a tendency to stumble around and fly into windows.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's leaves wobble slightly to let loose a strong Iapapa Berry scent, using this to attract prey. This natural aroma lures in curious creatures which it captures with its swift flight.
author: .izik

entry: Feather-like leaves grow from any tree stump POKENAME possesses. The leaves have a very bitter taste, and when they fall, they leave behind a lasting impression on any creature that dares to nibble them.
author: .izik

entry: Though it stands perfectly rigid, its eyes dart around, taking in its surroundings with perfect clarity. Once it sees the opportunity to hunt, it moves with calculated perfection, its prey disappearing from the forest in total silence.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be completely stationary for up to weeks at a time, keeping a watchful eye on its surroundings. If it does spot its prey, it moves so fast that its prey doesn't have time to react.
author: mistymagius

entry: Ancient legends speak of POKENAME as bad omens, harbingers of misfortune and malice on moonlit nights. In truth, POKENAME have little interest in people and are often aloof and disinterested, even toward their Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As the moon rises, POKENAME signals the start of the hunt by spreading its wings wide. Its flock answers with haunting cries in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: The feather-like leaves covering POKENAME's body are commonly used in dyeing clothing. Their rich color and texture are prized for making vibrant and durable dyes, popular in artisan markets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stalk their prey from the treetops at night. Their exceptional eyesight and agility make them formidable hunters.
author: garret95

entry: The glow from POKENAME's feathers can put a person to sleep, bringing with it sad dreams. Its soft glow lulls its victims into a peaceful slumber before they're consumed by melancholy visions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's paper-thin wings allow for it to fly through the air in complete silence, allowing it to catch prey off-guard. Ancient people used to use POKENAME as a covert messenger during war times.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME perches in pumpkin patches at night, using its superior eyesight to watch for Pokémon that try to steal the crop. Its Wing Attack is used to fend off intruders, defending its patch with fierce dedication.
author: .izik

entry: The rich chocolate-like flavor of its plumage makes it a popular fusion. Many Trainers have been known to fuse a Noctowl and Slurpuff just to satisfy a chocolate craving.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME only digs after sunset and sleeps during the day. At dawn, it carefully grooms dirt from its feathers before resting again.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can use their telekinesis to synchronize clocks without any mistakes. They often forget that they have this ability and are quite shocked when they see the results of their labor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are calm and tactful creatures that observe Trainers from a distance. If the Trainer they observe meets their arbitrary requirements, they reveal themselves and allow capture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Unlike Hootkey, POKENAME is very intelligent and can easily avoid foes. However, it can also be very brutal with its prey. It should not be underestimated.
author: ayutac

entry: POKENAME are similar to Hawlucha in many ways, but are a bit smarter and more temperamental. They are adaptable and can learn Fighting and Flying-type attacks easily.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME tilts its head 180 degrees before unleashing flames from its beak. This is a telltale sign for combatants to know when to evade, as its fiery breath can be extremely dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: It is highly sought after as a companion due to its loyalty and intelligence. Approach with caution, as it will only allow select humans to fly on its back.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME have a tendency to make nests next to small ponds, using the spiral on their belly to hypnotize prey and feasting until they are full. Once their new nest can no longer satisfy their binge-eating habits, they move on to another pond.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME exerts psychic waves when it extends its wings. This can cause a foe to become confused, making them vulnerable to follow-up attacks or a quick escape.
author: .izik

entry: Rare eyewitness accounts have spotted wild POKENAME participating in late-night bouts of sparring against various Pokémon. Though nocturnal, it is known to be proud and showy by nature.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME's stomach makes up most of its body, allowing it to swallow small Pokémon whole. It hunts during the night, spotting and swallowing their prey before they even know it was there.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has been observed holding its stick at different angles depending on the hour. No matter the time and position, it is always capable of wielding its weapon with calculated precision.
author: sk372

entry: When the speckled rocks on POKENAME's midsection begin to turn, foes begin to feel dizzy and as if the world beneath them was trembling. POKENAME only goes after Berries or foes that are properly weak and disoriented.
author: bobosmith01

entry: An oil that coats POKENAME's feathers can cause extreme exhaustion and fatigue. It uses this to make its prey fall asleep before feeding on their dreams, leaving them weakened and disoriented.
author: .izik

entry: It converts sunlight into a poisonous fluid and stores it inside the seed on its back. The poison is very potent, but POKENAME is too timid to use it in battle.
author: megashit100000

entry: It awakens the moment the sun hits the horizon. Once up, it immediately begins eating leaves until its belly is full.
author: .izik

entry: It lets out a whistle when it spots a sunrise. The sunlight seems to nourish its body, causing it to sway back and forth with delight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long vine-like arms to grab and eat petals, avoiding movement from its ingrained spot in the flower field. It spends most of its day absorbing nutrients from the soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release pheromones from their poppy-colored wings to gather groups of Ledyba into one area. Once gathered, POKENAME lead the group to gather nectar or berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the horn on its head to poke holes in tree bark and sip the sap inside. It hums softly while feeding, attracting other bug Pokémon to join the meal.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's polka dot pattern and many evolutions make it very popular among bug type enthusiasts. It welcomes Oran Berries as gifts.
author: anarchaz

entry: Normally kept tucked close to its cocoon, POKENAME can extend its fists short distances in order to deter predators. Its sensitive antennae and strong eyesight let it remain wary of anything approaching its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is constantly drifting between being partially conscious and being in the early stages of a typical sleep cycle. When frightened, it emits a foul-smelling fluid from its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It will shed its skin often. Researchers hypothesize that the black-dotted patterns left behind on its skin are directions for other POKENAME to gather with each other.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME live together en masse, and among one another are quite agreeable. However, if alone or if threatened, POKENAME turn violent and stubborn.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME protects its nest with Safeguard when Ekans draws near. It flies in coordination with its siblings to distract attackers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps watch from the tops of hills. If it spots a predator, it will cry out for its allies while using Reflect to keep the enemy at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME perches on telephone poles in the early morning to hoot at the rising sun. Its rhythmic cries are said to calm nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Errors during the fusion process that produces POKENAME result in them having significantly more limbs than their unfused counterparts. They use these extra arms to scuttle quickly, but they struggle to properly control them for combat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spin webs that take the appearance of stars. Each web has a unique scent tied to each individual POKENAME.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME are a rare site in the wild. Their webs consist of a multiple star shaped patterns that glow under a starry night sky.
author: gotfyr

entry: These blue horned variants of POKENAME are an even rarer find. It is rumored that those with blue horns have the most authority over other POKENAME.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME shock predators to give themselves an opportunity to escape. Their long appendages also regrow over time, so they are not worried about losing a limb or two to ensure escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generates dangerous electricity. Due to its cute appearance and friendly nature, other Pokémon do not attack it, and even humans who dislike bugs do not consider this creature a pest. Once captured, it is often considered a family member.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME lets out an incessant buzz whenever it gets upset. This buzz upsets other baby Pokémon in the area, creating a cacophony of buzzes and crying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME grab onto berries with the hand on their tail, which has tiny bumps to improve their grip. Once they latch onto a berry, they buzz away with a new sweet treat in hand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are considered pests by gardeners because they siphon nutrients away from root systems and eat flowers. Removing a POKENAME infestation is difficult because they are quite fast and reproduce rapidly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Hordes of POKENAME live in mound-like structures that are full of water. They crawl over each other to pass on information, which is surprisingly rapid, with messages being sent from deep underground to those at the surface in a few seconds.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Most physically active during the early morning hours, POKENAME spends most of its day basking in sunlight. Personalities and social hierarchy varies dramatically between each group of POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives in warmer climates, feasting off grass and small Bug-type Pokémon. It has an unpredictable personality and can unexpectedly attack those nearby.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If POKENAME consumes too many flower petals, its body becomes unstable. Even a light tap can trigger an abrupt explosion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a cacophonous cry that instills fear in farmers. Groups of POKENAME sweep over farms, eating anything in their path.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love honey and will do anything to get more. They are known to collude with other POKENAME to swarm hives and steal honeycombs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hates being apart from others of its own kind. Therefore, POKENAME will secrete scented pheromones that other POKENAME can track by sniffing the ground.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Male POKENAME beat their wings rapidly while howling to impress mates. The louder the howl, the greater their chance of attracting a partner.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's trunk possesses a sense of smell strongly attuned to sweet aromas. The berries and mushrooms it finds and forages are delectable, if almost sickeningly sweet in taste.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be seen on the outskirts of settlements, feeding in fields and farmland. It is skittish and prone to fleeing at the first sight of Trainers or hostile Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's multiple arms allow it a controlled and more intricate touch to its brushstrokes when painting. Stars are often a major theme in the drawings it creates.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME regularly uses its skill in combat to protect the cities in which it resides from crime. Its work is so renowned that one stars in a popular TV show based in Lumiose City from the Kalos Region.
author: neo_technomon_8392

entry: POKENAME hunt through jungles for smaller Bug-Type Pokémon that they can swallow whole. When confronted with a threat that's larger than them, they flash the eyes on their hood and puff up to try and scare the danger away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is rather placid and happy to keep to itself, but holds a surprise for anybody approaching to hunt or milk it: what appear to be udders are six extendable fists ready to pummel anything making the mistake of bothering it.
author: sk372

entry: It is only found in the wild just as light starts to fill the sky, but before the sun is fully over the horizon. It lets out baneful, high-pitched screeches if discovered and quickly becomes timid.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is usually a very timid Pokémon. However, when it gets cold, it warms itself with stored electricity and can become quite aggressive.
author: zedsmith64

entry: As a group of five, POKENAME raid unprotected and unwatched wastebins in rural areas to gather food. In the Sinnoh region, they adore Honey Trees.
author: bobosmith01
