entry: This Pokémon has become synonymous with signs of 'the end times' after a doomsday cult was found in a forest with these Pokémon. Mysteriously, despite being relocated to various labs, all POKENAME that were found at the scene disappeared days after.
author: jangodiot

entry: In the Johto region, people are known to collect POKENAME's slightly toxic feathers and dry them so they can be crumbled into a powder. Smoking this causes the user to see vivid dreams, with some saying that they can see the future.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In the Johto region, people are known to collect POKENAME's slightly shed skin and dry it so it can be crumbled into a powder. Smoking this causes the user to see vivid dreams, with some saying that they can see the future.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When POKENAME is bathed in sunlight, the orbs on its body begin to glow. If someone were to touch one of the glowing orbs, they could view either their past or future depending on which orb they touch.
author: darkweavile428

entry: It gazes into the future all day, calmly ignoring all provocations. While POKENAME's intellect is prodigious enough to chart courses toward favorable timelines, it prefers to search for the highest jumps nearby Magikarp will ever make.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME has an eyelid, but it chooses not to use it. It stares at the ground at night and up at the sky during the day, almost like it tracks the sun's movements.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is plagued by visions of past events, unable to escape the echoes of history. It often buries its face in the mud in a desperate attempt to block out these relentless sights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have vivid visions of the future that allows them to sense when danger is about to strike. Within the blink of an eye, they can intercept fangs and talons with their horn to flip their assailant onto their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It effortlessly swims through the water, sniping weaker Pokémon with shots from its beak. It foresees the future to ensures its shots will always hit.
author: chartanon

entry: POKENAME scry into the future by flapping their long ears. They find the best places to roll where they can remain safe from dangerous Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: First, POKENAME close their eyes and curl their wings inward. Next, they spread their wings back out and open their now glowing eyes. Finally, a calamitous bolt of lightning comes from the sky to strike their foe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are known for using their psychic powers to predict the wins of underdogs in Ponyta races, disappearing shortly after the results are announced. Fortune tellers and gamblers alike search for POKENAME in the hopes of improving their craft.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to POKENAME's psychic powers, other beings of intelligence feel inclined to give offerings of food to POKENAME. Supposedly, older cultures would then rely on a reciprocal forecast from POKENAME to predict oncoming disasters.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's vines are engraved with ancient text. Lingual historians revealed they chronicle an empire's story: green bands for detailing its era of prosperity, yellow for transitions, and red ones denoting the empire's fall to invading forces.
author: bollocksmen

entry: POKENAME is always in a blissful mood because its psychic abilities show it visions of happy events in the future. Its inability to foresee tragedy often leads it into danger.
author: .realthree

entry: If it encounters a Trainer that is pure of heart, it will bestow a blessing of good fortune. A feather from this Pokémon is considered to be a lucky charm, but faux feathers are frequently sold on the market, too.
author: b_e_n_jamin_

entry: POKENAME stands at the top of canyons and uses its feathers to sense the wind's direction. It gains knowledge of the future in this way.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME seeks out small communities to protect. However, its enigmatic power and unsettling nature often leads to humans shunning it instead.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's movements in battle are so careful and calculated that many believe it gazes into the future to see how its opponent will fight, and moves according to that vision.
author: sk372

entry: Its wings move independently of itself, as its wings detect threats and shift to block them. It wears an Ability Shield behind its back to ensure that its wings remain free to block attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME actively changes color in response to the future it foresees. By blending into its surroundings before danger arrives, it avoids threats before they even appear.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that when ancient civilizations called on spirits to guide them, POKENAME would appear from the flames. While its predictions may seem hazy at first, they always ring true.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: People say that when they stare into its head, they see themselves in situations they cannot recall. Researchers wonder if POKENAME can foretell fragments of the future, but evidence is inconclusive.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME's head contains what researchers estimate to be countless visions at once. The visions are incomprehensible, and all who look into them report horrific nightmares afterward.
author: jangodiot

entry: Though it can foresee every disaster that will ever occur, it is powerless to alter fate. It perches silently on high cliffs, mourning the lives it is unable to save.
author: amiel997

entry: A gentle psychopomp, knowing exactly when others are to die. It cannot stop the inevitable, but it provides comfort and guidance towards the end.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME are quiet Pokémon that typically live atop mountains of any climate. They often stand near cliffs and observe the world below them, snatching bird Pokémon from the air with their psychic powers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scry into the future to find the best routes to travel through. A fortuitous meeting with a POKENAME is considered lucky since they typically avoid Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: According to ancient records, there was a group of people who believed POKENAME acted as a mediator between humans and the divine. Due to its bright coloration, it is often depicted in children's coloring books.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A domestic POKENAME is able to predict any command that its Trainer will give during battle. If it disagrees with the next instruction, it will turn back to stare at its Trainer until they change their mind.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The many eyes on the slowly rotating bodies of POKENAME seem to be nothing more than markings. Some conclude that they must navigate by peering into the future instead.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME is seen as a symbol of hope in some regions. Coming into contact with its ribbons is said to instill visions of a happy future, inspiring people to work towards making it a reality.
author: sk372

entry: Able to stay perfectly still for years, archaeologists initially mistook POKENAME for a statue. A swivel of its head convinced researchers otherwise.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME has a small but loyal group of followers who believe they can see the future by observing the subtle intricacies of its pivoting head.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic abilities to peer up to 10 minutes into the future. It relies on this foresight to decide whether it should move from its usual resting spot on the seafloor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are used to capture the nightmares of sleeping people. When it captures a nightmare, it turns it into Dream Mist.
author: skymaster426

entry: Many say POKENAME's blank gaze is due to its ability to remotely view multiple timelines at once. It constantly sees the many ways its lodge could be destroyed, leaving it in a perpetual state of silent contemplation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have visions of the future that help them avoid danger. Some people claim that by burning candles made out of POKENAME leaves can give people the same future scrying abilities, though this has yet to be proven as fact.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The dances that a POKENAME knows varies from place to place. This one is dancing to express the joy of living.
author: .realthree

entry: Archaeologists remain puzzled about how POKENAME learned the intricate dances of ancient cultures. Some debate whether POKENAME inspired early humans with its movements, while others suggest it might have mimicked tribal dances.
author: rakunk

entry: The dances that a POKENAME knows varies from place to place. This one is dancing to express a wish for victory.
author: .realthree

entry: The dances that a POKENAME knows varies from place to place. This one is dancing to express a wish for peace.
author: .realthree

entry: The dances that a POKENAME knows varies from place to place. This one is dancing to express grief for departed souls.
author: .realthree

entry: A mysterious aura seems to surround POKENAME, cursing any operators of polluting machinery that come near it.
author: zotobom

entry: POKENAME produce a thick sap that is under heavy scrutiny by scientists. The ongoing research of POKENAME for their ability to see into the future has led to many of them being raised in captivity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's psychic powers and keen hearing allow it to hear sounds from the future. Only the quietest and stealthiest Pokémon can fool it.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME goes completely limp while it is experiencing visions of the future. Because of this, it cannot prevent small children from picking it up and playing with it as if it were a toy.
author: .realthree

entry: Gifted with mild foresight and a fine physique fit for battle, POKENAME are deceptively tricky combatants to face. Their signature move is a Flying Press guided by their foresight, and thus is feared by many.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have the ability to see the future. They use this ability to ensure they rarely fail at capturing prey in the deserts where they live. Because of this, Cacturne are their greatest rivals.
author: odditylad

entry: Due to their psychic abilities, POKENAME are superior desert hunters compared to Cacturne. Occasionally, Cacturne will dress up as POKENAME to mock them. These Cacturne are rumoured to begin thinking they are POKENAME and develop abilities.
author: odditylad

entry: An older POKENAME is said to be a desert oracle. By basking in the heat and looking into the sun, they can tell what recently happened in this desert and what is to come in the near future. These predictions are quite cryptic.
author: entomoxie

entry: It is said that POKENAME has the power to create songs that reflect the true heart of any person it has met. If anyone disturbs its song, it will open its eyes and release a deafening screech.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: These Pokémon have the mysterious power of being able to see into the future. They sing and dance with frivolous joy when they foresee bright and sunny days and they dance with ominous glee when they foresee stormy weather.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's clairvoyance abilities are weak, so it can only see parts of the future. Because of that, many POKENAME are afflicted by a persistent phobia of the future, and they're prone to anxiety attacks.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME scatter sticks to burn in special rituals, reading the way the smoke drifts from the fire to predict the future. Offering a stick to a POKENAME will give them an anchor to read your future specifically.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is often found perched motionless atop the peaks of mountains. Sages and gurus will bring gifts of coal for it to eat in hopes of receiving a portent of the future.
author: badtothebow

entry: POKENAME scatters a shimmering powder that forces prey to relive horrifying visions of its past hunts. Paralyzed by fear, its victims become easy targets for capture.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stands completely still near ponds while remotely viewing the past. The lilypad on its head glows pink during this trance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rely on visions of the future and prudent judgement to help couples get together. They telepathically relay visions of the potential future that are usually filled with joy and romance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because of POKENAME's overwhelming psychic energy, it is in almost constant agony. For this reason, many Trainers oppose creating this fusion.
author: nowhereandanywhere

entry: POKENAME moves slowly and methodically on land, walking in an odd and uneven gait. When in water, it prefers to travel downstream, effortlessly avoiding any obstacles in its way.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Through the power of fusion, they can perceive countless possible futures due to increased brain capacity. It is said that when POKENAME uses its full psychic power, it can influence the course of fate.
author: agtl05

entry: POKENAME wears a belt that restrains its mental and physical abilities from becoming uncontrolled in combat. It likes to begin each day by meditating while watching the sun rise, which is believed to grant it a prophetic vision.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME remains completely still when first engaged in combat, as it is foreseeing different outcomes of the battle. When it predicts a path to victory, it lashes out with lightning-fast punches and wing slaps.
author: pjporwoll

entry: These Pokémon are so keenly aware of their surroundings, even while running, that some believe them to have foresight. They will rear up and open their weak wings to intimidate foes.
author: infinex21

entry: Their innate, keen awareness of their surroundings makes them popular in races even though they are picky about who may ride them. Their flames flare up when they feel threatened and they will rear up to stomp away threats using their hooves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can see into the future, but its reaction is delayed due to its slow movements. This causes it to respond to events only when its vision is already unfolding, making it appear eerily well-prepared.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's three heads respectively see the past, present, and future. The middle head often has to protect the other two from dangers happening in the moment.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: POKENAME are able to put themselves into a hypnotic and suggestible state. Whilst in this mental state they receive visions of the future, committing the coming events to memory.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME approach sleeping Pokémon and people to feed on their dreams. They replace the stolen dreams with visions of the future, often causing discomfort and nightmares to follow.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The pole it carries acts as a battery to store the excess electricity built up within its thick wool.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME rubs its gem-like bones against its fur to create static electricity. According to many, it gives great hugs.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME are generally very energetic and can run for long periods of time without stopping. They are able to sense where thunderstorms are happening using their front horns like divining rods.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: This Pokémon flutters gracefully through the skies. Static electricity flies through the air as POKENAME does.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME regrows its wool when it grazes on grass. For some reason, shearing always results in perfect cubes of wool.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It rubs its woolly palms together to gather immense amounts of static electricity, creating powerful orbs of lightning to hurl at foes. The orb on its tail can emit powerful stunning psychic pulses to further incapacitate opponents.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rubs the wool on its tummy to gather electricity and fling it from its claws at others. Though it has a small mouth, its teeth are still quite sharp, so its bites cause quite a bit of damage.
author: sk372

entry: Flapping its wings generates large amounts of static electricity, which it stores in its wooly down feathers. Flocks of POKENAME that roost on power lines often cause localized blackouts.
author: fancyskunk

entry: A domesticated POKENAME's favorite thing is having its belly rubbed, but owners should be careful; rubbing too fast stirs up the electricity in its fur and could lead to a sharp little shock to their hand.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a thick layer of woolly feathers that keeps them warm at night. As they sleep they generate static electricity that clings to their body. When they awaken at dawn they have built enough electricity to power cellular devices.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's electrified webbing is made from its own wool, so it uses minimal webs to hunt so it won't run out. Some factories use the sheared threads to help increase the conductivity of manufactured wiring.
author: sk372

entry: Shoals of POKENAME live in the deep ocean, their lights reminiscent of constellations in the night sky. They can adjust the flashing of their lights to communicate with one another across the darkness of their abyssal home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can expediently charge its Trainer's devices in a hurry because it is brimming full of energy. Sometimes it is too enthusiastic about helping and ends up frying the electronic device it charges.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a massive coat of wool so thick it can't walk, forcing it to roll to move around. Despite its cute appearance, it is a tough Pokémon, capable of unleashing devastating electric attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's wool grows significantly faster than other Flaaffy, which if not managed properly can start to impair its movement. However, its wool has a weaker electric charge as its electricity is spread over a larger area.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME generate a powerful static charge that they use to hover above the land and travel using the winds. Several Trainers have been electrocuted after making contact with a POKENAME that was blown off-course by a sudden gust.
author: alumed

entry: The flower on POKENAME's head spins as it floats through meadows. Should it get tired, its wool padding helps cushion its fall, preventing injury from a clumsy descent.
author: .izik

entry: At night, the meadows of Johto glow faintly with the lights of POKENAME drifting overhead. These flickers let them communicate over great distances.
author: tuneless.towa

entry: POKENAME love to tease other Pokémon by zapping them with the electrical bulb on their tails. Despite their mischievous nature, they make great helpers for electricians because of their small yet nimble bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME emit signals from their tails that attract Electric-type Pokémon so that they can take care of POKENAME. These signals mysteriously fail to work at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME is in the water, its wool sticks close to its body and becomes an insulating layer. When it leaves the water, its tail absorbs electricity, and causes its wool to stand on end, making it appear more than twice its size.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME gnaws on underground wiring and absorbs the electricity, storing it in its wool. This makes it more powerful and able to use electricity-based attacks when needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's thick wool keeps it warm during winter and naturally sheds in the spring. The secondary head on its tail glows brightly when channeling Psychic-type attacks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME congregates inside clouds to gather static electricity. When its fluffy fur is touched, POKENAME releases a burst of static electricity, then runs away.
author: equation8573

entry: While gliding low over meadows, POKENAME releases electricity from its tail. The sudden shock is used to stun predators before it escapes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are affectionate creatures that love to give out hugs. When they have a static charge around them, they can accidentally shock those they hug.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Feathers shed by POKENAME retain faint electricity gathered from rubbing against its wool. These feathers are a popular novelty quill, as ink written with them will glow in the dark for a few days.
author: sk372

entry: In the middle of the night, POKENAME will steal entire flocks of Mareep from farms. Farmers have nicknamed it "Little Bo Peep".
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's thick, positively charged wool keeps it safe from the cold. Its nose can smell food buried under the snow, helping it find nourishment in harsh conditions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME coils up in its own fluffy wool to stay warm. If agitated it will shake its tail furiously, flickering a bright light to blind the nuisance and give POKENAME time to slither away.
author: sk372

entry: The eyes of POKENAME also function as projectors. The way these projectors show the dreams of POKENAME created the popular thought experiment, "Do Porygon Dream of Electric Mareep?".
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME's ability to easily interface with electronics has led to some people leaving it in charge of their computers. It behaves obediently, but when the computer is placed in sleep mode, it can be seen generating images of Mareep.
author: .realthree

entry: In the wild, rival POKENAME will attempt to cow the other to submission via displays of electric power. The one who can create the larger arc of antler-shaped lightning above their head is considered superior.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's wool is extremely poisonous and often left all over the battlefield. It uses static from its tail to make the wool cling to foes, preventing their escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's long tongue courses with electricity, allowing it to deliver electric shocks when threatened. The tongue is both a tool for combat and a unique source of power.
author: .izik

entry: Although it looks like wool from afar, a POKENAME's "wool" is actually rock hard. It uses its tail as a lightning rod.
author: bluefire7_9

entry: What seems like wool around POKENAME's body is actually a mass of curly down feathers. Pillows made from POKENAME's down are renowned for their sublime softness and comfort.
author: mepp.

entry: When it gets stressed from the emotion it feels around it, it rubs its large fluffy head. This allows it to charge its electricity in case of danger.
author: skymaster426

entry: It rubs the wool on its body vigorously before a battle or hunt. The static charge this creates internally coats its extendable tongue in electricity, allowing it to shock foes or prey into submission.
author: sk372

entry: Since POKENAME's jaws are covered with wool, it will often discharge static electricity on its prey whilst chewing.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME build up static energy as they run, steadily gaining momentum until they're ready to attack. To make up for their wool cushioning their headbutts, they release electricity on impact to shock their pinned opponents directly.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Despite its insistently snuggly nature, the bodies of POKENAME are rock hard. Much to the disappointment of first-time POKENAME Trainers, what appears to be fluffy wool is actually tightly woven steel fibers.
author: something_smith

entry: Although the fluff on its head is soft, it still nullifies most attacks. POKENAME's wool is often harvested and used as a component in batteries. This can sometimes leave POKENAME vulnerable to attacks, so many regions have made the practice illegal.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME preys on Mareep, disguising itself amongst the flock. It will pick them off one by one, snatching them during the night and bringing them back to its den.
author: mistymagius

entry: The thick wool covering its massive body cushions impacts against rocks or ships, acting like a soft barrier. Just before releasing a powerful electric discharge, the tip of its tail glows brilliantly.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The wool of a POKENAME can grow so large that many children think of them as walking clouds. The electricity that surges within their wool can grow so intense that their wool can look like it is a thundercloud.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives in arctic environments and is usually found huddled together to use its body heat and thick wool to ward off the cold. When large numbers of them gather, their combined electrical field disrupts compasses, making navigation difficult.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's woolly tail generates static electricity by rubbing against itself. This energy is transferred to its blade.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It braids its voluminous wool with an incredible mastery of static electricity. Its graceful but innocent nature has inspired many an artistic spirit.
author: miecreates

entry: POKENAME's soft wool and friendly disposition makes it popular among farmers. Its tail serves as an anchor to keep it from drifting off when asleep.
author: howlingstarr

entry: The static that its wool produces lightly shocks those nearby as it floats in the breeze. Packs of POKENAME play together before severe thunderstorms.
author: fountainihili

entry: POKENAME's wool is actually massive amounts of webbing used for warmth. The soft material helps it survive in colder environments, while also serving as an effective trap for prey.
author: .izik

entry: During heavy thunderstorms, they can be spotted on mountain ridges, stretching their heads upwards to be struck by nourishing lightning.
author: chorb33

entry: As POKENAME zips through the air at high speeds, it leaves a trail of static electricity from its wool behind. If multiple POKENAME fly together, their trails may intersect and cause a dazzling array of sparks to erupt.
author: sk372

entry: When stressed, POKENAME's wool comes off in clumps, leaving behind a trail of discarded fur. Its tunnels are often full of tufts, which predators like Sandslash use to track it down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generate energy by singing, using their tail as a microphone to amplify their voice. The resulting electric waves are strong enough to fully charge a smartphone with just one song.
author: _kuke_

entry: POKENAME's wool is used as insulation in wiring that helps machines run more efficiently. This makes it a valuable resource for engineers and tech-savvy individuals.
author: .izik

entry: After every twelve rotations of the gear a small burst of electrically-charged wool particles bursts out from POKENAME. The particles are harmless, only causing an hour of ticklish tingling sensations.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's wool forms a thin layer that is naturally woven from eclosion. This fabric charges static energy easily and transfers it to the orb to be stored.
author: lucioleuh

entry: The orbs surrounding its hands can attract electrons and protons respectively, allowing it to generate electric discharges of varying intensity. Its wool can release toxins that, once refined, are used to perfume certain varieties of fragrances.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME likes to float around playgrounds and schools. They entice children into touching their yellow spheres, violently shocking them.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME's fur stores static electricity that it generates while running. However, it will end up shocking itself if it stores too much energy.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its bioluminescent coating glows and becomes charged when it feels strong emotions. The resulting charge occasionally causes it to levitate; as a result, it is often mistaken for ball lightning or will-o-wisps.
author: staghorn

entry: Entire herds of floating POKENAME can be seen on windy days in the hills. Sometimes, they end up colliding with a power line and cause a power outage.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's body is powered by the electric orb on its chest and will appear during thunderstorms to recharge its orb. If one POKENAME wanders away from its herd, the rest of the group will follow.
author: mistymagius

entry: They can fend off predators before they can even walk or fly. In the nest, a POKENAME's thick wool rubs against that of its siblings to generate a formidable static charge.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's wool is extremely thick and can ensnare any prey that steps on it. Once trapped, it lets loose a powerful bolt of lightning to incapacitate its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wool is coated with poison, which is used in a variety of inks for its luster. However, harvesting it requires a skilled hand, as the poison can be dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: When it dances, its thick plumage rubs together and builds up a static charge. The electricity is channeled into the pom-poms on the ends of its wings, which can release the charge all at once to shock foes.
author: hophoppip

entry: The fleece on POKENAME's head generates abundant static electricity. It uses this energy to charge the orb on its tail so it can glow brightly, drawing curious passersby into the woods in hopes of making friends.
author: arcul

entry: POKENAME floats within thunderclouds with little concern. Its fluffy wool insulates it from the harsh electrical surges that occur within the clouds, keeping it safe.
author: .izik

entry: It grows its thick fur to fortify the barrier around it. Those who make contact with this Pokémon may suffer from paralysis or cardiac arrest.
author: alliveir

entry: As POKENAME swings its fluffy wings about during pre-fight poses, small electrical discharges burst out and add to the flair. The orb on its torso glows brightest during its victory pose.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME infiltrates herds of Mareep in an attempt to clandestinely steal one away to eat. However, this behavior sometimes causes it to be targeted by Mareep's predators.
author: .realthree

entry: According to legend, POKENAME watches over the dreams of humans and Pokémon alike, keeping evil spirits away with the light it can emit from its tail. It is said that anyone who touches its soft wool will fall into a deep, sweet sleep.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As it builds static charge by walking, the fur in POKENAME's ears puffs out, making it appear larger. Touching it in this state can cause severe electrical burns.
author: potatoforged

entry: While POKENAME's wool may look like candy, it is not. Its wool is thin and sticky from its own sugary saliva, causing the wool to get stuck to hands when touched.
author: musicsheep.

entry: If static electricity builds up too much within POKENAME's fur, it develops strong migraines. Periodic controlled discharges and regular shearing will ensure a healthy, happy POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: When it is ready to fight, POKENAME's tail begins pulsing in sync with its frenzied heartbeat. The soft fleece covering its body acts as a cushion, absorbing the impact of opposing attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a sturdy shell that protects its statically charged wool from the surrounding seawater. Over time, the wool's amassed electrical energy condenses into a brilliant golden pearl that naturally attracts lightweight objects.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: It builds up its psychokinetic abilities through the static electricity in its wool. A herd of POKENAME can be seen from miles away from the light they emit from their static buildup.
author: melodydelune

entry: The silver spoon it carries with it acts as a crosshair aiming its electrical attacks. It can aim its attacks so precisely it can hit a target from 100 yards away.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME withdraws into its shell to avoid conflict, blocking up the holes with its static wool. It is most often found grazing in marshlands since its wool repels water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: They live together in herds for protection. If even one is in danger, all of the herd will release a powerful poison from their mouth.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have coarse, matted wool that protects their body whenever they roll around. After collecting rocks and twigs in their wool, they shed the outermost layer of wool so they can keep rolling as usual.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In combat, POKENAME will throw its static wool at its opponents. The wool contains large amounts of electrical energy that somehow attracts lightning strikes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME idolizes the Matoise in its herd, and trains to help them in defending the group from predators. It watches beyond the grazing members of the herd and will flash blinking signals with its tail to alert them to danger.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lets loose bolts of lightning from its beaks, shocking anything that gets too close. This makes it an unpredictable and dangerous foe in combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME protects its flock by firing electrically charged clumps of wool from its cannons at any perceived dangers. Its woolly back must be shorn often as it hardens quickly into a tough shell, trapping detritus within.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Pillows made with POKENAME's wool are said to remove the ability to have nightmares. Its calming, soothing effect on those who rest with it is well-documented.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's plume of feathers and large wings protect their bulbs from any threats on the ground. They spend most of their time flying through the air, spreading their wings to let sunlight shine down on their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Despite its lack of wings, POKENAME is capable of amazing flight. Its sticky, yet feathery body allows it to fall hundreds of feet from off of trees unharmed to feast on nectar on the surface, and floats back up from the slightest breeze.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME uses its bone like a boomerang, striking other Bird Pokémon out of the sky. It will then steal any leftover bones and feathers to decorate itself with.
author: mistymagius

entry: Because of its curved-out body shape, POKENAME will often fly a bit too high for its comfort. To counter this, it hardens its body, giving them enough weight to come back down  and not float off into space.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME has trouble stopping after they begin running, often leading them to run off cliffs throughout the mountain ranges they inhabit. Thankfully, their wings allow them to glide to safety and avoid crashing into the ground below.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME cuts through the water at blistering speeds, making it a fierce hunter. By blinding prey through quick movements and spreading ink around, it can take down fish much larger than it in mere seconds.
author: sk372

entry: Other bird Pokémon are easily frightened by POKENAME due to its doubled pair of wings that give it lots of air control. However, its intimidation factor is what allows POKENAME to protect the Caterpie and Metapod it has bonded with.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: This highly territorial Pokémon attacks without warning anyone who enters its territory without permission. POKENAME was once hunted because its horns were considered a valuable trophy; for this reason, it now lives mostly within Safari Zones.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It has extremely sharp eyesight that allows it to spot Pokémon and people even while flying high in the sky. POKENAME was once hunted because its horns were considered a valuable trophy; for this reason, it now lives mostly within Safari Zones.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME flap their wings to create blinding swirls of dust to defend themselves from predators. Their undeveloped stinger and small beak prevent them from using other means of defense.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's many feathers crackle with electricity, which they will often scatter during battle to shock their opponent. Wild POKENAME have been seen flying through active storm clouds to recharge and refresh themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME break open Shellder by jabbing into the hinge joint and forcing them to expose their soft organs. After eating the softer parts, they crush and consume the shell as well.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME avoid getting eaten by mimicking the cry of a Pidgeot to scare away other Pokémon. This mimicry also causes other Pidgeot to leave the area, fearing that they entered into rival territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Sour Curry is not a popular choice for many Pokémon, but it is one that it takes to ensure other Pokémon in the party can eat well. It nourishes itself on tart and sour dishes so that other Pokémon may thrive eating their favorites.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These gorgeous POKENAME can be seen on pristine, snowy days, its blue feathers radiate a beautiful blue glow as it flies. As it swoops down to catch their prey, their wings become coated in small ice crystals.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME jabs its prey with its large stinger to pump them full of venom. Once its prey is rendered immobile, it carries the prey to its nest where its chicks are waiting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a very strong Pokémon, and it will whip up a tornado if threatened. Its blue feathers look like waterfalls and contain an ancient power.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a very strong Pokémon. Its claws are razor sharp, and it will whip up a tornado without effort if it feels threatened.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: During its monthly molting, POKENAME cannot fly until its feathers grow back. Trainers support POKENAME during this process by feeding it seeds, nuts, and berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME performs acrobatic feats to swoop past tree branches and surprise its prey. This surprise allows it to jab its stingers into prey with a quick snap, ensuring that the venom swiftly activates.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In an unlikely situation where Pidgey can't agree on their share of prey, this Pokémon steps in to settle the dispute. Its leadership resembles that of a seasoned flock leader, ensuring order among its group.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It sets itself apart from its flock with its unique hunting method. It lures prey in with its gorgeous feathers and tears them apart with its sharp talons.
author: cheroace

entry: POKENAME can fly at Mach-3 speeds, causing devastating windstorms that knock down large sections of forest. The plumage on its head is admired by Pokémon of all sizes for its brilliance.
author: mistymagius

entry: The bright, colorful feathers that this Pokémon has are a sign of strength and vitality. It can fly for days on end without stopping to rest.
author: soup1900

entry: The bright, colorful feathers that this Pokémon has are a sign of strength and vitality. It can fly for days on end without stopping to rest.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have a shrill cry that startles their prey into panicking. Once their prey is fleeing, they snatch up their prey to bring back to their nest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produces a slime that it uses to make its feathers glossy. For competitions, some Trainers even give their POKENAME Moomoo Milk to mix with the slime, as it brings out the shine even more, catching the light almost like a precious gem.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can be seen gliding down hills for entertainment. It releases spores as it glides, which leaves a sticky residue on grass below it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Those who keep Pidtata long enough to evolve into POKENAME are rewarded with a very loyal companion. Its feathers are well-cleaned and soft to touch.
author: vaporvenator

entry: This powerful Pokémon emits an otherworldly energy that disrupts the concentration of those nearby. Legends say its flight can inspire visions of ancient knowledge.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A POKENAME was sighted invading a flock of 30 Spearow and Fearow on its own. By the end of the encounter, just 5 minutes later, the POKENAME had become the flock leader.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: While its wings allow it to fly at Mach 2, POKENAME mostly uses them to regulate its body temperature. Its talon-like pincers are made of steel.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME doesn't attack unless provoked. All Pidgey and Spearow fear POKENAME from appearance and demeanor alone and will give up their meals, hoping they will be spared from its razor-sharp talons and beak.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: During fall, POKENAME clash against each other by ramming their antlers into one another to fight over the best places to hibernate. Once the victor has been decided, the loser flies off to find a different place to fight over.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's powerful talons enable it to cling to walls while executing intricate combat maneuvers. It trains relentlessly to perfect aerial techniques that outmaneuver its foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME do not like being disturbed, especially when they sleep. When other Pokémon get too close and too loud, the serpentine tail will inject potent venom into the disturbance.
author: teatedtiten

entry: If POKENAME does not consume three trees' worth of berries daily, it will chirp loudly in frustration. Trainers raising one must always have a plentiful berry supply on hand.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever it sees a plate of Sweet Curry, it is filled with thoughts of winning the Little Cup. Now that it is too big for those events, it cheers for the Trainer's baby Pokémon whenever it gets the chance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each of its feathers holds a potent magnetic charge, even after being shed. Digital recordings of it consistently have a "halo" effect, as a result.
author: staghorn

entry: Some ancient ruins depict murals of POKENAME, revering it as some type of guardian deity. It fires magnetically charged feathers that can move independently and strike multiple targets.
author: sk372

entry: Prideful yet anxious, POKENAME does not seem to enjoy the company of strangers. It will attempt to model an intimidating and stoic persona if there is anyone watching it. As POKENAME grows older, its mood tends to stabilize.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's glossy mane lets it soak up a maximum amount of sunlight for photosynthesis. In battle, it vigorously flaps its wings to shed razor-sharp leaf-like feathers propelled by the gusts of wind it creates.
author: sk372

entry: Strong wings and sharp claws allow POKENAME to hunt in the wild. The red spikes along its side prevent attackers from harming its prized wings.
author: therider

entry: Many Black Belts mimic POKENAME's moves in the ring. They never back down from a challenge, their kicks and punches landing lightning-quick before they jump on top of trees to dive into an Aerial Ace.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are extremely agile in battle. They are capable of fighting gracefully both on land and in the air.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME has a gentle and magnanimous nature that encourages other bird Pokémon to use its back as a nest. Whenever it and the nest on its back are attacked, it releases toxic spores that only target the threat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At the crack of dawn, it emerges from its nest to hunt for bugs or exposed roots. This burst of early morning activity catches most prey by surprise, so it brings plenty of food back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With a single flap of its wings, POKENAME can take to the skies at speeds reaching 70MPH. Its take-off is so powerful that it releases a shockwave, and it always leaves a single glowing feather behind after it flies off.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME usually swoop down from on high before delivering devastating kicks with their talons. They abduct their prey before their peers can even react, leaving nothing but confusion and feathers behind.
author: frink203

entry: Though they may seem vain and antisocial, POKENAME are carefully keeping track of the Pokémon that live near them to act as a protector. Should trouble arise, they're quick to chase off the perpetrator, then resume watching from their nest.
author: chinigan

entry: The origin of POKENAME's threatening variant is unknown. They will hunt anything, seemingly for fun. Despite their fearsome behavior, POKENAME sometimes enjoy peaceful lives and are quite intelligent. Walking along the shore seems to calm them.
author: chinigan

entry: In times long past, POKENAME were known as the weapon of choice for many infamous pirate captains. They valued this Pokémon for its keen mind and keener blade.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The swords fly at mach 1 separated and mach 2 while flying together. They are such effective hunters that they most often hunt for sport.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Their curved blades have made POKENAME a popular Pokémon among pirates. During the night, they hunt down bug Pokémon by cutting off the branches that the bugs sleep on and carry them back to their nests in the mountains.
author: leandermalurt

entry: When it believes its group is in danger, POKENAME won't hesitate to hurl itself at its enemies, attempting to pierce them with the poisonous horn on its forehead. Its wings are so strong that they allow it to reach incredible speeds when diving.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It protects its domain with sharp claws and by unleashing electric bolts from the sky. Those who win its trust are rewarded with a loyal companion.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME forms a bond with its Trainer so strong it could be mistaken for telepathy. If it senses that its Trainer is in danger, it is liable to break free from its ball and burn the threat to ashes.
author: octolinggrimm

entry: In combat, POKENAME will spin its body at high speeds to create large twisters. Scientists have been researching if POKENAME's abilities could be used as a source of wind power.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME will often perch on the shoulders of Trainers it trusts. It emits a soft, cooing sound around Trainers it likes.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME aggressively defends its territory with its sharp claws and beak, darting through the sky to land quick blows on its aggressors. It has a frail body, however, and needs to constantly balance its aggression with keeping a safe distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: During nights of the full moon, POKENAME fly at high altitudes and dance in synchronized patterns. These patterns resemble constellations in the night sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cannot fly well due to its bulky size and small wings. Despite this disadvantage, its sheer strength and devious tactics make it a terrifying opponent.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME soars through the skies with its majestic wings. POKENAME typically guard ancient ruins where they will create eerie and powerful winds to scare off any intruders.
author: nightwingjay

entry: POKENAME has mastered the skies and soars on updrafts to view its territory. It can rain pellets of fire on its opponents on the ground.
author: elite01.

entry: Its feathers shine like sleek obsidian. A single plume under your pillow can keep you warm throughout the night.
author: ozydamians

entry: Despite it's small stature, POKENAME is a ferocious battler. It's gorgeous head feathers dance as it stomps on it's foes with it's sharp talons.
author: asyoko

entry: POKENAME is too heavy to fly, instead it uses its powerful legs to sprint across open plains in pursuit of prey. It ambushes smaller Pokémon with sudden bursts of speed and drags them back to its hidden nest.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME's bite force is strong and much more painful due to their hooked beak. Recent discoveries suggest POKENAME may be closer to what Tyrantrum originally looked like than what modern science has recreated, but many still debate about this.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The feathers on its head emit a scent that mimics a fancy plant, allowing it to hide among bushes and lure unsuspecting prey into its trap. A single beat of its wings is enough to create devastating whirlwinds that leave no escape for its enemies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is dangerously territorial. Groups of them claim whole mountainsides for their kin. They frequently clash with migrating Rhyhorn.
author: schwaus

entry: Its feathers have adapted to work efficiently even when covered in debris. They are found hunting in deserts or beaches depending on the season.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME lives in treetops, where it feeds on leaves and dead wood. The fungus on its back robs it of any sense of pain.
author: chorb33

entry: The scales of a POKENAME's wing resemble small feathers and are coated with POKENAME's spores. POKENAME shed feathers throughout the forest to mark their territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On sunny days, its feathers glow like a shimmering rainbow. In medieval times, the most illustrious manuscripts were said to be penned with POKENAME quills.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME lines its tunnels with loose feathers for its young. The soft bedding provides warmth and comfort while they sleep.
author: .izik

entry: Incidents have been reported of POKENAME using its head feathers to restrain quarreling couples. Though historically limited to Kanto, habitat disruption has caused this behavior to spread to neighboring Johto.
author: linhasxoc

entry: POKENAME uses powerful wings underground to dig through solid stone. It spends hours daily tunneling to patrol its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its wings to fly at impressive speeds. It's said that this Pokémon came from another world. Its friendly disposition makes it a good partner. If its Trainer is in trouble, it will grab them and fly away.
author: ghost.moth.666

entry: POKENAME are often tasked with taking care of baby Pokémon at their nest. This duty gives them many headaches, especially when POKENAME have to rescue their siblings from danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME teach Pidgey flocks on how to steal food from picnics. Some parks have resorted to installing hostile architecture to discourage the presence of POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are cunning creatures that love to steal picnic baskets. They train flocks of Pidgey to distract parkgoers before snatching the basket.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It takes pride in the glossy length of feathers extending from its head. Anything touching these feathers will quickly send POKENAME into a flapping, screeching frenzy.
author: sk372

entry: The feathers on POKENAME's body become rigid and erect when it flies into a rage. In this state, it attacks anything nearby, flapping its wings violently to strike with razor-sharp gusts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an ancient creature woven into the folklore of many civilizations. Countless statues depicting it stand guard at old temples. It is said that glimpsing one in flight brings unimaginable good fortune.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is an ancient creature woven into the folklore of many civilizations. Countless statues depicting it stand guard at old temples. It is said that glimpsing one in flight brings unimaginable good fortune.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The tip of POKENAME's maw can shatter boulders. If in danger, it can whip up intense fiery whirlwinds with a flap of its wings.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The tip of POKENAME's maw can shatter boulders. If in danger, it can whip up intense fiery whirlwinds with a flap of its wings.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have massive wings that are hard to tuck into their shell. Their small beaks limit their diet to berries, which they pluck from bushes with ease.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp beak to dig into marble deposits and consume the rubble. The minerals it ingests strengthen its bones, making it an even more formidable flier.
author: .izik

entry: Many tales about majestic, flying steeds were inspired by this Pokémon. It has such control over its flames that they will never hurt anyone other than its foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can quickly leap backwards with a flap of their wings that allows them to pull small prey out of their burrow. They spray their prey's fur with water to make escape difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A special oil secreted from POKENAME's feathers allows it to glide effortlessly in water. With enough speed, it can dive beneath the surface and propel itself like a torpedo.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swoops through sewers, looking for Rattata or other prey to snatch. It leaves trails of gooey residue that reek of garbage.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fire bursts of water from their back cannons that can knock down trees. When hunting, they fly into the sky to identify a good target before releasing a torrential force that stuns their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is capable of taking flight by angling its cannons downward and blasting streams of water to launch itself into the air. POKENAME is very proud of its feathered crest, the longer the feathers, the healthier the Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Orphaned Mareep are under POKENAME's protection, carried safely within its pouch. Electricity stored in the orb on its tail can be discharged at any time in protection of its child.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fleece generates electricity constantly, making it dangerous to touch. When approached, it dissolves into nearby bodies of water, leaving the surface electrically charged.
author: krivaswell

entry: POKENAME has a very spoiled nature. It causes catastrophic damage if upset, so it is usually raised by wealthy people who can satisfy its needs.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The wool scattered from POKENAME's wings is softly scented like honey. Clean sheets made from this wool are renowned for their fresh smell.
author: .realthree

entry: If it feels threatened, POKENAME begins waving the fluff on its head around. The wool's rotation charges up electricity within it, letting it release it in bursts to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: It loves the strong updrafts caused by lightning storms and seeks them out. The thrill of soaring through charged skies fuels its adventurous nature.
author: .izik

entry: With antennae coated in waterproof fluff, POKENAME produce very diffuse lighting with their electrical powers. They are popular Pokémon for deep sea exhibits in aquariums as they light up the tanks without being overwhelmingly bright.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It's commonly mistaken for a Shiny Mareep. The thickness of its wool and the voltage of the electricity it generates, however, is much closer to that of a Flaaffy.
author: staghorn

entry: Most of POKENAME's power is generated by static electricity from its natural cotton. Because of this, it tries to avoid getting wet whenever possible.
author: phantom640

entry: The orb it carries glows a deep cerulean as it ascends, dimming as it descends. This enchanting glow is especially beautiful on moonless nights.
author: .izik

entry: The puffballs it floats with are filled with static electricity. It redirects this energy into a Thunder Wave to stun attackers.
author: .izik

entry: The exposed areas of POKENAME's skin ooze a slick film both to protect them from drying out and from zapping themselves. After a particularly refreshing nap, POKENAME's tail shines brightly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: While swimming, the orb on its tail reacts to the cool water, glowing with a soft blue light. This process charges its body with electricity.
author: .izik

entry: Fascinated by yellow objects, it collects them to line its nest. It uses electric shocks to stun foes before stealing their valuables.
author: .izik

entry: When it bites an enemy, it releases a burst of sparks. If enraged it will unleash a powerful Thunder Shock to knock out the foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often zaps people by frizzing their hair to mess with them. Its ghostly attire protects it from shocks and helps absorb fearful emotions.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME makes its home inside old manuals and schematics for electronic devices. It stays near machinery, secretly absorbing electricity from unattended equipment.
author: .izik

entry: The orbs on its body store static electricity collected from its wool. Once fully charged, the orbs drop off, allowing new ones to grow.
author: .izik

entry: It wiggles the orb on its antennae before releasing bolts of lightning at intruders. This shocking defense ensures its safety.
author: .izik

entry: It flies effortlessly through thunderstorms, absorbing lightning into the orb on its tail. This energy fuels its powerful electric attacks.
author: .izik

entry: It channels electricity through the orb on its tail, unleashing a powerful Discharge while hunting. This tactic stuns prey and ensures an easy catch.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME gets sick from producing too much milk and wool, they are fed plant-based jerky to revitalize them. The jerky is digested several times, as their cud-chewing biology allows them to obtain more nutrients from a single bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It loves the feeling of static electricity, so POKENAME rubs its wool and tongue against various surfaces to transfer electrical charges.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It lines the inside of its den with soft tufts of wool that it sheds. These tufts keep its home warm and cozy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will often discharge its electricity simply as an exercise, as it is concerned about having less wool with which to generate it.
author: mossybanana

entry: The dome on its head is always electrically charged. Getting too close with loose coins in your pocket might cause small shocks.
author: something_smith

entry: Many small Pokémon make their nests on POKENAME, climbing up onto it at night to sleep. If it is ever backed into a corner, POKENAME expels a massive electric charge, standing its fur on end, and jolting the Pokémon on it awake.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Large colonies of POKENAME can cause problems with nautical and polar navigation; its combined electrical fields play havoc with navigation equipment. Its tail gives off soft light; in antiquity, it was used similarly to lighthouses.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The wool of POKENAME is waterproof and very cold-resistant, allowing it to swim in arctic waters without feeling the cold. The lights on its tail create dazzling underwater displays, drawing tourists from miles around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wool generates more electricity, and its body is more resistant to shocks. Electrical arcs form when it nears conductive materials.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: When POKENAME sees the full moon, sparks fly off their body. Distant dazzling light displays when the full moon is high in the sky may be a group of POKENAME dancing in glee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It floats among storm clouds, passively absorbing a charge. If startled, it drops its orb, which explodes in an annihilative electrical discharge.
author: staghorn

entry: The orb on its head stores vast amounts of electricity, despite its size. If utilizes this energy to attack with bolts of lightning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores static electricity in its wool, which is often heard crackling softly under the moonlight. It is known to sneak up behind Trainers and zap them playfully before skipping off in delight.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Flaaffy's soft wool mixed with Whimsicott's great cotton makes the ultimate fabric. This special fiber is used in many boots, vests, and hats.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The webs covering its nest can be charged with electricity, creating a powerful trap. Intruders are left stunned and immobilized.
author: .izik

entry: Its conductive wool quickly distributes electrical energy to its body. It tries to attract lightning with the extension on its head and tail.
author: chorb33

entry: Downy wool shed from POKENAME is exceedingly popular as material for plush toys, both as stuffing and fabric. The orb on its chest is thought to be the source of its psychic power.
author: chibitales

entry: The velvety soft fur on POKENAME's tails is often used in heated blankets due to its ability to hold heat very well. POKENAME raised for their fur are often treated like royalty and have developed haughty attitudes because of it.
author: chibitales

entry: It drifts lazily through pond waters on its back, exposing its orb to the air. If startled, it releases electricity into the water, stunning everything nearby.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME live in packs, their most common natural competition is also their packmates. They argue and get into violent fights amongst one another for things such as food or the best napping spot.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While Flaaroth live in packs, their most common natural competition is also their packmates. They argue and get into violent fights amongst one another for things such as food or the best napping spot.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It clings to the bases of windmills to absorb electricity, which can be a nuisance for locals. The collected energy powers its electric abilities.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produce twice their body weight in wool on a weekly basis. Their wool is sheared, washed, and spun into yarn that goes into cashmere sweaters, dresses, and scarves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The brighter the orb on its tail glows, the more electricity is stored in its feathers. When large thunderstorms roll in, its white feathers will start to turn dark grey.
author: mistymagius

entry: When attacking, it clamps its jaws onto a foe and releases sparks from its wings. This dual assault overwhelms its prey.
author: .izik

entry: By rubbing the button-like orbs on its chest, it stores static electricity. It can release powerful Electro Balls from its paws when threatened.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur carries an extremely strong static charge. Even a gentle touch can result in a life-threatening shock.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME can use its electric powers to shine bright beams of light from its tail or certain spots of its shell. Some venues paint over these spots to color the beams and have POKENAME create vibrant light shows.
author: sk372

entry: Its orb-like eyes glow a bright cyan before releasing Sleep Powder. The mesmerizing glow lulls foes into a deep slumber.
author: .izik

entry: The wool-like material covering POKENAME's lower body is highly conductive, storing powerful electrical energy. It discharges this electricity with a powerful headbutt when provoked.
author: .izik

entry: It produces electricity to power a microwave with how often it pulls up its pants made of fleece. It is said that in one day of storing static, it has enough electricity to cook a pack of Instant Noodles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often flies near passenger jets to absorb power. Collisions with wings are harmless, though they sometimes launch it for miles.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME's orb flashes faint light signals. These pulses quicken when a thunderstorm is near, warning others with rhythmic blinks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME draw lightning strikes to their tail and absorb the electricity to supercharge their bodies. They harness the power stored in their tail to set tall grass ablaze.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are regularly sheared by their Trainers to prevent them from getting itchy. If they end up with an itch they cannot scratch, they will continue to try even if it gives them a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME kicks its legs powerfully when swimming, easily outpacing other Pokémon. The wool on its head and shoulders remains fluffy even underwater.
author: pattybgoode

entry: The iron bands on its ankles regulate its electrical energy. When it punches, it releases pulses of electricity for devastating strikes.
author: .izik

entry: By frantically flapping its wool-covered wings, it can charge them with static electricity in an instant. When flying through storms, the blue orb on its tail captures lightning energy, which POKENAME then converts into nourishment.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The oil that POKENAME secretes is incredibly conductive, making it not only useful for its shiny coat but also empowering its attacks. It has also been used as a component in some batteries.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: The static electricity it builds up in the fleece around its head stimulates its brain, amplifying its psychic abilities.
author: melodydelune

entry: The orb in its mouth shines brightly as it prepares to Wrap a foe in its wool. The glow intensifies with its excitement as it absorbs their essence.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wool is hydrophobic, allowing it to pursue prey in its estuary habitat without becoming waterlogged. It produces a briny milk, infused with a small, energy boosting electric charge, which is made into a crumbly cheese.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's wool is hydrophobic, allowing it to pursue prey in its estuary habitat without becoming waterlogged. It produces a briny milk, infused with a small, energy boosting electric charge, which is made into a crumbly cheese.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The orb on POKENAME's back performs photosynthesis to stay alive. At night, any excess energy is burned away by the orb's glow.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are very unique, as they don't have any enemies. They are a popular choice among young Trainers because of their humorous smirk.
author: the_smirker

entry: A POKENAME's three orbs each play an important role in the flow of electricity throughout its body. The orb on its tail charges electricity, the orb on its head stores and distributes electricity, and the orb upon its club discharges electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: Its fists glow brightly whenever it throws a punch. Some have been trained to communicate in rhythmic beats via a series of punches.
author: staghorn

entry: It uses the light it emits at night to gather nectar to produce honey. This light is also bright enough to ward off predators by blinding them.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME flashes its tail with bright colors into the outer reaches of space. Looking directly at the flashing tail can cause temporary blindness.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME become very destructive during thunderstorms. This behavior is a rising concern in some regions, often being mentioned in weather broadcasts.
author: vaporvenator

entry: After fusion, this Pokémon has a calmer attitude, but increased power. It's a bad idea to swim with it around.
author: creeps_jr

entry: With its shell glowing brightly like a beacon, this kind Pokémon guides ships during dark nights, helping them maneuver between sea rocks and moor to the shore. Underwater, small Pokémon gather around POKENAME's light for protection.
author: milchik

entry: The fur of a POKENAME is always warm to the touch, though it is also always crackling with static electricity. Still, many Trainers choose to endure this static for the sake of experiencing their soft, warm fur for themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME meet at the sea floor, they communicate by flashing the orbs in their shells at each other. Mass gatherings of POKENAME can cause glows of light visible even above the water's surface.
author: sk372

entry: The orb upon POKENAME's head glows and its hair crackles with electricity whenever this Pokémon thinks. Although it mostly fights with psychic attacks and lightning bolts, it is plenty capable of delivering devastating Thunder Punches as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is volatile both in personality and in power. When the fire on its neck flares, sparks fly around it wildly, shocking any standing too close. One POKENAME can produce enough electricity to power a small city.
author: nyoomymph

entry: When POKENAME gets hold of its prey, it violently rolls while generating lethal amounts of electricity. The prey is completely charred before being eaten.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The bright light that POKENAME can emit from their antennae can shine through even the deepest parts of the ocean, making it valuable in sea-based rescue missions. However, the light is so bright it can cause eye damage without proper protection.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wool carries so much electricity that thunder can be heard from it. The bulbs on its tail, when lit, are so bright that they can cause permanent eye damage when looked at directly.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's wool carries so much electricity that thunder can be heard from it. The bulbs on its tail, when lit, are so bright that they can cause permanent eye damage when looked at directly.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's wool carries so much electricity that thunder can be heard from it. The bulbs on its tail, when lit, are so bright that they can cause permanent eye damage when looked at directly.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon flies above lakes and creeks. POKENAME will sometimes zap the water to knock out weak fish Pokémon. Those fish Pokémon become its meal.
author: themicelegion

entry: When cleaning POKENAME's hair, never use water. Instead, it must be brushed with steel wool to scrape out the mud inside.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's hair is stiff with mud. When soaked in water, it becomes loose and weak, unable to generate electricity properly.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It doesn't like being seen, but its tail is constantly giving off light. Because of this, POKENAME hides in bright areas.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The different segments of POKENAME's body can rotate individually. This seems to be how it generates the electricity that fuels it as it burrows deeper and deeper underground.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often control other dog-like Pokémon and make them its servants. If they don't comply, they get a whack to the face.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME acts very high and mighty like royalty, despite its entire wealth being ill-gotten. It is actually quite weak and folds easily.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It is often mistaken for a car's taillights at night. In reality, POKENAME is shining its lights at possible predators to intimidate them.
author: musicsheep.

entry: When POKENAME break into a sprint, a small but bright explosion occurs, followed by a thunderous boom seconds after. The light from this event can be seen from miles away.
author: frokachu

entry: By rubbing the orbs on their tails together, POKENAME can generate enough static to pick up most items without using their hands.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME can control their electricity in the water thanks to their rubbery skin and crystal orbs. They can communicate with others in their group by channeling signals through these orbs.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME produce powerful flashes of light at night, their tails blinking in rapid repeating patterns to communicate with one another in the dark. Large swarms of POKENAME can cause problems for human settlements due to light pollution.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Wild POKENAME will conceal themselves within storm clouds as they search for prey. Each strike from their pincers is not only strong enough to break rocks, but also charged with enough electricity to even stun Grass-type Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME make their homes within the tallest trees so they can use their tails to draw and capture lightning that they then store within their bodies. Each orb along its back will light up as it prepares to fire lightning from the tip of its tail.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME acts as a shepherd to lost Mareep, guiding them back to the flock with the mystical light of their orbs. Farmers consider it a blessing when one appears, as it keeps the flock calm and safe at night.
author: ultrazombie929

entry: POKENAME's tail glow is very faint. It is said that it helps guide ghost ships to the afterlife.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The fluffy mane of a POKENAME will crackle with electricity during battle. They imbue their Aura Sphere attacks with enough electricity to stun foes thrice their size.
author: infinex21

entry: The orb on its back absorbs solar energy, while the gem on its forehead blasts the energy back out. Touching POKENAME's skin can cause warts to grow.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are treasured for the quality of their fur, which is often used to make static-resistant clothes.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME lives on the abyssal plains of the ocean. There it lights up the pitch-black ocean and attracts prey that swims straight into its mouth.
author: chorb33

entry: With its powerful light, POKENAME sweeps the shoals where it makes its home. If prey is spotted, they subdue it with a blast of electricity.
author: caladria

entry: POKENAME lives on the abyssal plains of the ocean. There it lights up the pitch-black ocean and attracts prey that swims straight into its mouth.
author: chorb33

entry: Its grand beard resembles rolling stormclouds. Crackling can constantly be heard from inside its fluff, suggesting it is always brewing a lightning storm within its fur.
author: something_smith

entry: POKENAME's beacon-like light attracts treasure-hunters and challengers it is eager to face.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME can supercharge its iron body with electricity, making it glow prominently as a warning for others not to approach or touch it. Its tail and primary horn can create intense light bursts able to be spotted from miles away.
author: sk372

entry: The rotating of POKENAME's gears builds energy, which it stores in the red cores protected in its wool. The cores are highly sought after to power large devices like lighthouses.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives in storm clouds for its entire life. Even if there is no rain, the clouds surrounding POKENAME will crackle with thunder.
author: musicsheep.

entry: During windy storms, POKENAME sends out nasty Thunderbolts. When the weather is calm, they hole themselves up in attics to chew on wires inside of homes.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME is known to be one of the most unique Krookodile fusions. Its tail shines bright when it's dark, and it can see farther than the human eye, though it is still quite the clumsy Pokémon.
author: wh3reverimayr0am

entry: POKENAME's three orbs can all glow with extremely bright light. If active simultaneously, its light can dispel darkness for miles around, making the darkest night seem like the brightest day.
author: sk372

entry: The golden core at its center is said to generate immense energy, powering its defenses and granting it the ability to control lightning.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Pokémon Trainers shouldn't be fooled by POKENAME's deceptive cuteness. It can deliver deadly electric shocks via its tail and spikes.
author: chorb33

entry: Its light is visible even in space. Domesticated POKENAME are used by astronomers to calibrate or realign space probes and satellites.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can soar into the stratosphere. When it gets angry, its clouds turn gray and it unleashes a merciless tempest.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can soar into the stratosphere. When it gets angry, its clouds turn gray and it unleashes a merciless tempest.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can soar into the stratosphere. When it gets angry, its clouds turn gray and it unleashes a merciless tempest.
author: chorb33

entry: The orbs at the ends of this Pokémon's nine tails can shine in up to nine different colors. It will bedazzle its foes with its many lights before finishing them off with lightning-clad flames. It never seeks out fights.
author: infinex21

entry: A mild-mannered herbivorous Pokémon, POKENAME creates large dams by rivers. It is never naturally aggressive in the wild; those who attempt to attack it are merely struck by a jolt of lightning as POKENAME continues about its day.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its tail glows brighter the faster it beats its wings. They create a loud, electrical, buzzing noise that can interfere with electronic appliances.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME loves to ride the gentle breeze. During storms, POKENAME is thrown around wildly as it uses Thundershock on everything around it.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The POKENAME with the largest plumage have the most powerful electric attacks. The ones with less plumage will often steal the wool from Flaaffy in an effort to look more powerful.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though this Pokémon is usually docile, it's quick to clobber anything with its crystal ball if it senses that its young are in danger.
author: coooooooookiee

entry: The light emitted from POKENAME is strong enough to pierce through the pitch-black waters it resides in. This light is used to lure in prey and can be seen for up to two miles.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are extremely helpful Pokémon that help lost sailors at sea. Each of their red orbs can shine brightly enough to cut through dense fog.
author: yoshimon

entry: As POKENAME flies, the clouds on its wings generate electricity. Its wings darken and lightning begins to arc from its orbs when they build up enough charge. Fully-charged flocks are often mistaken for distant thunderstorms, driving citizens indoors.
author: chibitales

entry: Said to dance upon the winds and sing with a crystal-like voice, POKENAME has long been called an angel. Guiding the lost, rescuing the drowning, and calming the frightened with its voice, it is revered as a gentle protector.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME coats its wool with a sticky slime to prevent it from falling off its body. This, however, causes the wool to become an insulator for its electricity, so it has to be careful not to put on too much.
author: soup1900

entry: Although it's good-natured, wild POKENAME tend to have a short temper. It will blind anyone nearby with its ability to produce light, then close in for a rib-crushing hug.
author: meltan808

entry: Often found in rock beds by lighthouses, POKENAME are drawn to their light, copying the rotation of the beam at night. After a high tide, lighthouse keepers should check for any POKENAME nearby, as too many may hinder sailors.
author: merclipse

entry: This Pokémon hangs out on the shore and shines lights to guide ships. What people don't know is that POKENAME is trying to sink those vessels for fun.
author: kiddivinegon

entry: The orbs lining an POKENAME's body shimmer with the lights of an aurora when it is active. They discharge electricity from these orbs whenever they feel threatened.
author: infinex21

entry: Some say that the light that shines from POKENAME's orbs shines brighter than the sun. It can't shine for very long unless it eats something with immense energy.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The white fur surrounding its body produces an irritating powder that bothers everyone except itself. It can generate high-voltage electric sparks from the pearls on its body.
author: fiordaliso
