entry: POKENAME can see into the future. If it senses danger, it will glow brightly and try to warn others with bright signals.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME can emanate so much light from its wand that it can brighten the entire night sky into appearing like its day.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: At times in the past it has been referred to as the “Storm Seer” Pokémon. Many cultures will consult POKENAME to determine when and where storms may occur. It will often assist by acting as a beacon during these storms.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The orb on its tail can be plucked off and will regrow. POKENAME uses these orbs to slam them into opponents, causing the orb to shatter violently.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME is often utilized in restricted airspace. With its bright lights, it alerts aircraft that they are entering a no-fly zone.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The wild POKENAME is known for using gentle electric shocks to cause the legs of swimmers to tingle, but not hurt them. Be careful, though, because groups of POKENAME have been known to carry away people accidentally out of affection.
author: roxie5228

entry: POKENAME work at lighthouses because they constantly need to release electrical energy. Their bright bill helps ships navigate to shore.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME dash across the lands at extreme speeds, the many orbs along its body aglow and casting it as a streak of red and yellow to the eyes of most. When it barks, embers spill from its mouth and sparks of lightning fly from its orbs.
author: infinex21

entry: When it channels energy into its fists, they shine brightly from all the condensed electricity. The signature move that defines POKENAME is undoubtedly Thunder Punch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is often seen working alongside farmers, herding large flocks of Mareep and moving heavy farm equipment. Despite its intimidating form and capable muscles, it's a very gentle and kind Pokémon.
author: vlavoc

entry: POKENAME struggles to control the brightness of the gem on its tail, sometimes accidentally releasing bursts that can be seen for miles around. It is easily embarrassed by these mistakes and will withdraw into its shell to hide.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Inside of POKENAME's mouth is an orb that emits a strong light. If taught correctly, you could utilize POKENAME as an extremely powerful flashlight.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's body glows brightly in dark areas. It has a great sense of direction and can help its Trainer navigate through cave networks.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The mane of a POKENAME is some of the softest and most flame-resistant wool ever known. Strict laws had to be established to prevent poachers from hunting them into extinction.
author: infinex21

entry: These majestic Pokémon can call forth lightning around themselves and will "catch" lightning with their marvelous horns. An enraged POKENAME's trampling will scorch the very ground they walk upon and call down bolts of lightning to split the earth.
author: infinex21

entry: When electric systems on board a vessel go down, the crew deploy POKENAME. The gems on their tails and head are bright enough to pierce the darkest fog, and they can be trained to signal other ships.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME no longer produces wool, dedicating itself to protecting members of its flock by launching electric blasts from its accurate cannons. Elderly members of the species congregate along shorelines, acting as natural lighthouses with their tails.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The light emitted by its tail is used to deceive sailors by sending out false S.O.S. messages. When it succeeds, it lets out a blood-curdling laugh.
author: mistershaokahn

entry: Using its fine control of electricity, it manipulates brainwaves to alter the memories of those it hypnotizes. Its glowing orbs lures in targets before subtly reshaping their thoughts.
author: amiel997

entry: With a robust diet of Wacan Berries, POKENAME will produce thick coats of electrically-charged wool. This wool is shorn with the help of Ground-type Pokémon so it can be used in producing heavy-duty clothing for utility workers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME eat thrice their body weight in leaves so that they have enough energy to maintain the flowers on their head. They rarely have more than two flowers on their head at a time because of how many nutrients that go into each flower.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME come in a variety of different colors and patterns. The more sunlight they absorb, the more vivid they are; without any sun, they can lose their unique coloration entirely.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's six individual units are connected through a strange power that strengthens under the sun. The less sunlight POKENAME has stored, the more dull its color. POKENAME of peculiar shades and hues are desirable among collectors.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME produces an aromatic oil from its leaves that is squeezed and pressed into soap. When gardeners need to produce more leaves, one of its heads is detached to grow a new plant.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cheerfully dances even when alone, especially loving to begin the day with dancing exercises. It spars with other Pokémon, coating its bone club in debilitating powders from the flowers on its head.
author: pjporwoll

entry: To POKENAME, combat and dancing are the same, and both must be tackled with skill and grace. It practices its movements constantly so that every movement in or out of battle is practiced and perfected.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produces bitter leaves that have a salutary effect on the digestive system. It is often found in the homes of herbalists, where its leaves are harvested to make medicine.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found in the tropics, POKENAME's flowers have a distinct peppery flavor that also boosts one's energy. One high-class recipe consists of coddled Chansey eggs garnished with these flowers.
author: mepp.

entry: Schools of POKENAME gather to conduct elaborate dance battles where their spins and synchronized maneuvers are shown off. Afterwards, the tired POKENAME become prime targets for predators, so they cluster to avoid being eaten.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is friendly towards other fish Pokémon in its habitat, making it a recommended choice for ponds in warm climates. Its joyful spinning movements have inspired a form of ballroom dancing in Kanto.
author: pjporwoll

entry: With a flap of its wings, POKENAME spread a powder which promotes growth and longevity in plants.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME actively hunts Bug-type Pokémon who attempt to devour dancing Bellossom. In quiet moments, it can be seen swaying through the air in a humanly impossible blade dance.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME dances whenever a volcano is about to erupt, but this behavior has caused rumors that the dance itself causes the volcano to erupt. It swings its tail around while it dances, causing it to accidentally ignite the surrounding wildlife.
author: soup1900

entry: When there's ample sun and fresh air, POKENAME behaves in a docile manner. Once the sun sets or the weather turns foul, however, it gets agitated, snorting and flaring about in frustration.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers living in sunny fields where it joins with others of its kind to wiggle in rhythm. Florists welcome it in their gardens since it has a sunny disposition and only eats detached leaves and other plant detritus.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is hailed as a miracle by botanists. Its spores, when contacting plants, transform into seeds that grow up to ten times faster and healthier than normal.
author: lucasdesouza7

entry: POKENAME hides among groups of Bellossom as camouflage to protect itself from predators. It can be identified among the crowd as the only "Bellossom" not dancing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may have a milder temper than its Beedrill counterpart, but the pollen stored in its abdominal bloom is as potent as a Beedrill sting. It's doubly so during springtime.
author: chazoplebas

entry: POKENAME works alongside aromatherapists to help patients treat their stress. The aromatic scents it releases are condensed into oil that patients carry throughout the day to calm themselves down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When the sun is at its highest and casts the most warmth, POKENAME dances its most vibrantly. It uses its flowery tail to lift itself up and make it more visible, so that more outsiders can bare witness to its joyous moves.
author: sk372

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's head release a crimson pollen that induces sleep in other Pokémon. Once they drift off, it emits quiet hoots that fill their dreams with terrifying nightmares.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tiny wings allow it to float gracefully from flower to flower, consuming pollen. It makes its home in vast daisy fields, blending in with the blossoms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME joyfully flies above flower fields, performing elegant spiraling motions. It lands occasionally to pluck flower petals, which it eats for nourishment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attach fallen leaves to their body using static electricity. They have a great love of music and will join in celebrations and festivities, dancing with great excitement alongside people and Pokémon alike.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Some ancient civilizations appear to have made offerings to POKENAME in exchange for its dances, said to bring good fortune. If it refused an offering, it was considered a sign of looming disaster.
author: sk372

entry: The flowers that grow amidst POKENAME's wool produce oils prized by perfume makers. Harvesting these flowers requires building a trusting relationship with POKENAME. Otherwise, it will discharge its electrical build up and destroy the flowers.
author: fancyskunk

entry: It turns sunlight into electricity, before firing off bolts of lightning. The darker the red POKENAME's flowers are, the more charged up it is.
author: ecovermination

entry: A POKENAME tail, although pretty, can have up to 1000 volts of electricity hiding inside. This Pokémon's flowers sometimes shine as bright as the sun.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME frolics in tropical fields where sunlight continually energizes it until it falls asleep in piles when night arrives. Its pollen is collected for use in medicine that helps induce restful sleep.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It spends its morning gathering seeds from plants throughout the jungle. It throws these seeds at travelers while swinging from tree to tree.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME experiences its first rain, it immediately travels far away until it finds a sunny place, taking a ball of mud with it. When it meets a Pokémon or Trainer they wish to be friends with forever, POKENAME gifts them the mudball.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's petals pale in the moonlight, masking it in shadow. It waits, blending into darkness until prey stirs.
author: anarchaz

entry: Many parts of a POKENAME have various salutary effects on the body. The petals help the digestive system, the bulb produces spores to alleviate headaches, and the vines add fiber to a person's diet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME build complex nesting tunnels under wildflower fields where they can avoid most predators. They seek out flowers to decorate their tree branch tails before performing dance rituals to attract a partner.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sometimes gather and form an arch over forest footpaths. The brightest blooms form the top, while the weakest draw nutrients from below.
author: leshii

entry: If it experiences emotional stress the flowers on its body will stop growing. When depressed, the flowers will dry out and turn grey.
author: .izik

entry: The blossoms on a POKENAME are made of steel petals that chime eerily in the wind. Farmers believe hearing them is a sign to abandon the land.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A fighting POKENAME is beautiful to behold. Adjusting its position with rhythmic wingbeats, POKENAME choreographs each graceful attack to land in time with its dance.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: The hollow clacking of POKENAME's coconut-like pincers serves as its own rhythmic backdrop for its dances, unique to each individual. Its music and moves have inspired several famous songs and dances in media.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spores prosper in harsh volcanic areas. Despite appearing to be boiling, its body is actually lukewarm and can be safely touched.
author: galactak

entry: The colors of POKENAME's body and flowers all vary on a variety of factors, such as nearby soil composition and how active the closest volcano is. POKENAME with pink hues are particularly rare.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's beautiful grass coat and gentle demeanor attract small Pokémon to rest on its back. While sleeping, it is barely distinguishable from an overgrown boulder.
author: pizzarcato

entry: Whenever it rubs against other flowers, its body produces nectar from the exchange of pollen. Its body eventually becomes covered in fig nectar, which forms a drippy trail behind it until it no longer has pollen to convert into nectar.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By shaking the flowers on its head, POKENAME creates frightening illusions to drive away predators. Thanks to this power, it earns the respect and goodwill of other Pokémon, which often live in its company and enjoy its protection.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Groups of POKENAME can be found galloping across flower fields at dawn every morning. Their hooves are imbued with a special power that greatly speeds up plant growth.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Because it was long hunted by poachers, POKENAME learned to use the flowers on its head to create terrifying illusions and keep hunters at bay. Each specimen has a unique, delicate fragrance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME loves to battle against challenging foes, even though it's always the underdog. When injured, it lies out in the sun to recover.
author: mepp.

entry: The sweet and mellow flavor of POKENAME's nectar is not only incredibly tasty, but it also seems to have a calming effect on those who drink it. Even a furious Primeape will relax after a single sip.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME only blossom once a year, and always on the same night each year. When their flowers blossom they will offer them to their favourite individual. When two flowers are exchanged between POKENAME this way they pair for life.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It gathers seeds in the mornings and takes great care to plant them around the jungle. The nectar that leaks from its tail is sprayed on these planted crops.
author: .izik

entry: It loves to dance and will incorporate all kinds of previously mimicked movements into an abstract jig. Very few Pokémon fail to get along with it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only blossom once a year, and always on the same night each year. When their flowers blossom they will offer them to their favourite individual. When two flowers are exchanged between POKENAME this way they pair for life.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME only blossom once a year, and always on the same night each year. When their flowers blossom they will offer them to their favourite individual. When two flowers are exchanged between POKENAME this way they pair for life.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are native to the jungles of Alola and can be found dancing together on Melemele Island. Local legends describe them as the caretakers of the guardian deity. It is considered to be a sign of good fortune to have them dance with you.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roam cold and warm regions alike, though they flourish beneath the sun. Often seen traveling in packs, they move in rhythmic unison in a dance-like ritual said to summon sunlight from behind the clouds.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME offers the flowers growing on its body to those who are sad. When it dances, a pleasing scent wafts from its body.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME helps gardeners take care of plants while homeowners are away on vacation. It is particularly good at pruning dead branches from shrubs and bushes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a very caring and motherly personality. It is often seen tending to groups of Bellossom as if they were its own children.
author: kittyluv090

entry: This Pokémon focuses its aura through dance. It synchronizes these dances to the sounds of nature and the music of humans.
author: keksalot2000

entry: POKENAME grow multiple beautiful flowers across their body and take great pride in showing them off to other Pokémon. They love to take part in Pokémon beauty contests, strutting across the stage with complete confidence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME produce different aromas depending on the time of day, their various flowers active depending on the light level. They are popular Pokémon for aromatherapists thanks to their variety of scents.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lures in Bug-type Pokémon with the scent of its flowers, then it opens its jaw to swallow them whole. The colors of its flowers deepen as it digests its prey.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: Native to tropical shores, POKENAME tends to flowering Birds of Paradise. When rowdy Water-types invade their home, these Pokémon call down a storm of razor sharp petals, rushing forward afterward to bowl the foes back to sea.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Where mass deforestation occurs, POKENAME appears and begins to prance. As it moves, it spreads nectar from its flowers that regrow downed trees. Scientists have found this substance can heal Grass-types in a pinch.
author: ghostslythe

entry: This bouquet staff uses the powers of flowers and sunshine to generate wondrous effects like parting clouds for sunlight and healing minor injuries.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: While POKENAME may appear intimidating at first glance, they are gentle giants at heart. As they move through the forest, smaller Pokémon in the area are calmed by their presence.
author: sirg44

entry: The blue core of a POKENAME absorbs and metabolizes sunlight, which ensures its many leaves may continue to spin. These leaves will glow brightly when this Pokémon charges a Solar Beam to be fired from its core at its opponents.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constantly challenges others of its kind by performing dazzling dances that scatter flower petals everywhere. By powerfully stomping its feet and tail, it can create vibrations strong enough to split the ground in two.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In displays of pride, POKENAME performs ornate dances, showering the field with petals to provoke rivals. With fierce stomps of its feet and tail, it unleashes tremors rumored to cleave the ground.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME may appear to be a harmless plant, but its entire body is crafted from lightweight, coloured metal that resists weathering. Its ‘blossoms' rotate gently to absorb sunlight, though no one is sure why it mimics photosynthesis.
author: eiskitsune

entry: The feather-like portions of its body are actually leaves. A tea made from these leaves can quickly cure most respiratory-based ailments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lounge in bright daylight for several hours, spreading their tails to absorb more of the sun's energy. When they cannot get enough light, they supplement their diet with berries, though their petals grow pale until light is absorbed again.
author: chibitales

entry: It helps farmers spread pollen by rubbing against flowers when it passes by. One of its favorites snacks is Moomoo Cheese, which farmers use to bribe it to stay in their fields.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its thorns to attach itself to trees as it absorbs sunlight. Its beautiful red flowers can be collected and made into a popular tea.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME enjoys sunbathing in the tropics, and flops about if it is rainy in an effort to bring back the sun. It emits a shock when agitated.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME is known for its cheerful dance that it performs on beaches. When it dances, everyone around feels refreshed.
author: pokebio

entry: The nectar that comes from the flowers on its body smells like a mixture of posies and Rindo Berries. There is a salon in Arrowroot Town that uses this fragrance in their shampoo.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME works alongside florists to create beautiful bouquets and flower arrangements. Its relaxed personality makes it easy to work with, and it spends a lot of time making minor adjustments to flowers to create the perfect bouquet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves to collect roses, spending most of its energy to keep them healthy. It will give these roses to new couples as a symbol of their love.
author: mistymagius

entry: While it dances, its leaves give off the soft scent of baked Hondew Berries. It occasionally finds seeds from an unknown source and hoards them.
author: .izik

entry: Sightings of POKENAME are a sure sign that springtime is nearly here. Catching one of their flowers is considered a good omen.
author: caladria

entry: When POKENAME walks, its 12 legs brush against each other to create a rhythmic shuffling sound. These legs allow it to anchor itself securely against the tide, ensuring it won't get swept out to sea.
author: pizzarcato

entry: Don't let the flowers and innocent demeanor fool you, the thorns on POKENAME'S appendages are not for show. One prick feels like a million paper cuts.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: The leaves on its wings fall to the ground while it flies. Culinarians gather these for their mild minty scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a deep crimson nectar from flowers that draws in pollinators. People who live around POKENAME harvest this nectar to use as syrup.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon's petals secrete a thick, green fluid that gives off a berry-like aroma when warm. POKENAME uses this scent to attract prey in even the most remote parts of the desert.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has become permanently rooted in the sand. It puts on adorable shows to attract others, hoping they will offer it nutrient-rich food.
author: ziggaway

entry: When POKENAME howls, the large flower on its tail releases a shimmering pink powder. This powder has medicinal properties, but excessive exposure can cause violent seizures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME howls while dancing wildly in flower fields. These frenzied movements kick up pollen, enriching the soil and helping nearby flora thrive.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's songs encourage flora and fauna surrounding them to thrive. It is said to appear in highly polluted areas.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME uses its bouquet wand to revive dead plants. As they work, these Pokémon dance in unison, having an immediate calming effect on creatures. In the harsh winters, they use flames in their dance, heating anything stuck in the elements.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME store assorted berry juices in the coconuts atop their heads. When the juice ferments, they gather together to share drinks with each other. These gatherings are filled with jubilant, if uncoordinated, twirling and dancing.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME displays its physical prowess by engaging in fierce, intricate dances with the fire blazing from its tail tip. Performers worldwide study its choreographies to improve their own.
author: tuneless.towa

entry: POKENAME emerges from the ground to let its beautiful flowers absorb sunlight, but if it starts raining, it hides underground again. This Pokémon can often be found in the gardens of villas and houses.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in large herds within clearings and forests, feeding on berries to help the flowers on its coat bloom. If it encounters a Pokémon frightened by thunders, it begins to dance and howl to disperse the storm clouds.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are popular Pokémon with gardeners as they will happily dig out soil to make space for flower bulbs to be planted. They have an uncanny knack for finding rare antique coins in the process.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Instead of hunting, it will lazily lounge in fields soaking in the sun's light. During days with high humidity, the flowers on its body will grow up to twice their normal size.
author: .izik

entry: Packs of POKENAME stay close to colonies of Beedrill so the flowers on their mane can be pollinated. In return, POKENAME chases off threats to the hive like Ursaring.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME loves to dance but flies into a rage when onlookers laugh at its somewhat awkward movements. The petals of its flowers have a calming effect on others when used in medicines or teas but do not seem to help POKENAME's temper.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can dance majestically in flight thanks to its broad wings, releasing a sweet floral fragrance all around as it moves. It is particularly active during the hottest hours of the day, as the presence of the sun strengthens its moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME channels psychic energy through its floral antennae, using graceful dances to lull foes into a trance. Its petals shimmer with power, blooming brighter the more knowledge it gains.
author: lilithxincarnate

entry: POKENAME are often not taken seriously due to their appearance. This only further strengthens their resolve to prove themselves in battle.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME communicate in the wild through calming dance moves, and easily pick up on Pokémon and human body language. They seek out humans who are unable to speak, and help communicate their needs with their vines signing Trainer-taught sign language.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME communicate in the wild through calming dance moves, and easily pick up on Pokémon and human body language. They seek out humans who are unable to speak, and help communicate their needs with their vines signing Trainer-taught sign language.
author: ghostslythe

entry: It releases a delicious floral scent from its mouth to attract prey. The leaves in its mouth can cause extreme drowsiness if consumed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects dew from its leaves each morning, storing it deep within its pitcher. This nutrient-rich dew accelerates its growth and enhances its vibrant coloration.
author: .izik

entry: The hue of POKENAME's body may slightly alter depending on the conditions of its habitat. For instance, higher salinity soil and water lead to yellow tints, while POKENAME in areas with lower salt content are slightly more blue.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's powerful and flexible limbs allow the otherwise aquatic Pokémon to traverse on land with surprising grace. However, it can only do so when the skies are bright and sunny.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although revered in some regions, POKENAME have been observed to do very little. They occasionally roll around to photosynthesize.
author: rawthorn

entry: As it runs, POKENAME leaves behind a trail of reddish flowers that sprout where its hooves touch the ground. The hotter the sun, the more energized it feels.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As it runs, POKENAME leaves behind a trail of reddish flowers that sprout where its hooves touch the ground. The hotter the sun, the more energized it feels.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It performs a very slow methodical dance on the shoreline during the evenings. When it finishes its dance, it will fall asleep in the sand.
author: .izik

entry: Now that the leek has blossomed, it doesn't taste very good. The flowers' aroma lures in Bug-type Pokémon, which is POKENAME's favorite food.
author: .realthree

entry: This Pokémon lures in prey with its sweet looks. It may look cute, but in fact it's extremely bloodthirsty. Its flowers smell like poppies.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME loves using its horn to pop floating tools from beachgoers in the ocean. It does this as a prank, using its flat tail to flee at high speed after the deed is done.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather together in flocks of about a dozen individuals, their large ears allowing them to hear other flocks across great distances. Interactions between flocks are joyful, with individuals sharing berries and playing.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Once POKENAME start rolling, they enter a state of near perpetual motion, ricocheting off surfaces with their five bouncy tails. They have evolved strong stomachs to handle the constant rotation.
author: houseoffallingflowers

entry: POKENAME love to perform on stage and are popular companions for aspiring celebrity musicians. They have an innate understanding of dance numbers for songs and will happily take part in concerts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's schools are often spotted near Navel Rock, where the sphere on their antennae bobs at the surface as they swim near the water's edge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to frolic in ponds and streams, playing with one another's tails and chasing each other through the shallows. They have a very unstable genetic makeup and are highly adaptable, changing form depending on their environment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often is found along shorelines comparing their shells to other POKENAME. The shell it inhabits is said to be that of an ancient Pokémon.
author: captainzscourge

entry: POKENAME forage for all kinds of berries and have a particular fondness for Kelpsy Berries. They often mistake their tail for an Oran Berry and end up running in circles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a nocturnal omnivore most often found by small lakes and rivers. It has an impeccable sense of time; all POKENAME migrate on the same date and hour instinctually.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives underwater but needs air to breathe, using a finely meshed web to capture air bubbles that it can take with it. In emergencies, it inflates its tail floats with gas and rises to the surface.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME waddle around with pieces of eggshell stuck to their bodies. They are fiercely loyal to their Trainer, to the point where they show disdain for other Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are far more buoyant than unfused Marill, and are able to trap air within their oily fur. They are so buoyant that they can sit happily on the surface of rivers if they want to, watching the world drift by.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME cheerfully dance amongst one another around forest streams, performing complex moves to communicate with one another. Their gatherings are meant to be secret and, in an effort to hide, they will freeze up if someone happens to see them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME float peacefully atop the surface of rivers and lakes, clustering together in large groups. When a storm blows through they will lift their leaves high and are plucked from the water, being blown to new homes in large clouds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They prefer cobblers over other types of sweets, as the soft, gooey texture allows them to chew without hurting their sensitive teeth. When they finish eating, they take naps to help with digestion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its tail to scoop up mud, then slaps it on its body to avoid drying out. Once coated, it will snack on any nearby brush, staying nourished and hydrated.
author: .izik

entry: Covered in water-repellent fur, a POKENAME will only enter a body of water for a trainer it considers worthy.
author: notsaying.

entry: With its waterproof fur and buoyant tail, POKENAME is well suited to its river home. They can often be found playing with one another near rapids, swimming down the fast-flowing water and scampering back up the banks to swim down again.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be found sliding along the surface of bodies of water. It is hydrophobic and lightweight, so it never immerses.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME hates it when its fur isn't constantly moist and is never seen far from a body of water. It spends most of the day floating on top of the water with its buoyant tail.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME puts on a cute display, and while it may believe itself to be acting in harmless fun, will often become a nuisance because it doesn't understand good behavior.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The ball on POKENAME's tail spins in a circle as it jumps out of waves. It races with others in its pod, creating a joyful competition in the open sea.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fiercely protects those it considers its pack, with whom it loves to roughhouse. It is trained to help on container ships by hunting vermin and rescuing crew that fall overboard.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses a special form of martial arts that involves using its ball tail as a bludgeoning weapon.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME love to perform and be the centre of attention, making them popular for Trainers taking part in Pokémon contests. They are unpractised in their movements but have great potential that can be brought out with dedicated training.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The first recorded sighting of POKENAME was reported in a remote part of Kanto. It was originally thought to be a strange unseen evolution of Pikachu before further research confirmed otherwise.
author: sk372

entry: It always tries to entertain Pokémon and people with aquatic juggling acts, but its inexperience often leads to funny mistakes and everyone ends up teasing it. When it is not performing, it can usually be found fixing its hairstyle on riverbanks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's tail dries out easily, so it regularly dips it in ponds to stay hydrated. It listens intently with its large ears for predators while submerged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of camouflaging most of their body except for their tails. Their blue tail can be curled into a ball or stretched out, but they cannot change its color to match the rest of their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be found floating in warm waters, using its oil-filled tail as a flotation device. Its body sits below the surface, snapping at any fish that come in range with its large mouth.
author: darklordarbitur

entry: POKENAME root around for food along river beds, controlling their buoyancy through the plant growing on their back. The flower of the plant can rapidly photosynthesise, filling with bubbles of oxygen.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When it senses a massive hurricane approaching, POKENAME swims toward the churning currents. It navigates the violent waves with surprising ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waits at the bottom of creeks for prey to get close before biting at them with its sharp front tooth. It drags its catch in with ease, using its strength to hold onto the prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is docile, and you can often find it playing with children. It lives in steep valleys formed by warm rivers.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is docile, and you can often find it playing with children. This one has a rare coloration.
author: .realthree

entry: Somehow, two meek Pokémon become a fusion full of confidence and battle spirit. It deftly kicks its own tail to strike opponents from any angle.
author: miecreates

entry: In many homes, POKENAME occupies a role somewhere between pet and decoration. Its flame is mostly harmless, producing only a pleasant glow and gentle warmth.
author: dylonk25

entry: The oil in POKENAME's tails fuels the flames inside its belly, allowing it to generate intense heat. The water it spits is scalding hot, capable of burning anything that gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are remarkably agile in fights, using their springy tails as launching platforms to leap around and confound their opponents. Their small statures are the main thing preventing them from posing serious threats to more Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a calm Pokémon that uses its sizable tail as its cozy bed. It does not move often, as it is always comfortable.
author: matpal6

entry: Greywater drains are often home to POKENAME, who play in the discharge's waterfalls. They squeeze through pipes to lay eggs in u-bends. When the young hatch, they feed on debris until they're strong enough to swim and unite with their parents.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's tail and body are filled with helium, allowing it to float at surprising speeds across the skies. It collects leaves floating in rivers for food, drifting peacefully through the air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live near bodies of water, subsisting on aquatic prey. The baubles of its tails act as water brakes, allowing it to quickly take off again.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME will dip its buoyant tail in a body of water and sense through slight vibrations where nearby prey might be.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME can't see, but it listens to encouragement very well. Because it can be convinced to do anything, POKENAME sometimes ends up among sketchy companions.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives in damp caverns. It dives into pools of water in search of prey, and sucks the blood out of anything it finds. The blood it draws from its prey is infused with the oil in its wings making them surprisingly buoyant.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME lives at the bottom of the river and if anything touches its tail, it will deliver a powerful electric shock. After large floods, large groups of POKENAME can be seen washed up on shore.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spits water in various patterns while dancing, expressing its joy through the strength of the spray. The more energetic the dance, the more powerful the water jets become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME schools are often seen along the coast of the Sevii Islands, where they bite at nearby cruise ships. This aggressive behavior makes them a nuisance for vessels in the area.
author: .izik

entry: Its body has a similar texture to water that has been mixed with xanthan gum. Its tail is theorized to hold some sort of chemical to achieve this, but it has yet to be proven.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: The sphere on POKENAME's tail leaks a powerful toxin when it sees prey. This serves as both a defense mechanism and a means of subduing its prey before it strikes.
author: .izik

entry: Filled with a sense of adventure, POKENAME loves to explore new lands with its Trainer. They will often run ahead in search of wild Pokémon to battle or befriend, based entirely on their mood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon is covered in tiny water-repellent scales. When fleeing, it moves at such a high rate of speed, the area left behind is spotless.
author: ggorehoundd

entry: The water POKENAME spits is green and filled with mold. This mold is highly corrosive if left on a surface too long, capable of damaging materials with its acidic properties.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME's body is hydrophobic, the flame on the tail isn't. However, the tail does not need to stay aflame; it just keeps it lit up for a threat display.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: The oil inside POKENAME's ball-like tail was once used for creating dishes on wedding nights, said to bring everlasting love. In reality, it causes severe abdominal cramping when consumed.
author: .izik

entry: After howling, POKENAME spits suds around its den to mark territory. The bubbles slow predators and alert its pack if disturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blows warm bubbles around its resting pack at night. The bubbles trap heat, keeping its allies comfortable while they sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunt for aquatic Pokémon by dipping their tail into water. Once they feel a fish Pokémon bite, they are reeled in with a zigzag motion to tire them out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are superb aquatic hunters that love to eat fish Pokémon. They are capable of chasing prey up rivers to secure their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although they typically eat various nuts and fruits, POKENAME are omnivores and may sometimes go after small Pokémon. They live by the water's edge, and are surprisingly adept and swift swimmers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spends its days eating oak leaves. If threatened, it spits jets of water at predators, the pressure depending on how much it has eaten.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME strolls through cornfields, watering crops it deems dry. At night, it burrows halfway into the soil, turning slowly as it sleeps to gauge the ground's nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: With their large ears, POKENAME hop across the ground listening for Bug-type Pokémon just beneath the soil. Once they find a target, they let out a screech to disorient it and Water Gun to soften the dirt. Then, they dig up their prize.
author: chibitales

entry: Flocks of POKENAME blow bubbles to startle beachgoers into dropping food. They swoop in to snatch the spoils before flying off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have small hairs on their legs that help them cling to the water's surface. Their rotund bodies can cause other Pokémon to mistake them for a floating Oran Berry and try to eat them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rub their bulbous behinds against trees to release pheromones that attract other Bug-type Pokémon. Once a sufficiently large group has gathered, they swarm through a forest to collectively grab every berry in the vicinity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body can emit fragrances that can attract or repel other Pokémon. It is diurnal in nature and could thrive almost anywhere, but it typically stays near other Volbeat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are made out of a muddy substance that resembles lapis lazuli. Their soft bodies are the perfect place for seeds to grow, so they often try to convince bird Pokémon to help them remove seeds from their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sleeps by curling near the shore and using the heavy ball on its tail as an anchor, preventing it from drifting away. Children in riverside towns are often accompanied by this Pokémon, as its tail can ward off minor currents.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME regularly gnaws at its ball-like tail if it has a toothache. This soothes it and helps ease the discomfort until the ache subsides.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME train by punching against trees and rocks with their sturdy hands. When they are in life-threatening situations, they can employ the use of their round tail as a third limb to punch with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are only really active when playing with others. Even then, they prefer using their psychic powers to play while they loaf around.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME's hydro-resistant fur allows it to dry off easily when exiting water. When it's not swimming, it feasts on berries to its hearts content.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME's bones have protruded its skin, causing its zombified-like appearance. POKENAME uses its spiked tail to bash its foes.
author: soup1900

entry: Angered at its skinning, it has evolved to be able to use its own tail as a club to defend itself. If you see one charging towards you, run.
author: soup1900

entry: Although it typically lives deep in freshwater reservoirs, POKENAME can still tread on land. It has incredible latent power; POKENAME that have reached peak performance are said to be able to kick through any material.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME trains by rhythmically punching the surface of ponds, creating ripples that echo across the water. Its gentle demeanor masks a precise and powerful fighting style.
author: mgfox_66676

entry: This Pokémon's adorable features make it a popular pet. However, POKENAME unwittingly breaks glass containers with its horn as it frolics in water.
author: ziggaway

entry: It wiggles its ears back and forth to store energy. Once it has enough power, it will propel its body with enough force to scale a waterfall.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are friendly and very curious Pokémon, often taking an interest in passing Trainers. They delight in showing Trainers their favourite places to eat and rest, leading them to seemingly random areas in the forests they live in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME perform at circuses as comedy firefighters, bouncing around the circus ring and getting in one another's way in humorous ways. Their popularity has been waning in recent years with many people finding them unnerving rather than funny.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME perform at circuses as comedy firefighters, bouncing around the circus ring and getting in one another's way in humorous ways. Their popularity has been waning in recent years with many people finding them unnerving rather than funny.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are a common sight in the theatre industry thanks to their love of performing. They can memorise entire scripts and routines on their very first read through, making them the perfect stage performers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME help lifeguards ensure everyone is staying safe. Their shell is easy to hold onto, which makes it easier to save drowning swimmers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have very fluffy and water repellent fur. When submerged in water, it captures air bubbles that are brought underwater with it. They use these bubbles to aid in buoyancy when swimming.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have very fluffy and water repellent fur. When submerged in water, it captures air bubbles that are brought underwater with it. They use these bubbles to aid in buoyancy when swimming.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Whenever POKENAME spends time in the water, it creates fire-filled bubbles from the flames stored in its body. The waters of the rivers and lakes where it lives can reach over 1,400 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: beatdoof

entry: The shell on its body makes it hard for POKENAME to properly swim in strong currents. It has resorted to tumbling along the sandy bottoms instead.
author: captainzscourge

entry: POKENAME protects arctic seas, creating bubbles along the water's surface then rapidly chilling them to create foundations for new glaciers. If it witneses melting glaciers, it will cast down blizzads across the area to chill them again.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME live beside waterfalls, climbing the rockfaces behind the falls and using the rushing water to mask their movements. They have powerful legs that can spring them through the air, letting them traverse cliff faces with ease.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though it possesses a misleadingly joyful demeanor, POKENAME uses its sensitive ears to constantly seek out prey. It flies silently with its four wings over lakebeds and rivers, deftly diving down to catch prey from the water beneath.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME flies silently throughout the night seeking prey. It often hunts around lakes, where it can fly close to the water and uses its blue skin to act as camouflage.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: In heavy rainfall seasons, POKENAME is often seen dancing happily in rivers. A folk legend claims it will dance so long that the rain never ends, over-watering crops and causing famine.
author: beatdoof

entry: It has the ability to roll its body into a ball and bounce across the water's surface. If it bounces for too long, it will get severe motion sickness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have floats attached to their tails that they can control the buoyancy of, enabling them to return to the surface of the water in seconds if they need to. They are a popular companion of lifeguards and are trained to rescue drowning people.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME cluster in mountain streams and will entertain one another by imitating other forest Pokémon. They will freeze up and pretend to be trees should a person walk by, but their bright blue colour makes their disguise obvious.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love to watch other Pokémon battle, floating above Trainer schools they make high-pitched cheering squeaks. When they see a particularly exciting battle they wave their fluffy hands quickly to signal their joy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love to watch other Pokémon battle, floating above Trainer schools they make high-pitched cheering squeaks. When they see a particularly exciting battle they wave their fluffy hands quickly to signal their joy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The sticky slime that covers its body smells like mint. There is an energy drink made in Celadon City that uses it as a main ingredient.
author: .izik

entry: It spends a great amount of time cleaning mud and dirt off of its body. It has trouble sleeping if even a single ounce is on its fur.
author: .izik

entry: Their powerful eyes, sense of hearing, and waterproof feathers allow POKENAME to fly even in extreme downpours at night. Around 15 POKENAME serve under a Honchkrow fusion.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME loves to blow soap bubbles before popping them with its sharp claws. If threatened, POKENAME will splash soap into its opponent's eyes before escaping.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The bubbles along POKENAME's body change color depending on how they attack. The bubbles turn red before POKENAME spray scalding water, black before they spray ink, and white when they finally rest.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are often found playing in fountains and ponds, blowing colorful bubbles out of its trunk at passersby.
author: inksans201x

entry: While POKENAME always behaves cute and silly, when in possession of a Light Ball, POKENAME causes havoc by turning its playfulness into terror.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME controls its lake through its Makrow enforcers and its powerful hearing, which helps it anticipate plots against it. It loves entertaining baby Pokémon with bubble tricks, but will only show this side among its most trusted allies.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's palms are coated in soapy oils, which allow POKENAME to freely make spinning razor bubbles as it attacks. These bubbles can cut down to bone.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Known for their superb hearing, POKENAME are capable of detecting the electric impulses of Pokémon on riverbed floors.
author: nelluc27

entry: POKENAME live in and amongst water lilies, using their leaves as platforms on which to play with one another on. Flowers bloom on their bodies, the colour of the petals depending on the plants they eat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Emerging from the water in a surrounded by bubbles, POKENAME slowly drifts at night in search of purpose. It creates solid bubbles that cast down shadows to try and pull people back into the water with it.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When diving, POKENAME keeps its ears above the water to listen for danger. If it hears the sound of an aerial hunter swooping down, it leaps out of the water and knocks the attacker out with the heavy ball on its tail.
author: sk372

entry: In the wild, POKENAME are highly motivated by self-improvement and can often be found in sparring pairs. When training alone, POKENAME will spend large stretches of time in meditation and self-reflection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In the wild, POKENAME are highly motivated by self-improvement and can often be found in sparring pairs. When training alone, POKENAME will spend large stretches of time in meditation and self-reflection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In the wild, POKENAME are highly motivated by self-improvement and can often be found in sparring pairs. When training alone, POKENAME will spend large stretches of time in meditation and self-reflection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swim by creating a raft of bubbles around the base of their flower, lifting themselves up and floating with the current. Smaller Pokémon will sometimes hitch a ride on a passing POKENAME, relaxing on their back.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Wild POKENAME wait in lakes, camouflaged in the water, listening for potential prey. Should anything step into POKENAME's lake, they'll be attacked by its giant jaws with huge strength.
author: bringmeadream_

entry: The devastating power of POKENAME comes from internal pressurized water aiding its overall muscles. Its physical attacks can level their surroundings and form even lakes.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Known to roam beaches at night, POKENAME usually frightens tourists as it enjoys a cool night swim.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Some say POKENAME guides the spirits of those who drowned into the afterlife. Its long ears can hear even the faintest of noises within strong rivers, enabling it to find those who've passed easily.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Due to the high amount of air in its body, POKENAME has trouble staying underwater. When a POKENAME sleeps, it slowly rises to the ocean's surface.
author: .izik

entry: Some believe life preservers were designed based on the ring around POKENAME's torso. It appears during great disasters at sea, using its powers to keep survivors afloat and carry them to safety.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME views it as its royal duty to cheer up nearby Pokémon when they are feeling sad. It often does this by performing a silly dance.
author: regula

entry: POKENAME functions as a Pokémon multi-tool for explorers. It can be used as a club, a auditory sensor, and an underwater air bubble dispenser.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME lives in an alternate world mirrored across the surface of water. Any poor fool caught in its grasp is dragged into its world and never seen again.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It cheerfully prances through puddles, kept dry by its fur boots. In battle, it fights in tandem with its tail in a wildly unpredictable dance.
author: miecreates

entry: A cautious Pokémon, POKENAME would rather flee than fight. Its strong legs allow it to swim at speeds up to 60 mph, but it can also land powerful kicks if cornered.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are graceful yet cautious, sensing faint movements with their long ears. Gentle and caring, they are skilled swimmers rushing to aid drowning Pokémon. Often found near rivers, they groom their ears obsessively and strike fiercely if dirtied.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME's incredible power makes it a Pokémon with few rivals or weaknesses. However, it is merely a friendly creature that is kind to almost everyone, only fighting when absolutely necessary.
author: altius

entry: POKENAME uses its agility and amazing hearing to quickly detect and react to any possible threat at alarming speeds. This makes it very difficult to spot in the wild.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: While its bubbles are frail, they will regenerate right away. When relaxing, it uses its bubbles like a pool float to drift in the water.
author: typhloquil

entry: When overburdened with bubbles, it can shed them from it's body. This has been known to trap small Pokémon, and larger specimens can even trap people.
author: wyattwintersoul

entry: Despite its cute appearance, POKENAME is an impervious opponent. It joyfully rolls around the field, flattening anything in its path.
author: togetik

entry: POKENAME is an indispensable resource in childcare centers and Pokémon orphanages. An unassuming, cute bulwark against anything that threatens the children. Its Aqua Jet can fly at speeds beyond that of an advanced military jet.
author: beatdoof

entry: After being fused, its personality becomes shockingly passive. This is usually fused as a safer way to raise Deino.
author: blitzydragon

entry: The two heads of POKENAME struggle when it comes to sharing food but they never get aggressive. It's still ideal to provide each head with its own food bowl.
author: blitzydragon

entry: Its hyperactive and is always found either bouncing the ball on its tail, or flailing its arms. Whenever a Pokémon nearby starts drowning, POKENAME will rush quickly to help.
author: markusknight

entry: Blubber from POKENAME was once used to create lamp oil in times long past. While it burns brightly, it is consumed quickly by a flame.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME submerges itself in the muddy edges of ponds and lakes so it can eat its fill of moist soil every day. If bothered, it spits a stream of muddy water to deter its opposition.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's ears can hear the heartbeats of living beings from far away. It will prioritize those with strong heartbeats when it searches for blood to nourish itself.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It creates bubbles to adorn its body when dancing and showing off to mates. It also uses these dances in battle, hoping to mesmerize foes into leaving it alone.
author: hophoppip

entry: While POKENAME may look cute with its little bubble-blowing burping, these bubbles contain a smelly gas that will assault the senses.
author: musicsheep.

entry: While they may look like soap bubbles, make no mistake. The bubbles created by POKENAME are made of toxic gases that can induce nausea when they pop.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME bounce along bubbles floating atop forest lakes. If they're startled, they will disappear in a flurry of popping bubbles, appearing to pop out of existence themselves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME sinks its heavy body to the bottom of lakes, finding relaxation at the deepest depths. It behaves sluggishly if it spends too much time out of the water.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are bold Pokémon that show a complete lack of fear in the wilderness. They make for excellent traveling companions, warding off dangerous Pokémon while also foraging for food and water for their Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is known to partake in playful water games and uses its buoyant tail to effortlessly float on the water's surface.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Its long antennae are remarkably sensitive, allowing it to detect and identify muffled sounds made by different deep-sea creatures. This compensates for its poor vision, which is exacerbated by the small size of its face.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: Despite POKENAME's short and bulky stature, it can hop and skip around at unexpectedly fast speeds if it detects anything bad with its surprisingly sharp senses. The pink egg it carries is said to bring everlasting happiness to anyone who eats it.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME ride along the waves, creating bubbles and hiding among the foam. It is said that encountering an POKENAME while surfing is a sure sign that love is on the way.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Three heads poke out of a frozen ice block POKENAME inhabits. Playful by nature, it greets others by showering them with three streams of chilly bubbles blown from each mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has such powerful legs that it can swim upstream against raging waterfalls without tiring. It's known to enchant onlookers on the riverbank by creating dazzling displays of steam, formed from the combination of its Water and Fire-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's attentive ears could sense motion in nearby bodies of water. If it senses anyone drowning, it will immediately go to rescue them.
author: noel5229

entry: Sinnoh researchers managed to resurrect fossils of their native Hisuian Electrodes after the regional form went extinct, resulting in POKENAME. The petrification process has altered them to be physically hardier than their extinct counterparts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though POKENAME's body resembles seeds, it is made entirely of stone. In the rain, its rocky surface turns muddy, so it avoids water whenever possible.
author: .izik

entry: When it snoozes deep in the forest, other smaller Pokémon nest or feed among POKENAME's foliage. Its resilient hide means it doesn't even notice the extra company most times.
author: sk372

entry: Young Bonsly are allowed to ride in POKENAME's pouch to feel safe and content. Though POKENAME tends to stay perfectly still, anyone approaching the child aggressively will find themselves slapped rather hard and suddenly.
author: sk372

entry: Though it prefers to spend time standing as still, POKENAME possesses strong parental instincts towards Bonsly. Those agitating the children find themselves struck hard from behind, yet POKENAME appears to never have moved...
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are seen active and smiling on summer days, drinking from flowers, but will freeze if approached. Come too close, and they release spores.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Rather than remaining rigid like Sudowoodo, POKENAME mimics realistic tree motions such as swaying with the breeze and seasonal color changes. It still has trouble convincing onlookers it is a tree, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tries to remain stationary most of its life, but the orbs growing on its limbs have a sweet scent and taste that attracts insects. It often has to shake the bugs off and relocate several times a week.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its serrated fangs to slowly nibble away at tree bark. However, because it eats so slowly, other Pokémon are often fooled into thinking POKENAME is just another tree.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME love nothing more than slamming into objects. While the large green bulbs on their body might look like greenery, they are in fact orbs of rock-hard muscle, leaving Trainers to call these hot-headed Pokémon 'Cannonballs of the Forest'.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME often pretends to be a fallen log drifting on the water's surface to hide from predators. It dwells quietly in lakes, avoiding conflict while patiently storing the energy it needs to evolve.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This fusion is popular in rural areas, as the body emerges every hour to the second and emits a cooing sound. Occasionally, it also lives in forests.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is a popular fusion for collectors of luxury furniture. It perfectly complements rather old-fashioned rooms and doesn't need to move.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME uses it antennae to detect small changes in the weather. Its green leaves can be soaked in water to create a tea that is extremely bitter, but has a nice, earthy flavor.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME often have a perturbed expression because they are in constant fear of upsetting their Trainer. To overcome this fear, they need constant reassurance from their Trainer that they are a valuable member of the team.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon is on its way to being the master of disguise. It desires to grow real leaves on its branches.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME are entirely made of rock but choose to mimic a flower to appear less intimidating. They have to replace the leaves on their head often to look convincing enough.
author: bradlybro199

entry: When cut, POKENAME produces a thick substance similar to sap to cover the wound. This sap is severely toxic to bacteria and is sometimes used in hospitals. If POKENAME tilts its head away from you, it is an indication of fear.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When cut, POKENAME produces a thick substance similar to sap to cover the wound. This sap is severely toxic to bacteria and is sometimes used in hospitals. If its head is tilting towards you, it is a sign of trust.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It has a placid personality, seeking to avoid conflict and indeed most interactions with others outside its species. It spends much time trying to pose in ways that make it look perfectly symmetrical, but fails often.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats through sparse forests and spins rapidly, launching large green seeds into the dirt around it. These seeds grow into mighty, sturdy trees later.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME pretends to be a small shrub whenever it withdraws its head into its shell. On rare occasions, it will sometimes hold some berries with its arms to mimic a berry bush instead.
author: soup1900

entry: Parks and reserves employ POKENAME as mascots and guides. They stand completely still, but if a person asks directions and then looks away, when they glance back POKENAME's arms will point them to their destination.
author: sk372

entry: If you see a POKENAME floating down a river at night, do not make eye contact with it, as it will try to coax you onto its boat to the afterlife.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The Sudowoodo on top of POKENAME's back is often unable to move. It is sometimes heard crying for help as it serves as protection from the rain.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The orbs on its antlers are attuned to wind and weather, letting it know when precipitation is imminent so it can seek shelter. Like a Sawsbuck, these orbs change color with the season.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is adamant about keeping its tree aesthetic. It selects the most crooked branches to put on its hat.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME cares for the tree it lives on throughout its entire life, alongside the other members of its family. Because it is very shy, if it spots a human it freezes completely, pretending to be made of wood.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The camouflage pattern on POKENAME helps it blend into forests better. It doesn't like the winter because the pattern stays green.
author: birchbot

entry: Due to its ability to change color, POKENAME can more easily blend in with its surroundings and the changing seasons. This causes it to gain the ire of jealous Sudowoodo in the wild.
author: sk372

entry: A thick green toxin leaks from the tip of POKENAME's rock-solid horn. Even brief contact may cause seizures lasting for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in tree hollows, its jaws sticking out. Prey mistake the jaws for part of the tree and nest in them, then are met with a sudden demise.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME hides in the bushes, waiting for someone to pass by so it can jump out and scare them. However, if it can't find a large enough bush, it will comically try to hide behind small trees and shrubs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is not made of wood, but rock; its core is made of graphite. It likes drawing trees on walls and hides its face when observed.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It mimics wooden training swords to avoid being used for real combat. However, its composition is closer to stone than wood, often resulting in unfortunate training accidents.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Rain weakens POKENAME's venom, sending it into a panic. To protect its potency, it hides in dry caves during storms.
author: .izik

entry: This fusion tends to vary wildly in personality. Some protect the weak while others pretend to be trees and try to scare passerby before running away.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME fires off razor sharp leaves at opponents in battle. Its expression rarely changes.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME stalks its prey from afar, camouflaging itself in the trees and bushes. However, due to its fur being an unnatural shade of green, other Pokémon often end up spotting it before it can strike.
author: mistymagius

entry: Supposedly, wild POKENAME are only found deep in forests that were once ravaged ravaged by fire and storms. They exhibit enigmatic behavior: They only move if they spot another being moving as well.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When a POKENAME is caught in a tricky situation, it will try to charm its enemy. Of course, this Pokémon is a liar, so it flees as soon as possible.
author: birchbot

entry: Its coloration allows it to hide well amongst the trees of its home, to better let it hunt prey suddenly and efficiently.  Between its camouflage and high-speed hunting, few have actually seen a wild POKENAME in motion.
author: sk372

entry: Legends say that POKENAME are born from wooden dolls that have been treated with so much love they come to life. In order to keep going, they need to drain the life force of nearby plants.
author: mistymagius

entry: Instead of pretending to be a tree, it pretends to be a bush. It likes to playfully ambush people just for fun.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME hides in devestated forests to teach lessons to lumberjacks about deforestation. It absorbs the soul of anyone who tries to cut it down.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME will find a spot isolated from civilization to take root. Legends said a POKENAME stayed in place for 100 years, and grew over 100 feet tall.
author: typhloquil

entry: Although POKENAME likes to remain motionless as long as possible, its many tails move instinctively on their own. When under attack, the orbs at the ends will ignite and fling scalding fire at any aggressors.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stalk Pokémon that they are fond of since they are too shy to initiate the relationship, and blend into their surroundings well enough to avoid detection. This leads to many one-sided relationships where they give unreciprocated affection.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wishes to mimic trees, but contains far too much pent-up energy to remain still for long. When it tries to stand motionless, visible strain can be seen in its eyes before it gives up and runs around wildly.
author: sk372

entry: Despite typically being an ocean-dweller, POKENAME may occasionally swim into rivers and plant itself in moderately shallow water just to look around and explore. Unlike Sudowoodo, it loves being watered.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are confident Pokémon that strive to inspire others to be their best selves, even if they stand out a bit. They often approach insecure Pokémon who need support and offer encouragement and praise.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME imitates a balloon to try and find a home. Given their heavy weight, this mimicry is only effective on young children and the easily fooled.
author: alestrius

entry: POKENAME sits on tree branches, camouflaging itself with its surroundings. The orbs on its body are made of iron and once they fall off, hunters will often collect them and use them as ammunition for their weapons.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME dance in groups, cheerfully shaking their branches in sync. However, they will flee in fear if anyone gets too close.
author: mistymagius

entry: It waves its wings with the wind, mimicking a shrub's billowing branches. Sometimes, it gets too enthusiastic with its gestures, accidentally ruining its disguise.
author: hophoppip

entry: When you enter a forest and feel a chill up your spine, not all may be what it seems. That tree in the distance may very well be POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When you enter a forest and feel a chill up your spine, not all may be what it seems. That tree in the distance may very well be POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself in small bushes, with its arms acting as branches. When its starts raining, swarms of them can be seen running for cover.
author: mistymagius

entry: A POKENAME is very slow and often sits still, which unintentionally makes a good bush disguise. Its movements are so sluggish that anything on its back barely notices.
author: glacierwing

entry: The main body has poor eyesight, so POKENAME uses the functional eyes on each green segment of its hands to better survey its surroundings. It goes through a variety of odd poses in order to maximize surveillance.
author: sk372

entry: It buries itself in dirt to disguise itself as a young tree. It resides near other trees, both to further sell its mimicry and to ensure that the dirt is rooted and won't wash away in rain.
author: hophoppip

entry: The green orbs on the end of some of POKENAME's spines act like depth charges. They detach from it before it swims away, before bursting explosively and launching sharp shards in every direction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very excitable by nature. They enjoy juggling and rolling their orbs back and forth to each other. If a POKENAME trusts a Trainer who is experiencing nightmares, the POKENAME will contain the bad dream within its orb to aid them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are very pleasant and kind by nature. They swing their orbs to soothe restless people to sleep. However, this technique seems to be most effective when their targets are standing up, granting them balance and protection as well.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are amphibious creatures that eat Bug-type Pokémon on land and in water. When they are full, it is common for them to form to sleep atop each other's lily pads in a small stack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on their tongue to grab berries from tree branches. By rubbing the glands on their cheeks, a Trainer can force them to open their mouth, which is perfect when they need to take bitter medicine.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be identified by the distinct lime color of their cocoon and the yellow swirl on their stomach. Their cocoon releases a thin gel that makes them harder to grab onto.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It covers its body in river plants to keep its body moist. It hides in riverbeds, camouflaging itself amongst the reeds to avoid predators.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME suffer through overpopulation in the wild, as the lakes they are from have no natural predators. After a particularly successful advertising campaign, locals have now adopted eating them as raw cubes of sashimi.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are endemic to a few lakes in the Kanto region and have no natural predators. They are a regional delicacy, and consumption is promoted by the scientists to reduce overpopulation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stretches bubbles into barriers that are surprisingly solid and can withstand against many forceful attacks. It acts as if it is a noble king, strutting with a pompous arrogance wherever it is.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME loves to dance in the rain while covered in mud. It likes to energetically spin its powerful pincers, as the raindrops wash over it.
author: d_numeritos

entry: POKENAME sleeps on top of large lilypads. It enjoys making people laugh with its silly facial expressions.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME bellows noises that sound like crackling electricity and thunder. These croaks scare other Jolteon and instinctively cause their fur to stand on end and discharge their electricity in response.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can eat almost anything, latching onto anything remotely edible-looking with its long tongue. Rumors persist of islands where POKENAME of all colors live in their own secluded society.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME croak loudly at the same time each day. Wild populations often synchronize their croaks, which helps drive away potential predators.
author: staghorn

entry: Their throats glow with electricity when croaking. Forests with POKENAME flocks look and sound beautiful at night.
author: blitzydragon

entry: POKENAME have a history of gathering into large pods and floating down fast rivers. Some say you can hear "croaks of joy" when you encounter them.
author: zeeroooo

entry: It often hops around on water, avoiding the need to swim. It always seems to be smiling, even when provoked to danger.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME fly around marshes and lakes, catching insects with their long, sticky tongues. When threatened by a larger Pokémon, POKENAME dive into the water to hide.
author: fancyskunk

entry: The curled hair on POKENAME's face can extend and grab things up to 2 metres away. The tips are coated in a sticky gel that ensures that anything they touch doesn't get away. POKENAME uses this on their children when they argue with each other.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hop across bodies of water by landing atop the heads of Lotad. Sometimes when they fall asleep on a Lotad, another Pokémon comes to sleep on the lily pad on their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are superb jumpers and can leap over 20 times their own body length. Their slippery bodies make them difficult for predators to grab, especially while airborne.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attract Bug-type Pokémon by releasing a sweet scent and producing various croaks. Once the bulb on their back is pollinated, some POKENAME opt to eat the pollinator.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is thought to help usher in the rainy season. This kind Pokémon will provide fresh water anyone who needs it.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME's transparent shell resembles the egg of an amphibious Pokémon. However, it is much more durable, with most attacks bouncing or sliding right off.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME only appear on rainy days, soaking up the water to hydrate its skin. When its starts getting dry, it produces a thick mucus that has been proven to be a fantastic skin moisturizer.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME must be careful when using its Fire-type attacks. As the attacks are laced with powerful toxins, even the embers or ashes of whatever the fire strikes can pollute the water it calls home.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME gathers along riverbanks at night to sing, beginning with a loud croak that trails off into a hiss. It desires attention above all else, so Trainers must pamper it, lest it decide to ignore orders.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME produce a highly soluble pigment from the fur on their tails. They use this pigment to paint landscapes on rocks and stones around the ponds they live in. Their artwork is ephemeral, washing away whenever the rains come.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has an impish personality and will tug on the feet of swimmers to startle them. It is often spotted playfully wrestling other Pokémon off rocks in the middle of lakes to be crowned champion.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME travels across time, recruiting Poliwag and Poliwhirl from different eras to join its group with it as the leader. When it lets out a loud croak, multiple time portals will open to allow its subjects to gather around it.
author: soup1900

entry: The magnetic field emitted by POKENAME is concentrated on its tongue-like appendage. Civic workers looking to keep city waterways clean often use POKENAME to dredge up discarded metal.
author: mepp.

entry: Because of POKENAME's positive demeanor and bulk, they are commonly found in Trainer Schools playing with children. Their antennae sway when they sense danger.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME build hierarchical colonies in lakes made from long dormant calderas. POKENAME takes great pride in its appearance, with the most well-groomed member of a colony leading the others in a deafening choir.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The POKENAME with the longest and sharpest ears is considered king. It sticks eggs to its back to protect and nourish them until they're ready to hatch.
author: potatoforged

entry: POKENAME are jolly, friendly Pokémon that live in lakes and swamps. In times of drought, groups of POKENAME will perform a mass Rain Dance to rejuvenate the land.
author: nyoomymph
