entry: If multiple POKENAME are gathered together, they will begin to sing a beautiful symphony. The curled hair on a POKENAME's head will form a tight spiral when it uses its psychic powers.
author: bacondlx

entry: When finding wood for building dams, POKENAME always observes its chosen chunk with the curl on its head before gnawing or carrying it away. It's not yet known what it ascertains from this method of examination.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have amazing camouflage abilities that allow them to blend into their environment. When their head is submerged underwater, they are indistinguishable from a normal lily pad.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are massive creatures that enjoy taking naps in the water. The lily pad on their back is large enough for several Pokémon to nap on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in large lakes, floating near the surface and soaking in the sunlight. When they need to leave the water they will do so by carrying gigantic lily pads with them to shade themselves from the sun and help keep them from drying out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Female POKENAME collect rainwater in their back jaws to keep eggs moist and safe. Males always seem to be playing in the water but are actually guarding the nest, attacking any intruders with a swift, crushing bite.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME, while lazy, are the kings of their ponds deep in the jungle. It spends its time either sitting or floating in the water and grazing.
author: tigerinnenumarmer

entry: POKENAME can only see through the single eye held by its tongue, which it raises to scan its surroundings in eerie silence. Those caught in its gaze report unsettling visions.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME uses its detached eye to scan vast areas, often spotting prey or intruders long before they're aware. It's favoured by watchmen in remote regions, who rely on it as a living security system.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME's mane constantly generates mineral-rich rain that helps nourish the ground and plant-life of the areas it travels through. It spends long periods of time growing plentiful flowers that attract the most delicious insects for it to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's large lily pad provides sanctuary for its fellow amphibians. It roams the wetlands, searching for weary creatures to take in.
author: thropp

entry: POKENAME usually inhabits ponds, where it battles other members of its species to dominate the waters it calls home. Its body is covered with yellow metal growths used for powerful attacks, the most distinctive forming a crown atop its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME absorbs water from ponds or rain. When the weather is dry, it croaks to attract Poliwhirl and Poliwag to shower them.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This amphibian Pokémon is known to sing all night in its pond, which is unfortunate for those sleeping nearby.
author: zerocipher

entry: A constant stream of clouds spews from its maw. The rain that falls from these clouds help to protect it against the elements.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME uses its bottomless and never-stagnating puddle to glide around instead of walking. Trainers should watch their step when POKENAME moves near them.
author: jacklemon

entry: POKENAME lures its prey with a sinister croak before ensnaring them. Once bound, it drags them into the darkness, never to be seen again.
author: anarchaz

entry: If you stumble upon a POKENAME in a mysterious pond and give it an item, it looks into your heart.  If your heart is pure, the item is strengthened. If not, the item will be incinerated and lost.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME pretend to be a lily pad and wait for Bug-type Pokémon to come their way. Once they are within range, they flick their tongue out to stick onto the Bug-type Pokémon and eat them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in large lakes, floating near the surface and soaking in the sunlight. When they need to leave the water they will do so by carrying gigantic lily pads with them to shade themselves from the sun and help keep them from drying out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When frightened, its horn releases a smokescreen and it scurries away. Its abdomen is heavy, so it only walks short distances, making its escape not very successful.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME can rarely be seen during rainy weather. It prefers to use its carapace as a wheel instead of walking since its spines allow it to traverse slippery terrain more easily.
author: mistymagius

entry: The frills on its neck can sense oncoming rain. It rules over the swamps, demanding respect and fear from all nearby Pokémon.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME are amphibious creatures that can both swim underwater and walk on land. They can be seen floating atop swampy water with their nostrils above the surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This happy Pokémon loves to spread positivity. As it cheers, rain falls from the clouds on its body, helping local plant life.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME opens its mouth to let the stinky aroma of its insides attract flies and other insects. Once enough gather, it lashes out its tongue, made of garbage, and snatches up a meal of bugs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is very proud of the curl on its head, meticulously preening it to just the right shape. It will cry for hours if something causes it to become dirty or disheveled.
author: sk372

entry: There have been very few sightings of POKENAME. It slumbers in icy waters for years until it senses a major disturbance in Poliwag and Poliwhirl populations. It then unleashes an ear-splitting cry, which calms all Poliwag and Poliwhirl that hear it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The curl on POKENAME's head is thought to be an antenna that can pick up any radio signal across the world. Its bellowing, metallic croak causes disruption in communication technology within a mile radius.
author: sk372

entry: It lives near the surface of seclusive swamps. Many light Pokémon rest on the leaf on POKENAME's head. However, the mucus over POKENAME's skin is highly toxic.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its watery mane keeps the rocks on its neck damp, so algae grows there. This relationship is symbiotic, as the algae provides oxygen underwater.
author: .realthree

entry: When this Pokémon hides from the predators in the ponds, the flower on its back floats on the water surface akin to a waterlily. At night, groups of POKENAME gather to sing together; their songs sound like a wind blowing over the reeds.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME devotes itself to meditation, focusing its breath while balancing dew gathered from its leaf. According to tradition, an encounter with this Pokémon near calm waters brings prosperity.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Calm and wise, POKENAME spends its days meditating atop lily pads. Some say its inner balance is so profound that the waters ripple at its command, moved only by its mental focus.
author: fiordaliso

entry: They are elusive yet energetic dancers, as they hide their dancing behind tall reeds like bulrush or phragmites. When they are spotted, they squirt a burst of water onto the onlooker before flipping into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Intelligent and possessing a regal disposition, POKENAME places itself as the king of ponds and swamps. When not imparting wisdom to young Water types, it spends much of its time preening its mustache to perfection befitting royalty.
author: sk372

entry: A sage of a Pokémon that retires itself to ponds, POKENAME often amasses a following of Poliwag eager to learn from its wisdom. POKENAME is known to offer advice to travelers and even adopt orphaned Water-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME will wrestle each other for prime positions in their ponds. They will grapple and push one another until one falls hard on its back, declaring the standing Pokémon the victor with the rights to move up the pond's hierarchy.
author: cobalt0135

entry: One head of POKENAME always takes the other head as food. Due to this, the second head is always fighting to not be eaten.
author: terminatphilippe

entry: Although seen as intimidating, POKENAME are often very kind at heart, and even begin making best friends with their Trainers and fellow party members.
author: spencerrdevv

entry: The lightweight eggs bundle together to avoid being blown away by strong winds. The one that grows leaves upon its head is the de facto leader of the group.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME release gas from their bodies to decrease the pressure within their bodies so that they can float. When they need to reach the ground, they inhale and compress air to increase the pressure instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME enters cold water, its leafy antennae turn brown. Exposure to warm sunlight revives its green hue and boosts its energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME band together in giant schools for protection and generally avoid confrontation altogether. Their tails are a preferred snack to Qwilfish.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is notoriously low on intelligence. Despite that failing, it lives a carefree life.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is often found accompanying groups of Hoppip floating across the breeze. It helps the Hoppip's journey by flapping its wings to adjust their flight paths.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME create pockets of webbing that catch on air currents and allow them to glide long distances. Many baby POKENAME rely on this method to disperse far from their home.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME weaves delicate, golden silk that carries a faint lemon fragrance. This silk is often used to line its nest, keeping predators at bay with its sharp scent.
author: .izik

entry: They normally float between flower fields to spread pollen and drink nectar. When those flower fields get popular, they get sick from food left behind after picnics, such as a Rage Candy Bar or other processed treats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drift through the night, following the path the moon takes in the sky. They love to settle at high altitudes where the skies are clearest, watching for the next full moon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is blown away by even gentle winds. When the sun is at its brightest, the songs POKENAME sings are are at their loudest.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is blown away by even gentle winds. When the sun is at its brightest, the songs POKENAME sings are at their loudest.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though its wings are too small to fly on its own, POKENAME can hop powerfully and is light enough for the wind to carry it once airborne. It is always staring at something on the horizon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's wool is soft and light as a feather, letting its leaves act like rotors. When the wind picks up it gently lifts into the sky.
author: .izik

entry: The flower atop POKENAME's head spins gently as it glides over fields of dandelions. Its drifting motion spreads pollen wherever it travels.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is very attuned to the breeze, small fluctuations letting it know when predators may be around on the hunt. Because of this, POKENAME rarely leaves its burrow on days with little to no wind.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fly around with the wing-like seed structures on their backs. They can deftly control these structures, reversing and turning with ease while flying at full speed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME scoops up mud with its long, leaf-like ears and smears it over its body. This keeps it cool during scorching summer days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are found living in great number in rivers, their small size making individuals difficult to spot as they dart about. During snowmelt they interlace leaves with each other to stop them being dragged downstream.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: With almost nonexistent wings, POKENAME flies by being carried some distance by the wind. Groups of POKENAME often congregate near fountains, attracted by the water and the coins tossed within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is usually found pecking at the grass in open fields, searching for seeds to eat. As it flies, it sheds feather-like leaves that are used by some to sweeten the taste of their tea.
author: sk372

entry: A great seducer, they try to flirt with every other POKENAME they come across. They have inspired most modern flirting techniques.
author: spagalapof

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time floating between berry bushes and gathering berries for winter. By giving them an Aspear Berry, they can tough out against the frost for a couple more days to gather essential food for hibernation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They continuously shed an outer shell that is easily swept into the sky. Many flowers grow on the shell, such as magnolia and camellia flowers, which float and scatter when the shell is swept away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leaf mask on POKENAME's face is ice-cold and used as a garnish in frozen desserts. Its chilling touch is said to enhance a berry-based flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaps from coral reefs to bask in sunlight as it travels. Its wide, leaf-shaped fins shimmer in the air before diving again.
author: .izik

entry: Once a month, POKENAME sheds the leaves on its tail and grows a new set the next day. These leaves are used to brew a tea that has become fairly popular in northern Kanto areas.
author: sk372

entry: Though having wings, it does not fly by flapping. Instead, POKENAME controls the air around them as propulsion, allowing it to glide to its destination.  POKENAME are often found leading flocks of Hoppip.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME mimics human gestures with its long, leaf-like arms. Children often mistake it for a puppet drifting on the breeze.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's favorite spot to curl up and sleep is in the dirt, just under the hardiest weeds. Although it can fly for short periods of time, it cannot stay aloft for very long. Despite having decent night vision, it is diurnal in nature.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME race through fields, challenging one another to go as fast as possible. On sunny days they will race to the highest hills they can reach to be the first to catch the midday sun.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gives off a Cheri Berry scent from its leaves when calm. It prefers tranquil ponds where it can float undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME adores the sensation of a warm and gentle summer breeze. Using its psychic powers, it levitates itself and lets the wind carry its lightweight body about.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found wading in the shallows of tropical islands, absorbing light for sustenance. Its bright coloration is a warning to predators, as tasting it will make most aquatic Pokémon ill.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is easily blown away by strong winds, so it uses its large ears to check the wind's speed. It uses its toxic barbs to attach itself to objects to prevent itself from being blown away.
author: darkweavile428

entry: The plant on its back allows POKENAME to quickly repair any damage to its armor, making it an extremely resilient fighter.
author: grassy311

entry: Its nectar is valuable because it is an ingredient used to produce a vial of Joy Scent. This is only possible during the spring when its body produces an excess of nectar to attract pollinators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drifts silently over meadows beneath moonlit skies. When it spots prey, it strikes with a sudden and eerie Shadow Sneak.
author: .izik

entry: A highly sought-after Pokémon, as it eternally gives off the smell of a fresh Gracidea. It's often confused with its dangerous, odorless reversed counterpart.
author: lordkai1

entry: POKENAME uses its leafy tongue to snatch kelp from the ocean floor. It floats just above the sand, drifting with the tide as it feeds.
author: .izik

entry: Due to POKENAME's impressive wingspan and light weight, one flap of its powerful wings generates enough lift to carry it around the world twice over.
author: grassy311

entry: POKENAME turn to face into the breeze and greatly enjoy the feel of the wind on their leaves. They love to play with electric fans and will sit in front of them for hours on end.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME turn to face into the breeze and greatly enjoy the feel of the wind on their leaves. They love to play with electric fans and will sit in front of them for hours on end.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will let the wind carry them until they land for a brief moment, then follow the breeze once more. They leave behind seeds of a highly invasive plant not of this world that kills off any other plants in its ecosystem if not weeded out.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's back are sharp enough to split small stones. It uses them while digging dens and feeds on tree roots it uncovers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen floating through the sky half-asleep while their tail keeps them suspended. By giving them a Rawst Berry, they can heal themselves of the sunburns they inevitably get while flying for long periods in the sun.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to changes in the weather and are used by some rural communities as a way of preparing for storms. When POKENAME gather out in a field it's a warning that a thunderstorm is imminent.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to changes in the weather and are used by some rural communities as a way of preparing for storms. When POKENAME gather out in a field it's a warning that a thunderstorm is imminent.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME prefer to play with one another during stormy weather, greatly enjoying the rain and high winds. Their leaves collect static charge and, when it's dark enough, sparks can be seen leaping between them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME loves to burrow in iron-rich soil. Not only does it strengthen its armor, it supplies the plant on its back with precious nutrients.
author: grassy311

entry: This Pokémon thrives in areas with iron-rich soil. The roots of its plant components help to strengthen the bonds of its armor.
author: grassy311

entry: When strong winds blow, it inflates its body to let smaller Pokémon travel alongside it, riding the air currents. Once its leaves absorb enough sunlight, POKENAME starts singing cheerful little tunes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are protected like jewelry because its sap is the main ingredient in a vial of Vivid Scent. However, because it only produces sap when injured, environmentalists push to ban the practice.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It produces a delicately sweet pollen that can only be harvested by pollinators. It is one of the reagents to produce a vial of Excite Scent, making the Pokémon and pollen expensive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are known to drift along fresh summer breezes. Children love to play with POKENAME during the summer months.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its fur smells like sweet, spring grass, which helps keep it in a positive mood. POKENAME's strong legs allow it to leap up to 12 feet in the air.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can create gentle breezes and drift around in them. However, strong winds typically overpower them. They are more active during the night, resting during the day.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's bubble-like coating is easily popped, but splatters a sticky coating of goo when it does. It regenerates this coating instantly and floats away while the bubble-popper is slowed by the goop.
author: sk372

entry: It wanders the jungle at night, carrying its yellow mask which looks like it is made of grapefruit. Whether it is because it reminds people of sad memories or of the tangy tartness of grapefruit, the mask makes people cry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon loves to float on gentle breezes. It can control its direction using its small wings.
author: grassy311

entry: The propeller leaves on its head give POKENAME incredible lift. In the summer, you can hear its beautiful song carry on the wind.
author: grassy311

entry: Lying flat among meadow grasses, POKENAME waits like a hidden trap. When prey approaches, it lashes out with a sudden Mega Drain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a pair of leaves growing from their heads that are covered in tiny sensory hairs. These hairs are sensitive to chemicals and pheromones in the air, letting them sense other Pokémon even without seeing them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's claws constantly grow throughout its lifetime and if they grow too long, it will be unable to run properly. Its body is very aerodynamic, allowing it to run through the forest at high speeds.
author: mistymagius

entry: It looks like any other weed when buried partway beneath the surface. If plucked, POKENAME begins to hop around in anger, spreading harmful spores everywhere.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It feeds on decaying organic matter to maintain its compost-like body. Dandelion seeds grow quickly when planted in its compost.
author: hophoppip

entry: As POKENAME floats through marshes, its leaves produce a ghostly sound. Even in sleep, its leaves sway with the wind, as if haunted.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME has a tree-like body, it is light enough to be carried off by strong winds. To stay grounded, it drives its roots deep into the soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's leafy wings allow it to stay aloft with minimal effort. When it grows tired, it gently lands among tulips and eats their petals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rides on warm air currents, lifting it high into the sky. Its leaves are covered in sharp thorns that somehow make its body more aerodynamic.
author: mistymagius

entry: The fungus on POKENAME is only found growing alongside dandelions. POKENAME has a sweet disposition, but a bitter flavor.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME spins its leaf-like tailfins rapidly to propel itself through water. The motion makes it difficult for predators to catch.
author: .izik

entry: Choosing only the strongest forest leaves, POKENAME make their own masks, leaving old ones to fertilize forests. To show dominance, they Headbutt rivals until one of their masks breaks.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME drifts above meadows at night, blinking a soft yellow light. Seeing multiple with the same pattern is said to bring great financial luck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats over wheat fields, swaying its heavy lower body. As it drifts, it releases pollen that boosts crop growth wherever it passes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in placid waters, as its weak swimming muscles and light body makes it easily swept up by any current. If it leaps out of the water, it may even be carried away by a strong breeze.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins its propeller to swim faster. It makes its home in large kelp forests and appears to have a positive effect on the life in its habitat.
author: evilgammon

entry: Every day, POKENAME polishes its body with the two leaves on its head. It tries to anchor itself to trees, though strong gusts of wind are known to blow it across the region.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME flutters down from trees by using the propeller-like leaves atop its head. The leaves can be made into kites with a couple of branches and twine.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's positive electric charge allows it to rise about a meter off the ground. Though it cannot sustain this for long, it helps POKENAME avoid Bug-type Pokémon that would try to munch on its tail.
author: dyanz0

entry: Due to its diamond-coated carapace, it is theorized that POKENAME have a lifespan of tens of millions of years. It feeds on ancient fossils, cracking them open with their crystalline pincers.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: It pulls off and consumes its own leaves to help soothe its aching head. It's only a curative for POKENAME, however; others consuming its leaves will develop a strong headache instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time digging in soft dirt for seeds and roots to chew on. The leaves shed from its tail can be ground up for medicinal powder, but the powder is extremely bitter to taste.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is extremely timid, trying its best to hide itself in bushes and trees. It has telekinetic control over plants and will defend itself using leaves and vines.
author: mistymagius

entry: Because of its light body, it gets carried along the wind without it even noticing. When properly cooked, its tail apparently tastes like radishes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Surprisingly, the propeller on POKENAME's back is strong enough to lift them off the ground. However, due to their laziness, they often don't bother.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME runs across fields and steals turnips and lettuce by pulling them out of the ground with its long beak. They are not popular with farmers.
author: chorb33

entry: Wild POKENAME devastate entire harvests. However, some farmers manage to tame them and train them to rapidly plow their fields instead.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's custard-like body is so light it can be carried by the wind. Despite its gooey form, it glides gracefully through the air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dutifully tends to small gardens at night, arranging plants to help them best gather sunlight in the morning. It gently brushes aside those that get in its way, often accidentally spooking them with its sudden ethereal touch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts in patterns across grasslands. If another pattern gets too close, it strikes with a sudden Giga Drain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slumbers in dormancy whenever the temperature cools down. Once it warms up, it awakens to seek out flowers, licking the pollen off of them to last it through its next hibernation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME release toxic gases from their body and cause Pokémon floating nearby to become dizzy. They shoot seeds at other flying Pokémon to incite fights while airborne.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in warm waters and feed on undersea plant life. The POKENAME with the most dazzling colors is the leader of its school.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME moves across the land, its gooey body dissolves nearly everything but grass. When many travel together, they leave behind a flattened grassy steppe.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME refuses to leave its shell. Therefore, it cannot move, as it is far too heavy. If the shell is kept out of sunlight, POKENAME will perish.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME has become a complete hermit, choosing to forever live in its shell. It decorates its new home with blooming flowers.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME meanders around flowering fields, scattering its petals and helping pollinate since pollen sticks to its fur. Its fallen petals are used to infuse perfumes and colognes with a sweet, slightly citrusy scent reminiscent of the idea of summer.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can be seen with a webbed parachute gliding through the forest. The remains of silk parachutes can be seen dispersed in many branches of trees.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It covers its web with lots of bright flowers, luring tasty Bug Pokémon toward its nests. It is a mostly friendly Pokémon; however, it will often pursue anyone who damages its web.
author: mistymagius

entry: They are often seen at night, rather than during the day. Their glowing antennae allow them to attract other POKENAME as they float on air currents.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME are popular amongst artisans as they love to decorate their pots with their flowers. The flowers grow in their wool, so picking them does not hurt POKENAME at all.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's wool carries a sweet scent of flowers, which makes it quite popular for making rugs and furniture. It generates its electricity through sunlight; its tail glows brightly when it's fully powered up.
author: mistymagius

entry: It enters an inactive state if the weather is too cold or cloudy. The flowers on POKENAME's head bloom in the sunlight; rarely, the flowers may bloom in different colors.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME enjoys hanging around ponds with lots of floral growth surrounding them. For fun, it tosses the ball on its tail into the air and attempts to catch it with the flower on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves drifting over flower fields. Sometimes it plucks a blossom and carries it far away, dropping it miles later for unknown reasons.
author: .izik

entry: The nectar in its flowers is exceptionally sweet and flavorful, so it is often harvested and sold as a sugar substitute.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME spreads seeds it finds by floating through forests and releasing them midair. It eats leftover seeds while spinning playfully.
author: .izik

entry: The patterns on POKENAME's stomach change colour depending on the pH of the water it is in, going from red in acidic water to blue in alkaline water, and green in neutral. The gene relating to this has been extracted and is used in research.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Flocks of POKENAME are common during the springtime, as they can be seen picking small flowers to take back to their nest. They have no need to eat as the flower on their head provides energy through photosynthesis.
author: mistymagius

entry: Spinning low through alleyways, POKENAME searches for unattended dumpsters. If startled while feeding, it uses Super Fang to scare off threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats through pitch-black caves by spinning its tail flower. As it drifts, it scatters a strange pollen that causes mild itching.
author: .izik

entry: Popular amongst Trainers who have gained a little bit of experience, POKENAME has a mildly confrontational nature that takes some skill to tame but is also a fast-growing Pokémon. When their trust is earned, they become fiercely loyal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hovers over crops to spray a natural insecticide that keeps bug Pokémon away. To prevent itself from being carried off by the wind, it sticks to the side of barns or silos when it is resting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME's boiling body gives off a strong scent of green tea. The head, which is extended away from the main source of the heat, is just cool enough to touch safely.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME likes to pluck the petals off of other flowers to decorate its wings with. It brings the sweet scent of freshly cut grass wherever it flies.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME nests itself between small rocks, absorbing sunlight through its vibrant petals. If POKENAME ever becomes ill, its flowers will wilt, and its body will turn a sickly green.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME collects fallen flower petals from the forest floor and will often give these petals to Trainers it likes. It stores its petals in its tail during the winter, keeping them alive until spring arrives.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME burrows so just its flower can be seen above ground. The petals are plucked to be used in a mixture for an antitoxin for most snake venom.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This Pokémon is commonly found during the warmer seasons. Its antlers project illusions of flowers to distract and disorient predators.
author: .realthree

entry: The flower on its head is naturally white, but it prefers to paint it—usually with the yellow paint from its tail. It can often be seen painting other flowers, as it only seems to like the color yellow.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only live in warm environments. Hiding in bushes and tall grass, they disguise themselves as a flower to attract prey.
author: bee4082

entry: The flower pattern on the inside of the hood of POKENAME is especially good at absorbing sunlight. Whenever the temperature gets too cold, POKENAME burrows to wait until warmer temperatures.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME secretes a sweet nectar from its udders instead of milk. Some believe this nectar has very potent healing properties.
author: kittyluv090

entry: You can tell how old a POKENAME is by the amount of brown spots on its leaf-like wings. When POKENAME's wings get fully brown, they crumble and flake off until it can no longer fly.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME can glide short distances by rotating its flower. It uses its long tongue to lap up flowers while drifting over daisy fields.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME splashes in puddles for fun. If its jump comes up short, it spins its flower to glide the rest of the way.
author: .izik

entry: Those who encounter POKENAME are filled with an eerie sense of foreboding, as if it holds the mysteries of life and death within its ethereal form.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME changes color to blend with the dawn sky while spinning through the air. If spotted, it unleashes Stun Spore before floating away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME draws from the aura of flowering plants to power its attacks. Its body is so light that it can spring into the air far above its opponent, using the blinding sunlight behind it to its advantage.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME rarely lives in one location long because it anxiously anticipates oncoming disaster, especially weather changes. Herbal tea brewed with its petals is used in divination which requires reading of tea leaves to warn of danger.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Despite its immense size and strength, POKENAME is one of the gentlest of giants. It meticulously and carefully tends to gardens of flowers in the wild, and faintly hums in joy when it feels the breeze against its body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME struggles to fly in strong winds due to being incredibly light. The petals on its head are specialised to absorb as much sunlight as possible, giving it energy through photosynthesis.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME commonly arise from dolls lost in wild fields. They go on long journeys to reunite with their owner, but they have a bad sense of direction.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME spins its flower to glide through silk-lined tunnels. Its nests are vast and sticky, confusing even experienced explorers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in clean ponds, extending its proboscis above the surface to absorb sunlight. It secretes a sweet-scented slime from its body that helps promote plant growth.
author: mistymagius

entry: As POKENAME floats through meadows, it jingles faintly. Its spinning flower creates soft, rhythmic chimes as it drifts.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon thrives in the sunlight. The energy it gets from the sun accelerates its already impressive flying speeds.
author: grassy311

entry: It pretends to be the stem of the flower on its head. When it's sure no one is looking, it moves into the sunlight to ensure it remains healthy.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME floats on wind currents by spinning its flower. When it lands, it digs near watercress to rest and absorb nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dam is covered in yellow flowers as it uses its vines to hold its dam together. After it chews down a tree, it will try to regrow the tree to restore balance to the environment.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's flower gives a strong, almost citrusy scent that invigorates everyone around it. It absorbs large amounts of sunlight through its fur, so it has no need for sleep.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sprints across large flower fields, its yellow fur glowing brightly in the sunlight. If it sees a traveler who looks sad, it will cheerfully lead them to its favorite flower patch.
author: mistymagius

entry: Trained POKENAME are known to grow extra bodies when they're well fed and healthy. If a bud grows too big, it'll pop off and continue as its own individual.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME's pollen induces vivid hallucinations, which helps it escape from predators. It lives in sunny meadows and hides among the flowers.
author: .realthree

entry: Since POKENAME is only active at night, it has to drain the energy from other flowers to keep its own flower from wilting. It will happily greet any Trainer that passes by its flower patch.
author: mistymagius

entry: When it senses sadness nearby, POKENAME's flower begins to spin. It releases a soothing floral scent that calms the heart.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrives in warm and sunny weather. It flies as high as it can in order to get closer to the sun.
author: grassy311

entry: POKENAME loves to bask in the sun. It will fly eastward at the break of dawn to sun itself for as long as possible.
author: grassy311

entry: POKENAME's cryptic coloration helps it blend in with the flower-filled fields it calls its home. Those who step on it will be attacked by an explosion of debilitating pollen.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses the delightful scent from its flower to lure in prey. During the winter, the flower dies, making it harder for POKENAME to feed.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME exude a sweet scent from their flowers that can carry for long distances on the wind. Their sense of smell is particularly sensitive to the smell of these flowers and they use it to seek one another out in dense forests.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite a close resemblance to its more aggressive cousin, Scolipede, POKENAME is known for its gentle and kindhearted nature. It delights in allowing children to ride on its back, leaving a trail of flowers in its wake.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME releases a sweet scent from the flower on its neck that keeps it in a positive mood. It can be seen frolicking around flower fields, unintentionally trampling the flowers in its wake.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME appears as soon as the snows begin to melt. The floral pattern found on it has inspired many spring kimonos.
author: .realthree

entry: Some POKENAME are active during the daytime, while others are active during the night; it all depends on what time POKENAME's components hatched. Larger POKENAME likely thrive in the morning, while the ones most active at night have stronger toxins.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME dances, the flowers on its body release large amounts of pollen. This pollen doesn't trigger allergies and is often collected for use in allergy medications.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It is rumored that if large amounts of flowers are placed on a child's grave, they will be reborn as a Pokémon. Groups of them can be seen regrowing trees and flowers after natural disasters.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME doesn't mean harm, it often scares away other Pokémon as it shambles around the forests. It munches on large amounts of flowers, yellow ones being its personal favorite.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spend their days in search of patches of sunlight. Its bright petals are a warning of the toxins POKENAME contains.
author: elite01

entry: POKENAME's syrupy coating emits a refreshing, citrusy smell. Certain upscale cafes have started using this substance to sweeten their teas.
author: .realthree

entry: In the summer, they travel in the direction of the wind, leaping and soaring in great bounds; all the while they spread toxic and foul-smelling spores.
author: bobosmith01

entry: During the springtime, POKENAME's body becomes covered in brightly colored flowers. Most of these flowers are yellow, but they can sometimes be pink, white, or even blue.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a spirit inhabiting a flowering compost heap. It is frequently found in gardens, where it leaves behind mineral-rich compost that exponentially aids the health of the plants.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME releases spores that vivify sleepy Pokémon, causing them to stay anxiously awake even when they are tired. It floats between different forests because other Pokémon get upset that it keeps them awake at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME points the fans on its head against strong winds, it is swept along. In this way, it glides several kilometers to new meadows.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME shows its affection to trusted Trainers by rubbing the petals on its neck against them. The pollen deposited this way has mineral-like qualities, and it's difficult to wash off.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME love to chase one another through meadows on sunny days, their brightly coloured petals trailing behind them in the wind. When they're happy, their flowers release a wonderful fragrance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A pleasant aroma is emitted from POKENAME's flower, so long as the temperature of its surroundings remains warm enough. If the temperature around it drops too low, the smell turns foul.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins its flower to hover above pumpkin fields. It watches for intruders, attacking with Leech Seed if disturbed.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME spins above pumpkin patches to patrol. It uses Absorb on any intruder foolish enough to approach.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunt in groups with their peers through flower meadows. They pull up large flowers to hide themselves as they approach their prey.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME tugs on its loose covering, a pleasant floral aroma fills the air. Because of that, POKENAME is sometimes depicted on packaging for fabric softeners.
author: .realthree

entry: Its plump body is surprisingly light. Using the flower on its head as a propeller, POKENAME flies on the wind with its mouth open, devouring pollen from the spring air. After the flowering season is over, POKENAME migrates south.
author: milchik

entry: When migraines strike, POKENAME's flower spins rapidly. If the pain is intense, it may accidentally lift off and float away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME twirls over lakes by spinning its flower. When it spots prey like Magikarp, it dives swiftly to catch them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a short temper and short range with their fists. However, they can deliver enough force to bend steel.
author: t.i.a.

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in its carefully landscaped gardens. It cultivates flower patches and decorative bushes along river banks with sparkling clean water.
author: ozydamians

entry: A sweet scent wafts from POKENAME's mouth, encouraging Bug Pokémon to come and pollinate its flower. Enthusiasts tend to prefer POKENAME with the largest flowers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME drifts above flower fields, dipping its sticky tail into blooms. Later, it eats the gathered petals one by one.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slime is a great fertilizer as it feeds on fallen leaves and dying plants. Flowers grown using its slime supposedly smell 10 times better, according to some surveys.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in tropical areas, absorbing large amounts of sunlight with the flower on its head. As it hates being stepped on, it will climb up large trees and sit atop them while it photosynthesizes.
author: mistymagius

entry: The seed on its back is covered in a soft white fuzz that causes irritation to anyone who touches it. To prevent strong winds from blowing this coating away, POKENAME hides in its burrow during particularly windy days.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME craft hovering rafts from nearby fluff to ride warm, southern winds across the sea, flying to foreign lands.
author: gentlesage

entry: POKENAME always has a happy expression, like it's nodding 'yes' all the time. Its soft punches aren't very effective against most Pokémon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is always seen floating around in something of a daze. It's not immune to its own pollen flow, so its allergies leave its heads constantly feeling heavy and stuffy.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME leaps out of the rivers it calls home, it flings out one of the pollen orbs on its tail towards the river-line. The pollen aids in plant growth, so rivers with POKENAME in it tend to be bordered by plenty of robust, colorful flowers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grow thick plant fibers from the horns on their head. They trap prey and berries with the tangled fluff.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME are subject to the caprice of the weather and can be whisked away at a moment's notice. Sometimes they transform into bird Pokémon to control their flight, but they cannot maintain that form for long.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME thrives in storms. Using its ability to become and travel through water, it climbs raindrops high into the sky and rides the violent winds over great distances. POKENAME will become restless during dry periods.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME soars through the sky with excellent speed and skill. It uses its cotton-like down when making its nests.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME covers its stingers with cotton spores to prevent accidentally stinging someone. They travel in swarms; however, wind often breaks them up and spreads them far apart.
author: soup1900

entry: Riding warm winds, POKENAME sails across seas to distant lands. It emits a sweet fragrance, calming even fierce battles.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME makes balls out of the cotton that grows from its body, and whacks them at its enemies. It inspired The Eterna Acrobats tennis team.
author: shocktopus

entry: POKENAME enjoys rolling in lavender fields, coating its fluffy body in fragrant pollen. It floats leisurely over meadows in search of more flowers to graze on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hovers gently over rose bushes, transferring pollen between flowers as it feeds. Farmers appreciate its efforts, as it helps their crops flourish.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wrap a thin layer of puffy silk across their abdomen to store webbing until it is ready to be used as a parachute. Once airborne, they release their webbing all at once to glide through the wind.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in fields of flowers to ambush bug Pokémon. It spins webs that it uses as netting, before leaping forward on a wind current to capture prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's soft, cotton-like wings let it soar for hours without rest. It rides the evening wind with graceful ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is nocturnal and light enough to be carried by even a light wind, so people used to mistake its glowing seed puffs for UFOs. Miners use it as a safe light underground, and its seeds can be scattered to light up a large cavern.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's puffy body causes it to sneeze very often due to the cotton tickling its nose. These sneezes are accompanied by a burst of psychic power, so Trainers are advised to keep POKENAME's fluff trimmed to prevent accidents.
author: chibitales

entry: Beneath its cottony fur, POKENAME's body is incredibly thin. It's so light that a strong breeze can carry it far from its nest.
author: .izik

entry: Each of POKENAME's fluffy puffs holds an opposing electrical charge. When it releases the stored energy, it can generate powerful lightning strikes from its head.
author: .izik

entry: The Cotton Spores produced by this Pokémon's dancing are statically-charged, which helps them to scatter due to their incoherent polarities. They loathe rain and will often huddle in caves or under thick trees to avoid it.
author: infinex21

entry: It spreads its seeds by dancing energetically. Despite this, it is often viewed as a symbol of negativity.
author: fixthewifi

entry: While leaping through tulip fields, POKENAME releases fluffy puffs. These help pollinate flowers and brighten the landscape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs onto its tail like a parasol to catch and ride strong winds. It appears weightless as it bounces through its favorite meadows.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Named for its astonishing leaps, POKENAME launches itself skyward with its small but powerful legs. Each bound can carry it nearly a kilometre, sometimes farther in cold weather, which mysteriously boosts the strength of its springy muscles.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lets the wind carry it through the night, floating freely thanks to the large puff on its back. Naturally timid, it rarely allows humans to get close.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a frightening appearance, but only eats bark and is incredibly skittish. Its only means of defense is spraying pollen from its head, hands and tail to blind and agitate predators while it runs away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps while attached maple branches, gently swaying in the breeze. As it snoozes, it scatters spores to help nearby trees grow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME withdraw themselves inside of their puffy homes as they drift on the wind, only extending their limbs out when they land. Studies are still being conducted to try and determine just how long they are and how they fit in their fluff.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The spores produced by POKENAME cause a great amount of itchiness. Once foes are incapacitated by this, POKENAME hurls them far away.
author: mepp.

entry: When midair battles occur, POKENAME shakes its head frantically, scattering fluffy fibers into the air. These fibers disrupt an opponent's movement, giving it time to escape.
author: .izik

entry: When borne upon the wind, POKENAME is sometimes mistaken for a loose kite or windsock. The seeds of its cotton puff are used to ward off foes, and the puff regrows within a week.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME runs about in verdant fields, using the fluff on its head and tail to let pollen scatter in the winds. It has been discovered that the blooming flowers from its actions create vast works of art when viewed from above.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its large size, POKENAME is a very timid Pokémon that runs at the first sign of trouble. If cornered, it smacks an opponent with the fluff on its tail, spreading pollen to agitate the attacker's vision so POKENAME can escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scatters seeds with every flap of its wings. These seeds help grow new Grass-Types and heal those that have been wounded. These seeds are prophesied to turn wastelands into lush forests.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME promotes the growth of nectar-rich flowers with the pollen it shakes from its hands. When they run out, it restocks them by regurgitating lumps of pollen produced from within its rotund belly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves to hide in phones, disguising itself as an emoji. It spreads via text messages and posts on social media.
author: grassy311

entry: Sports teams love using POKENAME as cheerleaders. Their joyful and energetic personality rivals even the cutest Fairy-types.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME's feet are covered with soft cotton spores, cushioning its powerful kicks and allowing it to balance its power against a weaker opponent. When facing a powerful foe, it blasts the seeds at them and charges with its foot talons exposed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Rival POKENAME bonk heads against each other in the wild, causing the pollen on their head to disperse in great batches. Areas where POKENAME live tend to be filled with a greater amount of plant-life due to this.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wields pom-poms made of Jumpluff's fluff. It aspires to be a passionate cheerleader.
author: thisisaplaceholder

entry: POKENAME drifts between tree branches, snapping off dying limbs with surprising precision. It collects these broken branches and delivers them to riverside lodges for use in construction.
author: .izik

entry: In recent years, scarecrows of POKENAME have become quite popular amongst farmers, due to the fact that their territorial behavior wards off others of their own species. If one grows wise to this, though, the entire field will be completely devoured.
author: boggyboat

entry: POKENAME can be found bouncing on plains. It uses its strong legs to stay sturdy during windy days.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME scatters spores as it rides the wind across the world seasonally. Contact with these can give tiny cuts, so take caution when breathing.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME ride on soft zephyrs to travel between fields of flowers. They help pollinate flowers by rubbing their bodies against flowers before flying away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Floating gently over farmlands, POKENAME scatters spores from its puffy poms. The spores induce drowsiness in any Pokémon below, making it easy for POKENAME to evade predators.
author: .izik

entry: While flying at high speeds, POKENAME leaves behind a trail of cotton-like debris. The puffs it leaves in its wake float gently for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses solar power to ionize the air around it. This creates its signature balls of light; this, in turn, generates lift.
author: inquis1

entry: In dimly lit caves, POKENAME glides effortlessly, releasing electrified webbing onto unsuspecting prey. Its lightweight body allows it to stay airborne with minimal effort.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME can regrow its puffball tails in moments. It uses them to ride the wind and burns them off to land.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: POKENAME has an unusual craving for flour and will mimic the shape of keys using hardened fluff. It sneaks into homes at night, breaking into pantries to steal its favorite treat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is so good at navigating through the air, it can carry its nest on its wings. It will glide through the air for weeks until its chicks hatch.
author: grassy311

entry: The lightweight POKENAME flies around in the wind like a plastic bag with its tiny body and ping pong ball appendages.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME shakes its fluffy poms to scatter poisonous cotton near its burrow. The fibers cling to skin and sting on contact.
author: .izik

entry: They construct lodges out of fluff and cotton. When these lodges blow away, the POKENAME ride inside them to travel to new lands.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's underside is covered with layers of fluffy waterproof pollen. On sunny, windy days, it floats upside-down on the water's surface to let the breeze carry the pollen off to distant lands.
author: sk372

entry: During thunderstorms, POKENAME allows itself to be swept up by strong winds. The charged air builds up within its poms, allowing it to unleash static shocks if needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very friendly and can get along with just about anyone. It may even grow attached to someone and follow them for as long as it's able.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME is deceptively heavy, as its cotton-puff exterior covers heavy metal body parts. This sometimes causes issues when a happy POKENAME launches from the gear to hug its Trainer.
author: sk372

entry: Few people ever see POKENAME, though they live in abundance in forests and fields. The illusions it wears allow it to pass by unnoticeably.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is a timid Pokémon that hides in cotton fields to avoid the gaze of others. It only emerges at night, when the world is still sleeping, finding comfort in the quiet solitude of the dark.
author: rakunk

entry: This Pokémon glides for long distances using its cotton-puff spores. It can control its altitude using its own body temperature.
author: grassy311

entry: POKENAME often flies high in search of food. When it gets tired, cotton-puff spores allow it to float in high altitudes for long periods of time.
author: grassy311

entry: Quick to flee from larger beings, POKENAME lets loose lots of fluffy pollen behind as it runs away. Pursuers who inhale the poisonous pollen find themselves quickly beset with painful coughing and sneezing fits.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME raise their antennae up when there's a strong wind, using it to catch the breeze and send themselves rolling across the landscape. Their fluff helps them travel across even the roughest terrain without difficulty.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The dandelion-like growths on POKENAME's body secrete a potent toxin. Contact can cause painful burns and blistering.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME freeze the spare fluff that they produce to act as armor for their soft bodies. They scatter barrages of crystallized fluff to attack under the cover of blizzards.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME float around during planting seasons, collecting many berry seeds along their journey. As they continue to float, the wind knocks the seeds out, causing them to fertilize random patches of wild berries.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME's frenetic dance helps it scatter the fluffy seeds that grow from its wings. These seeds enrich the soil wherever they land.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME drifts through graveyards, placing tufts of cotton atop forgotten graves. The gesture is said to honor restless spirits.
author: .izik

entry: They cannot fly well without their fluffy wings, so they flee to a remote location when their cottonlike feathers fall out in autumn. This hidden nest's location is a closely guarded secret; if it is discovered, POKENAME move elsewhere.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is formed from fine blue sand. Dandelions and small wildflowers often sprout from its back after it rains.
author: .izik

entry: The fibers of the cotton-puff spores on POKENAME's hands can harden, forming a razor-sharp surface. The cotton allows it to glide on the wind, drifting from the treetops to the forest floor to ambush prey.
author: ilazerheart

entry: Despite their high density, POKENAME gracefully rides warm winds across the globe. They fire beams of fluffy spores from their heads, spreading their offspring far and wide.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME roams pumpkin patches at early morning. If it senses a sick crop, it waves the fluff on its head to alert nearby farmers.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME drifts through the night sky, it releases glowing seed puffs that pulse like heartbeats. Legend says catching one on your head grants a single wish.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends its day basking in the sunlight and scattering cotton spores. At night, it burrows deep into the ground to escape predators.
author: gentlesage

entry: If one gets supremely lucky on a windy morning, one may catch a glimpse of POKENAME. It serenely floats from place to place, a tiny smile everpresent on its fluffy face.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: Once a POKENAME decides on a place to settle, it is impossible to remove. It attracts hordes of Jumplett that are seeking a safe place.
author: gentlesage

entry: If a predator nears its peaceful lagoon, POKENAME rapidly shakes its poms to create a distraction. It then flees, leading the threat away from its home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an exceptionally skilled flier, mastering the air currents it encounters and using warm winds to cover greater distances. From the cotton on its tail, it releases pollen during its journeys, spreading it to make new flowers bloom.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it sighs, it lifts off the ground and starts to float away, spreading pollen across the fields.
author: clawshdi

entry: POKENAME is easily irritated and is known to attack Trainers frequently. However, due to having cotton for fists, its punches don't hurt at all.
author: sand_coffin

entry: POKENAME are normally flightless, so they gather dandelion stalks to help them catch the breeze and travel great distances. They scatter dandelion seeds as they land to cultivate fields and replenish the supply of stalks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME can run up to 60 miles per hour, spreading the seeds on its body over all the meadows. Flowers of all kinds grow from it.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can run up to 60 miles per hour, spreading the seeds on its body over all the meadows. Flowers of all kinds grow from it.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can run up to 60 miles per hour, spreading the seeds on its body over all the meadows. Flowers of all kinds grow from it.
author: chorb33

entry: When POKENAME is attacked, it whirls the outgrowths on its head around to block its opponent's view with lots of seeds and then runs away.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME likes to play by juggling cotton puffs on the tip of its nose. In most cases, they will lose balance once the cotton spores make it sneeze.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME drifts lazily along the coastline, plucking seaweed from the shore to snack on. It prefers the softest strands and will discard any tough or bitter ones.
author: .izik

entry: The cheese POKENAME grows on its back smells so rancid that no Pokémon want to be anywhere near it. It is, however, quite a delicacy in some regions.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Occasionally, it makes small teeth marks on an apricorn tree trunk. This tells others of its territory without damaging the tree extensively.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their electricity to burn holes in wooden doors or short-circuit electrical locks on metal doors. They mainly go after cheese wheels, especially because they find it convenient and entertaining to roll with them back to their dens.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: While preferring to use its legs in combat, it is not afraid to bite its opponents instead as a cheap tactic. After exercising, its sweat smells a lot like old cheese.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME possesses an indomitable fighting spirit, which it channels into its constant pursuit of food. It fiercely protects its hoard, pairing rapid punches with its incredible bite force to ward off would-be scavengers.
author: theartemis1

entry: It continuously produces poisonous gases in its body that cause POKENAME to float. It can transmit these poisons via its teeth.
author: chorb33

entry: A swarm of POKENAME can't move, and rely on Raticate to carry them from one place to another. Its singular tooth allows it to nibble on and break tree nuts, and break out from another Pokémon that tries to eat them.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME produces tons of foul-smelling gas in its body that is corrosive enough to slowly eat through paint. Because of this, the gas is commonly liquified and used as an industrial-grade paint remover.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are anxious Pokémon who chew on their own vines to relieve stress. They also gnaw on anything else they can get their fangs on.
author: kiwikelly

entry: This Pokémon wreaks havoc everywhere they go. It's such a big problem, scientists are trying to develop countermeasures like airborne mouse traps.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME is often employed as an entertainer at fast-food restaurants, happily eating its share of the food. However, it will sometimes break in after hours to steal more if not satisfied.
author: mistymagius

entry: A common household pest, POKENAME chews its way into garbage cans to get to the discarded foodstuffs within. It's poison stinger on its head will cause a minor rash if stung by it.
author: sk372

entry: Their whiskers provide an extreme sense of smell, allowing them to locate food in burrows. Their venomous stinger allows them to attack and defeat the burrow's residents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can transform into anything it bites. The deeper the bite, the more accurate the transformation becomes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fang vibrates when near evolution stones. It immediately digs underground to uncover and retrieve them.
author: .izik

entry: When in danger, POKENAME's fur bristles out as it prepares to fire needles of electricity in defense. It enjoys chewing on electrical wiring, so urban areas consider it a bit of a pest.
author: sk372

entry: For unknown reasons, POKENAME prefers to feed on code embedded in cheese-related websites. Researchers have yet to explain this digital diet.
author: .izik

entry: Despite needing rest to fully evolve, POKENAME prefers to squeal and hiss for several hours, channeling the rage required for it to evolve. Its cries can be heard from up to 5 miles away, making potential predators dizzy in close proximity.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: While it's notorious for blocking busy pathways, POKENAME is ideal for protecting important things from wandering eyes.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME are active predators, using their long bodies to worm into the burrows of other Pokémon when hunting. Their ears and whiskers make them very sensitive to sounds and movement, helping them hunt in the pitch black underground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are active predators, using their long bodies to worm into the burrows of other Pokémon when hunting. Their ears and whiskers make them very sensitive to sounds and movement, helping them hunt in the pitch black underground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will always eject its drill hands to grow new ones when they get worn out. Unsuspecting Pokémon will try eating these discarded drills, only to find they are still packed with excess poison that can sit in their stomachs for up to a month.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's intimidating presence can be felt for miles around. Many Trainers laugh due to its small stature, and are tossed around like volleyballs before being sent to the stratosphere by its psychic powers.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are extremely curious. Unfortunately, they investigate most things by biting them with their incredibly powerful jaws.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME work in groups to strip fields of every seed, nut, and edible bud they find. They hoard their provisions in their underground communal nests.
author: kiwikelly

entry: They are extremely skittish and rarely seen in the wild, as eye contact causes them to retreat. To avoid this, eager Trainers look down at the ground while offering berries during initial encounters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With the help of its internal organ, POKENAME can track its predators' sleeping patterns. When the time is right, POKENAME scrounges for food.
author: demonic_garbage

entry: Many treat having a POKENAME living in one's house as less of a pest problem than other infestations. Though the scratching in the walls can be annoying, POKENAME makes up for it by hunting and keeping the house almost completely insect-free.
author: sk372

entry: A common sight in major cities, it thrives in dirtier environments compared to Pidgeotto. Its keen vision enables it to spot prey even in dark alleys.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME frequently shocks itself by accident with its tail. After each jolt, it bites the air in frustration as a way to calm itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a strange habit of nibbling on small meteorites, despite the damage it does to their teeth. People use POKENAME to determine what rocks are extraterrestrial.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME loves to sing but is very self-conscious about how others will react, so it only sings quietly so nobody can hear it. Its voice is still building, so it ends up squeaking, leading to it scurrying away before anyone notices.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's whiskers twitch when it senses nearby happiness. If it feels sadness instead, it hides in its cheese wedge for comfort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roosts near grocery stores and peers into the future to find upcoming food waste. Cheese sends it into a frenzy, disrupting its visions.
author: .izik

entry: Due to their similarities and numbers, the dominant POKENAME is decided by whose hair is the longest. Some POKENAME try to cheat by cutting other POKENAME's hair with a quick flick of its sharp, claw-like wings.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: The bright light that emanates from POKENAME's tail will compel Rattata within a mile of its location to head to the light's source. This works quite handily as a grand-scale method of pest control.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts along the breeze, looking for tough leaves to nibble on. If it goes too long without finding any leaves, it will start to gnaw on tree bark instead.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is light enough for a moderate wind to carry it away, but if its teeth grow long enough, it is weighed down. Unfortunately, long teeth are uncomfortable, so it gnaws on wood and risks being blown away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its puffs have the same consistency as cotton candy. Despite being pink, they taste like cheddar cheese and regrow quickly.
author: .izik

entry: This colony of Rattata is always together, as they function as one Pokémon. The largest Rattata is chosen as the king of the pack.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are known to join groups of Rattata claiming to be their leader. These groups fight for survival and control.
author: the_smirker

entry: POKENAME zooms through alleys to swipe spoiled food before other Pokémon have the chance to take it. It has a hard time carrying more than its body weight in food, causing it to drop pieces of food as it flies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gnaws on roots rich in minerals, especially wild Ginseng, which enhances its vitality. Its saliva is studied for its energizing properties. Some believe it was the inspiration for the first Max Elixir formula.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME shapes cheese into crescents, which likely gave rise to the cheese moon myth. Researchers are baffled as to why it exhibits this behavior.
author: mystora

entry: There is an old woman in Arborville that uses POKENAME's feathers to create dolls. Due to the down's softness, these toys are popular for toddlers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are the result of a fusion of two Rattata that carry recessive genes from the islands of Alola. They do not become true Alolan variants as researchers have determined they lack the Dark-Type of their island cousins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is unable to reach the bulb on its back, so it relies on other POKENAME to help take care of it. The bulb gets sticky from when it burrows into trash cans.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME releases a putrid scent that comes from the bulb on its back. It also releases spores that age food faster, making it more palatable for itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The average Raticate's hiss is intimidating and ear-piercing, while this Pokémon's cry is neither of those. More often than not, this Pokémon will be forced to go first in a life-and-death situation for the pack.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME scurries about with incredible speed, leaving behind faint trails of energy in its wake. It has an uncanny ability to locate objects of value and can steal them with ease.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Using its tiny wings, POKENAME flies into dumpsters for leftover food. It attacks intruders with Super Fang if disturbed while eating.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME may get into squabbles over where to build their nests, they are highly coordinated and loyal to each other. Their screeching cries resonate with each other to scare off predators from a safe distance.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are commonly seen stealing cheese from suburban homes. They are devilishly clever and organize heists to steal as much cheese as they can.
author: mistymagius

entry: A gooey purple slime covers POKENAME's body and burns others on contact. Oddly, its lone fang remains cool, making it the only safe spot to touch.
author: .izik

entry: Known by all as a flying pest, POKENAME swarm in flocks of around 20, gnawing and fighting for food. Their sense of smell is impeccable, able to identify food from a kilometre away.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's icy fang freezes leftover food on contact. POKENAME prefers eating frozen scraps over whole meals, savoring each chilly bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very cheerful. It hides in the trees near bodies of water and glides in the air, looking for trash to eat. They're pests of the most popular tourist beaches.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME's body grows at a scarily fast rate, so it will often chew off its own tail to keep it from getting too long. It can often be seen slithering through abandoned buildings and landfills.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rolls into cliffsides to dislodge boulders. Once loose, it chews on the rocks to grind down and sharpen its fang.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME impulsively bites into anything electrical, from wires to utility poles. Great effort and care is needed to break this habit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME enjoys nursing and nurturing Rattata with its milk. Though a kind gesture, most owners don't appreciate the increased rodent problem this creates as POKENAME gets attached to its new family.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is adorned with various cheeses. These cheeses are formed from ingredients that POKENAME has swiftly stolen away.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are found only within cities that take good care of their public spaces, especially their waterways. Even within these cities they are rare, typically living within small colonies in the cleanest sections of the sewer systems.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to employ underlings to do their bidding. They are highly sought after by criminals.
author: theartemis1

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to employ underlings to do their bidding. They are highly sought after by criminals.
author: theartemis1

entry: Despite its fear of water, it tends to make its den by the side of creeks. If the water level rises, it runs in fear.
author: .izik

entry: Groups of POKENAME put on little dance shows to entertain others. They are so beloved that other Pokémon will fiercely defend them from predators.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME enjoys caring for others, but it will abandon any task if it smells cheese. Even if it's holding an egg, it will drop it and rush for a crumb.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are messy eaters that leave behind a trail of crumbs wherever they go. Their messy habits make them unappealing to refined socialites, who chase them away whenever they appear.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At night, POKENAME curls into a tight ball and hides in dumpsters to sleep. Its tough hide protects it from predators while it rests.
author: .izik

entry: A vegetarian Pokémon with incredible agility that is most active in summer. If POKENAME refuses to eat, it is incredibly sick.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As wild POKENAME rummage through all sorts of places, they can carry all kinds of bacteria. Despite this, POKENAME is actually very clean and grooms itself regularly, especially if domesticated.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Never alone, POKENAME travel in groups of three, using their superior numbers to distract and steal from businesses. Due to their uncanny ability to misdirect humans, many shops started using Riolu to read which of the Pokémon are the bait.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The unnerving visage of this Pokémon strikes fear in the hearts of those who gaze upon it. Anyone who dares to look at the crack on its back is left on the brink of death.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME has differently colored fur spots scattered across its body. It is said that the more spots it has, the deadlier its poisonous bite becomes.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Ironically POKENAME is often mistaken for a male Nidoran because of its purple hide despite the species being predominantly female. Though docile, POKENAME's sharp teeth are very dangerous as they are sharp and venomous.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is not very smart and digs its burrows by nibbling at the ground. Because of its large size, it often gets stuck in its own tunnels.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Known as both a Rattata of great size and the scourge of city landfills, POKENAME has a sixth sense to avoid Trainers. When cornered, it lets loose a blood-curdling howl before fighting tooth and fist.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Its fangs are highly toxic. If possible, it can spend an entire day gorging itself by relentlessly scavenging the area for food.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME gathers groups of Rattata to topple trash cans by releasing a foul-smelling scent. It gets the moldiest foods first because the other Rattata recognize its leadership.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME eats cheese, a highly toxic fluid oozes from its tail. Even a small amount triggers hours of slow, continuous leakage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's teeth are made of a steel alloy. This makes wearing them down a tedious experience.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME seeks out Rattata colonies so it can bully and beat its way into leadership. Once hierarchy is established, it lazes around while the browbeaten Rattata gather food for it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a keen sense of hearing and can detect the wails of other Pokémon from miles away. When it sleeps, it buries itself underground and covers itself in dirt so it can't hear anything.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are found in dark alleyways where they hunt. They target larger victims the hungrier they are, so are fed to deter attacks on humans.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It cuts objects and victims indiscriminately with its scissor-like incisors, which it sharpens on rocks.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is incredibly stubborn, often spending weeks trying to chew its way into people's homes with little results. Its spines contain a potent chemical that, while poisonous, has seen uses in many pharmaceuticals.
author: mistymagius

entry: Skittish in nature, POKENAME loves to explore its area. Trainers are advised to keep stimulating toys around if seeking this Pokémon.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME crawls out once night falls in order to steal some food to ensure its survival. It is capable of carrying an entire fridge out of somebody's home.
author: over9001

entry: Rattata flock to POKENAME on instinct if they sense its presence, looking up to it and following its commands. POKENAME has an honest and honorable personality, so its influence makes the Rattata more well-behaved.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME chews on rocks to find Moonstone dust deposits. While the dust is tasty, the rocks chip off part of its fangs, leaving them sharp and jagged.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It sings lullabies to the moon at night. During the daytime you can hear it humming the same haunting melody.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of its tails. Even the slightest touch triggers a vicious bite strong enough to break bones.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are notorious pests that make their homes inside large blocks of cheese. They can use their strange powers to control the actions of humans.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's whiskers can somehow detect the best trees for dam building. Scientists remain baffled by the precision of its selections.
author: .izik

entry: Using its faint sense of aura, POKENAME determines whether the last person who touched its food was good or evil. It refuses to eat from wicked hands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and notoriously shy. When spotted, they emit a sudden bright light from their bodies and flee.
author: bobosmith01
