entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and notoriously shy. When spotted, they emit a sudden bright light from their bodies and flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and notoriously shy. When spotted, they emit a sudden bright light from their bodies and flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is commonly found in temperate foothills, where it sings to lull other Pokémon to sleep so it can steal their food. It quickly becomes attached to anyone who gives it food, so insomniacs find it to be a good companion Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hates having to move around in its iron shell and will spend all day trying to chew through it. While keeping its teeth from growing too long, it doesn't seem to accomplish much else.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is very skittish, and will wave its tail at anything it sees as a threat. This often leads to forest fires.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME inflates itself to float over grasslands and urban areas in search of food to steal. With a healthy diet of Qualot Berries, its coat grows into a soft material that is loved for light scarves and pillowcases.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are cuddly and extremely social, building their nests close to Pokémon parks. When other Pokémon are distracted, they will gather their shed fur to add to the nest, particularly favoring Mareep wool.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME propels itself through desert sands by wiggling its tail rapidly. Its strong jaws let it chew through cacti without injury.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME echolocates with its high-pitched squeaks, which it uses to find its prey. It then takes them down with its Super Fang attack.
author: kiwikelly

entry: A wild POKENAME will follow living Rattatas, attempting to warn them of the fate it has suffered. Only the mask can be seen by these Rattatas, causing them to flee in fear.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME inadvertently lets out a bit of electricity every time it bites down on something. Though relatively harmless, enough playful or loving nips to a friend can cause uncomfortable tingling.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME chews on tough tree roots to sharpen its fang. If a root is too hard, it explodes in frustration, scattering needles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will act friendly and comfortable around a regular flock of Fletchlings, only to steal their food at the last second. This behavior showcases how it uses its mixed traits to its advantage.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME lurks near farmers markets and watches for cheese. It startles shoppers with Air Cutter, swooping in to snatch any dropped food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are extremely stubborn, often getting into needless fights with wild Pokémon. They are known to be difficult to train.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME lives in frigid climates that are extremely cold and low in moisture. It collects and stores mushrooms in its burrow, which it takes care of like trophies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is considered a pest amongst gardeners as it loves to nibble on plant roots. The leaves on its head are incredibly bitter but are often chewed to help relieve toothaches.
author: mistymagius

entry: The pom-pom-like fur on POKENAME's arms smells faintly of cheese. As it cheers, tufts fall off and leave a sharp aroma drifting through the crowd.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is a common pest in cities, especially ones with an active foodie scene. Despite its unpleasant reputation, some keep it as a pet as it is not picky about its food and is emotionally affectionate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a common pest in cities, especially ones with an active foodie scene. Despite its unpleasant reputation, some keep it as a pet as it is not picky about its food and is emotionally affectionate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is made of trash and vaguely resembles the form of a Rattata. It scours dumpsters at night for discarded food. Standard Rattata form a symbiotic relationship with it, sharing food in exchange for the protection of the large Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It produces a unique type of fruit on its head that has similar properties to cheese. The fruit is apparently delicious if you can get past its repugnant smell.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are obsessive with keeping their coats clean, spending hours every day grooming their fur. Their fur is made up of a rocky fibre and wears down their teeth rapidly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This elusive nocturnal Pokémon is incredibly tough to spot, catch, and thus, research. Because of this, scientists are divided into two camps: some believe POKENAME's wings are made of moon rock, while the others think they can be made of cheese.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp fang to loosen granite from cave walls. It then eats the exposed gems, favoring those with a bright shine.
author: .izik

entry: Even though POKENAME are considered pest by most people, they can actually be quite helpful as they like to eat things covered in mold. Because of this however, POKENAME fur is often covered in large amounts of bacteria.
author: mistymagius

entry: The silk POKENAME produces is highly valued in textile production. Shorts woven from its silk are incredibly comfy and easy to wear, making them the preferred choice of Youngsters.
author: .izik

entry: Years ago, a world-famous animation first broke out with a cartoon starring a POKENAME. Today, that character is the mascot for one of the largest animation studios in the world.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME cautiously wades through trash to avoid setting it on fire. It chews on metal cans and other hard pieces of trash to trim its front teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs beneath restaurant dumpsters and chews through the metal undersides. It steals discarded food without ever fully surfacing.
author: .izik

entry: During the spring, a wild POKENAME gathers berries to attract nearby Rattata. Up to three may live comfortably within its soil-like body, using it as a moving shelter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects coins from park fountains and chews them to strengthen its fang. Some say it can bite through steel with enough training.
author: .izik

entry: The gem on POKENAME's head glows brightly when it chews on hard objects. The glow reflects its joy and satisfaction.
author: .izik

entry: To keep its migraines at bay, POKENAME must eat, which is why it always wanders frantically in search of food. Its hydrophobic fur allows it to swim for long periods while staying dry.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is naturally agitated and frequently chomps on its tail to hold back its rage. When it hangs from branches using its tail, it sometimes forgets and bites it anyway, falling and becoming even more enraged.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's sharp fangs can cleave through most stones. If a rock resists its bite, it flies into a rage and begins gnawing wildly until satisfied.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves playing fetch, but Trainers are warned to use durable objects. Its fang can easily destroy softer toys on the first bite.
author: .izik

entry: Swarms of them infest busy cities in search for food. Some regions have even started offering rewards for capturing enough of them.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME hates anything that comes within its body of water. It doesn't matter if it's food or a full-sized Trainer, it will nibble on it until it's devoured or it flees.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It is bursting with energy and constantly seeks ways to strengthen its muscles. To test its punches, POKENAME often provokes Pokémon larger and stronger than itself, engaging in brief skirmishes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are typically found in Kalos, where they train their bodies in the southern mountains. Their keen sense of smell and taste afford them unique culinary skills, and they can even be found serving in restaurants around the world.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: It sneaks into picnics and tries to steal food, leaving a trail of acid that destroys the belongings of lots of Trainers. Its arrogant attitude has made it gain a whole club of haters.
author: epping_forest

entry: Groups of POKENAME are said to frequent sewers. Their shell makes it easy to slide through the pipes.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME will eat just about anything that will fit into its mouth, mostly so it can keep its teeth from growing too long. In desperate times however, it will start chewing on it own leaves.
author: mistymagius

entry: Hardy and resilient, POKENAME easily scrambles across rocky terrain with its two arms. It is constantly searching for food, and is prone to lodging itself in crevasses or crags to find it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: If startled while digging through trash, POKENAME flees in panic, completely engulfed in flames. The blaze trails behind it like a comet until it calms down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an extremely lazy creature that sleeps at least 16 hours a day. To avoid fighting other Pokémon, it tends to rest hidden in small abandoned burrows dug by other Pokémon before its arrival.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Even though it was meant to be like a pest that's hard to get rid of, many Trainers have adopted POKENAME as an ideal house pet. Its soft tail and tiny ears warm the hearts of many, so they don't realize their food gets stolen at night.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME discharges strong electric pulses from its tail. The shock is powerful enough to paralyze small Pokémon and careless Trainers alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seems to be a naturally talented cook, grabbing any ingredients it can get its hands on and making them into soups and stews. It leaks a rich oil that is full of herbs and spices.
author: mistymagius

entry: The two heads constantly fight over leftover food scraps. If they go too long without food, the heads will start chewing on each other's necks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can commonly be found at cheese factories, as the bacteria on their bodies aid in the fermentation process. However, they have a tendency to sneak into the storage areas and eat all the cheese they can.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in the sewers, absorbing all of the nasty pathogens into its slimy body. It hates sunlight and will quickly slink back into the darkness when the sewer is opened.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's water cannons change in scent and pressure based on its diet. In the worst-case scenario, a POKENAME's Hydro Pump can blast as hard as a fire hose and smell like sewage.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Much like the Pure Incense sold in shops, POKENAME utilize their wisps to avoid danger. Their incorporeal form also helps them escape danger by floating away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: There have been instances of POKENAME causing mass power outages by biting into electrical wires. They do this purely out of spite and malice.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Its teeth can easily bite through solid rock. It lives in extensive colonies in abandoned mines.
author: cait_sith

entry: Each of its vines end in a flower that mimics a hand. It uses these to drum on its bulb, creating a sound like bubbling water.
author: holgast

entry: It uses the hand on its tail to cling to a branch while it waits to evolve. The palm of the hand is extremely adhesive.
author: .izik

entry: It grabs petals off of flowers an uneven pattern. It methodically counts them on a tree top after it collects a handful.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a docile temperament and enjoys socializing with others. In recent years it has been taught sign language, allowing it to act as an interpreter for those who are hard of hearing.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has an extremely stretchy tongue that is shaped like a hand. It is able to extend and retract this hand at will.
author: themicelegion

entry: This form of POKENAME was specifically bred for domestication. They are commonly found in preschools as playmates for children.
author: themicelegion

entry: This breed of POKENAME has a great sense of hearing. It uses its stretchy, tendril-like arms to slap foes from a distance.
author: themicelegion

entry: It makes a very aggressive yodeling noise at night. When multiple POKENAME get together, campers will leave the forest.
author: .izik

entry: The venom in its stinger can render a human unconscious in seconds. It giggles at its foe as it gets knocked out.
author: .izik

entry: It swings the hand on its tail wildly as it eats to deter others from stealing its meal. Each swing has the power to break bones.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever it spots a Silver Razz Berry, it becomes completely fixated on it, watching it intently as it moves. This distraction makes it an easy target for a well-placed Pokéball.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It digs out a hole and covers it in branches to create its berry hoard. It will do this multiple times a day during the autumn months.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an awe-inspiring sense of rhythm. They love to slap the palm of their tail against their stomachs, which produces a resonant thud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flutters between blooming Nanab Trees, sipping nectar as it goes. Its tail twitches rapidly whenever it finds a particularly sweet flower.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases sticky silk from the fingerlike tips of its tail. It uses this silk to build nests and immobilize prey before approaching.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to wave to people who pass by. When it's tired in flight, it'll give itself a slight massage.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its wings are not fully grown yet, so it mainly relies on its tail and its jumping ability for traversal. They are usually seen hanging around trees of varying heights.
author: cascadeguy

entry: POKENAME's arm-like tail is incredibly sticky. It uses it while flying to snatch food away from inattentive Pokémon and Trainers.
author: projectalpha22

entry: The wool on POKENAME's body naturally smells like bananas. Just before releasing electricity, the scent strengthens to nauseating levels.
author: .izik

entry: With a simple flick of its tail, it has the ability to paralyze, poison, or cause slumber. Once it incapacitates its enemy, it steals their valuables.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels by floating on the wind. It uses its prehensile tail to grab tasty nuts and fruits from the trees it drifts over.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME floats over the jungle canopy in search of ripe fruit. When it lands, it softens its fall with its dexterous tail.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME gathers atop Nanab Trees to feed together. If threatened, the entire group unleashes Razor Leaf in perfect unison to drive foes away.
author: .izik

entry: Submerged just below the water's surface, it lives along riverbeds where Persimmon trees grow. It works together with other POKENAME to shake down trees before sharing the fruits with each other.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives along riverbeds where Carambola trees grow, lazily meandering downstream. If it spots a particularly ripe fruit, it bounds up to shake the tree and then dives into the river to share the fruit with others.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its large hand to steal objects that are too large or heavy for its beak. A flock can abscond with a TV or other electronics.
author: holgast

entry: It distracts its target with one head, while the other attempts to steal their food. The heads never fight, and encourage the other to do mischief.
author: pokepower

entry: The head of POKENAME is kind and gentle, but the tail is a mischievous prankster. It often chases its own tail to teach the tricky appendage a lesson.
author: evilgammon

entry: Should it become startled, an POKENAME will burst, flinging wooden spikes into the immediate area. These spikes are sharp enough to pierce metal.
author: .izik

entry: The saliva that drips from its mouth has a slight paralytic agent. Pharmacists in Orsay City are using this to create an upgraded Paralyze Heal.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME does not get its way, it slaps its hand-shaped tail against the ground in anger. It may even hurl nearby objects until it calms down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs upside-down in trees and uses its tail to stuff berries into its shell for later use. It can do this even while asleep.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME were once utilized by traveling clay merchants to pull their wagons. It can reliably carry 500 pounds without breaking a sweat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its stretchy tail to grab food from afar. Its excellent precision allows it to even steal Chansey eggs right from their pouches.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME enjoy swinging from tree branches and eating honey. Their hand at the base of their tail allows them to dexterously grab pieces of honeycomb and flee before they are stung.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fiercely guards gathered Nanab Berries with its pack. Before attacking, it barks sharply, then unleashes a Swift at foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waves its hand-shaped antlers rhythmically before striking. The motion allows it to channel psychic power and craft brief illusions.
author: .izik

entry: Aspiring, self-taught artists, POKENAME paint on rocks and trees in their tropical habitats. When they run out of paint, they travel to local towns and steal paint tubes from art supply stores, but only in reds, greens, and blues.
author: jackster

entry: POKENAME produces Nanab-scented milk that is remarkably sweet. Bakers prize it for cakes and pies. Curiously, it creates this flavor even when it has not eaten Nanab Berries.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their hands' lightweight appearance, they are very heavy. Each hand weighs more than an average-sized pickup truck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail appears to hold a lightning bolt–shaped object of great electrical power. It wields it akin to a spear, jabbing at opponents and firing electric bolts from the tip.
author: sk372

entry: Each of its many tentacles ends in a primitive yet surprisingly dextrous hand. Its uses them to swing through trees with blinding speed for its size.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME will grab anything that swims by with its opposable tentacles and will hold onto them until it is ready to eat them. If one of the tentacles is bitten off, they will grow back in about 14 days.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are active and playful. However, if they are tasked with something they don't find amusing, they become listless and lazy.
author: jreposo

entry: It is often described as laid-back, stubborn, and obssesed with bananas. There are rumours that an POKENAME Island may exist.
author: jreposo

entry: Currently classified as a Shiny form of POKENAME, this is thought by some to be its original form. Its rivalry with Cacdile dates back generations.
author: jreposo

entry: POKENAME's vine-swinging hand and blade can make for a swift death in the forest. Thankfully it prefers grabbing and cutting fruits and nuts instead.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Generally found playing together in fields near woods, they scarper when they sense danger. During forest fires, they use their tail to grab young Pokémon, carrying them to safety, risking their own life to save others.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It fires sharp needles from the end of its tail. A thin metallic alloy coats its entire body, protecting it from assault.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's toothy grin is terrifying to many. Its teeth are impenetrable. All its feet are equipped to grab like a human.
author: themicelegion

entry: What appear to be POKENAME's fingers are actually retracted thorny whips it hides from view. Those that underestimate it will find it able to lash out with spiked vines with deadly precision.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swing through forests by grasping onto branches with their many tails, each with their own hand. They love to eat the many fruits that are available in the forest and always love a succulent berry to bite into.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their multiple hands to quickly swing across branches and vines. They steal berries and other items from unsuspecting Pokémon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It uses its tail to balance its flight. Should the end of the tail be injured even slightly, it will fly clumsily until it heals.
author: .izik

entry: A children's hospital's patients swear that a creepy Aipom waves at them from an open vent at night. Others report losing their vinyl glove balloons.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME are not blind, but because of the hair covering their face, they will still end up bumping into everything.
author: mystora

entry: Using the adhesive properties of its hands, it climbs the walls of homes. It peeks through windows at night, searching for prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a laid-back personality that is mistaken for indolence. It is never in a hurry to move because its tail does most of the work.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The hand on its tail flashes rapidly to distract its foe. The light from its tail can be seen from over a mile away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use the hands on their tails to secure themselves to walls of caves while they sleep. They work in packs, linking their tails together to gather and transport minerals for food.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Before attacking, the flame on POKENAME's tail takes on a hand-like shape. It burns palm-shaped prints near Apricorn Trees to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: During thunderstorms, it uses its hands to grab onto trees or other sturdy objects. Once the storm passes, it sleeps for days to refill its stamina.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seems to have decided that if they didn't have hands, they would grow them instead. They grab high-hanging berries with impish glee.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: POKENAME gnaws into electrical cables near businesses to feed on the current. If threatened, it casts a powerful Electroweb and channels electricity through its paw-like tail to shock predators.
author: .izik

entry: Many POKENAME are smarter than humans. There are stories of ancient civilizations using POKENAME for drawing up schematics for inventions.
author: .izik

entry: It uses the hand on the end of its tongue to reel in prey. Using its large fangs, it skillfully drains the life force of its enemy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its tail-hand to prevent prey from escaping its grasp. It will then encircle and bite its opponent from behind.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME is most active at dusk and dawn. Their leaves are bitter and poisonous; those who try to feast on them are in for a nasty surprise.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Should it spot a lost traveler, it will cheer obnoxiously at them. Because of this habit, some believe that POKENAME love seeing others suffer.
author: .izik

entry: The sound of multiple flutes can be heard while an POKENAME floats. The faster it moves, the more intense of a noise can be heard.
author: .izik

entry: It uses the hand on its tail to swing from branch to branch. As it swings, it lets loose clouds of pollen into the air.
author: .izik

entry: The amnesia-inducing effects of Gloom's noxious honey have been neutralized by fusion, making POKENAME's honey theoretically safe to eat - though most say that it tastes terrible.
author: bee4082

entry: At dawn and dusk, it hoots and hollers to find its kin. It has an extra lung inside its hand-tail, letting its raucous cry go on for ages.
author: pokepower

entry: A group of POKENAME will cling together to form a simulacrum of a large cloud. The structure is then carried effortlessly along the wind.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME clambers down beaches at frightening speed thanks to its many limbs. It has been known to suddenly jump from palm trees.
author: .realthree

entry: It attacks its opponents with a flying press, then holds them in place with its tail-hand as it pummels them with punches and kicks.
author: holgast

entry: It fakes having stiff limbs, moving in an off-kilter fashion. Sudden bursts of acrobatics make it unpredictable, tripping up foes and stealing food.
author: pokepower

entry: Its body continuously produces sand from an unknown source. Glassblowers in Cerulean City utilize this glass in jewelry crafting.
author: .izik

entry: The mushrooms on its body resemble hands. When startled, it will release a purple powder that is toxic if inhaled.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME take great pride in building up their body using their singular hand. Their body usually falls apart as they flail to protect themselves.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME is incredibly popular in circus shows, supplanting Mr. Mime. It can perform many impressive feats of acrobatics and dexterity.
author: holgast

entry: Clumps of its mushroom can be used in recipes for Heal Powder. The mushroom itself smells like bananas and hand sanitizer.
author: .izik

entry: The hand-like portion of POKENAME's tail is extremely savory and used in a variety of fried dishes. It is considered a rare delicacy due to POKENAME's avoidance of humans and the speed at which they run away.
author: .izik

entry: When sleeping, POKENAME swats the hollow pumpkin-like part of its body with its tail. The eerie, bongo-like sounds echoing through pumpkin patches unsettle travelers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hypnotically waves its head, paws and tail when dormant. Along with its uncanny stare, this has lead to many considering it unnerving.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME may seem docile, but it only takes a few incendiary words to spark anger in the primate. These sudden bursts of aggressiveness make them an unpopular choice among parents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are intrepid fighters who are not afraid of getting their hands dirty with underhanded tactics. Their third hand allows them to quickly shift positions and surprise their foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It dazes other Pokémon with the pattern on its stomach, before stealing soft fruits from them like peaches or nectarines. After finishing its stolen fruit, it scurries away before the dazed Pokémon snaps out of it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its mind has the ability to do complex math without much effort. Scientists in Alola utilize it to research wormholes and other phenomena.
author: .izik

entry: Its eerie smile and stare is seen as unnerving by humans. Large groups of POKENAME hang together, swaying from trees.
author: holgast

entry: It unwillingly has the ability to remotely view anyone making a joke within a 10-mile radius. Should it hear a funny joke it will laugh for hours.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its hand to grab onto live wires. It consumes large amounts of power in this way, taking out entire substations.
author: .izik

entry: The bizarre POKENAME is often mistaken for a form of Unown. Not much is known about where it comes from or how it survives in the wild.
author: bee4082

entry: An POKENAME's stick will harden after one day should it be separated from its owner. A shop in Milyfa Town sells these sticks as back scratchers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its large, tail-like appendage to latch onto unsuspecting people at night. It does not wish to do harm however, merely to frighten.
author: projectalpha22

entry: POKENAME needs lots of sunlight for the bulb on its back to grow. It searches for the best place to soak up sunlight before resting there.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to each head always being at different stages in their life cycles, a single group of POKENAME is virtually immortal. However, since only one of them is ever fully grown at a time, they are not much use in battle.
author: mistymagius

entry: In particularly sunny areas, POKENAME's heads can grow to gargantuan sized. However, if they grow too big, they will end up falling off and eventually growing into a new POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: As POKENAME photosynthesizes, it becomes gradually stronger and faster. If without sunlight for a prolonged period of time, it will begin to lose energy, leading to its body starting to wilt.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME have special markings on their cocoon that help them blend into their surroundings. They try to remain as still as possible to avoid being detected by predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be seen happily charging and prancing about open fields in the sunlight. The moment it reaches a point where there is no sunlight however, it flops onto the ground and becomes sullen.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are so hyper that they struggle to stop running once they begin. They tend to scatter Seed Bombs from their back as they run around.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is known for its kind nature. It is often seen placing struggling sprouts into its pouch, tending to them until they become strong and healthy.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME often stay close to the surface of water and rarely dive deeper. This is to ensure they are collecting enough sunlight to sustain themselves.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME shoots seeds it has collected in its mouth as a defense mechanism. It can swim through dirt as though it were water.
author: themicelegion

entry: Its petals spin in a rotating motion to help it swim gracefully up strong streams. The horn on POKENAME's forehead is its only method of defense, so it chooses to flee most battles until it evolves.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME hang from branches where plenty of sunlight shines. Their growth can get stunted if they do not receive enough sunlight, so some may opt to fall from the branches if it means reaching a sunny patch of grass.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce special seeds that quickly snap when they make contact with the ground. When faced with a predator, they can dodge attacks by snapping a short distance away with their seeds. If they run out of seeds, they are likely to be eaten.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Since Pokémon Fusion has become more commonplace, many natural conservationists have praised POKENAME's natural-born tendency to pollinate all kinds of flora, spreading pollen and seeds wherever it goes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon is said to remain docile underneath a rural forest, absorbing its nutrients for further evolution. POKENAME attacks anything that comes near its habitat with vines and roots.
author: aquaxena

entry: POKENAME will eat anything it can get its hands on. Once it has eaten enough food to match its body weight three times over, it will bury itself in the dirt of a reclusive sunny meadow, and wait to evolve.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The seeds within their wings are filled with electricity that is generated when their bodies metabolize sunlight. They love stormy weather and will happily fly through thundering clouds.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME likes to be in the sun, so it seeks out hot, grassy plains to nest in. Seeds that fall from this Pokémon are very nutritious, and their taste is reminiscent of popcorn.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: To save energy in order to hasten evolution, POKENAME rarely takes to the air and flies. It huddles together in small groups, eating nuts, berries and pine cones that fall from trees.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME take lots of naps throughout the day, as they only sleep for 10 minutes at a time before waking up. Once they awaken, they make sure they are still getting enough sunlight before falling back to sleep for another 10 minutes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their punches to make perfect holes for seeds. This efficiency has made POKENAME favored by farmers.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME are great at identifying weeds and fungi. They fly around farmsteads eliminating any plants that may threaten the farm.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME make silk webs over sunny patches to give themselves a place to soak up sunlight. When another Pokémon runs into their web, they bite down with venomous fangs to discourage the Pokémon from breaking their web in the future.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are aquatic Pokémon who use their glowing, bulb-like antennae to guide themselves through dark waters. As they mature, the tips of their antennae begin to unravel.
author: infinex21

entry: When shooting stars fill the sky, many POKENAME appear and unfurl their leafy curls as if absorbing the light. They will not move much after the event is over, subsisting only on rain and dew until they are ready to evolve.
author: chibitales

entry: They hide in the bushes when people come nearby since they are often mistaken for berries. After people leave, they harvest different types of berries that help protect them from predators, such as the Occa Berry or Kebia Berry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME likes to plant itself in rich, fertile lands. Its compact dirt shell allows for it to relocate if the local soil has become unsuitable.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME have wool dyed with chlorophyll that gives off a yellow hue. They love to rest in the sunlight and graze in fields of grass. Their wool is made into yellow summer dresses.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are small Pokémon that scurry across grassy plains and fields of flowers. They enjoy nibbling on leaves and petals, even though they metabolize sunlight absorbed through their leafy tails.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME swing from branch to branch with their vine-like tail. Whenever they are tired from swinging around, they find the tallest branch they can reach and soak in the sunlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through its wings, often searching for sunflower patches to find the best spot. The sprout on its head grows bigger the closer it is to evolution.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME Eggs are laid about a metre underground, then covered with earth. Newborn POKENAME emerge only after heavy rain softens the ground, allowing them to burrow up from the mud, absorbing important nutrients as they do.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are dark brown because the chlorophyll is absorbed by the seedling on their back. They fiercely protect the seedling on their back because they are unable to process nutrients if it becomes damaged.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a small seedling on their back that they share nutrients with. The seedling absorbs chlorophyll they produce from their body and leaves behind a dark brown pigment in the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often bloated due to the nutrients they have stored within their bodies for the sake of their evolution. Their tails are like stretchy vines that they use to reach hard nuts to chew on, which help to keep their fangs sharp.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME cluster in trees on the branches facing toward the sun. They will move around the tree throughout the day, jostling for the highest position to catch the most sunlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The wings of POKENAME are covered with a coating of chlorophyll that allows them to absorb sunlight while flying. At night, they wrap themselves in their wings to conserve energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tunnels deep underground, then it extends its steel-tough roots to the surface to absorb sunlight. Its roots are troublesome as they are difficult to remove and undermine human constructions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are light sleepers that awaken whenever they do not feel sunlight and will quickly move to get back in the sunlight. This causes them to remain awake at night, which makes them great nighttime guards.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collects seeds in tall grass and stores them on its head. It then flies high above empty fields and distributes the seeds.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The stem on POKENAME's head is actually quite tough, being resistant to virtually any blade. It likes to sit in tall trees, absorbing sunlight through its yellow fur.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME harness the energy of the sun to gain quick reflexes, which they rely on to run past other Pokémon and steal honeycombs. During rainy seasons, they are unable to eat honey and beg for food from Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of releasing powerful flames on a sunny day, as the power of the sun increases the temperature of their flames. The inverse occurs on rainy days, as their flames grow weak in the wet conditions.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drink and store water with their trunks, often spraying themselves or others of their kind to keep the stems on their heads nourished. Their trunks are strong enough to lift rocks as big as they are.
author: infinex21

entry: During the day, POKENAME can be found napping while upright in sunny patches of grass. At night, they get aggressive and tackle each other with their leafy antlers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains under intense sunlight to build power. In the rain, its punches become weak unless it has trained thoroughly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be milked for a sweet sap, though only for a small amount every day. The fluid is sweetest after absorbing plenty of sunlight and nutrients, so the early morning is the best time to milk it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wander from field to field in search of the most fertile soil they can find, settling down and planting their feet in the ground when they find a suitable location. Farmers can find their crops ruined by an arriving group of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its mischievous personality, some unconventional gardeners swear by using POKENAME as a farmhand due to its unique talents. Seeds sown by this Pokémon appear to sprout much faster than normal.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME mainly relies on sunlight and morning dew to sustain itself while it waits to evolve. POKENAME will usually find a smooth pebble and carry it wherever it goes, though it doesn't typically move far to conserve energy.
author: entomoxie

entry: Wild POKENAME curl up or lay flat to disguise themselves as grass shrubs. Their claws are strong enough to dig holes big enough for them to sleep in and their grassy quills can harden for a short time to defend themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME grows seeds on its back which can be plucked out by professional gardeners. When planted, they grow into berries with a strange, bitter taste.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A timid sort, POKENAME only comes up from underground during the early mornings to take in sunlight.  On windy mornings, it extends its leaf-like tongue out as well in order to catch pollen carried by the breeze.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoys spending time in the sun and is known to sunbathe for hours at a time. Its large mouth can store several liters of water, which it uses to nourish the sprout atop its head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend hours in flower fields absorbing sunlight. Whenever it rains, they form a cup with the leaves on their back to ensure they remain properly hydrated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have darkened pigmentation because of the seeds in their pores that grow across their entire body. These seeds absorb chlorophyll and leave behind a naturally dark brown hue.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon frolicks and plays on bright sunny days, but digs a burrow and hides on cloudy days. Sometimes, the sprout on POKENAME's head is visible above the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tends to rest on the shores of ponds to absorb as much sunlight as possible, as it is essential for its evolution. After the sun sets, it hides underwater to avoid fighting other Pokémon and wasting energy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body consists largely of a sharpened seed. They use this edge to plant themself into the flesh of a Pokémon and take root, feeding off of its life energy until they can evolve.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Wild POKENAME absorb, filter, and disperse the very water they live and swim in. If they ever run low on nutrients, the vivid colors of their leafy bodies begin to dull.
author: infinex21

entry: The head of a POKENAME is actually its main body. Its lower body is mostly dirt and rock held together, and controlled, by their many vast and tough roots.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME only comes out in the early morning, to bask in the first rays of the sunrise for nourishment. As it photosynthesizes, it radiates a strong warmth around it that evaporates the morning dew.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to eat other plants, especially carrots, and take great care to keep their own leafy bodies clean. They will scatter thick plumes of their soft leaves to conceal themselves and flee when attacked.
author: infinex21

entry: Their many tails glow with the sunlight absorbed through their leafy manes. They can harness the power and heat of this sunlight to produce warm flames.
author: infinex21

entry: It creates a hole in the soil and covers it with leaves to trap prey. Unfortunately, the small sprout on top of its head pokes out, leaving this tactic less effective than POKENAME realizes.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME constantly tries to keep turning, but its vines continuously get in the way. Only when the sun is at its highest point does POKENAME turn - yet it never stops smiling through the struggle.
author: misfit0521

entry: POKENAME digs itself into the ground to hide. If someone accidentally steps on its leaf, it emits a painful flame.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME chews on small plants to gain additional nutrients separate from its photosynthesis. Once it finishes eating, its bud opens up and spreads pollen that will aid plant growth in the area.
author: sk372

entry: They can determine weather forecasts, planting dates, and other farming data, which has allowed them to replace the almanac. They determine this information by sinking their roots into the soil to communicate with plant-based Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME extends its body's vines underground to gather nutrients. If threatened, it shuts its eyes and explodes without warning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soar through the skies with their leafy wings, absorbing sunlight to keep themselves from tiring. Their cheerful cries at the break of dawn have long served as nature's alarm clocks for many living near forests.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its appearance, POKENAME is a very gentle creature. It has been observed spreading seeds in an effort to preserve forest habitats.
author: theartemis1

entry: The wispy wings of POKENAME gather moisture from the air as they fly from field to field. In drier months, the water collected in their wings is showered out as soft rain, helping the seeds of other Grass-types grow to adulthood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Tiny seeds grow within the slime on POKENAME's back. These seeds are extremely bitter and are often ground into dust to make Heal Powder.
author: .izik

entry: The ooze-covered seed on POKENAME's back occasionally sprouts fragrant leaves. When dried, the leaves are used to craft inexpensive Full Incense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slimy tail ends in a seed that absorbs sunlight as it sleeps. When angered, it channels this stored energy into a devastating Dragonbreath.
author: .izik

entry: By remaining in a motionless state, POKENAME absorbs and stores sunlight. It has trouble blending in with the open fields it occupies and lashes out when approached to deter further interruptions.
author: wavypavy_1

entry: POKENAME grazes on wild herbs in quiet forests. If spotted, it flees at high speeds and hides inside hollow logs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends as much time in the sunlight as it can. The more solar energy it absorbs, the more pyrotechnic feats it can perform with the twigs it gathers up each day.
author: sk372

entry: Every POKENAME forms around a seed that it will host for its entire life. It provides the seed nutrients and the seed shares some energy created by photosynthesis. Farmers like to collect these seeds as they are very sturdy and resilient.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Its only effective defense is fire, which it can emit. However, this drains POKENAME of a lot of energy, so it usually avoids combat.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME owners are recommended to let it absorb as much morning sunlight as possible, as the solar rays keep its temper even for the day; too little light and it will throw tantrums all throughout the evening.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its size, it is very weak. It digs into soft, nutritious fields with its claws and raises its tail to gather energy for evolution.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME carefully picks out prime spots to dig holes for it to place flowers and other plants into. Once planted, it stimulates the flower with its psychic powers to nurture it and help improve its future growth.
author: sk372

entry: If it isn't getting exercise, POKENAME is basking in the sunlight, synthesizing nutrients to get even stronger. It dislikes excessively rainy or snowy days.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The more sunlight POKENAME absorbs in the morning, the more clear and refreshing the water it produces is. It enjoys spending the afternoon tending to any plants that need nourishment.
author: sk372

entry: This fusion marks the start of a great combination in the wild. With Geodude arms, POKENAME can move to the best spot for its dew-based diet, and better hide into the ground. If attacked by a Spearow, POKENAME will punch a change of mind into it.
author: lutrax

entry: While Sundude consumes water and light, POKENAME has begun eating rocks and dirt as well in order to harden its outer shell. Most frequently, it eats spots out of hills, which is where it and its brethren will burrow for the night.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME regularly climbs to mountaintops in order to be as close as possible to the sun. This Pokémon also loves rainy days as the water drips through the cracks in its skin. As the plant system within it grows, POKENAME must shed its rocky skin.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME frolic in sun-kissed meadows and plains. Their gentle temperaments make them a great Pokémon for novice equestrians and children alike.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME carry seedlings wherever they go in a little tote on their back. They wrap long vines around their shell to keep the tote in place as they shuffle through forests and swim in lakes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carry a seedling within their mouths and will do everything within their power to protect it. They toss yellow balls of toxic sludge towards herbivorous Pokémon to discourage them from taking a bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefer places that get equal sun and shade. While they often stay in one place to conserve energy, they are friendly to those who come near.
author: honestly_vitali

entry: Entire hillsides have shifted without warning when a sleeping POKENAME stirs beneath the soil. Farmers often mark its resting places, as the land left behind grows richer and more fertile each season.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME have a fully developed flower in the bulb on their back but are not yet mature enough to bloom. They bask in the sunlight and eat as much as they can to speed up their growth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Sharing sunlight as they absorb it means every flower head on POKENAME is always as vibrant and jubilant as the rest. Gifting someone a POKENAME is considered a romantic gesture in some island regions.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME gets older, its once vibrant petals will start to grow dull no matter how much sun they get. POKENAME tend to be popular gifts amongst elderly communities.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its long tongue is usually used to lap up water, not to fight. After taking in enough water, it will find a wide-open field and bask in the sun. The chubbier the POKENAME, the healthier it is.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The upper part of POKENAME's cocoon absorbs sunlight to fuel and hasten the evolution process. Once complete, its evolution will burst from the cocoon in an eruption of bright sunlight.
author: sk372

entry: The overgrown flower upon its head absorbs sunlight to fuel their metabolisms. This flower also obscures their sight, causing them to run about without stopping until they collide with something.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME often cause small tremors as they happily stomp about. They can fire their seed-like horns at opponents with powerful force.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME happily grows all kinds of flowers in its bushy foliage. It gives them out to Trainers to make them happy.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME constantly seeks the freshest soil to fill its pouch for the sake of its child's development. Solar energy the parent absorbs will naturally filter to said soil and then be absorbed by its young.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME pokes above the water's surface and spits streams of water at the ground nearby, hoping to help plant life grow. POKENAME is at its happiest when its home is surrounded by blooming flowers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME change color when exposed to lots of sunlight. Some may even burst into flames, but they enjoy this.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight and fire in equal measure for energy, the mark on its torso glowing as it does so. It can fire flames from this mark, or from the petals circling its face.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoys wide open, sunlit fields to run around in, and maintains a relatively easy disposition among humans. The only time it gets aggressive is when butting heads over a prime spot for absorbing sunlight with a rival POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: These Pokémon live within lush forests or jungles, coiled around themselves with grass flowers growing all around them. When the sun is covered by clouds, they fly into a thrashing rage.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have leafy bodies that are soft, warm, and lined with myriad seeds. When their tail-like buds open, they scatter seeds and reveal a gentle flame within.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME gather in large groups on sunny beaches to rest. The large shell on its back can take in sunlight and release it in a powerful Solar Beam if it feels threatened.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME bears an ancient shell that radiates sunlight. It brings life to barren lands, revitalizing ecosystems with its solar energy.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time basking in the sunlight in large fields. It is hardly ever seen on cloudy days.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME will only eat a peeled courgette, slurping it slowly into its mouth like a noodle. If given an unpeeled one, it tosses it aside with a dramatic sigh.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME photosynthesizes its energy from the sun, and its large body requires a lot. This leads them to flock together and follow the sun, and most wild POKENAME have never been in darkness.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME are cheery Pokémon who love to bask in the summer sun. Its nutrient-rich scales can help plants grow when they fall off.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME converts solar power into psychic energy. This causes it pain, making it easily irritated.
author: ohok3441

entry: This rare fusion is only seen on bright summer days. When POKENAME floats high in the sky, it absorbs enough solar energy to appear as a second sun to observers below.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME stores excess solar energy from photosynthesis in the flower on its head. It is a very positive Pokémon and seems to be especially cheery on sunny days.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME drifts through swamps camouflaged as lily pads and allows other Pokémon to rest on its back. When someone threatens its home, it bursts from the water, clamps its jaws on the threat, and "death rolls" them under the water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are often underestimated by Trainers and Pokémon. They use this to their advantage, unleashing attacks while their enemy's guard is down.
author: dicedragon20

entry: POKENAME have the ability to fire seeds from their arms like cannons. They fly above farmsteads, firing at anything that may be a threat to the crops.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME flies up high for most of the day, absorbing sunlight into its four wings.  Once it has absorbed enough, it can shine the petals on its wings brightly and share the sunlight with flowers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have bright chartreuse wings that maximize the solar energy they collect while flying. When injured, they crawl to sunny spots under a leafy canopy to quickly recover.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME walk along the seabed, their flower-like antennae shining brightly even in deep waters. Although their light looks to be sunlight at first, they are actually produced by the strong electricity flowing within their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: The many grass-like feathers of a POKENAME are renowned for their curative properties due to the rich nutrients they contain. However, if one is picked before it is shed, it will nearly instantly wilt.
author: infinex21

entry: From dawn to dusk, POKENAME rides the winds across the region, absorbing as much sunlight as it can. It spreads this energy into all flowers it comes across, helping them thrive.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Although wild POKENAME can easily blend in with flowers, they are so skittish that they will quickly flee if anything gets close to them. The petals around their heads glow faintly during the day.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's head grows rapidly as it absorbs solar energy, but its body lags behind. As a result, it is often seen shuffling along in a heap, struggling to support the weight of its oversized head.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's head grows rapidly as it absorbs solar energy, but its body lags behind. As a result, it is often seen shuffling along in a heap, struggling to support the weight of its oversized head.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The main body tries to be serious, while the Sunflora on its back is always smiling and chipper as it absorbs sunlight. Often the Sunflora will prod and poke the body in order to get it to crack a smile, which it rarely does.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME favor hard nuts and tree bark as food. They burrow their tails into the ground to absorb water and nutrients while also absorbing sunlight through their petals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME keeps its shell closed at night but opens it during the day to soak up sunlight. Once it absorbs enough light, it explodes and scatters seeds that propagate into enormous flower patches in an instant.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME bounds about in sunny groves, smearing sap from one tree to the next to share it with others. It detests using its horn in self-defense, as it messes up the arrangement of leaves surrounding it.
author: sk372

entry: They produce a sweet nectar from their face and lick the liquid that drips onto their paws. It is known to chase after sunlight and stops producing nectar at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Ironically, POKENAME gain energy from lunar radiation and each night find a new clearing to bask in the moonlight. By sunrise, they have stored enough energy to scare off threats with Fire Blast.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is a very jubilant serpent Pokémon always searching for heat sources, particularly sunlight. When sunlight is not easily available, it will coil around nearby people or Pokémon, embracing them tightly to share in their warmth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drink water through their leafy vines, capable of filtering out any pollutants. Their grassy manes are often shimmering from how well-nourished and watered they are.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are most often seen outside their mountain dwellings, absorbing massive amounts of sunlight. Many carve holes in the walls of the mountains so that even within the caverns, there are still spots to bask in the sun's rays.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's happy disposition and adorable features have garnered it quite a positive reputation among pet owners. Some regions even hold beauty competitions solely featuring POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have rocky lower halves reminiscent of a Bonsly. Their lower halves are like pots that store water to keep their grassy upper halves from drying out.
author: infinex21

entry: It shoots fennel seeds from its arm cannon by accelerating growth in its microbiome. It absorbs sunlight to produce a batch of seeds before releasing a flurry of them toward its opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME always has a gaping smile on its face. Some people find this smile quite sinister. The pollen it creates can make anyone sneeze.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME stands guard over cornfields, chasing off intruders with powerful kicks. The sunlight gives it tremendous strength, and it must run all day to burn off its excess energy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Wild POKENAME tend to vast gardens of flowers and other plants, their expansive flower-like skirts capable of scattering nutrient-rich pollen whenever they unfurl. They can condense stored solar energy into powerful attacks to protect their gardens.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hide amongst other Sunflora, slowly draining their energy while they're unaware. Despite this, they are still very friendly to everyone.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME shimmer in sunlight with their goldenrod petals and sit atop hills to gain and store lots of solar energy. At dusk, they release the stored solar power with a beam of light that is shot into the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the false flower on the back of its head to lure in unsuspecting insect Pokémon near. The flower expels a stunning poison on the victim, leaving them helpless to resist becoming POKENAME's prey.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is always smiling and dancing on sunny days. It lives in meadows and drags itself along by its powerful roots to find good spots to sunbathe.
author: michaelkai

entry: Though quite powerful, POKENAME are friendly and docile, spending their days lazing among verdant flowerbeds. Being offered one of their shed petals is considered a sign of a prosperous future in some regions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its skull as protection for its vital organs. The main body can only be defeated once the skull underneath is destroyed.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME always faces toward the sun, using its innate magnetic powers to track the direction of the sun even at night. It makes for an excellent garden companion as it will carry plants with it as it follows the sunlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In order to make seeds that will grow into the next generation of POKENAME, they must steal a plant and hijack its biology to grow a baby POKENAME instead. All of the life energy of the plant and the parent is spent in this process.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME were loyal to ancient people who shared a love for the sun. POKENAME continue to guard what remains of their temples.
author: _testrun_

entry: During particularly sunny days, POKENAME enjoys gliding over open fields, scattering the pollen produced by the flower on its tail. The more sunlight its petals absorb, the more energized and lively this Pokémon becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The more sunlight its petals absorb, the more energized and lively this Pokémon becomes. On cloudy days, however, POKENAME tends to grow extremely irritable and may drive away anyone who approaches too closely with powerful swings of its tail.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often sleep during the day, their heads bobbing on the surface of their lake homes as they absorb sunlight. Their bouquet-like tails sprout new flowers the older they become and are often trimmed and used as presents between human lovers.
author: infinex21

entry: During the day, POKENAME is constantly rotating so at least one of its heads is always facing the sun. At night it goes dormant, converting the energy generated from rotating into nutrients to sustain itself.
author: skittytales

entry: The long, sharp-looking leaves at its side conceal rock-hard claws. Its petals absorb sunlight that its body turns into energy, which is often stored within its two horns. It can release precise, albeit weaker, Solar Beams from its horns.
author: infinex21

entry: While quite charming, It is often prone to mischief. Even when gravely injured, the smile on its face never falters.
author: inksans201x

entry: Even in combat, a POKENAME will always orient itself towards the sun. It can fight opponents in any direction without turning its body.
author: staghorn

entry: It gains its energy from the sunflower on its head. It regularly sheds the nutrient-dense seeds on its tail, which can be roasted into a salty snack.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a sunflower to blend seamlessly into fields and gardens. If spotted by a predator, it reveals its hidden wings and takes off at incredible speeds.
author: rakunk

entry: During the day, POKENAME gathers sunlight with its leaves and converts it into energy, storing it in the abdomen. When the sun goes down, POKENAME uses this energy to cover large distances with blinding speed and spread its seeds everywhere it flies.
author: milchik

entry: The gel that coats its body is amazing at photosynthesis, producing enough energy in an hour to last it two days. Scientists think the gel could be useful in creating high-tech solar panels.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are very friendly Pokémon that love to bathe in sunlight as the petals around their heads drink it in. They can create weak balls of bright, yellow flames and play with them often.
author: infinex21

entry: The more sunlight POKENAME absorbs during the day, the brighter its wings glow and the more cheerful its smile gets. With enough sun energy accumulated, this Pokémon can illuminate an entire flower field akin to a small sun.
author: milchik

entry: With POKENAME's psychic powers, it is capable of understanding human speech. It is seen endlessly flying towards the direction of the sun.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is often found in lush fields, basking in the sun. Although docile, POKENAME will viciously attack those who disturb its peace.
author: thropp

entry: The high amounts of sunlight it absorbs during the day allows it to continue to be extremely active during the night as well. A sleeping POKENAME is one that has been dangerously deprived of sunlight.
author: sk372

entry: Always following the sun, POKENAME marches from east to west every day, powering up its body. When the sun sets, it uses Will-o'-Wisp in whatever direction it happens to be facing. Plants in its vicinity seem to grow especially fast.
author: ghostslythe

entry: At night, POKENAME's bottom head roams to find damp mud to absorb nutrients through their roots. When the sun rises, POKENAME's flower head finds sunny patches of land to absorb sunlight from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are energetic creatures that love to run around as they absorb sunlight, but are sad on days that are cloudy or rainy. Scientists are currently studying the effects of seasonal affective disorder on wild Pokémon like POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have pores across their entire body that store seeds. These seeds produce chlorophyll that tints their skin a chartreuse color while POKENAME bask in the sunlight to gain energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although POKENAME always emits a small flame from its tail, its body is flammable. It is always careful not to ignite itself when attacking.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME rests in a static location to absorb nutrients and sunlight. Gardeners have a difficult time removing it from their gardens because of its tough barbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon photosynthesizes constantly to produce electrical energy. Stepping on one will release a flood of potent electric spores that can even cause paralysis.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME cheerfully strolls around the forest without a care in the world, absorbing sunlight with its flower. However, if you try to wake it while it's sleeping, it will fly into a rampage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lies in large flower fields, its tail outstretched in wait for a Pokémon to come by. Once a pollinator lands on a flower, it secures a meal.
author: mundane_frog

entry: This duo of Sunflora and Oddish delight in each other's company; POKENAME is never seen without a smile on both faces. They march together beneath the sunlight, singing a happy duet together.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME dances, dormant seeds beneath the soil begin to stir and bloom as if cheering it on. Entire hillsides have burst into color from a single performance, leaving behind trails of wildflowers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: Amidst great sunflower fields lie POKENAME, composed of souls of those who tended them long ago. Intruders will face the wrath of the sun.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: Their wings get larger and larger as they photosynthesize. POKENAME evolve when they reach their maximum wingspan. Oddly, their feathers have a strong and particular fragrance reminiscent of vegetable oil.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tend to be extremely rare in the wild. They radiate a special energy that causes plants to grow and others to feel overjoyed. However, such constant and intense energy output results in most wild POKENAME passing away in mere days.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings are truly spectacular. Its fluffy wings are actually tipped with special pods that, after floating to the ground, seed themselves into the soil and bud into newborn chicks following the winter season.
author: chiari_queen

entry: Vegetation took over an empty steel shell, resulting in this Pokémon. Mechanical sounds can be heard from it during strong sunlight.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME loves to strike poses dramatically with the sun behind it before leaping into battle. The more it is allowed to bask in the sun before a fight, the more bombastic its moves become.
author: sk372

entry: As long as it receives sunlight, POKENAME is always very nice and friendly. However, as soon as night turns, its demeanor turns violent and angry, lashing out its frustration by using Razor Leaf against objects.
author: soup1900

entry: Known as 'Devourer of the Sun' in ancient myths, POKENAME reflects sunlight off its body as it blots the sun, causing floral mutations and anomalies to sprout from all living beings near it.
author: beatdoof

entry: These Pokémon lay in great, open fields for most of their lives as they bask in the sunlight cast upon them. When they get up to dance away their excess energy, they also scatter around countless seeds that become fields of beautiful flowers.
author: infinex21

entry: Often nicknamed 'Gentle Giant', smaller Pokémon tend to follow POKENAME around for their friendship and protection. Wherever it travels, entire ecosystems and flower fields sprout in its place.
author: rakunk

entry: Its umbrella-shaped leaf is capable of storing a massive amount of luminous energy, which is subsequently released in the form of flames. It also uses it to cover itself from bad weather.
author: tioghi

entry: Because of how fragile its leaf-like wings are, it only takes flight when the weather is clear. It prefers to walk on the ground most of the time, its feet drawing water and nutrients from the soil beneath.
author: mistymagius

entry: An unattended POKENAME will run after the sun twice daily, at sunrise and sunset. Trainers often have to track them back down by following the sound of their joyous song.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: POKENAME will often sit in other people's gardens, cheerfully absorbing sunlight. While some people see POKENAME as a nuisance, others welcome their positive attitude with open arms.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stands rigidly in forests or fields and absorbs sunlight. If an enemy approaches, it launches fire that has been known to light forest fires.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME produces leaves that are harvested for its ability to neutralize stomach acid, which helps with acid reflux. It requires lots of sunlight and plenty of clean water to sprout big leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It tries to remain in sunlight for as long as possible. This is because it begins suffering intense headaches the moment it no longer feels sunlight on its skin.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME absorbs large amounts of sunlight even as it dashes quickly through grassy fields, often seen as a mere blur of yellow and green due to the speeds it can reach. Its grassy fur is extremely warm to the touch.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constantly absorbs solar energy. Once it has collected enough, it can ignite entire firestorms. But it has to be wary of its flammable body.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME thrive on sunlight, their slender bodies growing longer the more sun exposure they get. During the summer month, sunflower oil will start dripping out of their mouths.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME takes food scraps and rotten produce and converts them into mulch inside its stomach. By resting in bright sunlight, it accelerates the rate at which the mulch is produced.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During the day, POKENAME climbs to the tops of mountains to absorb sunlight. At night, this Pokémon digs shallow burrows to rest, and while sleeping in said burrows, it appears to casual bystanders as just a simple rock.
author: lutrax

entry: If you happen to be on the peak of a mountain during a sunny afternoon, you could see a myriad of POKENAME enjoying the sunlight; however, be careful when climbing in the evening, as during that time herds of POKENAME may be rolling down carefree.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME devours nutritious soil in order to stay healthy. Excess energy is used to repair and replace rocks on its body. Some POKENAME have been seen creating compost piles in the wild.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME used to be a popular Pokémon racing breed. However since its speed depended on the sun, it was deemed too unreliable.
author: codewolfie

entry: This Pokémon lazes by sunny riverbeds, happily swirling its tail in the water and taking in the sunlight. Some have described it as being the pinnacle of blissful ignorance.
author: sk372

entry: It runs across the land at high speeds during the day, keeping its heads in the sunlight for as long as possible. Only when the sun is hidden does it finally stop moving and rest, until it detects the next ray of sunshine.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to laze on cold surfaces due to how warm their bodies get as they absorb sunlight. When they clap their leaves together or their tail against the ground, they scatter small leaves and petals from their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends its day planting seeds wherever it can. The most beautiful gardens are said to be around areas where this Pokémon gathers.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME spends its day planting seeds wherever it can. The most beautiful gardens are said to be around areas where this Pokémon gathers.
author: noel5229

entry: Despite their wings, POKENAME are flightless Pokémon. They use their wings to communicate with one another through dense forests, the trees filled with loud buzzing through the summer months.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It is said that it evolves when it is able to sustain supersonic speeds for long periods of time, which is why it is given unnecessary X Speed boosters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each portion of its body flies in a fixed pattern. It coordinates flight patterns each night before it falls asleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its keen eyesight and aerial maneuverability to ensure its devastating blows connect with its opponent.
author: grayslashjay_8566

entry: Its wings allow it to to escape from danger with ease. Its eyes can detect even the swiftest of movements.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fly just above the surface of the water, struggling to lift their body with their small wings. Even a small ripple in the water can send them off-balance and send them splashing down.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME crawl across the forest floor with amazing speed in search of the tastiest leaves. They rarely use the venomous stinger on their head because they can always make a speedy escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With 360-degree vision, those that try to sneak up on POKENAME will find it transforming to defend itself before they even get close. It typically excludes changing its eyes during transformation, so that it may retain its vision as a precaution.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its developing body being restrained by its cocoon, POKENAME can still actively avoid danger thanks to its light weight and strong wings. Its wings never stop moving until evolution is finished.
author: sk372

entry: It lets out a high-pitched shriek when the sun goes down. The sound is loud enough to cause the water on a pond to ripple.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather in large swarms once the sun sets, buzzing their wings in harmony with each other. The vibrations from all their wings can cause an entire house to shake.
author: mistymagius

entry: With Yanma's 360-degree vision and Noctowl's 180-degree head rotation and acute night vision, no attack can take it by surprise.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME's feathers are made of a thin chitin, creating a crackling sound as it flies. Its Bug Buzz is strong enough to break apart boulders, making it a powerful force when needed.
author: .izik

entry: It can be seen flying in a zigzag pattern all across lakes. The beats of its wings generate a plethora of static electricity, which it uses in battle.
author: schwaus

entry: Too heavy to fly, POKENAME use their wings to charge up static electricity and shoot shock waves as its main form of attack.
author: t.i.a.

entry: POKENAME fly so quickly that most only see streaks of the light produced by the orb on their tail. They flutter their wings at increasing speeds to generate electricity within themselves before they take off in search of food.
author: infinex21

entry: Quick fliers with superb senses of sight and hearing, POKENAME are experts at stealing food. One need only look away for a moment, and it will have snatched a new meal from them with hardly a sound.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can move at incredible speeds thanks to the constant flapping of its four wings. Its tail has prehensile properties and can grasp fruit or other objects, which it then carries safely back to its nest.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The wings atop POKENAME's head spin like a rotor. By day, it rests in sunlit clearings; at night, it buries its face in mud to absorb nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes extremely precise movements with its wings and can fly through gaps no wider than its body by folding its wings down as it passes through. POKENAME shows are held during Kanto winters with Trainers from all regions travelling to them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its body is too stocky for its wings to lift it, so POKENAME uses them only to produce powerful buzzing sounds. To shield itself from the sun, it rolls in mud, keeping its skin cool and moist.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's keen vision and amazing speed allows it to effortlessly take down prey. It's commonly seen hunting after the sun sets.
author: mepp.

entry: It does laps around local landmarks to time itself and improve its speed. It will make a minimum of 50 flights per day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME whir their wings to pump air inside of their bulbs, keeping the opening closed as they build up the internal pressure. When they are ready to release seeds they launch them using the stored pressure, able to fling their seeds many metres.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's goggle-like eyes allow it to see clearly beneath the water's surface. It dives from the sky with precision to catch its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME skims the water's surface at high speed. If anyone approaches its nest, it crashes into them and self-destructs.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its 360-degree vision, POKENAME possesses a fragile constitution. Still, it maintains composure in the face of danger.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME uses its high speed and sharp claws to effectively raid Beedrill nests for their honey. However, if another POKENAME tries to raid the same nest, they will end up fighting with each other instead.
author: mistymagius

entry: Courageous little thrill-seekers, POKENAME enjoy pushing the limits of what their aerial capabilities can do. A favored exercise is leaping from tall mountains and free-falling to see how close they can come to impact before flying off.
author: sk372

entry: It constricts its body around prey hard enough to break bones. Should it notice an enemy nearby, it will fly away with the prey still imprisoned.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME speeds across marshes with unmatched agility. When it spots prey, it delivers a midair punch with astonishing force.
author: .izik

entry: The sound of crackling static can be heard when POKENAME flutters its wings. Catching one can prove difficult, as it moves sporadically and can paralyze others on contact.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The flames within POKENAME's body intensify as it flies. Its glowing body leaves behind a faint trail of heat in the air.
author: .izik

entry: The flap of its wings can electrocute other bug Pokémon it flies by. Large groupings of POKENAME create elaborate lightshows at dusk.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME flies so fast that time slows down around it. Because of this, POKENAME's lifespan is about 50 percent longer than other Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: From POKENAME's tail and fluttering wings, unpredictable sparks are formed. POKENAME has incredible vision and can easily snipe faraway targets with electricity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is driven by a strong desire to help others. Though it has great potential, it doesn't know how to tap into this power.
author: jackythewannabe
