author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME seems to believe it is faster than it is. It will dart towards something only to stop just short of it. This makes it a terrible predator, so it gets most of its calories from plants.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It floats silently near children playing in swamps, using a quick Water Gun to push them into quicksand. As they struggle, POKENAME cackles with glee at their panic.
author: .izik

entry: When startled, POKENAME causes sudden ebullition in nearby water, releasing steam and static. It often slips into household appliances, especially humidifiers, which it uses to create soothing fogs or play harmless pranks on unsuspecting Trainers.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When startled, POKENAME causes sudden ebullition in nearby water, releasing steam and static. It often slips into household appliances, especially humidifiers, which it uses to create soothing fogs or play harmless pranks on unsuspecting Trainers.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When startled, POKENAME causes sudden ebullition in nearby water, releasing steam and static. It often slips into household appliances, especially humidifiers, which it uses to create soothing fogs or play harmless pranks on unsuspecting Trainers.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Previously residing in cyberspace, POKENAME now actively seeks out Trainers to befriend in the real world. Once it finds a Trainer it likes, it won't leave them alone. Ever.
author: inksans201x

entry: When startled, POKENAME causes sudden ebullition in nearby water, releasing steam and static. It often slips into household appliances, especially humidifiers, which it uses to create soothing fogs or play harmless pranks on unsuspecting Trainers.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The gel encasing POKENAME is believed to shield the fragile Pokémon within. When combined with Red Nectar, a refined version of this gel can be used to create X Speed. However, the raw substance is highly toxic and potentially fatal if mishandled.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Sometimes seen skipping over the sea, POKENAME migrate with the tides, their journey guided by the gentle pull of the moon. As they travel, they leave shimmering footprints on the water's surface that are briefly reflected, before vanishing.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME produces a hydrophobic substance that it covers itself in, allowing it to swim without getting wet. It teases small fish Pokémon by tickling their underside with its cotton, delighting in the panic it causes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is foremost a hoarder of gold, known for conning people out of their valuables. It creates illusions of deceased loved ones in water, demanding payment to sustain it, though it merely reflects what already lingers in the person's mind.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is foremost a hoarder of gold, known for conning people out of their valuables. It creates illusions of deceased loved ones in water, demanding payment to sustain it, though it merely reflects what already lingers in the person's mind.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hide under mud, waiting for prey. Anything that steps on their tough shell is pierced by steel spikes that inject a venom and decrease the target's speed. If a Trainer experiences this, the advice is to mimic Fearow noises.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite living underwater, POKENAME's flame never extinguishes. This was used as proof by pre-modern scientists for the existence of phlogiston, a colourless, odourless, tasteless, weightless substance existing in all combustible objects.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hide in marshes, their light barely visible above the surface. They are said to be souls that have drowned and are unable to pass through to the next life. Looking directly at them can cause feelings of nausea.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Due to the power of fusion, POKENAME has a rather timid disposition. If it falls down, it uses its powerful tail to push itself back up on its feet.
author: typhloquil

entry: An ancient text exists that seems to be a transcription of a panegyric praising a group of POKENAME for fighting off a group of sea monsters and saving the city. They continue to do what they can to protect people and their Pokémon.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: An ancient text exists that seems to be a transcription of a panegyric praising a group of POKENAME for fighting off a group of sea monsters and saving the city. They continue to do what they can to protect people and their Pokémon.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: An ancient text exists that seems to be a transcription of a panegyric praising a group of POKENAME for fighting off a group of sea monsters and saving the city. They continue to do what they can to protect people and their Pokémon.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME prefers extremes: extreme heat or extreme cold, extreme humidity or extreme dryness. As a result, POKENAME can be found in many places around the globe. It can cool itself down or warm itself up by controlling the flame sac inside its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives near reefs, where it burrows into the sediment on the ocean floor. Its slimy body blends in perfectly with the murky surroundings, making it nearly invisible to predators.
author: .izik

entry: For POKENAME, attractiveness is measured by how shiny it appears. It produces a glossy saliva that it rubs into its body to enhance its sheen. Known to collect and proudly display sparkling objects, some have even been found carrying Glitter Mail.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hides beneath a muddy cloak, mimicking the appearance of a drowned Wooper. It avoids sunlight and is often found lurking in bogs. Those who try to peek under its disguise report overwhelming sorrow, and never speak of it again.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME synthesizes strong webbing by digesting mud, spinning it into traps that radiate gentle heat during winter. Drawn in by the warmth, prey willingly enter and are lulled into an endless, painless sleep from which they never awaken.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Found living in underground lakes, POKENAME spends most of its time in the murky bottom. Anything that falls will be consumed, even inedible things like rocks. It produces a special mucus in its stomach that allows these things to pass through it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Each head of POKENAME has a mind of its own, fighting over food or direction. Despite their aggression, they are fascinated by ephemera, brief glimmers on water, falling leaves, or bubbles, which briefly distract them from their constant squabbling.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The tails of POKENAME harbour heat‑loving microbes in a remarkable symbiosis. Fuelled by the Pokémon's body heat, these microbes split water molecules and release a steady stream of oxygen, letting POKENAME breathe effortlessly underwater.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's power is directly tied to the gem in its centre. If the gem is critically harmed, it secretes a protective liquid to prevent further injury. Each time the gem is restored to its former resplendence after damage, POKENAME grows stronger.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Human lifetimes seem to pass by very quickly for POKENAME. It bonds with a single Trainer for the Trainer's entire life. It is not known if POKENAME mourns their passing, instead choosing to fall asleep for a millennium.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: While digging into the mud, POKENAME releases a thick slime that coats its entire body. This makes it incredibly slippery, allowing it to escape from predators with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gets irritable around flowing water, but it's too lazy to build dams like others. Instead, it prefers to live in mud, where it hydrates by sinking its gills into the muck, which draws out moisture, then licking the water off afterwards.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME emits a faint aura it uses to communicate with others of its kind. The signals travel best in cold air, so they gather in polar regions. Just before evolution, its entire body begins to glow softly, a sign of its growing inner strength.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time in the wild lingering around muddy areas. It scoops up mud to smear on itself to keep cool, and feeds by lazily picking at bugs and worms that scurry by.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is known for being rhapsodic, always displaying its emotions. When sad, it secretes a liquid from all pores on its body, with researchers believing these are its way of crying. The tears cause those that touch them to get suddenly energetic.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Some circles speak of a vaticination foretelling a land-dwelling POKENAME, normally impossible, as they dry out quickly. It is said this one will heal all the world's ills, drenching it in blessed water expelled from its great nostrils.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite its cute looks, POKENAME is feared at sea. Its beautiful song carries for a mile; inexplicably luring listeners to jump overboard. Once in the water, the music envelopes them, and they fall asleep, unable to stop themselves drowning.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME absorbs trace metals from seawater to prepare for evolution. However, due to rising pollution, it now takes in metals faster than it can grow, often evolving prematurely. This stunts its development and limits its long-term potential.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Depending on the rocks it consumes, POKENAME's protective slime changes flavour and properties. When it feeds on sapphires, the resulting film, if refined, can induce feelings of exultancy, making it a prized but rare material in certain regions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's wings move so quickly that they have to spray mist on them to keep them from drying out, though they are not very good at remembering to do so. Trainers notice this if they hear a susurrus from their Pokémon and remind them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Once dismissed as weak, POKENAME is now sought after for the mucus it secretes, able to be refined into a Fine Remedy. When threatened, it emits a flash of light so sudden and intense, scholars liken it to fulguration in the deep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME travel across oceans, using the energy from the tide to rotate around each other to move. This is a long process, and their peregrination can take over 100 years. Once they arrive at a new continent, they lay eggs and repeat the journey.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are often found together as a pack. There is no hierarchy and when one decides to get up and move, the others follow. They seem to be able to draw in nutrients from the soil by burying their tails in the ground.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The tuft of fur on POKENAME's head and tail is so incredibly soft that royalty once used it to stuff pillows. Sadly, illegal farms have begun breeding POKENAME solely for their fur, harvesting it and discarding the Pokémon.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: During summer, POKENAME's gills unfurl and secrete a sweet nectar that attracts pollinators. As the insects feed, they leave behind pollen. Once enough has built up on its body, POKENAME will evolve, completing a unique symbiotic cycle.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is known among horticulturists that a single POKENAME can turn a good garden into a great garden. This is because POKENAME can brush their oil-dappled flowers against any other plant, causing it to flourish and produce prize-winning produce.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME emits a fine, sulphurous mist that helps it fly. It is collected for scratch-and-sniff books, offering a whiff of what polluted rivers once smelled like during the height of industrialisation.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spend their lives at sea, though their swimming technique involves their ears thrashing about and makes it look like they are drowning. POKENAME is used as a nickname for an Ensign in the Navy, referring to their lack of experience.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Touching POKENAME without gloves causes intense pain, though leaves no lasting damage. There was a fashion a few hundred years ago to wear the treated mushroom from POKENAME pinned onto a suit and was considered sartorial elegance.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME loves to spook people by splashing water on them, though most times it's confused whether that person is spooked or laughing.
author: dodoowner_

entry: In some parts of the world, paper dolls resembling POKENAME are hung in windows in order to invite rain.
author: staghorn

entry: The gooey membrane around its body is extremely adhesive, allowing POKENAME to attach itself to tree trunks or rocks before dozing off. Once asleep, it remains motionless for hours as wind blows leaves and dirt that covers POKENAME.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME gather on the undersides of icebergs, filtering water through their gelatinous bodies to absorb nutrients and microorganisms. Their colour changes based on water quality. Recently, rising pollution has caused many to darken noticeably.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Carried by ocean winds, POKENAME is at the mercy of the elements. To survive, it coats itself in a hydrophobic film and curls into a ball, allowing storms to toss it about without harm, an odd but effective adaptation to its drifting lifestyle.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Researchers use POKENAME to monitor desertification. They only drink water near deserts, where sand and silt help them synthesize a special gel that keeps their bodies from drying out.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Nearly all subterranean lakes host habitats suitable for POKENAME. It primarily forages for food underwater and seeks rest by flying to the ceiling.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME sometimes carries a piece of Bead Mail etched with the face it had in a previous life. An agelast by nature, it never smiles, only weeps quietly when alone. Some believe its tears can etch memories into stone if they fall on ancient ruins.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It makes its home near hydropower plants, resting in the water to absorb residual electricity. POKENAME will emerge periodically to discharge static energy before returning to the depths.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's gills are as hard as stone and can be launched like projectiles when it feels threatened. While they regenerate over the next few days, it buries itself in mud to remain hidden and safe from predators.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME burrow through riverbanks with their tusks, searching for mineral-rich mud to eat. Their gills filter the water as they dig, and their tusks grow sharper the more they eat. They are friendly by nature, but fiercely territorial when nesting.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite the advanced science used in their creation, they are redolent of an ancient time where people and Pokémon depended on each other for survival. Some say that being touched by one causes you to experience all human emotions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite the advanced science used in their creation, they are redolent of an ancient time where people and Pokémon depended on each other for survival. Some say that being touched by one causes you to experience all human emotions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME live close to the poles. They are diurnal and only sleep when it is dark, which means they stay awake for up to 22 hours a day in mid-summer. The edges of their eyes go crusty due to this, so they produce a liquid to keep them hydrated.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hatches in swamps and grows by feeding on roots, plants, and even the mud itself. Researchers believe the mud plays a role in preparing it for evolution. Its colouration varies slightly depending on the soil type of its native habitat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The antennae atop its head are actually gills.  When possible, it will sleep dangling from a low ceiling, its gills submerged in a shallow pool.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Its drooped appearance is due to its spine having evolved to curve backwards, allowing it to lie flat and hide completely in mud. Politoed are known to seek them out, performing Belly Drum on their backs for fun, much to POKENAME's distress.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its drooped appearance is due to its spine having evolved to curve backwards, allowing it to lie flat and hide completely in mud. Politoed are known to seek them out, performing Belly Drum on their backs for fun, much to POKENAME's distress.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its drooped appearance is due to its spine having evolved to curve backwards, allowing it to lie flat and hide completely in mud. Politoed are known to seek them out, performing Belly Drum on their backs for fun, much to POKENAME's distress.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME wanders estuary mudflats in search of oysters and Shellder. By pressing its gills to the shells, it can sense if a pearl is inside. If so, it gently opens it, removes the pearl, returns them to safety, then greedily devours the gem.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME secretes a rare fluid once mistaken for Max Ether, believed to restore energy to Pokémon. Its rolling motion generates sudden impetus, letting it lunge forward with surprising speed when agitated or defending its muddy territory.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Many Trainers teach their POKENAME Poison Jab, as its numerous gills naturally secrete trace amounts of venom to deter would-be predators. With training it can weaponise this ability to pierce opponents dozens of times and inject them with poison.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: With its strong jaws, POKENAME can bite through cars, even though it has no teeth. It never bites cars that have their ignition on, as it is scared of the noise they make. In fact, it is scared of much of urban life, keeping well clear of cities.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite evidence proving POKENAME was an apex predator, its lack of arms has puzzled the scientific community. Some theories even suggest that POKENAME did have arms, but they have all been lost to time in the fossils remaining.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Traditions claim that POKENAME will visit houses that receive snowfall; it is custom to leave frozen Lemonade outside for them. There have been fewer reports in recent times, as scientists believe they are struggling to adapt to climate change.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME bob along on lakes, absorbing sunlight through their head leaves. When they spot anything smaller than themself, they devour it in a frenzy, often damaging their leaves. Most of the energy they gain ends up going into healing the damage.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A brand of soda called Psycho Soda uses POKENAME as their mascot, due to its seemingly limitless energy. It has developed a unique way of removing excess heat from its body, by producing a cold gel in its pom-poms and releasing it with a shock.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A brand of soda called Psycho Soda uses POKENAME as their mascot, due to its seemingly limitless energy. It has developed a unique way of removing excess heat from its body, by producing a cold gel in its pom-poms and releasing it with a shock.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has adapted to life in polluted waters, taking on the appearance of a plastic bag. Those who attempt to untie it often report being injected with a mild but unpleasant toxin as a defence mechanism.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: This Pokémon is unaware of the raw power it possesses. Instead of tearing prey to pieces it prefers to cuddle. Many Pokémon and Trainers get hurt over this act of affection due to POKENAME's rough skin.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME floats through marshy areas, mimicking sounds it hears in its surroundings. Though it believes this to be playful, many find its imitations unsettling, as they are eerily off-key.
author: .izik

entry: Simpleminded creatures that live around forest lakes and ponds, POKENAME spends much of its time keeping the waters clean of detritus. It takes fruit from nearby trees to share with the Pokémon that live in the water.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME submerges itself in swamps. They continuously draw in water, absorb its nutrients, then expel it from the top of their heads. This purified water is often the cleanest around, attracting many Pokémon to drink from it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is completely blind and lives in dark, cold caves. What appear to be eyes are actually specialized organs that detect chemicals released by ripe fruit. Incredibly sensitive, they can pick up these signals from over five miles away.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is completely blind and lives in dark, cold caves. What appear to be eyes are actually specialized organs that detect chemicals released by ripe fruit. Incredibly sensitive, they can pick up these signals from over five miles away.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is completely blind and lives in dark, cold caves. What appear to be eyes are actually specialized organs that detect chemicals released by ripe fruit. Incredibly sensitive, they can pick up these signals from over five miles away.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hates dirty environments and will use their gills to dust. Care must be taken not to disturb them when they are doing this as there have been reports of POKENAME using Aerial Ace on even their own Trainers!
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME constantly oozes a sticky slime that creates a warm, moist layer teeming with bacteria. A brief trend saw people keeping them to "boost immunity," but it quickly ended after a surge in hospital visits from infections and allergic reactions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME constantly oozes a sticky slime that creates a warm, moist layer teeming with bacteria. A brief trend saw people keeping them to "boost immunity," but it quickly ended after a surge in hospital visits from infections and allergic reactions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME squirts a highly acidic goo onto its targets, reducing them to nothing more than a Purple Juice. Small quantities of this goo were once used to treat animal hides, before modern chemicals were brought into use.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In the wild, POKENAME is often found amongst its pre-evolutions. Although it seems as though it is trying to teach them things, they are often much better than it, as evolving has seemed to cause it to lose proficiency in most areas.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although made of rocks, if parts of it fall off, they quickly degrade into Blue Juice that is sticky to the touch. This is believed to have been the final Wooper fusion to be discovered and added to the Pokédex.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: From afar, POKENAME looks like it is made of ice, but the shine is actually caused by a gel it secretes all across its body. This gel never decays so researchers have been able to accurately figure out how POKENAME migrated over millennia.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: An ancient Kalos oriflamme bearing a motif of POKENAME remains nearly untouched by time. Historians believe POKENAME used to symbolise royal power, loyal enough to serve, yet strong enough to obliterate anything that stood in the monarch's path.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: An ancient Kalos oriflamme bearing a motif of POKENAME remains nearly untouched by time. Historians believe POKENAME used to symbolise royal power, loyal enough to serve, yet strong enough to obliterate anything that stood in the monarch's path.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The petals of POKENAME are coated in a sticky sap that can crystallize in cold climates, preserving fragments of its DNA. This has allowed scientists to trace the evolutionary history of POKENAME with remarkable accuracy over millions of years.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sleeps for a century, its body forming fertile ground for wetlands. It grows by absorbing refracted light through water. When it finally stirs, the sudden shift sends ripples through the delicate ecosystem that formed around it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME enjoys soaking in water, so much that its owners should take precautions; if POKENAME senses someone taking a shower or bath, it will barge in unexpectedly in order to join them.
author: sk372

entry: The mucus coating POKENAME's body is highly toxic, capable of deterring even the most determined predators. It buries itself in wet, muddy areas, lying in wait for unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME buries itself in swampy terrain, absorbing nutrients from the mud. Any waste it can't digest is transformed into venom, which it injects into predators or intruders. The toxin varies by region, making a universal antivenom impossible.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its gills are very sensitive to its environment. If it is threatened it will swallow large amounts of water, inflating its body to hopefully intimidate its opponent.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is able to direct air into sacs at the base of its spines that, when inflated, expel the spines at close to the speed of sound. A gel is then released to cover the hole that has great healing properties, allowing a new spine to grow quickly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Though it appears sandy from afar, POKENAME's body has a jelly-like texture that naturally repels grains of sand. This unique trait is harnessed to produce a liquid used after beach trips that, when applied, will shed every last speck of sand.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME nestles in rocky crevices of coral reefs, remaining motionless for days at a time. To avoid predators, it secretes a scent-masking substance, but this also attracts parasites, many of which end up living on its body permanently.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: To survive, this Pokémon absorbs cold from icebergs, storing it in its gills to prevent overheating. Unfortunately, this accelerates melting, posing a threat to nearby species, especially as the climate crisis reduces sea ice.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME roams the ocean floor, moving as a quadruped would on land, despite its ability to swim. The frills on its neck reflect light all around it into its eyes, allowing it to see even in the murky depths.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Evidence suggests ancient ocean tribes once lived alongside POKENAME. It can dive deeper than humans and was used to scare fish toward the surface to be caught.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's elegant spinning inspired a dance where performers pirouette faster and faster before leaping into a mid-air split. It's even more stunning when POKENAME does it, spinning flawlessly on slippery mud with perfect control.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: On nights when it is cold enough to see your breath, POKENAME can sometimes be found playing at the water's edge, its beautiful scales glinting off the light of the moon. This stunning sight has been known to move people to tears.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite having no teeth, POKENAME's jaw strength is powerful enough to break bones. It thrives in shallow marshes, ambushing unsuspecting prey with crushing bites.
author: .izik

entry: The gills on a POKENAME seem to have a mind of their own and can steer POKENAME to a food source out of their sight. Scientists once thought they had a strong sense of smell, but extensive tests suggest that, in fact, POKENAME cannot smell at all.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME appears unstable, as if caught between two forms. Observers report seeing both Wooper and Ultra Necrozma flicker separately in their peripheral vision, but when viewed directly, it remains whole, adding to its mystery.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lounge half-submerged in tarns at high altitudes where many larger Pokémon struggle to breathe. Due to a lack of natural predators, they are very friendly and their scales glow with joy when Trainers approach them in their natural habitat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The scales on POKENAME's head are used to indicate its health, the brighter and shinier they are, the healthier it is. Potential threats are often scared away when POKENAME crouches low, directing light from its scales into their eyes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The scales on POKENAME's head are used to indicate its health, the brighter and shinier they are, the healthier it is. Potential threats are often scared away when POKENAME crouches low, directing light from its scales into their eyes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Though seen as a pest for living in pipes, stealing food, and making noise, POKENAME is rarely removed. It secretes a naturally antibacterial gel that cleans surfaces as it moves, so after its nightly sorties, many wake up to a tidier home.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Often found behind waterfalls, POKENAME hums when it is in a calm state, which can last days. Some people listen to recordings of this as a form of white noise to help them concentrate or sleep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Happy POKENAME emit a refreshing scent, reminiscent of lemongrass, but when distressed, it shifts to that of rotting fish. Some theorise it affects brain chemistry as Trainers grow deeply attached and tend to them with care one might give a child.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The word "whooping" is believed to have been derived from POKENAME's call. When happy, they make a noise that resembles a mix of cheering and laughter. Some children's dictionaries even include an image of it next to the word.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The gills on a POKENAME seem to have a mind of their own and can steer POKENAME to a food source out of their sight. Scientists once thought they had a strong sense of smell, but extensive tests suggest that, in fact, POKENAME cannot smell at all.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends hours a day styling their hair with a gel that they secrete. Vain Trainers keep these Pokémon to use their gel, and to get inspiration for their own hair.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Known for its gentle nature, POKENAME rubs affectionately against anything it meets. It can produce an ink-like gel from its gills, which it uses to craft a Leaf Letter, often primitive in its language, but unmistakably heartfelt in its intent.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Known for its gentle nature, POKENAME rubs affectionately against anything it meets. It can produce an ink-like gel from its gills, which it uses to craft a Leaf Letter, often primitive in its language, but unmistakably heartfelt in its intent.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The stick POKENAME carries helps it channel energy to locate geysers. Here, members of its kin gather to socialise, performing dances in the steam. They rarely stay together for long, as they feed on mineral-rich clay and guard their personal supply.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The stick POKENAME carries is bestowed upon it by its elders when it evolves. When it points it upwards and concentrates, it is able to see the future. Many point it downwards instead, as doing so lets them picture the perfect mudbath.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When POKENAME jumps, its tail also extends to give it more power. It has been recorded jumping over 50 times its own height. It does this both to escape predators and to play.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When POKENAME jumps, its tail also extends to give it more power. It has been recorded jumping over 50 times its own height. It does this both to escape predators and to play.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Early prototypes of the Jetpack used coal as fuel, inspired by how POKENAME converts it into energy. Ironically, POKENAME are terrified of flying and prefer to stay underwater close to geothermal vents, where they feel safest and most at home.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If you hear the faint squelch of mud while alone in a field at night, a POKENAME may be nearby, harmless, but eerie. A popular comedy-horror film follows one such POKENAME, unknowingly terrifying a group of teens despite just trying to make friends.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME consumes plants and, using its saliva, converts them into maltodextrin, a highly digestible sugar it stores in its body. Scientists now produce this compound synthetically, which is used in food or to feed sick POKENAME.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sings with a voice that trembles like it's holding back tears. Its mournful melodies sometimes sound like they're lamenting a lost Lone Earring. Some funeral companies even offer them to provide haunting background music for the grieving.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Male and female POKENAME are identical, though there is an easy way to distinguish them. The fur on males is much sweeter, and they also produce a syrup-like substance that is used in some areas as an ice cream topping.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's skin grows constantly, forming wrinkled layers that slow it down if not managed. In the wild, it scrapes against rough bark or rocks to shed the excess. When raised by Trainers, it enjoys soaking in mineral baths and being brushed clean.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME live amongst Wooper colonies and are fiercely protective of young Wooper. They play with them, letting them splash about in the water in the leaf on its head, which builds essential skills for the young Wooper.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME evolved frictionless skin for speed in water but dried out quickly on land. To adapt, they developed a water-storing pad to keep their skin moist. This adaptation slowed them down as they swam, leaving researchers puzzled by the trade-off.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME rolls along the seabed, moving faster in colder waters. When mature, they gather at hydrothermal vents, where the sudden heat triggers a response that launches them out of the sea and into the atmosphere.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: As POKENAME matures, gills erupt through gaps in its hardened spikes, which fall away over time. Each of these spikes will grow into an identical copy of itself, with no idea who its parent is.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are able to draw in moisture from the air and can spray water from their tail. There have been multiple reports of a POKENAME preventing a house fire by using its tail to douse the flames.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME dig through rocks in the shallows to build winding tunnel systems to live in that can be hundreds of metres long. Although this is much longer than necessary, POKENAME never stops expanding their system.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Historically, monarchs that have domain over the ocean have been expected to harness a gem from POKENAME. This was an arduous journey, as POKENAME are extremely rare. The trials the monarch would face during this would prove their rule as legitimate.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME swims around small ponds, leaping into the air whenever it senses a happy couple nearby. Some say it does this to share in the joy, while others believe it simply enjoys the attention.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dig through rocks in the shallows to build winding tunnel systems to live in that can be hundreds of metres long. Although this is much longer than necessary, POKENAME never stops expanding their system.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are rarely seen, spending their time mostly under the seabed. Their tunnels contain an area that is filled with discarded Old Rod and Good Rod lines, which has led to debate on whether they snap anglers' lines or clean up ocean pollution.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: There was once a trend among surfers to paint their Surfboard gold coloured, so it would catch the sun and impress onlookers. This didn't last long though, as wild POKENAME would steal them when not being guarded.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: There was once a trend among surfers to paint their Surfboard gold coloured, so it would catch the sun and impress onlookers. This didn't last long though, as wild POKENAME would steal them when not being guarded.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: There was once a trend among surfers to paint their Surfboard gold coloured, so it would catch the sun and impress onlookers. This didn't last long though, as wild POKENAME would steal them when not being guarded.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's whiskers are so sensitive to changes in air currents that they have even been seen to outmanoeuvre a Fast Ball being thrown at them. Their speed doesn't necessarily equate with agility though, as they often crash into nearby obstacles.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Aquariums love to have POKENAME in their exhibits, as it is great at cleaning up excess waste and algae. It will happily clean the tanks it is assigned to, commonly kissing the glass at passing trainers.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME are typically found around brackish water, where they live sedentary lives feeding on aquatic plants. They are often slow to react to danger but have latent psychic powers that activate when threatened.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A slimy coating covers POKENAME's skin, capable of inducing severe migraines if touched. The symptoms fade after a full day's rest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very playful and enjoys soaking swimmers that are bracing themselves to get into cold water. They say it helps them acclimatise to the water quicker, and if they are ever in danger, POKENAME carries them to shore.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A popular brand of Climbing Gear shares its name with POKENAME due to their ability to climb seemingly unscalable cliff faces. They can even use their gills and tail to hold them in place if their arms get tired.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can be found in the deep depths of the ocean where they are covered in a special mucus that protects their pearls and prevents deformities from forming. As a result, their pearls are some of the most valuable pearls that can be harvested.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A popular brand of Climbing Gear shares its name with POKENAME due to their ability to climb seemingly unscalable cliff faces. They can even use their claws to hold them in place if their arms get tired.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The drop in intelligence when this Pokémon gets angry is barely noticeable as it is already very dim. It follows any instruction from its Trainer to the letter, so great care must be taken when issuing commands.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: There was once a rumour that to get a Wooper and Growlithe to fuse, you had to capture them both using a Level Ball, then feed them a popular brand of vanilla ice cream. It has since come out that it was a publicity stunt by the ice cream company.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Watching a POKENAME race across expansive plains is a breathtaking sight, its tail trails behind like a ribbon, rippling for hundreds of meters in the wind. In ancient times, people revered it as a steward of the land and worshipped it accordingly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Generally, POKENAME are gentle creatures, preferring to stick close to other Water Types. But if they become furious, POKENAME can cause torrential rain from spraying water uncontrollably from their tail.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The tips of POKENAME's gills twitch rapidly when it's happy. It secretes a poisonous slime with a scent that changes based on its diet, after consuming a PP Max, it is said to smell oddly like butterscotch.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is coated in a mucous-like film that, while unpleasant to touch, can be used as a base for a Clothing Dye Kit. By steeping dye pigments in the film, it enhances their colour and helps them soak more evenly into fabric.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: According to superstition, if a POKENAME is hooked with a Super Rod, it must be caught in a Lure Ball, or else it will summon a raincloud of frogs over your house. This may explain why most Trainers prefer using other rods entirely.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: According to superstition, if a POKENAME is hooked with a Super Rod, it must be caught in a Lure Ball, or else it will summon a raincloud of frogs over your house. This may explain why most Trainers prefer using other rods entirely.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME were one of the Pokémon extensively studied during the development of the Teleporter. They were calm and friendly with researchers and, when rare accidents occurred, were able to regenerate lost limbs without distress.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME were one of the Pokémon extensively studied during the development of the Teleporter. They were calm and friendly with researchers and, when rare accidents occurred, were able to regenerate lost limbs without distress.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME remained unindexed for a long time, as it would hypnotize anyone who saw it into forgetting it existed. Even Trainers who raised a Woobra and watched it evolve would forget this stage once it changed again.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It's difficult to tell if POKENAME is smug or simply vacant, as its expression never changes. Rather than swimming in the traditional sense, it manipulates water molecules around its body, allowing it to glide effortlessly without moving a muscle.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Never hand a POKENAME Bricks as they'll immediately try to headbutt them in half, thinking they're being helpful. Some construction companies have even banned them from worksites due to the costly misunderstandings they cause.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Never hand a POKENAME Bricks as they'll immediately try to punch them in half, thinking they're being helpful. Some construction companies have even banned them from worksites due to the costly misunderstandings they cause.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Galley captains once prized POKENAME for their incredible rowing strength, able to match human rhythm but deliver over 100 times the power. On sunny days, however, their skin would dry out, forcing them to abandon the oars and swim alongside instead.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Galley captains once prized POKENAME for their incredible rowing strength, able to match human rhythm but deliver over 100 times the power. On sunny days, however, their skin would dry out, forcing them to abandon the oars and swim alongside instead.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A world record was set for the biggest edible sculpture of a Pokémon. The likeness was of POKENAME and featured some of its favourite treats. Cannoli for gills, a blueberry pie as the left pec, and a scone forming the centre of its belt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Galley captains once prized POKENAME for their incredible rowing strength, able to match human rhythm but deliver over 100 times the power. On sunny days, however, their skin would dry out, forcing them to abandon the oars and swim alongside instead.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A world record was set for the biggest edible sculpture of a Pokémon. The likeness was of POKENAME and featured some of its favourite treats. Cannoli for gills, a blueberry pie as the left pec, and a scone forming the centre of its belt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's weak neck muscles give it an appearance of a permanent stoop. This posture inspired a squat variation named after it, where athletes bend at the hips until their torso is at a 90-degree angle to the floor before performing each rep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's weak neck muscles give it an appearance of a permanent stoop. This posture inspired a squat variation named after it, where athletes bend at the hips until their torso is at a 90-degree angle to the floor before performing each rep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's weak neck muscles give it an appearance of a permanent stoop. This posture inspired a squat variation named after it, where athletes bend at the hips until their torso is at a 90-degree angle to the floor before performing each rep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME constantly dribbles gruel-like liquid from its mouth, both foul-smelling and incredibly potent. When a Chesto Berry steeps in it, the mixture attracts Steel-types, who seem to enjoy the tingling, foaming sensation it produces on their skin.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are very playful and are usually found in large groups. One of their favourite games involves jumping as high as they can out of the water, then tucking into their shell to create the biggest splash.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: During the day, POKENAME hides under the earth and extracts nutrients from mud by chewing it. At night it emerges and expels the mud as a spitball, looking almost like a brown Strange Fruit.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Found in wetlands, POKENAME spend most of their lives half-submerged in mud, remaining totally still as they wait for prey to wander close. To lure targets, they produce a Vivid Scent that clings to their body, drawing in Pokémon from far and wide.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Be cautious when using a Box Link near POKENAME. If their tentacles make contact, they can somehow poison the Pokémon stored inside. Their incredible regenerative abilities are now being studied for potential breakthroughs in treating aging.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives a simple life, filter feeding in muddy mangrove forests. Its tentacles are harmless, used only to pull itself through dense undergrowth.
author: dylonk25

entry: Docile and content to watch the world pass by, wild POKENAME happily let miners hang Lanterns over their gills for extra light. Their tough skin and mucous coating encourage algae to grow, giving them a mossy appearance.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's greatest joy in life is curling up into a ball and rolling down waterfalls, making waterfall swimming in their territory quite dangerous. There is a company at the top of Tohjo Falls that uses POKENAME to deliver Tropic Mail to the bottom.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life underwater, surfacing only on the coldest day of the year to shed its skin so it can grow. This rare, discarded skin is a prized ingredient in the crafting of a Heavy Ball by master artisans.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The surface of POKENAME's skin is covered in a sticky gel containing copper. This causes the flames it produces to burn blue. When it sneezes, it is engulfed in a temporary inferno, much to the delight of the internet, which finds it adorable.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Unlike its previous form, POKENAME is highly disliked in contemporary culture. This is because it is known for attacking newborn Pokémon. It does this to absorb their energy, which fuels the flames along its back. If they go out, POKENAME dies.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Docile and simplistic to an extreme degree, POKENAME "hunts" by floating along the rivers with its mouth open and half-submerged, hoping something will float into its waiting maw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have lost all the playfulness they exhibited as a Wootle. They now spend their time hunting alone and preening but still get lonely if they are away from others for too long.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A cruel Trainer once tried to pry the Shellder from a POKENAME's tail with a Pickaxe. Ever since, POKENAME have shown a fear of the tool, releasing a sticky sludge from their gills whenever they see one, an involuntary response to fear.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Throwing a Safari Ball at a POKENAME rarely works as expected, as its natural magnetism disrupts the ball's trajectory and causes it to veer off course. This effect has not been observed with any other type of Poké Ball.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is made up of three linked bodies that emit low-frequency magnetic waves. These pulses keep it suspended just above the ground. During storms, it hums softly, and the mucus it generates becomes highly conductive, glowing with static charge.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Able to regrow any part of its body, POKENAME are far less cautious than most Pokémon. It is said that they are only able to perform Air Slash after they have lost their wings, as once regrown, they return even stronger than before.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is said that, on rare occasions, a POKENAME is born with only one head and possesses superhuman intelligence. There's no evidence to support this, and may simply be a comforting myth, as most POKENAME are incredibly dull and often forget to eat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The first recorded incidence of this Pokémon was after an unfused Wooper and Dodrio were smashed into each other by a Draco Meteor. Rather than knocking them out, it only seemed to make them stronger – though not smarter.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is playful and affectionate, making it seem like the perfect pet, until it leaves the water. To protect its skin, it secretes a harmless but putrified-smelling slime that quickly drives most people away.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's breath is so cold it creates a constant mist around its body, helping to keep its delicate skin moist. Often found lounging on drifting icebergs, they can pose a hazard to sailors, who must rely on Defog to safely navigate around them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its thick, ink-like coating smells strongly of Belue Berries, masking its presence in quagmires. This sticky substance clings to anything that brushes against it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME oozes through sewers absorbing pollutants and leaving behind a trail of toxic leachate. Water quality is slightly improved if POKENAME moves in, as it can digest some pollutants, but its stench is so reprehensible that even Grimer avoid it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME often fight each other for fun using the water cannons on their backs. They are fierce protectors of Wootle and Wootortle, ready to lay their life down to protect the group.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Once considered a delicacy in Hoenn, POKENAME were so rare that a single serving of their meat cost the equivalent of three months' wages. Thanks to fusion tech, a popular fast-food chain now offers them in a weekly promotion: "POKENAME Wednesday".
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Once considered a delicacy in Hoenn, POKENAME were so rare that a single serving of their meat cost the equivalent of three months' wages. Thanks to fusion tech, a popular fast-food chain now offers them in a weekly promotion: "POKENAME Wednesday".
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is said that POKENAME was first created when a Wooper was struck by Embargo mid-evolution, severing the link between body and soul. The result was a soulless Quagsire, and the birth of POKENAME, a spectral being with echoes of its former self.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is said that POKENAME was first created when a Wooper was struck by Embargo mid-evolution, severing the link between body and soul. The result was a soulless Quagsire, and the birth of POKENAME, a spectral being with echoes of its former self.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Young POKENAME are mischievous, constantly playing pranks and vanishing into mist before they're caught. Mature POKENAME can use Dark Pulse to incapacitate Pokémon over 100kg.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hides within the ripples of the sea, only glimpsed from the corner of your eye. Swimmers who drift into sudden cold patches may find one clinging to their legs, dragging them downward. The only known escape is to strike it with Comet Punch.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Spending most of its time tunnelling under the seabed, it needs to come to the surface occasionally to harden its skin. It bursts out of the sea at such velocity it almost looks like it is flying, and is commonly misidentified as a young Gyarados.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: As POKENAME draws near, a strange sense of disorientation and light-headedness washes over those nearby, resulting in the word "woozy" originating from this effect. Prolonged exposure often leads to sudden, dreamless sleep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is incapable of feeling pain and, as a result, may be unaware of any injuries it sustains. Fortunately, its body regenerates quickly.
author: noel5229

entry: Even small morsels of food can cause a feeding frenzy in POKENAME's territory. They are very social and live in large colonies but always squabble when it comes to mealtimes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME dream of exploring the world but are too lazy to swim far, so they cling abaft the undersides of passing ships. Highly social, they pick up accents from the beaches they visit and no two POKENAME sound exactly the same when they speak.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME love to rest in swampy water where they absorb nutrients through their skin. They are careful to keep their flower bud above the water to absorb sunlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Scientists have been unable to determine if POKENAME is either too damp or too lazy to explode. It stays completely still for long periods of time.
author: duskrd

entry: It constantly sticks its tongue out, either to be funny or because it has to. It swims around in marshes and swamps.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME floats through the air, releasing a thick, polluting smog. It lacks any malicious intent in this; it is simply oblivious to the toxic nature of its own gasses.
author: fancyskunk

entry: Performers known for theatrical, flashy shows once called themselves "POKENAME" after its elegant fins and graceful movements. The name stuck, and many still wear ornate costumes inspired by its vibrant appearance and flowing style.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME regularly takes a dip in water between flights, as its wings don't function well without sufficient moisture. Its favorite meals are plants and mushrooms that grow in the muddy edges of ponds and lakes.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME slashes with its blades, it sprays smelly water from the tips. The odor distracts opponents just long enough for a follow-up.
author: .izik

entry: It regularly gets lost in the ocean while swimming. A school of POKENAME were seen on Rind Island during their migration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives near large rivers, scooping up fish from the water's surface. It is always in a good mood and can be seen peacefully taking naps in the shallow water.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives and sleeps in deep mud banks. While under the mud, the only evidence of a POKENAME's presence is often the bubbles it creates rising to the surface.
author: bee4082

entry: It can spit clumps of mud and gushes of water to deter foes from approaching. It prefers to feast on the nectar from flowers growing by still lakes and small rivers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's disproportionate limbs make flight awkward, yet it doesn't seem to mind. It has quickly gained popularity among younger generations.
author: char_latte3412

entry: When POKENAME discharges electricity, its skin dries rapidly if out of water. It must re-submerge quickly to prevent painful cracking.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores air in a special sac in its tail, allowing it to float lazily downstream while napping. Its thick skin protects it from sharp rocks and predators. Children sometimes mistake its bobbing tail for a toy and try to reel it in.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME loves to just sit in the riverbed, absorbing the water into its skin. It has an incredibly relaxed and positive attitude, and plenty of other Pokémon will laze with it to enjoy the peaceful vibes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rolls around in mud, which sticks to it due to a sticky film that coats it. Sometimes insects and small Pokémon get caught up along with the mud, which POKENAME happily plucks off itself and snacks on.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME rolls around in mud, which sticks to it due to a sticky film that coats it. Sometimes insects and small Pokémon get caught up along with the mud, which POKENAME happily plucks off itself and snacks on.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: This fusion is said to be the king of all Quagsire. The larger and more decorated the crown, the more respect it has.
author: valtsuri

entry: POKENAME absorb nutrients from mud through their skin to nourish the leaves on their tail. Whenever the sun shines in their eyes, they shade themselves with their leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is very sluggish and unmotivated. It will often just lie down on the ground with its mouth open, waiting for something to wander in. If someone watches POKENAME do this for long enough, they can even see its fangs grow in real-time.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME has a toxic membrane surrounding its body and is seemingly oblivious to the outside world. It gathers with other POKENAME at seemingly random points in the day and dances, which is an enigma that scientists are still studying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME leaves its mouth open until prey wanders into range, at which point it moves at great speed and devours it. It then tightly closes and slowly digests its food; a single meal can keep it satisfied for several months.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's slimy body causes it to slide around and repeatedly bump into cave walls. The indents left behind by its steel-hard body can be used to track down its movements.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME love to splash in large ponds and puddles, flapping their wings to coat them in water. They are clumsy in flight and will frequently fly into any person unwary enough to be sat at the water's edge when they take off.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time swimming at the surface of rivers, occasionally diving under the water using their broad wings to propel themselves. Whilst they can fly, they are very clumsy and inelegant in the air.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rests lazily among coral reefs, gnawing on coral when hungry. If injured, it uses Recover to heal any damaged parts with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits an ink-and-mud mixture at any passersby, emitting a loud cry once the blob impacts its target. At first it was thought to be territorial behavior, but apparently this is actually considered a friendly greeting for POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: When elated, POKENAME prances around and happily flails its wings around, scattering its grimy feathers around. These dissolve into the ground over time and help nurture the mud and soil.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are extremely playful in nature and adore splashing in large bodies of water. If it stays in too long, the water will boil.
author: pankiwi

entry: A stealthy swamp-dwelling Pokémon that likes to eat smaller amphibians. It's unknown how it survives in the wild, as captive-kept POKENAME are often confused by prey even when they're right in front of them.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lives near large lakes, decorating its antlers with all sorts of aquatic plants. Its strong hooves allow for it to walk through the muddy terrain without getting stuck.
author: mistymagius

entry: A POKENAME slowly follows prey across river bottoms, releasing poison into the water. Their mouth opens wide to catch the meal when it stops moving.
author: peachesparfait

entry: It is said a single yawn from POKENAME could cause a tsunami. POKENAME lives placidly at the bottom of the sea, completely undisturbed by any physical contact it receives.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are little fairies who protect the forest with their combined magics. While dopey and carefree, they never forget what happens in the forest.
author: theeggoverlord

entry: When POKENAME overeats, it often falls asleep while swimming without even realizing it. Since it has no trouble breathing underwater, it can spend hours napping on the riverbed, using mud and algae as a comfortable bedding.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Whenever POKENAME moves suddenly, its oversized tongue flails uncontrollably, splattering anything nearby with thick drool. Some Trainers resort to gently securing its tongue to prevent getting soaked during battles or travel.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Though passive by nature, POKENAME lashes out with vines when disturbed. Once it traps a threat, it resumes napping without concern.
author: .izik

entry: It brings blessings of guidance wherever it floats. Those who follow the wake of a POKENAME are led to the choicest swamps in the area.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME's back quills drip with a blue fluid that smells awful. Though only mildly toxic, it causes intense itching on contact.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME is very lazy, since it lies around all day. When the sun gets in its eyes, it uses its tail as a shield.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: In prehistoric times, POKENAME grazed on aquatic plants. It is so absentminded that it rarely notices predators until it's far too late.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is quite rare in the wild, as it does not put a lot of effort into looking for food. Instead, it just lazily floats along the river, waiting for any fish to swim within reach.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's default offensive strategy consists of headbutting its opponents, though its head is too squishy and empty to do any significant damage.
author: sandguything

entry: It defends smaller Pokémon on instinct, but its simple mind holds no ill will towards aggressors either. Those that are halted by ramming into its solid skull wind up getting a friendly lick from POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: In the early days of first discovering POKENAME, it was thought that the slapping of its tail against the ground was play behavior. It's since been discovered it's actually an attempt to communicate and warn of impending disasters.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often inadvertently scares away potential playmates by popping up from marshes with a startling cry. It is entirely harmless, so those that don't run away will find a blissful friendly companion eager to travel with them.
author: sk372

entry: In the past, they were hunted for their nutritious blubber, as one POKENAME could sustain a group of ten people for an entire winter. After this practice was banned, they continued to live for decades, and many alive now are hundreds of years old.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live a slow-paced life where most of their days are spent napping. Conserving energy is vital for these large creatures, as it takes a lot of energy to move a few feet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trudge through swamplands to find fresh water. Whenever they find something of interest, they get a rare burst of agility that allows them to waddle towards whatever piques their interest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME reside in muddy marshes, where it lounges in shallow water. Its low speed means it will not be going anywhere fast.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves to entertain others, particularly young Pokémon. Its signature act has it spurting water from its head and causing its "hat" to fly off and fall back on it, pretending to be knocked out by the impact.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon lives and raises its young on the muddy hills by riverbanks. Its body has a poisonous film around it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's glossy coat contains a moisturizing solution that keeps it from drying up as it crosses over land.
author: .realthree

entry: During the winter season, they find a friend and swim into underwater caves in search of a place to hibernate. It is said that they always choose the same friend every time during hibernation season, as they help each other feel safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME appears beside a recently deceased Pokémon, all others instinctively step aside. It's believed they sense its supernatural presence, allowing it to carry out what many consider sacred funerary rites.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is mostly inactive, requiring only water in order to survive. It always seems to be in a good mood, shrugging off most attacks without even noticing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are very protective of young Wooper and will often hover around marshes with large populations of Wooper. They will lift the young Pokémon to safety if they sense danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Each of its tails is very heavy, but it never seems to struggle to hold them up.  The mucus its skin excretes glistens brilliantly in the sun.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME has been known to make an imposing entrance, its towering form emerging from impossibly shallow puddles of swamp muck. After this, it bumbles around with no apparent goal.
author: dylonk25

entry: The twin water-like limbs of POKENAME give it a long reach to touch and curiously explore its surroundings. These limbs can purify small bodies of water, turning them fresh and crystal-clear in an instant.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is quite lazy. It can sit in the mud for so long that the earth will dry around it, leaving it immobilized until it rains again.
author: blitzydragon

entry: Whenever it rains, POKENAME will start splashing and throwing mud violently. Territories of POKENAME are usually covered in dried mud because of this.
author: blitzydragon

entry: The friendly smile of a POKENAME is enough to soothe any swimmer that happens to pass by. POKENAME enjoy drifting above the waves, carrying tired people and Pokémon on their backs to help them to shore.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its clumsy nature makes POKENAME wobble when it walks on land. Despite seeming harmless, it can coat its fins in electricity in an instant to defend itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Because of its terrible memory, it sometimes forgets that it is chasing prey and abandons the hunt altogether. In the water, POKENAME moves as fast as lightning, and a single swing of its tail is enough to propel it several meters forward.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lies in a pool of mud and waits for prey to wander into its open mouth. It is almost never successful.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME usually live in smaller seas. If POKENAME get sleepy, they cover themselves with their wings and burrow into the seabed.
author: niseria

entry: POKENAME rests in fast-moving streams, letting the current turn its gear-like body to store energy. It releases this power in bursts, propelling itself with its tail at great speed. Its life is spent slowly journeying upriver to lay its eggs.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: As long as POKENAME's body is submerged in its gel, it can regenerate any body part within a few hours. Scientists theorize that if a cut-off limb is kept in the gel, it will grow into a new POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: As the sun sets, colonies of POKENAME emerge from caves and collectively dive into nearby lakes. They hunt, mouths agape, for any algae to feed on.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Though lacking fangs, it occasionally attempts to bite people or Pokémon to draw blood. Victims are left covered in an uncomfortable, slimy film.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME flattens itself out as much as possible and waits until something comes along and treads upon it. Once something does, it lets out a joyful cry, as it treats being stepped on like winning a game.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lays down for long periods, using the soft beard as a cushion while waiting for prey to accidentally walk into its open maw. It is incredibly calm but loves to be pampered like royalty.
author: pjporwoll

entry: They are cold-blooded Pokémon that do not generate their own heat, yet their blood does not freeze when exposed to sub-zero conditions. Their blood acts similar to anti-freeze, which keeps the blood pumping in frigid conditions.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because it loves feeding on the grime it finds in water, POKENAME is often used to keep public pools clean. It is a very sociable creature, but since it doesn't smell pleasant, it is often avoided.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swims quickly through brackish waters with a trail of Wooper in tow. It frequently slows to ensure none of them are left behind.
author: .izik

entry: It swims with enough force to scuttle any ship on contact. Sailors must douse their boats with Skuntank odor to prevent POKENAME from coming close.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME happily sits at the bottom of the river, catching small fish that swim by with its tentacles. While its skin secretes a toxin that it uses to incapacitate its prey, the poison can't get through human skin.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME remains unnaturally calm unless its school is threatened. When it senses danger, it releases a powerful Psyshock to drive predators away.
author: .izik

entry: Its affinity for sunbathing has lead some to speculate that its head can photosynthesize, but it ducks its head down whenever someone tries to check.
author: bukie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time curled up in narrow crevices, protected by its tough armour. When it finally uncurls and stands, it often forgets its size and bumps its head, causing small tremors that ripple through the ground.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Unlike many other Carbink fusions, POKENAME lacks the ability to float in open air. They fare better in freshwater lakes, eating microbes and occasionally small fish and bug Pokémon.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME has poor eyesight but uses its antennae to develop a picture of its surroundings. Its fur is covered in an oil that lets it speedily swim and irritates predators that come in contact with it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives in marshy areas, playfully throwing mud at each other as a form of competition. When dried a little, its mud can be turned into a rich clay that is often used in pottery.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME perches for days, blissfully unaware of anything that happens around it since its wings leak powdery scales with a strong numbing effect. This powder is collected to be used in a variety of pain relief medications and anesthesia.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME calmly basks in river shallows, absorbing sunlight with its lily pad. It only becomes active to dance with other Pokémon, especially enjoying entertaining young Pokémon like Wooper.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are coated in a thin mucus layer that keeps their skin moist even when they leave the water. The mucus is highly flammable and POKENAME will use it as kindling when they want to cook food for themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME communicate through a complex language of clicks, bubbles, and body movements. After years of study, researchers believe their most commonly used phrase roughly translates to, "I'm hungry, let's eat".
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME communicate through a complex language of clicks, bubbles, and body movements. After years of study, researchers believe their most commonly used phrase roughly translates to, "I'm hungry, let's eat".
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although POKENAME are very lazy, they wake up at exactly 6 a.m. every morning and let forth a loud horn-like bellow, before promptly falling back to sleep. Some military bases use this sound as a reveille to wake up troops.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME will float along rivers accompanied by Quagsire for company while it meditates in the water. POKENAME psychically connects with the dim-witted Quagsire's dim-witted mind to help empty out its own thoughts and concentrate on meditation.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Incredibly lazy, POKENAME considers a stretch to be a full workout. Despite this, its lithe muscles allow it to effortlessly dodge attacks and flop back down before its opponent even finishes their move.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Not much has changed in the feeding behavior of Quagsire or Gulpin when they form POKENAME: they wait for prey to enter their wide-open mouth. Anything that enters, from Pokémon to trash, is soon eviscerated in its powerful stomach.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Incredibly lazy, POKENAME considers a stretch to be a full workout. Despite this, its lithe muscles allow it to effortlessly dodge attacks and flop back down before its opponent even finishes their move.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its body is covered in a thick layer of mucus that can cause migraines if ingested. The mucus will dry if it stays out of the water for too long.
author: .izik

entry: It has developed an inferiority complex of sorts, being compared to Golsire. It wishes for a more well-built body, hiding its envy behind a smile.
author: megaban

entry: It bumbles through the sky without a care until it notices a swamp. Letting its steamy wings dissolve, POKENAME plummets downward and lands with a joyous squelch.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME has a lovable but dim-witted personality. Its massive size is matched only by its childlike enthusiasm. With wings made of soft clouds, it soars lazily through the skies, often getting distracted by the slightest breeze or shiny objects.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME drift down lazy rivers on their backs. They effortlessly push debris aside with their well-developed arms.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME is a nocturnal being that still sleeps through most of the day. It feeds by using psychokinesis to force small, weak, or injured Pokémon into its mouth before dozing off again.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME needs to be constantly exposed to water, otherwise its body will start to dry out. As it requires very little food to survive, it will often let other POKENAME hide in its mouth.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME was long thought to be a discoloured version of Tentacool until a researcher on beach vacation discovered a dead one and classified it as a separate species. They are sought for their ink, which has a special dark blue tint.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME is friendly but doesn't seem to realize its tentacles are covered in stinging barbs. It will hug those it meets, who are left with a burning rash.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gooey, mane-like fin on POKENAME's back is dangerously hot. Its temperature increases the faster it runs, making it difficult to ride.
author: .izik

entry: In the water, POKENAME is an almost peerless swimmer in speed and agility. On land, however, its gait is slow and clumsy, constantly tripping over itself and flopping onto the ground.
author: sk372

entry: Even while asleep, POKENAME's tail wags steadily. It slaps the mud or water with its tail, sending rhythmic signals to friends nearby in ponds or swamps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is so clumsy it often collides with icebergs or ships while swimming. It uses its icy breath to slow down prey swimming ahead, making them easier to catch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is an easygoing and dim-witted Pokémon. It leaves its mouth open in the water and waits for prey to wander inside, eating their life force and leaving the physical body behind.
author: bee4082

entry: Whenever POKENAME are nearby, people report feeling sleepy or groggy. This is because the mucous membrane around their skin releases pheromones that cling to receptors in people's noses.
author: quackquackattack

entry: People report becoming drowsy whenever POKENAME are nearby. This is because its mucus membrane releases pheromones that cause lightheadedness and dizziness. It is also known to eat dreams when people fall asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swing their vial of Mystic Water to hypnotize. People report having dreams of being swallowed by fish, which comes as a result of POKENAME using Dream Eater.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores its psychic energy in the bulb on its back. Its twin-tails are actually sensitive vines that it uses to sense the emotions of other Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME survive in the wild by reading the minds of those around them. By tapping into the thoughts of predators, they can avoid detection by hiding before getting noticed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Anyone who approaches POKENAME will be overcome by uncontrollable sadness. When frightened, POKENAME will lash out with its immense psychic powers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME always begins a fight physically wielding the bone it carries, but shows its true strength as the fight goes on, manipulating the bone psychically to distract opponents while it hits them from elsewhere with powerful Psybeams.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scares predators away from an area by speaking to them with telepathy. Predators mistake these thoughts for the thoughts of much more dangerous Pokémon, so they often leave gifts for POKENAME as a plea to leave them alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On the longest day of the year, POKENAME will gather in big groups. That day, they will dance for as long as the sun is out.
author: rosemagwin

entry: POKENAME's rigid ears serve as a conduit for its psychic power. If its ears are covered and kept away from sunlight for too long, it will lose its telekinetic abilities.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are usually found in herds known as collectives. When in a pinch, the collective will attack with a giant psychic blast.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME have a diet of bitter herbs that foster their psychic abilities. They are capable of lifting and restraining many Pokémon at once, which helps them avoid getting eaten by predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The red gem on its forehead reads the exact proportions of an opponent. It uses this data to perfectly mimic their form.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever it needs a boost, Trainers give it an X Sp. Atk to help it shine through a tough battle. The booster is said to produce a stronger effect during the day, though this could be an exaggeration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's psychic abilities are especially attuned to predicting and navigating aquatic disasters. It is often a companion to sailors and rescue workers as it is adept during storms and floods.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME reserve most of their energy for growing within their cocoon. If a particularly persistent predator bothers them, they release psychic waves that cause the predator to experience headaches.
author: quackquackattack
