entry: In ancient times, POKENAME's feathers were woven into ceremonial headdresses. These were believed to help wearers release deep-seated grief.
author: .izik

entry: Although technically an omnivore, POKENAME's rear head is usually dominant and decides the diet. On rare occasions, the heads are equally dominant, leading to a mixed diet of meat and plants.
author: krune

entry: While running through the forest, POKENAME's rear head bobs in delight. If it feels very happy, it emits a cheerful chittering sound.
author: .izik

entry: Its specialized nervous system prevents the head from getting dizzy, no matter how quickly it spins. The same does not apply to the tail, however.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME often hides within tunnels near fields, waiting for intruders. When other Pokémon venture into its territory, it strikes with its tail, delivering a venomous bite.
author: _kuke_

entry: What appears to be a tail with a mouth is actually the organ with which POKENAME produces milk. Most farmers who have POKENAME confess the sight of its milk production can be a little unsettling.
author: sk372

entry: It is said to run at the speed of lightning, using its two brains to effortlessly manage high speed movement and react to obstacles in an instant.
author: kiwiarms

entry: When angered, both the head and tail fight in unison. A single prick from its tail's barbed tip can melt a foe from the inside.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME's tails react to water quality, allowing it to know what's safe to drink. The left prefers cold water, and the right prefers warm.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME builds static along its body to immobilize approaching predators. Once they are stunned, it unleashes a rapid series of telekinetic blasts to drive them off.
author: .izik

entry: After evolving, POKENAME relies even more on its additional heads. It hardly uses its upper body for anything.
author: slaphappygrandpa

entry: POKENAME itself is rather docile, but the head on its tail is rather vindictive. Even if POKENAME would rather flee than fight, the head will hurl dark magic from its mouth and instigate battles on its own.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's eyes have completely disappeared. It instead uses its ball to look around, tossing it from hand to hand to get a full visual.
author: jackskipper

entry: Various cultures have spun tales of POKENAME sneaking into children's bedrooms to drain their blood. However, despite these myths, POKENAME have only been observed using venom to subdue much smaller prey.
author: rakunk

entry: Despite seemingly being two separate Pokémon and having different personalities, the two parts of a POKENAME can never be separated.
author: lyrebird.rainwing

entry: POKENAME channels its telepathy through its tail, reading the minds of all nearby. Should it feel threatened, it will spit flames before fleeing, using its fire to ward off potential dangers.
author: .izik

entry: Using psychic powers, POKENAME avoids water mains and power lines while digging. This precision keeps its tunnels safe and efficient.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flames ignite mid-strike, guided by instinct sharpened in countless fights. The heat of its body rises with each attack, fueling its final blow.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME is known to be jovial, though it is prone to bouts of despair. Its tail is said to have its own personality.
author: .towerxvi

entry: The head on POKENAME's tail wields venomous fangs to paralyze enemies. Its serrated bite leaves a lasting impression in battle.
author: .izik

entry: The head on POKENAME's tongue has its own mind and is actually the only one between the two that is capable of experiencing the sensation of taste. The mouth on POKENAME's main head is used only for communication and little else.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME uses telekinesis to control water flow while constructing its den. This ensures its home remains stable even during heavy rains.
author: .izik

entry: There is a second head hidden in POKENAME's throat, which finishes off any prey that fall into its enormous maw.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The rear head will occasionally sense a separate disaster from the main head, influencing POKENAME and leaving it torn on which to assist with, often freezing up and helping neither.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon can only move by floating. It feeds on algae by plunging its neck into the water.
author: spagalapof

entry: POKENAME are often seen walking in circles, as the front head tries in vain to eat the leaves sprouting from the rear head.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME's tail head constantly grooms its fur using poisonous saliva. This habit keeps its coat sleek and adds a layer of defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's blade and tail are naturally hostile to most who approach it. However, vegetarian offerings to the hilt's side will calm it down.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The living shield keeps watch while the blade sleeps, and vice versa. Unfortunately, this means that one of them is always tired when they engage in battle.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It uses telekinesis to immobilize foes before striking with its razor-sharp claws. POKENAME regularly scrapes its claws on stones to keep them sharp.
author: .izik

entry: The large mouth covering POKENAME's central head has its own powers that radiate sleepy energy. The discomfort of having the large mouth over its head is released as nightmares upon all who slumber around it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's secondary head has a powerful cannon for a nose. It is advised to stay far away from POKENAME during allergy season.
author: kiwiarms

entry: This Pokémon's soul is so strong that it forms a protective aura around the body, resembling a mighty beast. When POKENAME sleeps, its aura shrinks, but never completely fades away.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The two heads specialize in different things, so they swap which is in charge based on the situation. The yellow head walks upright, while the brown one runs on all fours.
author: kiwiarms

entry: In ancient times, goldsmiths used POKENAME's flames to melt precious metals. The intense heat allowed for intricate craftsmanship.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its claws to dig up and steal crops from fields. It stuns farmers with psychic energy before making its escape.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME pretends to be unaware of its surroundings, its tails, actually a disguised head and jaws, watch for predators sneaking up on it. When they strike, the maw snaps closed and devours its prey, frightening off the victim's allies.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The two faces of POKENAME share a single brain. Despite this, they often try to move in opposite directions, leading to them going in circles.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME's two heads work together to solve problems, communicating telepathically with one another. Nobody knows what happens to food the smaller head eats, as it lacks a digestive system.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME floats over crop fields, scattering pollen from its leaves. Inhalation causes vivid visions of multiple possible futures that baffle researchers due to their occasional accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's antlers help focus its telepathic powers in order to locate prey from great distances. This ability makes it a skilled hunter in dense forests.
author: .izik

entry: The gem thinks it's in charge, telepathically commanding its partner to carry it around. The partner uses the gem as a blunt weapon against foes, to its dismay.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME's false head is so convincing that nobody knows which end of the Pokémon is the real front. It shuffles as if pulling in 2 directions, an act which lulls foes into a false sense of security.
author: robosoup

entry: Small but fierce, POKENAME uses psychic force and mighty stomps to protect its friends. It can hold on with a powerful bite, thanks to its strong jaws.
author: curazy

entry: The spores POKENAME produces can cause unusual effects when inhaled, such as causing the sensation of an out-of-body experience, visual distortions, and uncontrollable vocalizations. POKENAME itself is shy and usually harmless.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME dance and shout, cheering for their allies. Every word of encouragement from the main body of POKENAME is met with jeers and scathing remarks from the heads on the ends of its hands.
author: kingd8

entry: The extra heads atop POKENAME alert them to predators and secrete a sticky, toxic goo upon biting. The heads also grab onto vines and pull the body up into trees for safety.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME emits an odd frequency from its ears that messes with its opponent's mind. This frequency also agitates its tail, and it will attack POKENAME with little remorse.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a cuddly and gentle giant despite its strength and size, but its tail is a bit rambunctious. It must be careful not to hold those it hugs too long, or the tail may try to bite them while in its embrace.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME spreads its cape wide, it releases a fear-inducing aura. It follows up with a devastating kick to incapacitate its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launches its sharp needles with deadly accuracy. Its telekinetic powers allow it to redirect these projectiles mid-air for a surprise attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roams beaches, consuming toys left behind by visitors. These objects sustain it as it waits for more prey to arrive.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very protective Pokémon, always having one member of their herd on lookout duty. If they see a predator coming, they will not only warn the rest of their herd, but also any other Pokémon nearby.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: If POKENAME psychically detects an intruder, it howls loudly from both heads. This display warns others to stay away from its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases pink powder clouds during attacks. In Johto, pharmacists once used this powder in poultices to reduce inflammation.
author: .izik

entry: The face on POKENAME's wings is just a pattern, but it seems to be alive. Stare into the eyes, and a strong presence whispers into your mind.
author: robosoup

entry: In dense forests, POKENAME telekinetically steals jewelry from travelers. It prowls silently, leaving its victims unaware of their loss.
author: .izik

entry: Powerful psychic forces keep POKENAME's secondary head from rolling off the main head. It would take three Machamp working together to pry them apart.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME is a surprisingly well-mannered Pokémon, as all the usual aggression appears to have been funneled into the tail. As a result, the tail gnashes and swings at anything approaching it, even when POKENAME sleeps.
author: sk372

entry: They can be found anywhere there is vegetation, even if they are rare in number. They exercise constantly in order to control their anger; indeed, POKENAME are usually far less aggressive than Primeape.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's second head reads its Trainer's emotions. It barks joyfully when it senses its owner's pride, eager to deepen their bond.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur is very protective, keeping it safe from physical harm and cold weather. The tail often spews fire to keep possible flankers at bay.
author: moopse

entry: The head controls the arms, while the gut controls the legs. Despite their differences, they work together well enough to handle even the toughest opponents.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME expels torrents of acid from its mouth to weaken foes. The quantity of acid increases significantly if it has recently eaten.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME moves quite awkwardly, but can chomp down with frightening speed. The larger face plays dumb, but seems to be the mastermind here.
author: robosoup

entry: The rear head of POKENAME is attached to a long vine. It wraps the vine around treetops while it sleeps to ensure stability.
author: .izik

entry: The two halves of POKENAME produce flames independent of each other. The front half uses its fire offensively, while the back half applies it for defensive maneuvers.
author: sk372

entry: The head on POKENAME's tail breathes fire in beautiful patterns while it runs. This flashy display shows off its agility and confidence as it races through prairies.
author: .izik

entry: The head is a herbivore, while the tail is a carnivore. While the head munches shoreside shrubbery, the tail is in the water, snapping up unlucky fish that swim by.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME enhances its Water Pulse with psychic energy. This ability allows it to curve the attack and strike foes from unexpected angles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carries its own tail, which contains a secondary head with its own tiny brain, close at all times. The tail can consume plants and fungi the main head cannot, giving it an alternative way to gain sustenance.
author: sk372

entry: Its second head will regularly nibble and gnaw on anything that gets too close. Due to its smaller brain, it will occasionally bite the other head, forgetting they share a body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses as much energy scouring the plains for food as it gains eating. Thus, even while sleeping, its tail-heads must search for its next meal.
author: spaghettimoe

entry: The ooze that houses the head has a minor awareness of its surroundings. To protect the head, the mouth will snap closed if danger is detected.
author: .realthree

entry: The ooze that houses the head has a minor awareness of its surroundings. To protect the head, the mouth will snap closed if danger is detected.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's hypnotic powers are all its own, not requiring the help of the small head it carries. It lets the head think it's crucial to the hypnosis effect so that it can feel helpful.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's claws each have a mind of their own, operating independently from the main body. Though symbiotic, they often get into minor disagreements over food.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME's claws each have a mind of their own, operating independently from the main body. Though symbiotic, they often get into minor disagreements over food.
author: theartemis1

entry: As POKENAME naps beneath the sun, it releases a gentle Pomeg Berry scent from its pinecone bulb. If disturbed, it awakens with a surprising bang.
author: .izik

entry: To keep its legs flexible, POKENAME sheds the bark that normally covers them. Though this leaves them vulnerable, its powerful kicks quickly drive away would-be predators.
author: soup1900

entry: It prefers to rest in berry trees while waiting to evolve. It is not uncommon to see packs of POKENAME in Grepa Trees outside of Silver Town.
author: .izik

entry: The child is more aggressive and combative than the parent. POKENAME is often forced to restrain the young, to keep it from leaping out of the pouch and exploding at something.
author: sk372

entry: Due to the unique texture, POKENAME makes a soft crackling noise with every flap of its wings. Sentret are known to enjoy gnawing on these crunchy scales when they shed and fall to the forest floors.
author: sk372

entry: Popular among bug catchers, POKENAME has rough fur that helps to protect it in the wild.
author: melodydelune

entry: If POKENAME senses the scent of a ripe berry, it can't help but run off to eat it. From its rigid tail, it can fire powerful electric shocks at anyone foolish enough to underestimate it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's cocoon is made of several rigid plates layered over each other. It constantly grows new plates to replace the old, so that its defenses remain strong until it completes its evolution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers pollen from flowers and stores it in its pinecone-shaped hive. At dawn, swarms descend on flower fields before vanishing with explosive speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a sturdy shell that smells like roasted nuts. They hang from trees where they eat leaves off of branches. They communicate with each other by swinging their tails to help one another defend themselves against predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME nests in pine trees and leaps at threats with rapid Fury Swipes. If defeat seems certain, it detonates in a fearless last stand.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a keen sense of time that rarely goes awry. Whenever it gets angry, it takes exactly 5 seconds from the moment it hisses to the moment it explodes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME nests in pine trees and guards its perch. It emits hypnotic waves from its eyes to lull intruders to sleep.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME consumes too many flowers, it panics and flies erratically. The instability causes it to detonate shortly afterward.
author: .izik

entry: It gathers the debris that fall onto its web and arranges them into a giant version of itself. When a bird Pokémon gets too close, it shakes the web to make its replica move like it's alive.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME clings to pine branches using its talons and sleeps upside down. It remains completely still during the night, blending in with the canopy above.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found where shooting stars have fallen recently, adding shards from the fallen meteors to their shell. They are easily surprised and quick to explode, so it is not recommended to disturb POKENAME groups during this time.
author: chibitales

entry: This Pokémon has a soft, spongy body that secretes sticky fluid. When the fluid hardens around bark pieces, POKENAME can be used to scrub surfaces.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME removes and offers tiny plates from its own body as gifts to those it is fond of. They grow back quickly, and the self-removal is painless, so there's no harm in accepting the present.
author: sk372

entry: During stormy nights, POKENAME receives intense visions. If a vision frightens it, it will detonate in a panic.
author: .izik

entry: During storms, POKENAME stands in open fields to attract lightning. It stores the charge and uses it to explode when predators like Houndoom threaten the herd.
author: .izik

entry: While drifting over pine forests, POKENAME watches for predators. It floats down gently with a disarming smile, then detonates on contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs from tree branches using its hand-like tail. When threatened, it drops down onto predators and explodes in a blinding burst of smoke and splinters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bury themselves just below the surface to avoid getting blown away by a gust of wind. If another Pokémon comes to uproot them from their spot, they explode and release a burst of seeds into the nearby area.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has a possessive streak when it seeks a tree to perch on. If Kakuna and similar Pokémon hang threads on its tree, it will use the beating of its wings to blow them all to the forest floor so it alone can remain.
author: sk372

entry: The shape of POKENAME's head protects it from flying Pokémon that would otherwise predate on it but restricts their field of view. They are very clumsy when walking on land and prefer to spend their time in muddy water, looking up at the sky.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's stiff, woodlike whiskers twitch as it scans for scraps. It thrives in city alleys, sniffing out discarded food with surprising accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees, attracting the attention of prey with its red tail, before dropping on its food. When it is attacked, it retaliates with an explosive burst of energy that flings much of its bark armor at the aggressor.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic sense to read others' intentions. If it detects malice, it bolts straight at the offender and explodes without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: Fusing a pair of Pineco together results in POKENAME developing an extra-dense coating of bristles, making them even more durable. They are also more prone to detonate than their unfused siblings, creating dangerous situations in the Johto wilds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Fusing a pair of Pineco together results in POKENAME developing an extra-dense coating of bristles, making them even more durable. They are also more prone to detonate than their unfused siblings, creating dangerous situations in the Johto wilds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME may leak out a sweet-smelling sap from its pinecone-shaped shell to lure other Pokémon closer before it attacks. The black body is both flexible and durable.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The bark-like hide on POKENAME's face keeps it from injuring itself when swinging its horn. If the horn breaks, it will explode in a burst of heat.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME have a tough scaly shell that allows them to endure many stings from Bug-type Pokémon. This is helpful when they steal honeycombs from hives.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dwells in coniferous forests and acts as a protector of the trees.  Many deforestation efforts have been brought to a halt due to its attacks.
author: bostroms

entry: It resembles a grenade as an adaptation to deter predators. Sadly, most of its predators don't know what a grenade is and thus are not intimidated.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME are very generous and kind to humans and Pokémon alike. They like to give nuts, Berries, and fruit to humans to spread the joys of nature.
author: lemmymaster

entry: POKENAME feeds on pine needles and cones to fuel the flames within its body. If threatened, it scatters Spikes around itself before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rolls much slower than other Pokémon. However, it is much more devastating if it manages to roll over its prey.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME rubs its body against tree bark in order to help scrape and snap off plates of its body that have grown excessively. The fallen pieces biodegrade quickly and provide more nutrients for soil and plant life.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME connects to electrified signs and cables to charge. If it absorbs too much power, it overloads and erupts in a crackling electric explosion.
author: .izik

entry: Although it retains Arbok's constricting instinct, it mainly puts them to use by holding on tightly to trees and tree branches.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME blasts fire from its pinecone-shaped head when excited. These fiery bursts can scorch nearby foliage or mark territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a layer of scales that protect them from bites. They produce milk that is tinged with a nutty flavor that is perfect for turning into ice cream.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides amongst the trees, using its bristled plating to camouflage against the trees. When threatened, it will fire off these plates like grenade fragments, charged with large amounts of electricity.
author: mistymagius

entry: If POKENAME grows frustrated while gnawing at a tree, it detonates in an effort to topple it. Its powerful blasts leave splintered stumps scattered across the forest.
author: .izik

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME wraps its arms around pine branches. Its body is lined with venomous microscopic spikes, making it dangerous to touch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME like to wander around the land peacefully. Other people and Pokémon are invited to camp on its back during the night.
author: funkytomate

entry: It allows weak bird Pokémon to breed on its back. POKENAME can shoot explosive pine cones from the large tree if anyone tries to disturb its guests.
author: chorb33

entry: Its ribbon adds blade-like bark to its sticky center to hit attackers with. As a last resort, it explosively breaks apart and slowly repairs itself.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: In battle, POKENAME charges with its horn. If defeat seems likely, it explodes in a last-ditch effort to bring down its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME paralyzes threats by scattering green spores from its body. If its kin are endangered, it will charge forward and explode in a selfless act of defense.
author: .izik

entry: Swarms of POKENAME burrow deep underground. If disturbed, they explode violently, leaving wide crevasses in the dirt.
author: .izik

entry: In battle, POKENAME performs swift martial arts strikes. For ranged combat, it throws its pinecone-like cap like a spinning discus.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in spruce trees and uses illusions to confuse travelers. It often disguises itself as a lone lumberjack working in the forest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rests in clusters beneath shady trees. When disturbed, it puffs out dark green spores that paralyze anything nearing its sleeping kin.
author: .izik

entry: If a Graveler enters POKENAME's caves, they swarm it from above. They detonate one after another in a synchronized sequence to drive it out.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eats pinecones and sleeps in tree trunks. If it doesn't consume enough fuel, its body somehow overheats and combusts from within.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep woods, disguising itself as a pinecone while it sleeps during the day. It bites into thick trees, drinking the tree sap inside with its hollow fangs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lies in wait, hidden among the branches, ready to drop onto the heads of unsuspecting passersby who get too close to its tree. Once it falls, it coats its body in electricity to prevent anyone from touching it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is extremely competitive and races other Pokémon around its coniferous forest habitat. To win a race, it will unleash an explosive burst of energy to catapult itself forward, after which it faints.
author: pjporwoll

entry: As POKENAME gently sways in its dance, the fringe makes a scratchy rattling sound as its bark-like feathers rub together. If something bothers it during the dance, POKENAME loses all semblance of calm and explodes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When tired, POKENAME possesses old pine stumps to rest. If roused, the entire stump explodes in a burst of ghostly force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nest in Trevenant's branches in colder forests. If danger nears, Trevenant hurls them like grenades, allowing them to explode on impact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drips a sticky Cheri Berry-scented sap from its mouth to lure prey. Once the target draws near, it detonates to stun them for its kin to feed.
author: .izik

entry: This ancient, glacial bug seals itself in icy crystal bark to ward off predators. When threatened, POKENAME releases a dazzling aurora from its shell that disorients foes before detonating itself with a chilling blast.
author: jitteryjared

entry: POKENAME burrows most of its body down into soft soil to sleep or feast on roots. If a predator should agitate the part that remains above ground, its plate-like mushrooms on its back will eject and burst into blinding, irritating spores.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats above crop fields with glowing red spotlights on its body. When it detects an intruder, it scatters Spikes and subdues them with a Rapid Spin.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME sees an intruder near its pumpkin patch, it dashes at them and explodes. It has very little instinct for self-preservation.
author: .izik

entry: If someone approaches its pond, POKENAME leaps out of the water dramatically and explodes to protect its tranquil territory. Many travelers avoid ponds containing POKENAME entirely for this reason.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often found milling around groups of Pineco in the wild. It crawls over them and eats small insects that will cling to the Pineco and bother them, grooming them while gaining sustenance for itself.
author: sk372

entry: When irritated, POKENAME explodes, scattering coins from an unknown source in all directions. Despite ample research, nobody knows where the money comes from.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wields its leek like a duelist's blade. It fights with flair but is volatile; should it stumble, it explodes with the force of its own embarrassment.
author: .izik

entry: The central head psychically commands the others, coordinating attacks with precision. Its cannon-like mouths unleash devastating Bullet Seed barrages.
author: .izik

entry: The saliva dripping from its tongue can paralyze foes on contact. This makes close combat with it particularly dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: The horn on its face launches Spikes around a prey's nest to prevent escape. These spikes are crafted within its body by consuming metal ore.
author: .izik

entry: It collects chunks of iron ore and stores them in its pouch for safekeeping. This ore is believed to enhance its defensive capabilities.
author: .izik

entry: The metallic clusters on its body grow like scales, forming a layer of protective armor. This natural defense is reminiscent of medieval knights.
author: .izik

entry: Its large eye allows it to see clearly, even in thick fog. This keen vision makes it an effective scout in murky environments.
author: .izik

entry: Its sharp eye analyzes enemy movements, allowing it to mimic them perfectly. This mocking behavior often throws foes off their game during battles.
author: .izik

entry: It wields its sharp arms like bayonets, delivering swift slashes to foes. It then scatters Toxic Spikes around its opponents to ensure they can't retreat.
author: .izik

entry: It releases Toxic Spikes from the horn-like cannons on its head. These sharp projectiles create a deadly trap for anything nearby.
author: .izik

entry: As its anger grows, the iron plating on its skull hardens. It repeatedly charges at foes, even long after they are subdued.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nests should be given a wide berth for safety's sake. Extremely territorial, it fires sharp spines from its front limbs, launching at high speeds from long distances.
author: sk372

entry: It fires stones from its arm cannons with rapid precision. These rocky projectiles can easily shatter obstacles.
author: .izik

entry: It stands in fields soaking up sunlight for hours. Once fully charged, it emits a sweet aroma that encourages nearby plants to grow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has two mouths, one on either side of its head. They open and close at such speeds that the nearby water heats up slightly, though they are not very precise and often miss their prey.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It fires sticky mud through the cannons on its arms to slow down foes. This allows it to escape easily when threatened.
author: .izik

entry: The horn on its head functions as a powerful cannon, glowing pink while charging a Zap Cannon. Its aggressive blasts can topple even large foes.
author: .izik

entry: It fires gallons of sticky, honey-like goo from the cannon on its chest. Scientists are still baffled by the mechanism behind its sweet secretion.
author: .izik

entry: After rolling through canyons, it uses its snout to collect displaced dirt. Later, it deploys this dirt as a defensive barrier against predators.
author: .izik

entry: Its elastic body allows for exceptional freedom of movement. Most attacks bounce harmlessly off its rubbery skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rests motionless on lakeside rocks, appearing to be just another stone. Its sticky shell naturally pulls in any nearby trash or algae, cleaning the water wherever it naps.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its vine-like tendrils are incredibly sturdy and can wrap tightly around foes. Once captured, it reels its prey into its tangled body for immobilization.
author: .izik

entry: Before mating with others, POKENAME will find the finest and strongest log and hallow it out. It will then raise its young there.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its floating spikes act like hands, and will transmit any sensations to POKENAME. It likes to dance and create shapes with its spikes in front of children for their entertainment.
author: darxer_

entry: The blades on its arms have turned into cannons and its attack patterns have become more unpredictable. Any damage to its armor causes it grief.
author: pokopish

entry: POKENAME build up pressure within their thickly plated body and use this pressure to shoot out seeds from cannons from their back. These projectiles can be fired up to a hundred meters away, though they are not especially accurate.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It tests the strength of its jaws by constantly biting down on objects. Anything it finds is fair game, from rocks to metal scraps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's aggression and paranoia have risen sharply since fusing. When provoked, it lashes the barnacle-like protrusions on its tentacles at speeds of over 50 kilometers per hour.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: Its metallic shell hardens if it senses an impending hurricane. Some researchers believe this reaction is an attempt to shield itself from debris carried by strong winds.
author: .izik

entry: It lingers near graveyards, offering seemingly comforting hugs to mourners. However, it absorbs their sadness to sustain itself, feeding off their grief.
author: .izik

entry: It is incredibly sluggish and slow, but it can fire projectiles surprisingly quickly from its cannons. You can only damage it from the underside.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's plates carry a strong electric charge. If touched, they can instantly char skin with a powerful shock.
author: .izik

entry: It seeks out iron-rich materials to eat, reinforcing its durable helmet. This habit makes it nearly impervious to physical attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Its helmet is as hard as titanium, giving it formidable defense. Every night, it diligently polishes it to maintain its eerie shine.
author: .izik

entry: When enraged, it unleashes fiery blasts from the cones on its arms. The intense heat leaves scorched paths in its wake.
author: .izik

entry: Its long, rubbery arms can extend up to 15 feet to fire Spikes with pinpoint accuracy. This extended range makes it highly dangerous in combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's meals consist of stone, dirt and other minerals in its home. As it digests, parts of the materials get compacted and stored in the pores on its sides, to be fired out at high speeds in self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: Although it appears gelatinous, the material covering its body is as hard as glass. This toughness helps it withstand heavy impacts.
author: .izik

entry: Its fluff is as hard as steel but malleable like cotton. It's used to make armor and other metal clothing since it's both soft and durable.
author: soup1900

entry: Its fluff is as hard as steel but malleable like cotton. It's used to make armor and other metal clothing since it's both soft and durable.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are clad in a metal shell with little to no openings. Because of this, their bodies are often at risk of overheating, so they regularly vent steam from the red ports around their necks.
author: infinex21

entry: It shapes and dyes its frozen shell to deter predators. Researchers note the subtle differences in each shell's hue and form.
author: pokopish

entry: POKENAME's steel armor conceals its form. By day, it hides underground, revealing only its poisonous leaves.
author: anarchaz

entry: Ever vigilant of the forests they tend, POKENAME will fire off discarded fragments of their metallic armor from their fingertips at intruders.
author: sandguything

entry: POKENAME drools an acidic saliva with a strong Ganlon Berry scent. It can launch this fluid from one of its three cannon-like appendages.
author: .izik

entry: It fires spikes from the cones on its fists with incredible precision. These spikes can reliably hit targets from over 100 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME avoids physical contact with others when able. In a pinch, however, it swings its metallic body with great force.
author: bukie

entry: Although its fungus is hidden by its shell, POKENAME spores can still infect others. It can retract into its large steel shell, like other Forretress.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The extra limbs on POKENAME can fire a multitude of psychic attacks. Despite this, its hard shell makes it better as a physical attacker.
author: ohok3441

entry: It fires Poison Powder from the cannons on its claws to debilitate foes. The toxic cloud it generates is difficult to avoid.
author: .izik

entry: Its abdomen splits open during battle to release Poison Powder. The toxic cloud envelops foes, leaving them incapacitated.
author: .izik

entry: The gem on its forehead grows warm when it spots something valuable. If the object is metallic, it consumes it to reinforce the shell on its skull.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time staring blankly into space, ignoring most outside stimuli. Should something manage to startle it out of its stupor, it instinctively creates and fires spikes made of psychic energy as a defense mechanism.
author: sk372

entry: The hard shell on its body leaks a fruit-scented toxin. This sweet yet deadly aroma lures in small Pokémon, which quickly succumb to its venomous trap.
author: .izik

entry: When startled, it spits spikes from its mouths and runs erratically. Both heads flail wildly, causing chaos in its wake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's impressive shell is capable of keeping it buoyant, as well as withstanding attacks from dangerous aquatic predators. Cargo ships take care to avoid groups of POKENAME floating on the ocean's surface.
author: caldonb

entry: It can charge and stab foes with the drill on its face. POKENAME's wings are purely vestigial: it cannot fly, for it is too heavy. They burrow deep in the dirt to rest.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Wild POKENAME are incredibly shy and only get along with those whose DNA is similar to their own. They use what must be foul-smelling secretions to mark their territory; although humans cannot detect the smell, other Pokémon seem to be repulsed.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its tiny wings allow it to hover near the highest branches, where it plucks White Apricorns with its vines. It prefers knocking them loose before collecting them one by one.
author: .izik

entry: When put on the defensive, POKENAME buries its tail into the ground to stabilize itself. Doing this allows it to become much more accurate in its ink shots.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have very long lifespans, living up to 200 years if they are lucky. However, as POKENAME ages, it will slowly lose the will to hunt for itself.
author: mistymagius

entry: Pressing the red circle on POKENAME's torso makes it emit a variety of funny noises, making it popular with young children. Pressing the red circle on its face hurts it, however.
author: sk372

entry: It seems like it would be good for transport with its gentle nature, but is too focused on sleeping soundly in the dirt to give a ride to anyone.
author: fountainihili

entry: POKENAME most often evolves in the wild by finding evolutionary stones while using its tail to dig through the earth. There are even instances of it drilling through walls and glass displays in stores to get to these stones.
author: sivanandi

entry: POKENAME was once used by game developers to dig realistic caves and tunnels in video games. It was replaced due to being too shy and digging in the wrong spots.
author: equation8573

entry: Wishing to become a true dragon, Dunsparce fused itself with Dratini to create POKENAME. However, it still has a lot of learning and training to do.
author: milchik

entry: This fusion tries its best to look beautiful and majestic. Despite its attempts, no one likes it because of its overly large head and silly face.
author: milchik

entry: Dunsparce's wish to become a real dragon came true with this fusion. Despite being quite powerful, POKENAME is actually pretty bashful and kind.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME lives in massive underground caverns dug out over hundreds of years. It's rarely seen by humans, but will appear in moments of need to rescue cavers from their untimely demise.
author: lasercraft32

entry: Its wings are too weak for sustained flight, but it spends hours attempting to flutter just above the ground. This persistent effort showcases its determination.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME detects prey like Nincada beneath the ground, it will dive from a branch and drill straight into the dirt. Its accuracy is so precise that it rarely misses its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a great storyteller. Trainers often visit this Pokémon's burrow to learn from its vast wisdom.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME uses the horn on its head to burrow through the earth. As it tunnels, it lines the walls behind it with thick yellow silk to reinforce them.
author: .izik

entry: Researchers are still trying to determine how POKENAME navigate caves with such speed and precision. They have been known to drill elaborate burrows for their families.
author: schwaus

entry: During heavy storms, POKENAME flies up to a cliffside and anchors itself by drilling its tail into the rock. This keeps it from being blown away by fierce winds.
author: .izik

entry: It feeds on gems found on cave floors, breaking them apart with its powerful tail. This diet helps its body sparkle faintly in dim light.
author: .izik

entry: Scientists are unsure if POKENAME exist naturally in the wild due to their obscurity and tendency to teleport away the moment they detect someone. Even a strong Trainer's POKENAME will weakly flutter around, unable to properly carry its own weight.
author: bobosmith01

entry: In the wild, POKENAME is usually found at the mouths of caves gazing contemplatively at the sky outside. It has become popular as a wise but absent-minded character in a children's television show.
author: sivanandi

entry: According to local Johtonian legends, when a POKENAME properly opens its eyes, devastating power is unleashed. However, this has never been properly observed.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME burrows underground using its drill tail to wait out droughts and cold weather. When the first rains start to fall, they emerge from their burrows and will sing loudly to one another across great distances.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The flower on its head spins as its wings carry it gracefully from tree to tree. Its drill-like tail serves as an anchor when it lands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always drill into sewers with their tails, making them a nuisance for people living in the city.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME live below silty or muddy rivers, using their tail to tunnel out of sight. They let small Water Pokémon use their tunnels if they need to swim against the river's current, and always chatter away to them, finding out about the world above.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: They are always happy, gathering in groups along the banks of lakes and rivers. They don't have to worry about any predators.
author: zerocipher

entry: POKENAME's massive fangs are strong enough to crush boulders as it tunnels. Some of its burrows stretch over 300 feet deep, forming complex underground mazes.
author: .izik

entry: Its rubbery skin absorbs impacts and swings back with even greater force. This counterattacking nature makes it a formidable opponent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows deep underground the moment it senses another presence telepathically. It relies on its eerie extrasensory abilities to avoid unwanted encounters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a larger and faster drilling tail. It has a few more small pairs of wings compared to unfused Dunsparce, but it cannot fly due to the added weight of two more segments on its body.
author: equation8573

entry: After drilling into an opponent with its tail, it injects a mild sedative. This tactic allows it to escape or subdue its target with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Rival POKENAME duel each other via swordfights with the drill tails they possess. Once a hierarchy is reached via victory, the loser forfeits some of its stored food to the victor.
author: sk372

entry: It drifts along sea currents, anchoring itself to the ocean floor with its drill-shaped tail when it finds a safe spot. With its docile nature and poor swimming skills, it relies entirely on its toxic body for survival.
author: amiel997

entry: Spelunkers often trip over this Pokémon when its limbs are retracted. According to legend, it can fly with the wings on its sides.
author: beespoon

entry: With its drill-tips, POKENAME mines for veins of sap in the largest trees. Once finished, it burrows inside the hollowed-out tree to digest.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: It smacks trees with its tail to loosen sap, then shoves its paw inside to gather it. Licking the sap from its paw is a favorite treat.
author: .izik

entry: Pressing its rear against a tree, it drills into the bark to extract sap. The steady stream provides a sweet reward for its efforts.
author: .izik

entry: It sifts through snow for seeds and berries, particularly after an avalanche. This habit helps it find food in even the harshest conditions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live near beaches where their khaki scales help them blend into the environment. They partially burrow themselves to hide their blue underbelly before ambushing prey and sinking their fangs into a fresh meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be spotted hovering in the sky, using momentum to lazily dig through rock and soil easily. It can be spotted in cyberspace just floating, oblivious to everything.
author: equation8573

entry: It swings its drill like a cestus, delivering punches capable of toppling buildings. Its wings offer great mobility in combat but cannot sustain flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME put raw stones into their rough skin pouch. They then slowly polish them into an egg shape by sanding it down with their bare hands.
author: blitzydragon

entry: It allows an opponent to hit it multiple times, smiling wider with each strike. The increased force it absorbs only seems to energize it further.
author: .izik

entry: Its heads make rattling sounds as it moves, mimicking the sound of baby toys. This peculiar noise often confuses predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen prowling around without a care, even allowing small Pokémon to climb on its body. However, it does not tolerate being attacked or stolen from: in these cases, it will fire drills from its palms and retreats to a dark cavern.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body parts are connected by buggy, thin strings of pure code that are invisible to the naked eye. When digging in the ground with its drill tail, its body parts often disconnect, so it reloads rather often.
author: equation8573

entry: POKENAME is a strange Pokémon that, despite having wings, can hover completely still without flapping for propulsion. It is believed that its drill is always pointing towards the spirit world.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Notoriously shy and incredibly elusive, wild POKENAME are prized by Poké Maniacs. Studies have shown that as long as they can hide and camouflage themselves, POKENAME will sleep in any environment.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It drools profusely when it sees something it desires, with saliva pooling in its massive mouth. The sloshing sound of its drool hitting the floor is both amusing and unsettling.
author: .izik

entry: By drilling its tail into the ground, it can detect seismic activity and sense earthquakes days before they occur. This ability makes it a natural warning system.
author: .izik

entry: The timid POKENAME tends to stay still in dark caves where miners used to work long ago. Although it appears it has the ability to consume residual life force, it never attacks others to sustain itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME burrows with its drill-tipped tail, dwelling near lakes to enjoy the lush surroundings.
author: anarchaz

entry: Its lance drills straight down into the ground to escape threats, or straight toward challengers in friendly duels.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: While digging, POKENAME uses its sharp head blade to crack boulders. Before sleeping, it scrapes moss from cave walls for a simple meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will dig tunnels underground with Dunsparce following it in search of prey. Despite digging all day POKENAME's blades never dull.
author: nelluc27

entry: It spins its body like a top, using its drill-like tail for propulsion. This dizzying motion is both defensive and playful.
author: .izik

entry: The underground nutrients POKENAME consumes are converted into strong electricity using the generator on its tail, which directs it through its body.
author: nellnast42

entry: Blindingly fast, POKENAME is rarely ever spotted. The few times it is ever threatened, it flies away backwards, as this is how it reaches top speeds.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME often digs into sheds using its drill tail to possess the power tools inside.  If seen, it will leave the power tool and dig away fearfully, searching for more power tools to possess.
author: equation8573

entry: POKENAME hovers above dandelion fields, using its small wings to stay airborne. It then kicks up a gust of wind with its drills, sending seeds flying across the landscape.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME use their drill-tipped tails to create burrows for their young to safely hatch within. Although they will craft elaborate electric webs to try and protect their young, they are easily startled and quick to flee.
author: infinex21

entry: When all of its drills spin in sync, a mysterious power supposedly manifests. It is said that if it and its Trainer put their minds towards a unified purpose with enough determination, its drills can pierce through any obstacle in the way.
author: elfail0

entry: It scours the ocean floor for seashells, which it devours by grinding them with its sturdy drill-like tail into powder. These shells provide essential minerals for its growth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends nearly its entire lifetime living underground to such an extent that it becomes blind. During this time it drills such elaborate mazes that even the keenest of navigators can become lost in them.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME uses its drill-shaped tail to burrow for metal to eat. The metal POKENAME consumes strengthens its armor-like shell.
author: ecovermination

entry: The wings on the back of POKENAME are not strong enough to allow for flight. This doesn't stop POKENAME from trying, jumping from trees and rocks attempting to glide.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME heats up its tail by spinning its drill at high speeds, helping it tunnel through thick soil. It can be seen lazing in the sun on hot days to keep itself warm.
author: mistymagius

entry: Using the drill tip on its head, POKENAME tills soil to make it it more nutrient rich for consumption.
author: melodydelune

entry: It uses its pointy tail to burrow into the walls and tops of caves. When it gets disturbed it quickly flies to a new location to burrow.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME are incredibly small Pokémon with drill-like bodies that they use to tunnel through caves in search of special magnetic minerals to feast upon. When startled, they will spew electric webs at the threat before digging underground.
author: infinex21

entry: Using its drill-tipped horn, POKENAME burrows through cave ceilings in search of iron deposits. It shapes the iron it finds into sharp spikes, using this as a means of defense against predators.
author: theartemis1

entry: This fusion is capable of drilling tunnels at incredible speeds, even through miles of solid bedrock. For this reason it became moderately popular among miners, who ride atop it and order it where to dig while it burrows away.
author: elfail0

entry: It navigates through caves with high-powered screeches. When threatened, it will drill into opponents with its tail.
author: schwaus

entry: In the wild, it strives to collect the largest gem it can find. If a bigger one catches its eye, it promptly discards its old treasure.
author: .izik

entry: When being watched, it performs a graceful swing-inspired dance. However, when alone, it krumps enthusiastically, showcasing its hidden wild side.
author: .izik

entry: Though unassuming, POKENAME are notorious for suddenly getting violent and attacking innocent Trainers. If you see one, a school of them is nearby.
author: sinistersama

entry: The skin of this Pokémon consists of a slimy membrane that dries out when the weather is too hot. The only hard part of its body consists of a drill that it uses to dig tunnels to hide away in to keep itself cool.
author: badtothebow

entry: POKENAME's fur is incredibly soft but prone to tearing if exposed to sharp rocks. Before burrowing, it carefully clears its tunnel of debris to protect its delicate coat.
author: .izik

entry: It peeks its head out from burrows to beg hikers for treats. If ignored, it will sneakily steal the hiker's bag with surprising dexterity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in massive colonies under the sea. When these colonies migrate, the vibrations may cause earthquakes.
author: munchyaxolotls

entry: It uses the giant drill on its head to break any shell on its prey. It is able to hover a little by whipping its tentacles around like a helicopter.
author: soup1900

entry: It frequently forgets it is supposed to be hunting, letting people walk on or knock it over without reacting. This absent-mindedness makes it a harmless presence on beaches.
author: .izik

entry: When it detects a complex tree root system, it eagerly burrows underground to retrieve the roots. It carries them back to its den as if fetching a cherished stick.
author: .izik

entry: Although many assume that POKENAME are combat-prone, given the large drill arms they have, they are actually very docile Pokémon. They typically only use their drills to dig new homes or to break open extremely tough nuts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME drills into the ground using its powerful tail, searching for gemstones like topaz and malachite. It consumes these minerals to strengthen its crystalline scales.
author: .izik

entry: By hovering just above the ground, POKENAME delivers powerful spinning kicks. It uses this technique to defend its tunnels from intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always stays in the ground, even when its tails are pulled. When fully underground, POKENAME uses its three tails to dig a nest deep in the earth.
author: equation8573

entry: It rubs its head vigorously to activate its sweat glands, releasing a fluid with an intensely bitter smell. This scent keeps predators at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME create burrows underground by drilling through the earth with their flaming tails. Whenever it rains, they return to these burrows to keep themselves dry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its drill-tipped tail to burrow into the ground backward. Its very flexible skin aids its movements both on land and in water.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME uses its tiny wings to hover just above the surface of lakes. With a sudden, powerful slap of its large hands, it stuns fish like Goldeen before scooping them up.
author: .izik

entry: It can balance perfectly on the tip of its tail due to a liquid it shifts within its hollow body. This unusual skill aids in precise movements and stability.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's pointed tail is quite powerful and sturdy. If it were rolling down a mountainside at top speed, drilling into the wall with its tail would cause it to stop in its tracks instantly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's drill-tail is an effective tool for burrowing through dirt, but it often forgets why it burrows and stops halfway within the ground.  It will often need help being pulled out of holes it dug for itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its leek as a cane because it doesn't have the best eyesight. It sometimes struggles to fly.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME dig with two of their heads and keep their tail upright for balance. The last head remains upright to ensure a steady flow of air.
author: equation8573

entry: When POKENAME wants to sleep, it uses its drill tail to bore a divot on the seafloor. If seen above water, POKENAME rapidly opens and closes its two shells to displace surrounding water, leading to a fast descent into the ocean.
author: equation8573

entry: POKENAME gathers water in its shell, then forcefully ejects it out its rear to build speed. It then uses this speed as momentum to dig a nest underwater using the drill-like horns on its shell.
author: equation8573

entry: When frightened, it becomes completely transparent, blending into its surroundings. This ghostly ability makes it difficult to track.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the ability to phase through metal and other earth-based substances. If it gets scared, the temperature of the room it is found in can drop by several degrees. The spiked tips of its body can secrete a powerful toxin.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The elusive POKENAME loves to goof around and make others laugh. However, it is timid and gets easily frightened itself, too. It can exhale toxic gas, but only voluntarily: getting it to chortle is perfectly safe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It burrows deep underground looking for rare stones. Any rubies it finds are hoarded and consumed at a later date.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scours the forest for thorny bushes, wrapping its thick tongue around them with ease. It devours these plants without being harmed by their thorns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in mud and stagnant water, lying in wait for prey. Its pincer is strong enough to cut off limbs.
author: fouguri

entry: POKENAME squirms its way into narrow spaces, waiting until it can leap onto another's face and grab onto them. This isn't an attack behavior; POKENAME is simply overly affectionate.
author: sk372

entry: When morning light appears, POKENAME buries its face in the dirt to sleep. Soft hooting sounds escape it as it rests through the day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME entangle their prey with sticky webs before jabbing them with their stinger. Once their prey is immobilized by their virulent venom, they wrap silk webbing to preserve their meal until they need to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Baseball players in Kanto train with POKENAME because of its agility, keen eyesight, and strong claws. Its quick reflexes make it a great practice partner.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME frequently rolls in dry soil to take dust baths. The process keeps its soft wool clean while protecting its skin from irritation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail contains a potent venom that can be heard sloshing after it strikes. This unsettling sound unnerves nearby foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight with the two leaves atop their head and get the rest of their nutrients by biting down on exposed plant roots. When they accidentally bite into the tail of another Pokémon, they gently lick the wound to numb the pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lurks beneath the surface of the water, waiting for unsuspecting Pokémon to come and drink. It then launches itself out of the water, puts its gills, which produce a mild fast-acting nerve agent, into their mouth, allowing POKENAME to feed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A group of POKENAME nests in the sides of craggy cliffs. Anyone who approaches is swiftly bombarded and have their shiny valuables stolen.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's rubbery skin repels attacks, often sending them back at enhanced power. It braces itself with its claws before enduring a hit.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drills its tail into large boulders to anchor itself during heavy storms. This clever behavior prevents it from being blown away.
author: .izik

entry: While it appears intimidating, this Pokémon is actually much less threatening than people think. Some people refer to it as the clown of the sky.
author: 8xviktor

entry: If denied what it wants, POKENAME attempts to sting the source of its frustration. Its stings cause mild fevers but fade quickly with rest.
author: .izik

entry: When hungry, POKENAME presses its tail to the ground to detect vibrations. It then digs underground with astonishing speed to locate food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME climbs mountains by digging its claws into rocks, scaling to high altitudes to reach nests of other Pokémon. It patiently waits for the right opportunity to steal eggs, before making the long descent back to the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If given honey, POKENAME will instantly trust the giver. It often forms strong bonds with those who feed it this treat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides from tree to tree, tearing open trunks to feast on the sap inside. It marks the trees it has fed on with claw marks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dives onto bushes, stabbing at the foliage with its tail. Scientists believe that it hopes to uncover hidden prey like Caterpie and Weedle.
author: .izik

entry: The blades on POKENAME's wings are coated with a thin blue liquid. This coating allows it to fly silently, surprising its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's agility makes it a star in Sinnoh's Pokémon Triathlon. Many Trainers favor it for its speed and endurance in competition.
author: .izik

entry: While rolling, POKENAME extends its stinger to jab at foes. This combined motion makes its attack both swift and powerful.
author: .izik

entry: The pincerlike antlers on POKENAME's head snap rhythmically when it uses its mind-reading abilities. The snaps can become extremely loud depending on how strong the foe's mind is.
author: .izik

entry: The bitter milk produced by POKENAME's udders acts as a potent antidote. Ancient doctors sweetened it with berries to make it easier for patients to consume.
author: .izik

entry: One of its favorite berries is the Nanab Berry, so when it finds a Silver Nanab Berry, it begins to drool and stop bouncing. It is known to stare at the berry for minutes at a time before eating it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wields its tail like a flail to defend its nest. It prefers to nest near clusters of thorny bushes for added protection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue heats up hotter than an oven. It quickly spits flames to burn shrubs before eating them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies on the ground near shrubs and camouflages itself green with ink dispensed from the spike on its tail. It hopes to avoid detection by anyone walking nearby.
author: .izik

entry: Spiteful and mischievous, POKENAME are known to break into the homes of Trainers that slight them and rearrange objects and furniture with their powerful pincer.
author: agentyoshi

entry: When it senses a tornado forming, POKENAME's horn leaks a thick silver venom. The substance is highly sought after for use in rare remedies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are almost indistinguishable from a Male Nidoran because their lilac bodies and poisonous horn. The only difference between POKENAME and a Male Nidoran is that POKENAME have a tail stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME strikes with its claws and tail before delivering a final blow with the blade on its head. This technique makes it a formidable opponent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME whips up a sandstorm by flapping its wings. Once its prey is blinded, it uses its long tail to inject its victim with poison.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: It floats above the ground, using its small wings to catch the wind. To keep itself tethered at night, it will stab its tail into a soft-barked tree.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME licks moss off cave walls with its twin tongues. Overeating can leave it enraged, attacking anyone nearby in frustration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs shallow burrows to create its home. If disturbed, it will sting intruders with its venomous tail.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its wings to make tight turns in the water. It is an excellent climber and will scale trees to gnaw at branches.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME is an accomplished angler, using its sharp stingers to skewer prey in streams. Its hunting precision makes it a fearsome sight near water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a nocturnal Pokémon that lives in social groups consisting of its own kind. Although aggressive, if it truly fears for its safety, it will sob and attempt to retreat back to its pack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While flapping its wings, POKENAME generates electricity. It releases the charge through its stinger in powerful electric attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes slurping noises due to its tongue not fully fitting in its mouth. Despite this, it can still lull foes to sleep with its singing abilities.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's metallic claws allow it to burrow into rocky cliffsides with ease. It clings to cave ceilings, waiting for unsuspecting prey to pass below before dropping down in a swift ambush.
author: .izik

entry: After snapping down on prey, POKENAME furiously licks the wound. Its saliva seeps toxins into the injury, weakening its prey.
author: .izik

entry: The pink metal covering POKENAME's body is lubricated with a toxic film. While dangerous to touch, this coating allows effortless spinning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reside in the mountains, training their gliding abilities daily. Despite their small size and jovial nature, their bites are extremely painful due to their fangs carrying superheated venom.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A group of POKENAME singing together creates a beautiful serenade. However, it frequently loses its balance while singing and uses its tail to steady itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases Toxic from the roses on its arms. It uses this as a powerful weapon against enemies and to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: It loves to kidnap people, but when it is presented with a Silver Pinap Berry, it will jump into the sky to seize the berry. This impulsive action causes it to drop what it may have been holding because it enjoys eating the shiny treat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's large ears give it a keen sense of hearing that aids in hunts. It swoops quickly and silently to strike prey, but flees in terror if the first blow does not finish the job.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's pincers are strong enough to crush stone. The only way to make it release its grip is to tickle the base of its ears.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their sharp back claws to dig into trees as they drink sap. POKENAME can glide on air currents, provided they jump from a high place.
author: totodile.

entry: When a predator nears its nest, POKENAME dives from the sky to skewer the intruder with its poisonous tail. It guards its territory more fiercely at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is lonely, so it searches the desert, looking for a Trainer who can be its friend.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: This POKENAME is extremely sad. Only a few Trainers have this variation of POKENAME that hides in the cracks of dry earth.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME are constantly sharpening their teeth and claws against any tough materials they can find. Many hikers who have caught an elusive POKENAME say it's best to carry a bag with all sorts of stones inside that POKENAME can interact with.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME marks its territory with angular slash patterns made by its tusks. These distinct markings warn others to stay away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is completely silent when gliding through the night sky, using echolocation to navigate dark environments. If it spots a target, it strikes from above, injecting venom with its fangs before escaping unseen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to cliffsides before releasing its grip to roll aggressively toward its foe. This technique can leave large gouges in the stone it rolls over with its claws.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its cape like a pair of wings, allowing it to glide down from tall cliffs. It thrives in icy conditions, using its claws to hang from cave walls.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wobbles under the summer sun, desperately seeking shade to avoid overheating. If exposed for too long, it collapses until nighttime cools it down.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME travels, it leaves behind a trail of sweet-smelling residue. It prefers to feed on clay found near water sources.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waits on the seafloor, motionless, for prey to approach. It injects its victim with mind-numbing venom before striking with an Acid Spray.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs dazzling acrobatics before striking its opponent with its tail like a mace. This move is as precise as it is powerful.
author: .izik

entry: Initially bred as adept climbers and hunters, POKENAME are now kept as novelty pets. As Pokémon made to work outside, their boundless energy is too much for most owners, ending in their all-too-common abandonment.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME reside in the mountains, training their gliding abilities daily. Despite their small size and jovial nature, their bites are extremely painful due to their fangs carrying superheated venom.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A POKENAME will routinely lick the gold coin on its forehead with its big tongue in order to keep it nice and shiny.
author: mx_wellman

entry: During the day, POKENAME buries itself in stones with its tail sticking up to sense air temperature. At night, it emerges to search for food.
author: .izik

entry: The thick, fleshy tail of POKENAME grows hotter as it runs. At top speeds, the tail bursts into flames, intimidating its opponents.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stabs electronics with its tail to absorb electricity from their wiring. This makes it a nuisance near power grids.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its claw for balance when running down canyon slopes. It can dig its claw into the ground to make an emergency stop.
author: .izik

entry: The fins on POKENAME's tail spin like propellers, allowing it to navigate through sand with remarkable speed and precision.
author: .izik

entry: The sludge covering POKENAME's body has an oddly sweet smell but causes chemical burns on contact. It uses this as a deterrent for predators.
author: .izik

entry: The slime covering POKENAME's body glows purple at night. This makes it highly visible, even on a vast and flat landscape.
author: .izik

entry: The claws on POKENAME's head are sharp enough to cut through marble effortlessly. It uses this ability to dig and expand its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs tunnels in soil that Caterpie inhabit for safety while POKENAME sleeps out in the open. Due to its steel carapace, those that would prey on Caterpie find their jaws useless in trying to take a bite out of POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: Its body is composed of highly durable steel. This resilient form allows it to burst with an explosion of electrical energy, while leaving its body intact and undamaged.
author: sk372

entry: The huge skull of Steelix is almost too heavy for POKENAME, hampering its movement in exchange for strong armor. It can hide its entire body within the steel skull to weather prolonged attacks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carved itself armor and weaponry out of discarded bits of Steelix. Using these, it considers itself a guardian of the defenseless, striking back at those who would pick on the smaller and weaker.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME charges through thick stone like it was tissue paper, smashing through everything in its path. Getting hit by one is equivalent to being hit by a car going 70mph.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eggs are actually coated in a tough metallic shell to deter predators and make effective weapons in battle. If it wishes to share one for consumption, it breaks the outer layer itself, revealing the nutritious contents within.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME mimics someone, the diamonds on its body start to glow. If you don't look away, you will be inexorably drawn into its mesmerizing charm.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lives in deep volcanic caverns, its iron hide tough enough to resist the extreme heat. It can be seen welding metal scraps onto its body using its flaming tail as a torch.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their metal bodies are said to be unbreakable against most attacks used upon them. The many cracks visible are said to be due to a POKENAME' own violent and powerful thrashing.
author: infinex21

entry: Mainly inhabiting watery tunnels and underwater caverns, before their discovery, the wailing and metallic cry of wild POKENAME was the fuel for many a seafaring ghost story and a warning for sailing ships.
author: sk372

entry: Its claws are made of diamonds, allowing it to easily cut through metals as strong as steel. It is similarly protected by an incredibly sturdy shell.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's body is adorned with crystals, with them helping to focus its draconic power. It fires destructive dragon pulses, amplified by the latent power of the crystals.
author: evilgammon

entry: Some of the deepest caverns in the world are known to be dug by POKENAME's drilling tail. Their genetic material is unstable and is said to produce various minerals on the surface of their bodies.
author: markusknight

entry: The extreme internal pressure acting on POKENAME's body causes it to release intense flames to cool off. The unique crystals on its back can reach 700 degrees without direct contact with the flames.
author: mistymagius

entry: A steel statue at daytime, a swift flier at night, this Pokémon has confused many a person. Weighing 400 kg, it is unknown how it is able to fly.
author: fr34kuency

entry: POKENAME glides on magnetic fields, steering sharply with its steel wings in silent and swift flight.
author: cybresamurai

entry: POKENAME soars through both caves and open skies, searching for rocks to pelt at Pokémon that have wronged it, even decades later. It often fights with Skarmory over territory.
author: wh3reverimayr0am

entry: POKENAME's front teeth constantly grow. In the wild, they keep them short and sharp through frequent use as they dig tunnels through stone.
author: .fedoraman

entry: It drills underground at high speeds. Its body allows it to resist the highest pressures. It has been rumored to cause the disappearance of cities.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME uses its poltergeist abilities to fling crystallised pearls from its necklace at intruding hikers. It does this from the shadows, melding into the cave walls to avoid being discovered.
author: evilgammon

entry: Metallic scraps float around this Pokémon in a ring pattern, protecting it from attacks in blind spots. It will chew and crush its prey and enemies with its jaws without hesitation if given the chance.
author: soup1900

entry: Giant crystalline spikes protrude from its body. These spikes have been tested to have a higher hardness than diamond, making them the new strongest crystal. A different form of this crystal appears between the segments of its body.
author: soup1900

entry: With its temper issues, POKENAME will often cause collateral damage around it. This Pokémon is seen in demolition sites due to its explosive power.
author: awiralonprime

entry: It's unknown how far POKENAME can extend its body, as it's been seen over 15 metres long. When under attack, it can instantly retract into its shell, which is nearly impervious to most attacks.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME lumbers through overgrown caves, feeding on cave plants and rocks. If anything enters its territory, it releases a deafening roar and charges at the intruder.
author: evilgammon

entry: The steel casing of its body holds tightly around the molten magma POKENAME constantly produces within. Between its nigh-impenetrable shell and its ability to belch streams of lava at will, few are considered a danger to POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were once relied upon by soldiers to carry them through battle. Their steel feathers deflected explosions from Voltorb while also protecting the rider.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rolls through caves, smashing through solid walls to carve out its tunnels. This charge is unstoppable, crushing anything unfortunate enough to be in its way.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME consumes large quantities of soil, storing away stones and gems swallowed while digesting the dirt. When it lets out a bellowing trumpet, the stored shards of rock and crystal shoot out and cut away at intruders.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers not to bite its prey. Instead, it constricts them with its metal body until they can no longer move. The pattern on its belly reflects intimidating shadows on the cave walls.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's tail is steel-plated, allowing it to do serious damage in battle. Its range is lacking, however, so it must get in very close to strike its opponent.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are in high demand for the metals inside their bodies, which allow for the production of first-rate stainless steel frying pans. Fortunately they do not need to be harmed in the process, as their frequently shed carapace is sufficient.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Its crystals have a similar composition to unrefined Mega Stones. It is theorized to be in a constant state of something similar to Mega Evolution as a result.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME isolates itself in the ground beneath the ocean due to the destructive potential contained within its body. When it senses other Pokémon in danger, however, it will not hesitate to unleash itself to protect them.
author: infinex21

entry: Whenever there is a lightning storm, POKENAME are struck several times before releasing the electricity as a large wave. This often leads to static buildup in the air and causes fur to fluff up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite the fact that this Pokémon's body is made of metal, it is still able to fly for long periods of time without exhausting itself. Its crystalline feathers are said to each shine with the colors of rainbows.
author: infinex21

entry: It loves to mimic anything going on around it. The crystal on its head can break and redirect light coming from any direction into its brain.
author: funkytomate

entry: The earth has polished POKENAME's metallic exterior and crystalline tail. The tip of POKENAME's tail is said to be formed from the purest energy, honed over countless years.
author: swagouille

entry: POKENAME can create dazzling, frozen crystals with its powers over ice. It conjures these crystals in patches in battle, making freezing traps for its opponents, then lashing out with a barrage of thrown crystals and icy claw strikes.
author: evilgammon

entry: The crystals on POKENAME are seen as a valuable mineral that can only be found on this fusion. The electromagnetic forces change the way the crystals look on the inside, and they are often harvested for this reason.
author: dyanz0

entry: A POKENAME's diet consists mostly of raw ores and various minerals, which in turn allow for its body to grow ever tougher. They fire Iron Balls from the holes in their hands to finish off their opponents and then eat the Iron Balls afterwards.
author: infinex21
