entry: In the past, poachers attempted to hunt POKENAME for the beautiful crystals on its body. This quickly proved fruitless, as once removed from POKENAME, the crystals turn brittle and crumble to dust.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can exert incredible pressure with its claws. This creates diamond dust, which it whirls around to sharpen its body or to attack.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME have bodies of very durable, yet very hollow, metal that accrue layers of moss due to them nesting within jungles. The crystals jutting out along their bodies are sharp enough to slice through a dense tree with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are able to create beautiful yet durable crystal spines along their back and launch them out during battle. POKENAME wield their heavy tails with surprising dexterity, smacking away any foes or thieves in an instant.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The crystals adorning POKENAME's body are prismatic, refracting colorfully as POKENAME fights. These crystals, however, are very fragile and break often, leaving shards along cave floors.
author: kingd8

entry: Folklore says that a Gallade will travel deep into a cave and defeat a Steelix.  The Gallade will then forge its weapon with the remains.
author: mundane_frog

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time hunting for iron ore, consuming 100 tons a day. If it can't find enough metal in the earth, it will often raid nearby junkyards for their scraps.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's teeth can tear through solid rock and grind it down for consumption. It eats to dig tunnels until it's underneath its opponent, then bursts from the ground to attack with its steel-plated blades.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME has become mostly immobile due to its massive horn, preferring to mimic the cries of other Pokémon to lure in prey before devouring it with the maw-horn rather than actively hunting. Its hide is most durable around the core body.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME live deep beneath the ocean floor. The movements of enough POKENAME in any given area can cause underwater earthquakes and tsunamis.
author: bee4082

entry: Due to its diamond-coated carapace. It is theorized that POKENAME have lifespan of tens of millions of years. It feeds on ancient fossils, cracking them open with their crystalline pincers.
author: mistymagius

entry: Nicknamed "The Living Dreadnought", POKENAME bellow a warhorn-like call that can be heard from land. Coming into contact with one swimming is deadly.
author: jokerswild

entry: POKENAME are covered with a metallic slate-colored armor that makes them nearly impervious to predators. This heavy armor also makes them move very slowly, so their siblings help them move around when they get tired.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME manipulates crystals into weapons it uses to strike with. These weapons can be changed instantaneously, allowing it to adapt its fighting style at will to counter the opponent's moves.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's body is impenetrable and can withstand the heat of the planet's core. Although slow, it can charge with enough power to break boulders.
author: jona_hehe

entry: Stone gears churn to power the crystalline core within POKENAME. Once fully charged, the gems fire off powerful beams of radiant light.
author: sk372

entry: Its diet mainly consists of various types of gemstones and metals. Groups of POKENAME have been sighted devouring scrap metal in junk yards.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The crystals on POKENAME's body are considered priceless in value. Gaining them is nigh impossible, however, as its chilling breath will freeze solid any who try to approach it.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon has only been sighted flying at night. During the day, it is thought to be deep underground to avoid sunlight.
author: cheroace

entry: This colossal Pokémon makes its home around an equally-large crystal said to contain the hopes and dreams of Pokémon and humans alike. Its entire body is harder than any known metal and parts of it are shaped into weapons that deter any threats.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its massive claws to pull huge boulders out of the wall. It throws these with enormous strength to crush its opponents.
author: chorb33

entry: After having so much trouble being hugged by Trainers for its rocky exterior, POKENAME worked night and day to make itself a new costume of steel instead. After seeing that metal was equally as hard to hug, POKENAME's depression only got worse.
author: redmagecole

entry: POKENAME has modeled its outer shell after popular fashion for young women in the hopes that it will be popular in turn. Its dress is startlingly resilient, and its barrettes are denser than tungsten.
author: griddle

entry: POKENAME feeds on metal ores, preferring strong metals like iron and lead. The two heads hate sharing and will often fight over who gets the better meal.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME emits a powerful aura, and it's rumored to contain ancient strength within its crystal tails. It embodies purity.
author: astrael1

entry: When these Pokémon molt, they leave behind exquisite gemstones. These gemstones beautifully reflect the moonlight at night.
author: mrbapcik

entry: When direct sunlight shines through POKENAME's crystalline tails, it creates a colorful and prismatic display which distracts its prey.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME feeds on iron deposits deep underground, smashing through the thick rock with its diamond horns. It doesn't care if the horns get broken, as they will grow back within a month or two.
author: mistymagius

entry: Blacksmiths of old used POKENAME to test the durability of their forged weapons. If one could strike the hardy shell of a POKENAME and not crack or break, then it was considered a work of true quality.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its iron tusks and jaws to dig through any kind of rock, allowing it to carve out its own caves. It is territorial and will fight any Pokémon it finds in its caves.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME uses its iron tusks and jaws to dig through any kind of rock, allowing it to carve out its own caves. It is territorial and will fight any Pokémon it finds in its caves.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's heavy body makes it nearly impossible for it to fly for more than a few moments. It uses its metallic wings and heavy tail as bludgeoning tools in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hoards any gems it finds as it stalks about in dark caves. In battle, it uses these gems as weapons, shooting them at its opponent in devastating volleys using its spectral energies.
author: evilgammon

entry: Only a few specimens of POKENAME are known, being only found deep underground beneath freezing tundra. Though it does not move, its gaze is said to be expressive and penetrating.
author: dylonk25

entry: Though made entirely of rock and incredibly heavy, POKENAME is a graceful dancer. Its powerful steps can bring down floors and leave a party in ruins or awe.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME produces amplified metal sounds from its ears to destroy its opponent's defenses and stun it momentarily. It then strikes with its razor-sharp steel wings or jabs with its pointed tail.
author: evilgammon

entry: Under POKENAME's thick, rocky shell, its body is made up of reflective slime. Parts of this slime occasionally crystallise, adding to its already strong layers of protection.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are rarely seen on the surface as they burrow deep through the permafrost. Their bodies are comprised of beautiful blue ice that is harder than steel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's heavy metal body is durable to the point of being nigh impervious, but its weight causes it to be nearly immobile. It fires powerful bursts of energy from its feet and hands to maneuver itself in short-distance increments.
author: sk372

entry: Rare golden variants of POKENAME are highly sought after for their unique coloration. Their bodies are notably lighter than usual, making them more mobile and harder to capture.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME seclude themselves away when they first evolve. They train and polish their body alone, protecting their manes with their lives.
author: ethewriter

entry: The spores POKENAME produces cause rock-like fungi to grow on most surfaces. Though harmless to humans, these strange mushrooms can be very harmful to Rock-type Pokémon, causing painful paralysis with a single touch.
author: sk372

entry: The unknown metal on POKENAME's head acts as a loud gong, with its booming clangs being heard for miles. This sound seems to whip POKENAME into a frenzy, increasing its aggression and strength in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: The gems making up the body of POKENAME are known as "Silver Diamonds." These crystals are considered to be one of the strongest materials in the world due to their near-perfect crystalline structure.
author: turron_turron

entry: The top row of POKENAME's teeth is flint-like rock, and the bottom row is solid steel. By chomping down, it creates a shower of sparks, lightly singeing anything caught in it.
author: evilgammon

entry: Their sense of earthly vibrations allows them to detect caverns below the surface. When the water reservoir of a geyser dries out, they are known to flock to that location to consume the rocks left behind.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME covers itself in gold, constantly flaunting it to the other cave denizens. However, it can't distinguish between gold and pyrite, so most of its bling is actually just fool's gold.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME consumes a rich variety of minerals that give its tail the ability to emit light. Because of this, they are popular companions for miners deep underground.
author: mepp.

entry: This Pokémon catches and refracts the light of the moon with its tail gem, projecting it onto the surrounding surfaces, painting them in all the colors of the rainbow. Such colorful performance attracts the potential mates and confuses predators.
author: milchik

entry: The tempered steel that makes up POKENAME's armor can withstand extremely high temperatures. It sets ablaze anything it strikes with its large hammer.
author: kduffradio

entry: At night, it seeks refuge in caves to replenish its energy. Its steel body radiates heat, and it always seeks confrontation.
author: astrael1

entry: POKENAME draws its psychic power from the gems outside its body. It has been seen meditating in deep caverns.
author: theartemis1

entry: The magnet in POKENAME's brain allows them to locate the highest quality minerals, which it then devours to further strengthen its powerful body made of alloy steel. If it is not sleeping or eating, it is likely training.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Only with a wide variety of martial training in various terrains can a Pokémon evolve into POKENAME. It has arms that can shatter steel and a body that can break nearly any weapon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's roots dig towards the world's core, making it unable to flee. It absorbs water and metal particles from the depths, hardening its head that even diamond can't scratch.
author: takopus

entry: POKENAME maintain a polished platinum body by scraping their body against sharp rocks while burrowing. They dig so far beneath the surface that they experience immense pressure and heat from the surrounding earth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives near large iron deposits, feeding on the iron to strengthen its metal hide. If it runs out of iron, it will smash itself through the earth until it finds a new deposit.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME shed their outermost layer of metal yearly, growing a stronger one shortly afterward. It's said that those reaching one hundred years develop impenetrable skin.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produce bright aqua flames from their bodies that grow incredibly hot. Their metallic bodies also have special hooves that help them climb near vertical cliffs. This ability to climb cliffs makes them difficult to track or capture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to living in caves with high amounts of potassium deposits, its flames have turned a gorgeous shade of purple. It rarely uses its flames, however, as it prefers to trample its opponents with its steel body.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite its heavy body, POKENAME can gallop at high speeds, trailing dark flames behind it all the while. It races to the highest peaks it can and stands watch over the mountain, cutting a striking visage.
author: sk372

entry: Despite the lopsided appearance, legs that look unchanged from Dodrio carry the three massive Steelix heads with only a marginal decrease in top speed. Scientists are still baffled by this.
author: sk372

entry: The metal shell covering POKENAME's body resembles the skull of another Pokémon, which helps it intimidate other sea Pokémon. It swims in the depths of icy waters, feeding on Pokémon that hide among rocks, which it can easily destroy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its steel shell to trap prey that unwisely approaches its position. To keep its metal teeth sharp, it shreds the permafrost that forms above the waters where it lives every day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME corners lost hikers in dark caves, attacking and stealing their souls. These souls are stored in the crystals growing from its body and used to amplify its ghost attacks.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive yet dormant Pokémon, often found camouflaging in metal mines. It sleeps beneath clusters of valuable minerals and attacks viciously if disturbed.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME uses its claw to crush coal into diamonds. The claw's appearance is designed to intimidate and confuse opponents by making them see double.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME have a small sapling sprouting from their back that produces pink berries. While they may seem delicious, they are quite poisonous to people and should only be fed to Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME defends its eggs with its life, charging and hissing at anything that gets close. Not even its Trainer is allowed to touch its eggs, though they are permitted to look.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is very proud of its big blue tongue, presenting it to any who would bear witness. It is prone to pouting if people do not compliment its size and hue.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rarely acquiesces to the whims of its Trainer, especially if the situation involves its egg. It eventually warms up when treated with respect and kindness, but that is a long process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a desire to avoid conflict, but this has come at its own expense. Its body grows faster than its shell and causes it to be dangerously compressed. This deters other Pokémon from attacking it but causes POKENAME to live a painful life.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite its scary face and large size, POKENAME is actually very kind and likes to have people play with or on it. It loves to eat a lot, but it can easily be scared into giving up food by any intimidating Pokémon.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME grooms its Trainer and young with careful beak strokes. Despite its scowl, it is calm and nurturing by nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are affectionate and social creatures that love spending time with others. A group of excited POKENAME will bark every second at the same time in unison.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When irritated, POKENAME spits sticky silk at the source of its frustration. Prolonged contact with the silk can cause itchy rashes on exposed skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are hard to build rapport with because of their juvenile tendencies. They never want to share their belongings, and cry whenever they do.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a pugnacious tendency to argue with its Trainer over trivial matters and can suddenly become picky over its food. This defiance is a way of testing boundaries, as it is still learning how to interact with others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are affectionate creatures that love to rub against their Trainer. This causes static to build around them and fluffs up their wool.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though its face appears grumpy, POKENAME is deeply affectionate. It spits water at those it dislikes, especially when near its Trainer.
author: .izik

entry: During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME can maneuver their clawed tail with terrifying precision to slice up their opponents. When they are not fighting, the claws on their tail give them extra grip when they swing between branches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bowlike sprout on POKENAME's head spins faster during spring. Researchers are unsure why, though some believe it signals excitement for summer.
author: .izik

entry: To show affection, POKENAME flays its ears. This forces its face into an unpleasant grimace, and many are put off by this. If it feels unwanted, it slinks off and makes a wall of mud around it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME have a small tree growing from their backs that produces pink berries poisonous for people to consume. They give out these berries to hungry POKENAME who need an extra boost of energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are affectionate creatures that love to give out hugs. Whenever their Trainer comes home, they are always waiting by the door to give out a surprise hug, flying into their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is incredibly picky and only eats the highest quality food, which causes it to occasionally wander out of its typical territory. Its bright coloration means it is easy for predator Pokémon to spot it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is incredibly stubborn but also incredibly non-confrontational. Even if other Pokémon try to shoo it away with attacks, it will simply tread along its desired path in a blasé manner. Its luxurious fur makes it a target of poachers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME travel around the world, giving out gifts to well-behaved pet Pokémon. Badly-behaved pets instead get a scolding wallop from the heavy sack of treats it carries.
author: sk372

entry: After locking its jaws on a foe, POKENAME unleashes a fiery breath. The flames it produces are hot enough to melt copper wiring.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its cutesy appearance to catch its prey off guard before striking them with its venomous bite. However, this leads to most Pokémon not really taking it seriously in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's soft antlers wiggle rapidly when it begins to pout. Soon after, it attempts to trap nearby foes using Imprison.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a rare but beloved housepet, renowned for bonding quickly, but unfortunately to the point of separation anxiety. Owners must take care, as its tantrums result in thick, acrid smoke billowing from it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME adores attention and will often shock its Trainer if they ignore it for too long. Oddly enough, it loves to be dressed up, and it is quite the popular trend to dress up POKENAME in all sorts of outfits.
author: mistymagius

entry: When tunneling, POKENAME uses its powerful jaws to bite through boulders in its path. Its tunnels stretch for miles beneath cities.
author: .izik

entry: With one crushing bite, POKENAME can shatter concrete. It follows up with venom that induces dizziness and hallucinations.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a tree sprouting from their back that produces pink berries. They offer these berries freely to Pokémon that want to have a quick bite and love when other Pokémon rest beneath their branches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's large ears can detect its Trainer's voice from over a mile away. It bounds toward them in joyful, clumsy hops.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their resemblance to magic wands, POKENAME are much more prone to simply and repeatedly bonk their heads against their opponents.
author: mx_wellman

entry: When a wild POKENAME gets upset, it will rapidly flail back and forth for attention, swinging its blades with reckless abandon. The only guaranteed safe way of calming it down is gently patting it on the back of the head.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Despite its appearance, POKENAME is incredibly timid and will flee if it thinks anyone is near. If trapped, it will let out a mighty roar in an attempt to intimidate those nearby. They begin using odd powers if they are still cornered afterwards.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Unlike a Snubbull, POKENAME runs around mimicking an angry dog, scaring small Pokémon and children.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Despite its appearance, POKENAME is incredibly timid and will flee if it thinks anyone is near. If trapped, it will let out a mighty roar in an attempt to intimidate those nearby. It begins using odd powers if it is still cornered afterwards.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hates being called cute and will try to fight anyone who does. It is very sensitive to others' emotions and will fiercely defend those who are feeling down.
author: mistymagius

entry: Once it clamps onto a foe, POKENAME discharges powerful electric bursts. Radios in the area flicker into static as it bites down.
author: .izik

entry: In spite of its tough appearance, POKENAME is quite timid. If it senses danger, it growls to hide its fear and discharges blindingly bright electricity from its fur.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME spikes out its fur and sheds sparks when threatened, growling strongly at potential danger. Unfortunately its strength is rather meager, so if the threatening display fails, there's little else it can do.
author: sk372

entry: Normally POKENAME has a placid personality, but when it chooses a spot to call its own to settle down and gather sunlight, it becomes more aggressive. It growls at and smacks anything that comes near with its large leaves.
author: sk372

entry: In crowded cities, POKENAME are a common nuisance. Even the faintest music will call them down from above where they then start to bark offbeat and disrupt any street performance.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The mushrooms on its back are prized for their sweet, candy-like flavor, but gathering them is dangerous, as POKENAME has a vicious bite.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is an extremely selfish Pokémon who will steal any sweet treat it can find without hesitation. It will throw a tantrum if it doesn't get the sweets it thinks it deserves.
author: mistymagius

entry: It makes a frightening face and growls to scare smaller Pokémon away and steal their things. Should it face opposition, however, it immediately turns timid and runs away in fear.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes for an incredibly well-behaved house pet. It is recommended to purchase a Poké Toy to indulge its playful nature.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME love to give out hugs to other Pokémon but often cling on for an uncomfortable amount of time. When they are inevitably pushed away, they get so anxious that they may develop a headache from the stress.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Socialites have begun seeing POKENAME as a fine trophy pet to pamper and preen. Competitions to see who has the most well-groomed and dressed-up POKENAME have become common in affluent locales.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love splashing in puddles and going swimming, but despise thunderstorms. They are most often found in the suburban countryside.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although POKENAME often shouts and grimaces, it is neither dangerous nor aggressive. It is a popular Pokémon for rookie Trainers.
author: chorb33

entry: Being in a constant state of anger, POKENAME growls and hisses at anything that passes it. However, its too lazy to act on this rage.
author: evilgammon

entry: For reasons still not entirely clear, each individual POKENAME has an extreme personality. Whether utterly over-affectionate, intensely stubborn, or vicious and aggressive, POKENAME is often regarded by Trainers as a handful.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's two heads are in constant disagreement. Their inability to get along turns mealtime into a hilarious display of bites and squabbles.
author: akujules

entry: POKENAME are rather argumentative, puffing up their feathers and spreading their wings to try and appear more intimidating. They fight over sunny spots in the treetops, leaving those that lose the fights to stay on the lower branches.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME nest in small crevices in trees. It will peck at humans who try to touch it, but, strangely, it does not usually attack smaller Bug-types.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Due to its round body, POKENAME struggles with flying, leading to a near-constant state of annoyance. If it becomes too angry, POKENAME explodes into a puff of feathers, which can set off a chain reaction in a flock.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME conceal bones within their wings to sneak closer to their prey. Once they are in range, they ambush prey with a flurry of bony boomerangs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It delivers devastating kicks to tree trunks to knock down prey hiding among the branches. With its martial arts techniques, POKENAME defends its hunting grounds fiercely from rivals who try to steal them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME chrysalises are made of a hard keratin that makes them difficult to penetrate. They kick up dust by flapping their tiny wings to escape predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tends to bully flocks of Spearow, yet at the same time defends them from larger Pokémon picking fights. It seems to believe that only it is allowed to pick on the little birds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by dripping venom from its stinger onto the base of its tree. If another POKENAME enters its territory, they will wrestle until one becomes tired and leaves the tree.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a very playful tiny bird Pokémon. It will attempt to play hide and seek with anyone coming near.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a very playful Pokémon. It will attempt to play hide-and-seek with anyone coming near. However, it fails due to its golden sparkle.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME prowls around tall grass, spearing bug Pokémon with its beak for meals. Its beak and wings are made of dried hardened leaves.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is considered an outcast to most Spearow. Its less aggressive behavior will often have it kicked out of any flock it tries to fit in with. Most POKENAME will never find where they belong.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Fiercely territorial, POKENAME guards the trees near its nest. Its eyes glow pink as it unleashes Hypnosis on intruders.
author: .izik

entry: Extremely territorial and quick-tempered, POKENAME uses Foresight to track and relentlessly peck at anyone disturbing its daytime sleep.
author: .izik

entry: The webbing that it uses is extremely thin. Despite how thin it is, it is able to hold multiple tons without breaking.
author: .izik

entry: The body shape and feather colors of POKENAME are enough to confuse both sides of its fused 'cousins'. Though unlike a similarly shaped fusion, Pidgerow, it instead attacks whoever has the most food on them at any point.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME fixates on the moon, keeping its beak pointed at it for as long as it remains in view. This behavior has puzzled researchers for decades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's melodic chirps carry a soothing tone. Prolonged exposure to its song can cause even aggressive foes to fall asleep.
author: .izik

entry: Though fiercely territorial, POKENAME uses psychic power to gaze into a trespasser's past. Only those without ill intent are allowed through.
author: .izik

entry: The light wool that covers POKENAME's body does not obstruct its ability to effortlessly soar through the skies. It drifts through meadows like a living cloud.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is barely different than a normal Spearow. POKENAME is just as territorial, loud and rude, only having twice the temper due to needing much more food than normal, and lacks the flowing, alluring hair of the Pidgeot half.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: As POKENAME drifts over meadows, its feathers release a peppery scent. This aroma calms nearby Pokémon and eases territorial tensions.
author: .izik

entry: One of the results of discarded DNA Splicers being found by wild Pokémon, POKENAME is close to being classified as a pest.
author: mx_wellman

entry: Seeds caught in POKENAME's feathers grow easily, sprouting tiny saplings each morning. Each POKENAME in a flock might have different herbs growing out of it.
author: .izik

entry: If, for some reason, it does not fly for a day, it will spend the next two days flying without tiring. It emits a hum while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: Even though consuming a Reviser Seed causes POKENAME to faint, they seem to seek them out in the wild. Researchers theorize that it reacts with their brain in such a way that it gives them an out-of-body experience.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME avoid being eaten by predators by releasing a hoarse caw and spreading their wings to appear larger. Meeting a POKENAME at night is regarded as bad luck, so they are chased out of towns and villages back into the forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME defends its territory by pecking other Pokémon or using its vines to whip them. Whenever it meets another POKENAME, a stand-off can occur where both Pokémon continue to puff up their chests until one of them surrenders.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its stout body, its wings allow POKENAME to glide gracefully over the plains while searching for food. From the bud sprouting on its back, scientists have synthesized an antihistamine that helps treat pollen-induced allergies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It can let out a piercing cry that rallies Speartata to its location. It has an gluttonous omnivorous diet, and uses much of its energy in order to fly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a spirited and noisy creature, often found darting about in chaotic patterns. Its cries are said to contain cryptic meanings, baffling Trainers and researchers alike.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is regularly in a bad mood, aggressively chasing any it deems an intruder to its territory. Fortune tellers watch its behavior for if the two heads are cooperating or arguing, interpreting that as signaling whether an idea is good or bad.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hang around high in tree branches chattering to one another in rapid high pitched chirps. They aggressively defend their trees, dropping from high branches and pecking at anybody passing underneath.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME makes its nest inside large trees, spending most of its time napping the day away. However, it is very territorial and will viciously peck at anything that comes near its nest.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME chirps sharply before lunging at foes with its barbed tail. A single strike is often enough to stun its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will constantly bully other members of its flock, thinking itself superior. It will even threaten its flock members into giving up their food, leaving them to starve.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's feathers give off a faint honey scent. It uses its sweetness to charm travelers into sharing their food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits searing flames from its beak, hot enough to melt solid boulders into pools of lava. It lives primarily near volcanic areas.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their usual brash nature, POKENAME engage in play with one another in an adorable manner. Few Pokémon have been observed giving piggyback rides to one another as POKENAME do, especially in bird-like species.
author: chinigan

entry: Having not evolved the long beak of its Fearow kin, POKENAME often has to resort to bullying flocks of Spearow away from food in order to gain sustenance of its own.
author: sk372

entry: It will disguise itself amongst flocks of Spearow, planning on taking their food while their unaware. POKENAME only produce a couple of steel feathers in their lifetime.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME slithers through the air like a serpent-like kite. Its sharp beak is coated in a mild toxin that can weaken prey.
author: .izik

entry: The playful POKENAME uses its wing-like ears to flutter short distances. It deftly plucks White Apricorns from trees with effortless skill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME paints its flockmates onto rocks and logs using pigment from its tail. When flying, it twirls its tail like a rotor to stay airborne longer.
author: .izik

entry: It flies without ever opening its wings. It mimics a kite as it sails silently through the air, waiting for prey to reveal itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's milk is a prized ingredient in fine cheeses. However, it viciously pecks at anyone it does not trust to defend its supply.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's beak crackles with electricity. In battle, it fires powerful shocks capable of stunning foes twice its size.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers are dense and rigid, harder than basalt. They rattle when it flaps its wings, producing a sound like stone scraping stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME circles city streets from the air, studying people's movements. At night, it gathers with others to mimic what it learned in eerie unison.
author: .izik

entry: While eating, it often swallows food without chewing. If it ever experiences an upset stomach, it will shriek for hours.
author: .izik

entry: The drills on its head allow POKENAME to pierce the mountain rock so it can carve out a theft-proof nest. Its body is so massive that its pair of wings can only keep it airborne for very limited periods of time.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is too heavy to fly, but it is an agile sprinter. Even predators that catch it will have trouble getting through its plating.
author: staghorn

entry: Its wings are not quite big enough to enable flight. In preparation for evolution, it darts around playfully, windmilling its arms.
author: busilisk

entry: It's not comfortable with flying long distances yet, but with gentle urging from its parents, POKENAME will one day leave the nest.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: The tip of POKENAME's beak contains potent venom. After a victorious fight, it joyfully flits through the skies in celebration.
author: .izik

entry: When startled, POKENAME's feathers shift colors to match its surroundings. It becomes nearly invisible among forest leaves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers fruit from Apicot Berry trees and brings them to its riverside lodge. Once its hoard is full, it curls up atop it and sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases sticky spores that leave behind residue on its back. It helps groom other POKENAME by pulling and pecking away at the hardened residue with its beak.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Toxic ink drips from POKENAME's beak, once prized for use alongside elegant quills. Nobles and foreign dignitaries proudly used its feathers for writing.
author: .izik

entry: When an earthquake approaches, POKENAME's beak becomes unnaturally warm. It begins to chirp loudly, warning others of the danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's large ears pick up the slightest sounds. If startled during rest, it bolts into the sky in frantic, erratic patterns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses magnetism to achieve something vaguely resembling flight. This takes a lot of energy to maintain, so travelers should be wary to watch for exhausted POKENAME falling out of the trees.
author: sk372

entry: While not very fast on their own, trained spear-throwers can make use of POKENAME's natural ability to hover to make an accurate long-ranged projectile. The base of POKENAME's tongue wraps around its skull, protecting it from concussions.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME's feathers are coated in a thin layer of poison. When frightened, the toxicity intensifies, making even brief contact dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: The blade-like feathers on POKENAME's arms are fragile but regrow razor-sharp overnight if broken during fights.
author: .izik

entry: Quick to aggravate, this Pokémon will incessantly peck at anyone who wanders into its territory.
author: melodydelune

entry: The wings of POKENAME are underdeveloped, so it can only fly for a short amount of time. POKENAME often have a hot beak as they learn to control their fire powers.
author: zyrum_

entry: POKENAME uses its beak to steal small objects from travelers. In its flock, birds with the largest keyrings are seen as the most prestigious.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can scale cliff walls without tiring. If it encounters tree roots, it will peck at them until sap runs out, then drink the fluid.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dozes atop fallen logs, letting out soft, rhythmic chirps. Its careless sleep leaves it vulnerable to sneaky predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather in small groups to caw in unison, showing off their wide vocal range. The resulting cacophony frustrates nearby Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tough feathers shield it from fierce sandstorms. Hidden in the dust, it strikes at prey with powerful jaws.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME controls the temperature of the flame emerging from its beak with great precision. Bakeries in Eterna City use it to bake Roseli Berry tarts.
author: .izik

entry: The egg-like bud atop POKENAME's body releases a Petaya Berry-scented sap that nourishes nearby plants. It is often seen clearing weeds from orchard soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glide through the wind by positioning their flower stalks in the direction of the breeze. As they fly along wind currents, they release pollen below them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hide in branches by folding their bronze wings close to their body, which blends in with wood. They surprise bug Pokémon and snatch them up with their talons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Beak-like spikes jut from POKENAME's body, launching sharp needles at anything that gets too close to its roost.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME have a slight wingbeat, their brick-colored wings make them stand out with any amount of light. They have an easier time hunting in caves than in forests for this reason.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can only fly a short distance without needing to rest. When it flaps its wings it releases toxic spores that can cause seizures.
author: .izik

entry: While flapping its wings for balance, POKENAME performs complex wrestling lunges. It favors aerial grapples against airborne opponents.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wags its tail feathers eagerly while waiting to play fetch. It bonds quickly with those offering stones or toys.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a symbiotic relationship with the living fungi on its body, which are known as Shroomites. The clicks of its beak and the thumps of jumping Shroomites combine to make an intriguing percussive beat.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is a nocturnal predatory bird that prowls city outskirts, drawn to streetlights or unattended trash. With a single flap of its wings, it releases dense clouds of Poison Powder to weaken or drive away its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During rainstorms, POKENAME's wings collect water like bowls. It slowly absorbs the stored water over the following days.
author: .izik

entry: When it is hungry, the flame on its tail burns weaker. POKENAME goes out hunting at dawn, using its strong wings to scout for food or small prey from above.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rely on their wings to shield their tail whenever it rains. They set fire to bushes to lure prey out of burrows before pecking with their sharp beaks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its primary habitat is rough and rocky canyons. POKENAME is rarely seen in the daytime, as it burrows underground and only emerges for short periods to forage for worms and grubs.
author: alice_alice

entry: POKENAME rapidly pecks at boulders from beneath the ground to shatter them. It tunnels onward to reach herbs, which it devours without surfacing.
author: .izik

entry: Small and ferocious, POKENAME travel in large hordes. They have been known to harass Trainers until berries are given. If no food is presented to them, the group of POKENAME will chase Trainers out of the area.
author: roniodove

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp beak to pluck coins from park fountains. It proudly decorates its nest with the shimmering prizes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will hoard any shiny baubles within its territory. If you find yourself to be target of its aggression, trade it jewelry for safe passage.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: Thanks to its sleek feathers, POKENAME moves with unmatched agility. It often snatches purses from city park visitors before vanishing.
author: .izik

entry: While it may look angry due to its eyes, a POKENAME will quickly grow emotionally attached to anyone who is brave enough to pet it.
author: .izik

entry: Short-tempered and wild, POKENAME lets out a sharp squawk before launching a flurry of kicks at anything that provokes it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attacks foes mid-rage by lashing out with its strong talons. It fights blindly once angered.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have comically small wings compared to their large bodies. They are easily taken out of the air whenever a Pokémon throws rocks at them, so they are rarely seen flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's muscled arms are covered in dense feathers. With one punch, it can easily smash through sheets of solid steel.
author: .izik

entry: The feathers of its wings clump together in the water so that POKENAME can use them as fins. It can also pedal with its stubby legs to accelerate.
author: chorb33

entry: While it flies it releases large amounts of toxic smoke from the hole in its belly. The smoke does not affect its own body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives inside caves where it breaks rocks down for consumption. Its loud cries can be heard echoing throughout caves and mineshafts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The feathers in POKENAME's mane heat up when it runs or flies. Careless touch can cause painful burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's mane feathers dance in the wind, resembling vivid flames. Many mistake it for a wildfire when seen from afar.
author: .izik

entry: When not hunting for fish, POKENAME spends much of its free time on secluded shores to preen its feathers to pristine condition. It shows remarkable ability to navigate through even extreme currents.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in metallic feathers that hum softly. The magnetic field around it can disrupt cellphone signals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are typically quite calm creatures but can act aggressively if they lose their leek-like baton. If they spot another Pokémon with their baton, they chase the thief relentlessly until they give it back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME become incredibly irate when they lose their baton, especially if it was stolen from them. When they inevitably find their baton, the immense relief they feel is released in happy little squawks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The new feathers on POKENAME's twin heads are incredibly soft and warm. Winter coats lined with them are prized by tailors across the region.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rely on their legs to roam around the world and rely on the charity of others if their legs are injured. Their heads often get angry at each other when they are injured as they blame one another for the misfortune.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME leaps high into mangrove treetops from the river in search of food. If it lands in a particularly unlucky cluster of branches, it may find itself unable to get back down.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME shoot jets of water with the cannons on their back. They prefer to remain grounded because their wings are not yet big enough to sustain flight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's rock-hard feathers somehow allow it to stay airborne for hours. Bird Keepers have studied its migrations for decades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels psychic waves through its beak to lull foes into sleep. It then feeds on their dreams while they remain unaware.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are loyal creatures and love to get hugs from their Trainer. Sometimes they get so excited that they release a cloud of toxic spores, so Trainers need to be wary of overstimulating POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will not accept any denigration from its Trainer, even if it means going without food. Being trusted to touch its egg is the highest privilege, awarded only to Trainers who treat it with kindness and respect.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It transforms into a copy of its foe to catch them off guard. Once the enemy investigates, it delivers a surprise bite.
author: .izik

entry: When raised with care, POKENAME is fiercely loyal to it's Trainer, oftentimes willing itself to keep fighting until the very end.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME brandish their fangs and bark loudly to protect flocks of Mareep from predators. If a predator is close enough, POKENAME gives them a potent bite that is sure to leave a lasting impression.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If a predator approaches its nest, it bites with a force strong enough to destroy a bank vault door. It is fiercely protective of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: Due to POKENAME's small body, it is hard to discern where its lower jaw ends and its body begins. It often pretends to be an egg by tucking in its ears and closing its eyes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's heavy jaws look fearsome, but it is timid and startles easily. When frightened, it releases a slippery film from its cheeks and sprints away on unsteady legs. Those who earn its trust find it fiercely loyal and surprisingly affectionate.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It bites nearly everything, offering weak playful nibbles to those it senses are friendly. Its clairvoyance helps it distinguish friend from foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love looking stylish and enjoy sitting for hours at a salon making sure they maintain their exquisite appearance. The bow on their back wraps around their flower bulb to restrict the flow of spores and keep themselves clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are loyal creatures and will use any means necessary to defend their Trainer. They can become sick if their Trainer does not allow them to get enough sunlight, so it is important for Trainers to go with them to sunbathe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its oversized teeth are strong enough to gnaw through wood and stone. It marks its territory by biting trees, leaving distinct grooves as a warning.
author: .izik

entry: It rolls across long landscapes and times itself during the journey. Spotting a cactus excites it, as it loves to stop and eat them with eager bites.
author: .izik

entry: Its huge mouth is actually so soft and gentle that a POKENAME can keep an egg in it without it being damaged. This goes so far that POKENAME often transport their eggs this way to guard them.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME's fearsome face makes small birds flock to be its underlings to avoid incurring its potential wrath. Few figure out that it is incredibly softhearted and will buckle beneath the slightest bit of opposition.
author: sk372

entry: Parts of POKENAME's lower jaw jut out from its face like tusks. During warmer seasons, these oversized teeth generate cold air to keep it cool and prevent overheating.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has very heavy fangs that cause its head to tilt to one side if left to grow too much. Therefore, it will file its fangs down on trees.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: In order to better protect its Trainer, POKENAME donned an intimidating appearance to scare off threats. If that fails, it lets out three terrifying barks that echo far out to sea.
author: cinnamoncreampuff

entry: POKENAME hoards treasure and will bark and bare its fangs viciously to protect it. However, in an actual fight, it is quite cowardly.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: POKENAME love to spend hours at salons where they are groomed and pampered until they look beautiful. The flower on their back has a ribbon wrapped around the base to make themselves look stylish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often enter into beauty pageants to flaunt their stylish look. The ribbon on their back wraps around their flower to prevent spores from getting messy while also keeping them looking fashionable.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are commonly used as guards for junkyards and similar establishments. However, their lax personalities mean most are more bark than bite.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's fearsome appearance and huge size cause many to treat it as a vicious monster, but it is in actuality incredibly gentle and even timid. Even when attacked it rarely retaliates, instead choosing to flee.
author: sk372

entry: It loves biting metal to test its jaw strength. Using its magnetic nose, it detects nearby unbitten items for further chewing.
author: .izik

entry: This is one of the Pokémon with the most-developed jaws. It has a strength that allows it to break almost anything with an single bite.
author: pof.whitebeam

entry: POKENAME is much cuddlier than its looks might suggest. They are easily startled and, when spooked, it will take off on a fear-fueled rampage.
author: genesisparallax

entry: It bites defensively when provoked, releasing a sticky slime that makes attackers slip away. Its strong jaws can crush small shells found on the beach.
author: .izik

entry: It's believed that this Pokémon has sparked legends of a three-headed dog that guards the entrance to the underworld.
author: naga_sake

entry: It uses its soft, stretchy fur to disarm opponents before biting unexpectedly. The fur puffs up when it's angry, making it look twice its size to scare off predators.
author: .izik

entry: Do not be fooled by its grumpy appearance. It would almost be the perfect Pokémon for children if it didn't have the tendency to bark at strangers coming too close to its owner. Some think POKENAME is, in fact, too approachable.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: It divebombs anything that gets too close to its nest. Trying to scare it off will only make it more aggressive.
author: cait_sith

entry: It rolls at high speeds, using its sharp fangs to bite through obstacles in its way. When threatened, it curls into a ball and strikes with powerful spinning attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a notorious antisocial rebel, stirring up trouble for no other reason than because it can. Even its own Trainer is not exempt from its unruly and disobedient behavior.
author: sk372

entry: Sap drips from POKENAME's massive jaw, releasing a scent reminiscent of Chesto Berries. This aroma attracts Bug-type Pokémon in the area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME moves its ears to try and locate others of its kind, howling if it cannot. Its small legs make it slow on land, though it can slide across ice at great speeds, looking like an approaching avalanche from a distance.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It uses metal chains to bind foes from a distance before delivering an extremely hard bite. Its bite is powerful enough to destroy concrete.
author: .izik

entry: It enjoys biting down on hot objects in the desert. If someone gets too close while it gnaws, it will fire out sharp pins to ward them off.
author: .izik

entry: Skull-shaped flowers bloom on its body in sunlight. If someone gets too close, it will bite with its strong jaws to protect itself.
author: .izik

entry: This fusion lures prey close by shifting its sandy body to mimic a rock. When the target approaches, it bites down hard and drags them into the sand.
author: .izik

entry: It can generate psychic waves by gnashing its fearsome teeth. Its tough appearance is a tactic to scare off opponents; when it does get into a fight, it swims away the moment its attacks fail.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful jaws to break logs into pieces to use as basic tools, then plants seeds in the soil it churns. It is often seen reforesting areas damaged by wildfires.
author: .izik

entry: They are prone to being poisoned due to their pastry-like bodies, and in extreme cases chefs have developed a special shortbread to help cure them. A single Shalour Sable helps a POKENAME metabolize poison and deal with other ailments.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's powerful jaws can crush iron with ease. It uses a disturbing Leer to scare others away from alleyways it wants to claim as its own.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to give out hugs to other Pokémon but often squeeze too tightly. Whenever the same tightness of a hug is reciprocated, the pressure can cause them to develop a brief headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its fearsome appearance, it is timid and avoids conflict. When cornered, it lashes out with swipes, but only as a last resort.
author: .izik

entry: Despite POKENAME having large fangs, they will often be too timid to approach their attacker unless they are threatened. Once enraged, the flame on their tail erupts violently into a vibrant pink as a show of inner strength.
author: npshi

entry: It happily gnaws on its spoon when idle. In battle, it unleashes terrifyingly strong telekinetic blasts, often catching foes off-guard.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits a Persim Berry-like scent from its leaves to lure unsuspecting prey. When they draw near, it bites down with crushing force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hut is made of incredibly robust obsidian and volcanic rock. With its well-developed lower jaw, it effortlessly crushes any rock.
author: chorb33

entry: Its jaws are so strong that it can easily crack open hard nuts and roast them using its flames. It tends to race with other Pokémon, its legs' muscles becoming well-developed in a year's time.
author: infinex21

entry: Its blazing speed is rivaled only by its jealousy of Galarian Rapidash. Rumor has it that its spiked apparel is just an attempt to outstyle its rival and serves no real purpose in battle.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Its blazing speed is rivaled only by its jealousy of Galarian Rapidash. Rumor has it that its spiked apparel is just an attempt to outstyle its rival and serves no real purpose in battle.
author: h0bojoe

entry: With poor eyesight, it nibbles on objects using both heads to identify them. Its bites are gentle but persistent as it explores its surroundings.
author: .izik

entry: One should take extreme caution when approaching POKENAME. The parent can control itself and not poison those it trusts, but the child lacks control of its toxins; any touch of its spines will be painfully poisonous.
author: sk372

entry: An alternate coloration of POKENAME often found in more tropical regions. Its different colors are likely due to a higher intake of fruit in its diet, and this variant is known to have less dangerously potent toxins in its spines.
author: sk372

entry: When cooking a POKENAME, it is important to let the barbs sit in cold water before removing them. This allows the toxins to disperse.
author: .izik

entry: It lives inside swamps and marshes but stays low to the ground so as to not get hit by lightning. Without a Wacan Berry, it will spasm every so often until its affliction is cured.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Research into this Pokémon's brain has revealed that POKENAME is literally incapable of feeling any emotion besides anger. It will swim at foes headfirst to try and skewer them.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It tends to move as little as possible to store the energy it needs to evolve. POKENAME can inflate its body by holding its breath, using its venomous spines to sting anyone who comes too close.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When threatened, POKENAME balloons to an enormous size, presenting its spines. When relaxed, it is surprisingly docile.
author: _sadfroggy

entry: The quills along its body contain a poison so potent they can knock out a Mamoswine within seconds upon striking them. The flames along its body are purple due to the toxic chemicals its body produces and can corrode most metals with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fires poisoned needles out of its stingers to heavily weaken prey before it attacks. Their nests are found in deep water and are often close together to form a colony.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME retains water in its body that it heats up to rapidly expand when frightened. When it believes the threat has passed, it releases bubbles through its spikes to return to its normal size.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME grows sharp toxic feathers all across its body. Trainers often see POKENAME launching its feathers at Pokémon that get too close.
author: schwaus

entry: It closely observes fellow Flying-type Pokémon to learn how to properly divebomb and catch sea-dwelling Pokémon. Perhaps in thanks to their unnatural psychic powers, a stare from POKENAME can intimidate even the largest of foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It knows when prey will come before they even swim near POKENAME. It flies above the sea, knowing the perfect time to swoop down and catch its food.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are covered in short toxic quills. Trainers that own a POKENAME must handle them with care to avoid getting pricked.
author: kitarchen

entry: Slow both on land and in water, POKENAME is easy prey for many other Pokémon. When danger is nearby, it tries to bury itself in mud but only ends up half-submerged. Its body has adapted to be extremely tough to digest, so most predators don't bother.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A sharp sting will hit your body when you are near a wild POKENAME. Because of these harmful interactions, they are considered bad omens by some.
author: jackskipper

entry: It uses the immense water pressure in its body to launch spikes from the hole in its crown at incredible speeds. With its psychic powers guiding each spike, it almost never misses its mark.
author: amiel997

entry: The fusion of two Qwilfish appears to have resulted in POKENAME taking on a form resembling an evolved Qwilfish of the past.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: POKENAME leads pearl divers to Shellder colonies, where the pearl divers help pry the Shellder open. It then eats the Shellder, giving the pearls to the divers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs toxins from polluted reef waters. The water it expels through its coral branches is completely purified and safe to drink.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can detach its poisonous quills, hold one in its mouth, and launch it at prey with a jet of water.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The poison in its spines can also be mixed internally with the ink it spews, letting it infect creatures near or far with its toxin. It's known to have a strong dislike of Malamar, turning aggressive immediately if it spies one.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME doesn't need to hunt prey, as any fish that swims into its spines will almost instantly succumb to its powerful poison. However, since it only has spines on its underbelly, POKENAME is usually safe to pet.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME fires poisonous needles from its elongated mouth. The speed and accuracy of its shots rival that of a finely tuned crossbow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME paints alongside rebellious teenage artists on the side of buildings or train cars. The paint is made of its own venom, so people who want to clean its graffiti off surfaces need face masks to avoid inhaling toxic chemicals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME inhales water and stores it in their neck, both to intimidate and mix it with their potent venom. In battle, they launch a painful combo of oil-like grime and thick spikes at their opponent to guarantee they'll be poisoned and weak.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME keep both toxins and milk in their udders. If a farmer comes up to milk it, they get splatted in the face with poison.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is able to rest on its spiky tail-orb without any sort of discomfort, even bouncing on it to alleviate boredom. Anything else that tries to touch the orb will be pricked and given a painful dose of venom.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are nothing short of malicious. They will purposefully affect those they dislike with a horrible stinging feeling.
author: jackskipper

entry: With venomous spines and lightning-fast reflexes, it strikes from the shadows with deadly precision. It poisons its victims before finishing them.
author: anarchaz

entry: By filling its body with water, it can survive for long periods of drought and appear more imposing to foes. With its bulky appearance and long, menacing spikes, few Pokémon dare to challenge or prey on it.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME is normally just six inches long, but its elastic body can expand to 47 feet when filled with water. It usually only hits this size when threatened.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live amongst coral reefs and use pieces of coral it finds as camouflage. It uses the quills on its shell to inject poison into predators.
author: mistymagius

entry: Said to be the spirit of a fisherman painfully killed by a Qwilfish's poison, POKENAME hooks and poisons mass amounts of aquatic Pokémon.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME determine which hook is dominant through duels of "Tug of War," seeing which can pull the other further. These duels also prevent their hooks from dulling.
author: gordogamr

entry: POKENAME uses the high pressure from its water-filled body to launch rapid punches at its enemies. The spike-like structures covering its body are actually glands that release poisonous spores when it's struck, making it dangerous to attack.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME exclusively eats plasma. When threatened, it will discharge pure energy to defend itself.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: Those expecting soft fluff are unpleasantly surprised by POKENAME's prickly mane, yet it is still shorn by some for use in textiles. It hates this.
author: bukie

entry: Those expecting soft fluff are unpleasantly surprised by POKENAME's prickly mane, yet it is still shorn by some for use in textiles. It hates this.
author: bukie

entry: POKENAME have a superfluous number of spines on their disguise because they want to ensure that their disguise is convincing enough to fool other Pokémon. Despite their best efforts, most of their spines fall apart when soaked in water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fills itself with water and rolls across the sea's surface. When fully inflated, its spines grow sharp enough to pierce ship hulls.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur is similar to barbed wire. Many speculate that there are metal particles in its fur.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME have barbs that are covered with tiny needles, which snap and rapidly inject venom into victims. Most of their venom is reserved for their barbs, so their fangs hold only trace amounts of venom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The heavy pom-poms on POKENAME's arms are filled with both toxins and electricity. It combines its dances in combat with powerful bludgeoning strikes that leave foes poisoned or paralyzed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly defensive of their territory. They will violently ram into anything that gets too close.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME have soft bodies that are built for buoyancy. If two fight, they'll headbutt one another with extreme force.
author: ohok3441

entry: When threatened, POKENAME's tentacles swell, firing toxic needles in every direction. The venom causes severe blistering on contact.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME grinds its teeth, it's building up poison behind its spines. It attacks aggressively after doing so, so stay clear.
author: .realthree

entry: This form of POKENAME was thought to be extinct. Its aggressive demeanor led to humans attempting to eradicate it.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is extremely defensive in battle, letting physical attackers slam into its poisoned spikes. Then, once it has absorbed the blow, it hits back with a powerful counterattack using its razor sharp claws.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME live in tropical reefs, making their home in and amongst corals. They are covered in spines; their leaves in particular carry a nasty toxin that can cause pain for several days.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite the bright colors, the petals dangling from the end of POKENAME's scythe-like leaves are not poisonous. In the past, these petals were once used to dye clothing, but the difficulty of raising POKENAME caused the trend to fade.
author: chibitales

entry: The pressure of seawater has made the spines on its back harder than iron, so no enemy dares to attack it from behind. Its muscular arms allow it to deliver powerful blows and move rocks that block the entrance to underwater caves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have barbs across their body, injecting poison into anything that touches them. They have been seen gathering together in attempts to replicate a Diglett's evolution, but they end up getting stuck together by their barbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has become infamous among couples, as it has a tendency to leap and attempt to sting those it sees behaving romantically. It's thought that this behavior is born out of little more than petty jealousy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a personality as prickly as its body. Finicky to the extreme, owners must work hard to earn enough of its trust and affection for it to retract its poisonous spines and allow itself to be pet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are adept swimmers that have heightened reflexes while underwater. When another Pokémon bumps into them while swimming, the barbs on their body break and stick to the clumsy Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME inflates its fists when it feels threatened, and uses the quills on its knuckles to fight back with fury. Unfortunately, since POKENAME is paranoid and very easily aggravated, it almost always is in this violent state of mind.
author: jangodiot

entry: This rough Pokémon loves fighting. No matter how badly it gets beat, it always gets back up.
author: themicelegion

entry: If it is angered, it inflates the two sacs on its head, allowing it to latch onto enemies. It then releases toxins through its spikes.
author: kittyluv090

entry: It defends its territory by launching the small Qwilfish on its head towards foes. It is unknown if the Qwilfish are bothered by this.
author: kittyluv090

entry: They are very bad at noticing their surroundings. It is not uncommon to find POKENAME covered in seaweed and barnacles.
author: .izik

entry: Though it moves sluggishly, the spiky creature on its tail has its own brain and will inject potent toxins into anything that gets too close. When in danger, POKENAME will try to avoid combat by making a angry face to intimidade the adversary.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME's hypnosis abilities are only effective on about 30 percent of people. When its pendulum fails, it simply hits the victim with it, injecting them with a toxin that quickly knocks them out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's heavy metallic form restricts its movement, forcing it to take a tactical approach to combat. It endures attacks while waiting for the perfect opportunity to retaliate with a punch so strong it knocks out a foe with a single strike.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its offensive and defensive strength, POKENAME is a bit of a braggart. It taunts foes by rapping its claws against its head or using them to crush thick stones to rubble before their eyes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME does not move very much because it is preparing for evolution. It possesses wings but is too heavy to fly.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME keeps its blades sharp by hunting Onix. Some say they can cut berries from trees as fast as lightning, in spite of the iron-hard chitin now covering its body.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When fleeing a predator, POKENAME cuts down any forest trees in its way using its great scythes.
author: kingeroyal

entry: The pincer on POKENAME's back is spacious and soft inside and ill-equipped for any sort of offense. Instead, it can safely store a number of passengers within to keep them warm and safe during its sea travels.
author: sk372

entry: It is thought that the coloring and eye-patterns of POKENAME's pincers have evolved to look like the skulls of fallen Pokémon. In battle, POKENAME uses this to intimidate its foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The genes of POKENAME's parent Pokémon are evident in its asymmetrical limbs. When hunting, POKENAME will hold its prey with its pincer, while using its scythe to cut it open.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The eyes of POKENAME can perceive their prey from very long distances through the dense jungle. These barbaric Pokémon will swoop down on their prey with swift precision as they ready their pincers to attack.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME is mostly found hiding beneath flowers and colorful plants. It disguises itself using the scent that is spread by the leaf on its head.
author: toniaglitched

entry: POKENAME stores explosive enzymes in its pincers. When it hunts, it grabs its prey and detonates close-range explosions.
author: .realthree

entry: They carry mail between islands and other locations in the Johto region that require heavy use of flying. Bluesky Mail is easily identified by POKENAME due to their sharp eyes, which allow them to snatch the mail they need before rushing off.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The patterns on POKENAME's flowers have an eye-like shape. When they dance, the shifting movement of these patterns disorient potential predators.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's claws contain tongue-like appendages it can fire out to grab and store insects for later consumption. The length and speed of the tongues also make them effective as whips in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME eats discarded meat and bones that butchers throw away. It crushes bones with its claws to break them into edible chunks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME only open their shell when they are attacking or eating. The color of the shell and carapace can vary.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME's jagged pincers cause it to rip things it grips into shreds. These pincers are also super heavy, causing massive blows when used to punch foes.
author: soup1900

entry: When battling for long periods of time, POKENAME's body will become very hot due to its high thermal conductivity. If left like this for too long, POKENAME's body will start to melt away.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's jagged pincers cause it to rip things it grips into shreds. These pincers are also super heavy, causing massive blows when used to punch foes.
author: soup1900

entry: A highly versatile Pokémon, POKENAME is able to use its pincers to knock down trees and its horns to destroy boulders.
author: incognito1234

entry: When exploring tropical lands, such as Hoenn, Trainers bring a POKENAME to clear the underbrush. In their native cold lands, villages use them to gather tinder for winter fires.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME has highly adept senses, allowing it to evade predators at a moment's notice. It can deliver a painful bite when defending itself.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a living weapon, nigh unstoppable once it starts moving. However, it's very susceptible to getting stuck on uneven terrain.
author: jaycielantern

entry: POKENAME skims just beneath the surface, using its bladed fins to steer with uncanny grace. Its claws, formed of condensed water, strike with chilling force before dissolving into mist, leaving nothing but ripples behind.
author: mgfox_66676

entry: POKENAME's defense is near impenetrable, its metal carapace shrugging off most attacks. It counter-attacks with absolute force, slamming and crushing anything in its way with blows from its powerful claws.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's claws hold the power to emit gale-force winds or torrential geysers of water. It uses these abilities to force back intruders to the solitary islands it claims as its home.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME charges its claws with electricity to make its strikes even more devastating. Energetic and fast, it dashes across the battlefield while frantically beating the wings on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's two tails end in pincers with incredible gripping power. Some have put it to work in junkyards and other jobs where it can assist by tearing apart large materials.
author: sk372

entry: The armor covering POKENAME's upper body contains no iron, but is still remarkably hard. Its stomach is unprotected, however.
author: faelocke

entry: A POKENAME will capture foes with the pincer at the end of its tail before releasing a powerful discharge of electricity into them. If this is not enough to defeat them, it will headbutt them with the tough horn atop its head.
author: infinex21

entry: Registering only as a red blur of motion to onlookers, POKENAME runs treetop to treetop at over eighty miles per hour. If it spots a threat below, it drops steel-tipped tail first, hitting with the force of a freight train.
author: ghostslythe

entry: This Pokémon resembles a fighter from a far-off land. A red dust follows POKENAME as it runs, resembling flower petals blowing in the wind.
author: mercsthorn

entry: This Pokémon resembles a fighter from a far-off land. A red dust follows POKENAME as it runs, resembling flower petals blowing in the wind.
author: mercsthorn

entry: POKENAME uses the wings on its back to dash at incredible speed, striking foes with its steel claws without mercy. It senses the aura of other creatures and roams endlessly, seeking powerful Pokémon to test its skills and grow stronger.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With razor-edged claws and fast wings, POKENAME darts through the air to challenge powerful foes. Guided by its ability to sense aura, it never rests until it finds a worthy opponent.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its wings to move faster than the eye can follow. It tracks strong life forces and relentlessly pursues them, sharpening both its claws and its spirit through battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is said that POKENAME can feel the presence of strength itself. Following invisible currents of aura, it races through mountain valleys, searching for worthy opponents.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's blade is naturally formed out of ultralight insect chitin that is also as hard as steel.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME resides in the planet's lower orbit. Upon re-entry, its metallic body becomes white-hot, so it then rests in the deep ocean to cool down.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME's chitin is weaker compared to other Bug types, but its ears each have their own mind. While the main body scavenges for food, each ear stands watch, reacting faster than a blink of an eye to threats.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is a hive mind composed of a swarm of drones and a coffin-like hive which is actually the queen. The drones hunt those that stole from the hive, dragging the prey back so the hive mind can feed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a very popular Pokémon for performers. It has the ability to create beautiful shapes out of the fire on its hands.
author: hiimbasil

entry: The pincers on its tails act as both defense and offense. POKENAME is very skilled with their fire, using its pincers as flamethrowers.
author: codewolfie

entry: To keep its carapace's color vivid, POKENAME must constantly feed, spending most of its time hunting. Its jaws are so strong they can crush even steel.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Attracted to city lights, POKENAME wreaks havoc in the streets. It often vanishes, using disembodied claws to prank innocent bystanders. It ends up claiming a city block as its pranking ground, testing its claw strength against cars.
author: ghostslythe

entry: While unable to fly, POKENAME's blade wings are razor sharp, able to cut through most metal in a single slice. Its agility is unmatched, despite its metal carapace and blade wings weighing it down.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME emits metallic screeches from its ears so powerful that they generate shockwaves. Using its wings, it can swiftly reach its enemies before striking them with its pincers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME appears to secrete grease from between its carapace plates. Its claws can crush its foes, while any attacker struggles to get a grip on it.
author: maxiundmicky

entry: POKENAME's petals serve as a shell to close up while releasing toxic spores to enemies nearby. They always overestimate how long these spores remain active, so they can stay inside for hours after the battle is over.
author: epping_forest

entry: Though it has wings, it's unable to fly due to the weight of its body. POKENAME still makes use of its wings, vibrating them rapidly to generate warmth in chilly underground tunnels.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's body has adapted to almost look like a fake head to scare away any creatures lurking in the deep sea. It can also be used to grab or bite anything that gets too close.
author: dodoowner_

entry: With its steel muscles, scythes and pincers, POKENAME is a destructive powerhouse like no other. Contractors have used it regularly to help in deforestation prior to construction efforts.
author: sk372

entry: Being able to retreat into its rocky shell, POKENAME is well defended. Its tactic in battle is to take to the air in its shell and come crashing down like a meteor.
author: evilgammon

entry: The body of a POKENAME is as hard as steel and resistant to heat, yet is often hot or warm. Its flames will never harm those it trusts, and its steel-hard body will feel cool to the touch for them as well.
author: infinex21

entry: The pincer at the end of POKENAME's stick makes it perfect for grabbing berries too high for it to reach normally. Its weight and metal coating also make it an efficient club to use for self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: The claws that Scizor possessed now have brains and can act independently of the main body. Mysteriously, if fused via DNA splicers, neither the claws nor the body's face seem to behave like the Scizor or either head of Doduo.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME possesses one brain that is divided into three main parts, much like the two hemispheres of the human brain; further studies into its biology are ongoing. In order to not overheat, POKENAME must periodically rest when running long distances.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME possesses one brain that is divided into three main parts, much like the two hemispheres of the human brain; further studies into its biology are ongoing. In order to not overheat, POKENAME must periodically rest when running long distances.
author: bobosmith01
