entry: POKENAME flies so efficiently that it can go its whole life without landing. Because it can make itself invisible, most people only witness it as the sensation of a cool breeze by riversides.
author: .realthree

entry: It habitually washes Bluk Berries in ponds before eating them. This fastidious habit makes it a surprisingly neat feeder.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes happy chirps that sound like singing during the evening hours. Those who hear it report falling asleep almost instantly, lulled into a peaceful slumber by its melodic calls.
author: .izik

entry: The beak within its outer mouth extends to snap at prey with precision. Its sharpness and force are enough to pierce through marble when threatened.
author: .izik

entry: Though nocturnal, it emits a high-frequency chirp through its wings each morning while sleeping. This signal assures its allies of its safety.
author: .izik

entry: It builds small bonfires to keep its nest warm and withstand the cold even in harsh winters. In battle, POKENAME relies on its long beak to deliver powerful strikes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its helium-filled body allows it to float effortlessly when not flapping its wings. This buoyancy gives it a serene and graceful appearance in the sky.
author: .izik

entry: It waves its feathered arms to spread a delightful aroma. However, the scent is so enchanting it can cause those nearby to faint if inhaled for too long.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefer to hunt alone and will try to pop each other with their sharp beaks if another POKENAME enter their territory. Despite being lightweight, it is able to carry items as heavy as a motorcycle.
author: mistymagius

entry: The feathers of a POKENAME are regularly used in the creation of artisanal Poké Toys in Vertress City. The feathers are sturdy and don't break easily.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a head crest that turns a bright burgundy whenever they are hurt. This happens often because they have to defend themselves from larger predators without the ability to see.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME patrols its nesting grounds in a circular pattern, watching for intruders. If a predator approaches, it dive-bombs at full speed, causing an explosive impact upon collision.
author: .izik

entry: It drinks sap from maple trees to fuel the energy burning within its body. When startled, it emits bright pink flashes from its chest as a defense.
author: .izik

entry: Using its sharp beak, it drills into trees to drink sap, favoring pine sap for its strong scent. This behavior sustains it in forested areas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's powerful legs and eyes make it a fearsome hunter. It can spot prey miles in the distance, run rapidly to catch up, and leap long distances to pounce and clasp its powerful jaws down upon them.
author: sk372

entry: Its long neck allows it to perform intricate sambas with grace. It often showcases its dances near children's parties, seeking admiration and applause.
author: .izik

entry: The goo that flows from its mouth is highly acidic. While flying, it will spit this acid to deter enemies or catch prey off-guard.
author: .izik

entry: Exceptionally coy around older humans, it seeks gentle pets and affection. When held, it coos softly to express its happiness.
author: .izik

entry: It collects Yellow Apricorns with its paws and stores them in hollow trees. Lumberjacks often find these bizarre stockpiles, leaving them puzzled by the peculiar hoarding behavior.
author: .izik

entry: The feathers covering its body are as thin as needles and dangerously sharp. This adaptation protects it from predators while in the desert.
author: .izik

entry: It spreads its wings wide to absorb rays from the desert sun. This energy sustains it during long flights over barren landscapes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is taught from a young age on how to corner escaping Pokémon. Its sharp eyes allow it to spot dead ends to pin down wild Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wing-like ears allow it to soar gracefully above deep canyons. The scale on its head is exceptionally sharp, capable of slicing through tough rock formations mid-flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME streaks across the morning sky, shedding feathers like stardust. Upon spotting prey like Weedle, it dives at incredible speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps low to the ground, as its heavy round body is difficult to keep aloft for long. If another hunter tries to compete with it for a meal, POKENAME fires short range beams of light from its eyes to deter them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its wide wings to shield the flame burning on its tail when heavy rain falls, preventing it from weakening. When hunting, it uses its long, pointed beak to reach prey hiding inside narrow holes in tree trunks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It extends its talons from underground to scratch at foes, surprising them with an attack from below. This tactic keeps it hidden while hunting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live alone in the wild but are often kept together in fish tanks in captivity. They approach the glass when people are close and purse their beak in what many believe is a kiss. When feeding, they tear apart their meal in a frenzy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's three heads can rapidly spin to drill through the ground with their long beaks. Nobody is sure where their necks begin or end.
author: bee4082

entry: While flying, POKENAME always maintains a majestic posture, never showing fear even before the most dangerous Pokémon. It tends to build its nest near small ponds so it can keep its long feathers clean.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses its long beak to steal jewelry from unsuspecting passersby. Preferring high ground, it often nests on the roofs of financial institutions.
author: .izik

entry: It nests on the roofs of banks and financial institutions, using stolen high-value clothing and currency to construct its home. Its thieving habits are notorious.
author: .izik

entry: When its headaches become unbearable, it channels psychic energy through the feathers on its head. This energy can create massive whirlpools in nearby waters.
author: .izik

entry: It performs elaborate displays of strength, splashing ponds with its wings to court potential mates. These rituals are both impressive and theatrical.
author: .izik

entry: With the precision of a professional boxer, it pecks its foes while using aerial agility to dodge attacks. Its speed and power make it a formidable opponent.
author: .izik

entry: When it doesn't get its way, it becomes uncontrollably enraged. By focusing its anger, its attacks gain enough strength to break bones.
author: .izik

entry: By coating its long beak in flames, it can deliver devastating thrusts. Its reliable nature and majestic wings have made it an exceptional companion for crossing entire Regions while riding on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By coating its long beak in flames, it can deliver devastating thrusts. Its reliable nature and majestic wings have made it an exceptional companion for crossing entire Regions while riding on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME latches onto bulky Pokémon with its talons to whisk them away back to its nest. Once it returns home, it roasts the Pokémon into a meal with its powerful flames. The resulting meal is then eaten by its chicks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses its wings to watch over its vast territory from above and dive down on enemies, catching them off guard. POKENAME can deliver extremely powerful punches, capable of cracking stone walls or steel plates as if they were nothing.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Normally found guarding desert temples, POKENAME descends psychically from above and hits intruders with its staff. Archaeologists who catch it find all their socks woven into a nest while it wears one of their hoodies.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME were once worshipped as demigods by certain cultures near the equator. It's said that when they blew into their warhorn, men who heard its cry miles away would take a knee, overcome by fear.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: Its long neck helps POKENAME to gasp for air when diving. Its wings are so stunted that it can only flap over short distances.
author: chorb33

entry: When it eats, the spikes on its mouth turn inward to keep its prey from escaping. It can only fly if its stomach is completely empty.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME breaks apart rocks with its large beak. When it has trouble breaking rocks, it will fly high into the sky before crashing down onto the rock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using its hard, stone-like arms, it smacks tree limbs to break them off and access sap. Once the sap flows, it sticks its beak in to drink greedily.
author: .izik

entry: When it flaps its wings, it releases flaming embers that drift gently to the ground like feathers. This fiery display both dazzles and intimidates its enemies.
author: .izik

entry: Its flaming mane creates stunning light shows as it flies through the night sky. It often perches near volcanoes, absorbing warmth through its down.
author: .izik

entry: It frequently stares blankly in a random direction. Legends state that this is because it knows a future disaster will occur in that area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME likes to drift through all kinds of water and moves leisurely with the help of its limbs. If it gets spooked, it takes off and runs away.
author: chorb33

entry: It fires bolts of electricity through its beak, each powerful enough to cause burns. This shocking attack adds an extra edge to its arsenal.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME happens to lose its leek, it flies in circles until it can spot it from above with its sharp vision. Its long, pointed beak helps ward off anyone trying to steal its cherished stick.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It squirts berry juice on its feathers to attract prey, but this leaves its body sticky and grounds it temporarily. Its resourcefulness is offset by its messiness.
author: .izik

entry: The 3 heads of POKENAME have very sharp beaks that can pierce through any prey when they swoop down from the skies. They often roost on high mountain ranges beyond the sight of those that live below.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME can move exceedingly quickly, both on land and in the sky. When threatened, its numerous heads will stare down dangerous opponents until they run. It uses its long, sharp beaks to viciously peck anyone that gets too close.
author: jadey.1557

entry: Despite its weight, POKENAME can fly with ease. The cannons on its back can shoot powerful jets of water, which it can use to accelerate or dodge.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME makes its territory in urban areas. It can easily remember human faces, and will protect those who give it food.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME makes its territory in urban areas. It can easily remember human faces, and will protect those who give it food.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME makes its territory in urban areas. It can easily remember human faces, and will protect those who give it food.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME makes its territory in urban areas. It can easily remember human faces, and will protect those who give it food.
author: noel5229

entry: It snaps its sharp claws loudly while flying, intimidating enemies into retreating. The claws are strong enough to cut through tree limbs effortlessly.
author: .izik

entry: Between its claws and beak, POKENAME can open up any shellfish. It steals prey from other Pokémon, then clumsily scuttles away to hide and eat it.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME's diet primarily consists of poisonous mushrooms. These mushrooms allow it to secrete a foul odor it uses to ward off predators.
author: midnightsoup

entry: POKENAME's saliva is frigid to the touch and drips almost constantly. One lick can freeze the surface of nearly any object it contacts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME encases itself in a thick shell of ice to protect itself until it's ready to evolve, at which point the shell will melt away.
author: midnightsoup

entry: With a snout adept at rooting for food, it guards its delectable eggs. They are savored by all, even those with waning appetites.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME hide in burrows for most of the year to keep their body temperature low. When winter comes, they emerge from these burrows to look for a mate.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Some styling schools keep a POKENAME as a teaching assistant. Its thick coat is ideal for practicing cuts and braids, and it gently guides students towards better techniques.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's pincers are very cold to the touch. It sniffs out succulent berries growing on trees, using its pincers to grab them, keeping them chilled and fresh until it's ready to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a hirsute exterior that sheds hair wherever they go. This hair is coated with a poisonous oil that causes predators to get sick.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though it has a strong nose, POKENAME often gets food stuck in its fur, causing it to run in circles trying to find the scent. It is a popular pet in colder climates.
author: frokachu

entry: Almost indistinguishable from a Swinub from afar, the telltale sign that this is a POKENAME is from its skittering motions it makes when it moves around. Its piercing blue gaze sends chills up people's spines.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME have a layer of feathers that lock in their body heat by creating a layer of hot air. Since they sleep outside in their nest, this allows them to remain warm during winter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appears only near cold, active mountain regions. It dislikes being alone and is often found sleeping in groups.
author: curazy

entry: Pieces of a POKENAME's outer shell are dissolved and used in the creation of less-potent Ice Heals. The shell regrows in minutes once broken off.
author: .izik

entry: It can sense whether a person is pure of heart by smell alone. However, it often mistakes the smell of kindness for the smell of food.
author: larky_

entry: POKENAME's potent sense of smell allows it to sniff out tasty mushrooms even from long distances. If it's caught the scent of something good, the orb on its tail glows brightly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rubs the tip of its tail against its wool to generate the electricity needed for its attacks more quickly. It lives in fairly large groups to reduce the chances of predators targeting it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its thick wool allows POKENAME to thrive even in the coldest environments without suffering from the low temperatures. The light from its tail can shine through blizzards, so this Pokémon is often used to guide expeditions in icy habitats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If POKENAME is startled while searching for food, it will attempt to flee using the wind. It stays in places with frequent wind gusts.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME loves snowballs so much that it carries three wherever it goes. It's rumored that its shape is the way it is because it ate a snowball once.
author: yorui3913

entry: POKENAME's front tooth radiates an intense chill just before biting. POKENAME prefers its food frozen and often ices berries before eating them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dashes through the air blindly, bumping into people and Pokémon alike. During the winter, it freezes in place to enter a deep hibernation.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME will sleep for weeks at a time, then wake up with a ravenous hunger. They will attack prey many times larger than itself, and against all odds, often come out on top. After this display of force, they become very docile and much weaker.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME, flat and silent, clings to icy cavern walls in the shape of ancient letters. If it senses a lost traveler, it reshapes into an arrow and leads them to safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's drill is covered in thick hair, allowing it to dig through the thick snow and permafrost. It stores berries in its underground den, so it has a reliable food source when large blizzards arrive.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME waits for other Pokémon to leave their nests, and then steals the nest for a napping spot. It is willing to become domesticated as long as it is provided with food and a cozy place to sleep.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its sense of smell has been enhanced even further, able to sniff out food and other items buried deep within the dirt. Its large size means it can accidentally bowl over smaller creatures in its eagerness to investigate a smell.
author: sk372

entry: Due to the increase of habitat destruction and low wild population, they meet the criteria to obtain endangered status. The caves they used to reside within are now too warm for them, so they are forced to migrate to find a new home.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME make many mistakes when giving gifts to children because of their poor eyesight. Despite their flaws, they are beloved by children around the world because of their perseverance and good will.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The older POKENAME gets, the longer it grows. It has a very sensitive nose that can locate mushrooms, Berries, and even hot springs buried under ice.
author: the_fireplace

entry: The icy antlers of POKENAME remain frigid no matter the season. In the height of summer, they can still freeze dew into tiny snowflakes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend their entire lives attempting to capture the beauty of the northern lights using their brush-like tail, which emits a layer of frost.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: With its eyes closed in focus, POKENAME strikes with elegant martial arts moves. Each hit leaves behind a thin layer of frost across the impact zone.
author: .izik

entry: As it grooms the fur on its head, POKENAME's nose twitches rapidly. It insists on using icy spring water to keep its coat pristine.
author: .izik

entry: Trained POKENAME can sniff out high-quality mushrooms beneath the soil easily. When it catches a whiff, it runs to the spot and leaps head-first onto the soil, its twin prongs marking the spot that needs to be dug into.
author: sk372

entry: The fur atop POKENAME's head grows hot enough to fry an egg. It releases fire from its nose which burns hotter if it's eaten spicy food that day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen cuddling one another to share their body heat during the winter. Their fur is incredibly soft, so they are popular companions for Trainers that live in colder climates.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is able to throw snowballs, which it uses to defend itself from predators. It loves snowball fights.
author: yorui3913

entry: POKENAME struggles to camouflage itself as it is constantly shivering from the extreme cold. Because of how little it can move, it has a very slow metabolism so it can store more energy.
author: mistymagius

entry: Rooting for food amidst volcanic craters, POKENAME is a fiery ice marvel. Its snout emits flames as it hunts for its next meal.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME adores mushrooms and collects them en masse. Sometimes, it gathers so many mushrooms it tires itself out to the point of exhaustion, and will fall asleep in the midst of eating one.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives a mostly sedentary lifestyle, making homes where fungi grow abundantly. It spends much of the day napping, using its long tongue to reach out and nab mushrooms when it's hungry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME survives the bitter cold of its home by expending as little energy as possible. As an adaptive mechanism, having to exert itself causes it to become unhappy.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME keeps its nose to the ground to sniff for food, often bumping into things in its environment as it does due to its stature. Any damage POKENAME takes from this is minimal thanks to its hardened skull.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME travel to villages in icy climates to warn people of cataclysmic hailstorms. Their fur locks in heat so they can safely remain outside while they escort villagers to a safe evacuation point.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The ice on its wings looks sharp but is, in reality, quite blunt. They are always tired from watching after their young.
author: zerocipher

entry: Trainers often try to use POKENAME as an Ice Pick but fail to realize how fragile it is. One wrong strike can cause its blade to crack and the Pokémon to faint.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It has an uncanny ability to sense where living things are. POKENAME have been fashioned into a sort of compass used to find lost people and Pokémon.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME needs to keep itself warm since its steel blades will become dull and brittle in the cold. It relentlessly hunts Swinub and Piloswine, using their fur as warm clothing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's strong sense of smell lets it easily locate mushrooms beneath the soil, which it then gathers up with its ribbons. It is especially adept at finding mushrooms that have soothing medicinal properties when eaten.
author: sk372

entry: This variant of POKENAME is found in more frigid northern regions, and is especially good at finding rare fungi beneath the snow. These mushrooms are particularly noted for their calming effects when cooked and eaten.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves to collect Ice Stones, as it likes the way they twinkle under the winter stars. Groups of them like to gather at the mountain's peak to watch auroras streak across the sky.
author: mistymagius

entry: It constantly sniffs the ground as it shuffles forward, smashing through obstacles it cannot see. Its snout picks up the scent of buried roots and cave-dwelling prey with unnerving precision.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Legends say that if anyone were to wish for food, POKENAME may grant that wish. People have woken up to hearty breakfasts because of this Pokémon.
author: birchbot

entry: Its body is protected by a thick layer of icy armor, which continues to thicken in the cold weather. However, if the armor gets too heavy, POKENAME will struggle to walk properly.
author: mistymagius

entry: It tends to hide beneath snow or thin layers of ice to ambush its prey. Thanks to its thick fur, it can remain perfectly still with jaws wide open for days, enduring the cold without discomfort.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live in cold mountain lakes. The icy fins on POKENAME glow, acting as a guiding light to anything that may have fallen through the ice.
author: codewolfie

entry: Groups of POKENAME bundle up during the winter as they can't keep growing while they are too cold. Its fur grows extremely quickly, leaving trails of shed fur wherever it goes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME live in the snowy mountains, their thick fur protecting them from the cold. When the weather gets really cold, groups of POKENAME will gather in small hot springs to keep warm.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME relies entirely on its sense of smell and hearing to navigate around the icy caves it calls home. It feeds on small dead plants.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME primarily lives in cold climates, where it buries its nose in the snow to sniff for food. Its tusks are frozen over from doing this constantly.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's body is a curious mix of fur and clay. It uses its sensitive nose to sniff out food before digging into the ground with arms permanently covered in ice.
author: glacierwing

entry: POKENAME is a bird Pokémon that can be found in cold regions. Its plumage is described as the warmest in existence.
author: spagalapof

entry: POKENAME's fur is a great heat insulator, preventing its wings from freezing over. It thrives in colder climates, however a global rise in temperature has reduced POKENAME's numbers.
author: mistymagius

entry: It lives a solitary life along snowy mountain slopes. Using its sharp claws, POKENAME takes great time in carving a block of ice perfectly to its taste.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's thick, frosty fur is laced with hidden venomous barbs. By brushing against a foe, it can silently deliver an illness without ever attacking.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will travel with a herd of Swinub and prove itself by poisoning any incoming threats that wish to harm the herd. When it cannot defend the herd, many of the grateful Swinub will surround and protect it.
author: redknight2030

entry: Its fur coat keeps it a little warmer than is comfortable, so it wears an icy cloak to keep itself cool. When strong winds pick up, powdered snow drifts off of the cloak in large amounts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME burrows into fresh snow to regulate its body temperature. When it starts to feel warm, its nose quivers, warning it to cool off.
author: .izik

entry: In its natural habitat, POKENAME spends most of its time searching for places to sleep. Its dense fur insulates it from extreme cold, allowing it to rest motionless in snowdrifts for days without stirring.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME swoops down on foes like snowfall. Its ground-rooting behavior complements its aerial acrobatics, creating a versatile combat style.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME can usually be found in pine trees, huddling together to keep themselves warm. Since the bud on their head isn't covered in warm fur, it tends to freeze over.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is said that a Swinub's sensitive nose guided it to a specific mound of snow. Theories suggest a paranormal relationship exists between the two.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME diligently gathers fresh snow to add to its mound, often seeking shelter within the mouth of its homemade refuge.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Children approach this Pokémon, expecting an intriguing sandcastle. Many are startled as POKENAME sniffs furiously at the new, incoming smells.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The ghostly ties between snow and Swinub are unbreakable. Working as one, POKENAME can both defend and repair itself, a feat previously unattainable.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The bristles from its fur are often used to make grooming brushes for other Pokémon. Its keen nose allows it to detect berries and hidden food buried beneath thick layers of snow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in cold climates and are usually found roaming in packs in tundras or above the snow line on mountains. They make excellent companions as they have a keen sense of direction, even during blizzards.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in cold climates and are usually found roaming in packs in tundras or above the snow line on mountains. They make excellent companions as they have a keen sense of direction, even during blizzards.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's nose is so sensitive it can smell gems buried in solid rock. It has a strong preference for alexandrite above all other stones.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are found in most snowy regions of the world. Due to being constantly burrowed in the snow, they sneeze often and have other symptoms of the common cold most of the time.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Without regular grooming, POKENAME's fur covers its eyes and causes intense headaches. When left unmanaged, its pain can spread telepathically to others nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rarely leaves the water, as its soaked fur would freeze almost instantly in arctic temperatures. When food is scarce, it sleeps on the seafloor to conserve energy.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a thick layer of fur that protects it from frigid environments. When it gets wet, it sneezes out embers to try to warm itself up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME only sniffs out the most precious of treats. It keeps a legendary flame within for warmth in the harshest of climates.
author: anarchaz

entry: It uses its flames to look for berries under the snow. Trainers from snowy towns will often travel with POKENAME to keep warm.
author: schwaus

entry: The ice crystals that form along the backs of POKENAME are a by-product of their ability to store ambient heat within their bodies. The temperature difference this creates between their bodies and the surrounding air has an extreme chilling effect.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With a lazy and simpleminded disposition, not much will rouse POKENAME from its constant slumbering. The best way to get it to wake up and move around is using the scent of mushrooms, its favorite snack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sniffs low to the ground searching for roots and mushrooms to snack on. Its highly skittish nature means that as soon as its heads have found food, they immediately run and hide to eat their meal in solace.
author: sk372

entry: To defend its den, POKENAME splashes intruders with freezing water before following up with a breath of ice-cold wind that locks them in place.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME clamps onto its family in a warm embrace, it gently nuzzles them with its chilled nose. It offers the same affection to humans it trusts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes little sniffling noises as it flies around frigid areas and leaves a trail of ghostly snowfall behind it. These flakes will give a person momentary chills on contact, even in warmer climates.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can smell food even through solid rock. If it catches a whiff of something intriguing, it will dig through an entire mountain just to get to the other side and investigate.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is a timid sort, likely to flee underground at the first sign of aggression. The scent of fresh mushrooms is usually enough to get it to venture out of its home.
author: sk372

entry: Though covered in fur, POKENAME's pincers are ice-cold. A tight clamp can cause cracks in the pincers that take days to heal.
author: .izik

entry: Its claws and shell are made of ice. It has a layer of fat and fur underneath its shell.
author: shadowpanther

entry: The bulb on its back is small, so it covers it with snow to keep it safe. Trainers will bond with their POKENAME by helping to decorate its snowball.
author: admiralvermin

entry: POKENAME dances silently in icy caves from sunrise to dusk. If it misses a session, its fur begins to fall out in clumps due to its stress.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swim in icy cold waters with a layer of fur to keep themselves warm. They have tufts of fur over their underdeveloped eyes, which protect them from bright lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: One of only a few arachnid Pokémon that are native to the taiga, its insulating fur helps it endure extreme cold. Its tusks and horn are made of ice.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME have incredibly thick fur and feathers that allow them to survive in frigid environments. When peaceful, steady snow falls, their power is said to peak.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sleeps for around eighteen hours each day, conserving energy for stealthily stealing food. It sometimes uses its claws to cut holes in icy lakes for people to fish, but will abscond with some of the catch when it sees an opportunity.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a rare sight, found in temperate forests and tundras, where it lumbers about searching for food to provide for its young. It often stealthily watches campers and rushes into their camp in a rage if it witnesses poor wilderness respect.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME presses its chilly snout against others in its herd to greet them. These brief snorts help maintain close bonds and signal emotions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are regarded by scientists as critically endangered because the caves they can safely nest in have been getting too warm for them to live comfortably. Ongoing efforts to domesticate POKENAME have been advertised to help preserve the species.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collects pinecones to give as gifts. Its thick facial fur causes it to make frequent mix-ups, gifting to strangers by mistake.
author: .izik

entry: Old scientists once claimed POKENAME's fur never sheds. This lore has been recently proven false, as it was discovered to eat its own fur with its long beak to help retain nutrients in frozen regions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are covered in thick ropes they braid from plant fibers that grow from their bodies. This growth never stops, so if humans don't harvest parts of these ropes intermittently, a POKENAME can become entangled in them itself.
author: sontyp

entry: The bristles of its fur are very resistant; in fact, they are used to make brushes for grooming the fur of other Pokémon. With its claws and fangs, POKENAME digs through the frozen ground to make its den as comfortable as possible.
author: fiordaliso

entry: After eating, POKENAME leaps through snowdrifts for hours. It despises feeling full and stays active to burn off meals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in frigid regions, using its tusks to root around the snowy ground for food. If it spots another creature chilled by the cold, it nuzzles close to warm them with its fur.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses an icicle to balance while sliding on frozen lakes. If it falls, its thick fur cushions the impact, keeping it safe regardless of speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its axe to cut down rotten trees containing nutritious mushrooms. Its thick coat can be used to brace itself when it delivers a swing.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's thick fur lets it remain nice and warm even in the heaviest of snowy conditions. With just a light brush of its ribbons, it can share its warmth with others, making it invaluable as a traveling companion through frigid areas.
author: sk372

entry: Though its overgrown fur leaves it mostly blind, POKENAME compensates with a powerful sense of smell. It can pick out a foe's scent with ease and use its extendable arms with potent precision.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has natural-born instincts that compel it to find, plant, and take care of Yache Berries. Once the snowy, wintry season hits, its fur coat grows longer and it lives off its Yache Berry horde.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rely on a keen sense of smell to identify different objects because they are blind. They steal pungent Charti Berries from other Pokémon to protect themselves from Rock-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME shivers, tiny flurries of snow burst from its fur. This phenomenon often heralds heavier snowfall in colder months.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires Ice Beams from its twin tusks. When agitated, its breath frosts the air around it to cause an icy fog.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's icy fur can freeze others on contact. It drags frozen victims into its cave, seeking company in the silent cold.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often partners with wild Swinub, providing shelter to their newborns. In turn, it receives food which it would otherwise struggle to obtain.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Cold to the touch and sickening to be around, POKENAME is said to cause people's soul to freeze, turning them into a heartless being. This Pokémon seems to have no relation to the Ground type despite its namesake.
author: the_lizard43

entry: POKENAME is often stepped on by people mistaking it for an ordinary pile of sand. This caused POKENAME to develop a hard outer shell of sand.
author: thefrenchchefyt

entry: Despite its fluffy look, POKENAME's fur is freezing to the touch. It sleeps buried in snow, absorbing the cold.
author: .izik

entry: The fur of POKENAME is incredibly soft and insulating. Many a climber have found themselves saved by wild POKENAME curling around them on long journeys up Mt. Coronet.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: The thick fur covering its body shields POKENAME from the freezing cold of snowy forests where it nests. Since the fur also covers its eyes, it often bumps into other Pokémon or objects while flying.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gathers large amounts of snow in its beak to hurl at enemies when threatened. Since the fur covering its body also hides its eyes, it often collides with Pokémon or obstacles while in flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME channel the power of their headaches to produce snow from their staff. The more pain they are in, the more snow comes out of the staff. Some particularly cruel Trainers overstimulate their minds to create headaches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dwells by frozen lakes. Its thick fur mats down in water, allowing it to swim gracefully in icy currents.
author: .izik

entry: While usually moving slowly and steadily to conserve energy, POKENAME has the ability to run suddenly at high speeds. Rarely does it ever seem to tire. It prefers a diet high in protein and fat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While usually moving slowly and steadily to conserve energy, POKENAME has the ability to run suddenly at high speeds. Rarely does it ever seem to tire. It prefers a diet high in protein and fat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It does not have eyelids, so the patch of fur atop its head serves as both protection from cold weather and a way to shade its eyes. If its Trainer removes this patch of fur, it becomes lethargic from overstimulation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have dense fur coats that help them survive the cold environments that they call home. Their fur is highly prized for its insulating properties and some Pokémon Breeders will maintain large herds of them for this.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lives by ice-cold waters and fishes using its tail, just like Slowpoke. If attacked, it will slowly but surely use its large body and slam into foes. It only becomes outwardly excited over a meal of mushrooms and seafood.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME live in herds where they compete by swiping tusks and horns at each other. Sailors traveling through icy waters keep them to clear icebergs, which the POKENAME crash into with their horns.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's tongue is extremely cold. It uses it to freeze kelp before eating, making the texture more brittle and easier to chew.
author: .izik

entry: Warm fur and a patient temperament makes POKENAME a perfect caregiver. It often works at daycare centers to help baby Pokémon sleep more comfortably.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME resides in warm oceans to keep the coral colony on its back alive. In exchange, the coral gives POKENAME energy through photosynthesis.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME don't move very often. They usually lay on the ocean floor, silently waiting for small fish Pokémon to come closer so they can eat them.
author: sottiwotti

entry: It sleeps atop palm trees, enjoying the warmth of the sun. From these heights, it keeps an eye on the reefs below, ready to protect them if needed.
author: .izik

entry: This aquatic Pokémon can fire a punch faster than a bullet. To further worsen the blow, POKENAME carries anemones in its hands, adding a painful sting to every punch.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME licks surrounding coral clean. If its tongue dries out, its entire body turns white.
author: themicelegion

entry: All it does is wait in its hiding place for the evolution that will free it from its shell. Its body is encased in a coral armor harder than stone, strengthened by the immense pressure of the ocean depths.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It attaches itself to oceanic toxic waste. It sustains itself by absorbing the toxins, purifying the waste in the process.
author: staghorn

entry: Ribbons of clean, warm ocean water stream out of its body. Ocean life prospers in areas POKENAME call home.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME wears itself out trying to fight bird Pokémon on the rocky shores it calls home. To recharge, it will bask in tide pools.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME wades in shallow waters, attempting to find and defeat Mareanie. If it succeeds, the bubbles spouting from its back intensify.
author: pizzarcato

entry: If a Water-type Pokémon needs to travel across land, it will seek out a POKENAME. The POKENAME then carries it in its water pouch to its destination.
author: staghorn

entry: Pollutants in the water are filtered through its coral branches, leaving the sea cleaner. Its presence is vital to maintaining healthy marine ecosystems.
author: .izik

entry: It makes its home near abandoned aquatic minefields, where it thrives among forgotten debris. The danger of its environment keeps most predators at bay.
author: .izik

entry: It glows more brightly during meteor showers, reflecting the starlight above. Many believe this luminous display is a sign of cosmic harmony.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live on and around coral reefs. They seem to soak up a strange, unknown energy from space to and use it to help revitalize ocean life.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME puts on fun beach side magic shows, blowing bubbles into surprisingly sturdy objects. At the end of its shows, it always blows small creatures and play swords and gives them to the children in the audience.
author: evilgammon

entry: They hide among colorful underwater plant life and generally avoid combat. As a result, very few POKENAME evolve in the wild.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They hide among colorful underwater plant life and generally avoid combat. As a result, very few POKENAME evolve in the wild.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME wanders tirelessly among coral reefs to watch over the integrity of its natural habitat. It becomes extremely aggressive toward boats and divers, driving them away at all costs due to its deep distrust of humans.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME dwell in cold northern seas and have few predators. However, climate change is threatening their numbers as the temperature of the ocean rises.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME latches onto groups of Corsola and extends their reach. In return they feed it leftovers from their meals. It also protects Corsola from oil spills by guiding the oil away from where they live.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's adaptive form makes it more resilient to changes in water conditions around it. Nature preserves are introducing it to Corsola colonies in the hopes it may spread this resilience over time and help the species's longevity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body has evolved to blend seamlessly among the corals found only in the purest waters. To fend off predators, it charges its spikes with electricity, releasing jolts strong enough to stun even much larger Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME shares a symbiotic bond with the Water-type Pokémon in its belly, providing them safety and food. In return, they alert POKENAME to potential threats while it sleeps through most of the day.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME have scales with a coral tint and an abrasive exterior. Marine biologists monitor the health of coral reefs by watching for discoloration of POKENAME scales, which become blue if they are ill from pollution.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME resides in warm southern seas. When threatened, the coral branches on this Pokémon's back can become hot enough to boil the water around them.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are popular as pets due to their brightly colored coats, which change depending on the time of day. Its cries sound faintly like whale song.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME's lures are actually small air pockets, allowing it to collect small items from the seafloor. However, it will often get pieces of trash stuck in its tubes, causing it difficulty breathing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in warm coral reefs, hiding itself with its camouflage patterns. Should the sea become polluted, its health will diminish.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: It floats gently in the sky above coral reefs, carried by ocean breezes. Its carefree drifting adds an extra touch of beauty to the vibrant reefs below.
author: .izik

entry: It sleeps nestled in kelp beds, swaying gently with the ocean currents. The flowing plants provide it with both comfort and camouflage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats around tropical waters, carried by the ocean breeze. It dances in midair when hovering over coral reefs, and some say these dances improve the health of the reef and its inhabitants.
author: sk372

entry: It feeds on lily pads, often munching on them as it floats along the water's surface. This diet gives it a surprisingly peaceful demeanor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a rare sight in warm oceans as they have very slow reproductive cycles. They always seek the shade, as direct sunlight can bleach the corals that grow on it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sleeps peacefully within coral reefs, barely reacting to disturbances. If a Swimmer brushes against it, it simply shifts its position and continues its nap.
author: .izik

entry: It spends most of its time resting underwater while its coral photosynthesizes. If a foe approaches from above, the coral's toxic stingers act as a defense.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME guards coral reefs, baring its fangs at anyone who dares come too close. It can thrive only in warm seas; if the water temperature drops too low, its coral growths begin to lose their color.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Small Pokémon live in the miniature reef in POKENAME's spongy hair for protection from predators, which are warded off by its wailing. Its screams were the source of old ghost stories of shipwrecks in tropical waters.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This kindhearted Pokémon protects weak sea life from danger, putting itself on the line for it's noble cause. It is quite weak however and often gets beaten quite badly.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME has gotten very strong and can protect innocent sea life from any danger it may encounter. This heroic Pokémon has earned itself the title of Protector Of The Reef.
author: evilgammon

entry: The venom it secretes causes intense nausea in anyone affected. Even a small amount can incapacitate a foe, making it a powerful defense mechanism.
author: .izik

entry: An invasive species, POKENAME seek out water purification chemicals as treats. This has led it to infesting public swimming pools, violently kicking out humans who attempt to enter.
author: ghostslythe

entry: If a Cursola were to stay alive, it's speculated it would resemble POKENAME. However, no way to make this happen without fusion energy has been found.
author: galactak

entry: This Pokémon can swim at speeds of up to 100 mph, darting through the water with unmatched agility. Its swift movements make it difficult to catch.
author: .izik

entry: It spits ink at prey to blind them, giving POKENAME time to strike or escape. The dark cloud it creates lingers in the water, confusing any nearby threats.
author: .izik

entry: Individual POKENAME seek out damaged Corsola that have lost their branches and gift them decorated replacements.
author: pankiwi

entry: This joyful Pokémon delivers Tropic Mail between islands, ferrying colorful shells and dried coral as souvenirs. Locals believe reading one under the sun brings luck at sea.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's movement is mostly directed by the Remoraid living on its back. It has an excellent memory.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME roams the coral reefs in the warm sea, driving away any ships that approach its habitat to protect its waters from pollution. It can shoot jets of water powerful enough to damage even the steel hulls of boats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are found hovering around billboards advertising oceanic vacations. Used as natural filters for fish tanks, they have the uncanny ability to escape confinement by flickering through cyberspace.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The coral that grows on its body produces extra zooxanthellae, making it remarkably vivid. It's able to exude some of its zooxanthellae through its tail, and uses it to restore color and life to bleached coral and Corsola.
author: hophoppip

entry: It hogs all the Muscle Mochi to itself and does not enjoy sharing with other Pokémon. It developed this snarky attitude when its home became polluted, and food was scarce.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The rigid branches of POKENAME provide useful cover for Tynamo. Together they combine their electricity to deliver nasty shocks to attackers.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME dwells in the ocean depths, feeding on algae near coral reefs. When threatened, it electrifies its coral tail and lashes out at enemies with brutal force.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The fish Pokémon in POKENAME's water-filled sac serve as vital organs; when they eat, POKENAME is also fed. It fiercely guards its internal ecosystem.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Compacted boulders of coral are blasted from its distinctive arm cannon. In its fervor, Corsola are occasionally launched by accident.
author: pizzarcato

entry: A compassionate Pokémon typically found in deep coral reefs. POKENAME are known to save drowning people by blowing clean air bubbles around them.
author: wyattwintersoul

entry: Despite its appearance, it is a healthy Pokémon that rarely gets sick. The water it creates is highly prized by medical researchers.
author: dicedragon20

entry: When threatened, it spits mud at predators to confuse them and make its escape. This clever tactic ensures it remains safe in even the most perilous waters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically live in warm, brackish waters. Unfortunately, their bright coloration makes them a target for Pokémon such as Swampert. Despite that, they remain friendly towards most Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Wild POKENAME try to maintain a tough image in order to keep themselves safe from potential predators. Thankfully, they have a powerful body that is excellent at both battling and swimming.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is said to be the guardian of the southern seas. It will give its life to protect the ocean and its creatures.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Restaurants and other shops in tropical regions often employ POKENAME to help serve clients. Customers are enamored by their vibrant appearance and impeccably professional service.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a reincarnation of the spirits of a deceased Corsola and all the coral polyps on its body. It's delighted by its new freedom of movement, and often flails about.
author: hophoppip

entry: Often mistaken for a drowning person, sailors will try to rescue this Pokémon only to be pulled into the ocean themselves. Its claws contain a paralytic venom to stop potential prey from escaping its grasp.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME seeks out the spirits of drowned sailors, guiding them to another realm. A Dhelmise aids it in locating and drawing in the spirits, sapping a small amount of life-force from each one as its payment.
author: hophoppip

entry: When happy, its coral glows in a spectrum of colors, creating a dazzling display. This vibrant glow serves as a beacon for its companions that take shelter along its body.
author: .izik

entry: Its large body serves as a home for many fish Pokémon needing shelter. As more Pokémon flock to POKENAME, its swimming becomes slowed until it shoos away the ones weighing it down.
author: chibitales

entry: Its large body serves as a home for many fish Pokémon needing shelter. As more Pokémon flock to POKENAME, its swimming becomes slowed until it shoos away the ones weighing it down.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME live by not too far from rocky bights where they get plenty of sun. Any water they intake is released as scalding liquid or steam through where a flame would be on Chimchar.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's sharp coral spikes contain a small amount of poison. While it doesn't intend to hurt others, contact with the spikes leaves the wound stinging for hours.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME tend to live far away from human civilization; sometimes, the areas they live in are even protected by Pokémon Rangers. Although they are usually found in water, they can swim towards and scale all kinds of surfaces if they must flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME assists lost divers by pointing north with the tip of its nose. To prevent its coral from deteriorating, it cannot live in polluted waters.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its head is formed out of dense coral. POKENAME patrols around underwater groups of Corsola to protect them from predators.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The duo of POKENAME patrols ocean reefs, safeguarding the coral and skewering large predators that attempt to harm it. Coral polyps grow on their prongs, migrating between them to evenly distribute the hard coral.
author: hophoppip

entry: When angered, a POKENAME will charge along the seabed, attempting to land a powerful blow with its horn. The poison carried in its horn can cause temporary paralysis, making piercing blows extremely dangerous.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME explores the ocean, seemingly never needing to eat anything. In reality, the coral branches atop its head provide its food through photosynthesis.
author: hophoppip

entry: Recent discoveries reveal that POKENAME's metal exterior is not part of its body but a shell housing its coral form. Due to climate change, it began living in abandoned diving suits to shield itself from harmful ocean conditions.
author: rakunk

entry: The ribbons on its body are actually tendrils containing stingers, used to sedate and capture prey. It gets along quite well with the sea creatures it isn't trying to consume.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME stomp around at the bottom of warm seas, forcing small sand-dwelling creatures into the water. POKENAME preys on the fish that swim over to feed on these smaller creatures.
author: fancyskunk

entry: The coral covering POKENAME's body shares many distinct traits with a long-extinct coral species. Various sea creatures take shelter on its body, with Pokémon revived from fossils taking a particular interest in it.
author: hophoppip

entry: Young POKENAME have pristine skin, free from algae buildup that occurs with age. Some trainers heavily value this clean aesthetic, and go to great lengths to preserve their POKENAME's youthful appearance.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME will anchor itself to a coral reef teeming with life for most of its existence. As the souls of the reef pass on, it collects them within the confines of its balloon body in order to keep their spirits safe.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The upper part of its body is filled with air and floats on the ocean's surface, producing energy through photosynthesis. This energy is shared with the lower part of its body, a large mass of coral deep in the ocean.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is considered to be a symbol of good luck by fishers. It is often spotted floating near the water's surface and pretending to be a buoy.
author: sivanandi

entry: POKENAME lives near secluded beaches where it protects the local wildlife. During nights of the full moon, it comes out of hiding to dance in the moonlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Clusters of POKENAME gather around sunken ships, drawn to the shelter they provide. If injured by debris in the waves, they can Recover and heal within minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in hydrothermal vents, ascending from the seabed only for mating season. A POKENAME never stops growing.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME sits near coral reefs, pretending to be part of it in order to lure in fish Pokémon to eat. It can go several weeks between meals, waiting for the perfect opportunity to strike. Despite its clunky appearance, it is quite fast underwater.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME desires to share the starry sky with the deep-sea Pokémon it grows up with. It uses its immense psychic powers to maintain its friends' habitat.
author: honestly_vitali

entry: It can dive deeper than most humans and Pokémon thanks to its hard, submarine-like shell. These deep-sea explorations help it discover hidden wonders of the ocean floor.
author: .izik

entry: The coral on its head rarely grows to full size. Because of its disproportionate body, POKENAME frequently trips and breaks its horns.
author: char_latte3412

entry: When threatened by a predator, POKENAME releases a cloud of foam to obscure its body. While it's hidden, the coral polyps on its body rapidly rearrange into the shape of a scarier Pokémon.
author: hophoppip

entry: After a rainy day, the branches atop POKENAME's head unravel, releasing bubbles into the air. This Pokémon lives by tide pools and loves to bask in the bright sun.
author: pizzarcato

entry: The jelly-like membrane on POKENAME's body possesses powerful restorative properties. If injured, it secretes a special fluid that allows it to heal itself instantly with Recover.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found in coastal cave areas, being highly active on sunny days. It hunts for small fish that typically mill near Corsola herds, snatching them from the water to drink their blood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a tricksy predator that inhabits coral reefs. Smaller Pokémon seeking shelter in the branches on its backside are quickly snapped up by its beak and consumed.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME disguise themselves as large masses of coral to lure lesser underwater Pokémon. They seem particularly fond of Mareanie and feast upon them so often that their own bodies have begun to develop toxic elements.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's bright coloring makes it stand out in murkier waters, making it struggle to sneak up on prey in dark areas. In shallow coral reefs, however, it's the perfect ambush predator.
author: sivanandi

entry: It's said POKENAME are children who have died in mishaps around the ocean. People near oceans have reported a voice luring them to jump in the water.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This kind-hearted Pokémon cares for and protects any fish Pokémon, allowing them to hide away in its seaweed from predators.
author: hypernovahusky

entry: POKENAME are only found on secluded shores in the pitch-black of night. Interestingly, they mostly spend time playing on the beach for their own enjoyment.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The bubbles that make up POKENAME's wings are filled with an odorless gas that allows it to drift effortlessly through the air. When startled, it releases a burst of this gas to change direction quickly.
author: regulavish

entry: It attaches itself to drifting icebergs, floating across frigid waters. This journey takes it to distant oceans where it establishes new reefs.
author: .izik

entry: Many POKENAME come together in order to mimic coral reefs. Any Pokémon that seek to hide in their reefs are consumed.
author: darkweavile428

entry: The flexible coral of POKENAME's tentacles regenerates even faster than its rigid branches do. When a coral branch grows long enough, POKENAME snaps it off and devours it with apparent delight.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME hides in reefs, blending in among the different colors. It also allows sea life to hide within its bunker if predators are around.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME that live in the desert store water efficiently in their hardened bodies. Their spines have become less sharp and taken on a rock-like sturdiness over time.
author: sivanandi

entry: POKENAME is a rarely seen Pokémon that dwells in warm oceans and sings in a beautiful voice. When marine biologists approach it, it guides them to areas plagued by pollution.
author: hophoppip

entry: It makes its home near piers, weaving through barnacles and pilings. The colorful reefs it maintains attract both tourists and Pokémon alike.
author: .izik

entry: When tired, POKENAME lies flat on the seafloor, resembling coral. It anchors itself by digging a claw into the sand to resist strong currents.
author: .izik

entry: It soaks up liquids into its body like a sponge, including oils and other biohazards it is not meant to digest. The most common way to cure these ailments is to give them an Antidote mixed with juice.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using its powerful psychic abilities, POKENAME defends its home by trapping intruders inside the bubbles from its staff and moving them far away. Those who continue to intrude are met with a mighty Bubble Beam barrage until they leave.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are extremely cautious, hopping between tidepools in search of the cleanest and safest waters. Seeing them in fresh water is extremely rare because they swim out to sea to try and avoid human interference or pollution.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The coral on its body can shift in color to match any background. It can remain motionless for hours or even days, kept alive by the energy its coral supplies.
author: hophoppip

entry: When exhausted from swimming, POKENAME perches atop buoys, wrapping itself in seaweed to block the harsh sunlight. If it overheats, it will drop into the water and sink to the seafloor to cool down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the calcium carbonate found in seawater to create beautiful coral reefs. Many Pokémon will come to live in these reefs and will revere POKENAME as their queen.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME make their home at the highest point of a coral reef, their rocky growths a combination of living coral and shimmering pearl. Reefs with a healthy POKENAME are said to be among the most beautiful natural wonders in the world.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The delicate coral on POKENAME's body regularly breaks off and regrows. Necklaces made from its coral are said to bring romantic feelings to the wearer.
author: .izik

entry: The coral reefs where POKENAME reside glitter like rainbows under the light, making them a popular scuba-diving spot. Some activists want to make these reefs inaccessible to the public in order to preserve them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is quick and agile, whether it's running or swimming. After being fused by a human, a POKENAME will run around excitedly for hours, likely fulfilling the dreams of the stiff-shelled Corsola.
author: hophoppip

entry: Its body is covered in hard scales made from calcium carbonate. Its preferred food is a species of plankton theorized to be the closest relative of common plankton in ancient times.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's beautiful kelp mane is a safe haven for small Pokémon. It guards colonies of Corsola, scaring off predators with its powerful bark.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lives a peaceful life on sandy beaches across Kanto. When startled, POKENAME dives underwater to hide. It can hold its breath for up to 30 minutes.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: POKENAME thrives in tropical waters, basking in the sun by raising its tentacles above the surface during the day. This behavior helps it absorb vital sunlight for its coral to grow strong.
author: .izik

entry: Its tentacles secrete acid, dissolving anything unfortunate enough to touch them. This defensive trait makes it a formidable presence in the ocean.
author: .izik

entry: Using its psychic powers, it splashes itself with water whenever it gets too dry. This curious habit keeps it refreshed even far from the shore.
author: .izik

entry: Rotting shipwrecks are its primary food source, as it breaks down the debris over time. This habit ensures the ocean floor stays clear of decaying material.
author: .izik

entry: This POKENAME grew up underwater, nestled within coral reefs. When it was caught, the coral stayed with the POKENAME and now lives on it, relying on it for sustenance.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME produces stunning blue pearls prized by jewelers for their unique matte finish. These pearls are often crafted into elegant earrings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME surrounds itself with a bubble made of a clear, poisonous liquid. This allows it to float out of water and travel alongside its Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It wishes to bring everyone into the ocean within its maw to play. It doesn't realize that anyone who enters will drown within minutes.
author: skymaster426

entry: It sifts through sand, meticulously picking out food hidden beneath the surface. This habit helps maintain the balance of life along the shoreline.
author: .izik

entry: It crushes boat hulls with ease, viewing them as obstacles to its territory. This destructive behavior has earned it a fearsome reputation among sailors.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its limited terrestrial locomotion, POKENAME loves to explore the land. It stores water for its little adventures in the bulb on its back.
author: jreposo

entry: Although many predator Pokémon initially see POKENAME as an obvious target, POKENAME has incredible speed that allows it to ensure survival. Even if caught, it may simply explode all of its contained energy to prevent itself from becoming prey.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its muscles to throw out water-powered punches. Its blows are said to land like a rapidly flowing river.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME is found near pools of sulfuric acid, idly floating above them while feeding off the fumes. Despite its habitat, the bubbles it produces don't contain any harmful chemicals.
author: lithuanian_shortstack

entry: Because of the weight of its cocooned body, POKENAME's swimming speed is rather low. It hides on the sea floor and defends itself with shots of compressed water fired from its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: The heads on POKENAME act independently of each other; when it feels threatened, they fill the surrounding area with a toxic black gas to cover its escape.
author: lithuanian_shortstack

entry: POKENAME leaps elegantly from the water before blasting airborne prey with a precise jet of water. Once the target falls into the river, it finishes them off with its sharp horn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pretends to flop helplessly on land to lure in unsuspecting small Pokémon. The moment they get close, it stuns them with a jet of water and knocks them into the river.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to form a mutualistic bond with Flying-type Pokémon where they share their food and clean one another. If the Flying-type refuses, POKENAME blasts them with water. If the Flying-type attacks, POKENAME's family intervenes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While it acts rebellious and hostile with strangers at first, POKENAME quickly warms up to them and becomes very affectionate. It prefers swimming in water over running on land.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While POKENAME itself is fearsome, standoffish, and overall difficult to get along with, it encourages its young to get along with other Pokémon. It eats a carnivorous meal and makes sure to slurp up all the fluids and juices for maximum calories.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME live in herds and tend to get aggressive over which Pokémon gets the tastiest Magikarp. These fearsome creatures hide a terrifying set of teeth, which can dig into even the hardest of shells.
author: skleegamer

entry: Cautious in the extreme, POKENAME listens for danger even while it is asleep. If it hears even the slightest disturbance, POKENAME will blast water from its mouth at high velocity to scare off potential predators.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME kept the need for water to breathe from Remoraid, but also the need for extreme sunlight from Sunkern. It lives in near constant pain whether above or below water.
author: omelhorthiagofranze

entry: POKENAME are abundant in large rivers, where they are an important food source for rare predators. Their affinity to mud keeps sediment flowing, though they are very sensitive to heavy metals and frequently get sick if there are mines upstream.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It can venture inland much farther than its pre-evolved form since the blooming bulb on its back now creates water. Its new pair of legs also helps.
author: jreposo

entry: This fusion cannot outcompete preexisting Remoraid and Corsola in the wild, failing to maintain a stable population. Once, they were captured and bred by the Johtonian Navy for use against invading vessels, but they could never remember their orders.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME fires rapid bursts of ink at flying Pokémon with uncanny precision. It aims directly for their eyes, ensuring they drop into the water where it can strike.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME's main form of offense is shooting compacted mud balls. Sometimes, hordes of them will gather on beaches to collect and eat wet sand, leaving a long trench on the shoreline.
author: glacierwing

entry: Whenever two groups of POKENAME run into each other, they will engage in a week-long conflict that only ends one side is completely annihilated.
author: falsedoll

entry: Adult POKENAME can be found lying along river banks ensuring younger POKENAME don't stray. They aren't aggressive, but they are extremely protective.
author: jreposo

entry: POKENAME swims along forest riverbeds, preferring clean, pure water. It can store a lot of water in its stomach, which it sprays at enemies with extreme precision.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME has a strategy for hunting flying prey: Striking it down with a water jet from its mouth and letting it fall onto its bladed horn.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This one seems to have an obsession with using its hand cannons to attack any Pokémon that enters its territory. Extreme caution is advised.
author: mercury_sc

entry: Legends have it that POKENAME perceives the last wishes of those who drown at sea. It seems to have grown numb to the unceasing calls for help.
author: jreposo

entry: POKENAME has copious amounts of energy, needing to be constantly moving throughout the day to burn it off before nightfall. It takes on foes to further burn off energy, often easily outmatching them with powerful jets of water shot from its mouth.
author: arcul

entry: Due to POKENAME's gentle and docile nature, it makes an ideal pet. However, it is also hunted often for its fresh, sweet taste.
author: sand_coffin

entry: It is capable of both swimming and flying. Yet, it spends most of its time gliding above the water's surface after making powerful leaps out of it.
author: jreposo

entry: Despite the popular assumption that POKENAME feeds on blood, research has proven it is incapable of harming others with its small fangs.
author: jreposo

entry: A Remoraid floats within the center of POKENAME, the body behaving similarly to its resident's instincts. The cannon on its arm can fire extremely rapid, accurate jets of water.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts slowly through seaweed beds. When it spots prey, it fires powerful jets of water to knock them out from a distance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME darts through streams to ambush prey like Magikarp with swift, piercing bites. If it spots flying prey like Pidgey, it will knock them out of the sky with a perfectly timed jet of water.
author: .izik

entry: While preferring close-ranged combat, POKENAME can fire pressurized jets of water from its claws to snipe prey from over 50 feet away. It hunts on the seafloor, mainly preying on small fish Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: It shoot water out of its finger at anything it points to. The range of these blasts have been reported to go as far as 200 meters.
author: gronkissimo

entry: Wild POKENAME tend to avoid fighting. If it knows it is being stalked by a predator, it will fire a powerful and accurate blast of water from its mouth. Only if that fails will POKENAME battle in close quarters.
author: bobosmith01

entry: An amphibious lifeform with the intelligence to craft tools made out of debris. It can hurl a spear from long distances with deadly accuracy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's twin mouths shoot powerful torrents of water at airborne Pokémon like Hoppip, sending them plummeting into the sea. Once submerged, it uses its tentacles to paralyze its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires jets of acidic ink at an extreme velocity in battle. While its accuracy hasn't been perfected, the liquid is extremely corrosive, able to melt through even rocks and metals.
author: evilgammon

entry: Many POKENAME have been found far from their natural habitat. This is because they have forgotten where they were going while attached to a Mantine.
author: gp423

entry: Its face is a rather perfect encapsulation of its skittish and timid personality. It steers clear of most anything other than its own kind, panicking and spitting ink at those that approach and startle it.
author: sk372

entry: With the body of this Pokémon being deep inside its shell, POKENAME have a limited field of view. This works to POKENAME's benefit as once it has its sights on a target, it cannot get distracted.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME burrows into mud and sand to hide from predators. It uses its right claw to blast down aerial prey with jets of water, and then drags them into its den with its left claw so it can feed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME contracts muscles in its oversized claw to launch jets of water with enough force to shatter Cloyster shells. It creates a symbiotic relationship with small fish Pokémon who will keep the claw clean and free of parasites.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The eggs shot out of its cannon hit like a tank. The orange star on its trunk symbolizes its allegiance.
author: funkytomate

entry: POKENAME's suction cups on its tail allow it to stick to the sides of coral inside of reefs when sleeping. It lets loose intermittent bubbles from its snout as it snores, creating a peaceful underwater ambiance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wraps its long tentacle-like tail around sunken freighters when it hunts, spitting out a forceful Bubble Beam to incapacitate prey like Magikarp. Its strategic use of the environment ensures a successful hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits globs of ink to disorient foes before striking with its sharp horn. The ink cloud can linger for up to an hour in calm waters.
author: .izik

entry: Though it swims at a leisurely pace, POKENAME is not to be trifled with; its many mouth tentacles can crush smaller prey with ease, and create and lob painful globs of ink at anything larger.
author: sk372

entry: On clear nights, POKENAME will beach itself to stare up at the stars for hours. If disturbed, it will do a Rapid Spin to return to the sea, seeking the comfort of its aquatic home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's suckers can conduct an immense amount of heat, leaving burns on the skin of those it attacks. When angered, its tail fire glows with a burning intensity and steam pours off of its body.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME wraps its tail around ocean buoys and flops about when disturbed. Though harmless, its sudden movement can scare off smaller Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tend to follow large ships out of a sense of precaution. Should disaster strike, they use their large body and many tentacles to hold and carry as many survivors to safety as they possibly can.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can use its unstable DNA to charge the projectiles it shoots with varying elemental power. Unfortunately, misfires often happen due to its lack of control over these elements.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME live within ocean waters, but they will spend most of their lives flying in the ocean sky. They will shoot down foes with ink-filled bubble bullets and use their tentacles to snatch prey, which they will drag into water to finish them off.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's serpentine body is mostly made up of muscle, allowing it to constrict and crush its prey with ease. It can be found inhabiting the remnants of shipwrecks.
author: mepp.

entry: The first person to witness POKENAME thought it was the scion of a timeless monster, but it is actually very gentle and curious about humans. It often helps tow grounded ships back to sea before disappearing in a cloud of ink.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME playfully sprays water from its tentacles to send itself flying in random directions, giggling if it bumps into something. When startled, it perfectly camouflages to match its surroundings and escape detection.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Combining its glowing antennae with agile tentacles, POKENAME surveys the ocean's surface. It collects garbage to help keep its territory clean.
author: .izik

entry: The suction cups on POKENAME's tentacles pulse with a yellow light before it unleashes an Ocatazooka. The light helps lure prey close enough for the attack to land with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its suction-cupped ears to cling to sewer grates near the ocean. It picks through discarded trash with its long tentacles, searching for edible scraps.
author: .izik

entry: The red body in the front works to defend the flowering body in the back while it photosynthesizes, sharing the energy between the two of them. It is said that POKENAME used to be stationed outside houses as primitive security systems.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME soup is a popular dish in some areas, its sweet, tender meat often served with parsnips and ginger. It has even made its way onto fast-food menus. POKENAME is known to scream and squirt ink in fright as it is farmed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Some Octillery will hitch rides on top of Slowking, replacing its crown. Its intelligence diminishes as a result, but it retains enough to function in tandem with its new passenger.
author: sk372

entry: The bulbous growth on the backs of POKENAME are filled with salt water. When POKENAME leave the water to feed, they use this supply to keep themselves hydrated.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The sound made by POKENAME's squirming tentacles is known to make its victims feel uneasy. When threatened, it will spray a dark cloud of ink that stains the attacker's skin for over a week.
author: mistymagius

entry: The POKENAME population has decreased due to an increased popularity in serving their delicate toxin-laced meat by experienced chefs. When it encounters danger, it sprays a cloud of ink, then puffs up inside the murky hiding spot.
author: pjporwoll

entry: If POKENAME finds styrofoam or other waste on its reef, it gathers the pieces with its tentacles. It then brings it ashore in hopes that someone will dispose of it properly.
author: .izik

entry: It braces itself in the sand or holds onto rocks with its suction cups before firing a jet of water with the power of a cannon.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: After fusing, POKENAME now sports armor plating to help its resilience in standing its ground and firing powerful ink shots at foes. There exist some records that indicate this may have once been POKENAME's natural form.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the sand, leaving only its tail exposed. It lures prey and enemies in with its rattle and catches them with its suction-cupped tail.
author: princessmilandria

entry: POKENAME uses its large mouth to create a powerful whirlpool that suctions prey in the ocean towards it. Once it has built enough energy by sleeping, it can spit streams of ink with enough force to knock even a Dragonite from the sky.
author: soup1900
