entry: POKENAME uses its extra-large mouth to create a powerful whirlpool that funnels prey in the ocean towards it. While the long mouth narrows the vortex, it also increases the strength of the suction.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is often farmed for its capability to produce ink instead of milk. The ink can be used for writing, but is also used in some recipes.
author: jaycielantern

entry: POKENAME can use their ink-jet mouths to control water around them and swim efficiently. They also use that ink to mark other Pokémon in the wild and even decorate patterns on their own bodies.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME charges the suction cups on its tentacles with electricity to paralyze prey once captured. Its spongy fur is commonly used to make padding for diving suits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Referred to by many as 'Sea Demons', POKENAME are cold, calculated killers of the water. If a Pokémon encounters one, it is immediately grabbed and devoured in what seems like an instant.
author: jangodiot

entry: Coated over POKENAME's body is dozens of tentacles. It fights by first delivering powerful kicks to knock their opponent down, then finishing the battle with a swift tentacle whip.
author: typhloquil

entry: The plants growing on the backs of POKENAME are able to sense the world around them. When threatened, they spit volleys of high-velocity seeds at their aggressors.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It uses its flexible neck to take perfect aim, shooting down even high-flying Pokémon. Remoraid flock to it, eager for both food and lessons.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME can store and expel absolutely massive torrents of ink for defense. A single POKENAME could fill multiple swimming pools with ink and still not have depleted half of its stored contents.
author: sk372

entry: Many works of fiction use imagery similar to POKENAME to depict evil deities. There is some historical records that some island civilizations made offerings to it in the past to ensure safe travels across the oceans.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dreams in a deep slumber on the seafloor. When disturbed, it secures itself to surrounding surfaces with its suction cups and ring, following this up with a devastating blast from its snout that can tear through tank armor.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME will anchor itself with its suction cups on the ground underneath. It does this so that it will be steady when it fires torrential barrages of ink or water at its enemies.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: On the rare occasion of large scale territorial disputes between Pokémon, POKENAME will allow others to aim its powerful cannon-like mouth to great effect. Many intelligent Pokémon seek to ally themselves with POKENAME for this very reason.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The earthquakes summoned by wild POKENAME deep underwater have been known to cause tsunamis. These Pokémon are hunted for sport in Kanto and Johto.
author: theartemis1

entry: The earthquakes summoned by wild POKENAME deep underwater have been known to cause tsunamis. These Pokémon are hunted for sport in Kanto and Johto.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME sprays powerful jets of ink from the suckers on its arms powerful enough to pierce through thick logs. Each POKENAME has their own unique ink pigment that they use to distinguish each other's territory.
author: mistymagius

entry: Wild POKENAME make their nests within beachside caves. Their tentacles allow them to easily cling to walls and ceilings as they fire electrified bubble-bullets at their prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME gathers flotsam and jetsam from shoreline trash, looping items that interest it on its tentacles until it finds something more interesting. It occasionally snatches up Remoraid to blast beachgoers holding items it covets.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hides under a rubbery disguise, but cannot find enough material for a full set of tentacles, so its own shadowy appendages complete the ruse. It is intensely curious about new objects and will try to show them to others to become friends.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Utilizing discarded items in the ocean, POKENAME creates a disguise resembling a tiny tank with arms. It tries to garner sympathetic attention by exterminating overly aggressive Pokémon in tidal pools or on beaches.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When bouncing on land, POKENAME uses the large suction cups on its tentacles to drag people and Pokémon along. It will then bounce into the water to drag them below the surface, using the water to assist in its movement.
author: .izik

entry: After luring in a foe with a beautiful song, it uses its tentacles to latch onto its prey. Once attached, it never lets go.
author: mrpeach774

entry: POKENAME are found in the ocean depths, and in high numbers around sunken ships. When attacked, it sprays the predator with a bioluminescent ink that attracts even larger predators while POKENAME escapes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can't move, which is why they are in constant fear of predators. However, nothing actually preys on POKENAME because of their spikes.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME rolls down the beach, leaving strange trails in the sand. On warm days, the beach is filled with these tracks.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME twists and releases its tentacles, giving it propulsion and allowing it to glide leisurely through the water with little energy expenditure.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can twist its tentacles into together to build up tension. When it releases them, it can cover long distances quickly thanks to the force.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can twist its tentacles into each other and build up tension. When it releases them, it can cover long distances quickly thanks to the resulting force.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME nests along shoals and near strong currents or whirlpools as defense mechanisms against powerful predators. It blasts gooey ink at prey to blind them before dragging them into these dangerous areas to prevent escape.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hides within its mane of tentacles, which are covered in venomous spikes. It peeks out from this cover to blast targets with water from its snout, including its Trainer if it feels playful.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's tentacles are covered in a toxic mucus, sickening predators that eat them so that they leave it alone in the future. The tiny core body can regenerate its lost limbs, leading to adventurous chefs experimenting with its tentacles in dishes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME bites at driftwood and floating debris, hoping to uncover food hidden among the waste. It has a strong jaw for breaking apart trash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fights using any tactics to win, including coating its claws in ink to blind foes and grappling them in its tentacles and claws until they are crushed. It clouds the water with ink to get the jump on an opponent.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The water at the tip of POKENAME's tail is boiling hot. When it is angry, the water turns into steam, which may cause third-degree burns if touched.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Tales state that a couple's portrait painted with POKENAME's ink will cement their relationship forever. Tourists clamor to coastal towns to buy vials of this ink for high costs, believing it to be a symbol of lasting love.
author: .izik

entry: It's advisable to give POKENAME a wide berth for safety; at any moment, it may experience a migraine that causes it to lose control of its bodily functions and spew ink all around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in the ocean but has no control over how it moves, getting taken with the current. Whenever a predator or prey gets too close, it can manipulate psychic energy to push them away or bring them closer, causing its tentacles to throb.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives in the ocean but has no control over how it moves, getting taken with the current. Whenever a predator or prey gets too close, it can manipulate psychic energy to push them away or bring them closer, causing its eyes to glow red.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives in the ocean but has no control over how it moves, getting taken with the current. Whenever a predator or prey gets too close, it can manipulate psychic energy by blowing into a clarinet to push them away or bring them closer.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's many tentacles are brutally powerful. With strong suckers scattered across them, escaping POKENAME's grip is extremely difficult. Foes who run are targeted with powerful ranged attacks.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will use its tentacles to travel over land when its habitat becomes unsafe. It spends most of its time squeezed into small discarded items like potion bottles or Shellder shells.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its tentacles to ensnare prey before spraying ink to obscure its escape. Once it has fed, POKENAME squeezes into a tight location covered by its bell to sleep.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It attacks prey by using odd moves from its facial orifice. POKENAME is sluggish and conserves energy by staying still; in the wild, it only about fires 5 moves a day. If it misses all of them, it goes into slumber to try again another day.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sticks to the sides of icebergs with the suction cups on its tentacle-like fins when resting. The cold environment helps it maintain its energy as it awaits its next meal.
author: .izik

entry: If a predator attempts to pry open an POKENAME shell, it will be met with a torrent of ink and water, launching POKENAME far into the distance.
author: .fedoraman

entry: While Octillery loves occupying abandoned shells, this is not one such case. POKENAME can remove its spike and throw it with great dexterity.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The suction cups on POKENAME's claws aid in traversing the steep coastal cliffs and aquatic drop-offs it encounters in the wild. It will expel copious amounts of foam from its snout to disguise the entrance to its den.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's tough, crown-shaped ridge on its head keeps it from being able to squeeze fully through tight spots to escape predators. Instead, it incorporates the shed shells of crustacean Pokémon into armor for offense and defense.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses the bundle on its back to store seeds it uses for nutrients. These seeds are able to grow in the snowy forests where it lives.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are often annoyed due to being constantly picked up by humans mistaking them for ornaments during winter holidays. Each time they're touched, they also explode, launching away any food they were carrying, adding on to their grumpiness.
author: soup1900

entry: People have to be wary of grabbing star-patterned ornaments during winter holidays due to them potentially being a POKENAME instead. It has to be really careful to not explode if this happens; otherwise, it may destroy the food it was carrying.
author: soup1900

entry: If POKENAME hits a bump while rolling, it explodes and scatters the food it was carrying everywhere. It typically hangs off of trees like tree ornaments, but its large size often causes it to slip off and explode upon landing.
author: soup1900

entry: The moment it sees snow, it sings carols for hours, despite the songs being off-key and wordless. Its relentless enthusiasm can either charm or annoy listeners.
author: .izik

entry: When wild POKENAME come of age and are no longer protected by others, they live a self-imposed lonely life away from others deep in mountain caverns. Despite this, they become overjoyed when given a gift and always go above and beyond to reciprocate.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME whacks an object with the bone it always carries around, the object's surface becomes covered in twinkling frost and snow. If it was given love and care as a Delibone, it tends to take in any lost or abandoned Pokémon to raise them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME whacks an object with the bone it always carries around, the object's surface becomes covered in twinkling frost and snow. If it was given love and care as a Delibone, it tends to take in any lost or abandoned Pokémon to raise them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It keeps small ice sculptures hidden in its tail, offering them as gifts. Each sculpture is unique, crafted with surprising detail and care.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can shoot lightning and frost from its fists, which discourages dangerous Pokémon from picking fights with it. During certain holidays, it always has a present for everyone, even Trainers or Pokémon that are mean to it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live on secluded mountain slopes, curiously following visiting explorers. They are fascinated by shiny rocks, collecting them in their tails.
author: mepp.

entry: A gluttonous Pokémon that takes any food it sees. However, it will also give rare Berries to any house it passes. It is beloved by farmers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flies around icy mountains. If it sees someone lost, it will fly them to safety and give them some food. Its feathers are surprisingly soft and warm.
author: crazynaturekitty

entry: POKENAME appears during terrible snowstorms to eat and store the violent weather in their crop. Later it will deliver the weather to its nest to keep its home covered in permafrost.
author: rockageddon

entry: POKENAME's jolly disposition brings a sense of wintry joy to all who meet them. The cane on their head sometimes gets stuck on trees.
author: pankiwi

entry: It enjoys prancing around snowy forest floors, waving its head around with a jolly glee. The plant on its head leaves a fragrance of pine in the air.
author: pankiwi

entry: The buds surrounding its neck will glow when POKENAME is filled with joy. It uses the plant on its head to attract potential mates.
author: pankiwi

entry: The ruffles around its neck depict a snowflake pattern. The aroma it gives off is said to remind people of joyful times with family.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME are ambitious delivery birds used to send small packets to the coldest of regions. POKENAME will try to deliver anything they can lift if they are not stopped.
author: rockageddon

entry: POKENAME delegates the task of giving gifts to other Delibird, but still helps out whenever they can. Some of the presents they offer have bites taken out of them, but children do not seem to mind.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will sit in a tall tree at night, watching for prey. After a long night of hunting, it spends the morning sharing its spoils with other Pokémon.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME are even better at flying than unfused Crobat since they always carry a heavy sack everywhere they go. Their silent flying allows them to quickly share food with even the most violent Pokémon before darting away.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME gives presents to particularly nice Pokémon and seems to always be in a jovial mood. It rarely stays in one place for long and flies between towns and cities to spread happiness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often hand out game cartridges as presents so that children can play on handheld devices. They also charge the devices by rubbing it against their cheeks so that children can jump into their new game right away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are cheerful little fusions. They have a fascination with evergreen trees and are often found hanging from their branches.
author: howlingstarr

entry: Trainers must take care to rein in their POKENAME. Eager to break its delivery record, they will overshoot their delivery, losing time instead of saving it.
author: rockageddon

entry: If someone's holiday isn't going well, POKENAME will attempt to lighten the mood. It will even be in place of the tree if there isn't one.
author: birchbot

entry: It makes its home in pine trees and is said to tell whether someone is "naughty or nice" with a single glance. This ability makes it a fascinating figure in local folklore.
author: .izik

entry: It manipulates icy winds to carry itself across long distances. This ability allows it to travel effortlessly through snowy landscapes.
author: .izik

entry: Because its body naturally drifts upward, POKENAME keeps small stones tucked into its tail to help stay near the ground. As it grows, these stones are gradually replaced.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME swing from branch to branch delivering gifts to Pokémon high above the ground. They can easily swap the gift bag between their three hands, making it nearly impossible to steal from them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If it plays too much, it can accidentally create snowstorms. These unintentional blizzards make it both endearing and troublesome.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to collect shiny objects and fill their bags with them. Once a year they fly around the region to distribute them to both young Trainers and Pokémon.
author: ghiragar

entry: POKENAME's bag is filled with such large quantities of Bead Mail, Fab Mail, and Harbor Mail that it struggles to carry them all. It refuses to give any of the mail away, even to its Trainer or closest companions.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME has a holly plant on its back in order to protect its seeds it carries in its bag from predators. The berries are said to be toxic.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME are foragers with a sweet tooth, sneaking into homes undetected to steal as many baked goods as they can. They have a selfish yet noble spirit, stealing gifts from others for those they have wronged and starting a vicious cycle.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME hangs in trees, dropping in front of passersby to give gifts to them. If the recipient refuses the gift, POKENAME may explode in frustration.
author: lemmymaster

entry: POKENAME is known for its jolly demeanour and the sweet scent it gives off, which lures others in during winter months. Despite its harmless look, it can deliver a surprisingly strong headbutt when startled.
author: eiskitsune

entry: Due to POKENAME's short body, it will be unable to fly if it carries too much food in its tail. Although it lives in cold places, snow will cause it to fly clumsily and even crash into the ground.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are full of small toys that they hand out to children. Sometimes their gifts are covered in Berry Juice, but children are often so excited to get a gift that they do not seem to mind.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It crafts toys from twigs and gives them to others as gifts. These handmade toys are cherished by both Pokémon and people.
author: .izik

entry: It can redirect snow and sharpen the flakes into razor-like edges. This ability makes it both a guardian and a fearsome opponent.
author: .izik

entry: Deliveries are sacred to POKENAME. Anyone that tries to steal deliveries will be mercilessly attacked for weeks. Package thieves are never safe, as POKENAME never forgets a face.
author: rockageddon

entry: The snowy-white beard of POKENAME and their red fur have caused multiple incidents where children report an injured Delibird and try to get help. Nowadays children are told that the Delibird are sleeping so they respectfully leave POKENAME alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon has an insatiable love for cinnamon, seeking it out wherever it goes. It is aware that humans keep this spice, which often leads it to human settlements.
author: .izik

entry: It fiercely guards its present, refusing to part with it under any circumstances. This defensive nature makes it difficult to steal from.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often closely entwined in human communities and show great pleasure in joining in festivities. End-of-year celebrations are a special favourite, and they will give gifts to young children that approach the water's edge.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite an unfused Delibird's generous nature, a Delibird double fusion is grumpy and mean. It only delivers coal, not gifts.
author: valtsuri

entry: It uses its sharp wings to carve ice sculptures of those it cares about. These creations keep it company when it feels lonely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gallop through forests and mountains to ensure that people living in remote places of the world get presents. All they ask for in return is a few snacks and a pat on their antlers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shoots erratic sparks from its palms, still learning how to control its electrical powers. It enjoys giving gifts to other Pokémon, even if the gifts are small.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A wild POKENAME will spend large amounts of time waddling around looking for the perfect place to nest. Researchers believe it prefers cool, slightly damp, and quiet spots near water, preferably in caves.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME is stern but affectionate. Being in the presence of the grateful and the giving causes the star on its chest to glow. The rude and deceitful being near, however, causes POKENAME to rampage.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME offers the two bags it carries to passersby, letting them choose which to accept a gift from. In one it carries entertaining trinkets, and in the other only useless junk, so every offering is a gamble.
author: sk372

entry: Those who have been overly cruel to others are said to risk being haunted by POKENAME. It comes in the dead of night, its cold whispering cry said to gift those it haunts with horrendous nightmares, as retribution for the anguish they've caused.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME happily hands out gifts from its bag, but it only allows itself to be the one to handle said bag. Anything that tries to touch it will be in for a nasty zap from its bolt-shaped tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries the food it collects throughout the day in its portable sack. They are seen most often in snowy or mountainous regions.
author: theartemis1

entry: This immature Pokémon tries to give out food to anyone it meets, but it has usually eaten most of the gifts by that time.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can unleash lightning storms and blizzards to protect its friends. Every holiday winter season, it gives gifts to everyone it can because it wants to inspire people to be their best selves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It delights in gathering berries and other fruits to give as presents. These thoughtful offerings make it beloved among both Pokémon and people.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels through snowy villages, shooting icy water at people so they drop anything they carry. It stores its prizes in its sack-like tail, making it a tricky and resourceful thief.
author: .izik

entry: This generous Pokémon likes to please others with small gifts. It would usually give one a drawing or a colorful clay craft as a present.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME enjoys giving presents to everyone around it. Sometimes it's too enthusiastic and can accidentally shower someone with gifts to death.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME can sense negative emotions within the hearts of others. If someone feels sad, POKENAME can find a perfect gift for them in its bag.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME spends around nine or ten months seemingly frozen in ice. When autumn rolls around, POKENAME will begin thawing out and singing.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME will do anything in its power to make its Trainer happy with a gift they wish for. It's strong enough to carry a bag twice as big as itself.
author: milchik

entry: Bound to a festive ornament, POKENAME is thought to be a collection of 108 different wishes made by children. It strives to grant these wishes by performing good deeds.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Tales of the one who delivers gifts at the holidays describe POKENAME as his assistants. As the stories go, this Pokémon can sense the auras of children to determine who is naughty or nice.
author: sk372

entry: The seeds it carries have now grown into festive snacks which it gives away to smaller Pokémon in the forest. The scent of holly surrounds them.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME enjoys the act of giving and sharing, but has no tolerance for greedy individuals and thieves. Anyone trying to take from another in its vicinity will be sent flying with a swing of its full bag of gifts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME arrive at places that have recently experienced natural disasters to give out gifts of warm clothes. The warm clothes often have a misprint on them, but that is a minor inconvenience compared to the lifesaving utility of the clothes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On dire winter nights, a POKENAME may appear right before a miracle happens. Believing POKENAME to be a savior, people will shower them with gifts, but POKENAME gives all their gifts to less fortunate and unfairly treated Pokémon like Absol instead.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: Urban legend says POKENAME chases down naughty children and Pokémon at night to stuff into its bag, which transports them into the spirit realm. At the end of the night, it empties the entire bag into the maw on its stomach to devour the victims.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a feared reputation of appearing in blizzards and kidnapping people. In truth, it rescues lost travelers in snow storms and provides for them until it is safe to continue their journey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME celebrates winter holiday festivals in remote towns and villages across the world, spreading joy and goodwill. It never remains in one place for long, making it nearly impossible to study.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Nutmeg is its favorite food, and it hoards as much of it as it can find. The spice seems to enhance its already festive nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in areas that frequently drop below freezing. When they spot a struggling traveler, they share warm and delicious treats with them. However, how POKENAME produces such desserts is not known.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Snow, wind and fog mean nothing to this Pokémon: it will trek through any condition in order to help someone it knows is in need. POKENAME vanishes into the night with an icy fog after giving assistance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon marches across icy terrain delivering Mech Mail in temperatures that would freeze steel. Its metallic body keeps each parcel insulated and intact during long-distance routes.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Wild POKENAME have been observed using their portable sack to steal various items from children. They are regarded as villains in holiday tales.
author: theartemis1

entry: Wild POKENAME have been observed using their portable sack to steal various items from children. They are regarded as villains in holiday tales.
author: theartemis1

entry: Wild POKENAME have been observed stealing various items from children. They are regarded as villains in holiday tales.
author: theartemis1

entry: Parents tell stories of POKENAME stealing away naughty children at night, trapping them in a world of merciless cold. In reality, POKENAME is rather amicable, but will play along to help scare misbehaving children straight.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME scamper through the snow to deliver the gift of warmth. Most of the presents they bring involve warm clothes, such as scarves, jackets, or sweaters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It makes its home on icebergs, drifting across frigid seas. These floating islands serve as both a shelter and playground for it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will return lost keys to their owners, only after it decides if they are nice or not. If not it will promptly throw them into the nearest hole.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME dash through the snow to deliver warm and cozy clothes to children. It is said that if a child pets one of their tails, they are blessed with years of good luck.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Known for its remarkable woodworking talent, POKENAME creates festive wooden statues around the holidays. Many young craftsmen seek its partnership to refine their skills and prosper.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: This Pokémon is often found giving food to starving children. Its flame burns with sympathy for the hungry.
author: notsaying.

entry: Trainers that don't pay attention to POKENAME will discover that toys tend to disappear around this Pokémon. Experts are not sure if the Pokémon likes to steal to make children cry or if it is a case of kleptomania.
author: rockageddon

entry: It constantly produces snow-like material inside its bubble that leaves it cold to the touch. POKENAME enjoys being held by others in need of cooling down, cooing softly as it shares its temperature.
author: sk372

entry: It collects gemstones from caves and gives them out to humans that it trusts. People used to sell these stones for astronomically high prices, so ever since, gemstones given out by POKENAME are worth much less than their original value.
author: jangodiot

entry: Once a year, POKENAME looks for children nearby to visit and bring gifts. Well-behaved and pure-hearted kids get glistening gems, while naughty children get coal and, in extreme cases, brimstone.
author: epping_forest

entry: Folklore warns that upsetting this Pokémon may result in an avalanche. The threat ensures it is treated with respect and caution.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME freezes objects near its den with icy breath, then offers them to nearby Pokémon. The gifts are often strange, but always cold.
author: .izik

entry: When it shakes its horns, a pleasant scent of pine sap fills the air. This fragrant aroma calms both allies and opponents alike.
author: .izik

entry: It holds out its bag with closed eyes, hoping someone will offer it a gift. If it receives one, it runs away delighted, carrying the present with joy.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is composed of the hundreds of toys and gifts that have been thrown away over the years, along with other substances. It will try to clean off the grime of one of the objects in its body and present it to someone who needs cheering up.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The bauble on its horn can hypnotize foes with rhythmic movements. Once mesmerized, enemies are easy to outmaneuver.
author: .izik

entry: Commonly known as the Birthday Bird, this Pokémon loves to surprise people and Pokémon with confetti presents. If it spots a party, it will always try to sneak away with a piece of cake.
author: rockageddon

entry: Urban legend says POKENAME will break off the black stones on its body and gift them to naughty children. The message this conveys to them is unclear.
author: iaobug

entry: POKENAME loves its present dearly and will fall into despair if it is damaged or stolen. If you give a grieving POKENAME a new present, however, it will treat you with the same affection as before.
author: mistymagius

entry: It can spit out an icy mist capable of freezing anything it touches. This frosty breath makes it a formidable opponent in cold environments.
author: .izik

entry: It has a curious habit of stealing items from one town only to gift them to another. This behavior leaves both towns confused, yet strangely grateful.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to sing festival carols while they deliver gifts. Many people and Pokémon sing along whenever they are around, as these carols are full of nostalgic joy from the past.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The nostalgic joy of the past comes through the hymns that POKENAME sing, reminding people to be kind to one another during the holidays. Even soldiers have been known to sing along, as POKENAME have facilitated many ceasefires.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rarely appears during winter season, singing all sorts of tunes that bring to mind holiday cheer and festivity. Rarely, it may sing more melancholic and longing tunes. If one tries to catch it, it may shift in appearance and flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rarely appears in secluded places around the world during the late parts of the year, bringing Berries and other small gifts. It seems to draw energy from the happiness of others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is most often spotted during snowy seasons, performing dances and miming ancient folk plays with other Pokémon. Endowed with incredible leadership and charisma, it can easily convince even rival Pokémon to work together to spread cheer to others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are light on their feet and can dance while giving out presents. Their fluid movements inspire many children to pick up dancing as a hobby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME has only ever been seen in the wild by a handful of people, it is largely dismissed as a myth. Nonetheless, it is often featured in holiday decorations.
author: ludacriswell

entry: The snow globe on POKENAME's back contains thousands of poisonous spores. If it breaks, the released spores can cause frostbite and shortness of breath.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: In the coldest reaches of Kalos, POKENAME is revered by small villages. Using a candy cane wand, it ensures heating fires stay lit, while pulling necessary food from its bag. Other regions have taken to using this Pokémon for Search and Rescue.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When water is splashed on POKENAME's shell, hot steam is produced. In cold regions, it is used in traditional saunas.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's round, icy body is filled with a cotton-like material that swirls inside like a snow globe when it moves. When it shakes itself, it releases a subtle pumpkin scent into the air.
author: .izik

entry: During cold snaps, POKENAME are often found pressed against doors and windows of homes. They desperately cling to any surface where they can feel warmth escaping from inside.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The fiery tip of POKENAME's tail is frozen solid and it leaves snowflake-shaped prints on the ground where it walks. Its beard is made of packed snow.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME give out many presents to children around the world, but they are often overwhelmed by the sheer number of presents they need to keep track of. Whenever they make a mistake, the added stress leads them to get a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its tail is packed with candy canes, which it throws with precision in battle. These sweet projectiles are both festive and surprisingly effective.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soar through the sky searching for children who need warm sweaters, scarves, and mittens. Their large size can be frightening to some children, so they employ the help of Charmander to help them give out the warm clothing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swims in cold rivers in search of food along the shore. It stores extra in its bag to share with other POKENAME.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Their bundles are actually detachable from their tails, as they use their actual tails for swimming at high speeds. They collect seashells and rocks.
author: pankiwi

entry: Its blazing speed makes it a favorite for carrying Orange Mail between distant mountain towns. The heat radiating from its mane sometimes singes the letters it delivers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The tip of its tail is extremely heavy, and it swings it like a maul. This makes it a surprisingly formidable fighter when needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME search for seashells, pearls, and other fun trinkets on the beach to give out to children. They can be found swimming to remote islands to ensure festive cheer reaches even the most remote places.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can separate itself into three pieces that roll through the streets searching for lost change. It then gathers the coins and leaves them on the doorsteps of those it believes are in need.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME seeks out a stalk sturdy enough to hold its large bundle of food. It travels across the land sharing or trading its food with Trainers and Pokémon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Sometimes POKENAME opts to carry a light stick for quicker travel. Even though it packs a light bundle of food, it is still no less generous with what it has and offers food freely to Trainers and Pokémon alike.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are most commonly encountered by people during festive celebrations, showing up with gifts in their beaks to give to celebrants. One head loves to give food and money, the other has a tendency to give coal and other stones.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It prefers to make its den within icebergs. Using its beak, it will chip off the ice in large chunks to dig out a home.
author: .izik

entry: Chefs prize its horn, which is said to taste like peppermint when properly prepared. This rare ingredient adds a refreshing twist to culinary dishes.
author: .izik

entry: The slime coating its body is intensely sweet, so much so that licking it can cause tongue pain. Despite its sweetness, few dare to try it twice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's blasters shoot out small gifts and confetti for small Pokémon to enjoy. The patterns on its shell depict various festive scenes.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME's present is surprisingly durable, able to withstand blows from a sledgehammer with relative ease. It dislikes people trying to unwrap its present, so it tries to hide away during the holidays.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its bag is filled with shiny trinkets it finds and wishes to share. Deep-sea divers hope to run across POKENAME during their dives, as it could potentially gift something very profitable.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a popular subject of winter photography. However, it is an extremely dangerous Pokémon, and several photographers are injured every year.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is a sociable Pokémon that stomps leisurely across the seabed, sheltering small Water Pokémon in its head outgrowths.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is a sociable Pokémon that stomps leisurely across the seabed, sheltering small Water Pokémon in its head outgrowths.
author: chorb33

entry: This Pokémon's surfing style looks awfully groovy. POKENAME has precise control in its leg muscles to direct its board, deftly navigating even the choppiest of waves.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME spits bubbles while jumping out of water, using them to stay airborne as long as possible. The bubbles also help cushion its landings should it land on a hard surface.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME sleeps by clinging tightly to coral using its tail. Marine researchers often deploy POKENAME near reefs as POKENAME can naturally filter toxins and sediments from the water.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is most often found in tropical waters near coral reefs. It feels a strong protective instinct towards Corsola species, defending them from any threats that swim by.
author: sk372

entry: Occasionally, small creatures will make POKENAME's back their home. POKENAME quickly grows protective and attached to them, and defends them with a ferocity not often seen in most Lapras fusions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME does not like sharing its hunting grounds with other Pokémon. It digs its fins and its claw-like legs into the sand, causing ripples to reveal or eject any hidden predators, then fends them off with Rock Slide.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: With its wings, POKENAME can swim effortlessly underwater, keeping watch for nearby threats. Its venom is harvested to create potent antidotes that protect countless lives annually.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are docile creatures that make nests made of scattered stones at the bottom of shallow waters. If another Pokémon threatens their territory, they simply find another place to make their home.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's antennae release a thick, sweet mucus that attracts Remoraid. These Remoraid stay near its nest, protecting it from predators while it slumbers peacefully.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefer to make their home in colorful coral reefs and dance for other Pokémon in the area, seemingly for no benefit of their own self. Their grace even during turbulent waters has caused humans to compare them to mythical water nymphs.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are reluctant to engage in battle and much more likely to sit and endure hits rather than dish them out. They have a fondness for treasure.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME possess a very genteel nature. They scoff at Pokémon battles and showcase their talents elsewhere, such as in hospitality and entertainment.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME swim as schools of hundreds. They use the algae growing on their head to glide over the sea by rotating them at high speed.
author: ayner

entry: POKENAME's gills fold in the water, making them more streamlined and able to cut through it efficiently. They play with other Water Pokémon as they swim, having races and bubble-blowing competitions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite their brutish bravado, POKENAME are rather loath to do battle. However, they will try their best if belly rubs are promised afterwards.
author: rooboid

entry: Despite their brutish bravado, POKENAME are rather loath to do battle. However, they will try their best if belly rubs are promised afterwards.
author: rooboid

entry: When POKENAME sees a threat, like Sharpedo, it bounces on the water's surface, inhaling air to make itself appear bigger. This defense mechanism helps intimidate potential attackers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps in coral reefs until it gets bored, gliding across the surface of the water to the next one. Its low attention span makes it difficult for it to stay in one place for long.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can jump up to twice as high above the ocean as Mantine, riding the winds to stay aloft for longer. Its wings allow larger Pokémon to swim alongside it for protection.
author: chibitales

entry: Its long ears function as fins, allowing it to ride ocean currents with ease. Using its tusks, POKENAME digs into the seafloor in search of food or treasures to carry back to its den.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The small, curious POKENAME lives half of its life in water and half on land. It feeds on aquatic vegetation and may blow bubbles when it's well-fed.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME's body is home to an assortment of small, aquatic Pokémon. When it grows in size, it will learn to feed off the power of its inhabitants.
author: rooboid

entry: Powered by an aquatic ecosystem within its body, POKENAME tears through the waves at a wicked pace. Its wings cut like blades; remorseless and fierce.
author: rooboid

entry: It is a seaside Pokémon whose tail flutters in the breeze. Some historians suggest that the image of its tail gliding high in the sky with the wind inspired the designs of the first kites.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its manta-shaped tail like a surfboard, riding turbulent waves with expert skill. It can absorb the power of lightning and channel it into even bolder stunts, earning the admiration of many sea creatures that gather to watch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME happily jumps out of the water alongside yachts, enjoying the spray and the attention it garners. It is often seen playing near the coastline in the presence of boats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its manta-shaped tail like a surfboard, riding turbulent waves with expert skill. It can absorb the power of lightning and channel it into even bolder stunts, earning the admiration of many sea creatures that gather to watch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: What appears to be a surfboard is actually part of a POKENAME's body. They have excellent immune systems and can survive through other kinds of illnesses other Pokémon can not, even if their habitat were to suddenly change.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Commonly found off the Alolan coast, POKENAME surf with other POKENAME and Mantine for sport. The one who performs the most tricks on the waters is deemed the leader of their squadron.
author: teatedtiten

entry: By changing the leaves on their tails, POKENAME adjust their speed when swimming. POKENAME are very friendly to passing Trainers, frequently offering them help across the seas.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME love to jump in puddles after a rainy day. Each one sports a unique dorsal fin pattern.
author: weirdtux

entry: Witnessing a POKENAME leap from the water is said to be a once-in-a-lifetime occurrence that signifies good luck for one month.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Some say a POKENAME is created when a Mantine and its Remoraid passenger pass away simultaneously. The ghostly spirit steers swimmers away from dangerous waters, and has saved many divers from ill fates.
author: sk372

entry: Despite having the ability to walk on land, POKENAME usually stay in the water for most of their lives. They burrow under the sandy seafloor to hide from potential predators, and even allow smaller Pokémon such as Remoraid to hide underneath them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is not uncommon for POKENAME's dorsal fin to be confused with Sharpedo's from a distance when it breaks over the water's surface. Despite that, POKENAME is friendly and will curiously swim up to nearby ships.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME prefers to hunt in the water as opposed to sand-swimming Garchomp. Cutting through the strongest currents, it can swim at break-neck speeds.
author: chiari_queen

entry: POKENAME's body consists mostly of cartilage and soft tissue, with few bones. For most of history, its fossils were mistakenly attributed to Lapras.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME is a very fast swimmer despite its bulk. It travels onto shore to lays its eggs and will guard the nest with its life.
author: snescontroller

entry: Groups of POKENAME were used during the ZERO-ONE's aquatic testing phases. They are valued for their strength and their mother-like care for anything struggling to swim.
author: .izik

entry: It swims through the deep ocean gracefully. Many Pokémon ride in its mouth for protection and safety.
author: imagine1.

entry: This Pokémon dreams of one day becoming a stalwart and heroic protector of the ocean. It dons a stylish cape to better embody this ideal.
author: regula

entry: POKENAME delights in doing evil acts, though most of its actions are inconvenient pranks at worst. It possesses a strange aversion to sea sponges and starfish, for unknown reasons.
author: sk372

entry: Like Manitar, POKENAME's stomach is host to a plethora of aquatic Pokémon. This ecosystem sustains itself and breaks down the food that POKENAME eats.
author: rooboid

entry: Like Manitar, POKENAME's stomach is host to a plethora of aquatic Pokémon. This ecosystem sustains itself and breaks down the food that POKENAME eats.
author: rooboid

entry: Schools of POKENAME can be seen floating aimlessly in the skies, especially on sunny days. It is considered a good omen to see a POKENAME, so many tourists take pictures of them before they float away, and no one knows where they go.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME accumulate electricity in their shells before releasing strings of shocking bubbles. Sometimes, they discharge the energy through their fins to skim across the ocean's surface.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME covers itself in slime to be able to glide across the ocean surface. It is able to bounce itself back into the ocean if beached.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME allows schools of Remoraid to cling to its chain as they transport them across the ocean. However, this makes them favored targets for larger predators.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its flexible wings are used for both swimming and flying, making it a highly adaptable Pokémon. Despite this, POKENAME isn't often used as a ride Pokémon due to its fickle and stubborn behaviour when met with anyone who hasn't earned its respect.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME rolls on the surface of the water, sometimes doing an odd bouncing motion to play with others in its pod. This playful behavior is a common sight among the Orange Islands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is made of rock, unlike Aron, who boasts a thick coat of steel armor. Because of this, POKENAME doesn't rust when it dives underwater.
author: rooboid

entry: Small, aquatic Pokémon live within the cracks of POKENAME's shell. Eventually, it will capitalise on this symbiotic relationship to gain power.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME float by popular beaches like buoys, warding tourists away from deep water. They're famous for their warbling singing voices and smooth skin.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME float by popular beaches like buoys, warding tourists away from deep water. They're famous for their warbling singing voices and smooth skin.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME spits high-pressure water if stepped on, using it as a defense mechanism. The force of the water can knock back even the strongest foes that dare approach it.
author: .izik

entry: This Oddish fusion can be found in the ocean. Species of Remoraid like to seek shelter from predators in its leaves.
author: uncookie

entry: POKENAME can glide out of the water for short distances to catch prey. They are also known to play with swimmers and latch onto boats for long rides.
author: totodile.

entry: Despite cutting a fearsome visage, POKENAME is very kind and docile, patrolling Sharpedo-infested waters to keep humans safe. It sometimes adopts young Carvanha and raises them to be equally even-tempered.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME sees a smaller friend in danger, it will shield them from harm by putting them in its bubble.
author: uncookie

entry: POKENAME are usually passive and caring, using their bubbles to shield friends. However, if necessary, it will use its bubbles to trap or stun foes.
author: uncookie

entry: During the day, POKENAME can be seen swimming near boats. In the evening, POKENAME will attach itself to the underside of a vessel and drain the life force of any nearby Pokémon, such as Quagsire, who are prone to bumping into boat hulls.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's antennae on its head attract prey, which it then ensnares with poisonous ink. The ink quickly subdues the prey, making it easy for POKENAME to catch and consume.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fins contain potent venom that can cause someone to fall unconscious in under five minutes. This venom acts quickly, making POKENAME a dangerous predator in its domain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attempts to build up as much speed as possible by swimming along a strong current in the ocean. When it has reached peak velocity it will spring out of the water into the air, performing an impressive dive bomb to subdue its foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME uses psychic powers to propel itself further than normal when jumping from waves. This allows it to leap higher and longer, making it an agile and elusive swimmer.
author: .izik

entry: Often spotted within coastline swamps, this unusual Pokémon resembles a flat-capped mushroom and feeds on rotten plants. Its gaze is soulless.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME glides just above the ocean surface for long distances. When tired, it lands on rocks and aims its lily pad toward the sun to recharge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to keep itself underground and away from the sun, as its skin dries out easily, causing it to weaken. Schools of POKENAME will congregate on rainy days and seemingly surf through the mud together for sport.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It is said that the water POKENAME spits out can be drunk to cure heartbreak, but in reality, it causes mild seizures. It uses this water to deter predators while it swims away.
author: .izik

entry: The mouths on its "head-antennae" constantly spout out water to make the ground it burrows through as muddy as possible. Doing this helps the Remoraid that accompany it to swim through the muddy water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Plagued by chronic headaches, POKENAME will resort to swimming to help relax itself. Intense migraines can compel POKENAME to swim in a trance-like manner, with some POKENAME being able to psychically dissipate storms so that it can swim unimpeded.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is commonly seen aiding lifeguards around the world. Quick on land and even quicker in the water, it can locate and retrieve a person in danger with the greatest haste.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME can be seen soaring above snowy trees with a flurry of snowflakes behind them. Rarely are they seen carrying their young.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME communicates with members of its family by blinking its lights. Scientists have found that each POKENAME has its own name.
author: .fedoraman

entry: After much effort and patience from both parties, linguists have decoded how POKENAME use their lights to communicate. It turns out that many wish to join humans in games of water polo.
author: .fedoraman

entry: An entire school of Remoraid can live attached to POKENAME's 80 tentacles. POKENAME will crush and ensnare any Pokémon who pose a threat to its symbiotic friends.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: This unique fusion has combined four species at once. A Remoraid and Shellder have fused to feed off of POKENAME's excess energy while they drive off pests POKENAME can't see coming in an example of mutualism.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Made mostly of greywater, POKENAME is not safe to swim in. Though surfers are tempted to ride its waves, those who fall in often end up sick for days.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Made mostly of greywater, POKENAME is not safe to swim in. Though surfers are tempted to ride its waves, those who fall in often end up sick for days.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Rounded by the flow of freshwater currents, the body of POKENAME shines in the summer sun, attracting small aquatic Pokémon to make their homes there.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME can be found in tropical seas, slithering amongst the coral reefs. Entire schools of Remoraid will swim alongside it, hoping for food scraps.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME cares very deeply for its adopted Remoraid. The Remoraid sometimes hypnotize other Pokémon by accident when playing with its pendulum.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME makes its home in shipwrecks, carefully watching nearby Remoraid to determine if the area is safe from predators. Its keen observation skills ensure it stays out of harm's way.
author: .izik

entry: The metal alloy in POKENAME's wings is strengthened as it consumes tree roots. Its metal feathers were harvested and used in constructing the prototype of the ZERO-ONE.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scavenges up a Skarmory skull for defense and some shed metal feathers for offense. It scrapes its feather blade against the skull to make a screeching noise that disorients predators.
author: sk372

entry: It trains its fists by destroying abandoned buildings. When one POKENAME challenges another, their metallic strikes won't stop until one is down.
author: mistershaokahn

entry: It protects its egg with its life, despite the fact that the egg is nearly unbreakable. Despite having wings, it cannot fly.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME can swim with surprising grace and travel in any direction regardless of which way it is facing. Since it also has a tough outer shell, it is not often targeted by predators.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME cuts through rivers with a steel dorsal fin that breaches the surface like a blade. It swims fast enough to appear blurred beneath the waves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME moves by quickly rotating its body like a propeller. It's very dangerous to approach in this state, as its bladed edges are capable of shredding nearly anything in its path.
author: mepp.

entry: When enraged, POKENAME's steel horns glow red hot. Its tails thrash wildly as it soars over savannahs, burning off fury in high-speed flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are too heavy to let it fly, instead used primarily as threat displays. The tips of each feather also contain a mild amount of toxins, should its warning go unheeded.
author: sk372

entry: Despite a heavy metal body making prolonged flight difficult, POKENAME is a surprisingly agile glider. It dives after prey and crashes into them forcefully,  before cutting at them with the sharp edges of its wings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's scales harden and grow stronger with each molt, making its hide resistant to many attacks. It defends itself by bashing threats with its steel helmet.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME can be found in forests in snowy areas of any region. Their swordsmanship is enough to overwhelm a Gallade and their poison is quite potent.
author: patch_bros

entry: When enraged, POKENAME releases flames from its back as an expression of its emotions. If the temperature rises too high, its steel body begins to glow bright red.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When enraged, POKENAME releases flames from its back as an expression of its emotions. If the temperature rises too high, its steel body begins to glow bright red.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in small flocks within large cities, feeding on iron scavenged from junkyards and abandoned buildings. Its metallic feathers allow it to strike with powerful wing blows that can trouble even larger Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME let out a piercing shriek whenever they are hurt, drawing the attention of their parents. Their metallic wings protect them from poisonous spores that fill their natural habitat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME soars through the skies in constant search of a battle, targeting the weaker opponents. With its powerful jaws, it tears its victims apart.
author: astrael1

entry: A truly aggressive Pokémon, it attacks anyone who dares enter its territory on sight, striking mercilessly with its steel feathers. It feeds on iron found on buildings, and is often seen chewing on gutters or TV antennas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME release a shrill cry whenever they find food and cooperate with others of their kind to take down large targets. They also care for their siblings, shielding them from fiery attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generate electricity by flapping their wings to create a static charge around themselves. Once they touch something that conducts electricity, they discharge all the energy into that point and create a burst of sparks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stands at the top of sunny mesas and uses its polished body to reflect sunlight into the eyes of small Pokémon below. Once the target has been blinded, POKENAME swoops down to finish off its prey with its sharp wings.
author: .realthree

entry: Electric charges from POKENAME's wool travel up its wings, letting it discharge bolts of lightning with strong flaps. It has a strong-willed personality, so few are allowed to shear its wool.
author: sk372

entry: It's said that a single beat of its majestic steel wings can bring down a small building. Since it requires a large amount of iron to stay strong, it's often employed to dispose of metal waste and help keep cities clean.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fiercely protect their offspring by brandishing their sharp wings. They slaughter bug Pokémon with their jagged talons and share their meal with members of their flock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tries to lure in its prey by letting out a serene smell. It then lures it to a cave to feed it to its young.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Wild POKENAME have lost the ability to fly and live on the ground, making large nests on the riverside. When unfurled, their razor-sharp wings are used to dig small trenches around their nest, and they attack anything that enters.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Wild POKENAME have lost the ability to fly and live on the ground, but dedicated Trainers can teach them this skill. When unfurled, their razor-sharp wings are used to dig small trenches around their nest, and they attack anything that enters.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Should an intruder approach POKENAME's territory, it will raise its arms and emit a cry of intimidation. Whether or not the intruder flees, POKENAME won't do anything else after its display.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have bodies of pure metal that are as light as feathers, keeping them safe as they dive for berries and nuts at rapid speeds. They are often drawn to shiny objects, including the shed feathers of their own kind.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is often seen gliding on warm updrafts high in the sky. When it spots prey, it plummets to the ground feet-first, trapping it between its talons.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: It sleeps on the sides of cliffs. A biodegradable substance somewhat similar to mercury leaks from its tail when it hunts. When two POKENAME fight, their cries reverberate throughout the area.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Their short wings are not well developed for flying. They communicate by scraping their steel feathers together in different patterns.
author: rhysanthemum

entry: POKENAME sheds its steel shell once or twice in its lifetime. Other creatures will often repurpose its leftover molts as armor.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME's metal coating is frigid to the touch. It moves faster in hailstorms, slicing through the storm with practiced precision.
author: .izik

entry: Thicker steel shields POKENAME's arms, allowing it to block heavy blows. Because of that combined with its wings, it deflects most attacks with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits molten metal at intruders nearing its nest. This can cause deep burns that deter predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long metallic beak to unleash powerful strikes capable of piercing through solid rock. The iron feathers that fall from its wings are often used as building materials for new homes in large cities.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a dangerous apex predator that hunts other bird Pokémon. It rams into its prey with its sharp, serrated feathers to knock them out of the air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its thick fur is made of thousands of sharp metal shards, making it incredibly hazardous to touch. It sheds these shards frequently, making them a good source of iron for metalsmiths.
author: mistymagius

entry: Since it constantly craves iron, it chews on the anchors of ships docked at harbors. It's a remarkably resilient creature, able to survive in both warm and cold waters.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It swiftly swims through the sea, cutting the water with its sleek, pointed metallic body. POKENAME is a skilled sharpshooter and can fire water projectiles with pinpoint accuracy even from great distances, stunning its opponents.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME anchors itself to any surface with its steel tentacles, keeping stable while firing powerful projectiles from its oblong beak. Its armored body and hostile temperament drive most marine Pokémon away from the territory it claims as its own.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME like to hang around post offices and act as loyal guards. Their blades also act as box cutters for hard-to-open boxes.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME is considered the terror of the skies: when it takes flight, its wings produce a metallic roar that sends other Flying-type Pokémon fleeing. It is a ferocious creature that brings down its prey with devastating blows from its steel beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is considered the terror of the skies: when it takes flight, its wings produce a metallic roar that sends other Flying-type Pokémon fleeing. It is a ferocious creature that brings down its prey with devastating blows from its steel beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It scrapes together the steel feathers adorning its coils to freeze its enemies' blood with fear. When a prey lowers its guard, POKENAME lunges forward in an instant to weaken it with its venomous bite.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body is made of a lightweight yet durable metal. When rolling at high speeds, it uses its winglike ears to control its trajectory.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's body is made of rustproof metal plates that exude deadly venom. In anger, it raises the crimson spikes on its back and grinds its coils, releasing piercing shrieks that unsettle anyone nearby.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rapidly flap their wings to create electricity. They were once trained to shock and disable electronic devices but now help people charge car batteries at many car shops.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is said that POKENAME appears after certain rituals are performed, though such rumors have never been confirmed. The metal plates on its cloak rattle, creating eerie sounds as it flies through the night.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses the toughness of its steel feathers to overpower nearby Honchkrow, seizing not only their territory but also their underlings. Its broad wings let it fly for long periods, and their edges are sharp enough to slice through solid stone.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME have murderous intent and can be quite violent. Be very careful if you meet it in the wild.
author: krune

entry: As it is very young, POKENAME does not know how to be paternal and throws its stone at others who annoy it.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME were once utilized by the military to overcharge and explode electronic devices. Nowadays they flap their wings to generate electricity for car shops, where there are many batteries for them to charge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are highly social Pokémon that form numerous tribes throughout the Ice Mountains. They spend their free time grooming each other's coats, ensuring that every claw, tail, and frill is sharp enough to cut through solid rock.
author: turron_turron

entry: According to all laws of aviation, there is no way that POKENAME can take flight. Its wings are too small to get its thick metal body off the ground.
author: its_cher_bicth

entry: POKENAME rolls into a defensive ball when threatened, deflecting most attacks with its resilient armor plating. If near a cliff, it may even curl up and roll away from danger, as its metal carapace will remain undamaged.
author: pjporwoll

entry: By flapping its steel wings fast enough, POKENAME creates a high-pitched screech that stuns and disorients prey. At top speed, POKENAME creates sonic booms that can shatter glass as it flies past.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME clings motionlessly to mountain crags, watching for prey, which it descends upon with incredible speed and incapacitate with its claws and tail blade. It is employed by gangs to blend in with gargoyles and buildings as territory guardians.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The earliest recorded cases of POKENAME date back to the Kalos War. The metal plating along its body was made so it could be ridden into battle.
author: patch_bros

entry: Its wing blades are so sharp that it fells trees as it flies. The jungles POKENAME live in never grow beyond a certain height as a result.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is known to seek the deep places of the world. It will tunnel to the mantle, where its armor partially melts to heal its wounds only to crystallize stronger than ever. Ancient members of this species are known to be stronger than steel.
author: mindrivet

entry: POKENAME are masters of graceful combat, effortlessly dancing through the air with high-flying kicks. They seem to enjoy sharpening and polishing their steely feathers when not fighting.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME are a marvel to watch in battle, as the species strikes with the grace and poise of a dancer. Elegant but pragmatic, they aim for pressure points to end conflict swiftly.
author: xillo

entry: When flocks of Skarmory get in territorial tussles, POKENAME descends from the heavens. Getting in between the feuding parties, it declares judgments with its scepter and ensures obedience with razor sharp bladed wings.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The body of POKENAME is covered with plates of pure steel that protect its vital areas, including the head. The red metal spikes on its back are infused with a potent toxin that poisons anyone pierced by them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's metal claws are soaked in a deadly venom. When it dives at its foes with its wide steel wings, it always aims to poison them to gain the upper hand during the fight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME delivers crushing bites in battle, with its jaw strong enough to crush stone. Its wings are also incredibly powerful, creating gusts of wind as it flies and flaps, knocking weaker Pokémon to the floor.
author: evilgammon

entry: Its metallic body is far too heavy for flight, so POKENAME uses its iron wings to hurl itself forward when charging. A single strike of its massive iron tail can topple towering trees.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When using Ghost-type attacks, POKENAME's silver armor glows deep red. During this time, it lets out a haunting chirp that echoes unnaturally through the air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is made of a rare metal not seen naturally on this world. The red feathers of its wings can detach and act independently of itself in order to better defend itself from those who would try to harm it.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME's metal body is incredibly hollow despite how sturdy it is, allowing this Pokémon to float through the air with every leap. Their small wings are mostly used by them to emit Screeches that immobilize prey.
author: infinex21

entry: Its steel body propels it through water at supersonic speed, cleaving through any obstacle in its path. POKENAME is a fearsome fighter that combines the brutal force of its iron wings with powerful jets of water fired from its beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME cuts through the ocean with blinding speed, its metal wings slicing water and rock alike. It launches bursts of water from its beak to obliterate almost any obstacle ahead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's fan of steel feather blades can fly like a bird. Its fallen feathers are easily made into knives.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's two blades are made of a steel material that stays sharp no matter how many battles it fights. It scrapes its blades together to create an intimidating and ear-splitting screech to make its foes cower before it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live only in the cleanest, purest waters so as to keep their metallic bodies as clean as possible. They regularly churn fierce torrents to forcefully polish their metal bodies, otherwise they can easily rust.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME only respect the most skilled of Trainers. Records show they fought alongside humans in wars long passed.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME keeps its metallic body so well-polished that it appears like a mirror. This reflection often shows Pokémon that aren't really there.
author: epolybius

entry: Its ribbons are made of a metal alloy that is both lightweight and incredibly sharp, allowing it to slice through its opponents with ease. However, the ribbons will start to rust away if exposed to water for too long.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hunt after thieves and criminals. They unleash flurries of sharp, ruby petals to cause painful lacerations against those who flee from justice.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have become the biggest pests at metal recycling plants. As they grow they add layers to their armor, hardening the already dense steel. When confronted, they run incredibly fast, bounding over any obstacles.
author: ghostslythe

entry: They say these Krookodile fusions have turned over a new leaf, working as security for many businesses. No rule-breaking escapes their gaze.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: Completely blind, POKENAME squawks to echo-locate through caves. Once it senses movement, it lashes out with blade-like wings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME builds extravagant structures out of wood and metal, using its sharp feathers to effortlessly cut them to its liking. Its work has inspired many projects by professional architects.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its razor-sharp wings to swiftly maneuver around its foes, dealing precise slashes in the process. It has yet to master long-term flight, however.
author: theartemis1

entry: Each gear has a specific purpose. One gear controls the legs, and the other slices foes with its single wing.
author: cait_sith

entry: To keep safe before they evolve, POKENAME may disguise themselves as other bird-like Pokémon. However, they sometimes find themselves adopted into unaware nests.
author: epolybius

entry: Its body is made entirely of sturdy metal plates that shield it from stronger Pokémon. During the cold months, POKENAME must rest on a bed of burning coals to keep itself from freezing up and becoming unable to move.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Metallic bulbs bloom on POKENAME's wings, each releasing a sweet Iapapa Berry scent. It uses the fragrance to lure unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: Clusters of thin metallic, cotton-like vines wrap POKENAME's lower body like armor. They insulate it from harsh winds and storms as it flies with incredible agility.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a dead Skarmory possessed by a Yamask. It can't fly, which is why you can hear POKENAME coming from a distance by the metal scraping against the floor.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME's iron tusks are capable of tearing through train cars. Its strikes leave long, molten scars across whatever they hit.
author: .izik

entry: While sleeping in caves, POKENAME wraps itself in its silver alloy wings. This reflective shield protects it from ambush by predators or rivals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME threatens travelers with its sharp steel feather. If they don't carry gems with them, they just leave disappointed without stealing anything.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME rolls at extreme speeds, its body encased in steel. At peak momentum, it can skip across water like a stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts for prey along mountainous areas, keeping its eyes out for food at all times. Its sharp, metallic fangs are strong enough to easily break boulders.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME usually swims near the surface, keeping its metal crown above the water to trick attackers. While it's meant to scare off threats, most Pokémon are just left wondering why a Skarmory is casually swimming in the ocean.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME fights even when its metallic pectoral fins and teeth become damaged since both grow back. It will chew through sunken ships because the ingested metals speed up this regeneration.
author: pjporwoll

entry: With its powerful wings and razor-sharp claws, POKENAME makes short work of prey and foe alike. When angry, POKENAME lets loose a rock-shattering roar rivaling that of a jet engine.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME's cloud-like feathers are made of steel wool, which is highly resistant to attacks. It will store scrap metal in its wool so it can repair its blades when they get damaged.
author: mistymagius

entry: A coating of mercury drips constantly from POKENAME's armor. As it slinks through canyons, the toxic trail it leaves behind can scar the ground for years.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's metal tentacles secrete a thin, clear poison that induces intense migraines. Even brief contact can leave victims dizzy for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME specializes in close-quarter combat, grappling with its powerful arms, slashing with its sharp wings, and pecking with its beak. It trains deep in the mountains.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME bursts from the water with a flash of metal and scales. Moisture makes its body shine brilliantly, dazzling prey and rivals alike.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME is hard to notice, being so small, it poses a danger to casual hikers. When it runs by in a flash, it uses the blades in its ears to score a long slash in one's legs.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME spends most of its days sharpening its feathers on the sandstone of its native desert. If attacked, it employs hit-and-run tactics, needling the foe's health with well-placed feather kunai.
author: ghostslythe

entry: As it flies, POKENAME sheds old iron scales from its wings, releasing a toxic rusty dust that poisons all who breathe it. It roams the forests only at night in search of prey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME floats without motion, its shell hardened and silver-coated. As the sun sets, it drifts silently toward prey, never blinking or breaking its gaze.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME streaks across the sky glowing a soft pink. Spotting several in one evening is believed to bring prosperity and good fortune.
author: .izik

entry: Its razor-sharp metal feathers are used to fiercely take on opponents. When the flame on its tail flares up, its steel skin grows red-hot and can burn anything it touches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body is made of polished silver that was once harvested for high-end jewelry. Some engagement rings still shimmer with scales said to come from its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are infamous pets of poachers because they are easy to train for the task. Poachers train them to disable endangered Pokémon by biting on the nape of the neck, leaving many valuable parts intact.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are at the center of controversy because of their affiliation with poachers. They are known to enjoy eating cuts of meat from endangered Pokémon, which makes them less desirable to many Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are baffled by their metallic body and often accidentally hurt Pokémon that they want to hug with their sharp edges. If another Pokémon refuses their apology, their intense groveling can be a headache to deal with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The teetering motions of POKENAME give them the appearance that they are dancing. These random movements are dangerous because their sharp wings can accidentally cut people or Pokémon that come too close.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its coils are covered in metal plates, so it no longer fears the sharp claws of its rival Zangoose. When POKENAME is about to bite with its venomous fangs, it vibrates the red crest behind its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body consists of a durable, waterproof metal that never rusts. Because of this, they have been nearly hunted to extinction.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME calms down by punching metal plates. If its fists aren't enough, it will tear them apart thanks to its sharp beak.
author: fouguri

entry: POKENAME's legendary iron armor is considered to be sacred by blacksmiths because it never seems to rust. The armor is also very lightweight, allowing POKENAME to dash and glide at very high speeds.
author: soup1900

entry: The steel plates covering its body like an armor aren't just for protection; thanks to their aerodynamic, bladed design, POKENAME can fly at incredible speeds and strike with even more powerful Flying-type attacks.
author: fiordaliso
