entry: POKENAME live in swarms in the jungle and are extremely territorial. If their nest is approached, they will fiercely attack, using their large tree-like stingers to inflict venom onto their perceived threat.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: What was once a lush bush on its back soon began burning. The sticks on its back burn forever; it has to be careful not to burn down its jungle home.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME's skin is sensitive to sunlight and dries out quickly when out of water. To counter this, it raises its large tail to shade itself. The tip is very sharp, so when in the water, it uses it like a spear to hunt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: While it lives in the tropical forests, it is usually found above the treetops. It enjoys the sun so much that one may hear POKENAME chirp while they explore the jungle. It uses its ability to predict the future to keep itself safe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The patterns on POKENAME's body are used for camouflage in the jungle. However, its bright yellow flower is quite visible, and as such, POKENAME is also skilled at defending itself.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the rainforest soil, staying close to the roots of trees. It uses vibrations sensed through said roots to locate intruders, tunneling up from beneath them to attack.
author: sk372

entry: It carefully harvests rare berries from the jungle, using them to create a delightfully tasty juice. They are often found in cafés making this drink.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The ooze from POKENAME's shell causes nearby plant life to burn away into ash. However, it is also mixed with extremely powerful nutrients; in time, the areas POKENAME previously eviscerated will grow back more lush than before.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are the terrors of the skies with seed-like feathers sharp enough to pierce thick tree bark. The orbs upon their backs harness sunlight that they will release as potent Solarbeams with frightening precision.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are silent hunters, the rattle of their tails blending in with the sound of leaves rustling in the wind. They expertly navigate the underbrush, only being seen when they strike their prey.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME sprint through dense forests in the dead of night. The only thing rarer than seeing them in person is seeing them stop their relentless trek through the wilderness. Despite their unreal speed, they travel while staying perfectly silent.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME are brought inside during the winter months because of their festive appearance. Once spring comes and they lose their festive colors, they are returned to the outside world.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It gathers shiny objects to decorate the evergreen frond on its head, taking great pride in this process of adornment. If a decoration falls off its frond and shatters, it may cry over the loss.
author: hophoppip

entry: The baubles on the body of POKENAME jingle with a certain festive ring. Many families bring them inside during the winter months out of a jolly spirit, keeping them warm while they celebrate.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many families keep POKENAME in lieu of a tree inside their homes to make cleanup easier. The baubles on their body have a festive jingle that is pleasant to listen to.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At home in humid Hoenn jungles, POKENAME flares its head crest to appear larger to foes and to cool off. When threatened, it runs fast enough to skim on top of water. If cornered, it shocks the enemy with an icy cold punch.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Though small, POKENAME are quite powerful and have exceptional dexterity. Their boundless energy leads them to often recklessly charge into battle.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME protects jungles from lightning by letting itself get struck. This doesn't hurt the Pokémon, however; instead, it stores this energy in the seeds on its back. It can use this energy to launch its tail at blindingly fast speeds.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME protects jungles from lightning by letting itself get struck. This doesn't hurt the Pokémon, however; instead, it stores this energy in the seeds on its back. It can use this energy to launch its tail at blindingly fast speeds.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp arm blades to cut down bushes and twigs for nesting material. It is agile both on land and in the water.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's bushy skirt is the perfect place for small woodland Pokémon to hide beneath when seeking safe shelter. It fiercely protects those that take refuge beneath it, repelling predators with powerful leaf storms and psychic blasts.
author: sk372

entry: Its immense weight means POKENAME accidentally tramples the forests and jungles it travels through. Treedums come along to reseed the trampled lands.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME prevents Bidoof from cutting down more trees than they actually need for their dams, and it often ends up arguing with them. Since it loves Peach Berries, it stores a huge supply of them in its den.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The seed pod on its back grows throughout its life. Upon death, the seed pod will burst, creating an incredibly lush area of flora.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME hunts in the jungle's rivers, where its seedpods allow the growth of lush aquatic flora. It can be tracked by following the path of plants it leaves behind.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME uses its brightly colored feathers to confuse and disorient foes. Ancient people often used POKENAME's feathers in ceremonial clothing.
author: kokoria_

entry: Smaller Pokémon often seek refuge within the canopies of the trees that grow from the backs of these Pokémon. While they do not seem to mind this, they will not tolerate troublemakers and shall go so far as to shed their trees to be rid of them.
author: infinex21

entry: With its ability to grow seeds and prune plants, POKENAME cares for the forest's flora. With its additional blades, it is its vicious defender.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's leaf-like plating is a durable as steel. They are also sharp enough to cut large trees, which they destroy to mark their territory.
author: mistymagius

entry: It flies swiftly over hot deserts in search of food. POKENAME have special lenses covering their eyes to protect them from sandstorms.
author: kingnekogamingyt_ttv

entry: POKENAME live at the bottom of jungle rivers, quietly slinking along the riverbed. It very rarely emerges to the surface where its body and leaves shimmer, which is why it has been dubbed as one of the most beautiful Pokémon of the jungle.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Miles below the ocean surface, POKENAME seeds lush undersea vegetation. Its home is the center of a deep-water forest so vast that none but it have managed to navigate through.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to fly endlessly in the ozone layer. It has only been seen descending when humans have attempted to fell an ancient jungle tree.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME uses its power to control time to grow large trees and plants in a matter of minutes. Entire forests have sprouted overnight due to this Pokémon.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME ambushes prey from the treetops, sinking its teeth in to inflict harsh wounds. If one of its targets tries to escape, it will relentlessly pursue them with astonishing speed.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME keep forests healthy by chopping down trees they deem necessary and nurturing young saplings. They are highly praised by rangers for their forest management skills.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME can spit out its sharp insides with great speed, impaling anything it hits. Unfortunate Pokémon hit by this will then be consumed.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is the apex predator of the jungle. With its astounding speed, it soars across the treetops and swoops down on unsuspecting prey.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME takes great care of all the trees in its territory. It shows no remorse to those who despoil nature, burning them with vengeful flames.
author: mepp.

entry: After an asteroid landed in the jungle, POKENAME emerged. It is able to alter its genetic structure to adapt to the harsh climate and catch prey.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen outside of winter. When it is spotted, Delibird and Stantler are often found in its wake, attracted by the rich nectar that forms on its leaves.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: A POKENAME's age can be determined by its tail. The flame will gradually burn down like a candle, the Pokémon passing once it's completely gone.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME climbs up to tree canopies every week to find the sharpest leaves it can hold in its mouth, which it uses to hunt weaker prey. POKENAME is also known to use its bulky tail to defend itself from predators while fleeing.
author: aurange

entry: POKENAME will cut branches off strong, healthy trees and graft branches from other trees onto them. This practice of grafting allows the trees to produce larger and tastier fruits.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Only found in dense tropical rainforests, it seeds and grows poisonous flora so its territory better suits itself. The yellow balls on its body can be detached and dropped in an emergency, releasing a cloud of highly concentrated poisonous gas.
author: snileaf

entry: POKENAME lived in primeval jungles over 100 million years ago. Its powerful jaws are capable of ripping through steel plates with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: Known as the King of the Jungle, POKENAME stomp around their territories, roaring loudly to assert their presence. Their strong jaws can split a thick tree in two.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is a very territorial Pokémon. Using its ears, POKENAME can detect an intruder on the other side of its forest and hunt them down in seconds.
author: alphamerican

entry: POKENAME leaves behind a thick slimy substance wherever it goes, which often grows moss within the jungle. It gets picked on for seeming soft and squishy, but in reality POKENAME has sharp claws and a powerful tail in which to defend itself.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: All the light POKENAME has absorbed led to a rapid rate of photosynthesis. This caused its body to sprout lush vegetation, able to be used as leaf blades in battle or expand into large, verdant wings to fly with.
author: evilgammon

entry: Once it finds a tree with delicious fruit, POKENAME claims it as its own. It drives off those who would steal from its tree via a terribly grating noise made from rubbing its tail across the scale on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grows chains of seed pods, which it will regularly shed and grow flora wherever it goes. These plants are often very rigid and sturdy, and were harvested in the past to create weapons.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is quite aggressive and fights off potential threats with its razor-sharp claws. The flame on its tail burns brighter the angrier it gets.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: POKENAME fills its pouch with water as a safe, fun space to care for baby Pokémon while others of its colony hunt for food. If a predator approaches, POKENAME shields the young and fires sharp leaves from its tail to drive away the threat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME attract lightning, which often sets the trees it resides in on fire. It can often be found searching for a new tree in frustration.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: It lives in extinct volcanos where no magma is left, but still causes them to erupt in a unique way. Instead of lava, the volcanos it resides in will spew out large yellow seedpods, which split on impact with the ground and grow lush areas of flora.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The fruit that grows on POKENAME's body has a bitter taste. They are used in traditional medicine as a remedy for stomach aches.
author: mepp.

entry: The oil extracted from POKENAME's seeds is primarily used for cooking, noted for its delicate fruity undertones. Long ago, this delicious oil was used in supposed “love potions”.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME uses its sucker mouth to stick to the side of trees. When prey walks below, it will release its grip and fall on top of it, sinking in its fangs to deliver a fatal shock.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME flies high in the sky, looking for vulnerable prey on the ground. When it spots something, it dives at incredible speed and snatches it up with its claws. It's quite skilled at using its bushy tail in combat.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: POKENAME loses a lot of the agility it could have had as an unfused Sceptile in exchange for unrivaled strength and a much larger body. They are often found defending small Pokémon against all manner of threats.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME can often be found in cafés serving as efficient waiters, able to carry double the amount of drinks as a human. Forgetting to tip this Pokémon may flare up its fighting spirit and result in a hard punch to the face.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is constantly seen setting fire to random things it comes across in the woods. Fortunately, POKENAME's flames are too weak to cause anything but slight discomfort.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME is a very resourceful species of Bug-type Pokémon. It uses the crest on the tip of its head to absorb sunlight to boost its otherwise mediocre Fire-type moves.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME can rarely be seen buzzing about warm areas, eagerly awaiting evolution as they con tourists out of their food with their adorable antics.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME is popular with young women due to its affectionate nature, warm body, and bright colors. When it evolves, its fighting style changes dramatically depending on who raised it and how they raised it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can sleep through even a mighty blizzard thanks to it always being warm. To cool off, POKENAME shakes its feathers until they fall off; POKENAME is naturally so warm that it doesn't even need them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's shed skin retains a strong warmth, and a spicy taste to it. While the spice is too strong for most, several strains of Fire-type Pokémon enjoy it as a treat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's thick fur radiates warmth in cold months. It lines its nest with the shed fluff to insulate and protect its Eggs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME only have a weak poison and rely primarily on mimicry to protect themselves from predators. Their abdomen mimics the appearance of Torchic, relying on the resemblance to the fiery Pokémon to ward away danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME toasts seeds as it eats them, but some become trapped in its gizzard, where they react with a gel it produces, creating a rich smoky flavour. These “ember pearls” are prized delicacies, leading to overhunting of wild POKENAME.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It playfully pranks people by floating by while invisible and rubbing its body against others, startling them when they suddenly feel something unnaturally warm and feathery rubbing against them.
author: sk372

entry: The rear head of POKENAME spews fire far hotter than the front. It occasionally unleashes these flames behind itself to boost its speed.
author: .izik

entry: Very protective of its territory, POKENAME flies around with others to find insects to eat. Multiple POKENAME will unleash a loud cry before using their internal flame sacs to launch fireballs if threatened.
author: sakuraneko

entry: It gathers Berries, corn, and spices to store inside its shell. The heat and acid within the shell simmer the mixture into a warm drink perfect for winter.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME dislikes staying still, no matter the environment, and they especially love the outdoors. Incredibly intelligent, they will light small fires to keep themselves warm on chilly nights.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME molts copious amounts of feathers during summertime. These feathers stay eternally warm, so companies have profited from them by making pillows stuffed with POKENAME feathers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stores its tepid body heat beneath a layer of fur to keep warm in winter. If it smells something delicious, it trudges through the snow to find the source.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its metallic armor heats up whenever it gets excited, reaching a maximum temperature of over 500 degrees Fahrenheit. Because of this, it lives in badlands without plant matter that it could accidentally ignite.
author: staghorn

entry: Its entire body radiates warmth, causing many smaller Pokémon to flock close to it during cold seasons. It flicks embers from the orbs in its antlers to protect it and the little ones it shelters.
author: sk372

entry: The fire it makes is blazingly hot. POKENAME has trouble expelling it with enough speed, however, so it will wrap opponents in its coils before torching them with a concentrated blast.
author: glacierwing

entry: Though unable to produce milk of its own, many farms in colder regions import a few POKENAME. Due to their constant warmth, the farms' Miltank flock to it and stay comfortable during the frigid seasons.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's eggs are highly praised for their nutritional value, making them the perfect choice for a hearty breakfast. It gives off a gentle warmth from its feathers to help incubate its eggs.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon hates water and hides in caves with its flock to wait out any rain. Bored POKENAME play with their fire while waiting, but their lack of experience sometimes causes a large fireball, setting themselves and their kin ablaze.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME has a powerful digestive system that can easily incinerate anything it cannot digest. Although POKENAME will eat almost anything, a diverse diet is needed to keep their plumage looking bright.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has a powerful digestive system that can easily incinerate anything it cannot digest. Although POKENAME will eat almost anything, a diverse diet is needed to keep their plumage looking bright.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME loves to eat eggs and will raid other Pokémon's nests to steal them. However, it only likes cooked eggs, so it will roast them with its fire breath before consumption.
author: mistymagius

entry: Before POKENAME plants the seeds on its back, it sets them ablaze to burn off the protective shells. In the weeks before new seeds grow from its back, POKENAME's resplendent tail becomes even more golden and fluffy.
author: .realthree

entry: The excessive energy from fusion has burned off most of its feathers. However, its three remaining feathers now burn as hot as an industrial blowtorch.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are affectionate and curious, their warm personalities making them ideal companions in cold climates. The heat radiating from their small bodies helps ward off the chill, bringing comfort to those around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: What looks like an egg is really a rock POKENAME carries within its water-filled blossom for unknown reasons. If you replace the rock with an egg, it's hard boiled within seconds.
author: sontyp

entry: The shell on its back is actually the one it hatched from, melted onto its back from the heat of its warm belly. POKENAME emits enough heat to make most things it touches melt. It uses this molten material to strengthen its shell.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME cheekily taunts anyone it deems weaker than itself. With that said, it doesn't hesitate to take on stronger foes, too.
author: .realthree

entry: Its club may look like delicious roast meat, but it is actually a tough lump of rust. It tempts gluttonous Pokémon with the prospect of a free meal, then knocks them out cold.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME hatch in clutches and will imprint on the first Pokémon they see. They follow and protect their supposed parent with great enthusiasm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME appears in people's dreams on hot summer nights. Witnesses cannot agree as to whether it acts as a villain or a hero in their dreams.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME relies on its tail as a substitute for its lack of arms. After achieving victory in battle, POKENAME will slap its Trainer's hand with its tail in celebration.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME release an aura that is brimming with eagerness and determination. They never back down from a challenge, even against larger opponents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Hoenn Pokémon Professors initially considered POKENAME to be an appropriate starter Pokémon for new trainers thanks to its docility and quick evolution. Unfortunately it is also very difficult to motivate and will sleep entire days away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The seeds stored within POKENAME's body are highly flammable, causing them to instantly combust when struck with enough force. To gather more seeds, POKENAME burns small plants to collect the leftover seeds.
author: mistymagius

entry: It becomes inactive during winter, preferring to stay buried in the dirt. The heat and energy POKENAME provides to nearby plants makes sure they can unexpectedly flourish even in the cold.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is quite popular amongst young children, giving them nice warm hugs. While generally harmless, the strange markings on its beak tend to unnerve many people.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is energetic and excitable, enjoying walks alongside its Trainer. Raising a POKENAME requires a lot of commitment due to its need for exercise to remain at a healthy weight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's long legs allow it to keep an eye out for danger in its grassland habitat. When POKENAME sees a threat, it alerts the flock by noisily banging its stick on the ground.
author: mepp.

entry: The oversized talon that POKENAME wields snatches heat out of the air and gathers it into a flame. If there's not enough heat in the air, it can't produce a fire.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives in nests near ponds, making good friends with the other Water Pokémon nearby. When stressed, POKENAME shoots boiling water from its beak in a tantrum.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME is commonly kept on farms because it persistently attacks predators that approach the barnyard. However, its aggressive demeanor often leads it to be a nuisance to the farmers.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME gathers in small groups after sunset, using shared body heat to endure cold nights. Its warmth is so comforting that Trainers frequently keep it close while resting.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: It uses its beak to dig and stir the ground in search of hidden seeds or berries to feed on. When POKENAME gets angry, it emits small bursts of fire from the hump on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can produce both regular flames and strange bluish flames that are freezing cold in temperature. It has poor control over which type of flames it creates.
author: hophoppip

entry: While it sleeps, POKENAME's body heats to over two hundred degrees, causing small grass fires. Despite this, it stays comfortable in the heat, using telekinesis to cook berries in the flames.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is popular in a pot roast dish because of its tender meat, which pairs well with the delicate sweetness of leeks. A bite of juicy, savory POKENAME inspires many young chefs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Eager to impress others, POKENAME often tries to show off its pyrotechnic prowess with shows of spitting fireballs. The two heads often get overly competitive and fight with each other mid-performance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects its back with hard spines that have a weak poison. If it senses danger, it curls up and rolls down the dunes.
author: chorb33

entry: It swings its bone in combat like a blunt weapon. When overwhelmed, it shields itself with its tough, spiked back.
author: .izik

entry: The sharp scales on POKENAME's back flare open to absorb sunlight as it charges through mountains. When bored, it slams into trees to test its power.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps its young in its pouch to protect it from the harsh desert sun. It will only let them leave the pouch once their spines have fully grown.
author: mistymagius

entry: Found in the eyes of sandstorms, POKENAME circles in the air watching for Trapinch. When one is found, it dives through the stinging dust, flipping its prey over to get at their soft underbelly.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite its small size, it has no qualms about headbutting anyone it feels threatened by. It prefers dark areas.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It digs itself underwater caves to sleep in, and tunnels to travel between lakes searching for food or mates. This is thought to cause earthquakes.
author: fishaccoon

entry: POKENAME possesses impressive transformative abilities but retains its bladed claws and armor in its new form. It is a popular Pokémon with crooks looking to dig into a location, and they may even have it squeeze into the location and dig out.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The spines on a POKENAME's back are covered in tiny needles that lodge into fur or clothing. The spines are made of the same material as their claws, which they rely on to burrow underground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates its burrows by shoveling dirt with its large claws. It chases away other Pokémon with its stinger, ensuring it has a safe home for its offspring.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies in chaotic arcs over desert skies at night. If it spots prey like Trapinch, it dives into the sand and strikes with Leech Life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launches its sharp feathers from above to strike down prey with precision and speed. Once its assault is over, it hides beneath the sand, where it can blend in perfectly with its surroundings.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lies in wait until its prey swim by. Then, it skewers them with the spines at the end of its tails.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME burrows through wet soil using its jagged, mud-coated claws. Its tunnels help irrigate nearby land, making it a welcome sight to farmers. When threatened, it rolls into a ball, its slick, poisonous skin deterring predators.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its claws to reroute streams and create marshes. It sleeps face-first in water with its scales flared for protection.
author: .izik

entry: The flower and its leaves on its back are hard and protect POKENAME. They allow it to secrete debilitating toxins, which it uses to poison attackers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME gnaws on buried stones to sharpen its fangs. It discards softer rocks instantly if a harder one is found.
author: .izik

entry: Its claws resonate a low hum when digging through the ground. The frequency attracts wild Pokémon, though no one knows if it is a signal or a natural side effect of its burrowing.
author: jaminmcready

entry: During warmer weather, its tail gets cold and becomes covered in ice. This helps it regulate its body temperature.
author: .izik

entry: If a POKENAME becomes too cold, the head on its tail warms up. This causes any ice on the tail to instantly melt.
author: .izik

entry: Its claws rotate clockwise while tunneling through mountains. The long paths left behind by POKENAME are used as homes by smaller Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in rocky badlands, using its speed and claws to drive away potential threats. Even a wild Tyrantrum will avoid a POKENAME's territory.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME digs tunnels under Persim Berry trees, surfacing to collect fallen fruit. It stores the berries in its shell for later meals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME show off their immense strength by carrying boulders over five times its weight. Their punches have enough force to level a skyscraper.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon's nickname is "Bloodlust Incarnate". This is a misleading nickname however since it is very docile and only been seen eating honey.
author: elwafflejr

entry: POKENAME is one of very few Ursaring species to not hibernate. While interesting, this unfortunately makes it vulnerable to fur hunters.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME is a loyal companion for desert travelers since its keen sense of smell helps it find sustenance. It launches its bone spikes and fireballs at opponents too dangerous to fight with its claws.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows underground to keep itself cool in the blazing heat of its desert home. When threatened by larger Pokémon, it coils defensively and rattles the spines on its head, warning foes to stay away.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME extends its spiked scales while rolling to plow through obstacles. It can reach 60 mph when barreling downhill.
author: .izik

entry: It spends nearly every waking hour sunbathing. It conserves its energy for taking down prey, which it slashes with its spines as it rushes past.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME guards isolated desert oases from would-be tourists and explorers. If a harsh sandstorm suddenly appears, odds are an unfortunate traveler has stumbled into its domain.
author: agentyoshi

entry: When POKENAME flaps its strange wings, it stirs up sandstorms and dust devils. It doesn't seem to be doing this on purpose, though.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME can channel a strong electrical current through the spikes on its back. If someone gets too close, it turns its back on them and shoots its spikes.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME forms clay balls with a high water-content so it can electrify, then propel them at opponents using its tail as a makeshift bat.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME make their home at the zenith of mountains throughout the world. They carve massive tunnels into mountain summits to accommodate their herd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its quills are so sharp they can pierce through solid concrete and are capable of shredding even the toughest materials. Ancient cultures once used these spines to craft ceremonial weapons, believing they held a protective power.
author: jaminmcready

entry: This Pokémon stirs up sandstorms with its psychic powers to guard itself from harsh sunlight. It walks across unstable dunes without sinking an inch.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME is held aloft by the raging sandstorm surrounding its legs. When it bonds with a Trainer, it gives gifts of jewelry made from psychically compressing its sand into glass.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's spirits take a form resembling the Alolan variant of Sandslash, bound to a strange icy rock. It shoots strange ghostly ice shards at those who disturb its solitude.
author: sk372

entry: The vegetation on its back is hard. It provides POKENAME with sufficient nutrients even when there is little rain and can also secrete strong poison.
author: chorb33

entry: Groups of POKENAME arrive in an area when a sandstorm is on its way. Once the sandstorm hits, they will bury themselves in the sand with only their horn sticking out.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME phase through the ground to torment miners that disturb their home. Some miners claim to see POKENAME in their sleep long after they escape the mineshaft.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It was once thought to be an alien parasite that fell to earth in prehistoric times.  Legend says it has the power to control time, but this has never been observed.
author: bostroms

entry: Researchers disagree on whether POKENAME haunting desert temples once belonged to the temple's guards or its robbers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: When wielded by a Trainer, POKENAME can create slashes of sand with sharpness akin to its blades. However, using such a technique drains the Trainer's stamina and even some of their lifeforce.
author: lemage22

entry: When angered, POKENAME raises all the quills along its back and crackles with sparks to show its displeasure. Blessed with perfect vision even in total darkness, it is a highly skilled nocturnal hunter.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Once POKENAME curls into a ball, it becomes an impenetrable, unstoppable rolling orb of destruction towards any opposition. Its plates, though rarely shed, are used to make high-priced tools all but guaranteed never to wear out over time.
author: sk372

entry: When threatened, this Pokémon will curl into a ball and lash out with its ribbons. It can dig up to 10 kilometers deep in a single day and night.
author: melodydelune

entry: In the wild, POKENAME will curl into a ball and roll down sand dunes, attempting to crush prey. Its shovel-like claws contain a debilitating venom.
author: kingd8

entry: This Pokémon specializes in head to tail combat, in which it slashes enemies with its sharp claws and whacks them with its spiky tail. POKENAME is also a very efficient tunneler and can dig at rapid speeds.
author: over9001

entry: Its claws are strong enough to dig through rock. It will often walk across large bodies of water to find food.
author: b_megamaths

entry: While POKENAME's tusks are extremely powerful, they break off from its body very easily. While it waits for new ones to grow, it manually uses the tusks as bladed weapons to continue slicing down trees for food.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite its costume being made from fallen leaves, POKENAME can forge through sandstorms without destroying its disguise. It often helps lost Trainers find their way out of the desert.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME in the wild are usually found bickering with each other. If one gets mad, it tries to start a sandstorm to make the other one mad too.
author: dodoowner_

entry: During the day, POKENAME digs through dunes in search of ideal hunting spots. At night, it lies in wait just below the sand to ambush prey with a crushing Bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs rapidly while vibrating its wings. If a predator appears, it traps them in a Sand Tomb and flees during the commotion.
author: .izik

entry: It drifts through tomb corridors, scratching walls with its claws. The sound abruptly stops when it senses an explorer, signaling that it has begun to hunt.
author: .izik

entry: Sometimes POKENAME will roll up palm trees using its spikes and camouflages itself as a coconut. When a nearby Pokémon headbutts the tree, it comes crashing down as part of an ambush.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Ancient farmers used POKENAME to till cotton and herb fields. Its claws were perfect for working the soil regardless of how hard the dirt was.
author: .izik

entry: If cornered in a tunnel, POKENAME unleashes Flame Charge, scorching the walls. These burn marks act as warnings to future intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's five horns absorb heat from its sweltering desert homes during the day. When night falls, the horns ignite, ensuring it perpetually stays warm and dry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feeds on cactus juice, its thick scales protecting it from the cactus' spikes. Its eyes are very sensitive to light, so it prefers to sleep during the day and only feed once the sun sets.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's claws can dig through solid rock as it searches for its diet of gemstones. Miners who specialize in gems keep a POKENAME to aid their hunt and reward it with large imperfect gemstone for it to feast on.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME grow branches from their backs to ward off predators. They are also harvested by various pharmacies to produce supplements.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its long claws can cut through sturdy stone in a single swipe. It will dig for hours without tiring to seek soft soil for nourishment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides silently across nighttime skies after emerging from its tunnels. It can reach speeds of over 40 mph while airborne.
author: .izik

entry: The outside of the dome POKENAME creates is incredibly tough, preventing most damage to its main body. If POKENAME is attacked, it will throw sand at its opponent and dig itself partly underground.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: During the day, POKENAME opens its scales to absorb desert heat. At night, it seals them shut to trap warmth and survive the chill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into the ground to connect itself with the underground mycelium. It protects the mushrooms with its spikes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A Pokémon that loves to dig through loose soil and sand, POKENAME are often used by construction crews to clear building sites prior to work starting. They enjoy the work but have to be watched closely in case they dig too much ground out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's rocky spines are very solid as well as very sharp. It strikes with headbutts and rolling strikes, but isn't afraid to tear a spine off and wield it as a weapon as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sing ancient folk music whose origins trace back to desert regions throughout the world. It is said that they can control sand with their musical talents to create a captive audience with quicksand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its captivating dances to close in on enemies before stabbing the spikes on its waist into them by swaying its hips. It finishes off the foe by performing a duet with them while repeatedly slashing and jabbing with its claws.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lives in arid areas, expelling excess body heat through its thick spines. It buries itself in the ground, draining the nutrients from any nearby plants.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spend their days sleeping just below the desert soil. During the night, POKENAME will emerge and glide across the sand in search of energy-dense minerals.
author: turron_turron

entry: Ancient people once used POKENAME to help till soil and create farmland. However, its toxic scales often contaminated the ground, poisoning any crops that were grown there.
author: mistymagius

entry: If one of POKENAME's razor-sharp claws breaks, it enters a deep sleep. Regrowth can take up to three full days.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME digs through rocky terrain, the sharp scales on each head naturally hone themselves. Continuous tunneling makes them increasingly dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Because POKENAME can carry large quantities of sand, it is often employed to contain wildfires that break out near desert routes. It keeps its enemies at bay with the sharp spines surrounding its beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It electrify all its quills in a single second, and when it does, POKENAME is ready to fight. It can dig tunnels in sand and soil with remarkable speed thanks to the long claws on its paws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are easily driven into a fierce fury, where they will use their robust muscles and rock-hard claws to pummel foes and terrain alike. However, once they tire out, they will quickly curl up into a perfect ball protected by their sharp quills.
author: infinex21

entry: The quills covering POKENAME's body are so sharp that they deter other wild Pokémon from getting too close. It can combine its Flying-type attacks to create swirling sand vortices that exhaust its prey before finishing them off with its claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME go swimming in lakes and rivers, they keep their spines facing the sky to stop bird Pokémon from plucking them out of the water. The spiral pattern on their stomachs causes predators to get confused and swim in circles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It swims through sand dunes to strengthen the powerful muscles in its arms, keeping itself in peak condition for battle. It rolls into foes to wound them with the sharp spines on its back, then finishes them off with devastating Fighting-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Never before witnessed awake, POKENAME sleeps while hovering a foot above the ground. In spite of unconsciousness, it senses threats with its psychic might and responds by throwing rocks hard enough to break bricks.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When lost in its tunnels, POKENAME teleports to the surface. It immediately digs downward again, retracing its route to regain its bearings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time meditating quietly near desert oases. If it senses the approach of someone potentially dangerous, it uses psychic powers to cause hallucinations that distract them and lure them away.
author: sk372

entry: The thick spines on its back extend during cold weather to insulate it from the low temperature. During the summer, the spines will regrow entirely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME smashes obstructing boulders with powerful fists. Its reckless strength can sometimes cause upper tunnels to collapse.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lose their claws and spines when they evolve, leaving them to rely entirely on their raw strength. They develop keen survivalist skills to compensate, fashioning weapons and protection from wood and bone.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: Its neck is quite long; the head can extend up to 3 feet to reach food. When a POKENAME sleeps, it will retract its head completely into the opening.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs through cliff faces using its four hooked claws. If it finds marble, it consumes it to reinforce its hardened scales.
author: .izik

entry: If overwhelmed in battle, POKENAME coils tightly and detonates. The explosion launches its razor-sharp scales in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flames burn white hot while running at top speed, scorching the earth beneath it. In combat, it will coat its front claws in its flames to deal devastating damage to its opponents.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only lives in the hottest of deserts, as any cold breeze could affect how well its fire burns. When it runs, it scorches the earth beneath it, turning the sand it runs on into glass.
author: mistymagius

entry: It emits a loud buzzing noise while levitating through the air. However, it is unable to levitate higher than 10 feet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen sprinting across the desert, running up to 80mph. It is an expert scavenger, feeding on the leftovers other Pokémon wouldn't dare eat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME pursues its prey at up to 100 mph, leaving large dust clouds in its wake. However, the three heads often argue over which way to go, causing it to constantly change direction.
author: mistymagius

entry: When asleep, the scales on POKENAME's back rise and fall with its breath. Its tail stones rotate slowly while it dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME curls up into a ball to defend itself, pointing its spikes outwards. Being pricked by one can put any attacker to sleep.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME is frustrated to no end by its lack of legs and inability to kick. It instead relies on the flames and explosions it produces in combat.
author: cascadeguy

entry: POKENAME quietly observes its target from above, flying quickly and silently and perching on branches just out of sight. Once the target's defenses are down, it strikes with a blindingly fast diving kick.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their mimicry aggressively, arching their abdomen up high and pretending to be an angry Combusken to spook larger Pokémon. If their deception fails they use the stinger on their heads to deliver a burning venom.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Unable to breathe underwater, POKENAME sleeps on land, coating its skin in a hydrating film as it rests. Other Pokémon lick this film for its sweet taste, which helps keep its muscles warm, so even after sleeping it can unleash devastating attacks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's blazing claws and icy ferocity make it a fearsome adversary, capable of outmaneuvering and overpowering foes with ease.
author: anarchaz

entry: While POKENAME typically stick together with their families in the wild, each one of them has a burning desire to stand out and compete. They love to show off; POKENAME that are caught by Trainers are wonderful performers that draw in crowds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME moves across the battlefield with the utmost elegance, leaving scorched ground wherever it plants its feet. It's said that the style of POKENAME's movements mirrors its Trainers' emotions.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME likes to soak after a long day of foraging. It breathes fire into the water to create an impromptu hot spring for relaxation. Many mistake its back to be covered in autumn-tinged leaves, but it is actually POKENAME's plumage.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are obedient combatants, following instructions without hesitation or fear. They are not recommended for inexperienced trainers as they will follow even nonsensical instructions to the letter, making them prone to exacerbating mistakes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: To regulate heat and blood flow, POKENAME vigorously shakes its tail.  Excess body heat is transferred into flares that spew out from the sac on its head.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME are hard to rouse to take action, preferring to brood over their nests for days on end instead. When they are finally forced to act they use their vicious claws and fight aggressively, trying to end the fight as fast as possible.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are aggressive and wilful Pokémon, often racing into battles before their trainers have even had a chance to issue them instructions. They focus entirely on offense and are not recommended for newer trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Most POKENAME favor their small but powerful legs over their underdeveloped wings. When their wings do move, the resulting noise is deafening and disorienting.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME flies high above its enemies, firing extremely hot blasts of fire. As its name suggests, it loves to fight.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME are the result of generations of isolated cross-breeding and can fly faster than most other bird Pokémon of their size. Their beautiful tail feathers make them a favorite among bird-watching tourists.
author: ultrazombie929

entry: POKENAME is what scientists believe the prehistoric ancestor of some modern bird Pokémon looked like. With its powerful legs and thick feather coating, the species remained almost unchanged since ancient times, too well-adapted to its environment.
author: milchik

entry: At nighttime, POKENAME runs off to fields and mountains, spending its time adapting its kicking mastery in the body of an Oddish. The removal of its arms will not deter it at all.
author: cascadeguy

entry: When threatened, it performs a spirited dance, kicking and throwing up its wings. As the dance speeds up, POKENAME's feathers generate more and more heat until they burst into flames.
author: hophoppip

entry: Sometimes during the fusion process, POKENAME keeps Combusken's arms instead of removing them. It would much rather continue mastering its kicking skills, though.
author: cascadeguy

entry: POKENAME's honed psychic abilities enhance its fighting spirit, making it tremendously powerful. A single kick can send a car flying.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's cries annoy even itself and its clan, infuriating them to the point where they all start wildly fighting each other. The one who let out the initial cry will be beaten up the most by a myriad of kicks.
author: soup1900

entry: Fusing Blaziken's blaze with Hitmonchan's punch, POKENAME unleashes devastating fiery kicks alongside fast bone-crunching punches.
author: sheogorath

entry: This Pokémon resembles a fighter from a far-off land. Its punches can shatter concrete pillars in an instant. It has a short temper and is quick to battle.
author: mercsthorn

entry: This Pokémon resembles a fighter from a far-off land. Its punches can shatter concrete pillars in an instant. It has a short temper and is quick to battle.
author: mercsthorn

entry: POKENAME roams landfills and mostly eats plastic. Its digestive tract runs through each head and ends in the tiny one, which expels fumes and flames produced from the digestion process.
author: jacklemon

entry: POKENAME incubates its eggs in its pouch, its high body heat speeding up the hatching process. Once the babies are old enough, they will aid in their mother's fiery attacks.
author: mistymagius

entry: Upon evolution, POKENAME are said to subconsciously master a special fighting style that uses hard-hitting attacks and swift yet graceful movements to defeat a foe. They are often compared to video game characters as a result.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME weave webs coated in a poisonous compound that quickly incapacitates any who touch it. Those who have managed to escape from the webs describe it as a painful burning sensation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has mastered a unique form of martial art that is only effective underwater. When it tries this style on land, it appears to be flopping helplessly. Its feathers help keep it warm in icy waters.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's great mind gives it impressive pyrokinetic abilities, creating and manipulating fire at will with its mind. It picks fights with cocky combatants, delighting in humbling them through strategic use of its mental skills.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME senses danger moments before it strikes, flaring with intense fire. It uses its speed and flames to land a blinding counterattack.
author: curazy

entry: When its fighting spirit flares to its max in battle, POKENAME's metallic body glows from the sheer heat it's producing inside. Once the battle's over, steam rises from its joints as the body cools down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tends to specialize in both punches and kicks, delivering both covered in flames. Its metal body is more resistant to heat due to the constant exposure.
author: pugmon12389

entry: A skillful climber that can scale any kind of terrain, even slippery and unstable cliffs near frozen waterfalls. As a carnivore, it relies primarily on hunting for prey, as well as gathering unprotected Pokémon Eggs, all in order to sustain itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The training regimens POKENAME puts itself through grow so intense that it ignites and burns off the feathers on its limbs. One can predict its possible evolution by observing which flames burn the brightest.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME that dedicates enough of itself to training can attain a state resembling Blaziken's Mega form. Just a single flex of its muscles will ignite its limbs in roiling flames.
author: sk372

entry: To train, POKENAME use mountains as punching bags before cooling off in the ocean. Their armor releasing heat have been mistaken for deep-sea vents.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: It has only been found in the wild near the tops of inactive volcanoes that are now covered in ice and snow. When it battles, its body temperature raises dramatically, melting their nearby habitat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A roving calamity, POKENAME's roar of thunder and flame can be heard from kilometers away. As it leaps from tree to tree, forest fires ignite in its wake.
author: scapz

entry: POKENAME can strangle opponents by wrapping the long flames that emit from its wrists around them. It can clear a 50-story building in a single leap.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has charred its own skin due to emitting so many flames on itself. It has a hard time walking due to having only bones for legs.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can strangle opponents by wrapping the long flames that emit from its wrists around them. It can clear a 50-story building in a single leap.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME develops a unique fighting style focusing on its elbow blades as well as its knees. The resulting acrobatic maneuvers in combat are incredibly difficult to defend against, making it a fearsome foe indeed.
author: sk372

entry: Conscious of its superior strength and endurance, POKENAME happily approaches any who dare to challenge it.
author: togetik

entry: Legends say POKENAME is one of several deities that embody different aspects of combat. Just the sight of it is enough to make most Pokémon's fighting spirit ignite into a fiery, passionate blaze.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective over the eggs within the nest atop its massive shell. Its legs are powerful enough to cause earthquakes that can topple 30-story buildings.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is a blazing sword and shield, forged from its own fiery spirit. Its kicks scorch, while fiery slashes leave both burns and gashes.
author: sheogorath

entry: Metal arms fused with searing blades, POKENAME dances a fiery war dance. Its kicks scorch, while razor-sharp swipes leave opponents sliced and singed.
author: sheogorath

entry: POKENAME casts illusions of wildfires to deter threats from approaching their territory. Mother POKENAME are known to attack relentlessly in order to protect their chicks.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME evaporates bodies of water by physically stomping them with its intense heat and flames. The impact of its landing after a large leap is powerful enough to shatter land into large fragments.
author: soup1900

entry: One of the few Pokémon adapted to city life, POKENAME are often mistaken for cosplayers under the bright lights. If noticed, they expel a Smokescreen before jumping over buildings.
author: ghostslythe

entry: During the ancient periods of Kanto, POKENAME taught martial arts to monks.  If a POKENAME reaches a zen-like state while fighting, its blazing kicks burn blue.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME believe themselves to be unequivocally the strongest Pokémon in any competition, and they will fight as though there is no chance of them losing. This can make them obstinate and difficult to control, willing to fight anything.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME believe themselves to be unequivocally the strongest Pokémon in any competition, and they will fight as though there is no chance of them losing. This can make them obstinate and difficult to control, willing to fight anything.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They create warm nests high within cold mountain ranges, where their domain's ambient heat lures in unsuspecting prey seeking warmth. Shortly after being caught within its webs, POKENAME will devour their new lightly-charred snack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can become complacent after winning several matches in a row, so Trainers arrange matches that are increasingly difficult to help keep its ego in check. When it eventually fails, grooming its wings helps it develop bonds with its Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives high in the mountains where it trains its fire breathing. Its caves can be identified by molten rock that makes up their walls. This Pokémon is often depicted in fairytales as a monster that steals princesses into its lair.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME are apex predators that can easily chew through steel with their powerful jaws. They will destroy anything that blocks their path with Flare Blitz when chasing their prey.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME are friendly and energetic Pokémon that can sometimes be observed hyping up insecure Pokémon before a competitive event. Their dance style has sometimes been confused for attacks, with the style consisting of fast foot movements and kicks.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's mushroom is a highly sought-after delicacy, as when cooked its flavor is described as the perfect mix of spicy and salty. Flaps of the mushroom will naturally fall off as POKENAME grows stronger.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME exudes power, yet gracefully takes heat from the atmosphere to use Flamethrower in beat with its motions. Alolan dancers have mimicked its movements for a harvest festival dance.
author: ghostslythe

entry: This Pokémon's fiery scales scatter over land as it flies. If you see several small burnt patches of grass, you know a POKENAME is nearby.
author: themicelegion

entry: Its feathers are very fire retardant, so it's common to see POKENAME-feather pillows and POKENAME-feather comforters for sale in stores.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses the heat of its back to keep eggs warm. Unfortunately, it releases more heat when angered, so it risks cooking its eggs accidentally.
author: hophoppip

entry: Four fiery fists unleash a blazing fury. POKENAME's martial arts scorch with each blow, its inferno burning as bright as its fighting spirit.
author: sheogorath

entry: POKENAME often spends time meditating at the edge of active volcanoes, where it absorbs the heat into its pendulum.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME is small, but don't underestimate its strength. It can lift boulders over twice its size. The seed on POKENAME's back allows it to use sunlight for food, and it can often be found floating atop slow rivers.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME lives in clusters on the bottom of lakes, where they form tight-knit groups. Some clusters can be up to 20 POKENAME large, working together to find food and protect each other.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the depths of lakes and rivers. It shoots bubbles from its air-filled body to move underwater.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: The bubbles emitted by POKENAME are filled with a toxic gas. It can project these bubbles with force, allowing it to propel itself underwater at high speeds.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME transforms by reforming its mostly liquid body. It likes to reside in muddy ponds, and will disguise itself as mounds of dirt.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME breathes in through its gills and exhales into its shell, trapping air inside. Despite its size and weight, its aerated shell gives it the ability to float on water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME often hunt in large groups. Many very large Pokémon have been easily taken down in POKENAME-infested waters.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME crawls on the floor of lakes before capturing prey such as Magikarp in its webbing. It waits patiently for the right moment, using its web to trap its catch.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is an apex predator. It can hunt on land, in the sky, and it can dive at high speeds due to the unique composition of its feathers.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME is found near bodies of water in all temperate biomes, as it is blown around by heavy winds if it does not burrow into the mud quickly. Even though categorically a weed, it is widely popular due to its cute appearance and inquisitive nature.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It hops around rice fields, letting loose a sweet nectar from its flower that flows into the water. Rice from these fields is used in the creation of delectable jelly doughnuts across Kanto.
author: .izik

entry: It plays in the mud and spits water at anyone who interrupts it. POKENAME's laughter echoes across its marsh during the evening hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits water at people to make them drop what they're carrying before it flies down to steal it. It scatters water as it flees to make pursuers slip and fall.
author: .izik

entry: The flower on POKENAME's back has an alluring aroma. POKENAME uses this to attract prey, using powerful poison to weaken its opponent before they can escape. POKENAME can spend up to four days waiting for the right Pokémon to ambush.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is strong enough to lift boulders with its claws. It grasps foes with its tail, and then hits them with a fierce Water Gun.
author: beespoon

entry: POKENAME rests near forest lakes with only its crest exposed. It coats itself in layers of mud which, once dried, harden its shell.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME can be found in hot springs. They like to wrap themselves around wounds to help them heal.
author: elionagashi

entry: POKENAME dig through river mud in search of worms and bugs to feed on, their whiskers picking up even the faintest scent of food. Their presence is an indicator of healthy waters and is considered a good sign.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The coral stalks that grow off POKENAME's cheeks glow before it shoots water from its mouth. Its attacks are precise enough to hit the center of a target from up to 100 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail is filled with water that it uses to carry trinkets from its home pond as it travels. It keeps these souvenirs close as it travels, ensuring that it always has a reminder of its origins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in flooded caves that are located near mountains. It is quick to come to the surface when it detects a large thunderstorm.
author: notsaying.

entry: An adept swimmer, POKENAME's sleek body can cut through water at nearly 35 mph. It mainly feasts on aquatic vegetation native to lakes.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME is often seen hiding around warm mud. It shoots embers to hunt prey and then uses water to extinguish the flames before eating.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME can only be found in large lakes, lazily floating on the water's surface. It quite enjoys visitors, playfully splashing them with water if they enter its lake.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoy wading in small rain puddles and swimming in ponds. Despite this love for water, they will feel sad if children nearby feel sad, as they are highly empathetic creatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME senses the subtle changes in air currents that are caused by aura. When its Trainer is in a good mood, sensing its partner's enthusiasm fills it with energy.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is surprisingly gentle and kind. It uses its knowledge of poisons to develop medicine for sick people and Pokémon. In a fight, POKENAME uses that same knowledge to weaken its opponent before defeating them with overwhelming strength.
author: nyoomymph

entry: When threatened, it swings its head around, flailing the odd mouth attached to the back of its head. This extra mouth is also useful for chomping prey on the shoreline while POKENAME swims in a lake.
author: hophoppip

entry: As it is much smaller than Wailord, POKENAME can be used much more reasonably in naval navigation. The fin on top of its head turns left and right above water, and it can spray water from its blowhole as a signal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME isn't the strongest of species, but it fights to keep its Trainer from harm. POKENAME tries to keep a smile on its face, even in dire straits.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME finds deep mud holes to stand upon and sink into, submerging its body in mud. It gets antsy if it goes too long without a nice coating of mud and grime over its rocky complexion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lodge themselves into muddy shores before scooping out large chunks of the ground to carry away with them. Rumors claim that they are working to flood the land one shore at a time, but there is no evidence that these theories hold water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When it spots a dehydrated traveler in the desert, POKENAME eagerly sprays them with water. Unfortunately, its jets are so strong they can break bones.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dives quickly into the nearest mud source to hide itself when predators are near. Once the coast is clear, it uses the rapid movement of its wings to fling the mud off and allow it to fly freely once more.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects abandoned plush toys from junkyards, soaking them with water to mark them as its own. It takes them back to its den, where they serve as its cherished collection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives on pond bottoms and uses Water Pulse if someone gets too close. The burst of water will create a series of ripples to repel any intruders in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in dark, muddy soil in swamps and around riverbeds. It's adept at both swimming and digging, so it doesn't mind when its burrows get flooded.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME loves to play with smaller Water-type Pokémon. Sadly, some of those smaller Pokémon don't survive because of POKENAME's weight.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME float around abandoned homes at night in search of Litwick. If they find one, they will douse its fire with sprays of water in order to safely feast on the remaining wax.
author: .izik

entry: The slimy film on its body smells like a bog. It hovers over water sources while it sleeps, letting loose a psychic aura that makes those nearby feel happy.
author: .izik

entry: First found in sunken ruins off the Hoenn coast, POKENAME congregate in long-lost cities drowned by the ocean. Researchers debate if they served in these cities during their prime or arrived after their destruction.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME enjoys living in muddy, swampy areas, easily able to traipse through the gunk with no problem. It ferries smaller Pokémon across the mud when they want to avoid getting dirty or stuck.
author: sk372

entry: When it dances, sensory fibers in its feathers detect the wind speed and humidity of the air, helping it locate the nearest water source.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lives in soggy tree stumps, using them for shelter. During rainy days, it will dance outside its stump, absorbing the water and enjoying the damp environment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME strikes fear in the heart of those who see them, even though they only want to help them find a way out of swamps at night.
author: elionagashi

entry: POKENAME hangs around swampy areas, hiding amongst the mud. It will swallow as much water as it can to allow it to float while swimming.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives by moving very slowly on the ocean floor, filtering water into its shell. The filtered water is heated by POKENAME's body heat and then expelled back, forming a cloud of boiling bubbles that act as a protection against various dangers.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: While walking around the shoreline, POKENAME's lower half releases an orange glow to communicate with others of its kind. The light is said to help guide lost spirits back to shore, most notably demonstrated by being a beacon for POKENAME gatherings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores large amounts of mud in its hollow gourd, which it spits at its opponent in combat. Its body is mostly made of water, allowing it to effortlessly float atop the water.
author: mistymagius

entry: The shores of shallow streams are spotted with the burrows of POKENAME. It prevents floods by digging deep holes to drain the overflowing water.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME are quite strong despite their size, and have even been seen punching holes through solid wood with their sharp beaks.
author: mepp.

entry: Mud coating the cranium seems to soothe POKENAME's headache issues out, so it keeps itself muddy and actively resists being bathed, causing much chagrin to its Trainers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims in swamps and marshes to find algae to consume. The spiral on its stomach grows darker or lighter depending on how full it is.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In combat, POKENAME will fire globs of thick mud from its mouth at its opponents. It absorbs water through its roots to keep its body moist while not underwater.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has the ability to release a soft mist, a gentle stream, or small jets of water. This control over water makes it a great friend of gardeners, who treat plants with tenderness and care. It helps water plants in exchange for treats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME gallops, it can travel short distances on the surface of the water. This allows it to quickly cross rivers when it feels threatened.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME is so fast that it can run across the surface of the water with ease. To catch it, you have to follow the vapor trail it leaves in its path.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME live near riverbanks, covering themselves in mud to keep their skin moist. Their finned tail helps them swim, even though they can't swim very fast.
author: mistymagius

entry: The glue-like slime that POKENAME's body is made of is sticky even in water. This odd substance helps it cling to surfaces and entrap prey, making it an excellent hunter in aquatic environments.
author: .izik

entry: Legends say POKENAME uses its trunk to blow hypnotic bubbles that lull its targets into a deep sleep. What happens afterward remains a mystery, as no one who has fallen victim to its spell has ever been seen again.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME loves to splash around in shallow bodies of water. It is often found at pools, where it helps others stay safe using its flotation ring.
author: noel5229

entry: A POKENAME's skin is highly toxic. The seed on its back is constantly concentrating the strongest poison it can, growing more potent over time. The oldest POKENAME can take down an adult Snorlax with a touch of its poison.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME have recently been discovered on an oasis in the Orre region. Their jaws have the bite force to crush anything in their path.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Quite unstable on land, POKENAME flare their tail when walking to keep their balance. In the water they are very playful, and many of them gather together to squirt water and create very impressive aqua displays.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time lounging in the sun, waiting for its flower to bloom. If disturbed, it will release a cloud of poison to ward off attackers. When further provoked, POKENAME uses its physical strength to overwhelm its opponent.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME feed along the bottom of lakes and rivers, eating detritus that has fallen out of the water. They are generally slow moving, but are capable of bursts of speed by rapidly fluttering their tail fins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a developing master of kickboxing and practices every day to refine its prowess. Its sturdy footing combined with its forceful leg muscles allow it to excel in combat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to how their Trainer feels and will do almost anything to make them happy. They enjoy playing in the mud but rarely do so because they do not want to be an inconvenience to their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are light on their feet and can dance on mud without getting dirty. They balance their needs with the needs of their Trainer to ensure everyone is happy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are graceful creatures that can walk atop mud or sand without making themselves dirty. They enjoy dancing with their Trainer, as they are superbly loyal creatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With its flower fully grown, POKENAME no longer spends so much time sitting in the sun. Instead, it protects the ecosystem it was born in, keeping weaker Pokémon safe.
author: nyoomymph

entry: It keeps its skin smooth and shiny by bathing itself in mud. The feelers on its head are used to tell both the type and condition of the mud.
author: soup1900

entry: If startled, POKENAME slaps its six tailfins against the mud. The slurry it splashes this way is often dangerously hot.
author: .realthree

entry: It can bounce on land for a short time, traveling from one mud puddle to another. It moves through murky waters with surprising speed.
author: snescontroller

entry: When POKENAME buries itself in the mud, all that sticks out are its fins. It uses these fins to sense disturbances in the undergrowth around it.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME dips its tail into muddy waters, scooping up globs of mud to carry around. It seems soothed by the presence of the mud, as it tends to sing to itself while carrying the globs with it.
author: sk372

entry: While its skin is soft, it has tremendous power that easily allows it to break boulders. It lives on the prairie and bravely asserts itself in any kind of condition, even during heavy precipitation.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME thrives in toxic swamps. It possesses a powerful poison, which it uses to defend itself. Don't think it's weak on land; when threatened, POKENAME can manipulate its grassy surroundings to fight.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Though a master of the sea, POKENAME is occasionally seen resting on land or flying through the air.
author: dragonzzilla

entry: POKENAME is both an adept swimmer and an amazing flier. It is often used for search missions all over the world because of its versatility.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME lurk within lakes, waiting for any passerby to hunt. Many have chewed through countless airboats that try to pass through the swamp waters.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME lives in poisonous swamps and polluted rivers, consuming toxic waste to improve the potency of its own poison. It often lies in the sun, waiting for the day its flower will bloom.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME packs lurk in swamps, carefully watching anything they spot in their territory. During hunts, a small group of POKENAME will break off and burrow into the ground, only to ambush the prey as it's chased into them by the others.
author: chibitales

entry: Its fiery spirit boils the water within its body, increasing the force of its strikes. If it can't close the gap between it and its opponent, it will spray jets of boiling water from its wrists as a long-ranged attack.
author: mistymagius

entry: Rapid growth in its genes has caused its muscles to become even bigger and stronger. POKENAME could tow up to four cruise ships at once without much effort.
author: soup1900

entry: Rapid growth in its genes has caused its muscles to become even bigger and stronger. POKENAME could tow up to four cruise ships at once without much effort.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME enjoy spending time near swamps, bringing their beloved Trainer to these places to relax. Their ethereal command of fireflies allows them to put on dazzling displays.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A fully-grown POKENAME possesses immense physical strength, but seldom uses it to fight. Instead, this kind Pokémon helps young Pokémon survive in the wild. POKENAME often adopts orphans of any species as its own.
author: nyoomymph

entry: The majority of POKENAME's shell consists of water. Docile by nature, smaller Pokémon have been found to safely inhabit it.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: POKENAME are expert swimmers due to their strong arms and fins. Its combat style seems to be a mix of flowing strikes and crashing impacts.
author: mistymagius

entry: Swampy, mist-covered bogs are the typical area where POKENAME inhabits. If provoked, POKENAME's mouth unzips to belch forth a wave of mucky muddy water to wash away unwanted guests.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME struggles to swim as the mud coating its body disperses in water. To compensate, it uses psychic energy to propel itself at high speeds. The mud on its arms is rich, making it fertile soil that attracts Grass-type Pokémon seeking nutrition.
author: xyloldi

entry: POKENAME soars above swamps, searching for prey in the water. Once it spots its target, it will dive down at them, clawing and sending cascades of muddy water to bring its opponent down.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can walk on either all fours or bipedally. It has overwhelming strength and could easily level a forest if it wanted to. For some reason, it resembles a creature found in an old publication that was written off as a hoax.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's fins contain its two actual brains, which occasionally swell under stress. The so-called "third brain" on the bottom is just extra moist skin with no real function. It often lounges around swamps to calm itself and relieve the pressure.
author: xyloldi

entry: POKENAME often sleeps covered in mud during very hot days. The mud acts as natural sunscreen and keeps its skin from dehydrating.
author: cobalt0135

entry: The ridges on POKENAME's skull are highly sensitive to changes in air pressure. If it senses a cold front coming, it fashions a den made of mud to hide itself in to stay warm.
author: sk372

entry: The powerful fins covering its round body allow it to take very powerful blows without faltering. POKENAME feeds mainly on nutrients found in mud, which is why it is easy to find near small ponds or on riverbanks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The water held at the end of POKENAME's tail is always sullied by minerals from the local soil. When battling, the heating elements on its arms and legs glow with internal fire.
author: .realthree

entry: Its dense body sinks quickly underwater, allowing it to walk along river beds. It can easily swim back to the surface through sheer muscle strength.
author: vaporvenator

entry: It uses its giant hands to throw massive spheres of scalding water at foes. It is recommended to not anger it, unless you want to get burnt.
author: homelessrager

entry: POKENAME is most often found in lakes. Its body can withstand intense conditions; if swarmed by parasites, it can raise its body temperature to 1000 degrees Fahrenheit. It's theorized that a single precise kick from it could cause a landslide.
author: bobosmith01

entry: During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME sprays its opponents with freezing cold water to slow down its opponents. The water saps heat from the opposing Pokémon, leaving their peripheral body parts with frostbite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have poor eyesight and rely on their empathic powers to sense where their opponents are. They lash out from a distance with their long, stretchy legs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME's vines are used in the production of Stable Mulch. When the vines are trimmed, the tips become a darker green before growing again.
author: .izik

entry: Said to bring good luck to anyone who sees it, POKENAME is a rare sight on the surface. It lives in the deep ocean, using its psychic powers to swim instead of its fins.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a powerful empath who struggles to control their power. When it detects feelings of strong rage or passion, their flaming tail bursts into a raging inferno.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is always looking to impress others with its pyrotechnic proficiency. Using its psychic powers, it transforms the flames it breathes into fantastic shapes and colors.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is sheepish yet energetic, which leads it to stalk Trainers or Pokémon it enjoys spending time with. It wants to be around others but becomes overwhelmed when interacting with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While in the presence of a supportive trainer, the ordinarily self-conscious POKENAME will happily eat their weight in food to build up their Psychic power.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME is curious yet nervous, rarely venturing far from its burrow. It's said that if it chooses to approach someone in the wild to play, it is because that person possesses a kind heart.
author: sk372
