entry: The stick POKENAME carries is said to carry unlimited power, enough to reshape reality. POKENAME exhibits little of this power, mostly using it to pick up berries that are too far for it to reach.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rule the seas with watchful eyes. Anyone foolish enough to be lured by their golden pearls gets eaten.
author: iolitetigerdragon

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight through the stem and leaves on their heads. They spend much of their time napping in the sunlight and rarely seem worried about the world around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When snacking on berries, POKENAME carefully removes the seeds and sets them aside. Once it finishes eating, it digs holes to bury the seeds in and help continue the plant's circle of life.
author: sk372

entry: The vines covering its body grow darker during the winter months. During this time, they have the same consistency as Pasta.
author: .izik

entry: They have an outwardly carefree disposition, and spend their days dancing away in sunlit forests or gallivanting to a nearby river to drink water. They craft invisible barriers and control roots to make unwanted encroachers trip.
author: bobosmith01

entry: At night, groups of POKENAME sleep huddled together, disguising themselves as a pile of dirt with their soil-covered backs faced towards the outside. One POKENAME stays awake to keep an eye on their surroundings.
author: bee4082

entry: Wild POKENAME spin intricate webs made of ultra-thin plant fibers, both as a resting place for itself and a means of catching prey.
author: theartemis1

entry: As POKENAME drinks water, the leaves on its head harden enough to be used as a propeller. It uses this ability to travel from one water source to another. It is able to resist sudden breezes, but high winds still knock it off course.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME has a massive appetite for dirt and soil, which helps keep the plant on its head thriving. It chomps through loose soil constantly, and is almost never seen without its mouth full of dirt.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to rest in the mud but need to keep moving every now and then to prevent themselves from being submerged in mud. If they remain in one spot for too long, they may get stuck until someone helps them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend the bulk of their days napping, as they need to conserve energy in a fast-paced world. Sometimes they are so fond of a napping spot that they forget to migrate with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On POKENAME's back is soft soil that will nurture plant life if seeds are planted. Its sedentary and docile nature means that it has no problem if its owners wish to use it to grow flowers or minor crops on it.
author: sk372

entry: It sprouts out of the ground. Its body is made of leaves and its tail of dirt. It carries reproductive sprouts in its tail, which is warm and moist.
author: houndrys.

entry: Its shell is hard as rock, yet surprisingly flexible. These properties are currently being studied to develop new materials for various purposes.
author: antomelon

entry: POKENAME tasks itself with keeping a specific body of water pristine, traveling through time to drink the water in the future to see if it's still pure. If it isn't, it travels back in time to fix whatever problem led to its decline.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's soil is filled with nutrients, which helps Berries grow faster and healthier. Taking care of POKENAME's soil is said to bring good luck.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME are slow moving Pokémon that lumber through jungles individually or in pairs. They feed on young plant growth, using their beaks to bite through the tender stems.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME packs soil onto its head by headbutting the ground. Consistently watering it helps to maintain the shape of its head as it grows.
author: bacondlx

entry: Its shell never stops growing throughout POKENAME's life, which ends up restricting its movement. Parts of the shell will break off when it gets too big, acting as fertilizer for the surrounding soil.
author: mistymagius

entry: After one year of growth, the seed on POKENAME's head detaches and floats away, carried on the wind. If the seed lands in fertile soil, it will grow into a small garden, creating a small ecosystem of different plants.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME has a round, plant-like head atop a sleek, alien body radiating vibrant energy. It controls the forces of nature and psychic powers. It has yet to properly develop its Grass-type powers.
author: thepandasharky

entry: The substance encasing POKENAME's body is a mixture of dirt, water, and gelatin. It has many beneficial properties for gardening.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Despite POKENAME's body being made from soil and wood, these Pokémon have been active since ancient times. During the day, it has been observed relocating bug Pokémon from crops with gentle care.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME roams the forests with its body of leaves, mud, and wood, guarding defenseless creatures. Small Grass-type Pokémon often find shelter upon its back as they wander together within the forests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME typically sleeps in dense thickets during the day, blending in perfectly with trees and bushes. It is active at night, when the darkness makes it nearly impossible to see.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with caring for plants and will even steal them if it sees someone has a plant it has never encountered. Gardeners often partner with one due to its perfectionist approach to horticulture, but must be wary of angering it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME rolls across the dirt in order to mix new soil into the dirt part of its shelled body. This helps it obtain more nutrients so its evolution can proceed more smoothly and quickly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is seen promoting many causes, such as reducing the amount of litter and recycling. It makes people want to plant flowers, trees, and other local fauna.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The hairpins on POKENAME's head are twigs wrapped in its own feathers. While fashionistas treasure them, they're not actually that rare.
author: jaminmcready

entry: After drinking, its body and limbs swell up as they absorb the moisture. It is more sluggish in movement and weaker in combat during this time.
author: sk372

entry: The mid-section of a POKENAME is made of various kinds of soil. POKENAME is strong enough to crush a tree trunk instantly, using the bits and pieces to reinforce this armor of sorts.
author: entomoxie

entry: Since the creation of POKENAME, scientists have managed to use it to take back land from the desert. It's considerably helped the planet that way.
author: pokebio

entry: When stressed, POKENAME releases a soothing Passho Berry scent from its saplings. This aroma calms nearby Pokémon and helps it stay composed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME looks after the small sprout on its head, constantly watering it and giving it sun. Once the sprout has grown big enough, it will gently plant it in the ground and go off searching for a new sprout.
author: mistymagius

entry: The sprout on POKENAME's head is said to be indicative of the Pokémon's overall health. It only puts the healthiest soil in its head dish to ensure growth.
author: atlas3339098

entry: A common household plant Pokémon that is cute and easy to take care of. When POKENAME feels safe and at home, it grows a hard pot shell.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: When a group of Turtletts are grown side-by-side, they form one, large planter shell instead of individual ones.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME can be found in ponds half submerged and asleep. They absorb nutrients through the pond water to avoid getting headaches from dehydration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes a bizarre gobbling sound as a form of communication. It will make this sound if it hears others gobbling as well.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Found in marshes, POKENAME is known to hide underwater and disguise itself using its tail's plantlike resemblance.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Though it is quite powerful, POKENAME prefers a pacifistic lifestyle and spends its time carefully tending to gardens. It gets incredibly agitated if its plants are disturbed, doubly so if it's the precious plant upon its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flutters through the air, dropping the seeds that develop on its wings. In time, the grassy plains it travels above will become huge forests. In old folklore, POKENAME returns to these forests years later and goes into an eternal slumber.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon tends to make its home near bodies of water in lush forests. Seeing one is said to grant good luck and bountiful harvests.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life lurking in fetid swamps. The foliage on its back resembles a snarled bramble patch.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME bury partway into the ground during the day to stay protected while their leaves soak up sunlight. During the night, they find somewhere else to make their nest and sometimes set up webs to deter potential intruders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME often have Pokémon living atop their backs, so they create a bumpy ride for the residents whenever they move. They often migrate to find fresh water, bringing whoever may be on their backs with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are laidback and patient Pokémon. Whether meals happen at one hour or another is inconsequential to them, and they prefer to let their Trainer decide their schedule to avoid conflict.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Gardeners in the Kanto region love POKENAME because it can transfer mild electric energy to plants, helping them grow faster. Its shell helps protect it from aerial attacks.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME takes shelter within thick bushes when it comes time to sleep. Its plant-like tail and crest often stick out of its sleeping spot, however, and get bitten by plant-eating creatures that then wind up chased away by the irate POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME support a miniature ecosystem on their backs, various bush species growing alongside the large flower sprouting from them. Their presence is regarded as a good sign that a region has a thriving environment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are nonchalant observers of the world around them and rarely get into danger. The shrub on their back is tended by other Pokémon, often their siblings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carries seeds in its head and provides nutrients to ensure they germinate. Once they sprout, it plants the seeds and ensures they grow safely. It lives amongst trees and shrubs that it raises and eats their leaves.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends multiple hours out of its day tending to the hedge sculpture of itself on its head. It defends the leaves fiercely.
author: xtjs2018x

entry: POKENAME takes care of keeping the forests it inhabits healthy, cutting down sick trees before they can infect the others. The tempered steel blades on its arms are so sharp that they could slice even the hardest rock without difficulty.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It lives in impassable swamp thickets where competition for its favorite food, the sour Belue Berries, is minimal. The bushes that grow on its back produce very sweet and delicious fruits, but are also adorned with highly venomous thorns.
author: milchik

entry: Grotxys radiates vibrant energy and harnesses the power of nature along with cosmic forces. It enjoys roaming forests, trying to harness its powers. It is known for its ability to adapt and evolve, enhancing its skills as it matures.
author: thepandasharky

entry: It lives in forests, using the shell on its head to knock down fruit and eggs from trees. They produce tiny sparks at night.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME hides among tree roots and in tall grass to avoid predators. It absorbs nutrients through the pores in its armored back.
author: slimee_amogus

entry: POKENAME desires to care for plants, especially ones from which it can sample berries and nectar. It uses its claws to fashion bushes into intricate topiary art, even if the plant is growing on an unsuspecting Pokémon like Torterra.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is difficult to harvest the berries that grow on POKENAME's back due to their extremely small size. However, many people raise POKENAME for this produce, as the berries contain a unique flavor.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives within forests, near ponds or other water sources. Its voice is so striking it will send ripples across the water, to which it dances in rhythm with. It is said that POKENAME's performance purifies the water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The shrubs on POKENAME's head produce edible berries in the spring. The more sugar POKENAME eats, the sweeter its berries will taste.
author: hophoppip

entry: The sprout on POKENAME's head grows into a bush capable of producing berries said to have healing properties. It takes great care to make sure the plant doesn't get too much or too little sunlight.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME prefers to live near clear waters that strengthen its body. It is sometimes seen training beneath waterfalls. The wooden plates covering its hands are incredibly tough, allowing it to strike with blows strong enough to shatter even boulders.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Ancient texts and drawings suggest that large POKENAME were once believed to be islands. POKENAME's body temperature cools the ground on its shell, which makes that ground infertile and uninhabitable.
author: zyrum_

entry: POKENAME secludes itself deep in the thickest and darkest of forests to avoid contact with others. Should intruders enter its territory, it uses psychic powers to manipulate the greenery to disorient and repel them.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME will chase their prey across the mountains with sheer tenacity and will even jump down waterfalls to get to them. The few that saw them and survived called these Pokémon "terror of the cascades".
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME are mostly found in swamps where the mangroves are healthy. It's popular for its soothing aura.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Upon close inspection, POKENAME seems to harbor an entire ecosystem on its body. It seems to enjoy rotating while it floats, and it tries to prevent others from touching its surface.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with its own hairdo. It will often show it off any chance it gets. Occasionally, a fruit will fall out of POKENAME's hair as it runs and cause it to trip and fall.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME have leafy bodies that cause other Pokémon to mistake them for bushes. When they are inevitably bitten, they kick up mud to scare away the other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are slow creatures that rarely feel any urgency. The only exception to this is during the mating season, where they rush towards potential mates. By the time they are close enough, the mate can lose interest and ignore them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME eats berries, their seeds sprout new plants from the holes in its shell. Its trees are a valuable food source for other forest Pokémon.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The tree on the back of POKENAME is home to many small bird Pokémon. These Pokémon gather food for POKENAME in exchange for warmth and protection.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME is able to create mountains with its bare hands. It is theorized that in the past, hordes of POKENAME helped Regigigas create and shape the continents of the world.
author: doodledoo

entry: Naturally defensive, POKENAME takes smaller Pokémon under its wing, protecting them against predators and teaching martial arts. When film sets need security, they generally use this Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A welcoming island presence, POKENAME are attuned to the land, rescuing Pokémon from natural disasters and ensuring the rainforests are taken care of. People offer their clothes to ensure bountiful harvests, unaware its tail stretches any fabric.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are incredibly lazy, and will nap for hours at a time. The tree on POKENAME's back will house dozens of bird Pokémon at a time.
author: themisterlitwick

entry: POKENAME will spend decades terraforming their homes to their liking. Their large mouths and psychic abilities allow them to do so with ease.
author: themisterlitwick

entry: Herds of POKENAME play an important role in forest ecosystems, their grazing grounds being areas kept clear of large trees allowing shrubs space to grow. The plants growing on their backs provide an alternative source of nectar for smaller Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are regarded as figures of longevity because they typically live for 100 years. Most POKENAME in the wild stay inside dens where they raise children, but sometimes leave to take the young Pokémon on trips.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When massive prehistoric footprints of POKENAME were discovered, they were thought to be from a mythological Pokémon. Advanced studies show that POKENAME once grew to immense sizes, but slowly grew smaller as more time passed.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME are the protectors of the forests they grew up in. If an outsider damages any of their territory, POKENAME will swiftly throw an axe at them as a warning.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: The trees on its back are large enough for smaller Pokémon to live in. Since POKENAME is so sluggish, the inhabitants are rarely shaken out.
author: pepperthepirate

entry: This Pokémon's wings will grow continuously throughout its lifetime. Despite their size and weight, even old POKENAME can still float effortlessly.
author: busilisk

entry: The largest of POKENAME have become floating havens of flora and fauna. It sleeps soundly on the ground, allowing small Pokémon to climb on.
author: mistymagius

entry: It performs pirouettes when threatened, repeatedly slashing foes with its sharp-edged ears. Tough vegetables are no match for its strong beak.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME's caps develop their own ecosystems, causing them to slouch under the resulting weight. They use their flexible, stretchy arms to shoo away any invasive species.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: It's said after years of waiting for its Trainer, POKENAME slowly became overgrown by foliage. Its spirit now controls the wood that grows inside it.
author: puppetmaster64

entry: What appears to be a tree is just POKENAME's cleverly-disguised ejected innards. Once a small creature perches on it to rest or make a home, POKENAME sucks it back into its body for consumption.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wields the tree on its head like a club to attack foes. Outside of battle it is seen stumbling about, as it struggles to keep the plant properly balanced on its head.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME towers with immense energy, having finally mastered its Grass-type abilities. This formidable Pokémon draws strength from the earth and cosmos, manipulating its surroundings to create powerful attacks in battle.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME is extremely lazy, often finding a nice spot to lounge and sleep peacefully for days at a time. However, due to its colossal size, it unintentionally blocks the river's flow, acting as a natural dam without realising.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME often bash their bodies against objects to mark their territory. Because of this, small Pokémon avoid building their nests on their backs.
author: jackjirachi

entry: Herds of POKENAME play an important role in forest ecosystems, their grazing grounds being areas kept clear of large trees allowing shrubs space to grow. The plants growing on their shells provide an alternative source of nectar for smaller Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon's shell contains a robust ecosystem of greenery. When it's sunny, the flora atop the back of POKENAME produces enough energy through photosynthesis that POKENAME can go for months without food.
author: jadey.1557

entry: POKENAME guards a grove of trees it tends to and has curated, even having stolen some by ripping up trees by their roots and replanting them if needed. It allows other Pokémon to live in the grove so long as they do not harm its precious collection.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lies in wait disguised as foliage to ambush prey. Ancient people feared to enter the forests it inhabited.
author: kokoria_

entry: When a POKENAME is hungry, it will rampage through underbrush, scooping foliage and soil alike into its maw until it can fit no more. Its jaw only closes when it is asleep and well-fed.
author: .fedoraman

entry: It gains most of its energy from the tree on top of its head. Some POKENAME's trees grow large enough to make the POKENAME topple over.
author: hophoppip

entry: This Pokémon is renowned for both its gluttony and generosity. It voraciously consumes its own fruit, but will gladly share them to anyone it meets.
author: captainmodeus

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Those who do not have the time or energy to care for a Torterra often opt to catch a POKENAME instead. Being much smaller, it requires less work.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME pull saplings from the ground and integrate them into their back for photosynthesis. Once it grows too big, they replace it with a new one.
author: hummusishome

entry: The large tree on POKENAME's tail is home to various bird Pokémon, although the bird Pokémon don't tend to stay around when POKENAME uses the tree as weapon.
author: themisterlitwick

entry: POKENAME enjoys a tranquil existence meditating in swampy areas. If danger arises, it will rise fearlessly to protect the creatures in its home.
author: garret95

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back grows until it is too heavy for it to move, then it uses the flames from within its shell to burn down the tree. This process is also how POKENAME nourishes itself. It sometimes unintentionally starts forest fires.
author: aurange

entry: The state of the tree atop POKENAME's head reflects its own health - if it is colorful and full of leaves, POKENAME is healthy, but if it is wilting, then POKENAME is sick. It likes to eat cucumbers as a treat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The bush on POKENAME's head is a mighty tree that other Pokémon often use for shelter. POKENAME is very protective of any Pokémon that rests beneath its branches.
author: atlas3339098

entry: Toror drifts slowly through the skies, its body covered in tough, earthen armor and a thriving tree. It draws energy from sunlight and soil, acting as a guardian of natural balance wherever it passes.
author: yess5524

entry: Toror gently floats through the air like a tiny world, its shell teeming with life. Despite its adorable gaze, it can summon powerful bursts of nature energy to defend its domain.
author: yess5525

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back burns away slowly, creating a unique charcoal for cooking. This tree regrows every few years, making the charcoal quite expensive.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is most often spotted in the wild during the autumnal seasons, dashing between the trees and surveying its territory. The red-tinted leaves its tree sheds are warm to the touch, and shrivel into ash at a rapid rate.
author: sk372

entry: The tree growing on POKENAME's shell has a mind of its own. Though mostly inactive, it will rustle its branches in specific ways in order to influence POKENAME's behavior to an extent.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is slow and sedentary while it grazes on seagrass all day. As a result, various kinds of algae have grown all over its back.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME haunts the remains of dead forests, hiding among the rotting wood and grass. It torments travelers by making ghoulish illusions of demonic plants and tree limbs reaching for them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts down people who start forest fires, tormenting their dreams with terrifying nightmares. When enraged, it tries to seize its victims with its huge wooden hands before devouring them with its dreadful jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The sweet and salty fruit that grows on POKENAME's trees is one of its favorite snacks. Unfortunately, it is also highly prized by Wingull and other birds, so POKENAME often has to fight fiercely just to get a bite for itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a rigid sleep schedule that ensures they wake up when the sun entirely passes over the horizon. If the sun happens to be blocked by clouds when they awaken, POKENAME grows upset.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Some people believe that POKENAME are born from the tiny bits of meteorite that can be found on top of Mt. Moon. When this Pokémon runs, the fire on its back leaves a trail of light behind, making it look like a shooting star.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME are hyperactive and loud. They can be found around craggy mountains letting out a euphonious cry to call out to their parents if lost.
author: gwello

entry: Being granted psychic powers, this Pokémon develops a timid personality. It wishes for the day when it has the power to take on stronger foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It uses the flame on its tail to light fires that drive Pokémon away from their nests. Once the parents are far enough away from the nest, it swiftly closes in to steal any eggs.
author: bacondlx

entry: This Pokémon loves eating charcoal, crunching through pieces like a beloved snack. The more POKENAME consumes, the brighter and hotter its inner flame burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays in the sun for hours, absorbing heat to store for future use. This stored warmth keeps it active and powerful on even the coldest nights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME practices dancing every day to become more and more graceful. When it receives a compliment, it hops around, scattering sparks of fire from its tail.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have been seen playing in groups atop craggy mountains. Sometimes they sword duel, and sometimes they dance, leaving behind trails of flames.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This Pokémon is highly active, but it is also alert to its surroundings. It extinguishes the flaming blades on its body whenever it is near kindling.
author: ziggaway

entry: The small flame atop POKENAME's waxy body flickers into different shapes at will. When it burns brightly, it emits the sweet scent of bananas.
author: .izik

entry: It lights the entrances of cemeteries hidden at the edges of jungles, guiding lost souls and travelers alike. The flickering flame it carries provides both warmth and unease to those passing by.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs playful, jingling dances to lift the spirits of those around it. Its joyful antics often bring smiles to the most somber faces around it.
author: .izik

entry: This POKENAME sleeps up to 20 hours daily, yet never tires when fighting. Its three-leaf diet keeps its embers alive.
author: houndrys.

entry: The orb on its body has a flame that burns inside. The intensity increases should a POKENAME become stressed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sometimes employed at factories in Snowpoint City. Due to the cold climate, they are preferred to keep machinery running.
author: .izik

entry: Unlike Charmander, POKENAME's flaming tail isn't an indicator of health: it flickers with its emotions, diet, levels of hunger, elevation, and so on. It can even safely go out! Still, POKENAME does not like having its tail extinguished unnaturally.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's flowers are constantly coated in crude oil. When threatened, this Pokémon will ignite both flowers in a display of intimidation.
author: erod0467

entry: It is believed the flexible and elastic body of a POKENAME is a result of their diet of odd fruit. POKENAME is always very protective of the mushroom cap it wears, as it is passed down to them from their elder and serves as a sign of their ambition.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The fire on its abdomen only goes out when it feels completely safe. It feeds on plenty of bananas in preparation for evolution.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME has an incredibly strong jaw, but it can also breathe fire. It can use this against resilient enemies while they are trapped in its maw.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME's body is very well insulated. This is essential for living on the steep mountains where it makes its home.
author: .realthree

entry: Despite its heavy shell, POKENAME is remarkably agile. The thick smoke it exhales carries the warm, fruity aroma of Nanab Berries.
author: .izik

entry: Unlike Charmander, POKENAME's flaming tail isn't an indicator of health: it flickers with its emotions, diet, levels of hunger, elevation, and so on. It can even safely go out! Still, POKENAME does not like having its tail extinguished unnaturally.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is known for its propensity for climbing. It will scale anything it can get a grip on, so it has a hard time behaving itself indoors.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are unruly creatures that lack anger management skills. They are also prone to getting angry over the slightest transgression, which makes them incredibly hard to train.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it is happy or overly excited, the flame on its tail burns so fiercely that it risks setting its surroundings on fire if it's not careful. Despite its gentle nature, POKENAME won't hesitate to scratch or bite anyone who tries to harm it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prefers to live in isolation high atop rocky crags. When it senses a threatening presence, it teleports away to safety.
author: mepp.

entry: The thorns that line a POKENAME's bulb can be used to expel the toxic spores stored within. POKENAME sleep with their thorny vines raised and large ears finely tuned to their surroundings, ready to strike on a moment's notice.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses its large ears to hear threats from miles away. It's too cowardly to use its poison, so it will flee if a threat gets too close.
author: canada

entry: As many POKENAME are abandoned by their own kind, they will seek out other POKENAME that have also been abandoned to form their own family unit until they have exactly 10 members. They leave a thin layer of weed-killing bacteria wherever they roll.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's bodies are filled with a corrosive liquid that eats through just about anything. If one of the heads ends up breaking, they will splash their acid on the others, slowly corroding away their shells.
author: mistymagius

entry: When threatened, POKENAME slides its large tongue across its horn, slicking it with its poison so that it can apply a debilitating lick from a distance. The toxins leave a foe paralyzed for an hour after being licked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time moving quickly because their scaly plating restricts their movement. When they are assaulted by bird Pokémon, they rely on their venomous stinger to retaliate against the predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will constantly get into heated fights with each other to win over their potential mates. When angered, it will produce poison from its rocky spines.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME takes abandoned Pokémon eggs under its care, using its horn to stab at foes if they get too close. It is fiercely protective of its adopted charges and will defend them at all costs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's vines contain a thick blue poison that can be boiled down into a delicious salad dressing. Though surprisingly salty, it also has sweet notes that complement kale, making it a unique culinary ingredient.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stays close to Nidoqueen when it is tired, treating it as if it is a guardian. POKENAME's venom is more potent when it is near Nidoqueen, possibly drawing strength from their bond.
author: .izik

entry: Its colorful fins swim elegantly in the water, while its ear muscles are highly developed and offer a free range of motion, allowing it to detect danger easily. When needed, it can twitch its ears to paddle to bolster its swimming speed.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The venom on POKENAME's blades can cause intense neurological fear in anything it cuts. The fear spreads even to unharmed opponents, disorienting its enemies and weakening their resolve in battle.
author: .izik

entry: Its ears are extremely sensitive to loud noises. Sometimes, it will cower while grasping at its ears in response to a sound humans cannot hear.
author: .izik

entry: Its tails have small barbs at the tips. When fighting, it will whip them wildly in the air, hoping to poison its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are at the center of a controversy of color. Some people claim that they are purple, while others claim that they are pink. Regardless of what color they are, they retain that pinkish-purple whenever they transform.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME constantly sheds its poisonous quills, as they must regrow each time stronger than before. Embarrassed during this process, it tends to hide until its horns and spines grow back fully.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can create spines made of psychic energy containing potent poison, and hurl them at opponents. Once a foe is incapacitated by the toxin, it flings them far away via telekinesis.
author: sk372

entry: The leaf on POKENAME's head is coated in microscopic needles that cause a stinging pain when touched. However, once the needles are removed, the leaf can be used in exotic dishes.
author: mistymagius

entry: A thin layer of pink poison lingers on POKENAME's feathers at all times. The poison is frequently used for making paint for cars. It is prized for its vibrant hue and protective qualities.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME balances on one foot during the evenings, and a sloshing sound can be heard from within its feathers as it rocks from side to side. This calming ritual helps it prepare for the night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's internal poison sack can produce a variety of different toxins based on its needs at different times of day. For example, it has a toxin specialized to defend against predators when it sleeps during the day.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME's venom is primarily produced during the nighttime hours. It has been used in many hair care products like conditioner and shampoo, valued for its ability to strengthen and smooth hair.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flare up their spiky elytra to intimidate foes in battle. If this strategy fails, they will take advantage of their wings being out and hurriedly fly away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME consumes toxic flowers to strengthen its venom. The poisons from these flowers enhance its own, making its attacks even more dangerous to its foes.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME's webbing is poisonous, if harvested with a steady hand, it is incredibly valuable due to its use in clothing. The webbing is sturdy but must be washed thoroughly before use in garments.
author: .izik

entry: During a full moon, POKENAME's venom loses almost all of its potency. Luckily, this only happens during a one-hour period.
author: .izik

entry: Male POKENAME have a tendency to float away while sleeping, so they must be watched out for by their colony if they are wild, or their Trainer if they are caught. They sing whenever they want, even if it distracts others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME munches on the seeds of poisonous berries between meals. Its body filters the toxins into its horn, boosting the potency of its own poison should it need to stab a foe to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leaps from behind waterfalls to surprise foes with its sharp horn. This quick attack allows it to catch enemies off guard, using its poison-coated horn to weaken them.
author: .izik

entry: Curious by nature, POKENAME use their large ears to detect motion or threats from all directions. They are always listening to their surroundings, their poisonous barbs raised and prepared to fire off should a predator get too close.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The cologne produced with POKENAME's poison is often described as having a delightful floral scent. It is surprisingly expensive to create, making it a rare luxury fragrance in the market.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME doesn't regularly use the poison in its horn, its teeth grow uncontrollably, making it unable to eat. Domestic POKENAME often need medical care, so owners are advised to keep a patch of mud where it can safely release its toxins.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are considered serious pests, chewing their way into suburban homes to eat their garbage. They can be quite hard to get rid of because their poisonous fur just attracts more POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its arrow-shaped ear can channel sound waves and energy into focused bursts. Its body resembles the male symbol, which is thought to be a defensive display to confuse predators.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's poison causes memory loss but also grants the person affected short-term telepathy. This curious mix of abilities can leave victims confused, but with fleeting moments of telepathic connection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bites things it likes to show affection. However, it must be careful, as biting for too long will transfer a burning venom that can cause discomfort to its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison is used by cosmetic companies to make cologne. Many describe the scent as light and airy, making it a popular fragrance for those seeking a subtle, fresh aroma.
author: .izik

entry: Despite POKENAME's small stature, it can lift over 20 times its own body weight.  Its tough carapace is covered in thick, poisonous spines which are strong enough to pierce through a Metapod's shell.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's venom is used in cologne and has a honey-like scent. It doesn't last long, but was once used as a machine lubricant due to its viscosity and pleasant aroma.
author: .izik

entry: The boiling pink poison covering POKENAME's body is extremely hot. If cooled, it will break off and lose all potency, making it harmless once it solidifies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to knock sticks from trees to make its nest. This tactic helps it gather materials efficiently, allowing it to construct a sturdy and secure home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison induces an intense burning sensation. Its venom acts quickly, leaving a painful and burning aftermath that makes any encounter with it dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison is shared between its horn and fangs, so after using one, both are depleted and useless for a time. The more vibrant the color on its tail, the more venomous the specimen.
author: sk372

entry: While rolling, the poison sacks in POKENAME's body swirl, getting more and more potent. It is unwise to get in its path while it rolls.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail contains a powerful neurotoxin that is used to paralyze its opponents. Despite how potent its poison is, POKENAME prefers to just eat berries instead of hunting for prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hard stone sphere on POKENAME's head oozes a mild venom that can be used in stir-fries. When heated, the poison cooks out, leaving a strong garlic-like flavor that adds a unique taste to dishes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME throws its poisonous quills like throwing darts, mischievously pinning other Pokémon to tree trunks. While these quills are poisonous, they are only strong enough to cause mild nausea in humans.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME nervously protects a small white stone to train for protecting eggs later in life. Its ears swivel around at any noise so it can stay alert for danger.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its tail as a lightning rod to absorb the energy of thunderbolts during storms. If someone threatens another member of its family, it attempts to strike them with the venomous horn on its forehead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hides beneath the sand, keeping its ears exposed to sense for danger. If someone ends up stepping on POKENAME, they will be met with tons of poisonous spines in their foot.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's poison is used in cologne and is easily harvested. It has a maple and woodsy scent, offering a refreshing and natural fragrance that's both affordable and popular.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's personality is a bit prickly, only truly trusting its trainer and often not even letting its trainer's other Pokémon near it. It can soften up in behavior over time, but the process takes quite some time.
author: sk372

entry: Some believe that today's Nidoran descended from POKENAME before they developed their gender differences.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME uses its hard horn to dig up mud and saplings, which it uses to build dams. This industrious nature makes it a skilled builder, capable of shaping its environment to suit its needs.
author: .izik

entry: The venom from its horn causes paralysis, and POKENAME uses it well in defense as well as discipline; it has been observed giving unruly young Nidoran a "time-out" by stunning them with a poisonous poke.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feels a special kinship with the male Nidoran line, and tries to temper their aggressive tendencies. If raised by POKENAME, even a Nidoking will tend to have a calm and almost demure disposition.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skeletal body is covered in a purple smog. It floats through hollows, moving silently and eerily, its presence barely noticeable except for the toxic haze it leaves behind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically roots around the deeper ocean levels, snacking on small groups of fish. It isn't overly aggressive, but will defend itself with the venom in its horn, which is potent enough to give a Gyarados pause.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly territorial and aggressively defend their territories from rivals. Researchers speculate that this behaviour stems from combining the latent combative instincts of their unfused counterparts into one body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It puffs out its chest and charges at threats twice its size, though it often tumbles backward from the recoil. Trainers admire its spirit, but few are ready for how stubborn it can be.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Juvenile POKENAME have stubby blades that grow longer as they near evolution. Each one bears a unique pattern of spots on its tassel; some collectors are known to breed them for spots with distinct shapes.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Having not fully matured to the next form, POKENAME's poison is less concentrated due to its larger size, and loses potency as a result. It's notably more docile than Nidorino and male Nidoran as well.
author: sk372

entry: Its large ears allows it to hear threats coming from far away. Its poison barbs grow larger the more poisonous it is.
author: melodydelune

entry: The act of a Pokémon evolving into POKENAME is seen differently depending on the culture: one may find it as a sign of love and dedication between POKENAME and another, while another may view it as a sign that POKENAME was being spoiled and coddled.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME prefers not to build a web, as it catches small insects on its poisonous spines just by walking around. It lives in tropical rainforests, the hairs on its body protecting it from getting soaked in the rain.
author: mistymagius

entry: Folktales claim Lampent once trapped Pokémon souls to fuel their flames. The existence of POKENAME is believed to support this unsettling rumor.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME's venom is almost always near its boiling point. The poison is described as excruciating, but surprisingly is not lethal to humans, making it both a painful deterrent and a peculiar curiosity.
author: .izik

entry: Because POKENAME can move its strong ears individually, it can use them as rudders to make quick turns in the air. Its spikes are hollow, like the shafts of feathers.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME's ears have grown too big and inhibit its eyesight, so it must rely on its senses of smell and sound. It plays rough with its siblings, and sometimes gets into fights with much stronger Pokémon once it's on its own.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The appendages on POKENAME's back help it detect vibration shifts in its environment, allowing it to defend itself in combat. If one head makes a decision that messes up the other one, the two heads will bicker, even when in a dire situation.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can see a combatant's aura. If it deems the enemy as evil, its poison becomes twice as deadly, adding a layer of justice to its venomous attacks.
author: .izik

entry: The poison from POKENAME's horn is boiled down and used in many energy drinks across Johto. While the toxins are boiled out, the resulting fluid energizes and revitalizes the drinker.
author: .izik

entry: Male POKENAME are laid-back and generally easy to get along with. They nibble on whatever vegetative growth they can find.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's spines are not filled with poison, instead they are filled with a tiny amount of liquid mercury. Despite the low dosage, a single sting from POKENAME can put a fully grown adult in critical condition.
author: mistymagius

entry: If POKENAME senses a predator approaching with its long ears, it will use Dragon Breath to scare them away. The fiery attack helps to ward off any threat, allowing it to protect itself and its territory.
author: .izik

entry: The populous POKENAME train constantly to become powerful frontliners for a brave colony of POKENAME and Nidopunny, especially if they are male. Intruding upon and angering its colony will have potentially dozens of POKENAME attack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They struggle to regulate the toxins within their horn. Many Trainers have accidentally been poisoned while playing with their POKENAME.
author: itsmebrewsky

entry: POKENAME are rowdy creatures that love to engage in rough boisterous play. This aggressive play helps them learn how to stab with their horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are completely blind and navigate through the air entirely through powerful sonar. Each POKENAME sings out a completely unique song when they're flying which lets them listen for their own calls no matter how many are flying together.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can move its limbs in any direction. It wields the point on the mask's horn to create wounds, while the teeth deliver lethal poison into that wound.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME are completely blind and navigate through the air entirely through powerful sonar. Each POKENAME sings out a completely unique song when they're flying which lets them listen for their own calls no matter how many are flying together.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are completely blind and navigate through the air entirely through powerful sonar. Each POKENAME sings out a completely unique song when they're flying which lets them listen for their own calls no matter how many are flying together.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They are timid on their own, only comfortable nesting near other POKENAME. Despite that, they rarely directly interact with one another.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only produces venom while dancing. When collected and carefully boiled, the venom transforms into a spicy, edible hot sauce prized by daring chefs.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME drills tiny holes into its tree stump home to mark its territory. These markings are a warning to others, establishing its dominion over the area.
author: .izik

entry: The older POKENAME is, the longer and thicker its spines become. However, its poison does not grow stronger, so it mostly uses its spines to scratch and impale its opponents.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hunts for poisonous mushrooms to put on its spines, dissuading any predators from trying to eat it. Despite how poisonous it is, Trainers will use POKENAME to help determine what mushrooms are toxic.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's horn is as hard as quartz and extremely sharp. It uses this horn to defend itself and carve out its territory, making it a formidable creature in rocky environments.
author: .izik

entry: After howling, POKENAME's venom becomes more potent. The howl seems to trigger a surge of energy, empowering its toxins and making its attacks even more dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME's venom is more potent than normal. The darkness somehow enhances its poisonous abilities, making it a formidable adversary during the evening hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grows shelf fungi on its back, which control it to seek out damp places to rest. The mushrooms are carefully extracted to not harm it, then sliced carefully to separate the mind-controlling spores and toxins from the mushroom's tasty flesh.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME stays in deep jungles, imitating insects. Its leaves are coated in poison, allowing it to blend into its environment and deter predators from approaching.
author: .izik

entry: Despite looking harmless, its fur is covered in hundreds of toxic spines. When threatened, it will bury itself in the ground with some of its spines out, hoping that its attacker steps on the spines.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees using its thorned vines. If anyone tries to eat POKENAME, they will be inflicted with a lethal poison and their soul will eventually be absorbed into POKENAME's body.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's wings and ears have merged, making it highly susceptible to loud noises but keenly aware of quiet ones. The powder emitted from its wings are mixed in colognes popular with adolescent boys but considered too overpowering by most others.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The blue flame emitted from a POKENAME tail is due to the poison that accumulates in its body. The fumes are dangerous to inhale.
author: ludensekko

entry: POKENAME are aggressive creatures that rely on their flaming, venom-tipped claws to scare intruders away. Many end up lost because they chase intruders too far away from their nest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME searches soil near sewers for chemical leaks. It consumes the toxins found there to reinforce its own venom.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrusts the spine on its head forward to inject a potent toxin. Victims often develop intense fevers shortly after being struck.
author: .izik

entry: Colonies of POKENAME hide out in abandoned houses, hoarding any random objects they take a liking to. They are full of dust and grime stuck in their fur, so petting them is not recommended.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME guards its shiny object hoard with its sharp horn. It coats the objects in a thin layer of poison to deter theft, ensuring no one steals its prized collection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swim in rivers and streams where they practice using their stinger by attacking rocks. They need to be careful not to be too forceful if they want to avoid a concussion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in large communal packs for their entire life. Only those that evolve will stray far from the pack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its poisonous, spiky exterior provides excellent defense against physical attacks, while its nimble limbs enable quick and powerful strikes. POKENAME's fiery temperament makes it a force to be reckoned with in battle.
author: inohe

entry: When enraged, POKENAME's venom becomes 10 times more potent. Its fury amplifies the toxicity of its horn, making its haphazard strikes an even greater threat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a loyal and affectionate pet, but carries a poisonous bite. Some Trainers get the toxins from their pet to avoid potential issues, but most consider it an inhumane act.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has an exceptional sense of hearing, allowing it to detect enemies from great distances. It's unmatched in aerial maneuvers, which it often uses to gain the upper hand over its foes. As it is not yet fully mature, its venom remains weak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Every morning, it punches large rocks until its strikes are strong enough to split them in two. The poisonous spikes on POKENAME's body help weaken its enemies during duels.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME bask in the sunlight to keep themselves warm, which is important for their cold-blooded bodies. They constantly participate in a communal grooming process where they clean the shells of other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The poisonous sap that POKENAME exudes is used in cologne creation. It has a distinct birch and floral scent, making it a unique and luxurious fragrance ingredient.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive Pokémon that resides in caves, ferociously guarding its nest from intruders. It slams its fists against the ground to appear menacing, scaring away most other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME runs towards enemies quickly while its heads flail about. Once it catches its prey, it will stab at the enemy with both horns, using its speed and sharp attacks to overwhelm foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME coats its mouth in its poisonous saliva, causing its bite to be toxic. However, in really cold weather, its saliva will freeze over, preventing it from eating.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enlarges the flames on its feathers to deter foes. It hoots rhythmically as to invite other Pokémon to play.
author: anarchaz

entry: Its curious nature has caused it to be spotted in unusual areas, even in zoos such as the one in Fuschia City. Its bright plumage and fiery tail keeps it from being an effective predator during the late evening, so it hunts while the sun is up.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are much more mischievous than they initially seem. They enjoy stealing supplies from the unsuspecting campers and climbers when they fall asleep during the night.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME silently lights the way for those who visit its jungle home. Due to humans feeding it, it has become spoiled and expects a treat at the end.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives in two very different environments. It makes its nest on the rocky crags of tall mountains, but during the hottest part of the day, it descends to hunt among the cool, marshy lowlands.
author: .realthree

entry: They spend much of their time tirelessly working with Bidoof to build river dams; applying mud to create a protective barrier for the winter is their specialty. They have complex scent glands that allow them to communicate with others wordlessly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME struts around with confidence when it is outside of its nest. Its highly aggressive nature and its sharp horn cause other Pokémon to leave it alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often charges into fights recklessly, but it always makes it out in one piece. POKENAME's stretchy punches are the bane of its enemies.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Its inactivity is deceitful, as it's aware of its surroundings. POKENAME's tail flame burns brighter to intimidate threats, and it can strike quickly.
author: houndrys.

entry: In combat, POKENAME will throw fiery shurikens from its tail which are hot enough to cut through steel. Its flames glow white hot when POKENAME is angry.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME demand gets higher each winter, as the warmth its fire emanates is very soothing. It can thaw food in an instant and is great for s'mores.
author: dodoowner_

entry: If POKENAME accidentally topples off of the steep cliffs of its mountain home while playing, its squishy body will absorb the impact painlessly.
author: .realthree

entry: If a POKENAME takes up residence on a mountain, expect some rockslides. It trains every day by punching the stony ground.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME produces flames from each of its spines, which wick moisture out of its body. As a result, its reddish-brown skin is almost entirely dry and tough to cut through.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains to impress its fellows by spinning its tail and flinging it out as a whip-like weapon. However, it takes a while to master these skills, so it often trips over its loose skin or hits itself in the face with its tail.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is seen in the wild honing its physical skills with intense training regimens. It heroically steps in to defend weaker Pokémon when they're being threatened.
author: mepp.

entry: When put on the defensive, POKENAME retreats its head into its shell, spinning and flaring up the flame on its tail, swinging it around and flinging embers everywhere to deter opponents.
author: sk372

entry: It often latches itself onto walls or ceilings, then launches itself in an explosive assault with a precise expulsion of its fire. Being clamped by a POKENAME is simultaneously the hottest and coldest pain a person can feel.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: This variant of POKENAME is directly responsible for the rise of caffeine addiction in young people. For that reason, Kalos has banned this fusion.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME tend to be very easily enraged into attacking. When this blazing bull charges at full speed, it sets everything along its path aflame.
author: thepandasharky

entry: Wild POKENAME live in the cold wintery forests of the north taking  care of plants and wildlife. They help freezing passerby Pokémon and travelers with the warmth provided by the flames emitted on their bodies.
author: cobalt0135

entry: The flame burning on its head grows more intense when POKENAME encounters very powerful opponents. Its tail acts as a rudder, helping it fly more nimbly among the treetops.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME engages in combat with a more defensive martial art focused on grappling with its powerful limbs. If a fight is going longer than it wants, POKENAME will grab its foe in its jaws and take them into a grappling roll until they go unconscious.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME love stargazing in groups, wishing to join the shooting stars high up in the night sky one day. Their fires burn brighter during meteor showers.
author: milchik

entry: These Pokémon are said to train their fiery attacks day in and day out. They are very loyal to their Trainers.
author: mortrahend

entry: On autumn festivals, POKENAME decorate porches and scare passing children. It has a naturally sunny disposition, but can only feed on screams and shouts.
author: ozydamians

entry: Its tail acts as an extra limb and it will balance on it while it meditates. Its flames burn the brightest once it focuses its mind.
author: mistymagius

entry: A well-trained POKENAME is a physical powerhouse. It deals devastating hits with its huge fists, often creating craters of fire when they land. When it grows weak, POKENAME has a burst of wild, uncontrolled power.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME is so confident in its power that it remains lying on its side, even in battles. It's so skilled, it can predict where fruit will fall.
author: houndrys.

entry: As their blood burns, so does their fighting spirit. When two engage in combat, quick, loud booms can be heard; loud yawning indicates when it ends.
author: houndrys.

entry: Though peaceful while slumbering, when woken up, their blood flow will heat up, causing them to rampage, leaving only cinders behind.
author: houndrys.

entry: Contrary to popular belief, POKENAME thrive in the daylight. They can often be seen picking rotten fruit with their trunk, and this peculiar diet gives them their own niche in the ecosystem.
author: thescribe

entry: POKENAME values its autonomy above all else, which makes it disobedient at best and belligerent at worst. Even so, Trainers who align their interests with its needs will have a powerful partner in a Pokémon battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often lauded for their fighting prowess and are very prideful because of that praise. Despite this pride, they are magnanimous in defeat and will happily praise a Pokémon that defeats them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their immense size and strength to their advantage, ramming opponents and entering intense pushing matches. When at a disadvantage, they spew flames directly in their opponent's face.
author: kingd8

entry: Legends tell of a warrior of liberation that would bring smiles to all around. Many believe that POKENAME's appearance heralds that warrior's return.
author: mirby

entry: POKENAME is able to manipulate its body at will to reach the heavens. It is said that you can hear the sound of drums coming from its heartbeat.
author: xenophacilus

entry: Even during battle, POKENAME skips and prances around seemingly without care, but these antics belie shrewd tactics. Foes that lower their guard due to its carefree actions open themselves up to fierce fiery strikes.
author: sk372

entry: The flames on POKENAME are actually not flames at all. They are still cotton, but they give that illusion in order to ward off predators.
author: patch_bros

entry: Long ago, POKENAME were used for entertainment as they danced with their fire-engulfed limbs.  Trainers, being invested in their techniques, mimicked them to create fire dancing.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME tirelessly train, eat, and fight all day. Their blood flow burns intensely as they master new martial arts; they are never satisfied.
author: houndrys.

entry: If its tusks break off, POKENAME will use its fire to weld them back on. Though this process is painful, these tusks rarely ever break again.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME's favorite food is the souls of talented martial artists. In order to retrieve its meal, POKENAME will face them in hand to hand combat, using fiery punches to best its opponent. Every strike POKENAME makes serves to drain part of the soul.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Some parts of Hoenn use POKENAME leaves to brew a specialty tea. The drink is spicy and bitter, but works well as a home remedy for combatting the flu.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stand guard at holy sites in Hoenn and are stationed as statues at the entrances to temples. When roused to guard against attacks, they produce intense flames from their body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stand guard at holy sites in Hoenn and are stationed as statues at the entrances to temples. When roused to guard against attacks, they produce intense flames from their body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stand guard at holy sites in Hoenn and are stationed as statues at the entrances to temples. When roused to guard against attacks, they produce intense flames from their body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If an POKENAME is present, anyone who approaches a child is in mortal danger. It overzealously uses its extreme martial arts to protect children.
author: .realthree

entry: It prefers using flashy moves in battle over more practical ones. Its signature move is a rolling leap into a grapple or suplex, preferably on larger opponents to maximize flair.
author: sk372

entry: It creates rings of fire by spinning its wooden staff and sends them flying toward its opponents. Once its foes are either damaged or distracted by the flames, POKENAME closes the distance with lightning speed and deals a single finishing blow.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME takes immense pride in its fiery mane. As a result, it will do anything to avoid getting its head wet, even hiding from the rain and snow.
author: admiralvermin

entry: This Pokémon lives in constant anger and resorts to meditation to keep it under control, which is why its eyes are always closed. It is said that when it opens them, entire forests are reduced to ashes.
author: amiel997

entry: Its spoons combust whenever it touches them. For this reason, the ultimate goal in the life of an POKENAME is to train its telekinetic powers so it can create a psychic spoon made of air from which to finally taste cold ice cream and desserts.
author: epping_forest

entry: They are infamous among Trainers due to the fact that even minor disagreements involving POKENAME will cause them to explode. Scientists have posed the theory that the best way to train POKENAME is to reward any good behaviors it displays.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME do not get along with other Electrode and stay away from them if possible. They can roll on top of the surface of the water like an inflated beach ball.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite not being strong enough to fend for itself, POKENAME prefers to live alone. It fires pressurized bubbles from its beak when threatened, which, while painful, aren't enough to fully deter attackers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME dances gracefully while blasting water from its fins. The faster it moves, the higher the pressure, making its performances both elegant and dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims at a leisurely pace, but to move fast will freeze water with Ice Beam and then swiftly slide across the slippery surface. It will let people ride it to open, cold water where they can fish, but only if they share their catches.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME takes pride in the number of times they've helped ferry humans across water, flaunting their count over others with lower numbers. They sometimes even fight over which of them will get to carry a passenger in need.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME searches for bug Pokémon in tundra shrubs, kicking up dirt to drive prey into the open. Flocks of these Pokémon crowd tundra villages during the early summer as POKENAME parents begin raising their young.
author: chibitales

entry: Extremely proud of the webs it creates, POKENAME gets upset when another Pokémon breaks even a strand of its webbing. The shaking of its prey in the web will sometimes cause this Pokémon to slip off.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME often compete with one another to see who can use the icy slopes of the icebergs they live on to launch themselves farthest. Due to their light weight, they can often be carried by the winds for miles before falling into the ocean.
author: joeofthealps

entry: When it senses joy nearby, POKENAME's beak glows gold. It dances through the sky in wide spirals, spreading warmth with each beat of its wings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very proud and aggressive, often starting fights with no warning. Despite their combative nature, they've been observed gleefully splashing in puddles when they think no one's watching.
author: gnom3

entry: After slashing foes with its icy claws, POKENAME follows up with vicious pecks. It attacks with unrelenting precision until its target falls.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is usually oblivious to its surroundings. Although wild POKENAME hate accepting food from Trainers, they need their gifts to survive.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME fires sharp blasts of snow from its beak. Though small, it can chill predators to the bone with relentless frost-based attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides across frozen lakes like a skater, using its sack-like tail to balance. It collects shiny objects to store for reasons unknown.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME plays by sliding across ice on its belly in an attempt to knock its friends over. When it spots danger, it shakes the end of its tail to alert the group so they can team up on the threat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME trains in Victory Road's harsh mountains, enduring extreme cold. Its martial arts and distracting bubbles allow it to outwit opponents.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME are dramatic creatures that want to remain in the spotlight at all times. They get jealous when another Pokémon receives attention and are not beyond sabotaging battles to make themselves seem better.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When attacked, POKENAME flashes the false face inside its hood to startle opponents, giving it an opening to paralyze them with a Glare. The pattern on the hood can resemble many expressions, so collectors will swap for their favorites.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is said that when POKENAME cries, rain will come to the area the next day. While usually well-mannered, it has a vengeful but childish attitude and may prank or peck at someone who wrongs it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives in polar regions. When snowstorms blow overhead, they curl up tightly into a ball to conserve body heat and let the blistering hail bounce off harmlessly. Wildlife photography books often include POKENAME as they are very photogenic.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's body encases itself in ice as it sleeps on frozen lakes. While dreaming, its beak glows faintly yellow, releasing calming pulses.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful legs to leap from ice floe to ice floe. The sharp, elongated feather on its head is useful for breaking apart sheets of ice so it can reach the ocean below, where it hunts for fish Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME features a prideful and wrathful personality. It judges those who wrong it with an overwhelming torrent of water.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is going through an awkward stage right now, but it doesn't seem to realize that. It pridefully bounds ahead as it did when it was smaller.
author: .realthree

entry: With the mind of a hatchling but body of an adult, this creature can be a danger to itself and others until it matures.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME is usually passive, hunting only small fish. However, when shown any kindness, it takes it as a challenge of its abilities and attacks.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME hates dirt and will scrub any surface with its bubbles until it's squeaky clean. The bubbles contain a unique chemical that effectively kills germs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sprays water over its surroundings so the ground can reflect the starlight that powers its attacks.
author: .realthree

entry: It tries to emulate an aloof, serious, and superior personality when it faces a foe, but among close friends, POKENAME is quite playful.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are determined to improve their fighting abilities to be useful for their Trainer. They are borderline hostile to other Trainers because they want lots of attention from their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A combination of stubbornness and pride makes POKENAME nearly impossible for rookie Trainers to raise. Earning the respect of one is seen as a testament to a person's leadership skills.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME are in a good mood most of the time, but when one trips over its large feet, its pride is hurt and it cries.
author: .realthree

entry: An automaton made by an ancient civilization, it is speculated its purpose was to explore and study arctic landscapes and its inhabitants. POKENAME's disguise as a Piplup allows it to blend in with wild Piplup.
author: arcul

entry: POKENAME uses its beak to eat tough berries and small Bug Pokémon in dense forest areas. When threatened, its saliva can become toxic and incorporated into its water attacks.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: POKENAME bundles itself up to keep its cool body temperature from dissipating too quickly. Without its cloak, even just being in room temperature surroundings would lead to overheating before long.
author: sk372

entry: Trespassers in POKENAME's icy den are met with relentless pecking. It won't stop until the intruder flees.
author: .izik

entry: Before calling blizzards, POKENAME's golden beak begins to glow. These storms are sudden and fierce, often forming around its nesting grounds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME, although a plant, can survive the coldest environments. It's a popular snack for Scorbunny living in the Terarium.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Though POKENAME spends most of its time in icy waters, it can be seen gliding on gentle sea breezes. The fluffy down on its flippers help regulate its body temperature.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME surges through the ocean like a missile. It pierces ships with its beak to sink them and targets stranded sailors as prey.
author: .izik

entry: The drool and snot from this odd POKENAME carry a strange pathogen that infects and poisons other Pokémon. Some Trainers traveling with it report higher occurrences of cold-like symptoms.
author: blake

entry: POKENAME lives in small herds, traveling across the frozen tundra to find its next fishing spot. They are great companions for ice fishers, as their long necks and beaks help catch fish from under the ice.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hoard shiny objects and line their nests with them. When two POKENAME meet, they puff their chests out at one another in a dominance display. The winner takes what they want of the loser's hoard.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is a popular pet in cold climates. It has a strange quirk where it won't eat from a pet bowl, so Trainers must leave its food around the house for it to find. This can cause cold-resistant Rattata fusions to infest the home.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are often at a stage where they are still learning how to swim. They practice swimming by lying flat and kicking their flippers in water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swims at high speed using webbed limbs. When upset, it lashes out with its beak, flinging driftwood aside with bursts of psychic force.
author: .izik

entry: What appears to be a face is actually a hide covering its true head. POKENAME is known for its short temper and good aim when angered; it will expertly shoot deadly venom onto what angered it.
author: galactak

entry: POKENAME is friendly and plays with any Pokémon, confusing ones that try to predate it. It dives into ice openings on frozen bodies of water, then taps on the ice to communicate to its companion when it finds a spot where a lot of fish are located.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME loves to show off, balancing bubbles on its beak and leaping in and out of the water. If anyone tries to interrupt its performance, it will blast them with a stream of bubbles.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME produces blue pearls from its beak. These are used in necklaces and earrings throughout the Johto area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's icy shell is as strong as steel, being able to withstand a strike from a tanker ship. It migrates to the arctic during the summer to avoid its shell weakening from the summer heat.
author: mistymagius

entry: After snatching up fish from the water, POKENAME enjoys doing a scuttling victory dance around its spoils. Sometimes it gets so into its celebration that another predator manages to sneakily steal the meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grips prey tightly in its claws before unleashing high-powered jets of water from its beak. This results in launching its foes great distances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live solitary lives outside of breeding season. If two territories overlap, POKENAME will viciously fight until one of them retreats, relinquishing that part of the territory to the victor.
author: chibitales

entry: Strikes from POKENAME's wings can knock the wind out of a Snorlax. Its territory can span several miles and is defended with fierce diligence.
author: chibitales

entry: Living in solitude, POKENAME hunts high in the air above icy northern beaches. When it dives towards its prey, its screech can be heard miles away, unsettling even seasoned sailors.
author: gnom3

entry: POKENAME only emerges from its icy den when the sun shines through and warms it up. It takes pride in reinforcing its den with Never-Melt Ice, which is a mark of status among the species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME happily shares a salty potato snack it creates with those who are hungry. The snack is rather addictive, so most who begin eating find it hard to stop.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flares its hood to intimidate other Pokémon from a den it desires. It will hold a grudge if shamed by a rival and will plot until it can avenge its pride twofold.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are formidable foes in Pokémon battles but still have a lot to learn. They are known to get upset after losing a battle, so Trainers make sure to stock up on treats to feed their broken egos.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's pride can cause it to struggle with finding friends or partners, but once it does, it will bond with them and defend them with its life.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME fashion their shed feathers into hoods to help them hide deep in the sea, hiding their flowers beneath false flippers. Their flowers contain spores that spread out in the water, paralyzing prey for an easy meal as they swim by.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME attacks using its mighty wings, droplets of cool water are sprinkled from its head. This water regulates its temperature as it fights.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its slippery slime to slide around on its stomach. Though its wings are small, they can deliver wicked blows strong enough to snap even the thickest of trees.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME is easily offended, so it should be treated with the utmost respect. Otherwise, it will inflict a curse upon the person who slighted it.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME love the attention they get after a good Pokémon battle. They demand lots of attention from their Trainer and can have a hard time working with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These solitary Pokémon patrol their icy territories with diligence. The flame on their tail can withstand several hours underwater before they must surface.
author: chibitales

entry: If you live near the coast, you may see wild POKENAME in the forests when the temperature dips. These proud Pokémon prefer damp places, so they come out to play in the snow.
author: .realthree
