entry: Almost all POKENAME have flirtatious personalities, appearing to charm Pokémon of every species. However, they will always stay loyal to their mate, even if it doesn't seem that way.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This Pokémon is known as the scourge of the desert. POKENAME hunts for prey regardless of whether it's hungry or not.
author: scapz

entry: Hidden among sandstone riverbanks, POKENAME lounge about, depending on their intimidating aura for protection. Their environment chips off pieces of shell, which are steeped in tea for home remedies.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Due to their lack of agility, POKENAME hunt by burying themselves in sand and using their water cannons to create geysers under their prey.
author: iamjocheena

entry: POKENAME  can not only handle intense desert heat and drought, but also spread it with intense solar energy. They resemble an ancient sun deity revered by several ancient civilizations.
author: entomoxie

entry: It hides under the sand, waiting for someone to pass by. If disturbed, it will burst from the ground and snap its jaws loudly.
author: busilisk

entry: This little mummy Pokémon always balances on its golden ball. The ball is filled with gunpowder and can easily explode.
author: zerocipher

entry: POKENAME unleashes powerful punches with both physical and spectral hands. If one defeats a Machamp, it will take its belt as a trophy.
author: honeslty_vitali

entry: These Pokémon were the unyielding servants of ancient pharaohs, said to have the power to peer into the souls of others. Though their ancient masters have long passed, they continue to guard their tombs from thieves to this day.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will rampage ceaselessly if its slumber is disturbed. The flower around its neck was once regarded as symbolic of the sun.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: POKENAME are secretive Pokémon that can only be found in the tombs of long lost civilisations. They grow aggressive in anything other than pitch blackness and will attack explorers and archaeologists that try to explore their homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will often place itself next to coffins or altars. Hiding within its egg-shaped shell, it poses as an urn and enjoys scaring mourners.
author: rihse

entry: POKENAME quietly stands outside of the structures it has predicted to be robbed from. Once the robbers it foresaw appear before it, it places a curse that eventually turns them into mummies.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME guard ancient tombs by grabbing onto intruders with an ethereal hand and escorting them out. Prolonged contact with a POKENAME causes hallucinations of hands appearing from the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These Pokémon are born from abandoned pots and planters of ancient civilizations. They guard their homes with their ghostly powers and will often try to drag their foes into their bodies using their singular, shadowy hand.
author: infinex21

entry: It is supposedly the reincarnation of an ancient pharaoh, but it's actually just a subspecies of Slowking interested in Egyptology. It is afflicted with a pharaoh's curse, however.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Incredibly defensive of its mask, POKENAME will grab at anyone who dares touch it. The weight of its headpiece makes it incapable of sustained flight.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME possess the golden funerary statues of a long-gone civilisation and can animate them, bending them to their will. The statues were originally intended as guardians of the dead, but now POKENAME will attack anyone who comes near.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often choose to nest near graveyards and assume guard over the deceased residents. These cemeteries are amongst the safest in the world.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME lives in ruins and will leave some of its treasure exposed for an explorer to discover and carry away. It can appear from any of its stolen treasure, leading to many museums becoming dangerously infested with POKENAME.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME guards a hoard of relics from would-be grave robbers, as it is able to grapple multiple opponents with its coils and hands. It will only find rest if a relative of those it guards relieves it of duty.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a tyrant of mountain regions that considers itself an unbeatable ruler over its domain. It will crumble a mountain to powder and reshape it to fit its own tastes and ego, regardless of other creatures living within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME guards a hoard of relics from would-be grave robbers, as it is able to grapple multiple opponents with its coils and hands. It will only find rest if a relative of those it guards relieves it of duty.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It guards the resting place of ancient kings. Tomb raiders who enter this Pokémon's territory are eternally cursed to see it in their nightmares.
author: awiralonprime

entry: A once inanimate statue now haunted by a cursed scroll. It is said that anyone who deciphers the hieroglyphs will fall deathly ill.
author: ninjakraken

entry: Recruited by ancient psychics to guard tombs, POKENAME offer researchers lavish meals. If accepted, those with pure intentions are bonded with. Any grave robbers suffer terrible curses.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A lonesome spirit that mourns its death. It is supposedly the pet of a long-forgotten pharaoh.
author: theheroict

entry: It has been written that POKENAME has dominion over the dead. It can deduce whether one has a pure or sullied heart with its unusual abilities. Those who are deemed impure and near the end of their lives are attacked.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A vicious creature that punishes grave robbers by dragging them into a tomb to lay for eternity. It's found inside ancient pyramids.
author: theheroict

entry: Although there is no scientific evidence to support it, there are numerous researchers that believe the mask on POKENAME's stomach resembles the faces of humanity's earliest ancestors. Those who touch a POKENAME see flashes of an ancient landscape.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have 1,000 hands that writhe and wrap around their body, each hand splitting into a great multiplicity of fingers. Whenever they sense a tomb raider in their ruins, the shadowy hands rush to dispose of the intruder.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME disguises as a gold-plated crook to catch would-be grave robbers. It hooks them by the neck and drains them of their life force.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: In ancient times, the highest-ranking of pharaohs were granted POKENAME as the guardians of their tombs. Its thick golden armor is nigh impenetrable, and it is merciless in how it treats potential grave-robbers.
author: sk372

entry: Found residing inside ancient pyramids, POKENAME's cogs are infused with the spirits of mummies. It uses its body to operate traps and obstacles which it defends its grave with.
author: nexusshenanigans

entry: A cruel pharaoh's spirit possessed its old body, creating POKENAME. It utilizes shadow illusions in combat to confuse and conquer.
author: yoshimon

entry: Myths state this Pokémon is the spirit of a long dead dragon that has returned through possessing its treasures from its lifetime.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME dwell in abandoned buildings, avoiding Trainers. On nights with a full moon, they emerge to bathe in the moonlight, which slowly turns their skin to gold. Only when their bodies have transformed entirely to gold can they evolve.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME tempt unsuspecting tomb raiders into its domain with illusions of their desires.  Once enticed, POKENAME uses its ghostly limbs to squeeze the life force out of them.
author: teatedtiten

entry: It uses its shadow hands to grab its victims and prevent them from escaping, then flies away with them. Children who misbehave are told that if they don't behave, POKENAME will come and kidnap them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Archaeologists theorized that POKENAME's ghostly spores were imbued with the spirits of ancient royals. In reality, POKENAME uses its spores to absorb the souls of their prey before leaving the bodies as dried husks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hides under the floors of pyramids, waiting to ensnare any grave robber that comes through. While it struggles to keep its prisoners bound, its ghostly appearance and sharp teeth scare them away anyway.
author: soup1900

entry: Supposedly, it's an ancient security drone created by paranoid pharaohs. It emits high pitched frequencies when it spots an intruder before attacking.
author: theheroict

entry: A long-deceased defender of ancient waterways, POKENAME buries itself in the riverbed and waits for polluters. Its bite inflicts a deadly curse.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME resides in mountain tombs, protecting them from grave robbers. Should it encounter one, it will consume their soul and mummify their body.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME live as dancers for exceptionally rich citizens. When fed gold nuggets, their dance will become mesmerizing.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It performs ceremonial dances outside ancient tombs to honor the dead. It is said that if a graverobber attempts to rob the tomb, POKENAME will collapse the entrance, sealing the thief in with the dead for all eternity.
author: agentyoshi

entry: POKENAME's body is made of solid gold that is easily damaged. It'll lay a powerful curse on those who harm it or steal from it.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME deceives others with its cute and cuddly look. When its victims drop their guard, it grabs them with shadowy limbs, squeezing until their strength fades. Legends say it was born from the frustration of abandoned young Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is said that a sailor got lost at sea and had his soul trapped in a cursed anchor, creating a POKENAME. POKENAME lies dormant on the ocean floor, consuming the essence of human divers who stray close to it.
author: tyler059

entry: POKENAME judge the souls of those who have died. If they are pure, then they are guided to the afterlife. If they are corrupt, the souls become sand.
author: skymaster426

entry: Found in deserts, it is believed it contains the soul of a ruler from ancient times. It commands certain Pokémon to build its body.
author: houndrys.

entry: Some say that POKENAME contains remnants of the spirit of a Lycanroc that was worshipped as a deity in ancient times.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME guard ancient ruins and the treasures said to lay within them, wrapping would-be thieves in their bandage-like feelers. These feelers siphon their life force until their ghostly hand-like tail can drag them down into the underworld.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a statue inside jungle temples. When it senses a grave robber, it waits until they are incredibly close, before jumping out to scare them and psychically pushing them deeper into the shrine.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Archeologists discovered POKENAME in an ancient tomb many years ago. Under the blazing sun it appears to only be a clay sculpture, but during cool desert nights it's said that spirits can be found circled around it performing a long forgotten ritual.
author: kianjp2008

entry: POKENAME pilfers ancient tombs in search of artifacts to add to its collection of toys. It will lead treasure hunters to gold as long as it is promised a portion of the spoils in return.
author: skittytales

entry: During ancient times, these Pokémon were seen as the embodiments of gods in some regions. POKENAME's face is said to be permanently etched into the memory of anyone who sees it.
author: jangodiot

entry: It is said that POKENAME has had a hand in making several ancient Egyptian weddings. However, after the societal expansion of Egypt, the people gave up on it, hence why it is a Ghost-type now.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: POKENAME is very proud of its appearance, its shadowy hands constantly focused on polishing its shell until it shines. If anyone tries to interrupt this process, POKENAME will glare at them with an eerie grin before the shadows drag them away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME ambushes and poisons grave robbers. It rewards behaving Trainers with riches. Some of these riches are worth millions.
author: planatical

entry: Haunting shipwrecks of ages past, POKENAME at first appears as bejeweled empty shells. Once a diver turns their back the disembodied hands shoot forward, dragging their victim to its dagger-toothed maw.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is an evil spirit that has been encased in a man-made shell. POKENAME despises humans for trapping it.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME makes its home close to where buried treasure is located, protecting it through ghostly powers and gnashing claws. Pirates of old clashed with it often in their search for ill-gotten gains.
author: sk372

entry: Legends say that the spirits of ancient royalty slumber within POKENAME's shell. The shadowy tendrils that surround POKENAME have ensured that no humans have ever seen the insides of their shells.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME ambushes bird Pokémon by lurking with its head among treetops and ensnaring unobservant or curious prey when they land among its claws and webs. During storms, it ducks its head low and hides within foliage to avoid lightning strikes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The tongue extending from its mouth is made of tightly entwined silk. This sticky appendage helps it cling to surfaces and capture prey.
author: .izik

entry: It drills into solar panels and weaves webbing inside to absorb electricity. This behavior has caused issues at solar farms near mountain ranges.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is cloaked in translucent silk, and each vine is coated with nearly invisible webbing. These webs are both sticky and surprisingly strong.
author: .izik

entry: A tailor in Brussel Town designs elegant hats with its silk. These hats are popular during spring festivals for their lightweight feel.
author: .izik

entry: Its bright coloring is a warning to potential aggressors. If provoked, POKENAME can fly circles around its foes while using its surprisingly strong arms to strike.
author: sivanandi

entry: POKENAME bobs and sways rhythmically at baby Pokémon so that they copy its movements and follow it around. It lures them until they walk into its electric web, where its dance becomes more excited as it prepares to feast on them.
author: soup1900

entry: It loves turning into a power cord and plugging itself into an outlet, resulting in it consuming a lot of electricity. Trainers caring for POKENAME are advised to baby-proof their outlets to prevent this from happening.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME sets up a number of electrified webs at the edges of the lakes it inhabits. It spends much of its time submerged in water, but can sense the dispersal of electricity when something is caught in its webs, alerting it to a captured meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a distant relative of the extinct Kabutops. POKENAME uses its yellow fur on its small arms to conduct electricity to power up its Electric-type moves.
author: antonio_9onzalez

entry: These Pokémon love to use electricity and puffs of their flames to roast nuts and berries before eating them. The spikes along their backs often exude an intense heat that deters assailants.
author: infinex21

entry: The spiky fur along a POKENAME's back will crackle with electricity as it prepares to spew flames from its mouth. The webbing it can spew from its mouth is capable of channeling its flames without burning for many hours.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME form nets out of webbing when foraging to help them carry the berries they pick. They are fond of Magost Berries because of the sweet flavor inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A shop in Luxuria Town specializes in bug nets crafted from its web. These nets are popular for their durability and fine mesh.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME weaves its web atop tall buildings in an effort to catch Flying-type prey. As they absorb electricity, the webs act as natural protection against lightning strikes, so humans leave it be so long as its web does not get in the way.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It digs up power lines to chew on the insulation. This habit often causes electrical surges in rural areas.
author: .izik

entry: A weaver in Emeragrove Town creates socks from its silk. The socks are celebrated for their unique ability to repel static electricity.
author: .izik

entry: Its silk is laid over flowerbeds to suppress weed growth. Gardeners in small towns rely on it to protect their plants.
author: .izik

entry: The cotton-like tufts from POKENAME carry a faint static charge. These fibers cling to surfaces, aiding it in creating complex webs.
author: .izik

entry: The tip of its horn has tiny, wall-crawling legs. It suspends itself from ceilings before ambushing prey with an expertly aimed web.
author: .izik

entry: When it hatches, its mother uses web and honey to knit a toy that resembles a baby POKENAME. It carries the toy wherever it goes. The sweet scent of honey combined with how soft the toy is helps this timid Pokémon to calm down whenever it's stressed.
author: milchik

entry: These Bug-type Pokémon carry a hive made of silk webbing atop their backs, where their young will typically be restlessly crawling inside of. They typically sleep in caves, their slimy bodies helping them to stick to the ceiling.
author: infinex21

entry: It carries its young in the pouch on its belly. If there is nothing in its pouch, it will adopt and carry any Pokémon or Egg that will fit.
author: cait_sith

entry: It spins a large web and waits on it, luring in prey with the glittering gemstones on its head. Sometimes, humans get caught in the web, giving rise to the term "POKENAME's glimmer" as shorthand for something too good to be true.
author: hophoppip

entry: It flings webbing from its tail to ensnare foes. Once trapped, it shocks them with a powerful jolt of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: Its glowing eyes allow it to see perfectly in the dark, making nighttime raids on farm plots easy. It can strip an entire field of crops overnight.
author: .izik

entry: It hurls sticky balls of webbing at foes to ensnare them. Once immobilized, the prey is left vulnerable to its electric attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the tallest trees it can find. It connects itself to said trees and absorbs the nutrients that the tree takes up.
author: themicelegion

entry: To fight, POKENAME will rapidly circle around a foe, spinning electrified thread around them. When the foe is unable to move, POKENAME attacks them viciously with punches and kicks.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will only reveal their bug-like legs around their trusted Trainers. Using their multiple upper limbs, they weave their webbing into accessories for their friends. These accessories glow with a harmless electricity flowing through them.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME conceal their lower limbs beneath their skirt-like fur to avoid ridicule and scorn. They value loyalty and kindness before all else and will use their electric webs to protect any and all of their friends.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME fight using electric threads that flow from their elbows and by jabbing at foes with their large, lower limbs. By weaving together their electric webbing, they can craft defensive webs that repel many attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: A tailor in Nimbasa Town crafts hair ties using its silk. The ties are praised for their durability and soft texture.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its sturdy body to assist with electrical work in hurricane-prone areas. Its silk helps stabilize power lines and prevent outages.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are playful Bug-type Pokémon who use the large leg-like horns sprouting from their heads to move around. Their fur is charged with static electricity, which often startles most people and Pokémon when they first meet.
author: infinex21

entry: A seamstress in Vertress City makes raincoats with its silk, infused with its venom. The coats are waterproof and surprisingly resistant to damage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's electric webs are as sharp as steel, slicing through prey with ease. Pokémon who try to fly through the webs often end up being sliced into pieces.
author: soup1900

entry: Shops in Camelia Town use its silk to create durable skirts. The material is highly sought after for its strength and flexibility.
author: .izik

entry: It scales lit street signs along highways to absorb electricity. These nocturnal climbs often disrupt nearby lighting systems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a venomous bite, but it isn't dangerous unless you have an allergy. It taunts spider Pokémon by plucking at their webs with its feelers.
author: wigglypon

entry: It spends the entire day in place charging itself up with electricity. At night, it goes on a rampage with its swarm, feeding on any unlucky prey.
author: skymaster426

entry: A weaver in Astilbe Town uses its silk to craft protective vests. These vests are prized by miners for their durability and comfort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can attach itself to other living creatures or electrical devices to suck out all their energy within a very short time. It then jumps to a new host to repeat the process.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME like to nest in temples, where they are well received because they generate light at night and catch other Bug Pokémon. Some even believe that they keep evil spirits away with their radiant light.
author: chorb33

entry: It stands as a sentinel near shipping docks, throwing its web to secure drifting debris. Sailors trust it to keep waterways clear and safe.
author: .izik

entry: It weaves its web onto a ring so it can carry it around as it moves. It can catch bugs in the air with its web, using it like a net.
author: greystorm101

entry: Researchers have infrequently observed Pokémon climbing into the web created by POKENAME to sleep. These papers are often accompanied by a warning.
author: fixthewifi

entry: It spits webs onto foes using its beak, immobilizing them. It then unleashes a powerful Ember to roast its prey.
author: .izik

entry: The friction of its wings generates enough energy to create shocking webs. Its body becomes hot enough to engulf anyone who touches it in flames.
author: cheroace

entry: The legs on its head are used to weave silk into intricate patterns. These patterns are often admired for their artistic beauty.
author: .izik

entry: The electricity filling POKENAME's body makes it unable to sit still for long. Its webs always end up messy due to its short attention-span.
author: fouguri

entry: Its electric web keeps gears in power plants running smoothly. Engineers rely on its high conductivity and lightweight consistency.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are only found in dense jungles, building their nests high in the trees. They are capable of spitting toxic webbing to trap prey.
author: mepp.

entry: People have reported meeting POKENAME in the dark of moonless nights, the Pokémon willingly approaching the person and offering the bundle it carries. Dozens of its eggs are contained in these bundles of silk, hatching not long after the meeting.
author: _pixelar_

entry: It will attach itself to other Pokémon to gather electricity. Once charged, it ambitiously tries to snare its ride with webs, often unsuccessfully.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Electricians incorporate its silk into power lines for tall buildings. The material's incredible strength ensures long-lasting stability.
author: .izik

entry: Having grown beyond its icy shell, a POKENAME is reborn as an unnerving creature. Most are unable to stand its sight for long.
author: mx_wellman

entry: It's said to manipulate ghostly forces with its many eyes. Researchers have discarded electromagnetism as the explanation for its floating.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME lies in wait for prey to stumble into its electrified webs. It is perceptive, and hears exactly when it must swoop down and finish the job.
author: nellnast42

entry: It fires large globs of webbing coated in Stun Spore at foes. This tactic paralyzes prey, allowing it to capture them with ease.
author: .izik

entry: It spreads its sticky silk across the water's surface to reel in floating ship debris. It will eat debris regardless of what it is.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits massive webs charged with electricity to ensnare prey like Corsola. Once caught, it drags them into caves to feed alone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are fiercely protective of those they consider family. Using their tails, they spin electrically charged webs to slow foes or create shocking barriers around those they guard.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME spin their yarn while dancing and singing a song, the thread reflecting the beauty and skill of the melody. Woven into expensive clothes or carpets, the yarn retains its vivid coloring, ranging from a royal blue to a dark thundercloud black.
author: _pixelar_

entry: It spits webs at lightposts to climb closer to the light source. After reaching the top, it rubs its snout against the bulb, absorbing its heat and energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carries with it a crystal charged with electricity. If not for the protective webbing the Pokémon covers it in, it would fry everything around it.
author: atlas3339098

entry: A merchant in Daybreak Town crafts scarves from its silk. The scarves are known for their soft texture and ability to retain warmth.
author: .izik

entry: Though it appears stone-like, its exterior is composed of tightly woven silk. This silk is remarkably resilient against physical attacks.
author: .izik

entry: It channels its electric power through its pendulum. The charged pendulum emits a faint glow, entrancing nearby foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores electrical energy in the fur on its arms. In combat, it will clamp onto its opponents with its powerful pincers, then shock them with over 15,000 volts of electricity.
author: mistymagius

entry: When transforming into an enemy, the vines on its body pulsate rhythmically. This motion redirects nutrients and fluids to aid in its transformation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sticks to the ceiling of damp caves, absorbing nutrients. It drops on water types, wrapping its arms around them to drain water for food.
author: thybrodiebyronbrown

entry: Its wings are immeasurably strong as they are able to keep POKENAME airborne despite its metal exterior. The barbs hanging from its stomach can extend to club opponents below it.
author: evilgammon

entry: Adventurers trying to catch a POKENAME must always watch above to avoid getting rained on by sharp spikes from POKENAME. When injured, they use their feelers to absorb nutrients until there are none left in the area.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME hunts by latching onto prey with the three prehensile claws on its tail. Once it gets a grip, it then uses its tail to savagely impale its victim on the sharp spines on its back.
author: .onionpug

entry: POKENAME's spines are very sharp and able to channel its electric energy. Even the sturdiest of Rock, Ground or Steel-type Pokémon wouldn't be able to endure a direct shock once its spines pierced into them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the spikes on its tail to climb more easily on any surface. It swoops down from above with agility to steal the caps of unsuspecting passersby, then runs away laughing.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Wild POKENAME often crawl along cave ceilings like Aipom on jungle gyms. In battle, they dig their metal claws into their opponent and strike them with a strong Headbutt.
author: infinex21

entry: The thorn on the top of its head holds the most nutrients. When ground up, it is used in the creation of X Attack and X Accuracy supplements.
author: .izik

entry: The metal tips of its tail-like vines pulsate with magnetic energy. When disturbed, it releases a powerful Thunder Shock to deter threats.
author: .izik

entry: Despite POKENAME's size and weight, it is incredibly acrobatic. Its steely thorn-tipped limbs allow it to swing and attach to all sorts of places; it can even resist being blown away in a hurricane.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The ends of POKENAME's tails are closed buds. In spring, they bloom into beautiful yellow flowers.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME latches onto the ceilings of caves and ambushes Pokémon that pass below. Despite this aggressive behaviour, its battles are playful, and it often heals foes with berries it grows itself.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME can inflate its body outwards, allowing its thorn-like protrusions to form a shield. Thanks to this, it is incredibly risky to attack.
author: p0opys0ck123abc

entry: Deep within caves, POKENAME lies in wait for lost prey to stumble into its spiked body. Once ensnared, escape is nearly impossible, as it can only be harmed by striking its exposed feelers.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: The metallic object attached to its vine resembles a spinning top. It coordinates its attacks with the top's movements, using the momentum to enhance its strikes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its mace-like tail to ferociously crush foes. It follows up a blow from its tail with furious slashing until the foe stops moving.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME sinks its five spiked feelers into cave walls to absorb nutrients. When threatened, it lashes them to defend itself. If exhausted or badly injured, it emerges outside to bask in sunlight, healing through photosynthesis as it sleeps.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The long, tail-like vine protruding from its rear can be wielded like a whip to dispatch foes. Its precision and power make it a fearsome weapon.
author: .izik

entry: If trespassers enter its territory, it transforms into their likeness. While they are confused, it attacks with a flurry of barbed spikes, forcing them to flee.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in gloomy caves, attached to the ceiling. If a careless visitor enters its territory, it suddenly drops down and abducts them.
author: chorb33

entry: The tips of its vine-like legs are magnetized, allowing it to attach to metallic surfaces. This adaptation gives it an advantage in industrial environments.
author: .izik

entry: If startled, a POKENAME will wrap its vines around its foe and torch them with its flaming limbs. Its steel shell was once used to make cookware.
author: staghorn

entry: It sleeps near jungle ruins, defending the tombs of ancient rulers. Its vinelike arms can extend up to 40 feet, delivering devastating punches to intruders.
author: .izik

entry: While resting, it extends its vines to nearby tree limbs, hanging high above the forest floor. If disturbed, it unleashes a Fire Spin to trap its foe before escaping.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pulls itself taut in a Y shape and waits. When it sees prey, it launches itself headfirst and bites down with enough force to break bone.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME hides among the trees, silently observing those who traverse its territory. Those it takes a disliking to are pelted with hard metallic spheres it creates from its hands and hurls down from up high.
author: sk372

entry: Sailors hate wild POKENAME, and for good reason. Bringing a ship within its territory nearly guarantees a damaged or even broken hull.
author: sivanandi

entry: Using the metal it gathers and its own spines, POKENAME creates a giant spiked wheel. It uses said wheel to fight from afar or block attacks.
author: hexx_vixtar

entry: When POKENAME grinds its teeth, it fires steel spikes from its body. POKENAME uses its psychic powers to control the spikes' trajectory.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME leaves Spikes and Stealth Rock around it everywhere to damage any opponent who tries to near it. Once they're weakened, POKENAME slashes its spiked vines at the opponent to finish them off.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME possess a steel shell that leaves them nearly impervious to harm. The weight of the shell makes their movements cumbersome, but tendrils that sprout from their back help them to navigate even the roughest terrain.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can extend its iron vines upwards, to clamp onto cave ceilings. Upon pulling itself upwards, it can proceed to burrow vertically, making this Pokémon exceptional at rescuing people who have been trapped in cave-ins.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME anchors itself to cave ceilings with its spiked tail tendrils, the peridot shards in its head and belly glowing in rhythmic pulses. Unsuspecting prey are lulled by its hypnotic moves before being shredded by a sudden rain of iron spikes.
author: potato_tub

entry: The plant-like maces it wields are adorned with platinum spikes. Using its telekinetic powers, it throws and redirects them with incredible accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon uses its many spiky tendrils to clamber across walls, floors, and ceilings. When it's in the right place, it strikes.
author: houndrys.

entry: The thorny bush growing from its neck produces sweet and nutritious berries. Pastry chefs in Snowpoint City use these berries to craft exquisite tarts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in dark areas, hiding away in corners to avoid contact with others. The only exception is lost children, who find themselves guided to safety by the light of POKENAME's candle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roam around old gravesites, licking everything in the area, from gravestones to nearby trees, and even the dirt it walks on. If someone is licked by their waxy tongue, the victim will feel deeply and unnaturally unsettled, even its Trainer.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Whenever POKENAME gets emotional, it erupts into an inferno. Witnessing the explosion is said to be soul-altering. POKENAME is an endangered species.
author: king_creepsta

entry: It flits through forests, lighting the path for lost hikers. This is not an act of kindness, as POKENAME lure hikers into their nests.
author: kandyman

entry: Its wax body rivals volcanic lava in heat and lethality. In battle, it blows out intense violet flames that leech the life force of anything it burns.
author: h0bojoe

entry: This Pokémon has been known to lurk around places where the recently departed rest. It is believed to linger in the area of ghosts to soothe their unrest.
author: pastelxlost

entry: Because of the perpetual flame in its stomach, POKENAME are always hungry. They can eat for days on end and still feel like they're starving.
author: blitzydragon

entry: POKENAME lures its prey with flickering flames. Its eerie glow and insatiable hunger make it a feared predator in murky waters.
author: anarchaz

entry: Lone POKENAME fly around listlessly, constantly looking for a flock. Flocks of POKENAME prefer to nest in warm, dry places. They eat very little, so one area can have many of them at once.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME's flame on their head flickers softly to lure Bug-type Pokémon into their webbing. POKENAME stop their prey from struggling by injecting them with a potent venom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flicker the flames on their back to lure prey into their webs. If their prey attempts to break out of the webbing, POKENAME light their webbing on fire to prevent escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The flaming plume of a POKENAME is the spirits animating and melting itswax body. The more passionate the spirit is, the faster its body melts.
author: geo_ominous

entry: While the flame on a POKENAME's head serves as a channel for draining vital energy, inexperienced POKENAME tend to emit it instead.
author: tuneless.towa

entry: If one sees a light bouncing in the distance while exploring a dark abandoned locale, it is likely to be a POKENAME prancing about. It can inhale large breaths to flare up its flame, but only for a short time before it gets winded.
author: sk372

entry: The bodies of POKENAME constantly drip wax wherever they roost. It is said that POKENAME only evolve once all of their wax has melted away.
author: geo_ominous

entry: Many urban residents loathe POKENAME because it drips hot wax onto cars and roofs while floating. Its wax is notoriously difficult to scrub off, often requiring the use of metal scratchers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: If a POKENAME still has gills, it is young. After a few years, the light on its head burns away and the gills light. This is a special moment in POKENAME's life, marking the transition away from youth.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If a POKENAME still has gills, it is young. After a few years, the light on its head burns away and the gills light. This is a special moment in POKENAME's life, marking the transition to adulthood.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sleep during the day to gather sunlight to fuel their psychic flames. Staring at the flame for too long will put you under its control.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flies around ancient gravesites, pecking at those who wander too close to its hidden nest. Some believe it is a guard of those who recently departed.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient royal customs called for POKENAME's pearls to be placed on deceased rulers. The heated necklace was believed to guide their souls safely to the afterlife.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generate a waxy substance inside their shell to fuel their flame. Harvesting POKENAME wax to make prayer candles or waterproof boats is a traditional industry in many coastal cities.
author: jacknerik

entry: Many Trainers use it to light up dark caves instead of Litwick, as POKENAME can light up larger spaces. It guides lost Houndour to safety.
author: dodoowner_

entry: As its body is made of wax, it can squeeze through any crack. The flame that blazes on its tail is said to bring disaster to anyone who touches it.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME instinctually seek out a master to train with. The position is unenviable, as they are known to be demanding, capricious students with little control over the fire on their bodies.
author: dylonk25

entry: When it spins rapidly, its limbs fling hot melted wax that singe targets. Those burned by the wax are said to be marked by POKENAME, so that it can find them and drain their life force no matter where they go.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME search for Kasib Berries near graveyards or haunted manors to help protect themselves against other Ghost-type Pokémon. They spend hours in front of mirrors to check if the fire on their head is still lit.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The purple flames that POKENAME emits are supposedly impossible to extinguish, and burn until there is nothing left of the ignited object.
author: chorb33

entry: The melting wax that comprises its body exceeds 1,100 degrees Fahrenheit. Whenever it exhales, purple embers capable of burning spirits are released.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME lives in haunted locales, coming to the side of any frightened explorer and offering them its candle as a light in the darkness. Holding the candle provides physical and emotional warmth, making it easier to brave the spooky surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: Guiding with its eerie light, POKENAME saps life from its unsuspecting followers. It wanders mountains, luring challengers with its sinister flame.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME form within long-abandoned power plants, drawing energy from derelict machines and engines. Engineers decommissioning these facilities often report eerie blue lights deep in the dark corridors and halls.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gems at the base of POKENAME's body were once ground by apothecaries and used to boil potions. Brews made this way were said to be incredibly potent.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever POKENAME's candle arms are fully lit, it begins rapidly draining the life energy of everything around it until its arms melt. It rebuilds itself by hunting wild Litwick.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Wild POKENAME often hide in trees outside city perimeters and leech off the life force of any passerby. Both its flames and its confidence grow the more life it steals.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME hunts by flinging scalding wax at unsuspecting prey from atop high tree branches. If the wax is ineffective, it will opt to leech as much life force as it can and flee.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME hunts by flinging scalding wax at unsuspecting prey from atop high tree branches. If the wax is ineffective, it will opt to leech as much life force as it can and flee.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It claims forests by coating the trees with its life-draining wax. The trees passively leech the life off all passersby for POKENAME, granting it extra strength and weaker prey.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME has a flickering purple flame atop its head that lights up whenever its happy and in a playful mood. It can ignite small sparks and flames, using its fire to spread its cheerful spirit.
author: thepandasharky

entry: Lit with everlasting flames, POKENAME leads stray humans and Pokémon to their doom. It leaves waxy trails behind as it goes.
author: _sadfroggy

entry: POKENAME capture swamp gas in their waxy bodies, protecting the precious fuel from the water as they dive beneath the surface. The gas burns an eerie blue, making them glow. When they surface, POKENAME emit a ghostly flame.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME capture swamp gas in their waxy bodies, protecting the precious fuel from the water as they dive beneath the surface. The gas burns an eerie blue, making them glow. When they surface, POKENAME emit a ghostly flame.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lurk along the edges of swamps and quagmires, their bodies burning an unearthly purple in the gloom. They use their lights to lure travellers off the safe paths through their homes, getting the hapless people stuck.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The flames of wild POKENAME burn without heat, creating an eerie purple inferno in the swamps. Their flames burn higher and stronger when they can feed on confusion and fear, and they aim to terrify travellers passing by.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are given to modern-day nobles to serve as servants. These Pokémon play with other Ghost-type Pokémon when they aren't working!
author: skleegamer

entry: POKENAME is sensitive to living beings. Their energy causes it to slowly melt. For this reason, it scares others away from its home using magnetic fields.
author: salt

entry: Now that it has a second brain, it starts pursuing life force. However, this makes its flame burn much brighter, slowing it down considerably. It can detect life force from 60 miles away.
author: salt

entry: POKENAME are generally stuck to the ground due to their melted body. They attract their prey using the light on their head, which they now control using their psyche.
author: salt

entry: Many POKENAME dwell in ancient treasure vaults, illuminating the space with haunting flames. Their bodies are said to contain the souls of treasure hunters who perished nearby.
author: .izik

entry: During evolution, the heat from its candle is contained. This allows its waxy body to solidify.
author: jpeggio

entry: Its fiery jaw has a mind of its own and will chomp at anything to consume its victims' souls. Despite this, the main body is oddly friendly and wanders toward Trainers it likes.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is said that eating food cooked over a POKENAME's flame will cause you to have vivid dreams of ancient, prehistoric oceans.
author: staghorn

entry: As POKENAME floats through graveyards, wax drips from its body, marking its trail. In ancient cultures, the wax was seen as a curse and was strictly avoided.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hollow body is encased in a brittle, wax-like shell. Its cries echo eerily from within its chest.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME wanders throughout the night, wax and stray embers drop from its body. The embers do not start fires, instead draining energy from the surrounding area before slowly floating back to and being absorbed by POKENAME's gate.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's wax was once used by royalty as sealing wax due to its high melting point, which allowed it to adhere to important documents for extended periods.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its appearance, the wax of POKENAME is quite durable. When angry, its flames will burn twice as fast, so it must replenish the wax frequently.
author: darxer_

entry: During sandstorms, POKENAME brightens its flaming violet wings to appear as a guiding light. In reality, it is leading its victims into a trap so it can absorb their life force.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The ghostly energy surrounding POKENAME is actually a thin electrical field that is prickly to the touch. When alarmed, its large eyes will brighten like flashlights.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME burn with a far more intense flame than their unfused counterparts. The ghostly flame is difficult for them to control and forces them to drain energy from the surrounding area to sustain it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon has been known to change the shape of its hat, as the wax is warm enough to be malleable. The shape won't stay for long though - heat from the flame will melt it back to its drooped shape.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME happily clutches its gathered keys, but its waxy limbs cannot hold them for long, eventually dripping to the ground. It panics and scrambles to pick them back up to calm itself, starting the cycle anew.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's wax tends to melt extremely fast, resulting in its eyes being covered up. It'll rub its face against nearby surfaces to then scrape it off.
author: typhloquil

entry: A highly intelligent Pokémon, POKENAME uses the lore surrounding Latios to entice curious Pokémon and humans to approach. It then keeps them close by displaying a docile nature, but all the while, its eerie purple flame saps their life force.
author: arcul

entry: POKENAME pretends to be a forest guide, tricking its prey into following it. Being near its flames slowly burns away one's will to fight, allowing POKENAME to attack unimpeded.
author: mepp.

entry: Legend says one can have their wish granted by blowing out POKENAME's candles on their birthday. This is untrue, and generally just causes the POKENAME distress.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The heat from its body causes the newly formed wax to melt. Due to this, it is constantly in immense agony.
author: jpeggio

entry: POKENAME lies in wait for prey to fall into its maw. It then snaps its jaws shut and cooks its prey with flames fueled by the victim's own life force.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: It hunts with flaming wings fueled by the life force of others. Should its fuel run out, hunting becomes nearly impossible, often leading to starvation.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are playful, almost childlike Pokémon that help guide those who lost their lives at sea to the afterlife. Their purple scales shine at night.
author: yoshimon

entry: POKENAME can be found floating eerily motionless in abandoned factories, dripping wax onto the floor. Somehow, it never completely melts away.
author: dylonk25

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME's waxy gears harden completely. Upon waking, it must heat its body quickly to begin rotating once more.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaves waxy footprints wherever it walks. It uses its fire to lead travelers astray and feed on their life force; the larger and brighter the flames on its head and body, the more recently it has fed.
author: alestrius

entry: This Pokémon drifts gently through the air, drawn to negative feelings. Its flame grows larger and brighter the stronger the surrounding emotions are.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME spend their days buried just under the surface of the sand, their flames creating a heat shimmer in the desert that fools travellers into thinking there is an oasis around them. They strike out at anyone that falls for their ruse.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swarm out of caves at sunset, their flaming heads lighting up the evening sky. Tourists gather from afar to witness the dazzling display.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have waxy bodies that are pliable and unpleasant to the touch. Their bodies are cold, a result of their eerie ability to siphon the life energies of Pokémon and people around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME floats eerily in old abandoned mansions, a melted wax core within flickering flames. Should it meet a Trainer, the flames will mold the wax into a facsimile of the human's face, twisted in an expression of fear.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scales the walls of ancient tombs using its wax-covered feet. The wax it spits is hot enough to rival lava.
author: .izik

entry: After consuming large amounts of malachite, POKENAME's waxy body hardens, and it enters a deep slumber. Its flames dim to avoid detection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appears to be fossilized remains reanimated by haunted candle wax. With every breath it flares up a flickering flame from its nose; the larger the flame, the more aggressive its current mood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME waves its waxy wings in slow, elegant dances. If one listens closely, a soft lyre melody seems to accompany its movements from an unknown source.
author: .izik

entry: A friendly creature of the night, POKENAME has trouble finding homes due to the stench it emanates being akin to burning refuse. It mostly finds company in small insects drawn to its flames and its odor.
author: sk372

entry: Using the flames on its head, it lures unsuspecting prey in whilst draining its energy. Once a victim is weak enough, it swallows them whole.
author: hypernovahusky

entry: It guides Pokémon though the ocean, draining their life force all the while. When the Pokémon passes away, POKENAME consumes their corpse.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's ethereal body glows like a smoldering fire, and its head leaks melted wax. In clearings burned by a wildfire, it leaves long trails of wax as it wanders amongst the charred trees.
author: pattybgoode

entry: The putrid smell POKENAME emits is worsened by the fire atop its head. It is aware of this and will extinguish its flame until needed in battle.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME flies in the skies singing a harmonious melody. Its song draws other Pokémon in, and it absorbs the life force out of them.
author: deciduowl

entry: Bug-type Pokémon lured by the flames on POKENAME's antennae are trapped in the trail of melted wax it leaves behind. POKENAME returns later to feed on their life force.
author: potatoforged

entry: As it travels, it leaves a trail of wax which soon hardens. Those who walk on the trail have their vitality slowly drained by the POKENAME up ahead.
author: wigglypon

entry: Its skin secretes a waxy substance, which it can fling in globs to immobilize prey. POKENAME then drains the life force of its helpless victim.
author: wigglypon

entry: Litwick's ghostly flame caused the mysterious energy coursing through Regice to ignite upon fusion, leaving POKENAME constantly melting.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME trains by performing acrobatic leaps from gravestone to gravestone, leaving behind waxy footprints with every landing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are difficult to get rid of because they can be observed absorbing things typically incompatible with their body. Their ability to absorb water and fire fascinates scientists, even if they cannot do both at the same time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: According to folklore, POKENAME was formed when the last flicker of a candle was imbued with a wandering spirit. Its waxy body can reshape itself to mimic various candle designs, making it nearly indistinguishable from ordinary objects.
author: rakunk

entry: When they're bout to die, POKENAME will be seen melting wax all over lawns, streets, and gardens. They do this as their wax acts as seeds to grow new POKENAME.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its skin is quite permeable, so its body is at risk of drying up in the sun. To protect it during the day, it secretes a thick wax and coats itself.
author: hophoppip

entry: Its waxy coating protects its skin from the heat of its flames. It absorbs human life force as easily as water.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is only spotted at night near volcanic areas, casting ethereal smoke from its flames. It must feed quickly, as its waxy body will harden and become immobile if outside its shell for too long.
author: sk372

entry: Merchants across the region prize POKENAME for its fragrant, clean-burning wax. A single candle made from its body can keep a room smelling like sweet lavender for over a week.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME uses its excess life energy to create a ghostly liquid that is kept in the wax dish on top of its head. When it spots a human, it mischievously tips this dish over to spill the ghostly fluid over their heads.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME use their caustic wax to dissolve and digest anything they eat. Anything not easily digested by their wax is fully consumed by the flame tongue.
author: entomoxie

entry: To keep the flames inside its body burning, it absorbs the life energy of humans and Pokémon alike. POKENAME uses its psychic powers to implant false memories into people's minds so they'll trust it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can shine their ghostly fire even in murky depths. The whiskers are sensitive to any souls drifting by.
author: entomoxie

entry: It appears to people seeking warmth on cold nights with clear skies. Those drawn to its gentle heat may have their souls slowly drained.
author: hophoppip

entry: At night, POKENAME wander through forests seeking companionship. However, their loud noises and bright glow scare off most potential friends.
author: gileme__

entry: When POKENAME is awake, it burns through life energy rapidly. Therefore, it spends most of its time asleep, only waking to feed on the life force of whoever comes too close.
author: calelian

entry: Despite its body being made of wax, it is incredibly strong. The wax hardens as it trains through exercise, operating eerily similar to muscle tissue.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: This Pokémon is notoriously difficult to pin down due to the wax that makes up its body. Once POKENAME has pinned a foe into submission, it absorbs their mass into its wax body, allowing the wick on its head to burn brighter and longer.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When danger is present, POKENAME easily withdraws its waxy body into its shell, leaving the flame at the opening as a protective ward. When a group of POKENAME play, they tend to get stuck together and need help disentangling their wax.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME floats in dangerous bogs with the haunting glow of its ears and tail acting as a lure for unaware prey it can leech life force from. It will lead lost children out of its swampy habitat unharmed, though it is unknown why it helps them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME zip through city streets spinning, accidentally scattering stray flames in their excitement. Their erratic movements frequently set dry structures ablaze, as they cannot fully control their purple flames.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's waxy body slowly melts off over its lifetime. You can determine a POKENAME's age from how skinny it is.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME can launch flame jets or molten wax from the cannons protruding from its shell. The arms and legs seem to be formed from a mixture of its wax and the flaming ectoplasm, hardening into limbs it can manipulate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's body is made of ethereal flames produced by a wax-like core. Should something douse the main fire, the core will jump to one of the other flames and flee until it fully ignites.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's flame flickers brighter when it gazes into someone's dream. It gleefully devours bad dreams, savoring the fear.
author: .izik

entry: While a POKENAME is able to produce incredible amounts of fire, it tries to hold back to avoid melting its smaller head. It balances the smaller head carefully, often spinning backwards to correct itself while floating.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's bladelike arms are made of fragile glass. When enraged, it superheats them and flings molten shards to burn foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to appear to those grieving a recent loss, offering a comforting yet unsettling presence. Some believe the Pokémon guides lost souls, while others fear it leads them into the depths of their sorrow.
author: rakunk

entry: A glowing, molten wax ethereally floats within the translucent horns of POKENAME. Urban legend says that whoever sees the lights of a POKENAME on a cold night will soon die.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When happy, POKENAME's tail glows with intense light. Its mane dances like fire but remains cool to the touch.
author: .izik

entry: As it gathers the energy to evolve from a pupa, it begins glowing from within. Groves of dozens of glowing POKENAME are an eerie sight at night.
author: sporkwizard

entry: If one wanders too close to their nest, groups of POKENAME will use their enchanting lights to lure the hapless traveler deep into the woods instead.
author: sporkwizard

entry: POKENAME were once used to deliver letters, their glowing flames helping them to be found even in the darkest of nights. Flocks of POKENAME still reside in abandoned rookeries to this day.
author: geo_ominous

entry: The flame visible inside POKENAME is powered by its life force. Strong emotions make it flare brightly. In battle, POKENAME uses this flame to create powerful Ghost and Fire attacks.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME has no concept of rest; its bright face keeps it alert at all times. It is rumored that it only lives on the sea floor to escort drowned souls.
author: thistleblower

entry: POKENAME roosting in forests are often mistaken for gas streetlamps at night, leading travelers astray. When spooked, POKENAME can fly off at Mach 2, leaving lost travelers in the dark.
author: geo_ominous

entry: POKENAME's light emits a faint illumination that other Rattata find irresistible, flocking after the hypnotic light. Trainers have begun using it to lure out pests from areas with rodent infestations.
author: sk372

entry: Contrary to superstition that it appears when someone is about to die, POKENAME is carefree and mostly harmless. Found in marshlands, it lounges, keeping a watchful eye over the evening antics of younger Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Mysterious flames burn from within the nearly flat faces of POKENAME, creating a glow beneath them as light reflects off their caps. They float around ancient caves, illuminating runes of civilizations lost to time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hangs from cave ceilings by hidden threads. As it dreams, the flame within pulses rapidly, casting strange shadows.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is composed of molten glass. It slithers up cave walls to sleep in safety, far from creatures that dwell on the ground.
author: .izik

entry: After howling, POKENAME's paws glow with a bright violet light. This glow boosts its speed, allowing it to swiftly chase down prey.
author: .izik

entry: It constantly creates purple flames in its body. These cause a pale light, which POKENAME can radiate evenly using the lampshade on its head.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's large, metallic antlers heat up when someone enters its hidden glade. It only lowers its guard if it senses kindness in their heart.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can launch four simultaneous streams of fire from its torso that can leave ghastly burns on those hit. While mildly aggressive, offering it fresh milk will placate it for a time.
author: sk372

entry: Those that gaze into a POKENAME's flames will find themselves transfixed as they hear whispers of odd incantations. Rumors say that those that stare for too long will find themselves surrounded by a POKENAME's cloak, becoming a POKENAME themselves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses its thick vines to shield its delicate lanterns during battle. The lights constantly shift position to avoid incoming attacks.
author: .izik

entry: It absorbs the spirits of the fallen to fuel the baleful fire in its arms. The fireballs it launches from them incinerate body and soul, leaving nothing behind.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are highly skilled necromancers, capable of bending life and death energy to their will. It is said that befriending one can grant eternal life.
author: klgb76

entry: Within the body of POKENAME, the spirit of a deceased fighter burns, but its small stature limits its combat ability to heated tackles.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME lingers around the feeble, wicking away their spirits as they pass on. It uses them to fuel the fire in its belly.
author: _sadfroggy

entry: POKENAME burns with a fierce glow, a spectral candle in its head that can illuminate a wide area. Known for its fighting instincts, it charges at foes with blazing ghostly attacks, igniting the battlefield in its wake.
author: thepandasharky

entry: Now fully embracing its fighting spirit, POKENAME soars from target to target in battle, striking them down in a single kick and absorbing their life force to heal its wounds.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME rests below downspouts after a heavy rain, as the water bounces off its dome-shaped head like a rain drum. Each drop creates an ethereal ring, forming a melody that is rumored to awaken the dead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is incredibly delicate; one careless touch can shatter it. It remains motionless unless fully prepared for danger.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon floats around, collecting energy from living beings. They are attracted to other POKENAME due to their strong magnetic powers.
author: salt

entry: Having broken free from containment, the souls within the flaming form of POKENAME now seek to grow their numbers. They have a distinct hatred for lanterns or similar structures, rapidly superheating them until they burst to free the flames inside.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Some have claimed to have seen POKENAME appear to their loved ones the night before they passed. However, this is purely superstition.
author: jpeggio

entry: POKENAME has evolved a transparent dome at the front of its body, through which its inner flame can be seen. In the darkness of the ocean, POKENAME uses this flame to lure its prey and to absorb their spirits.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME leaps through treetops with fiery agility. It roasts Nanab Berries over its tail before eating them mid-jump.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appears at the sites of concluded battles to collect the spirits of fallen soldiers. They shine brilliantly during wartime.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Faintly glowing as they drift through the night, POKENAME are always on the hunt for a worthy opponent. They strike on sight, as if resuming a battle that they never got to finish.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It mimics the voice of the last spirit it absorbed to lure prey into the desert. A mute POKENAME, one that has never taken a life, has yet to be discovered.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It can sense when the life of a living being is fading thanks to its spectral ribbons. When POKENAME encounters dying creatures, it makes the flame on its head shine to bring peace to their final moments.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME darts through swamps with incredible speed. Its head flashes in short bursts, hoping to catch the attention of a mate.
author: .izik

entry: When frightened, the black wax on POKENAME's head melts rapidly. It scatters the wax behind it to slow pursuers while fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: Many ghost light sightings in tunnels are thanks to POKENAME. The deeper these Pokémon go, the brighter they burn their lights. Many tunneling crews assign employees one in case of electrical failure.
author: ghostslythe

entry: In deep-sea caves, POKENAME raises its small lantern to guide lost scuba divers toward safety. Its light is soft but reliable.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to abandoned castle walls after collecting forgotten keys. It lights up every night, hoping to return them to owners who never come.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME defends its abandoned hotel home with fiery claw swipes. It uses bursts of Smog to disorient and trap unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: Several POKENAME will form a trail to lead lost travellers further into the desert. They then wait for the victim to pass on to absorb their spirit.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME's wingbeats kick up heat hazes that cause weary travelers to faint. It then feeds on their spirits to further fuel its flames.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: POKENAME prefers dark rooms, where it floats motionlessly in the shadows slowly rotating. People who stumble upon it are often frightened, as all they see are its glowing eyes staring back at them in the dark.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's gear-like base rotates slowly while its head glows purple. The sudden flash can briefly stun foes during battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats through abandoned castle courtyards in the evening, its lantern dimly glowing. Staring too long at its light is said to bring terrible luck for the rest of the night.
author: .izik

entry: The flame inside POKENAME burns hotter as it sleeps, causing the goo encasing it to bubble and shimmer with heat.
author: .izik

entry: A shy Pokémon that nevertheless does not stray too far from others; it must be in proximity to another to feast on their fear, and, rarely, their life energy. It is thought that only when they devour enough fear that POKENAME evolves further.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME dangles from pine trees in deep forests, its purple flame flickering. Travelers often mistake them for ghost lights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tusks burn with violet flame, which it uses to carve symbols into trees. These glowing marks warn others of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rests deep in desert caves. While sleeping, the light in its abdomen glows faintly, giving off gentle warmth.
author: .izik

entry: It appears to those who get lost at night, beckoning them to follow it to the afterlife. POKENAME will take them there by force if they decline.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME's tail orb glows deep violet while biting down on a foe. As its grip tightens, the glow intensifies to a piercing brightness.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has a grisly attraction to humans about to pass away. It stalks lost hikers to freeze and absorb the souls of its poor victims.
author: tr3bles

entry: POKENAME consumes airborne pollutants to fuel its fiery attacks. If the flames become too hot, however, POKENAME's glass body will start to melt, causing it to become deformed and misshapen.
author: mistymagius

entry: Lampent's iron body made for the perfect casing for POKENAME upon fusion, allowing it to control the ghostly flame inside it without melting. However, its full power still remains untapped.
author: phantom640

entry: The flame on POKENAME's shell changes color based on its diet. Consuming sulfur can turn its fire into a radiant golden hue.
author: .izik

entry: Its body glows with a light that attracts large swarms of nocturnal insects. Those that approach have their vitality rapidly drained by the POKENAME.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME wants to be helpful to travelers that find themselves lost among dark caverns by helping illuminate their surroundings. Its tendency to suddenly appear from beneath the ground near people tends to startle them, though.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME haunts abandoned hotels, using its bright glow to stun intruders. While they recover, it silently steals their valuables.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's constant bouncing pumps air into its flame chambers to keep its fires burning. Besides oxygen, the fires are also fueled by the life energy of plants, Pokémon, and people.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME carries a pair of spirits in its hands that emit ghastly moans to frighten its foes. In combat, it releases them to aid it by keeping an opponent distracted so it can get in close and deliver a decisive flurry of punches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is most frequently seen in cities with canals, where it supposedly leads recently deceased souls out of the city and into the afterlife. The material of the shell is incredibly dense, especially in contrast to its glass face and belly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's singular purple orb will start flashing if someone who is nearing death is nearby. It then wraps around them with its tentacles and doesn't let go until they pass on.
author: soup1900

entry: Groups of POKENAME are seen swimming near the sites of water disasters. The ghostly tail gets larger over time, and urban legends say it increases in size with the amount of souls POKENAME has eaten.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME battles by blasting repeated fireballs from its cannons. It is a tradition in South Galar to leave bristly poles around graveyards as this Pokémon enjoys cleaning its shell against them and becomes docile afterwards.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Curiously this Pokémon only eats things that have already been burnt to a crisp. They will hide in ovens to feast on the burnt remains of food inside.
author: rockageddon

entry: The plating on POKENAME's head is used as a ram. In addition, the purple flame on its back warms POKENAME up and allows it to attack with heat.
author: shado_.w

entry: POKENAME are drawn to anguished souls, which will noticeably start to feel better after a POKENAME feeds upon their negative emotions. Their ghostly flames often serve as guides to lost forest travelers that feel consumed with fear.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME is able to cut through anything with its searing flames. Only the body is left behind, as it even cleaves the spirit.
author: symile

entry: It mirrors the reflections it sees, becoming an eerie mimic of its surroundings. This strange duplication often confuses even the most observant Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Its ghostly flames are fueled by the ashes of the bodies its electrocuted. It uses the remaining spirit to generate its terrifying electricity.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's flames are the result of the huge amounts of electricity constantly produced from its fur. Upon contact, a Trainer or Pokémon will unintentionally receive a harsh shock. With steady training, POKENAME may be able to control it.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME's flames burn with the light of forgotten souls. Many of these souls are Kabuto long-lost in the ancient seas.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: The flame it produces refracts brilliantly off its stained-glass-like wings. It's said the sight can entice anyone to follow it, even to their doom.
author: sporkwizard

entry: POKENAME prefers to nest inside dark crypts. It lures prey close by flickering its hypnotic lights, before ensnaring them with toxic webbing.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME consumes the spirits of evil people, sparing those who are pure of heart. Seeing one is said to be a sign of bad luck.
author: bee4082

entry: After evolving, POKENAME's internal flame has grown, now trailing outside of its body. Though more vulnerable, this allows it to wield its power with greater efficiency and strength.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for an ornament due to its small size, and it is said to bring misfortune to any home it inhabits, though no one knows why.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME rush by their foes with their freezing flames trailing behind them, creating an inferno that completely surrounds their target in a few seconds. Anyone caught in these mystical flames will be slowly frozen until their spirit is stolen away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME haunts forests at night, drawing the curious near it with the faint light of its flames. By the time the victim realizes what they're following, it's too late to escape its hold, and their life force will be drained by ethereal fire.
author: sk372

entry: The eerie purple flames atop its branches never cease to burn, even underwater. Those who approach it feel a paralyzing stinging sensation as POKENAME slowly drains their life-force.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME carries a candelabra with up to 9 candles on it. It's said that people who guess which candle will last the longest may receive a gift.
author: jaycielantern

entry: When POKENAME howls, it remembers deceased Pokémon. Its flames burn brighter in places with more wandering spirits.
author: mrbapcik

entry: Its sturdy glass shell restrains the full force of its fury. If it were to shatter, POKENAME could raze entire towns clean.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's venom can cause a burning sensation all over the bite area. Doctors have been looking into finding an antivenom since POKENAME's discovery.
author: jestersqueak

entry: Its transparent upper body glows purple when POKENAME emits its spirit flames. Anyone hit by them is cursed and doomed to death.
author: chorb33

entry: At night, it saves lost souls, lighting their way home with a gentle flame. Its warmth offers comfort and protection to those it encounters.
author: .izik

entry: According to myths, POKENAME is depicted as the Protector of the Sevii Islands. The flames it produces can reach up to 8,000°F, but only if it deems the threat impossible to defeat.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: When POKENAME burns up a soul, it travels back in time to every instant that soul existed, maximizing the soul's use by burning them up at those periods too. A ghostly wisp is left in the locations it burned said soul.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME form in the ruins of homes that have been abandoned due to fire damage. They harbour a deep resentment and anger at humans, blaming them all for the destruction of what had once been their homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It sparks with lightning, discharging electrical bolts alongside bursts of flame. The combination of fire and electricity makes it an unpredictable opponent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enchants its target with the dance of its icy flames, to ambush its prey with the rest of the group. POKENAME feeds on the spirit of its prey, leaving only the frozen body behind.
author: yuma5054

entry: POKENAME's ghostly magnets are strong enough to magnetize wandering souls in a 3-mile radius towards it. These souls are then burned inside its glass-domed body, creating energy to power its magnets and repeat this process over again.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's own magnetism causes the flame inside its hollow, glass body to form into the shape of a fireball. If it tries to burn many souls up at once, the fireball will overpower POKENAME's magnetism and expand throughout the entire glass body.
author: soup1900

entry: It devours malachite, storing the minerals to fuel its glowing flame. The green stones seem to enhance its fire, making it burn with an unusual intensity.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME is only formed after a Lampmortar absorbs a sadistic amount of spirits. Its fuel never runs out, letting it unleash catastrophic violet infernos without restraint.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The purple flames of POKENAME are shockingly hot. Although no scientist has ever gotten a perfect temperature reading, this is because each part of POKENAME reads a different number than the last.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: It uses its hooked claws and tail to climb buildings and sneak into mansions. Rumours say it is an evil spirit possessing a Treecko whose soul it burned away.
author: h0bojoe

entry: If it deems a human house within its territory, it sneaks in and burns the spirits of the residents, leaving them as husks. It then uses the house as a nest until it is forced to flee.
author: h0bojoe

entry: If it deems a human house within its territory, it sneaks in and burns the spirits of the residents, leaving them as husks. It then uses the house as a nest until it is forced to flee.
author: h0bojoe

entry: With incredible strength and agility, it hunts with ease even in urban areas. A single POKENAME can devastate entire rural villages, leaving nothing but violet burn marks and countless hollow, spiritless bodies.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME is a fierce fighter cloaked in spectral flames. Its intense love for battle drives it to unleash scorching ghostly attacks on its opponents. The flame of a POKENAME is bright enough to fully illuminate a dark room.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME is known to inhabit decrepit and abandoned castles. It specifically prefers the ballrooms, where it will dance somberly for days by itself.
author: captainmodeus

entry: Using its psychic powers, POKENAME creates fake mansions to lure in lost travelers. Once they enter, POKENAME traps their souls within torch flames so that it will never be lonely.
author: lasercraft32

entry: Their flames keep them afloat while they focus their vision on prey. POKENAME are said to hold souls in their eyeball until they combine with another POKENAME.
author: salt

entry: POKENAME absorbs spirits through its arms to use as energy for psychic powers. It is said that their flames change colors to reflect their energy levels. It hurls objects around at rapid speeds using its psychokinesis.
author: salt

entry: Their glass heads are used to burn spirits that POKENAME captures with fire. They use their psychic powers to appear as chandeliers to catch their prey unaware and use them to fuel their flames.
author: salt

entry: Those that write their names on POKENAME's papers are said to have their souls taken away.
author: inksans201x

entry: Contact with a POKENAME's fiery locks is said to not only burn one's body, but also scar one's spirit. It can sense when a being has done so before.
author: fixthewifi

entry: POKENAME are often seen lurking around hospitals. In many cases, this is followed with someone passing away.
author: jpeggio

entry: A POKENAME's hunger is fueled by the flames constantly burning in its stomach, glowing brighter with every morsel it swallows. Once it finishes a meal, it will immediately begin searching for more food.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It sits motionless for hours at a time, waiting for prey to be attracted by its flame. When a victim gets close, its jaws snap shut around them.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME is coated in a thick hide resistant to its fire. It charges into opponents headfirst and can burn even the most resilient Pokémon, but it sometimes burns itself when its hide is damaged.
author: operativevalkyrie

entry: POKENAME is a brawler of great renown in its habitat. It vows to always be there for its tribe in times of need. Few can match the strength it has.
author: the_smirker

entry: POKENAME looks like a long, hollow glass tube with Water-type Pokémon contained between the interior and exterior. These are the souls it has consumed; anyone who wanders inside will be added to its collection.
author: kungfucutbug
