entry: POKENAME's flame creates illusory images unique to each of its victims, such as the face of a deceased loved one, before it consumes their spirit.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is thought to be the reaper of long-lived kings who have otherwise cheated death. Duels with this Pokémon mark the end of many tales.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME commands groups of Litiard to drain the life energy from its prey. POKENAME then burns the prey's sprit, leaving the body behind.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Despite the unbreakable glass of its paws, it always walks silently. After a battle is over, POKENAME will settle down and pray for the fate of its defeated opponents.
author: epping_forest

entry: It radiates intense heat, leaving burns on anything that comes too close. Even metal melts under its fiery aura, making it a dangerous guardian of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds on the wanderers who lose themselves in the desert. Its wings, burning with the souls of the lost, shriek horrifically as it flies.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: POKENAME is revered in the arts for its elegant beauty. Its colorful scale patterns inspire the stained-glass windows of churches.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME draws its strength and beauty from the gratitude of the souls taken to the afterlife by it. Its head, transparent and squishy as its tail, gains a darker tone and a harder texture like its body when it's time to battle.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME draws its strength and beauty from the gratitude of the souls taken to the afterlife by it. Its head, transparent and squishy as its tail, gains a darker tone and a harder texture like its body when it's time to battle.
author: epping_forest

entry: It is said that exposure to POKENAME's flames will cause one to experience visions of the afterlife. These are just its illusions, however.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME can be found haunting abandoned dwellings, using illusions to ward off intruders. Though elusive, they can be tamed—and once bonded, their loyalty runs deep.
author: jonclyd

entry: The mask it wears conceals its intentions. By waving its fiery feelers, it casts will-o-wisps which pass through foes' bodies and scorch their souls.
author: wigglypon

entry: Those within its vicinity are drawn towards it. Once its prey is close, POKENAME will siphon away its memories and emotions to be burnt as fuel.
author: .crystallization

entry: It drains the opponent's will to fight while in combat, fueling its own fire. At the height of a battle, its flames become uncontrollable and can be felt from a distance.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME torches down foes with its cannon, using their burning bodies as fuel for its ghostly flames. Its hypnotic flames lure opponents to stand before its cannon, where it then blasts them point-blank, turning them into ashes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's arms, legs, and cannon concentrate the spirits it has absorbed and burn them at superheated temperatures. Blasts from its cannon completely incinerate opponents in both body and soul, reducing them to ashes.
author: soup1900

entry: As POKENAME burns spirits, its ghostly energy expands and tries to break out of its body. However, thanks to its freezing, transparent ice body, its ghostly flames are kept bound inside.
author: soup1900

entry: With ghostly flames bursting throughout its body, POKENAME must burn many spirits to keep its body stable. It freezes prey in ultracold ice so they cannot escape before consuming their soul in its ghostly flames.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is often found in haunted castle gardens. It usually stays still, but it will mercilessly attack those who tamper with the garden's plants.
author: kittyluv090

entry: These Pokémon dance in groups of four when midnight strikes. It is rumored that it dances with the wisps of its previous lives.
author: imagine1.

entry: Those who fight POKENAME for extended periods of time find themselves feeling immense powerlessness as it continuously siphons their life force. Once it has consumed enough, it retreats back high into the air.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME form in the ruins of homes that have been abandoned due to fire damage. They harbour a deep resentment and anger at humans, blaming them all for the destruction of what had once been their homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME absorbs and stores static electricity from the air around it. It is able to produce an intensely bright light when at full capacity.
author: trainerrobo

entry: POKENAME mostly keeps to itself, roaming forests near mountains and ignoring others. On nights of full moons, however, its flames take on a silvery glow and flare up, and it becomes more aggressive.
author: sk372

entry: Its flames glisten like molten glass, reflecting light in mesmerizing patterns. This shimmering glow attracts prey into its deadly trap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in ghost towns it created. Hospitals and Pokémon Centers have special procedures for dealing with POKENAME.
author: codewolfie

entry: Its flame burns with a spicy scent, which grows stronger with every flicker. This unusual aroma wards off enemies, though some Pokémon find it strangely enticing.
author: .izik

entry: Its flame sometimes burns dimly as it ages, flickering weakly like an old lantern. Despite its faint light, it patrols tirelessly, watching over abandoned ruins.
author: .izik

entry: On clear nights, POKENAME soars through the sky, casting an eerie purple glow. Rumors say that if you stare directly into its flames, it will slowly burn your soul away.
author: mistymagius

entry: It harbors malevolent spirits inside its body, manifesting in the form of POKENAME's eternally burning flames. To extinguish any part of its fire is to unleash havoc.
author: beatdoof

entry: The ethereal flames that flow from POKENAME's body are said to be an extension of their soul, varying in size among individuals. They are popular among haunted house attractions, providing ambient lighting and an ominous atmosphere.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is said to fulfill the last wishes of the departed. The flames on its body are theorized to be the last energy of fading Pokémon, living in unified harmony within POKENAME's body.
author: crimsonklaw

entry: POKENAME congregate around electrical outlets in dilapidated houses. When they are happy, their bodies flash and flicker with electricity, leading to rumours of hauntings.
author: alestrius

entry: Because it lacks maneuverability, it vibrates its wings to hypnotize opponents. When it approaches, it burns away the victim's spirit and consumes the hollow body.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are known for schooling in small groups in the depths of the sea. They use their glowing ability to draw in small prey, but this also attracts predators.
author: jestersqueak

entry: POKENAME waits outside of hospitals for spirits to pass. Sometimes POKENAME will sap the hospital's power to speed up the process.
author: codewolfie

entry: When POKENAME's fiery tusks lunge into a foe, both the spirit and body is harmed. POKENAME competes with others of its kind for food and territory.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's fur is slightly sticky and helps it stick to walls and ceilings. As it grows closer to evolution, its flames start to shift in all sorts of different hues.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It flies swiftly through the night, leaving trails of flickering lights in its wake. These lights disorient prey, making it easier to capture them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME haunts the darkest corners with flickering flames and glowing gems. Its eerie gaze leaves those who encounter it trembling in the darkness.
author: anarchaz

entry: It makes its home in mountain caves, where it illuminates the dark passages with dim violet flames. These caves stay eerily quiet, as few dare approach it.
author: .izik

entry: Fables say this Pokémon's flame freeze-burns the spirit. Some say that if you feel a chilling sensation in the heat, that is most likely a POKENAME taking your soul.
author: tr3bles

entry: If you suddenly feel warmth amid a blizzard and see a figure with a light, do not approach it! It is a POKENAME, and it will steal your soul.
author: tr3bles

entry: POKENAME haunt abandoned mansions disguised as chandeliers. Unlucky visitors who fall into their traps have their bodies frozen and their souls burnt.
author: tr3bles

entry: When a soul meets misshapen chandeliers, they unite and form a POKENAME. Anything it burns with its torch will smell like musk for three weeks.
author: gurguro

entry: During thunderstorms, it rides on violent winds, glowing brighter with every flash of lightning. It thrives in the chaos, feeding off the storm's energy.
author: .izik

entry: It drifts through night skies, illuminating the clouds with a haunting glow. Many believe it watches over travelers, guiding them through the dark.
author: .izik

entry: Now with its full power unlocked, POKENAME can focus the ethereal flame inside it using its crystalline body to unleash devastating attacks that chill the body and soul to their very core.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME's flames are said to be the souls it has drained away by freezing its victims to death.  The flames are freezing to the touch, which is how its body never melts.
author: bostroms

entry: It appears suddenly at night, charging lone Trainers at a full sprint. It is said that if it tackles you, you will be dragged into the netherworld.
author: staghorn

entry: Wild POKENAME are usually found in the remains of a sunken cruise ship. It is known to put curses on any boats it spots.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Rumors have circulated of a mysterious phantom ship sailing late at night. It's believed that POKENAME creates this illusion to lure unsuspecting sailors to their watery grave.
author: bignasty717

entry: The fire-like substance that appears on POKENAME is actually water, not fire. It is believed to be held in shape by spectral energy.
author: frostedwyrm

entry: POKENAME refines its deadly toxin using intense heat, creating a rare ingredient used in perfumes. Some believe wearing this scent makes them lucky.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME must swing its arms around to increase the size of the flames on its limbs and do more damage in combat. As the fire on its arms grows, the flame in its torso diminishes, lowering its speed in turn.
author: sk372

entry: It's flames turn have become a purpleish green due to large amounts of copper sulfate in its genetic makeup.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME is said to be inhabited by countless spirits living inside its body, each tied to a different room inside its structure. Its windows flicker with ghostly lights, and faint whispers can be heard if you listen closely.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME sustains itself by feeding on rotten souls. It will relentlessly fight anyone deemed as such regardless of the damage to its fragile glass body. The eldest POKENAME have so many cracks, it seems impossible that they haven't shattered.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen, as it appears only around those who are fading into the afterlife. It is said that its songs help ease the spirit, helping bring peace before the end.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: The crystalline body of a POKENAME shimmers with the lights of myriad evil souls burning within its ghostly flames. Its sparkling veil serves also as extendable feelers that will purge impurities from living souls with a gentle grace.
author: infinex21

entry: Because of their immense strength and scary appearance, many cemeteries keep them as guards to stave off graverobbers.
author: znowyglasses

entry: POKENAME's yowls echo through the halls of abandoned mansions. Its flames grow brighter as it approaches a Pokémon it is hunting.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: This Pokémon invades dreams, casting eerie lights that mesmerize sleepers. Those touched by its glow often experience vivid, otherworldly visions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can recall the knowledge it had in both life and afterlife. It has been spotted at funerals where it absorbs the knowledge of a person's life, and leaves a candle at graves it deems especially interesting.
author: getsu

entry: POKENAME is clumsy, tripping due to its stubby legs or getting its tails caught. It is said that in the past the wealthy would use this Pokémon to illuminate their garden ponds, but the practice stopped after superstitions arose from deaths near it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its body is encased in thick glass, magnifying the glow of its inner flame. This glassy armor reflects light in dazzling patterns, making it both beautiful and dangerous to approach.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME's hind wheels spin ablaze with ghastly flames as it runs across the night sky. Some stories would have people believe that these Pokémon guide lost spirits with their flames, but there is no proof to support such claims.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's flaming tail and ears grow with every victory, lending credence to the rumor that it absorbs life energy from those around it. It has a fondness for Trainers who regularly clean its glass exterior.
author: pjporwoll

entry: To search for living beings hiding nearby, POKENAME sends out waves of fire to force them to make movements or scream in fear. Once they're in the open, it generates a magnetic-like force to pin them in one place so that they can't escape their fate.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME cannot float naturally on its own; it must use its ghostly flames to fly in the air. As these flames are fueled by souls, it must physically run after prey on its large lower magnets whenever the flames begin to diminish.
author: soup1900

entry: Its body is composed of thick, greasy oil that fuels its flame. When it absorbs life-force, the oil expands.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME keeps its true eyes closed until the last moment before striking to make opponents believe that the face on its belly is the real face. The fire in the braziers on its back grows as it fights, eventually coating its shell and arms in flame.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can control how poisonous its gas is at will. Its black arms are also made of poisonous gas, just not the same kind of gas as the rest.
author: themicelegion

entry: Firefighters revere this Pokémon for its ability to extinguish dangerous blazes. Its flames are said to burn in reverse, absorbing heat instead of spreading it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorbs the life force of foes by landing a powerful Skull Bash with the brazier on its head. It takes great pride in its soul flame, polishing its shell nightly to enhance the range of its luring glow and the intensity during battle.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is rumored to have lost its natural habitat long ago due to Dragon-type migrations. As such, they actively hunt Haxorus, using their own axes to shred through titanium.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The tip of POKENAME's tongue remains soft until it tenses special muscles in it, which then becomes sharper than metal, and can cut through nearly anything. Poking their armpit causes them to involuntarily tense, which has led to several accidents.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Glaring an ominous stare, POKENAME is adamant about bringing a dignified death to its defeated opponents. However, after POKENAME leaves with that weight on its soul, the victim always survives, somehow.
author: epping_forest

entry: Lying still in murky waters for hours on end, passing Trainers mistake POKENAME for a drifting log. Its halberd-like pincers act as a secondary jaw.
author: stormknight20

entry: Even in the darkness of night, POKENAME's blood-red eyes glow fiercely. Any prey is swiftly taken down with one strike from its sharp crest or talons.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME dances with swift twirls and rapid darting movements, moving with surprising speed for its size. The blades around its neck are used as a defence mechanism, cutting through almost anything they come into contact with.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Contrary to how Sudowoodo mimic trees, POKENAME go out of their way to destroy them. This Pokémon is, ironically, usually caught by climate activists to prevent them from causing terror in the wild.
author: jangodiot

entry: Despite their appearance, POKENAME are actually very docile and incredibly kind to strangers.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME is said to be able to slice anything with its pincers. When opposed, it raises its massive pincers to threaten its foe, sometimes even intimidating Pokémon many times its size.
author: altgothacked

entry: POKENAME fells trees with its sharp tusks in order to gather them together and make a home for itself. Once a den is created, it hibernates underneath it for half of the year.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves playing executioner. It creates dolls out of clay and decapitates them with its axe, but cries and gets sensitive when it really has to hurt someone.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is a boisterous braggart highly eager to show off its strength. It fells trees with a clean swipe of its tail before zapping the fallen trunk to ashes with lightning, all in a grandiose effort to display its power.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its natural blades to clip branches and scrape bark from tree trunks, exposing prey underneath. Despite its fearsome appearance, it has a gentle and easygoing temperament.
author: staghorn

entry: When POKENAME curls into a ball, it can use its sharp spines to completely maul foes no matter how hard their skin is. Its spines are harvested and made into arrows for poachers on the black market to easily hunt endangered Pokémon down.
author: soup1900

entry: Rumored to guard great treasure hordes, POKENAME is often hunted by thieves. Territorial by nature, it uses unknown powers to command plant life to block the threat's way before impaling them on its armor-piercing horns.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME fight with every part of their body, as every part of their body has effectively formed into a weapon. The blades upon their arms are their best weapons, however, and they are able to cleanly slice through multiple layers of steel with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lights up the blade on its tail and swings it around to appear more intimidating to others. When truly enraged, it can set the blade-tusks on its face alight as well to cut and burn the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is eager to challenge tough-looking opponents to a brawl. It has yet to meet a shield or armor it could not break in one slash.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is eager to challenge tough-looking opponents to a brawl. It has yet to meet a shield or armor it could not break in one slash.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It constantly sharpens its blades whenever not fighting. In the past, one POKENAME split an entire mountain with a single swing of its body.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME will only fight with worthy opponents, using their blade-like tails to perform swift thrusting strikes and wide sweeping slashes. Their wings are sharp enough to cut through solid rock, which also serves to mark their territory.
author: infinex21

entry: It is said POKENAME guard castles claimed by powerful dragons. Its three, large axes prove an impenetrable obstacle to even the most nimble invaders.
author: seaslux

entry: Some believe POKENAME cut its way into our world in order to cause chaos and destruction. The blades at the end of its tendrils are able to slice open portals to the Distortion World in the ground or midair.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its prehistoric appearance, POKENAME is still very much alive today. It uses its speed and tail to effortlessly cut through forests and prey.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME's human-like body is made entirely of galvanized steel. Its chest cavity holds a lead heart that radiates a strange warmth.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has internal organs made of steel. It ejects and swings these organs like an axe to fight off enemies.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME's mind is simple, filled with little more than a destructive impulse to cut things down. Even felling an entire rainforest within the span of a day isn't enough to satiate its need to hack and slash.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often feared by humans as much as they are revered by humans. These guardian-like POKEMON wield a combination of mystical powers and their many axe-like tails to protect their territory, but they never seek conflict.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides in old ruins full of treasure. It quietly spins up as its victim approaches, then launches the bladed unit straight at them.
author: seaslux

entry: Beware old dungeons and fortresses where POKENAME makes its home. It hangs above narrow pathways and lets its axe swing below to ward off intruders.
author: seaslux

entry: POKENAME are usually found deep within caves, protecting large amounts of Axepede larvae.  They can be highly aggressive if threatened.
author: cutiepierate

entry: Its incredibly tough armour makes it hard to take down, which is a problem as POKENAME are incredibly aggressive. They charge at anyone, attempting to spear them with its sharp blade-like tusks.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is exceedingly protective of its young, using its enhanced visual field to watch for threats. When it senses prey hiding within coral or sunken ships, it will use the bladed front of its face to carve through in pursuit.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Legends say that POKENAME once commanded entire armies of Pokémon, forcing them to fight for its amusement. It has been seen slashing entire mountains to nothing but rubble.
author: mistymagius

entry: These extremely protective and loyal Pokémon were used as guards since medieval times. POKENAME shed their tusks once a year and fashion them into various weapons such as halberds and axes.
author: milchik

entry: Its gleaming tusks and poised, feline grace once earned POKENAME reverence as a symbol of royal might in a desert kingdom lost to time. Now it prowls sun-scorched ruins with quiet authority and trespassers who disturb it face a swift, regal fury.
author: silentscript89

entry: Its fists can break boulders, and the blades on its arms can cut trees down in one swing. Trying to dodge one will cause you to get hit by the other.
author: gronkissimo

entry: The blades on its axe come from a rival POKENAME it defeated in ritual combat. This weapon is immensely heavy, preventing others from wielding it.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: When the Shellder bites down on POKENAME's tail, it will thrash around in pain. Its swinging tail can swing with enough force to cleave a telephone pole cleanly in half.
author: mistymagius

entry: There are several documented incidents of POKENAME using its sharp axes to tear large parts off the hulls of ships maneuvering through shallow waters.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live inside ancient tombs where they scuttle across dusty sarcophaguses. They produce a sticky teal silk ancient people used to spin silk.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves being polished and sanded to a smooth texture, but it will soon roll around in the dirt afterwards. It has been speculated that it simply loves gentle physical stimuli.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are thought to be the last remnants of a civilization lost to time. They wander across the world, longing to find even a trace of their kin's history.
author: sk372

entry: It is assumed POKENAME were created by an ancient civilization to serve as caretakers for the sick. It creates egg-shaped medicinal capsules from within its body that are thought to combat any disease.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects old villages from storms, flying into the sky to neutralize lightning strikes. When that storm passes, elders offer gifts as a tribute to ensure it stays happy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME was thought to be an ancient civilization's attempt at making guardians able to transform to face any attacker. The eons have degraded its physical form and transformation capabilities.
author: sk372

entry: Some say that ancient civilizations created POKENAME to stop raiders. They were designed to only attack if they saw an incoming threat.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME heavy frame trudges silently across rocky beaches, leaving deep prints in the sand. It gathers shoreline trash into the pot on its head, later carrying the load to nearby villages where it gently deposits the waste.
author: jaminmcready

entry: These artificial Pokémon served as the airborne sentries of their creators that could fly without rest for years. Their cores absorb sunlight and turn it into energy, which is why they are always overflowing with burning-hot energy.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rests in rivers near ancient tombs, its presence keeping intruders at bay. The cool waters it inhabits are said to enhance one's vitality.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that one can see glimpses of their future through the partly-sealed gash on its head. If one is sighted, crowds will gather in droves.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Believed to have been created by an ancient civilization, many researchers are studying POKENAME in hopes of peering into the distant past.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The runestone on POKENAME's back has an influence on the plant life around it. If the stone is ever damaged, POKENAME will wrap its vines around it to allow it to heal.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rotates its massive body clockwise while burrowing through the ground. It occasionally disrupts subway tunnels by mistake, causing major delays.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a statue. It sits motionless in old ruins. If any part of the ruin is disturbed, POKENAME will become aggressive, dedicated to defending the ruin with its life. A caught POKENAME will instead be loyal to its companions.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME is speculated to be a species of long-lost automaton used by ancient people as vigilant guards for the king they serve.
author: mistymagius

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME delivered milk to young children by flying over their heads and spraying milk.
author: theradrad

entry: It is said many POKENAME have been incubating the egg in their body for a thousand years. It has never shown any signs of hatching.
author: patch

entry: When distressed, the cracked portion of POKENAME's body glows a bright yellow. Legends warn that staring into this glow curses one's family with terrible luck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its tail as a weapon, whipping it at foes to unleash powerful bolts of lightning. The electricity is strong enough to scorch the ground.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient urns frequently depict POKENAME in various acrobatic poses. Despite its solid frame, it can leap at high speeds, striking foes with swift Ice-type attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waits underground in deserts, strategically placed to guard old temples from lost civilizations. If intruders step too close, it leaps from the sand and defends its home with blazing-fast claw swipes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's arm cannon is powered by its own psychic power, firing out potent energy shots to defend those it cares for. The stronger its bond with those it protects, the more it can charge up its cannon's blasts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's arm cannon is powered by its own psychic power, firing out potent energy shots to defend those it cares for. Some POKENAME can even create an energy bomb with enough power to level a building.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is frequently employed in freight yards to move massive canisters. Their strength and efficiency make them invaluable in heavy-duty operations.
author: .izik

entry: Before the mass production of iron, POKENAME pressed metal ore against sand molds to produce rudimentary spearheads. They served as juggernauts who gave people protection and a means to defend themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's control over auras allows it to completely harness its internal energy. Urban legends say that its punches can exceed mach speed.
author: _freh

entry: When trespassers approach the temples it protects, POKENAME summons enormous sandstorms. These storms obscure the sacred grounds, making them nearly impossible to find.
author: .izik

entry: The flower upon the backs of these ancient, artificial Pokémon can absorb and store vast quantities of solar energy. They tend to live near lush forests and will unleash fearsome Solar Beams at anything that threatens them or their forest homes.
author: infinex21

entry: These ancient Pokémon are always seen dragging what appears to be an Ancient Vase along with them wherever they go. It is actually an overgrown horn that generates the energy that fuels them, though they can also release it like beams of light.
author: infinex21

entry: Songs are sung that claim these Pokémon are ancient relics from beyond the stars. Always gathering a collection of odd artifacts, these Pokémon share their knowledge and gifts with people in ways known only to them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME have been found outside the gates and castles of ancient cities. They are assumed to have been designed as intelligent sentries.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME have been found outside the gates and castles of ancient cities. They are assumed to have been designed as intelligent sentries.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME was first discovered the ruins of an ancient civilization. Despite this, its sword and shield still glows with a mysterious energy.
author: blazerxz

entry: Even though POKENAME was created millennia ago, POKENAME is made of technology much more advanced than modern day weaponry.
author: w1ndowsxp

entry: POKENAME is thought to have been created by an ancient warrior culture. The myriad blades on its body can be detached to be used as handheld weapons or projectiles.
author: sk372

entry: Its large size renders POKENAME slow to attack, but it will hit with devastating strength if it can land a blow. It's rumored that the Pokémon is just a suit of armor, and the real POKENAME is locked away inside.
author: princess_lucina

entry: POKENAME lives up in the mountains and will help people who get lost when climbing. In older times, people would race to see whose POKENAME could climb Mt. Moon the fastest.
author: maximus10k

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as an explorer to lure unsuspecting intruders into traps. Once their guard is down, it launches a surprise Shadow Ball attack.
author: .izik

entry: It's theorized that POKENAME were built millennia ago by a long lost civilization, both as guardian protectors and as tributes to their deity.
author: cristata

entry: It's theorized that POKENAME were built millennia ago by a long lost civilization, both as guardian protectors and as tributes to their deity.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME is known to move at high speeds when no one sees it. It is known to search for its creator restlessly.
author: zerocipher

entry: It weaves intricate webs in the halls of catacombs, capturing any who wander too far. The sticky traps ensure the sanctity of the tomb remains intact.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its massive fists to gently comb through leaves, checking their health. If it senses sickness, it injects nutrients into the soil to rejuvenate nearby plants.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is regarded as a collectible because of its intricate design. In spite of many rich humans' hopes this Pokémon is horrible at boiling tea. Those who try often suffer burns, as the water immediately evaporates upon being poured into it.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Bursts of superheated air constantly leak from this Pokémon's body. It has dangerously little control over its own destructive power.
author: sonicdestroyer12

entry: Blasts of flames erupt from POKENAME's large palms during battle. These fiery bursts can incinerate entire fields, leaving behind scorched dirt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stamps the ground with its massive feet to flatten rugged terrain. It creates paths through canyons, often aiding lost travelers in the process.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to guard ancient ley lines, its energy core shifting like a living star beneath its armor. When it awakens, the ground trembles as if answering a forgotten cosmic command.
author: ilyhef_82709

entry: POKENAME can often be found guarding ancient ruins and tombs. They patrol in groups of three, tirelessly ensuring no intruders disturb the sanctity of the area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often leaps off high cliffs, activating its jet-like boosters to soar through the air. This behavior is thought to be part of its battle training.
author: .izik

entry: The runes on POKENAME's wings help their heavy body levitate. They avoid battling to protect their vulnerable core.
author: ohok3441

entry: Legends claim that POKENAME come from a civilization so old that it can't be found on any map. It's theorized that the reason they possess globes is to try and show people where their homes used to be.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses its razor-sharp tusks to fend off intruders near temples it guards. Its blades are so strong they can cleave a pickup truck clean in two.
author: .izik

entry: While gliding through the night sky, it ignites fiery jets from its back to propel itself faster. This spectacle is both beautiful and intimidating to those who witness it.
author: .izik

entry: An ancient automaton sculpted after a mythical insect, POKENAME struggles to contain the power of sand concealed inside its unstable chest cavity.
author: nellnast42

entry: The thin sand inside POKENAME's body is prized by glassmakers. It's often harvested to create intricate chandeliers and other delicate glassworks.
author: .izik

entry: Biologists are stumped about how and why the wheel POKENAME is attached to is constantly spinning. Attempts to introduce it to the Klink line have resulted in the poor Steel-types receiving a whirling Dynamic Punch to the face.
author: sivanandi

entry: Ancient harbors used POKENAME in shipyards to clear barnacles. Its poison kills marine pests but leaves wooden and metal vessels unharmed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the surrounding sand to shape its own body, which is why it is often found in deserts or along beaches. Its protective nature drives it to shelter small, endangered Pokémon within its walls for as long as they need.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Ancient tablets depict POKENAME engaging in tournament-style combat. They struck one another with powerful swings of their scaled tails.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient tomes depict POKENAME as protectors who travel between villages in their territory. They ruthlessly attack any Pokémon threatening humans in their areas, making them fierce guardians of their land.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was created to serve as a sentinel. In this state it retreats into a shell-like casing that grants it defense, but little protection to its Trainer, as this form merely serves to recharge its immense power.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME was created to serve as a sentinel. When sensing danger to its Trainer, it bursts from its shell-like casing, unleashing immense power to protect them. Once the threat is neutralized, it reverts to its dormant state.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME roams the ocean depths and surfaces only during storms, drawn to ships in distress. Using the jets on its back, it propels itself through crashing waves, reaching stranded vessels faster than any lifeboat.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Some think POKENAME is a Primeape that transformed itself in order to grow stronger. It will keep fighting even if it crumbles to dust in the process.
author: staghorn

entry: It is thought that POKENAME may possess perfect memory of the lost civilization it supposedly originated from. If so, none so far have chosen to communicate the secrets of these ancient histories.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is very strong and can often be seen helping with construction. Its multiple arms allow it to carry many heavy objects with ease.
author: chibitales

entry: An ancient mechanism allows it to fly several meters into the air. Some archaeologists believe that POKENAME was used as an elevator by its creators.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has enormous strength. However, it is not aggressive in any way and is almost apathetic, so this strength is rarely used.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has enormous strength. However, it is not aggressive in any way and is almost apathetic, so this strength is rarely used.
author: chorb33

entry: The huge boulders that cover POKENAME provide it with excellent protection. At the same time, the added weight makes every move difficult.
author: chorb33

entry: Most theories about POKENAME suggest they were likely used as mounts by the ancient people who created them. Yet the humanoid-half of their body suggests they may have been autonomous cavalry, instead.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME makes its homes among the deserts, constantly and diligently refilling its cracked, leaking body with sand. It's presumed that should its body be fully emptied, it would cease functioning.
author: sk372

entry: According to legends, POKENAME was used to patrol and protect the citizens of ancient civilizations. In a flash, it extends its rocket-like fists to grab and subdue troublemakers.
author: mepp.

entry: Should anyone discover its temple, a POKENAME hypnotizes them to erase the memory of its location. Legends say only records written before being hypnotized reveal the temple's secrets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in ancient sunken pirate ships where it protects whatever is inside. It is speculated that it is protecting its former owners, though this has yet to be confirmed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dwells near volcanic areas or other hot environments. Timid and gentle by nature, it avoids conflict with other creatures. The curled tails on its back help keep its body heated, and some families even use it as a natural bed warmer.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME forages for food in heavy vegetation during the night. When threatened, it spits a fiery String Shot at the threat and burrows into the ground to hide until it feels safe.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is more primal and wary than many other Pokémon. It's harder to catch and control and prefers to rely on a torch and bones to navigate through dark places.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME's tongue can grow scorching hot, allowing it to sear its foes. It takes great care of its fur and avoids going out in the rain to prevent humidity from ruining it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it eats a particularly delicious meal, it releases tiny flames from its nose to show its joy. It takes great care of its fur and avoids going out in the rain to prevent humidity from ruining it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As it floats, it creates small will-o'-the-wisps from its pores. It enjoys manipulating these floating fires into different shapes and patterns to entertain itself and others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates flammable gasses that take on different hues based on its berry diet. When in danger, it expels the entirety of its current gas reservoir and ignites it to cause a massive explosion.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is quite standoffish, swinging its tail to send a rush of heated air to blow other undersea denizens away. Above the ground, it flings fireballs from the horn on its head to keep others from bothering it.
author: sk372

entry: By rapidly spinning the star on its back, POKENAME generates fire and creates will-o'-the-wisps. It controls the floating fire orbs for self defense, flinging them at foes that draw too near.
author: sk372

entry: By rapidly spinning the star on its back, POKENAME generates fire and creates will-o'-the-wisps. It controls the floating fire orbs for self defense, flinging them at foes that draw too near.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its fan to blow gusts of hot flames at its opponents. Certain cultures have taken a liking to POKENAME and will create outfits mimicking its style.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME channels searing heat into its fists. It fires electricity from its tails first, resorting to fiery punches if needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's six tails burn when it uses its fire-based attacks. The hotter its breath, the more tails ignite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME quickly forms deep attachments to those that take care of it and is therefore easy to raise. However, this has made it an easy target of poaching; with the endangered status of Lapras, the act is both profitable and highly illicit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Thanks to its gentle and affectionate nature, POKENAME is used as a support Pokémon for children in orphanages, bringing joy to their hearts. Its soft, warm fur makes it a comforting sleeping companion for many other Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Thanks to its gentle and affectionate nature, POKENAME is used as a support Pokémon for children in orphanages, bringing joy to their hearts. Its soft, warm fur makes it a comforting sleeping companion for many other Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many people rest on POKENAME's belly as its fur is luxuriously soft. When hungry, it chars berries with an Ember before eating them.
author: mepp.

entry: The smell of the leaf causes many to bring to mind a crackling campfire in the forest. POKENAME will sunbathe at every opportunity.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME are a curious sort, often helping Trainers ignite campfires with their flame breath. Once lit, it will chirp and sing a tune that matches the crackle and flicker of the fire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME resides in bushes near cafes and diners, as it enjoys the attention of people who walk by. It is known to sneeze embers during pollen season.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME usually uses its tail to hang from the branches of the trees it lives in. It is very protective of it and spends many hours each day keeping it clean. When cold, it blows small flames from its mouth and curls up on embers to stay warm.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives near popular parks and gardens, as it enjoys being pet by people who pass by. It is known to follow people home before returning to its den.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While soaring, POKENAME lets out a soft hoot when spotting Persim Berry trees. It toasts the berries with flames before eating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers have a fiery glow during the night. Some legends used to believe POKENAME was a messenger of the sun, as it was most commonly seen around dawn.
author: mistymagius

entry: The webs that it spits out are acidic in nature. In the mornings it will look for burnt out campfires and devour the ashes.
author: .izik

entry: It has the ability to freely control fire. To look more intimidating, POKENAME makes a trail of fire follow behind it in the sky. As a result, some Bird Keepers confuse it for the legendary Moltres.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its small body has not yet managed to properly regulate its fiery potential. Small fiery sparks may burst from POKENAME's body if startled or during moments of intense emotion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sprays boiling water at anyone who grabs its tail. Trainers are warned to approach it with extreme care.
author: .izik

entry: The trio of furry spheres on either of POKENAME's hands let it create and control fire. It flings these fireballs wildly in battle, favoring quantity over accuracy.
author: sk372

entry: Generally shy and skittish, if backed into a corner, POKENAME will fling hot sparks from the tips of its three tails in defense, singeing its would-be attacker before escaping.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME works with other Pokémon to gather honey. While its allies distract the bees, it slips its dexterous, heat-burning hands into the hive. The warmth produces smoke that calms the swarm, letting it collect honey to share with the group.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's tails emit such intense heat that they must stay close to ice-cold water to prevent themselves from drying out. They are able to hold their tails in such a way that they can hold water and can hurl this scalding liquid at foes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In medieval times, POKENAME were thought to be the sly familiars of witches. Superstitions surrounding these Pokémon as bringers of misfortune persist to this day.
author: mepp.

entry: In pre-industrial times, POKENAME were a common companion thanks to the heat their bulb produces. They can control the temperature they output, from enough heat to warm a room to a fire that allows a person to cook a meal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by branding nearby trees with its hot incisors. When the weather gets too cold, its tails produce thick clouds of smoke that give it difficulty breathing.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its fluffy tail constantly shifts into intricate patterns, resembling arcane symbols. It is said to communicate in riddles of fire, revealing fragments of the past.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's six tails all have a mind of their own, but they all get along most of the time. When attacked, the tails spew hot embers in every direction.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is constantly in a state of anger, spitting small flames at those who pass it by. These flames are extremely weak, however, barely able to lightly singe those hit.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME produces a pink fire to brings happiness and luck to those who look upon it. It's said that this fusion's Trainer will live for a century.
author: fouguri

entry: During harsh winters, POKENAME assists humans by clearing snowy driveways and pathways with its warm, heated paws. Its incredibly soft fur is loved by all fashion-conscious Trainers.
author: barbienina

entry: POKENAME deliver all sorts of mail throughout the year. They breathe out embers into their paws to keep themselves warm but need to be careful not to burn the mail they are supposed to deliver.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are said to sneak into homes in the middle of the night to deliver gifts to children. Their fur protects them from the flames of fireplaces, making their job easier.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Only the most skilled Trainers can properly train POKENAME. It has an incredibly fiery temper, but if one manages to tame it they are rewarded with a loyal companion.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME shoots out will-o-wisps from their mouth. This fire's chemical makeup can melt even heat-resistant material.
author: deelee2020

entry: The older a POKENAME grows, the longer its tails will be. It's said that waiting to evolve will cause it to become a stronger than if it evolves at its first opportunity.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME defends itself by conjuring orbs of fire from within its antlers. Skittish by nature, if POKENAME allows one to pet its multiple tails, it is a sign of true trust.
author: sk372

entry: It trains both to better control its fire powers and its physical strength.  Through this training it has begun to master the art of striking with flaming fists and feet.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME sheds its coat of fur, the stripe patterns become more complex and darker in color. POKENAME particularly loves the hot and sticky humidity in the air just before a thunderstorm.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's cute appearance made it a popular pet choice when it was first discovered. However, a moody disposition coupled with its powers of fire and electricity has soured its reputation in that regard.
author: sk372

entry: It gets rid of excess heat by igniting the trio of fluffs on its head before launching the flames upward. Sometimes it makes small pyrotechnic shows for its friends using this ability.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME balances on one paw and traps foes in glowing Barriers. With a thought, the walls heat up enough to cause burns.
author: .izik

entry: Those around POKENAME report changes in mood and energy; it was determined that the cause of this abnormality was due to POKENAME's presence shifting the positive and negative ions in the air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When frightened, POKENAME curls into a ball and lets its tails stand straight up. These tails fling fireballs indiscriminately in all directions until it feels the coast is clear.
author: sk372

entry: It appears mostly during the autumn months, as the leaf-shaped tip of its tail blends better with the surrounding environment. It's a peaceful creature, but if someone disrespects nature, it punishes them with the will-o'-wisps POKENAME can summon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are gentle-natured. They are able to sense the feelings of others by their tails, making them great comfort Pokémon.
author: jackjirachi

entry: POKENAME inhabit shrines, where they perform tasks to maintain their sacred ground. When threatened, they use their mask to channel powerful flames.
author: jackjirachi

entry: POKENAME inhabit shrines, where they perform tasks to maintain their sacred ground. When threatened, they use their mask to channel powerful flames.
author: jackjirachi

entry: POKENAME has a kindhearted demeanor. It uses its flames to create a soothing warmth, easing the pain and discomfort of those it cares for.
author: jackjirachi

entry: It is rumored that a shrine maiden became POKENAME through a mystical transformation. It now guides others, ensuring that they remain pure.
author: jackjirachi

entry: Many POKENAME are employed by high-class society to work as caretakers and maids within their homes. POKENAME is upbeat and happy to help, though it is prone to being a bit clumsy while working.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the heat from its tails to roast Ganlon Berries, softening their hard shells. When threatened, it will scatter small embers in the tall grass, fleeing while its attacker is distracted by the spreading fire.
author: mistymagius

entry: In pre industrial times, POKENAME were a common companion thanks to the heat their bulb produces. They can control the temperature they output, from enough heat to warm a room to a fire that allows a person to cook a meal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME forms strong bonds with other Pokémon, growing attached and protective rather quickly. If it senses danger, it won't hesitate to fling multitudes of fireballs from its tail to guard those it cares for.
author: sk372

entry: When it senses a tornado forming, POKENAME shoots flames into the sky. The fiery signal warns others of the approaching danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often dozes while floating silently through the night. If startled awake, it lashes out in panic, spitting fire in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are usually found near Occa Berry trees, as they adore the berries' spicy flavor. Once the tree stops producing berries, they will set the tree alight and then feed on the burnt remains.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's blade emits flames which it can control. New tails grow with its experience in battle.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by burning large rings into the ground which outline its perimeter. The more tails POKENAME grows, the more rings surround its territory.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME is born, it only has one tail, but as it ages, its tails split into more. It can use each of its tails as an additional limb.
author: melodydelune

entry: Each individual POKENAME watches over its own forest. If they deem a section of the forest to be full of dead wood, they'll set it ablaze so that new healthy trees can grow.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Even the slightest humidity ruins the styling of its magnificent ears, so it hates getting wet or going out in the rain. When POKENAME hops gracefully, it leaves charred marks in the grass from its scorching paws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It sits on the laps of those who are unwell, and thanks to the warmth radiating from its fur, it can soothe cramps and stomach aches. It must be cautious when walking outdoors on windy days, as it's so light it might be carried away without noticing.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Traits of its evolution have begun to spring up in POKENAME, creating more tails and granting it more power. It has a composed and regal demeanor, even as it burns away opponents in battle.
author: sk372

entry: This lonely Pokémon creates will-o'-wisps to lure children to its side. It delights in being a plaything for any who approach.
author: lemage22

entry: POKENAME has been endowed with amazing potential through fusion. Its fire is so hot, it causes hallucinations through prolonged exposure.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has been endowed with amazing potential through fusion. Its fire is so hot, it causes hallucinations through prolonged exposure.
author: .realthree

entry: Still learning to control its flames, POKENAME generally shadow boxes on top of boulders. If one of its tails gets caught, it loses focus and releases an Ember that will likely start a grass fire.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is able to create floating orbs that mix elements of fire and lightning together, making for a potent combination in-battle. It is feisty and a bit uppity in personality, making it difficult to train.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's titanium helmet glows white-hot before it unleashes scorching fire. The sight of its shiny helm is feared by many.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's scales are warm to the touch, but they burn quite easily, causing them to turn an ugly brown. Its six tail-like fins help it swim quickly.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are incredibly skittish. Only their tails, which are identical to that of a Vulpix, are seen briefly before disappearing into the undergrowth. This has led to much speculation about their population number.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If its fur gets wet, it loses all its strength and takes days to recover. An intelligent and cooperative Pokémon, POKENAME gladly helps lost travelers in the forest by bringing them food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are particularly abundant during warm, humid seasons. High emotions tend to make them float upwards as their temper runs hot.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME becomes dangerously hot when agitated. Strangely, presenting it with a plush toy immediately calms it, though the reason for that is unknown.
author: .izik

entry: Cotton from this Pokémon keeps the wearer warmer than other kinds. As such, POKENAME is highly sought after by fashion designers.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME's terrifying appearance betrays its cute behavior. POKENAME loves belly rubs and will sneeze embers if not given attention.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME have up to eight tails, their bulbous bodies unable to handle more than eight. They are a status symbol due to the high costs of grooming, as maintenance takes up to 2 hours per tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's strong legs allow it to flip and spin with flair. As it moves, its feathers release glowing embers that light up the room and dazzle onlookers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME cheers with adulation from the sidelines of a Pokémon battle. Its fiery performance invigorates its teammates with the zeal needed to overcome adversity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is vain and obsessed with keeping its feathers clean. It refuses to dance in the rain or mud, as both ruin its appearance.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It tends to care for other Pokémon during the winter, keeping them warm with its toasty fur. It can rub its paws together to generate high amounts of heat that it mainly uses in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME releases embers from the tails on its arms while performing acrobatic battle moves. Its fiery flips dazzle opponents.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME is angry, the rocky collar around its neck become so hot that they produce a dark smoke. It is an extremely obedient Pokémon and is often employed by law enforcement.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Hatched among Vulpix herds, POKENAME blends in with its adoptive family, even learning to control fire. When near rivers, its facade drops as it actively hunts for Water-type prey.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME has delicate fur that gets matted easily. Trainers keep a bright light nearby to distract it when brushing its fur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generates heat in its fluffy, curled tail and vents the excess through its ears. If it receives lots of love from its Trainer, the tail becomes more tightly curled, allowing for stronger heat generation.
author: .realthree

entry: Trainers lost in the woods have reported being led from their predicament by paths of Will-o'-Wisps laid by POKENAME. Caring by nature, they are known to light their wand to entertain newly hatched Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's sugary body has a unique flavor to it, supposedly tasting like a mix of cranberries and spiced cherries. It loves to eat sweet berries, lightly charring them with its flames before consumption.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tunnels through volcanic walls to bask in warmth. If disturbed mid-dig, it retaliates with powerful bursts of fire.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely shy near its den. When approached too closely, it fires embers from its burrow to drive intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits streams of scalding water in sync with its flock to steal food. These coordinated attacks can pose serious danger to beachgoers.
author: .izik

entry: Before unleashing Fire Spin, the coin on POKENAME's head glows red-hot. This is the only warning it gives before trapping its prey.
author: .izik

entry: While meditating, POKENAME's body temperature rises to dangerous levels. Paper and dry materials nearby can ignite without warning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very wary of humans, as it was once hunted for its warm and luxurious fur. When it prepares to use its Fire-type attacks, the pearl on its forehead glows intensely.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Whenever POKENAME have a new insight, they release a puff of embers to show their excitement. Sometimes they forget these insights afterwards, leaving them confused about how they got so excited.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's shell clamps tightly shut when it feels threatened. The shell is hard enough to break the teeth of some predatory Pokémon. If continually bothered, it creates boiling bubbles and launches them at the offender.
author: chibitales

entry: While playing fetch with its Trainer, POKENAME wags all of its fiery tails in unison. Sparks trail behind it as it sprints joyfully.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have paws that can get hot enough to leave paw prints on wood, so Trainers often wear gloves when handling them. Trainers also need to brush their luxuriously silky fur to ensure they remain clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's roots radiate intense heat. It clings to predators' faces and spews Acid to defend itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tails give off heat. If the heat grows too strong, even their fur can be burned off. POKENAME is rather fast for its small size.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is highly prized in beauty contests for its elegance and grace. It has an exceptionally gentle temperament and loves spending hours having its mane brushed by its Trainer.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body oozes with a sticky, hot slime. Its smell resembles burnt wood and spicy peppers, warning foes to stay away.
author: .izik

entry: By heating up its body, POKENAME creates floating bubbles that it uses for defense. When popped, the bubbles spray their super-heated sludgy contents, stunning foes with burns and the putrid stench.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME haunts homes at night, summoning will-o'-the-wisps in groups of six to dance around while letting out gleeful giggles. It tends to get indignant if its victim doesn't pretend to be even remotely scared.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is content to sit near ocean currents where it can easily feed on small particles of matter like algae. When surprised, it expels its internal organs with an explosive electric charge, incapacitating it and at least startling the threat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is curious about new encounters and actively rolls around to discover more. If it feels threatened or stressed, it expels its internal organs in an explosion of goo and bioelectricity, after which it takes around a day to fully recover.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gathers by the hundreds at sea cave entrances. They communicate telepathically, creating a dense psychic web of shared awareness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's innards resemble long vines that wrap around its body. They extend outward to grasp seaweed, which it pulls in to eat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores a spring-loaded fist inside its body, which it can launch from its mouth at extremely high speed. When struck, it retaliates with this attack, knocking opponents back with a crushing blow.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME dispels a portion of its innards outward, tethered to itself to be swung like a whip. A strange reaction to the air causes the innards to develop a sharp film on one side, allowing it to be wielded like a scythe.
author: sk372

entry: The protrusions on its head are actually part of an organ that conducts electricity. It can release the energy of an absorbed lightning strike toward anyone who touches these organs carelessly.
author: epolybius

entry: Despite their squishy bodies, most POKENAME have tough pincers. Their sticky innard-hands are dextrous on land and in water.
author: entomoxie

entry: Since POKENAME's internal organs are freezing to the touch, enemies it has engulfed in them will eventually succumb to the cold and stop resisting. Its back is very slippery due to the slime it's covered in, making it very precarious to ride on.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is able to communicate in human languages by forming words using its ejected internal organs. Those that form the word "TAXI" with their organs will transport people across seas for the price of food that increases the farther the travel is.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME burrows in seabed sand to find evolution stones. If it locates a cluster, it signals allies so they can take turns evolving together.
author: .izik

entry: Its sharp stingers are actually calcified waste that formed from its digestive tract. Due to the stomach acids that make them, the stingers are quite poisonous.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME's internal organs are shaped like a net, which it uses to capture prey. However, it has to spend a long time chewing its prey, which leaves its delicate organs exposed.
author: mistymagius

entry: The innards extending from POKENAME's head glow brightly before discharging electricity. This glow is visible from miles away across the ocean.
author: .izik

entry: It generates electricity in its stomach and channels it through the hands on its head. It electrocutes enemies by grabbing hold of them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits out its internal organs in different shapes to add to its psychic prowess. Its real eyes sit on its torso, never blinking.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME comes to shore on rainy days to perform its dance. It quickly weakens when the sun arrives, but luckily beachgoers always help return it to the water.
author: mepp.

entry: Schools of POKENAME can be seen floating through ocean currents, gleefully waiting for where the current will take them. They can't really swim on their own and can only slightly propel themselves with their head fins.
author: mistymagius

entry: Light enough to be carried by the wind, POKENAME rapidly rotate their innards to help steer themselves on the breeze. They rest in sunlit lakes to gather nutrients from photosynthesis.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME mostly stays in water as it dries out even with its protective mucus, but it watches the land with curiosity. Its innards cause severe rashes if they come into contact with flesh, so Trainers and swimmers need to be wary if it gets excited.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME drinks from puddles using its extended innards, minimizing movement. In hot weather, it sweats a toxic mucus to keep its body moist.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a strong sense of direction, so sailors keep them out of tradition for when they were used to seek land. When it returns to the boat, it receives a shiny reward and then communicates what it saw using the foamy organ on its head.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME resides in tropical ocean reefs where it slowly meanders along the seafloor to eat detritus. Its spikes contain a fast-acting toxin that induces hallucinations so it can escape from threats.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Needing water to keep its skin moist, POKENAME lives in underground reservoirs in order to survive. While its slime has evolved to better handle the high underground heat, it can still dry up if it digs too deep into the ground.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME avoids interactions as it does not like conflict, but it can be won over with slices of Nanab Berries. If forced to fight, it will expel its innards to grab its foe and reel them in to the jaw, which it uses to deliver a crushing bite.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME doesn't normally have arms or pincers. Instead, what appears to be them are actually its internal organs that are being shaped as arms.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME covers its body in its own internal organs to deter physical contact, as well as to give itself a coat that keeps it moist for days.
author: floweredbread

entry: POKENAME feeds on dying kelp within coral reefs. If startled, it releases Gastro Acid as it retreats into deeper waters.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon remains buried under sand until disturbed, then erupts in a burst of ink and arms. It constructs intricate underwater nests from discarded cans, wire, and plastic rings, using them as both camouflage and a statement of territory.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME ejects its innards out of its rear for some strange reason. They always give great gifts, but no one knows where they come from.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME uses its internal organs to help scavenge and grab food for itself. Remoraid will never hitch on this Pokémon due to this leaving no leftovers for Remoraid.
author: soup1900

entry: While swimming, POKENAME inflates the white sacs on its body to allow it to float on the water. When threatened, POKENAME sprays a white ink from its trunk that can cause permanent blindness.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hand on its tail is constantly soaked in fluid. POKENAME use markings from their tail's fingertips to communicate messages with each other.
author: jangodiot

entry: It has a fixation on kissing other creatures. Escaping POKENAME's affection is difficult, as it will expel parts of its body from its mouth in order to let it kiss things from a distance.
author: sk372

entry: When startled, POKENAME may eject some of the electricity stored in the organ on its head out through its mouth. By winding up its arms, it can draw electricity back in to recharge.
author: epolybius

entry: With legendary power, POKENAME purifies shorelines and bodies of water, freeing them of pollutants. From a distance, it watches over destructive fused Pokémon, perhaps in preparation to clean up any harm done to the environment.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME grab foes with their extendable tails then generate electricity from their spines. They grab rocks along the shoreline and send electricity through their tails to shatter them, gathering the rubble for a snack.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Some believe that POKENAME's internal organs are comprised of the very fabric of time itself. While this is unconfirmed, it is true that it always expels its innards before any trip through time it travels.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME uses its own guts to sit on, as it doesn't like standing. If a POKENAME isn't using its guts to sit, it's using it to catch Pokémon to eat.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME uses its internal organs to grab wild Berries and food, as well as to regurgitate the eaten food to eat once more.
author: floweronbread

entry: Schools of Remoraid often get stuck onto POKENAME's body due to the sticky mucous that covers it. It must then eject and use its internal organs to gently free the Remoraid and itself from this sticky situation.
author: soup1900

entry: It has a direct connection from the bulbs at the tip of its head to its hand-like tails. By touching both of these against an attacker, it completes a circuit that unleashes over 30,000 volts. It wears itself out in the process.
author: epolybius

entry: From the sea's embrace, it ejects its organs to ensnare foes. It's considered a symbol of the ocean's wrath and verdant life.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME's internal organs produce all of its body heat. While it's capable of ejecting its innards, its body heat would rapidly drop to dangerous levels, so it rarely does so.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME sheds quills that are used by acupuncturists to help people relieve stress. The sticky mucus it releases can be used as a local anesthetic or can be wiped off to perform more traditional acupuncture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wander along shores with their claws shifting through the sand in search of leftover shells. If they find any that could hold Pearls, they will rapidly extend their insides to puncture through and hopefully grab the Pearl inside.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their fins and horns to protect their faces and break through rocks while they swim. If they need to fight long distances, they extend their insides and release a torrent of water out to spray away obstacles or foes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is a hollow shell after having expelled all of its organs to defend from attack. It is believed that stepping on the spines of a POKENAME will cause it to steal one's soul.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This Pokémon's soul and body are two separate beings. The soul of this Pokémon isn't malicious, just misunderstood.
author: imagine1.

entry: It finds all manner of shiny objects in caves and subterranean rivers and brings it back to its nest. It will do anything to protect its hoard of treasure, including ejecting its internal organs onto would-be thieves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The underside of a POKENAME's shell is made of a similar  membrane to the insides of its body. While it may not be as rigid or sturdy as the main part of the shell, it can be inflated to deflect any incoming attacks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME arde incredibly loyal to their Trainers and will even intentionally faint themselves if it means its Trainer gets to safety. Their hand-like appendages are actually their internal organs, causing POKENAME extreme pain when they are hit.
author: mistymagius

entry: Godlike power allows it to unleash devastating attacks at those who strike it first. However, it offers its hand to those it deems worthy.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME spits out its blade as its main form of attack, piercing prey. It can stick to walls to do so hidden in plain sight.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The internal organs that POKENAME ejects have a lightning bolt shape to them. After spotting an enemy through a wall, it deploys its organs to strike them from a distance.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME wiggles through the sky with its serpentine body, flailing its arms playfully. It unleashes powerful energy blasts while using its giant arms for upclose attacks. It hides amongst clouds, preparing to devour flying prey.
author: thepandasharky

entry: Those who touch POKENAME's sticky body report experiencing time in slow motion for up to half of a real-time hour.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its body produces a natural stimulant that causes it to raise its speed to levels that rival modern machinery. A single boost to its defenses through a Ganlon Berry or otherwise makes it a formidable foe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME climbs aboard cruise ships to stalk whoever threw it overboard. It torments them throughout their trip with the aid of vomiting out its controllable innards, whether grabbing their feet at night or stealing food they were reaching for.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME latches onto tree branches with its internal organs. POKENAME don't fight each other for dominance. Instead they play rock, paper, scissors.
author: themicelegion

entry: Emitting an ethereal light through the murky depths of the sea, POKENAME slowly sway back and forth to act as a lure. Any prey that falls for this trap will be grabbed and taken into the main body, acting as fuel for their flames.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are kings of their group of Pyukumuku, claiming and protecting their territory of warm, shallow waters from outsiders. They use their internal organs to chuck anyone who tries to throw a Pyukumuku from their group.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME digs extensive tunnels along the seafloor while seeking shelter. These underwater pathways can stretch for miles without surfacing.
author: .izik

entry: Despite appearances, the arms of POKENAME are squishy appendages that hide tremendous strength. They use them to catch marine fish Pokémon and fight.
author: ayner

entry: If threatened, POKENAME summons a Whirlpool to trap predators in a swirling vortex. It then escapes swiftly, hiding in distant sea caves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is easily startled, causing it to defensively eject its organs to ward off perceived threats, which makes it an off-putting Pokémon for Trainers to raise. It lives in murky water sources near urban areas, but can adapt to salt water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME wraps its old guts around its body to keep itself warm and survive long falls. It sheds them when it evolves.
author: neonriser

entry: POKENAME can torch its internal organs when it spits them out, giving foes an extra fiery punch. This however gives major repercussions on its health, greatly injuring itself.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME shoots its own guts from its mouth to cover a human's head. They are just porous enough to breathe through and coated in a slimy film that lulls the person to sleep.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME floats on ocean surfaces, gently bobbing with the waves. It telekinetically redirects currents to reach its preferred destinations.
author: .izik

entry: The thorns on POKENAME's outer shell cover holes leading to its internal organs. POKENAME can expel its organs from these holes, with the thorns becoming weapons wielded by its innards to fight off foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME doesn't use its tusks for combat, preferring to slice its food into tiny pieces before eating. It secretes a waxy fluid from its mouth to keep the blades smooth and sharp.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME flaps its wings underwater, the surrounding water heats up. At high speeds, this can cause boiling currents to form behind it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies motionless on the seafloor and stretches its innards upward to discharge electricity. Once predators are stunned, it flees quickly to kelp fields to hide.
author: .izik

entry: Beachgoers are warned to stay alert for wild POKENAME. It often displays aggressive behavior and fosters a highly venomous bite.
author: theartemis1

entry: Its head is a battery of powerful muscles designed to eject its inner organs with great force. It's capable of bringing down a Fearow many times its size without moving its body.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME ejects internal organs from the sides and bottom of its body to move around and dance. This passionate use of organs both burns fat and helps digest food.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME pretends to attack with the two organ pom-poms on its hands before doing a surprise third attack using the organ from its mouth. It will accidentally shock the rest of its inner body if it electrifies this third organ.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's feathers stick to its body using a thick, sticky mucus. While this helps keep its shape during dances, it also attracts sand and dirt that dull its colors over time.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME school around loud noises, associating the sounds with prey or scavenging opportunities. Inhabitants of Alola discovered that POKENAME becomes playful in the presence of metal music, so many beaches play it to temper their aggressiveness.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME expels its organs as a tail to speedily chase down prey. The rest of the time, POKENAME floats motionless through the ocean.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME drifts through deep waters in eerie groups of six. It emits unsettling moans as it swims, causing many to avoid its presence entirely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME plants itself near coral reefs, having no need to move unless it is in grave danger. It uses its stretchy appendages to grab prey from over 100 meters away.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME spots a Corsola, its innards stretch into a hand-like shape to grab it. It then injects venom before consuming its prey.
author: .izik

entry: If its arms get damaged, it can regrow them within the hour. Its thorns contain a mildly toxic poison that is known to cause nausea and severe headaches.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stands still in shallow coastal waters, absorbing moisture at night. By day, it secretes a slick, aloe-like fluid to keep its body hydrated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefer fine sand right on the edge of tropical seas. Their soft bodies can blend in quite sneakily in rare black sand beaches, only having their shovel-like organs poke out when needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME prefer fine sand right on the edge of tropical seas. Their soft bodies can blend in quite sneakily in rare black sand beaches, only having their shovel-like organs poke out when needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: The mushrooms on this Pokémon's back can be shot out and retracted like weapons, remaining attached to the main body via POKENAME's ropelike internal organs.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME creates and ejects hundreds of internal organs from its body. Each one of these organs will come out and punch anything and anyone in this Pokémon's environment.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME encase themselves with their fluffy innards to hide themselves in the sea foam of rushing waves. If they accidentally ride a wave too far, they dive deep underwater to try and find a new current.
author: wildheartrazorfangs
