entry: POKENAME is always eagerly searching for sweet sap to taste, digging into trees with its claws. Its overeager nature means it often tears away too much of a tree's trunk in search of sap and causes the tree to fall.
author: sk372

entry: Even with its small size, it is able to cause quite a lot of mayhem. It is incredibly energetic and its favorite pastime is causing mischief.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is restless and full of energy despite being encased in a hard, immobile shell. It moves in brief, erratic hops, which usually cause it to land on its side and become stuck.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME runs wild across the plains, trumpeting constantly. It's thought that it's attempting to create music, but its overly energetic nature results in atonal, discordant songs that repel listeners.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cannot sit still: the overwhelming energy in its body prevents it from properly resting or focusing for very long. If it cannot constantly channel its energy, its already-dangerous levels of stress can cause severe physical complications.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is in constant pain, struggling to move as it flails frantically. It is incredibly dangerous, as a single swipe from its tail claw is enough to cut a tree clean in half.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME impulsively shoves any small objects it can grab into its mouth, seemingly not caring if it can digest them or not. If it can't find something to fit in its mouth, it will constantly lick random objects.
author: mistymagius

entry: At dawn, POKENAME's vines flail unpredictably, grabbing anything in reach. It remains restless until calming down late into the evening.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to ambush random Pokémon, bombarding them with a flurry of quick strikes before they can react. While usually nocturnal, POKENAME has enough energy to go five days without sleep.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are usually found in the jungle, frantically climbing trees and swinging from vines. They love Custap berries as their bodies need lots of sugar to fuel their energy needs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoys dancing for others, but its hyperactive nature causes its dances to be unfocused and disorienting to most observers. It sulks and runs off if not applauded for its efforts.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon regularly faints because it has more power than its body can handle. POKENAME is always creaking because its body is always close to bursting with excess energy.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: If sleep-deprived, POKENAME secretes a red toxin that energizes others on contact. Victims become restless, unable to sleep.
author: .izik

entry: Because its body is so hyperactive, POKENAME has little to no control over its color change ability. Its constantly changing hues shift in an almost psychedelic pattern that can disorient friends and foes alike.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's clear poison grants bursts of hyperactivity followed by deep fatigue. It secretes more of this toxin when provoked in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's massive jaws are highly impulsive and react on instinct, chomping wildly at the mere scent of food in its vicinity. It takes considerable effort on the main body's part to reign it in once it gets going.
author: sk372

entry: It is considered highly dangerous due to having Slaking's strength with Vigoroth's inability to calm down. Even vicious and territorial Pokémon flee when POKENAME is seen rabidly charging through the area.
author: sk372

entry: If one spots pillars of light rapidly appearing and disappearing in the distance, it's likely a sign that POKENAME is present. Full of boundless energy, it cannot stay still and teleports constantly to blow off the excess steam.
author: sk372

entry: In its den, POKENAME coats the entrance in poison using its horn. It attacks intruders with Throat Chop before they can flee.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its wild personality and unstoppable amounts of energy, POKENAME is quite friendly towards its Trainer. However, be cautious, as POKENAME loves to tackle them at full force to show affection.
author: mistymagius

entry: Always brimming with excessive energy, POKENAME's ribbons whip around frantically at all times. One should keep their distance, as these ribbons are tipped with sharp claws that can cause painful gashes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's ribbons constantly thrash about around it due to its excessive energy. When on the defensive, it can sharpen the edges of the ribbons, using them to cut and slash at anything drawing too close.
author: sk372

entry: Chilan Berry-scented spores drift from POKENAME's head as it runs. Breathing them in triggers bursts of energy and erratic, playful movement within its own body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is perpetually in motion, flying around in random haphazard patterns to burn off a limitless supply of energy. Even the few moments it spends sleeping, its body still vibrates and its wings still twitch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins its webs at an incredible speed, creating complex woven structures in mere minutes. It moves so fast it builds up electricity, transferring it into the webs, which crackle and arc as it spins.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's flame burns with surprising vigor as it dashes through the forest to light up dark spots. However, it often crashes into trees by accident, sometimes starting small wildfires.
author: mistymagius

entry: A claw extends from POKENAME's mouth to crush coral with ease. It's highly selective, spitting out pieces it deems unworthy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets out a bellowing roar when it spots prey, sending them fleeing. It revels in the wild chase, driven by its boundless energy.
author: .izik

entry: Using aura senses, POKENAME searches for energetic Pokémon. Once found, it challenges them to rapid-fire sparring bouts.
author: .izik

entry: When the red tuft on its head suddenly stands on end, it is a sign that a storm is approaching. POKENAME moves swiftly among the tree branches it inhabits, using its long claws to cling to trunks while gathering fruit.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rotates furiously as it moves, radiating chaotic energy. This motion builds electricity that discharges on contact.
author: .izik

entry: In order to intimidate, POKENAME inflates its body before exhaling, waving its arms about while hooting wildly. For most, this has the opposite effect and makes it look rather comical instead.
author: sk372

entry: In groups, they watch Pokémon and Trainer alike with disdain and pull pranks on them. The length of their hair indicates their rank in the hierarchy.
author: ayner

entry: In combat, POKENAME spins its metal body while surging with energy. While spinning, it focuses to unleash devastating attacks.
author: .izik

entry: During early mornings, POKENAME is brimming with energy. It slams tree trunks with its finned head, leaving deep grooves to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME almost never sleeps, so it has to gobble down as much food as it can find to keep going. It can drain an entire watermelon of all of its fluids in less than 30 seconds.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME yearns to release all of its pent up energy, but it is too busy shivering in the cold to do anything about it.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME is completely blind, as the fruits on its head have eye-like markings to distract predators. While the fruits are incredibly bitter, they contain as much caffeine as fifteen shots of espresso, making them incredibly dangerous to consume.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its body constantly produces large amounts of adrenaline, so it ends up rampaging all over the forest. Despite how violent it can get, POKENAME doesn't like to intentionally hurt humans.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME leaps around frantically from tree to tree, spreading its spores. If inhaled, these spores induce hyperactivity and aggression in those affected, lasting a few hours before they collapse from exhaustion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cannot sit still if it tried, constantly twitching and shaking even while unconscious. While it has not been confirmed, Scientist theorize that POKENAME has the fastest heartbeat of any Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME never sleep and can be seen zipping around the forest all day and all night. However, they need to eat a lot of berries to keep going, usually feeding on Custap and Salac Berries specifically.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME floats on high to crash down into the ground at breakneck speed, before repeating the process. It does this to burn off an exceedingly vast supply of surplus energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's strong limbs and almost limitless energy allow for it to pursue its prey for up to 12 hours without tiring. Its hunts don't last that long, however, since POKENAME can run up to 60 mph.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's metabolism has hypercharged its psychic powers to the point of overwhelming its mind. It waddles around in a daze, its telekinesis uncontrollably lifting and flinging things around it without it even noticing.
author: sk372

entry: An overabundance of stamina means it's all but impossible for POKENAME to remain in one place. It teleports around constantly, seemingly at random, just to burn off excess psychic energy.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its lack of limbs, POKENAME struggles to sit still due to its boundless energy. Its tongue is coated in a potent stimulant that can cause insomnia for up to 3 days.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME raises its arms high so the eyes on its limbs can give it a better view of its surroundings. If it spots something interesting, it makes speedy leaps and bounds to hunt down the object of intrigue.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roll around on popular beaches, and due to their appearance, many tourists assume them to be volleyballs. Those unfortunate enough to use it for a game will get soaked by gallons of water when they decide to bump or spike it.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Walking is difficult for POKENAME as they are constantly off balance. They would walk on all fours if the size of their head was a bit smaller.
author: hummusishome

entry: It enjoys floating in the shallows with schools of its kind, releasing playful jets of water. These gentle currents provide protection to smaller sea Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: It gracefully glides through the water, spinning in circles to create mesmerizing whirlpools. These whirlpools help it catch smaller prey with minimal effort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dwells near the water's edge. While it will go ashore to play with people and Pokémon, it must be careful not to be played with too roughly: it cannot easily regenerate limbs like Staryu.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon uses its tooth comb to catch its food. With its nutrient rich diet, it grows fast.
author: _sadfroggy

entry: POKENAME trudge close to the banks of ponds and drag their leaves across the surface. In this way, they wet them with drops to cool themselves down.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME regularly jumps into lakes and rivers to cool off. In doing so, the buds on its body soak up water. They can hold it for months.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has a gentle and sociable disposition, which makes it a popular partner for Pokémon Trainers. It can emit refreshing water from its neck.
author: chorb33

entry: It produces pulses of light while swimming in the deep sea, guiding lost Pokémon toward safety. Fishermen have learned to follow its glow to find schools of smaller fish Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Its glowing orbs are visible even in the darkest ocean depths. Many sailors mistake it for a guiding light, unaware of the deep-sea creatures lurking nearby.
author: .izik

entry: It bounces playfully on the ocean's surface, using its rubbery body to create large splashes. Coastal towns often see them playing together during festivals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waddles through shallow waters with a carefree smile, using its tail to stir up mud. Though it looks harmless, it often causes trouble by accidentally dislodging fishing nets and dragging them to the depths.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME travels in small, tight groups, using their spiked bodies to protect one another. They communicate with low frequency calls to coordinate their movements as they drift through the sea in search of food.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It enjoys resting on coral beds, covering its body in shards of broken coral for camouflage. When startled, it spits them out at high speeds as a defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful tentacles to propel itself through the water with surprising speed. Its enormous mouth can vacuum up large schools of fish, which it then spits out in concentrated bursts to stun nearby prey.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It enjoys riding ocean currents alongside large groups of its kind, sometimes hitching rides on larger sea Pokémon. The smoother the current, the happier it seems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are hatched and raised for some time in underground lakes before leaving with their parents to go out to the ocean. The larger they become, the closer they are to evolution.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flies thanks to the steam it produces. The chemicals in its wings change color based on temperature.
author: ohok3441

entry: Despite its internal temperature, POKENAME's thick skin makes it safe to ride. It can travel long distances in both sky and sea.
author: ohok3441

entry: Its playful nature makes it a favorite among divers, often approaching them curiously. It emits joyful squeaks while gliding just beneath the waves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a clumsy but ambitious creature. It often trips and falls while walking on land.
author: neonriser

entry: POKENAME is found near dams made by other Bidoof and Bibarel, where it bathes in the sun and enjoys the fruits of the other Pokémon's labour. In return, POKENAME uses its body to temporarily block any leaks in the dam.
author: thescribe

entry: POKENAME spends its days rolling around the shore, using its inflated body as a giant cushion to bounce off rocks. Its massive size often causes unintended chaos, sending waves crashing and startling local wildlife with its clumsy antics.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Wild POKENAME eat pearls and use the magnetic field to traverse the seabed to hunt for Clampearl that hold them. They also hunt Spoink whenever POKENAME are on land.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Wild POKENAME use the magnetic field to determine where to migrate across the vast ocean. They often travel in groups and will use their magnetic waves to communicate with each other.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME only harvests the life force of schools of small fish. It enjoys splash-offs with beach goers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Though it smacks the life force out of small schools of fish, POKENAME also enjoys splashing water at beach-goers and being hit like a beach ball.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME are typically found stalking along the flooded shoreline in the aftermath of tsunamis. Pokémon Researchers actively debate why they do this, the leading theory is that they are brought ashore by the powerful currents creating the tidal wave.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It likes to play fight with its stretchy arms. When POKENAME drinks a lot of water, its tail inflates to the size of a beach ball, being just as bouncy as one.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time resting on the ocean floor by using their spiny appendages to latch onto rocks for stability. POKENAME have become a notorious pest to fishermen, often attaching to boats and stealing catches.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It can absorb over a ton of compost in a day. When its stomach is near to bursting it belches out a massive spray of spores.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME lives inside a bubble that provides it water to breathe with. When the bubble pops, POKENAME suffocates.
author: barry63_madrel

entry: POKENAME blow jets of water to scare nearby Pokémon. When threatened, they can leap even higher, showing true fear to any who witness this rage.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME hunt in small groups. It is very cowardly on its own and roams the ocean until it finds a new group if it loses its old one.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME hunt in small groups. It is very cowardly on its own and roams the ocean until it finds a new group if it loses its old one.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME collects air through its nostrils, which it stores in its body. When it sees prey, it expels it for additional acceleration.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME will release diluted, poisonous water from its blowhole when threatened or when it gets too excited. It often latches onto the bottoms of boats and uses its powerful jets to blast away any dangerous Pokémon that approach.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME need very little water to survive, but will swell larger to hold any excess water within their bodies. Once a year, a flower will bloom atop its head. Smaller POKENAME tend to have the prettiest and most fragrant flowers.
author: darkweavile428

entry: This buoyant Pokémon has no concept of personal space and excitedly crashes any boat party it sees.
author: .realthree

entry: Its vibrant blue scales shine brilliantly under the sun as it floats near coral reefs. If disturbed, it unleashes powerful psychic waves to scare away threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME duel on sunny beaches, but will immediately stop if either begins to dry out under the harsh rays. Due to this, many fights don't last over an hour.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hops along pond edges searching for prey like Ledyba. It launches into the air and dispatches them midflight with a powerful Bounce.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is most commonly seen on farms near large lakes and oceans. Farmers enjoy its presence because it naturally regulates water levels. Its bioluminescence allows it to see clearly in the dark.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is most commonly seen on farms near large lakes and oceans. Farmers enjoy its presence because it naturally regulates water levels. Its bioluminescence allows it to see clearly in the dark.
author: entomoxie

entry: When two POKENAME play together, their heart-shaped fins create elegant water patterns. Many believe seeing them leap together is a sign of everlasting love.
author: .izik

entry: It playfully races against fast swimmers, using jets of water to propel itself forward. Trainers believe swimming alongside it enhances endurance.
author: .izik

entry: When surfacing for air, POKENAME sometimes knocks over small boats. It mistakes the people in the water for its playmates and tries to play by bumping into them. Thankfully, it only lasts for a few minutes before POKENAME gets bored and swims away.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is a fun-loving Pokémon that enjoys relaxing on the beach. Its favorite means of relaxation is trying to fight other wild Pokémon.
author: usaginezumi

entry: The brain of a POKENAME is slowly being eaten away as the Tentacool provides too much of a suction effect. The Wailmer spends all its life in pain.
author: watermelonchild

entry: POKENAME is often seen drifting in shallow waters, with its tentacles twitching in unexplained patterns. Researchers have been unable to determine its purpose, but its presence seems to cause strange disruptions in local marine ecosystems.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME often waddles onto land by using its small fins to support its bulk as it shuffles through city streets. While harmless, it often causes minor chaos by blocking roads and sneaking into markets in search of food.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME makes the star on its tail shine brightly whenever it feels threatened. It can produce a delicate, luxurious silk used to craft elegant evening gowns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME wears the skull of a deceased Electric-type Pokémon of great power so it may grow as strong as its parents. Although its head is too large for the bone, it serves its purpose by boosting POKENAME's morale.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Despite the poor camouflage of POKENAME, they are rarely attacked by larger Pokémon. When researching why this was, it was discovered that their chrysalis carries a static charge that causes painful shocks when touched.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have wing scales that each carry a slight electrical charge. When they feel threatened, POKENAME can send an electrical pulse through their wings that causes them to abruptly light up, blinding their assailants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is able to flatten itself paper-thin and course electricity through its body. It often hides on trails or in doorways and shocks unsuspecting Trainers who step on it.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME generates electricity by absorbing sunlight, its yellow leaves glowing brightly when fully charged. Campers often keep POKENAME as they act as solar-powered batteries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can rub its fur together to build up static electricity. The individual strands of hair on its body form a network that channels this energy into a single point on its back.
author: danonzer

entry: POKENAME flares up the electric patches of its body as a way of socializing with others of its kind. Showering sparks on each other is considered a gesture of deep friendship between POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: They are most active just after rainy days, when bug Pokémon scurry out of their dens. While wild POKENAME have an aggressive disposition, properly trained POKENAME are quite friendly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is just light enough for its tail to lift it into the air. It uses this to appear taller and to see above tall grass.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through the talons on its feet. It often perches high in trees and drops down to shock unsuspecting Trainers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: If it concentrates hard enough, POKENAME can use its electricity to make the spots on its back light up. Groups of them playfully compare flashing patterns and colors when gathering together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's webbing contains a faint electrical charge that causes it to glow in the dark. This light attracts insects into the webbing at night, allowing it to capture plenty of potential meals.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly rubs its cheeks to ease the ache of stored electricity. Sparks leak from the star on its tail when it struggles to hold the charge.
author: .izik

entry: It relies on its parents and siblings to avoid being picked off by buzzard-like predators, as it has few methods of self-defense. One such method requires inhaling lots of air before exhaling all at once to fly away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail lights up to communicate with partners in the dark. At night, a flock of POKENAME resembles the stars in the sky!
author: alliveir

entry: They float on the winds to move around. If they encounter a thunderstorm, their bodies glow with electricity.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: POKENAME has a capricious personality and are easily distracted by its surroundings. Trainers tend to bribe it with food to ensure that it focuses during training.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME crackles with energy from the feather on its head. The brightness of the sparks reveals its health and mood.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has a love for Honey. It can be found by hives of Combee, using the light emitting from its tail to distract them while it eats its fill.
author: curvingapollo

entry: POKENAME travel in groups of three to four for safety when moving about in the woods. If one of them becomes separated from the others at night, they light up with a flare of electricity to make themselves more visible and reunite with their friends.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's thick fur shines when it eats. It uses its tail to send jolts of electricity through the nearby ground to immobilize small prey.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME is very hyperactive, always running around and attempting to play-fight anything it sees. As it runs, small sparks of electricity jolt and crackle all over its body.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME coils tightly around its foe while rattling its tail. As it tightens, it builds a charge, then releases a burst of electricity all at once.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sneeze out bolts of electricity from its snout. These flashes of electricity can momentarily blind people or other Pokémon but are otherwise harmless.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It creates paintings under UV lights with the solar charged paint from the tip of its tail. POKENAME shocks those who mock its art.
author: luludracon

entry: POKENAME is incredibly energetic and can go for almost 3 days straight without rest. Its fur stores large amounts of static electricity, causing its strikes to give its opponent a powerful shock.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME zips across the sky on its star-shaped tail, leaving bright streaks of light behind it. It must recharge its tail after flight, generating more electricity by absorbing starlight.
author: mistymagius

entry: While dancing, POKENAME stores electricity in the pom-pom on its head. Interrupting its routine often results in a shocking retaliation.
author: .izik

entry: While tunneling, POKENAME builds electricity in its tail. Electricians study its tail tip, which can deliver precise shocks strong enough to disable larger foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prowls the forest with feline grace. Its agile movements and powerful strikes make it a formidable hunter in the dense foliage.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME is quick to form psychic connections with those it considers friends. When in the presence of intense emotions, it converts its psychic energies into a latent, static charge.
author: turron_turron

entry: Rumors claim that POKENAME are the souls of Shinx that never got to live past a very young age. The halo-like item above its head supports that theory, but there is no scientific study that confirms this.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME nibbles down trees using its big buck teeth. After they fall, it brands them using electricity and its star-shaped tail.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Despite its look, POKENAME's tail is stiff and made of steel. Its tail is notorious for accidentally breaking nearby objects when POKENAME gets excited.
author: retrodox

entry: When the sky gets dark and stormy, groups of POKENAME come out of hiding and play in the thunderstorm. They absorb electricity through their fur, their tails glowing brightly when fully charged.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon fights with a steel blade which it infuses with electricity. It is incredibly adept at parrying every attack that is thrown its way before retaliating with a single decisive strike.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME is known as 'Thunder Cloud' by some for being as soft as a cloud and the constant static it emits. Its fluffy coat requires daily brushing, often leaving its Trainer's hair to be just as fluffy as a result.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: The star-like parts of POKENAME's tails glow red-hot during battle. The stronger its electric attacks, the hotter they burn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly energetic Pokémon, playfully running around all day and night. It stores large amounts of electricity in its fur and is able to channel it into powerful physical attacks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body crackles with electricity, giving it short bursts of energy that make it extremely hyperactive. Once this energy wears off, it returns to its lazy state.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME makes for a horrible pet. While it may seem cute with its gigantic forehead, many pet owners forget about its equally big bite. Countless pieces of furniture fall victim to its dreaded "biting fit" that even reinforced steel fails to stop.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME mimics humans using illusions while it hunts. Tiny sparks left in its footsteps are the only clue it was ever there.
author: .izik

entry: The star on its tail emits flickering lights that vary in intensity depending on its mood. By rubbing its teeth together, POKENAME can generate small sparks, which it uses to ignite tiny fires to stay warm while it sleeps in its den.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME glow as they float aimlessly through the night, providing light to anyone they pass by. Sometimes, children who sneak out of the house at night will hold onto a POKENAME to use as a lantern, though these children don't always return home.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME  are formed of a dense and sticky gel that carries a potent electrical charge. Trainers are advised to avoid handling them for too long as POKENAME tend to release powerful shocks if they become too agitated.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As it flies, POKENAME releases shocks from its tails to stun prey. It then swarms the target with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is the perfect partner for any rookie Trainer starting their journey. It has a strong bond to its Trainer and will always be by their side.
author: funkytomate

entry: Whenever it is in the presence of a pack of carnivores, it jabs the nearest predator before flicking its tail to dash away. Whether being chased through the jungle or not, POKENAME continuously zips around in search of food or safety.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Flocks of POKENAME travel in thunderstorms, storing electricity in their wings. However, they sometimes get knocked out of the clouds by large hailstones.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are highly affectionate, but also highly independent Pokémon. Trainers whose POKENAME go missing can often find them following the nearest storm.
author: geo_ominous

entry: Static builds within POKENAME's cottony body as it moves. Even a gentle hug can result in jolts powerful enough to leave mild burns.
author: .izik

entry: A tenacious hunter, POKENAME can paralyze its prey in multiple different ways. They have been known to challenge Pokémon much larger than themselves.
author: leonian1586

entry: All POKENAME have a form of synesthesia that makes them able to see sounds. Because of that, they have a greater understanding of sound and music.
author: voxary

entry: POKENAME is skittish and shy, sending spores out at any creature who comes too close. It has multiple methods of paralyzing its foes. It seems to have lost the confidence it had when it was small.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME uses its photosynthetic fur to take in sunlight to generate electricity. When threatened, a POKENAME will release a pleasant aroma that can blind its foes so that it may run away.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME's long, stiff fur easily conducts static electricity. Some POKENAME even end up sticking to one another if enough static is built up.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses the lily pad on its head to absorb lightning during storms. It stores the energy to shock predators that get too close.
author: .izik

entry: The fur of POKENAME builds up static charge through its restless movements. In danger, it unleashes this energy, causing the yellow bands on its coat to shine dazzlingly, blinding its enemies while it flees away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Static electricity allows POKENAME to stick coins and bottle caps to its fur. It treasures anything shiny and builds small hoards.
author: .izik

entry: Excitable and friendly, POKENAME's fur quickly charges with static electricity. During play, it can unintentionally shock playmates, so it is mostly found around other Electric-type Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: When playing fetch, POKENAME becomes overjoyed. Sparks leap from its fur as it dashes, leaving a trail of static behind.
author: .izik

entry: It swims with its tail above water so as not to electrocute other aquatic Pokémon. Unfortunately, this acts as a perfect lightning rod during storms.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME sits near the coastline, its ears perking up when a thunderstorm is nearby. It communicates with blinking lights from its tail, even though it will often forget what these signals mean.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME bury themselves in the ocean floor with their claws poking above the water. They blind their prey with bright flashes from their claws before dragging them below the sand.
author: floopussoupus

entry: POKENAME touches its tail to electric poles to absorb power. If it takes in too much, it will explode violently.
author: .izik

entry: Although it often appears to be a single lopsided individual, POKENAME is a clutch of six separate pieces. They move as one singular unit to better combine their electricity powers for defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME emerge from their nests as thunderstorms approach, sparks dancing across their wings as electrical potential builds in the air. They are sometimes drawn to power plants, mistaking the generators for incoming thunder clouds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is fierce and entitled. It prefers to swim in pristine lakes or private pools filled with filtered glacier water. POKENAME allows itself to be easily caught so it can be pampered.
author: princessmilandria

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as electrical equipment near power substations. When unobserved, it feeds on stored electricity with a faint hum.
author: .izik

entry: The pointy fur on POKENAME's body is always coursing with electricity. When frightened, it discharges more power than a lightning rod can handle.
author: .izik

entry: During thunderstorms, POKENAME watches the lightning in awe from tree branches. If a large strike is coming, it hoots in excitement.
author: .izik

entry: Their only means of communication deep undersea are the sparks from their antennae. The POKENAME will sometimes lose control, shocking anyone nearby.
author: currentlymuffin

entry: POKENAME gnaws on wires in power plants. When startled, it discharges enough electricity to knock itself out.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long tail to launch bursts of electricity, knocking Nanab Berries from trees with expert aim.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies in Z-shaped patterns over lakes looking for prey. If it spots a Magikarp, it unleashes an electrical shock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends its days watching people talk, imitating words it hears. If it feels it hasn't done a good job, it will release sparks from its tail in frustration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME communicates telepathically by controlling the electrical impulses in the brains of others. It is said to be able to ease memory-related illnesses by manipulating these same impulses.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME use solar energy collected by their leaves to create an electrical charge within their body. Their bulb carries the bulk of this charge, and touching the petals can deliver a painful shock to the unwary.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME discharges enough electricity from its front teeth to electrify a small pond, using this ability to knock out prey like Goldeen. It will glow yellow before a powerful attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels electricity into its claws to attack, divebombing prey under the cover of night. Its claws are strong enough to crush tree trunks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will clean its fur meticulously to help channel electricity through its body. Its exceptional eyesight can pick out movement in dense brush. Once close, it will let loose an Icy Wind to slow its prey before striking with charged claws.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME flies through storm clouds to absorb electricity, glowing yellow if it gathers too much. During this period it will be extremely irritable.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires bright sparks from its tail to scare away predators. It shields smaller Pokémon behind its insulated, floppy ears to protect them from the sparks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME places its tail on electric appliances to steal power. If overcharged, it moves rapidly from one point to another, unable to slow down.
author: .izik

entry: The eyes on POKENAME's pattern flash every time they use an Electric attack. Their mane puffs up with the static as well, making POKENAME look even more fearsome.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME gather in closely-huddled groups for better self-preservation. By keeping their tails in contact, they can share and combine their electricity into massive amounts of voltage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be heard chanting an odd cry during thunderstorms. It is not a known language, and many assume it is chanting a curse of some kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers crackle with static as it flies, calling down lightning to strike anyone near its nest. It sparks even while asleep due to the high voltage coursing through its body.
author: .izik

entry: It passively stores electricity in its claws while it rolls around. A fully charged slash can cause even the mightiest Pokémon to faint.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It passively stores electricity in its claws while it rolls around. A fully charged slash can cause even the mightiest Pokémon to faint.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Drawn to magnetic materials, it loves to bat at Nosepass like it was a ball of yarn. Its sharp claws pulse with potent electricity.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's softer head is often mistaken for Shieldon's more sought-after, harder head. While in wild grass, both have their heads poking out, but you can differentiate them by the spike on POKENAME's.
author: retrodox

entry: When POKENAME faces an opponent it truly wishes to battle, the flame atop its head flares brightly. During combat, its fur crackles with static sparks, keeping its body charged with energy until the fight is over.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its blades glow when it uses its electric powers. It can touch blades with other POKENAME to combine their electricity into a more powerful attack.
author: cait_sith

entry: Because of its middling defenses, POKENAME hunts with sneaky tactics. It floats silently down to prey before zapping them unconscious with its paws, making it easy to carry them away without a fuss or fight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's brass rings crackle with electrical energy, jingling as it floats through the air. It is extremely energized during thunderstorms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs into the dirt to create tunnels. Its excitement for digging somehow generates electricity, which builds as it enjoys its task.
author: .izik

entry: From its riverside lodge, POKENAME senses threats with sharp instincts. At night, it releases powerful lightning strikes to keep predators away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channel electric shocks through their steel armor, which is made from discarded Aron shells. If a particularly large or well-armored Aron is sighted, POKENAME will form packs to hunt it for its shell.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME floats through power plants, checking equipment with its tail. If it detects an issue, it lets out a loud screech to alert the workers.
author: .izik

entry: The size of the sparking flame on POKENAME's tail indicates how much electric power it has in reserve. It channels this electricity into its claws, or for short bursts of lightning breath.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME surround themselves in an electrically charged gel, protecting their small and vulnerable bodies. They defend themselves with their electrokinetic powers, enabling them to fight without physical altercation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gelatinous membrane encasing POKENAME's body stores excess electricity like a battery. Sparks constantly dance across its surface as it floats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases bolts of electricity from its tail to stun foes, then sucks their blood afterward. It prefers to only hunt at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays on cave floors waiting for prey. If stepped on, it unleashes enough electricity to charge the skin of its attacker.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME consumes e-waste to absorb latent electrical energy. Sifting through dumpsters is its primary way to find food, as even small scraps can sustain it for weeks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather together on power lines and rub their wings against each other, creating powerful static shocks. Power plants often need to shoo flocks of POKENAME to prevent them from damaging the lines with their static.
author: geo_ominous

entry: The yellow stripes on its arms glow with electricity and will scorch pawmarks into trees to mark its territory. While hunting, it will run on all fours to increase its speed.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME performs acrobatic movements while jumping from tree to tree, pulsing with electrical energy. The air moving through its wings somehow charges its body.
author: .izik

entry: The small crystals around its neck collect static electricity from the surrounding area. When the crystals are charged, POKENAME becomes more energetic and will release the electricity in small bursts.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight into its fur to charge electricity within its body, unleashing the energy from its maw. Its fur will stand on end when fully charged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME touches its tail to outlets to gather electricity. When fully charged, it releases a scent similar to Razz Berries.
author: .izik

entry: It's rumored that POKENAME can predict where lightning will strike. Whenever these Pokémon gather in numbers, people tend to stay indoors.
author: archserpent

entry: POKENAME that find their way into the wild are formidable predators, using their electrical, webbed claws to swim at incredible speeds and hunt aquatic prey with ease.
author: bigblue

entry: As POKENAME ages, its fur darkens and grows longer, trading off swimming speed for protection. As it grows stronger, it prefers hunting prey on land to avoid electrocuting itself.
author: bigblue

entry: POKENAME's tail flutters as it floats above buildings. The fur tuft on its head is made of trillions of tiny metal wires.
author: .izik

entry: After feasting on dreams, POKENAME's body surges with electric energy. It crackles with power, sometimes even gleefully discharging shocks from its ears after eating pleasant dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME meticulously maintains its fur and zaps anyone who ruins it. Recent fashion trends in the region have been influenced by its appearance.
author: noel5229

entry: Inside the bulb on its back, POKENAME hides a microphone that amplifies its songs and sounds like a speaker. Anyone who listens to its melodies inevitably falls asleep, which is why POKENAME is often used to treat insomnia.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many people who see its shape mistake it for that of a regular Voltorb, but it's in fact just a Jigglypuff seen from above.
author: nasho1908

entry: As a gesture of friendship, POKENAME love to sing for their friends. Their soft lullabies will put anyone to sleep.
author: smashbear

entry: The singing of a POKENAME can reach far and wide, often putting entire villages or towns to sleep at once.
author: smashbear

entry: Every morning, POKENAME can be found practicing their singing. Weak or unenthusiastic singers risk being kicked out of the group.
author: busilisk

entry: POKENAME sings slow, plaintive songs into the microphone it carries. Those that fall asleep to the song dream of happy times with family.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases psychoactive fumes that cause a state similar to drunkenness. The sound it produces when releasing them is also pretty mesmerizing to hear.
author: epping_forest

entry: If POKENAME's song is heard by an unfused Metapod it can be thrust into a deep rest. For an unknown reason, upon waking, no matter how short their rest, the Metapod will immediately evolve.
author: bradlybro199

entry: If POKENAME finds a sleeping Pokémon in the wild, it gently places them in its pouch. It then hums a soft melody to ensure they rest peacefully.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has very slimy, gooey skin, but is able to manipulate it to appear soft and delicate. It loves to be petted and approaches Trainers and Pokémon. Should anything it approaches become aggressive, it sings a sweet melody to pacify them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's haunting, melodic cry echoes through the deep, luring creatures ever closer until its tentacles strike without mercy. Fossils of POKENAME have been discovered embedded in ancient seafloor mudstone, surrounded by the remains of its prey.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME sings the same ancient melodies that were present in prehistoric times. It sees no need to innovate or change the lullabies it sings, even when Pokémon no longer fall asleep listening to it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Hikers often run into POKENAME during high-altitude expeditions, the snake-like Pokémon being highly curious and unafraid of humans. When hungry, POKENAME will actively seek out people and sing them to sleep, stealing food from their backpacks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The songs that POKENAME sing are soothing to both people and Pokémon. So soothing, in fact, that those who hear it fall into a near-endless slumber.
author: chiari_queen

entry: The songs that POKENAME sing are soothing to both people and Pokémon. So soothing, in fact, that those who hear it fall into a near-endless slumber.
author: chiari_queen

entry: Wherever POKENAME sings, flowers bloom and Flying-type Pokémon gather. If angered, it uses a shrill Disarming Voice, calling forth the army of flyers to destroy its aggressor.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME hunts near watering holes and uses its lullabies, which sound more like soft soothing growls than actual singing, to put its prey asleep. Its lung capacity allows it to sing or hide underwater for hours without the need to breathe.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's preferred method of attack involves latching onto its opponent's face with its powerful jaws and letting out an ear-piercing shriek. It exhibits violent and overtly confrontational behavior, so rigorous training is almost always required.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's preferred method of attack involves latching onto its opponent's face with its powerful jaws and letting out an ear-piercing shriek. It exhibits violent and overtly confrontational behavior, so rigorous training is almost always required.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are known to perch themselves on tree branches and survey the area below. They often scare children due to their large and watchful eyes.
author: adam941

entry: Groups of wild POKENAME are known to be gentle and friendly. Their song is so potent that they are known to put themselves to sleep.
author: robbery_666

entry: Flocks of POKENAME sing all throughout the night, slowly lulling anyone who hears them to sleep. They cheerfully sway to the melody as they sing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sings with a prosaic voice that sounds closer to speech than music. People who listen to its song fall asleep out of boredom. Some Pokémon come to listen to its song at the same time every night to ensure they fall asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME chirps out a lullaby every sunset that helps other Pokémon fall asleep. Once they are asleep, POKENAME swoops down from tree branches to pick off bug Pokémon that are not in their burrows.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have weak muscles in their arms, so they rely on their musical talent to escape danger. Their adorable babbling beguiles many Trainers into keeping them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As they enter Pokémon contests, Trainers may give them a Pink Scarf for good luck. They flaunt their shells to emphasize their rotund form, and the scarf helps give them a rounder, cuter look.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pecks at trees with hollow points to determine which will grant it the best reverb. Once it finds a suitable hole to hop into, it sings short songs and enjoys the echo it gains.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME can be seen singing in monotone during the twilight hours of dawn and dusk. Their singing is actually a form of meditation.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME's lightweight body allows them to clear the average house in a single jump. These Pokémon nest along lakes, using their excellent hearing to track prey beneath the water.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME seems to resemble an ancient depiction of Jigglypuff. By inhaling deeply and expanding its body, it belts out an ear-splitting scream that disorients those around it. It uses its long hair to force foes to be closer before it screams.
author: chibitales

entry: Its leaves can come in a few different colors. It uses them to float around in the wind. It sings happily as it drifts, relaxing those who hear it.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME doesn't use much energy while waiting to evolve, gathering in places where both moonlight and sunlight can shine clearly on its leaves. It will sing with others as a last resort, putting predators to sleep before fleeing to safety.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's wings buzz in different tones depending on how they steer or travel during flight. Groups of POKENAME gather together to fly in complex routines to perform whimsical melodies together.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Those who meet POKENAME often become entranced by its gaze, unable to look away. While they're mesmerised, it softly sings, easing their worries. Overwhelmed by emotion, listeners often burst into tears that POKENAME gently collects and drinks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Those who meet POKENAME often become entranced by its gaze, unable to look away. While they're mesmerised, it softly sings, easing their worries. Overwhelmed by emotion, listeners often burst into tears that POKENAME gently collects and drinks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When its Trainer falls ill, POKENAME sings gentle lullabies to help them fall asleep and recover. Its soothing abilities are cherished by Pokémon Center staff, and it is often found accompanying the nurses.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body is filled with air. It uses its fangs to clamp down on surfaces to avoid floating away while sleeping.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon uses hypnotic illusions to lull threats to sleep. Using this ability, it's a perfect aid for those who suffer from insomnia.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: Carvings of POKENAME can be seen on the walls of ancient ruins. They form the notes to a lullaby that can make you sleepy just by looking at it.
author: serversizeme

entry: Multiple POKENAME will line up in a pattern that mimics musical notation. Anyone who tries to decipher what the song is will drift into a deep sleep.
author: serversizeme

entry: POKENAME's body can withstand immense pressure due to being full of air most of the time. Because of this, its ability to counterattack is limited, as even a small hit sends it flying.
author: evilgammon

entry: When threatened, POKENAME puffs up its body to endure the attack and lull the opponent to sleep. If it's successful, it goes for a counterattack soon after.
author: cascadeguy

entry: After putting a foe to sleep, POKENAME uses its strong claws to grab them tightly. It prefers to strike from above, dropping in silently after its lullaby takes effect.
author: .izik

entry: No matter the color of the berries POKENAME consumes, the resulting berry juice always comes out a light shade of pink. POKENAME's juice is regarded as a highly effective sleep aid.
author: sk372

entry: After eating honey, POKENAME's voice becomes wildly off-key. Despite this, it continues to sing with great enthusiasm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sings at the entrance of tunnels to lull the inhabitants inside to sleep. It then uses its long beak to reach in and pluck out unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can puff their bodies up to twice their size, sucking in air to scare off predators. When they exhale, they do so slowly, making surprisingly soothing songs that can carry across vast distances.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are trained by musicians to perform short songs. They can be difficult to work with because they frequently get hungry during practice.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The milk POKENAME produces has potent sleep-inducing properties. Strangely, even touching the milk without drinking it can cause sudden drowsiness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME take great pride in having the most stylish and well-maintained curls. They are often seen absentmindedly staring into a lake while trimming them. Though exposed to predators while doing this, their brute strength keeps them safe.
author: leandermalurt

entry: They say POKENAME makes mirrors with a magic wand. It mimics other Pokémon, but sometimes pretends it can't make any sound.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME makes its burrows amongst tree roots, using the extra structure of the roots to reinforce its underground home. At night, they often come to the mouth of their burrows and sing out to one another to communicate.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME trains with others of its kind, boxing with its puffy claws and racing across tree branches. When it feels prepared to strike out on its own, it travels into the mountains in search of a Moon Stone to evolve.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME adores repeating music it hears with a variety of boops and beeps. It likes to insert itself into different mediums to continue singing.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME have beautiful singing voices that capture the attention of everyone listening, putting them into a trance. They use their emotional sensitivity to tailor their songs for their audience, making every performance unique.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have beautiful singing voices that capture the attention of everyone listening, putting them into a trance. They use their emotional sensitivity to tailor their songs for their audience, making every performance unique.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have beautiful singing voices that capture the attention of everyone listening, putting them into a trance. They use their emotional sensitivity to tailor their songs for their audience, making every performance unique.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is lauded for its beautiful singing voice. It is most commonly seen either on the stage performing small concerts, or working in nurseries providing the most soothing of lullabies to children.
author: sk372

entry: Colonies of POKENAME communicate with others across their mountain homes by singing in harmony. Each colony has a unique chorus, and experienced hikers can use these songs to navigate when lost.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With a rubbery body and naturally playful attitude, POKENAME often puts itself into dangerous situations trying to befriend much more powerful Pokémon. Even those it does get close to don't often stick around as it's prone to biting.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wards away rivals from its caves with loud songs that can be heard for several miles. Their songs are unpleasant and atonal, meaning many other Pokémon also keep away from them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The harmonies produced when POKENAME sing have a mesmerizing quality. Unwary Trainers may find themselves waking up in the wilderness with their backpacks raided for berries.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Unlike many other Jigglypuff fusions, POKENAME wants others to fall asleep during its concert performance. It gets angry and violent towards anyone still awake when it finishes singing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in abandoned houses to be all alone. Sometimes, groups of POKENAME can be seen doing some sort of ritual.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME lives in abandoned houses to be all alone. Sometimes, groups of POKENAME can be seen doing some sort of ritual.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is many people's worst nightmare. It behaves similarly to a Jigglypuff, but it instead puts its targets into sleep paralysis with its song.
author: kermeros

entry: POKENAME's gentle cry can be heard from miles away. Anyone who hears its cry feels a sense of serenity and relaxation.
author: mistymagius

entry: The garden on its back is said to be able to even calm down the most angry Primeape. Many Pokémon like to gather around it to sing.
author: funkytomate

entry: POKENAME sing soft melodies to lull larger Pokémon into slumber before shuffling past. If the Pokémon wakes up before POKENAME can sneak past, then they attack with their venomous horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME vibrates its blade which hums a beautiful lullaby. When its opponent falls asleep, it finishes the job.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME have a sharp, venomous horn that is capable of taking down a Rhyhorn. They prefer to lull larger Pokémon to sleep instead of tackling them head-on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves to lure lost sailors to its lair with its beautiful singing. Many old maritime tales were told by those who claimed to have seen it.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: POKENAME is popular amongst daycare workers due to its soothing singing voice and ability to calm fussy toddlers with its ribbons.
author: melodydelune

entry: On full moon nights, POKENAME sings directly to the moon. When five or more gather, their combined voices are said to evoke deep sorrow in anyone who hears them.
author: .izik

entry: Commonly found in cities, these Pokémon love attention and showing off, singing and dancing happily. They pay close attention to the latest trends.
author: cristata

entry: Commonly found in cities, these Pokémon love attention and showing off, singing and dancing happily. They pay close attention to the latest trends.
author: cristata

entry: The music played by POKENAME has strong soporific qualities. Much like Jigglypuff, POKENAME becomes enraged when its audience cannot stay awake until the end of its song.
author: alestrius

entry: At night, it stares into the sky before beginning to sing. It will do this until morning, and will not remember doing so afterwards.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME catches other Pokémon's attention with its beautiful eyes, then uses its melodic voice to lull them to sleep. Next, POKENAME weaves a cocoon of electrically charged web around its prey and devours them.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: This Pokémon enjoys singing to others, and listeners of POKENAME's songs find them eerily soothing. However, cases have been found of Pokémon and humans alike dying after listening to their songs for too long.
author: dahappycute

entry: POKENAME flutters from tree to tree with its small wings, singing a gentle tune. It pauses only to nibble on freshly budding leaves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sing sorrowful songs in search of companionship from others of their species, crooning from high in the treetops. Unfortunately their songs send other POKENAME to sleep, lulling them into inactivity.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can inflate its hollow tail with gas, which allows it to leap to great heights. Its voice has a distinct melodic quality that lulls listeners to peaceful sleep when it sings. It will use this chance to steal food from its victims.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME love to perform and seek out large gatherings of other Pokémon to sing to. The effects of their voice are even more soporific than those of unfused Jigglypuff. Very few Pokémon have the willpower to stay awake through the whole performance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Fused POKENAME bear a striking resemblance to an alleged 1-billion-year-old Jigglypuff found in a paranormal magazine. It's currently unknown why this happens.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME sings atop volcanic plateaus, its voice carrying over the fiery landscape. The glow of lava below gives its performances an almost hypnotic allure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known to be melancholic and enjoys laying on the ground, doing nothing. It makes chilling music that's very popular for Halloween.
author: galactak

entry: POKENAME often sings as a form of sonar to detect obstacles. They may also sing to put predators asleep.
author: phrotonz

entry: POKENAME's tiny body makes it difficult to locate before its entrancing voice sends listeners to sleep. It then snuggles up to them and absorbs static electricity for its own use.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME's fusion has matched its playfulness with a ferocious streak. Games of catch amuse it endlessly.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: POKENAME waddles through grasslands, doing nothing in particular besides absorbing sunlight. If it stores up enough sunlight, it can fire beams of solar energy from its single eye.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are tolerated in nests of other Pokémon because their soft bodies and fluffy wings make them comfy to sleep with. They also sing lullabies that make for a pleasant sleeping experience.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can puff up to more than twice their starting body size thanks to having an extremely elastic skin. They use this stored air to sing to one another across vast distances, their yodels being audible from miles away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often gets mistaken for a cute plush doll. If it gets picked up by unsuspecting children, it flails its arms incredibly violently until put down.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: This Pokémon loves to battle. However, it is notorious for its showmanship. POKENAME will always sing a "walk-up" song to hype itself up before entering a battle.
author: mbo1064.

entry: During cold, winter nights, Herds of POKENAME can be heard singing a sweet and calming tune. Each POKENAME herd has their own unique lullaby but will happily sing along with other herds.
author: mistymagius

entry: The beautiful songs POKENAME sings are able to put any who hear them into a restful sleep. Melodies recorded from them are sold all over the world as sleep aids.
author: chibitales

entry: Its color and fuzzy appearance make it quite popular with young girls. It prefers lingering in areas with low light, singing soft little songs that put itself and others at ease.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats gently through the night sky, singing with joy. Most who hear its lullaby can't stay awake long enough to hear it finish.
author: .izik

entry: A muffled song echoes from within POKENAME's rocky shell as it drifts through the sky. If it senses someone isn't listening, it will explode in a fit of rage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's singing voice is so comforting that Trainers and Pokémon alike sleep soundly when they listen to it. POKENAME also relaxes when it sings, its flame calming it, feeling like a warm campfire.
author: sockedpuppetart

entry: POKENAME sings cheerfully while digging alongside others of its kind. The melody is soothing enough to lull nearby tunneling Pokémon into sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's three heads sing in perfect unison when someone approaches. The melody entrances prey, luring them toward hidden pitfalls.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sings a soft lullaby to lull Pokémon to sleep. Once they are certain other Pokémon are asleep, they snack on berries without worrying about Electric-type Pokémon zapping them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lulls other Pokémon to sleep with their melodic singing. They make sure that other Pokémon are sleeping before eating to avoid the risk of getting hurt by a Rock-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Flocks of POKENAME circle above beaches while singing softly. Once beachgoers fall asleep, they swoop down to steal unattended food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very playful and hyperactive. Once it gets going, it bounces around the room for minutes without stopping thanks to its flexible body.
author: chorb33

entry: Its meowing has an incredibly soporific effect, which is why it is particularly popular with people with sleep problems.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME love to sing but often forget their songs put other Pokémon to sleep. Once POKENAME realize their audience is asleep, they move on to another crowd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME sings, snow begins to gently fall. Watching the snowflakes from a POKENAME's flurry is a great way to fall asleep.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME keep their fur tidy by rubbing their fur against rocks, which leaves tufts of fur behind. They practice their musical howling when they are not grooming themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If its Trainer is worried about something, it sings to ease their anxiety. Its pink fur is extremely soft and warm, so much so that other Pokémon often use POKENAME's coat as a cushion to sleep on at night.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has the vocal power of a tenor and can carry its songs across the entire valley it calls home. Its broad wings allow it to reach high vantage points from which it lets its melodies descend.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME inhale lots of air into their stomachs before a performance. Many audience members are mesmerized by the pattern on their bellies and the gentle song that POKENAME sing, which causes most to fall asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a musical melody spiraling around its stomach. Those that replicate this melody find it to be an incredibly effective lullaby.
author: gronkissimo

entry: When faced with an opponent stronger than itself, it will swallow extra air to make its muscles look bigger. However, it tends to overinflate itself, causing it immense pain.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME whistles a delightful tune said to help plants grow. It can often be found in the middle of daisy fields, singing softly as flowers sway around it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely affectionate and cuddly, which makes it a popular pet. When it feels comfortable, it hums gently to itself.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME uses its hollow body as a means of amplifying the sound of its songs. During the rainy season, it is filled with rainwater, altering the types of sounds it can produce.
author: .7soul

entry: POKENAME is confident in its singing and will not hesitate to use its powerful fists to wallop anything it thinks is mocking or ignoring it. Its vocalizations invigorate listeners, pumping them up for physical feats of strength.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's fur clumps up with dirt and stones as it wanders about its habitat, leading to a rough, bumpy appearance. When it rolls downhill, the clumps become dislodged and are collected by nesting Pokémon, like Geotto.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's lack of care for its coat has turned the clumps of fur into dense tufts that impede its movement but aid in protection. It is lighter than its appearance indicates, which can be witnessed as it bounces along mountain ranges.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME accompanies its soporific singing with a rhythmic dragging of its tail. It protects its flexible body with a hard shell.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's soft body crackles with electricity while it floats near power plants. When it sings, tiny sparks escape its mouth and fall to the ground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often float by people as they walk, looking at them with a pleading face. If given a gift, it will sing happily before floating away. Some children have even made a game of giving POKENAME increasingly elaborate gifts.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME digs large tunnels all through its cavernous homes to make for better acoustics for its music. Its song echoes through every chamber of the cave, putting every other creature to sleep so it may roam freely.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME store toxic spores within their body and release them through the holes in their body. These concentrated bursts of spores can knock out an angry Mankey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eats leaves from bushes near factories and are capable of consuming the ash-colored soot that ends up clinging to leaves. Their powerful stomachs neutralize the poisonous soot to convert it into nutrients.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a tungsten shell, allowing it to roll across rough landscapes with ease. If interrupted while traveling, it unleashes a powerful Electro Ball.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME were once trained by soldiers to explode after crossing a battlefield. The force of the explosion can create tremors in the nearby area.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It wears the shed armor of its mother as a hand-me-down, the last thing it has to remember her by.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The steel that makes up an POKENAME's fins is extremely flexible and malleable. Schools of POKENAME blind predators by reflecting sunlight off of their metallic bodies.
author: alestrius

entry: When POKENAME spins its metallic body rapidly, it can generate violent whirlpools. It searches for metallic objects buried beneath the seafloor sand to feed on them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic abilities to locate scraps of metal on the seafloor. Occasionally it can be found near the surface anchored on cargo boats, posing a great risk as it eats through the metal hull.
author: mepp.

entry: Its teeth can shred anything in seconds, which is why it's often used in offices to dispose of waste or documents. Despite its menacing appearance, POKENAME is an extremely obedient and calm Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have a metallic shell around their body that protects them from large predators. Their sharp hooves are made of steel, which can cause deep cuts when they kick other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's weak swimming muscles combined with its heavy metal shell leaves it spending most of its time at the bottom of lakes. With considerable effort, it can swim about ten feet at a time before needing rest.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon dislikes gamblers immensely. A foolish Trainer once suggested playing a game of chance using the markings on POKENAME's body as score.
author: fixthewifi

entry: It relies solely on curious Trainers to roll it in order to get around. Rarely, ones with seven- or eight-spotted sides have been seen.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME buries its claws into the sand and filter-feeds on small organisms. It rarely moves, and its sturdy and heavy metal shell means that few predators have the strength to pick it up or bite into it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in an armor of thick steel plates, which it warms beneath the sun. The leaf on its head stores energy and filters out chemicals that could rust its armor.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses the flames on its back to heat metal, making it easier to consume. When angry, its armor becomes hot enough to leave burns.
author: lbbacca

entry: With a hotter flame, POKENAME smelts large quantities of ore into metal before feasting upon it. When ready for battle, it stands to the side with its head facing the enemy, ready to burn them with its flames from head or tail.
author: lbbacca

entry: POKENAME's heavy armor prevents it from floating, so it spends most of its time lying in wait on the water's floor for an unsuspecting Pokémon to swim above. It can remain submerged for up to 24 hours.
author: gamblingdie

entry: POKENAME leads a sedentary lifestyle, resting along the shoreline for long periods. If disturbed while sleeping, it flies into a rage and attacks anything in sight. It no longer spends much time in the water.
author: gamblingdie

entry: POKENAME are coated with a metallic exoskeleton that protects them from almost all danger. They consume any exposed metal they can find to fuel their growth, making them an unwanted pest at construction sites.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have metallic plating growing throughout their exoskeletons, providing vital protection against their predators. These metallic plates are segmented, allowing greater freedom of movement than more solid plating would provide.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Scientists recently spotted clusters of POKENAME drifting through space. For some reason, they do not require food once they leave the atmosphere.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pecks at mining equipment with its metal beak, occasionally consuming small pieces. Afterward, it sometimes experiences visions from the most recent user's life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME acts as a living lightning rod to protect vital buildings from the dangers of storms. Be careful about contact with this Pokémon, as its metal plates are very conductive.
author: evilgammon

entry: Its body is made of very light but resistant steel. POKENAME can regularly secrete oil from its tail, allowing it to swim on the surface of the water.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of very light but resistant steel. POKENAME can regularly secrete oil from its tail, allowing it to swim on the surface of the water.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can't swim, instead walking along lake beds for food. Its heavy body helps it spin its tail at high speed like a hammer thrower.
author: pokepower

entry: Its body is robust, able to float due to the light weight of its armor and the oil in its tail. It can expel water through the holes to move around.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is robust, able to float due to the light weight of its armor and the oil in its tail. It can expel water through the holes to move around.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME frequently cities with high traffic and often stand on the side of roads for long periods of time. This causes quite a lot of confusion, and can lead to accidents.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME quickly take over any cave they can live in. Their small bodies allow them to live in all kinds of nooks and crannies.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME's hand-like tail is harder than iron. It smashes it into cliff walls to knock loose chunks of marble, which it eagerly consumes after grinding it up with a powerful Metal Claw.
author: .izik

entry: Bathed in lunar radiation, POKENAME's fur hardens until it is tough as steel. It becomes more energetic at night, making it especially popular with security guards working night shifts.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME were once trained to release spores through the holes in their body to pacify soldiers. The practice is now banned in many places, so they often find themselves in sanctuaries where they live peacefully.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It chews its way through any tough material. Serious infrastructure damage has been caused due to wild POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for screws due to their tendency to drill inside of metals and then stay dormant for long periods of time.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME uses its silvered claws to smash cave walls and knock loose Hard Stones. It collects these rocks to decorate its underground den.
author: .izik

entry: The steel plates on its hands are as sturdy as the metal of its skull, letting it effectively guard itself from attacks. It also gives POKENAME punches potent enough to easily crack boulders.
author: sk372

entry: Rarely, certain POKENAME can be observed with what appear to be eyes visible from the holes in their fists. These specimens fight with a much more aggressive ferocity than others, for some reason.
author: sk372

entry: Its steel exoskeleton is extremely hard to penetrate. POKENAME eats rocks to makes its exoskeleton even harder.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME have markings on their metallic skulls in the shape of certain phases of the moon. When the moon overhead matches the shape on their face, they exhibit greater combat strength.
author: sk372

entry: It prefers to keep its body as cold as possible. During the winter months it sleeps in frozen caverns, keeping its internal temperature low.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in reefs that have grown on shipwrecks, where it hunts metallic Pokémon. It is considered a pest at ports since it will eat through the hull of boats when it is failing to catch prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME flicks out its blue tongue in deep caves to smell for Blue Shards. Upon finding some, it rams its head into the wall until the shards break loose.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME acts as a sort of big sibling to young Aron or Phanpy in the wild. Quick on its feet and with a sturdy iron coating, it can easily take on Pokémon that would otherwise trouble the others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is found by iron-rich cliffsides, slowly teetering back and forth to peck at the stone with its steely beak. Since it seems to have an incredibly long lifespan, it doesn't care how long it takes to dig its way to the metal it seeks.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME consumes a variety of metals to meet its daily nutritional needs. It is thought that what POKENAME evolves into may depend on the balance of its diet.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are artificial Pokémon that are capable of self-replication. They assemble one another with great care, aware of the relative fragility of their bodies compared to larger Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME produces milk rich in iron, often used in vitamin supplements. It generates more milk than usual during the spring months.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stands tall with pride, even when looked down upon. When it evolves into Aggitar, it spares those who haven't wronged it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME typically gather in packs, moving as one. They go from scrap metal to scrap metal, quickly devouring them.
author: incognito1234

entry: The fluid it secretes from its eyes is highly acidic. This helps to dissolve metals for easier consumption.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME's diet consists primarily of things rich in iron and minerals. Rock and stone are most typical. Metal scrap is considered a treat, and gemstones are a delicacy to be savored.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slams its metal head into the ground to startle prey like Diglett. When they surface, it finishes them off with a powerful Bulldoze.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's connection with plants seems most potent with foliage near the presence of steel and other metals. As such, most wild sightings of POKENAME have been in abandoned buildings experiencing overgrowth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is attracted towards areas with high mineral deposits, using its floating limbs to dig through soil to find the richest stone to consume. Occasionally, its head and torso will swap positions for a time, for unknown reasons.
author: sk372
