entry: A thick iron shell shields POKENAME's head from cave-ins and ambushes. It constantly searches for iron ore, which it consumes to reinforce its armor.
author: .izik

entry: The heavy plating on its hands and ears makes it hard for POKENAME to move quickly. Instead, it uses these plates to bat away threats and moves to a safer location.
author: chibitales

entry: Ancient records tell of POKENAME aiding in mountain rescues. Its heavy plating allowed it to march through avalanches unscathed, carrying survivors to safety.
author: .izik

entry: Due to their protective padding, POKENAME can be incredibly reckless, often headbutting Pokémon far stronger than themselves. When they are bored, the two heads will start headbutting each other for fun.
author: mistymagius

entry: In tight-knit packs, POKENAME scuttles through caverns in search of silver ore. A single group can consume over 50 tons in just one week.
author: .izik

entry: Because of it's accelerated growth due to fusion, POKENAME has tripled it's normal shell size to accommodate for it's quickly growing body.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME rarely ever moves until it has evolved. The plates that composed the outer armor for POKENAME are oddly warm to touch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The heaviness of POKENAME's shell causes it to weigh down aerial Pokémon it clings onto. The more static electricity it absorbs, the faster the cells within its body change, and the closer it gets to evolution.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's scales are quite resistant to damage, but it doesn't grow them quickly enough to really aid it in battle. It usually hides away in isolated caves, only coming out once it has grown enough scales.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME glides through tunnels, emitting sonar pulses from its metallic body. It can map an entire cave system in pitch-black darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is tough but elastic, allowing it to roll on any terrain it chooses. They tend to roll down large hills to build speed; once they start rolling, they are almost impossible to stop.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a heavily armoured back that protects it from larger Pokémon. When threatened, it curls into a ball to shield its softer underbelly from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While it mostly stays in its shell, it has a tendency to headbutt passing Trainers. It doesn't move very much, usually getting around by rolling around in its shell.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME often gets into sparring matches with one another, they pride themselves on their defensive maneuvers. Their scales are both tough and flexible, preventing them from being bent out of shape.
author: mistymagius

entry: In battle, POKENAME hoists its loose skin over its head and stiffens it into a metal-like shield. POKENAME charges headfirst into foes, confident in its armor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a protective band of muscle that absorbs the impact of any blow. It soars through the sky with majesty, challenging others of its species to see who can reach the highest altitude.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can revolve so fast and generate so much electricity that they eventually explode.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This strange gear assembly launches its components at a force that can easily crack a skull.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's long, metallic tongue crackles with stray sparks as it eats discarded electronics found in junkyards and landfills.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generally hides away in junkyards, where the shape of its metal cocoon lets it masquerade as a simple scrapped gear and be ignored by most until its evolution can complete.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME spots something in its territory, its gears churn at high speeds to power up a running charge. Once it hits something, the impact temporarily shorts out its gears, leaving it stunned.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME adores mimicking machinery by turning its gear-shaped head. Although it delights in this, many people find it creepy or off-putting.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Unfortunately, POKENAME's steel bodies are quite susceptible to rust. They would likely be extinct if not for their fast rate of reproduction.
author: dylonk25

entry: The gear spinning inside POKENAME's body generates the energy needed to fuel a transformation. The bigger the form it wants to change into, the longer it has to churn before it can transform.
author: sk372

entry: Often found near landfills, POKENAME digs through heaps of discarded electronics. Its gears whirr and spin furiously while it feeds.
author: .izik

entry: Some think that POKENAME's body has a defective design, as the gears in its chest occasionally jam and leave it unable to use psychic powers. It can forcibly turn and start its gear on its own, but doing so seems to be a painful effort.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME needs to rid itself of excess heat by venting dark flames from its back. The fire creates acrid black smoke as well, and some have raised environmental concerns about the potential pollution it could cause.
author: sk372

entry: Before using its strongest moves, POKENAME readies itself by revving its internal combustion, making flames erupt from its tail. The sound has been likened to a miniature version of a car's engine.
author: sk372

entry: The key on its back can be wound to increase POKENAME's electric powers in battle, but caution is needed; winding it too much will cause it to overload and uncontrollably send jolts of lightning all around it.
author: sk372

entry: They are known to float using an Air Balloon, helping them avoid damage from sand, dirt, and grit. They work in factory facilities that are recovering from toxic spills, as they double as backup generators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generate electricity by rotating the gear around their neck. They work in factories where they power large machinery that produces car parts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tilts its head back and forth as it walks. The motion is necessary for forward momentum, as mechanisms in its head connect directly to those in its feet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are Pokémon powered by clockwork, the speed at which their gears turn varying depending on how much sunlight they receive. Under the midday sun they are warm enough that their gears can run at peak efficiency, letting them move at speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME glides through construction sites at night, chewing through bulldozers. It digests metal to reinforce its own grinding gears.
author: .izik

entry: Despite POKENAME's steel exoskeletons, they are lighter than a Heracross. They are notorious among Bug Catchers for breaking traps set for Bug-types with their jagged limbs and eating the bait.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: Its hand extends with multiple tools, each designed for a different task it faces. When POKENAME is agitated, thick smoke pours from the vents on its head, growing heavier with the intensity of its emotions.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME constantly eats coal or soil, which it burns in its body to power itself. It can reach speeds of up to 35 mph.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's heavy body and stiff movements make flying nearly impossible for it. It's blade-like wings can be fired off as projectiles that will return to POKENAME's body after use.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME charges across wastelands while rolling at high speed. Sparks fly from its gear as it discharges bursts of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to prance daintily through the forest, but most onlookers describe its movements as strange and uncanny. Odd radio waves seem to emanate from its metallic antlers at night.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its home in abandoned textile factories, gnawing on forgotten machines. Its body hums with electric energy as it feeds and powers up.
author: .izik

entry: Though highly elusive, POKENAME has been sought out due to a curious functionality it has exhibited. Machines that have stopped functioning due to water damage will begin working again after a short amount of exposure to POKENAME's presence.
author: sk372

entry: It can temporarily detach its limbs to attack from afar, though they must return shortly  before they run out of power. If deprived of all its limbs, it radiates intense magnetic waves to disorient others until it can retrieve its body parts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's telepathy allows it to predict its foes' attacks in battle. Its determination increases to meet the aggression it senses in its opponents.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: The individual gears rotate and generate energy, which is converted into magnetic waves via the antenna on the head.
author: chorb33

entry: Researchers have occasionally mistaken a curled-up POKENAME for some sort of sandy, mechanical artifact. Trying to pick it up will result in it burrowing deep into the ground.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME lives near factories and power plants. It can be seen absorbing carbon dioxide from the smokestacks.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's strength has been significantly improved thanks to its cybernetics and can see targets from up to 200ft away!
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME works alongside people in factories and construction sites, where its small size allows it to reach into tight spaces. It enjoys the tactile sensation work provides, needing reminders from its Trainer to rest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's large ear-gears are finely tuned to its surroundings, giving it excellent hearing and senses. When startled, the gears churn quickly and enhance its mobility so it can better flee from danger.
author: sk372

entry: An oily coating allows POKENAME's metal body to shift color with its surroundings. It hides in derelict factories, perfectly camouflaged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME operates heavy machinery by using its psychic power, its advanced calculations allowing it to produce precise movements. It helps researchers working with corrosive acids to discover and produce new chemicals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses subtle psychic waves to influence factory workers during repairs. It finds deep satisfaction in watching machinery run smoothly.
author: .izik

entry: When fed logs, it dispenses planks of wood which it then uses to construct simple crafts.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME has protective instincts, primarily for young and small Steel-type Pokémon. The large gear on its back can churn at high speeds to let POKENAME breathe a hot steam that obscures the area, facilitating escape for it and its charges.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fire burns an odd silvery color. It will become furious if one attempts to stop the gears from spinning.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME's large ear-gears are finely tuned to its surroundings, giving it excellent hearing and senses. When startled, the gears churn quickly and enhance its strength, improving its ability to combat danger.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME remains stationary until its key is turned. Once properly wound up, it marches forward at a steady pace, puffing out steam from its large nose with a high-pitched whistle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's gears cause its blade to vibrate, cutting into the body of its victims. It is continuously powered by the life force it harvests.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME starts combat in a defensive stance, absorbing blows and gathering energy through its rotating gear-shield. Once fully charged, it enters attack mode, unsheathing its blade as the light on its gear turns red.
author: sk372

entry: The many gears comprising POKENAME's internals work in conjunction to provide it energy and mobility. Churning at max power simultaneously, POKENAME can move incredibly fast, but becomes incredibly aggressive as well.
author: sk372

entry: If the gear on POKENAME's head is halted, it becomes frozen in place, unable to attack. Once the gear restarts, it continues with furious speed.
author: deelee2020

entry: Many gears turning across POKENAME's body give it vast reservoirs of energy for offense and defense. Its tactics in battle are incredibly basic though, smashing about with little strategic thought involved.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a colossal being made entirely of steel, with massive indestructible gears that keep its limbs in constant motion. Legends say it has enough power to reverse the world's rotation if it ever wished to.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Originally thought to be ideal for assembly-line labor, this Pokémon has adapted its functions to suit combat situations. Its cannon modulates based on enemy composition, feeding on external data to predict and counter its opponent's moves.
author: jaminmcready

entry: These Pokémon were found to be extremely useful as high-output capacitors when linked to machinery through the gear on their backs. While it is unknown how much energy they can store, they are able to output at 100,000 MWh for extended durations.
author: the_cardinals

entry: Its bulb emits a natural blue glow that shifts in intensity with its emotions. When calm, the light flickers gently, but during moments of excitement or fear, it blazes brightly, illuminating its surroundings.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The blue lightbulb in POKENAME's core resembles a flame but emits no heat. At night, it perches atop cranes, letting loose tiny sparks as its bulb glows.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME claims abandoned electronics warehouses as its territory. If disturbed, it emits a piercing metallic cry and discharges static bursts.
author: .izik

entry: As it burrows beneath Lum Berry trees, POKENAME's neck gear spins rapidly. It knocks Berries loose by releasing bolts of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: The dams POKENAME builds are made of a mix of metal scraps and wood. Despite this, they never seem to rust.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME loves playing around children. Its tail sparks with static energy as it runs excitedly, but the charge often shocks kids who get too close, driving them away before it can make friends.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's gears spin faster the more fired-up it is. Interlocking with other gears is dangerous, as it can grind to a halt if they don't fit perfectly.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME's flower-shaped gears hum with electricity. It uses stored power to defend its kin from aerial predators like Skarmory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats above wild habitats to scan biometric information for scientists. Its metallic shell stabilizes its movement in tough weather conditions, which makes scanning easier.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each POKENAME will eventually develop a different diet from one another: some will only eat organic foods, while others will just consume minerals. Rarely, there are POKENAME that only rely on magnetic energy in order to live.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The fluff on this Pokémon's body resembles steel wool. It's used frequently to clean medical equipment as it never rusts.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME are mechanical, artificial Pokémon that are used to search hostile environments during search and rescue missions. Despite their small size, they are strong enough to carry travellers to safety from the depths of the desert.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often shelters within abandoned factories, where the remaining machinery acts as its primary food source. Old industrial plants swarm with this Pokémon.
author: daemonkill22

entry: POKENAME defends ancient tombs by unleashing horrifying Shadow Balls. Its tail gear vibrates with ghostly energy before each attack.
author: .izik

entry: While absorbing electricity, POKENAME's gears spin at high speed. It can retain power for months depending on the intensity of the charge.
author: .izik

entry: The metal surrounding POKENAME's body is constantly hot. High-end grills are rumored to use parts from it for consistent heat.
author: .izik

entry: It absorbs the iron in the blood of its prey to heal and add onto itself while leaving scraps on its pressure plate to attract its next prey.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Tiny holes across POKENAME's tin body leak a thick, green poison. Contact with the fluid causes severe irritation.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon's interlocking body allows it to speed through the forest like a mountain bike. It is the source of many natural dirt trails.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its movement is stiff and slow, but it is determined and persistent.  If it chooses to bite at something, it will pursue them no matter the time or distance it takes, until its jaws clamp around its chosen target.
author: sk372

entry: The thick steel shell covering POKENAME is freezing to the touch. Rain freezes instantly upon contact with its frigid frame.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaves are surprisingly healthy, and they're a good source of iron and fiber. They don't taste all too well, though.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is an autonomous Pokémon that was designed to fill itself with garbage, empty itself in the nearest dumpster, and repeat the process.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its gears work like a wind-up motor. The longer POKENAME rotates it, the faster it can whizz off in one direction.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are said to be born from the spirits of working children during the industrial era. It wanders around abandoned factories and will chase out anyone who tries to rebuild it.
author: mistymagius

entry: It hovers using the magnetism generated by its spinning wings. Flocking POKENAME link wings when at rest; if a predator approaches, it only takes a single POKENAME spinning up for the entire flock to take flight.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME is typically found living near abandoned, rusted machinery. The mushrooms on its back appear normal but are actually made of metal, and can only be safely consumed by Steel-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers with a POKENAME can determine its mood by how fast it's interlocking gears are turning. It contains a near infinite energy, some Trainers aren't able to keep up with POKENAME's playful nature.
author: schwaus

entry: The keys on the backs of POKENAME rotate to help power their joints as they move. POKENAME release steam from the vents in their shells to help power the constant turning of their keys.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Though it appears fluffy, POKENAME's metallic-colored candy floss tastes awful. Survivors describe the flavor being similar to battery acid and oil.
author: .izik

entry: The pants-like rubbery skin around POKENAME's legs protects its allies by preventing accidental electric shocks while it trains or battles.
author: .izik

entry: This aimless drill Pokémon absorbs mineral deposits in the ground it mines.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: As a group, POKENAME can coordinate with each other to perform tasks like flattening terrain.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: A very unfortunate Pokémon: POKENAME's gears must turn in order to generate the energy needed to live, but every turn of the gears distorts its cranium and causes excruciating headaches.
author: sk372

entry: Turning the gear on POKENAME's tail one direction will temporarily assuage its bad temperament, while turning the other will boost its aggression. Trainers are advised to quickly memorize which way to turn when raising POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME prepares to spray water from its mouth, the gears on its shell begin rotating faster. Even though it lives mostly in aquatic environments, its steel never rusts.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is popular in circus performances, where fire eaters or acrobats ride on it and perform dangerous stunts featuring its uncontrolled fire.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is composed of a system of gears, aiding in propelling it through water with surprising speed. Its polished surface reflects light like metal, which allows POKENAME to glimmer underneath the water while swimming.
author: rakunk

entry: The huge gear in POKENAME's back is apparently supposed to provide it with great intellect as it churns. However, it turns so slowly that POKENAME rarely sees any benefit.
author: sk372

entry: Researchers were able to prove that POKENAME constantly rotates an invisible magnetic field around its own axis, which it uses to protect itself.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME uses the gear on its underside to stimulate its self-generated magnetic field, with which it can orient itself even in absolute darkness.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can interlock its heads and then make them rotate rapidly. This protective mechanism is exploited by some to generate energy.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of sturdy but lightweight steel. Each of its three heads have different, defined tasks, which makes POKENAME an effective fusion.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of sturdy but lightweight steel. Each of its three heads have different, defined tasks, which makes POKENAME an effective fusion.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of sturdy but lightweight steel. Each of its three heads have different, defined tasks, which makes POKENAME an effective fusion.
author: chorb33

entry: The gear on its body spins jerkily as though struggling to move. POKENAME's touch slowly rusts most metals, which it then consumes as a snack.
author: deelee2020

entry: Some have tried to remove the gears from within the gooey sludge, but learned this is detrimental to POKENAME's health; without the sludge, the gears are unable to turn, and it could perish if separated too long.
author: sk372

entry: A pair of floating spectral gears that tend to haunt abandoned factories, it's said that POKENAME are the spirits of broken-down machines left to linger around their former homes.
author: sk372

entry: The tastier the dream POKENAME eats, the faster its gears spin. The method of how they consume dreams is unknown.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME roll laterally along the ground, occasionally purposefully striking the large gear on their back against the ground. Once the gear charges up enough energy, the POKENAME will explode in a series of sparks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Multiple looters who've attempted to take the energy core component at the center of its assembly have been fatally wounded.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The slenderness ratio of its neck is so high that it starts buckling when it feels tired, due to the weight of the upper gear. Its movements look clumsy, but its attacks are surprisingly accurate.
author: epping_forest

entry: The smaller gears turn to fuel POKENAME's powerful running charges. If it looks to be charging into a wall, the largest gear spins in reverse to force the body to hit the brakes and stop.
author: sk372

entry: Research shows that its perpetually shifting DNA has a correlation with the position of the gear upon its back. For example, a DNA sample will closely resemble some Fire-types' when it is drawn while the gear tooth above POKENAME's head is red.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The rear halves of POKENAME contain a large spool of a metallic silk-like thread produced within their bodies. The precise tips of their legs are used to weave this thread into various shapes, traps, and tools.
author: infinex21

entry: As the gears of its body turn, crackling electricity can be seen within the orb on its tail, an indicator of its current energy level. The gears never stop turning completely, even when POKENAME sleeps.
author: sk372

entry: The cogs on POKENAME slow as its internal electricity depletes. At night, it enters a deep sleep to restore its charge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hovers near factories and power plants, gently spinning as it absorbs sunlight to fuel its Electric-type attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cogwheels are made of lightweight aluminum, allowing it to drift effortlessly through factories and scrapyards.
author: .izik

entry: Scientists theorize POKENAME has enough power in its body to take itself to orbit under its own power. It instead prefers to hover around quiet lake areas and stare at its reflection in the water.
author: sk372

entry: Its steel body moves in jerky motions, following the rotation of the gears on its tail. When it flies, it emits metallic screeches that disorient anyone nearby.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has replaced its wings with a gigantic gear, which it uses as a shell to protect its back. Its increased weight allows it to get enough leverage to fling Pokémon much larger than it.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: POKENAME uses the oil it runs on to slide along the ground. However, because of the shift to renewable energy, their numbers have dwindled.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its internal furnace is always creating new flames, fueled towards whichever head is actively in attack mode. In times of desperation POKENAME can burn with both heads, but it risks depleting its reserves completely should it do so.
author: sk372

entry: The gear on POKENAME's back repels various minerals in an effort to keep it clean and able to spin. Anything it is unable to repel can be excreted through its trunk.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The rotation of its frontal gears subtly stimulates the airwaves in front of POKENAME, causing disorientation in those within range. Once stunned by this display, POKENAME can coil around and crush its targets with ease.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME visits industrial cities to fix machines damaged by excessive water damage or rust. Its water attacks exponentially increase in power the faster the gears on its head turn.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME will turn the gear on its chest in order to boost its energy and mood, becoming dour if it hasn't charged itself in a while. The gears on its head turn along with the one on its body, but appear to serve no function.
author: sk372

entry: The motor on the inside is protected by hard glass. POKENAME constantly generates energy via this motor, which it can convert into magnetic waves.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME uses its conveyor-belt-like tongue to scoop up metallic scraps. It digests the metal slowly, absorbing trace energy from each piece.
author: .izik

entry: A flame burns within its metal body, keeping it constantly active. When its gears begin to spin faster, it becomes surrounded by thick, dark smoke to prevent POKENAME from overheating.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A flame burns within its metal body, sustaining its continuous operation. As its gears accelerate, dense black smoke envelops it to keep POKENAME from overheating.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME considers itself trapped in a never-ending spiral of faints and revives. It chooses to protect any nearby Klalade as if they were a Trainer.
author: tokenoracle

entry: POKENAME calculates every movement down to the millisecond, making its strikes virtually impossible to dodge. Many cities have deployed it as a last resort peacekeeper.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It prefers to remain near human civilization. The gear-like appendage around its abdomen contains many secrets.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: When using fire-based attacks, the cogs on POKENAME's body spin furiously. Sparks fly from its joints as it heats up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME functions both as a vibrating blade and combat chainsaw. It effectively harvests iron and life force from its victims.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME moves with stiff, mechanical motions, resembling a wind-up toy. It strikes enemies with the dagger-like blade on its left arm.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient legends have stated that the world is actually a giant gear system made by POKENAME and that earthquakes are caused when the gears don't mesh properly. POKENAME has been shown creating minigears to spin around its own large gears.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's gears carry a faint residue that allow it to cling to surfaces, even when vertical or inverted. Be cautious if you find tracks left by POKENAME; the residue it leaves behind is mildly charged with static electricity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME nests atop electrical poles, channeling currents through its body. It lights up brightly to lure prey like Venomoth closer.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME spins, it consumes the life energy powering its flames and gradually dwindles. When the smaller gear melts away, the big gear must find another partner with which to connect or it will die.
author: pjporwoll

entry: A blue bulb glows within POKENAME's head, resembling a cool flame. Upon waking, it releases a blinding flash from the bulb.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a popular companion for various handymen due to its tendency to collect tools and link them to itself. It collects so many items indiscriminately that it often gets confused when asked to provide a specific tool, however.
author: sk372

entry: The gears have meshed together in an unorthodox fashion. As a result, POKENAME may occasionally get its gears stuck mid-turn, halting functionality until it or another fixes the issue.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is able to absorb and deactivate even the most potent toxins with ease, making it valuable in cleaning up contaminated areas. As a result, studies into POKENAME have been ongoing at Celadon University.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Due to its diet of old factory machinery, POKENAME has developed a larger metallic body. Its body collides with others when flying in a swarm, creating the sound of grinding gears.
author: daemonkill22

entry: POKENAME's round nose heats up beyond commercial oven temperatures. A single touch can leave severe burns on even the toughest Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: The energy core on its pressure plate allows POKENAME to shock whatever steps on it to reduce their chance of escape.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Though its actual capabilities are only moderate, POKENAME vainly considers itself the pinnacle of machinery. Should someone imply otherwise, it angrily spits high-velocity gears at the detractor in petty defiance.
author: sk372

entry: If it sees prey or intruders, its eyes glow a menacing red. POKENAME is often used in underwater bases for security purposes.
author: chorb33

entry: If it sees prey or intruders, its eyes glow a menacing red. POKENAME is often used in underwater bases for security purposes.
author: chorb33

entry: If it sees prey or intruders, its eyes glow a menacing red. POKENAME is often used in underwater bases for security purposes.
author: chorb33

entry: Even while asleep, eerie mechanical noise can be heard from inside its body. It will patrol around areas with strong magnetic fields.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's head rotates slowly as it walks. It senses nearby mechanical failure, growing hot to the touch when something is wrong.
author: .izik

entry: It causes noticeable ground tremors with its large drill and energy core.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This trio mining in unison has triggered several earthquake warning systems.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It flies around by rotating the gear underneath it at high speeds. Its body secretes a grease that ensures the gears never get stuck.
author: gronkissimo

entry: When POKENAME gallops, it emits boiling steam that ignites the landscape behind it. This and the echoing of its steps sound like a locomotive.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME charges forward on piston-driven limbs, with steam hissing from vents along its spine. Its horn spins at a high velocity, slicing perfectly through obstacles as if guided by unseen calculations.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The gears on POKENAME's tail are primarily responsible for regulating its balance, especially underwater. If they become damaged, it can no longer swim properly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME surrounds itself with a protective electric field. As it travels around, this defence measure causes nearby machines to go haywire.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: The oddly-arranged machine Pokémon occasionally separates itself before rearranging the three units' positions. It's thought that the differing arrangements help POKENAME focus on specific functions like battling or computing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME´s head rotates continuously in a clockwise direction. The springs on its legs enable it to jump over ten meters into the air.
author: chorb33

entry: A devious prankster of a spirit, POKENAME sends out ghostly gears into machinery to cause them to malfunction. Factories and other such buildings consider it a menace due to this and how difficult it is to properly exorcise and eject it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is powered by steam. Its movements are very robotic. At first glance, some believe POKENAME isn't a Pokémon at all and that it is just a robot.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME frequently disguises itself as an elderly person wandering darkened woods. If someone gets too close, it spits a sticky silk thread to capture them, leaving them for others in its nest to feed on.
author: .izik

entry: Using a mysterious illusion-based ability, it pretends to be a pile of leaves while resting. It will cower and shake violently if it senses danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically eat honey and flowers, so they rarely need to fight other Pokémon for food. As such, they change their appearance to avoid needless fights with stronger Pokémon, only fighting to claim their share of any nearby food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME changes so it looks just like its foe, tricks it, then uses that opportunity to flop and splash. It sometimes takes the form of a silent baby.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME pretends to be a crying infant deep in the forest to attract unsuspecting passersby. The moment someone gets too close, it injects them with venom and disappears into the shadows.
author: .izik

entry: This fusion has significantly dampened the mischievous streak of POKENAME without impacting its ability to transform. As a result, it has an almost childlike innocence and playfulness, treating its ability to transform like a game.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME is incredibly vain. It assumes a form that is similar to Eevee but keeps some of its old features because it believes that it looks better that way.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME can hardly move before evolving, so they change their appearance to avoid being detected by stronger Pokémon. This gives them time to evolve.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME will defend themselves and their friends fiercely. However, when they encounter larger and stronger Pokémon, they disguise themselves to keep themselves safe.
author: entomoxie

entry: A pleasant basil-like scent wafts from the tuft of fur on POKENAME's head. Many find this aroma oddly calming, though it may be a trick to lure unsuspecting victims.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a solitary creature guarding the cave it calls home. It takes on the form of larger, more fearsome Pokémon to scare off intruders; if that illusion fails, it unleashes devastating Fire-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During the day, this Pokémon spends most of its time resting while wreathed in an illusion that disguises it as a tree branch. During the night, its dark plumage and silent wings make it nearly undetectable outside of its haunting cry.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME are weak, so they typically change their appearance to avoid stronger Pokémon. They are most active at night, when they are less easily seen and can gather energy from starlight.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are typically shy and prefer to change their appearance to avoid fights. Their feathers are particularly rare and prized commodities as a result.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are naturally timid, hiding in bushes and changing their appearance to avoid confrontations. When they are particularly scared, they release electric shocks from the tufts of fur on their heads.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are naturally timid, hiding in bushes and changing their appearance to avoid confrontations. When they are particularly scared, they release electric shocks from the tufts of fur on their heads.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can sing beautiful melodies for hours at a time. However, they are often too timid to do so, changing their appearances to avoid even showing their faces.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can soar through the skies for hours at a time, changing their appearance while flying to stay undetected. Their feathers are as beautiful as they are rare, fetching a high price for collectors.
author: entomoxie

entry: It can transform its head flowers into normal looking roses. It likes to hide in bushes and do this to prank people into picking them.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: POKENAME drift through the air on gentle winds, often falling asleep mid-flight. Legends say that bad dreams are unintentionally spread through the skies by groups of this Pokémon when they fly by.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME dislike conflict and take on the appearance of a drowned family member if approached with malice. Anything that grabs them becomes covered in a sticky goo, creating enough distraction for escape.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Anything that shines or sparkles catches any POKENAME's eye. They can change their appearance to get away with stealing any valuable trinkets, though they are also speedy in their flight when their disguises fail.
author: entomoxie

entry: A very passive Pokémon, POKENAME moves little and pretends to be a part of the tree that it feeds off of. Hundreds of them can live in a colony on a single tree without anyone passing by ever knowing they are even there.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME travel in flocks to protect themselves from bigger Pokémon and attack as a team when one is threatened. They are known to disguise themselves as Spearow to obtain breadcrumbs at parks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tend to style their fur and adorn themselves with human accessories. Their aesthetics vary across individuals.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME seek out nests for food, stealing food from them. They can change their appearance to blend in when needed, though they prefer eggs from unguarded nests.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are tricksters, frequently pulling pranks by taking on the appearance of others. However, they can be loyal and serious to those whom they trust dearly.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are tricksters, frequently pulling pranks by taking on the appearance of others. However, they can be loyal and serious to those whom they trust dearly.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME creates illusions of itself to mess with people. Its favorite prank is to pretend to run out in front of vehicles and cause road accidents.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can hide in dense thickets, disguising themselves as stronger Pokémon when not hiding. Their fur can store immense static electricity for hours at a time, releasing the energy as needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are typically shy and disguise themselves to avoid confrontations with others. They carry an egg-shaped pebble wherever they go to comfort them.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME disguises itself with illusions, switching up the projected appearance by ducking around cover while in battle to throw off opponents. It can make imperfect imitations of most Pokémon cries, so it will make incorrect sounds to confuse foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sometimes receives premonitions of disasters from an unknown source. In order to warn humans, it will use illusions to disguise itself as a human child to approach them and show them the nature of the danger it has foreseen.
author: elfail0

entry: If a person wanders off the path at night, they may encounter a child in a fox mask. This is actually a POKENAME in disguise. They will either attempt to lead the lost person back to the path or deeper into the woods, never to be seen again.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as ordinary objects to avoid conflict. It only ambushes vulnerable prey when they are alone.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses illusions so its sheathed sword appears uncovered, and it makes its unsheathed sword look as if it's covered. If it feels that its opponent has figured out the trick, it reverses the illusion at random.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can change their appearance to approach unsuspecting Pokémon without themselves being threatened. Only after their sharp claws cut deep do they show their true colors.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can release gas from its mouth. This gas can make anyone who breathes it hallucinate POKENAME as any Pokémon or person it wants.
author: themicelegion

entry: It plays harmless pranks on other Pokémon in an attempt to become friends with them. It shies away from humans, often only approaching under an illusory disguise.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It plays harmless pranks on other Pokémon in an attempt to become friends with them. It shies away from humans, often only approaching under an illusory disguise.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It plays harmless pranks on other Pokémon in an attempt to become friends with them. It shies away from humans, often only approaching under an illusory disguise.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have strong arms and claws, though they rarely like to use their strength for fighting. They can change their appearance while resting to avoid fights, and they are only active for around 2 hours each day.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME often transforms into a child to blend in at playgrounds, happily playing alongside other kids. However, if it spots a bully, it will punish them with a well-placed electric shock.
author: .izik

entry: Only one gear exists, but if something should happen to keep POKENAME from producing the illusion of the second gear, it stops spinning entirely.
author: .realthree

entry: The black spores POKENAME produces can cause hallucinations when inhaled. It only releases them when a perceived threat comes too close to its den.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hides in the darkest corners of caves to avoid being seen. When cornered, it transforms into the appearance of its provoker to startle them, then flies away.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is able to change the reflections in its mirror and will often try to trick passersby with it. For some unknown reason, POKENAME seems to hate looking at its own reflection.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can roll around at high speeds, though they struggle to turn around when doing so. They can change their appearance to avoid being identified whenever they can't move around on smooth terrain.
author: entomoxie

entry: Known to disguise itself as a lost traveler to avoid danger, POKENAME unintentionally leads would-be rescuers into blizzards.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME can bury their bodies, only letting some fur on their head poke out. They can make these tufts of fur look like leaves to stay completely hidden in forests, still detecting nearby motion while lying in wait.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME change their appearance to avoid fights with stronger Pokémon. The large pom-poms on their paws store much static electricity and can shock unsuspecting targets with a single jab.
author: entomoxie

entry: Because POKENAME can create an illusion of itself to look like any stuffed toy, it's very difficult to find. Toy stores sometimes have a hard time taking inventory because of this Pokémon's antics.
author: .realthree

entry: The mushrooms on POKENAME's back are potently hallucinogenic, which deters predators. Because of this, it fearlessly runs wherever it wishes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME tend to hide in dark treetops and caves, waiting for prey to approach. They can change their appearance to avoid detection whenever they can't comfortably hide.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are natural-born thieves. They invade shops and homes late at night to steal valuables.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are natural-born thieves. They invade shops and homes late at night to steal valuables.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME uses its magic pendulum to induce strong daydreams, which helps it avoid danger. It will only reveal itself to those it trusts deeply.
author: noel5229

entry: The cactus on POKENAME's back contains a flammable toxin. POKENAME can release the toxin from the spikes for defense or ignite it for attacks.
author: raza

entry: The bulb of a POKENAME is capable of producing a corrosive acid that can dissolve metal. This acid is the fuel for the flame on its tail.
author: benevolent

entry: POKENAME produce a flame-resistant silk. Many chefs wear aprons made from this material when cooking.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME have a hard time controlling the flame on their tail. They are known to accidentally start small bushfires, but they are easy to put out.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It often takes groups of young Cubone under its protection to teach them the art of survival. When POKENAME battles, it sets the bone club it wields ablaze to make its strikes even more powerful.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Any kick from this Pokémon, with its powerful flaming legs, will cause some serious damage. Its footsteps leave seared marks on the ground.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME can ignite the saliva coating its tongue to scorch anything it licks. To keep the flame on its tail burning bright, it feeds exclusively on extremely spicy foods.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The gas inside of POKENAME's body is highly flammable, and when threatened it will ignite the gas with its tail to cause a fiery explosion. The gas is also caustic, causing lung damage if inhaled.
author: mistymagius

entry: To defend itself from predators, POKENAME spits lobs of flaming silk. This has been known to inadvertently singe nearby plants.
author: mepp.

entry: In ancient times, humans used POKENAME as living lanterns. Many historical fires are thought to be caused by mistreated POKENAME.
author: staghorn

entry: A flame singes the tips of its wings, scattering ashes that coat and protect it. This process is harmless to POKENAME but hazardous to others.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME release so much body heat from their hot bodies that they draw the attention of cold-blooded Pokémon. Many cold-blooded Pokémon are too shy to hug POKENAME, but the few that do find that they both enjoy the experience.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its fiery horns are the source of its life essence. When it is damp or raining, POKENAME will burrow into the ground to protect its horns from being doused.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's temper is about as short as a toothpick. Because of this, in addition to its physique, no matador has ever bested it.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME is a gentle creature that fights only to defend itself from predators. As it beats its fiery wings while searching for food, it scatters fine ash that makes the soil remarkably fertile.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have distinct personalities and preferences. If a POKENAME eats its favorite kind of Berry or leaf, the flame at the end of its body will glow in a brilliant fuchsia color.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME continuously stores electrical energy in its body to fuel the fiery collar around its neck. Hot-tempered and impulsive, it may sometimes act without waiting for its Trainer's command.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME continuously stores electrical energy in its body to fuel the fiery collar around its neck. Hot-tempered and impulsive, it may sometimes act without waiting for its Trainer's command.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its shell stays constant aflame as extra defense. At the first sign of rain, POKENAME tucks into its shell and rolls away to find immediate shelter.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have distinct personalities and preferences. If a POKENAME eats its favorite kind of Berry or leaf, the flame at the end of its body will glow in a brilliant fuchsia color.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It instinctively hangs from high branches in order to avoid predators. Unfortunately, the flame on the end of its tail often burns through a branch before its evolution is complete, causing it to fall to the forest floor and become vulnerable.
author: sk372

entry: Although it is slow, POKENAME's thick shell protects it from predators. The fire in its tail burns even when it is underwater.
author: _._starry_._

entry: Every time POKENAME molts, the flame on its tail consumes the shed skin and burns brighter. As the flame strengthens, its size and power grow.
author: linhasxoc

entry: Every time POKENAME molts, the flame on its tail consumes the shed skin and burns brighter. As the flame strengthens, its size and power grow.
author: linhasxoc

entry: The age of a POKENAME can be determined by measuring the length of the flame on their tail. The flame grows each time they shed their scales, which can be ground into a powder that is used in traditional medicine.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The pollen it harvests combusts from its high body heat. Its scales disperse the heat to two razor-sharp stingers, reaching over 415 degrees Celsius.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: When a POKENAME's leaf burns down to its root, it is ready to evolve. The bulbs on its neck emit a pleasant aroma reminiscent of potpourri.
author: volvonovic

entry: The intensity of the flames covering its back reflects its mood; when POKENAME becomes angry, they emit thick black smoke. It is extremely afraid of thunderstorms, to the point that it refuses to fight or obey its Trainer when it is raining.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are energetic creatures that sprout flames from their back and love to chase other Pokémon. They also love to bite down on anything they are presented with, and training them to suppress this urge can be difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be difficult to train because of their urge to bite down on anything in front of them. They often feel remorseful after biting another Pokémon or their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can produce embers from their mouth to roast berries before they eat them. Their urge to bite whatever is in front of them can momentarily be suppressed by giving them berries to roast.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its feathers are coated in a thin layer of ash. It flaps around wildly when frightened, kicking up a cloud of smoke.
author: ozydamians

entry: Wild POKENAME are able to protect their flaming tails from rain much more easily than Charmander by quickly flying to nearby shelter.
author: oxitape.

entry: With its tail feathers, POKENAME fans warm embers over the eggs in its nest. When a predator tries to steal its eggs, POKENAME whips up a smokescreen and slashes haphazardly with its talons.
author: ozydamians

entry: Jewelers in Castelia City will employ multiple POKENAME to work on melting precious metals. Necklaces made by a POKENAME's flame are in high demand.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sneeze out embers when they are sick. Each time they sneeze, so much air is expelled from their body that it causes their eyes to water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The heat it produces also creates a "warm and fuzzy" feeling in humans and Pokémon. For this reason, they're a common partner for therapists.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME often stops walking and stares into the distance. Scholars believe it sees glimpses of past moments in time, and when its vision ends, it sneezes small bursts of flame.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was once mistaken to be a chubby Moltres. Dark clouds of smoke trail behind it as it flies, so the military employs POKENAME to send coded messages across long distances.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME scurry around towns with their tails sparking to help them see during the dead of night. They gnaw holes into gas tanks to drink the fuel inside.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's mischievous nature has given it a reputation as a menace. It picks up objects with its tail, igniting them before throwing them at passersby as a rather dangerous prank.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME secretes an oily substance from its tail that keeps its flame burning. They are not born with it aflame, so one of their parents ignites it. When upset, they seek out others to combine flames, a gesture that seems to soothe and comfort them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When it is in the company of people it likes, the flame on its tail crackles with cheerful pops. It possesses strong psychic abilities that allow it to foresee its opponents' moves in advance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its flames are still maturing, so it spends the nights gathering moonlight to restore its energy. Out of fear that its Trainer might get burned when petting it, POKENAME often keeps a shy and distant demeanor.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its flames are still maturing, so it spends the nights gathering moonlight to restore its energy. Out of fear that its Trainer might get burned when petting it, POKENAME often keeps a shy and distant demeanor.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its flames are still maturing, so it spends the nights gathering moonlight to restore its energy. Out of fear that its Trainer might get burned when petting it, POKENAME often keeps a shy and distant demeanor.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME sneaks through the night, stealing hats from unsuspecting travelers. If cornered, it spits fire to distract its pursuers before making its escape.
author: .izik

entry: The flower bud on its back resembles a flame-tinged blossom. The bud releases a fragrant smell full of toxins that will burn your eyes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has a habit of gnawing on charcoal. Chewing on the hard stone helps keep its teeth strong, and consuming the charcoal itself keeps its fire, both on its tail and within its body, healthy and stoked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feeds its flames with the solar energy stored within the crystals along its body. Once it charges enough energy, it can keep burning brightly even on rainy days.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: The flame that burns underneath it is an indication of the potential of its psychic energy. Trainers have claimed to see it burn blue under starlight.
author: fixthewifi

entry: POKENAME glides through the dawn sky in search of prey like Oddish. It scorches them with embers before swooping down to finish the hunt.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME comes across a nest more impressive than its own, it spits embers at it out of sheer jealousy. Its competitive nature often leads to feuds with other Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has begun to gain popularity in colder regions, as the berry juice created within its shell is piping hot, making it excellent for creating a warm beverage to counter the cold temperatures.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often go out of their way to burn down other Pokémon's nests, especially if they appear tidier. The only thing that dampens their temper is the rain, which causes them to stay put to avoid extinguishing their tail flame.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It consumes tree branches to keep the flame in its belly burning. Without constant fuel, its internal fire would weaken, leaving it vulnerable in colder environments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have fiery hot talons that can sear through cocoons of Bug-type Pokémon. Their wings burn through whatever they touch, which can result in wildfires if they light tree leaves on fire.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protects its flame by curling into a tight spiral. Its scales produce heat through friction, burning anything it manages to constrict.
author: baverbrugge

entry: POKENAME leaves behind scorched trails wherever it rolls. Its superheated body ignites dry grass and dirt in its wake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are energetic yet maladroit creatures that set fire to nearby bushes whenever they roll down hills. They are the source of many wildfires.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It carves paths through the tundra with bursts of flame, melting snow and ice in its way. These fiery trails allow it and other Pokémon to move freely through frozen landscapes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scares away other Pokémon from its territory with the pattern on its hood. It relies on this fear to protect its territory because its fire-breathing abilities are still developing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoys eating spicy food purely for fun, seeking out the hottest ingredients it can find. The intense heat only fuels the flames within this Pokémon's body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces milk that can soothe burns when splashed onto an injury. Despite its fiery nature, it is known to help wounded Pokémon recover.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can hear a rumbling stomach from a mile away. It's only just learning to cook, but every meal is made with love.
author: leshii

entry: POKENAME desiccates moisture from the air by kicking up sand to wick water from plants and small ponds. Its tail is extremely sensitive to humidity, so it creates sandstorms wherever it goes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have shells that are hot to the touch that absorb moisture in the air. Excess moisture rapidly cools down their body, which can cause their cocoon to crack if submerged in water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME do their best to be gentle, but their raging temper often leads to scary tantrums. Many end up as loners because other Pokémon are scared of them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flick their tails back and forth to generate sparks that can grow into dazzling flames. During storms, they draw in lightning bolts through their tails to keep their flames burning and prevent damage to trees.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are partially composed of coal and other organic rich rocks meaning that they are flammable. They can sustain this flame for extended periods of time without ill effect, but are hazardous to surrounding plants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are partially composed of coal and other organic rich rocks meaning that they are flammable. POKENAME that burn too hot will sometimes abruptly collapse due to heat stroke after using all their fuel, necessitating a trip to a Pokémon Centre.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are usually rowdy when they're younger. They often play without care, and when that happens, their hat can set things on fire.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The intensity of a POKENAME's flame is a sign of its energy level and emotions. If a POKENAME notices that its flame is about to burn out, it will discharge any and all electricity it has stored to re-ignite its tail in a brilliant burst of sparks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME tend to be alone. It is extremely shy and will try to hide its face at any chance possible. It prefers to stay quiet in the dark.
author: krsgaming

entry: POKENAME has large cannons for arms. Shooting fire out of these cannons is an important part of regulating their body temperature, which is indicated by its shoulder flames.
author: robbery_666

entry: If startled, POKENAME will curl into a ball, unintentionally igniting its surroundings. Its important to train it on non-flammable surfaces such as concrete.
author: linhasxoc

entry: How old a POKENAME is can be determined by how far its tail has burned down. Its tail is long enough for it to last up to its next evolution.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: When it gets too hungry, the flame on its tail begins to fade, so POKENAME always makes sure to keep food stored in its den. Its sharp claws are not only useful for keeping other Pokémon away but also for expanding the size of its pantry.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is covered in flames that act as a natural compass, allowing it to sense the direction of nearby objects or locations. It is said to shine brighter at the sight of its Trainer.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME gets lots of energy from heat, but must be careful not to dry out. To deal with this, it plays in the mud near hot springs.
author: shocktopus

entry: Female POKENAME have a stronger sense of smell than males. They lead packs toward food, often ending up in human settlements, drawn by aromatic meals.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME blends in with the volcanic terrain, shifting its skin color to match nearby rocks and lava. This camouflage allows it to ambush prey before unleashing fiery bursts.
author: .izik

entry: The flower bud on its back resembles a flame-tinged blossom. The bud releases a fragrant smell full of toxins that will burn your eyes.
author: soup1900

entry: The flame that's on the tip of its tail gives it its own source of light for its flower. Its leaves have yellowed due to too much exposure to light.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite their docile nature, it is not recommended to handle wild POKENAME. When frightened, their barbs protrude and the flame on their tail roars.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME will often roast Berries and meat before eating them. If their flames are an odd color, it is most likely due to their diet.
author: mossybanana

entry: Only existing in captivity, POKENAME are very possessive of their toys and other items in their enclosure. When their favorite items are taken away, the flame on their tail roars.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME spits flames wildly in town squares when it senses an incoming hurricane. Its fiery warnings often go unheeded until the storm arrives.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its large size, this Pokémon lives a fragile young life. Without legs it has to live in the water, but if the flame on its tail extinguishes, it will die. This may be nature's countermeasure to its incredibly dangerous evolutions.
author: ecstaticwoop6455

entry: POKENAME often travel in small packs during the day, but the sound and smell of campfires can wake them up and attract them to your campsite.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME uses the flame on its tail to regulate its body temperature. During dives, it envelops it in an air bubble to prevent it from going out.
author: chorb33

entry: It can heat its down to over 140 degrees, regardless of outside temperatures. As it glides over the snow, it leaves a steaming trail in its wake.
author: chorb33

entry: On impact, this haunted pick instantly turns metal or flesh red hot. It wanders mines and only attacks if disturbed while mining.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Under the hot sun, POKENAME are the most energetic, but also the most aggressive. At night when the temperatures lower, so too does POKENAME's temper.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Its body remains hot at all times. It will chop off portions of trees so that it can feed the burning flame in its stomach.
author: .izik

entry: It is also known as "The Flame Swordsman". It's said that within POKENAME's blade arm sleeps the power of a dragon that will destroy all.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: A playful companion that leaves burn marks wherever it goes. POKENAME is very protective of its companions and the flame on its tail.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Domestication has resulted in this Pokémon never developing the competitive spirit its species is otherwise known for. Its quick feet, dexterous hands, and attentive mind make a swarm of them an invaluable asset when traversing the desert.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The happier this Pokémon is, the warmer its body feels to the touch. It often seeks to cuddle with a trusted Trainer.
author: melodydelune

entry: Only existing in captivity, POKENAME is prone to sudden temper tantrums that last until it tires itself out. Keeping its enclosure below room temperature has been found to cool its temperament.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The fire on a POKENAME's tail grows stronger in direct moonlight. Groups of POKENAME gather together on nights of a full moon to create one large bonfire between all of their flames. For a moment, the light of these flames can be seen from space.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It sheds incredibly flammable fur on just about any surface. Trainers of this Pokémon are required to take a fire safety course.
author: capwolfbane

entry: Its hands are hot to the touch. The spores it creates can be used as a seasoning for spicy dishes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are greatly mischievous. It is recorded that in ancient times, they would burn down villages for fun.
author: theartemis1

entry: Dancing delicately while framed by flickering flames, POKENAME glide across the sky at night in groups resembling meteor showers. The fires on their tails can burn brightly even in the vacuum of space.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's fluffy cotton mane retains its warmth even when detached from its cute body. For this reason, its fur is used to make padded clothing and blankets that stay cozy at all times.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME train alongside their kin to learn the discipline necessary to keep streets bright at night. In their current state, many lack the stamina to last more than four hours.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is overenthusiastic when using its tusks, resulting in it cutting down too many trees or damaging metal beams if improperly trained. It seeks to please those it respects, so it is easy to teach for Trainers that can gain its trust.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME experiences pain whenever any of its tails are put out, so it avoids places where there is a lot of water. It spends a long time carefully grooming each of its tails that it rarely has time to play with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The flames on POKENAME's back deter foes from trying to touch this Pokémon. Its skin is often very dry due to the intense heat it always endures from its own flames.
author: soup1900

entry: It flares up the flame from the lighter it carries in order to dissuade others from pilfering its keys. People often keep it around to help them light campfires and the like.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tries to make its costume as authentic as possible, including using real fire. Unfortunately, cloth doesn't mix well with that.
author: howlingstarr

entry: Some old tales say that if all nine of a POKENAME's tail-flames are extinguished at once, it will perish. These legends claim the POKENAME's soul will curse the one responsible, haunting them to their final days.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's claws heat up to a white-hot temperature as it burrows into the ground. Its tunnels are often lined with charred soil from its intense digging.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has learned to ignite its aura, allowing it to emit fire. It delights in showing off its newfound abilities.
author: solori_roznie

entry: POKENAME often never make it to full maturity due to their slothful nature. They slumber indignantly even as the rain extinguishes their tails.
author: scapz

entry: Cheerfully playing around in warm waters, POKENAME always tries to keep its tail above water. When diving, they surround it in a water bubble and come back after air in the bubble runs out.
author: markusknight

entry: In Kanto, POKENAME is mostly used to teach young children the ropes of Pokémon care. Keep it away from carpets for your own safety.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Often found playing in packs, these humorous creatures have been known to prank travelers passing by.
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME's body becomes extremely hot before it inflates and floats. It can reach heights of over 100 feet, leaving behind a faint trail of embers.
author: .izik

entry: The metal on POKENAME's body was once harvested by blacksmiths to forge ingots. These ingots were prized for their superior heat dispersion properties.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live atop active volcanoes where they shuffle towards cooling lava. They crush and rip into volcanic rocks with their claws until they are edible shards.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs deep tunnels at night to hide the light emanating from its tail. To further hide itself, its metabolism slows and its flame shrinks to a faint flicker.
author: .fedoraman

entry: In a swarm of its kin, POKENAME remains at the bottom of the pecking order due to its lack of fighting spirit. When raised in captivity, this docility is cultivated and they never develop the fiery temper their species is known for.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Recessive, dragon-like alleles become dominant when two POKENAME are fused. It tends to have a fierce nature, and its tail is difficult to extinguish.
author: atomicdiamond

entry: Its bud hides a small flame that POKENAME needs to live. The flame is fueled by flammable sap and the bud remains slightly open to let in the air it needs to burn.
author: lucioleuh

entry: POKENAME always produces a flammable sap to keep its flames ignited, but it can control the intensity. A trained POKENAME can even alter the smoke its flames produce, changing the color, toxicity, smell, and quantity.
author: lucioleuh

entry: Its ears only curl up when it battles, using them to deliver swift fire attacks in battle. On cold nights, some don't curl into their warm fur and some still do out of habit.
author: torterraguy26

entry: By using its flames, POKENAME melts sand to create dens made of glass. These shimmering dens serve as both glittering shelters for this Pokémon and also befuddling traps for unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: Though its wings are strong, it struggles to stay aloft for long, often tumbling in bursts of flame. It clings to rocky ceilings to rest, leaving scorch marks in perfect circles.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME often struggles to eat, as the flaming mask on its tail turns much of the food it scavenges into ash instead. If it does eat, the flame burns intensely and displays a medley of bright colors.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME's fiery tusks change in size depending on its emotions. Regardless of how it is feeling, if it does not receive a balanced diet of berries and ore, the flames will extinguish.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's fiery tusks change in size depending on its emotions. Regardless of how it is feeling, if it does not receive a balanced diet of berries and ore, the flames will extinguish.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is overconfident in its abilities in battle because its armored crest has extended down its back. The tusks are beginning to harden under the flames, so if its diet is disrupted, the tusks may insufficiently grow before evolution.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's tail is extremely warm to the touch, and heats up if excited or frightened. It communicates with others of its kind by tapping tails together in a series of patterns.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are incredible Bug-type hunters that sear their prey with flaming drool from their gaping maw. They help keep wild populations of Caterpie and Weedle under control.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Mischievous in nature, POKENAME love to play pranks on other Pokémon, usually by startling them. If it does not eat enough jewels, the fire on its tail will grow dim and weak.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME frequently becomes confused about whether to breathe flames or snow, often switching between the two. This unpredictable nature makes it difficult for opponents to anticipate this Pokémon's attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Pokémon researchers have observed POKENAME moving across their glacial homes in huddled groups of four or more. The current theory is that they do so to protect their flames from abrupt gusts of wind or blizzards, letting them stay warm as a group.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME relies on its brightly colored leaves to signal to predators that it is poisonous. It releases toxic spores that make it sneeze out embers, which in turn causes it to release more spores.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The flower of flame that burns atop POKENAME's head isn't very hot. However, the large stem in the middle can project flaming-hot noxious toxins.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME leaps effortlessly from cliffsides, spinning mid-air while spitting flames. These fiery displays are meant to impress others and assert dominance.
author: .izik

entry: Its spines radiate heat, scorching anything that touches them. These fiery spines make it difficult for predators to approach without getting burned.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME are hard to come across, but when seen in the wild, they are always roughhousing with one another. As Trainer-kept Pokémon, POKENAME are quite friendly and fiercely loyal to their owners.
author: itsthenewisaiah

entry: Even if the flame on its tail goes out, POKENAME won't die until the flame inside its shell also goes out. It can also stick its tail through an opening of its shell to reignite either flame that went out.
author: soup1900

entry: Its flames have now become ultra hot. No amount of water can put out the flame on its tail.
author: soup1900

entry: It has taken on a darker appearance, and flames come out of its mouth. Kalos experts claim it has similarities with Mega Charizard X.
author: soup1900

entry: It is a pretty calm Pokémon and won't viciously attack unless absolutely necessary. It becomes slightly afraid when facing tough opponents.
author: soup1900

entry: The ground around POKENAME heats up the longer it stays still. To prevent wildfires, it constantly relocates to cooler soil.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME encounters a couple who breaks up, it gets depressed, and its tiny flame shrinks in size. Trainers must be wary about the emotions they show and make sure they share plenty of love with others to keep this Pokémon happy.
author: soup1900

entry: The soil around POKENAME heats up as it digs. To avoid causing wildfires, it carefully keeps distance from tree roots.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its gentle-looking face, POKENAME is a patient hunter, able to remain hidden for hours before striking with sharp claws. When sick or weak, the flame on its tail flickers and fades.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is in the paradoxical position of needing and fearing water. Its tail wicks moisture from the rest of its body, which causes headaches if dehydration is severe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are terrified of water because they fear extinguishing their tail flame, yet become so dehydrated that they develop headaches. The pain can grow so severe that they can only scream.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite having a flame that can remain lit underwater, POKENAME have an instinctual desire to keep the flame from getting wet. This leads them to swim much slower than they are capable of.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can conjure storms of ash and embers that drift like snowflakes. It fares well in extreme temperatures, whether hot or cold.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME have a vehement hatred of water that borders on irrational. Whenever a person takes a sip of water or comes near them with it, they become enraged and lash out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roost around craggy cliffs. They aggressively attack any traveler that passes by, but they're rarely a danger to any but the most inexperienced of Trainers.
author: .realthree

entry: Without warning, POKENAME can erupt into a violent fit, thrashing at anything that comes near, including its Trainer. When calmed down, its flaming fur dies down to a smolder, leaving POKENAME extremely weakened while it rests.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are loyal Pokémon that will do anything its Trainer asks it to. This also makes them subject to neglect, as some Trainers forget to bring them inside when it is rainy or windy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though large in size and boisterous in ego, its battling capabilities are middling at best. Its vanity simmers as it nears evolution.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME waddles near puddles, ponds, and lakes to find berries to eat. It loves to spew embers to char the berries before eating them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its fiery spirit makes it train constantly to hone its muscles. As it grows in strength, the flame on its tail burns more intensely.
author: sk372

entry: Its appearance of being engulfed in fire is its natural state, the flames on its body providing a potent deterrent to predators. Dousing the flame will not harm it, but will leave it weak and defenseless.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can temporarily extinguish the flame on its tail to swim. To find a POKENAME, look for streams with unusually warm water.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME rarely fights, usually only to defend itself from predators. When it feels threatened, it sets its own tentacles ablaze to scorch its foes and spits a slimy poisonous acid from its mouth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many POKENAME forge hammers alongside blacksmiths, as they heat and reheat steel to form the hammerhead. Their fists strike one side of the hammerhead to flatten the steel into shape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many POKENAME assemble garden shears inside factories, heating blades before dousing them in oil. They then join the two blades together, creating a valuable tool for gardening.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a valuable asset for blacksmiths, as its control over fire allows it to mold steel into whatever shape is needed. Its large fists can also strike steel in lieu of a hammer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trots in fields of grass alongside pack members. It sneezes out embers on occasion, which it stamps out to prevent wildfires.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME canters alongside its pack to stay safe. When confronted with a threat, it launches a kick with its flaming hooves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often forgets the flame on its tail is a part of itself. Running from its own tail or accidentally burning itself with it are common occurrences.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will tuck themselves into their shell, using the flame from their tail to stay warm as they sleep. Attempting to disturb a sleeping POKENAME will cause them to release fire from the holes in their shell.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With its tail aflame, it channels psychic power. Once serene, now it battles with fiery determination.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME thrives near lava pools, absorbing intense heat into its body. The hotter it becomes, the stronger and more erratic its Thundershock attack grows.
author: .izik

entry: Analysis of internal organs reveals each of POKENAME's parts could function independently if they were separated. However, they are considered different from Charmite, and are stronger together than apart.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME waves its fiery baton to appear menacing. It loses its composure when around water because it is scared of the fire being put out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While usually not visible, it has tiny arms beneath its orange feathers. At night you can identify POKENAME running through the fields by their glow.
author: .izik
