entry: POKENAME lives deep beneath the surface, the high heat and pressure causing crystals to form within its body. It will only come up to the surface on the darkest night of the year.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME glides through cave systems, pulsing with a faint purple glow. When it spots a gem cluster, it crashes into it and devours the shattered pieces.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoy eating rocks and spitting them out as a sort of blown glass. Finding one of these sculptures could bring you into a large sum of money.
author: thatguy4115

entry: It chews through rock effortlessly while seeking out gemstones, its favorite food. However, POKENAME much prefers to steal from miners' gem caches, and are considered nuisances.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's mating displays are very colorful and elaborate. It spends tens of hours searching for the shiniest things it can find and decorates its nest with them, hoping to attract a mate. Some larger displays are advertised as tourist diving spots.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Its diamond claws can cut through stone — perfect for spelunking through the caves to find precious gems that it can snatch.
author: diriector_doc

entry: When POKENAME finds a really large gem, it will protect it at all costs. Sometimes, the determination in its eyes is enough to drive intruders away.
author: diriector_doc

entry: POKENAME live on damp cave walls, not slipping thanks to the sticky oil they secrete from the ends of their legs. They won't move unless disturbed, pretending to be gemstones until the very last moment before scattering in fear.
author: milchik

entry: These Pokémon are found hovering above all sorts of cave reservoirs. With their wings and legs glowing in the dark, sparkling like precious gems, they lure Sableye into the water where they're less likely to escape a group of hungry POKENAME.
author: milchik

entry: Unsurprisingly, POKENAME is extremely greedy towards valuables. No coin nor jewel is safe from POKENAME's gluttonous thievery.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It swings and scrapes its claws against stone to the point of exhaustion. This is a training regimen for POKENAME, as it yearns to be able to dig deep into caverns barehanded and unearth the finest of gems to collect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME meditate for long periods of time to ensure they are well-rested before roaming into caves to search for gems. By punching chunks of rocks out of cave walls, they unearth gems to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A natural-born hoarder, POKENAME will get its claws onto any valuables it can find. When it senses something to steal, the gems lining its body glow and light up the surrounding area to make finding hidden trinkets easier.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: A natural-born hoarder, POKENAME will get its claws onto any valuables it can find. When it senses something to steal, the gems lining its body glow and light up the surrounding area to make finding hidden trinkets easier.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME loves to take shiny stuff and stick it to its fur. It also sheds some glittering dust that sticks to furniture, making it very annoying to keep as a pet.
author: nugamallow

entry: POKENAME's powerful stomach acid dissolves gemstones extremely fast. This allows it to eat large crystals with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: Deep inside caves, trainers can hear POKENAME eating large crystals residing inside the walls. If they toss some gemstones into its mouth, it will spit up some reserves to share.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME emit a bright light from their many gems, each capable of hypnotizing others. It is rumored that they were trained to be guards by ancient civilizations.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A wild POKENAME relies on food from a mother Walrein or scraps left by other Pokémon. POKENAME compete relentlessly for food and snatch what they can, leaving runts to struggle through harsh winters.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have powerful senses of touch and smell and use them to hunt and communicate with other POKENAME and Sealeo. When full, they happily slap their fins against their firm bellies.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is almost entirely colorblind, so instead of jewels like Sableye, its diet consists of smaller Pokémon that dwell deep under the sea where no light reaches; it can stay underwater for days at a time before coming up for air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its fists are coated in a layer of diamonds, which makes its punches absolutely devastating. It desires precious gemstones and will destroy entire mountains in search of them.
author: mistymagius

entry: It collects gems and gnaws on them until they are shaped like bones. When it is excited, the crystals on its body are hot to the touch.
author: greystorm101

entry: Its intense avarice for metals and gems is only matched by the intensity of its flames. It sometimes 'collects' its Trainer as a twisted form of love.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME obsessively hoards as much wealth as it can find. If even a single coin is stolen, it will rampage across the land until it is returned.
author: rakanadyo

entry: POKENAME believes itself to be the ruler of the underground caves it lives in. It's incredibly territorial, and even gets into fights over the smallest of gems.
author: gronkissimo

entry: POKENAME offers dubious advice to lost travellers to keep them wandering for hours. It is easily placated with the gift of small gems or a shiny spoon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Thanks to a diet comprised of very specific gems, POKENAME can flex its muscles to a ludicrous size. It loves the attention from awestruck bystanders.
author: 8xviktor

entry: There have been many accounts of POKENAME using their slings to take down larger foes. Groups of POKENAME will often engage in friendly competition with one another.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME mesmerizes prey with its hypnotic, glowing eyes before striking. When threatened, it withdraws into its shell, which is said to be as hard as the precious stones it consumes.
author: zaffery88

entry: POKENAME grows crystals from its body for a variety of uses including decoration, protection, and digging tools. When the crystals become chipped, it eats them to regenerate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunts gemstones to eat and build energy for evolution. Depending on its diet, in rare cases it can start to build a golden sheen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunts gemstones to eat and build energy for evolution. Depending on its diet, in rare cases it can start to build a golden sheen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME grows crystals from its body for a variety of uses including decoration, protection, and digging tools. When the crystals become chipped, it eats them to regenerate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows deep into the earth searching for the most beautiful gemstones to devour. The more it eats, the more extravagant its hide becomes until it becomes encrusted in crystals and evolves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows deep into the earth searching for the most beautiful gemstones to devour. The more it eats, the more extravagant its hide becomes until it becomes encrusted in crystals and evolves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows deep into the earth searching for the most beautiful gemstones to devour. The more it eats, the more extravagant its hide becomes until it becomes encrusted in crystals and evolves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's gemstone shell is highly valued by traffickers, but nobody was able to even scratch it. It's the only thing POKENAME will fiercely fight for.
author: epping_forest

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME crawls along cave floors in search of gems to eat. It moves so slowly and uses so little energy that one small gem can take months to digest, keeping it satiated the entire time.
author: alestrius

entry: As gemstones are non-magnetic, sometimes POKENAME struggles to attract other POKENAME with which it can evolve.
author: diriector_doc

entry: POKENAME greedily consumes any shiny gemstones it comes across. It doesn't appear to need them for nourishment, but merely because it enjoys feeling beautiful as the consumed gems float to its surface and decorate its exterior.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to be extremely greedy. They steal valuable objects wherever they can find them and hoard them within its toxic body.
author: theartemis1

entry: The clarity of a POKENAME's gemstone shell often reflects its health; the shinier the shell, the healthier the fusion.
author: howlingstarr

entry: The bodies of POKENAME are shrouded in glittering clouds made of pulverized gemstones. It is said that they can dominate the minds of greedy people with a single look.
author: staghorn

entry: If you discover large caverns or deep tunnels lacking all shiny minerals and jewels, these incredibly rare Pokémon have likely passed through previously. POKENAME seek out these materials to consume, eventually causing their bodies to glitter, too.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This is an intelligent fusion that uses hypnosis to put Rock-type Pokémon to sleep, then eats them. Its neck fur is made of pure, hard diamond.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: The POKENAME feeds on shiny rocks and minerals. They are often seen in treasure rooms.
author: terminatphilippe

entry: POKENAME are very greedy fusions, and will do anything to steal a coin. It is hard to get coins back due to its big, meaty claw.
author: homelessrager

entry: POKENAME's epidermis is coated in a paralytic poison; predators quickly learn to stay away from it as a result. The arrangement of darker spots on its body is unique to the individual POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It strips pine trees' bark off in great quantities with its mouth. Once it has several pounds gathered, it will eat it all in under five minutes.
author: .izik

entry: Though they can move individually, the separate pieces of POKENAME prefer to move as a singular unit, following behind the leader of the clutch. When resting, the other five surround the sixth to protect it from harm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's strong stomach lets it consume even the most poisonous of mushrooms. The digestion helps give the venom in its claws and stingers even more potency.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a feisty personality and will charge horn-first at anything with little provocation. The horn contains a mild venom that weakens the muscles of anything that gets stung.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly protective of its egg, using its powerful venom to fend off attackers. While incredibly potent, its venom can be used as a universal anti-venom.
author: mistymagius

entry: A solitary Pokémon, POKENAME keeps to itself in the wild and eats from small flower patches. If confronted, it spreads a very potent paralyzing poison from its wings.
author: sk372

entry: In battle, POKENAME moves with agility and stays on the defensive. Its scythes are tipped with venom, so it waits for the perfect moment to strike and deliver a painful dose to its foe.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's venom is mild, but its pincer-like stingers have a powerful grip. It grabs prey and holds them tight, constantly injecting venom until they're totally paralyzed and an easy meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a large antenna on its head with which it can locate vibrations in its immediate vicinity. It can eat even the most poisonous plants.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME attacks anything it thinks it can eat from the sky before using its saw-like jaws and poison to finish its prey. Avoid leading it to urban areas at all costs.
author: torterraguy26

entry: During the day, POKENAME sleeps on poisonous plants to absorb their toxicity. It uses this at night to go on a fierce hunt.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live in large flocks, feeding on small seeds and berries. They carry poison in their beaks, and while one sting isn't lethal, it can be incredibly dangerous if you are swarmed by a flock of them.
author: mistymagius

entry: These small Bug Pokémon are so often trampled that they have developed irritable temperaments as a result. They will rapidly bite enemies with their poisonous mandibles, though the poison is only capable of inciting an itch.
author: infinex21

entry: Though POKENAME is small, it has few predators. The electricity it discharges lingers and acts like a neurotoxin.
author: .realthree

entry: Covered in soft, fluffy fibers, POKENAME appears harmless. Touching its wool causes intense numbness that lasts for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses sensors on its head and tail to discover prey. The tail is also covered in a buoyant oil to help catch prey on water. When it catches the located prey, it will inject venom through its bite to paralyze the now hopeless prey.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: POKENAME is an expert hunter, able to sense drowning prey in water with both great hearing and highly tuned feelers. If another POKENAME is struggling in the water, others will help by blowing air bubbles.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: POKENAME is highly opportunistic when it comes to procuring food: it waits until it spies another Pokémon capture prey, before swooping in at high speeds to poison and paralyze the predator so it can eat the hunted meal instead.
author: sk372

entry: When anything touches its antennae, POKENAME goes into a rage, running around and shooting Water Gun at anything that moves until it faints. In some regions, people trap POKENAME in arenas and bet on how long it will last before it faints.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME rely on agility and instinct to avoid predators. Cunning by nature, they poison small POKENAME and follow them until their demise before feeding.
author: notmax22

entry: POKENAME slumbers in snowdrifts, blending in with the terrain. If touched, it releases a sweat-like venom that can paralyze on contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a large poison sac attached to its body, which it uses to deliver potent venom when threatened. When feeling cornered, it grips its tail tightly, using it as an intimidation tactic to ward off potential threats.
author: rakunk

entry: It produces poison from the stingers on its tail, creating globs it flicks onto its antlers. It flings blobs of poison from both its tail and antlers when it feels threatened.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers who pass through bug-filled forests sometimes end up with kiss shaped marks. These are actually poisonous bug bites from POKENAME, but they are easily treatable.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME lives in the mountains, its tough carapace protecting it from falling rocks. It is very aggressive and will try to fight other Pokémon over food.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can swing its tail forward to strike opponents with its paralyzing spikes. When it can't reach the berries it loves to eat, it uses its tail as a step and then jumps on them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's antennae are extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air, so it can scan an area as it flies. A poisonous powder drops from its wings, causing minor harmful effects to those below it.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's resilience to the elements allows it to thrive in many corners of the world. Desert POKENAME enjoy a diet of cacti, while marshland POKENAME nibble away at ferns and nettles to survive.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME grazes on fruit tree leaves, leaking green toxin from its barbs. It only activates this defense when startled or cornered.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides along the jungle floors, waiting to ambush its prey with a poisonous bite. Its antennas detect movement in the air, while its wings feel vibrations on the ground, making it impossible to sneak up on.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME secretes a very strong hallucinogenic when nervous, not too dissimilar to sweat. The perspirant is often sold illegally across the region at a high value.
author: big_clanker

entry: In fall, POKENAME hoards dry leaves to eat. It will fight kin over leaf piles, spraying poison from its spiked back when challenged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make loud chirps to communicate with one another across a forest, inhaling deeply and inflating to twice their size to make these noises. Their tendency to chirp at sunset makes it difficult to camp in regions where they make their home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is very aggressive, and it can be seen headbutting other Pokémon in territorial disputes. However, if its head is badly injured, its poison will start to pool under its carapace, causing it immense pain.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME buries itself beneath almond trees, waiting for nuts to fall. It absorbs amygdalin from them to fuel its toxic secretions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep marsh, headbutting nearby trees to knock down berries. Its spores are highly acidic and will slowly start to melt through anything it comes into contact with.
author: mistymagius

entry: While airborne, POKENAME spits globs of neurotoxin with alarming precision. In caves, swarms use this to overwhelm weakened prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts tiny creatures by lobbing webbing at them as if casting a net. Even if captured prey escapes, the webbing is coated with poison that will exhaust them in time and allow POKENAME to catch up.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME mark their territory by gnashing trees with their venomous tusks, leaving behind a corrosive poison that eats through bark and wood alike.
author: johnneh_

entry: POKENAME is incredibly aggressive and will perceive basically anything as a threat. It sprays boiling-hot acid from its antennae to attack, which leaves its victims in agonizing pain.
author: mistymagius

entry: A two-headed form of Venipede. They are exceptionally rare to find, as most don't live for very long.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: The fusion process causes POKENAME to develop additional body segments as well as increasing the potency of their venom. Their exoskeleton also becomes covered in extra spines, making them dangerous to touch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The fusion process causes POKENAME to develop additional body segments as well as increasing the potency of their venom. Their exoskeleton also becomes covered in extra spines, making them dangerous to touch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Something of a step between evolution stages, POKENAME retains mobility but loses some venom potency and the sturdiness of its shell. It skitters away from trouble, avoiding conflict until it can evolve further.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME brutally kills anything in its vicinity with its remarkable strength and venomous horns. The only exception seems to be other members of the Venipede family.
author: torterraguy26

entry: POKENAME becomes deeply sorrowful when music ends which is a major problem in clubs. Its tears carry a powerful toxin, and even a faint whiff can cause people nearby to collapse in seconds.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When POKENAME possesses a stump, poison ivy mysteriously sprouts from it. The mechanism behind this remains unknown to researchers.
author: .izik

entry: The fruits on POKENAME's head are incredibly poisonous, and most that try to eat them will succumb to them in less than a day. The fruit smells sickly sweet, which lures certain Bug Pokémon to try and eat them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have eyes that are poorly adapted for seeing in daylight, so they rely on their keen hearing to navigate. They make high-pitched chirping noises that carry well through dense undergrowth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have eyes that are poorly adapted for seeing in daylight, so they rely on their keen hearing to navigate. They make high-pitched chirping noises that carry well through dense undergrowth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Toxic impurities are constantly produced and build up within POKENAME's body, causing it extreme discomfort. It releases the excess by unleashing beams of highly concentrated and caustic poison from its body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often used as a mode of transportation in urban areas. While quite reliable, it produces clouds of toxic smog as it drives.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME proudly shows off its vibrant scales, which act as a warning to would-be opponents. Its scales are laced in a powerful toxin that can debilitate its opponent in less than a minute.
author: mistymagius

entry: A unique type of poison concoction is produced from the tips of POKENAME's claws. Normally causing illness in those it scratches, if its claws scrape a gash into a tree, fungi begin growing in the scratch marks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME guards its fungal patches deep in cave systems with fierce intensity. Its claws hold a powerful venom that cause seizures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME acts as a two-faced trickster in the wild. If spotted by a larger creature, it pretends to flee in terror, then doubles back in order to leap at its foe when their guard is down and apply rapid venomous bites.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in dense rainforests, hiding amongst damp foliage. It will leap at prey from above, sinking its venomous claws into their heads until they are too weak to stand.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is not particularly aggressive, but its fur produces a highly poisonous secretion. It also has weak psychic powers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME hates being touched, as it will quickly prick its foe with its poisonous thorns before fleeing. It is exclusively nocturnal, using the dim lights from its belly to see in the dark.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are incredibly aggressive and will swarm anyone that enters their territory. The venomous barbs on their heads contain a powerful neurotoxin that can cause paralysis with a large enough dose.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's antennae can detect the presence of coins in a large radius. When it detects something, it will dart around excitedly, eager to scoop the coins up before anyone else.
author: evilgammon

entry: As POKENAME purrs, toxins gather at the tip of its tail. When threatened, it lashes out, swinging the tail like a poisoned flail.
author: .izik

entry: The poison-creating glands residing in its head give it massive headaches if too much is produced without release. It is forced to bite and inject anything it can with poison to relieve its own pain.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is covered in a toxic film which is irritating to the touch. If the pattern on its belly is punctured by an attack, it will secrete a more potent poison.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are incredibly aggressive and will spew a mildly corrosive acid onto anything it deems a threat. When properly distilled, this chemical can be used to make extremely sour candy.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fire is fueled by its venom gland, which gives the fire a distinctive hue. It trots along rainy marshes where it rarely causes wildfires.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its pointed beak to pierce through thick tree trunks, feeding on the small insects inside. However, its beak is coated in large amounts of poison and can be dangerous if a small Pokémon is pecked by it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a mixture of thistle and maroon markings on their bodies, which marks them as poisonous to potential predators. They enjoy rolling down hills because the physical sensation of rolling gives them an adrenaline rush.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Densely-packed tendrils form a swirled shell around POKENAME's body to protect it while it develops. These vines are quite solid, and can lash out and wallop anything that gets too close for comfort.
author: sk372

entry: Once it gets tired of flying on its relatively fragile wings, it simply lands upside down and wheels along. The edges of its wings are much tougher than the spindly inside, allowing it to withstand rough terrain.
author: something_smith

entry: POKENAME are able to conjure invisible objects out of thin air that only the eye on their stomach can see. POKENAME are very fond of circular objects; they are especially interested in spinning motions.
author: kianjp2008

entry: Though its weighty carapace gives it low agility, POKENAME has potent defenses and offenses. The blades on its arms and head are sharp and venom-tipped, and even its wings are pointed enough to cause damage.
author: sk372

entry: The shell on POKENAME's head can open up, revealing rows of razor-sharp teeth. Its horns grip prey, pulling it into the shell to be devoured.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME roll down hills to avoid predators before crawling back to the same spot to eat leaves. Their mauve bodies make them easy to spot, so they hide in bushes whenever they see a predator nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Highly toxic substances are formed in its abdomen through chemical processes. POKENAME uses this poison, lethal to humans, for hunting or defense.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME rolls through its habitat with burst of fire from its back to accelerate, leaving charred circles of undergrowth in its wake. Motorists have taken to it as a symbol of speed that they mount on the hood of their cars.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Highly toxic substances are formed in its abdomen through chemical processes. POKENAME uses this poison, lethal to humans, for hunting or defense.
author: chorb33

entry: Their bulbous abdomens are surprisingly sturdy due to the amount of loose silk webbing they store within themselves. POKENAME can curl upon their large bodies and roll along walls and ceilings due to many small hooks lining their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME usually floats on water without moving, using its senses to try and find prey without spooking them. The camouflage pattern makes POKENAME hard to see, allowing it to lash out at unsuspecting prey.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: When many POKENAME come together and spin quickly in the air, they can create tornadoes. They are very calm when they aren't in groups, and they enjoy naps.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME can oftentimes be found sitting on a muddy riverbank while sucking on its tail, staring off at nothing. This action helps it build resistances to other poisons since, when out of water, its body is covered in a highly toxic film.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Known for its mischievous pranks, POKENAME haunts victims from the shadows before it finds the perfect opportunity to strike. The spinning beads on its necklace have powerful hypnotic powers, able to put victims to sleep for up to 2 weeks.
author: kianjp2008

entry: From its claws, POKENAME secretes a red toxin that induces vomiting and fever. Once latched on, it won't release until the fluid is fully drained.
author: .izik

entry: When closed, its mouth helps complete a protective shell around its head. Timid despite its imposing appearance, POKENAME will bite attackers with its powerful jaws, while also delivering poison from the tips of its fangs.
author: sk372

entry: It usually crawls around at a slow pace, until it ducks into its shell.  Then it is able to roll across the ground to quickly escape from predators.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME's wings are coated in a corrosive poison that can eat through stone. It preys on Aron, using its powerful wings to slice through the environment and catch its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rolls down slopes at high speeds, then uncurls itself to unleash its electric attacks. Those shocked by one may have a hard time walking.
author: .realthree

entry: Due to their large appetites, POKENAME are constantly fighting with each other over prey. They will exploit the gaps in each other's thick carapace by jabbing their sharp horns into them.
author: mistymagius

entry: While usually motionless, POKENAME form a ball to crash into opponents, spewing fire on impact. The resulting blaze leaves the ground scorched and smoldering.
author: kriznick

entry: It attacks with a flurry of poison-laced kicks. Wild POKENAME will not stop fighting until either it or its opponent faints; the longer the battle draws on, the more spirited POKENAME gets.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME dances in erratic tumbles, splashing venom across the ground. Its movements mark the edges of a toxic, defended territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its speed to ambush smaller prey. The rear antennas release excess energy built up so POKENAME doesn't overheat while chasing its target.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Often mistaken for stones, POKENAME rest by lakeshores, blending seamlessly with their surroundings. When thirsty, they roll to the water's edge, startling onlookers.
author: kriznick

entry: POKENAME prefers to keep itself sheathed and avoid combat where possible. If forced, it strikes with swirling, circular swings of its blade that deflect attacks and disorient foes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME doesn't move much, as it wants to keep its protective shell from falling apart. If it does fall off, it will hunt for a Caterpie nest to use the larvae's sticky silk to stick its shell back together.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sweats a poison that irritates the skin of anyone who touches it. Preferring solitude, it will roll to remote areas to find a safe place to sleep, away from any disturbances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is actually two Pokémon held together by an unknown source. When threatened they will both begin spinning against each other to build up enough friction to release massive stored up energy attacks.
author: kianjp2008

entry: POKENAME's blossoms emit a scent like Pecha Berries, masking their danger. A single touch can spread a fever-inducing poison through the skin.
author: .izik

entry: The circular markings on the liquid exterior of POKENAME can be shifted around at will. For self-defense, the core strikes these circles, which send out pulses of potent psychic energy on impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins rapidly as it drifts through forest skies, trailing poison behind it. Its motion is graceful but hazardous to those below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME used its wheel-like body to traverse small crevasses in the cave walls. It hunts in pure darkness, impaling its prey on its venomous horns.
author: mistymagius

entry: It can use its wheel-like feet to reach speeds of up to sixty miles per hour. Most of the time, however, it moves at a leisurely pace in order to conserve energy.
author: staghorn

entry: It's a Whirlipede that fused with itself, giving it more stability and speed. However, it sacrificed some of its maneuverability for these boosts.
author: soup1900

entry: The big one in the middle is the leader of the pack. The small ones around it carry it around. They move around similarly to a car.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME grows red feathers in strange circular patterns across its body. These can be ground into a poisonous powder that only POKENAME can safely ingest.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME can swim at speeds of up to 75 mph. It's certainly not required to; it'd be unreasonable to expect it to be at peak performance all the time.
author: redhaering

entry: POKENAME remain still and serene in their groves, blending into the environment. If disturbed, they rush forward to curse intruders with dark energy.
author: kriznick

entry: POKENAME's large ears produce an earwax so toxic that groomers must use gloves. Though dangerous, it must be cleaned often to prevent buildup.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is usually found in highly polluted areas, spewing clouds of smog from inside its body. However, since it feeds on toxic materials, some people don't consider it a nuisance.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rolls its cotton-soft body across forest floors in a wheel-like form. A noxious poison seeps from its fur, causing blurred vision on contact.
author: .izik

entry: Due to its eyes being on its arms, it is basically blind during combat. To remedy this, it will blindly flail around in hopes of hitting its opponents with its poisonous claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: The eye atop POKENAME's head operates independently of the rest and possesses 360 degree vision despite its appearance. It helps POKENAME direct bursts of spores in defense should something attempt to sneak up on it.
author: sk372

entry: Most commonly found in tropical rainforests, POKENAME can curl into a ball to navigate around its environment. It deals with threats in two ways: plowing over them while curled up, or simply calmly rolling away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its tough body allows it to roll across nearly any kind of surface. When the moon hits its body as it rolls around, it begins to glow a golden hue that disorients predators.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can even roll over uneven terrain. There are places where Pokémon rally races are held, where POKENAME is particularly popular.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME guards pumpkin patches by rolling silently through the fields. It strikes intruders with Venoshock from its twisting vine arms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a toxic substance into its pond to ward off outsiders. The poison harms none of its kin, allowing peaceful swims among allies.
author: .izik

entry: If anyone nears its stash of glittering treasures, POKENAME rolls into them at speed. Its fur, laced with toxins, delivers a burning sting.
author: .izik

entry: It will roll rapidly to respond to any threats. POKENAME's rolling seems to alleviate its headaches.
author: leonian1586

entry: Those who tell their POKENAME to 'roll over' may have a hard time getting it to stop. It instinctively speeds away while rolling.
author: .realthree

entry: Though its shell-like exterior is sturdy, POKENAME must constantly shield its weak spot: the eye in its tummy. The spiral patterns on the top of its body begin to swirl when it nears evolution.
author: sk372

entry: The curled stance that POKENAME is often seen in is believed to be a strategy for cooling its body temperature.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME in peak physical condition chases after motorcycles to show its dominance over its packmates. These races often occur during sporting events, where people bet on the motorcycle or the Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The circles on POKENAME's body glow when it uses its hypnotic powers. When in danger, it curls into a sphere and sends psychic waves all around it to repel aggressors.
author: sk372

entry: Using psychic powers, POKENAME lures travelers into its nest by causing delusions. Once inside, it subdues them with a potent Venoshock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's kicks are able to tear through even the thickest steel. It has no sense of honor, and will use any advantage it has to win a battle.
author: soupalicious

entry: Despite Porygon only being programmed with basic actions, POKENAME causes other programs to exhibit unintended behavior when inside of an electronic device. In battle, POKENAME can let out a Screech that can cause electronic devices to malfunction.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have two maroon horns that sting flying bird Pokémon that try to peck at their cocoon. The venom from a POKENAME's stinger causes inflammation, which causes the faces of predators to puff up with swelling.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After gorging on poison ivy and toxic mushrooms, POKENAME lies still in dense forests. Its toxic breath causes dizziness and nausea.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces toxins in its body, which it can release through pores all over its body. Just touching it leads to painful poisoning.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is known to be highly toxic and highly aggressive. It is a competitive loner; a single individual can lay claim to up to five miles of forest. Despite the danger it poses, a trained POKENAME can be very sweet and kind.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME is often trained as a mount due to its high speed and adaptability to most terrain. It also has a very agreeable temperament, bonding quickly with its Trainer, especially if offered Salac Berries and antennae scratches.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The large horn upon their heads is strong enough to clash with a Honedge without suffering damage. The purple silk webbing they can spin and weave is soaked thoroughly with a paralytic toxin that quickly immobilizes their prey and foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME divebombs prey with venomous fangs. It refuses to fly during the day as the sun hurts its eyes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is highly aggressive, using its camouflage patterns to hunt in water. When prey wanders close, POKENAME lashes out with its ring of teeth, injecting the prey with deadly venom.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: The puffballs on POKENAME's limbs are filled with tiny poisonous seeds. It scatters them mid-flight to incapacitate prey.
author: .izik

entry: While its horns are filled with a powerful neurotoxin, they are also incredibly brittle. Fights often break between themselves, and they will break off their own horns to use as a melee weapon.
author: mistymagius

entry: It sticks to walls to keep an eye out for intruders. Whenever any enters, it flies down and bites any parts of their bodies, injecting a fatal poison.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME hops through forests at night hunting for toadstools. If threatened, its horns explode in a spray of poison.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME climbs trees to gather Pecha Berries. The juice it brews is dangerously poisonous, but when cooked properly, it becomes a delicious syrup.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's sharp horn leaks an acidic toxin that eats through bark. It uses this to access and consume tree sap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lures small creatures into its bag by putting sweet-scented treats at the entrance. Once they draw near, it closes the bag, which is filled with poisons, and traps them while the toxins take effect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prances at an astonishing speed, its powerful leg muscles sending it surging forward with every stride it makes. With this speed, it builds momentum, which is used when it curls into a ball and rams its opponents.
author: evilgammon

entry: Its milk is toxic and undrinkable. Savvy POKENAME farmers instead use it as an incredibly effective all-natural pesticide.
author: soupalicious

entry: POKENAME are trusted matriarchs within Scolipede colonies, left in charge of freshly laid Venipede eggs. They care for the colony eggs as though their own, with some particularly protective POKENAME using their own bodies to shield them from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Because of its many wings, POKENAME never lacks feathers to gift to those it finds worthy. However, its prideful nature means no one has ever met its lofty expectations, and it has yet to give away a single feather.
author: soupalicious

entry: POKENAME's relentless poison afflicts its targets with intense dread. Its mere presence accelerates the maturation of all plant life around it.
author: alliveir

entry: POKENAME is very aggressive and territorial. If it spots you in its forest, it won't hesitate to discharge all of its electricity as an attack.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME curls into a ball to ram into fruit trees. It greedily devours any fallen fruit, often eating twice its weight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is surprisingly mobile, able to scale up a tall mountainside from base to peak in mere minutes. The rocks it launches from its hands get coated with a terribly potent poison as they're fired, making them doubly dangerous.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly temperamental, pursuing anyone that dares enter its territory. It is able to stretch its arms over 50 feet, allowing it to slash its opponents with its poisonous claws from a safe distance.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hunt prey by pouring the liquid from their stomachs into hives and nests, draining the inhabitants of their vitality.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME are highly aggressive and territorial Bug-type Pokémon that charge down their opponents with startling speed. They secrete a potent poison from their tails as they swing them around with enough force to crack a tree.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is fiercely territorial, slicing and poisoning any and all invaders. Even those who flee its territory are continuously pursued until slain.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is known for its menacing walk that shakes the earth. The reason for this creature's weight is the strong exoskeleton it uses as armor.
author: puppetmaster64

entry: POKENAME forms tunnels in iron-rich mountains, making them its lair. Only the bravest dare to challenge such a strong and tough creature.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME releases a potent toxin which tints the sea around it a deep magenta. Its tough exoskeleton protects it from the pressure of the deep oceans.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: At first glance, POKENAME appears to have two large strands of hair on its head. These are actually extra limbs, spiked and highly maneuverable in combat.
author: dylonk25

entry: During combat, tiny toadstools grow all over POKENAME's body. It spreads poisonous pollen when it successfully dodges an attack.
author: .izik

entry: During nights with prominent moonlight, POKENAME's body leaks a poisonous sweat. It flings this sweat at predators to drive them away.
author: .izik

entry: Late at night, POKENAME rolls through its tunnels seeking prey. It strikes with a sudden Poison Tail to quickly overwhelm the victim.
author: .izik

entry: If someone openly insults its singing abilities, POKENAME gets revenge by spitting venom at them. The position of its antennae indicates its mood: when they are pulled back, it is preparing to strike.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are highly aggressive, especially when fighting over food. Their sturdy bodies can exude a deadly poison to fend off attackers.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME stains city walls with strange symbols, using the venom secreted from its body as paint. If caught in the act, it inflates itself to appear larger and intimidate anyone trying to chase it away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Whenever it is stepped on, POKENAME will quickly react and stab the victim with its two horns, which inject a lethal poison. If ineffective, it will instead clasp them with its horns and slam them into the ground by flopping repeatedly.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME constantly carries around its shed skin to use as both a protective shield and a blunt weapon. If POKENAME ever loses it, it hides away until it can create a new shed skin.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME appears to be on the crux of achieving its final evolutionary stage. In this transitive form, it lacks full mobility, but its toxin and aggression levels are at their peak, making it very dangerous to approach.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lengthen and grow many extra legs following the fusion process. In collaboration with palaeontologists, Pokémon Researchers have concluded that POKENAME revert to a body form from millions of years in the past.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As POKENAME sleeps, tiny poisonous leaves sprout from its horns. It prefers to rest on damp, rotting tree stumps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in forests. Its harsh colors are a warning to trespassers.
author: ohok3441

entry: If two POKENAME meet, they'll fight until one is injured. The winner takes claim of the loser's territory, while the loser retreats to repair itself.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME hates being touch and will thrash around violently if anyone tries to pet it. Despite its small size, it can run faster than most professional athletes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Hiding in pumpkin patches, POKENAME waits for lonely farmers. When alone, it soaks them with Venom Drench and hides while they struggle.
author: .izik

entry: It flies through forests at night, its eyes acting like a radar. If POKENAME spots prey, it shoots it over long distances with a paralyzing poison.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live only to battle, always training for their next fight. This makes it easy to tell young and old POKENAME apart, as the latter's claws will be marked by the scars of their countless past battles.
author: moose1._.

entry: Ancient scripture declares POKENAME to be a god amongst insects, commanding locusts with its mighty howl.
author: gurguro

entry: POKENAME is aggressive, especially with others of its species. When two POKENAME meet, they use their horn-like ears to fight for dominance.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are very aggressive, often starting fights with other bird Pokémon. Once properly cleaned, its leek has a strong sour flavor that often pairs well with noodles.
author: mistymagius

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads uses a different type of venom. It attacks its prey with all three heads, ensuring that at least one will be effective.
author: linhasxoc

entry: POKENAME feasts on fear. It creates hypnotic pendulums that causes those afflicted to hallucinate being swarmed by poisonous insects, letting it feed on the terror created from this illusion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scuttles with relentless speed, using its powerful legs to chase down prey along shorelines and cliffs. Its claws secrete an acid potent enough to melt through metal, leaving scorched trails wherever it feeds.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME eats scraps left from other hunters' meals, keeping the bones to chew on. Ordinarily timid, wearing a skull over its head instills it enough bravery to fight back against its foes.
author: sk372

entry: Great care must be taken in raising POKENAME, as though affectionate to owners their massive jaw strength means that even a playful bite from it could be disastrous to property or person.
author: sk372

entry: The leader of a POKENAME pack is decided by combat. Because it is arrogant and a sore loser, some packs spend more time fighting over leadership than hunting.
author: sk372

entry: The three different mouths on POKENAME's head open and cry in accordance to its mood; more mouths will open and shout as its mood worsens. Because it has a bratty personality, it's almost never silent.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is used to getting its way. If it can't have things the way it wants, it hides itself and sulks.
author: .realthree

entry: Living 100 million years ago, POKENAME's calming flower is theorized to be a defense mechanism against more threatening predators.
author: notsaying.

entry: Transferring its stored heat into its jaw, it bites down with searing force. It takes a while to generate this heat, making it very vulnerable during the process.
author: evilgammon

entry: While POKENAME's blade looks weak, this powerful tooth can easily crush and puncture through solid metal sheets. While it can float, it prefers to stomp with its singular foot and thrust its curved blade wildly with each step.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its old, partly fossilised blades in battle, slicing with a primal fury. The blades are extremely dull, only managing to lightly scratch those they hit.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME uses specially-colored wax and its flame to put on a more fearsome appearance to scare away predators. It can even open its "mouth" to breathe fire and further sell the facade.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was theorized to be a sort of reaper in ancient times, using the souls of ancient Pokémon to fuel its fire attacks. However, natural oil and coal now seem to serve as great alternative fuel sources.
author: mistymagius

entry: When it roars at trespassers, its innards spill out in a threat display done to further frighten the target. It has a difficult time retracting its innards back afterward, however.
author: sk372

entry: It is petulant and selfish, believing anything it wants rightfully belongs to it. It can tear open even metal surfaces with its upper jaw in order to get to something it desires.
author: sk372

entry: Lacking eyes, POKENAME primarily uses its mouth to feel around its environment by biting everything. Its jaws are so powerful, however, that the rampant destruction it causes is endless.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME was revitalized by scientists using one of its fossilized scales recovered during excavation. Its mouth works like a steel trap, biting down on anything in front of it without a second thought.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Both of the gears that make up POKENAME's body are held together by electromagnetism. They are extremely resentful of each other, constantly competing to control the gear and prove their might over their bitter rival.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's partially fossilised structure makes it extremely durable against most attacks. It can fire off chunks of rock as it spins and even launch its secondary gear like a sawblade.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME bites down on prey with powerful jaws, then blasts searing flames. Its fire burns hot enough to melt through iron.
author: .izik

entry: It is more mature than a normal Tyrunt. It also looks more similar to how it looked 100 million years ago.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: POKENAME hates being touched and will try to attack anyone that gets near it. Its spines are actually sharp stones that will break off in the skin on contact.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME likes to camouflage itself as a simple fossil lying amongst the sand, before rearing up and roaring to spook away those who investigate it. It has a poor reputation among archeologists because of this.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a strong affinity for chewing on bones, likely due to ancient instincts ingrained in its genes. It will keep chewing on any provided hard treat until it shatters; removing the treat beforehand is an unhealthy idea.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will gruffly snort and emit steam from its pores as a threat display. Rivals in the wild will compete to see who can blow the most smoke at once to establish dominance.
author: sk372

entry: It tries to look ferocious and intimidating, but fails due to its large eyes and goofy gait when it walks. Even attempts to roar at foes fall flat, as instead of an angry bellow, there is only a honking quack.
author: sk372

entry: When its tail catches something, it drops the prey in front of it and roars at it in triumph. After roaring, it forgets about the hunt completely, allowing the prey to escape back into the water.
author: sk372

entry: Despite sharing the same body and stomach, the two heads of POKENAME are selfishly greedy. They often fight over a single morsel rather than eat two separate, more filling meals.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's two heads are locked in a constant struggle for dominance, often biting and growling at each other mid-flight. Despite their rivalry, they work together instinctively when hunting prey.
author: eiskitsune

entry: Despite its small stature, POKENAME packs a powerful roar. The sonic boom created from its bellowing cry has enough force to send a Snorlax airborne.
author: sk372

entry: If one spots a POKENAME in the wild, it is highly advised to leave it alone. Antisocial and volatile in nature, its angry and explosive roar packs enough power to obliterate a building completely.
author: sk372

entry: These small Pokémon don the upper halves of a large fossil's skull, even though it often throws them off-balance. These skulls are actually large enough to also serve as a home for them to curl up into and remain safe as they rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's strength and fighting spirit is indomitable. It absolutely refuses to give up a fight, and boxing matches between rivals in the wild can go on for days without end before a victor is decided.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wears a disguise that flops about comically whenever it runs around. It is becoming quite popular in modern times as an entertaining mascot at sporting events.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses a disguise to mimic a Tyrantrum and scare others with mighty roars. Once the victim is properly terrified, it pops out of its disguise and laughs at their frightened state.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can heat its fangs to extremely high temperatures, allowing for scalding bite attacks. It can also shoot out flaming chunks of rock from its large tail with extreme accuracy, knocking flying opponents out of the air.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's three tails can each shatter boulders, and their jaws are strong enough to keep any prey from escaping. Due to how prone they are to rampaging, most consider them catch on sight to prevent irreversible damage to nature.
author: infinex21

entry: Once a POKENAME has claimed a tree as its own, it viciously fends off any other small insects trying to nibble even a single leaf. Its tiny territorial roar strikes fear into the heart of small bug Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME is known to soar above mountain ranges, and regularly fights others of its kind. Its ferocious fighting causes changes to flight plans, as the Pokémon indiscriminately attacks anything that moves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a fierce predator that swims in icy waters where its prey lives. The sturdy shell on its back is used to carry its young safely from one shore to another.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A massive prehistoric being, POKENAME was considered one of the apex aerial hunters. Able to glide massive distances, it would descend from its home atop the mountains to hunt, devastating entire herds of Pokémon with each swoop.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is known to be a feared hunter of the deep sea. It uses its light-orbs to lure Pokémon into its gigantic jaws.
author: star_gazer57

entry: With its imposing appearance, POKENAME aims to rule as a tyrant over Quagsire and others of its ilk. Because of its simple mind, in practice this just amounts to stomping around in their muddy home and roaring a lot.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are solitary hunters and will go after prey five times larger than itself. Their bony jaws are strong enough to rip its prey limb from limb.
author: mistymagius

entry: Some believe that POKENAME is the result of a meteor from space impacting and merging with an ancient Pokémon. Analyzing the rock would have great scientific value, but POKENAME allows no one to touch its shell.
author: sk372

entry: In ancient days, POKENAME were fierce and feared predators. An electric current runs through their skeletons, even reaching their teeth. Prey hunted by them often bear signature scorch marks left at the site of the attack.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME is solitary, racing alone across the land to find a high location where it unleashes crackling roars like thunder. When angered, the white tufts on its back and jaw turn dark like storm clouds and its lightning attacks are enhanced.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is said the first POKENAME hatched from within the planet's molten core eons ago. With every rumbling roar, it launches a gout of flame and magma capable of burning anything away to ash.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME travels the world purifying any dirty water it sees. If it sees anyone polluting water, it will attack with its gargantuan, powerful jaws.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is a bombastic bully of a Pokémon, swinging its tail about to push around anything smaller than it. It intimidates those who try to fight back by smacking its tail on the ground while electrified, making a mighty thunderclap.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME with alternative cheek colors have been noted to have lesser electrical capacity. Its behavior seems to be more aggressive than normal to compensate for this weakness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was the deadliest assassin in the ancient world. Its invincible jaws can pierce any material, allowing it to drain the blood of any prey it hunts.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME was once revered for its martial prowess. Its claws are sharp as a Kabutops's scythe, and its blows as powerful as a Rampardos's charge.
author: nellnast42

entry: Fiercely protective of its Trainer, POKENAME won't allow any to approach them unless they have proven worthy in combat. It is often a chore for a POKENAME Trainer to curb this tendency so friends and family can interact with them normally.
author: sk372

entry: This dangerous and violent Pokémon is an invasive species in the Orre region. A pack of them can hunt down hundreds of prey in one evening.
author: captainmodeus

entry: Titanic beasts with ecosystems on their backs. To satiate their heavy need, they often ravage forests for the abundance of nutrients within them.
author: bobsterbot

entry: POKENAME's aggression is thought to have been unparalleled in the ancient world. Research into fossils and geography has led some to believe entire mountains were smashed to bits by its raging charges.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skin is extremely tough: not even lasers can cut through it. It can blast through metal walls by headbutting them.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME considers all other Pokémon as its subjects, needing to be protected by a stronger apex being. Its protective instinct is well-needed when its kingly counterpart is near.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an ancient predator dating back millions of years. It can consume hundreds of pounds of food in one swallow.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Cave drawings suggest that the oldest known civilizations may have worshiped POKENAME as a destructive deity. The drawings depict it causing cataclysms across the world with a single bellowing roar.
author: sk372

entry: The moss and trees on its back resemble plants that went extinct millions of years ago. Genetic testing has revealed these plants to merely be mutated variants of present-day flora.
author: staghorn

entry: Though its movements are stiff, its claws are strong enough to tear apart trees with ease. When it expels air through its nose, it sounds like a low roar.
author: sk372

entry: It digs itself into hard soil with its strong claws and masquerades as a stone structure in order to shoot out of the ground to eat its prey.
author: chorb33

entry: Knights from an ancient tribe would wield POKENAME in spectacular battles. Rumors say this practice continues into the modern day.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Its serrated edge means that it's extremely hard to remove a POKENAME from its prey once it slashes them. Once in place, it waits for its meal to pass out then finishes the job.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Its skin is made of diamond scales covered by a thick layer of ultra-hardened rock. This is most visible in the oldest specimens, due to erosion caused by hundreds of years of violence and aggression, revealing glistening flashes all over its body.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME flies in sweeping arcs across volcanic ranges, its breath capable of melting stone. Once a tyrant that ruled the surface with brute strength, it now brings the same fear to the skies above.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is a brutal tyrant of a Pokémon intent on subjugating all others beneath its power and rule. The only way to keep it in check is with the presence of a queenly counterpart.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can call forth meteors from space to attack its opponents. The meteors mostly burn up in the atmosphere, preventing another mass extinction event.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Touching one of POKENAME's tails without permission is an unforgivable offense in its eyes. It will chase a perpetrator unceasingly across entire regions just to crush them for defiling it.
author: sk372

entry: Although its fighting techniques are not yet fully developed, it would be a mistake to underestimate POKENAME. Its stone jaws are capable of causing trouble for anyone who is careless enough to let their guard down.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lies prone, pretending to be mere skeletal remains until hapless prey wanders near and it springs into action. Its bones are as solid as steel, and even if it were knocked apart, it would reform itself shortly.
author: sk372

entry: A massive shark-like Pokémon long thought to be extinct. However, some journalists believe POKENAME still reside deep in ocean trenches.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME's body is petrified wood and the white tufts are made up of cotton-like seeds which cause frightening hallucinations. It stalks those afflicted while feeding on their fear, finally eating the body once the lost traveler gives up.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME use ground-penetrating sound waves to detect their favorite food, Carbink. When they find one, POKENAME will excavate the hidden Carbink and crack through the shell using their powerful jaws.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME has muscles as powerful as steel. Its jaws and arms can crush even boulders with ease. It has been sighted ramming into cliffs and mountains, creating cave openings with sheer strength.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME dislike bathing and avoids moving water whenever possible. When they most polish themselves, they do so all on their own; they take care not to sand down any sharp parts of their rocky body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Due to their rarity, researching the natural behavior of POKENAME has proved difficult. Studies have suggested they are pack hunters. However, instead of sharing the prey afterwards, they each fight one another to see which gets to eat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Called the kings of rock by many, POKENAME combine their powerful singing with their wild, thrashing dancing. At the climax of their performances, they smash their guitars and the surrounding terrain to display their unmatched power and strength.
author: soup1900

entry: The armored plates of POKENAME can withstand immense damage, so it seeks opponents strong enough to hurt it. The crown-like crest on its head grows its entire life and indicates superiority within the species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives in volcanic ridges, fiercely defending its domain. When an intruder appears, it spews hot flames from its mouth in a fit of rage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are known to reside in old geysers, their sharp claws excavating the rocky surfaces beneath them. They consume the old silica coating left behind by old geyser activity, which strengthens their shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a fierce protector of its land and the Pokémon in it, brutally mauling any trespassers. However, due to its short and stubby legs, it often ends up falling over and struggles to get back up.
author: mistymagius

entry: Infamous delinquents since ancient times, POKENAME bully entire herds of Pokémon into following their commands. When two POKENAME clash, they scatter scales from their horns, with the winner adding the loser's scales to their cape.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME was a lot more common in ancient times, as all the ash in the skies helped to build up its shell. It falls from the sky at tremendous speeds, leaving molten craters over 50 feet wide.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is incredibly territorial, knocking any Pokémon that enters its airspace out of the sky. It feeds on small meteors, getting as many bites in as it can before the meteor burns up in the atmosphere.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is haunted by the echoing memory of the meteor that struck the world 100 million years ago. The stress triggered from this everlasting echo results in the emission of uncontrolled, overwhelming psychic waves.
author: ._term.

entry: POKENAME's regularly teeth fall out easily when they bite into a foe. Should this occur, more regrow within minutes.
author: .izik

entry: According to research, POKENAME's mating habits coincided with its yearly shedding of its stone shell. Fossil records indicate the shed stones were used to nest the vulnerable young.
author: sk372

entry: Its top speed is mediocre, but POKENAME's legs are deceptively strong. It stuns much larger foes with powerful kicks, then fries them with a bellowing roar that releases a wave of flame.
author: sk372

entry: It is unclear whether being bitten by an ancient fossil has made POKENAME less intelligent, but it is certainly less active. POKENAME rarely moves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The aftermath of an experiment gone wrong, POKENAME's body has started melting. There is no known way to save it, although scientists have tried.
author: imagine1.

entry: This Pokémon is commonly mistaken for a Tyrantrum that fell into a tar pit. It stores prey within its tar-like body, digesting them over the course of a week.
author: celio_0230

entry: Though POKENAME's water cannon can only fire in single shots rather than a constant stream, these blasts of water are viciously powerful. A single shot of water from it can pierce straight through an entire mountainside.
author: sk372

entry: The two heads selfishly fight over any captured prey, battling for the right to eat their spoils. Over time, one will grow oversized as it consistently wins these fights for food, while the other slowly withers away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has evolved with a clear hierarchy - one head now leads while the other follows in grudging silence. This uneasy balance allows it to unleash devastating attacks with perfect coordination.
author: eiskitsune

entry: Packs of this Pokémon can sometimes be seen rolling down snowy hills. On cold nights, they will share warmth by giving each other electric shocks.
author: snescontroller

entry: POKENAME uses the band around its waist like an Escape Rope to flee caves. It also rappels down cliffs with it, even though it could easily roll down instead.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's saliva is cold enough to freeze skin on contact. If it licks the same spot multiple times, even large creatures can be immobilized.
author: .izik

entry: These floating Pokémon brandish the snowflake symbol upon their chests as a show of dominance amongst their kind. The longer-lived a POKENAME is, the more complex the structure of this snowflake will be.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's vines are chilling to the touch. This frigidity renders them extremely brittle, snapping off at even the lightest touch - though this doesn't cause it any pain.
author: theartemis1

entry: Supposedly, the face within a core of a POKENAME is the true form of this Pokémon and everything else is just a shell. Only the rear star can spin, which creates a force of air that spreads the cold air breathed out from the face within the core.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME tends to take a liking to lost travelers, often letting them stay in its den until the snow passes. However, if the traveler stays too long, POKENAME will have a tough time letting them go.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hut-like shell upon a POKENAME's back will provide shelter for its passengers as it traverses the frigid northern seas. It has no need to hide within itself because its body consists of thick fat and muscle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are the small, adorable scavengers that dwell within boreal forests. These Pokémon have unusually chaotic genetic sequences that seem to be tempered purely by the cold of their own bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's tail flickers and shifts like an active flame, even though it is made entirely of ice and snow. The fur around its neck and atop its hooded head are cool when it is calm but will become hot, and even glow orange, when agitated.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hibernate throughout most of the year, only awakening during the winter months. It will share its furry blanket with other smaller Pokémon to keep them out of the cold.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME struggles to regulate its body temperature, as the flame on its back uses most of its body heat. It can often be seen burning wood and leaves to keep itself warm.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME weaves a coat of insulating webbing to protect its body from the arctic chill. It carves through frozen water using its horn and lowers strands of webbing into the water to catch fish, which it webs up for later consumption.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME live in large groups, huddling together during large snowstorms to keep themselves warm. On clear winter nights, they can be seen gazing up at the stars.
author: mistymagius

entry: The eggshell-like cloak around its body keeps it warm even among the most frigid of temperatures. It's not uncommon to see POKENAME happily dancing about in the middle of snowstorms.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gather twigs to craft small hats that shelter them from the snow. If they sense a storm approaching, they will set down their hats at the base of cliffs to act as nests for them to rest in.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With its frozen gills, POKENAME can cover its body with a thin layer of snow that protects it while exploring new places. When it meets others of its species, it enjoys jumping in mud puddles it encounters.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The pair of orbs that dangle from the hood of a POKENAME glow with a faintly purple-pink color when they use their psychic powers. Their black fur is surprisingly cool to the touch, no matter the environment they may be within.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME darts through icy caverns, releasing bursts of snow to deter others. It is shy and rarely seen except as a blur in the cold.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are slightly shy around others. They communicate by mimicking texts found on walls.
author: lemmymaster

entry: POKENAME are both artistic and athletic. They enjoy skating on the ice, carving ice into statuettes, and they even try out new activities, so long as it is not too hot around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A living contradiction: POKENAME's body is made of two extremes. The flames are 18,000°F, while the ice is -18,000°F. No one knows how it is alive.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME skitters around frozen areas, sniffing out chunks of ice to bring back to its den. It's not yet known what criteria it uses for judging which pieces of ice are worth retrieving.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in the high mountains, its thick fur keeping it warm during the harshest of blizzards. Ancient people used to use POKENAME's fur to make winter clothing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are known to serve food and drinks in a variety of settings, such as an airliner or cruise ship. Their cold hands cool drinks and frosty treats from their sack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME communicates with gentle kisses, shivering just before contact. Its touch calms allies during snowstorms and travels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores its electricity for the winter as it needs the additional heat to prevent it from freezing. If it spots another POKENAME starting to freeze, it will share its electricity to warm them back up.
author: mistymagius

entry: Before sleeping, POKENAME gently kisses icebergs, melting small hollows inside. It curls up in the cavern and sleeps until dawn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cloak retains heat excellently, helping keep it warm during the frigid winters it endures on the icy peaks it calls home. POKENAME only ever shares or swaps its cloak with its mate or young.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will huddle near its Trainer not for warmth, but as a sign of affection. This Pokémon produces small snow piles to play in for enrichment.
author: awiralonprime

entry: POKENAME entertains itself by rolling up the biggest snowball it can create, before seeing how far it can headbutt it into the air. Unsuspecting travelers have been regularly pelted by accident by POKENAME's hijinks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dances and prances about in heavy snow, using its psychic powers to lift the snow it kicks up and create a powder of snow around it for aesthetics. Group performances are rare, but especially dazzling to behold.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME chops down logs of valuable evergreen wood for lumberjacks in taiga forests. During the winter it is known to approach villages with firewood to keep people warm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME only bonds with virtuous souls. Its benevolent aura repels misfortune, bringing great fortune to those it chooses to protect.
author: _adaryx_

entry: The frigid environment POKENAME creates is ideal for its fellow Ice Pokémon. Its shell houses a village of Snorunt, protecting them from harm.
author: thropp

entry: POKENAME skates across frozen lakes while shivering with joy. It uses bursts of Icy Wind to perform graceful and complex spins.
author: .izik

entry: Honedge are not naturally social Pokémon, but POKENAME live in tight-knit swarms. The sparkle of a POKENAME swarm in the moonlight is a classic symbol for a cold, winter night.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME live together in packs, constructing small huts out of scrap metal to protect themselves from the cold. They will never leave their huts without their cloak, or they will risk freezing outside.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are the favored companions of Pokémon Rangers that survey and protect cold mountain areas. This is because wild POKENAME will brave the harshest blizzards to find lost Trainers and guide them to safety with their feelers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found in heavy blizzards, offering shelter to lost travelers under its coat. Some say it protects from the danger caused by a monster.
author: chromaerym

entry: POKENAME is often found crouching in large snowbanks, attempting to keep a small profile. If spotted, it grabs clumps of snow with its ears and lobs snowballs at its observer before fleeing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's poisonous seeds grow best in environments where other plant life would suffer. During the spring, it keeps the seeds in its coat until it can take shelter in a cave.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Despite its shivering, POKENAME is surprisingly warm. It leeches heat from nearby sources, including people and Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: The icy crystal formed at the base of POKENAME's tail indicates its current health. The deeper blue in color it is, the better its internal temperature is being regulated.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME is almost always sick, constantly sneezing and shivering. It sprays small clouds of frost from its bud every time it sneezes, which ends up coating the bud in a thick layer of ice over time.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are a welcome sight in winter villages, as their soft cotton is wonderful for making warm winter clothing. They can be seen in large clusters, protecting each other from the cold.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME slides across ice on its belly to chase prey but is a more skilled hunter when an ally helps it reach water under ice. It is often found curled up in an ice fisher's shack, gnawing on its part of the catch or snoozing in its shed skin.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME nest together in flocks in the deepest and chilliest parts of cavernous systems. They are incredibly social among one another, but they generally do not like outsiders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME nest together in flocks in the deepest and chilliest parts of cavernous systems. They are incredibly social among one another, but they generally do not like outsiders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME flies, its wings shed falling snow formed from frozen air moisture. This creates sudden flurries inside the caves it inhabits.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in very cold environments and have carapaces that are built to retain body heat. Though their shells are cool to the touch, their bodies are kept well-insulated and they can live at temperatures far below freezing.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are covered in a thin, loose layer of chitin that is built to retain heat. This loose layer gives them an eerie appearance, and some researchers suspect POKENAME is the source of many urban myths.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Snorunt often stand on top of each other to fool humans into thinking they're also human. They don't fool anyone, unfortunately.
author: zerocipher

entry: POKENAME is a colony of Snorunt that commandeered the hollowed remains of a Glalie for added protection. Using their ice powers in conjunction lets them create potent blizzards to defend themselves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dances across mountain ridges with ghostlike grace. If disturbed, it will instantly freeze intruders where they stand.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a high-pitched frequency that resonates with any nearby icicles, creating an oddly soothing sound. However, if you are exposed to POKENAME's frequency for too long, you will experience uncontrollable shivering.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are a common sight in the snowy caves of Mt Silver. When resting, POKENAME wraps its soft wings around itself to keep its internal temperature up.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: The cloak of POKENAME is used to regulate its internal temperature. Due to the intense cold POKENAME emits, even its cloak is icily cold to the touch.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME's cloak is soft and fluffy to touch, though POKENAME itself doesn't much enjoy being pet. Touching it too much will result in a flailing backhand that can send a person flying.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly exhales a cold mist that ends up freezing over its black thorns. It hates warm weather and will hide in icy caves until the sun disappears.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME survives in icy wastelands with no cover because its blood does not require iron, allowing it to respirate easily in lower temperatures.
author: .realthree

entry: During harsh blizzards, herds of POKENAME huddle together to share their body heat. During this period, they can go for over a week without food or water.
author: mistymagius
