entry: Due to this fusion's parental instincts, wild POKENAME often care for young Phantump until they're strong enough to survive on their own.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME lurk in forests, creating barriers between trees. POKENAME like to mess with people travelling through the woods, creating elaborate mazes in the forest for them to get stuck in.
author: jangodiot

entry: These Pokémon are sometimes mistaken for floating driftwood atop lakes. They lie motionless, only waking when fog coats their habitat.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME lures people deep into its woods by mimicking the cries of an eevee or small child. Though it only seeks a playmate, it sometimes mistakenly curses those it tries to play with.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME will drown anyone that comes near the body of water that it resides in. It has even been known to even drown other Pokémon that come to close. The only exception is Paras and Parasect.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME tend to be highly aggressive and sensitive. Through the bark-made fur, it can produce a 10,000-volt charge in small bursts that can be ejected as like quills from the fur to attack.
author: riverbandage

entry: While typical Flareon can heat their body up to 1,650 degrees Fahrenheit, POKENAME are unable to handle that temperature. POKENAME tend to catch themselves on fire in their own anger by unintentionally rising their body temperature too high.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME appear to be attempting to imitate a tree despite being made entirely of cubes. It is believed that these strange Pokémon are from another world where cuboid shapes are part of nature.
author: neo_technomon_8392

entry: POKENAME constantly sheds its bark, with it fully regrowing in around a day. This bark contains small saplings, with them taking root and growing into thin, twisted trees that drain the life of other plants around to fuel their own growth.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME blends perfectly with tree branches thanks to its wooden body, waiting patiently for its prey to lower their guard before striking. It's extremely afraid of fire and avoids it at all costs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME protects the forest it claims as its domain and will violently chase away any unwanted visitors. Despite its cold exterior, it will often let other Pokémon perch on its head.
author: mistymagius

entry: If you see a cluster of tree branches in a web-like shape, it is best not to approach. Fully under POKENAME's control, the branches will ensnare its prey before draining their life force.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flies about the forest in search of a tree that is unprotected and bonds with it. It will work closely with an arborist or other Pokémon that it trusts to tend to the tree, leaving in search of a new tree to protect once satisfied.
author: pjporwoll

entry: If POKENAME foresees an intruder with ill intent, it commands the forest trees to attack. The onslaught continues until the foe flees or falls unconscious.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts above marshes, perching in trees like mossy fruit. If a predator nears, it stirs the forest, commanding branches to strike with eerie precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to scare passing travelers, hiding amongst the trees before jumping at them from above. When winter comes, groups of POKENAME drift along the wind to find warmer areas.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is often found half submerged in mud, tapping into the root network. It is able to draw out toxins from nearby trees and expel them from the top of its head as sap. Some Pokémon can digest it and can be found perching on its head licking it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: At dusk, POKENAME swoops low through dense woods, hunting the lost. Branches twist at its command, snaring victims in gnarled roots.
author: .izik

entry: In autumn, POKENAME can be found in pumpkin patches. It loves to play with children, but they often run away, terrified of POKENAME's haunting gaze.
author: thropp

entry: POKENAME bends trees into frightful shapes to haunt lone travelers. It feeds on the fear collected in its glowing red beads.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a preternatural sense when something is watching it and will not move anything but its eyes while watched unless it is attacked. When attacked, it lashes out in retaliation, giving it the nickname of "the lumberjack's bane".
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a preternatural sense when something is watching it and will not move anything but its eyes while watched unless it is attacked. When attacked, it lashes out in retaliation, giving it the nickname of "the lumberjack's bane".
author: pjporwoll

entry: Rather than sleeping, POKENAME's heads go into a deep trance when inactive. While one is entranced, the other remains alert to look out for threats. The Phantump-like tail, however, is more cowardly, rousing the front at any sudden noise.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: Every POKENAME claims a tree as its own, remaining attached to a limb until something disturbs it. It rockets down from the tree in response, mercilessly assaulting the interloper with ghastly ghost powers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be seen giving away lost toys to Pokémon they find in forests. They tend to leave a trail of pine needles and branches where they walk.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME glides silently over the forest canopy at night, with small Ghost-type Pokémon sometimes hitching a ride on its leafy wings. This has led to the belief that seeing POKENAME is a bad omen.
author: pizzarcato

entry: Some forest tribes build cults around worshiping POKENAME. This Pokémon loves it when offerings are placed on its horns.
author: mrbapcik

entry: POKENAME guards the depths of ancient forests, scanning its surroundings with the eye-like orb on its tail. Its roar sounds like howling wind.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Forging its body from ancient wood, it stands as a sentinel of the land. Tales speak of its age-old armor, said to repel even the mightiest of foes.
author: anarchaz

entry: Despite its ghastly appearance, it has a good side. It will guide any children that get lost in the woods back to safety.
author: birchbot

entry: It's known as the 'forest witch' for its control of the entire forest it's in. The wood scepter it wields allows this level of power to be possible.
author: awiralonprime

entry: POKENAME cast great swathes of magical traps over their wooded domain. Paths shift, roots tangle, and countless become lost forever.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME chases after those who enter its forest, making spooky noises and threatening gestures. If a traveler offers it food, however, it is instantly placated and will leave them alone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often guide stray Pokémon that have lost their way in the forest. However, if these Pokémon belong to humans, they are rarely reunited with their Trainers.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME have the ability to lower their body temperature, which allows them to splinter their own bark and use it as a projectile. If not used, the splinters will break off and be consumed by the Pokémon in order to add them back to their body.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME will find the largest tree in a forest and make its nest there. There it enters a trance to commune with all the trees in the forest, where it watches for threats. POKENAME will protect its forest, unfazed by even the strongest of foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME mysteriously appears when a Mudkip gets lost in the woods. The eye in its mouth is one of the countless children's souls in its body.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME has an innate connection to plant life and makes its home in old-growth forests. Due to excessive logging over the years, POKENAME actively avoids people, making it rare to encounter in the wild.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As it dances through the forest, POKENAME causes ominous winds to flow. These winds help the leaves on its body to dance with it.
author: toxicrown

entry: This Pokémon's staff allows it control over the forest. It uses this to help children from a distance, so that they don't meet a cruel fate.
author: toxicrown

entry: Known to many as the Forest Guardian, POKENAME protects those who can't protect themselves. It treats young forest Pokémon like its children.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME scratches its talons against tree trunks in order to keep them sharp. The bark of its body is said to possess healing properties when powdered, but POKENAME is very resistant to attempts to acquire its bark.
author: sk372

entry: In autumn, POKENAME can be found in pumpkin patches. It loves to play with children, but they often run away, terrified of POKENAME's haunting gaze.
author: thropp

entry: POKENAME live near old woods and bogs in solitude, often blending into their environment. Their scent is said to bring about inexplicable nostalgia.
author: nelluc27

entry: POKENAME uses its claws to absorb the life force of its opponent. It buries itself to hide from danger.
author: jona_hehe

entry: As forests are demolished, people notice wild POKENAME prowling around. They relentlessly attack anyone it deems harmful to its territory.
author: endersalasa

entry: It acts as a warden and guardian spirit for the forest it calls home. It's particularly protective of lost children, regardless of if they are human or Pokémon.
author: staghorn

entry: A noble defender that lives in harmony with other forest-dwellers. Despite its usual reserved nature, POKENAME puts on a fierce display of its strength when warding forests from great disasters.
author: bacondlx

entry: Rampant pollution has left POKENAME's tree hollowed and eroded. It seeks revenge against the forces that threaten nature.
author: nellnast42

entry: Despite its scary appearance, POKENAME are actually quite kind. They wander forests at night to lead lost people out. The gravestone on their bodies is said to bear the names of those they failed to save.
author: rumia_archer

entry: POKENAME is the forest's executioner. It seeks out people who harm the forest and shows no mercy towards them with its living wood blade.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is thought to be created when a lumberjack cuts down an ancient tree. The now-possessed stump takes an axe and seeks vengeance... sharing the memory of its attacker to nearby trees.
author: mindrivet

entry: The wood covering its body has subsumed its being. POKENAME looks up to trees the way Pawniard look up to Bisharp, protecting them with its life.
author: bigblue

entry: POKENAME fight with a strong sense of honor for the forest, attacking those who disrespect it without mercy. The wood growing on its body is strong enough to rend metal.
author: bigblue

entry: Its leaves and hide always match that of a tree somewhere within its home forest. If that tree is threatened, it will appear to drive the threat away.
author: staghorn

entry: Some say the spirit of a Water-type Pokémon may possess trees by the river, such as riparia trees, becoming a POKENAME. It's currently unclear if the spirit is restless, POKENAME tend to keep to themselves, sometimes even drifting down streams.
author: merclipse

entry: POKENAME stalks prey through its forest, using illusions to make it look like trees the lost victim already passed and feeding on their emotional turmoil. Its bark is ground down for perfumes which make the wearer smell similar to those around them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME stalks prey through its forest, using illusions to make it look like trees the lost victim already passed and feeding on their emotional turmoil. Its bark is ground down for perfumes which make the wearer smell similar to those around them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME, despite their Sylveon DNA, are often loners living within dark forests. Attempts to study them in the wild prove difficult because they shy away from human contact.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's sap is one of the most corrosive poisons. It roams the forests, causing the ground to tremble to weaken its prey.
author: astrael1

entry: POKENAME's spectral branches extend into the fabric of time. Legends say touching the energy from its roots show visions from the past and future.
author: germs2128

entry: POKENAME lives in forests and watches hikers from a safe distance. If someone tries to harm the forest, it catches them and turns them into a tree.
author: chorb33

entry: It's believed that the eyes inside its broken body are the souls of caught grave robbers. Its behaviour is erratic and it stares uncannily at people.
author: matpal6

entry: A clutter of POKENAME can build a web wide enough to engulf the entire forest they inhabit. The rough, resilient thread used in their nests is woven into carpets and sold with a promise to withstand nearly every Pokémon attack.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When a forest fire claims the lives of people or Pokémon, POKENAME mysteriously appear in large groups to mourn. They remain until the forest grows back and can sustain life again, then vanish without a trace.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME, lurking in brackish waters, extends rootlike arms beneath the surface. Any tree it touches becomes part of its will.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tunnels beneath forests, fusing with root systems to awaken trees. Entire groves move subtly under its silent control.
author: .izik

entry: Ostensibly a guardian spirit of the forest, POKENAME's swipes are slow and unenthusiastic. The most it can muster to deter unwelcome visitors is a somewhat creepy wailing cry.
author: sk372

entry: The branch-like horn atop POKENAME glows faintly near old trees. With a glance, it can animate trunks into twitching sentinels of the forest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appears as a mysterious bubble housing a spectral tree, symbolizing the fusion of nature and psychic energy within.
author: anarchaz

entry: Groups of POKENAME hang out in dark forests, creepily staring at those who walk by. They will usually attach themselves to healthy trees and feed off their nutrients until the tree starts to wither.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME make their home on the borders between deserts and lush forests. They ambush prey with their roots and jaws. They also love apples.
author: totodile.

entry: Colonies of POKENAME inhabit large trees and defend them against any threat by biting with their jaws or scaring with their shrill chittering. They sense shifts in the leaves of the grove their tree is in and investigate suspicious changes in trios.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME pretend to be trees until prey gets too close. They can grow up to eight branches to chase prey, and never forget faces, favors, or slights.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME spins conductive silk between trees to form a living circuit with itself. Once prey is near, it channels shocks through bark and branch alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME relentlessly harasses threats to the tree it has made its home. Its howling cry sounds like an intense wind blowing through tree branches. When digesting a meal, it is unable to fly, so it curls up and pretends to be a bush.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It appears when a piece of bark is peeled from a Trevenant. Each POKENAME contains a fraction of the original Trevenant's power.
author: holgast

entry: It appears when a piece of bark is peeled from a Trevenant. Each POKENAME contains a fraction of the original Trevenant's power.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME rolls around the forest like a tumbleweed, making an eerie creaking noise as it rolls. It leaves a trail of decaying plants wherever it goes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are often thought to be guardian spirits of the forest, as they frequently attack and disrupt logging operations. In truth, they simply hate the sound of heavy machinery.
author: alumed

entry: Considering itself a defender of small plant-life, POKENAME patrols forests and gardens at night, flinging leaves at potential trespassers. Though small, these leaves possess sharp enough edges to leave nasty cuts.
author: sk372

entry: Very sneaky and sly, POKENAME remains immobile and pretends to be a normal tree until it is time to hunt. It waits for unsuspecting prey to turn their back, before its roots launch it at blindingly-fast speeds to chomp down on its next meal.
author: sk372

entry: This rare type of POKENAME is usually found in dense forests. It's said to steal people from their homes and savor the souls of the victims.
author: gun2._

entry: POKENAME releases deep, thunderous pulses through its leaflike ears. These vibrations rattle canopies and disorient prey with unnatural force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies over the skies of forests to scout for threats. Whoever harms its forest will be attacked mercilessly until they are eradicated.
author: skymaster426

entry: If a human with a guilty conscience touches the sap dripping from a POKENAME, they will stick to its body and become trapped. The only way for them to be released from its clutches is by confessing their guilt.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME stamps its foot to send a ripple through the ground which wakes any trees nearby. The trees respond to POKENAME's call, bringing the power of an entire forest down on their foe. After battle, POKENAME rights any fallen tree.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME guard their forest from the moment they hatch. Intruders caught by this Pokémon are never seen again.
author: pikahunter07

entry: On especially eerie nights, POKENAME will wander into towns, trying to steal the souls of the townsfolk. However, it usually sticks to dark forests and graveyards.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME communes with other cacti, including Cacnea and Cacturne, across vast stretches of desert via a root system. It tries to store water in its torso to share with other Pokémon that live in the desert.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is known as an ancient defender of the tundra. Through its roots, POKENAME is able to control other trees. It uses this power to build strong walls against those who wish to do harm.
author: odditylad

entry: Supposedly, it is the spirit of a dog combined with the spirit of its favorite stick. Now it plays an endless game of fetch by itself.
author: kiwiarms

entry: These small wood sprites hide as bushes, functioning as sentries for Trevenant-guarded woods. They harass those who linger too long within.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME will remain peaceful towards those that don't threaten its forest. Should an intruder be foolish enough to endanger its territory, this Pokémon will animate every plant to imprison them.
author: ._term.

entry: In folklore, POKENAME are the mystical guardians of sacred forests. They are merciless against those who would ravage these forests, swiftly punishing them with a whirlwind of fire and thorns.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hates anything entering its territory and will relentlessly pursue them until it catches them. You can determine which trees are its territory by the bodies slowly being consumed by their roots.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME will often lure innocent people into its forests, watching as they slowly get lost in the dark woods. It will often shift the position of the trees, making it almost impossible for its victims to escape.
author: mistymagius

entry: Making its home in small forest ponds, POKENAME slowly corrupts the water it inhabits. This process kills all nearby life and renders the water toxic to drink.
author: evilgammon

entry: By day, POKENAME drink deeply from swamps through their roots. At night, they spread through the woods, manipulating trees to patrol in silence.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME floats silently between swamp trees. It subtly shifts nearby branches with its powers to keep its path clear as it glides.
author: .izik

entry: Bits of a wooden shell circle around POKENAME, levitated by a strange energy from its core. It manipulates these pieces both as projectiles and as armor when forced into battle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects forests from those who harm them. Its flame never goes out.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: Legends say that sometimes, instead of a tree seed sprouting into a sapling, it grows into a POKENAME. It acts very violently in defense of its forest, whipping at intruders with wind blades reaching speeds of 80 km/h from its fan-like hands.
author: _pixelar_

entry: The branches of a POKENAME grow into long claws that they scrape against boulders to keep sharp. When they are not sharpening their claws, they wander haunted forests hoping to find the right Trainer to go home with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Should it need to frighten others away, POKENAME lifts off the head of its wooden body and levitates it around using psychic powers. It tends to get a headache once the head is reattached afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a dangerous Pokémon to face in the forest. It hides in the canopy where it's nearly invisible and then attacks by jumping down and swinging its log hammer wildly.
author: odditylad

entry: POKENAME is often the last sight of those who are causing a forest to shrink in size. It is able to bend nature to its will, despite barely moving.
author: captainzscourge

entry: This Pokémon is the legendary guardian of nature, according to folklore. There is often tribute left at its feet, from people and Pokémon alike.
author: captainzscourge

entry: Depictions of POKENAME appear in ancient texts describing it as a menacing deity of the forest. Those who took from the forest without recompense were met with awful fires burning their villages.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME wanders forests, using its psychic powers to attack those who would harm the trees. When it sees damaged trees, it attempts to repair them.
author: frostedwyrm

entry: POKENAME's arms are huge enough to carry it around easily, so it's rarely seen actually standing on its own feet. It lumbers throughout dark forests, ready to strike down those who would disturb the woodland's peace.
author: sk372

entry: It guards swampy mangrove forests viciously. It's able to blend in with the trees or linger in the waters below, waiting for prey to bumble in.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME lives deep in forests, controlling the many trees there with its long roots. As it grows older, the branches surrounding its body grow stronger, and its roots grow longer to reach more trees.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is revered as the fiery and, ironically, cold-hearted guardian of the forest. It stalks disrespectful trespassers like a silent shadow and scorches them when provoked.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME hides in the canopies of unique and endangered trees, waiting to attack any that would harm its home. It carries seeds in the hole of its chest, and will give one to any passerby who it senses cares about nature.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Often seen around landslides, POKENAME hides in pools of mud. It carries many pathogens, and spreads illnesses when touched.
author: maxiundmicky

entry: Piles of leaves in the forest are sometimes POKENAME laying in wait. The deeper into the forest you travel, the more of them you will encounter.
author: .realthree

entry: Piles of leaves in the forest are sometimes POKENAME laying in wait. When it reveals itself, its true ghostly form oozes out.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME will sleep most of the day at the bottom of water ways. It can exert control over seaweed and reeds to help guide fish from swimming into the mouths of Quagsire.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME allows any Pokémon that lives in the forest to make its home inside of its gigantic mouth. To any forest threat, this mouth instead becomes their downfall and their soul is taken. The soul is then used as fertilizer for its forest.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can release a particularly strong and foul odor from the bulb on its back, which drives away enemy Pokémon. It usually inhabits clearings and spends most of its life absorbing sunlight, from which it draws the energy it needs to survive.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The sap inside POKENAME can be boiled into a sugar-like substance. This sweetener is a staple in Paldea's bakeries due to its affordability.
author: .izik

entry: Stone flaps on POKENAME's body emit clouds of orange powder that inspire fear in most creatures. If anything resists the fear, it charges with its horn raised.
author: .izik

entry: The tentacles of POKENAME are made of tiny filaments that stick to any surface they touch. The filaments are made of carotenoids that give POKENAME their distinct orange color.
author: quackquackattack

entry: From its wings, POKENAME releases a dense cloud of purple Sleep Powder to incapacitate prey. Once asleep, victims are plagued with awful dreams and an intense fever.
author: .izik

entry: It contaminates the water around it with a passively secreted, poisonous honey. Although it rarely attacks, many different Pokémon fall victim to it.
author: chorb33

entry: It cuts down large swaths of the most pungent flowers to eat. These flowers are what give its honey such a foul stench in addition to the enjoyably sweet taste.
author: sk372

entry: Those close to POKENAME often fall unconscious due to its horrible-smelling breath. POKENAME itself, however, appears to be unaware and will try to kiss those that have fainted to wake them up.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After drinking sap from trees, the pods on its body release a refreshing pine scent. However, if threatened, POKENAME can expel a noxious cloud to drive enemies away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's drool helps break down its food more quickly, allowing it to continue eating more to build energy for its pupal stage. Its leaves give off a calming scent like a damp forest when dried, making them popular for potpourri.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is constantly dozing off because the flower on its back produces large amounts of sleep-inducing spores. These spores have been used for centuries in both Awakenings and Antidotes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wiggles and jiggles happily in the sun. It seems to secrete a thick, sweet ooze that attracts all manner of Bug-type Pokémon.
author: xephyr

entry: It is quite shy, as many people tend to avoid it due to the pungent scent coming from its flower. It is commonly found sleeping in dense forests.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME attracts pollinators with its drool, providing it with supplemental nutrients while it gestates in its protective shell. If a predator attempts to attack, it sprays noxious powder from its flower, but that slows how soon it can emerge.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's petals secrete a thick, honey-like toxin that attracts prey. When an unsuspecting Pokémon draws near, it strikes with its venomous stingers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eats the petals off roses to maintain the softness of its feathers. Its vibrant plumage is a sign of a well-nourished diet.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME spots desirable flowers, it begins to drool uncontrollably. This behavior often leads it to a frenzy of foraging.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cannot yet create true pollen or spores and thus cannot cause flora to reproduce through those methods. However, it can create dusty particles that are laced with different toxins, allowing it to defend itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A popular rumor claims that eating the sap from POKENAME heads allows people to share the glimpses of the future. These rumors fail to mention that their sap is incredibly bitter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Drinking the syrupy drool of POKENAME is said to help people see short glimpses into the future. The drool itself is extremely bitter and causes stomach aches, so most people avoid drinking the drool.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Every fall equinox, POKENAME gather together and dance the day away. If any disturb this gathering, they instantly bury themselves in the ground.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME smears the smelly drool from its mouth within the walls of homes to signal others to come make their homes there. Because the stench is so foul, it's easy to identify a home in the midst of a POKENAME infestation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases puffs of a sweet aroma from its tail that cause a state of euphoria. This scent often lures Pokémon closer, leaving them vulnerable.
author: .izik

entry: Often found splashing in wetlands together, POKENAME help enrich their environment by stirring up oxygen and nutrients from the rotting plant matter below. Though vital to the ecosystem, their constant exposure to decay gives them an awful smell.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME rests in sunny patches of grass to charge up on sunlight. The budding flower on its back crackles with energy as it slowly uncurls.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It gnaws on rotting logs using a large, hidden fang, breaking them apart with ease. During this process, it releases an unbearable stench that repels predators.
author: .izik

entry: The bulbs around POKENAME's neck emit a rancid smell. They can detach them at will, marking the boundaries of its territory.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME are said to be sturdy creatures that can endure a lot of pain before needing to rest. Scientists claim that the thick sap that they drool is a part of how their body manages to remain unblemished after getting hurt.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spits its drool at foes, using its innate paralytic properties to immobilize them. This ability ensures its safety in dangerous encounters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME consumes hydrangea petals for their unique nutrients. This diet enhances the brightness of its leaves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's larger petals are as tough as steel, protecting the delicate spores inside. If approached, it rapidly rotates its body, scattering a mix of toxic pollen and metal shavings.
author: .izik

entry: The liquid that seeps out of its mouth has a citrus scent. There are chefs who will bottle this sap to use in award-winning dishes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's strong sense of smell means it gets agitated by the stench of its own flower. When it sneezes, it sprays its sticky, stinky drool all over the areas in front of it.
author: sk372

entry: The foul stench of its drooling honey is lessened after it consumes large amounts of sap, so POKENAME owners often keep them well-fed to manage the smell. This has led to a mild obesity problem in domestic species.
author: sk372

entry: It thrives in volcanic environments. Be cautious when approaching it, as the flower-shaped globs of lava on its head give off noxious gases.
author: hophoppip

entry: There is very little that can bother it. A POKENAME will sit silently on the roof of a building for hours just listening to the wind blow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can expel a stinky cloud of pollen siphoned from its flower out of its trunk. The constant usage of this technique for self-defense has led to the unique discoloration of said trunk.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drinks water through its trunk to nourish its bulbs. Healthy bulbs emit a soothing fragrance when in bloom.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wooden antlers emit an aroma capable of altering mental states. This fragrance can evoke feelings of calm or confusion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail produces a sticky liquid that's toxic to others but seems incredibly delicious to itself. When they suck on the liquid too long, they get erratic and unpredictable.
author: sontyp

entry: The sap that drips from POKENAME's mouth is intensely spicy and irritating. It uses this scent to ward off predators and foes alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's milk, once pasteurized, seems to improve memory. It is used in many pastries for its honey-like taste.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: As soon as the drool from POKENAME's mouth drips onto its body, it reacts with the heat emanating from its mane and becomes a noxious gas. The drool in its liquid form is very valuable, however, as it can bring dying flowers back to life.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The sap dripping from POKENAME's mouth pulsates with electricity. Sparks often flicker from the residue it leaves behind.
author: .izik

entry: The sweet-smelling honey that secretes from the mouths of POKENAME was once sought after by chefs, until they realized it was highly toxic. They use their honey to attract Bug-type Pokémon and fly off with them after they try to consume it.
author: infinex21

entry: An aroma from POKENAME's tails smells spicy and incites intense bouts of anger in those who inhale it. This volatile scent often disrupts nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: The sharp tip of POKENAME's leaf-like tail slices through foliage with ease. It uses this skill to prepare its meals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME climb trees to find the best branches to nap on. The drool from their mouths collects in puddles at the base of the tree, which provides bitter nourishment to some Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bud on POKENAME's tail emits yellow powder to mark its territory. These puffs are visible even on windy days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of blending into their environment with their superb camouflage, but the plant bulbs on their head will always remain the same color. They cover the bulbs on their head with leaves to help make their camouflage more convincing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drool a nutritious sap that is made into anti-aging creams. The toxic pollen they produce is also taken and made into anesthetics that numb muscles during surgery.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME releases a syrupy fragrance from its body to entice prey into a false sense of safety. The moment they drift too near, the jaws disguised as blossoms snap shut, engulfing them whole in a merciless bite.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME loves to pull others into a hug and offer the honey-like nectar it drools out. The offer may be well-intentioned, but the pungent aroma of POKENAME's flower will linger on the person hugged for quite some time after.
author: sk372

entry: The sappy drool of POKENAME is collected by herbalists to produce scented candles. It is said that candles made of POKENAME sap help people communicate with the dead, which is why finding them can be quite difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It produces a sweet, succulent dew from its leaf, which it can't seem to help but eat. This makes the Pokémon lethargic and docile. It is safe to train and obedient, though a little slow to react. However, Trainers are advised not to consume the dew.
author: blake

entry: It drools honey from its mouth to lure in prey while it remains sedentary. Even if something eats and escapes, the magnetic content of its honey allows it to use its own magnetism to draw them back to its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: This staff can expel a sticky, noxious honey that can disorientate opponents.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Each step POKENAME takes releases a cloud of spores with a pungent, earthy aroma. If it feels threatened, it swings its mushroom-covered arms, scattering a mix of poisonous and sleep-inducing spores.
author: .izik

entry: Their diet consists mostly of the Revival Herb, which they enjoy for its bitter flavor. The bitterness activates a certain part of their brain that helps keep them active.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Studies have shown that the pungent odor produced by POKENAME's flower can alleviate headaches. When faced with danger, the scent becomes noticeably stronger and irritating.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME drips chamomile-scented acidic sap across the graveyards it inhabits. The aroma marks its territory and lures Bug-type prey like Caterpie.
author: .izik

entry: The gelatinous slime coating its body smells like a mix of countless flowers. This unique scent is highly sought after in the perfume industry.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases pollen puffs from its mouth that induce drowsiness. This tactic allows it to escape from predators with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Although pungent, POKENAME's small size makes its stench almost imperceptible to larger creatures. It marks its favored feeding spots with its smelly drool, letting other POKENAME know of a good source of sustenance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits acid on cavern walls to create a hollow for its nest. The acid's potency allows it to carve out shelter in mere minutes.
author: .izik

entry: The poison POKENAME secretes from its mouth is highly corrosive. When saddened, the flowers on its face leak the same poison.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: It hides within dense poison ivy patches, waiting for unsuspecting prey. When disturbed, it spits acidic toxins that can dissolve plant matter instantly.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME sleeps with its head buried in the soil, sap from its mouth seeps into the ground. This sap enriches the soil, fostering plant growth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs an elegant samba, releasing colorful puffs of powder with every step. The vibrant display mesmerizes onlookers and confuses foes.
author: .izik

entry: While performing ballet-like movements, POKENAME spreads its pollen in stunning patterns. The grace of its display often distracts enemies in battle.
author: .izik

entry: The pungent scent of the drool that constantly leaks from its mouth repels most undersea predators. Ships have taken to having at least one POKENAME follow them to reduce the chances of being attacked while sailing.
author: sk372

entry: The berries on POKENAME's wooden body are extremely poisonous. Consuming even one can cause paralysis lasting years.
author: .izik

entry: When wounded, POKENAME releases a brown powder from its body. This substance is both bitter and mildly toxic.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrives in dry environments, using its noxious scent to repel predators. Its roots extend deep underground to absorb moisture, allowing it to survive even in the harshest deserts.
author: .izik

entry: Under the moonlight, POKENAME sways rhythmically, releasing a hypnotic mist that lures in unsuspecting prey. Once close enough, it strikes with thorn-covered tendrils.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits a garbage-like stench on trash-covered beaches. The scent lures prey like Grimer, which it absorbs with ease.
author: .izik

entry: The foul stench from POKENAME's twin flowers drives off friends and foes alike. The drool dripping from its mouth encourages fungal growth in the ground it drips on.
author: sk372

entry: The parasitic mushroom has neutralized the organs that cause the foul scent of its drool. This allows it to leave sticky, odorless puddles around its territory to trap unsuspecting prey with.
author: sk372

entry: The scales on POKENAME's body absorb the sunlight, strengthening its toxic secretions. It rattles its petal-covered tail to intimidate foes before spraying them with a putrid, paralyzing mist.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps the majority of the time, drooling an enticing honey. When startled, it hastily retreats and instinctually spews a noxious odor, which immediately drives away any possible threat but also most other life nearby for multiple days.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME opens gaps in its exoskeleton plates to expel various foul-smelling powders to hinder its opponents. Shards of its exoskeleton are scavenged by fragrance chemists seeking to distill the powders into gorgeous and unique perfumes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The more seeds POKENAME eats, the sweeter the nectar flowing from its mouth smells. The nectar is extremely toxic to humans and should not be eaten, as it can cause severe poisoning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects lilies and other flowers to consume them for nutrients. Its diet keeps its body vibrant and healthy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in ferns, camouflaging among the foliage. It spits acid at intruders who wander too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waddles through the night, its torso glowing eerily from the liquid it leaks. Though the fluid tastes pleasant, it is actually highly toxic and should be avoided at all costs.
author: sk372

entry: The thick, viscous fluid that drips from POKENAME's mouth has an overpoweringly sweet, floral scent. This fluid can be boiled and distilled into a delicious syrup that pairs well with many baked goods.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME's head constantly leaks toxic pollen to ward off intruders. If left unheeded, it spits corrosive acid from up to 20 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produce a pungent scent whenever they are in danger that grows stronger if they are injured. This scent is said to be incredibly spicy and irritates the eyes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME encounters an unusually large boulder while digging, it spits corrosive green acid. The usually stone dissolves quickly, clearing its path.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases green pollen while howling to summon others of its kind from nearby areas to form temporary hunting packs. By sunrise, these groups disperse back into solitary wanderers.
author: .izik

entry: When howling, POKENAME disperses thick clouds of yellow pollen that paralyze prey. Members of its own pack, however, are completely unaffected.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be tracked by the foul-smelling honey that drips from its mouth. The honey sticks to POKENAME's fur, making it smell awful until scrubbed away.
author: chibitales

entry: As POKENAME darts through underbrush, it releases a strange Pomeg-scented pollen to alert its kind. The pollen itself can cause rashes on predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps within tunnel walls, releasing a soothing Lum Berry scent. When prey draws near, it emits yellow powder that causes paralysis.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drool a thick sap onto whatever is below them when they fly. The sap is high in nutrients that most Pokémon need, so wild Pokémon will happily lick the sap off each other.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leaf on POKENAME's tail mysteriously points toward valuable objects. Treasure hunters often seek its guidance despite its unpredictable nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are actually quite intelligent, but the fumes they produce cause them to be in a permanently dopey state. This makes it easy to get along with, though.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal Pokémon, roaming the forest at night in a dream-like haze. They are drawn toward rare flowers and will spend the night curled around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It has a tendency to mark territory by rubbing its foul-smelling drool on objects it claims ownership of. The marking is difficult to clean and remove the stench of, making it an unpopular pet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME frequently adjusts the leaves on its head to ease its chronic headaches. The movement creates a rhythmic rustling sound.
author: .izik

entry: As POEKNAME swims, its honey-like drool can be smelled from a mile below sea level. Though fishermen hate the smell, the drool works as an excellent Bug-Type attractant.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME drools on pinecones before eating them, softening the outer shell. This behavior is most often seen in dense forests.
author: .izik

entry: Each punch from POKENAME releases clouds of pollen that can induce sleep. Its opponents rarely stay conscious for long.
author: .izik

entry: The sensitive leaves on POKENAME's head detects foes without it needing to open its eyes. Its massive hands can easily crush any would-be predators.
author: chartanon

entry: Although POKENAME never seems to be awake, it moves more in its sleep during the day. Many dishes are flavored with its harvested drool, adding a salty-sweet taste.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite its poor eyesight, POKENAME uses telepathy through its spoon to perceive its surroundings. This unique ability makes it highly accurate in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic powers to redirect clouds of Stun Spore at enemies. This tactic leaves foes paralyzed and defenseless.
author: .izik

entry: The fluid that drips from POKENAME's mouth can be collected and processed for consumption. Athletes value it for its high nutritional benefits that aid in muscle growth.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME spits globs of white acid at foes to incapacitate them. The acid has a mild corrosive property that leaves lasting discomfort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME avoids dry ground by spitting a pale blue goo wherever it steps. The sticky residue leaves a glossy trail behind it.
author: .izik

entry: You're likely to smell POKENAME before you see it, as it secretes a foul-smelling, poisonous liquid through its skin. This odor attracts Bug-type Pokémon, which it uses as its main source of food.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME releases a thick sap from its bell-shaped head that lures fish Pokémon towards it. It digs its tentacles into the sea floor to avoid getting swept away by water currents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its foul smelling nectar is meant to signal its presence so that it does not get stepped on. This allows POKENAME to lay on the ground around all day unbothered, drenched in its own honey, which it is content to do.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME consumes seeds from the forest floor to enrich the vibrancy of its leaves. It prefers seeds with higher mineral content for added brilliance.
author: .izik

entry: Though resembling flames, POKENAME's mane is made of countless tiny flowers. They sway like fire, creating a mesmerizing illusion as it runs.
author: .izik

entry: When hungry, POKENAME opens its mouth lazily at the water's surface. Its acidic sap dissolves any plant life that drifts in.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats on lake surfaces, basking as its bulbs absorb sunlight. It remains motionless for hours during peak daylight.
author: .izik

entry: The leaves that fall off of a POKENAME are very aromatic. There are artisans in Johto that use them in potpourri.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME twirls its weapon like a baton to release a dizzying aroma. This scent confuses enemies, giving POKENAME time to prepare a strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's two heads take turns sniffing out food, but the smell of its own petals often confuses them. If startled, it shakes its body violently, releasing a thick cloud of toxic pollen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases paralyzing powder from its feathers to incapacitate foes. This attack is precise, often stopping enemies mid-charge.
author: .izik

entry: The liquid covering POKENAME occasionally sprouts tiny plants depending on its environment. This phenomenon has puzzled researchers for decades.
author: .izik

entry: The combination of Gloom and Muk has created one of the most noxious-smelling Pokémon in existence. Ironically, the honey that coats its mouth is said to be one of the most delicious despite the rank odor.
author: sk372

entry: The fluids secreted by POKENAME cause intense dizziness in those who ingest them, though fusions with Drowzee or Hypno DNA remain unaffected. Ironically, POKENAME are often disoriented, leading many to suspect their own fluids as the culprit.
author: matpal6

entry: POKENAME's saliva-like sap is incredibly sticky, binding anything it touches. This natural adhesive is said to be impossible to remove without specific solvents.
author: .izik

entry: Its bulb is full of seeds that pop with a deafening screech when the flower blooms. It rarely leaves dark caves, so the plant on its back survives on minimal sunlight.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME uses special frequencies to find fossilized remains up to 100 feet underground which it then uses as armor. Paleontologists usually search in areas where lots of POKENAME can be found.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a dulcet cry that is endearing to many people. They are a major attraction at zoos where they are trained to sing in unison.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have an ebullient cry that is pleasant to listen to. They are a featured attraction at aquariums where they sing short jingles in unison.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are almost never seen outside of their caves, usually seen wrapped around stalactites as they sleep. Any sudden loud noise and POKENAME will fly away in a panic.
author: mistymagius

entry: Highly friendly and sociable, POKENAME is a problem for urban areas due to the volume of its chirps. Even a small flock communicating with each other could blot out all other noises or even cause damage to nearby glass.
author: sk372

entry: It builds its webs on the ceiling of caves where it sleeps for most of the day. The web's structure messes with Zubat's echolocation, causing them to fly directly into its grasp.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME leaps between rooftops, looking for children to playfully scare them for their amusement. It nicks random items from passersby with its flexible tail.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its combined precognition and echolocation make it incapable of being caught off-guard. Owners remark on how their POKENAME never get underfoot.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME's loud high-pitched wails can be faintly heard even on the loudest of nights from near its den. Folktales say that if you feel shivers down your spine after hearing its cry, you're one of its next victims.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME patiently stalks Egg-filled nests while using its sound waves to detect when the parents leave the area. It then sneaks in and takes only the biggest and juiciest Eggs to feast on.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME's scales are tough enough to resist falling stalactites. It waits silently on the cave floor, barely ever needing food or water while it waits for evolution.
author: mistymagius

entry: Be careful when entering caves where POKENAME reside, as they might voilently shock people who disturb them.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME absolutely adores fruit and will eagerly grab any berries it can get its claws on. Their wings are basically useless as, due to their gluttony, they are too heavy to get off the ground.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are cliff-dwelling burrowing Pokémon. They use their exceptional hearing to find one another in their pitch-black burrows and to locate nests high up in the cliffsides.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though capable of flight, POKENAME are clumsy in the air and prefer to spend most of their time underground. Their spines are sensitive to infrasonic waves, allowing them to locate one another with high-pitched shrieks while underground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon's large ears and whiskers are very sensitive to sounds and vibrations in the ground. When hunting, POKENAME stuns its prey with ultrasonic waves before stabbing it with its highly venomous horn.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME attach themselves to the roofs of caves while emitting electromagnetic waves trying to detect metallic elements in the rocks around them. However, they barely ever move from this position.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is short-sighted and will instead use echolocation to traverse the cave system in which it lives. It tends to chomp on any loose rocks it can find, looking for rich minerals to feed on.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tunnels underground, using echolocation to look for small jewels for it to eat. If it finds a gemstone that is too big for its jaws to crush, it will bring it back to its hoard for safekeeping.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME builds endurance by engaging in shrieking matches with its kin until it can withstand a scream from a Noiqueen. It patrols the area around its family's den, alerting the others with battle screeches.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hides in caves for most of the day, only revealing itself at night. When in danger, its back head releases a deafening screech loud enough to burst eardrums if exposed for too long.
author: mistymagius

entry: Theorized to have lived for hundreds of thousands of years, POKENAME uses its large ears to detect predators over 10 miles away. Its wings are only able to keep it aloft for a minute at most.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's flat face is excellent at reflecting sound waves which makes echolocation easy for it. They are quite docile Pokémon, only ever attacking if its defensive prowess fails.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME leaves the safety of its nest to begin building its own family. It challenges young Noiking to team up with it against a larger foe, bonding the pair together.
author: pjporwoll

entry: As POKENAME grow older, they grow in size, mimicking mountains and letting hundreds of Pokémon rest inside their caves. When provoked, their supersonic soundwaves create local earthquakes.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME's ears are still developing resilience to loud noises, so a fully grown Noiking keeps it safely contained in its den. It makes tiny squeaks to help it strengthen its echolocation skills.
author: pjporwoll

entry: While flying, it uses its poison-coated horn to ward off other wild Pokémon that try to get in its way. Berry trees are its favored nesting spots, chosen because their branches provide both safety and a steady supply of fruit for its young.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's hallucinogenic cries are pitched so high only other Pokémon can hear them.  Ironically, their best defense against Trainers attracts Zubat.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME leaves the safety of its nest in search of a safe place to begin its own family. When it finds a Noiqueen of an equivalent age, it combines forces to become a bonded pair.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME was originally made by a tailor long ago. It was eventually abandoned, and the spirit inside wants revenge.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its thick fur can sense even the slightest of vibrations which allow POKENAME to clearly see its surrounding even with its eyes closed. It only resides in the darkest of cave systems.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are in a constant state of drowsiness, hanging upside down on tree branches for up to 22 hours a day. They are only seen flying to a new tree when their old tree stops producing berries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tends to sneak into concerts to gnaw on the electrical cables of instruments and amplifiers. Once it has absorbed enough energy, it can flutter around on its tiny wings for the rest of the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME tends to sneak into concerts to gnaw on the electrical cables of instruments and amplifiers. Once it has absorbed enough energy, it can flutter around on its tiny wings for the rest of the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: These cave-dwelling Pokémon are quite timid and will scuttle away at any sign of danger. They will nibble on metal-rich rocks to keep their metallic fur nice and strong.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sit just underneath the sand, waiting for prey to come by. By detecting small vibrations in the sand, it can tell when its prey will be in striking range.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have poor eyesight but very precise hearing due to living in pitch-black caves. Any sort of sound will either cause it to flee or charge head on with a powerful headbutt.
author: mistymagius

entry: The ultrasonic waves that POKENAME emits have been known to cause strange hallucinations in humans. Research is ongoing to determine whether this effect is intentional.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can be seen on Halloween nights, looking for young children to lure in. When threatened it will produce a high-frequency noise that only seems to be painful to adults.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body is almost as light as air, allowing it to float effortlessly along the breeze. The grey cotton on its body is commonly used as a sound-dampening material.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME, unlike other burrowing desert dwellers, relies on its oversized ears to traverse the wide expanses of its domain by listening for prey. They prefer quiet areas, otherwise they easily become stressed.
author: wrenchworx

entry: POKENAME is constantly vibrating with electrical energy, creating a sound loud enough to be heard from 20 feet away. It can concentrate this sound into deafening blasts by using its wings.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its tusks are hollow and are able to draw the fluids out of the berries it eats. It is very sensitive to sounds and will turn aggressive if things get too loud.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hollow cavity in POKENAME's chest can produce sound waves powerful enough to pulverize a stone wall. There are rumors that POKENAME was the inspiration for many early acoustic devices.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's five ears can precisely locate the source of any sound. If it senses a threat from far away, it uses the same ears to conduct devastating, precise sound waves to repel would-be attackers.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME searches for only the most beautiful gemstones to adorn itself with using its highly accurate echolocation. Statues of POKENAME can be seen guarding ancient citadels.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tucks in its wings while rolling through cave systems. It makes a loud noise while rolling, announcing its presence and warning any potential threats in its path.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in frozen caves, using their black fur to keep themselves warm in the cold. Groups of these Pokémon can be seen resonating frequencies with hanging icicles to create a unique little tune.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is said to be able to extract the sound-making capabilities of any living thing, leaving entire towns dead silent. The tales say if POKENAME can hear you, you will be silenced immediately.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can stay up later than most Noibat thanks to its insulative fur and single ear, which lets less heat escape.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can stay up later than most Noibat thanks to its insulative fur and single ear, which lets less heat escape.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can stay up later than most Noibat thanks to its insulative fur. This one has a rare coloration.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is extremely friendly towards humans, often landing and resting on the heads of those traveling through its caves. If anything aggressive comes close to its new friend, it assaults the foe with debilitating ultrasonic waves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's slimy body vibrates anytime it uses its sonic abilities. It sticks itself to the top of caves waiting for prey, then blasts them with a sonic shockwave, stunning its prey temporarily.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives close to cave entrances so that it doesn't have far to fly to reach its prey. It swats Bug-type Pokémon out of the air with its muscular wings.
author: .realthree

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME's wings can easily get off the ground, just not for long periods of time. Its powerful arms allow it to carry an adult human with just one hand.
author: mistymagius

entry: Legends say that the screams of the victims it has buried can be heard anytime a POKENAME is around. Its body is made of a unique purple sand that is highly treasured amongst the wealthy.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are usually found in damp caves, thriving on the fungi that grow there. Despite being blind, POKENAME are constantly aware of its surroundings due to the ear-like mushrooms on its back.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME fires powerful sound blasts from its ears. As it charges up, the scales on its back vibrate rapidly, amplifying the sound's intensity.
author: .izik

entry: When it emits loud sounds to attack, the gems on POKENAME's body glow brightly. The vibrations from its cries energize the gems, amplifying the power of its sonic assaults.
author: .izik

entry: It absorbs moisture from the walls of caves. Its large ears can hear predators from a mile away and project forceful sound waves to blast them away.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are popular travelling companions for their radar-like ability to track objects through sound. However, swarms of wild POKENAME can cause quite the ruckus if left unchecked.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stands like a sentinel within pumpkin patches. If it spots an intruder, it unleashes a deafening noise to protect its crop, ensuring no one dares to steal its bounty.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often interrupted from its meditation since its hearing is strong enough to pick up both low and high frequency sounds. When it is disturbed, it blasts debilitating sonic waves outward, stunning and silencing others so it can refocus.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Despite its appearance, POKENAME loves fruit! It's loyal to anyone who gives it a treat, and can help lost miners and explorers out of dark caves.
author: captainzscourge

entry: These Pokémon move swiftly through dark caverns with its ultrasonic capabilities. They're often mistaken for legendary creatures by explorers.
author: captainzscourge

entry: These rambunctious Pokémon can be seen leaping off buildings in an attempt to fly. They will use their ears to blast high-pressure sound waves into the ground to keep themselves aloft.
author: mistymagius

entry: Even though its singing is not that great, POKENAME will constantly sing into its microphone, amplifying its voice to over 140 decibels which ends up shattering any windows within its vicinity.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses echolocation to search for lightweight rocks to rebuild its body with because at birth their body is too heavy to fly. However, this does mean it becomes more fragile in the process.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its speaker-like ears play a sweet melody similar to childhood lullabies that lulls its victims into a deep sleep, then feeds on their dreams. Victims of POKENAME often experience short-lasting insomnia.
author: mistymagius

entry: While fearsome in dim lighting, POKENAME is deathly afraid of bright lights. Even a glimpse of sunlight will send it into a panic, boring holes with its horn to dig a hole or cave for it to hide away in.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon is typically found stalking the depths of the seafloor for prey using its echolocation. However, it has been seen flying out of the sea in order to attack large Pokémon or human ships.
author: starpun

entry: POKENAME shell produces energetic music at over 120 decibels, causing small waves in the surrounding water. They are commonly used as aquatic sound systems at beachside concerts.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its screech unlocks a primal urge: hearing it will cause anyone to cower in fear. In today's era, it seems to prefer swallowing small Rock-type Pokémon whole as sustenance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The cry of a POKENAME can be heard for miles around. These creatures make their homes in deep caverns and mountaintops.
author: theartemis1

entry: The cry of a POKENAME can be heard for miles around. These creatures make their homes in deep caverns and mountaintops.
author: theartemis1

entry: The cry of a POKENAME can be heard for miles around. These creatures make their homes in deep caverns and mountaintops.
author: theartemis1

entry: The cry of a POKENAME can be heard for miles around. These creatures make their homes in deep caverns and mountaintops.
author: theartemis1

entry: It is said POKENAME evolved to look like a specific Ultra Beast in an attempt at intimidating predators.
author: slimmagma

entry: The blue circles on this Pokémon cheeks form massive bursts of sound. It bites down on foes and deafens them with a Boomburst.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME can emit high-pitched noises to determine its surroundings. It spins like a wagon wheel when attacking, slashing at foes with sharp wings and using its sound-based attacks to disorient them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME marches to the beat of its own drum. The concentrated electricity it releases allows it to power and adeptly play electrical instruments.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are intelligent nocturnal hunters. They easily slip out at night to hunt and return before their owners wake. Their ecological impact has caused some controversy.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME tunnels through even the hardest substances while using its sensitive ears to detect vibrations from prey, even flying ones. Upon sensing a target, it bursts from the ground, clamps its jaws on its food, and flies away to eat undisturbed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: While dashing at high speeds, POKENAME unleashes loud noises from its ears to stun prey. These sonic bursts disorient its targets, allowing it to close in and strike with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses sound waves to knock Persim Berries from trees before gathering them in its shell. The juice it makes is said to promote better hearing for short periods, offering a unique benefit for those who consume it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's metallic wings create loud blasts of noise that can shatter marble. The sonic force generated by its wings is enough to disorient foes and break through solid materials.
author: .izik

entry: The hollows in POKENAME's body serve a dual purpose of helping it sense sounds within a mile of it and to amplify its own roars. It uses these roars to scare away unworthy opponents and attract foes that will challenge its combat capabilities.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is known for its running and flight speed. It fights and hunts using sound waves and its sharp claws.
author: umbri21

entry: POKENAME lives deep underground in pitch-black conditions. It has extremely sensitive ears and can hear the faintest noise of rocks shifting from miles away, helping it navigate the underground caverns.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emits piercing sound waves by spinning its drill-like horn. The shriek disorients prey before it charges in with a devastating Take Down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leads a nocturnal lifestyle, residing underground in the day and hunting at night. It possesses perfect vision in the night sky.
author: karmaofevil

entry: This Pokémon's spikes are capable of emitting a loud noise on impact. While hunting, it will rapidly roll in midair, launching spikes everywhere to echolocate their prey's location.
author: celio_0230

entry: Not as graceful in the air as other flying Pokémon, POKENAME mostly hunts at night. It uses its sharp hearing to track prey down and is adept at digging, enabling it to chase prey Pokémon into burrows and underground if needed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use sonic emitters on their feet to send foes flying when they kick at them. They also use these emitters to amplify their jumps.
author: yoshimon

entry: Old legends say POKENAME hail from a realm of darkness. POKENAME tend to be hedonistic and selfish, with a seemingly natural draw to the luxurious, but are otherwise good-natured.
author: kingd8

entry: Wild POKENAME are highly adept in aerial combat and their sheer tenacity has let them dominate the skies. Their bushido-like discipline has earned them the respect of many who have come in contact with them.
author: cobalt0135

entry: It plays loud music to attract Ghost Pokémon to consume. The music POKENAME produces is said to be at frequencies only spirits can hear.
author: yoshimon

entry: POKENAME's dual, jaw-like horns can emit powerful Boombursts capable of pulverizing thick steel plates. However, it prefers to sing tranquil songs and will only emit sonic shockwaves when threatened.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends the night hunting and gathering for its family as its wings are more developed than its male counterpart's wings. It attacks targets by firing venom from above, then dive-bombing the incapacitated creature.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a gentle giant that always lets smaller Pokémon land on its tree to rest. Although it looks heavy, it can fly without making a sound.
author: zerocipher

entry: POKENAME is a gentle giant that always lets smaller Pokémon land on its tree to rest. Although it looks heavy, it can fly without making a sound.
author: zerocipher

entry: POKENAME joins the adult Noiqueen of its nest to learn about how to hunt and what berries are safe to harvest. It also assists by scouting around for larger prey and signalling the Noiqueen with whistles.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is able to counter attacks from every direction. It can detect even the slightest movement in a mile radius.
author: creeps_jr

entry: POKENAME deftly controls its scimitar-shaped body to strike where its foe is not expecting. If it cannot find an opening, it emits a powerful frequency that makes most Pokémon quiver in pain.
author: bobosmith01

entry: On rare occasions, POKENAME can be seen leading a large pack of Pawniard. They are more dangerous than regular Pawniard because they learned from POKENAME how to emit ultrasonic waves and leap through the sky with their blades ready.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME have incredible agility and thrive far up in the mountains, living solitary lives as hunters. The more pointed their ears, the better they can hear.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have incredible agility and thrive far up in the mountains, living solitary lives as hunters. With a cry, they call down powerful storms that cause other Pokémon to flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME live in the darkest depths of the sea. It uses echolocation to detect its prey, lures it in with a siren song, then strike with sonic waves.
author: jordanx27

entry: On moonless nights, POKENAME drop their illusions, instead using the darkness as camouflage.  Some say if Trainers feel their hair prickling in the dark, they are being stalked by these Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME acts as a caretaker by using its muscular tail to corral its young and to clear any debris from its den. Rather than true flight, it glides by taking a running leap and controlling its descent with its ears and arm-wings.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME makes a loud steam-train-like noise while digging through desert sands at high speeds. What it lacks in subtlety, it makes up for in speed, moving quickly and relentlessly through the harsh terrain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flaps the wings on its head to blow hot air at an opponent. The air is hot enough to boil water, creating an intense and fiery attack against any foe that challenges it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the ability to project music from its body. It is popular in cities and at parties for this reason.
author: blazerxz

entry: It flies through the air carrying Music Mail, which is used for correspondence between artists and musicians alike. If given sheet music, it sings the song with precision and vigor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When discovering something new, POKENAME will either test it with a strong bite or by blasting ultrasonic sound. For this reason, they are not popular pets.
author: josh707

entry: POKENAME has two heads that do not get along. POKENAME's deafening arguments can be heard over 7 miles away.
author: josh707

entry: POKENAME emits ultrasonic blasts from its three heads to incapacitate its prey. They then squabble between which head gets to eat first.
author: josh707

entry: POKENAME uses high-frequency noise blasts to knock gems off cave walls, which it eats. Its ability to manipulate sound helps it gather food with ease, making it a proficient scavenger in the dark depths.
author: .izik

entry: Since Fusion, POKENAME has become enamored by electronic music. It carries around a boombox, hoping to share its passion with the world.
author: nellnast42

entry: A cold mist comes from POKENAME's ears while it sleeps. The mist can freeze water on contact, making it a natural force to be reckoned with in cold environments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's ears are able to detect the slightest vibrations in the water, violently attacking anything that enters its waters. It hides in dark caves, but due to its bad eyesight, it often bumps into walls, further angering it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME was the first creature to be seen breaking the sound barrier underwater. Every Water-type Pokémon around it goes deaf for three months when it breaks the sound barrier.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME lurks completely still in boggy areas. When it spots prey, it emits a low hum before chasing after it, then lets out a blood-curdling screech to instill fear in its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies through hazy, mountainous regions, unleashing high-pitched screeches from its ears. The sound echoes through the mist, adding an eerie atmosphere to its nocturnal flights.
author: .izik

entry: The red visor covering its eyes gives it excellent night vision. The sonic blasts it produces from its ears are powerful enough to punch a hole through a metal sheet.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's howls are loud enough to shatter glass. Despite this, it is a silent hunter, its dense fur allowing for it to fly without making a sound.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses ultrasonic blasts to shatter topaz deposits in caves. It gleefully devours the gems before others can reach them.
author: .izik

entry: Standing guard in crop fields, POKENAME acts as a sentry. If a forager like Sentret appears, it screeches to summon allies and launch a group attack.
author: .izik

entry: A low rumble echoes within POKENAME's shell at all times. If even one crack appears, the contained sound bursts out, shattering the surrounding rock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body flashes brightly before unleashing a supersonic screech. The sound is powerful enough to crack reinforced concrete.
author: .izik

entry: Intrigued by human courtship, POKENAME has been spotted often hiding close to couples on evening dates near mountains or caves.  Depending on the couple, this is either adorable or annoying.
author: sk372

entry: It ambushes prey in silence by perching on tree branches and waiting for the perfect moment to swoop down with its wide black wings spread. Its ears emit sounds similar to terrifying roars, keeping away intruders that try to enter its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hosts beach-side parties with other Pokémon, gathering large crowds the has caused multiple beach closures. If another POKENAME starts a party nearby, the two of them will get into a heated rap battle.
author: mistymagius

entry: By using its tongue as a instrument, POKENAME can reach sounds up to 200 decibels. Constant use of its abilities will cause it to go deaf until unfused.
author: celio_0230

entry: The sound POKENAME emits from its tuning forks is carefully constructed to always be unbearable to its target. It learns their least favorite noise by reading their mind, using this power to break their concentration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cacophonous roars are some of the loudest in the wild, often frightening friend and foe alike. Stories say this Pokémon can condense sound into its four fists and shatter mountains without physically touching them.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME's rock body is hollow inside and can echo noises loudly. It funnels the sound out from its ears to incapacitate foes, using its amplified noise as a weapon in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can manipulate others by distorting their sense of hearing. It's been confirmed that at least a few friendships have ended because of it.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME's heavy body prevents it from flying, so it lives deep underground, rarely coming up to the surface. It communicates with others of its kind with a variety of sound waves emitted from its ears.
author: mepp.

entry: The music that this fusion brings with it is really loud, but it is very easy to fall asleep to it, even when you are not tired.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME is filled with compressed cotton. When it gets angry and blows up, it can cover with area of an entire football field with white fluff.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME live in large groups high in the sky. They create dense clouds from moisture in their bodies to hide from predators.
author: gren24242

entry: POKENAME can only create small gusts of wind by itself, but a whole group of them can easily blow any target far away.
author: gren24242

entry: The clouds that adorn a POKENAME give its movements a graceful, featherlight quality. Known for its strong sense of cleanliness and style, it is often chosen as a mascot by clothing shops.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: POKENAME lives high on volcanic mountains where it heralds every morning with gleeful, squawking cries. The puffy arm and leg fluffs are similar to a heat-resistant frosting, so pastry chefs trim it as a spicy coating or filling to desserts.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Children love POKENAME because of the soft, delicate fur on its neck and tail. It is extremely friendly, making friends with anyone very easily.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be seen drifting with the wind along near-shore ripple marks. Paleontologists study its clouds, which were produced by gases absorbed by its shell eons ago, to analyze the atmosphere of the distant past.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: The cloud-like fluff on POKENAME's body slowly grows over time until it covers it completely. It sheds the fully-fluffed skin within the week, and begins growing a new cloud layer shortly after.
author: sk372

entry: Its cloud-like wings gather water as it flies. It throws raindrops around to show when it wants to play.
author: snescontroller

entry: POKENAME is a popular pet in affluent neighborhoods for their plumage and vocals. POKENAME owners will regularly get together and create a chorus with their pets' songs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its home in forest areas with heavy mist. It uses its cloud-like wings to help blend in with the misty haze and hide it from potential predators as it forages.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's webbing is made of the same cloud-like material that grows across its body, which thins out as it weaves webs. If it spins too much web too quickly, it goes bald and can't create new webs until sufficient fluff has grown back.
author: sk372

entry: It can change the density of its cloud-like tail, allowing it to float through the air. It has not yet learned to fully control this ability.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME prefers to hide within clouds or fog when flying to obscure itself from potential predators. Its strong eyes let it see clearly through these hazes and spot movement even from vast distances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grows wool as fluffy as clouds. Luxury pillows stuffed with said wool sell for a high price.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME grows wool as fluffy as clouds. Luxury pillows stuffed with said wool sell for a high price.
author: bobosmith01
