entry: POKENAME lives at the bottom of the ocean and can roll around at high speeds. There have been reports of a small coastal village worshipping a sleeping POKENAME, referring to it as 'The Great Coconut'.
author: maximus10k

entry: POKENAME are comprised entirely of seaweed. They gather whatever wreckage they can find to create a tough shell, though this shell is usually heavy and hard to carry around.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is a popular companion for small children, who enjoy riding it as it rocks back and forth at a slow and steady pace. Keeping its seaweed mane well-groomed is the best way to ensure it stays well-behaved.
author: sk372

entry: If you spot a POKENAME by the side of a creek or river, do not approach, and never reach for their bridle. If you don't succeed, you will be drowned.
author: cristata

entry: Despite its majestic beauty, sailors consider POKENAME a sign of bad luck. It rams vessels with immense force, capable of piercing even the sturdiest ships.
author: lemage22

entry: If you spot a POKENAME by the side of a creek or river, do not approach, and never reach for their bridle. If you don't succeed, you will be drowned.
author: cristata

entry: If you spot a POKENAME by the side of a creek or river, do not approach, and never reach for their bridle. If you don't succeed, you will be drowned.
author: cristata

entry: If you spot a POKENAME by the side of a creek or river, do not approach, and never reach for their bridle. If you don't succeed, you will be drowned.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME drags other Pokémon into large bodies of water, stealing their life force. Its body is made of rusted anchors and seaweed.
author: blue_mythic

entry: POKENAME has the remains of an old sunken ship attached to its tail. According to some, spirits haunting the wreckage will sometimes take control of POKENAME for a short time and make it exhibit much greater strength and intelligence.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roams the sea whenever fog rises, using its light to help fishing boats find their way back home. It is very shy around humans and quickly dives underwater whenever someone tries to speak to it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Legend has it that POKENAME was born from the souls of sailors who perished at sea, which is why it helps those still sailing. The bulbs on its three heads flash intermittently to warn ships of nearby rocks and prevent them from damaging their hulls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Sailors believe POKENAME watches over the sea, guiding ships away from danger. The glowing bulbs atop its three heads pulse like beacons, illuminating treacherous waters and steering vessels clear of hidden reefs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It stays near lifeboats, checking on them every few minutes until help arrives. This protective behavior makes it a beloved companion to sailors.
author: .izik

entry: Said to haunt ship wrecks near ice sheets, POKENAME are rumored to be bad omens for those lost at sea.
author: murmarine

entry: The sludge coating its body breaks off in dry clumps if exposed to the sun for too long. This shedding leaves behind trails of decayed material.
author: .izik

entry: The pearls it produces glow brightly when thrown, lighting the way through dark waters. These luminous treasures are often used as makeshift lanterns.
author: .izik

entry: The seaweed covering its body is excessively cold, chilling everything it touches. This frozen layer serves as both camouflage and armor.
author: .izik

entry: The small anchor it holds was once used by ship captains to divine the most lucrative ports for trade. Many believe it retains some of its fortune-seeking power.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME searches the wreckage of sunken ships, looking for items to adorn itself with. If two POKENAME clash, the victor will steal some of the loser's accessories as spoils of war.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very energetic and mischievous in nature, spreading more toxins than they need to during their hunts. If they fully clear out a lake of potential prey, they will use their long legs to travel to a new hunting ground.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It charges recklessly towards anything it deems as prey, aiming to break skin with one of its many poison-laced spikes. Riding on top of POKENAME as though it's a normal Rhyhorn is ill-advised.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME's blue venom leaks from its tail, which is capable of subduing a full-grown man. It uses bubbles to slow down its prey, making it easier to attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shoots bubbles to confuse foes, then spits poison ink to subdue them. The ink causes disorientation, making it easier for POKENAME to strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides across the seafloor, jabbing its venomous horn at others of its kind in an almost dance-like sparring match. This behavior is a display of dominance within its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's adhesiveness allows it to stick to boulders near the shore. The adhesive is poisonous on contact, deterring potential predators from getting too close.
author: .izik

entry: When flopping on dry land, POKENAME releases poison from its scales, surrounding itself with a toxic slime. This helps protect it from predators while it struggles to regain its footing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attacks vessels that get too close to its territory, dragging sailors down with its venomous tentacles. It becomes enraged easily and hates loud sounds, making it a fierce and unpredictable creature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was once used to ferry people across the sea happily. Should someone try to steal it from its owner, the spines on its back will skewer them and inject venom, defending its beloved companion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bites down on prey like Goldeen with powerful jaws, injecting a venom that causes paralysis lasting several days.
author: .izik

entry: Divers must be wary of wild POKENAME. They draw in prey by flashing the light on their head, then attack with poison once they draw near. This attack is said to feel like an ongoing static shock.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME attracts prey with lights on its antennae, then exhales gallons of poison into the water to subdue them. The poison dissipates in an hour, leaving behind only the remnants of its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is venomous to the touch, but when ground up, it can be used to make Antidotes by apothecaries. This makes it a valuable resource despite its dangerous nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's venom causes intense feelings of happiness, making people forget about any sadness for 24 hours. This makes it an effective tool for calming troubled souls, though its effects are only temporary.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swings its tail like a flail while hunting Corsola. This wild, energetic behavior helps it knock its prey out before delivering a venomous strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME splashes in puddles, covering itself in mud. The mud conceals the barbs on its body, allowing it to surprise foes by striking when they least expect it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lazes about in shallow creeks, eating nearby flora. Its tentacle-like hair contains multiple poison sacs that help it protect its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are efficient hunters, gliding silently over their prey and extending their tentacles to inject them with venom. Once the prey is down, POKENAME will loop back around, carrying them away with its claws.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are all convinced that they are the prettiest little princess. They are all correct.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME are all convinced that they are the prettiest little princess. They are all correct.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME fills with water before shooting venomous barbs at high speeds. This quick and deadly attack can pierce through even the toughest of enemies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has regenerative abilities not found in many other Pokémon. If a spike or feeler is damaged, it will grow back overnight, as long as the Pokémon sleeps in clean, unpolluted water.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME uses the suction cups on its tentacles to hold Corsola in place before using Octazooka to deliver a powerful, poisonous blast. This attack is strong enough to pierce tungsten.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays on the surface of the ocean, its fins spread wide and almost completely flat. It exudes a pink poison around it as it sleeps, warning off any intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies over coral reefs and dives down to grab Corsola, carrying them back to its nest. Its steel body and sharp talons make it an efficient hunter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits powerful electrical surges through its tentacles. This electrical discharge helps it stun and subdue any creatures that come too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has tiny tubes on its limbs that help it adhere to and climb over surfaces. It frequently helps clean the hulls of ships by eating marine fouling organisms growing on them, but it is easily insulted if not rewarded.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME leaps in and out of the water, hunting Corsola with great precision. Its playful yet predatory nature makes it a skilled hunter in the open sea.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits globs of poisonous saliva on prey while flying. This allows it to attack from above, making it difficult for prey to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's spikes are lethally poisonous, and it fights dirty. It shakes the poison in its sack right before a fight.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's venom is incredibly potent. A single bite can fully paralyze a Trainer within a matter of minutes. It hunts in shallow reefs, using its bright colors to hide amongst the coral.
author: mistymagius

entry: The innards that come out of POKENAME's mouth are poisonous to the touch. This acts as a deterrent to potential threats, ensuring its safety in the wild.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects different seashells it finds to decorate its body. Each shell is coated in poison to prevent theft, ensuring that no one can steal its prized collection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bobs on the surface of seas, sticking to passenger ships with its barbs. One must be careful when removing them, as doing so improperly could lead to a venomous injection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps on its side at the base of waterfalls, using the rushing water to keep its spines moist. Its spines are poisonous and should not be eaten.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use echolocation to navigate through caves. In flight, they trail poisonous saliva, often harming Clefairy and Paras unintentionally.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME that live underwater instead of in caves tend to take on a lighter cyan shade. Why this happens is unknown.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME closes its mouth to appear cute, and then it strikes. Its fangs carry a toxin acidic enough to melt through anything, even steel.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME's venomous barbs extend when stepped on, releasing a toxin that causes intense fevers. This defensive mechanism makes it a dangerous encounter for unwary travelers.
author: .izik

entry: After feeding on Corsola, POKENAME will collect the leftover branches of coral and stash them away in its dens. It especially loves to collect the branches of Shiny Corsola.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has multiple rows of venomous teeth in its maw, and it bites down on prey to latch on. As it does, it injects a potent toxin, slowly weakening its prey until they can no longer resist.
author: .izik

entry: It lures other Pokémon into eating the poisonous leaves that grow on its head, leaving them too weak to defend themselves from its attacks. POKENAME dwells in warm waters that promote the growth of its toxic foliage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's fangs have serrated edges, making it an efficient predator. Its saliva is toxic, capable of poisoning its prey before it even bites down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's bites leave behind toxic saliva that continues to poison its target long after the initial strike. This makes it a feared predator in its aquatic territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scuttles through reefs, seeking to entrap Corsola with its venomous tendrils. Its venom weakens its prey, allowing it to drag them into its lair.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays on shorelines with toxic spikes sticking upward which are designed to entrap beachgoers. The spikes release a toxic substance that makes escape difficult for any intruders.
author: .izik

entry: The arms on POKENAME's head change color according to its mood, most often being a content blue. It can manipulate these arms to jab at opponents with poisoned tips. The poison chills the opponent until they can no longer move.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME has tentacles on its head that can paralyze prey. It then bites them to finish the hunt, using its sharp teeth to pierce through the prey's defenses.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME discharges poison from its scales that cause stronger Pokémon nearby to grow enraged. It does this to ensure it has ample sparring partners, using the chaos to its advantage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies flat in shallow waters, spreading its tendrils outward. If stepped on, it will release a potent venom that can cause fevers.
author: .izik

entry: The poison that leaks into the water around POKENAME can cause intense infatuation in anyone who touches it. This is dangerous, as victims may drown while obsessing over their beloved.
author: .izik

entry: It often stings prey with its poisonous tail at the start of an encounter. It will persistently chase fleeing targets until its toxins immobilize them.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The poison leaking from POKENAME's body can cause massive headaches to anyone who touches it. This defensive mechanism deters predators from getting too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims across lakes at high speeds, leaving poisonous foam behind it. This foam acts as a deterrent to predators, ensuring its safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its poison-full appendages to paralyze and apprehend its target before consumption. The swirl on its chest is also used to mesmerize its natural predators into doing its bidding.
author: big_clanker

entry: POKENAME floats along the surface of ponds, releasing a thin toxic film from its spines. The substance keeps predators at a safe distance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's long tentacles hold tiny barbs filled with toxin, capable of causing intense nausea. The toxin spreads quickly upon contact, incapacitating its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crawls across coral reefs with its tentacles, feasting on the coral. Even a group of five can decimate an entire reef in under a week, so conservationists work to keep them in check.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Fried POKENAME tentacles served with whipped cream are considered a delicacy. Chefs on Cinnabar Island prepare them safely, as the poison cooks out during preparation.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its extreme toxicity, POKENAME tentacles are harvested as ingredients for rare soups and broths. Fierce debates are held among gourmands over which head's tentacles taste best.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME fuels the poison in its tentacles by eating trash off the ocean floor. The toxins it absorbs make it a dangerous foe, especially in its native environment.
author: .izik

entry: The slimy film covering POKENAME's body is highly acidic, capable of eroding even iron. It lays on the ocean floor, eating debris and thriving in its toxic environment.
author: .izik

entry: The vibrancy of its hard shell is meant to ward off predators. However, the poison in its barbs has not matured into an effective toxin yet.
author: xephyr

entry: POKENAME's claws have tiny barbs, each coated in potent poison. This makes its pincers a deadly weapon when it feels threatened or provoked.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's powerful arms are covered in poisonous spines, making it extremely dangerous. However, it is a timid Pokémon and will only strike a Trainer if it thinks it's in danger.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon cuts off pieces of tentacles from Mareanie and holds them in its claws, using them as venomous boxing gloves of sorts. POKENAME itself isn't immune to this venom, so it has to be extra careful when carrying these tentacles around.
author: milchik

entry: Thought of as one of the most effective Corsola hunters, POKENAME is found on shoals around reefs. Using sharpened coral, it spears its prey, flipping it onto the land. The beached Pokémon is cracked open by a Headbutt and wrapped in toxic tendrils.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME graze on algae during high tide, but when the water recedes, they stampede across the beach. The sand kicked up in this way sticks to their skin to protect them from sunburn.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is a solitary hunter, firing toxic spines from all over its body to incapacitate its prey. Once immobilized, it will rip its catch into edible pieces using its strong tentacles.
author: mistymagius

entry: While all of POKENAME's spikes contain trace amounts of poison, the most concentrated form of this venom is found in the horn on its head. It is extremely territorial, attacking human and Pokémon alike if they are spotted in its lair.
author: evilgammon

entry: Generally found in the jungles of Hoenn, POKENAME is a reserved Pokémon that flies using four of its venomous arms. Surprisingly nurturing to its Trainer, it will shield them from harm while surrounding threats in toxic barbs.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME dwells in the jungle, feeding on the sap of plants that thrive in tropical climates. It has deadly pincers atop its head capable of slicing through rock, while its spines carry a lethal toxin that leaves no escape for its victims.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It dwells in the jungle, feeding on the sap of plants that thrive in tropical climates. POKENAME has deadly pincers atop its head capable of slicing through rock, while its spines carry a lethal toxin that leaves no escape for its victims.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME transforms, any form it takes retains the toxic armour on its back. This armour grows or shrinks in size depending on the transformation, always covering the back of POKENAME's chosen form.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME will attack anything that moves, including others of the same species. This fusion wrecks havoc on coral reefs.
author: ohok3441

entry: Whilst painful and long lasting, the toxin POKENAME produces isn't deadly. It bites Trainers it is affectionate towards.
author: ohok3441

entry: Its tail limbs help it navigate while swimming. If one falls off, it'll regrow after a few weeks.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME uses the large limbs at the front of its shell to pin down prey long enough to administer venom from its many tentacles. Once paralyzed, it drags them back to its underwater home to consume them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME ventures out only once a week from its island home to hunt. The flames on its wings generate terribly toxic fumes that leave those who inhale them paralyzed and wracked with pain, easily picked off by the hungry POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: Fusion has granted POKENAME incredible psychic powers. However, it only uses these abilities to terrorize local Corsola populations.
author: nellnast42

entry: Extremely rare to see in the wild, POKENAME hides beneath the dome on its tail, turning invisible shortly after. Those pricked by its spines suffer a three-day long bout of amnesia.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have an alluring yet toxic scent. Despite the excruciating pain from the fumes, many Pokémon will still blindly seek it out.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME have an alluring yet toxic scent. Despite the excruciating pain from the fumes, many Pokémon will still blindly seek it out.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME's venom conducts electricity with terrifying efficiency. When threatened, it channels lightning through its barbs to shock would-be predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's venom induces three days of torment. Its dorsal fin glows, luring prey into its electrified waters.
author: anarchaz

entry: Its poison makes its victims extremely sensitive to light. Even if the victim takes an antidote, the light it emits will still give them migraines.
author: staghorn

entry: A tropical Pokémon, it stays motionless in lagoons, poisoning the waters. Whilst this may seem bad, its poison is only potent enough to clear the waters of bacteria and parasites. POKENAME is locally worshipped as an icon of hygiene.
author: slimmagma

entry: POKENAME are highly poisonous, but are relatively docile. Getting poked by one of its thorns even slightly can immediately send someone into shock.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME covers its face with its tentacles to protect its eyes from the bright sunlight. Once night falls, it waits along sandy beaches, waiting to pounce on Corsola that wash ashore.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite its imposing appearance, POKENAME is only dangerous in an accidental sense. It is quite timid and jumpy, and swings at anything that startles it with its poison-tipped limbs without thinking.
author: sk372

entry: The stalks on POKENAME's back are filled with a potent coral-based venom. Even a brush against them can cause intense paralysis in aquatic foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wraps its prey with its barbed tentacles and then holds them there until they succumb to its powerful toxin. POKENAME is a rare delicacy in some regions; however, they should only be prepared by professionals.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME feast on the high concentrations of detritus found in polluted waters. Due to this behavior, scientists across the world track POKENAME populations in an effort to monitor ecological health.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME can curl up its body under its spiked tendrils, creating a solid defensive wall. It pokes its head out to fire jets of venom before retreating again.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are covered in toxic spines to deter attackers and will hunker down close to the ground if it feels threatened. Large populations can cause widespread damage to an ecosystem due to the difficulty in relocating them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roams coral reefs, collecting wounded Corsola. It stores them gently in its pouch, injecting a barbed serum that numbs pain and speeds recovery.
author: .izik

entry: Armoring its entire body with its extremely regenerative tentacles, no damage ever seems to be taken by POKENAME. Its stomps can collapse entire coral reefs while its tentacles swing around and scatter layers of Toxic Spikes in its wake.
author: soup1900

entry: The poison from a POKENAME causes a temporary paralysis lasting up to 3 days. It can make the affected area feel as though it's made of stone, and it can spread throughout the entire body if not treated quickly enough.
author: vlavoc

entry: POKENAME constantly surfs through the air, using Magnet Rise to keep itself elevated. In battle, it slams foes with its spiked tail, crippling them with a combination of lightning and poison.
author: evilgammon

entry: The jungle is a dangerous place with POKENAME around. It will lie flat on the ground, and stepping on its tail will result in a sting so painful that one will be in agony for three days straight.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME instinctively bullies Corsola by snapping off their branches. When Corsola starts to cry, POKENAME hesitates and leaves.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's shell plating is as strong as steel, able to shrug off powerful physical attacks with ease. Despite its armor, it is surprisingly agile, using impressive maneuvers to dominate its opponent.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME lives in large clusters with others of its kind deep under the ocean. Other Pokémon know not to approach these dangerous areas.
author: .realthree

entry: This bloated creature floats just under the surface, disguised as an abandoned research dome. Anything curious enough to approach is met with a dozen barbed limbs and a deafening shriek.
author: jaminmcready

entry: As POKENAME takes great pride in its appearance, it is often seen meticulously sharpening its spines on rocks. Flocks of POKENAME typically consist of four to five members.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lies still on coral reefs, posing as coral. When Corsola wander too close, it snaps shut its jaw, which is powerful enough to shatter steel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME skulks across the ocean floor, disguised as a harmless sea creature. This lets it easily sneak up on unsuspecting Corsola populations.
author: nellnast42

entry: A guardian of the deep that sleeps below the seafloor. Predatory in nature, it will lunge from the depths to grab and devour any it deems a threat.
author: theeggoverlord

entry: It waits patiently sheltered under its spiky dome. When Corsola swim by, the dome opens up, and POKENAME fires off a lethal toxic bullet.
author: nellnast42

entry: This Pokémon is very violent. POKENAME will wrap its venomous tendrils around its prey and never let it go. It will target nearly anything its large eyes lay sight on.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME do not build webs, as they prefer to hunt around coral reefs. It produces a paralyzing venom from its spines, powerful enough to immobilize a Corsola within 2 minutes.
author: mistymagius

entry: It lurks in hidden nooks, only emerging when Pokémon are stunned by its web's electrical charge. If prey manage to escape, POKENAME will stalk them and weave a second web in their path, coated with a deadly toxin.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: The bodies of POKENAME contain various toxins that burn with distinctive, neon flames. Prolonged exposure to the vapors produced by POKENAME is said to reduce one's lifespan.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME is known as a terror of the sea, with sailors swapping stories of its horrific brutality. Its long, grasping limbs rip sailors from their boats and pull them into its cavernous maw.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME toxins produce high amounts of heat when exposed to oxygen. They use this property to cook their prey prior to consumption, protecting their sensitive stomachs from bacteria.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME slumbers while wrapped in its spiky tendrils. If someone approaches it to abuse its power, it will unfurl its tendrils before striking them with a neurotoxin that will trap them in an illusion of their greatest fantasy.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its glowing red eyes can sense heat, which allows it to see through the darkest depths of the ocean. POKENAME prowls on the ocean floor hunting Corsola wherever possible.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME live in underwater caves, patiently waiting for its prey to swim by before ambushing them from above. Despite having an incredibly potent poison in its spines, POKENAME prefers to just bite its prey in half.
author: mistymagius

entry: Due to the toxins it secretes, POKENAME is an apex predator. If it merely scratches you, the toxins will lead to your demise in under a minute.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME is exceedingly brutal, ripping into foes with its teeth and launching venomous needles at attackers. The caudal fins allow POKENAME exceptional maneuverability, making it a popular Pokémon in aquatic competitions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME will hide in jungles to trap, poison, and then consume its prey. However, due to POKENAME's noticeable exotic colors, it's not very stealthy.
author: layspark

entry: When hunting, POKENAME wrap their stinger-laden wings around prey, injecting a weakening poison. They seem to prefer hunting smaller Pokémon, as the poison takes hold much quicker.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's barbs anchor deep into ship hulls as it drifts with the current. Sailors often mistake the damage for barnacle corrosion, ignoring it until it's too late.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME plagues beaches across every region, often washing up on shore and burrowing into the sand. Once settled, it is extremely difficult to remove due to its highly poisonous barbs.
author: evilgammon

entry: Greedy by nature, POKENAME stakes a claim over desert oases and forbids others from approaching. Those that try get pummeled by painful backhands from its long arms, with spikes that each contain highly potent toxins.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slowly cross the floor of cold seas in search of their favored prey, Corsola. After chasing Corsola into a set of Toxic Spikes, they stalk the weakening Pokémon until it is too weak to move.
author: chibitales

entry: Herds of POKENAME roam arctic seas, searching for prey to suit their large sizes. They work together to corner their prey by summoning walls of ice covered in Toxic Spikes. Their veils shimmer in bright colors depending on their mood.
author: chibitales

entry: Its lips have the ability to release a numbing agent that prevents prey from feeling the bite that is sure to follow. However, due to its cruelty, the cunning POKENAME rarely uses this ability.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The poison from the punch of a POKENAME contains compounds that cause paralysis. Efforts are being made to see if the compounds could be safely added to anesthetics.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME ambushes its target, using its grasping arms to pull its prey into its chest cavity. Once the victim is trapped, spikes extend from within, pricking and poisoning the unfortunate casualty.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is a brutally efficient predator. It stalks coral reefs, using its bright colours to blend in with the environment, and pounces with deadly accuracy upon its chosen target. POKENAME utilizes toxic poison to eliminate its foes and prey alike.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME's body faintly glimmers, mimicking the shine of a Heart Scale. If any divers are fooled by the disguise and approach, it will lash out with its venom-laced barbs.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is often seen hunkered down on beaches or floating in water, clutching its head in an attempt to relieve constant headaches. The poison in its spikes can cause similar pain in those it strikes.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's venom weakens a target's mental defenses. With a single psychic pulse, it floods the mind with vivid and terrifying hallucinations.
author: .izik

entry: Even a lone POKENAME can devastate a coral reef in days, tearing pieces from Corsola for food and trophies before letting them regenerate. Conservationists train Bruxish to drive them away from sensitive habitats.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are incredibly dangerous as the poison in their spines is potent enough to take out a whole Wailord. They mostly hunts large fish Pokémon, ripping them apart with their powerful claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: Documented as one of the most toxic ocean-faring Pokémon, entire beaches will have to be evacuated if even one POKENAME is spotted in the area.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME is extremely heavy and can only swim thanks to its incredibly powerful legs. It's feared by sailors due to stories of it grabbing boats with its grasping limbs and dragging them to the ocean floor.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is almost always seen hunkered down, with only its tail poking out. It uses this tail to snag small sea creatures on its venomous barbs, then draws them into its shelter to eat.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can extend its tongue to extreme lengths, using it like a hook to retrieve distant objects. It lowers the tongue into the water to fish, snagging prey with the poisonous barb at its apex.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME uses its armored spikes to smash through ice sheets above frozen seas. Once through, it hunts above the surface for sleeping prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very aggressive and if anything tries to disturb it, it will clamp down on them and inject them with a powerful neurotoxin. It will not let go until it either runs out of energy or is pried off by force.
author: mistymagius

entry: Exposure to sunlight causes POKENAME's skin to become hard and dry. During the night, POKENAME venture out from their caves and attempt to trick people into giving them food.
author: turron_turron

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it will extend out the tentacles on its head as an intimidation tactic. Its claws hide a bunch of toxic barbs which it uses to weaken and then tear apart its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is very picky about the leaves it eats. If another Pokémon attempts to eat a leaf it craves, it will fly high in the air and then deliver a devastating body slam.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME barrels into foes at high speeds. While it cannot rely on standard wrestling techniques, it can still knock and trick foes out of the ring.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME barrels into foes at high speeds. While it cannot rely on standard wrestling techniques, it can still knock and trick foes out of the ring.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The type of flavors POKENAME tastes before a fight influence its combat style: sweet for defensive, spicy for offensive, etc. Many POKENAME Trainers work tirelessly to find meals with the perfect flavor combo to create the perfect fighting style.
author: sk372

entry: Constantly full of energy, POKENAME release clouds of adrenaline that will motivate people to fight. The more dynamic the battle, the louder they cheer and the more smog they release.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its vines can shape and extend to some extent, giving it more range for strikes and grapples than a first glance would suggest. It will even shape its vines into taunting or victorious gestures to psych out opponents.
author: sk372

entry: It throws down lightning bolts in front of it before every battle. This is primarily meant for dramatic flair, as POKENAME prefers to use its physical prowess in battle over projectiles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is found primarily in areas with active volcanic activity. A favorite pastime (and method of showboating) for POKENAME is to leap from on high into a pool of lava, leaping out and shaking off the molten liquid, unharmed and unfazed.
author: sk372

entry: Its favourite activity is to watch boxing, martial arts and wrestling matches on TV. This way, it can transform into the human fighters and copy their combat style.
author: epping_forest

entry: Its favourite activity is to watch boxing, martial arts and wrestling matches on TV. This way, it can transform into the human fighters and copy their combat style.
author: epping_forest

entry: This Pokémon loves fighting and brings attention to itself with its bright feathers in order to initiate a battle. If defeated in a fight, POKENAME may become so ashamed of itself that it'll start losing its feathers out of stress.
author: milchik

entry: This Pokémon was created via genetic manipulation as the ultimate wrestler. It uses its powerful wings to attack from above, a move that almost always wins.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME often get into fights over nesting area in the wild. After a spirited round of combat, it's customary for the winner to pluck a few feathers from the loser to use as part of the nest it later builds.
author: sk372

entry: Constantly full of energy, POKENAME bounce as high as they can to try and practice flying. They often try to tackle each other from above, but only end up bouncing off each other and flying away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its sharp eyesight allows it to detect even the faintest twitch of movement from its opponent, giving it exceptional reaction speed to attacks. It uses its tiny frame to dodge attacks until the foe is too exhausted to avoid its counterstrikes.
author: sk372

entry: It shuffles and trots in place, rubbing its fur together to create a static charge that makes its tail shine brightly. This bright glow serves as the backdrop lighting for its dramatic moves in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are much more passionate about observing battles than participating in them. If many gather together to watch a fight, their supportive dances and cheers can even bolster the strength of the combatant being cheered for.
author: sk372

entry: It stands stock-still in battle, waiting for an opponent to make a move it can counter. When the chance arises, it devastates the attacking foe with dramatic jump strikes and stunning throws.
author: sk372

entry: It is known for its stunning displays of acrobatics. They often compete with other POKENAME to see which one can do the more impressive jumps and flips.
author: sivanandi

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight so that it may produce a bright shine like a spotlight on command. It does this to support allies in battle, providing dramatic lighting to give their performance added flair.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has slight precognitive capabilities, which it uses to its advantage in battle. The gem on its forehead shines briefly when it successfully counters a move it saw in advance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME challenges others of its kind to combat, with the loser forced to give up prized possessions to the winner. The fighting may be honorable, but the items fought for are often ill-gotten gains.
author: sk372

entry: Some say the head on its back half is its evil side. While a bit playful, it does seem that while POKENAME wants to fight honorably, its back end seems to encourage the use of dirty tactics.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon is known as a dirty fighter. It will blind its targets with dirt before neutralizing them with a debilitating grapple.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME tries to sneakily poach the belts away from others of its species. Direct fights are uncommon, as POKENAME considers a successful steal as a stronger example of its prowess.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its expert combat skills, POKENAME is actually quite cowardly. If it's locked in a fight, it thinks it can't win, it will bite its opponent with its powerful jaws and quickly fly off while they're distracted.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME love to make flashy and inefficient moves during a fight, more to impress a watching crowd than to quickly win. This tendency makes them popular with inexperienced Trainers who have yet to learn the best way to win a Pokémon battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME jumps like an acrobat around snowy landscapes, using its keen senses to locate buried prey. With a powerful stomp, it sends tremors through the snow, unearthing hidden food sources.
author: .izik

entry: It only shares the feathers it molts with those it deems to have an honorable spirit. People believe accessories made with POKENAME feathers grant the owner a boost to vitality.
author: sk372

entry: When readying itself for battle, POKENAME will blow a tune with its trunk, hyping itself up with a personal theme. It will compose additional themes for its allies when it observes their battles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been observed taking in stray Phanpy and tutoring them in its ways. In particular, it teaches them how to roll and unfurl from said roll with the maximum amount of dramatic flair.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is always itching for a good brawl to keep itself in shape. If no others seem in the mood to practice with it, it will use faint hypnotic powers from its antlers to stoke their fighting spirit and make them raring to fight.
author: sk372

entry: The battle prowess of POKENAME eclipses the fighting ability of their peers. Their flexible athleticism and theatrical fighting moves give them an edge in both strength and style.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appear in some historical records as a feathered, serpentine deity that struck awe and fear into many. None can escape their constrictive grasp, especially not after they deliver their poison with a single, deep bite.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's size and robust body make it a potent powerhouse in combat, good for any Trainer's team. However, most find themselves quickly put off by its victory celebration, where it sprays milk above the heads of it and its teammates.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leaps and glides around opponents, blasting them with lightning. It's very proud of its fighting skills.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME appears during festivals and parades, invigorating everyone with a lively spirit. Teenagers often go hunting for POKENAME to make their parties even more wild.
author: mistymagius

entry: The vines comprising its wings and back flutter in the wind, giving the illusion of a cape. This illusion lulls foes into forgetting they are just as prehensile as the rest of POKENAME, giving it an opportunistic advantage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are powerful fighters and natural showboats. They often sacrifice power and speed for flashy combos, aiming to impress onlookers real or imagined.
author: kingd8

entry: In combat, it moves with practiced and calculated grace and strength. Those who have observed POKENAME in battle are torn between describing its movement as fighting or dancing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a distaste for using its camouflage abilities unless absolutely necessary. Hunters that think it will be easy prey because it stands out will be taught otherwise when grappled and tossed aside by its prehensile tongue.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is remarkably strong for its size, capable of wrestling bigger foes. Its second head seems to act on its own and bodily slams into foes.
author: houndrys.

entry: With its scythe-like claws, POKENAME's savage blows are guaranteed to pack a critical punch. However, these attacks are very inaccurate.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME will compete in wrestling matches with one another, putting the food they have gathered on the line. The losers often care more about their bruised egos than going hungry.
author: cheroace

entry: POKENAME is protective of all the young Pokémon in its domain, considering itself their guardian. It makes sure they watch its fights, so it can extol virtues of strength and honor as well as teach them self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: Some naysayers believe POKENAME causes disasters just so it can look like a hero saving people from them. This is patently false; POKENAME simply believes it can help people and look cool while doing so, but rescue is always the first priority.
author: sk372

entry: If you see two Hawlucha fighting above POKENAME, you'll see its tail lift to strike the bell, signaling to the Hawlucha that it's time to wrestle.
author: creamy_art

entry: POKENAME love to wrestle with other Pokémon, especially when there is an audience. They harness the power of their flames to make their attacks look flashy but hold back to avoid hurting their opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These Pokémon are very agile. They can jump from high up when they notice a target. They love to battle using their shiny, sharpened blades. They can sometimes be seen gliding between trees.
author: salt

entry: POKENAME are proud fighters that will never strike their opponent's back, no matter what. Their signature move is a powerful suplex where they take their opponent into high skies before diving down swiftly to the earth with a dive bomb.
author: infinex21

entry: Often called "The King of the Ring," POKENAME is incredibly bombastic and lives for the spectacle of battle.  It only fights with opponents it knows will give it a challenge, as a fight that ends too fast is no fight at all.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fights in a dance-like state, expertly dodging and attacking without faltering. Its fluid movements and reaction time result in an elegant avoidance of attacks, making the opposing Pokémon seem like part of the dance.
author: slimmagma

entry: These Pokémon gather in valleys to train together and fight in mock battles, putting on a show of agility, speed, and strength.
author: cristata

entry: These Pokémon gather in valleys to train together and fight in mock battles, putting on a show of agility, speed, and strength.
author: cristata

entry: It searches for opponents while soaring across the lands. If a POKENAME sees something that looks stronger than it, it will attack mercilessly.
author: gurguro

entry: POKENAME's body glows faintly in the darkness, its flame flickering with every movement. It performs mesmerizing combat dances, slowly draining the energy of those who watch for too long.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its flame powers to force an opponent's movements in battle. It flings fireballs from its six tails to make them dodge and dip around until they're in the perfect spot for POKENAME to land a critical strike.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME consistently practices its battle techniques in order to add more flair to its movements. On occasion, it will steal trinkets from passersby, refusing to return the objects until they watch it show off its new moves.
author: sk372

entry: It is known for using fiery ribbons to add to its displays of acrobatics. Since they are not Fire type, however, reckless POKENAME often end up scorching themselves.
author: sivanandi

entry: The two heads on a POKENAME often fight with each other in a sibling rivalry but work together as needed. Their unpredictable attacks throw opponents off-guard. The head with darker colors shines more than the head with lighter colors.
author: entomoxie

entry: Whenever a Hawlous evolves into POKENAME, one of the heads takes full control of the body. The other head splits, turning into fierce arms that can attack on their own. The dominant head can control the arm heads as needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: Whenever a Hawlous evolves into POKENAME, one of the heads takes full control of the body. The other head splits, turning into fierce arms that can attack on their own. The dominant head can control the arm heads as needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: Whenever a Hawlous evolves into POKENAME, one of the heads takes full control of the body. The other head splits, turning into fierce arms that can attack on their own. The dominant head can control the arm heads as needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: It can jump over 50 times its body length thanks to its catapult-like back legs. It is an extremely capable grappler and can flip and throw Pokémon several times its size.
author: staghorn

entry: Leaders of their pack are identified with a trophy they wear, such as a Power Anklet. They spar each other for the right to wear the trophy, and stealing it is nearly impossible due to their reflexes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Always seeking attention, POKENAME inflate themselves before releasing triumphant battle cries to declare they're ready for a showdown. If anyone falls asleep during a POKENAME's performance, they will be met with a flurry of plush fists.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME ambushes prey by diving from above and pinning them in deep desert pits. Its powerful beak can crack through the hardest exoskeletons with a single strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cogs detach and reattach to perform intricate wrestling moves on an opponent. They move so fast that even a seasoned wrestling pro cannot keep up with its rapid techniques.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaps between tree branches, practicing martial arts techniques. After defeating a foe, it shoots flames into the air in celebration.
author: .izik

entry: Masters of spectacle, POKENAME inflate themselves to lift into the air before delivering devastating drop kicks to their opponents. They enjoy organizing battles almost as much as the battles themselves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When diving at prey, POKENAME cannot resist the urge to add aerial acrobatics such as twists and loops. Sometimes it gets so caught up in its flourishing performance that its prey escapes.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever they need an extra accessory to help them win Pokémon contests, they are given a Red Scarf to help them project a cool aura. Their daring personalities help them stand out, as they are willing to take calculated risks to amaze judges.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Young POKENAME develop their fighting and flying skills simultaneously. They perform a Flying Press from their nest, then fly as high as they can for another, until they're able to dive from the highest branch.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME rolls at high speeds to disorient its opponent before striking with a precise, venomous jab. Its rapid, unpredictable movements make it difficult to land a clean hit on it.
author: .izik

entry: It attacks with vicious speed and deceptive tactics. Some Trainers consider its tactics interesting to watch.
author: b_megamaths

entry: POKENAME's piercing cry is said to freeze opponents in their tracks, leaving them wide open for it to strike. It coats its entire body in solid ice before careening into an opponent with devastating force.
author: sk372

entry: Despite living in the most frigid of areas, POKENAME has a personality that can only be described as "fiery." It practices its moves by creating ice statues of other Pokémon to grapple and toss around.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME seeks out strong opponents and challenges them with its unique style of martial arts. Should it best its opponent, POKENAME will freeze them and take them back to its den as a trophy.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Most find POKENAME endearing for its strong sense of justice and friendship, and its eagerness to prove itself in battle. Because it practices its moves in garbage dumps, however, its friends must learn to endure its pungent stench.
author: sk372

entry: When two POKENAME meet on the field of battle, it's customary for both to engage in pre-combat song and dance rituals. Refusing to participate is considered a vicious snub towards the other's honor.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its soft, cloud-like wings to absorb incoming blows before countering with a powerful kick. Its graceful movements make it appear as if it's dancing mid-battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slimy body allows it to slip effortlessly out of an opponent's grasp. It coats its feathers in a sticky mucus before striking, making it difficult for foes to recover after a hit.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is usually the leader among groups of Hawlucha, flexing its powerful wings and bulging muscles with pride. It performs dramatic aerial moves, showing off its strength while still loving a flashy entrance.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME's large body bolsters its extra strength, letting its attacks pack even heavier blows than before. Its powerful muscles shrug off most attacks, allowing it to showboat extravagantly without worry of counterattack.
author: soup1900

entry: It grants water and safe travels to those lost within the desert sands, then disappears like a mirage. As those reporting it were exhausted survivors, POKENAME was thought to be a hallucination until recent times proved it to exist.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is large enough to engulf several fighters who enjoy an extra challenge. The fighting spirit inside a POKENAME is unmatched.
author: entomoxie

entry: It can create cold gusts of wind to chill and slow its opponents in battle. It also has the side effect of making POKENAME's wing-like flaps flutter in the wind, giving it a dramatic flair that it relishes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME usually hang around festivals out of sight from the human eye. Those who see one, though, are considered good luck.
author: mr.sans2010_67506

entry: When POKENAME fights, the feathers on its body puff up, making it look more intimidating. POKENAME is an extremely proud Pokémon; if it loses even a single battle, it may lose the will to fight for months.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME wears a slimy, sweet-smelling mask. Its cake-like aroma lures in prey, which it finishes with a devastating Flying Press.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs complex combat maneuvers with incredible agility to any who get close to its territory. It balances on all fours and bounces across rooftops like a trained gymnast.
author: .izik

entry: It seems generally unresponsive to outside stimuli, but if fierce battles take place in front of it, it can be observed shifting slightly with the faintest of lights flickering within its hollow eyes.
author: sk372

entry: Its eyes are alight with the fighting spirit burning from within. POKENAME charges into foes with full-bodied tackles from the air, impacting with force akin to a falling meteor.
author: sk372

entry: Expert tree climbers, POKENAME leap from tree to tree looking for strong opponents to fight. Its favorite move is to fly high above the treetops and then suplex its opponent into the ground.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are normally meek and passive. Any Pokémon that so much as touches one, though, will be hit by a bone-breaking suplex.
author: staghorn

entry: An amazing fighter, POKENAME traverses both sea and sky to whittle opponents down from all angles. It focuses its telekinetic powers with its yellow orbs to create a flashy display and toy with its foe before dealing a finishing blow.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has boundless energy, so prospective owners should be aware of how excessively it tends to act. Even a simple game of fetch will end up with parkour added so POKENAME can add flair and burn off more energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME prides itself as a master of hyping up the beginnings of a battle. As it chants sharp cries into its mic, everyone participating will be more fired up, eager to make a spectacle worthy of POKENAME's hype.
author: sk372

entry: With its massive intellect, it formulates dozens of counters for its opponent's moves. They say a POKENAME can calculate 1000 outcomes before the battle even begins.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has embraced a more acrobatic style of fighting, Dance. When it dances, it whips up blades of wind to hurt its opponents.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME likes to get up close and personal in battle, assailing foes with spinning jump kicks and karate chops from above. Because of its leaf arms and spindly root legs, these strikes aren't as effective as it would like.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME balances on its head vine before performing intricate acrobatics, using its flexible body to evade attacks. If cornered, it spits a blinding acid before flipping away to safety.
author: .izik

entry: Matches between POKENAME in the wild consist of pushing and shoving to see which fighter can push their opponent's heavy body out of bounds. POKENAME is known to have a strong rivalry with Hariyama.
author: sk372

entry: The poses it strikes in battle are controlled by the Shellder on its tail, biting on specific nerves to trigger a reflexive movement from POKENAME. In victory, the Shellder even makes POKENAME take a bow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically stay in the air with their light bodies and electromagnetism. They can use this electromagnetism to charge at their opponents at high speed, rarely missing.
author: entomoxie

entry: Its wings are tucked away and barely visible, too small to achieve flight.  Combined with POKENAME's running leaps, however, it can manage to glide for exceedingly long distances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in circuses and water parks, reveling in the joy of entertainment. Aquatic acrobats and acts of juggling are its forte.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME likes to haunt venues where nighttime Pokémon battling is common. It loves to interrupt fights with its sudden appearance, taking on both sides of the initial battle at once and turning the moment into a true spectacle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's small arms are deceptively strong, allowing it to grip onto rock walls with ease. It uses this to help it strike from ceilings and make more acrobatic maneuvers when fighting in its cavernous home.
author: sk372

entry: The seeds it carries scatter easily, taking root wherever they land. Other Pokémon often follow in its wake, hoping to benefit from the plants that quickly grow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wanders the desert systematically, protecting its territory. Mature POKENAME have flowers blossoming on the top of their head. The flesh of a POKENAME is as sweet as fruit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its limbs extend far beyond what seems possible, catching foes off guard. It uses this ability to surprise enemies from a distance before reeling itself back in.
author: .izik

entry: It dodges with expert precision, weaving between attacks like a seasoned fighter. Its movements are fluid, with each dodge leading seamlessly into a counterattack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue secretes a sticky sap that smells like cactus nectar. It uses this to coat its spines, trapping insects before consuming them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell has hardened so much that it limits its movements, so it uses its thin spines to ward off predators and other nuisances. It can survive for months without water thanks to the nutrients it stores within its cocoon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It buries its body in the sand and peaks its face out to absorb nutrients from the sun. Should it begin to rain, it will open its mouth wide to inhale any falling water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body soaks up water like a sponge and can endure days in the sun before returning to a water source. It hurls retractable spines at enemies while spinning at high speed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic powers to temporarily detach spikes from its body and fire them at opponents before causing them to float back to it again.
author: chorb33

entry: Found surrounding desert oases, POKENAME only move during arid rainstorms. Due to other Pokémon attempting to drain their water, they sharpen their quills daily to pierce hardened hides.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A POKENAME's body is highly effective at absorbing and retaining moisture within itself, so it is never seen drying out in the desert heat. If it comes across thirsty travelers, it shares some of the water within its body to rehydrate them.
author: sk372

entry: It uses clouds to mask its presence, hiding until the perfect moment to strike. With each movement, fine sand falls from its wings, camouflaging it further.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a fisherman's nightmare. When caught in a net, its thorns will likely tear the mesh, freeing everything caught with it.
author: antomelon

entry: With a surprising grace, it performs playful dances to attract companions. Its rhythmic movements leave soft trails in the sand, enchanting those who follow.
author: .izik

entry: When flash floods sweep through the desert, POKENAME rushes to leap into the flow. Trusting its buoyant tail to keep it at the surface, POKENAME greedily absorbs enough water to sustain itself through months of drought.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: If you see a wild POKENAME in the desert, you can be sure there's an oasis nearby. The bigger its flower, the more beautiful its oasis is sure to be.
author: cristata

entry: If you see a wild POKENAME in the desert, you can be sure there's an oasis nearby. The bigger its flower, the more beautiful its oasis is sure to be.
author: cristata

entry: It hovers just above the ground, drifting gently on passing breezes. This floating ability allows it to evade ground-based attacks with ease.
author: .izik

entry: To survive the harsh temperatures of the desert, POKENAME absorbs heat during the day. It releases the heat gradually as the desert temperature drops.
author: .izik

entry: It thrives in marshes, where its spines absorb moisture from the humid air. The damp environment keeps it active and ready to defend its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME survives in the desert where there is a paucity of food. It can be found eating bones of other Pokémon as the nutrient-rich bone marrow helps it stay strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its tough appearance, it is surprisingly wimpy in confrontations. It tends to bluff aggressively, hoping intimidation will prevent actual combat.
author: .izik

entry: Its body oozes a thick slime. It's typically too hot to safely touch, but cooled down samples of the slime can be used as lotion.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's body drips a moist sap, allowing it to slide along the ground. Drinking the sap, however, will cause digestive problems.
author: mistymagius

entry: It circles its prey multiple times before stunning it by throwing the cactus it carries. It can easily fly in even the worst sandstorms.
author: .izik

entry: A layer of frost covers its spines, chilling anything it touches. It uses this icy protection to fend off attackers and stay hidden in cold climates.
author: .izik

entry: Its body retains moisture despite living in dry environments, helping it survive harsh conditions. It camouflages itself among rock formations, waiting for prey to approach.
author: .izik

entry: They collect cacti and the flowers and fruits that grow on them. Drinking the cactus juice is said to be very quenching but can have unusual results.
author: pankiwi

entry: Known for acts of thievery, it sneaks into campsites to steal food and trinkets. Its quick reflexes make it difficult to catch in the act.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's skin is very absorbent, allowing it to survive on the little rain the desert provides. They can stretch up to 15 feet when striking their prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: It spins rapidly to deter predators, kicking up dust clouds as it whirls. This spinning technique also helps it gather food scattered across the desert ground.
author: .izik

entry: It moves swiftly by rolling across the landscape, flattening anything in its path. Its spiny exterior makes this rolling technique both an attack and a defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to give other Pokémon a surprise smooch. Since its mouth is rough and thorny, most Pokémon prefer to keep their distance from POKENAME.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live in deserts, surviving off of water stored in their body. They can swing their arms to electrify the water, however it is quite tiring.
author: currentlymuffin

entry: Some hikers have suffered nasty burns because they mistook the frightening POKENAME for a normal cactus and approached it without caution.
author: chorb33

entry: Multiple POKENAME come together at night to practice a sort of dance. It cries and retreats if caught off balance.
author: pokopish

entry: Despite their barbed outer layer, POKENAME are otherwise quite soft to the touch due to their expert ability to harvest and store water. They keep this fluid behind the sharp outer layer, making them shockingly squishy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tunnel beneath arid deserts to eat cactus roots and drink from underwater reservoirs. They rarely come to the surface because everything they need to survive is underground, so many POKENAME are startled by bright lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leaves that grow on POKENAME's back are nutritious and contain a lot of moisture within. It offers them to desert travelers to help keep them hydrated beneath the sweltering sun.
author: sk372

entry: It splashes in puddles, enjoying the cool water on hot days. Other Pokémon often join in, drawn to its carefree nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can survive indefinitely without water, drawing nutrients from magical sources instead. Though tiny, it is left alone due to its spines.
author: hellaluyeah

entry: In the vast emptiness of the desert, POKENAME has room to dance emotionally. If it spots someone watching, it will leave the voyeur with many pricks.
author: hellaluyeah

entry: POKENAME is a master of camouflage, using its spiky skin to blend into the desert landscape. It shifts through sunset colors to startle foes.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME eat Kebia Berries to reduce the risk of poisoning themselves after eating Poison-type Pokémon. In the harsh desert where food is scarce, being able to eat Poison-type Pokémon allows them to thrive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's flesh is saturated with clean, drinkable water. When a thirsty predator nears, it detaches the spheres on its back and makes its getaway.
author: staghorn

entry: Its body emits a faint magnetic field, which it uses to navigate through deserts. This ability allows it to find hidden minerals buried deep underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores water in its club-like structure. It shoots off its thorns in addition to bludgeoning its victims.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME defends itself by rotating at high speeds, shooting needles in all directions. This may even harm its Trainer, which is why many avoid it.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME and Aiking are eternal rivals. Typically described as cruel, it is ruthless, unstable, and shows no mercy.
author: jreposo

entry: POKENAME's petals have been noted to contain a chemical that gives them a spicy taste if bitten off in battle. The chemical appears to assist with expelling excess heat to avoid burning the more fragile cactus body.
author: ohok3441

entry: Its body secretes aloe-like sap, which soothes and hydrates its spines. This natural gel protects it from harsh sunlight, keeping it healthy in dry, arid environments.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon thrives in intense heat, absorbing sunlight to power its movements. It builds complex dams even in arid conditions, relying on its resilience to endure the blazing sun.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME trains by rapidly striking rocks with its spiked fists. The impact releases small bursts of energy, which helps it sense the emotions of nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dwell within oases, helping tend to the nature around them to help them stay lively and refreshing. Lost travelers often assume friendly POKENAME to be mirages until directly feeling their needles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME leaves small yellow fur with a sharp needle inside that can give an electric shock and a dose of poison. In arid places, POKENAME is often seen shaking with electricity when preparing to attack.
author: riverbandage

entry: Its fur can store a tremendous amount of static electricity, as well as concealing the sharp thorns that cover its head and back. It curls up into a ball when it sleeps, keeping its soft belly protected.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: The thorns on its body are extremely nutritious and taste similar to Yache Berries. Many chefs use these thorns to flavor their curries.
author: .izik

entry: Sunlight energizes it, allowing bursts of rapid movement through the desert. It glimmers under the sun, leaving mirage-like reflections as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: The air around it feels scorching, as it radiates heat even while standing still. When agitated, it can release bursts of intense fire, scorching the ground beneath it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaps into desert oases and soaks up large amounts of water, its body growing larger and more rotund as it does so.  It then carefully waddles away to spray and share the water with others who need hydration.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spines release a fine green powder that smells faintly of fresh herbs. This powder encourages plant growth in the arid environments where it lives.
author: .izik

entry: With incredible agility, it can jump great distances, easily evading threats. Pairs often practice leaping contests, developing both speed and coordination.
author: .izik

entry: A translucent membrane covers POKENAME's spiny body, keeping it hydrated even in extreme heat. If its fluid levels drop too low, its spines become brittle and break off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend lots of time getting nutrients from the sun, drinking with their mouth or planting their feet in soil. They headbutt spines in foes.
author: totodile.

entry: Screeching fills the air when it senses danger, warning others to keep their distance. It uses its voice both as a defense mechanism and a way to locate others in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: Disembodied whispers seem to follow wherever it goes, unsettling those nearby. These eerie sounds often lead travelers astray, as if urging them deeper into the desert.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly difficult to spot in the wild and will release jolts of electricity if stepped on. This fact makes it difficult to study, so most Trainers wear a set of heavy-duty boots to absorb the shock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon rolls in sand to sharpen its tiny spines, keeping them ready for defense. It glides smoothly across dunes, blending into the shifting landscape.
author: .izik

entry: It scatters embers with every flap, leaving tiny sparks in its wake. These glowing trails act as both warnings and lures, attracting curious Pokémon into traps.
author: .izik

entry: Its white fur is composed of thin but extremely sharp spines. The fire it produces is hot enough to melt desert sand into glass, which it uses to reinforce its spines.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME makes its home in greenhouses, camouflaging itself among potted plants. Under the cover of night, it quietly consumes the vegetation around it.
author: .izik

entry: A haunting wail echoes from deep within its body, unsettling those nearby. It moves slowly through forests, blending in with the shadows cast by ancient trees.
author: .izik

entry: The fruit on POKENAME's head isn't naturally poisonous, but POKENAME's sticky sap is. Because of this, the fruit needs to be thoroughly decontaminated before it can be eaten.
author: mistymagius

entry: The cactus head of POKENAME grows from the large bundle of dead bramble that makes up most of its body. It is unknown how it can fly, but scientists theorize that there may be clouds hidden inside the bramble.
author: soup1900

entry: Only growing in sandy areas heavy with metals, POKENAME are surprisingly dense and resilient. They are often revered as heralds of an ancient power.
author: quant9690

entry: POKENAME is often kept as a home defence system in warmer climates. It sits in a pot by its owner's front door and hugs any potential intruders with strong arms covered in spikes.
author: odditylad

entry: While absorbing sunlight with its thorns, it will hold the same pose for hours. Should it be disturbed, it will hop up in alarm and skitter away at great speeds.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient ruins are its preferred resting spots, where it camouflages among crumbled walls. It absorbs remnants of old structures to strengthen its defenses.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon wanders miles of desert looking for oases to absorb water and nutrients from. The round cactus on its back holds the water it needs to keep cool in the blistering heat.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's spiny body is covered in a tough, bark-like shell that hardens over time. It absorbs sunlight to fuel its rapid growth, sprouting small leaves along its arms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hollow body glows faintly at night, luring wandering travelers deeper into the desert. The eerie flicker is said to resemble a lost soul searching for home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travel across the desert holding water with their elastic pouches to make sure that their roots stay properly hydrated. If anyone tries to take a POKENAME's water, they will be met with a powerful headbutt laden with needles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME expands and absorbs rainwater during torrential downpours until it is full and replete. It slowly shrinks in size as it endures weeks or even months without water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rest in clusters under the hot desert sun. When it absorbs enough heat, it will grow a small yellow flower on its face.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soars high above dry deserts. Its preferred method of attack is dive bombing prey exhausted by the sun's heat.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are capable of rapidly absorbing water through their singular foot, which they balance on to keep themselves upright. This ensures that their bodies are well hydrated after a long drought.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon throws nuts with surprising accuracy, often aiming at unsuspecting targets. It takes delight in this playful mischief, though it quickly flees if confronted.
author: .izik

entry: Its temper flares when the heat becomes unbearable, making it dangerously aggressive. During hot days, other Pokémon keep their distance, knowing its mood worsens with rising temperatures.
author: .izik

entry: It is seen living in desert environments where the topsoil is no longer present. They mingle their roots underground so they can share nutrients and remain grounded.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The seeds POKENAME scatters from its mouth are highly fertile and can take root even in the driest desert sands. Many cacti fields owe their existence to the wandering travels of this Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: These mischievous Pokémon are known for swinging their club-like appendages to break objects in play. Though chaotic alone, when grouped they show remarkable coordination and act as one seamless unit.
author: big_clanker

entry: Topaz shards embedded in its body gleam under sunlight, giving it a dazzling appearance. These gemstones are known to attract treasure hunters, often leading to conflict.
author: .izik

entry: Often appearing tired, it moves slowly even in the hottest sun. Its sluggish nature belies the power hidden within its thorny body.
author: .izik

entry: Its magnetic field is unusually strong, allowing it to pull in small objects from a distance. It uses this ability to collect metal scraps, which it stores for unknown purposes.
author: .izik

entry: Small pins cover its body, which it uses for defense and gathering food. When agitated, it flails wildly, sending these pins flying in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: It thrives near hidden oases, where it stores water for dry spells. Other desert creatures often follow it, hoping to discover these life-saving havens.
author: .izik

entry: It collects discarded soda cans, hoarding them inside its hollow slimy body. The rattling sounds it makes often confuse opponents, giving it time to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a desert spirit that only comes out in the late evenings. If several congregate together, they can conjure up an illusion of a watery oasis to trick travelers.
author: sk372

entry: It wanders through the desert, searching for an opponent. It's a formidable fistfighter, and its hands are studded with painful spikes.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME float by drawing dew into their bodies as water vapor and heating it. If threatened, they expel all of the steam at once, shooting spines in every direction.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a regular cactus by desert-dwelling Pokémon. If disturbed, it relentlessly blasts the aggressor with a powerful water blast. Despite this, it remains near the bottom of the food chain.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME roams through deserts singing. It shakes its thorny body rhythmically to add rattling noises to its rapid singing.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are crucial to the desert ecosystem as they provide other Pokémon with the nutritious water they produce. Few are left in the wild because of hunting by humans trying to sell the exotic drink.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME needs to absorb water often to maintain its liquid-like consistency. It looks for sources like ponds and other Pokémon to drain water from.
author: 8xviktor

entry: The fire on its back is the condensed energy it absorbs from the sun. The POKENAME with the brightest flame is the alpha of the pack.
author: gurguro

entry: It performs graceful, ballet-like movements, mesmerizing onlookers with elegant spins. Each step releases a soft aroma, making it as captivating as it is dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Rumors say that if you spot a wild POKENAME during the night, you'll start seeing strange visions. However, this Pokémon is friendly during the day.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME have adapted to live in deserts, and now live in large burrows instead of trees.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is a weak Pokémon that stays still to conserve nutrients and moisture. It waits for strong winds to carry it to desert towns, where it relies on helpful citizens to care for it until evolution.
author: mepp.

entry: In desert communities long ago, Trainers kept POKENAME as guards. They would spew thorns from their gills as strangers approached, the colour of these thorns would indicate if the strangers were welcome.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME spends the day meditating, awakening at night to patrol its desert home. With its incredible intellect, it skillfully commands Remoraid to aid it in disciplining unruly Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: Its movements induce dizziness in foes, leaving them disoriented and vulnerable. The unique rhythm of its steps confuses even the most experienced opponents.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME is always looking for bigger cacti to use as segments for its body. Members of the species often fight over large cacti.
author: gurguro

entry: It succumbs to sudden bursts of rage, attacking anything in its path. Despite its anger, it can be calmed with careful handling.
author: .izik
