entry: POKENAME cannot see the details of objects very well, but its eyes are extremely sensitive to any motion. As a result, it can even see a newborn Joltik slowly inch throughout a field of corn.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered in dense, prickly fur. At night, it propels itself with poisonous gas.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME stores spare food within the recesses of its fuzzy back. Sometimes it offers to share with friends, seeming confused when they refuse to partake in the fuzz-covered snacks.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its hulking size, POKENAME is a rather timid creature, hiding away deep in forests and caves and refusing to come out unless it sufficiently trusts someone. It seems afraid of potentially hurting someone due to its size.
author: sk372

entry: As it burrows, POKENAME sheds colored poison dust that marks its tunnels. The powder's microscopic patterns are unique to each individual.
author: .izik

entry: In a Pokémon battle, POKENAME rely on their compound eyes to pinpoint weak spots on their opponent. Once they find a suitable target, they release a flurry of leaves that overwhelm their opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in boreal forests where there is plenty of snow to play in. When threatened, they release a chilling frost from their compound eyes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's furry coat lets it survive in cold environments. This was a rare Pokémon during the Ice Age, as most Bug types died out from the cold.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are quite timid, quickly climbing up into the trees at the slightest sense of danger. The hairs are both toxic and hard to get rid of, causing immense displeasure in those who try to eat them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in countless fine furs, making it very soft and fuzzy. It loves to give embraces to others, which are pleasant but leave the hugged person feeling slightly itchy afterward.
author: sk372

entry: Concealed within POKENAME's coat are venomous barbs. A single prick can induce fatigue and sluggishness in most predators.
author: .izik

entry: It can change the color of all of its body except for its eyes. It hides away from sight, using its powerful eyes to scope out the faint movement of small insects, before its tongue lashes out at lightning speed to catch and eat them.
author: sk372

entry: Despite formidable strength and speed, POKENAME is jumpy and prone to panicking. When startled in the wild, it's not unheard of for it to cut a tree down in a single swing, just to cover its rapid escape.
author: sk372

entry: Venomoth appear drawn to the pollen stored in POKENAME's flower. POKENAME detests the unwelcome visitors, to the point of attacking Venomoth on sight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sheds its poisonous fur on a daily basis, which keeps predators away from its den. Its antennae are very sensitive to loud noises, so it lives in more remote areas.
author: mistymagius

entry: It always acts distant, even in battle. Some theorize that the cause of this may be the fact that each lens of its compound eyes is staring at something happening in a different universe, leaving only one lens for what's happening here.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME live in polluted areas, feeding on leftover scraps and garbage. They will sometimes team up with each other to steal larger meals from suburban homes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its sheath looks just like a hairy bug, so bird Pokémon often peck at it fruitlessly. By the time they realize their mistake, it is too late - POKENAME has already begun draining their life force.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: A foul-smelling poison seeps from the fur on POKENAME's horn. It rarely uses the horn itself, relying on intimidation to avoid battle.
author: .izik

entry: The fur covering POKENAME's entire body is coated with toxic dust, poisoning anyone who dares to attack it. When it accumulates electricity in its body, its antennae glow with an intense yellow light.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Their eyes act as radars, scanning for small bugs and prey to to eat. Their ribbons allow them to dig up grubs.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME floats near illuminated cottages, waiting for residents to lower their guard. Its sensitive antennae can detect emotional states.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sheds a faint powder while walking, which thickens under moonlight. The powder's color shifts with each lunar phase, baffling researchers.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its compound eyes to see in the dark while dispensing sticky webs to trap prey. These webs carry an electrical charge, stunning anything that struggles too much.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the shadows, with insects and Bug-type Pokémon. It throws off its disguise and unveils its horrendous form to eat its prey whole.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It prefers dark areas, and its fur is covered in a purple powder that scatters as it moves. Despite its poor eyesight, it uses its fine hairs to sense nearby prey.
author: .izik

entry: Said to release an unknown poison that can instantly prove fatal, POKENAME is an extremely fast Pokémon. Its species was only recently documented by bug experts.
author: riel.vndxgrxvnd

entry: Swarms of POKENAME gather near rotting berry trees, eating all the scraps they can. When threatened, they will loudly vibrate their wings, creating a painful cacophony of buzzing.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hairs on POKENAME's body are incredibly sensitive, allowing it to sense the emotions of other Pokémon. However, the hairs are coated with small amounts of poison that cause strange psychological effects.
author: mistymagius

entry: The poisonous dust in POKENAME's fur is constantly irritating it, causing it to rampage all over the place. The dust has been commercially harvested as a powerful stimulant, but only in minuscule doses.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fur is made of fine metallic strands. The powder it stores within can cause mild burns upon contact with skin.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME is amongst abundant plant-life, it will open its bud and release special pollen. It doesn't realize that its pollen is toxic, however.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME is filled with a poisonous gas that is heavier than air. Unlike Drifloon, it struggles to kidnap children because it can barely keep itself afloat.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Floating gently, POKENAME swings its antenna like a pendulum. It channels psychic blasts through it with eerie precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often inhabits abandoned buildings, as it loves to feed on the dust that builds up there. Coming into contact with its poisonous fur will cause severe rashes that last up to 5 months.
author: mistymagius

entry: Possessing powerful eyesight and echolocation, POKENAME makes it nearly impossible to hide or evade it when it's on the hunt. Fortunately for most, it only tends to hunt small insects.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME moves, its fur crackles with faint static. It releases electrical pulses through its antennae when excited or alarmed.
author: .izik

entry: Its eyes blink a vibrant red light while it senses for predators. Its body is made up of tiny metal shards. Any attacker that bites it will end up with a mouthful of jagged steel dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME claws at trees with its sharp tusks before releasing acidic powder from its fur. The powder quickly dissolves the weakened trunk.
author: .izik

entry: As it flutters through the night, it shakes loose poisonous powder from its fur. The toxin lingers in the air, making it difficult for predators to follow.
author: .izik

entry: Laying traps at night, POKENAME lurk on forest floors waiting for unsuspecting victims to walk over them. When stepped on, their stiff hairs latch onto the target, releasing a weakening poison.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can curl up and roll away, reaching surprising speeds. Their fluffy fur cushions collisions like an airbag so that it does not injure itself.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can spin like a tire when stationary and then race off at high speed. Its fur protects it in the case of collisions.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can spin like a tire when stationary and then race off at high speed. Its fur protects it in the case of collisions.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can climb any slope, no matter how steep. If it is attacked by a flying Pokémon, it can drop down and cushion the fall with its thick fur.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME covers its body in its poisonous pollen, dissuading any other Pokémon from eating it. It loves damp weather and groups of them will gather together before rainstorms.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has no feathers but thick fur instead. It dances joyfully, yet its rapid spinning tangles the fur into hopeless knots that only a few expert groomers can untangle.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When cheering, POKENAME's antennae bob wildly and often tangle. Its pom-poms are bound with a sticky, toxic secretion harmful to humans and Pokémon.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's fur is coated in a mucus that induces sleep when smelled. As it dances, it leaves a slimy trail surrounded by dozing humans and Pokémon.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Though it looks like it has wings, POKENAME's flaps are just excess fur shaped to mimic feathers. It dyes the tips red with its own poisonous saliva.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Light filters through the ethereal body of POKENAME, making it very hard to see as it hides among the trees. This camouflage is its only defense mechanism, leaving it quite helpless when spotted.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: POKENAME hide their bodies and wait for prey to brush by their leaves, which are covered in a sticky, cloying toxin. Then, they pop out and bite.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME are generally quite docile, preferring to play in the dirt and jumping about carefree. They like to eat different kinds of dirt.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME gathers in small groups living among the roots of large trees. The mushrooms on its back, if properly prepared, can be used in a concoction that helps improve eyesight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a danger if left unchecked, as both the pollen it spreads and the mushrooms grown from its spores can cause lengthy bouts of blindness in those who come in contact with them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scuttles along seabeds, using its large radar-like eyes to scavenge for food. The stiff hairs covering its body offer it protection from underwater predators like Mareanie.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME is a very persistent pest. It can feed on most plants, resort to eating wood, and even hunt small Grass-type Pokémon. When it finds a tasty meal, it emits a pheromone cloud to call its peers.
author: lucioleuh

entry: There's no evidence its body is made of anything except stiff hairs. Even x-rays can't penetrate the dense fur.
author: pokepower

entry: The smoke billowing out of POKENAME's body contains a pheromone highly attractive to Venonat. It's very common to see small groups of them swarming and playing amongst POKENAME's clouds.
author: sk372

entry: A fusion of two Venonat causes the DNA of POKENAME to develop rapidly and begin expressing traits of their evolved form. Their over-developed bodies require a greater amount of food and trainers are advised to bring extra rations on journeys.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a common house-pest in rural areas, drawn to outdoor lamps and lanterns. Its scales are highly toxic, so it's recommended to call a professional if one is spotted.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eyes flash crimson when its territory is breached. It then scatters a fine acidic powder to repel the intruder.
author: .izik

entry: When flying through the air at high speeds, POKENAME sheds excess fur from its body. This fuzz burns up quickly, creating a colorful trail of sparks behind its flight paths, akin to a comet's tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps near the surface with its antennae exposed to sense danger. When threatened, it releases thick clouds of paralyzing dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a spicy powder prized in many burrito dishes. People often harvest it from abandoned tunnels, though exposure can cause irritation.
author: .izik

entry: It can fire off unusual moves from the speckled, red jewel on its forehead. Its fuzzy body quickly picks up dust, spores, seeds, and dirt, so it spends most of the day trying to clean itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's fur is coated in a poisonous dust that can be dangerous if inhaled. However, due to the toxins constantly flowing into its brain, POKENAME suffers from constant migraines.
author: mistymagius

entry: If something flees from an angry POKENAME, it will find it difficult to truly escape; its vision is highly acute, and its stubborn personality means it rarely gives up a chase, even after hours.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is most active in the evenings, using its dimly glowing tail as a lure. It feasts on bugs attracted by this light.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lives in the damp marsh, feeding on soaked leaves and roots. Its fur is covered in a toxic oil that causes skin irritation on contact.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's spiral spins rapidly as its eyes glow bright pink. This hypnotic combination can lull foes into sudden sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can detect the slightest change of the wind with their sensitive fur. If they suspect a Trainer is nearby, they teleport away before they are spotted.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roots itself near nettles and consumes their thorns as a food source. If disturbed, it retaliates with a sudden Psybeam.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are covered in sensitive fuzz used to detect movement. The fuzz is not waterproof, so when swimming, they tuck everything but their limbs into their shells.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME ambushes its prey by dropping from high tree branches and draining their fluids with their hollow fangs. However, it takes them almost a full day to climb back into the trees.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a pernicious acid inside its bell that slowly digests bug Pokémon. Whenever one falls in, it releases spores to lull the prey to sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A faint scent emitted by POKENAME's hairs induces drowsiness and contentment in those who smell it. Many enjoy using it as a pillow to nap on, which POKENAME doesn't mind at all.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their antenna to feed on the energy of radio waves present in the air. As a result, POKENAME can often be found emitting radio broadcasts from their bodies, and have become a staple amongst campers.
author: turron_turron

entry: It flaps its wings before releasing a Psybeam from its compound eyes. The sudden gust of wind it creates can spread its sleep-inducing powder across an entire field.
author: .izik

entry: It stands on the top of hills and shakes its body, letting loose a blue powder. This powder can stun others in the area with the smallest sniff.
author: .izik

entry: If it sees someone it loves with its compound eyes, it will flail its arms wildly in happiness, splashing inky slime everywhere. This affectionate display has ruined many Trainers' clothes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body composition is a strange mixture of fuzzy and sludgy. Should some part of a person come in contact with its residue, that spot will remain itchy for days, even after removing the goop.
author: sk372

entry: It uses Sleep Powder to put prey to sleep before feasting on their dreams. Its antennae twitch when it detects a particularly vivid nightmare.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reflects a pattern of light bursts off of its pendulum, which induces different types of dreams. Its fur is incredibly soft and smells slightly of lavender, leading to the belief that pillows using its fur will lead to sweet dreams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME rubs the bulb on its back against stones and trees to strengthen the shell, shaving off weakening sections. The red spikes on its nose, ears, and bulb secrete the poison gestating within the bulb.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are used in therapy, as they absorb emotions and release them as a gas that a therapist can experience. Their tough shell protects them from harm, so even overwhelming anger is carried calmly, making them reliable partners in emotional care.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The leaves that grow from POKENAME's arms are actually incredibly dense and sharp. They function as dangerous weapons, especially when detached and thrown.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME tend to be very easygoing. They calmly carry out any Trainer's command without hesitation. However, POKENAME will even listen to the orders given by people who aren't their Trainers.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's great weight makes it ideal for running into trees to dislodge ripe fruits. It shares these with Pokémon that bring its favorite food, a berry that grows on thorny bushes and requires more dexterity to pick than it has.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's body is covered with sturdy plant materials to protect it from any attack. POKENAME takes great care maintaining its territory, which includes periodically planting new trees.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME battles by smacking opponents with its mace, which it will ignite if it believes the battle will be challenging. It takes special care in growing the spiked nut that it uses for the mace, protecting trees that produce them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME collects scattered foliage and sticks it to itself using adhesive saliva. It then rests in canopies, blending into the scenery. They are largely kind and non-confrontational in nature.
author: prolucario_

entry: POKENAME train their strength by catching charging Quilladin with their arms. Rumors say that the wails of spirits can be heard whenever it deflects an attack with its body.
author: soup1900

entry: The glowing end of POKENAME's tail is always red-hot. It uses it to burn marks into trees to denote its territory.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has a very short temper, even the sounds of falling leaves send it into fury. It increases its level of violence extremely quickly, jumping from frolicking in flowers to using Mega Punch on boulders.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME never starts a fight out of anger. It spars in friendly matches with other Fighting-type Pokémon to nurture their natural talents.
author: ozydamians

entry: Although it lives independently, a wild POKENAME happily reunites with its family every spring; the group will celebrate and compare one another's strength. The fluffy orange fur on its head and tail has a festive nutty aroma.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME charges into trees, knocking them down to create walls around its nest. While the nut on its back contains a poison too dangerous for human consumption, the shell is delicious and nontoxic.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It takes smaller Pokémon under its protection and rules over them fairly as the leader of the pack. POKENAME prefers to solve conflicts peacefully, but if its packmates are in danger, it'll fight fiercely and defend them at all costs.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's elevated shell protects the tree nuts underneath from bird Pokémon, especially since the shell now produces a poison that can be transmitted by its spikes. It lies in sunlight to strengthen the defensive prowess of its shell.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is quite protective of others, shielding them from harm with its body. Despite its small stature, its body is incredibly durable; a charging Steelix would be stopped dead in its tracks if it collided with POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: Covered in a thick armoured hide, POKENAME move about their grassland homes with little fear of attack. When threatened by something powerful enough to pose a danger, they will band together and present a spiky shield-wall with their bodies.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME defend their Trainer from harm with their shield and lance. Their prickly personality slowly melts into affection as they bond with their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the elevation of its protective shell with specialized muscles of the treetrunk-like growth on its back. This protects or exposes the branches that grow tree nuts, which are widely used as snacks and as salad toppings.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME takes advantage of aggressive opponents by letting them attack its diamond-hard body while it takes a defensive posture. Once the foe has tired itself out, POKENAME finishes them off with a powerful tackle without having taken any damage.
author: soup1900

entry: The chestnut at the end of POKENAME's tail combusts if touched. Because of that, POKENAME wards off threats by striking its foes with the unnatural nut. The large spikes on its back work in the same way.
author: .realthree

entry: It was once said by a philosopher that a Trainer who grows old with POKENAME at their side will lead a long and fulfilling life. It is deeply loyal and highly affectionate.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME shed the armor from their bodies in favor of fashioning it into a weapon to use directly in battle. Despite the bulk of their new mace, POKENAME are dexterous and calculating, always landing precise blows.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's shell is impenetrable even against the most intense forces. It can use its power over roots to anchor itself and become immovable, even in soft sand. For offense, it rams into root-bound opponents with its spiked shell.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME attacks using vine-like sticks that sprout from its back. If these touch its hot ears, they may accidentally burst into flames.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME often flies among tree branches in search of spicy berries that can strengthen its still-weak flames. The fur growing from its ears is so soft and fluffy that other Pokémon try to steal it to build their nests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's fur constantly smolders, leaving faint scorch marks wherever it walks. It is fiercely territorial and has been seen drawing glowing patterns in the dirt to warn intruders away.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It is a high-maintenance creature because it needs to be sheared daily. Its wool was originally used in the process of creating a Fluffy Tail, but nowadays it is spun into yarn for elderly people.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its fleece is considered to be some of the warmest material in the world, however sweaters made from it give wearers a nasty static shock. After a few hospitalizations from these occurrences, POKENAME fleece was recalled from international markets.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME attacks using vine-like sticks that sprout from its back. If these touch its hot ears, they may accidentally burst into flames.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight and eats twigs to nourish the bulb on its back. When overheated, the bulb vents air exceeding 390 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME burrows deep underground, melting any boulders in its path with intense flames. Some tunnels left in its wake remain superheated for hours.
author: .izik

entry: The yellow, mud-like substance coating POKENAME's body can reach temperatures comparable to molten lava. Without meaning to, it frequently starts wildfires, forcing it to live in desolate areas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME balances on its tail to help it reach the higher twigs that it likes to snack on. It sometimes gets brief visions of the future that cause it distress.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its sensitive ears to feel people's emotions. It is known to eat twigs to power up its teleportation if threatened.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's nose glows red-hot just before it unleashes a powerful fire-based attack. The accumulated heat lets it sense changes in the air, allowing it to react quickly to threats.
author: .izik

entry: When it vents heat from its body, its altitude lowers. As a result, when it spits Fire-type moves from its mouth, POKENAME will start sinking to the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Many Trainers attempt pursuing POKENAME through the woods, but they rarely catch up to it. It is theorized that a POKENAME can memorize the location of as many as 300 different hiding places.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME dedicates hours to honing its strength and speed every day. When it strikes, its punches are so fast that its fists catch fire.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: When in danger, its muscles function to create tremendous amounts of electrothermic energy. The puffs of embers from its ears may momentarily blind foes.
author: anemonics

entry: It rests in one of the burrows sprawling through the desert, hopping between abandoned desert homes daily. Nomads travel alongside it as part of a mythological tradition, though of what origin and purpose has been lost to time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds on twigs, fallen leaves and other decaying plant matter. When threatened, it spouts a flurry of Embers as it attempts to escape.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME's fangs can heat up beyond the temperature of a commercial furnace. It leaves glowing bite marks on its prey, which continue to smolder long after the attack.
author: .izik

entry: After spotting its prey, POKENAME unleashes a blood-curdling roar before lunging in to bite with its molten-hot fangs. Its scorching bite is said to be strong enough to melt iron.
author: .izik

entry: Spinning in fiery circles, POKENAME performs an intricate dance that mesmerizes those who watch. As it moves, embers flare from its feathered body, creating dazzling displays.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are usually solitary, desert-dwelling Pokémon that feed on Bug-type Pokémon and other small prey, but from time to time, they form large groups, allowing them to hunt larger, meatier species.
author: .realthree

entry: The more dry twigs POKENAME eats, the thicker the smoke that billows from its shell. Its breath smells faintly of charred wood.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launch themselves from the ground to snap twigs off of trees. Bigger, nutrient-rich branches help their bodies burn brighter and for longer.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The fluffy tip of POKENAME's tail is the center of its heat production. If it loses the fur there, it has a hard time staying warm enough.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is in a constant state of overheating, leaving the Pokémon in a semi-conscious state. Its ears and mane give off enough heat to start forest fires.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's ears bounce as it dashes, scattering tiny embers with every step. Its fiery fluff burns hotter the faster it runs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can unleash flames from each of its three heads, reaching temperatures high enough to melt tungsten. When enraged, its combined fiery breath creates a searing whirlwind around it.
author: .izik

entry: The stick on POKENAME's back is a living part of its body. It stretches it like a vine and sets it ablaze to deter predators.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are known to wander aimlessly and cast spells without care for the consequences. This often results in forest fires.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME eat rodent Pokémon and rely on a clever ploy to coax them out of burrows. They shove sticks into burrows and set them on fire. As the fire burns, the burrow residents are drawn out to where POKENAME are waiting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Vine-like sticks grow from the bulb on its back and are used in battle. The more sunlight it absorbs, the hotter their flames burn.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME crackles with static as it sleeps, charging the branch in its tail. When the branch is drawn from its tail, static builds up and sets the tip ablaze.
author: gekkou.

entry: POKENAME's telekinetic abilities allow them to create a friction from the air to light up their twig. They use it in combat as a catalyst for their abilities.
author: sylia

entry: Only twigs plucked from thorny bushes are suitable conduits for its elemental energy. Be careful when you play fetch with POKENAME, it returns what you throw aflame and covered in poisonous saliva.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME can release spores from its tail that ignite at a moment's notice. Like a conductor, it directs these flames using the stick held in its mouth.
author: busilisk

entry: POKENAME can be seen performing with street magicians to amaze audiences. They take breaks on nights of the full moon to bask in the moonlight and recharge their magical powers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's flaming wings trace cryptic patterns in the air, weaving hypnotic embers that lure spirits to its ghostly dance. Mocking its ritual ignites vengeful flames, which cling to offenders as ceaseless, haunting reminders of their disrespect.
author: vhscopyofmeangirls

entry: POKENAME carry a flaming stick with them wherever they go to illuminate the area around them. When confronted with a dangerous Pokémon, they can shoot flaming razor-sharp leaves to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fires they stoke sparkle like stars. At night, they lob magnificent fireballs into the sky to communicate with allies. Meteorologists often mistake these fireballs for meteorites when they rain back down.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME has a hard time pulling its stick out of its tail. Luckily, it can still ignite the wood without removing it by striking it against a rough surface, just as a matchstick.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME shows its caring nature towards any wild Pokémon in need, providing them with shelter and healing their wounds with its psychic powers. It dislikes humans though, and will turn any Trainer who disturbs its peace into a Tepig or Spoink.
author: milchik

entry: Traveling between volcanoes, POKENAME appears within a rising spiral of flame. It commands all flames around it, shining in vibrant hues of orange and gold as it glides along the wind.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME live near volcanic mountains where they love the scent of ash. They often start wildfires if there is too much greenery on their mountains.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon is commonly portrayed as a companion to witches and wizards alike in many fictional stories, be they good or evil. There are theories, though, that claim POKENAME once were humans that either became Pokémon by choice or by curse.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends days using its tusks to meditatively carve a log, with the carvings glowing like embers. While it can use the log like a magic staff to augment its spell-like attacks, it tends to just wallop opponents with the log.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Martial artists actively seek out POKENAME to learn the way of the burning branch, a style of armed combat focusing on foreseeing opponents' moves. When not training, these Pokémon can be found in deep meditation.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME uses their divination abilities to protect their Trainer at all costs including their own life. As a last resort, they creates a fireball that sucks in the threat.
author: sylia

entry: POKENAME gathers up sticks to set alight and gaze into the flames. Within the fire it glimpses potential future disasters, allowing it to work towards preventing the catastrophes from taking place.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sing gleeful melodies as they propel themselves through the sky with dazzling displays of fire. They are curious and creative by nature, collecting plants along their travels to brew new medicines and beverages.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When winter strikes in Lumiose City, POKENAME are lured into the streets. Each of their tails radiates over one hundred degrees of heat, allowing pedestrians to stroll comfortably.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME have doting fans that extol and sing praises for its music. The fiery dances it performs mesmerizes and amazes its loyal fans, who love both music and pyrotechnics.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME overflows with enchanted light, with each color of light giving a different effect to those hit by it. When this light is used on its fiery vortexes, they become a catalyst, spreading the magical powers even more.
author: soup1900

entry: Due to its fuzzy sleeves, POKENAME has difficulty bringing its claws to bear. Instead, it attacks by lighting a branch on its magma-hot fur. When alone, it cleans mud from its hair to keep its bright coloration.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME form from bewitched plants in the autumnal harvest. They become very possessive of the inanimate plants that were around them when they form and will try to scare off farmers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME's flames can burn as brightly as a star. For reasons yet to be explained, they tend to frantically wave their stick around only hours before intense meteor showers are predicted.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The mesmerizing flame at the end of POKENAME's tail draws onlookers in. Though those who have stared at it claim that they were on the verge of receiving a vision, nobody has ever reached such a point due to being attacked by the Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: Legends claim that POKENAME was born from the flames and ore nestled deep inside the world's volcanoes. Those who peer into its incandescent flames are said to witness revelations of their futures.
author: mepp.

entry: The branches growing from POKENAME thrive in extremely hot and arid climates, turning absorbed heat into blazing fire. If the wood experiences too much moisture, it can rot and fall off, hindering a POKENAME's ability to survive.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's are especially good at ranged combat. They take to the skies and imbue fire with psychic energy to create potent fireball projectiles that cause small bursts of fire on impact.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: When POKENAME gazes into the flame at the end of its wand, its brain cells and IQ multiply. If POKENAME concentrates long enough, it will become smart enough to determine the course of the future.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME gather in groups to develop unique ninjutsu techniques. They primarily focus on using the poisonous bubbles on their back to stun and paralyse foes.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are deceptively difficult to battle or catch, since when they are threatened they produce bubbles that appear to make their body longer. When these sections are disturbed in any way, they simply dissolve, leaving POKENAME unharmed entirely.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Don't let its cute expression fool you. This aquatic menace camouflages itself with springy bubbles that lessen the force of attacks. POKENAME's penchant for ambushes makes it especially dangerous in water.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME lies lazily in rivers, sometimes spitting water at leaves to test its own accuracy. The furthest shot recorded by researchers was 400 ft, showcasing its impressive control and skill with water.
author: .izik

entry: The foamy growth on its back expands when it is happy, releasing a fresh scent that soothes nearby Pokémon. Divers often use POKENAME to find calm waters and avoid dangerous currents.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's bubbles have a special ability to block radio waves. It sometimes encases itself with these bubbles to block unwanted transmissions from local networks.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME considers itself the protector of ponds in its forest homes, defending others who would intrude upon them. Though its strength is lacking, none can doubt its staunch conviction.
author: sk372

entry: The skin on POKENAME's abdomen is especially thin, making it useful for absorbing moisture from the ground on dry days. To protect its abdomen, it secretes a coat of bubbles to cover it.
author: hophoppip

entry: It spews out protective bubbles whenever it believes it is in danger. When a Trainer refuses to listen to its desires, it shoots a burst of bubbles to demonstrate its frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in underwater caves during the evening. If threatened by predators like Huntail, it releases torrents of foam to obscure its escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME constructs a Froakie disguise to capitalize on the Pokémon's popularity beyond even frog enthusiasts. Its aptitude for jumping is limited due to its small legs, but it can use its claw to propel itself into the air to mimic its disguise.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It generates bubbles from a small spout on its head to help keep its skin moisturized while on land. POKENAME enjoys playing with others by spraying them with these foamy bubbles.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it surrounds itself in a mass of bubbles. These bubbles are charged with electricity, but touching them only causes a minor static shock.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME secretes bubbles from its thick skin and uses psychic powers to launch them at the opponent. The bubbles don't do much harm, however.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME hates drying out, so it uses its large ears to dissipate excess heat. It launches bubbles from its mouth to hunt prey.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: The foam produced at the end of POKENAME's tail is extremely hot. Even so, it doesn't burn POKENAME, so it tends to be careless with it.
author: .realthree

entry: It's common for heart plushies to be blue or adorned with ribbon, taking inspiration from this Pokémon. Among surfers, seeing POKENAME is a sign of true love to come.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME loves to play with the bouncy bubbles on its tail, but it always keeps a watchful eye on its surroundings. If it senses danger, it can jump up to eight feet in the air to avoid attacks and make its escape.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME continually dribbles a cloud of bubbles which can be blasted to entrap foes, allowing for either a quick escape or follow-up pinches. Its hardiness has helped it to survive and spread to multiple regions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME secretes a pliable film of bubbles to protect its meaty fists. Should this padding be damaged in battle, it will fly into a blind rage.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME floats near the ocean surface, releasing toxic bubbles at prey. Once stunned, it strikes with lashing tentacles.
author: .izik

entry: Its tongue is covered with sea foam that allows it to filter impurities from the water. POKENAME feeds on algae to strengthen the shell that protects it from attacks by other Pokémon living in the ocean.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Using its pendulum as a focus for its power, it psychically manipulates water. POKENAME spends many hours a day silently honing its abilities.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's keen eyesight allows it to effortlessly navigate its swamp habitat, even when it is filled  with dense fog. When hunting, it plunges its long neck into the water to grab prey.
author: mepp.

entry: Because its fangs are too dull to inject venom, POKENAME will instead spray alkaline bubbles at its prey, slowly melting them. It covers its den in these bubbles as a line of defense.
author: mistymagius

entry: It surrounds its opponent with a flurry of bubbles, some of which stick to and slow down the opponent. Afterwards, it releases a shock towards the opponent, which ricochets from bubble to bubble in close proximity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates a mushroom-shaped bubble on its back to create visual distortions to distract predators. If the bubble pops, it scuttles into hiding until it can safely rebuild it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: An incredible tactician, POKENAME waves its bubble-covered stick in the air to communicate with its allies. It's great at devising battle strategies.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: In battle, POKENAME peers its head above the surface of water, shoots a highly precise Water Gun, and then quickly retreats back underwater. It is too swift and nimble to properly study its lower body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The foam that floats out of POKENAME's tail and neck contains a chemical that combusts when it makes contact with any carbon compounds. If you come across any wet spots in the rocky lands where POKENAME live, it is best not to touch them.
author: .realthree

entry: Using rough river rapids as cover, POKENAME tracks unsuspecting prey while gathering energy for an ambush. It breaks the surface with a mighty jump, throwing a Water Shuriken before landing an armor-piercing kick.
author: ghostslythe

entry: In battle, POKENAME uses its dexterous tongue to hurl electrically charged Water Shurikens at its opponent. Depending on the amount of charge stored, a single hit can down an enemy over ten times its size.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME use ionised water as a means of attack, floating low over water surfaces and using their magnetic powers to create water shurikens. They are cumbersome in the air, however, only able to use their powers to float or to attack.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a cunning Pokémon, nearly impossible to hit thanks to its unmatched agility. It can curl into a ball in an instant, shielding its weak points with its shell, and hurls sand bombs to hinder foes while executing swift evasive maneuvers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME use both their superb agility and skin pigments to appear nigh-undetectable in the darkness of night. Even when eyes can hardly see, they use the sensitive tongues to analyze their surroundings.
author: entomoxie

entry: Nicknamed the desert Sand Sharpedo, POKENAME circles shallowly underground, feeding off the water from cactus roots. When its dorsal fin above ground hits a Trainer or Pokémon, it explodes from the sand, confronting foes with solid water scythes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A POKENAME acts as a sort of traveling dojo for Froasaur, helping to teach them the art of ninjutsu. If anyone threatens the Froasaur inside, the POKENAME will rapidly spin the water shuriken on its back and launch razor-sharp droplets.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Despite honing great illusions and ninjutsu skills, POKENAME has a fatal flaw: its tongue. If discovered mid-disguise, it will lash out with it before retreating.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are known for being incredibly fast both in the air and on the surface of the water. The fastest POKENAME in the world are hard to even see because they use their speed to deliberately disappear or deceive onlookers.
author: entomoxie

entry: This slippery shinobi shows a strange interest in shiny items, such as gold and jewels. POKENAME has also been seen nearby Fuchsia City.
author: saberman3885

entry: POKENAME is rarely spotted at rest, often maneuvering at high speeds in an effort to protect the flame on its tail. When threatened, it hurls a flurry of small but volatile throwing stars formed from compressed water, buying itself time to escape.
author: theartemis1

entry: Despite its size and weight, POKENAME is an expert climber, able to crawl up the jungle trees with its small claws or stick to wet river cliffs with its finger pads. That way, this stealthy predator sneaks up to its prey, catching it with its tongue.
author: milchik

entry: A master of ambush tactics, POKENAME is both silent and lightning-fast underwater. Several reports claim to see POKENAME vanish mid-chase only to reappear in front of its prey, delivering a devastating Bite.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME can react so fast that it is believed it can see the future. It wields its nunchakus with incredible precision and speed. Despite its unfriendly looks, it is incredibly loyal once it takes a liking to someone.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: Despite its best efforts, POKENAME is somewhat slower than the average Pokémon. To compensate, it releases thick steam from its body in large bursts, masking its presence from foes in a pinch.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME uses its sticky tongue to scale cliffs and walls. As it does so, it leaves scorch marks behind, as its saliva causes a chemical reaction that raises the temperature.
author: .realthree

entry: A constant stream of smoke rises from the seed on its back, sometimes containing toxic substances. POKENAME must eat dozens of berries each day to keep its body temperature high, or it risks falling ill.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME release a hot smoke that wicks moisture from the area around them. They are sensitive to moisture in the area, so by constantly releasing smoke they can adjust the humidity in the air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The clouds of smoke emanated from POKENAME have an ashy and earthen scent to them. The smell has been used by some to help Pokémon from volcanic areas feel more comfortable when away from their natural habitat.
author: sk372

entry: Steam within the shell keeps POKENAME's tentacles moist and able to move it around. Because the steam escapes as it moves, it only moves in short bursts, lest it risk its limbs drying out.
author: sk372

entry: The steam vented from POKENAME's ears can be manipulated to form solid barriers. Excess smoke pours from its core, creating a constant haze around it.
author: evilgammon

entry: Before battle, POKENAME's tail flame burns white-hot. It spits blinding smoke to obscure its foe, then strikes with searing embers.
author: .izik

entry: Domestication of this Pokémon is difficult, as it has a short temper and is prone to run amok over the slightest inconvenience. Once it calms down, it expresses deep remorse over its lost temper.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is unable to dig up coal for itself, so other Pokémon and people must hand it food for its survival. The soot it creates pollutes the rivers and oceans that it lives in, making them unlivable for any Pokémon except for other Magikarp.
author: soup1900

entry: When under attack, POKENAME releases plumes of thick smog. This smoke contains a weak poison that irritates the skin and eyes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME rampages through towns, turning them into ashy, smoke-filled wastelands. The Eruption it launches can completely melt away entire neighborhoods in one blow.
author: soup1900

entry: As it consumes coal and other materials, puffs of smoke rise from its head. The clouds shift into the shapes of other Pokémon, even mimicking their behavior before dissipating.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tail holds a fiercely burning fire. When in peak health, the flames glow brilliantly inside its rock-hard tail casing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates its smoke by feeding off of images of coals inside of computer systems. However, if it can't discern the image format of the picture of coal, it will refuse to eat the image even if it hasn't eaten in days.
author: soup1900

entry: During battle, POKENAME blows thick smoke from its nostrils to obscure itself and gain an advantage over its foes. It prefers to live in caves rich with coal and other minerals.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME blows out lots of soot as it grows larger, meaning it must continuously eat and burn coal to survive. This constant use of energy and need for coal is why so few exist in the wild.
author: soup1900

entry: Wild POKENAME enjoy living on mountainous remote islands rich with coal. They create smoke signals to guide lost sailors away from dangerous rocks or violent storms.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's threads can radiate warmth, even in the coldest of climates. They are often used to line the inside of expensive Sleeping Bags for mountaineers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME makes nests atop volcano cliffs because the high temperatures help incubate its eggs. After the eggs hatch, it feeds its chicks molten rocks until they are able to fly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives near volcanoes and eats molten rocks. Contact with water rapidly reduces its body temperature, so it will send out a pulse of electricity to vaporize and avoid contact with water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: For POKENAME, having a dirty coat is a sign of good health. The soot in its coat keeps pesky bug Pokémon like Joltik away.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME produces a white smoke that absorbs moisture, which effectively neutralizes water used against it. It is known to wander beaches and lakes where it absorbs the beauty of the natural world.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pumps out white smoke from its body, which absorbs moisture from anything it touches. It can be found near lakes where it admires the scenery for long hours at a time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME engages in overly complex reasoning or calculations, the headpiece on its head emits thick plumes of black smoke. It tends to live in volcanic regions, where it uses its patience and wisdom to guide and assist younger Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's developing body causes it to create an excessive amount of steam vented from within its shell. The constant production and subsequent expulsion of steam leaves it tired and lethargic.
author: sk372

entry: Fueled by the burning coal it finds on volcanic islands, POKENAME nurtures a volcanic bulb on its back that releases bursts of fiery pollen.
author: zgaroff

entry: POKENAME is a gentle giant living a very sedentary lifestyle in volcanic regions, usually not far from human civilization. It is friendly enough that it even allows others to use its hot, steaming body as a makeshift sauna.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live on foggy mountain peaks where the mist helps keep their body temperature down. They are easily excitable and, if well fed, can cause an area to heat up rapidly to uncomfortable levels.
author: chibitales

entry: Due to the shell over its magma-like body, POKENAME rarely moves. It sticks its head out from the holes in the shell in order to feed and vent excess steam from its pores.
author: sk372

entry: It is one of the slowest-moving Pokémon recorded; a POKENAME moving at top speed for 24 hours would travel only a scant ten feet at best.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will use anything it can find to fuel the fire in its shell, causing the smoke it exhales to be heavily toxic. It is a reclusive Pokémon, hiding away in volcanic regions where no one will disturb it.
author: mistymagius

entry: The steam emanating from POKENAME is rumored to give visions of one's future, so people get steam baths made by it to receive prophecies. It reads their minds, then feeds off of their happy emotions when it puts positive outcomes into their heads.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME spends its time in the mountains attempting to use its magnetism to gather coal. Unfortunately, coal is not magnetic, and it ends up with loads of other minerals instead. POKENAME then trades these minerals with miners in exchange for coal.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Its umbrella radiates heat to keep it warm while shielding its body from volcanic ash in the air. It's known for being elusive, walking out from the smokescreen it billows, and vanishing into those same clouds.
author: sk372

entry: It projects an image of its face within the steam it expels, but this is just as incorporeal as the smoke. In olden Hoenn times people would burn incense near it, believing it held connections to their ancestors' spirits.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly billows out smoke from its massive jaws, which needs to be constantly vented to prevent toxic accumulation in its body. In Pokémon battles, its massive jaws can shoot out fiery plumes of lava, or bite onto its opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The smoke excreted by POKENAME smells like the sea, as the water it evaporates is very saline. With the pressure of the steam exhausted from the bottom of its body, it somehow manages to float mid-air just fine.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: On occasion, the volcano on POKENAME's back erupts, sending magma cascading out. Some of this magma settles on it and cools, creating sturdy plates that function as makeshift protective armour.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME houses molten rock in its shell and spews hot ash from its vents. It is found in hot, arid climates, as any moisture in the air causes it great pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Agile and mischievous, POKENAME swings through the rafters of abandoned mansions. It chews on old wood to warm itself when cold.
author: .izik

entry: It pokes its head out of the stone body in order to eat or release large amounts of steam. Some resorts in Hoenn have taken to employing them as a part of their saunas.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produces its smoke by burning collected life energy inside of its mace. These souls then inhabit and control this smoke, using it as their hand to wield POKENAME for their own purposes.
author: soup1900

entry: Groups of POKENAME work together to collect large amounts of coal for them to burn. They use jets of pressurized smoke to effortlessly cut through the rocks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's method of flight consumes a lot of energy, so it only awakens once a year, eating enough to last another 51 weeks of hibernation. These nights are infamous as POKENAME break the sound barrier and create supersonic booms to stun prey.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Their prey undergo seasonal nuptial flights, swarming in the night sky. On these nights, POKENAME awakens and rockets itself into the swarm, consuming up to three times its body weight before returning to its den and sleeping for another year.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME is a mystery to physicists and biologists alike because its shell is too heavy to float, and it produces an unending plume of smoke without ever landing to eat. It's hard for these questions to be studied, as it must keep moving to live.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Its tiny body is too small to haul its massive shell around normally. When POKENAME needs to move, it retreats into the shell and uses expelled steam to propel itself forward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly spews a great column of smoke out of its top. Occasionally, a lost soul will be seen swirling in the smoke, which is channelled into its ghostly attacks.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME produces large amounts of thick smoke from its body and is often used as an excellent outdoor heater. They seem to be most popular among campers and hikers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME ejects black soot in the shape of a hand from its mouth to hold back predators that near it. It can also use its smoke to create hand signals across the sky to communicate with other POKENAME across nearby shores.
author: soup1900

entry: As pressure builds inside POKENAME, its keys rattle faster and louder. Moments later, scalding steam erupts, capable of melting metal.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sings, puffs of thick, hypnotic smoke rise from its shell. Campers once mistook its snores for volcanic rumblings and evacuated the area, only for the rangers to find it dreaming peacefully.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its gears churn slowly but steadily to give it life energy, releasing small bits of smoke as it does so. Some liken the sound it makes to the slow chug of a steam engine.
author: sk372

entry: The spinning gears generate steam to dissipate excess heat. The main gear stores intense pressure within, releasing it to launch the other gears forward in self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME burns as little coal as possible in its tail, as the fire inside its shell-like casing dictates its life. When it becomes angry, it burns coal at a faster rate than usual, which it needs to keep its fire blazing.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's grey roses release clouds of smoke and ash when POKENAME feels threatened. They are often used by honey collectors as their smoke seems to prevent Beedrill from becoming agitated.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uproots carrots and blows tiny embers over them to roast the vegetables before happily eating its meal. When sleeping, it will expel small flames from its ears.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's leaves are intensely spicy and have been prized in Hoenn cuisine for generations. Chefs use them to enrich special stews.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flocks to volcanoes to eat molten rocks, and releases smoke that builds up while digesting rocks. When threatened, it spits out balls of fire to scare away predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's many spikes help it attach to rocky surfaces. It can be occasionally seen inhabiting chimneys, feeding on the soot that drifts up.
author: mepp.

entry: Toxic steam constantly leaks from POKENAME's body as its antennae grow hot. The more coal it consumes, the denser and deadlier the fumes become.
author: .izik

entry: It lengthens the distance of its leaps by expelling vast amounts of smoke from its nostrils to propel it further. The smoke takes on an appearance similar to wings, making POKENAME appear to be flying.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME vents steam from its nose to propel itself extremely fast through the air. Its supply is limited though, so it is often seen dormant on the ground while more steam builds inside itself.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME consumes coal to keep its energy high as it gallops around its territory. The craters on its back vent excess heat and poisonous smog.
author: chibitales

entry: When POKENAME lets out a roar, the small plumes of steam it releases intensify into a singular geyser of smoke. It often tries to beat its own personal record for roar and eruption power.
author: sk372

entry: Archaeologists believe POKENAME may have been the apex being within ancient volcanic regions. A long neck, powerful jaws, a sturdy shell and smoke production all combined to make it a formidable prehistoric hunter.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's leaves are made of a tightly packed warm ash. Once a month, the leaves "shed" into a dusty pile on the ground. It buries itself into the pile afterward and waits for a new set of leaves to grow back.
author: sk372

entry: The steam that comes of the head of POKENAME becomes thicker as the beat of the music becomes faster. This natural process makes it a popular sight in clubs, where it serves as a living, high-grade smoke machine.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's arms are hidden by dense steam. It claps to charge the vapor with static, though its hands remain invisible through the thick cloud.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME gently sways around to prevent thickly packed smoke from being released from its body. This is done to maintain the air quality and health of those around it, especially those who may have breathing problems.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME flies through the air on wings made of smoke. It is very timid and tends to avoid conflict by hiding in smokescreens rather than engaging in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME constantly produces smoke, which it uses to scare prey out from their burrows. As prey leaves its burrow, POKENAME releases blazingly hot fumes, cooking its prey instantly.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: It belts out increasing amounts of steam from its tail depending on how happy it is. POKENAME may also release excessive steam if hugged too hard by its Trainer.
author: sk372

entry: The shell surrounding POKENAME's head is heated by the coal it consumes. Water-type attacks from this Pokémon are scalding hot and likely to cause burns.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME roasts nuts and treats on an open fire when frost nips at people's noses. People and Pokémon alike cozy up by its fire, helping everyone keep warm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a docile, yet powerful Pokémon capable of producing vast heat waves up to 650° Celsius. They store energy by submerging their rocky bodies in lava, then expel it through their gemstones as gleaming light that is said to cure any illness.
author: aurange

entry: Thick smoke pours from POKENAME's large ears, carrying the distinct scent of burnt wood through forest paths and volcanic slopes. It snacks on small twigs that fall from trees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can pull heavy cargo with the strength of a freight train while it's full on coal. Its heavy plating deflects away rocks and other debris that may fall onto it while it's searching for coal.
author: soup1900

entry: It collects coal to burn within the base of its body, which is covered by a hard shell. The holes where the glow of coal burns brightly are said to guide lost souls who died in cave-ins.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Many have observed that POKENAME smells faintly of freshly baked bread. Its naturally warm body makes it a popular Pokémon for companionship.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME wanders for its first year before choosing a place to settle. If it nests in a bakery, it is seen as a mark of excellence. After a hearty meal, it vents fragrant steam said to smell even better than the treats it consumed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME wanders for its first year before choosing a place to settle. If it nests in a confectionery shop, it is seen as a mark of excellence. After a hearty meal, it vents fragrant steam said to smell even better than the treats it consumed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME likes to rest in lava lakes, venting steam from the top of its head. Campers love to have POKENAME around as its head acts like a portable stovetop.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME whips its tail around in battles to fill the area with thick, hot smoke. Once the foe is blinded and burned, it finishes the battle by burning more coal to power up a final fire breath attack.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME will blow hearts of smoke at people it thinks could be a potential couple. On the contrary, couples it thinks aren't going to last will instead be blown broken hearts made of black soot.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME will remain motionless for hours while it meditates, spewing hot smoke all the while. Saunas like to pair POKENAME with a Water-Type Pokémon to create a steamy environment for guests. POKENAME enjoys hot yoga classes as well.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME constantly release smoke from their bodies to ensure that they keep their bodies as hot as possible. If their bodies cool past a certain temperature, they experience a chill that causes them to shiver.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cloak themselves in soot from the fires they produce. Powerful individuals can spread their ashes over the skies for many days, blocking out the sunlight and lowering the temperature.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are very docile creatures, spending their days drinking a lot of water and boiling it inside their bodies, turning it into scalding steam. Laundry workers enjoy having a few POKENAME on hand to iron and dewrinkle clothes with their steam.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When POKENAME is low on coal, it burns parts of its wings for fuel, leaving them with many holes over time. Entire cities must evacuate when it blows out its burning smoke, as it ignites anything it touches and spreads fires over great distances.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME stacks discarded shells on its back as a form of weight training. If it lacks shells to use, it may instead request other Pokémon or even Trainers to stand on it as it works out.
author: sk372

entry: It flexes before every attack, expelling smoke from the holes in its shell as it does so. The more holes emitting smoke, the stronger the attack it's about to unleash.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME exhales smoke that causes nearby plants to grow twice as fast. Botanists highly covet this rare and potent fertilizer.
author: .izik

entry: When angered, POKENAME's rocky head vents thick smoke like a steam train. It feeds voraciously on lumps of raw coal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's rocky shell is completely hollow, allowing for its built-up fire and smoke to be stored inside. In battle, it releases this pressure, causing a devastating eruption of lava and smoke.
author: evilgammon

entry: Despite having a low top speed, POKENAME prides itself on its galloping ability. What appears to be smoke billowing from it is actually a soft, ashy fur.
author: sk372

entry: All three heads possess the capacity to breathe out steam, but as the center head is the most temperamental of the bunch, it is the one most associated with and seen using the ability.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have pieces of shells and obsidian in their body, which constantly shift to keep their body hot. Whenever it rains, they push the shell pieces to the exterior of their body in an attempt to ward off moisture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has the unique ability to blast both flames and water out of its spouts. When fired at the same time, steam is created that is said to be good for muscle aches.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME floats freely through volcanic regions, delighting in scaring travelers who stray too close to bubbling lava pits. It laughs loudly when its victim screams in fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's claws emit constant steam due to their heat. Though effective for offense, it prefers creating a thicker cloud of steam to obscure itself and flee from potential dangers.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its giant clamp to slow-cook its prey, then eats it alive as soon as the fight is won. Wild POKENAME tolerate medium rare meat, while trained specimens prefer well done.
author: epping_forest

entry: Both of POKENAME's claws produce copious amounts of steam, but the larger actually contains and produces boiling water. Any who agitate it risk being hit with a scalding spray.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME often find secluded areas of shallow water, heating the area with its hot body. Different Pokémon often gather to enjoy these makeshift hot springs alongside the POKENAME.
author: mrsspace

entry: POKENAME is most commonly found in the autumn, appearing within the fields of rural communities. They are friendly and easily trained, enjoying the company of young Trainers as they explore the Pokémon world.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: During storms, POKENAME secures pumpkins to the ground with strong silk. The threads are resilient enough to withstand hurricane winds.
author: .izik

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads grows dark brown vines that connect at night. These shared roots transfer nutrients and whisper thoughts in unison.
author: .izik

entry: Using its brown vines, POKENAME overtakes wild Tangela and then spreads its body beneath the soil. These hidden traps ensnare any who near the crops it protects.
author: .izik

entry: The vine on POKENAME's head sharpens into a venomous needle. A single jab causes painful fevers in predators bold enough to approach its patch.
author: .izik

entry: Its body glows with soft flames. If you rest in the warmth of its fire's heat for a while, you may witness memories from lives long past.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME tends to appear in October, when it gathers with others of its kind to haunt wheat fields. However, it is said that spotting one brings prosperity and good fortune, so farmers never drive it away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is always on the lookout for predators, using its excellent night vision to navigate during the night. When frightened, it will jump into the trees, its fur blending in with the dark foliage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME scurries around forests and farmland, scavenging for food to take back to its burrow. During harvest season, it can be persuaded to help out with an offering of Colbur Berries.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lets out long, haunting hoots late in the evening, calling out to others of its kind. Once a month, flocks of POKENAME gather in the forest to sing an ethereal harmony together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for another car by nighttime drivers due to the glowing holes in its belly, which are actually used to blind prey and frighten predators. Autumn nights are fortuitous times for people hoping to spot this skittish Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its vines to parasitize Ledyba colonies, converting them into seed-spreaders. It fiercely defends the meadow, attacking all intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins translucent threads across pumpkin fields. If one is touched, the swarm is alerted. It traps intruders using Sticky Web to prevent escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME only hunts at night, able to detect prey in pure darkness using its excellent night vision. During the day it hangs from decaying trees, hoping to blend into the dark foliage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME emerge during the full moon of an autumn festival and live quietly inside caves during the rest of the year. They happily dance and celebrate the occasion alongside others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Legends claim that consuming the goo brewed in POKENAME's pumpkin cauldron bestows visions of the future. A splash of the liquid is sometimes added to dessert frostings or beverages to induce a woozy feeling.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its tail is a lantern; one look at the light from the hole of this lantern can put one under its control. POKENAME can easily detect spirits with its ears' sensitive hearing.
author: doctorjazznumber6215

entry: Flocks of POKENAME drift along the wind, the light from their lanterns only visible during the night. Spectators describe POKENAME sightings as looking like small stars moving across the night sky.
author: mistymagius

entry: On particularly dark nights, clusters of POKENAME can be seen drifting on the wind, illuminating the ground below in an eerie light. They bring the oddly sweet scent of pumpkin wherever they go.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lures young children into the forests, hypnotizing them with the eerie glow of its lantern. No one knows why it wants these children, but they are often never seen again once they enter the forest.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only come out at night, cheekily playing pranks on anyone that passes by. Its favorite prank is to hide inside hollow gourds and waiting for someone to pick it up.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flashes the pumpkin-like orb on its tail mid-flight to communicate. If the light flickers red, it signals danger to the swarm nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's head is always caked in mud, even while submerged. No one knows what lies beneath, as legend warns that anyone who tries to wipe it clean will be cursed. Whether myth or truth, even the boldest Trainers leave the mud untouched.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The light shed from POKENAME has the unusual effect of causing the plants it shines on to act as if it were nighttime. Day-blooming flowers close and nocturnal blossoms open in the presence of this Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are popular in farming communities, their ethereal connection to the harvest making them invaluable for maintaining a healthy crop. They have an innate ability to sense when a crop is ripe for picking.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its shell reminds people of Lychee, especially since its shell is the same color. When its shell is damaged, it also oozes out syrup that tastes like the fruit too.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores Pumkin Berries in its shell, rolling to mix them into a juice. In Kanto, this sweet drink is praised for its aroma and flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves melons and pumpkins and will often raid local farms to get its hands on them. However, anyone that tries to steal its stash will be relentlessly pursued and attacked.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME invades Teddiursa dens to parasitize them. It practices and mimics their cries to lure in Ursaring, which it ambushes for nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burns unwanted plant life by chewing it to ash and spitting it onto pumpkin fields. It avoids burning useful flora unless resources run low.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in coral reefs, shining a soft light from its chest at night. Divers often mistake it for treasure until it vanishes into the dark.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects seeds from decaying pumpkins and stores them in its sack-like tail. It lays them out to dry in the sun before eating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses Phanpy herds to roll through fields and churn planting rows. The resulting pumpkin patches are heavily guarded by hostile attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are common companions in agricultural communities, used as a deterrent to keep Flying-Type Pokémon away. They will pick fights with Pokémon that disturb the crops under their protection, even if they are unlikely to win.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are common companions in agricultural communities, used as a deterrent to keep Flying-Type Pokémon away. They will pick fights with Pokémon that disturb the crops under their protection, even if they are unlikely to win.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon smoothed out a pumpkin holding a spirit into a ball and now travels on it, mimicking the actions the spirit once took in life.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: The electric lights that glow within POKENAME's hollow head are thought to attract Bug-type Pokémon to pollinate the pumpkin flower on its tail. These Pokémon are commonly seen throughout fall, but they hide away at the first sign of winter.
author: .realthree

entry: During the day, POKENAME nap lazily in sunny places. Once twilight falls, they can re-emit the absorbed light to guide their way as they travel.
author: .realthree

entry: Weary travellers of the jungle may encounter POKENAME at night. It's a friendly spirit that will offer a slice of pie made from its own body to adventurers.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME grow long spikes on their back that resemble candy corn. Many children have tried to bite off a delicious-looking spike, only to lose a tooth while biting down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME parasitizes Mudkip colonies to water its pumpkin fields. The Mudkip spray water while it uses Bullet Seed to keep scavengers away.
author: .izik

entry: This childlike Pokémon has a tendency for knocking on doors at night to ask for treats. Citizens of Lavender Town have taken to leaving small baskets of candy out on their front steps, lest they get tricked by the spirit instead.
author: chiari_queen

entry: On close inspection, POKENAME appears to float just above the ground. Researchers believe it is to cover up the fact that their tiny legs lack the locomotion to get anywhere faster than a crawl.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME is territorial of a patch of its meadow, launching venomous needles at intruders. A Galarian baker discovered that baking it in a pie with Kebia Berries made it edible and produced a pie with a slightly sour flavor with a smooth texture.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gathers pumpkin innards and smears them around its riverside lodge. The scent marks its territory and keeps other Pokémon at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits sharp seeds which inject foes with an endurance-sapping poison. It prowls farm fields near harvest season, looking for prey scavenging the last of the crops.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is known to use its natural cuteness and bright lights to lure in and carry lost souls to the afterlife. If no lost souls are around, it will draw in other living creatures before tearing them apart.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME slumbers during the day, covering its eyes with its large leaves. At night, its eyes glow with a mysterious but welcoming light, inviting all who see it to join in POKENAME's festivities.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME floats through graveyards, blinking its chest lights in eerie patterns. Local legends claim staring too long can curse your family line.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flocks descend on Nidoran families to harness their hearing. With its sharp horn, it patrols pumpkin fields and drives intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: Spores shaken from POKENAME's body smell like ripe pumpkins. They cause limb numbness that can take several days to fully wear off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME communicates with soft glows from its torso. Its innards are tangled vines that extend to grab and consume sea plants from afar.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME colonies parasitize sleeping Nincada to collect nutrient-rich soil. They glow yellow underground as they prepare vast pumpkin beds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appear during certain spirit festivals. The yellow fur on their bodies flickers like fire and is believed to drive away malevolent spirits. The flicker is more intense and a fresh pumpkin smell is produced when POKENAME are excited.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME live in dark forests, the bioluminescent fluid inside its body helping them to see their surroundings. Parents will often give their child a POKENAME to act as a nightlight.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME loves to spook passersby by camouflaging itself amongst the trees. While mostly found in dark forests, it will also inhabit abandoned homes and mansions.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME bites into power lines to absorb electricity. When fully charged, the light inside its body flashes rapidly like a blinking lantern.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal, using their glowing feelers to illuminate the darkness. When threatened, POKENAME will spew out a hot, orange liquid from its mouth similar to pureed pumpkin.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME eats poison ivy and poison sumac to enhance its toxins. When its venom peaks in potency, its body glows a brilliant orange instead of yellow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps in pumpkin patches during day. If disturbed, it strikes with venom so potent it can cause temporary blindness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dance weaves hypnotic hues, guiding lost souls to rest while ensnaring the living in a trance. Those who disrupt its rhythm risk becoming spectral prey, bound to wander as the spirits it once ferried.
author: vhscopyofmeangirls

entry: After POKENAME possesses a rotting pumpkin, it struggles to get around without risking its body falling apart. The pungent scent of decay follows it wherever it goes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is said to be a wandering spirit that is drawn to large gatherings of costumed people and pumpkin patches. It loves to join spooky festivities, adoring the thrill of a good scare.
author: chiari_queen

entry: At night, POKENAME patrols crop fields using the eerie glow from its chest and paws. If it spots an intruder, it charges while screaming a sound that many state sounds like a tornado siren crossed with radio static.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's vines stretch across the ocean floor, detecting vibrations from far away. Sometimes its vines completely overtake sunken ships.
author: .izik
