entry: POKENAME blasts mini-heads from its cannons. Somehow, nobody knows what the bottom of these mini-heads look like.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a Dugtrio by burying half of its body. When Trainers get too close, it attacks with psychic power.
author: themicelegion

entry: Somehow, its sand makes people fall asleep.  Scientists tried to make it into an insomnia remedy, but it has no effect unless POKENAME sprinkles it.
author: empty_set

entry: During the day, POKENAME uses its radar to sense where clean water is located before swimming to the location at night. Toxic dust is released if a Pokémon tries to take a ride on top of it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is an extremely territorial creature that attacks anyone who approaches the fruit tree it is feeding on. It is mainly active at night, as any source of light that is too bright bothers it too much.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME maintains top physical form by independently cultivating a garden of fruits which it dusts with powder from its wings. It shares its brews with people and Pokémon in lively parties, which it alone cleans up to continue its fitness regimen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME loves to pretend to be a large acorn and spook Pokémon and Trainers alike. The leaf on its tail absorbs sunlight while it sits still and provides energy.
author: chibitales

entry: Unable to gain nutrients from the sun, POKENAME burrow into the roots of trees, leeching vital nutrients. When sensing other pests attacking their meal, they quickly latch onto the other Pokémon and drain its power.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME collects acorns using its long tongue. When startled while eating, its skin flashes red and brown rapidly before it explodes.
author: .izik

entry: Sensing an incoming hurricane, POKENAME rushes to the center of town and detonates. Though meant as a warning, the act often worsens the destruction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces leaves that grow from its shell, which are used in bubble teas for their sweet, energizing flavor. Its tough acorn shell can also be ground into a spice that resembles nutmeg.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After flying through heavy storms, POKENAME's fluffy wings sprout tiny green shoots. These sprouts dry out and fall away within a day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats in small ponds where it waits for berries to fall into the water. It takes small nibbles from them and needs about an hour to finish one berry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's rounded head sloshes with stored water as it moves. It sprays foul-smelling liquid to mark its territory and ward off rivals.
author: .izik

entry: While searching for the acorns they buried for the winter, forest-dwelling Pokémon sometimes dig up POKENAME accidentally. Being unearthed makes it unable to absorb water and nutrients from the ground, so POKENAME reacts with hostility.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is a very rare Pokémon that is only found in summery forests. It invites people and Pokémon that need growth and healing to its cozy grove.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are considered scavengers. During the day they hide in leaf piles, most Trainers believing they are Acorns. At night, they burst from the leaves, tracking down people who passed during the morning to steal food from their campsites.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME attaches to tree branches by its head and tail to absorb nutrients. Its pinecone-like fur makes a rattling noise as it moves. When POKENAME is tired, it descends to the ground and digs a small burrow to rest in.
author: chibitales

entry: In spring, small vines sprout from POKENAME's thick fur. As summer heat arrives, the vines dry up and fall away naturally.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is tough, having begun to harden in preparation for evolution. When it begins to evolve, it sheds the spines along its back, which have a nutty flavor and are used as a topping or ingredient for ice cream.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME nests in trees near Seedot communities, standing guard for days without rest. It drives off predators with concentrated Giga Drain attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Flocks of wild POKENAME are often seen engaged in competitions with one another, ramming their sturdy heads against each other in impressive aerial battles. Whichever falls first is forced to find a new flock.
author: campadascleric

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in forest ponds. The hard wooden cap on its head helps protect it from aerial predators.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME forms swarms of bug Pokémon by flickering its glowing tail. It leads the swarm to tall trees where they hang from the branches and eat leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lures bug Pokémon into forming a swarm by releasing a sweet aroma. It finds healthy trees and leads the swarm to rest in the branches, where they feast on the leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's furry exterior is composed of thin wooden fibers. A careless touch can embed splinters in anyone who pets it the wrong way.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clamps onto approaching Zangoose with a powerful bite. If overwhelmed, it resorts to a desperate point-blank Explosion.
author: .izik

entry: Its strong arms give it a much broader range of mobility compared to a Seedot. After being fused, a POKENAME will use its new arms to strike various proud poses.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's hollow wooden body produces a soft whistle as it flies with its flock. On windy days, people travel just to hear their melodic calls.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a sturdy wooden stump atop their head and often ferry other Pokémon across bodies of water. They often release a happy whistle whenever the Pokémon they help give them a reward for their help.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Leaves sometimes sprout from the wooden disc atop POKENAME's head. It trims them carefully, keeping only a single leaf to grow.
author: .izik

entry: During extreme heat, POKENAME's leaf spins rapidly as a warning signal. The rotation helps vent energy and prevents sudden explosions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have tiny leaves on their legs that allow them to float on water. They keep ponds and lakes clean by eating leaves that fall into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME strips bark from trees with sharp claws to feed. If the bark tastes off, it discards it carelessly, leaving a scattered trail behind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blends in with its forest habitat to ambush unsuspecting prey, constricting them in its powerful, wooden coils. When threatened, it whistles an unnerving melody and rattles the seeds in its tail-knots to frighten off foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's head change shape depending on the local weather, showcasing its remarkable adaptability. Highly territorial, it drops from tree branches to strike intruders who dare to enter its home.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It blows in on wintry winds and finds a tree to attach itself to.  Forming a symbiotic relationship with its host tree, it absorbs its nutrients while scaring away any troublemakers.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME has a feisty personality and likes to battle other bird Pokémon in the air. Its twin tails coupled with its aerial maneuverability make it quite adept at clubbing other foes out of the sky.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries Pokémon Eggs inside the reinforced nest on its back. It gives off a high amount of heat, often helping the protected eggs hatch more quickly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME despises cold seasons, so when autumn arrives, it migrates far away in search of a warm and pleasant place. If its crest droops, it is s a clear sign that the Pokémon is unwell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often try to intimidate larger Pokémon into giving up their food by chirping loudly and spitting globs of fire from just out of reach. They quickly pick up on Pokémon that can be easily scared away and which to avoid.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME tends to fly around large trees after long days to relax. This action calms it down and prepares it for the next hunt.
author: retrodox

entry: When trapped in its underground tunnels, POKENAME flings dirt into its foe's eyes. It follows up with quick pecks while they're disoriented.
author: .izik

entry: Though it tends to lay about for most of the day, POKENAME is known to be protective of small bird Pokémon; the only time it's been seen moving quickly is rushing to one's defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME float in the air by expanding their feathery bodies. They often form flocks because they want the company of others and are prone to feeling lonely.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is often chosen as a household companion thanks to its inclination to sing sweet melodies and keep lonely people company. The colors of its plumage become vibrant when it is happy, making it easy to tell when it's being well cared for.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is known to eat mud after a long rainy season. The smell of petrichor lingers on its beak as it pecks at the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy taking baths whenever they get dirty. They often gather at waterfalls in groups to help each other clean their fluffy wings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will persistently chase its prey through land or sky. It will let out a loud bark from the top of its home tree to mark its territory.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is known for having unlimited energy and a feisty attitude. It constantly challenges other Pokémon to prove its strength.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME will periodically flap its wings and mimic chirping noises to appear more bird-like. Because of this, its most common predators are often fooled and leave it be.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME crawls into Taillow nests to disguise itself as an egg. It decorates the nest with silk, which lets other POKENAME know that the nest is occupied.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME crawls into Taillow nests to hide from predators. It pretends to be an egg and wraps the nest with silk to let other POKENAME know the nest is occupied.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a large wingspan that they often struggle to control. They practice performing complex aerial maneuvers to develop their wing muscles. Sometimes they hit tree branches or other flying Pokémon and tumble as a result.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoys quiet solitude and long naps deep inside caverns. If disturbed, it may retaliate against the rude awakening with angry chirping so loud it shakes the stone walls around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very energetic and will often flock together to play by swooping through the air in wide circles. If threatened, they attack fearlessly, battering foes with their wings and tails.
author: skittytales

entry: Scrappy by nature, POKENAME isn't afraid to pick fights with those bigger than it. It may not be strong, but its stubborn nature and quick teleporting make it a tricky foe to those who underestimate it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's sleek build lets it cut through the air quickly, particularly when swooping downward. It's just as likely to dive from the air to pick up prey as it is to latch onto a person and give them a full-body hug.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME dives upon prey from above, it has a habit of swallowing them whole if able. If it has hatchlings, this can result in it hunting for hours.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME flies up to the nests of bird Pokémon to consume the Eggs there. The lower half of its beak extends so it can swallow a Pokémon Egg in one gulp.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME sprints extremely fast, capable of outpacing even a seasoned athlete. This speed allows it to take down fleeing prey easily.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME runs at speeds rivalling Johto's Magnet Train, assisted by its lithe body shape. Even at such high speeds, it has little trouble clocking prey and attacking with powerful kicks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME possesses near unparalleled speed and maneuverability in the air, and keeps to itself near the ozone layer. Many avian Pokémon look up to it and dream of soaring alongside it someday.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME float through the sky by expanding their feathery bodies with hot air. They have great precision when flying and can display this precision when they fly through hoops at circus shows.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to keep their wings clean. They can spend hours at a time under waterfalls ensuring that they leave without a speck of dirt on them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME spots prey, it swoops down from great heights, gouging them with sharp talons. It has been used for many heraldic designs, symbolizing bravery.
author: mepp.

entry: It deliberately flies in a zigzag pattern to confuse its enemies, then at the right moment lunges at them with its beak to strike with all its strength. Despite its broad wings, it builds its nest on the ground by digging it out with its feet.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME alternates between speedily running and gliding to scout its territory for prey or intruders. It is a playful companion as it loves to chase round objects, also making it a beloved competitor in agility competitions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are skilled at performing aerial maneuvers but lack a properly sized beak to hunt for large prey. They rely on small nuts and berries to sustain them until they evolve and grow a larger beak.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME struggles to sleep unless surrounded by its flock. They rest on seaside cliffs, huddling together against strong ocean winds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in solitude, roosting high atop trees. Highly aggressive, they viciously attack anything they perceive as a threat.
author: mepp.

entry: If anyone dares to misplace even a single one of its feathers, POKENAME flies into a rage. When it spots prey, it performs graceful leaps to catch it with its sharp claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To conserve energy, POKENAME glides on sea breezes. When it spots prey below, it shoots out a powerful blast of water to stun them before diving down to finish them off.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are often found creeping up the sides of cruise ships, seeking food. Their plenitude over coral reefs has led to some cruise lines employing Trainers to fight back the wild Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: Though POKENAME's body makes it far too heavy to glide, that doesn't stop it from trying. It runs and leaps from tall seaside cliffs to attempt to fly, causing a massive splash once it inevitably plummets into the ocean.
author: sk372

entry: Most of POKENAME's body fat is reserved for when it needs to fly; its body shape makes doing so very difficult! It instead prefers to float on the water's surface. It hibernates during the winter.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Most of POKENAME's body fat is reserved for when it needs to fly; its body shape makes doing so very difficult! It instead prefers to float on the water's surface. It hibernates during the winter.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flocks in droves around beachfront restaurants and shops, picking up any and all discarded food items it can find. Particularly brave POKENAME will even enter the shops and steal items directly.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME are often the leaders of a flock of Wingtata. With the combined force of the flock, beachgoers have no choice but to give up their tasty snacks.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's calls sound like eerie laughter and screeches. They call loudly to frighten humans, then absorb their fear for nutrients.
author: hophoppip

entry: If it spots discarded food on the beach, nothing can stop POKENAME from trying to eat it. Entire coastlines have been reshaped in the pursuit of french fries.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME nests itself on cliff faces overlooking the ocean. Over time, the area it nests in will develop large amounts of moss and other plant life. Once the cliff becomes full of vegetation, POKENAME migrates to a new cliff.
author: sk372

entry: Despite the sturdy feathers on POKENAME's arms, POKENAME can't fly. It makes up for its lack of flight with its impressive running speed, sprinting through beaches with its stolen picnic foods.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is highly in-tune with the changing winds at sea, able to sense the air currents for miles. This has made it invaluable to sailors, and few ships leave without at least one in tow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is rarely found near the ground. Hunting alone, it soars among the clouds and blends into the sky, waiting to swoop down on unsuspecting Magikarp.
author: retrodox

entry: If a small crowd of POKENAME quietly perches near someone's home before flying off, someone in the home is about to be very ill. In the distant past, doctors dealing with strong illnesses would wear masks fashioned after POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's titanic size makes it able to carry large amounts of people through the air and across the sea as a type of luxury cruise. It is somewhat easily distracted, however, so professionals must be on hand to keep it on-course.
author: sk372

entry: With hollow bones, POKENAME is always able to stay on the surface of the water. Its back serves as a giant nest for many aquatic flying Pokémon.
author: gnom3

entry: This minuscule Pokémon is suited to urban environments, where it feeds on discarded food scraps. It purposefully feeds on rotten food to coat its beak in germs, granting it a sickening defense mechanism when predators attack.
author: hophoppip

entry: Though POKENAME cannot fly, it can unfurl its wing-like tails to glide a moderate distance. It's often seen running and gliding behind flocks of Wingull, dreaming of migrating alongside them one day.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lulls people around them to sleep before eating any food they may have on them. Many people resort to wearing earmuffs to avoid falling asleep and losing their snacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is most often spotted in coastal areas, particularly places where Wingull gather. It tries to join the flock, but its appearance and eerie cry instead sends the birds flying away in terror.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME greatly admires creatures able to take flight. Its often seen at beaches, gazing up at passing Wingull flocks and calling to them, waving at them and hoping to make friends.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scatters blue powder from its wings when it spots beachgoers eating fruit. The powder induces sleep, allowing it to steal food undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's soft feathers are highly sought after by collectors. It is said that sailors who see flocks of POKENAME while at sea are blessed with a safe voyage.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME burrow around beaches looking for scraps of food left behind by beachgoers. It is not uncommon for someone to be suddenly surrounded by a group of POKENAME. Despite their numbers, they are skittish and easy to scare off with loud noises.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME sneaks around beaches to steal shiny objects and valuables from beachgoers. If confronted, it howls to summon more of its pack. If given an opportunity, it will flee with the valuables in its mouth.
author: chibitales

entry: On moonlit nights, POKENAME packs gather in oval formations and flap their wings while howling in unison. This display occurs only once per night and never repeats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prowls around lakes where fishermen gather. As soon as a fish is reeled in, it dashes forward at lightning speed to steal the catch. This usually ends in success since most fishers won't bother chasing it.
author: chibitales

entry: Its small body is the perfect size for wriggling into bags of chips. POKENAME is despised by many Trainers for its food-thieving ways, but some find it amusing.
author: hophoppip

entry: Brave and bold, POKENAME often accompanies sailors south of Hoenn. It can eat all sorts of food, so it is generally easy to take care of. However, it also detests blizzards and will flee if snow and ice litter the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can soar confidently even during violent storms, and because it never loses its sense of direction, sailors rely on it to guide them safely back to port. Playful by nature, it enjoys splashing both Pokémon and humans it takes a liking to.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can soar confidently even during violent storms, and because it never loses its sense of direction, sailors rely on it to guide them safely back to port. Playful by nature, it enjoys splashing both Pokémon and humans it takes a liking to.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To ensure that its white plumage remains shiny, POKENAME tries to steal food from beachgoers who are camping on the beaches; it is crazy about sandwiches. Its flying ability allows it to face any kind of sea storm with determination.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hoard the fish carcasses they gather in seaside towns. They seem to have limited counting ability, as they can immediately tell when one of their precious carcasses has been stolen.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME meditates for hours on seaside cliffs, breathing in time with the crashing waves and ocean spray. When hunting, it uses its psychic abilities to spring off of the surface of the water while snatching Remoraid in its fists.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME always makes sure it has plenty of room to build up speed before it leaps into the air to take flight. The running generates internal electricity, and lets it leave a trail of sparking lightning behind as it glides through the air.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME seemingly conjure lightning out of nowhere by howling. They harness the power of electricity to hunt aquatic Pokémon and shock them with their claws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generate a positive electrical field around itself, which gets stronger when it is raining. This field draws in lightning from thunderstorms which gets converted into static.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produces a negative electrical field when it rains, which redirects electricity around itself. It likes to stay near its Trainer to protect them during thunderstorms.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers near beaches and parks, watching humans for a glimpse of food before it descends in a feeding frenzy. It does not always correctly distinguish food and will expel inedible objects with a sheen of toxic fluid.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME scrounge beaches and ports, consuming anything from Berries to trash. Their populations were originally encouraged since they eliminate litter, but now they harass people for food and are too hardy to drive away from population centers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: To remain cool, POKENAME stores cold sea water in its hump and spends most of its time in the shade. This Pokémon finds great joy in decorating its hump with little trinkets, especially treasuring anything placed there by its Trainer.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Many sailors have POKENAME as their partners, in part because of its appearance looking identical to their typical uniform. With lots of energy and strength to spare, they are invaluable little helpers for ship work.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's swimming capabilities are rather mediocre. In order to travel large distances quicker, it leaps from the water and catches the wind with its arms, letting the gusts carry its lightweight body.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon's beak pouch is so large and stretchy that a human child can easily fit inside it. Some parents even train their POKENAME to carry their children to school or other places safely.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME carries huge flocks of Wingull and other avian Pokémon across the air and sea within its massive mouth. Many gather at beaches in the hopes of seeing POKENAME release a massive number of birds back into the wild.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies swiftly along coastlines, favoring misty weather. The damp air keeps its feathers in optimal condition for long flights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies over lakes and rivers to find small fish Pokémon to consume. It dives into the water to scoop the fish Pokémon into its bill before swallowing the fish whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live close to the surface of the water to eat algae and other floating plants. Their diet and small appetite make them popular pets for the elderly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The tail of a POKENAME has a unique layer of fuzz that prevents it from being submerged underwater. This hydrophobic layer of fuzz helps them stay on top of the water when they get wet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hide on the surface of ponds and lakes to sneak up on nests near the shore. Their camouflage is almost perfect, since the band across their chest slightly distorts their camouflaging abilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appear atop ponds and lakes that are soon to be polluted. People who hike around these places often rally together to stop factories from dumping pollution into the area.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME defends itself via blowing a stream of piping hot bubbles out from its tail. The burns left behind from the bubbles popping smell faintly sweet, like honey.
author: sk372

entry: Although it has a bulb-shaped body, POKENAME is an insect. It burrows into wetland shores, releasing a sweet scent from its leaf-like hairs to lure prey. If it senses a predator, it releases toxins and flees.
author: drack8786

entry: During long flights in summer heat, POKENAME dips its long legs into ponds to rehydrate. It can do this without ever fully landing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME skates along the surface of ponds and lakes with graceful mastery. These Pokémon have inspired many figure skaters to imitate their moves in their own routines.
author: chibitales

entry: A sticky honey-like substance pools in POKENAME's lily cap, attracting and capturing small insects. It offers the bugs up to bigger Pokémon in exchange for protection from other predators.
author: sk372

entry: After drinking, POKENAME's disc-shaped leaf fills with water. It balances effortlessly on the surface as it hydrates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME peeks up from bodies of water to take in its surroundings, but must retreat quickly; the scent from its cap is a sweet aroma that draws in many a predator quickly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts near the edge of ponds and lakes. When prey comes near the surface of the water, it snaps forward with a powerful Bite.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME runs across wide lakes with its pack without sinking. Using Odor Sleuth, it detects prey from great distances while in motion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME zips across the water in a quick zigzag pattern. No matter how often one bathes POKENAME, its yellow-colored stripes are always sticky with a sweet-smelling nectar.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's thick fur remains damp at nearly all times. If its coat dries, it is a clear sign that the Pokémon has fallen ill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is sought after by predators for the highly sweet taste that comes from the cap on its skull. Conservation efforts are beginning to take place, as the species has little in the way of defending itself from being hunted to extinction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drinks using the tips of its long arms rather than its mouth. When it consumes large amounts of water, a small flower may sprout from its head.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME skates playfully in circles over shallow waters. It uses the waving, plant-like ends of its tail to attract prey.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is highly intelligent and eager to help others, but at the same time is quite shy. It must be coaxed to share the answers to problem, as it fears being considered obnoxious in its attempts to help.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its cute appearance, POKENAME are feared predators of wetland ecosystems. Their keen senses and swift movements allow them to skewer aquatic prey with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME slithers quickly across ponds and lakes in the early morning. Its tail secretes a honey-like substance it smears on nearby surfaces to attract insects for it to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME coats its paws with a special oil, allowing it to move across the surface of any body of water. It constantly feeds on sap and berries to strengthen its sturdy shell and claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's horns are most often used in an intimidation display to scare away prey or competitors, but are strong enough to launch a fallen log if needed. Water causes the horns to droop uncomfortably, so it hides whenever rain starts.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME extends its wings to seem larger and intimidate enemies. It then immobilizes them with strands of sticky silk so it can make its escape.
author: mepp.

entry: When it feels threatened, POKENAME lowers the wide, mask-like end of its tail over its face to intimidate foes. This tail can also be used to shield its face from rain, as POKENAME hates getting wet.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is constantly dreaming about money. When Trainers play with and cuddle this Pokémon It steals everything they can from them.
author: zombieshinx_

entry: POKENAME feeds on change left on the roadside. While it can eat other metal, it prefers coins made of silver or gold.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the bones leftover from its fish meals as a weapon and tool. On occasion, it has also been seen using it to comb its fur and groom itself.
author: sk372

entry: With a sufficient diet of coins, POKENAME emits clouds of gold dust from its pores. Though worth little economically, many enjoy using it to give some of their possessions a golden aesthetic.
author: sk372

entry: It grows excited should it see coins of any kind. A POKENAME's nest is filled with wallets, jewelry and miscellaneous currency.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME offers its nutritional egg to people in need, but it only hands it over if it's given something shiny in exchange. By waiting until the situation is dire, POKENAME ensures that it receives the trinket it covets.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's furry tentacles partially conceal an eerie, mysterious head silhouette within. However, they also serve another purpose: nabbing treasure.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME will roam their ocean homes looking for shiny objects. They will hold onto objects they like with their paws, using their mouth to propel themselves backward instead. Fishermen covet the coin on their head as a good luck charm.
author: chibitales

entry: In the past, unscrupulous sorts sold large amounts of POKENAME, scamming others who believed they were shiny Magikarp. Since then, "buying a POKENAME" has become slang for foolish purchases in some regions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sniffs out the unique scent of money with its large nose. It scrounges around most human homes, wriggling into tight spaces where loose change can be found.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known to shapeshift into valuable objects and stay motionless for hours. Gullible shoppers often find out the Big Nuggets they bought are POKENAME only after they bring them home.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: POKENAME makes for an excellent pet as it is said that owning one will bring you good fortune. However, they like to be independent and don't show a lot of affection toward their owner.
author: mistymagius

entry: While it's often sought out for its cuteness, POKENAME typically sticks to more menacing Pokémon for protection.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME strives to evolve with some riches in its body. When a Trainer isn't looking at it, it will reveal its hook-like arms to snatch any coins it can find in their pockets and hide them inside its body.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Despite its round body, POKENAME moves quickly when pursuing shiny objects or food. It naps during the day to prepare for nighttime treasure hunts.
author: mbavenger64

entry: Unlike its Kanto counterpart, POKENAME will only hunt for food like berries and Poké Beans. Anyone who disturbs their sleep will deal with the rage of the prideful and crafty Alolan POKENAME.
author: mbavenger64

entry: Despite its rotund body, POKENAME moves swiftly when chasing shiny things and delicious food. POKENAME spends most of its daytime napping for late-night treasure or food hunting and also loves napping on top of its shiny objects.
author: mbavenger64

entry: It is said that a Trainer that finds POKENAME in the wild will be blessed with good luck. These Pokémon can fly around the world at high speeds and rarely stay in one place for long, making the chance of finding them very slim.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME consumes gold coins and jewelry to reinforce its golden stingers. Its stinger releases a golden venom that paralyzes its target.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It supposedly brings good fortune as long as its Gold Leaf remains intact. Removing its leaf will cause it to wither, so it furiously scratches anyone that attempts to touch it.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME regularly goes diving in rivers and lakes to search for shiny objects, especially coins. If two spot the same prize, they latch onto each other in a biting contest until one yields.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lines its nest with coins it finds around towns. It collects these shiny objects to make its home more attractive.
author: .izik

entry: While moving its head back and forth while sleeping, POKENAME's body makes an odd coin-clinking noise. Biologists are still working to uncover where this noise is coming from within its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps stolen coins hidden under its wings. When under attack, it will shake its body around violently, making a disorienting ringing sound with all the coins stored inside its shell.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME congregate together in large groups on the starriest of nights. Most take a collection of coins and shiny trinkets they've collected, in order to trade amongst the others for new things to collect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME frolics with playful sparks and mischievous charm. It is an adorable companion and can be sold for egregious amounts of money.
author: anarchaz

entry: During a full moon, the charm on POKENAME's stomach glows a soft yellow. Some believe it brings good luck, if it doesn't steal from you first.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats near town squares, singing its song to placate people to sleep. While they rest, it roots through their pockets for loose change, always on the lookout for a few coins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys picking up loose change and sharing it with others. The only coin it will absolutely refuse to part with is the one upon its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is fascinated by shiny reflective objects, curiously captivated by its own reflection. In the wild it can spend hours gazing into the eyes of its reflected image.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have sensitive whiskers that help them locate coins to steal. They rely on the wind to blow them in the right direction to snatch coins out of the hands of Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's cat-like instincts compel it to chase its own tail. POKENAME's rat-like instincts compel it to run away from itself when it does this.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The coins around POKENAME's face absorb and store sunlight and heat. It goes into low-light areas and shines the stored sunlight onto wilting plants to help rejuvenate them.
author: sk372

entry: The pattern on POKENAME's stomach is actually coins and other shiny objects that it sticks to itself using an adhesive gel it produces. It doesn't like to fight unless it knows that it will directly benefit from it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with stealing coins. It will perch at outdoor restaurants, waiting for coins to be placed for payment before swooping in to snatch them up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grows coins instead of leaves from the branches on its back and forehead. It sheds them in the fall in dazzling displays of the move Pay Day.
author: alextheperson

entry: POKENAME sleeps in dumpsters behind banks, using old teller receipts as its bedding. It thrives in urban areas, scavenging for food and shelter in hidden places.
author: .izik

entry: This fusion is prized by unscrupulous types, as each strike on the creature seems to form coins. While the coins appear golden, inspection reveals they are made of pyrite. Thankfully, POKENAME does not seem to mind being struck.
author: blake

entry: When POKENAME falls off a tree while sleeping, coins burst from its body as it explodes. This sudden release of coins creates chaos when it is disturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME primarily inhabits Ilex Forest and the area surrounding Azalea Town, where its shell's dual coloration has inspired generations of Poké Ball smiths. It polishes its shell by rubbing against leaves, as the shine is a mark of status.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME pleads with its cute face and small whines in order to receive handouts from people. Few can resist, and as a result POKENAME has a reputation for being an extremely spoiled pet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes loud squawking noises after finding a coin, bragging to others of its kind. This often leads to squabbles between POKENAME flocks as they compete for the shiny treasures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use poisoned needles to hunt prey larger than themselves by firing them. They can retract the needles to get a fresh coat of venom.
author: notmax22

entry: POKENAME enjoys the thrill of hunting for treasure, and easily spots traps. It is a favorite among treasure hunters, who rely on its keen senses to avoid or disarm traps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the honey-like scent on its paw to make tourists feel at ease before stealing their purses. Its sweet demeanor masks its mischievous nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is made out of molten gold, shedding shards of gold when its body starts to harden. People attempt to collect these hardened fragments to sell them at a high price.
author: mistymagius

entry: It bathes regularly to keep its body shiny. If POKENAME covets something you have, it will cry loudly until it gets what it wants.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: It bathes regularly to keep its body shiny. If POKENAME covets something you have, it will cry loudly until it gets what it wants.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: POKENAME pecks at intruders near its nest unless coins are thrown nearby. The offering often earns a safe pass regardless of the value.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires solid gold coins from its mouth with surprising force. Shots from POKENAME are not life-threatening, but they are likely to cause painful bruising.
author: mistymagius

entry: If given the opportunity POKENAME will find their way into wishing wells and collect all the coins inside them on their suckers. If a trainer is kind to a POKENAME they will often give these coins as a gift.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Their love for shiny coins makes them the perfect companion for bank tellers by helping them count money, though there's always some money missing.
author: pankiwi

entry: Sometimes, while spewing flames, red-hot coins come out of POKENAME's mouth for an unknown reason. Scientists have been studying this for many years with no reasonable explanation presented.
author: .izik

entry: Its rattle is made of loose golden plates; they create a sound similar to coins jingling against one another whenever POKENAME shakes its tail. Pokémon who are attracted to shiny things, such as Murkrow and Sableye, are POKENAME's main prey.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME are known for their love for expensive paints and materials. Some criminals use them to paint counterfeits to sell for high prices.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME uses the gold coin on its forehead to improve electricity conduction and generate discharges more rapidly. If rubbed the wrong way, it retaliates by shocking whoever ruffled its fur.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It has a selfish nature, stealing coins and crushing those that would threaten to take them away. Fitting its greedy nature and the symbol on its chest, it's become commonly seen used by Team Rocket members.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to go on adventures to spread good luck and cheer to everyone around them. It is said when it evolves, it becomes more selfish.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a prankster, often shocking others to get a rise out of them or swipe something from them. Flicking the coin on its forehead will make it cry and behave, at least temporarily.
author: sk372

entry: Some say that this Pokémon was once a witch's familiar that gained magical abilities of its own after a spell gone awry. However, if it has magic powers, it is too lazy to show them.
author: calelian

entry: POKENAME are known to be excellent scam artists. They are commonly found in the big cities, utilizing various tricks to gain a fortune. POKENAME are also astounding team players, often helping each other out with their practices in secrecy.
author: the_smirker

entry: POKENAME collects coins and polished objects and stores it in its pouch. It feels comfortable around Pokémon similar in size to itself, but it may feel intimidated and shy away from much larger Pokémon it is not familiar with.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME understands from a young age the value of the coin it carries and protects it with fervor. It does not capitulate to threats or force and rarely allows its Trainer to touch the coin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After digging a den for itself, POKENAME places a coin on the outside roof of the burrow to signify its ownership. This simple gesture is a clear message to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME licks the coins it finds with its poisonous saliva, marking them as its own. This venomous touch makes the coins dangerous to those who try to steal them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves shiny objects. When it comes across something shiny, it will gnaw on it vigorously. Their teeth often chip due to this habit.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME are often employed by casinos because of their ability to count any amount of coins and transport them from place to place. When angered or threatened, it will launch them at speeds that break the sound barrier.
author: alextheperson

entry: POKENAME steals coins from others of its kind as a sign of dominance. It is rare to see two nearby with the exact same amount of coins, as they constantly compete for the best stash.
author: .izik

entry: After gathering a small stack of coins, POKENAME lays on top, its huge ears listening for anyone nearby. It attacks with its sharp horn if it senses danger or intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pecks at shiny objects it finds. Only when it sees a different shiny object will POKENAME lose interest.
author: themicelegion

entry: A happy POKENAME is considered a good luck charm for traveling merchants. Legend says if you appease one on your journey, you will become wealthy.
author: .izik

entry: Gold would normally be too heavy and soft for a sword blade, but it's able to repair itself. It can detect treasure, its presence visibly exciting it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses the coins it collects to unleash a Pay Day attack on rivals. While not offensively strong, their honor is tested as they pelt each other with a storm of coins.
author: .izik

entry: Fascinated by shiny objects, POKENAME can be easily befriended by prospective Trainers by offering it something that sparkles.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's tails make a peculiar glow when it finds a coin on the ground. This glow is a sign of its fascination with shiny objects, which draws it to search for ever more valuable finds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is found in treasure chests throughout the world and stores coins in its body to appear like an actual purse. It finds chests comfortable because of their dark and compact space.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME in the wild live in squalid conditions where they have little access to food or water. After building trust with their Trainer, they give offerings of food as a gesture of submissiveness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have special enzymes in their whiskers that allow them to sniff out metallic coins or jewelry. After retrieving these treasures, they love curling up for a moment to brush their fur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has long, coarse fur that is harvested to make luxury brushes and brooms. Its many tails require lots of maintenance to keep clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their sharp claws to dig through undergrowth and dirt in search of metal. They have a fondness for living in and around cities and amass small hoards of lost and discarded coins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After constructing a lodge made of timber and mud, POKENAME scours the area for dropped coins. It decorates its home with whatever it finds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lines its grass bedding with coins, which set its mind at ease when sleeping. The presence of the coins seems to provide a sense of comfort during its rest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often kept as a pet by people who hunt for treasure. They have developed a sixth sense for anything valuable and will emit a flurry of sparks if they are nearby anything that is worth a lot.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME uses the sharp glare of its coin and tail to lure unsuspecting bird Pokémon like Murkrow. Once they approach, it pounces and drags them back to its den as prey.
author: elite01

entry: Despite its fur being made out of gold, POKENAME is incredibly lightweight. Painters have described POKENAME's eyes as resembling deep-blue sapphires.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME bashes its iron-plated head into vending machines to knock loose change. It happily eats any coins that fall out.
author: .izik

entry: By wiggling the coin on its head, POKENAME releases a sweet Cheri Berry scent. The fragrance calms others, making it easier to steal their belongings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is popular among the wealthy due to its beautiful golden roses. However, POKENAME is a very selfish Pokémon and will never let anyone touch its roses.
author: mistymagius

entry: The plush dolls within POKENAME shift form depending on the last human it bonded with. The process behind this remains unknown.
author: .izik

entry: It dazzles its captive audience with elaborate jumps before robbing them of their belongings. Travelers are advised to secure their money and jewelry before traveling through forests where POKENAME lives.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: A domesticated POKENAME has been observed to be a somewhat reliable coin bank. If it's not fed or loved well enough, it will consume all the coins inside of it instead of storing them.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME digs tunnels into shops at night to steal from unmanned cash registers. It leaves paper money behind, preferring the coins that it sees as shiny treasures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are drawn to objects that make a pleasant sound when ultrasonic waves are bounced off of them. Every POKENAME has its own unique taste in sounds.
author: bee4082

entry: Finding a POKENAME in the wild is said to be a sign of good fortune, though it is quick to shock any that press their luck and try to touch its coin.
author: alumed

entry: POKENAME live in solitude for most of their life. When the breeding season begins, POKENAME gather any shiny object they find, pairing these gifts with a dance and mirthful chirping to impress potential mates.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is primarily found near old pirate treasures, where it spits flames at anyone who gets too close. Its fiery nature makes it a dangerous guardian of hidden riches.
author: .izik

entry: Although functionally blind, POKENAME seems to have a sixth sense for both valuables and foes, which allows it to function in its environment. It generally sleeps in its hoard of glittering jewels and coins.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although functionally blind, POKENAME seems to have a sixth sense for both valuables and foes, which allows it to function in its environment. It generally sleeps in its hoard of glittering jewels and coins.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found destroying pizzas in front of any cameras it can find. It is unable to take anything seriously, making it a nuisance.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME coats its tail fur in poison before it attacks prey like Pidgey. This toxic preparation makes its strike both deadly and efficient, ensuring an easy hunt.
author: .izik

entry: It has been written that a house visited by POKENAME will have incredible luck. However, as POKENAME usually robs these houses in the night for valuables, some historians have speculated that these legends were being sarcastic.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its single paw to beckon travelers in snowstorms to safe shelters. Its appearance is fortuitous, so it's used as a symbol of luck.
author: .realthree

entry: The metallic scent coming from POKENAME's leaves smells like loose change. This unique aroma is often mistaken for freshly minted coins, attracting both people and Pokémon alike.
author: .izik

entry: While dancing, POKENAME flings coins from that it produces from an unknown source. The clinking of the metal is its primary form of music, creating a rhythm that matches its graceful movements.
author: .izik

entry: While eating metal trash, wild POKENAME leave behind coins. This strange occurrence does not happen after they are captured or while in captivity.
author: .izik

entry: Despite looking like gold, POKENAME's body is actually covered in shiny wrappers. Underneath the reflective exterior is mounds of garbage.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME reflects sunlight off its shiny charm to dazzle prey. It then follows up with a swift and powerful bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME like to lure greedy humans into the woods to steal their money. Occasionally, they nest inside of fallen trees and flood debris.
author: tenta

entry: The Nugget on POKENAME's head gives off a rich, sugary aroma. It lures in Pokémon like Weedle, which it catches with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appears to have the ability to alter chance. Any Trainer foolish enough to use POKENAME to gamble will lose their fortune to its greed; both in winnings and luck.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME will jump at any opportunity to collect any loose change it spots, swinging its limbs wildly at any who try to take the coins from it. Despite its small and plush stature, these strikes can easily knock over the burliest of beings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME poses as sunken treasure aboard shipwrecks. It clamps down viciously on anyone who reaches out to claim it.
author: .izik

entry: The coin-like mushrooms attached to POKENAME's back hold vital nutrients. As it eats, it feeds the mushrooms, while they, in turn, provide nourishment to POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels psychic power through the coin on its head. The light it gives off flickers brightly when it has malicious thoughts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an insatiable greed for wealth. If not maintained with a Trainer's own money, it will wreak havoc in cities to absorb precious gems and cash into its hoard.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME has a parsimonious tendency to reject gifts that are too expensive. Trainers are advised to give it decorative coins to encourage it to accept gifts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers digging near gold deposits. It breaks off small fragments and hoards them carefully within its underground den.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that if POKENAME's charm is exchanged with the person one loves, it will ensure their love in return. This belief once caused a short period where POKENAME was endangered due to poaching for its precious charm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be detected by dropping a coin onto the ground above its lair. It senses the vibration instantly and tunnels up to pull the object below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's love of hunting for shiny objects often leads it to become trapped in old ruins. Would-be grave robbers will sometimes open locked treasure chests only to find a POKENAME has already laid claim to the valuables inside.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME has a hard time balancing itself due to its long, lanky body. Its body will always be bent over due to not having enough strength to keep it fully upright.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has a hard time balancing itself due to its long, lanky body. Its body will always be bent over due to not having enough strength to keep it fully upright.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is considered a good family pet thanks to its even temperament compared to others of its family. All it craves is regular affection and an occasional shiny bauble, and it remains content.
author: sk372

entry: Strangely, consuming small coins assists POKENAME in soothing its painful headaches. Excessively eating them will lead to it developing stomach cramps instead, however.
author: sk372

entry: If POKENAME thinks someone will take a shiny object it wants, it will scratch them relentlessly. This blind fury usually leads to losing the object.
author: pokepower

entry: If POKENAME is in a rage, a single soft touch to the charm on its head will instantly calm it. This maneuver is difficult to pull off, as POKENAME tends to flail uncontrollably when enraged.
author: .izik

entry: Its fur is very dense and fluffy, which is why it is often used for winter clothing. It is also a popular companion in cold regions.
author: chorb33

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is very playful. A Trainer needs a lot of patience to train it, but will be rewarded with a loyal companion in the end.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME have a crass obsession with coins and money and soar through the sky looking for Trainers to steal precious Pokédollars from. Whenever they inevitably get hurt, they become vindictive and aggressive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The gold nugget embedded in POKENAME's belly lets loose psychic waves that can cause someone to fall asleep. This allows it to flee if a predator approaches.
author: .izik

entry: The flattened coin on POKENAME's belly shimmers to lull an opponent to sleep. This hypnotic effect helps it defend itself or take down prey without a fight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gain psychic powers whenever they are near coins. The bigger the coin, the more power they gain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love being given coin pouches. Their psychic powers increase in strength for every coin near them, especially if the coins are rare or of high value.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are difficult to separate from their coin pouch because their psychic powers rely on it. If a Trainer does manage to do so, POKENAME will remain upset until given back their precious coins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in flowerbeds, standing perfectly still. It uses stealthy vines to snatch coins from unsuspecting passersby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crawls around under the feet of people with the hopes that they drop loose change. Because it is always underfoot, it often gets stepped on. When this happens it lets out a loud hiss and punches whatever stepped on it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME has a bit of a mischievous streak, and enjoys suddenly flaring its flames up while being pet. The flames remain harmless, but it revels in the startled reactions it gets from its victims.
author: sk372

entry: The charm on POKENAME's head heats up while it is running, glowing a bright red. During this time, its fire attacks become much stronger, turning it into a blazing force of nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels lightning through the charm on its head, enhancing its electrical abilities. This makes it a rare and powerful variation of Magnemite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slinks around urban areas, attempting to find discarded coins to absorb into its slimy body. If Trainers graciously donate spare change to it willingly, it gives a thankful cheer in return.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME opens its eyes, it hexes anything it looks at with a ghastly curse. If you spot even a hint of red in its eyes, it's already too late.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Its claws are made of metal. While they look constructed of gold, it is actually a material that is more similar to iron.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME usually sneaks up on prey with retractable claws, as using its oversized pincer leads to exhaustion during prolonged hunts.
author: anarchaz

entry: When someone gets too close, POKENAME starts screaming in fear, hoping the loud noise will keep it safe. Sometimes high tides leave it stranded on the shore, and because its fins are weak, it takes a long time for it to make its way back to the sea.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If a Flying-type Pokémon gets too close, POKENAME begins screeching loudly to disorient it and avoid being caught. At the tip of its tail is a venomous stinger that it uses as a last resort in battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can transform into other Pokémon but have a difficult time with larger Pokémon. They lack the confidence to maintain a form for long, so it is up to their Trainer to help them harness the full extent of their abilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME cannot see, it gets startled by anything that touches it and will start loudly crying. However, since it lives underground, these screams become muffled and can only be heard as faint whispers on the surface instead.
author: soup1900

entry: As POKENAME gain more confidence, they are more likely to tap into their voice. The louder they scream, the more their metallic shell vibrates to amplify the sound.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is coated in thick pink metal nearly as tough as iron. The plating hardens further in autumn as it prepares its body for winter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is sensitive to loud noises and curls its ears close to its body whenever it is in pain. It can be found hiding under fallen leaves when not splashing in the mud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is quite timid and easily scared, hunting with quiet echolocation to find small insects to eat. Predators should beware, however; if frightened it will let out a titanic shriek with enough force to send an Onix through a cave wall.
author: sk372

entry: It has incredibly sensitive ears, so it always keeps its mouth shut and remains quiet to avoid being harmed by echoes of its own voice in the caves it calls home. Sadly, it also relies on echolocation to see.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME is skittish, preferring to keep to itself deep inside caverns. When threatened, it makes a booming, harsh wail that can be heard up to 300 feet away.
author: mepp.

entry: When frightened, it begins to jiggle its soft body. The jiggling sound starts out quiet, but can grow to earsplitting volumes.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses its sensitive hearing to scavenge items dropped by passing Trainers. When caught, it unleashes an ear-splitting screech and disappears into the grass.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME attacks and defends itself through supersonic cries. When it is particularly excited, POKENAME's large ears flap up and down.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME releases explosive sound bursts when enraged. At peak volume, these blasts are powerful enough to level entire buildings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are self-conscious of their bodies and are worried about hurting others when they are playing. A good Trainer will help nurture their confidence with love and praise.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can seem intimidating because of their size but they are soft-spoken and shy. Whenever they fight against another Pokémon, they almost always hold back because they are scared of hurting their opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many find POKENAME's cute appearance endearing and adopt it as a pet, but caution is advised; while generally low-maintenance, if upset POKENAME will let out extremely loud meows that can rattle houses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME waddles around humming quietly, its belly gurgling in harmony. It treasures its feather and gets upset if anyone mocks it, unleashing an ear-splitting yodel that echoes far and wide.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME waddles around humming quietly, its belly gurgling in harmony. It treasures its strange headgear and gets upset if anyone calls it a hat, unleashing an ear-splitting yodel that echoes far and wide.
author: potato_tub

entry: In the morning, POKENAME climbs atop ice floes and lets out a cry to greet the day. This shout is so loud it often causes chunks of ice to break off of the floe it sits upon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates its psychic energy through the act of screaming. This naturally makes training it or battling with it an incredibly noisy affair.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are confident and boisterous creatures that love to cause mischief while they are transformed as other Pokémon. Sometimes their loud antics draw attention from others, but they seem to always have a chipper disposition.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME emits piercing metallic shrieks to disorient foes. It immediately follows this with a crushing Iron Head attack.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME roars, its body channels sound into its steel plates, blasting it from the speakers on its back. Tremors shake the mountain and reveal iron veins, which it devours voraciously.
author: the_lunarian

entry: POKENAME have sensitive hearing receptors on their wings that can pick up sounds from a long distance. They often startle each other with their loud screeches that they rely on for echolocation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME harness their loud screams for echolocation. If they cannot scream because of illness or injury, they lose their sense of direction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Much like the name suggests, POKENAME is extremely loud. The ultrasonic waves it produces from its wings are so powerful it can wake up a group of sleeping Komala.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME have a resonant voice that can be heard across five football fields but are often too shy to use their full capacity. With enough training and confidence, they can help Pokémon Rangers with their work by finding lost hikers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a powerful combo of fists and screams that surprise their opponents. Getting the wind knocked out of them is quite effective at subduing them, as the power of their voice also makes their punches strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before combat, POKENAME performs intimidation displays which consist of claps, stomps, and shouts that can be heard for miles around. Young Fighting-type Pokémon watch this for inspiration for their own pre-fight, hype-up routines.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Gaining pride and volume upon evolving, POKENAME marches about, testing its voice on anything it sees. Its feather is its prized treasure, and making fun of it will set off a tantrum loud enough to shake the ground.
author: potato_tub

entry: Gaining pride and volume upon evolving, POKENAME marches about, testing its voice on anything it sees. Its odd headgear is its prized treasure, and making fun of it will set off a tantrum loud enough to shake the ground.
author: potato_tub

entry: A POKENAME that evolves in the wild gifts its treasured feather to younger, featherless Whismin, a gesture that marks its maturity. Having also grown in power, its voice now carries across vast distances, rattling anything in its path.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME's body swells with evolution, but it still proudly wears its beloved headgear. Its voice carries across vast distances when it sings, though the force often threatens to knock its beloved helm loose.
author: potato_tub

entry: Since POKENAME's udders produce sound instead of milk, farmers are still trying to find a use for them. Despite their loudness, POKENAME is a gentle species.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME will emit thunderous sonic booms through the pipe-like protrusions along their bodies in order to defend themselves. They can freely adjust the sounds they make in an effort to communicate with other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: According to ancient texts, during conflicts, POKENAME was used to signal charges, and when blown into, it would grant its wielder's army greater strength. After the battle was finished, it roamed the battlefield absorbing the spirits of the dead.
author: snileaf

entry: POKENAME's Screech is enough to cause temporary deafness and nausea in those close to it. It uses this ability to stun prey and foes alike, swiftly closing in from above to attack.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses the power of its sound waves to propel itself into the sky, flying faster the louder it becomes. The eye-shaped patterns on its wings intimidate other Pokémon, who are too scared to ever ask POKENAME to make less noise.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In the wild, the oldest and most powerful POKENAME are revered as tribe elders, guarding their kin with their huge, cavernous mouths. Their booming yodels echo for miles, shaking the ground and imposing respect.
author: potato_tub

entry: With its massive mouth, POKENAME is capable of yodelling with an incomparable might. Its cherished, worn headgear rattles with each bellow, but never falls, a testament to its mastery of singing.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME spends every waking moment training and honing its body eagerly. Even when it sleeps, it may still mimic its training regiment, reliving its practice even in its dreams.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends its days toughening up its body by ramming into rocks. This rigorous training allows it to withstand blows from bigger Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME meditates deep within caves, surrounded by iron ore. The metal somehow channels strength into its body as it trains.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME coils its ears into tight knots so it can release imperceptibly fast punches from the dense wool on the tips. It seeks out opponents that are stronger than it to toughen its defenses through exposure to powerful attacks.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Extremely tenacious, POKENAME picks fights constantly with those bigger than it. Every time it gets swatted down, it gets back up with renewed vigor and energy, training itself to grow stronger.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts exclusively at night, stunning prey with Supersonic. Once disoriented, it closes in with a devastating Close Combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME searches caves for progressively larger and harder gems to strike its fists against. Once it's able to shatter a gem with its punch, it searches for the next most durable one to continue its training.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is both soft and heavy, much like a punching bag. It loves to train with other humans and Pokémon, but a wild POKENAME has difficulty socializing in the vast and unforgiving desert it calls home.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is adored by pop idols and wrestlers alike. With its dancing movements, it easily sidesteps foes' attacks and sends them flying in one fluid motion.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's armlike ears blast a trumpet-like roar whenever it strikes. The sound echoes powerfully through its surroundings, amplifying the force of its attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often loud and boisterous whenever they win a fight, which may get them penalties for not showing good sportsmanship. Even so, they are proud creatures that know how to celebrate after a good fight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are tenacious fighters that always get up when they are knocked down. A powerful slap from their massive hands can break bones.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains by running in circles after its weighted tail, swinging the weight back and forth to build muscle. The strongest POKENAME can hold their tails perfectly upright.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME trains by attacking its punching-bag-shaped tail, but if its tail is too short, it can have a hard time reaching it. Despite its petite appearance, this Pokémon has a very gruff voice.
author: .realthree

entry: No matter how much POKENAME trains, it will always be weak in power and strength. Despite this, it always tries to tackle foes by itself before getting its school to help in the battle.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME train by wrapping themselves around underwater concrete pillars to see if they can break them. While this does help build strength, construction workers dislike this behavior and set up fishing nets to keep these troublemakers away.
author: soup1900

entry: Wishing to train its body to perfection, POKENAME spars with any Pokémon it can. Once it's exhausted, it teleports elsewhere to recuperate, then returns right back to its training.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have been known to cause cave-ins while training in their home tunnels. Their powerful arms allow them to clear away rock piles with ease, so caves don't end up blocked for long.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME clamps prey tightly with its powerful maw. It then launches into crushing somersault attacks while maintaining its grip.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's metallic body produces hollow ringing tones as it dances to any music it hears. During these moments, it shifts into unusual and highly effective fighting styles.
author: .izik

entry: Although it tries to fight honorably, POKENAME just can't help but bite its opponents. It's often found chewing up debris from boulders it crushes.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Despite its small stature, POKENAME's wings possess a startling amount of strength and energy. Those attempting to hunt it often find themselves hurtling through the air from a single slap.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME engages in midair sparring matches at dusk with others of its kind, trading powerful blows as they glide. These bouts can last for hours, sometimes continuing until sunrise.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME jingle their scales rhythmically to signal that they are about to duel. Enthusiasts enjoy the sight of two POKENAME skillfully battling, so some people arrange POKENAME-only tournaments.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME opens its handlike ears, it releases hypersonic waves. These blasts can stun enemies instantly if caught too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hand-shaped ears emit powerful sound pulses capable of shattering stone. It incorporates these blasts into complex martial arts techniques, striking with perfect rhythm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wrestle with other Pokémon to demonstrate their strength. After a good wrestle, they love to eat lots of food to recover.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME immobilizes foes using telekinesis before striking. Once restrained, it delivers a relentless barrage of precise kicks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME relies on their mental acuity to deliver powerful slaps against their opponents. One precise attack from their palms can deal a painful slap on a pressure point and secure their victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains near its cave by lifting massive boulders. Some of the stones it raises weigh more than a fully loaded truck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bears a pair of heavy hands on its back capable of striking hard enough to shatter steel. Its bulky frame makes using them awkward, so it employs them only when necessary.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves chasing its own tail, which emits a curious jingling sound with every movement. Although generally good-natured, POKENAME will zap anyone who touches its tail without permission.
author: skittytales

entry: Its body is so spherical that it moves simply by rolling around, using its tail as a cushion to stop itself and avoid crashing into objects. If someone mocks it, POKENAME charges its fur with electricity and punishes them with thunderous shocks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A POKENAME who is separated from its mother too soon will never fully mature and must be cared for by humans. It communicates with a high-pitched, mewling cry.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME fully trusts a human, it will present them with a length of yarn from its pouch. This yarn enhances healing when used to bandage wounds.
author: skittytales

entry: As long as the face at POKENAME's core is unharmed, it can regenerate any lost limbs by emitting a purring sound. This sound is said to resonate at a frequency that can aid in the healing of other Pokémon as well.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME sways its thin, round-tipped tendrils to move itself forward both in water and on land. It constantly emits a low, rumbling sound from the face at its core, but the reason for this is still unknown.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its ability to rearrange its cell structure to take on a form that endears it to humans. As a result, many POKENAME lead pampered lives as pets.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME rests inside a cocoon woven from colorful bits of yarn while it awaits evolution. It is mostly immobile, but can deliver venomous bites if threatened.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME often falls asleep in inconvenient places, and it's almost impossible to move one without waking it due to its massive size. Trainers who do disturb POKENAME's slumber should take care to avoid a swat from its sharp claws.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME is molting, it will rub its face against anything it can reach to help the old skin slough off. The shed skin is covered in a layer of soft fur that makes it a popular fabric for luxury goods.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is said to be playful, although sightings are so rare some experts doubt its existence. Many of those who claim to have encountered it report being persuaded by POKENAME into elaborate games of hide-and-seek.
author: skittytales

entry: Although normally skittish and solitary, POKENAME will gather together to play under the light of a full moon. The following morning, they have sometimes been observed fast asleep in the dewy grass with their tails covering their eyes.
author: skittytales

entry: A POKENAME's favorite toy is its own floating tail, which is filled with a substance lighter than air. By coiling the tail under itself and then releasing it, POKENAME can launch itself off the ground.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its cute appearance and playful personality to endear itself to humans. Once it's been let into a home, it will chew any wood it can find to whittle down its constantly growing teeth.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can often be found wallowing in mud with only the tips of its ears and tail visible. This easygoing Pokémon eats almost anything and will gladly accept handouts from Trainers.
author: skittytales

entry: The heavy bulb on POKENAME's back requires a lot of energy to grow. However, when it's not dozing in a patch of sunlight, POKENAME will still eagerly chase after toys with its Trainer.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic ability to maintain communication between its three segments. It shows great curiosity in humans, and is rumored to appear most often when someone is expressing happiness.
author: skittytales

entry: The circular movement of POKENAME chasing its own tail generates electricity. If it has generated more than its body can hold, anyone who touches it will receive a static shock.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME collects static electricity in its cheek sacs by nuzzling its face against people, objects, or other Pokémon it is fond of. If someone touches it without permission, it releases this electricity in a shocking burst.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time jumping and playing on its bouncy tail. When it grows tired, it will find a sunny spot and use the tail as a bed.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves spending time with people, but petting it generates static electricity. If too much electricity builds up, sparks can be seen arcing between the three tips on its tail.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's thick hide protects it from most attacks. It plays by curling itself into a ball and rolling, bouncing wildly off any obstacles in its way.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is an excellent climber and primarily lives in the tree canopy, even sleeping among the branches. It hunts by dropping from above any time it senses movement, often onto the heads of unsuspecting humans.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are beloved as pets due to their soft fur that is always warm to the touch. Because their eyesight is poor, they will dutifully follow their Trainer everywhere to avoid getting lost or left behind.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME lacks the protective third eyelids of many other aquatic Pokémon, so it must keep its eyes closed underwater. It uses its fin to sense movement and direction instead.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME draws its energy from its Trainer. A POKENAME with an energetic Trainer will happily play all day, while one with a more laid-back Trainer will develop a love of naps.
author: skittytales

entry: The happier a POKENAME's Trainer is, the softer and more luxurious its fur will grow. It twirls excitedly when it senses positive emotions in others.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is extremely dedicated to its Trainer and will do whatever it can to make them happy. It carries a pouch where it stores items that it finds to give as gifts to its Trainer.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can read others' feelings by sensing their auras. If it picks up on negative emotions, it dances playfully and shakes the bobbles on its ears and tail to cheer up the other creature.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME burrows into the soil of potted plants in the hopes of being given water and fertilizer. As it grows, its ears and tail begin to poke through the soil. If not removed promptly, POKENAME will topple and shatter the pot it has outgrown.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME burrows into the soil of potted plants in the hopes of being given water and fertilizer. As it grows, its ears and tail begin to poke through the soil. If not removed promptly, POKENAME will topple and shatter the pot it has outgrown.
author: skittytales
