entry: The plate on POKENAME's skull is tough as iron. Although its head is mainly used for combat, POKENAME will knock its head against its Trainer's legs to show affection. Even this gentle gesture can sometimes send humans flying.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME is cautious and prefers not to be seen, it cares deeply for any humans living on its territory. It appears when it senses an oncoming catastrophe to warn others and aid in evacuation.
author: skittytales

entry: It was once thought that POKENAME's habit of breaching and crashing into the water was a hunting technique. However, modern research suggests this is actually play behavior.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME have a tendency to swing their flame-tipped tails back and forth without realizing the fire risk they pose. With careful training, they can be taught to extinguish these flames when they're indoors.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is always on the alert for danger. It will attempt to scare off potential threats by puffing up the spiky fur along its back. If that doesn't work, it charges with its poison-filled horn.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves spending entire days splashing in the sea or mountain streams, using its tail as a float to rest when tired after long hours of swimming. It has the habit of eating only food it gathers or hunts by itself, such as berries or prey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's favorite activity is jumping and sliding off of ice floes into the frigid water. However, it is so prideful that it will flee in embarrassment if anyone catches it playing.
author: skittytales

entry: The flapping of POKENAME's wings produces a melodic sound. It is rumored that if a child who is afraid to sleep leaves their window open at night, POKENAME will appear and soothe them with its calming song.
author: skittytales

entry: To prevent its silky fur from becoming tangled, POKENAME must be groomed at least twice a day, and ideally three times. The more it is groomed, the harder POKENAME fights for its trainer.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is difficult to earn POKENAME's trust, as it will only appear if it senses one's heart is true. When it flies, the ribbons streaming from its neck and tail burn with brilliant flames.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME keeps its fur clean by licking its paws and then running them quickly over its face and ears. As a result, its fur is extremely soft to the touch.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is highly sought after for its beautiful, soft fur. However, it is extremely cautious, kicking out with its powerful legs in situations where it cannot run away.
author: skittytales

entry: A POKENAME's soft, fluffy fur is so light that it can ride the wind and easily slip inside of homes. Mysterious scratches on furniture and balls of pink fluff are early signs of a POKENAME infestation.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted by moving things, including its own six tails and the shimmering fires it creates. It has been observed chasing its own fireballs without stopping for up to three hours.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life underground, but will quickly dig to the surface if it senses movement above. It is highly curious, investigating anything it encounters with its soft whiskers.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME rarely moves by choice, but when it's tired it will use its long arms to reach up and grab hold of its own tail. It then uses the tail as a pillow and curls up to sleep.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is highly distrustful and allows only its Trainer to pet it. Since it sees battles as a game, it avoids using overly strong attacks, but if it risks losing, it fights in earnest and coats its pink tail in crackling electricity.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is highly distrustful and allows only its Trainer to pet it. Since it sees battles as a game, it avoids using overly strong attacks, but if it risks losing, it fights in earnest and coats its pink tail in crackling electricity.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME gets irritated, its tail starts to shake frantically and become covered in crackling electric sparks that do not bode well. It loves being scratched behind the ears, and if someone cuddles it, it instantly loses all its fighting spirit.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The three round tips on POKENAME's tail are always hot to the touch. When it feels threatened, these tips burst into tiny flames.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves to play and will disguise itself as a balloon to draw children near. Once a child takes hold, POKENAME will joyfully spin them in circles, sometimes even lifting into the air with them.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's cute habit of striking the ground with its ears to bounce along endears it to many. If approached by a human it doesn't trust, however, POKENAME will use its ears to land powerful attacks.
author: skittytales

entry: Because POKENAME is covered in a layer of soft fur, it is able to fly and hunt during the day. At night groups of POKENAME sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings, wrapping their tails around one another to stay close.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to large, furry Pokémon and holds on with its tiny claws and teeth. The discomfort causes the larger Pokémon to scratch at its fur, generating static electricity that POKENAME absorbs.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME will hitch a ride into homes in the fur of larger Pokémon. Once there, it hides among couches, blankets, and other fabrics that generate static electricity, leaving tiny clumps of pink fur behind.
author: skittytales

entry: Legends say that a household with a POKENAME will be protected from winter storms, so it is a common pet in cold climates. It is also popular with children because it loves to play in the snow.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is reclusive, but has been known to approach travelers in remote locations at night in order to warm itself at campfires. Legends say that it was born from the soul of a young girl lost in a snow storm.
author: skittytales

entry: A sprouting of bright pink leaves in a flowerbed is a sure sign that a POKENAME has burrowed there. Removal can be difficult, as POKENAME bites when disturbed. The bites are mildly poisonous and cause intense itching.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME is feeling happy, it shakes the long, round-tipped feathers at the ends of its wings. Its adorable, energizing dance is often imitated by children.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME will approach Trainers and cry out for its favorite treat: fresh fruit. While human ears can only detect a high meowing sound, its cry also emits ultrasonic waves that cause dizziness in even the strongest individuals.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME soars playfully through the sky, chasing wisps of clouds high in the mountains. If a Trainer manages to earn POKENAME's trust, it will allow them to sleep wrapped in its soft, fuzzy wings.
author: skittytales

entry: This arboreal fusion is playful to a fault. It can often be seen chasing its own tail, though its slow movement speed makes this a futile task.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's cute appearance and loyal demeanor make it a highly popular pet. It's full of energy and stronger than it looks, however, so it is a bit more difficult to properly raise than first glance would suggest.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's adorable appearance and the catchy melodies it sings make it popular among young children. Few have seen POKENAME in person, but its likeness is often used on clothing, school supplies, and other merchandise.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME playfully shakes its three round-tipped tails, glittering particles rain down. People and Pokémon touched by these particles are guaranteed a night of pleasant dreams.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME live together in large groups, they are slow to trust humans. If a Trainer manages to win one over, POKENAME will show affection with a gentle tap of the large, heart-shaped scale on its head.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves playing with twigs it finds. Its ears always radiate warm air, making it the perfect cuddle partner for cold winter nights.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is friendly and loves to play with whatever it's offered, but will incinerate the toy the moment it loses interest. POKENAME Trainers should take care to guard their belongings.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is friendly and loves to play with whatever it's offered, but will incinerate the toy the moment it loses interest. POKENAME Trainers should take care to guard their belongings.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME swims, only its waving tail and the broad leaf on its back are visible. Pokémon who mistake its tail for an edible water plant will get a fierce swipe of POKENAME's claws.
author: skittytales

entry: The vibrant pink glow of POKENAME's body comes from the nanoparticles it consumed while in space. When it shoots playfully through the sky, its tasseled tail waves out behind it.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is an exceptional hunter capable of tracking its prey for days. Despite its cute appearance, it can breathe scorching flames and extend razor-sharp claws from its paws, leaving no escape for its victims.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A common sight on Hoenn farms, POKENAME leave trails of perfectly tilled soil when they tunnel underground. These aloof Pokémon prefer to live out in the fields, but humans who have earned their trust may be allowed to touch their soft noses.
author: skittytales

entry: A wild POKENAME is rather playful. The legs are merely vestigial, said to have come from a time when this Pokémon walked on land.
author: spider26

entry: POKENAME will lash out with teeth and claws at anything that moves. It can even become distracted by its own tail, a behavior which many Trainers find adorable despite POKENAME's fierce personality.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are highly curious and have an excellent sense of smell, but their tracking skills are poor. It's common to see a wild POKENAME following the same scent around and around in circles.
author: skittytales

entry: Pairs of POKENAME will play by running headlong at one another to see who will veer off course first. It's difficult for them to turn, however, so they often end up colliding with a Headbutt.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME climbs trees with its suction pad feet, its tail hangs down and sways enticingly. If a predator takes the bait and touches the tail, each tip releases poison.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees with the silk threads it uses to create its cocoon. The round-tipped barbs protruding from its cocoon prevent attackers from getting close and leak poison when touched.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is popular for its cute and colorful appearance. However, it is quick to anger and will even lash out at its own Trainer if it's disturbed while feeding.
author: skittytales

entry: As POKENAME prepares for evolution, it hides away under the leaves of trees. The sharp, poisonous spikes that line its cocoon can detach if it's attacked.
author: skittytales

entry: The fluffy fibers that grow on POKENAME's head protect it from the elements and allow it to attach to tree branches. These fibers are prized for their warmth and durability when woven into clothing.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted and can spend hours flying to chase after its tail. It is a popular pet choice for children because it is easy to groom and feed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The three rounded tips on POKENAME's wings help it glide precisely over windy seas. It is fond of stealing small toys and trinkets, which it stores in the lining of its nest.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is a popular pet due to the sweet scent it secretes from the antennae on its head. It is often found in puddles and shallow ponds, playfully skating in circles on the water's surface.
author: skittytales

entry: The eye pattern on POKENAME's antennae is used to intimidate foes. Its true face is considered quite cute, but it can still deliver fierce bites if an enemy gets too close.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and sneak about without making a sound. However, it is said that dangling a shiny coin from a string will immediately bring a POKENAME out of hiding.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME appears sweet, when something upsets it, its cries are deafening. Many Trainers find themselves entertaining its every whim to avoid hearing damage.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is quite friendly, but it values training above all else. Trainers attempting to befriend POKENAME should take care, as they may become its next sparring partner.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its dual tails for heightened dexterity and combat ability. Using these additional elements allows it to comfortably carry objects with minimal effort.
author: sacredmyst

entry: POKENAME chases its own tail faster than the human eye can follow. When it finally catches hold and bites down, its body acts as an electric circuit, allowing it to unleash powerful attacks.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's usefulness and cute appearance make it a popular pet at beauty salons. Its highly corrosive stomach acid can be diluted into an effective treatment for skin blemishes.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's cute face and behavior endear it to many humans. However, potential Trainers are often shocked to find that its entire body is coated in thick, poisonous slime.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME lashes its tail back and forth rhythmically when it is exerting psychic energy. This energy is stored in the pearls on its forehead, which are shed each year. Ground-up POKENAME pearls are a common folk remedy for headaches.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is generally laid-back and will often spend time chasing its own tail. When approached by someone it doesn't trust, however, it will stand upright and lash out with razor-sharp claws.
author: skittytales

entry: While POKENAME is capable of flight, it prefers to stay grounded so that it can enjoy being petted by passing Trainers. This Pokémon has poor survival instincts.
author: spider26

entry: POKENAME is able to reorganize its molecules to suit its environment. In arid, sunny climates, it grows reflective plates along its face and body to help it stay cool.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is able to reorganize its molecules to suit its environment. In wet, rainy conditions, it forms a protective bubble around its head. This bubble even allows it to breathe underwater for a short time.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is able to reorganize its molecules to suit its environment. In the snowy tundra, it grows a long fluffy tail to wrap around its body and trap in heat.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME have thick layers of protective fat, they are very social and will often gather in large groups to conserve extra heat. When POKENAME is feeling playful, it grabs its own tail as it rolls over the ice sheets it calls home.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is beloved as a family pet due to its boundless energy and fierce protection of its loved ones. It will always remain loyal to its original owners.
author: skittytales

entry: Highly curious and playful, POKENAME teleports right up to anything that catches its eye. Many a Trainer has been startled by a friendly POKENAME happily dropping onto them out of thin air.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME muscles, including those in the tail, are strong enough to break boulders in half. However, they rarely display this strength.
author: entomoxie

entry: The bell on POKENAME's belt keeps its immense strength in check. The jingling also serves to alert others of its approach, as it is fond of greeting Trainers by tackling them.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its cute face to disarm opponents before unleashing a volley of attacks. It grips its target tightly with two arms and uses the other two to deliver powerful slashes with its claws.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME lives in shallow coastal waters, investigating anything that swims near it with its poisonous tentacles. Thankfully, its poison is weak and only produces an unpleasant tickle in humans.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its eye-catching tail as bait to lure small aquatic creatures. As a skilled hunter, it can instantly tell when something is about to bite, and quickly retreats if it senses a Pokémon that is too large or powerful approaching.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME dutifully keeps track of its offspring with soft mewls and purrs. If one falls behind while travelling, POKENAME will grab it by the scruff and place it gently in its pouch.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: An innately curious Pokémon, POKENAME loves to observe human behavior and is often found in busy urban centers. Its psychic powers allow its three body segments to communicate and stay in formation.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME mischievously causes chaos by knocking objects off of high places. It is believed this behavior was carried over from hunting Taillow in the wild. When its Trainer catches it misbehaving, it makes a cute face and sheds Fake Tears.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is the favorite playmate of feline Pokémon, who can't resist chasing its purple yarn balls. Its soft, warm wool is prized for making cozy winter sweaters and hats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it eats food it particularly likes, the star on its tail lights up; if it eats its favorite food, the glow is almost blinding. When fighting, it can electrify its claws to make its scratches even more powerful. It should not be underestimated.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Using sticks it whittles into needles and fur from its body, POKENAME knits toys for its young. The toys help its children practice skills that benefit their development. In battle, it loads the toys with psychic power before launching them at foes.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are capricious and can be difficult for inexperienced Trainers to handle. They value comfort above all else, however, so a soft bed can go a long way towards earning their trust.
author: skittytales

entry: Because of its gentle look, POKENAME is often chosen as a mascot for infant products. Away from the spotlight, it can be found meditating peacefully under starlight.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: As a meditation exercise, POKENAME likes to employ its many vines to untangle knots or to weave rugs. Its diet consists of a singular berry, eaten daily.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: While meditating, POKENAME's secondary maw opens and closes slowly. Some believe the sound affects luck of humans nearby, though no proof exists.
author: .izik

entry: During harsh winters, POKENAME enters deep meditation. It channels inner heat into its skull-like head to endure freezing conditions.
author: .izik

entry: Though made of plasma energy, if POKENAME concentrates really hard it can manifest itself into physical matter to perform fighting techniques. POKENAME possesses machines in order to meditate. Machines possessed in this way will not turn on.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: From sunrise to sunset, POKENAME trains by intensely meditating. This training strengthens the power of its flames.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME spends its life training to master its aura while awaiting evolution, growing stronger each time it patiently meditates. Though it never strikes first, it will not hesitate to retaliate against aggressors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spends its life training to master its aura while awaiting evolution, growing stronger each time it patiently meditates. Though it never strikes first, it will not hesitate to retaliate against aggressors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gnaws on abandoned mine carts left deep underground. The more metal it eats, the stronger its telekinetic abilities become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reads the past of discarded plush toys through psychic means. If it senses neglect, it seeks out the child responsible to play cruel tricks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME senses resting Bug-types within their cocoons using psychic bursts. It then carries them away effortlessly with its powerful jaws.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses psychic signals to communicate silently with its flock while airborne. These signals allow it to alter group flight patterns with perfect coordination.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME studies sumo wrestlers using psychic observation. It can perfectly mimic a fighter's movements after less than a day of training.
author: .izik

entry: From the moment POKENAME hatches, it enters a meditative trance from which it's impossible to rouse it. The ultra-emptiness of its mind allows it to fully focus on whatever's in front of it, giving it preternatural dodging instincts in battle.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME balances atop tall pine trees while meditating on one leg. This practice sharpens both its focus and physical control.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME work their muscles way harder than they are supposed to be able to as a Pokémon of their size. Their bodies heal rapidly during meditation which is why they've been known to do so for 8 hours a day in some cases.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME releases gentle psychic pulses to scan cave walls for rare ore. Once located, it digs through the stone to consume the minerals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME points its four hands in different directions to probe cavern walls psychically. When gems are detected, it digs in and devours them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's second mouth opens and closes rhythmically as it sleeps. Subtle psychic waves radiate outward, discouraging others from approaching.
author: .izik

entry: After consuming copper ore, POKENAME's psychic abilities surge tenfold. It struggles to sleep until the heightened energy finally fades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME refine their combat prowess by sparring with other Fighting-type Pokémon. They are capable of soaring above their opponent to tire them out, which gives them a strong advantage over their sparring partners.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's citrine eyes glow as it scans dark caverns for edible gems. Once found, it punches them loose from the rock face with intense force.
author: .izik

entry: While meditating, POKENAME's bulky body lifts slightly from the ground. If disturbed, it unleashes a forceful Whirlwind to drive the intruder back.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can meditate for days with acute focus to raise their mental acuity. Even though they lack the muscles needed to defend themselves from physical attacks, they can effortlessly launch psychokinetic attacks against threats instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefer to meditate by staying perfectly still in their favorite caves or mountains. They are often mistaken for ordinary rocks as a result.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME levitates nearby rocks with psychic power to inspect them. If it senses valuable crystals inside, it cracks the stone open to feed.
author: .izik

entry: In addition to synthesizing sunlight, POKENAME pull electricity out of the air to sustain themselves. If you see a large horde of POKENAME gliding by, it's a good idea to find shelter, as a thunderstorm is about to arrive.
author: .realthree

entry: Once a day, POKENAME run around in circles, generating massive electricity from the friction. They are then able to spend the rest of the day sleeping, as anything that touches them will get a nasty shock.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME stores electricity in its feathers. Trainers must be careful when handling it or risk getting a nasty shock.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's fur changes color while it sleeps, revealing its charge level; red for low, yellow for average, and blue when full. The color fades when it wakes.
author: .izik

entry: The cotton covering its body stores large amounts of static energy, allowing POKENAME to produce sparks in battle. It emits a lemon-like scent that feels invigorating to anyone who breathes it in.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Anesthesiologists rely on compounds made with POKENAME to dull pain for people who are about to have surgery. Hospitals can place bounties on POKENAME to incentivize harvesting their leaves during busy seasons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Often employed to search for lost Trainers, POKENAME sense electrical currents given off by all creatures. Once located, they protect their charge at all costs, howling and sparking intimidatingly at any perceived threat.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME generates electricity in its fur by running about in a zigzag pattern. The more it runs around, the greater the electrical burst it will inevitably discharge.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates electricity while running, gathering more internal energy the faster and longer it runs. After a point, it even begins leaving trails of crackling lightning behind it as it dashes around.
author: sk372

entry: Flocks of POKENAME can be seen often during storms at sea. They fly directly into the storm clouds, coming out crackling with electricity they've absorbed from within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME runs nimbly through grasslands and forests to catch its prey. Despite its deft speed and skill at taking down rodent Pokémon, it is unable to keep up its sprint for long.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can cross a football field in a blink, fueled by their powerful and electrified leg muscles. They love to play fetch with their Trainer, though their Trainer rarely gets to keep up with their energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on its small size and lightning-fast speed to win battles. In a pinch, it is known to absorb electricity from nearby devices to generate more voltage for attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When its friends start losing, POKENAME stimulates the muscles in its hands to cheer them on harder. As long as its friends are losing, it will keep on stimulating its muscles to cheer, even when they become extremely sore and worn.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME converts energy from its meals into electricity. When threatened, it spits out a sticky substance to impede its foes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME will rub their fur against prey to completely paralyze them. To train for evolution into an Eelektross fusion, it stimulates the muscles in its paws to be able to temporarily crawl on land.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is a very lazy predator, waiting for hours with its tail dipped in the water, hoping that some prey will take the bait. When it gets tired of waiting, it releases electric shocks into the water to bring something to the surface.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is known for its greedy nature, stashing away anything it deems valuable in its den. Items recovered from these dens have included coins, rare berries, and even gemstones.
author: mepp.

entry: If a POKENAME notices a traveler wearing fine jewelry, it will attempt to steal the trinket with silky string. Due to its poor aim, it usually fails.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attracts loose coins using static electricity. If startled while counting them, it may explode in a shower of sparks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are arrogant fighters, but have something of a code of honor. They prefer to fight a weapon-wielding opponent, if only so they may dramatically disarm them in battle and gloat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often spend much of their time taking catnaps because they are unable to move until they evolve. They often purr when they are stressed, which confuses predators long enough to lose interest in eating them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its ruby horn to dig in cave walls in search of gems or rare ore. It will mine for hours if the scent of gold is strong.
author: .izik

entry: While normally a kind and helpful Pokémon, it jealously guards the gem it carries. It will hold a lifelong grudge against any who attempt to take it.
author: knilk

entry: It carries a large egg-shaped gem in its pouch. POKENAME establish a heirarchy based on the size and redness of their gems.
author: staghorn

entry: Not all of the yarn in POKENAME's body is attached to it. There are several extraneous strands that have been dragged along for the ride.
author: .realthree

entry: Though difficult to take care of, POKENAME adds an air of regality to home aquariums. Scientists debate on whether the color and size of the gem on POKENAME's head is influenced by its diet of microorganisms when it's young.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's forehead gem shines before it lashes out. During combat, it swings its blades wildly at anything nearby.
author: .izik

entry: The gem on the head of a POKENAME is coveted by poachers. Its shine and purity increase based on how angry the POKENAME gets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swarm in groups of ten, nesting in old shacks by clinging to walls with their sticky feet. They store shiny objects to lure in prey like Murkrow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rules its waters with cold precision, its glittering form gliding past like a serpent. Other Pokémon part before it, knowing it does not tolerate disobedience.
author: mgfox_66676

entry: POKENAME are incredibly proficient hunters, using their transformation abilities to hide almost perfectly, then pouncing on flying Pokémon when they land to rest.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: Its diamond-hard claws allow POKENAME to crack through the shells of other Pokémon. It adores shiny objects and will commonly grab lost jewelry or small pearls to take back to its den.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses Foresight to predict when someone with treasure will pass by. It ambushes them with uncanny timing.
author: .izik

entry: Its wool is incredibly soft and valuable, so POKENAME is always treated with the utmost care to keep its coat in the best possible condition. It is a mischievous Pokémon that enjoys shocking even the humans who care for and feed it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME jealously guards its favorite gem by wrapping its tail around it. It will leap to defend it at the slightest provocation.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME decorates its den with shiny refuse like tin foil and soda tabs. Sleeping near the shiny objects gives it great comfort.
author: .izik

entry: It's often claimed that POKENAME was the reference for creepy Jack-in-the-boxes. They are sometimes seen crawling on city walls and roofs.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME is very popular among children. It loves the attention, even if there is a little roughhousing. It especially loves being stroked on the tufts of fur protruding from its face and purrs contentedly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is very popular among children. It loves the attention, even if there is a little roughhousing. It especially loves being stroked on the gills protruding from its face and purrs contentedly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: They are considered a lucky Pokémon to raise, as their pheromones release Luck Incense into an area. These pheromones only work on people and help promote a magnanimous feeling after losing a battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pecks at passersby while its flock rummages through pockets to steal valuables. They vanish before the victim notices.
author: .izik

entry: While scavenging, POKENAME will abandon food the moment it finds shiny trash. It always carries treasures back to its den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs from strong tree branches using its strong tail while using its whiskers to sense disturbances in its environment. When it senses prey, it drops and snaps its tough jeweled shell around the target.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME harness their feline charm to beg their Trainers for food. Most Trainers capitulate to their demands, causing them to become quite spoiled.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's head gem blinks in patterns to signal its flock. Together, they attack rival bird Pokémon that enter their turf.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a fierce hunter, but also a highly finicky eater. It hunts and eats only certain parts of prey such as Arbok and Raticate, then leaves the rest for scavengers to pick at.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME paralyzes humans with venom before dragging away their valuables. It sleeps coiled atop piles of stolen coins.
author: .izik

entry: If startled, POKENAME unleashes psychic waves from its forehead gem. Most threats flee before a second blast is needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's limber and flexible body allows it to easily fit into places other Pokémon its size could not. With its speed and the ability to freeze those who gaze upon it with a sharp Glare, wild POKENAME prove very elusive to catch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is carefree to the extreme; it is difficult to ruin its good mood. However, it lacks the same devotion as Blissey, and does not feel the need to heal others in the wild. It may do so if asked if given glittery and shining trinkets.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rarely parts with the gem it holds, even when munificent gifts are offered. If anyone tries to steal the gem, it ferociously claws the assailant to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a crepuscular Pokémon. Strong sunlight hurts its eyes, so it often squints during the day.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's yarn-like vines move like nimble fingers. It's so dexterous it can pickpocket Trainers without being seen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME buries coins in shallow holes throughout its territory. Its memory is so precise, it never forgets a single spot.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits seeds at passersby from treetops, then swoops down to steal trinkets. It vanishes into the canopy with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME will stalk Trainers with large amounts of wealth and slowly steal away their valuables when they're not looking. Once all their wealth is gone, it will finally take their soul.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly picky eater, refusing food until it finds the berries it wants. It hates being touched and will jab its Trainer with poisonous barbs if they try to pet it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME smears toxic liquid from its whiskers onto the coins in its den. The scent keeps rivals and thieves away.
author: .izik

entry: Respected by humans and Pokémon alike, POKENAME is the ultimate feline. It only shares food and fortune to those it truly trusts.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: It treats most other Pokémon with disdain, since its sheer size has left it with few natural predators.
author: dicedragon20

entry: POKENAME protect their grand treasures with tricky riddles. If a person fails to answer their riddles, it is said that they are transformed into a Pokémon until they learn the correct answer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME secretes paralyzing venom from its whiskers to immobilize targets. It strikes quickly to steal jewelry.
author: .izik

entry: Moving with feline grace, POKENAME fights using a peerless martial style that uses slicing maneuvers to weaken its opponent. The more it weakens an opponent, the more wildly it fights, as if delighting in its increasing advantage.
author: ocxin

entry: POKENAME's nose always turns toward nearby gold. Prospectors follow it through caves to find ore veins hidden underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME functions as a finely forged sword as well as treasure detector, determined by the mood of the Persian head pommel.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This POKENAME was once wielded by a legendary treasure hunter. The explorer was said to have been able to verbally communicate and understand it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME steals shiny objects from its own kind to assert dominance. The largest hoard earns the highest status.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has many admirers, though prospective Trainers should be warned it is fickle about who it shows it's affection to.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME thinks of itself as king in a literal sense and will attempt to rule over other Pokémon living in the same area.
author: snugglessam

entry: This variant of POKENAME is very popular in the fashion world. Many men's clothing lines will feature POKENAME sporting the latest trendy fashions.
author: char_latte3412

entry: With its aerial speed and quickness of claw, POKENAME is adept at taking anything it wants. Most often found in urban areas, it will snatch up prey and human meals in equal measure.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME steals shiny objects from junkyards and slashes at anyone who tries to stop it. Its claws leave strange cuts that shimmer under moonlight.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME is extremely obsessed with its appearance, it spends most of its time grooming itself. It unleashes a furious assault towards anything foolish enough to test its patience.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's thin fur grows dangerously hot when it sees coins. Scientists are baffled, but collectors use it as a coin detector.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sports thick, coarse fur in place of armored plates. However, its ability to groom its coat is often impeded by its axe-like tusks.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME sports thick, coarse fur in place of armored plates. However, its ability to groom its coat is often impeded by its axe-like tusks.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME are a popular choice among Trainers with allergies because of their hypoallergenic fur. Breeders sell them for large sums of money at auction because of how popular they have become.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very popular pets as they are both docile and do not require much food. However, if its habitat gets too dirty, the gems on its back will become dull and brittle.
author: mistymagius

entry: Vain and territorial, POKENAME will not suffer the indignity of anything being in close proximity to it. With a disdainful backhanded flap of one wing, it spreads embers all over any who would dare invade its space.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME keep their disguises clean to appeal to their Trainer. Whenever they eat, they reserve a piece to give as an act of submissiveness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have tongues with special backward-facing barbs that help them clean their fur. They spend a significant amount of time cleaning their body because their fur can easily get matted, especially their tails.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME senses a mischievous aura, the gems on its body pulse pink. Trainers say it glows brightest near casinos.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gets extremely excited over shiny objects and will take anything shiny without a second thought. It will sometimes even get mesmerized by its own golden claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is highly independent and hates being touched. Those that try to pet it without its trust and approval will see it hiss and shed sparks from its fur, the only warning they get before it uses its claws and electricity in full.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is smug and egotistical, intensely proud of the flame on its tail and regularly flaunting it towards others. If enough attention isn't paid to the beauty of its flame, it uses it to set things on fire as petty vengeance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sings soft lullabies in campsites to make travelers drowsy. It then floats off with stolen valuables.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reads minds to locate valuables, then levitates them away while victims sleep. Its lair is always perfectly organized, placing differently colored objects in their own pile.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are known for stealth, often seen ambushing small prey or stealing food. Their soft paws let them scamper about silently.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME screeches at a high pitch to confuse cave explorers. While they cover their ears, it snatches rings and earrings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stalk their minuscule prey before pouncing. They're equally apt to chase the light from a laser pointer.
author: hophoppip

entry: Sharp red gems grow from POKENAME's back. It fires them like darts at intruders, later retrieving the ones that glitter most.
author: .izik

entry: The velvety soft fur and feathers of POKENAME make it highly sought after by the wealthy. If unhappy, it will violently flap its wings, releasing shining embers in frustration.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME stalks city rooftops, diving to bump into pedestrians and steal whatever they drop. Its eyes glint with mischief shortly before a strike.
author: .izik

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME lies flat on warm rocks, soaking up heat. Its fur stands on end, crackling with slight amounts of static.
author: .izik

entry: The rubies on POKENAME's sides glow deep red when its venom reaches peak potency. This glow often signals it's about to strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME barrels into travelers to scatter their belongings, then zips away with anything that sparkles. It can roll faster than 70 mph.
author: .izik

entry: Its leaves are used as a calming remedy for Pokémon like Meowth and Persian, who are particularly drawn to their fragrant aroma. Though POKENAME is naturally peaceful, it doesn't hesitate to fight back with fierce headbutts if disturbed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Anything POKENAME touches will turn into a toxic, gold-like metalloid. Its entire body is comprised of this mysterious substance.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The only thing it loves more than wrestling is money. POKENAME are known to take dives in matches for comically small bribes.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME have a rebellious and condescending attitude that makes them difficult to train. They only listen to confident Trainers and refuse to obey commands from those who show nervousness or doubt.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will spread spores on spots it claims as its territory. The spores are harmless but irritating to the eyes and nose of anything but itself. Trainers have found that spraying POKENAME with water helps discourage this behavior.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very playful and love to play with all types of random objects. If you plan on owning a POKENAME, it best to get them as many toys as possible.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is often used by evil teams, using its toys to distract enemy Pokémon. However, it frequently gets distracted by its own toys and ends up flying in circles instead.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME launches coins from its burrows using Pay Day. The closer intruders get to its home, the faster and harder the coins are fired.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps clustered inside cavern walls. Its deep, rumbling purr echoes loudly and can be heard from the opposite side of solid rock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted by shiny objects. A single coin tossed away can keep it busy for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's headaches ease in the presence of coins. Some Trainers tie a coin to a string and fasten it to their POKENAME out of kindness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a very fickle species that refuses to live anywhere but the cleanest of ponds. It has been known to attack its handlers when displeased, but grabbing it by the whiskers makes it docile.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are vain and pretentious Pokémon who always want to impress others. They make flashy poses while in a Pokémon battle that leaves openings for their opponents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME becomes violently enraged if anyone approaches its coin hoard. Even eye contact can trigger an outburst.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a very difficult Pokémon to raise due to its behavior. Spoiled and moody, if it doesn't get what it wants, when it wants, it flies into a tantrum of swinging fists and slashing claws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live together in small packs. The one with the most magnificent beard is the leader, who is accepted by every pack member without exception.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is an extremely proud Pokémon that only obeys experienced Trainers. However, it would even risk its life for one.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in the ruby on its belly and can often be seen near rivers trying to clean and polish it. The unique spiral pattern on the jewel makes it highly sought after by collectors.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME floats yarn out of shop windows with psychic waves. It weaves the strands into nests lined with velvet and coins.
author: .izik

entry: When basking in the aroma of an Odd Incense, they transmit thoughts of their desires to creatures and people nearby. Typically, this results in vivid imagery of a desire for milk or fish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are known as great conquerors of the seas. With their claws, they invade islands and seek to control entire archipelagos. For them, wounds are synonymous with courage, and they show them off with eye patches or by striking a pose.
author: spagalapof

entry: POKENAME's aggressive combat style has been dubbed the "Fist of the Beast King." It's popularity resulted in a supporting role in a popular television franchise, though its roles often suffer an unfortunate fate.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects its precious silky fur by retreating into its shell whenever it senses danger that might threaten its beauty. Though it dislikes fighting, it won't hesitate to scratch anyone it dislikes with its small claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will gallop wildly if lured with a shiny object. Trainers sometimes toss coins to coax it into races with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sees something shiny, its flames flicker red and blue, forming a cumulative near-purple glow. Some believe these flame colorings make it run faster.
author: .izik

entry: Domestic POKENAME are often reported as showing highly spoiled behavior. The three heads constantly fight over food, toys and affection.
author: sk372

entry: It can fire deadly electric blasts from its metallic claws as if they were cannons. Despite its entire body being made of steel, POKENAME is capable of moving at astonishing speeds.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As this Pokémon runs at lightning speed, electricity builds in its arms and crackles wildly off its wrists. A single Thunder Punch from a fully charged POKENAME can level a building.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are energetic creatures that can seamlessly change their camouflage as they run. The only thing that matches their speed is their boundless love for their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is prone to attracting thunderstorms. When lightning strikes POKENAME's shell, its plates may vitrify into Thunder Stones. This phenomenon is why it is common to see Pikachu living on POKENAME's back.
author: pjporwoll

entry: One should be wary of provoking a wild POKENAME. The dust clouds its wings kick up are also supercharged with its electricity, leaving its foes blinded and beset by powerful discharges of lightning on all sides.
author: sk372

entry: All the yellow sections on POKENAME's body glow slightly at night. When POKENAME flies nearby, any lights will flicker until they have passed.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME makes its nests where lightning has previously struck. It collects items that are left behind by Trainers and stores them in its nests.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's warm fur thickens in winter. When startled, its static surges and every strand stands on end.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's electrified powder allows it to paralyze almost any Pokémon in seconds. This same powder also causes Pokémon to be more susceptible to electric attacks, further weakening them against this Pokémon.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME shocks the water with its electricity, then snatches up stunned prey that floats to the surface. POKENAME are often seen in large groups squabbling over food.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can overstimulate its muscles with all of its electricity to run faster than lightning. However, its muscles will become very sore afterwards, so it must painfully rub its paws along the ground to create enough friction to recharge.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME summons thunderclouds that drop gigantic lightning bolts over enemies. The width of one of these lightning bolts can span over many feet.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME zips around from place to place, its speed being described as similar to a lightning bolt. It uses this kinetic energy to generate its electricity.
author: soup1900

entry: Reports of lightning streaking across plains are attributed to POKENAME herds chasing storms. The electricity in their bodies causes their hooves to heat to high temperatures, leaving burned hoofprints where they run.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are known for being popular choices of partners for Pokémon Rangers. They use electricity to vibrate the strings of their ukuleles to play uplifting tunes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's wool has a strong positive charge. When in herds including negatively-charged Mareep fusions, they get stuck together in a massive ball.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME has more control over its magnetic charge. It seeks out negatively-charged Pokémon to increase its power.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's tail acts as an extremely powerful, positively charged magnet. If it smacks against something with a negative charge, violent thunderbolts occur.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are powered by positively charged electrons due to their specialized fur reacting to the sun's light. Sunlight can be converted into electric power that is used to devastate their foes.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME's body consists of battery acid, powering its electrical attacks. It's friendly in nature, but Trainers should approach it with caution.
author: hophoppip

entry: The most cheerful Pokémon of the jungle, POKENAME will rub against tree trunks to build up static electricity. It will then reroute this electricity to its hands, using it as pom-poms to cheer others on.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME cheers on allies from the sidelines, its dances and chants creating psychic pulses to boost them. POKENAME's cheers are said to make an ally's greatest strengths even greater.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME sneak into nightclubs to practice their cheering sessions for their fellow Pokémon. They leave trails of red static cotton that can shock anybody who touches it after the session is over.
author: doctorjazznumber6215

entry: POKENAME sings chipper, upbeat songs to cheer on its allies and boost their morale in battle. It rubs its cheeks to create sparks that it can fling into the air to add to the flair of its performance.
author: sk372

entry: Bursting with positive energy, being around POKENAME has been proven to raise the serotonin levels of those nearby, improving their mood as a result. While the exact reason has yet to be pinned down, POKENAME's cheerful attitude may help contribute.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME repel other Pokémon that have a positive electrical charge. This leads them to live solitary lives, afraid of pushing away the friends they care about.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's song and dance routines are meant to boost the spirits of its friends while they fight. Pokémon on the offensive fight even more fiercely when POKENAME's cheers back them up.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wander tall grass looking for berries or scraps to feast on. Whenever they meet another of their kind, they fight over the food until one prevails.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME enters a cloud, it can kickstart a storm as its body charges electricity over time, transferring positive charges upon contact.
author: lucioleuh

entry: POKENAME carries a steady positive charge as it runs through meadows. If a negative charge is detected nearby, its electrical power intensifies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gorges on batteries or old electronics Trainers leave behind. Its stomach develops a positive charge when it is full, repelling other POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a naturally cheery disposition that brightens the day of all the creatures it meets. If POKENAME attempts to fly in an area rich with metal, electricity discharges from its body uncontrollably.
author: weirdmageddonprepper_93813

entry: POKENAME loves to fight in the ring for an audience, firing punches in lightning-fast volleys that spark on contact. The louder the crowd cheers for POKENAME, the faster it can punch.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME are known for being popular choices of partners for Pokémon Rangers. They use electricity to vibrate the strings of their ukuleles to play soothing songs.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's wool carries a negative charge. A herd must have equal amounts of negative and positive charges, or else the herd will scatter.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME has better control over its negative charge. It awaits positive-charged Pokémon to seek it out so that it may lend them its power.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's tail is an extremely powerful, negatively charged magnet. If it smacks its tail against something with a positive charge, a storm may appear.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are powered by negatively charged electrons after bathing in moonlight. The radiation of the moonlight converts into electricity within their bodies as though they are living panels.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Clacking POKENAME's claws together produces small spurts of blue sparks on contact. POKENAME often uses this ability as a way to soothe and entertain its young when it gets upset.
author: sk372

entry: Regarded as the calmest Pokémon of the jungle, POKENAME finds an energy source that harmonises with its own. It then allows that energy to flow through its body, emitting an aura said to boost vitality.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME cheers on allies from the sidelines, its dances and chants creating psychic pulses to boost them. POKENAME's cheers are said to boost an ally's weaker traits and reduce their shortcomings in combat.
author: sk372

entry: When excited, POKENAME erupts in a shower of sparks, which can be dangerous for those around it. It recharges by dancing under the light of the moon, though some Trainers urge it not to do so, as this makes it safer to be around.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: At maximum speed, POKENAME's rapid movements leave behind blue-tinted afterimages of itself. Visible for only a split-second, these copies dissipate in a quick burst of blue sparks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a negative electric charge that repel other POKENAME. Despite this, they form spacious groups to protect themselves from predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's song and dance routines are meant to boost the spirits of its friends while they fight. Pokémon at a disadvantage get a powerful second wind when they witness POKENAME's cheers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hide in tall grass before hunting prey with a supercharged pounce. They team up with others of their kind to bring down Pokémon larger than themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A negative electrical charge is generated and stored in POKENAME's wings as it flies. If it builds up too much, it will discharge a Thunderbolt to get rid of the excess. This oftentimes leads to short power outages in areas with beaches.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME keep their distance from other POKENAME because they experience electromagnetic repulsion. When they find a Pokémon that they are attracted to, they become best friends with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wander through tall grass to eat batteries and other electronics Trainers throw away. Its cheeks develop a negative charge when it is full.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever POKENAME are near positively charged ions, the magnetic field causes them to develop a headache. The closer they are to the field, the stronger the headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By making its tail glow as it flies over bodies of water, POKENAME creates stunning light effects. It feeds exclusively on Berries that grow near sources of fresh water.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME blinds enemies by flashing its bright tail. This creates an opening for it to swiftly crush them with its powerful jaws.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are found in urban environments. They stand at the edges of their territory and light up their tails to communicate their borders. If you continue despite their warning, they will leer and posture intimidatingly before finally attacking.
author: .realthree

entry: The electricity within their abdomens helps them stay aloft as they dart across night skies, their streaks of light drawing myriad shapes when swarms dart about. They use statically-charged webs as nets to collect vegetables and fruits for later.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sleep submerged in the earth until nighttime; at that time, several of their organs begin to glow. Their spore output triples when around Illumise or fusions with Illumise.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME provokes weaker Pokémon to fight by exposing its glowing rear end and letting out a mocking laugh. If it ever finds itself outmatched, it releases a blinding flash of light and makes its escape.
author: fancyskunk

entry: The POKENAME with the biggest tail-light is the leader of the pack. They hunt at night, and the rapid flashing of their lights signals that prey is near.
author: mepp.

entry: Highly territorial, POKENAME flashes its tail-light with a specific rhythm to alert its pack about any trespassers. It prefers making its dens near clean ponds.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME zigzag everywhere in search of the sweet aroma of Illumise. They light their tail with others of their kind to draw geometric shapes, but because they always zigzag when walking, it is difficult for them to create straight lines.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME grow the quickest during the nighttime; their bioluminescence is a byproduct of using the nutrients they had accumulated to mature. Before evolution, multiple POKENAME meet and perform some sort of ritualistic dance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's tail glows as a signal for nearby Illule that it is seeking friends with whom to fly through the night sky. It aids its allies by firing sparkling pom-poms from its hands in geometric patterns that distract opponents.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a standoffish attitude. They travel in groups, usually trying to impress Illumise with their bright features. The strange hair atop their head feels greasy to the touch.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: The light from its tail can be seen from great distances, which is why POKENAME is often used to explore dark areas or navigate through thick fog. It gets along well with both Volbeat and Illumise, and it's often spotted flying alongside them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During mating season, hordes of POKENAME gather together in the dark of night and demonstrate their glowing oral cavity to one another. The wider one can open its mouth and the brighter it glows, the more attractive POKENAME is to its fellows.
author: milchik

entry: Due to its strictly nocturnal nature, POKENAME is only sent into the ring during nighttime matches and special evening events. When its powerful punches hit their mark, its gloves emit a faint, glowing light.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME gets excited, its antennae start flashing on and off. Because its DNA is incredibly unstable and prone to sudden mutations, it remains a subject of great interest among many Pokémon researchers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME release a sweet scent to gather Bug-type Pokémon into one place. They swing their bulbous tail to conduct the ensemble to create a symphony of sound.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a highly social creature that loves to perform Moonlight whenever it meets someone new, dazzling them with its elegance. If it feels threatened, it builds up electrical energy within its body and releases powerful discharges.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a highly social creature that loves to perform Moonlight whenever it meets someone new, dazzling them with its elegance. If it feels threatened, it builds up electrical energy within its body and releases powerful discharges.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its antennae can sense the emotions of both Pokémon and humans, so if it encounters someone feeling sad, it tries to befriend them to lift their spirits. It can release a sweetly scented, glittering powder that attracts wild Pokémon to its location.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its antennae can sense the emotions of both Pokémon and humans, so if it encounters someone feeling sad, it tries to befriend them to lift their spirits. It can release a sweetly scented, glittering powder that attracts wild Pokémon to its location.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME battles others of its kind to decide who will become the pack's leader. When it spots prey, it signals the rest of the group by making the tip of its tail glow, calling them to hunt together.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its primary source of electrical energy is vegetables, which it digs up and dissolves into a goo for later consumption. Farmers largely consider it a pest.
author: hophoppip

entry: When POKENAME focuses its energy to breathe fire, the antennae on its head light up from the effort. It spends the night foraging for berries to store in its den, so it can eat and rest during the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME thrives in places where electricity is abundant. The excess energy POKENAME absorbs is stored in its abdomen, which produces a soft glow, a harmonic buzzing sound, and a scent comparable to ozone and orange soda.
author: hophoppip

entry: If a predator gets too close, POKENAME flashes the antenna protruding from its leafy body at full brightness to blind its attackers and make a quick escape. Its leaves secrete a toxic oil that can cause digestive distress if ingested.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME emerges from its den after sunset and communicates with others of its pack by flashing its glowing nose in rhythmic patterns. When it finds food, it becomes so happy that even the tip of its tail shines brightly.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gather around other Bug-type Pokémon that release a sweet scent. POKENAME produce a hollow thud whenever they are tapped or bumped into, which makes them a valuable percussionist if they are part of an ensemble.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cheers on allies by generating glowing, electrical orbs on its hands and waving them around like pom-poms. It will also wave the energy orbs around to attract the attention of nearby Volun, leading to a blindingly bright gathering.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a very timid Pokémon that hides the moment it hears a suspicious sound. Fearing stronger predators, it always travels with Volbeat or Illumise so it can rely on their protection in case of danger.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's eyes are more adapted for low-light conditions, so it has to squint in order to see in daylight. Some Trainers tie a thin cloth around their POKENAME's eyes to give them some relief.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can digest most things within their bodies and quickly swallow said things whole. Their stomach fluid is a very effective material for conducting electricity and many researchers are still studying ways to safely use this fluid.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME loves to eat coals, no matter how hot. Its iron stomach breaks them down to fuel its fire. The flame on its tail burns brighter while it eats, and the stench it emits grows stronger.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME loves to eat coals no matter how hot, as its iron stomach breaks them down to fuel its fire. The flame on its tail burns brighter while it eats, releasing a smell similar to burning trash.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME is typically found in lush routes by the water. They devour any trash that washes up ashore during the evening. Large waste is no problem: POKENAME's body can expand up to four times its size.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While scrounging around for food, POKENAME aren't afraid to fight off competitors. When they get too excited from an intense battle, they puke up acid and any food not fully digested.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: While scourging around for food, POKENAME aren't afraid to fight off competitors. When POKENAME gets too excited from an intense battle, it regurgitates acid and any food not fully digested.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME have an omnivorous diet of berries and small rodent Pokémon. Their stretchy cheeks and powerful stomach acids allow them to digest most of their meal before swallowing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to the hardened adornment on POKENAME's head cutting the air, POKENAME should be more aerodynamic than the common Wingull; but because of their significantly heavier body, they don't tend to be very fast.
author: retrodox

entry: POKENAME can open its jaw to startling lengths and swallow larger creatures with relative ease. As it digests and gains nutrients, sparks of electricity run across its body.
author: sk372

entry: An upbeat Pokémon with a squishy body. It loves all sorts of Berries, but when it eats its favorite, it burps up sparks of electricity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Even if dropped from a high height, POKENAME merely bounces. Scientists have hypothesized that, if purified and then ingested by a human, POKENAME mucus may be beneficial to the heart.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME forms feeding groups led by a single, massive individual. The leader always eats first, claiming the best food before allowing the others to feed.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME have highly acidic stomachs that allow them to break down tough bark and other hard materials. They often forget that they have these powers and are surprised when they can melt biological matter with their stomach acids.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often feels unwell after eating because of its constant spinning. If overfed, it wobbles uncontrollably, venting out eruptions of foul gases.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: An aquatic fusion adapted to the deep ocean. Its mouth may look small, but it can open to ten times POKENAME's size to swallow large swaths of prey.
author: hophoppip

entry: Its lower jawbone is split in two, allowing its mouth to greatly expand when it's eating. It's been known to prey on Pokémon over ten times its size.
author: hophoppip

entry: It cannot close its mouth, so it remains motionless, hoping smaller fish foolishly swim into it. Then, its powerful stomach acid does the work.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Because POKENAME swallows large quantities of hair while grooming itself, it has developed extremely strong stomach acid. If attacked, it defends itself by spitting up globs of the corrosive acid.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME establishes dominance over its brethren, forcing them to forage on its behalf. Any that disobey or return empty-handed are swiftly devoured.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: To increase the toxins in its body, POKENAME feeds on any poisonous plant it encounters, even preying on other Poison-Type Pokémon. It can spit extremely corrosive acid from its mouth that can dissolve anything it touches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live near active volcanoes where the arid climate makes them feel comfortable. The smog that they release from their bodies is a dense toxic substance that kills grass on contact and leaves little place for herbivorous Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail glows bright gold when the water sacs inside it overheat. The water it spits during this time becomes hot enough to scald skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very sensitive to changes in humidity because moisture saps their natural body heat. Whenever it rains, they find the nearest shelter to avoid getting hypothermia.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers to eat igneous rocks, which its body metabolizes into a molten liquid that it trails from the hole in its back. If startled, POKENAME releases a cloud of smoke and mysteriously vanishes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Whenever it rains, the shell of a POKENAME forms cracks from the rapid cooling but can just as easily heal after the rain ends. They live on volcanoes where the hot temperatures and low humidity keep their shell well-heated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME bounces on its spring tail to release steam out of the orb on its skull. It must do this constantly, or the steam building up within will cause debilitating health problems.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are fueled by the heat inside their bodies and eat coal to keep themselves warm. They are unable to train for battles in the rain because it saps heat from their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release a thick sludge that trails them wherever they go. If they are caught outside when it rains, their sludge slowly begins to solidify as it loses its heat. Some succumb to hypothermia if they cannot find shelter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME territorially patrols the maze-like nests it builds within volcanic calderas. To deter predators, it mercilessly blasts them with molten honey, which, after it cools and hardens, is a luxury treat made famous by Lavaridge Town.
author: pjporwoll

entry: In volcanic craters, POKENAME absorbs the heat of the magma. It converts this heat to energy, allowing plants to grow along the crater of the volcano despite the harsh environment.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME can often be found placidly soaking itself in volcanic hot springs, unfazed by the boiling waters. It erupts similarly scalding water from its back should it need to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is proud of its strength and quick to start a fight. Its forceful headbutts are strengthened by its rocky head, which can spew lava when POKENAME is facing a strong foe.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME often sleeps in the craters of volcanoes, eating molten rock as fuel. However, when too much magma builds up inside its humps, it goes into a rage, spewing nonstop until empty.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: This Pokémon lives near volcanoes and is typically shy. When it approaches humans without hesitation, it's usually a sign that the volcano will soon erupt.
author: hophoppip

entry: It suffers from severe anger issues, so it practices yoga daily in order to stay calm and keep from blowing its top.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The volcano on POKENAME's back is always active, constantly spewing lava. When the lava cools and turns into stone, it creates a layer of protection for POKENAME against enemy attacks.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME stores so much magma inside its body that when it finally erupts, it takes hours for it to completely empty out. It stuffs lots of prey inside its body, melting all traces of them as they simmer for days in its magma.
author: soup1900

entry: The pearl on its back is very important to POKENAME as it is the source of its psychic powers. It uses its spring-like protuberances to deflect physical attacks that threaten to hit it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's heart beats in sync with the bouncing pearl on its head. When an ally is distressed, these bounces emit psychic vibrations that gently steady their pulse. Therapists often study this ability to improve their relaxation techniques.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: Supposedly, if one balances POKENAME's pearl on their head, its spirit will possess them. Thankfully, nobody has ever done this.
author: kiwiarms

entry: By leaping constantly, POKENAME charges the jewel on its head with stored energy. It feeds on sunlight through photosynthesis, always seeking out the brightest treetops to bask in.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have superb jumping abilities and can leap up to six times their body length in a single jump. This allows them to quickly escape when they steal coins and other trinkets from Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The faster POKENAME bounces, the hotter the pearl atop its head becomes. Touching it at full heat can easily cause third degree burns.
author: .izik

entry: The pearl wedged in its fontanelle keeps POKENAME's constant migraines under control. Unfortunately, it must temporarily remove this pearl to make full use of its psychic powers.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME's psychic potential is directly tied to its muscle strength, so it trains virtually nonstop. Whenever it flexes its muscles, the orb on its head glows brighter.
author: sk372

entry: The only cure for POKENAME's headaches is the herbs growing on its bulb, which it is unable to reach on its own. As a result, it often follows Trainers with the hope they will help ease its pain.
author: rakunk

entry: It spends most of the day among the tree branches, snacking on the tree leaves. Should it get a surging headache, the psychic pulse may cause all the leaves on the tree to fall off at once.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generate electricity from the stress they experience. When they are stressed enough to cause headaches, they explode and release all the electricity that has built up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are moody Pokémon that generate electricity from their various mood swings. When they are so stressed that they have a headache, they explode to vent that frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wears the skulls of other Pokémon and lives in solitude. It does not spend much time with other Pokémon because its frequent headaches flare up when it is overstimulated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers to live alone, as it easily develops headaches when overwhelmed by other Pokémon. It wears skulls of other Pokémon both for protection and to ease its loneliness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains hard every day to improve its skill in boxing. As a result, it is both physically and mentally healthy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A delusional fusion, POKENAME believes itself to be a world-renowed boxer. Despite its mediocrity, its skill increases with its headaches.
author: pory

entry: POKENAME are fastidious at cleaning with their tongues and hate places that are dirty. If placed in a room where they cannot clean or organize, they develop headaches from the resulting stress.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gets headaches whenever it is itchy for long enough, but it has no limbs to scratch that itch. It can only wobble hoping another Pokémon comes to help alleviate the itch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produces a unique gas that causes severe migraines in anyone exposed to it. However, POKENAME is in constant pain because of its own gas.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are easy to agitate into an anxious state. Once they start rampaging, it is difficult to stop their manic state. They often feel remorseful for the destruction they cause, even if they forget part of what happened.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rev up a charge with their hind legs before they run into foes with their sharp bill. They can punch through boulders with enough force, but the resulting impact also leaves them with a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The eggs POKENAME makes are particularly effective in alleviating headaches when consumed.  Because of its constant migraines, POKENAME is constantly eating its own eggs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's vines are made out of a rubber-like polymer that helps it effortless float in water. The vines can be melted down and is commonly used in making rubber toys.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are enraptured by coral reefs that surround them. They often stare blankly at the coral reefs to ease their persistent migraines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever it sheds its outer layer of fins and scales, they are ground up for use in traditional medicine. It also produces a liquid from its fins that produces numbness, which locals tap into to use as an anesthetic.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It gets lost easily because of its short-term memory, which lasts for 12 hours in the wild. It can extend its memory span through intense mental training, which also causes it to develop headaches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME help each other scratch itches by using their horn as a crude backscratcher. If an itch is unable to be scratched, they will swim in circles until they develop headaches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME coats its wings with sticky pollen and refuses to let Trainers clean its wings. This is because the pollen helps it calm down and neutralizes the pain that comes from a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hate being picked up and will try to scuttle away when people or Pokémon try to do so to it. When they are taken out of the sea, they quickly become dehydrated and develop a headache until they are back underwater.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of creating grand and over-the-top performances but are often forgetful of where they place barriers. When they eventually run into one of their psychic barriers, they develop a severe headache from the concussion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The blades of POKENAME's arms are actually soft membranes akin to webbed feet. Though ineffective at cutting, those struck by its swings develop crushingly painful migraines shortly after.
author: sk372

entry: Its hair is able to detach from its head. When it locates a clean water source, it will take the wig off and wash it thoroughly.
author: .izik

entry: Using the pincers on its skull gives it a headache afterward. The more force it exerts, the stronger the headache; trying too hard to crush something with its pincers may cause it to pass out from the migraine.
author: sk372
