entry: POKENAME navigates the depths with grace. Its shimmering scales and its red jewel make its appearance very popular in its habitat.
author: anarchaz

entry: Often mistaken for a dress, the red skin on its body is extremely sensitive to hot air. If it becomes too warm, it will scream loudly in anger.
author: .izik

entry: Lurking under the surface of murky lakes and ponds, POKENAME lies in wait to ambush unsuspecting Pokémon. It uses its gigantic pincers to drag its targets underwater, making them easy prey.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Lurking under the surface of murky lakes and ponds, POKENAME lies in wait to ambush unsuspecting Pokémon. It uses its gigantic pincers to drag its targets underwater, making them easy prey.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a large bill that scoops algae into their mouths. During fall, they can be seen hopping up waterfalls to reach lakes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The orbs on its head glow more intensely the more pressure they're under. This lets it know if it's going too deep underwater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME helps lifeguards at resorts protect people from drowning. It monitors deep water to ensure that swimmers remain safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a special layer of fur that remains fluffy even when underwater. They often roam around the wilderness looking for evolution stones, as many are eager to evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are incredibly fast swimmers that can cross lakes in a few seconds. Their webbed tail and flippers allow them to effortlessly glide through water without stopping.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME leave a trail of sparks wherever they swim. These sparks protect them from predators, who have a difficult time avoiding the sparks while chasing them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can produce special flames that can burn while underwater. They use these flames to roast seaweed, which adds a satisfying crunch for them to consume.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of slicing through targets both in the air and at sea, as the webbing between their wings also acts as flippers while underwater. They are almost always moving since they tend to get restless if they are bored.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often fall asleep at junctions after an attempt to cross railroads. Many solutions have been proposed to help prevent these instances, including relocating POKENAME to a lake that resembles their natural habitat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is antisocial, tending towards keeping itself far from other creatures. It has a soft spot for Psyduck, however, using its vast mental abilities to alleviate the headaches that plague them when it comes across them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME builds its nest near deep lakes and rivers, where its prey is most abundant. When it prepares to unleash a burst of water from its beak, the gem on its forehead shines intensely, revealing its full power.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are crepuscular Pokémon that are most active during dawn and dusk. They hunt groggy fish Pokémon in lakes by grabbing them with their webbed talons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are incredibly fast creatures that buzz through both the sea and air with precision. They often gather in groups and migrate from forest to forest so that they can grab berries as soon as they ripen.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can spot hidden prey underwater from incredible distances thanks to its flawless eyesight. With a single beat of its wings, it can dive in and demonstrate its unmatched swimming prowess, continuing the hunt below the surface.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live in the dark depths of the sea where they lure aquatic Pokémon towards themselves with two bright red bulbs. If they manage to crack one of their bulbs, they release a jolt of electricity until healed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME draw aquatic Pokémon towards themselves with two bright red bulbs. The red glow that is produced can cause some Pokémon to act aggressively, so they protect themselves by zapping the aggressor before swimming away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather far in advance thanks to its ability to see into the future. When the jewel on its forehead glows, it is telepathically communicating with its kin.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can summon dangerous waterspouts simply by rapidly flapping its mighty wings. It migrates once a year, flying for days without rest until it discovers a new lake to call home.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has transient psychic abilities that appear when it wags its tail. After clairvoyantly locating an enemy, the gem on its tail glows bright as it delivers a Thunder Shock.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME rides ocean breezes due to its light, fluffy body. While two of the puffballs on its airy plumage, the top one is a clear orb that sometimes functions as a third eye.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME rides ocean breezes due to its light, fluffy body. While two of the puffballs on its airy plumage, the top one is a clear orb that sometimes functions as a third eye.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME take up an unusual habit of protecting nature, people, and Pokémon from the sometimes-chaotic nature of wild fused Pokémon. With their widespread population and psychic powers, some believe all POKENAME can communicate with one another.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is able to use psychic powers, using its gills to amplify them. However, this can become too intense if sustained, so it coats its gills in mud to dampen the signal.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's layers of fat are its pride. The most optimal complexion decides the pack's leader. POKENAME are docile in nature and like hugs.
author: megaban

entry: POKENAME live in swamps where the cattails on their back blend in perfectly with their environment. They are sensitive to the motion of the swampy water, which makes them difficult to sneak up on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The whiskers of a POKENAME will grow slowly while it sleeps. It will panic and dive deep into the water at the slightest noise.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME patrol underwater ruins to keep ancient secrets safe. When they find a Trainer within the depths, they release a loud quack that summons other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has incredible aim, able to hit Flying-type Pokémon from hundreds of feet away with its aqua cannon. Its shell is protective, but it's heavy enough that it causes POKENAME to sink in water.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME spends its entire life inside its thick armored shell. It shoots jets of water from its retractable cannons to blast itself from place to place.
author: leonian1586

entry: The bright red feathers and gems on a POKENAME are seen as status symbols. POKENAME with larger, more vivid feathers are typically seen as more agile. POKENAME with brighter gems are seen as clever and worthy of respect from peers.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can fly and swim excellently due to its unique feathers. Its long neck and tough beak let it poke its head into otherwise hard-to-reach areas for food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can walk on dry land, but it prefers to stay in or near vast lakes. Its plumage keeps it warm even in the coldest environments, though it is less active in subzero areas due to a need to conserve energy.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME thrives in colder climates due to its remarkably thick plumage. Its beak and tusks are tough enough to break through ice sheets and get otherwise hard-to-reach food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is typically found in cold mountains all around the world, always doing everything with other POKENAME. Its tail can store enough food to keep it and its peers going for weeks.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can fly great distances due to its lightweight but oddly tough plumage. Its tough feathers also allow it to fly in the rain and swim expertly.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME marks its territory with paint-like substances from its tail, with markings varying vastly depending on the water where it lives. Some prefer freshwater while others prefer saltwater. No two POKENAME produce the exact same paint.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME live high up in mountains and spend their time seeking out mountain springs to relax in. Their bodies run at very high temperatures meaning any spring they climb into quickly heats up and becomes pleasant to bathe in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Due to its sheer size and weight it sinks to the bottom of the ocean. However POKENAME will often train strenuously by swimming to the surface every day.
author: baz2600

entry: POKENAME can ride ocean currents with its mostly flat body, though it can also maneuver expertly when riding them. It is deeply familiar with the patterns of ocean currents where it lives.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can fly underwater as if it were still in the sky. Many rescue teams use it to save people who are lost out at sea.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME produce leaves that slow down their bodies when swimming. They often let other Pokémon snack on the leaves so that they can swim faster.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight through their leaves to gain necessary nutrients for survival. Once they have enough nutrients, they allow other Pokémon to eat their leaves so that they can swim unencumbered.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME glides across its icy lake home, forming slick trails of frost beneath its feet. Its movements are elegant and silent as it hunts for prey.
author: .izik

entry: When using its psychic powers, the gems on POKENAME's forehead and back shimmer. It swims effortlessly through the jungle's rivers, easily escaping predators.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME jet through the water to slice up their opponents. They always fight with honor and dignity, refusing to resort to underhanded tactics to achieve victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dive into the sea to tear open fishing nets and grab onto whatever aquatic Pokémon that escape. Many fishermen have upgraded to tougher fishing nets because of the damage POKENAME cause to traditional rope nets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME effortlessly slice through fishing nets to release the aquatic Pokémon trapped inside. They have earned the ire of fishermen everywhere for eating the aquatic Pokémon that were supposed to be trapped in nets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stalk places fishermen frequent to get easy access to Water-type Pokémon to eat. These opportunistic creatures often clash with fishermen who are angry with POKENAME for stealing their fish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are surprisingly fast swimmers that leave a trail of pollen wherever they go. The pollen gets absorbed into other plants, which end up making sections of the swamp quite toxic to herbivores.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives on the shores of lakes. Its tough exoskeleton, sharp claws, and strong tail allow it to easily hunt for prey and defend itself.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME is often seen swimming in lakes. It uses its telekinetic powers and enormous claws to punish those who pollute its home.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME have a large red dome atop their heads that absorbs the shock from their headbutts. It is said that if it ever cracks, a wave of psychic energy is released.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend much of their time sleeping while holding onto their fishing rod. They often reel in Psyduck, which they toss back into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME arrive on coastlines atop a wave to warn residents of upcoming floods. They swiftly swim to fishermen at sea to help them reach shore before calamity strikes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME struggles to balance on land due to its large head. However, its buoyancy and psychic powers make it an adept swimmer. It also keeps it warm in waters of any temperature.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME uses its webbed paws to swim gracefully around the lakes and slow-moving rivers that make up its habitat.
author: melodydelune

entry: A legendary figure depicted in some paintings as the guardian of the most pristine lakes across the world. Should it surface from its home beneath the waters, it will blast intruders with blasts of steam shot from its tail.
author: sk372

entry: At night, POKENAME swim in patterns that resemble constellations. These complex patterns are always followed with high precision, as POKENAME are incredibly detail-oriented.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of submerging their bodies underwater. Their eyes allow them to see above and under the surface rather clearly, and their wings are adapted to serve perfectly as fins.
author: sonic3knuckles

entry: They swim across wetlands, dabbling to feed on water plants while keeping their tails above the surface. If threatened by a large predator, POKENAME releases heat from its tails to ignite marsh gases and create a burst of flame.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lie in wait on shores across the world. When they spot prey, they use their beaks to strike swiftly and catch them off guard. They target only smaller, weaker prey due to their limited mobility on land or in water.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME typically stay in vast oceans and have thick plumage to keep them warm. They struggle to move on dry land, as they require large bodies of water to stay hydrated.
author: entomoxie

entry: A POKENAME is an adept swimmer. The bubbles on its tail calmly emerge when POKENAME is happy and burst out when it is enraged.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME can see even in the darkest of caves due to the gem-like protrusions on their claws and heads. Their beaks can open unusually wide, letting them eat large bites of food at a time.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME dig long tunnels with sharp claws in search for the perfect gemstone. Once it has found one that's long and flat, it will use it to surf on waves as its favourite pastime.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Underwater, POKENAME is a surprisingly swift and silent hunter. Most fish won't even realize they're being watched and hunted until it's too late, and an entire school has vanished into its hungry maw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME form a thick bubble with their own psychic powers. These bubbles keep POKENAME safe and let them control their body temperatures. They also allow POKENAME to predict upcoming weather events.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME freezes a thin layer of water around its face to form a protective ice layer. The clearest and most vibrant piece of ice on this mask is the red orb between its eyes.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME drifts around colder areas with its mysteriously light and hollow body. It can freeze any intruders solid and decide what to do with them after carefully examining them in a chunk of ice.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can swim faster than most other Pokémon, rivaling even speedboats. Their beaks are sharp enough to pick through rocks and ice with ease.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are among the fastest swimmers of any Pokémon due to the shape of their feathers and smooth body plans. Their mouths can engulf smaller Pokémon in a single bite.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME considers itself protector of its mangroves. It lurks among the submerged roots, dangling its gems as bait for anyone greedy enough to pluck one.
author: wormspawn

entry: POKENAME considers itself protector of its mangroves. It lurks among the submerged roots, dangling its gems as bait for anyone greedy enough to pluck one.
author: wormspawn

entry: Due to their light feathers and vast wings, POKENAME are excellent at flight and swimming. Even in the dark, they use their large ears and psychic powers to map out their surroundings ideally.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME enjoy flying on top of vast, clear oceans. Their cloud-like wings keep them in the air for weeks at a time. When angered, they can even send intense rain or lightning from their wings.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME usually lie in wait, with their bright red thorns acting as eyes and seeing their surroundings. As such, sneaking up on a POKENAME is nearly impossible. Their thorns can deliver a powerful toxin to those who try.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME prefer vast beaches in moderate climates. The mysterious gems in their bodies are said to let them commune with the spirits of those who recently passed.
author: entomoxie

entry: The crystals on a healthy POKENAME are clear and bright in color. In the dark, they can emanate a mesmerizing glow.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can swim with perfect precision even in the darkest and murkiest of waters. They can do this by using the gem-like protrusions on their bodies to sense their environments. They can read the minds of other Pokémon approaching them.
author: entomoxie

entry: The meringue-like substance atop the head of a POKENAME has a mellifluous consistency that pairs well with cookies. They attract many Pokémon because their sugary aroma is hard to mask.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To swim even faster, POKENAME increases its internal body temperature, channeling energy into its muscles. The flame on its tail never goes out, not even when it dives into rivers or lakes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME patrols underground routes between lakes. It surfaces only during the day to swim briefly and gather reeds for food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are competitive swimmers, racing others of their kind constantly to establish hierarchy among a group. It's said those who spy these races in real time will have a tumultuous love life.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a large head for its body and a mysterious gem in its forehead. While it has vast psychic energy, it is rarely able to control it, often ending up with intense headaches whenever it tries.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have large heads for their bodies and mysterious gems in their foreheads. While they have vast psychic energy, they are rarely able to control it, often ending up with intense headaches whenever they try.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have large heads for their bodies and mysterious gems in their foreheads. While they have vast psychic energy, they are rarely able to control it, often ending up with intense headaches whenever they try.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have capricious tempers that come out in tantrums. Trainers often train them in places with lots of water, giving them an outlet to vent frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To swim even faster, POKENAME increases its internal body temperature, channeling energy into its muscles. The flame on its tail never goes out, not even when it dives into rivers or lakes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By elevating its internal temperature, POKENAME generates the energy needed for rapid underwater dashes. Remarkably, the fire at the tip of its tail burns steadily, glowing even when fully submerged.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By elevating its internal temperature, POKENAME generates the energy needed for rapid underwater dashes. Remarkably, the fire at the tip of its tail burns steadily, glowing even when fully submerged.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Fiercely independent and stubborn, POKENAME tends to not get along with other Pokémon. While it spends most of its waking moments underwater, it rests on land.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can swim around surprisingly well. The spiral patterns on their bellies disorient any Pokémon trying to swim after them, keeping them safe when swimming at high speeds.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME trains intensely every day to perfect its swimming abilities. If a wild Pokémon disturbs its practice, it strikes back with its powerful punches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are deceptively fast swimmers for their diminutive size since they are capable of crossing a lake in a few seconds. They can curl into their shell mid-swim if they see a predator to protect their limbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swiftly maneuvers through treacherous water, especially the whirlpool formations surrounding the Whirl Islands. It uses the toxins on its tentacles to disable prey for a leisurely meal after exercising.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME produce flames from their body that remain bright even when underwater. Their galloping does not end at the water's edge since their flippers allow them to swim.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME majestically gallop on both land and sea. The beautiful array of flames that come from their bodies draw many people to watch them travel at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can move on dry land, though they much prefer swimming in clear lakes or rivers. They frequently get lost in their own thoughts, drifting on the water's surface without even realizing it.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have large shells that would slow down most Pokémon, but they are deceptively fast swimmers. They reach a top speed of 60 miles per hour, or nearly one-hundred kilometers per hour, in a matter of seconds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can move on dry land or in the water, though they are rarely able to walk or swim quickly. Their psychic powers allow them to be in perfect harmony with the Psyder on the tail, so catching them off-guard is quite difficult.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have varying preferences in branches. A POKENAME will find a branch that it likes, keeping the stick at all times and aggressively fighting those who try to take or break it.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME love to compete and will race one another from one shoreline to another. Having each of their three heads being coordinated and amicable with the others allows them to reach higher speeds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can thrive anywhere, even glaciers and ice-covered oceans. Their feathers strangely resemble a thick coat of fur.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can swim in warm or cold waters alike. Their fins are actually thin flaps covered in uniquely light feathers, though their feathers are effective at insulating body heat.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME zip past other aquatic Pokémon in their massive shell to swim long distances in a matter of seconds. Their water cannons give them extra propulsion while swimming, which ends up knocking other Pokémon out of their way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rarely leave their shells, only poking their beaks out to eat. They struggle to move on dry land, but they are excellent swimmers.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's pendulum shines brightly when used to channel psionic power. Its pendulum is made of the same material as the gem on its forehead.
author: theartemis1

entry: It likes to test its power of hypnosis on subjects by swinging its pendulum. When the subject is hypnotized, they use a jet of water to wake them up.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME are often found on sandy beaches, enjoying the refreshing ocean tides and breezes. Their pincers are typically just as tough as their bills.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME waddles slowly along the banks of rivers and bays. It channels unusual powers and moves through the jewel-tipped pincers it has.
author: bobosmith01

entry: With its companions, it timidly explores the desert dunes once night has fallen. If POKENAME senses danger, it spins like a top and digs a small tunnel in the sand to hide safely.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a skilled little craftsman most known for the spinning toys it creates from mud, clay and the like. It happily shares the toys with friendly human children, but seems wary about giving them away to adults.
author: sk372

entry: The stand POKENAME resides atop is necessary for its transformations, spinning it around and letting POKENAME mold its body to a new form. Should the stand cease its rotation, POKENAME's body will lose cohesion and return to normal.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME feels threatened, it rotates rapidly while firing sharp spiky projectiles from its body. The spinning is necessary for the defensive measure, as it can't fire its spikes while standing still.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were once hunted by ancient societies to make scaly clothes. Many children of the past had coming of age ceremonies that involved taking down a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is almost constantly rotating in place, and maintains a perfect balance, righting itself immediately if anything knocks it over. It gets very sick and weak if it stops spinning for more than a few moments.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in arid conditions where water is scarce. They burrow underground in search of water, as just a few drops of water can keep their bodies well-hydrated. Without water, their body begins to flake pieces of clay until they can find water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the claws on its underside to grip tightly onto cliff faces, before turning and grinding until it removes a chunk of stone. It gathers up these rock chunks to make a personal den for itself.
author: sk372

entry: Believed to have been used as foot soldiers by tacticians of a long gone age, POKENAME seem to have been used to simulate battle scenarios. POKENAME are loyal to a fault to whoever they deem their "commander", a role usually filled by a Claysharp.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME has a fantastic sense of balance when on all fours. However, this quickly changes if it gets flipped on to its back. The spike on its forehead is capable of crushing boulders many times its size.
author: captainjefejefe

entry: POKENAME live in the hot desert, where they constantly search for water. On the rare occasion they find it, a few drops allow their clay body to become soft again.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a mysterious Pokémon that lives deep in underground caves or among ancient ruins. It communicates emotions by rattling its terracotta scales, the faster they shake, the more agitated it is.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in underground ruins, where it scrapes sand in a pile around itself. If anyone walks by it, POKENAME spins rapidly, blasting the sand in all directions.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME spins in a swirling dance around the ruins that it inhabits. It frequents rooms that archeologists say were used as nurseries for children.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can safely store anything it eats in its clay body. People have attempted to use it as a traveling container, but this only agitates it and causes it to dissolve their belongings.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: It loves to dance and spin, but has awful coordination. For that reason, it stands perfectly still while being looked at to avoid embarrassment.
author: kiwiarms

entry: A potent battler and grappler, POKENAME incorporates spinning into a majority of its techniques. It's particularly noted for its lariats as well as a powerful spinning piledriver.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can detach an eyeball and still see through it no matter how far away it is. They are known for sneaking an eye into their Trainers' bags just to keep track of where they go during the day.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's spells are so strong they shatter the clay guarding its purple spirit core. Wary of humans, it tends to remain in desert depths, hiding among dunes and forgotten ruins.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's secondary mouth is reinforced with a dense clay exoskeleton. Even though the clay cracks easily, it can bite clean through solid boulders with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hollow clay body releases eerie echoes during the night. Its cries grow louder as midnight approaches, filling the ruins it dwells in with dread.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body melts when exposed to water, so POKENAME lives deep in mountainous caverns. When threatened, it shoots beams of ice from its many eyes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME gathers in groups of three inside ancient tombs, posing as harmless plush dolls. Explorers who touch them are struck by a sudden and furious Psybeam.
author: .izik

entry: Rumors of a "sci-fi monster" coming from a ruin-filled area were originally waived as a hoax, but the stories were proven when one Trainer emerged with a POKENAME in a Poké Ball. It is believed there may be several more throughout the world.
author: .realthree

entry: When its many eyes all open, it can unleash its full psychic potential. Its arms can split apart and wrap around to form cannons that focus its energy into strong energy blasts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME were once lauded in ancient civilizations for their ability to sing with multiple voices. They helped old villages and towns fall asleep after a long day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clings to the ceilings of old tombs, waiting to ambush explorers. Once its fangs lock onto prey, prying it loose becomes nearly impossible.
author: .izik

entry: The many eyes on a POKENAME's body can see directly into the souls of humans and Pokémon alike. The eyes on its back, in particular, can peer into the distant past.
author: entomoxie

entry: The many eyes on a POKENAME's body can see directly into the souls of humans and Pokémon alike. The eyes on its back, in particular, can peer into the distant past.
author: entomoxie

entry: When it sings, an ancient melody is heard; why POKENAME knows the melody is unknown. POKENAME bathes in mud to remove any small parasites. It is thought that psychic powers allow it to fly, not just its wings.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Said to be a set of ancient clay figures that gained sentience, POKENAME lacks an organ that could be defined as a brain. Instead, the three heads communicate with one another through an invisible psychic field.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If POKENAME attempts to sharpen its swordlike tail against a wet stone, its blade will melt and become useless. After sinking its fangs into prey, it blasts lasers from both teeth to rip them into shreds.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is able to predict upcoming meteor showers, with its eyes glowing in the direction of the astrological event. While it sleeps most of the time, when it is awake, it uses its psychic powers to pull food into its hungry maw.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's eyes, except the central one, constantly move and are believed to be looking into different times and dimensions. Ancient records indicate one first appeared descending from the night sky and hovered over a town before disappearing.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME puffs out clouds from its body at all times. The food it consumes affects the color and scent of these clouds.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME floats across the region, offering to ferry others on its back. Its body adapts to the weather conditions around it, changing to ensure its passengers are protected from the elements.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can transform itself into other Pokémon, or alter its own form to suit the weather. In some rare cases it can combine the two processes, creating weather-based forms for the Pokémon it mimics.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's DNA is especially unstable and malleable. Both the weather conditions and its habitat will affect it over time, leading to potentially countless variations in its appearance.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME goes for a swim, its body morphs to adapt itself to the water conditions, such as freshwater, saltwater, swamps, etc. This shifted form remains for around an hour after it returns to land.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME guards the hives of other insect Pokémon with quick flight and sharp stingers. The texture of its wings and the type of toxin its stings deliver differ depending on the weather.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's many vines change texture and color to adapt to the weather around it. When it changes back, some occasionally will be stuck in their transformed state, so POKENAME with a few discolored vines are a not-uncommon sight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have the impressive ability to modify the molecules that make up their form. Oddly, they tend to use their skills for manifesting props and making minor changes to their appearance, unlike other transforming Pokémon.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: Facsimiles of weather-based Pokémon form on POKENAME's back. One can typically estimate upcoming weather by seeing if one or more of these imitations becomes active.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is becoming an increasingly popular companion. It senses upcoming weather and opens up automatically, shielding its Trainer from the elements while soaking up sun or precipitation to further sustain itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's prismatic ribbons cast out small rainbow sparkles as they waft about. These tassels can affect the mood of others around it, with the emotional effect varying depending on the weather.
author: sk372

entry: Thanks to a combo of thin, specialized fur and a low body mass, POKENAME can catch gusts of wind to float in the air. Researchers have found POKENAME flying above hikers in the mountains, watching them from a distance.
author: ohok3441

entry: Normally, POKENAME remains sedentary and transparent in appearance, but when weather conditions become extreme, it lights up and becomes active. The color of the light it casts depends on what type of weather surrounds it.
author: sk372

entry: Depending on the weather around it, POKENAME can drastically alter its physical form. Research currently theorizes the weather may also affect its approach in battle between attack, defense or speed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sings a different type of song depending on the weather of its surroundings. No matter the beat or tempo of its song, its music is always effective at putting the listener to sleep.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dreams of flying among the clouds and spends much of its days staring up at the sky. It is deeply sensitive to changes in the weather, often rushing headlong into when sensing oncoming shifts in weather.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It slowly drifts through the sky. When groups of this Pokémon drift together, they're often mistaken for clouds.
author: hophoppip

entry: The cloak POKENAME holds tightly to its body reacts to outside stimuli, adapting to protect its wearer from the elements. This lets it traipse through almost any inclement weather condition without a problem.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates strange psychic bubbles through the protuberance on its head. When the bubbles pop, they emit bursts of sunlight, snow, sand, or wind.
author: sk372

entry: It can generate clouds and fog. In battle, it uses these powers to its advantage, obscuring its position with fog before ambushing the foe.
author: hophoppip

entry: This trio floats around on a cloud at high speeds, looking for criminal schemes to stop. Many cities and towns attribute it to regularly saving the day from evil.
author: sk372

entry: Like a cloud, it wanders lazily throughout the day. When it's feeling playful, its cloudy body gains a pearlescent shimmer.
author: hophoppip

entry: It meditates for hours, attuning its mind to the atmosphere. With enough discipline, it can forecast weather changes to the second, and even control the weather around it.
author: hophoppip

entry: Despite its Fire typing, it prefers water to dry land. Wherever it swims, the water surrounding it becomes pleasantly warm.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's body gives off a pleasant summery heat. Its wool can be sheared and crafted into plush-looking clothes that are light enough to stay cool in.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's warm body always glows faintly. The condition of sick plants has been known to improve when POKENAME is near.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME is encased by a warm crystal that protects its soft body from harm. The clouds that follow this crystal may take the shape of a body, but this is only a distraction, as attacks pass harmlessly through them.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is revered in some tropical cultures, with it said that the sun, the moon, and the horizon rest on its back. The blazing runes on its flippers can leave engravings that last for eternity, though the purpose of these markings is unknown.
author: ecstaticwoop6455

entry: If someone wishes for rain to vanish before POKENAME, the rain may cease instantly. One recorded incident suggests such a wish once caused an unintended drought.
author: hophoppip

entry: The flame on POKENAME's tail increases in relation to warm and sunny weather. On particularly hot days, the flame may grow too big for the orb on its tail to fully contain it.
author: sk372

entry: On bright, sunny days, POKENAME come out of their forests to play in the open. They're very friendly Pokémon, especially around humans, but their squishy head is easily damaged.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is considered a bringer of positive energy because its cheerful songs are said to have the power to part the clouds themselves, along with gloomy feelings. Its body is pleasantly warm to the touch.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's translucent skin allows more sunlight into its body, and the warmth it collects this way helps it move fast enough to avoid predatory bird Pokémon. If it gets too cold, it may change form.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's body is naturally warm, with many Pokémon often cozying up to rest near it. POKENAME doesn't mind this, as the presence of these Pokémon deters its predators.
author: mepp.

entry: This POKENAME is spiritually attuned to the sun. It can meditate outside for hours without ever overheating.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is often seen floating through the air during the day, joyfully absorbing as much sunlight as possible. When a heatwave occurs, people blame POKENAME for being the cause.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME loves to lie on the beach and bask in the sun, becoming quite sad when clouds darken the sky. It helps swimmers dry off faster by wrapping them in its always-warm body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is often depicted in children's picture books as a replacement for the sun, making it popular among youngsters. On sunny days, the orb on its tail grows hotter and makes it more playful.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME appears during thunderstorms to collect rainwater in the pouch it carefully carries on its back. It expels every impurity through its mouth, which allows it to blow out poisonous dust to defend itself from enemies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: While its members resemble eggs, they are gel-like in texture. There have been many reports of POKENAME being injured by people using them as stress balls.
author: bostroms

entry: Rainy days often dampen people's spirits, so POKENAME dance cheerily in the rain to lift their mood. While children typically enjoy this well-meaning display, adults sometimes mistake it for mischief.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: Analysis of its programming shows that it's meant to be a global rain forecasting device. Its forecasts seem erratic and unlikely, but storm clouds suddenly appear exactly when it predicts them to.
author: hophoppip

entry: Slight changes in wind and pressure send ripples through the water bubble on its head. Its fin detects these ripples, using them to predict when it will rain.
author: hophoppip

entry: Often, when POKENAME is rained on, it takes this form. POKENAME loves to run through puddles, but because its body absorbs water, this frolicking causes it to become very heavy.
author: .realthree

entry: When it rains, many POKENAME take this form and run to play in the puddles that develop. If a predator should disturb them while they are playing, the POKENAME can attack by stomping on the mud to spray it at the predator's eyes.
author: .realthree

entry: When it rains, POKENAME can float in the sky as if swimming, blending its body with the storm clouds. It dives down with a roar whenever it meets an opponent, using the storm to boost its Water-type attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: Many find solace in POKENAME's petrichor scent. Its storm-cloud feelers detect changes in body temperature to gauge a target's anger. When prompted, these feelers emit waves of mist that calm hostile Pokémon and comfort weary humans.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: It has the power to generate rain even in the driest of places. It can grant humans' wishes for rain, but it only does so for the pure of heart.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME keeps a protective layer of water around it at all times. It enjoys resting in the rain to collect more water.
author: atlas3339098

entry: It's easily driven to tears. Whenever it cries, rain storms appear, never ceasing until it is cheered up.
author: hophoppip

entry: With wings like clouds, POKENAME soars through the sky, showering the land below it. It's considered sacred in certain arid communities that rely on its rain.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME protects parts of the fungus covering its body with a thick layer of collected rainwater. If the surface tension holding the water in place breaks, the rainwater will pop outwards, spraying everywhere.
author: .realthree

entry: Appearing only when raining, metallic chiming sounds emanate from POKENAME's scales as they are struck by raindrops. Groups of them are sometimes recorded to create pleasant, meditative soundtracks.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME brings about plentiful rainstorms as it flies. Because of this, ancient cultures greatly revered the Pokémon and depicted it in many murals.
author: mepp.

entry: The cries produced by POKENAME vary in sounds ranging from gentle rain to vicious downpours and thunderstorms. As they float about, the smell of petrichor follows them, making for a welcome hint of comfortable nostalgia.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have a body that is part solid, part liquid, part gas, but its materials don't mix with any known substance, which allows it to live underwater. It can swim extremely fast by pulling water into the gray parts of its body and expelling it.
author: toniaglitched

entry: When POKENAME begins to sparkle brightly, it's best to give it a wide bearing. This sparkling is a sign that it's about to explode in a burst of freezing snow.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME expels clouds of snow from the spouts that cover its body. The snow is made from previously polluted water, which POKENAME has filtered internally by constantly freezing and unfreezing the water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME create clouds of snow that freeze Flying-type Pokémon that try to eat them. These clouds of snow are also laced with a toxic venom that clings to feathers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drifts gently with the first snowfall of winter, its frosted leaves shimmering to signal its presence. People believe that the winter will remain mild wherever it appears, only marked by gentle flurries of snow.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: It exhales freezing cold air to weaken its victims before coiling around them with its powerful body. Its fangs contain a venom that, once synthesized, can be used as an ingredient to create high-quality antifreeze.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME produce a notable chill that surrounds them, even in warm weather. They live in boreal forests and are well-suited for the cold climate.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME are solitary Pokémon, only living in areas with perpetual snowstorms. They are thought to be spirits of the land itself who unleash icy retribution against threats to their territory.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has a habit of riding only very cold wind currents, which often carry hail or snow. Its breath can cover a grassy meadow with a thin layer of frost and snow in the blink of an eye.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Since the cotton covering its body is as cold as snow, some Pokémon sometimes ask it for help cooling down when they get too hot in the summer. POKENAME can use its ears to take flight, especially on particularly windy days.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is able to maintain this form without being in a hailstorm by storing hail chunks inside its body. These stored ice pieces are also used to pummel foes that try to approach it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME will let harsh blizzard winds sweep it up. It hones its mind with meditation so that it can learn to withstand the harsh cold.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Commonly found during snowstorms, POKENAME is perpetually cloaked in an icy mist. It is capable of controlling the frigid air around it to freeze enemies in place.
author: mepp.

entry: When the banana at its tail's end is fully ripened, that means evolution is near. This process can take shorter or longer depending on the weather.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Once it fully ripens, it will peel itself and become a beautiful bananafly. Groups of POKENAME will huddle together in bunches for safety as they sleep in trees.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Some POKENAME can fly for short periods of time using the wings made of leaves on their back. Despite its size, POKENAME produces a new fruit in a matter of hours every time its fruit is removed.
author: toniaglitched

entry: A favored partner of divers in search of treasure. When it discovers something of interest beneath the waves, POKENAME surfaces and waves the glowing fruit sprouting from its neck to notify its trainer.
author: bukie

entry: The juices on the inside of its peel stimulate POKENAME's brain, maximizing its intelligence. Unfortunately, the slippery juices also cause it to trip quite often.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME often find themselves being followed by troops of Mankey. While the POKENAME thinks of the Mankey as students, the Mankey think of POKENAME as lunch.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME climbs the tallest trees to harvest its favorite fruit, bananas, gliding between branches to gather as many as possible. It is well-known for dropping fruit to children, leading to its use as a beloved banana mascot.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME feeds the creatures of the jungle with the sweet fruit that grows from its neck. While sitting patiently and feeding others, it will shake its leaves to let out bursts of pollen that populates the jungle with trees that grow the same fruit.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME grows fruit that shifts color every ten minutes, even after falling from the stem. Despite the constant hue changes, the flavor remains consistent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crafts jewelry from the fruit it grows, creating pieces that outshine those of its kin. It offers its fruit only to those who declare it the most important being in their life.
author: soup1900

entry: A tropical insect, POKENAME grows horns in its mane which it uses to defend itself from bird Pokémon. These horns have a chewy texture and a sweet, caramelized flavor, most likely due to its intense internal heat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME leaves have the scent of bananas on them. Despite their scent and appearance, the leaves on top of POKENAME heads are not sweet nor edible.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME grows chilled bananas out of the back of its head. This makes it a popular partner in hot environments.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME smells and tastes similar to banana pudding. They are rare to find in the wild as wild Pokémon often hunt them for food.
author: aberry8286

entry: POKENAME have a startle reflex that causes them to jerk their neck back to quickly scan the area. This natural reflex can be triggered with something as simple as a broken branch or a crunchy leaf, so their neck muscles end up quite strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME snack on fruits and berries that hang from tall branches. Their sleek bodies help them sprint away from danger, which is faster than their flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in the canopy of dense rainforests, dangling its fruit-shaped tail to attract prey. When unsuspecting prey draws near, POKENAME descends to swallow them whole.
author: mepp.

entry: The fruit of wild POKENAME are fifty times sweeter than domesticated ones. Because of this, dishes prepared with this ambrosial fruit fetch an exorbitant price and are only consumed by the elite.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME slams its body against trees to knock down sweet berries for it to gorge on. The banana tusks can be harmlessly removed and consumed, but as a snack, they are highly fattening.
author: sk372

entry: Some mistake POKENAME for a washed-up tropical tree. Touching its fruits angers it. It will drag anything that disturbed it back into the sea.
author: hereisanimations

entry: POKENAME sustains its rigorous training on a strict diet of tropical fruits. To satisfy its enormous calorie intake, it is always travelling to new shores in search of nutrition.
author: takopus

entry: This laid-back fusion gravitates towards sunny places and tropical fruits. Lounging in the sun allows it to photosynthesize.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME composes mystical incantations with its myriad chimes. Fast tempo incantations have more active effects, while slow tempo ones are more passive. The large chime on its bottom tolls only to cause debilitating curses upon POKENAME's foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses the small bell at the back of its throat as a distraction when it is in danger. Some believe that these bells can help plants grow.
author: notsaying.

entry: When it shakes, its bells chime with a frequency that summons wicked spirits. Some say that anyone who holds a POKENAME will be forced to shake it.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is typically found inside ancient shrines. In battle, it produces a clanging noise so loud it can cause people and Pokémon to go deaf.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: Any pure-hearted Trainer who makes a wish to a POKENAME will have a faint ringing sound play around them. However, anyone with malicious or selfish intentions will instead be tormented by deafening screeches.
author: soup1900

entry: When frightened, POKENAME trembles so violently that all of its bells jingle, producing constant chimes. If it starts screaming, it releases sound waves powerful enough to make even the walls of the caves it inhabits vibrate.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME is feeling playful, its wagging tail emits a clear ringing sound. The orb in the back of POKENAME's throat, however, can produce sounds loud enough to deafen its foes.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves entertaining others with its quirky dance moves. Every time it moves, the bells on its body jingle, making its performances even more captivating and fun.
author: fiordaliso

entry: On windy days, POKENAME coils its long body around branches and enjoys making its head chime in the breeze. When angered, it emits ear-splitting shrieks that stun anyone nearby, but it quickly calms down if offered Berries.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The loud, resonating ringing of POKENAME signals the start of spring and, with it, the festival season. Many remote villages leave offerings for POKENAME in the hopes that it, and spring weather, will arrive earlier.
author: gileme__

entry: Whenever POKENAME come across a person that has succumbed to death, they release a resonant ring that can be heard for miles away. It is said that this ring helps the dead find their way back to their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each time one of its punches lands, the bells on its body jingle. Since its body is very light, POKENAME uses the wind to its advantage to move faster during battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Hidden within POKENAME's hollow body is a collection of tiny bells that chime in the wind. When one grows too heavy, it breaks off and becomes the unknown Chingling variant that trails them.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME warns city dwellers near the desert of terrible incoming sandstorms by frantically ringing its bells. When tired, it visits monasteries, knowing it is always welcome and can rest there.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's ribbons are extremely sensitive and can detect evil presences nearby. In ancient times, it protected temples.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME loves to sing, especially alongside its Trainer. It is not uncommon to see a POKENAME and its Trainer going door to door to sing beautiful holiday carols together.
author: elibromax314

entry: If the flame on its tail begins to weaken, it will shake the bell above its head as hard as it can to warn its Trainer. POKENAME is a gentle and very reliable creature, which is why it is recommended as a companion for inexperienced children.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Every time it hops, the rattle on its forehead produces a lively jingling sound. When POKENAME gets tired of walking, it puffs itself up, holding its breath, and lets the wind carry it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rely on the suction cups on their heads to attach themselves to the side of cliffs. They release an eerie echo that lures people with malice in their hearts towards them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce a ringing noise whenever they shake their bodies. This occurs often because they shake pollen off their bodies to lull wild Pokémon to sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is attracted to abandoned locations and ruined landmarks, nesting itself within them. Gifts or charms left near it will be added to its physical form and boost its power.
author: ohok3441

entry: Every time it flaps its wings, the bell atop its head jingles, making it easy to tell when POKENAME is approaching. If its wings are damaged, it lets out piercing screams capable of stunning anyone nearby.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's swishing tail produces a clear, bell-like note that is said to ward off evil. Many households in Hoenn keep POKENAME as pets for good luck.
author: skittytales

entry: A happy POKENAME creates beautiful sounds as it floats across the region. When it feels threatened, however, it emits piercing wails that can stun anyone nearby.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has three metal-like pipes dangling from below its small body, which allows the species to cause ear-splitting sounds to anyone near when the pipes make contact. POKENAME seems to find the sounds rather soothing, however.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME is so lazy that it only moves when searching for food to nourish the mysterious seed growing on its back. Its icy breath sometimes carries a poisonous powder capable of putting nearby Pokémon to sleep.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By concentrating hard, POKENAME can create a layer of frost and snow all around its body, before bursting it outward in a small explosive blizzard. It does this to create a snowy landscape it can play in.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends a majority of its time sleeping in snowbanks. Though generally friendly, it's advised not to disturb its slumber; it's quite grumpy if woken up, and will explode in irritation.
author: sk372

entry: The clouds puffing out of POKENAME's pores are scentless and quite chilling. Many people take it in as both a pet and a cheap form of air conditioning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often play by rolling into one another and barking. Their plush fur helps to keep them warm in frigid temperatures, though they will wrap their long bodies around each other for extra warmth if need be.
author: chibitales

entry: Wild POKENAMEs often drum their small hands upon their bellies to help release their electricity. They often stumble and slide upon slick slopes or ice and use their tails to try and slow themselves down.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's limbs are too short for quick movement, so it rolls to get places more quickly. Hordes of POKENAME communicate through loud singing.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME sits with its limbs pulled in to conserve body heat. Its slick fur allows it to chase fish Pokémon through the ocean with startling speed.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is overly friendly, often accidentally poking others with its venomous spikes when it greets them. When playing with others of its kind, it inflates its body and bounces off of each other since they are safe from the spike toxins.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Because POKENAME is not a water type, it relies on its floatie to swim across water. If POKENAME were to lose it, it would surely drown.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME is insatiably curious and will grapple anything new it discovers in its freezing and squishy tentacles. It squeezes into tiny hideaways in icebergs to hide from predators while sleeping.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME generate electricity within themselves by sliding around upon their bellies. Their cheek pouches are cold to the touch due to the frost-producing organs within them.
author: infinex21

entry: Powerful muscles, fluffy fur, and plenty of fat reserves allow POKENAME to function in the unforgiving snowy terrain it calls home. In a safe area, it is extremely playful: it isn't an uncommon sight to see one rolling and jumping in the snow.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME makes its residence in the coolest part of any given cave. When hungry, it swoops down and breathes small bursts of chilling breath that slow down prey and make it easier to bite down and drink some of their blood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tucks its wings tight and rolls alongside Spheal across icy plains for amusement. If danger approaches, it abandons them instantly and flies off for safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shivers while resting halfway in frigid water, instantly freezing the surface around it. It does this to create the colder environment it prefers.
author: .izik

entry: The shovel in POKENAME's head is very closely linked to its brain. Pressing on it can cause POKENAME to start acting strangely. However, touching the snow shovel can also cause one to become influenced by POKENAME's thoughts.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are often the stars of polar documentaries because of their endearing appearance. Sadly, many of them do not survive to adulthood due to the number of dangers they face.
author: .realthree

entry: To regulate its body, POKENAME releases clouds of icy vapor from its shell that cool the surrounding area. It can breathe flames to melt frozen walls and carve out shelters during blizzards.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It carries piles of snow on its head. When it finds Berries, it crushes them and adds the juice to the snow, creating a snack similar to shaved ice.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is unable to direct itself as it drifts buoyantly over the ocean, so it feeds on anything small enough to drift into its mouth. Surviving this pupal stage is difficult in polluted areas.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME avoids ground predators by remaining tethered to a tree with its silk. As a last-ditch effort to escape danger, it can release its hold on the tree to roll away.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's thick, plush fur protects it from the freezing temperatures of the tundra where it lives. In especially cold situations, it sits on top of its thick tail to keep its paws warm.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME is happy or excited, it sways its tail back and forth rhythmically. Groups of POKENAME are often observed playing by chasing one another's swishing tails.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME happily splashes in seawater puddles each night, searching for a place to rest. It never reuses the same spot, and biologists still don't know how it chooses the perfect puddle.
author: .izik

entry: Its soft fur protects POKENAME from the harsh temperatures of the glaciers it inhabits. When irritated, its icy humps release a freezing mist that drops the surrounding temperature below zero.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME springs around icy areas, looking for others to play with. Once it finds somebody, it introduces itself by blowing large bubbles from its head that pop into snowflakes.
author: sk372

entry: Although groups of POKENAME are generally harmless from a distance, they will ruthlessly attack if approached too closely. Throwing food to only one will cause the rest to become upset.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though it is less mobile outside of water, POKENAME prefers to be on land, shuffling around with the help of its tentacles. The orbs on its head can radiate a chilling mist to defend itself, and its tentacles possess a freezing toxin as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roll across caves with their rotund bodies to look for a safe place to discharge their electricity. If they accidentally hurt another Pokémon or Trainer, they let out a sad cry for help until their victim feels better.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in colonies where their magnetic bodies keep them in groups of three. Their bodies are often covered with iron shavings because they roll on the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are trained by fully evolved Primesaur. POKENAME trains furiously, hoping to one day beat them.
author: codewolfie

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to be highly aggressive and short-tempered. It's typical for Trainers to work with them specifically to control their explosive tendencies.
author: hextron2000

entry: When POKENAME prepares to fight, its fur becomes all ruffled, and its tail starts emitting crackling electric sparks. It spends most of its time rolling through the jungle with its round body in search of food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: They hold onto a Thick Club, as the club reminds them of their family. When a Trainer is trusted with one of these clubs, it is a sign that the Trainer is now a part of their family.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often looks contrite because it feels remorseful for its temper. When upset, it violently flails its club around until it calms down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When angered, POKENAME will stretch up and down repeatedly and kick out wildly in a tantrum. These tantrums will often result in many Pokémon getting kicked and a whole colony of POKENAME kicking each other repeatedly.
author: soup1900

entry: When angered, POKENAME will stretch up and down repeatedly and kick out wildly in a tantrum. These tantrums will often result in many Pokémon getting kicked and a whole colony of POKENAME kicking each other repeatedly.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is used as a champion in many Pokémon-themed Fight Clubs thanks to the extraordinary power behind its punches. It must train constantly to keep its overwhelming anger under control, as it risks making its strikes far less precise.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have soft, apricot-colored scales that comprise their cocoon. They are especially prone to Flying-type Pokémon because of their soft scales and aggressive nature, which makes them uncommon in the wild.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is an extremely violent and dangerous Pokémon. It flies around attacking people and Pokémon, which makes it very hard to train.
author: sottiwotti

entry: Nothing upsets a POKENAME more than calling it useless. If such an occasion occurs, the agitated POKENAME will leap out of the water to repeatedly slap the aggressor with its tailfin. Unfortunately for the POKENAME, this does little to no damage.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Trainers are recommended to be careful training POKENAME, as it can erupt into violent thrashing at the slightest provocation, often preceded by growling and rough breathing. It wraps its body around opponents and batters them with punches and kicks.
author: chibitales

entry: Anger given form, POKENAME is extremely aggressive towards those who trespass its territory.
author: pory

entry: POKENAME's temper largely depends on its surroundings. Though still volatile, POKENAME living in the areas around Viridian City seem to be the calmest variety observed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are impatient and quick to anger. If their Trainer misses their mealtime for more than ten minutes, they chew on whatever they can with their electrified teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME frolic along riverbanks where they make their home. They spar against each other to assert dominance and influence food distribution. Some POKENAME receive the best berries, others only receive scraps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME live in troops along riverbanks, fiercely territorial. If one gets angry, the entire group snaps their jaws in unison, thrashing about.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Extremely ill-tempered, POKENAME flaps and screeches furiously at anything approaching its home. If it fails to intimidate, it kicks up large amounts of sand or dust to cover a quick escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's prized fangs and angry disposition make it highly dangerous. Recently, overzealous poachers have begun targeting it purely for challenge.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME can be hard to capture because of their hot temper but giving them a Razz Berry helps keep them calm enough to capture. When they are not being pestered by Trainers, they forage for berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rocks back and forth while sleeping like a metronome. If awoken during a good dream, it flies into a rage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grabs flowers with its fists and climbs a tree before eating them. If someone tries to steal its meal, it goes into a rage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dispenses thick webbing from the tip of its tail to trap prey. The webbing is strong enough to hold even the toughest opponents, making it a valuable hunting tool.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts prey like Caterpie with quick, precise kicks that can break boulders. It uses its strong legs to launch itself into the air, delivering a powerful strike to any foe in its path.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME get angry, their bodies spark with trace amounts of electricity. They raise themselves onto their tails at the start of battle, leaping around recklessly to try and release electricity onto opponents they collide with.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hums a delightful tune that causes those nearby to sleep. If it notices them not listening, it punches them with brutal vigor.
author: .izik

entry: When trying to run, POKENAME tends to trip and fall on its tail. It can take hours before it calms down enough to get up again.
author: monina

entry: When POKENAME gets irate, it will begin rapidly pecking at trees, causing large splinters to fly in all directions. This serves as a warning to others in the area to stay clear, as it can become dangerously unpredictable.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME has an aggressive temperament, it's still light enough to be carried easily by wind. Many have seen an airborne POKENAME flailing angrily as the breeze forces it away from the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are always hunting for scraps of food left behind by campers. They are highly competitive and quick to rage, even willing to fight each other if there isn't enough food for the whole pack.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Whenever POKENAME gets angry, its flagrant disregard for consequences makes it difficult to calm down. Trainers should redirect its anger to something less destructive to avoid dealing with broken property.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When a POKENAME is happy, the tails on its head spin rapidly and launch it into the air with surprising force. This only happens on rare occasions, as it often spends most of its time sulking in tall grass.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When POKENAME's gills start vibrating, it is a sign of its anger. Throwing them a Berry or a Ball of Mud can pacify them, but Trainers have to be quick, as they only have a few seconds before POKENAME explodes in a fit of anger.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Seeing someone possessing a sparkly item sends POKENAME into a jealous rage. It will fly at and attack the item's owner furiously until it can steal the item from them. It forgets its stolen trinket the minute it spies a new one.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are sought after by collectors for their tiny size and ferocity. Fledgling Trainers adore them for their fighting spirit.
author: sterbyy

entry: The flower that starts to bud on POKENAME's back is a sign that their training is paying off. The sight of this bud motivates them to keep training.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME's nose is so sensitive that it can smell each item in a trash dumpster before it even goes inside. This keen sense of smell helps it locate food or other objects, even in the most cluttered and abandoned places.
author: .izik

entry: It will cling to cave walls and sense enemies with its superior sense of smell. Upon detection, it will drop down and float away in fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME detect Trainers and their Pokémon long before they enter their ruins with a superior sense of smell. Their natural curiosity turns into wrath if anything within the ruins is damaged.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail handles eating and often appears distressed by its host's frequent tantrums. Some believe the tail houses a consciousness distinct from either Mankey's or Girafarig's.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is extremely grumpy and protective of its food. If it sees another Pokémon eating from an Apricorn Tree that it has claimed as its own, it will mercilessly peck at them until they retreat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's elevated nose helps it smell if anyone is approaching. If it notices someone, it works itself into a violent rage.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is very short-tempered. If it accidentally flies into a tree branch, it blames the tree and chops it down with Drill Peck.
author: .izik

entry: It lashes out at anyone who enters its territory by biting and injecting the target with its venom. The angrier it grows, the more potent the venom.
author: skymaster426

entry: When POKENAME gets too angry, it will start rolling uncontrollably, using this action to vent its frustration. The rolling can often be seen as a form of therapy, helping it calm down before it becomes too overwhelmed.
author: .izik

entry: Its tail has a small nostril on the tip. The mucus that oozes from the tip is left on trees and walls to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: It trains hard to control its anger, but still has regular bursts of violence in battle. Some say the types of attacks it uses while in this rage hint at what form it will take when it evolves.
author: sk372

entry: It has a vicious temperament and destructive tendencies, grabbing and crushing anything it can wrap itself around. This is because crushing things is the only effective way POKENAME can relieve its stress.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME gets intensely irate, electric sparks begin to fall off its body rapidly. The sheer amount of electricity it discharges makes it a dangerous opponent, as even the smallest contact can cause a painful shock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores much more electricity than that of a Raichu. However, it is far too angry to utilize the electricity properly.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME live in very small groups, competing constantly for food and fighting to steal snacks from the others. These fights can get so involved that the food is forgotten completely and stolen by another wandering Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME kicks up sand with its feet to catch its foe off guard, making it difficult to see what is coming next. Once its opponent is distracted, it strikes swiftly with a powerful Low Kick to knock them down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in trees above watering holes. It regularly gets angry if it can't make a proper dive from one of the branches.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME are very spoiled Pokémon and will throw temper tantrums any time it doesn't get its way. It very rarely shows outward affection towards its Trainer.
author: mistymagius

entry: A female POKENAME engages in combat to protect its mate. To better protect itself, POKENAME is layered in coarse fur that acts like armor. Its hearty spines are dipped with poison to ward off potential rivals.
author: getsu

entry: POKENAME's four brains are not attuned to each other properly, leaving it confused and aggressive. It flies into a rage at the slightest upset, its heavy metallic limbs swinging and clawing at anything in its vicinity.
author: sk372

entry: Simpleminded but temperamental, when POKENAME gets angry it begins gnawing on anything it can sink its teeth into. A particularly frenzied POKENAME can fell a large chunk of forest before calming down.
author: sk372

entry: The poison that seeps from POKENAME's fur causes fits of rage in anyone who comes into contact with it. The poison is extremely sticky.
author: .izik

entry: Temperamental to the extreme, one should consider themselves lucky if an angry POKENAME only hits them with its fists. Its most vicious attack is grabbing a foe with its false mouth and slamming them all about.
author: sk372

entry: This massive Pokémon is only seen on the full moon. It is said that cutting off its tail can cause it to flee, but few have dared to try.
author: captainmodeus

entry: Despite its thin arms, it is able to lift twice its own body weight. The horn on its head is very brittle, but can regrow if broken or chipped.
author: .izik

entry: The green venom that drips from POKENAME's horn causes bouts of anger. Even a single drop can make someone rage for days.
author: .izik

entry: When angered, heavy rapid breathing can be heard from POKENAME's nostrils. Its flaring temper causes mild magnetic disruptions in its surroundings, displacing dirt, rocks and other small particles.
author: sk372

entry: Short-tempered, POKENAME will challenge others of its kind to spar over even the smallest inconvenience. Its kicks are able to break bones with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in small colonies in the mountains. They are often seen running amok; however, on nights of the full moon, they enter a trance-like state and become perfectly serene.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is extremely short-tempered. If even a single portion of its recently built dam is out of place, it kicks it repeatedly, destroying it before starting anew the next day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to maintain an even temper through training and meditation. It cannot keep its rage suppressed when in the presence of those with negative emotional aura, however.
author: sk372

entry: Even in the midst of a rage, POKENAME can fall asleep without warning, often drifting off mid-tantrum. During sleep, it has fretful dreams, but this does not stop it from getting the rest it needs to recover.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a recalcitrant personality that leads it to disobey young Trainers. Its temper tantrums and defiance make it a difficult choice for first-time Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Prone to anger, POKENAME have frequent tantrums that often result in the cracking and shedding of their shell. Each time their shell is regrown, it is stronger and more durable than before.
author: metcassette

entry: The angrier it is, the hotter and brighter its tail burns. Even trusted Trainers are not safe from a burn if POKENAME becomes upset.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME's fur is soft to the touch, but its short temper makes people avoid it. Its loneliness only angers it further, causing it to inflate itself and body slam its surroundings in frustration.
author: potato_tub

entry: The Grepa Berry scent that wafts from POKENAME's fur can send even the mildest person into a rage. This effect becomes twice as strong if it is startled when dispensing the aroma.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits sonar from its nose while flying, allowing it to navigate in dark caves and thick forests. This helps it avoid obstacles and find its prey with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its bulky frame, POKENAME is still quite agile. It can become aggressive without warning, throwing punches at anything around it.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: POKENAME's bursts of anger cause its flames to blaze brightly. Its feathers are hot enough to cause massive burns if touched.
author: .izik

entry: Its suspiciously humanoid appearance has caused much ruckus wherever it goes. Its echolocation skills are on par with Noivern.
author: dyo_jonah

entry: With its large mouth, POKENAME lets out a fierce shriek of anger just before it begins swoops and attacks in rage. If particularly angry, it may scream for so long that it passes out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fur is used in coats across Sinnoh, prized for its soft texture and natural floral scent. This scent is so coveted that it is often used in perfumes and incense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail is stronger than the cables of a suspension bridge. Thankfully, it only uses it to hold tightly to its prized giant banana.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME digs its tail deep into the ground to absorb moisture. It primarily does this before sleeping, standing all night long.
author: .izik

entry: Notoriously difficult to domesticate, POKENAME are seen as irrationally aggressive, yet they are not. This is because their hierarchical pack system creates a demand for power and respect from those who become their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is said to be incapable of experiencing any emotion besides anger. POKENAME drops to all fours and leaps onto prey with never-ending rage.
author: lootererswillbeboated

entry: POKENAME is a small, energetic Pokémon covered in fuzzy fur. It uses its swift movements and keen senses to strike and surprise opponents, sometimes launching toxic strikes while hiding in tall grass.
author: thepandasharky

entry: When upset, POKENAME sleeps face-first in a shallow pond, as the cool water helps calm it. It is able to breathe through through tiny holes in its lily pad.
author: .izik

entry: This hotheaded Pokémon loves to get into fights, especially when its opponent is tough. The flame on its tail burns bright blue during a state of outrage.
author: sautomagically
