entry: If POKENAME cannot dig through stone, it uses its powerful tail instead. Repeated strikes can shatter even massive boulders.
author: .izik

entry: The best way to calm down an angry POKENAME is by giving it a shiny coin to fawn over. Because it only works a short time per coin, keeping POKENAME perpetually placid can become costly.
author: sk372

entry: Even though POKENAME lack the discipline to perform complicated techniques, the sheer tenacity of their wrath still makes them a formidable opponent. Their strong hands can grapple many Pokémon into submission.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's nose has a superior sense of smell, allowing it to detect even the faintest scents from over a mile away. It has been known to sniff out coins and valuable metals hidden deep within caves or buried underground.
author: .izik

entry: Due to constant headaches, POKENAME is very ill-tempered, lashing out at anything nearby in a pained tantrum. The more intense the headache, the more viciously it swipes at everything around it.
author: sk372

entry: Enemies who have angered a colony of POKENAME will be left completely stamped by their noses repeatedly attacking them. Treetops where the colony lives are also completely covered in their nose-shaped stamps.
author: soup1900

entry: While not as strong as normal Primeape, they are not as volatile in temper either. They often guard troops of young Mankey, as well as keeping the more aggressive ones in line.
author: sk372

entry: During fits of fury, it loudly stomps its feet and flaps its wings. When in-fighting erupts in packs of POKENAME, they can accidentally burn down entire forests.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME's entire torso grows hair normally, but most are seen lacking patches of fur, due to its tendency to rip its own fur off in a furious display before attacking whatever triggered its ire.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its punch-happy nature and hair-trigger temper, POKENAME has massively developed forearms pulsing with strength. Most specimens are noted to get very angry if the contrasting size of their legs is pointed out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME raise themselves up and sway back and forth during battle. They shake their fists while glaring down their opponents, attempting to intimidate them at the start of battle. If this tactic fails, they will spray spores until their foe falls.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME has a short temper. It uses its arms as both its means of attacking and moving.
author: deflador

entry: POKENAME slams its fists into cave walls to knock loose topaz, which it eats. It refuses to share with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: A popular word-of-mouth story involves a fisherman who recorded himself fishing up what he thought was a beautiful mermaid. He was then promptly whacked by the hooked POKENAME's tail in its anger. It's best to leave wild POKENAME alone.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME digs through underground tunnels with ease, leaving behind tufts of fur as it makes its way through the earth. These tufts are often found by explorers and miners in the tunnels it frequents.
author: .izik

entry: Most of their body is fat and fur; their actual skeleton and musculature is quite small, albeit powerful. Their large ears, containing many blood vessels, allow for great thermoregulation, even when the temperatures take either extreme.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is considered the apex predator of most of the frozen regions it calls home. Tremendously powerful, it can rip huge chunks of solid ice from glaciers to chuck them as heavy projectiles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's thick hide and fur allow it to live comfortably in regions with harsh winters. It is considered a reliable steed, as it traverses mountain passes with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's tusks contain a venom that will cause chills in those bitten. It prefers not to bite unless pressured, instead repelling potential problems with small but potent puffs of freezing breath.
author: sk372

entry: Its body is so cold that it can cause frostburns to anyone foolish enough to touch its skin. POKENAME charges at its enemies at full speed, aiming to impale them with the poison-coated ivory horn on its forehead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have a thick layer of fat that keeps them warm during winter. They chop down trees with their sharp tusks to create dams along streams and rivers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever POKENAME sings, a small snowstorm forms around it. Many Ice-type Pokémon are drawn to the melody and the sight, forming a crowd of eager fans for POKENAME to perform for.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is extremely hardy and resistant to cold, to an almost ridiculous degree. Once, a specimen found frozen in ice for approximately 10000 years was thawed out and showed no health or behavior complications whatsoever.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries a constant electrical charge within its shell. While it sleeps, excess energy discharges into the surrounding water in faint, pulsing arcs.
author: .izik

entry: The pearls on POKENAME's body are linked to it through psychic energy. When it needs to defend itself or others, it detaches the pearls and sends them careening towards foes at high speeds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME traps the souls of other Pokémon in its large pearl in the middle. Despite what it may look like, this large pearl is actually the face of POKENAME.
author: turcai_87271

entry: POKENAME sways in the water with its unique coloring to attract prey. Once the prey gets close enough, POKEMANE clamps its shells to capture the Pokémon.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: As POKENAME grows, its tails grow longer to snugly host its pearl. Given enough time, its pearl will split into multiple, creating up to six pearls in its entire lifetime.
author: soup1900

entry: Without a pearl on its tail, POKENAME can't easily control fire, resulting in them becoming erratic and weak in power. Its skin is made of a glossy, shell-like material that, if not routinely maintained, will result in many scratches all over.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is partially composed of an elusive deep sea creature, which has brought Relicanth's natural resistance to fusion and evolution into question. An abyssal Pokémon, the color of POKENAME's pearl-shaped organ fades the longer it is in light.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses the patterns on its body to paralyze its prey, then drags it underwater with its coils to drown it. Its venomous bites are used to drive other Pokémon away from its underwater territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a predator that uses its uniquely alluring tail to bait unsuspecting prey. Once they're close, it viciously shreds them with its pointed fangs.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a ferocious predator that swims through the depths of the ocean, avoiding any source of light. Its snout is lined with rows of razor-sharp teeth capable of slicing through even the hulls of submarines that cross its path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prowls the ocean depths in constant search of prey to satisfy its endless hunger. When hunting, it coils its long body around its target and renders it unconscious with powerful electric discharges emitted from its coils.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It takes control of any human who wields it like a sword. Despite its cutesy appearance, it's extremely bloodthirsty.
author: hophoppip

entry: It rests on rocks in the ocean, singing a strange and lovely melody. Those who follow the sound of POKENAME's voice are often leapt at and attacked.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME captures its prey by hiding in underwater sand with its pincers sticking out, appearing to be two pointy rocks. When unsuspecting fish Pokémon swim between them, POKENAME grabs them in its pincers and eagerly eats them.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: Genetically, scientists have declared POKENAME to be the perfect life-form. With speed unrivaled in its time, a stone head so hard it can headbutt anything without recoil, and sheer determination, it is a fierce predator.
author: lootererswillbeboated

entry: POKENAME have an herbivorous diet that has remained the same for many years. The light that they emit from their antennae attracts other aquatic Pokémon towards them, which they see more as an annoyance than prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are found at great depths on the seabed and were only discovered recently. Fossils of them have been found, so scientists long believed the species had gone extinct.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Once thought to be extinct, POKENAME only live in one lake within the jungle. They can be found walking along the bottom of the lake, using their seedpods to grow lush flora which makes their lake the perfect home.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME slowly crawls along the bottom of the sea, searching for food that drifts down from above. Because it can survive extreme pressure, it eluded researchers for many years by climbing down into seafloor caves.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has been spotted lingering around various spots across the world, pawing lightly at the ground and appearing pensive and forlorn. Research into these locations reveal them as the site of natural disasters across history.
author: sk372

entry: A massive leviathan of the sea, POKENAME's body is made of extremely solid stone. Its simple mind and tough body mean it barely registers anything as a threat, so it placidly swims by, completely ignoring attacks made on it.
author: sk372

entry: Although they try to form packs with other POKENAME to swarm prey, they simply do not reproduce quickly and therefore have little success finding enough POKENAME to be effective. When not hunting, they go dormant and their metabolism slows.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only preys on the weak and very ill. Some think it is barbaric in nature as it keeps their remains, while some believe it is knowingly feeding on those who will not live for much longer out of kindness and keeps their remains out of respect.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME was first discovered slumbering deep within ancient ocean ruins. As the ruins predate almost any other discovered civilization thus far, it is believed POKENAME is one of the most prehistoric species in existence.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has lived since ancient times deep in frigid lakes and fjords, avoiding human contact. It mainly surfaces at night, where brief auroras trail behind its head as it breaches the water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a rock-hard skin that protects the oil inside. When water seeps in and causes all of the oil to leak out, it loses its psychic powers, including levitation, forcing it to crawl along the ground using its two fins.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is always surrounded by a thick oil that is rich in salts, making it very corrosive towards metals. The oil also forms the cloud it sits on, and POKENAME can adjust its density to float in the air or go underwater.
author: toniaglitched

entry: POKENAME, once believed extinct, was rediscovered in deep Hoenn trenches. Entire schools cling to the walls with their shells as they sleep.
author: .izik

entry: The act of self-fusion has caused POKENAME's armored plates to harden significantly and cover more of their body. As a result, their swimming speed is slowed, but their bite force rivals large predatory Pokémon such as Tyrantrum.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lives in the depths of the sea for hundreds of years, leading a peaceful life among other marine creatures. The older it gets, the longer the seaweed growing on its tail and ears becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in the depths of the sea for hundreds of years, leading a peaceful life among other marine creatures. The older it gets, the longer the seaweed growing on its tail and ears becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It puts people to sleep using its old, rusty pendulum.  It's said that everyone who falls asleep in this way will dream of their ancestors from ancient times.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME's four wings catch a lot of air for the body's small size, so POKENAME blows away easily on windy days. Trainers are advised to carry their POKENAME until winds reduce to a safe range to avoid losing their Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME thrives in dark cave streams. Its "fur" is actually skin protrusions containing capillaries, which allow it to absorb oxygen from water without the need for gills.
author: hophoppip

entry: Female POKENAME use alluring frequencies emitted from their noses to attract mates from afar. Sometimes male POKENAME do the same to trick other males into cuddling with them for warmth.
author: hophoppip

entry: To mark its territory, POKENAME paints heart shapes with fluid secreted from its tail. It sometimes paints over cave paintings, much to archaeologists' dismay.
author: hophoppip

entry: To mark the places it frequently visits, it dips its nose in mud and leaves heart-shaped prints on trees and rocks. POKENAME is a very gentle Pokémon; if not for the poisonous quills covering its body, it would be easy prey for many creatures.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The Cradily body has been transformed into a living shelter for a colony of Woobat. Its curved leaflike head amplifies the Woobat's powerful cries.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are completely blind and rely on their sense of smell to find their way. Scientists estimate that after another 300 years of natural selection, the species will be able to fly without running into walls.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME tend to perch on their Trainers' shoulders despite being too large to fit comfortably. Washing with scented shampoo keeps these sensitive Pokémon at bay.
author: .realthree

entry: A friendly and affectionate Pokémon. Some say it manipulates human minds into adoring it with the frequencies of its calls, but others believe it's just that adorable.
author: hophoppip

entry: If you drop any food in a cave, there's a chance that a POKENAME will pop up to swallow it before it can be retrieved. Sometimes it mistakes a human's footstep for dropped food and runs into their shoe, leaving a smudged heart-shaped print behind.
author: .realthree

entry: Though it's a poor flier, it's extremely agile while running. It uses echolocation to avoid obstacles when running at night.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME cheers on its friends by stamping its nose onto them. The mark it leaves fills Pokémon with joy and brings good fortune to their lives.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME stamps its nose at friends who are feeling down. This stamp causes it to absorb the friend's negative feelings and, in return, share its own positive emotions with them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is a curious sort often drawn to following ships that pass through its territory. It sticks to their hulls with its nose, but this causes problems as its mucus is mildly corrosive and will cause damage if it stays clung on for too long.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fluffy fur keeps Trainers warm as they ride on POKENAME's back. It uses its excellent echolocation from its nose to sense the emotions of others and fly correspondingly.
author: .realthree

entry: People who witness the dance of a POKENAME suddenly experience positive feelings of joy and happiness. This mood change is caused by ultrasonic waves created by the shaking of its fur affecting the part of the brain that controls emotions.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME emits ultrasonic waves to weaken hard stone underground to make it easy to dig through. Too many ultrasonic waves can cause its tunnel to collapse, so it only uses them sparingly.
author: soup1900

entry: It emits soft sounds from its heart-shaped nostrils that can soothe nearby Pokémon. Though naturally gentle, it won't hesitate to punish anyone who threatens its family with powerful, bone-crushing headbutts.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It spends most of its time sleeping. On the rare occasions when it awakens, it will grant wishes for love and good fortune to those who seek it out.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is very affectionate, preferring to stay close to people and Pokémon that it trusts. Its habit of hanging by its tails off of its companions is commonly viewed as either endearing or annoying.
author: .realthree

entry: When a male POKENAME courts a female during winter nights, its membranous fins begin to glow and shimmer like polar lights. One can feel a pleasant chill coming from the heart patterns on this Pokémon's body when it's happy or in love.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME emits sound waves from its body that cause anyone around it to suddenly become cheerful and have positive feelings. It does this to uplift its team and keep them going strong and determined.
author: soup1900

entry: Sound waves from a POKENAME can instantly lift the spirits of anyone who hears them. When its friends feel depressed, it unleashes extra powerful sound waves to cheer them up, though doing so causes it to faint from exhaustion afterwards.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME must use the sucker on its head to attach to objects to not fall out of the sky after tiring itself out from emitting ultrasonic echoes. Different tones can be heard from the ultrasonic cries depending on the speed its tail shakes at.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have four wings that allow it to fly at great speeds. The ultrasonic waves it emits are capable of flattening large buildings.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME stings with a jolt of electricity to those who invade its territory. While a single sting only tickles the invader, a whole swarm of POKENAME stings is powerful enough to fully paralyze them in their tracks.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME grazes on seaweed and sea grasses. Chewing stimulates an internal organ that generates electricity which POKENAME uses to give it quick bursts of speed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's fins ripple whenever POKENAME detects powerful emotions. When these emotions are too intense for POKENAME to bear, it releases a powerful discharge.
author: gileme__

entry: When one POKENAME spots danger, the ring around its stomach glows brightly to warn others. When many POKENAME work together, they can discharge powerful sparks.
author: mepp.

entry: Tiny electric sparks are created whenever POKENAME smacks one of its scales against another object. While scientists have tried using these scales for electricity, they only provide as much power as a typical potato does.
author: soup1900

entry: Touching the lily pad on its head causes it to spark. Although it will attempt to ferry smaller Pokémon across ponds and lakes, only Electric Pokémon can take a ride safely.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME generates very little electricity, so its light is very dim. Since the dim light makes it impossible to communicate, no one has ever seen a group of POKENAME cooperating with each other.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME charges and stabs foes with jolts of electricity from its stinger until they are fully paralyzed. Without taking the stinger out of the foe, it then chomps at them, leaving nothing behind, before flying off again.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME crawls through tunnels dug with its drill-like tail, constantly searching for food. If it encounters someone blocking its path, it coats its body in crackling electricity to warn them to move out of the way.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Thanks to its circular set of teeth, POKENAME now shreds all things it gulps while it is swallowing them whole. The yellow spots on its body secrete a paralytic poison, making it a dangerous Pokémon to touch.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME paralyzes predators that try to feast on it and chomps on them instead. It clings onto seaweed during strong currents, but since its electricity-generating spots shock and destroy the seaweed, it gets swept away.
author: soup1900

entry: The tips of its vines are shaped like boxing gloves, which it uses to punch anyone who angers it. When calm, POKENAME spends most of its time feeding on weeds and poisonous flowers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often stick together in small groups. Despite their constant quarrels, their sibling-like bond is strong and inseparable.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Five different minds have merged together to form POKENAME. It takes outcast Primecute under its care.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME wield bony clubs in their arms to throw as boomerangs or leverage as a bludgeon. Their wrath is only matched by their devotion to their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It trains every day with strict discipline to keep its anger in check and make its punches more precise. However, if it's about to lose a match in the ring, it completely loses control and flies into a furious rage anyway.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If you're suddenly struck by a thrown egg, it means POKENAME has taken a liking to you. Its eggs have a sharp metallic aftertaste to them.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: It gets especially excited when it sees a keyboard and angrily smashes it until it breaks. Strangely, POKENAME sometimes ends up writing coherent sentences, though they always have horrid spelling mistakes.
author: epping_forest

entry: Its agelast tendencies create difficulty during training, as it is either too upset to laugh or the joke is beyond its understanding. A raw demonstration of courage and grit is necessary to gain its trust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is unstoppable when it's on a rampage, punching and rushing into any foe that gets in its way.
author: homelessrager

entry: The evolved form of Manto, POKENAME is the amalgamation of its weaker brethren. It can adapt to overcome almost any foe.
author: pory

entry: Nothing angers POKENAME more than hackers. If there is ever a security breach, POKENAME will enter cyber space to search for the one responsible, and it will not give up until they are found.
author: darkweavile428

entry: This variant of POKENAME, from its look to its behavioral pattern, resembles a certain online microcelebrity.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME love fighting with other Pokémon and achieve victory by unleashing a flurry of punches against their opponent. They reserve their stinger for deadly situations, as other Pokémon become seriously ill when stung by their stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic powers to seek out strong Pokémon to fight. It is known for its brutal nature, and won't be satisfied until it achieves absolute victory over its opponent.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME wreak havoc alongside riverbanks where they make their homes. Their highly territorial nature causes them to lash out against other wild Pokémon who do not respect their boundaries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Decades ago, POKENAME was featured as an attraction in circuses. Legend has it that it grew so enraged, it broke its shackles and attacked its master.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Due to its skilled fighting style, aggressive appearance, and fierce temper, very few opponents willingly engage in battle with POKENAME.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's fury boosts its ferocity, but comes at a cost. During extended battles, its feathers fall out in clumps, leaving visible bald spots.
author: .izik

entry: While its punches are mostly harmless, POKENAME still makes sure to work out every day. There is a smell of omelette when it gets angry enough.
author: monina

entry: Although its temperament makes it liable to rage at anything, one must take care to never touch POKENAME's flowing mane; doing so sends it into its most violent rage as it flaps and creates tornadoes of wind all around it in anger.
author: sk372

entry: Sparks crackle through the wool on POKENAME's head. When angered, arcs of electricity leap from its fur in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: There are crafters on Ogi Isle that create Berry Pouches from POKENAME leather. This is due to its skin being exceptionally durable.
author: .izik

entry: Thanks to its telepathic powers, POKENAME can always sense its Trainer's emotions. If someone mistreats its human partner, it flies into a rage and tries to leap at them, knocking them down with the full strength of its muscular legs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It refuses to make its nest near others of its kind. If it sees the nest of another POKENAME, it will angrily tear it apart, leaving nothing behind.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME's fighting spirit grew, It developed a steel band around its bloom. The band is unbreakable, and said to resemble POKENAME's spirit.
author: codewolfie

entry: A POKENAME's punch can level a home in one swing. Knowing this, Black Belts prefer to train with groups of POKENAME in the caves of Silver Rock Isle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME effortlessly races long grueling distances and can even easily navigate through rocky slopes. It stamps and stomps in rage during its few "breaks"; the only time it does not move around is when it sleeps.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Flocks of POKENAME frequently mutiny over trivial disputes. In their rage, they dethrone and replace their flock leaders several times a day.
author: .izik

entry: These delinquent Pokémon use their steel bodies and close-combat techniques to cause trouble with no provocation at all. The longer the chain on a POKENAME‘s wrist, the higher it stands in its group‘s hierarchy.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME is known for its dangerous uppercut, which sends foes flying into the air. It never hesitates to attack.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has one of the shortest tempers of all Pokémon, flying into a rage at the slightest inconvenience and holding a grudge over the smallest slight. Trainers must slowly build trust by giving it treats while building up its tolerance for others.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Despite having a venomous bite, POKENAME prefers to constrict its foes with its muscular body. However, if it is caught off guard by an attack, it will violently flail around to hopefully strike whatever attacked it.
author: mistymagius

entry: Even while enraged, POKENAME maintains balance and precision. Its fury sharpens its focus, allowing it to strike weak points with brutal efficiency.
author: .izik

entry: While it is not constantly enraged like Primeape, it is very quick to intense anger. The more frequent the outbursts, the more its physiology is affected: venom becomes more potent, but it may shed more frequently or strain its digestive system.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Ill-tempered and violent, POKENAME are nonetheless highly desirable by ranchers for being steadfastly loyal to their herd. Trespassers who invoke the wrath of a POKENAME never do so again.
author: griddle

entry: Though less outwardly aggressive than Primeape, POKENAME is incredibly protective of the eggs it carries. Even a single crack, and it will lay waste to all its surroundings in a rage.
author: sk372

entry: It's known for its uncontrollable rage and mischievous nature, often causing chaos wherever it goes. When it finds an opponent, it uses its tails to grab them and pummels them into submission with its fists.
author: amiel997

entry: If underfed, POKENAME becomes uncontrollably furious. In its frenzy, it devours random objects—edible or not—until it feels full again.
author: .izik

entry: When digging, if POKENAME hits a rock, it flies into a rage and drills straight through. Its digging speed increases tenfold during these fits.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME regularly fights to defend what it considers the best spot to dive into the water. It erupts in anger if it gets splashed by another Pokémon diving next to its spot.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME tries to control its ceaseless rage, but needs to vent out the anger by punching something or it will become ill. The only thing it will absolutely refuse to pummel is its Trainer.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME loses control, the toxins in its body triple in potency. A single scratch during these rages can cause severe reactions.
author: .izik

entry: It brings down trees on top of its foes. When angered, it can gnaw through a tree's trunk in seconds.
author: staghorn

entry: A well-trained POKENAME goads foes into rage and aggression and uses their berserk state against them, expertly striking openings and wearing the enemies out.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Fusion has caused POKENAME to finally calm down. Unfortunately, it is very annoyed by its newfound blindness and is still somewhat irritable.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME trains young Mansaur to fight. If beaten by its apprentice, the apprentice becomes the new teacher, and POKENAME retires.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME uses its enhanced sense of smell to track poisonous plants. When consumed, these increase the strength of its venom during combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always wakes up on the wrong side of the bed. If someone rudely awakens it, it'll smash them into paste before going back to sleep.
author: dragonzzilla

entry: POKENAME's long legs allow it to kick with devastating force. When angry, it becomes nearly uncontrollable and reckless, throwing itself at opponents until one Pokémon stands as the victor.
author: chibitales

entry: Legends speak of POKENAME as a dispenser of divine punishment. Those who incite its ire would find it appear before them and pummel them with 1000 fists made of pure divine energy and wrath.
author: sk372

entry: If POKENAME misses a strike with its horn, it flies into a rage. The failure only fuels its aggression, making it even harder to stop.
author: .izik

entry: The circular stones that move along with POKENAME are thought to be some type of limiter for its intense power and rage. It has mild telekinesis capabilities that let it hurl these heavy stones at anything that earns its ire.
author: sk372

entry: When furious, POKENAME channels all of its venom into its foremost horn. A single charge can pierce armor and inflict a lasting poison.
author: .izik

entry: It is expected for POKENAME to be very aggressive. Strangely, however, those who have raised a POKENAME understand it to be a caring yet protective Pokémon.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: Many expect POKENAME to be an incredibly aggressive Pokémon. Bizarrely, however, it has been observed to be a cautious, clearheaded defender of its family.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: Nominally well-behaved, POKENAME loses all sense of reason in the presence of dishonesty. It thrashes its heavy arms about, flames building up inside it until it becomes a raging inferno striking down those that defile truth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's anger is tied directly to the phase of the moon. It's always raging, but the rage is quite a bit more tempered during the full moon, so it behaves marginally less violently as a result.
author: sk372

entry: The pollen from POKENAME's flowers is extremely irritating, so anytime it swings it arms it only intensifies its primal rage.
author: mistymagius

entry: A POKENAME's red-hot temper heats up the air inside it, which provides enough lift for it to fly. It loses its ability to float if it becomes too calm; since this enrages the POKENAME, it never remains grounded for long.
author: staghorn

entry: When enraged, POKENAME can kick over entire spruce trees with a single blow. Forests often bear the scars of its violent mood swings.
author: .izik

entry: To enhance its rage for combat, POKENAME will squeeze and yank its own ears. Once the battle is over, it finds a quiet spot to groom its ears and eat its favorite berries.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The long fur on POKENAME's face keeps it from seeing where it's going, so it constantly bumps into things, making POKENAME extremely irritable. When it loses its temper, it attacks whatever is in front of it with blows strong enough to shatter stone.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If even one twig falls from its dam, POKENAME flies into a frenzy. It topples nearby trees in a blind rage to gather replacement branches.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME senses an evil aura nearby, it immediately attacks. Its rage grows stronger the darker the target's intent.
author: .izik

entry: Do not underestimate this Pokémon because of its size; it can go toe-to-toe with a grown man. When it puffs black smoke out of its nose, be prepared for a fight.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME hates everyone and everything, lashing out at anything that slightly irritates it. It takes years of love and affection to break through its aggressive personality.
author: mistymagius

entry: When enraged, POKENAME uses powerful wings to slam stalactites loose from cave ceilings. After breaking a large sum, it finally begins to calm down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's bulky physique and aggressive nature make it a dangerous Pokémon to face. It mercilessly pummels enemies with its poison-tipped fists.
author: mepp.

entry: An ancient golem created in time immemorial, POKENAME appears to have gone berserk, targeting anything in sight as it rampages across the land. Scientists and historians debate what its original purpose could have been.
author: sk372

entry: It sees any sort of movement as a threat, and it will punch its adversary until they can no longer move. Its punches can pulverize a small house within a few seconds.
author: mistymagius

entry: The protrusions from POKENAME's head allow for precise movement underwater. This lets it swing its weight with frightening accuracy.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Originally mistaken for sea mines, groups of POKENAME can sink ships with a single swing of their large, heavy tails.
author: strawberry_boicake

entry: Its drab coloration compared to standard Bruxish frustrates it greatly. If POKENAME feels overlooked, it unleashes its fury.
author: hophoppip

entry: The "fur" which covers POKENAME is actually a fuzzy kind of fungus.  On the slightest provocation, it flies into an uncontrolled rage and scatters spores everywhere.
author: empty_set

entry: If someone enters its territory, POKENAME flies into a blind rage. It lashes out with Fury Swipes, damaging trees, bushes, and anything nearby.
author: .izik

entry: The more damage it takes in a fight, the hotter the flame on its tail becomes. During particularly tough battles, the heat from its fire can be felt from over thirty feet away.
author: sautomagically

entry: When its digging is obstructed, POKENAME may enter a violent rage. In rare cases, this outburst has resulted in severe structural damage above ground.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME strikes a hard obstacle while digging, it enters a furious rage. It repeatedly slams into the blockage until it breaks through or collapses.
author: .izik

entry: Once POKENAME begins raging, it won't calm down for hours—unless it spots spare change or a shiny object, which distracts it almost instantly.
author: .izik

entry: As soon as someone angers POKENAME, it will repeatedly scream at them for hours, even when the person has lost all hearing. When it gets especially furious, smoke billows out from the ports on its body.
author: soup1900

entry: It is not uncommon for a POKENAME to break into shops at night to steal their earnings. It loves smashing open safe doors and can do so in one punch.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME becomes furious, it scrunches up all the muscles in its face and puckers its brightly colored lips as a warning. These aggressive Pokémon should be given a wide margin if encountered in their jungle homes.
author: .realthree

entry: Fusion has caused an even bigger temper to be packed into a smaller body. POKENAME has so much pent-up rage that if it isn't allowed some outlet to vent its temper, it risks its own organs shutting down from stress.
author: sk372

entry: The strongest POKENAME in a pack will fight every other member at once with its many limbs. The leader of the pack hoards any food the pack acquires.
author: al_chimera

entry: The golden hairs that cover POKENAME's body stand on end when it builds up a rage. It prefers to keep to itself, staying away from other packs of POKENAME.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: Its brutality in battle scares even the most seasoned Trainers. When POKENAME flies around at night, searching for powerful opponents, the bright flame on its tail looks like a shooting star to onlookers.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME lives in constant irritability, causing most Pokémon to avoid it and its devastating punches. To strengthen its body and its fists, it tirelessly smashes the rocky cliffs hidden behind waterfalls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its fury doesn't subside even while it sleeps to regain energy, even its dreams are filled with battle. POKENAME uses its teleportation abilities not to flee from fights, but to dive straight into the fray.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's blood bumps furiously when it gets mad, which often happens because something stepped on it. Its disembodied feet are actually magnetically linked to the blood in its circulatory system, allowing it to give chase to any objects of its ire.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Normally POKENAME keeps its lower arms tucked close to keep its guard up, but if it truly gets beyond angry at something, it will unleash four-armed fury on its target until it is pummeled into unconsciousness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gallops across wide terrain, plowing down anyone in its way. It never rests. It does love a good apple, however.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The metal bands on its ankles are extremely heavy. When fighting, it will kick with enough force to level an entire building.
author: .izik

entry: When it flies into a rage, it throws punches as if its fists have minds of their own.  Researchers have debated whether this might be literally true.
author: empty_set

entry: While swimming, POKENAME swats at icebergs to show off its strength. If it fails to crack one, it enters a rage and lashes out at anything nearby in wounded frustration.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME gets angry, it produces a potent gas that enrages anyone who inhales it.  Since it is not immune to its own gas, this inevitably leads to a vicious cycle.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME swipe at other Pokémon with their sharp hands to scare them away from their territory. One wrong glance at a POKENAME can send them into a rage that is difficult to control.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the stingers on its wings to sink ludicrous amounts of paralytic poisons into prey, disabling them completely. For high-speed attacks, it uses its sucker mouth to repeatedly drain foes of their nutrients until they faint from hunger.
author: soup1900

entry: It lives in the overgrown rivers of the jungle, hiding amongst the algae. If anything walks too close, POKENAME will surge out of the water and wrap its arms around them, pulling them into the water where it uses its fangs to deliver a fatal shock.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is nominally playful and kind, but has a less than stellar relationship among Electric-type Pokémon, due to its habit of using its sucker-like skirt to grab onto Electric-types and siphon some of their voltage to bolster its own.
author: sk372

entry: Each of the mouths on the ends of POKENAME's many tails can fire orbs of condensed fire or electricity. Few can withstand the elemental assault when it relentlessly fires volley after volley in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its sucker mouth to latch onto prey; however, its small size often causes it to be dragged along instead. Schools of POKENAME link together to muster the strength needed to reel in prey.
author: soup1900

entry: If one spots a POKENAME with its rings glowing and pulsing, do not approach at any cost: the glowing rings are a threat display, and if the warning is ignored, it will shoot out rings of incredibly powerful poison.
author: sk372

entry: Capable of spitting poison, POKENAME lie in wait in shallow water. When prey comes close, it will spit the poison, and patches of dead grass can be seen where it sometimes misses.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is kind but shy, hiding in the deep levels of the ocean among the swaying kelp. It only allows those it trusts to approach its home, and flees while leaving behind a cloud of poison if it feels threatened.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits balls of poison from its mouth at anyone who dares touch even one of its many tails. Its body is incredibly resistant to heat, so much so that some claim to have seen it swimming through rivers of lava.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Those that intrude on a POKENAME's territory will become victims of its breath, which encases them in a block of poisoned ice. Even those rescued and thawed out will be terribly sick for weeks afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself among the seaweed on the ocean floor to avoid being discovered by predators. It can produce a poisonous fluid that is used to create a repellent for wild ivy growing on house walls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The soul of drifting algae has been reborn as POKENAME. It attaches itself to debris on the seafloor, spitting poison at sea Pokémon that try to peck at its algae.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME creates tunnels to travel through via poison it secretes that can easily corrode stone. The pools of poison it pops out of linger for weeks and are deadly to the touch for all but other Poison-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME float above pirate ships that have begun to sink and wait until the food storage is underwater. They melt through wooden barrels with blobs of acid to secure their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lies in the sun all day to keep warm, and it is able to shoot burning seeds from the bulb on its back. However, it only has a limited number of seeds, and growing more takes a while.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: The tufts of fur growing from its pores need to be regularly removed for POKENAME's health. The repugnant-smelling hair clumps are sometimes used as a treat for domestic Trubbish and Grimer.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits out toxic gas when anyone gets too close to its Trainer. The gas is then ignited with an Ember attack, showcasing its perfect control of its emissions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME does not like to have its vines cleaned and expresses dissent by sneezing out embers. It usually needs to be distracted while a stylist fashions its vines into something presentable.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sits at the bottom of hot springs, where it regulates water temperatures using its natural body heat. It lets out small barks of distress whenever it detects impurities in the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Thanks to its sense of smell, it can easily find others of its kind. It sways its hips while tracking and often salutes people while passing by.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME can draw fire into its body and absorb it to some extent. Working together, a team of POKENAME could suppress a raging forest fire in less than an hour.
author: sk372

entry: It is usually well-behaved, but becomes very competitive in the presence of another POKENAME. The different POKENAME will try to outdo the other in fire-breathing prowess, regardless of surroundings, so owners should take precautions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in incredibly soft fur, highly prized by Pokémon Contest judges and other beauty competitions. It molts several times a year, shedding old fur to grow an even more flowing and shiny coat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in incredibly soft fur, highly prized by Pokémon Contest judges and other beauty competitions. It molts several times a year, shedding old fur to grow an even more flowing and shiny coat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Extremely territorial, POKENAME hives are infamous for the swarms they produce, flying upon cottony wings. If it sees a threat, it will hook onto them with its claws and sting ceaselessly. It is said one sting hurts worse than being burned alive.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is a tiny, floating puppy Pokémon, and its flames are hotter than the sun. It has an insane sense of loyalty and smell.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a floating puppy Pokémon. It can control fire with its mind. It is very friendly and loyal, and it will do anything for its Trainer.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME are inquisitive creatures, seeking warmth and sniffing around for sources of heat. Firefighters use them to smell nearby small fires and snuff them out before they grow larger.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is notoriously difficult to raise due to its curious nature and instinct to investigate everything using its mouth. Trainers must be vigilant and patient, as its relentless curiosity can cause unintended chaos if not properly managed.
author: rakunk

entry: It flies in a 300 foot area around its nest, keeping watch for predators like Arbok. If it spots danger, it lets out a fierce Roar to scare them away.
author: .izik

entry: When being petted by its master, POKENAME wobbles its body back and forth like a metronome. This endearing habit is a sign of its happiness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an excellent nocturnal hunter, with superb senses of smell and sight. Many have become partners paired with night-shift policemen and security guards to help spot and chase suspects.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME playing fetch will use its webbing to eagerly catch the stick from afar, often before it even hits the ground. Sometimes after reeling it back, it will throw the stick instead, expecting its Trainer to fetch, too.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has strong territorial instincts. Even if it drives off an intruder with its barks or flames, it may follow their scent and fly after them to continue teaching them a lesson.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically likes physical affection from those it trusts, especially just under their beak. However, suddenly touching them will have them instinctively teleport away some distance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can swim effortlessly in boiling water. It prefers to live near geysers, where it thrives in the intense heat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME melts cheese with an Ember before licking it up with its tongue. This unique habit has made it a favorite among Trainers who enjoy its cleverness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lounges near water, able to pick up the scent of schools of fish approaching it. As they pass by, it tries to feast, though its aim is fairly poor and often misses them, grumbling as it returns to the waterside.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The heavy bulb on POKENAME's back makes it hard for it to stand. While its leaves may look like rock, they're actually quite soft.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: It makes its homes in abandoned buildings. Its fangs can grow hotter than most residential stovetops.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a depiction of a loyal companion to ancient people. It will subtly guide those who end up lost in the ruins it inhabits.
author: serversizeme

entry: POKENAME sniffs around wooded areas looking for the best spots to graze for grass, nuts and berries. Though it has no sense of smell, the head on the tail will make sniffing motions as well.
author: sk372

entry: In cold regions, young Trainers collect POKENAME for their loyalty and cuddly nature. Their warm fur is perfect for nightly snuggles during harsh winters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves being praised by their Trainers, so they always do their best during a Pokémon battle. Whenever they feel scared, they whimper and try to find their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME frequently reflects a desire to get along with everyone. Reaching into its fluffy tail, it presents a tongue of flame as a gift, confused at the panic it causes.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Law enforcement agencies have begun training POKENAME for special units and operations. Their sense of smell and natural-born teamwork skills make them efficient partners, particularly for search parties.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may seem intimidating but are some of the most loyal Pokémon in existence. They are a reflection of their Trainer and will do anything from mundane obstacle courses to heinous crimes to please their master.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes for an excellent tracking companion for hunters. With its sense of smell and its thin body, it can sniff out and give chase to a target into all but the tightest of hiding spots.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in grasslands as a pack. Unfused Ekans flee from them in fear, while unfused Growlithe may rarely hunt them, leading to little interaction between the species.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's antlers detect the heartbeats of anyone approaching its territory. If a predator is near, it unleashes a powerful Roar to protect its home.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon use swift movements to intimidate and confuse the opponent. When the opponent is dazed, they spit fire as a finisher.
author: mystora

entry: If POKENAME gets enraged, run away as fast as possible. It will start spinning in circles whilst shooting fire in all directions.
author: mystora

entry: When POKENAME finds something it enjoys, it leaves a firey kiss mark on it. It hates being dirty and will clean itself up as soon as possible.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME barks during thunderstorms, timing its cries with lightning strikes. This playful habit makes it popular among Trainers who love its energetic personality.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is often carried about in ladies' purses. Its pompadour takes a lot of styling to maintain.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's fluffy spheres can get very hot when it is scared. Sneaking up on POKENAME in the wild is unwise, as it will spit hot pebbles at foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dig deep into the dirt to store objects it finds valuable. For recreation, one out of a group of POKENAME will curl into a ball, while the other POKENAME chase it around.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spits poison at enemies to slow them down before finishing them off with a fierce Ember. This combination makes it a skilled hunter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its brightly colored flower to absorb energy from the sun. It can detect others' emotions with its sense of smell, and the aroma of its flower is known to calm people down.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: POKENAME's fur emits a faint, toxic mist when threatened, discouraging predators from getting too close. It fiercely protects its territory, barking loudly before delivering venomous bites.
author: .izik

entry: Normally well-behaved, a POKENAME acting out is a sign of it trying to tell its Trainer something. For instance, digging many holes in the yard suddenly is a sign an earthquake is approaching.
author: sk372

entry: When playing fetch, POKENAME's large ears twitch rapidly. After retrieving the item, it shoots flames into the air with delight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME allows itself to be wielded by those it considers to be a noble hero, but lights itself ablaze when it senses evil intent in another.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's sharp fangs drip with a mild toxin, weakening prey before it strikes with fiery breath. If enraged, it charges fearlessly, coating its body in flames to increase its attack power.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME casts an illusion over itself to take on the form of a person's most cherished pet. It does this because it wants to make as many friends, make them happy and play with them as much as possible.
author: sk372

entry: One of the most popular pets among non-Trainers, POKENAME are extremely loyal and faithful to their owners.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME adores its Trainer and spends as much time as possible by their side. It subtly slows the flow of time, just to extend how long they can be together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's six tails glow bright orange when it plays fetch. When it gets too excited, it may unintentionally spit flames at those nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur crackles with static, sparking with electricity whenever it gets excited. When playing with its Trainer, it joyfully pounces while releasing harmless bursts of flame and lightning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release hot air from their bodies to keep Trainers warm. When it is especially cold they light twigs on fire to ensure everyone is comfy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eats hot rocks near volcanoes to keep its core warm. This fiery diet makes it resilient to extreme heat.
author: .izik

entry: Friendly and curious, POKENAME floats around sniffing and memorizing hundreds of scents. Carnivals often offer POKENAME up to children as a prize for winning at their games.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dips itself in ash before floating over recently burnt forests. This behavior helps regrow local flora by dispersing the ash evenly.
author: .izik

entry: Its sense of smell is so strong that it can accurately track any living thing within its cavernous home, no matter how far away. The scent of a new arrival always takes priority.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rolls along, lighting the ground on fire with sparks. When on its back, its soft, warm tummy invites trusted companions to rub it.
author: .izik

entry: The leaf-like hair on POKENAME's head tends to ignite when it feels threatened. The burning flame also makes it emit an acrid aroma that helps deter predators.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will greet a Trainer returning home with a welcoming dance and cheerful barks. It radiates heat during the movements, so those coming in from the cold find it very refreshing.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its cute and fluffy nature, many Trainers seek POKENAME in the wild. Unfortunately, when excited its barks echo louder than a concert, and it flies around in circles spreading thick smoke.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's body is as squishy as cotton, making it surprisingly soft. It sets logs ablaze with its flames, creating warm ashes for a comfortable sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are fiercely loyal and protective, their warmth and fluffiness making them popular companions and mascots. They often have some trouble controlling their own strength, but their plushiness usually keeps anyone from getting too hurt.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME works alongside police officers, subduing suspects with powerful, non-lethal hugs that leave targets unable to move.  Its comforting appearance often disarms criminals long enough for capture.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME leaps from trees with ease, delivering flaming kicks to foes. Its agility and precision make it a fearsome predator.
author: .izik

entry: It acts like a puppy to get food and shelter from humans. Its insectoid movement and behavior is eventually noticed, which usually creeps people out.
author: pokepower

entry: The soil POKENAME passes through remains warm for hours afterward. If it becomes agitated, the temperature of the dirt increases dramatically.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows through volcanic ash to consume it in large quantities. Once full, its body temperature rises to dangerous levels.
author: .izik

entry: It is recommended to teach a POKENAME early about respecting ownership; its affection for shiny coins and its Trainer often leads untrained POKENAME to steal coins to present to its Trainer as gifts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are an incredibly lazy species, lazing around homes and pestering owners to cook its favorite type of pasta. It is most lethargic in the mornings, preferring to conserve its energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is extremely loyal to its Trainer, never leaving their side. The sheen of its striped fur and the brightness of the flame on its tail reflect its health; when the fire dims, it indicates that the Pokémon is sick or weak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its superior sense of smell to detect anyone approaching its pond. When a threat is near, it releases hypnotic waves to drive them away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps its mind sharp by playing a game of fetch with itself. It flings its spoon into the distance, catching it with its psychic powers and bringing it back, testing how far it can throw and how quickly it can retrieve it.
author: sk372

entry: To impress its Trainer with its muscular strength, POKENAME performs at least one hundred push-ups every day. In battle, it ignites its fists to deliver scorching punches capable of burning its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To impress its Trainer with its muscular strength, POKENAME performs at least one hundred push-ups every day. In battle, it ignites its fists to deliver scorching punches capable of burning its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will pull down vines and burn the severed pieces to ash before burying it in the dirt. The mulched mixture is an effective fertilizer for helping new plant life grow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bears a striking resemblance to historical depictions of Growlithe from the ancient Hisui region. Because of their round, portable shape and loyal nature, many Trainers will travel with POKENAME hugging their backs.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME gallops through meadows, playing games of fetch with others of its kind. Tiny embers spark from its mane, creating a beautiful display at night.
author: .izik

entry: Too lazy to get up, POKENAME uses its psychic powers to pull food toward itself. If it spots an intruder, it prefers to go back to sleep, so it is not ideal as a guard Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME floats around factories to ensure devices remain at a safe temperature. If any device begins to overheat, it will attempt to absorb the excess heat by pressing itself against the device.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME like to hang around waste disposal areas, helping with getting rid of trash. It burns up piles of garbage before gobbling up the smoldering refuse that remains.
author: sk372

entry: It knows its messy form and nasty smell make it difficult to be near, but it still pines for companionship. Many kind souls take pity on its plight and adopt it despite the goop and stench.
author: sk372

entry: When upset, POKENAME puts enemies into a deep sleep filled with terrifying fire-filled nightmares. It uses this ability to cause lasting trauma in its foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its searing whips to keep dangerous individuals away from its teammates. When nervous, its soft fur becomes coated in poisonous dandruff.
author: fiordaliso

entry: People have long revered the sight of POKENAME running swiftly through lava. Beneath its majestic fur is extremely tough hide.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Its speed and grace are spoken of in ancient Eastern legends. POKENAME can travel thousands of miles in one day, leaving trails of embers behind as its wings flutter. Inhaling the smoke it releases when flying can poison you.
author: nyoomymph

entry: The heat emanating from POKENAME's scythes are comparable to the heat of a Magcargo. It can easily cut through thick steel.
author: themicelegion

entry: Ancient texts tell that it walked along people, granting them prosperity and warmth. If it blows a kiss, a storm of fire will follow.
author: houndrys.

entry: The nest of an POKENAME is usually found in coal-powered power plants. It is made up of barbed wire, soot, and construction insulation.
author: .izik

entry: From POKENAME's large beak, it can unleash scorching flames capable of melting even the toughest metals. It is an absolutely loyal Pokémon that would do anything to protect its Trainer, even at the cost of its own life.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Researchers theorize POKENAME can fly for several days without tiring, even at extreme speeds. The Flamethrower it spews from its beak is hot enough to melt steel.
author: chibitales

entry: With its long ears, POKENAME can pick up even the faintest whispers. It uses this ability to rush to the aid of people calling for help, even from far away. Its fur is always warm, and when it becomes angry, it turns scorching hot.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is known for its legendarily carefree attitude. It loves to let its beautiful mane absorb water while lounging in the sun.
author: shadanks

entry: Known for its resolute heart, POKENAME never defies a trusted trainer's orders. It has been depicted across history as a symbol of loyalty and bravery.
author: mepp.

entry: Trustworthy and intelligent, POKENAME tries to become a mentor to its Trainer's other Pokémon. It often confuses them instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of its Trainer and will not hesitate to attack anyone who dares come too close. Its fangs can grow scorching hot in an instant, making its bites devastatingly powerful.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME propels itself by shooting intense flames from its wings. It can fly up to 180 mph, impaling its opponents with its powerful horn.
author: mistymagius

entry: Old folklore speaks of POKENAME's ability to summon claws at will.  Trophy hunters claim the claws vanish overnight when put on display.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Research indicates that POKENAME possesses the ability to freeze nearby air moisture to craft its vicious claws, which melt away when not in combat.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Despite its fearsome appearance, POKENAME is wary of humans and hides deep within the forest to avoid them. However, if anyone threatens its young, it flies into a rage and unleashes fiery blasts powerful enough to burn entire woods to ashes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This nimble Pokémon can often be seen rolling around wherever it goes. It can roll for over 6,000 miles without needing to break.
author: melodydelune

entry: For a long time, scientists were unsure if POKENAME actually existed due to its prominent worship in some cultures. They are said to arrive before the birth of a benevolent ruler to bring peace to the lands.
author: rakunk

entry: Despite being clumsy, it's said to inspire even the coldest heart. By blowing a kiss veiled in psychic power, it brings a pleasant feeling to anyone.
author: houndrys.

entry: Depending on its mood, listening to an POKENAME's chanting can bestow both good and bad luck. It glides swiftly around the battlefield, leaving small patches of fire in its wake.
author: spartan_ct

entry: POKENAME make their burrows at the base of active volcanos to keep themselves warm. They wrap their tail around their body whenever they fall asleep to insulate their body heat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME retains the dog-like demeanor of both its fusion components. Its leaves are coated in a highly concentrated and fragrant capsaicin.
author: captainmodeus

entry: It is believed POKENAME adapted to the changing weather following the ice age. Its heavy, insulating fur necessitates its habitat in cold climates.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Despite its bulk, this POKENAME variant is very agile. During the peak of its species in the ice age, it traveled thousands of miles between seasons.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It dedicates its very life to defending its young. If it detects danger, its fur stands on end. When it finally relaxes, POKENAME enjoys rolling in dirt and mud.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is incredibly loyal and will only fight to protect those in need. Because of the risk of friendly fire, POKENAME will only use its flames at close range.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is said to be made up of the souls of Arcanine that perished but refused to move on. Bound to a keystone in hopes of rebirth, it unknowingly sealed its fate, forever unable to live again.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME is really lazy and only moves to find fruit, but when its Trainer is sleeping, it stays awake to guard them without even blinking.
author: drip_capybara

entry: POKENAME does nothing but loafs and stares at its opponent. However, if the opponent dares to attack it, it will tackle them at unrivaled speeds.
author: p0opys0ck123abc

entry: POKENAME is revered as a legendary guardian of the afterlife. It is said that it guides those who have passed away into the spiritual realm.
author: captainzscourge

entry: A pack of POKENAME has on more than one occasion been confused for a volcanic eruption. They surge across dry environments like pyroclastic flows, enveloping any unfortunate prey they find in a flurry of claws, flames and dust.
author: frink202

entry: The loyal POKENAME can travel more than 250 miles per hour. It's said to search for a hero who was separated from it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Ancient tales told of a legendary warrior who would fight with blinding speed and blazing fury. Some scholars believe these tales to be early records of POKENAME, long before modern-day fusion.
author: phantom640

entry: Legends say that POKENAME can judge the hearts of the sailors. If they deem them unworthy, a firestorm will surge from underwater to evaporate a large portion of the sea, making the ship violently fall into the bottom of the ocean.
author: epping_forest

entry: Hailing from the far east, POKENAME has been prized since ancient times by regals and royalty for its loyalty and loving nature.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's loyalty and devotion to its Trainer is peerless. It might even go back in time to rewrite history if it would even slightly improve its Trainer's life.
author: sk372

entry: Legend has it that POKENAME can block access to Pokémon and humans in the Distorted World by generating walls of fire around portals. Its flames are so hot they can incinerate anything they touch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This old chew toy was burned, but somehow survived the pyre. It enjoys being thrown about in games of fetch.
author: greystorm101

entry: POKENAME will settle on the front doors of houses, and dutifully protect them from any would-be intruders. As such, they're beloved by homeowners.
author: admiralvermin

entry: POKENAME flies at a high speed through deserts, generating heat waves by violently flapping its wings.
author: mistershaokahn

entry: POKENAME is filled with rage. Despite its well developed jaw, it barely causes any harm when it bites. Heat builds up inside its body, but because of the cool water it lives in, the heat rarely erupts.
author: zyrum_

entry: POKENAME's combat specialty is great balls of fire lobbed out of its powerful jaws. These condensed flame orbs are said to hit with speed and force akin to a meteor impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gives aggressors a chance to walk away, intimidating them with short growling roars and small bursts of flame from its mouth. Those that persist bothering it typically wind up thrown across the horizon from its titanic strength.
author: sk372

entry: The mane of flowers growing off of its head let loose a mild sedative when it runs. When it is scared, the sedation effect becomes stronger.
author: .izik

entry: As it slithers, POKENAME leaves behind a highly flammable slime trail; if it's not careful, it may accidentally start fires. It is an extraordinarily loyal Pokémon that always stands in defense of its Trainer.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a popular first Pokémon for kids. It's very loving and surprisingly intelligent.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME are popular first Pokémon for kids. After being cherished for many years, their stripes may fade, however, that love never will.
author: cristata

entry: A young Trainer once woke up transformed into this Pokémon. While it may look cuddly, its wild emotions allow it to utilise fire to defeat its foes.
author: hypernovahusky

entry: Many claim POKENAME is from Sinnoh's Distortion World, using its fast speed to jump between the sky islands. What has been observed is it changes its flame colors to attract Flying- and Bug-types to devour.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME incorporate various precious jewels into their bodies, having a preference for jaspers and rubies. They use these jewels to channel their elemental powers, storing heat within them to be projected out later.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME digs through wildfire zones searching for lost Pokémon. Once found, it barks loudly to guide them toward safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases powerful howls from beneath the ground before giving chase. The sound echoes through tunnels moments before it attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Although POKENAME is small, it runs at incredible speeds, leaping over vast expanses of land in a single bound as if flying. It is very proud of its appearance and protective of its thick, luxurious tail.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME always carries itself with elegance and pride. A Trainer of POKENAME must dedicate time to grooming its thick coat or risk facing its ire.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's heart pumps blood that can melt ice. It is incredibly fast and warm, so merchants will often ride it through freezing mountain passes to transport goods from town to town.
author: lupa

entry: Despite its restless temperament, it becomes extremely obedient when properly trained by its Trainer. Thanks to its versatility and strength, POKENAME is often employed by special police forces to break into criminal hideouts.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During combat, POKENAME's body temperature rises rapidly, the flame inside its body reacting to the Pokémon's determination. This raises the intensity and speed of its punches, but this can lead to overheating if not managed.
author: glacierwing

entry: Herds of POKENAME walk almost 250 miles in a day to search for food and water in the prairies they inhabit. The leader of a herd is decided by a speed competition and regularly has to defend the title from other eager competitors in the herd.
author: _pixelar_

entry: It tirelessly swims under the frigid ocean at high speeds. The mane helps it keep warm in its natural environment around glaciers.
author: bionic_man

entry: Due to its inexperience with Fire-type moves, POKENAME often allows its Arcanine head to fight on its own. It stays in warm waters around volcanoes.
author: creeps_jr

entry: POKENAME can be found in dry, hot places. The bulb on its back is popular for many dishes because of its rich, spicy flavor.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: POKENAME sprays silk through the fire on its tail. While the silk itself is resistant to burning, it can still carry the flame, allowing POKENAME to better aim its fire and create burning traps.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With every kick POKENAME makes in battle, the flame on its tail grows, flaring in tune with its fighting spirit. A battle between rival POKENAME can turn into a blazing inferno of fire and feet.
author: sk372

entry: Its body burns so hot that even the gloves covering its fists scorch its foes. The wings on its back help it reposition swiftly, giving it an edge in dodging and counterattacking.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A never-ending flame burns within its body, producing toxic gases that it vents through its pores. When facing a powerful foe, flames burst from every opening, raising the risk of an explosive outburst at any moment.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME leap great distances through the air, rapidly swirling their fiery tails to create updrafts to carry them. They harden their bodies to help brace for landing.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is a short-tempered creature that recklessly charges at anyone who dares stand in its way. Its large wings can only keep it airborne for a few minutes due to the heavy weight of its body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME feels particularly threatened, it combines its Water and Fire-type attacks to create a cloud of steam between itself and its foes, allowing it to escape. It often uses its wing-shaped fins to glide across the water's surface.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When provoked, POKENAME can generate blazing whirlwinds by flapping its wings. Its scales insulate its body's heat, preventing its temperature from dropping too low while it swims in the sea in search of prey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hide amongst volcanic rock, waiting for its prey to swim by before cooking them with a blast of fire. When prepared by an experienced chef POKENAME is considered a popular delicacy with their meat being described as juicy and tender.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME begins migrating at the end of autumn to live in more tropical locations. It leaves the tropics just before wildflowers begin to bloom in other nearby regions.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can summon powerful flames that erupt from the gem at the center of their body. These flames intimidate dangerous Pokémon into leaving them alone, and return into the gem they came from when the threat is gone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME summon powerful flames from the gem on their body to scare away dangerous Pokémon. These flames embody the spirit of a fierce Fire-type Pokémon that only listens to Trainers with as much passion as they have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME glide around beaches helping Staryu and Starmie back into the water after they are stranded at low tide. Their flames and telekinesis are said to grow stronger for each Pokémon they help throughout their lives.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME compete for food by getting into powerful grappling matches, slamming their pincers against one another. If the battles run long enough, their pincers even ignite as their fighting spirit flares up further.
author: sk372

entry: When enraged, the flame on its tail blazes so intensely that its body temperature rises. If it encounters another POKENAME, it feels compelled to charge and clash horns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME struggles to fly with its wings because of its small body. It overestimates the necessary force needed to remain airborne and cannot maintain a straight flight path as a result.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is extremely territorial and aggressive. It patrols its forest from above, attacking intruders without hesitation.
author: silver175

entry: It uses its wings to quickly move from branch to branch, collecting berries from trees. After eating enough, the horn-shaped flame on its forehead grows stronger, boosting the power of its Fire-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Greatly feared for its appetite for destruction, POKENAME is incredibly dangerous. Ancient literature claims that it was responsible for reducing several kingdoms to ash.
author: mepp.

entry: A POKENAME is not classified as a dragon by the scientific community. Many fantasy authors claim to draw inspiration from it when crafting dragons in their stories.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Festivals are held on its annual migration, for it loves dancing amongst the hot fireworks, and would otherwise burn towns for entertainment.
author: robosoup

entry: Both halves of POKENAME have mega-evolved in synchrony, and it can hold this form indefinitely. It has a great urge to destroy.
author: robosoup

entry: A POKENAME is not classified as a dragon by the scientific community. Many fantasy authors claim to draw inspiration from it when crafting dragons in their stories.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME will ferry travelers across the oceans, but only after it has been bested in battle to prove the passengers' worth. It guards those it ferries with fierce flames and piercing shards of ice.
author: sk372

entry: Its spiky fur constantly stores static electricity, which also fuels the flames blazing on its tail. It uses its wings to glide short distances and to speed up its movements on the battlefield, making its attacks even swifter and more unpredictable.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME was introduced into the virtual world to protect private networks from harmful files, acting as a living firewall. The more complex the malware, the more eager this Pokémon becomes to face it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME attacks anything that comes close to the branch it hangs from. It flails its flaming tail and large wings to scare away other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite their small size, POKENAME are extremely territorial. They are well-known for attempting to chase beachgoers away by burning their feet.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME have been found in many parts of the world, often getting into vicious territorial disputes with other Pokémon. During battle, the flame on their tail burns hot enough to rival magma, causing POKENAME to become even more vicious.
author: chibitales

entry: This Pokémon was first fused to guard an old king's vault. But, POKENAME prefers to spend its time asleep, so most treasure has been stolen.
author: volvonovic

entry: Its blue underwings are not actually part of its body, but concentrated heat so intense it changes color. POKENAME's tail flame cannot be extinguished due to the extreme intensity caused by the fusion.
author: grilled7up

entry: Whenever POKENAME needs an extra boost of speed, it ignites its tail stinger to propel itself forward like a rocket. This allows it to chase down honey thieves with terrifying speed, making escape difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It flies high above the ground where the air is cold and thin. A birdkeeper legend says if POKENAME spends too much time on the ground, its feathers burst into flame.
author: ozydamians

entry: The flame burning at the tip of its tail is so hot that it keeps POKENAME warm during winter, meaning it never needs to migrate from its nest. It moults its feathers once a year to keep its wings strong.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The flame burning at the tip of its tail is so hot that it keeps POKENAME warm during winter, meaning it never needs to migrate from its nest. It moults its feathers once a year to keep its wings strong.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When a battle becomes tough, POKENAME cloaks its head in crackling flames, ready to give its all. Its feathers stay warm even after they fall off, which is why they are often used as padding in certain types of winter jackets.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its eyes are more powerful and precise than even the strongest telescope. From miles above, it rains down superheated motes of fire.
author: ozydamians

entry: It generates enough heat and air to safely insulate its Trainer even at the edge of space. From far below, you might mistake POKENAME for a legendary Pokémon.
author: ozydamians

entry: When it detects a forest fire, it will waft the flames away with its wings. It feels guilty whenever it accidentally sets plants on fire.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME spends its days in flight, searching for challengers to alleviate its boredom. If it spots a fitting rival, it pauses and ignites its plumage, blazing in the sky like a miniature sun, before plummeting down with a terrifying screech.
author: baverbrugge
