entry: It wraps its arms around its face before being struck. Afterward, its body shimmers gold as it unleashes a deadly Mirror Coat to retaliate.
author: .izik

entry: The wings of a POKENAME will fall off and regrow as it ages. The discarded wings can be ground and used to create soaps and lotions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their claws as hooks to dig into the sides of cliffs, quickly and effortlessly scaling mountainsides. They glide around the cliffside with their tails swaying slowly, waiting to dig up ore deposits for their meals.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It loves eating agate above all other gems. It will dig for up to two days to search for even a single piece before reluctantly consuming less-preferred gemstones.
author: .izik

entry: Because it eats small rocks as well as berries that grow near mountains, POKENAME's juice is described as having a slightly grainy texture. It's a popular beverage choice among hikers and campers.
author: sk372

entry: The moon-shaped stone on its head emits a honey-like scent that puts foes at ease. It uses this fragrance to lure prey closer before striking.
author: .izik

entry: The golden ring on POKENAME's rocky body emits a honey-like scent. This aroma lures prey such as Sentret before it strikes with Bulldoze.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is made of incredibly hot mud, allowing it to live within volcanic walls. The heat it radiates makes the surrounding rocks glow faintly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will only move around outside if it has absorbed enough warmth, either from a nearby volcano or from the sun. It searches for stones to eat; the inside of its body is so hot that these stones melt into a liquid.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its body is covered in fluffy feathers that mimic the texture of stone. It smacks tree trunks to knock down prey like Weedle, which it devours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME forms in rock deposits near hot springs. As it ages and battles, its rocky outer layer crumbles away, revealing the gemstone underneath.
author: capwolfbane

entry: POKENAME live near volcanoes where they use the arms on their backs to gather molten rocks to make into armor. They're rather playful by nature, leaping and splashing around lava as if it was water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME often play with each other by using their trunks to grab rocks, throwing and dodging the stone projectiles. Unfortunate Geodude and Roggenrola sometimes get used in these games as well.
author: sk372

entry: It rolls at such high speeds that it can scale cliffs effortlessly. Its trunk is used to break citrine from cave walls, which it consumes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates sculptures by chiselling stone with its sharpened tail. It works alongside sculptors to create realistic statues that are displayed at museums.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When startled, it delivers a devastating punch that can reduce a boulder to dust in one strike. It often trains by smashing smaller rocks into powder.
author: .izik

entry: It carefully spits a putrid green acid, using it to loosen fossils from caves. These fossils are then added to its rocky body as decoration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's strong body can crush large boulders just by constricting them. It likes to collect fossils and show them off on its body. The strongest of POKENAME can have up to 20 different fossils on their bodies at a time.
author: mistymagius

entry: There is nothing a hiker fears more than a herd of POKENAME rolling down a mountain. It will easily roll over any obstacle in its path.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME's second pair of arms are useful for both combat and labor. They are excellent at digging and building.
author: v0rtre

entry: At this stage in its evolution, POKENAME begins to condense itself. It becomes tougher and tougher the more it condenses.
author: v0rtre

entry: It generates energy internally by curling up and rolling about the mountains. It enjoys charging up enough energy to shoot bolts of lightning at large rocks to shatter them to pieces.
author: sk372

entry: It shatters large rocks into bite-size pebbles with the large arms on its head. Afterward, all four arms will take turns shoveling the stone morsels into its hungry mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a sturdy shell and can survive deadly rockfalls. One was sent into space before humans to test cosmic radiation. When it returned, its body had become even tougher, its shell glinting like polished stone under the stars.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It rubs its back against stone walls to grind down the rocky spines on its back when they grow too large. Spears using broken-off spines as the tip have been found dating back to ancient Kanto.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME keeps strangers at bay by pelting them with small stones using its four arms. Since it is not a particularly social Pokémon, it pretends to be a stone statue whenever it wishes to avoid interaction.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A tangle of plant matter and rocks grows on its back. It likes to roll around on its back, collecting more rubble and weeds, causing its back-mass to grow even larger.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Few things are as dangerous as a POKENAME rolling downhill, as its mass and momentum crushes all that is in its way. In its wake, it leaves an earthy sulfuric smell.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: A powerful stone jaw rests atop POKENAME's head, capable of crushing iron in one bite. Junkyards often rely on it to break down metal debris with ease.
author: .izik

entry: It can sense large earthquakes before they happen and warns townsfolk by throwing rocks onto roads as they walk. This act is often misunderstood as a bad omen.
author: .izik

entry: When standing still, POKENAME will swing and rotate its multiple arms with no discernible pattern. Researchers theorize these movements adjust and regulate its internal magnetism.
author: sk372

entry: Its arms can hurl boulders, opponents, or itself; its preferred mode of travel. The boulders it sheaths into ensure its landings are not graceful.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: To maintain its bulk and sturdy body, it will eat up to a ton of rocks on a daily basis. Its favorite rocks seem to be those covered in moss.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME dwell deep within Mt. Moon, building up rock formations to protect the precious Moon Stones within. They study their constructions meticulously should they ever seek to evolve using these Moon Stones in case of a threat.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME goes up a mountain, it moves delicately. In contrast, it tumbles down the mountain when descending.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME greet each other by seeing who can point at the other first with their large, hand-shaped ears. The loser is expected to pretend to faint; if they don't, the winner will pelt them with rocks.
author: griddle

entry: It will sleep face down on muddy surfaces during the day, snoring loudly. At night, it springs awake and sings to the moon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers stones from riverbeds to build sturdy dams. Smaller rocks are eaten to reinforce its rocky body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rams into rocks to break them into edible chunks before scooping them into its mouth with its claws. If it cannot find any rocks to break, it thrashes around violently until it finds some to consume.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it rains, POKENAME will dig alcoves into cliff faces for shelter in order to protect its burning tail, which sustains its life force.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Its body is completely hollow and filled with an odd gas. Despite its rocky surface and weight, it can float for short distances.
author: .izik

entry: It flies swiftly to catch prey like Venonat, using Supersonic attacks to disorient them. Once the target is stunned, it delivers a ferocious Bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME causes issues for clay target shooting competitions. It confuses the flying discs for members of its species and snatches them up because it believes they are in danger.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME use their large teeth to break through rocks in order to grind them into dust and gather minerals from within. They scatter the leftover dust as they fly, blinding opponents or intruders to their territory.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Using all four arms, it digs through caverns in search of raw precious gems. After successfully snatching some, it cannot resist prancing about in triumph before consuming its crystalline meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME help farmers infuse the earth with essential nutrients for local wildlife. After releasing nutrients through the soil, they are released into the wild where many maintain their role as a forest guardian.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is used as the mascot and cheerleader for the Pewter Power Gems. If facing the Indigo Ice Beams, it shakes its rock-poms even harder.
author: .realthree

entry: When Graveler overpopulate an area, POKENAME appears to force them out. Many believe it serves as a guardian of mountains, keeping Graveler from devouring excessive amounts of rock.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME spews foul-smelling spores and dust wherever it goes. It is unclear if this action is entirely conscious or not, but POKENAME have been observed purposely firing dust and spores into the eyes of aggressors.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It pecks at cave walls to loosen zircon and smashes the gems into dust before eating. Its downy wings keep it safe from sharp shards while foraging.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its rocky appearance, its body is composed of a hard, cactus-like substance. It thrives in arid deserts where dry air keeps its body sturdy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are regarded as an unlucky catch by most fishermen. They are mostly made out of scales and bones, and the little meat on their body is as rough as gravel. Their rocky scales can also cut fishermen that try to pick them up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME crawls atop large boulders and siphons nutrients from them. The boulders turn hollow and brittle as a result, crumbling to dust once POKENAME has fed from them completely.
author: sk372

entry: The glowing scale on POKENAME's head allows it to control nearby stone. With a flick of its head, it can launch chunks effortlessly using Rock Throw.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hot stone body can reach temperatures beyond commercial ovens. Some restaurants use it in place of grills due to its precise heat control.
author: .izik

entry: At night, a POKENAME wanders through mountain passes looking for travelers who fell. Instead of assisting them, it will stand next to them and stare.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lumbers up and down mountains, looking for tough opponents. In battle, it enjoys spewing up molten rocks that it chews up beforehand.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME digs through canyon walls in search of granite deposits to consume. After overeating, it embeds itself in the rock face and sleeps while digesting.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever POKENAME needs to train they wrestle with other wild Pokémon. They are difficult to take down because of their rocky bodies and superb strength.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After winning several duels, POKENAME claim a mountains as its own. It will crush boulders and throw debris to keep rivals from climbing its peaks.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME meditate in caves to improve their mental acumen. Their rocky bodies allow them to continue meditating even when they are approached by other Pokémon that try to distract them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME meditate and train atop mountains to improve their fighting prowess. Their rock-solid bodies make them tough opponents to take down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses all four arms and even its tail to grab stones in order to pelt them at trespassers. Should this warning be ignored, it will fly into a deeper rage and roll at its target, howling all the while.
author: sk372

entry: Each fist can punch a hole in stone with ease, making POKENAME a formidable opponent. A raging POKENAME once reduced an entire mountain peak to dust in a day before it calmed down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can dim the flame on its tail to blend perfectly with the stone walls of caves. It enjoys startling unsuspecting explorers by suddenly emerging from its hiding spot and flapping its wings.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fashion spoons out of minerals they gather in order to focus their psychic powers. They primarily use these powers to compare various minerals and see the composition of caves around them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It uses psychic pulses to loosen ore from cave walls before consuming them. Its appetite for rare minerals drives it to dig deep into the earth.
author: .izik

entry: Its strong rocky forearms make for a potent offense. Its other set of arms seem malformed, but in actuality it keeps them tucked close to help protect weak spots on its torso.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's flexing isn't just for showboating; every flex temporarily stores more energy in its stony arms. If allowed to flex enough before release, a single punch could crumble an entire mountain range.
author: sk372

entry: It pounds rubies into powder with its fists before consuming them. This mysterious diet somehow strengthens both its muscles and its rock-hard body.
author: .izik

entry: It shovels onyx into its large, gaping mouth whenever it finds it. The stone is melted instantly within its powerful, acidic saliva.
author: .izik

entry: Commonly mistaken for regular Graveler, the main distinction of a POKENAME is its lack of feet. It almost always keeps its newly developed second pair of arms by its side, as if it doesn't even realize it has them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME gather rocks around themselves to protect their bodies as they prepare for evolution. They often seem confused on which set of arms to use, as if trying to decide which one they prefer.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The fist on its tail is used to smash stones into chunks small enough for it to eat. When it chews on the rocks, sparks can sometimes be seen as it crunches on the stones.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have been found in depictions of royal houses in historical Galar and Kalos. High-ranking knights would ride them across dangerous territory, where speed and defense were both paramount to survival.
author: sk372

entry: Despite their magnetic powers, POKENAME prefer to use the magnets they carry as blunt maces. They rapidly spin in place, smacking their opponents repeatedly while pulling them back and forth with their magnets.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The three parts of POKENAME maintain a connection via a strong grip, rather than any magnetism at work. Curiously, the bond this way is even stronger than the magnets; nothing has been seen able to pull them apart.
author: sk372

entry: It throws stones at other Pokémon while racing them across rugged terrain. The rear head watches for pursuers, ensuring it always has the advantage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home at the bottom of cold underground lakes. Records indicate some Lapras have been saved from poachers by POKENAME rocketing from the depths and attacking the interlopers.
author: sk372

entry: Typically, POKENAME's arms are vestigial in nature and serve no clear function. However, some POKENAME have been witnessed using them to hurl large boulders at foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Once POKENAME picks a spot to settle, it rarely moves. It uses multiple arms and telekinesis to fend off attacks from all directions as it sits still.
author: noel5229

entry: Burrowing into rocks at the bottom of underground caves, POKENAME only surface to gather more rocks for their shelters. They crush rocks into dust in their grip then release the dust into the water to fill it with minerals that will help them grow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its body oozes nitroglycerin, which crystallizes to coat its lower half. It can detonate the crystals to launch itself if threatened- or just for fun.
author: wigglypon

entry: Rivals compete to see whose explosions make the largest craters. It is known to raid construction sites and gobble up their dynamite stockpiles.
author: wigglypon

entry: Its hardened stone body and powerful drill horn give it incredible offense and defense capabilities. POKENAME are known to battle Tyranitar over territorial claims for mountainsides.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been spotted several times in ancient ruins, where it acts as a kind of security drone. Its exact origin can no longer be reconstructed.
author: chorb33

entry: This enigmatic Pokémon was found deep within a mine. It is largely inert, but some Trainers swear they can hear chimes coming from POKENAME's core.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME has been spotted several times in ancient ruins, where it acts as a kind of security drone. Its exact origin can no longer be reconstructed.
author: chorb33

entry: Popular with Miners, POKENAME's claws are sharp as diamonds and well shaped to pick at stubborn ores. When they come across a gap in the tunnel, they swiftly fly across to continue mining.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME inhabit pristine underground lakes. Ordinarily a creature of solitude, should travelers need to cross its lake, it will oblige them. It sings a rumbling song that echoes across the cavern as it does so.
author: sk372

entry: Its mud-like form allows it to slip beneath minecarts unnoticed. It greedily consumes spilled ore, leaving no trace behind.
author: .izik

entry: Scientists developed POKENAME for fertilizing and crop harvesting in mountainous regions. Some untamable specimens managed to set themselves free and now cause havoc in local ecosystems.
author: leviath

entry: POKENAME sleep best at high altitudes. When asleep, they curl into a perfectly round, boulder-like shape that often sends them rolling down mountains, destroying anything in their path while they remain fast asleep.
author: bradlybro199

entry: The many rocks clinging to POKENAME's body are filled with a fast-acting accelerant that ignites the moment it is exposed to air. In fact, this is how it will often fight, by pelting its opponents with its natural bombs.
author: infinex21

entry: Flying through deep caverns and abandoned mines, it hunts stealthily. While resting, it tucks its wings in tightly, resembling an ordinary boulder.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often spotted atop mountain peaks, living as a hermit far from the chaos of large cities. It is said to have a deeply peaceful nature, guiding lost travelers down the right path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is sometimes mistaken for a Caterpie from a distance. There are many reports of young Trainers attempting to battle POKENAME, only to be rushed to the nearest Pokémon Center. After a battle, wild POKENAME celebrate by jumping into water.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Fur manages to grow from POKENAME's rocky skin, forming a coat that sheds once a year. Carpeting made with its fur is popular in some regions due to emanating a natural earthy scent.
author: sk372

entry: To defend itself, a wild POKENAME will coil up tightly and build up pressure within its body. After biding its time, its outer mineral layer explodes, causing sharp shrapnel to cut deeply into any nearby foe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is encased in a brown metal, with sharp clusters of stones embedded for additional defense. These features help deter potential predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home near cave edges under Pomeg Berry trees, storing fallen berries in its shell along with pebbles. The juice it produces from these berries is highly regarded for its exquisite taste.
author: .izik

entry: At night, street racers pick a lane alongside POKENAME and race against each other for prizes. POKENAME have heavy bodies that help them build momentum throughout the course of a race.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is an expert at excavating and digging through hard ground, making it highly prized by construction workers. It digs by using its head as a drill, its rock-hard body widening the holes it digs out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are commonly sighted after a volcano erupts, seeking to bring joy to any affected locals. Its soft and sturdy body ensures no harm befalls its egg.
author: cheroace

entry: Now fully condensed, POKENAME prepares for its final evolution. It retracts its arms to give itself as much power as possible.
author: v0rtre

entry: With a heavily armored body, POKENAME roams many different landscapes. It is usually seen in mountains and volcanoes, often dwelling in a cave.
author: v0rtre

entry: Tough training has allowed POKENAME to be nearly invulnerable to any squeeze or squish. When rolling around, it uses its tail to change direction or bounce up to gain height.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are always producing electricity within their stony body; if not released periodically, the built-up energy will explode out of it. Entire chunks of their mountainous homes have been destroyed this way.
author: sk372

entry: When coiled, it extends sharp spikes from the gaps in its rocky body. These spikes make it a formidable defense against predators.
author: .izik

entry: The ruby-like portions of POKENAME's body glow intensely when it senses an enemy's aura. This light can even illuminate dark caves, making escape difficult for foes.
author: .izik

entry: While its secondary set of jaws sharpens its crystals while mining ores, POKENAME's main body is forced to subsist on subterranean mushrooms. When threatened, it allows hits to bounce off its rock armor before using a deadly Crunch.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME has exposed bones that make it appear deceased, but it still rummages through rocks. Its skeletal body is tough enough to withstand blows from the strongest of forces without getting scratched.
author: jangodiot

entry: It clads itself in the highest-quality rocks it can find, wearing them like royal regalia. When it replaces a rock, it gifts the rock being replaced to one of its young.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME have an innate sense of how stable rock and stone in the area is. Those in the mountains have come to know that if one sees a POKENAME running past them, they should follow, or be caught in a landslide.
author: sk372

entry: Forged in the fiery depths, it haunts the shadows of ancient caverns. Its grasp is capable of crushing mountains with spectral force.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME is said to ferry souls lost in rockslides to the afterlife. It's also said to have caused those accidents in the first place.
author: barthandelus_real

entry: It holds immense power, which it uses to alter the shape of the earth's crust. A single swipe of its hand can destroy an entire island.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME dwells in volcanic craters atop lofty peaks, shaping the land with its immense power.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME mines and stashes the toughest stones it can find to use as weapons. These stones can't be cracked by humans with any handheld equipment.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This Pokémon's spinning maces are strong enough to smash through solid rock, making it the preferred tool of miners over a traditional Pickaxe. Its strikes are clean, fast, and relentless.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The stones on its body are tougher than iron, granting it immense durability. Using its massive tail, it smashes cave walls and devours any fossils that fall.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shred through entire mountains looking for the toughest rocks to rebuild their rock-like scales. In a rampage, they will divebomb into the ground with the force of a meteorite.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME often use illusions to make their rocky armor look like gems or polished metal. It is said that staring into the gem on its tail will show you a vision of your ideal self.
author: sivanandi

entry: POKENAME are popular among gardeners for their shedded skin, which hardens and crumbles, becoming a nutrient-rich soil for plant growth.
author: melodydelune

entry: The purple portions of its tail excrete toxic dribbles, weakening foes. It uses its rocky arms to slam opponents who resist the poison's effects.
author: .izik

entry: It is rare to see POKENAME near the surface as they prefer to reside near underwater volcanic vents. If seen, it could be an early sign of a flood coming.
author: kitarchen

entry: Its rocky abdomen stores billions of silk strands that it uses to ensnare prey. The silk becomes brittle and fragile when exposed to sunlight.
author: .izik

entry: It drills tendrils into cave ceilings before dropping onto unsuspecting explorers. Its stony body has a shale-like texture, blending with the environment.
author: .izik

entry: It clings to cave ceilings, blending seamlessly with its surroundings. Small wicks on its rocky body light like candles when others draw near.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carefully remove, crush and reshape parts of the mountains they reside in over time. It is thought that they are attempting to turn these mountains into vast temples for a civilization that no longer exists.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has to carry its costume, which is made of rocks, at all times on its head, since the costume is too heavy to balance upright. It makes for a good defense when in battle.
author: jangodiot

entry: The hot rocks covering its body lose their heat when out of direct sunlight. Under sunlight, however, they can reach searing temperatures hotter than a stovetop within seconds.
author: .izik

entry: Researchers speculate that POKENAME's unstable genome was altered by contact with a foreign virus from space. The resilient stones encasing its body serve as a natural defense, protecting its vital core from harm.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The spines along a POKENAME's body are composed of nephrite jade. POKENAME will use their sturdy bodies to carve out spots to burrow within caves, eating the minerals inside to help grow their spines.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It latches onto prey like Arbok, draining their life force with a powerful bite. Its stone body makes it immune to the prey's final struggles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carves a large shield out of a boulder when it is young and carries it around. Should it find a gem deposit, it will break them apart to eat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats in shallow waters, using its electrified tentacles to paralyze its prey. Schools of POKENAME can be seen washed up on the beach after large storms.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its rocky exterior made it near invulnerable in the ancient world, helping it claim large amounts of territory for itself. Its only weak spot is a small area on the neck where its stone skin is least durable.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to appear in mountains being drilled or tunneled with no regards to the Pokémon dwelling within. It enacts a terrible vengeance on those who do not respect the mountain's inhabitants.
author: sk372

entry: It emits loud screeches while flying through the night, disorienting foes. Once its target is dizzy, it strikes with the rock-like portion of its tail.
author: .izik

entry: The mucus dripping from its body hardens into a stone-like material after prolonged sun exposure. This hardened mucus is widely used in hospitals for crafting inexpensive casts for broken limbs.
author: .izik

entry: When its rocky petals become cracked, POKENAME excretes a viscous sap that seeps into the fissures and preserves the petals' structural integrity.  While this resin is effective, its smell is unbearable.
author: emtpy_set

entry: Its soft, plush-like body is encased within dense, unyielding stones. If an attacker approaches, it retaliates by hurling boulders to drive them away.
author: .izik

entry: Lying motionless on sun-soaked beaches, it appears lifeless during the day. At night, it uses kelp-like appendages to drag itself to graze on grass.
author: .izik

entry: Quartz spikes grow from POKENAME's tentacles, sharp enough to pierce ship hulls. It clings to cave ores underwater and gnaws on them for hours.
author: .izik

entry: Wherever this Pokémon walks, a quake can be felt, along with a drop in temperature. Its rocky scales are cold to the touch.
author: houndrys.

entry: The many stones that cover POKENAME's body hold a mystical power. Those lucky enough to find one are said to be blessed with peaceful slumber.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME possess several rings of rocky debris that orbit them. While they are normally peaceful, they are able to psychically manipulate these stones and cobble them into weapons and shields in the heat of battle.
author: moopse

entry: When using its powers in battle, the seams between the stone plates of POKENAME's body glow brightly. Its said that beneath the stone is a crystal so radiant it would blind a person instantly if beheld.
author: sk372

entry: Living in the calderas of active volcanoes, POKENAME melts and regrows the rocky armor on its back, until it's as hard as diamonds. It is sensitive to colder temperatures, so it carries around embers whenever it leaves home.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Inside POKENAME's rocky body are glowing red crystals that pulse as it sleeps. If disturbed, it awakens and launches a furious Rock Blast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats slowly across the night sky, its gaze fixed on a single constellation. It refuses to look away, even when attacked.
author: .izik

entry: If disturbed while gazing at the stars, POKENAME's body explodes. The explosion flings sharp stones in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hollows out massive boulders by eating their cores. Its den has a single hidden exit beneath the stone that leads directly underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's reputation is incredibly divisive among couples. Some believe seeing it is a sign their relationship will endure like a mountain, but others see it as an omen that their love will end in a landslide of heartbreak.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: Its psychic abilities and robust body enable it to absorb shocks and send them back. Its massive memory makes it also an unparalleled underground guide.
author: mistershaokahn

entry: POKENAME can spend decades searching for the perfect boulder, forming a deep bond with it. Even while sleeping, it holds the chosen rock close within its muscular grip.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs powerful uppercuts to knock stones loose from cave ceilings. It consumes these stones as part of its rocky diet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will add rocks to its torso to increase its strength. A POKENAME with many rocks on its torso is the leader of its pack.
author: gtrwya

entry: Clinging to cave walls, it punches through rock in search of Iron Balls. When it finds one, it swallows it whole for nourishment.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME is propelled into space, it assumes this form. The planet formed on POKENAME's body appears habitable.
author: rkmaster25367

entry: POKENAME's rocky plating does nothing to slow down its rapid speed. This plating can also withstand extremely high temperatures and can be shot out for a burning ranged attack.
author: evilgammon

entry: It embeds itself into rocky terrain and bites those who step on it. Its three heads rarely agree on anything.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Despite the weight of its boulder-like body and three heads, POKENAME can become dangerously fast. Once it accumulates too much speed, however, it may stumble and roll into its surroundings with devastating force.
author: sontyp

entry: The spikes it shoots from its head are similar to cave stalactites. Trying to prevent its shell from closing is as difficult as holding up a collapsing cave ceiling.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The stone at the end of its pendulum has a slight magnetic charge. It is just as hard and unyielding as POKENAME's rocky body.
author: .izik

entry: Monstrous POKENAME lurk in the deepest parts of the sea, forever on the bottom from their own weight. In an attempt to hunt, they hurl huge boulders at passing Lanturn or Wailord, usually with little success.
author: ilazerheart

entry: The mane of POKENAME is coated in magnesium, which enables it to burn underwater. Fishermen call it the "Mars of the Ocean" due to the distant red glow seen in deep water at night.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME charges after prey with searing speed. Once caught, it grapples them using blistering-hot claws that leave scorch marks on impact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are agile Pokémon, jumping over creatures adjacent to them. Strangely, they always move in an L shaped fashion.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: Its body is still developing, so POKENAME's flight capabilities are rather poor. It flaps vigorously just to stay airborne, flinging countless embers around it with every swing of its wings.
author: sk372

entry: When it sees a bush blocking its path, POKENAME unleashes a blazing Ember to burn it to ash. This ensures nothing slows down its blazing speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travel in flocks searching for pastures of grass to feast upon. They have to be careful not to burn the grass they eat, especially since they sneeze out embers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME peck old logs in search of their next meal. When they find an edible morsel, they gently roast the exterior with embers before consuming it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be found perched above trees looking for the perfect morsel to eat. They are particularly fond of berries, which they roast before eating.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in volcanic regions, using its keen eyes to spot prey when soaring high above the terrain. It was once thought to be the fledgling of the legendary Pokémon Moltres.
author: mepp.

entry: Flocks of POKENAME arrive after wildfires, feeding on the burnt seeds and berries left behind. They seem to have a strange prophetic sense that allows them to predict where wildfires are likely to occur.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fangs can heat to temperatures hotter than commercial fryers. A single bite can sear metal, making it a dangerous ambush predator.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has soft, webbed hooves, which helps it swim. It struggles to stand with them on land, so it secretes a gel to cover them, making them hard enough to walk on. To remove the gel, it must hold it to the fire on their tail and burn it off.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sleeps submerged in lakes, unaware that the water around it begins to boil. Entire patches of plant life die without it realizing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are heavily despised pests that crawl into homes and cause serious damage. When they are agitated, their flames can start house fires.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: Its eyes glow red when it spits fire from its mouth. It can use its psychic abilities to cause an enemy to spontaneously burst into flames.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gallops to cliff edges and glides for miles. Its flight path leaves behind shimmering trails of heated air as it coasts on thermal currents.
author: .izik

entry: Flocks of POKENAME race on foot and in flight. The winning team launches flames into the sky, lighting up meadows with celebratory fire bursts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores Berries in its body, which it regularly roasts. The process produces an alcoholic distillate that is used for various liquors.
author: chorb33

entry: It looks for vehicles and gas stations to steal naphtha, kerosene, and diesel just to drink them. If you voluntarily hand over the fuel, they'll take it and go away to steal something else.
author: epping_forest

entry: Yellow, bubbling liquid coats POKENAME's body. Even brief contact causes massive burns, making it one of the hottest Pokémon to touch.
author: .izik

entry: Though it races with others of its kind, POKENAME is painfully slow. Even short competitions can stretch into hours due to its molten body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers radiate enough heat to cause mild burns. Once shed, they cool almost instantly and are sometimes used to start campfires.
author: .izik

entry: They create elaborate burrows in grasslands. During dry seasons they have been known to disrupt the environment by causing wildfires.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME runs swiftly with its talons, but once airborne, its speed triples. Its wingbeats leave streaks of heat in the sky behind it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stomp alongside Donphan and Phanpy, joining them along their travels. They protect their herd from poachers with their fiery breath, and in return POKENAME have a family they can be a part of.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME traps its prey with a two-pronged attack: it stuns victims with disorienting color patterns from the horseshoe marking on its chest, and slithers around them quickly, trailing fire to create a circle of flame that leaves them with no escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known to gather above particularly fast-moving wildfires to ride the flames like waves. It often pulls pranks by hiding in a room and slowly heating it up. If befriended, however, it will often help a person keep their home warm.
author: quietcognition

entry: POKENAME use the fire growing on their arms and head to defend themselves, flashing it into any attackers' eyes to distract them.
author: glacierwing

entry: When POKENAME is relaxed, its spines cover its back flames, making it safe to touch. Artisans will place small pots and bricks on its back, acting as a makeshift kiln.
author: mistymagius

entry: A fiery machine. POKENAME can accelerate to speeds far beyond planes with its thruster arms.
author: rkmaster2637

entry: While oafish and sluggish in appearance, POKENAME is capable of alarming bursts of speed. A charging POKENAME's mane grows to obscure its whole body, granting the appearance of a blazing comet.
author: .fedoraman

entry: A POKENAME's orange rings are hot to the touch for all but their most trusted Trainer. The longer they run, the hotter their flames burn.
author: infinex21

entry: It prefers to live in long stretches of terrain, moving north constantly until it tires. Only then will POKENAME wander around to devour nearby dirt and plant life.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Often mistaken for a kids' toy, anyone who holds its reins can ride it like a real pony, but similarly must develop a relationship with it first.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its flames double as both a method of attack and an exit strategy, launching itself away from battle with expulsion force from its flames.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Due to their high jumping and fast running, POKENAME are excellent herding Pokémon. Only those it trusts can touch its mane without burning.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME produces spicy, soot-like spores from its mane, which it spreads as it hops and trots around. Some people use those as a condiment.
author: mx_wellman

entry: When a POKENAME's body is compressed, even if just by a strong hug, it will spew their inner flames. Some people will often have one of these Pokémon to help light fires.
author: infinex21

entry: Born with feeble strength, POKENAME's fur evolves into a radiant golden sheen over time, symbolizing its enduring spirit and grace.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME sprints along riverbeds to patrol its dams. If it spots even the smallest maintenance flaw, it halts everything to make repairs immediately.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's claws are harder than diamond. Luckily, it only has enough energy to root up the plants it eats.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Packs of over a hundred POKENAME charge from sunrise to sunset, trampling plant and animal alike for hundreds of kilometers. Even sheer cliff faces do little to slow a stampede that climbs as fast as it runs.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The flame on a POKENAME's head burns even when fully submerged. The flame when not in water can burn hot enough to burn oil spills off the water.
author: bradlybro199

entry: One half of POKENAME is safe to touch, but the other is always hot enough to burn on contact. If it spins rapidly enough, this half grows hotter, combusting and firing a gout of flame in front of it.
author: sk372

entry: Orange roses bloom from POKENAME's arms, coated in fine powder that flickers like fire. The powder is both toxic and capable of causing burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cotton is highly flammable and can be for over a day without trouble. Campers with often take a POKENAME with them as the cotton is an excellent firestarter.
author: mistymagius

entry: A flock of POKENAME will coordinate their efforts to put on shows for nearby towns. They coordinate in the sky to create glowing designs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME races up vertical cliffs, rolling faster than the eye can follow. It scorches the ground behind it, leaving trails of burnt soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggles with balance due to its large head, often falling over while running. Its legs are incredibly powerful and its hooves are harder than diamonds, letting it shatter boulders with a single kick.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The stony growths on POKENAME act as shock absorbers for when it crashes into obstacles during a run. The flames on its body grow in intensity as it accelerates.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME floats over flower fields, scattering pollen from its hooves as it drifts. This pollen helps plants regrow in fire-scarred regions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's soft body is filled with ash. It roams burnt forests, feasting on charred remains to absorb lingering nutrients from the fire.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dashes through forests searching for the perfect twigs to chew. Despite research, no one understands how it selects its favorites.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its stout build, POKENAME is compelled to try and trot at high speeds. Flames rise high from the pores in its shell as it trains to reach speeds higher than the average human walk speed.
author: sk372

entry: At dusk, POKENAME emerges to gallop across open prairies. If noticed, it becomes timid and immediately burrows underground to hide.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers coins from alleyways and city streets. Back at its den, it melts them into shimmering trophies of its nightly runs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a bit vain, preferring to keep its fur and flame stylized and groomed in a specific way, avoiding the touch of others that may mess it up. Thus, only those it truly trusts are allowed to pet it.
author: sk372

entry: It doesn't have flames when it is born. As it gets older, the flames get hotter and brighter.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME always finds a way to wear down its horseshoes, so it needs frequent visits to a blacksmith. It replaces its horseshoes often because of its highly active lifestyle and loves to race with other Pokémon until it is tired.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME goes on long daily runs in order to keep its muscles strong, its legs especially. It can run at top speed for an hour straight before beginning to tire.
author: sk372

entry: Cracks in POKENAME's rocky body glow with intense heat. Touching its surface can scorch skin, even when it appears motionless.
author: .izik

entry: These POKENAME have much more developed bodies with stronger muscles. Their bodies metabolize food quicker to produce greater flames and to support their frequent running.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME races up and down volcano slopes with its kin. They wait for eruptions to signal the start, making each race a fiery spectacle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the physique of an incredible runner, but the Shellder biting its tail secretes a numbing venom that tires it out. The fiery tail slowly cooks the Shellder to fainting, neutralizing the toxin and inspiring Ponybro to train.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME trots across the land with a quick, if slightly clumsy, gait. Eating mostly seeds, the two heads will hold their food above the other's flame, lightly toasting their meal before consuming it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are famous for being amazing runners, only being beaten out by its evolution. Its flames are astonishing as it zips past you.
author: dodoowner_

entry: When casting Hypnosis, POKENAME's flames burn at their brightest. The consumption of the dreams of its victims seems to be what keeps its flames burning, as a hungry POKENAME's flames are dim and flickering.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's churning drill fuels its fiery mane: the faster the rotation, the more billowing its fire is. Its large size hides an incredible top speed; POKENAME can burn across vast distances in minutes, trampling everything underfoot.
author: sk372

entry: Its wings are composed entirely of flames, spreading sparks with every flap. It has complete control over these flames, so the sparks and embers will not burn anything unless POKENAME wills it.
author: sk372

entry: It craves speed in all its forms, and is particularly fascinated by vehicles. Some POKENAME will try to cause car crashes by creating invisible walls on roads and raceways.
author: griddle

entry: Enterprising Trainers occasionally attempt to use POKENAME as a beast of burden, hoping to combine the strength of a Tauros with the speed of a Rapidash. Unfortunately, they usually overlook Tauros's bad temper and Rapidash's flames.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME's gelatinous body heats up enough to cause mild burns. However, it will never harm those it considers friends or family.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME often veil themselves in flames as they quickly encircle prey. Scorch marks from the walls of fire they form to entrap their prey are a common sight in certain fields.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME love to soar through the sky and enjoy the feeling of air against their faces. They only come down to eat grass and rest in tree branches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A POKENAME's sharp horn is very poisonous and very durable. It will often clap its hooves together to create sparks that ignite the webbing they can spit, which they then fling at foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses ferocious electric pulses to stun its prey and traps them within superheated currents. Old Fishermen songs warn how entire schools of fish vanish in its wake, with nothing left behind but a trail of light leading into the abyss.
author: silentscript89

entry: POKENAME release embers as they glide through the sky. They race against each other to determine who is fastest and perform complex aerial maneuvers to dodge anything in their way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a small Ponyta and uses the confusion to steal as much food as possible. It rarely settles in one place, wandering constantly.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME can run so quickly that it is able to flit along the surface of water. The heat it generates causes the surface of the water to heat up greatly, dragging small Pokémon to the surface, where POKENAME snaps them up.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME produces a flammable oil from its skin, allowing the flame on its back to burn indefinitely. It spends most of the day lazing around and munching on the surrounding grass.
author: mistymagius

entry: The fur of a POKENAME will stay warm to the touch for months after it is shed. Because of this, weavers in Unova use it to make winter clothing.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME's fiery mane vanishes, one should take immediate defensive or evasive action; the fire is all being stored in the tail, which it will spew out in a massive jet of flame at its target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tunnels deep below volcanos, the heat and pressure hardening its spikes into diamonds. It is coveted as a partner by Pokémon Rangers as it can dig trenches around disasters to mitigate danger while being safe from blunt damage and fire.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Turning its body at high speeds lets POKENAME become a flaming drill able to tunnel through bedrock with ease. The tunnels it digs this way smoulder with still-burning flames for hours after it's finished digging.
author: sk372

entry: Flocks of POKENAME race one another in long competitions. A race only ends once every member of a flock crosses the finish line.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME bashes foes with its pincers at an increasing pace, the flames within them grow and intensify. Once it's swinging at foes at max speed, it finishes the battle by opening its pincers and blasting them with a burst of fire.
author: soup1900

entry: The fires that rage in its shell heat it up to the temperature of a blast furnace. This makes POKENAME a popular partner Pokémon for potters.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME marks fruit-bearing trees with its horn to claim territory. It will summon a swirling Fire Spin from its paws to drive away intruders.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME flaps its wings, its flames crackle loudly. Sleeping with one of its feathers under a pillow is said to bring vivid, pleasant dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can often be tracked by the scorched mushrooms it leaves behind, dug up during its search for a meal. These burns mark the territory it has recently explored.
author: garret95

entry: Though its legs are short, POKENAME is surprisingly fast over long distances. It leaves behind melted paths in the snowy regions it calls home.
author: garret95

entry: As it rolls, POKENAME scorches the ground beneath it. The faster it spins, the darker and deeper the burn marks it leaves behind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often attempts to paint something with its tail when its Smeargle instincts take over. Sadly it forgets that its tail is no longer made of fur and paint, but instead is a scorching hot flame. Most POKENAME suffer constant burns as a result.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: A reclusive artist that uses its own tail to dry its paint faster. It is highly accident-prone and clumsy, however, leading it to burn either its own artwork or itself. It practices its work on boulders, yet the meaning behind them remains unclear.
author: merclipse

entry: POKENAME slithers rapidly, leaving trails of fire where it moves. It uses these trails to entrap its prey, slowly creating a smaller flaming cage until there is nowhere left to run or escape.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME arrives during the summertime, bringing warm temperatures and summer rain. Areas where it resides are covered in a blanket of heavy fog.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stamps its feet atop mountains to challenge friends to races. Though clumsy and slow, it waves its flaming tail with fierce determination.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's main habitat is in hot scrublands and deserts, where groups come out at night and race through the air. From a distance they look like flickers of ethereal flame dancing just above the horizon.
author: quietcognition

entry: POKENAME channels fire all across its body to aid in defense, while keeping vast stores of electricity built up inside. When it needs to attack, it channels all the lightning into its horn and fires powerful bolts from the tip.
author: sk372

entry: This fusion becomes extremely vile and sadistic. It scratches and burns its defeated opponents, thinking their screams will please their Trainer.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME struggles to contain its blazing flames. Because of this, it is often found secluded away from both people and Pokémon.
author: crustyglowstick

entry: Its body is constantly burning, leaving a thick trail of ash behind it. At the same time, its body regenerates so quickly that it never goes out.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is constantly burning, leaving a thick trail of ash behind it. At the same time, its body regenerates so quickly that it never goes out.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are often seen near the site of bushfires, and theorized to cause many of them. However, these fires clear the way for new life to flourish.
author: carameldog

entry: Its flames are so intense that they completely cover its body. These creatures are seen as an environmental threat, rapidly melting the snowy landscapes they call home.
author: garret95

entry: An attempt at overclocking Rapigon2: POKENAME achieved higher speeds at the cost of its normalcy.
author: pory

entry: POKENAME challenges others of its kind to digging races. Its fiery spines ignite as it digs, lighting the tunnels it carves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flames have minor healing properties that it bestows to its loved ones. Against hostile enemies, POKENAME uses its fire to burn them to ash.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a fearless warrior that fights bravely to protect the weak from mistreatment. It can manipulate its flames, shaping them into a spear that it wields with remarkable skill.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME runs across open plains, leaving flaming trails in its wake. Its fiery mane symbolizes its unwavering spirit and unmatched agility in battle.
author: sheogorath

entry: When moving at top speed, POKENAME's flaming headbutts can tear apart almost any obstacle. Once it starts running, it's best to stay out of POKENAME's way, since it won't stop no matter what is in its path.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Despite its heavy body, it's been recorded to reach a top speed of 45 mph. The constant fire on the metals have made them heat absorbant.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME is extremely lazy, so it's seen sleeping in the fields. When attacked, it gets up and runs away to a place where it can continue to rest.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: Farmers have put its immense strength and endurance to work, but are stumped by its equally large laziness and appetite. A POKENAME requires so much food as motivation that it eats more than a farm produces, leading all its owners into bankruptcy.
author: .fedoraman

entry: With its quick feet and precognition, POKENAME quickly evacuates those it perceives as being in potential danger. Emergency response teams across the world are beginning to recruit POKENAME into their ranks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tend to be naturally aggressive, chasing away anyone who gets too close. On the flip side, POKENAME are incredibly loyal to those they manage to form a bond with.
author: ohok3441

entry: Galloping with earth-shaking strides, POKENAME bears a flaming forest upon its back. Flames dance amidst foliage without ever burning it down.
author: anarchaz

entry: Near magnetic fields, POKENAME's flames intensify. This phenomenon is often seen in locations like Chargestone Cave.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME live within secluded lakes, radiating enough warmth to turn them into large hot springs. Few are ever fortunate enough to find such lakes, and even fewer still are lucky enough to witness the beauty of this Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the heat haze from its fiery hair to create mirages and illusions. It's said that these illusions do not appear to those it trusts.
author: nyoomymph

entry: In herds of POKENAME, the fastest runner is the leader of the herd. They are very competitive and will race anything that they see as faster.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME wanders lands far and wide, usually floating above plains or fields.  Its burning flames propel it to incredible speeds. A few have attempted to use POKENAME as a means of transportation, but its flight patterns appear to be random.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME release the full might of their flames when faced with a strong opponent. They will often veil their axe-like tusks in these very same flames to further overwhelm and conquer their enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite appearances, POKENAME has no Mudsdale or Zebstrika DNA. Because of this, many theorize that Rapidash shares a close common ancestor with these Pokémon. All three of POKENAME's head seem to behave closer to a Rapidash than anything else.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: Fueled by the mystic power in its tails, POKENAME can reach 200 mph, leaving behind nine light trails. It spends its 1,000 year lifespan racing as much as possible.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME have flaming tails that are capable of razing forests with a single blast of fire. They live in caves where they can safely unleash their fire against cave walls.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Packs of POKENAME leave bare canopies and trampled underbrush in their wake as they romp through the jungle. The destruction they wreak is a part of the jungle's natural life cycle as it allows for new plants to grow in its place.
author: .fedoraman

entry: It races other POKENAME to see who can dig the most pit traps. It races from pit to pit to catch any prey that has fallen in before they can escape.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME runs swiftly across grasslands with its wings tucked. During disputes, it spreads its wings wide and paces side to side in a show of dominance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are raised on vast, open ranches to race against each other in local tournaments. They love winning races, so they train relentlessly throughout the day to improve their speed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's head are extremely hot. When POKENAME is upset, they ignite and fall off, regrowing within a day if it's well nourished.
author: .izik

entry: Herds of POKENAME stampede through the sky, leaving streams of fire where they gallop. They are a peaceful but proud Pokémon.
author: caladria

entry: As POKENAME performs a dance, it instinctively creates a blazing Fire Spin with its movements. POKENAME's feet move incredibly fast, and it will often dance to wherever it wishes to go with the speed of a galloping Rapidash.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: As POKENAME scuttles about, it releases small embers containing spores that sink into the ground. From these spores will eventually grow a type of mushroom noted and sought for its spicy flavor.
author: sk372

entry: Some say POKENAME is the avatar of flame itself. It appears in the middle of forest fires, controlling the blaze away from Pokémon nests, before vanishing in a rain of cinders.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are very competitive with one another and can be seen racing through the sky. Anything burned by their flames gives off thick smoke that is incredibly toxic.
author: mistymagius

entry: When encountered while galloping, POKENAME dives beneath the soil and releases swirling blasts of fire. This display is meant to frighten pursuers away.
author: .izik

entry: It will awkwardly run for long distances to show off its fiery mane. It is extremely vain, stopping for anyone who admires it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fiery mane burns brightest during the summer and will rage into an inferno when POKENAME is enraged. However, if it starts raining, its mane will turn into a bellowing cloud of smoke.
author: mistymagius

entry: If it stops running for even a moment it will fall to the ground due to its odd weight distribution. It will use telekinesis to hoist itself up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's powerful legs allow it to run up to 80mph, even though it prefers to just teleport to its destination. Its masterful pyrokinetic abilities allow it to overwhelm its opponents with pure firepower.
author: mistymagius

entry: For a long period of time, Scientists thought that ancient murals of POKENAME were just an artistic misrepresentation of a different Pokémon. It gallops freely about the woods, swallowing any insects in its way.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's stones are hot enough to warm soup. In some regions, it's believed this can cure sickness faster when used in meals.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME are found exclusively near active volcanoes. Hikers consider spotting one in the wild to be a warning sign to vacate the area.
author: theartemis1

entry: With a smaller, more developed body, POKENAME can reach greater speeds than before, though it takes time to acclimate to its new top speed. Its new potential gives it a bit of an ego and temper, so its behavior is rather volatile.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was first discovered after a herd of them was mistaken for a raging wildfire. The size of their flaming manes seems to determine the leader of the herd, who will protect their brethren with their life.
author: chibitales

entry: It makes its home near coal-fueled power plants. When none are available, it will hide in the chimneys of residential homes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers grow hotter the faster it runs. At full speed, its body may erupt in flame, though it remains completely unharmed.
author: .izik

entry: One of the speediest Pokémon on the land, POKENAME can race across an entire region in a few hours. As it runs and leaps, it leaves behind flaming hoof-prints in its wake.
author: sk372

entry: Past legends claim that POKENAME were once used as underwater mounts for a sea-dwelling race. The water-like manes of content POKENAME are warm and safe to touch, but when angered, their manes can skyrocket to boiling temperatures.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME ignites fires for others, aiding in tasks like cooking and metallurgy. Feisty by nature, they will only obey those who've earned their trust.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME is incredibly slow. Even if a predator is actively chewing on it, it will not react.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: Often called "The Sea Mine," POKENAME is known to explode when reeled in by fishermen. Even veteran anglers are cautious about fishing in its habitat.
author: melodydelune

entry: Five of the clutch mindlessly join together by biting their tails, surrounding the smarter sixth member in the center. This protects the center one physically, letting it protect the others with its psychic powers.
author: sk372

entry: Orphaned due to Slowpoke Tail poaching, POKENAME wields its mother's tail as a weapon to defend other Slowpoke colonies from suffering a similar fate.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tongue contains a special compound in its saliva that induces extreme drowsiness when it touches a living thing. This chemical is theorised to be what causes its intense laziness.
author: evilgammon

entry: It produces a gas from inside its body that causes POKENAME to become numb and lethargic. The gas is commonly used as an excellent anesthetic for medical procedures.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its body has completely hardened as it begins its metamorphosis into a new evolutionary stage. Since in this state it is totally defenseless, POKENAME tries to remain still, hiding among the riverbank algae until it can emerge from its pink shell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It charges at anything approaching its territory, but with its small legs and heavy upper body, POKENAME moves at a snail's pace. It gives up long before it does any damage, and often forgets why it tried to charge in the first place.
author: sk372

entry: It has vines that resemble Slowpoke tails, which it shakes and wiggles to lure in small vermin to eat. It basks in the sunlight whenever it loses a few vines in battle, which absorb sunlight to store enough energy to regenerate vines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is slow to react to its surroundings, as it enjoys floating atop a water's surface. On occasion, it will snap awake during a lightning storm to find one of its friends got zapped twice without getting hurt.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is slow to react and enjoys lazing about all day, especially when it has no predators to worry about. Its fins spread out in a mesmerizing pattern that looks like a ballroom dress when it rests, giving the illusion that it is swimming.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its body has completely hardened as it begins its metamorphosis into a new evolutionary stage. Since in this state POKENAME is totally defenseless, it tries to remain still, hiding among the riverbank algae until it can emerge from its pink shell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: After its evolution, POKENAME developed four magnificent wings that allow it to fly just above the water's surface. Since it is very absent-minded, it often forgets where it was heading and wanders aimlessly until it grows tired.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are a common delicacy in many parts of the world because of their unique regenerative properties. The consistent harvesting of their tails allows chefs to plan how much food to prepare for one day while minimizing waste.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It dances at a slow yet rhythmic pace, with the gyration of its body swaying like calm ocean waves. It takes a long time to react to any changes in the environment, as its passive dancing is hard to break from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Unscrupulous sorts once thought POKENAME would be the key to profit by tripling Slowpoke Tail production. However, POKENAME tails were far too bitter to be edible, ruining the plans.
author: sk372

entry: One of the most unaware Pokémon discovered, POKENAME is often witnessed swimming in a straight line, bumping into an obstacle, shifting its course barely, and restarting the cycle. It is easy to care for as it uses little mental or physical energy.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its frightening expression scares off intruders and hunters, but POKENAME is as dim-witted as its Slowpoke brethren. While swimming, it may mistake its own tail for prey and accidentally injure itself.
author: sk372

entry: An overly trusting Pokémon, POKENAME has long been the victim of poachers harvesting its large tail, leaving the confused Pokémon struggling to swim. Trainers have taken to watching over and protecting herds of POKENAME with the aid of Dewgong packs.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Using psychic senses, POKENAME can detect buried evolution stones. However, it often forgets and wanders off before telling anyone.
author: .izik

entry: Though harmless and friendly, sighting POKENAME on one's devices is considered a nuisance. Its presence causes technology to lag and run at a weaker and slower pace.
author: sk372

entry: Its lethargic lifestyle means it rarely gets up and moves around for any reason. It takes so long to do so that by the time it is on its feet, it has forgotten the reason it wanted to move in the first place.
author: sk372

entry: The so-called “drills” on its arms are identical in appearance to Slowpoke tails. POKENAME will often fish with all three appendages simultaneously. If its territory is encroached upon it will chase others away, albeit slowly.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When able to think properly and fully concentrate, POKENAME utilizes incredible psychic power. These moments of clarity are incredibly rare and brief, often going years between minute-long displays of potential.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME doesn't pay attention to where it's floating. It will frequently bump into things, but it doesn't mind that much.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: Due to a strange chemical imbalance in POKENAME's body, its tail seems to grow from its head instead of its rear. The tail has a unique flavor because of this, being a lot sweeter but a little less tender.
author: mistymagius

entry: Rarely does one see flames burning on its back, as it signifies emotions of anger or surprise; feelings that do not come easily to POKENAME.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Whenever it starts its seasonal migration, it follows the same air current to find warm land each time. No matter what distractions it encounters on its path, it always has a strong sense of direction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends the majority of the day stretched out sunbathing by the water. When it does move, POKENAME strolls at a steady pace with a peaceful smile.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME makes its home in damp caves, spinning its webs near waterways to catch a variety of prey. It often does not react to Pokémon caught in its web, instead just watching as the captive struggles and eventually breaks free.
author: pjporwoll

entry: While other bird Pokémon may get confused or lost, it has a strong internal compass that allows it to find the way home. Its ability to return makes it a beloved lifelong pet, as it never forgets kindness given to it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are always wary of wild Langoos; they has learned to fear its orbs. This has led to them to occasionally be scared of the moon.
author: not_stakings_alt

entry: The white part of POKENAME's tail crackles with stored electricity. Mechanics in rural towns sometimes use it to jump-start engines.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time hibernating, as it doesn't have the strength to even crawl effectively. Occasionally in its sleep, it begins levitating as its dormant cosmic powers begin to awaken.
author: evilgammon

entry: They enjoy reading books but are remarkably slow at doing so. Trainers who want to help their POKENAME should flip to the glossary section and read alongside them, as unfamiliar words tend to be difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has extremely bad memory issues. Should anyone wrong a POKENAME, it will forgive the transgression within two minutes, forgetting it entirely.
author: .izik

entry: It is swept through the air on a breeze, the soft zephyrs it floats on remove the need to deal with predators. During the rare times it needs to eat, it floats down to the ground to eat a clump of grass before hopping back up into the air currents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its flower has enough nutrients to last a month without eating, which is the only time it ever comes down from the sky. It is capable of sleeping in the sky because its lightweight body gives them a natural buoyancy that keeps them in the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It sleeps in the mud near marshes or lakes to remain cool throughout the year and prefers to stay within the confines of a muddy area when it searches for food. It has slow reaction times, as it struggles to catch berries tossed its way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It stays cool by covering itself in mud, especially whenever the sun is high in the sky during the summer months. It is not physically active, so it rarely gets hungry enough to leave a muddy area.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It will spend its time attempting to balance on floating logs. Due to its poor weight distribution, this usually results in it falling off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's lower brainwave measurements support the claim that the venom from the Shellder crown aids in Slowking's intelligence boost. It often looks around and scratches its head as if it can tell it is missing something, but then proceeds to nap.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It very frequently forgets to eat and drink. Due to this, it will lose weight rapidly unless someone else feeds it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME chews lazily on whatever is in front of it: fruits, rocks, and even sleeping Pokémon. Oddly, those who are bitten actually have their external wounds healed after a few minutes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite its goofy face, this fusion has indignant behavior and bites everything passing by. Its fur smells sweet.
author: fouguri

entry: Whenever something tries to cut off any of its tails, POKENAME springs from its slumber and mercilessly claws the offender. As soon as it is finished attacking, it curls up in the coldest spot and sleeps.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its sharp attention to detail and internal compass allow it to guide others in its flock without getting lost. When spring arrives on the horizon, it flies back to its home to pick off bug Pokémon that are slow to wake up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail secretes a sweet glaze that chills instantly on contact. Its tail is used widely in sorbets and gourmet ice cream.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use calcium from the environment to build up their coral. Their calm nature makes them good partners for newer Trainers.
author: totodile.

entry: Some POKENAME grow legs and migrate to shallow lakes when displeased with their environment. They run faster than might be expected at a glance.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME is quite the curious Pokémon, often sitting on crowded beaches to watch what the beachgoers are doing. It doesn't seem to notice when it loses a tentacle as it will regrow again within a day or two.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME collects discarded treasures on beaches and riverbanks. Clumsy and forgetful, it often drops and finds them anew.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME is very loving and makes a great housepet for families with children, but it struggles with learning commands and is tricked easily when playing. In the wild, POKENAME relies on luck, scraps, and charity to survive as it rarely catches prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is very loving and makes a great housepet for families with children, but it struggles with learning commands and is tricked easily when playing. In the wild, POKENAME relies on luck, scraps, and charity to survive as it rarely catches prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME takes its time to ensure that its paintings are perfect. The watercolor dyes produced by its tail are highly sought after by painters.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME is very vain, always fixing its hair any chance it gets. It is also extremely lazy, using its telekinetic powers to levitate its food into its mouth.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives in a post-meal hibernation. They deter predators by secreting a toxic drool that causes harm to anything that touches it.
author: danarchist

entry: When spooked, POKENAME flares its hood, the imagery of which causes attackers to be stunned and confused as their minds are suddenly overwhelmed with inane questions and half-baked thoughts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often unaware of danger, as most Pokémon that try to eat it will be met by a powerful electric shock from its tail. It feeds on small fish, keeping its tail in the water until something bites it and becomes fried.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are rather forgetful bird Pokémon that may even forget if they have already eaten. Because of this, they are almost always perched atop rocks or sticks near rivers and use their tails to fish for aquatic Pokémon to eat.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon loves the taste of its own tail. It will slowly gnaw it off and devour it. POKENAME feels no pain from this, and its tail regrows.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME tails are a delicacy. They are known to dock their own tails by trying to eat them and are named one of the region's slowest Pokémon.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME is very slow, so slow that you can go about your whole day before it does a thing. Curiously, people started organizing POKENAME races.
author: pokebio

entry: Before digging, POKENAME spits water on cave walls to soften them. Its tunnels stretch for miles but may take years to complete due to its pace.
author: .izik

entry: It flies around beaches and lakes to look for the best place to catch fish. It stalks fishers from a distance before it settles in a nearby spot to begin fishing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in the sandy seabed, leaving only the spines on its back exposed. It surfaces only when prey swims too close. When it curls into a ball, it loses the ability to swim against the current and is carried away from the shore.
author: fiordaliso

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME grows irritable. Its tail glows bright blue before it spits mud at anything that gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's ability to change its color to match its environment is poorly executed, changing colors long after it has left the associated location. Many predators leave it alone, fearing the poor camouflage is due to it being highly toxic to eat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Many have claimed that POKENAME are not very smart. However, reports have been made of POKENAME being spotted using basic tools to acquire food.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME uses its mouth-like appendage to hunt for fish, dangling it into the water and waiting for a bite. However, since its mouth has no tastebuds, it will often not notice if it has caught something inedible.
author: mistymagius

entry: Lazy and not terribly intelligent, POKENAME have been observed trying to eat their own tails instead of gathering food. Since their limbs regenerate fully, there is no lasting damage from this behavior.
author: sontyp

entry: Scientists believe fusion gave POKENAME more precise augury. However, because it's simple-minded, it can't decipher its own visions.
author: matpal6

entry: POKENAME drifts aimlessly through lakes, its tiny scales shimmering in sunlight. Trainers often follow just to glimpse its radiant body.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its multitude of ribbonlike feelers to fish. If their ribbons break off, they will regrow quickly, and POKENAME will feel no pain.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME lazes on beaches and islands, catching fish with its barbed tail. If disturbed, it furiously rampages, intent on destroying the one that interrupted its rest.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME possesses the power to move the earth through potent psychokinesis. It uses this power to reshape the ground into the perfect napping spot.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME possesses a slight cosmic power, able to levitate small objects. This uses a lot of energy, so it is mostly found resting and eating to recover its strength.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME harbors a deep grudge, but it can't remember against whom or why. As a result, it just floats around happily, blissfully unaware of its forgotten vendetta.
author: amiel997

entry: With six sweet-tipped tails, it's able to fish for food much more efficiently. Thanks to this feeding strategy, POKENAME can go days without leaving its fishing spot.
author: hophoppip

entry: It is primarily a sedentary species, as it does not move often. Whenever it gets hungry and needs to eat, it ejects its inner organs to hunt anything that comes nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It cannot fly more than a few inches off of the ground. While it hovers it will drag its tail across the ground, making a line in the dirt.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME senses happiness nearby, it secretes a pale film from its tail and ears. In Sinnoh, this rare substance is used in fine desserts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME naps along riverbanks, its fur humming with static. The sparks grow stronger during storms and sometimes jolt it awake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is considered a good beginner's aquatic pet due to being very low maintenance in both food and behavior. Many children find its vacant stare gazing back at them through a tank incredibly endearing.
author: sk372
