entry: POKENAME's cannons can alternate firing high-power water spouts or bolts of lightning. Firing both simultaneously for too long may cause it to explode from excessive energy output.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME possesses water jets at the back of each foot. The powerful force of water expelled gives its kicks extra speed and power in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has waterspouts on the back of its hands which it uses to add extra power to its punches and attack opponents that have flanked behind it. Much of its shell has softened to increase its agility in combat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gigantic water cannon in POKENAME's mouth is dangerous to approach, but because of its weight, POKENAME can't aim it very well.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME needs to balance the mobility of its water cannons and the rigidity of its shell. It startles predators with its cannons but also depends on its shell to defend against pecking.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shakes berries off branches with jets from its water cannons. Its wings provide both an emergency escape and added height for berry gathering.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are the arrogant, stubborn bullies of the seafloor. Their shell is nearly impenetrable, and every limb is packed tight with muscle, which they will often flex to psych out opponents. Lost limbs may regrow, albeit much weaker.
author: chinigan

entry: It is really controlled by a tiny Blastoise. Using jets of water to bombard foes and move with incredible agility, it's as skilled as a fighter pilot.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME can be seen performing for children at water parks. The sack on its back is filled with all sorts of water-themed party tricks.
author: patch

entry: POKENAME is difficult to pin down, since it is a versatile fighter. If the blades on its arms aren't enough to finish an opponent, it bombards them with water projectiles from its twin cannons.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When this brutal Pokémon eats, it lays flat on its stomach, shredding apart anything remaining underneath it with one thousand teeth.
author: fivetailedfurret

entry: POKENAME is very protective of its territory, charging at any intruders it spies. Once it gets at point-blank range, high-pressure water from its cannons launches its target across the horizon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leap out of the water to shoot berries out of trees with their cannon. If POKENAME fails to land back into the water, they flop around until they fall back in.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has miniature cannons which can shoot lasers. They don't have any effect since the cannon is not strong enough.
author: watermelonchild

entry: POKENAME is heavily armed with strong water cannons and an impenetrable armored shell. During the war, they fought in many naval battles.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: It patrols its territory, blasting any unruly Pokémon with a deluge of water. Unlike Lapras, it goes berserk if anything tries to ride on its back.
author: pokepower

entry: Contrary to popular belief, POKENAME actually fires clouds of boiling steam from its sprouts. It usually uses this ability to cook its usual prey, mollusk Pokémon, boiling them completely in a matter of seconds.
author: lemage22

entry: POKENAME fires its water cannons at anything that disturbs the branches it hangs from. Sometimes the recoil from the water cannon knocks it out of the tree.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives a solitary life residing in areas with frigid waters, and does not take kindly to intruders. The water shot from its cannon instantly freezes over when it hits a target, leaving them frozen solid.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hangs from branches and shoots water jets at other Pokémon that come too close. Whenever it fires its water cannons, it is flung back from the recoil.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is equipped with three water cannons that shoot powerful jets of water. It marks its territory by spraying a mist laced with toxins, which also scares away other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can fire a toxic slime that eats away at living matter. It has a thin film over its eyes that acts like a set of goggles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME channels psychic energy through its cannons, launching powerful telekinetic water blasts. It can control water with its mind, forming waves to strike down opponents.
author: thepandasharky

entry: In combat, POKENAME creates leaves and vines out of water, which it uses to attack. During forest fires, groups of POKENAME will put themselves in danger to douse the flames.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a singular cannon that shoots out streams of water. It is strong enough to knock down berries from trees, which makes up a large part of its diet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on its cannons to propel it through the air. It has a peculiar muscle spasm that causes it to bobble its head once a second, even while flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can accurately fire water jets from the cannon on its shell while moving extremely fast. They are utilized in the military in place of attack drones.
author: soup1900

entry: When preparing to strike, POKENAME coats the feathers on its wings with a dense layer of water before diving at full speed. The shell covering its body shields its most vulnerable spots from enemy attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It fires high-pressure water jets from its two antennae to puncture its prey. Combining these two blasts can create ocean currents of over 60 mph.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's cannons sway hypnotically in the water, drawing the attention of curious Pokémon swimming by. When they get close enough, it blasts its unsuspecting prey with powerful beams of water.
author: cartoonhostage

entry: The cannon in its mouth fires water at exceptional power. However, POKENAME is so frail that it flies backwards afterwards, leading to some POKENAME using it as a means of travel.
author: imaginaryneon

entry: POKENAME shoots electrically charged squirts of water from the pea-shooters on its back. However, the wattage and hydrologic strength of these attacks is so weak, it does little more than give its opponents a little uncomfortable shock.
author: richardcareylol

entry: POKENAME dances on rocky beaches during clear nights filled with many shooting stars. It uses the water from its cannons to create mesmerizing displays.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME flies through hurricanes and tropical storms without the risk of being whisked away. Its large water cannons stabilize its flight so that it does not get knocked off course.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The force of a water jet from a POKENAME's cannon can knock down small bird Pokémon. It swims faster than it crawls, so it is rarely found far from a body of water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoys pranking others by spraying them with water from the jet on its prehensile tail. Its overzealous nature and the strength of its cannon often cause the target of the prank to be knocked out by the blast.
author: sk372

entry: The force behind POKENAME's cannons is so great that it can propel the Pokémon backward. However, it produces a gel that anchors it in place. Without proper training, it cannot sustain long bursts of fire.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The Seed Bomb it fires from the mortar on its back can explode midair, creating a colorful boom. People use it to create beautiful fireworks shows.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are too big to fit into their shell but instead have access to cannons that fire jets of water. They can quickly knock down berries from branches that hang over water and shoot down their predators as well.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's massive cannon gathers and fires concentrated psychic energy. When fired, the recoil is so immense that it often sends this Pokémon flying through the air.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME hunt for bug Pokémon by flooding their burrows with water, forcing prey to escape or risk drowning. Once the Pokémon reach the surface, they pounce to secure their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The water jets on POKENAME's back provide momentum that lets it achieve a frightening amount of mobility for its size and weight. Those expecting a slow and lumbering foe will quickly find themselves clamped by its sturdy pincers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stalk Caterpie back to their burrows before flooding their burrows with water. If any Caterpie manage to escape through a different tunnel, POKENAME can fire long range jets of water to knock them unconscious.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has two heads that communicate to launch accurate attacks from over 1000 yards away. Sometimes it gets dizzy from the two viewpoints.
author: dusknoir64

entry: POKENAME rarely fail at hunting because of their ability to sneak up on their prey. If they ever manage to escape, POKENAME unleash a torrent of water to overwhelm and subdue their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can fire pressurized jets of paint from its tail powerful enough to punch through wood. It creates its paint by collecting rainwater in its shell and mixing it with different berries.
author: mistymagius

entry: As POKENAME spins its body, it kicks up a small wall of water with enough force to topple a fully grown person. The water creates a slippery surface that allows for POKENAME to spin even faster.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stabilizes itself with its tail as it fires jets of water at prey. This method of confusing prey allows it to come close enough to deliver a toxic bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are proud, prideful creatures that always demand respect from others. Other Pokémon fear POKENAME because of their ability to cause earthquakes and flood the area around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME battle, they usually engage in duels reminiscent of cowboy standoffs. It frequently has feuds with Octillery.
author: teatedtiten

entry: Although it can't do much, POKENAME cares deeply about the cleanliness of beaches and the ocean. It often picks up plastic bottle caps and stores them in its pouch, and is known to bother people who litter on the shore.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME has a powerful tail cannon that shoots jets of water and lightning bolts. Its flexible tail allows it to fire shots even when curled up in its shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Armies employ POKENAME as a long-range drone during recon missions. Since POKENAME is attuned to magnets, it can find its way back to its Trainer via magnetic signals and blast water or electricity from its cannons during combat.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is capable of shooting rocks and water from its cannons. When it feels threatened, it will hide in its shell and use its tail as a mace.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME drink liquified clay to nourish their bodies and often surface with clay all over their bodies. If another POKENAME is nearby, they take turns giving each other a pressurized bath from their water cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's twin cannons function independently of its body and can fire fierce jets of water with great strength and accuracy. However, on occasion they may go haywire, spinning and spraying water in every direction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the waterspouts that protrude from its shell to leap even greater distances while hunting down its prey. This makes it a very loud hunter, but that hardly matters if it reaches speed levels that are invisible to the naked eye.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME live near clay deposits and eat clay to nourish their bodies. Whenever the clay dries up and becomes hard, they hose down the clay to turn it into an edible slurry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The hard material comprising POKENAME's shell is actually dried mud. It can smash pieces of the shell into shrapnel and fire them at speeds that could dent a Shuckle's shell.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: POKENAME uses a pair of twin water cannons on its arms to protect those it cares for. Once the high-pressure water is shot, it telekinetically manipulates the water to ensure it strikes even the most evasive of targets.
author: sk372

entry: Haunting especially polluted mountain springs, POKENAME scares off trespassers while purifying the water. Their aqueous ring maintains perfect purity, and is sought for mead production.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When threatened, POKENAME will hide in its shell and then curl into a ball. POKENAME can still fire its bullets of water while in this form, and its high speed tackles hurt even more thanks to the spines on its shell.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME fire corrosive gel at prey through the cannons on their back. Due to the pressure that comes out of the cannons, they often lose their footing and end up missing their target.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In addition to changing the colors of its body and shell, POKENAME has mastered changing the color of its water. When it is happy, the colors are paint-like and vibrant. When it is nervous, the colors are oily and murky.
author: sockedpuppetart

entry: With scales hardened like armor, POKENAME stalks challengers under the waves. It ambushes by using its arm cannon followed by breaking the surface with a deadly Mach Punch.
author: ghostslythe

entry: It launches seeds from the two cannons on its back to plant them in high places it cannot reach. It can fire Seed Bombs over 30,000 feet.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME protects their nestmates by standing guard at the entrance of their burrow. They vigilantly stand ready to shoot corrosive gel from their cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its jaws now function as a water cannon. As a result, POKENAME is a favorite amongst firefighters.
author: mossybanana

entry: Research shows that the jets of POKENAME build up water pressure as they sleep. Due to the constant naps POKENAME takes, it is theorized that with enough time they could grow strong enough to level a mountain.
author: atlasmountain

entry: POKENAME zealously protect their nest from danger, and they are always ready to blast threats with a burst of corrosive gel. Their diligence is rewarded with affection and berries from their younger nestmates.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shoot water out of their cannons when they surface for air. Their massive bodies can store a week's worth of air, but they enjoy the act of shooting water from their cannons, so they come to the surface almost daily.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Multiple high-power water cannons grow from POKENAME's shell, giving it a strong area of defense. The cannons are powered via nutrients from the soil that POKENAME absorbs through the palms of its feet.
author: sk372

entry: A legendary gun-sword said to be possessed by a shipwrecked, sunken pirate lord. It sinks ships to make others face its fate too.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME charges directly at its prey, relying on the shell that covers its entire body as armor before slicing them with pressurized water jets. Consequently, more than 50 ships sink per year due to this Pokémon.
author: aglt05

entry: From its tail, POKENAME can fire high-pressure jets of water strong enough to pierce the walls of a building. By rubbing its mane against its body, it builds up enough static electricity to unleash powerful electrified blows.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its ribbons have adapted to spout highly pressurized bursts of water. These ribbons can fire water hard enough to tear through solid stone.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME glides silently through deep ocean trenches, its shell generating immense water pressure to crush obstacles. Ancient mariners revered it as a guardian of the sea's darkest depths.
author: segmoph

entry: POKENAME fires water as well as pointy rocks out of its cannons at incoming threats. Psychologists found out that this Pokémon doesn't like its blue colored scales, because they remind it of Kyogre.
author: over9001

entry: POKENAME has perfect vision and accuracy with its cannons, able to snipe targets from its home miles up in the skies. It's thought that at max power, its water shots could pierce completely through the planet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was once revered as a sacred fountain with an endless flow of water. Its deeds have since faded into myth.
author: squawkabairdy

entry: POKENAME have a kingly influence over their territory that allows them to command other Pokémon to do their bidding. In exchange for this influence, POKENAME are obliged to protect Pokémon with their tough shell and powerful cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is capable of firing intense streams of water from its mouth. Many racecar circuits use multiple POKENAME to keep the stands clean and in case of emergency.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can shoot water with such pressure that it propels itself back many meters. It likes to use this as an unconventional escape method.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME, lacking any limbs, creates a miniature crew from its fused genetic material to man and reload its cannons. POKENAME often follow boats, protecting them from more aggressive Pokémon.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: POKENAME blasts across the sky with its 200-PSI water jets. When it starts raining without warning, it is said that a POKENAME is nearby.
author: rkmaster25367

entry: POKENAME is a guardian of orphaned or abandoned Squirtle. It can sense the hearts and minds of people, and will only allow kindhearted Trainers to adopt one of its charges.
author: gerbopotato

entry: POKENAME is capable of unleashing highly pressurized water from each of its tail-cannons. It possesses control over the water it expels.
author: winchbeef

entry: It aims its tails like a fire hose, jetting out a scalding steam. Each of a POKENAME's nine nozzles specializes in spraying either fire or water, the number of which differs from one POKENAME to another.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The bubble on its back has now fully grown into a flower. Most POKENAME live underwater where the sun can still reach them, as their flora are aquatic.
author: soup1900

entry: A clumsy Pokémon, POKENAME constantly sets fire to things with its tail. It then uses its cannons to put out the fire, usually using too much water.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME prefer not to use their cannon and display it proudly as a trophy. If provoked, however, the cannon on a POKENAME can fire a near-endless supply of piercing water.
author: crumple_2

entry: While POKENAME may appear to be wrapped in cloth, the material is sturdier than stone. POKENAME blasts precise streams of chilling water, almost seeming to detect where the target will be before they move.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME dances slightly slower than its pre-evolutions due to its heavier shell. The boiling water it shoots from its cannons can reach a temperature of 212 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME are often found in filthy rivers and lakes, eating the trash that has polluted the water. The trash it eats mixes into the water it shoots out of its cannons.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME uses its blistering speed and rock-hard skull to take down even the largest ocean creatures. Many Hoenn sailors believe that a school of POKENAME was responsible for the great tragedy of the S.S. Cactus.
author: mbo1064.

entry: The water from POKENAME's cannons contains a substance that can be extracted and refined to make a potent weed killer.
author: kittyluv090

entry: A valiant and rare woodland Pokémon that dwells near rivers, POKENAME can fire accurate pressurized blasts of water that could easily pierce the hull of a ship. It selflessly takes blows meant for other Pokémon, even strangers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME angers easily, becoming hostile at even the slightest provocation. It will then blast the agitator with scalding steam from its cannons.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME fires muddy water jets from underground at extreme speed. The pressure is strong enough to pierce solid stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swallows water and expels it through its tails, using them like thrusters to propel itself with surprising speed. Engineers have studied this unique method of movement as inspiration for developing more efficient pump-jets.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME blasts torrents of water from its tunnels to knock prey from trees. It drags stunned targets like Venomoth beneath the dirt to feast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is incredibly tough, shielding it from foes it often battles. Thanks to its agility, it can climb to the tops of trees, from where it takes aim and blasts its enemies with powerful water cannons.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME extends and retracts its water cannons in response to stress. Whenever it experiences a headache, the cannons contract and make it difficult to shoot water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce a torrent of water from their cannons that propel them swiftly through the water. The cannons help them reach speeds that rival motor vehicles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on the cannons on their back to propel them through water since their round bodies lack the muscle mass for them to swim effectively. They often accidentally bump into other Pokémon, but few Pokémon get angry at them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The angrier POKENAME gets, the higher the pressure and accuracy of its cannons. Its exceptional arm strength makes POKENAME an incredibly strong swimmer.
author: steamedveggies.

entry: The cannons on POKENAME's shell are capable of generating intense blasts of both flame and water. This versatility makes them highly popular among foresters and park rangers.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are equipped with two powerful cannons used to shoot high-pressure streams. They are often loyal pets of firefighters because of their agility and strength.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It ejects scalding steam from its cannons. This steam can cause 4th-degree burns, meaning it'll burn through your skin and potentially kill you.
author: soup1900

entry: Its body is frail from years of nonstop meditation. In combat, it will summon a pair of powerful cannons that shoot water with great force.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: Fusion has granted POKENAME more flexible cannons with which to aim. Its water blasts have increased in power, as well as precision.
author: skymaster426

entry: The shells that POKENAME gain upon evolution have grown to accommodate the cannons growing from their back. They tuck themselves into their shells during battle, preferring to stay on the defensive and blast water from afar.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A POKENAME's body is partly clad in a tough, armor-like shell. Though it often fights using horns and blasts of steam, it can unleash scalding water from cannons along its sides.
author: infinex21

entry: When cornered, it fires pressurized jets of water from the cannon on its tail. However, POKENAME's reflexes are quite slow, and it often launches its attacks too late, risking missing the target.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME polish their cannons with their fuzzy tails, making sure that they both shine the same brilliant white. If their tails get dirty, they will spray the entire area with water until they wash the dirt or the offender away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's cannons are actually controlled by Shellder on its back. As a result, it's able to shoot extremely accurately and have no blind spots.
author: voxposs

entry: POKENAME has precise control of its two cannons by manipulating magnetic waves to reposition them at will. Its keen eye can easily aim to hit targets from over 160 feet away with pulses of electrically charged water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is a semi-aquatic Pokémon of action with a secret identity. It is seen battling a Bimime and winning a large majority of the time.
author: aregularbigjoke

entry: The water cannons growing from POKENAME's body have rudimentary functional brains of their own. POKENAME's main head can influence them to an extent, but they can act impulsively and fire water shots on instinct when startled.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME shoot chilling beams of water from their back cannons to push past floating ice as they swim through the world. These beams of water can quickly cause hypothermia in Pokémon that are not used to the cold.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Fusion energy has fused POKENAME with its dormant DNA. Its shell is now indestructible; not even cannon fire can harm it.
author: zoroark73

entry: POKENAME lives similarly to Blastoise: its powerful shell allows for great protection, and the cannon allows for overwhelming offense. However, POKENAME is found far more often by the sea than it is other bodies of water.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are found in humid environments where they conjure bubbles that contain spirits of the dead. Each bubble is capable of blasting a burst of water before popping, which releases the spirits inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fires spiraling streams of water from the cannons on its back. Despite not being particularly powerful, the streams seem to put its opponents into a trance, making them unable to attack.
author: mistymagius

entry: Blasts of water shot from the cannon in POKENAME's claw hit with enough force to dent solid steel. It primarily uses it to repel other predators competing for the clams and shellfish it scrounges up for food.
author: sk372

entry: While at first glance this Pokémon may just look like a regular Blastoise, it has many unique markings on its body. These markings have been proven to be veins where the fusion genetics flow through.
author: soup1900

entry: Its appearance is extremely similar to that of Mega POKENAME. The large cannon on its back makes it look like a tank with legs.
author: soup1900

entry: Its appearance is extremely similar to that of Mega Blastoise. Unlike Mega Blastoise, however, it has many markings over its face and shell where fusion genetics are most visible. These markings glow faintly when it uses powerful moves.
author: soup1900

entry: Its appearance is similar to that of Gigantamax POKENAME. It has 31 cannons on its shell that it barrages endlessly against its foes.
author: soup1900

entry: Fusion has caused this Pokémon to awaken part of its Gigantamax genes, causing its appearance to be similar to that of Gigantamax Blastoise. It can volley a multitude of blasts using the many cannons on its shell.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME protect themselves with tough shells discarded by other Pokémon, attaching them to their back with a sticky sap. The sap they use contains a mild paralytic toxin that causes a numbness in anything that touches them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While bubbling playfully, POKENAME sometimes spits out a pearl by accident. These rare gems are prized by collectors and sold at auction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sheds its thick scales every month, leaving itself vulnerable until they grow back. It usually swims along the seafloor, looking for small seashells to eat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME climbs waterfalls in search of quiet pools. There, it creates and hides its dazzling pearls far from prying eyes.
author: .izik

entry: Its hair is extremely hard and will only become malleable when wet. The fibers are used in clothing that is worn in fashion shows.
author: .izik

entry: Schools of Magikarp often integrate POKENAME into their ranks for aid in survival. While unable to swim as quickly, POKENAME's tough shell means hunters will waste time futilely trying to prey on it while the Magikarp flee to safety.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME nestles itself in rocks and patches of barnacles, disguising itself as a large shell. Any unfortunate diver who gets close will be met with its thrashing tail and snapping jaws.
author: evilgammon

entry: Riding on a POKENAME is said to be very safe, as its tough shell is strong enough to survive multiple Sharpedo attacks. It needs very little food to keep going, only needing one or two berries a day.
author: mistymagius

entry: The fossilized remains of POKENAME have been discovered in coastal caves. Its tough shell plating that covers its body is as hard as steel.
author: mepp.

entry: Wild POKENAME usually live in Kanto, but when it gets too hot, they migrate to other regions. Most travel to northern Sinnoh, though many do not survive the perilous journey and faint, washing up on desolate islands or distant shores.
author: duskit___

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME generates faintly glowing yellow pearls. Charged with residual electricity, the pearls are left behind like a breadcrumb trail as POKENAME travels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep ocean, its durable shell protecting it from the crushing pressure down there. Its lure gives off a dull red light, allowing it to see in the dark without giving away its location.
author: mistymagius

entry: It holds onto a Tropical Shell that stores static electricity, which turns the shell a bright red. Whenever it discharges the electricity in battle or otherwise, its shell returns to a greyish purple.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collect objects, then polish them with their tongues until they shine. Some treasure hunters keep them to help clean their findings.
author: rhysanthemum

entry: It licks objects with its long tongue when it has a fondness for them. Wild POKENAME are often seen licking shiny objects vigorously.
author: aberry8286

entry: Groups of POKENAME are used by sailors to send messages to other members of their fleet. Their shells are soft and able to change shape at will.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nest in river beds using their tongue to make a small hole. They do this so they can clamp on the tails of Slowsparce that put their tails in the water.
author: equation8573

entry: A mischievous and impish Pokémon by nature, POKENAME attacks other mollusks to steal their pearls, which it sees as trophies. As it ages, the shell protecting its head grows at an increased rate in comparison with the rest of its body.
author: pjporwoll

entry: After crafting pearls, POKENAME tucks them into its thick fur. It later uses them to decorate its icy nest with intricate care.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shuffles along the seafloor, eating any small creatures in its path. It can't climb over rocky terrain, so it will instead use its strong tusks to break through rocks and coral in its way.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its fins are too small to swim, so it must drag itself along the ocean floor to move. When threatened, POKENAME will burrow into the sand, leaving only its hard shell exposed.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME hides in the seafloor, posing as an empty shell. When prey swims by, it is caught in the blink of an eye by POKENAME's deceptively long tongue.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Overnight, POKENAME forms glistening pearls in its tail. By morning, it swims ashore and gently gifts them to unsuspecting beachgoers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's periwinkle camouflage allows them sneak up on nests of aquatic Pokémon. Their bivalve shell has the ability to unhinge and swallow eggs whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives near frozen lakes, smashing through the ice with armored, hair-like appendages. Despite how heavy it is, it is able to swim effortlessly without sinking.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME buries itself into the mud near swamps in order to keep cool. It is easily spooked, and uses its tongue to scoop up muck and toss it at anything that gets too close for comfort.
author: sk372

entry: It moves by releasing a pressurized blast of seawater from its rear to launch itself. It's not the best at angling these blasts, and tends to crash into objects as it flies.
author: hophoppip

entry: It sleeps nestled in underwater caverns, using its thick tongue to plug the entrance and block currents. Some believe a massive pearl lies deep within its body, but no one has ever retrieved one from a wild specimen and lived to tell the tale.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME slides across frozen lakes, spitting out bright blue pearls as it glides. The number of pearls it leaves behind changes with its mood.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's pearls shimmer with three ever-shifting hues. Under proper lighting, they seem to ripple like water, fetching steep prices from nobility.
author: .izik

entry: The hardened shell on its face will protect it from most damage. When they fight, they will close their shells and charge head first into foes.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME has a very friendly disposition, often licking others affectionately with its large tongue. If threatened, it turns tail and retreats, releasing fireballs from the shell on its rear.
author: sk372

entry: A large tongue extends from POKENAME's shell to gather kelp and algae. It eats very little except during autumn, when it feeds almost nonstop.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sings at a frequency that resonates underwater so that it can put other Pokémon to sleep. Divers wear specialized headphones that produce static noise to avoid falling asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Most of POKENAME's body is covered by a hardy calcium-based carapace that keeps it safe from incoming attacks. While its limbs are stiff and clumsy, it uses its large, agile tongue to grasp and manipulate objects.
author: regulavish

entry: POKENAME has been noted to be self-conscious of its appearance and rather shy, remaining still and shut when others are around. It only opens up in the presence of those it implicitly trusts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can produce pearls in its shell-like bud, making up to 5 pearls a week. It is very protective of its pearls and will swing its bud at anyone that tries to steal them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wears a shell as its mask. Despite not having eye holes, it proudly wears the mask to defend itself from dangerous Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its shell serves as a lightweight yet durable helmet. It uses its tongue to sense air currents and navigate through dark caves.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME rely on deceptive tricks to obtain jewelry. They leave their shell open to entice people to reach for the pearl inside before snapping shut. Once they have a hand nestled in their shell, they remove any jewelry the person may have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attempts to frighten others away by roaring and flailing its large tongue about wildly. It gets embarrassed and hides its face within the shell on its neck if this tactic fails to scare its target.
author: sk372

entry: The pearls made by POKENAME are so cold they freeze most surfaces instantly. Touching one barehanded can cause frostbite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has cool breath and a tongue that's cold to the touch. It's popular in warmer regions for helping cool down its owners on hot days.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME creates icy blue pearls that remain cold even in sunlight. High-end cafés use them as elegant drink chillers for their elite patrons.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell resembles a Sharpedo, scaring off potential predators. Grit caught within the shell becomes polished into a pearl, which it blasts out of the star-shaped hole in the shell top, shattering the pearl into the shape of sharp teeth.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It's said children who have drowned turn into POKENAME, instead of Phantump. POKENAME constantly shake and shiver from the icy waters they come from.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Sometimes divers report reaching for a cluster of 4 pearls on coral reefs, only to be attacked by a wild POKENAME. If its pearls are polished regularly, it reflects the most beautiful version of its beholder.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME crawls along coral reefs and licks up meals of detritus from the safety of its venomous dome. Even though it is dangerous to harvest, its core body is sweet and tender, but very finicky to cook as it will burn and turn rubbery quickly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Clamshell mushrooms grow on POKENAME's back. It's common practice to use these mushrooms as an ingredient in seafood dishes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can't actually swim, so it wanders the seafloor looking for small mollusks to eat. The horns on its head contain poison, which can cause shivering in its victims.
author: mistymagius

entry: When threatened, POKENAME spits shimmering pearls at predators. With a flick of psychic energy, it curves them mid-flight, creating a distraction while it escapes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME inhabit shell-like structures resembling pumpkins, and researchers remain uncertain of their origin. No one has ever observed a POKENAME outside of its shell.
author: elite01.

entry: Its body can compress until it is entirely enclosed within its two shells. Each year, POKENAME produces a single heart-shaped pearl, and if you find one by pure chance, you are said to be fated to find love.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME periodically produces small violet pearls as it digs through soil. Jewelers collect these pearls to craft modestly priced accessories.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emerge as noxious fumes from abandoned graves. The musty air chokes and suffocates those who seek to pilfer these forgotten resting places.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME is quite timid and will keep its shell tightly shut to protect itself from danger. However, if the shell remains too tight for too long, it can begin to suffer from severe migraines.
author: mistymagius

entry: If exposed to too much sunlight, the shell on its head will dry out and crack. The saliva that drips from its tongue is edible and has a tangy flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in swampy areas along the coastline. They use their tongue to reposition themselves if they fall over.
author: elite01

entry: POKENAME is incredibly meek and hides within its bell, which is actually a lightweight but durable shell. It positions itself in a sunny location so the light reflecting off the shell's gems lures in prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has outgrown its protective shell, leading to cracks and its soft body becoming exposed. The tentacles transfer a powerful toxin, which scientists have been studying for medical use in small doses.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME loves Slowpoke tails and can be seen chewing on each other's tails. If left undisturbed, long chains of POKENAME can be seen lined up on the beach.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME may look like a Slowbro, it is actually quite different in many ways. It often fights with Slowbro for territory.
author: kittyluv090

entry: A strange and curious Pokémon that appears almost like an odd-colored Slowbro. Science remains baffled at the fact the main body can retreat completely into the much smaller shell.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME smashes holes in icebergs using its blunt horns. It stores pearls inside the frozen cavities like a secret vault.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies on the seafloor, enclosing its thick shell when larger predators get close. It has trouble getting around as its heavy shell is attached to its underbelly.
author: mistymagius

entry: Packing much greater size than a normal Shellder, POKENAME has minimal offenses, and instead possesses a very rigid and sturdy shell. It often helps smaller Pokémon by letting them hide within it while it clamps shut.
author: sk372

entry: Spirits that linger where Shellder have passed away, POKENAME have a very sullen, sorrowful disposition. Being licked by one will cause a person to be overcome with an urge to cry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been observed pinching its own tongue on occasion. It's thought that this stimulates the muscle in order to keep it highly sensitive to its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's oversized claw possesses a tremendous gripping force when clamping down. It crushes large objects within its claw as a threat display to deter predators from bothering it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be seen chiseling away at its bony helmet to create its signature spiky appearance. It fires daggers of compressed water to attack any foe threatening it or its young.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME need plenty of nutrients to evolve, so in addition to their indigo cocoon they have a small, hinged shell that allows them to eat. Whenever they are attacked by predators, their hinged shell slams shut.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It latches its mouth onto coral and uses pressurized water to break it apart. The coral it eats contains nutrients it needs to strengthen the spikes on its body.
author: .izik

entry: It shoots bubbles at high speeds from its nose to break coral into smaller pieces, which it then feeds on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live near waterfalls where the cascade of water protects their pearls. They typically leave other Pokémon alone to keep the location of their pearls hidden, but may offer one as a reward for helping them escape a hungry Ursaring.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will grow spikes on its shell where it has sustained substantial injury. Those with the most spikes are assumed the alpha of their clan.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME hates people trying to ride them, intentionally trying to jab them with its spikes. Its sturdy shell is strong enough to withstand an entire iceberg falling on it.
author: mistymagius

entry: With a shell too heavy for long flights, POKENAME instead lived as a fierce undersea hunter. Its wings allowed it to swim at high speeds, firing spikes from its shell at schools of fish, feasting on the skewered victims.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are a migratory species that travel from one beach to another throughout the year. Many are unable to complete the long journey because they are picked off by Flying-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It follows tankers across the ocean, drawn to the noise and movement. Sailors often spot it clinging to the hull, riding along, hoping to be unnoticed.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to live near lighthouses, where it basks in the glow of the beacon. Its presence is considered a sign of good luck for sailors.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of quickly swimming away from predators and only rely on their shell when they hunt for food. They clamp down with their shell to snap tentacles or fins off of other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eat bleached coral because of their sickly-looking color. As pollution in the sea continues to spread, colonies of POKENAME grow more numerous.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Sailors rely on POKENAME to communicate with other ships when their equipment fails. Their malleable shell allows them to morph into basic messages that can be seen with a telescope.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rests at the bottom of the sea floor, opening its solid shell partially in order to filter-feed. If it catches sight of something approaching, it quickly closes its shell and fires off pointed ice projectiles from the holes on its sides.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME ingest sea water to inflate up to 4 times their size. This water is then expelled to allow its round body to swim. They can often be found by sandbars, terrorizing wild Kingler.
author: bass.

entry: Its streamlined shell allows for it to cut through the water as it propels itself backwards with a stream of pressurized water. Unfortunately, it can't ever see where it's going.
author: .fedoraman

entry: It thrives in tidal waves, using the powerful currents to propel itself forward. The chaos of these waves makes it feel most at home.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon shoots burning hot steam at enemies from its mouth and the protrusions in its armor. Solitary but violent, POKENAME prefers to be left alone but will fight relentlessly if provoked.
author: frokachu

entry: Fishermen call POKENAME the "Dragon of Warfare". It hides behind a powerful shell, only opening for the briefest of moments to fire a shot in the opponent's direction, before retreating back under cover.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses water propulsion to move among the waters. It releases stored electrical energy to maintain homeostasis. Excess energy discharged from POKENAME ensures stillness among life amid the waves.
author: anarchaz

entry: Sometimes, POKENAME is found underneath the piers of port towns, resting until the coast is clear; when no one is around, it will surface above water and bask in the sun.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME glides across cliff sides to attack prey. Its natural armor is incredibly tough, but chips easily in water.
author: themicelegion

entry: It endures the heat by wading in mud or greywater and may do so for an extended period of time. Once it awakens, it shakes off everything atop its back, sending mud and water everywhere.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wields a spear and wears armor created by the remains of Cloyster it has defeated. It can imbue the spear with aura in order to make it much more powerful in battle.
author: sk372

entry: During floods, it moves swiftly through submerged areas, providing aid to stranded Pokémon. Its resilient shell allows it to traverse fast-moving waters with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Even in the hands of trusted Trainers, it is needy and vain. If its pearlescent mace isn't polished regularly, it will slowly sap its Trainer's life force until they polish it well.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: When threatened on land, POKENAME will shed the pearls strung along its feelers; its pearls will be replaced in only a matter of a few days.
author: melodydelune

entry: A common tactic POKENAME uses in battle is to fly around and perform strafing runs with its Spike Cannon attack. Onlookers note that it looks akin to a fighter plane from war times when it does this.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME float above the sea to hunt for prey. They typically eat Flying-type Pokémon that dive into the sea for food, but can also eat Water-type Pokémon that leap out of the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has plating on its hands and its mask that are made of the same material as shells. It can be shy and cautious because it is worried it may break its mask.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Yachts often attract this Pokémon, where it glides alongside in search of food. Its presence near luxury vessels adds a touch of the wild to tranquil waters.
author: .izik

entry: It can propel itself forward in the sea at great speeds, but has trouble with making turns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts close to the seafloor, its pearl-like head glowing a deep blue as it sleeps. If disturbed, it retaliates by unleashing a powerful Aurora Beam.
author: .izik

entry: A clever, sneaky fusion that favors stealth over full frontal assault. Blame it if you witness a barrage of Icicle Spears seemingly from nowhere.
author: jaycielantern

entry: Despite its looks, this Pokémon can conceal itself in any terrain. POKENAME waits for the right moment to strike, launching spikes deep into a foe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It scavenges dead coral for food, breaking it apart with its powerful shell. This habit keeps reefs clear, allowing new coral to grow in its place.
author: .izik

entry: The pressure of the deep sea has made POKENAME's shell as tough as an iron suit of armor. It exposes a single opening in its defenses only when it lunges forward to strike with its claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The pearls POKENAME creates emit a natural cooling aura. It stores them deep in its den during summer to keep itself comfortable while resting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are part of a popular game where new lovers open their shell to reveal the pearl inside. It is said that lovers that pick a large pearl will have a long-lasting relationship, which inspires many lovers to stick through tough times.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often wears a malicious expression. It thinks that its shell protects it as it causes mischief, but it actually has several weak spots.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's smooth-looking body is merely a facade; opponents who attempt to bite it may even break their teeth! While it cannot move forward in a straight line, it moves with surprising agility, especially in moister conditions.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME often live near coastal cliffs or grottoes. They devour hard seashells and sometimes even Shellder with a sickening crunch.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It clings to underwater cliffs, using them as both shelter and vantage points. From these heights, it watches for prey passing through the depths below.
author: .izik

entry: Its body can withstand the extreme pressure of some of the deepest portions of the sea. Its body can quickly burn if exposed to too much sunlight.
author: .izik

entry: The sludgy part of its body is normally fluid, but it quickly hardens when struck forcefully, protecting POKENAME's inner core from harm.
author: hophoppip

entry: A valuable pearl lies hidden within its shell, polished by years of ocean currents. Many seek it, though few manage to claim the treasure within.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME imbues the pearls it creates with psychic powers, using them to hypnotize others so it may consume their dreams. The pearls have an ethereal luster to them that makes them fetch a high price among curio collectors.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient tribes utilized discarded POKENAME shells for creating armor. The pincers were fashioned into gauntlets used in combat.
author: .izik

entry: It patrols near cruise ships, scavenging discarded food and scraps. Passengers sometimes catch glimpses of it from the decks and marvel at its sleek shell.
author: .izik

entry: The shells on POKENAME's arms can clamp down with powerful force, though it disdains close-range combat. Instead, it creates and fires large pearls from the shells to pelt foes from a distance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tethers its spirit to a broken egg, which it hardens with its powers to protect itself. Without shelter, it risks dissipating.
author: darxer_

entry: The spirit of a desecrated body possesses the Cubone who dug it up and wields its bone as a weapon.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The ghostly energy surrounding POKENAME's bones resembles that of Marowak. These Pokémon do not seem to eat or drink and are often spotted trudging around cemeteries. Research is ongoing into POKENAME and its habits.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME inhales smoke from crematoriums, mixing it into its toxic gas. This enriched vapor makes its haze particularly noxious.
author: .izik

entry: Possessing a long-deceased Rhyhorn's remains, POKENAME intimidates foes with its imposing new body. If attacked, the stone plates separate to avoid strikes, then reform to counterattack.
author: sk372

entry: Childless Kangaskhan often die of heartbreak. However, in the case of POKENAME, the deceased child persists by sheer will to support its parent.
author: mattyzer0

entry: Found under corner street lamps, POKENAME stands eerily still. When spotted, it floats into the air without using its wings and chases its victim as if possessed.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's ethereal gases fuel their firepower. However, they can also lead to unintended and dangerous blazes.
author: garret95

entry: Gastly possessed a Tauros in order to cause damage and mischief. However, their possession has caused the Tauros to become incorporeal, so their once-destructive charges no longer cause actual property damage.
author: sk372

entry: The gas surrounding its body burns with incredible intensity. Even a brief touch can leave searing burns on the skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float around places where paleontologists dig up fossils looking for bones that were once part of their body. Once the complete skeleton returns to their rightful place, they are depleted of ill intentions and roam calmly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produces a gaseous form of potassium chloride that is expelled from its head, mouth, and tail. This is what causes its purple-colored fire.
author: gp423

entry: In spite of it possessing strong jaws, POKENAME only feed on carrion. Due to their gassy composition, they can't stay submerged in water for too long.
author: 8xviktor

entry: When many POKENAME gather together in the wild at night, they entertain themselves by rapidly falling to the ground in sequence in an imitation of a meteor shower.
author: sk372

entry: Almost invisible at night, this Pokémon's trek across the sky is responsible for the phenomenon of "dark meteors".
author: hushpuppy

entry: POKENAME loves to haunt and prank the residents of the homes it haunts, floating before them and making spooky noises. However, its body is so lightweight that even air from fanning one's hands will send it tumbling away through the air.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cries ceaselessly. It is said it cries because of its foreshortened life; it had just been an egg and now has passed from this world into the next. Few Trainers have ever managed to soothe it.
author: inquis1

entry: Its skirt is made of possessed dead petals. Many florists offer dead flowers to them as a peace offering.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: POKENAME are considered pests of great nuisance, due to waiting until residents are asleep and then waking them with incessant spectral scratching noises in the walls.
author: sk372

entry: When exposed to the moonlight, POKENAME's gaseous petals glimmer radiantly. Under bright sunshine, they shine like fire.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME are an ephemeral presence that dart aimlessly through haunted forests. People who wander through those forests often report a POKENAME zipping by on a gust of wind.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drifts silently over marshes, leaving behind a trail of damp mist. Its gaseous body smells faintly of pond water. If angered, it releases a burst of swamp gas that causes dizziness and uncontrollable laughter in those who inhale it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is said POKENAME is formed from fog dissipating on a moonless night. Its favorite haunts are abandoned cabins in the woods, where it startles unaware hikers before taking shelter for the night.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME steals offerings left on graves, hoarding them in abandoned crypts. It protects its stolen treasures with a dense, toxic fog.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is frequently seen in abandoned areas where it seeks to pull pranks on youths snooping around the location. Its impish demeanor makes it a common trickster character in stories.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Tales tell of it burrowing into headstones to absorb memories of the deceased. If it deems the person cruel in their past life, it shatters their grave marker in disdain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits a chilling fog that makes those nearby feel constantly watched. This haunting presence can drain the resolve of even the bravest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found around active lava flows, forming from the gasses that are released from the molten rock. Their presence is noxious to living creatures, but they do not travel far from the flows that birth them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME resides near cemeteries in hot climates. Its body is composed of molten, purple tar. This strange substance emits a faint, otherworldly glow at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drift toward lost hikers in snowy mountains, gathering around them. It is said they guide rescuers to those who succumb to the cold.
author: .izik

entry: The gaseous antlers of POKENAME radiate an unsettling energy. Psychics claim it allows them to see far into the past.
author: .izik

entry: Anything which comes in contact with its gaseous tail will be stained purple, as if airbrushed. Strangely, the color always fades by midnight.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME balances atop gravestones to train its focus and agility. This habit is curious since it can effortlessly float when needed.
author: .izik

entry: Children are often told that POKENAME were once kids that played with electrical sockets. Of course, there's no actual truth to this whatsoever.
author: enemyphase

entry: POKENAME release dangerously hot and toxic gases. A person trapped in a closed space with them will lose consciousness within minutes.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME are an evanescent presence in Johto forests and travel through timelines to guide ancient spirits. It is rumored that they pass messages from loved ones in the distant past, though this has yet to be confirmed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME projects illusions of unfulfilled desires to distract its prey. These mirages keep victims wandering in circles, unable to escape.
author: .izik

entry: Legends tell of POKENAME luring travelers in swamps to witches' huts. Those who follow risk losing their sanity to the swamp's shadowy curse.
author: .izik

entry: It disguises itself as a potted plant, often resting on graves. Visitors who linger too long might find themselves startled by its sudden movements.
author: .izik

entry: The wings of a POKENAME have an evanescent quality, as they vaporize into a mist before anything physical hits them. POKENAME chase after baby Pokémon out of haunted forests, often over long distances.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Supposedly surpassing death, POKENAME has given up its body to turn into psychic energy, making it much more powerful and protective.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME is said to appear before lonely souls at night, silently compelling them to pursue it. It is said those who follow it vanish without a trace and never return.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is strictly nocturnal and typically lives in secluded tributaries. It has a singular goal: create dams ad infinitum. When a dam begins to cause more harm than good, it takes it down before starting again elsewhere.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Gastly has become the main spirit in control after fusion, the other 107 seeing it as the leader. This allows it to use the other spirits to focus and enhance its own ghostly abilities.
author: sk372

entry: It lurks in trees above cemeteries, waiting for the right moment to strike. It often devours food offerings left for the departed, leaving mourners baffled.
author: .izik

entry: This Shield Fossil has become possessed. With an iron face and a vaporous body, POKENAME has no physical weak points.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME haunts ancient temples dedicated to the worship of Pokémon in the past. It has been observed possessing statues and changing their positions, but to what end it does this is not yet known.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's handle and head are gaseously linked. Though its mind is in the handle, its head embodies the grief of the dead.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's "blade" may seem harmless as it is made of gas, but once it permeates flesh, it poisons it from the inside.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It appears in the homes of people whose pets have recently passed. Despite being made of gas, Trainers say they feel it when it lays on their laps.
author: melodydelune

entry: Legends say it manipulates the spirits of children, using them to play pranks on graveyard visitors. The laughter of unseen children is said to echo through the air when it's near.
author: .izik

entry: It was once believed POKENAME's possession of radios let it channel voices of the dead. This has been disproven.
author: .izik

entry: It possesses candles left on graves, lighting them with its eerie presence. It stays hidden within the wax until the candle completely melts away.
author: .izik

entry: It manipulates smoke from nearby fires, directing it toward foes. This choking haze is often used to incapacitate those who cross its path.
author: .izik

entry: Pushing down on one of POKENAME's nails will agitate it to the point of unleashing a Curse on those who disturbed it in revenge. It creates a gaseous hand to poison and suffocate enemies.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon is unfathomably fast because it is nearly weightless. It scours the skies in search of a victim to scare, as it can move without making a single sound.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME is usually seen wandering cemeteries at night, stopping at each grave as if in mourning. It stays longer for those who have not been visited in a long time. Once dawn arrives, it slinks back into the forest to await the twilight.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME wear talismans on their bodies because they can cause great calamity if left to their own devices. When granting wishes, they corrupt the wish into an effect contrary to what is desired.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME phase through solid objects to escape Trainers and never leave a single scintilla to prove they were there. Their elusive nature causes some people to doubt they exist at all.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It plays mischievous tricks on miners, shutting off their equipment unexpectedly. This often leads to confusion and frustration deep underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME linger in old factories where they operate machinery with their ethereal bodies. It is said that they carry the will of workers who were harmed by the factory's machines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stalks around schools and playgrounds, causing mischief directed at school bullies. Because of this, it is thought to be the combined malice of children who are being picked on and seeks revenge on their behalf.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME fiercely defends its mausoleum home from intruders. Its powerful Shadow Ball serves as a warning to keep graverobbers away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes mournful wails that echo through graveyards at night. The sounds are thought to be its way of calling to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME likes to prank people. It appears in someone's sight and then quickly vanishes, scaring the person and making them wonder where it went.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME is fiercely territorial and will defend its nest at all costs. It's impossible to run away from as it will phase through anything to reach its foe.
author: archserpent

entry: POKENAME appears in nightmares and can break out of the dreaming world into the waking one. It only has enough energy to expel a ghostly breath that sows the seed for more nightmares to follow, before fading back into nothing.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If its pranks fail to amuse, it retaliates by letting loose shrill, horrible screeches. These sounds can disorient and frighten even the bravest of souls.
author: .izik

entry: Most of a POKENAME's body is light and gaseous, centered around a heart gemstone. They typically stay in caves to stay safe from the wind and eat the gemstones found within.
author: entomoxie

entry: The individual flames on a POKENAME are said to each be the soul of a child who died in the forest. POKENAME take life energy from plants around them to keep their own bodies from withering away.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME needs either steady winds or no winds at all in order to stay in place. It loves playing tricks with people and other Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Drifting high in the atmosphere, the wings of POKENAME are composed of a very thin mist. As light as their bodies are, POKENAME are often dispersed by the jet stream and can be found all over the world.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's body is composed of 47.5% gas, and is light enough that it no longer needs to fly.
author: shayzis_ozaki

entry: POKENAME can control the air around them, reducing stormy gales to gentle breezes. They need to do this because their bodies are delicate enough to dwindle away otherwise.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME possess ancient steel effigies, their gaseous bodies animating and filling the statues as a means of protecting themselves. They roam through these old ruins deep in the night, the clanking of their movements filling the night air.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME reside inside sunken ships at the bottom of the sea where their heartbroken cries can be heard for miles. They collect old, decrepit skeletons inside the ship as though they were mourning a nautical crew.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Tales claim POKENAME digs up the graves of the dishonest, revealing hidden secrets. Its eerie actions unsettle those nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is as light as air. It tends to hover over its Trainer's shoulder. This gets annoying after a while, but it's too affectionate to understand.
author: .realthree

entry: Some say if anyone touches POKENAME's ectoplasmic mane, they will be tormented by restless spirits. Worse yet, any who touch it will endure a crushing Shadow Claw.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME extends its tongue to lick gemstones found in caves. If it discovers a particularly tasty cluster, it laughs uncontrollably for unknown reasons.
author: .izik

entry: If touched, the blue flames amidst POKENAME's gaseous ears and tail will cause an intense burn. Victims are said to only find relief if they offer POKENAME a sincere apology and some of their life force.
author: fancyskunk

entry: The gas POKENAME expels induces chills and foreboding feelings in those immersed in it. Haunted house attractions employ POKENAME in order to help further the spooky ambience with its smog.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were once believed to be born out of dying flames. In reality, the light from the fire just kept them at bay.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME is notorious for seeping into the cracks of old buildings. People exposed to its gases have reported unsettling hallucinations.
author: busilisk

entry: When there is an accident in a mining shaft, some say a POKENAME is born. Wild POKENAME dislike intruders and perform harmless pranks and dangerous stunts to make sure none invade the desolate place they call home.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When there is an accident in a mining shaft, some say a POKENAME is born. Wild POKENAME dislike intruders and perform harmless pranks and dangerous stunts to make sure none invade the desolate place they call home.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME adore collecting shiny objects. They will hide from strong winds in abandoned buildings, looking to outsiders like eerie, flickering lights.
author: essie

entry: POKENAME releases phantasmal bubbles that store the energy from its headaches. When the bubbles inevitably pop, it will experience another headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME surrounds itself with clouds of toxic gas mixed with water vapor. It can also freeze these clouds to create poisonous snowstorms.
author: hophoppip

entry: An angry spirit that haunts the ocean, POKENAME creates ghostly rocks to fling at all who come near. The only creatures that escape its ire are Relicanth and its related fusions.
author: sk372

entry: The gas this Pokémon produces causes extreme anger in anything that breathes it. Don't drive with POKENAME, it will give you road rage.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is incredibly vengeful, never forgetting the faces of those who hurt it. It'll drag people who've wronged it to their grave.
author: ohok3441

entry: When calm, the mist POKENAME produces is cool to the touch. In battle, it rises in temperature to burn opponents.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME flood the battlefield with gas indiscriminately. It takes a Trainer with a strong will to gain the respect of a POKENAME and teach them control.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME roams cities at night hoping to find leftovers of unfinished meals. If it is encountered during a meal by a Trainer, it hypnotizes the Trainer and forces them to find food for it.
author: skleegamer

entry: A lively Pokémon that lives for the hunt. POKENAME haunts prey from a distance. Once it has gathered enough fear, it leaves the prey alone.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's body is made up almost entirely of a toxic gas that resembles a Bellsprout. It can rarely be found in forests where it blends into the darkness in order to capture prey of any size.
author: sakuraneko

entry: Targets struggle to perceive POKENAME's dark, gaseous body in the shadows before they are incapacitated by its paralytic breath. Few POKENAME have ever been successfully trained.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Being incorporeal, POKENAME has a very weak magnetic charge inside. Even when right next to something its magnets should attract, the objects will only move slightly and slowly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a particularly mischievous creature that enjoys scaring people who venture too close to icy shores. Its pranks, however, often save lives by moving people away from waters so cold they could cause drowning.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Due to its unstable anatomy, it can barely stay upright. Sightings of POKENAME swarming abandoned areas inspired some of the oldest horror stories.
author: leeto64

entry: POKENAME is barely able to keep any semblance of form in its body. As it moves, pratically anything will be engulfed whole in its mass of sludge.
author: leeto64

entry: No stranger to battle, POKENAME knows the rules, and so does their Trainer. They are always thinking of a full commitment and would never give up.
author: fauxblue

entry: A Haunter that retained its more gaseous state from Gastly, POKENAME is often preferred to normal Haunter, as its mischievous nature seems less malicious than the norm by comparison.
author: sk372

entry: There are ancient tomes stating POKENAME originate from ancient curses. They are said to turn humans into their kind.
author: pokebio

entry: It shadows the elderly, ensuring they are never alone in their final days. Though eerie, its presence is often comforting to those it follows.
author: .izik

entry: The source of many tales of haunted caves, POKENAME hides itself within cavern walls, waiting for the perfect moment to snake out from solid rock and spook unwary visitors.
author: sk372

entry: Only able to be found in the liminal state between wakefulness and sleep, POKENAME delights in feeding on the nightmares of young children.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME hides in the shadows and looks for people it can put to sleep. When its successful, it will absorb the sleeper's soul to increase its power.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME are depressed ghouls mourning the loss of their mother. You can hear the sounds of its wails on dark, rainy nights.
author: dodoowner_

entry: With control of their limbs across the astral plane, POKENAME can launch kicks that otherwise seem physically impossible.
author: entomoxie

entry: With control of their limbs across the astral plane, POKENAME can launch kicks that otherwise seem physically impossible.
author: entomoxie

entry: Both of POKENAME's heads are skilled hunters. They often split up and try to see who can feast on the most prey.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is typically found in dark, shadowy areas. It uses its rhythmic red light to attract unsuspecting victims, before latching on to them to drain their life force.
author: vlavoc

entry: POKENAME are found in large groups wherever lightning has struck recently. Several Trainers have witnessed them harnessing the leftover electricity and sharing it around with weaker Haunkids.
author: excelline

entry: Fables state that POKENAME will cause fires to attract a large amount of people in one area. Once gathered, it consumes their souls to grow stronger.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Ancient myths suggest POKENAME were once part of a tribe lost to a volcanic disaster. Their burning tongues feed on heat and energy from others.
author: garret95

entry: Once considered to be a malicious Pokémon, POKENAME are now believed to be the ones that ferry souls to the afterlife. They often are spotted near shipwrecks, and some even use the wreckage as a den.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME despise having bones removed from their bodies, which makes excavating fossils difficult for paleontologists. Their level of aggression is correlated to how many bones they are missing, so paleontologists excavate fossils of Kabutops last.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A ghostly dragon spirit that haunts remote islands, POKENAME is not particularly malevolent, but much prefers solitude. It conjures up fearsome illusions of dragons to dissuade people from approaching its home.
author: sk372

entry: Though POKENAME is covered in spectral flames, its body is quite cold to the touch. It is most active on moonless nights, stalking its victims silently.
author: mepp.

entry: Usually found haunting battlefields, POKENAME originally was seen as a specter of death. It was discovered it seeks out the wounded and feeds them a tincture made from its ghostly leaves, stabilizing their conditions.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME seeks out buildings with new inhabitants and then pulls pranks, such as tapping people on the shoulder while invisible or throwing items around rooms. It is easily chased off by pets like Houndour, leading it to find a new place to torment.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are ethereal beings that phases through dense objects, such as trees or branches. They often torment and chase other Pokémon while zipping through the forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Surprisingly, POKENAME is very friendly. It motions for those nearby to approach, and if they do, it sneezes a gel onto them that, upon contact with skin, causes uncontrollable laughter and triggers dopamine release.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A Raticate that was once a key battler in someone's party. It came to its end and was buried in Lavender Town, where it came back from the grave.
author: theheroict

entry: POKENAME feeds on fear, so it maliciously haunts urban areas with dangerous tricks. The red orb necklace glows brighter as it absorbs more fear, making it harder to hide until it consumes the stored fear.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME find detritus and rubble left over from lava flows and possess them, reanimating the rocks and creating a simulacrum of the molten rock that once carried them. Their bodies glow with an eerie purple light from the gases they produce.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swoop over prey with their aubergine wings and pick them up with disembodied talons. They are particularly fond of Mareep because they are easy for their talons to grab onto.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In several cultures, there is a superstition that believes POKENAME travels around the world to sap creativity from artists to the point they give in to despair. No matter the weather conditions, the paint-like fluid on its tail is runny yet cold.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Childlike in demeanor, POKENAME often trick Trainers into holding their hand under the guise of seeking comfort. They then administer a harmless electric shock and run away chortling.
author: enemyphase

entry: POKENAME bring messages from people who have long passed in an effort to help grieving families. Their efforts have mixed feelings attached and may cause anger in some people who are not ready to hear the message.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in abandoned cottages. It invites lost travelers into its home, where it cares for them while also draining them of their vitality.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The Fire Blast from POKENAME is capable of melting metal in seconds. The sheer force of these flames destroys their arms, which swiftly regenerate.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME can enter into a momentary incorporeal state that allows them to phase through physical objects. This is handy when chasing other Pokémon or Trainers when they toss obstacles their way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drifts unseen, blending perfectly into its surroundings. Those who linger nearby report feeling drained and aging faster. It is believed that POKENAME feeds on the vital energy that seeps from its unsuspecting victims.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is territorial and often winds up fighting others of its kind for the right to haunt a specific locale. When their ghostly hands clash against each other, eerie metallic screeches course through the air.
author: sk372

entry: Many find wild POKENAME unsettling as it rarely moves; it merely stares off into the distance until morning comes, where it fades away until the next night. It was recorded once that, when one vanished for the day, it exploded into toxic gas.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though POKENAME appears threatening, it is actually one of the friendliest Ghost-type Pokémon fusions. However, should its trainer be threatened, it will not hold anything back.
author: wh3reverimayr0am

entry: It cries for hours and hours. No one is aware of the reason.
author: bucklin

entry: It cries for hours and hours. No one is aware of the reason.
author: bucklin

entry: Ignore its ribbon's beckoning and stay clear of the range of POKENAME's chain. Its teeth quickly suck its victims' lives away.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME can turn intangible while they run, phasing through trees or boulders. Whenever they feel mischievous, they emerge from the ground to scare Trainers and Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses illusions to make its territory shift and squirm. Anybody caught in the illusion is promptly licked by POKENAME, draining their life force and feeding the illusion.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: This Pokémon, despite its unnerving appearance, is very affectionate. Unfortunately, its licks have been known to paralyze its Trainer.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's flowers hide its ghostly vines, which it uses to draw the life force from its prey. They can be seen around graveyards, stealing the flowers recently left there.
author: mistymagius

entry: Since its arms are not connected to its body, POKENAME can strike its opponents from a safe distance. However, POKENAME will only pick fights with other Ghost-types.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its nine ghostly tails to create illusions that deceive both people and Pokémon. It is said to lurk in dark forests, mischievously waiting to scare unsuspecting victims.
author: thepandasharky

entry: It uses multiple hands to beckon victims in different directions. It cloaks itself in shadows while it sleeps.
author: .towerxvi

entry: POKENAME has the ability to shift and change forms, using it to disguise themselves as objects or people. When something gets too close, POKENAME will lick them with a long tongue, draining their life force.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: POKENAME thrives in the darkness. If you see a lonely red flame in the shadows, flash it with light to dispel it.
author: .fedoraman
